First I want to say that the leasing and office staff are awesome and helpful. My floorplan and the amenities are both great at this place as well, but it's an older building and it shows a lot in the little things. I've been here less than two months and I've already dealt with four major maintenance issues. I generally really enjoy my apartment here, however, sometimes it feels like I'm just waiting for the next maintenance disaster to strike.

I like the MAA Medical District a lot, close to workplace. Kroger is just next door. The leasing staff are super friendly and very helpful. Couldn't give 5 Stars because the stomping noise during midnight time from the neighbors upstairs has been annoying. Try to cope with lack of sleep and fatigue everyday. Not sure if building 4 have more problems.
It is a very old property with constant break ins, homeless people, and gun shots.

Overall colonial reserve at medical District is a decent place to live. But do not expect flashy over the top amenities or much leasing office/community involvement.  This property  consistently increases rent rates to keep up with the market but obviously does not reinvest that money for the betterment of the community.  It appears ok on the outside, but  take the time to walk the property yourself if possible. You’ll be glad you did.  Car break-ins are the norm but as is the case in the general area.  As we all know,  crime doesn’t have an address-  but you sure have a choice on what to call “home”.
Very nice and friendly staff.

The complex is nice, quiet and convenient. The workers are nice. Unfortunately, the surrounding area has become more untidy and there are increasingly things needing maintenance or attention which are slipping. It is still better than many complexes in the area.

Genuine staff in the leasing office and on the maintenance team. Rooms are cozy and the location is second to none. One of the best parts about Colonial Reserve is that they are one of the few apartments in Dallas that accept all dogs breeds (even the "aggressive" breeds). This has made my stay here 1000x better.
I?ve enjoyed living here. It?s my second year here.
Property is amazing. Office staff is incredibly friendly and does a great job planning social events. The maintenance staff is bar none.
Good complex, good staff.

It?s a safe community, the people are friendly. The leasing office is super helpful and everyone who works there is really nice (especially Cynthia!!) The property is kept clean and maintenance does a great job.

I love living at Colonial Reserve Medical District! The building is maintained well, the staff has always been top notch, and the convenience of the location has exceeded my expectations. This has been the best apartment experience I have ever had.

I like my apartment a lot, good location good price, quiet. My car was broken into which is a bummer, I wish there was WiFi in the workout room, and having a better package delivery or pickup system would be great

I have lived here for about 2 weeks. It has been quiet and nice. It?s very close to the hospital where I work. I do wish some things would get updated. However, I would recommend this as somewhere to live if you work nearby. It sure beats the traffic.

I call maintenance and they take care of the problem ASAP! The office is always having great meet and greet your neighbors and offering cheap breakfast and dinners! Not to forget to mention the great dallas skyline view. Great place to live.

Everything is pretty simple at this complex. It's not flashy or over-the-top, but it's no dump either. It's just right for those who seek comfortable living. The location is great! Especially for those who work downtown/uptown(5 min drive away) or in Medical District. There is a Kroger next door which is very convenient. The DART station is literally across the street, giving you access to all major areas of Dallas. Only complaint is there are no resident social events put on by the staff. Overall a good place to stay.

I've lived at Arpeggio for a while. My experience has been a mixed bag. There are definitely some pros: the location is great, garage parking is ample, and the staff is nice. They also host some fun resident events, and depending on the concessions you manage to snag, the price can be fairly affordable.

However, the cons are hard to ignore. The maintenance team seems pretty lazy, often leaving things unfinished or taking too long to address issues. The building isn’t as secure as it appears either, which is concerning.

But the biggest issue by far is the irresponsible pet ownership here. Dog owners frequently don’t pick up after their pets. It’s common to see dogs running around off-leash. Worst of all is the constant barking—at all hours of the day and night. Whether it's in the halls or the dog park, which is inconveniently located right outside people's windows, the excessive barking is out of control. The noise echoes throughout the halls and you can hear it loudly in your apartment. 

This isn’t an occasional problem; it’s an ongoing issue that makes living here unbearable at times. Especially when it ruins your sleep. If the dog situation were under control, Arpeggio could be a decent place to live. Unfortunately, this one con overshadows any positives the community has to offer.

Arpeggio was one of the first apartments to catch my eye when I was looking and man, i took an in-person tour and never looked back! Living here has been an absolute dream and the maintenance and leasing office staff are fast, friendly and all around amazing. Krysti in the leasing office is literally THE BEST. Arpeggio is the best kept secret in Dallas imo

It has been amazing living here so far. The maintenance team is amazing and very fast at providing service after a request is submitted. The location is very walkable to so many restaurants, workout places, bars and other attractions! I’ve never once felt unsafe while living here and feel like the property is very well maintained. I would recommend this apartment to anyone! Especially if you like the convenience of being next to the American Airlines Center!!

Horrible management!! Horrible communication and a lack of professionalism. I will be homeless due to their negligence. I have paid a deposit and signed paperwork and they still keep giving my apartment away.
Great space, comfortable living in a great location that puts you in the heart of Dallas innovation surrounding my multiple amenities within walking distance.

I rented a studio apartment thats very nice and the design is  great and very functional.
Good JOB!

Pests. Unkept grounds and trash rooms. Management doesn’t care. Fire alarms have gone off for years at random and have lasted for hours. It’s a nice apartment in a nice area but you will regret moving in here. Find another building in the area.

I have never written a review like this in my life and would give 0 stars if possible. Trust me when I say this DO NOT MOVE HERE. I have never lived at a place that is so poorly managed as this place is. The fire alarms have been an issue for years and they constantly go off throughout all hours of the day and night. I have tried to contact local management, upper management, fire Marshalls, the Dallas city hall and there has not been any fix. The fire alarm has gone off 13 different times just over the last two months. There is rusted stagnant water that has been sitting near my unit the last two weeks. The trash has not been emptied in lord knows how long and the trash rooms are piled up with garbage posing health and pest concerns. You might as well just throw away $2k+ a month if you choose to live here.

I lived hear for a year, and it was horrible. 

Pros:
1. Location: location is great, please find any other apartment complex in the neighborhood.
2. The maintenance men are good and hardworking.

Cons:
1. Management: The management is horrible and never takes responsibility for any problems in the building.They will lie straight to your face. When I toured, I was shown the rooftop pool which would be opening soon. It opened 9 months into my lease. 
2. Broken elevators: In the 12 months that I lived here the elevator in my building was out for 8 months. The freight elevator was out the entire time. Any time I would ask management for an update, they would tell me that the elevator would be back up by the end of the week.
3. Flooding: my apartment flooded, and management did nothing about it.
4. Gates/Security: The gates were ofter broken and homeless people come in and hide in the parking garage. Multiple cars have been broken into and management will do nothing about it.

10. Fire alarms: Fire alarms would go off randomly throughout the entire building and not stop for at least 45 minutes, so good luck if you WFH.
Ravello is a great place to live really close to downtown Dallas! Been living there since october and I have enjoyed it ever since. I totally recommend this apartment complex to be your next home!
There have been a lot of great amenity updates since I’ve moved in. Still leaves a bit to be desired, but no major complaints. A great property in a great location!
Great location, great space, maintenance and amenities could use a little upgrade. Amenities are outdated compared to close by apartments.  Otherwise a nice apartment.

I current live here and have been living here since October 2024. Gables Republic Tower is Awesome! The view is amazing especially for the price. I love the staff who have been amazing with getting repairs done in a timely manner. My apartment had leaking issues. It was fully repaired with minor issues but the fact that they took out the walls which gives me a sense of relief in knowing that I don’t have to deal with mold. I lived in an apartment in which I had a ceiling leak and it was not repaired properly that lead to me dealing with mold. Management at that apartment did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING! Well, that’s not the car with Republic Towers. I haven’t had any issues with the elevators since I’ve been here. What I like the most is that there are less apartments on each floor. Needless to say, I’m going to live here FOREVER! Great location, great parking, great staff, etc! There is no perfect apartment but Republic Towers is perfect for me!

The inside of the apartments are nice and most come with a view of the city. The maintenance staff is also friendly. The issue is the elevators are always down. It can take up to 25 minutes for an elevator which is unacceptable with a building that houses over 200 people. Would not recommend living here.

I would love to be able to post a positive review. Love the location and it's one of the few buildings downtown with decent visitor parking. However, elevator situation has made this building unbearable at times. LITERAL wait for the elevator is consistently 30 minutes as of late. While the management at the building is apologetic and equally frustrated, that doesn't make the situation any more bearable. There is a capital investment that needs to be made that Gables corporate isn't willing to make. With so many other options downtown, there ARE better options.
I’ve lived at Gables Republic Tower for 2 years now. I still love ?? it like the first day I moved in. Everything I need is in walking distance.

Living at Gables is a good experience. Location, apartment size, and soundproof walls are my favorites.  Admittedly, the upkeep of the building has gone down since covid.  Could be due to staffing issues.  Hopefully corporate can get the upkeep and maintenance back on track to make experience living here even better.
Unfortunately elevator's maintenance sometimes are a problem. For the most part, good service, very centric! I love that I can walk to work!
I would recommend the Georgian Apts. Kind and friendly people and very professional.
The pricing is affordable and it is centrally located- which is good.
Good clean community staff professional and always helpful. Safe place no problems.
No me sirve el baño ni la tina ni el refrigerador lavamanos viejo inodoro nunca a funcionado y nunca me han querido arreglar el problema o cambiarme el inodoro
The Community is clean and very quiet! Neighbors are really nice!
The office staff used to be great. Now I avoid the office staff as they don't care what so ever. The maintenance staff is awesome, the office not so much.

I lived here for three years. The complex is not maintained at all and the office staff does not care about anything but collecting rent.

If you like dog waste everywhere, this complex is for you.
If you like repairs not being done, this complex is for you.
If you like roaches, this complex is for you.
If you like overflowing dumpsters, this complex is for you.

Don't let them fool you with "newly renovated apartments". It's the same roach infested building with a fresh coat of paint.

Management will talk a tough game in emails and text messages about lease violations, but they never actually DO anything. It's all empty words.

I'm not just making things up. I had to sue them because they couldn't be bothered to fix a leaking bathroom ceiling for THREE MONTHS. My A/C didn't work from September 2022 until I left in April 2023.

And to top it all off, I was charged for renter's insurance for the last year of my lease when I already had a policy. And they throw in a bogus "Building and Facility fee" that's not on your lease.

They don't care and you should stay as far away as you can.

Absolutely disgusting and disturbing how this place is managed. 

My oven has been out, for 6 months, which they have “fixed” 3 times but it still doesn’t work. 

I have counted 36 days without hot water in the last 10 months, 3 times going a week or two without hot water. (Water bill still $130 a month, even though I have to shower and cook elsewhere)

The roaches just got under control but they are still there.  I can not wait to get the hell out of here. 

The people in the housing offices are nice and try to help, but their management is pisspore and should not be allowed to operate. 


Not to mention my neighbor was shot and killed 10 feet away from me. What did the housing office do? Sent me a text message the next day and say rent is due. It took them 2 months to get windows and sliding doors replaced from the bullets. 

Stay away if you plan on keeping your sanity, I broke my peace and cussed them out on behalf of the Residents of the Slums of McCallum North.

If you are not able to afford anything else and have nowhere else to go, maybe these apartments are ok. 2 stars only for affordability . The staff was nice, honest, and I'm sure the tenants are for what it's worth. Being poor or down on your luck doesn't make people bad.

This is expensive poverty though.

The office was being remodeled and you could not easily walk through and nobody tried to make a path. They were not enthused or "customer" focused, not like other places. I feel like they were just filling a seat and not in a career, just someone who needed a job with no real training (I could be wrong on that who knows). Again, they were super nice and honest but lacked enthusiasm. Not that I need that, but it gives you an idea of the atmosphere here. It feels downtrodden, like the owners don't care or don't have the money to actually care for the apartments. Some of the stairs were showing signs of having moved or sinking right outside the office and other locations as I drove around.

As I was in the office a tenant came in to talk about a problem that was not being dealt with yet. Then the apt she showed me smelled and was falling apart naturally from lack of maintenance, granted it was "about" to be renovated. Maybe someone just moved out, but why let them destroy the apt that way. The whole time, she was so matter of fact about the condition. She seemed to have no issues with how it was, like this is the norm. When I asked if this was how all the apts are, she shrugged yes. I believe they also had vinyl rolled "wood" flooring not real wood. I get it, it's being remodeled at some point, but don't show potential tenants that, honestly, just say I have nothing to show, Please.

All the  A/C vents I saw were nasty on the outside and inside the vents, even in the office. I can't say every, but every car I saw was dented or not well taken care of either.

They have a shady "hold" fee, another deposit fee the same price, an App fee, and still an Admin fee. PLUS the actual deposit based on your credit. This just about doubled your initial move-in cost. I could live here if I had to, but it would be uncomfortable for sure. Even their lowest price doesn't justify the condition. This is lack of care of a business or a failing business model, one or the other.

I'm sure they'll respond and rationalize all of this, but let's be real, it's not the worst but right above that. I'd rather you didn't respond... I'd prefer it actually.

The McCallum Meadows Apartments can be rated as average, considering the amenities and services available there. It is also very similar to the other block of apartments located within the same vicinity, and it has a number of students( from University of Texas at Dallas), occupying it as well. It was built in the early 80's and I would suggest that an overall renovation should be carried out on it. Some of it's facilities are old or worn out.
Ok apartment with high rent, use exterior paint instead of interior paint, and toilet makes semi flushing noises without me being around it.

3700M really focuses on building a community that is fun, inclusive, and engaging. The weekly events and activities provide residents with new ways to connect and meet one another. I just moved to Dallas from a different state and the staff and residents made me feel so welcome!
Great building, love the apartment, love the staff, and the amenities. Would love for communication to be worked on, that’s about it :)

Love the location and amenities here if you're looking for somewhere walkable this is the perfect location and feels very safe. However we did have a pretty disappointing move in experience with our apartment not being ready at all, the maintenance is very quick and efficient which we quickly learned. I don't think this experience necessarily defines the complex as a whole and still recommend it to others looking to move in.
The community is beautiful, clean, and welcoming! Our move in process was very efficient and stress-free with the help of the amazing leasing team. So excited to for this new season of life at 3700M!
3700M great place to live in the perfect area with food, shopping, and recreational activities in walking distance. The staff managing the props amazing and very thoughtful of its residents.

The elevator is always out of service in building 1 and creates problems for package deliveries. I don’t understand why in 2023 they haven’t installed some sort of package locker system to make things easier for delivery drivers and residents. The leasing office also refuses to hold packages.

It seems like the new owners don’t really care about maintaining the property and keeping their residents. I’ll continue to update every few months/weeks. The only positive that has come with the new owners is they added onsite security

This place seemed great in the beginning, but quickly fell apart. Toward the end of my lease the property was acquired by another company. The entire property is covered in trash, they have one person cleaning the two buildings and surrounding property. Trash rooms are atrocious. Management was supposed to input my intent to vacate, and straight up quit. I was then made responsible for their own mistake. I attempted to make contact with the office and corporate with poor customer service. After months of calling, and emailing without any return correspondence the property continued to make us financially responsible for their own error and placed the charges on my partners credit report. This place is the worst and not worth the headache. Run….
Terrible …… between maintenance men breaking and making situations worse , no one to ever pick up the phone and also rats in the hall save yourself time and money . Worse two years of my life

This place doesn't deserve a star. Lived here for 2 years and just moved out!! Has gone downhill tremendously. Got new owners that don’t care. So bad that all employees quit and there’s only 1 person in the office and 1 maintenance person. The halls haven’t been cleaned in over a month!!! Car break ins every week and the only employee says she can’t do anything about anything!

My roommate and I lived here for almost three years and once they got the new management it has gotten bad. Management is very unfriendly and hard to talk to. Good luck with move out because you’ll get charged an arm and a leg for things you shouldn’t be charged for. I would not recommend anyone living here. Also not the safest area. I had a scary encounter and called the apartment complex management and they did absolutely nothing about it.
I feel like the whole time I have lived here I have gotten the short end of the stick. Very disappointed in what should have been a great experience, especially for the price.

**Great Value and Luxury Living in Downtown**

I absolutely love living here! You get incredible bang for your buck with these luxury units in downtown.

**Parking:** The parking is secure, with a gated entrance and hotel valet on the first floor, meaning there’s constant activity 24/7, which helps deter crime.

With only 150 units, it’s easy to get to know your neighbors, which is a big plus!

The rooftop pool is fantastic, with an attached TV room and restrooms. It’s rarely crowded, and you almost never see strangers up there.

There are great amenities like a full dog wash, an art studio, a music room, and more.

A huge bonus for me is the park across the street, where my doodle loves to explore.

If you’re considering moving downtown, I 100% recommend checking this place.

This place will file all your paperwork wrong, overcharge you to move in and never give you your deposit back. The rooms are small and depressing and they will say anything to get you to sign a lease. If you like to walk out of your home and have homeless people harass you then this is the place for you.
It was an amazing experience living at 1900 Pacific and I would highly recommend that anyone looking for residence in Dallas to take a look at 1900 Pacific.

1900 Residences are wonderful!!! It is more than an apartment, but a community of fun loving people. The large shared room is perfect for business and get togethers with friends and the artistic decor throughout makes for a very chic living experience. I love that there are so many restaurants and attractions within walking distance as well.

I've been living at 1900 Pacific since it opened it has been a fun experience watching this property continue to develop every single day.  The community here is unlike any other and the staff are dedicated to helping the residents.  I love my A1 floorplan - perfect size, great kitchen, but the shower/tub combo in the bathroom is my favorite.SO much value in this property, I am very lucky to have found it!

You can hear every move you neighbor takes above you. The apartment never recovered from the freeze, ongoing construction for months that just stopped with no clean up. Cars are broken into frequently. Management is slow to get anything fixed. There are much better apartments.

Do not move here.

Random toilet in hallway with broken fire alarm, exposed wires, taped over fire sprinkler and alarm, nails, dumpsters sitting for months, materials taking up parking spaces and attracting vagabonds, etc.

Extremely unsafe conditions that get worse everyday with no response from management. I have literally asked for lights in the stairway and hallways  over 5 times, even after we had an intruder arrested by the cops múltiple times, Including one time near said stairwell.  Still waiting for lights in the stairwell. Still waiting for trash policy to be enforced, the hallways are filled with trash and roaches.  Had to wait over 3 weeks to get a key fob to even open the gate because they "were out".  Broken glass in front of my garage, constant smell of marijuana sifting through my air vents.  The construction from the storm has been ongoing and done in an extremely unsafe manner, open walls, nails, paint, open insulation, piles of construction trash in front of your door, piles of trash in the stairwells.  The construction crew just stopped showing up. there are piles of wet insulation and materials everywhere, ripped open exposed walls, etc.  Roaches infested my oven and the exterminator the apt uses told me to get a new oven and the apartment refused.

Don't lease- choose another option nearby. The pool is always packed with people that aren't from the apartments and it makes it hard to enjoy, the apartments have been under construction for months and the management does not care, trash pick up is spotty but they bill you consistently, and they just hit me with a $945 fee even though my lease is coming to an end. I lived here 3 years and now absolutely regret having spent so much time and money. The gates don't like properly and the crime nearby is a problem. Choose another complex.

Apartment we rented was smaller than the one shown to us and were not made aware of the size difference
New countertops were shown in the model and told they would be in our unit, they were not.
Carpet in living room was not replaced and had to live in a work site for the first few days as they had misplaced the paperwork after I had confirmed remodel had been complete 3 times.
Maintenance comes into apartment even when you request a time be set up.
No onsite security or cameras to watch the lot, have witnessed multiple vehicle break ins and the person get away as cops are called.
No adequate guest parking and no way to allow guests to park in the complex.

The apartment is nice and the amenities are great but they need to improve the parking situation and also improve the security on the property.

I moved into this apartment in March of 2017, and they have gone through 2-3 office managers since I've been here. 

We were originally told that we would have an upgraded apartment with the Bluetooth speakers... we moved in and that was not the case. 

Shortly after that my car got towed. 
I was not informed nor was the boyfriend that we needed parking permits. When I called.. the front desk the guy laughed and Said I'm surprised you made it this long without getting towed. I did not think it was funny and explained I never got the memo. He promised he would call his boss and call me back... nothing. I call back, and he says well we issued parking permits back in February. I MOVED IN IN MARCH! It was 220 to get my car out,  the tow company messed up my brake lines. They did, however, take it off my rent... a MONTH later. 

Shortly after that... 
Our car got stolen.... there is never enough parking, so we have to park on the street right in front of our balcony. (we work late nights and get home around 11 pm)
We constantly have people stealing chairs and stuff off our patio. 
I'm re-writing this review now because... I just watched a guy try to break into a truck,  I scared him off & reported it to the police. 

We chose this apartment complex because it had an awesome dog park... After moving in, we noticed old trees in the park were dead, and branches were falling off. We and other residents made quite a few complaints. NOTHING GOT DONE!! Until a massive branch fell and demolished a bench! A bench that residents sit on and dogs lay under. 
Finally, they closed down the park to get the trees removed... FOR ALMOST TWO MONTHS. We have a golden retriever and a Yorkie.. and no place to take them. 

Overall the staff is horrible... except the Main Boss lady Priscilla (I think that's the correct name)

Love the actual apartment and complex but can't enjoy it hearing everything your neighbors do.  I can hear side neighbors showering and even talking when I'm in my bathroom. When the child next door takes a bath and I take a bath at the same time it's pretty weird hearing him play and whatnot. I  hear every single step above neighbor takes. Literally pounds through my ceiling and shakes the light fixtures, he is only 160 pounds at most. I can hear drawers closing, toilet flushing, vacumming, anything being moved across the floor. I can't even drown it out with tv or music. I have complained to office and written above neighbor a polite letter. Also many units have built in Bluetooth speakers, which I love, but would love to just hear mine not neighbors as well. Road noise is also loud. This is an industrial area and right behind is the main post office so you hear 18 wheelers and trucks all through out the day and night.

I almost did not write this review- as I don’t want the embarrassment of living at this apartment building reflected onto my personal history-even though it was only for 14 days that I lived there- in which I had NO HOT WATER. The entire time- and I’m not the only one- which management reminded me of.

I had a “conversation” in person with management that I can only describe as traumatic. I’ve never been spoken to or treated this way by anyone in my life. They did not care that I moved in two weeks ago and had no hot water the entirety of that time-they tried to break me down-make me feel powerless and intimidate me into putting up with it. They talked in circles, would not answer my questions, lied countless times. Imagine a criminal defense lawyer interrogating a victim. I can not believe I paid this “company” MONEY and this is what I got in return.

Some other fun facts:
-They knew there was no hot water before I applied, signed my lease, and moved in
-You have to pay your first months rent by Moneygram at a CVS or Walmart (in person)
-my washing machine didn’t work-they replaced it with one that smelled NAUSEATING of mold and mildew. All of them do.
-maintenance ran it with bleach etc and it did NOTHING to help the smell
-I found 4 spiders in my apartment after moving in
-the hallways smell atrocious
-the elevators are like stepping inside a dumpster
-my carpet was SHAVED in various spots to hide stains- and then the shaved spots were filled with loose carpet to make it camouflaged. Until I vacuumed up the shreds....
-the parking garage is filled with spider webs, and extremely crammed.


And before someone from management responds to this telling me to email them... I’ve sent countless emails over the past week that have been ignored- and voicemail to your office.

I will admit, there was a brief period of time in which I honestly enjoyed living here. However, RSF has become an absolute joke. A cesspool, to put it bluntly. 

RSF is located directly (and I mean directly) next to a nightclub which attracts plenty of unsavory characters. Sure, it’s Dallas, but there was a murder committed in the street right outside the complex's front door in February 2019, and the area has only become more dangerous since. It’s normal to feel uncomfortable walking into the building at night. 

While I can’t imagine having a street-facing apartment, having a pool-facing unit isn’t any better. Your windows and walls will be thin and your neighbors will be inconsiderate. I promise. I understand it’s Uptown, but this place is unreasonably loud. Parties are held frequently, and your inconsiderate neighbors will leave their balcony doors open to let a breeze in. Often, they’ll go for a swim around 2:00am after a night out (the pool closes at 10:00pm, supposedly). This will cause the noise from their parties to reverberate off of the walls of the pool area, and travel directly to your ears through your single-paned, poorly insulated bedroom windows. If you request for the window gaps to be caulked to try to drown out some of the noise, or that the pool keyfob access be restricted after the pool closes, you’ll be told that this is a “fire hazard”. Your friendly management team will then smile and suggest that you contact their courtesy officer if you need help after hours. This officer is utterly useless. If you call him, he’ll call you back (sometimes), and when he does, he’ll ask irrelevant questions and make you feel guilty for bothering him. He’ll then say that management doesn’t empower him to really do anything about noise or to enforce pool quiet hours. This, ladies & gents, is the RSF customer service spin cycle. See where this is going?

The hallways will constantly reek of marijuana, pet (hopefully?) urine, and garbage. Oversized garbage will be stacked inside of the trash room because residents are too lazy to walk it down to the dumpster themselves. (This is irrelevant really, because the chute is often clogged and overflowing.) On top of this, the elevators will frequently be broken or out of service for “preventative” maintenance. I’ve seen BMWs that require less maintenance than these things do. I’m all for fitness, but lugging your groceries up 7-8 flights of stairs from the parking garage gets old after a while.

After about 2 years of living, I have to say that I am extremely satisfied with Routh Street Flats!

The complex is always very clean and stays pretty quiet, considering you live, basically in the heart of uptown. 

The management is amazing! Especially, the new manager Veronica, she truly goes above and beyond to hear you out and help you with anything you really need! She is incredible, and the whole stuff works really hard to make sure you are satisfied living here. 

I would definitely recommend this place!! 5 stars!
Love this property! Love this staff! Parking could be improved, but the staff totally makes up for it! I would recommend that you check this place out!

I moved into this property in January, and I have been impressed with all aspects of Routh Street Flats. First and foremost, the staff is what sets this place apart. Coming from a bigger property where service and staff were sub-par, this has been extremely refreshing. From the beginning, I could tell that Shayla was a huge asset to the community. She toured the community with me and really sold me on the amenities and apartments (brand new!) When I signed my lease, her great attitude and service has not stopped. If I am walking by the leasing office and she knows I have a package, she'll wave me down. Various members of the staff know my name. If I need help or have a question, they're always available. Shayla is very patient and puts up with my "get-togethers" on the rooftop (does a daytime party on the roof encourage or discourage people touring from moving in ?? lol) Shayla really is  A . [Also I love Lindsay and JR!]

Speaking of the rooftop, the amenities are insane in Routh Street! The rooftop is seriously unreal. My friends always want to come have a drink or hang out by the fire pit while enjoying the skyline views (hence my "get-togethers ;-)) The pool is also very nice, as is the gym. I also like the underground parking garage. 

Last, the apartments are finished out very tastefully. I love the light grey floors, roomy kitchen island, and granite. My closet it also nice and roomy.

Overall, I would recommend this property to anybody! In fact, I have recommended it to every friend whose leases run out who want to enjoy the best of uptown with the GREAT service that comes with a smaller property. -CJ
i feel i live with a dog apartment . i have to watch every step cause we have residents who let their pets pee just anywhere and don't wait to get to the dog park.

I moved out after about a year and half.  It is FULL of college kids. They party around the clock and the “security” who enforces noise orders doesn’t do a thing. I easily called them every night for a week and the neighbor kept going. A friend I made in the building has terminate his lease early because his neighbor would blast music at 3am. Awful place to live. Don’t be fooled.

I lived here for two years and although the experience started great the management of this property is horrible. It is not well maintained and has serious security issues. The garage door was broken for over 6 months and resulted in car thefts, a resident being robbed at gun point as well as cars stolen elsewhere being stashed in the garage. The bicycle room was also broken into several times. The elevators, hallways and pool are consistently dirty. I emailed management many times about all of the above issues and although they'd eventually reply (sometimes after several emails) nothing was ever done.

We recently visited an apartment for my daughter, who just graduated from medical school, and were shocked by the poor upkeep condition of the place. Despite the promising online photos, the apartment was filthy, with grime covering the surfaces and an unsettling number of bugs crawling around. It was a stark contrast to what we had expected for her first home as a new doctor. The experience was disheartening, emphasizing the importance of thorough in-person inspections before committing to a lease.

I completed my application and later that night i decided to take drive  around and inside the apartments since the gate was open at 9pm at night. Dirty mattress was laying in the back of the building along with other junk. Inside the parking garage is worse ,overflow trash cans , food bags everywhere, debris on every floor,  dirty and with bugs/flies. This is not a luxury apartment. If cleanliness is your top priority this is not the place. Not to mention i sent an email and it took  4 days for the lease office  to reply over something so simple as  me asking about security for the apartments. They did reply back and let me know  security is not on premise, and they do not  provide security for the apartments. You've been warned. And if you don't believe me take a ride inside the gate (that gate will be open) and the back of the building.  I was approved however, I  did let them know I will not be moving forward with the apartment.

Maintenance is slow. In general, the staff just has little to no resolve when it comes to the various issues that arise when living in an apartment. The main selling point when I toured was the valet parking for guests. Of the 3 times I’ve tried to have my guests use it, twice they were told I didn’t have that service and that they’d have to pay. This was literally by the same valet parking attendant that I have tipped cash before - and that I speak to every single day. My heat went out on a Thursday right before a very cold weekend. When I followed up on a Friday evening about getting it fixed, they told me nothing could be done until Monday. And nothing was done until Monday. I could go on - but frankly don’t have anymore energy to give this company. Had I known the customer service would drop off so drastically between my tour and now, though, there’s no way I would’ve picked this place. Especially because they’re priced so much higher than comparable lofts. I mean there are literally some on this block a whole 30-40% cheaper but the same size! Also, looks like the ceilings are quite literally coming down. Kind of scary considering the age of the building.

The building is beautiful and speaks for itself -- I would recommend to anyone based solely on this. Maintenance has been speedy when a request is placed online, however there was a lapse with maintenance saying one thing on the note they leave behind in the apartment (stating that a curtain/blind specialist would arrive the next day to complete a repair) however this did not occur (it was during the holiday period, so I understand their could have been delays). Building management has taken this and corrected the mis-communication in the interim. Building management, as a whole, has been friendly and responsive to my needs, and I am thankful for their support.
Roach infested. The leasing office never answers calls. Apartment has been falling apart since day ONE and you ask them to fix what’s wrong with it and they don’t care to fix it.
Amazing reception and customer service, clean environment, the gym is very specious, the employees in the leasing office are very friendly and helpful

It’s has been well. They pretty much handle everything that needs to be done with the apartment right away & the grounds are always nice. The name has changed a few times since I’ve lived here though.
Love the apartment layout! And the vibe is so unmatched here. The other residents are super friendly. One of the best amenity is the valet trash

I have only lived here for a week and the management and staff are very friendly and helpful. My first day moving in I had issues with the toilet and they came right in and fixed it. ?? Thank you Wray North staff. Keep doing a great job, you all are amazing!

I absolutely love living at Wray! Everyone in our community is so kind and quick to help. The way we are taken care of here is unlike any place I've lived. This is the exact reason I plan on staying here for as long as I can! 10/10 gold stars for me!
Great apartment, great location., competitive rents. Great value! Management very responsive as well as maintenance staff! Huge effort put into safety and security.
Lived here almost 5 years! It has been a great time. The staff has been great and the neighborhood is very walkable, especially for dog parents.
I have not moved in yet, but my experience so far with the lease application and approval has been smooth with strong communication by the lease management team.

Seville uptown is amazing! I would recommend any one looking for an apartment in a location where you’re close to many things (downtown, main freeways, etc). The management and maintenance staff here are great and always tend to your requests and truly care about all residents here. My favorite part of this complex is the pool, it’s so beautiful and such a vibe in the summertime.
The location is great. However, the move-in experience and cleanliness and maintenance of the unit were unacceptable.

The staff have been very helpful. Had some maintenance issues resolved right away and the move went very well. Have no issues with the community and the local hangout and eateries are easy to get to. The biggest issue and not the apartment issue is the amount of construction that is constantly all around.
Great apartments, very big and nice. The management are caring and ready to answer your questions. Uptown is a great place to live in and it’s convient to be right near Katy trail.
I love gables Villa Rosa! Amazing environment, maintenance crew, amenities, and location! I have enjoyed living here, and look forward to living here for a while!

I want to share how happy I am to live in these apartments. The amenities are amazing; from the pool to the gym, there's always something to do to stay active and relaxed. Plus, the location is perfect, with easy access to shops, restaurants, and parks. But what impresses me the most is the impeccable cleanliness and maintenance of the common areas and apartments. You can really feel the effort of the team to provide a comfortable and welcoming environment for all of us! I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a quality home.
10/10- no complaints! Villa Rosa has been the BEST and I highly recommend to anyone looking for a new apartment or moving here! The staff is so friendly!
I love living here. The staff is super friendly, maintenance is timely, and the features feel luxurious. Hard to find this in Dallas at such a great price
So far go great. I feel safe and I love the area. Spacious closets and adequate living areas. I can’t wait to entertain guests and meet new people down at the lounge

The parking spaces at MAA Worthington are extremely narrow with a lack of room for all tenants when accounting for large trucks that need spaces.  The building allows a towing company to come and tow cars on a nightly basis if you are over the line by a small fraction.  I have been towed twice and everyone I know in the building has been towed at least once.  I am sure the towing companies pays MAA a fee to be able to come tow their tenants so frequently.

In addition to this, they lose packages regularly.  Two weeks ago they lost a package of mine with over $1,500 worth of valuables.  You will find better amenitities elsewhere.

I have lived in MAA Worthington for two years. The parking spaces are extremely tight (you will have to squeeze into your car) and people always park over the lines.. it's a nightmare, they tow cars frequently too. The  gate is also always broken to get in/out of garage.  For the entire time I've lived here, elevators break weekly, sometimes only one working at a time, which is such a pain if living on a higher floor. The biggest downside to living here is the crime on McKinney Avenue, all week you will here street racing, gun shots and people outside, no matter the day or time. Although, it is relatively safe during the day I would stay inside from 11 pm-5 am. The building offers zero security unlike other buildings nearby. Doors are often left unlocked too, I have called the police numerous times to notify them of guns going off, people sleeping inside the stairways and parking garage. In my time living here I have witnessed multiple accidents (caused by drunk drivers and road rage). It's sad the area has gone so downhill but this complex does nothing to protect it's residents. When notifying the management team of any issue they constantly have an attitude and only care about getting your money. One positive experience has been the maintenance team who for me personally have been attentive and kind. Everything else about this complex is garbage, the trash rooms are always overfilled and the hallways are dirty and smell. MAA charges an absurd amount and offers nothing but bad service. LOOK ELSEWHERE!
This place is terrible, falling apart, and the front desk not maintenance will help you with any of your troubles. Save your money.

I am currently a resident at Post Worthington and I have been here for a few months. 

1. The entire complex has a funky smell. 
2. The sky lounge is never open. So just assume it does not exist. 
3. They charge you a $30 convenience fee to pay your rent.  
4. There was only 10 parking spots for guest when I got here. Which is a joke. Then to make it worse, they got ride of 5 of them. They did not tell us they were going to get ride of them nor did they even bother to provide a solution.

Just moved here 10 days ago and would like to share my experience with anyone considering moving to this building. The initial process with the Leasing Office Staff was very pleasant. However, once you sign the paperwork and move in, they have a management office in the building that you have to deal with from here on. Issue 1: Moving my furniture was a hassle. I reserved the elevator and when I brought my furniture, I was told that they couldn't find my reservation and that was that. They offered no further help; I was on my own. Issue 2: they tell you that they will fix anything that needs to be fixed within 24 hours. 11 days later, I still had my bathroom sinks leaking water, AC not working, Window and Kitchen Cabinet door broken among other things. Issue 3: when I went to the management office to ask for a timeline, I discovered that none of the issues above are the real problem, the real problem as you will discover if you ever move here, is the rude, incompetent, uncaring and dismissive office staff. I don't want to generalize so I will mention that the person I spoke with was the Assistant Manager, who lacked professionalism and basic communication skills. Rolling her eyes at me and telling that this was not her problem, it's a maintenance problem. Offered no help whatsoever except make me feel like I'm not worth her precious time. I have lot more to say but I will conclude with, if you're looking to move into this building, I highly recommend that you pay a visit to the management office, ask a few questions (if you find anyone there) and see for yourself. It's worth knowing what and who you will be dealing with. In the short time I've been here, I have heard other people share similar stories. Also, keep in mind that they have a broken elevator that has not been fixed for over a month now and when asked, I was told they ordered a piece for it. A button piece does not take over a month to arrive. Huge inconvenience to everyone who lives in the 5th floor. I really hope this helps future residents as well as the management office. My feedback is work on your communication, be polite, show empathy, and try to do your job.

Management is horrible. They do not wish to help with issues. They assure fixing them within 24 hours but have not completed any of the issues. Its been day 6 since issues have been reported and still no fixes for any of them. 

The worse part is that there is zero motivation from management to get the issues resolved. The people inside the management office just do not care to fix any of the problems. The worse part is the attitude in trying to fix anything. Its nothing but "uh huh" and "okays" from them with an attitude as they provide zero information about what will be done. 

If you plan on moving in just be ready for nothing being done by management to fix any issues you have.

I’ve been living in this apartment community for some time now, and I can’t say enough good things about it! The location is perfect for me, making it incredibly convenient for work and exploring. I work downtown so the commute is ideal, but I also get to work from home some days. Those days are my favorite because there is still so much around me I can access quickly - plus the views are way better than my office :P

I’ve never dealt with such unprofessional management in my life. The leasing office is a nightmare — they never answer emails, are rarely in the office, and don’t bother answering phone calls. When they do finally respond, it’s often full of excuses or outright lies. There are never any updates or improvements made to the building, and it’s falling apart.

Roaches are a constant problem, and the walls are so thin you can hear everything happening next door. To make matters worse, the elevators are constantly broken, and they offer no guest parking, which is incredibly inconvenient. Overall, this place is a disaster, and I highly recommend you look elsewhere if you value your sanity and peace of mind.

What a nightmare.  The apartment was in bad shape (cabinet doors fell off), and it was hard to get maintenance.  Many of the other apartments on my floor were used for Airbnb's, and so the nights got noisy, and trash was frequently left out causing the hallway to smell.  Most annoying, they had a problem tracking rental payments, so although I never once made a late payment, I got a late notice on most months (and even received an eviction notice a couple of times).  

But none of that would cause me to write a review.  I'm here because of my final experience there.  I was ready to move on at the end of my 1 year lease, but a couple of weeks before there was a some problem that caused a flood in parts of the building including my 18th floor unit.  I woke to ankle deep water.  I grabbed my dogs and evacuated to the safety of a friend's home, which is where I was when the building manager called to make sure I had a place to stay.  He seemed very concerned, and even gave me some suggestions of what restitution I should ask for from the property/management company.  By the time I got back in, just in time to pack to move, all of my furniture that was on the floor was stacked up into towers, there were  6 or 7 loud industrial blowers going, and the space smelled of mildew.  Shoes and handbags that had been on the floor of my closet were destroyed.  A contracted clean-up company was pressuring me to hurry and get out so they could demo my unit for the rebuild, while I had days left on my lease.  The contractors sent a guy into my apartment to stand there and stare at me (while I was packing) who I had to yell at to make leave.  Then after all this, I reached out to the management company to request reimbursement for the days that I couldn't live in the apartment (flooded, evacuation, mildew, loud blowers, stacked furniture, pressure from contractors) and I was told by the 'concerned manager' that nothing happened in my apartment.  He said it wasn't flooded, I wasn't evacuated, and I experienced no inconvenience.  I didn't engage in a lawsuit or fight, because it didn't seem worth the headache for not a lot of money, but they really deserved it.

LTV Towers is one of the worst apartment complexes in Dallas. Management is horrendous and does not answer phone calls and is never on site to assist residents. Maintenance requests take weeks at best. The hallways always smell like weed and the parking garage arm is never working, therefore the garage is always closed for repairs, blocking in my car. Oh and did I mention the elevators have been down for 5 MONTHS!! since the winter storm and have still not been fixed. I have to wait a minimum of 15 mins to get an elevator as there is only one working for a building with 32 floors. And when I finally get an elevator, I have to share it with 20 other residents. Please do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. I wish I had.

I lived at LTV Tower from Feb 2016 - Feb 2017 and only moved due to my dog's fear of traffic. The interior of the apartments were great - from the lobby, elevators, hallways, and of course the actual apartment. I had a 1 bd/1 ba and it was more than enough space for a single person. The living area and kitchen were also great for hosting friends as the areas was spacious and very open. Soundproof walls were also a plus; I think I only heard my next door neighbor a handful of times. The staff were also very accommodating and always available it seemed. Also, it's right downtown near several restaurants and bars, and only a short walk to uptown with even more nightlife! It is an ideal location!

We recently moved out of Marquis at Texas Street. While the apartment complex may seem attractive at first glance, several issues make living here a highly frustrating experience.

Elevator Issues
The elevator in the building is notorious for being unreliable. It barely worked throughout the entire year we lived there. On the rare occasion it was fixed, it would only function for a day before breaking down again, leaving residents inconvenienced for months at a time.

Mold Problems
The bathtub in our apartment developed significant mold, despite our best efforts to clean it with every product available. When we reported this issue to maintenance, their solution was to spray paint over the mold. This quick fix would fade away quickly, and the mold would reappear. To add insult to injury, when we moved out, they charged us over $200 for the condition of the bathtub, which was completely unacceptable given the persistent mold problem and inadequate maintenance.

Stove Charges
Upon moving in, we noted that the glass top stove had visible scratches, indicating previous use. However, when we moved out, we were shocked to be charged over $600 for the stove. This charge is outrageous and unjustifiable, especially since the stove was not in perfect condition when we arrived.

Security Concerns
Security is a major concern at Marquis at Texas Street. During our stay, there were at least five incidents of vehicles being stolen from the parking lot. The management's response was lackluster, treating these serious incidents as if they were routine and offering no real solutions or increased security measures.

Mailbox Break-Ins
There were also at least three break-ins at the mailboxes during our tenure. The only response from management was to send out an email, which did nothing to prevent further incidents or reassure residents about their safety.

Garage Gate Issues
The garage gate frequently broke down and would take days to repair, leaving the parking area vulnerable and residents inconvenienced.

Invasive Maintenance Practices
One of the most troubling aspects was the maintenance staff's disregard for our privacy. Despite explicitly stating in maintenance requests not to enter without permission, they would enter our apartment without notice. This invasive practice was unacceptable and made us feel unsafe in our own home.

Prospective tenants should be aware of these significant drawbacks before considering this complex as their home.

two days ago an emergency sprinkler head leaked outside of my apartment door causing my entire apartment to flood. I promptly contacted the emergency maintenance line, which no one answered. I took what I could and got a hotel for the night. Hours later I received a call saying that maintenance was on the way. In the morning I called my property manager who was less than concerned and more irritated that I was calling to see how this situation could be rectified. I could barely get a word in as I was interrupted by her minimizing my concerns, without offering any real solution other than to take it up with my renters insurance. I attempted to reach out to corporate headquarters formally filing a complaint that I felt my concerns weren’t being taken seriously. Upon my return to my unit, my once spotless apartment has been turned into a mud room, the carpet has been removed from my bedroom with nails exposed everywhere, a humidifier is humming in my ear as my dog and I hide away from all the noise. I decided to speak to the property manager in person about how we could find some solutions and navigate through this process. I was eventually seen. she once again tried to explain what caused the water leak but nothing about how to remedy the discomfort that I have experienced throughout this entire ordeal. I suggested that my rent be prorated, and the days in which I was unable to live in my apartment be credited to my account. Her response was something along the lines of “I’ll ask but we don’t typically do that.” I also brought up that I believed my unit to be unsafe to live in right now, in which I was again interrupted. Realizing that my concerns were falling on deaf ears, I left the leasing office in tears, feeling completely helpless, and unheard. So to sum up it up, I have two loud humidifiers humming in my living room, I have been unable to work from home missing many opportunities and deadlines, many of my belongings have been ruined by water damage, I have spent close to $700 out of pocket for lodging and food. I have a pile of wet carpet padding on my patio, exposed nails , hours of filing a hefty insurance claim ahead of me, and seemingly no help or hope of any sort of rectification for my missed work opportunities, housing displacement, or the damaging of my belongings. I am beyond stressed and extremely disappointed that this is the community in which I must stay in until April when my lease is up.

Your attitude caused they loss many potential clients, and have a bad review on apartments.com. However, one good thing about this property (WHOEVER LIVES ON THIS PROPERTY IS SO POLITE AND AMAZING!)

If you have any qualms about noise levels, I suggest you STAY AWAY.  I live on the 3rd floor and I hear my upstairs neighbor - every - single - day.  I don't hear her TV, I don't hear her music, I don't her screaming or talking.  No.  I hear her walking.  Up and down the hallway - up and down the hallway - in the bathroom - out of the bathroom.  When I toured this place, they said there was sound proofing between the floors.  And just like on the Maury show, that turned out to be a LIE.  I lived in an older (1980s) complex before "upgrading" and moving to this completely brand new unit with luxury amenities and never heard the guy who lived above me as much as I hear my upstairs neighbor.  Maybe she has lead feet.  And what can I do about it?  Complain?  "Oh, sorry, could you walk softer?"  I'm sure that would go over well. I never hear any other noise from her so I can't really complain.  Now I'm paranoid about how loud I'm walking!  I live across from the parking garage and it never bothers me.  Also, ANT infestation in the bathroom not long after I moved in and like the previous reviewers - would wake up with bites.  Bought some ant baits at Target and they seemed to do the trick.  Dishwasher doesn't dry dishes all the way - everything is always still pretty wet after the dry cycle.  If you live near the courtyard - all the dog owners use it as their personal dog park and let their dogs run free - now I love dogs, but sometimes it sounds like that scene in 101 Dalmatians where all the dogs are barking all over London - right - outside - your door.  My friend who also lives hear says there is a resident portal, where you can pay rent, see your rent plus utilities total, etc.  I was never given this site nor any login information to any portal.  I never knew it existed.  I called one day to gain access, the front desk took my e-mail.  I've still never seen this portal.  So I just add my apartment utilities to my rent and hope I'm in the clear - it's like a guessing game.  All of these perks for the price of a mortgage.  Now I do enjoy the gym, the parking, the balcony is spacious, and most importantly, the location.  Had to throw in a few positives since I'm stuck here for the next year.

The online portal is a complete joke. They literally told me that they get too many emails to check them all so to come in during business hours if you need something. So if you like the floor plan, the amenities and location, but can live here without interacting with these people EVER, you'll be good to go. :)

Considering the price of rent in relation to it's location, this place has good value.  It's a little bit on the older side of apartment complexes compared to the new high rises currently going up all over Uptown and could use some TLC in some places, but it's still nice.  Pretty good pool scene on the weekends during the summer. Lots of parking available here too.

This apartment has everything I need for my first apartment in Dallas. The location is very close to my school and work places and allows me to walk to many restaurants to meet up with friends. The maintenance crew is always very helpful and quick to respond to any requests (almost always next day!) If there are ever any questions or problems I have, the managers are happy to help with whatever I need. The pool is very nice with enough chairs to use even in the summer months. The gym is quite small and doesn't have all of the equipment I would like it to have, but it gets the job done most of the time if there aren't other people in there.
Very quiet neighborhood, well shaded and private. Apartments are well priced and functional. Maintenance is quick and responsive.
Overall, I like the community. It is centrally located to restaurants and shops

The pool is a little small, they also have a nice outdoor deck, grills, a fitness center and small business center. It can be hard to find outside parking for guests, and if you don't live in the building with the garage, it can be a bit of a walk to get there. The staff and maintenance have been great. Location is great, you're about a mile or less walk to Klyde Warren Park, McKinney Ave, AAC, Aquarium and more. I feel safe and I do enjoy living here.

I have had mostly postive experiences living at the property! It would be nice if that was prevented - It would be nice to have a package service again. As one who struggled with Luxer before, I am not suggesting to switch back to that service. And the leasing office has been great, just sometimes difficult to get a package during the week based on work hours. Potentially a package locker scenario? I have several friends who have those in their apartment, where you will receive a code like Luxer, enter it, and then one of the lockers will open up with your package (for oversize ones, they are sent to leasing office still)
It's been excellent & I have resided here since 2007.

Management is great and organized. No shady business. They are extremely proactive in handling frustration if situations like the laundry card machine being out. Great neighborhood feel, affordable rates, and friendly staff. Would like a wider time range to pickup packages though.

This apartment is amazing. A five minute walk from a beautiful park where events take place almost every weekend. If you want to live in Uptown Dallas, this complex is for you!

I also appreciate how fast maintenance fixes problems around the apt. I get email notifications if there has been criminal activity around here. Many great things. If you want to live in the city without breaking the bank live Here. The staff is incredible and will do anything they can to make you feel at home. I moved from CT without setting foot in Dallas and I am so happy I chose Post Uptown Village. I feel like I am at an Italian Villa when I sit by the pool!

Being in uptown village really has captured the correct image. On the border of uptown and downtown Dallas, it still manages to be calm and peaceful. Inside its gates houses little small squares that are sanctuary to those who live there.  The amenities are numerous, with laundry facilities, a gym, pool, and parking garages. This place is amazing for the price, and would definitely recommend to anyone looking for quiet within Dallas proper.

Shockingly, the manager admitted she hadn’t even looked at the photos before making this claim. Instead, I was told that if I “really cared,” I could buy my own mold testing kit and send it in to be tested.

Even with proof, management doubled down, refusing to acknowledge any wrongdoing. Ive a number of issues with AVANT on Market Center in the year I've lived here. 

Elevators.  Don't be deceived when you go on a tour of the place.  They will take you up on an elevator and then down another elevator, perhaps even a ride on the third elevator.  Those are the only three elevators.  Placed perhaps 15 seconds apart, which fails to prepare you for the 140 yard walk to your apartment.   That's nearly one and a half football fields!   Heaven forbid you've groceries or left something in your car!  

Or consider this, the weekend comes for you to move into your fourth floor apartment and suddenly ALL of the elevators are out of service.  Yes, ALL of them.  You phone the office, they don’t answer.   Saturday, you walk into the office drenched in your own sweat to hear “they will be here Monday to look at it.”  But your moving truck is due back Sunday.  It won’t fit in the parking garage.  So anything you aren’t willing to haul up the four flights of stairs, you instead have to put on a wagon and make the long spiral journey to the fourth floor of the parking garage — Reaching your 4th floor destination is simply the beginning, you still have 140 yards to go!  Management’s response to this is “we apologize for the inconvenience.”  
 
Towing.  Its nothing short of predatory.  The town company makes their rounds 6-8 times a day, slugging the normal traffic (residents trying to get to their own apartment) as their tow truck lurks slowly down the ramps along side a poorly dressed counterpart wildly running around with a flashlight peeking in every vehicle, anxious to find another victim.  How did they get in the parking garage to begin with?  Well, Management gave them their own keyless entry device… sounds like they are looking out for their residents for sure!

They frequently tow authorized vehicles.  Don’t believe this?  The problem has gotten so out of hand they've had to implement a new policy for the tow truck driver, who is now required to photograph the vehicle before towing it!?  I'll let you marinate on that one for a moment.  

Staffing.  There is more turnover here than a college Sonic. I’ve lived here less than a year, there has been four, perhaps five assistant managers since I arrived.

FIVE star maintenance!!!  I really mean that.  These guys are fast, friendly and do a great job.  They are the highlight and only appreciable part of the “AVANT experience.”

Very thin walls, and cheap flooring. you can hear your neighbors take every step.... Smoke from your neighbors will travel through vents into your room. Very Shady Management. Kristen "the manager" talks down to tenants and is very disrespectful. Worst Complex in DFW.

They charge 50 dollars a month for each reserved space, but do not enforce delivery people and other tenants and guest from parking in your spot.. have to call and wait 30-60 in for a tow, and park on the roof in the mean time.

Security does nothing ... does not even enforce parking just sits in their car.. only a security officer not a true courtesy or peace officer as they had when I moved in.

Several work orders: caulking around faucets in bath tub doesn't hold up, issues with insects near trash, vertical blinds always falling, wallpaper over cabinets comes off, leaking hoses around sink, and they never change your filter for your ice maker and water dispenser in your fridge. 

office staff is friendly, but management is not.

Hotel next door has events in the parking lot Saturday evening til 11/1130 and it is loud!

No discounts for military or law enforcement only those that work at UT southwestern and parkland and you basically get your washer and dryer free to rent.

No concessions for inconvenience.

Pros:
-My apartment amenities are exceptional and rent price is very reasonable considering the location (Design District)
- Personable office staff...I don't visit the office often but they still remember my name and ask how I've been.

Cons:
-Only 2 ways to access building 2 from the parking garage (1st floor and 3rd floor) - I live on the 2nd floor of building 2 so bringing in groceries can be difficult (if I don't find parking on the 1st or 3rd floor, I have to take the elevator to either of those floors in the garage, walk across, then take another elevator to the 2nd floor)--not to mention the elevators are very slow.  Also, when I have guests over, they have to drive all the way up to the 5th or 6th floor, walk down 2-3 flights of stairs (again, because the elevators take forever), walk across the 3rd floor crosswalk, then take the stairs again down to the 2nd floor.  Too much when there could have been walkways from all levels put into the plan prior to construction.
-Neighbor noises - I've read plenty of reviews for this complex that complained about noises that could be heard from neighbors, as far as talking, TV's, bathroom and bedroom noises etc.  I actually never hear my next door neighbor, however, the person that lives above me sounds like they are trying to create a hole in their floor.  They walk around A LOT and they walk hard, all day.  This is definitely a case by case situation because I didn't experience this issue with the previous tenant.

***Overall - My 2 con's are things I can deal with considering its part of apartment living.  The garage could be better but it's not horrible.  The traveling does get annoying at times but it's not a killer.  The hard walking from my neighbor is definitely annoying but you can't really expect your unit to be completely soundproof while paying less than $1200/month.

My husband and I have moved here from out of state two months ago. In these two months I have gone to the office more times than the apartment complex we lived at previously for two years.
When we moved in we were asked to fill out an "inventory and condition form". In our experience the items that get marked as an issue on said form will be approached by the office/maintenance staff and corrected within the first few days. We quickly realized that this was not the case and approached the office concerning the major issues we found; i.e. front door not closing properly/fully, missing appliance, ancient stove, front porch light not working, kitchen plumbing issue... Two weeks later and I just checked again - still no new stove.
For the average person this may not be an issue, however I have an autoimmune disease and must cook my own food. I even shared this with the office and maintenance staff but... nothing. While I have been using the stove for the last two months, it has proven to be extremely difficult and unreliable - cook something twice and one time it's fine, next time it's burnt. The cheap rent, the close proximity to highways, whatever reason/excuse you can come up with being interested in The Edge, is not worth compromising your safety. Fingers crossed no more shootings while I'm living here. DO NOT MOVE HERE!!!

tl;dr - You're paying luxury apartment prices for an admittedly nice apartment, but mediocre complex in a somewhat bad part of town.

The Good
- Nice apartment interior, not gonna lie. High ceilings, nice appliances, blah blah.
- Air conditioned/heated halls between apartments.
- Maintenance is pretty quick, about 2 days turnaround.
- No bugs after initial move-in spraying.
- Parking is good, it's just enough. There's usually about 3 spaces left at the end of the day.
- I've only dealt with management a couple of times, and they're nice and helpful with common issues.

The Bad
- Water shuts off almost weekly for a few hours due to leaks in the garage.
- All trash goes through one chute, which fills up almost every other day if you live on the 2nd floor. So you either go up or down and dump, or leave the trash in the trash room and risk a fee. At least the halls are air conditioned.
- The hallways are a meeting place for some people, and you can hear their conversations about 2 apartments down.
- Airplanes fly low and directly overhead many, many times a day. They slows down a lot at night, but it's noisy enough to drown out the TV and make falling asleep a chore sometimes.
- Not an issue for some, but the hallways almost always reek of weed.

The Ugly
- Security is a very real concern. The whole place is VERY gate reliant. People check door handles for unlocked cars, there are no working cameras, and most of the exterior doors have partially broken handles, broken glass, or broken hinges because people try to break in. Homeless people sometimes try and follow you into the side entrances to hang out in the staircase. Someone broke into a bunch of the mailboxes once, it's just not near friendly people. Anecdotal, but I had my car broken into, and my motorcycle was stolen when the gate was broken for a couple of weeks.
