The only positive is the vicinity of Umstead Park which is nice.

Mislead and lied to. We are moving for another part of the state. We settled on Seasons at Umstead and when it came time to move in we found out the apartment was nothing like expected. So, we backed out and let them know we’d be back to collect our deposit check. When we returned, we were told they had already deposited it and now we must wait to get the check back. Will update if that happens.

I love living at The Seasons at Umstead Park!! When I moved away for a year I missed the location so much that I came back, with close proximity to the state park and shopping/restaurants. We originally signed because of how wonderful the office staff treated us and it really makes a difference in an apartment living community. They also put on events every month for the residents and have food trucks multiple times a month. Maintenance staff is friendly and are quick to fix any issue. I love the gym equipment and access to the computer lab 24/7. Plenty of visitor parking and beautiful building exteriors. The apartment renovations that have been done since we have left are very classy, with the hardwood floors and beautiful kitchen upgrades. The price for a 3bedroom is very fair and I plan to call this apartment complex home for a long time.

If i could grade just on the staff it would be a 5 star, but unfortunately they aren't the issue. I moved from out of state which was a breeze however i wish I would've looked at the apartment before moving in. I was under the impression I would be receiving a different layout than was given which was very disappointing for me. 

A couple issues have happened within living here in a month
there is a bad case of bugs here that get into your apartment on the first floor. I complained about it before because they are even coming up the water pipes in the bathtub and so far only a door sweep has been installed, but the bugs are still making their way in. Apparently huge water bugs are culture here, but it looks unclean having a huge roach on your floor. 

Also the dishwasher since day one has spit out dirty brown water. they said they fixed it, but it hasn't improved. Also, when it rains bad here my kitchen windows leak which is definitely a bummer. I have also noticed the unit doesn't stay cool long with the air on..I'm only comparing this to other properties I've lived in. 

Again, staff is great... but this isn't a place I would stay at if I could get out of my lease. I would personally go up the road where they have more square footage and a better layout for the same price. (1br )

I lived at The Seasons in the 1 bedroom floorplan for almost a year. I originally moved in only planning to stay for 3 months because I was in the process of trying to find a home to buy. I thoroughly enjoyed my apartment with the new upgrades and the community as a whole. Key word being "community". The staff at seasons were like family and really make it feel like home with how personable and responsive they are. I definitely recommend The Seasons at Umstead and would not hesitate to move back in if I ever need another apartment.

Just renewed our lease here in December because we love the community! Staff is awesome as are most of the residents I've met so far! Only tiny itty bitty complaint I would have is parking is sometimes a pain on the permit only side. They're reasonably priced, quick to respond to service calls (which those guys are awesome too!) grounds are well kept and the salt water pool is simply awesome, not many around the area have that amenity but we do!! Keep up the great work Seasons and JMG!

I have lived here going on 5 years. I must say, each year they keep getting better at making this a great place to live. There has been several changes in ownership with each new owner trying to take the property to another level. I have seen new lighting installed around the property, a dedicated car wash area installed, a community gas grill installed, with a new patio and outdoor firepit, a new computer lab and revamped fitness area, screened in patios and many more improvements. It's not perfect, parking can be a struggle at times, but it is better than 90% of the other properties in the area. It is near the highway so you can get to the furthest areas in 30 minutes or less. The best part is the staff - they all call you by name and recognize your voice on the phone they really make you want to stay!!!
Plain and simple I love this complex. It's quite, the office staff is like family, and I love living here.

I have lived here for almost 8 years, but it is time to move on.  The apartments are a pretty good size, and they are doing some needed upgrades to them. However, the price is getting out of hand.  When I moved in trash, water and sewage were free, but now we pay for all three and it is not cheap.  I live alone in a one bedroom loft and my water and sewage runs about $60.00 dollars a month!  When they first started charging us(about three year ago) it ran about $15.00, so that's a big hit. I will say the grounds are well maintained, and the people that live here are pretty nice.  The office staff is very helpful and so is the maintenance staff.  You must like dogs to live here because there is a lot of them, I have one myself.  Although there are 5 dog stations on the grounds a lot of dog owners do not use them (sigh). Pool is small for this size of complex, but the common areas for the residents are nice, fire pit, BBQ's , sand volleyball etc.  To sum up, pretty good apartments ("if" you get the upgraded apt.), great location, utilities are too high, rent is a little high too! * Only 
about 1% of the apartments have been remodeled so far.

My husband and I have been living at Four Seasons at Umstead Park for just about 2 years.  The staff is amazing.  They are really friendly and instantly welcoming.  It is not like the apartments where you only see the staff when you turn in your monthly rent.  They are constantly saying hello and stop to ask how our day is going. The staff makes sure exciting events are always  happening around the complex as well.  We have food trucks, monthly get-togethers and lots of parties.

We first moved here, we moved into a 1 bedroom apartment because we were saving money to get married. After we got married, we upgraded to a 2 bedroom apartment.  The staff was great working with us to meet all of our requests for an apartment.  We were located exactly where we loved, on the floor we wanted, and with the upgrades we were looking for.  They even worked with our deadline of moving.

Four Seasons at Umstead Park is a clean, safe place with great amenities.  We love going to the pool, volleyball court and always use the washing station (for our dog and our cars).  You will not be disappointed!

Four seasons at umstead park is a great place to live.  It is located near so many great stores, restaurants, state parks and the airport.  We looked at a lot of different apartment complexes and they all treated us like a number, except for four seasons.  The staff cared about us and wanted to find us the best apartment they could.

The amenities are great!  The pool is always packed on the weekends with friendly neighbors.  

I highly recommend this apartment complex.

My husband and I have been living at Four Seasons at Umstead Park for just about 2 years.  The staff is amazing.  They are really friendly and instantly welcoming.  It is not like the apartments where you only see the staff when you turn in your monthly rent.  They are constantly saying hello and stop to ask how our day is going. The staff makes sure exciting events are always  happening around the complex as well.  We have food trucks, monthly get-togethers and lots of parties.

We first moved here, we moved into a 1 bedroom apartment because we were saving money to get married. After we got married, we upgraded to a 2 bedroom apartment.  The staff was great working with us to meet all of our requests for an apartment.  We were located exactly where we loved, on the floor we wanted, and with the upgrades we were looking for.  They even worked with our deadline of moving.

Four Seasons at Umstead Park is a clean, safe place with great amenities.  We love going to the pool, volleyball court and always use the washing station (for our dog and our cars).  You will not be disappointed!

Four Seasons Umstead Park is a great apartment complex for many reasons. The management staff is wonderful and helped me feel comfortable right away. After a long and difficult process trying to find an apartment in Raleigh I finally found this one, and I'm so glad I did! The rent is reasonable for the apartment, and the location is great. It's close to the mall without the high prices that come with living near the mall. Everything I need is nearby, the grocery store, the movie theater, the mall, work. 
Another important thing to me was a quiet apartment because I have a dog who is not used to apartment life. I never hear my neighbors and neither does she! Which means not a lot of barking which makes everyone happy. Highly recommend Four Seasons Umstead Park!

I have been at link for about a month now, apartment itself is great with very attentive leasing and maintenance team.  HOWEVER, the plumbing work is poorly done that whenever someone turns on the hot water, loud constant banging noise comes from the bedroom wall at 5:00am to 5:30am.  The management team considers this as an non-urgent maintenance and it has been going for a week now.  I am a pretty heavy sleeper, I sleep thru the train noise, but this banging noise is so bad that it gives me a shock to wake me up.  I will be updating this review once I get a resolution, hopefully soon.

He vivido aquí desde hace 3 años, y puedo decir que la convivencia ha sido muy buena, el lugar es muy limpio, el personal administrativo es muy amable, el señor Milton siempre está presto a ayudar y el señor Billy de mantenimiento siempre está pendiente de cuidar los apartamentos para q todo funcione bien.

Lived here from May 2021-May 2022.  Really good price-point for the location.  Within 8 minutes of Harris Teeter, Target, and Crossroads.  Close to I-40 for commuting.  Only complaint is noise during the day, it is adjacent to a middle school, but otherwise calm.  Safe area, walked around at night many times.

With the rising popularity of the Triangle area, the price of rent here is much more reasonable than other "luxury" apartments. Would definitely live here again.

We lived in Ashborough for just over a year and had a great experience there. This was the only apartment complex we've been genuinely sad to leave. The apartments themselves are well-laid out, feel pretty new, and are well-maintained. The office staff was friendly and helpful without fail (they even helped us pick up some items we had forgotten in the apartment when we moved out), and maintenance was quick and super friendly! The office even followed up for some maintenance cases to make sure we were happy with the results. The location has shopping nearby and it's easy to get to highway 64 and interstate 40, but it still feels tucked away in a good way. Our apartment was near the woods and it was awesome - it felt private and had a great view. We never had issues with neighbors, and the office actually enforces the no smoking policy (which is rare in my experience), and that was highly appreciated.
Only cons: the one dumpster in the complex did sometimes get way too full by the end of the week, and since it's near an elementary school there is heavy traffic when parents are dropping off/picking up kids from school, so you might need to plan an extra 3 min or so into your driving schedule if you'll be leaving during that time.
Overall, it's really a great place!

I've been living in this apartment complex for two years already and during these two years I had primarily positive experience. The neighborhood is nice, quiet and clean. The staff is friendly and easy to communicate with, the service support provided prompt responses (obviously COVID created some interference but prior to that problems were solved within 1-3 days depending on urgency/technical side).You may rarely see bugs in the apartments (typically when the temperature outside drops or when it rains heavily) but staff reacts to solve those problems whenever they occur.

My boyfriend and I just moved in- we were scheduled to move during a recent hurricane, but for our safety they let us get in a few days early so we wouldn’t have to move through the storm. This place is amazing. Everything is fully renovated, the grounds are gorgeous, but above all I have never experienced such kindness from a leasing and maintenance team in my life! The day we moved in a few members from the maintenance team chatted with us to make sure everything was up to par and let us know to just give them a hollar if we needed anything— while they were also boarding up windows to prepare for the storm. 

Everyone here seems very friendly, including the other residents. We’re so close to everything! The prices are great for the location and upgraded units as well.

Would 100% recommend stopping by and speaking with Milton or Amanda ( or im sure anyone else in the office) to check the place out. It was a huge breath of fresh air to sign the lease.

The office has probably one person who does anything. There is a weekend guy who should be fired. They can't seem to ever get packages out in a timely fashion. I had one package sit in office for 5 months. I asked... They "checked" nothing. I happened to see it when getting another package. Stuff never gets logged. The guy is probably the laziest person I have ever met. He knows nothing as well. The day of the pool opening the gate was locked. A large group of people asked the guy to open it.. we had to break in kinda after a hour plus. He never did get the key. I think he saw us in pool area and just dismissed the whole group of tenants. Lazy....he is always on his cell phone in office. Just to add to it he is rude to boot. If he is in office, just leave...worthless person for sure. I think he is just a weekend meat suit.

Cigarette Smoke – I have been dealing with second hand cigarette smoke in my apartment since my first complaint 10/9/17.  I moved here from a smoking complex specifically because the website states they offer smoke free living.  If you are concerned about second hand smoke, ask what the smoking detection/resolution methods are.  Although they adopt a smoke free policy, the lease also states there is no warranty of a smoke free environment – I have been reminded of this twice now.  I don’t know how you can have it both ways, but read this section carefully. I was told in an email from the complex on 10/16/17 that several residents in the building reported the same issue with smoke in response to an email sent by the complex.  An email 10/18/17 stated location was pinpointed and a direct violation letter was sent.  When the cigarette smoke continued, I asked for a meeting with the manager.  She sends another email to residents  11/16/17 and said she received no responses this time.  Also said she spoke with the tenets thought to be in violation and they assured her they weren’t smoking.  Apparently, this is the complex detection/resolution policy for the situation.  Simply question residents and if they say no, you’re done.

Lived in Ashborough for a year and was a terrible experience for the price we paid. First we had mold all on our walls the entire time we lived there. Every time we contacted maintenance they said there was nothing they could do except keep cleaning it off. The mold started in the living room but somehow reached the kitchen cabinets and everywhere else. The maintenance staff was pretty good and lended a hand with everything they could but I guess fixing the mold was out of their jurisdiction. The front office wouldn't even give a price break on rent for the inconvenience. 


We gave a 45 day notice to move out but apparently they require a 60 day notice. This fee was $100/day!! We were told if we moved out early then they would waive the fees so we moved out a month early but lo and behold the fees are not being waived and "theres nothing they can do". Really wish the people who leased me my apartment were still in charge because these new people are nothing but unpleasant to deal with.  You can find much better apartments in the area for way less money and mold

I've had the pleasure to deal with Ashborough throughout my moving process. They've easily been the most attentive, helpful and flexible groups I've ever dealt with. If you find yourself moving to Raleigh / Cary NC in the near future, I highly recommend looking them up, because not only will you get to live near me, but also be a part of a group that makes you feel welcome before you've even signed anything.

Special shoutouts to Megan and Amanda, who've responded to any concerns or questions immediately and with the utmost kindness and respect.
Milton and the Ashborough team have been impeccable with their outstanding service, making the tour and move-in process a breeze! -Jael R.
The entire experience has been great. Apartments were very nice and Milton was very helpful and attentive to the needs and requests that I had.

I recently went and applied at this complex and I must say I was very pleased. The people were very energetic and very professional. I love the space and the quotes for this complex. You won't regret applying here so do it today !!

I must have looked at hundreds of apartment communities and Ashborough Apartments was by far the best! Not only did it meet all of my requirements but exceeded them by having top of the line washer/dryers in every unit, carport, and a fireplace for the best rate around! Donavon and Jenna were extremely helpful during my relocation which can be very stressful. Thanks to them, I feel relaxed and ready to move in :) So happy to be home at Ashborough!!!

The worst property management I've ever dealt with. A bunch of pity thieves manage this property and the only respect that they have is for their pockets. Every interaction with the management is a hassle, from getting your package from the rental office to getting them to fix something in the apartment. I lived there a year a I will never go back even if this place is the only one on the planet.
The maintenance turn around is a little slower than I expected but in general they are good. The apartment is luxurious, specious and quite. It is a smoke free place and we are loving it.

Perfect area. Right at the crossroads shopping area. Huge apartments n have a huge garage. Well kept up inside & out. Big windows, which i love, that overlook the beautiful property. Nice big covered balconies with concrete floors n good ceiling so u dont have to worry about your upstairs neighbors leaking down into your space. Huge closets. Good windows. (Have had mildew windows at other complexes) occasionally can hear muffled sounds of neighbors but that doesn't bother me. It IS an apt after all. Has to be expected. GREAT office staff & maintenance team.  Honestly cant say im unhappy with anything here. Its been a great experience.  And on top of it all....good prices.

Ashborough Apartments in Raleigh, NC is truly convenient to nearby shopping and parks as well as good access to major highways. Also, there are local schools and North Carolina State University nearby. The super awesome management team are always on top of issues and ensuring a nice clean, quiet atmosphere for all to love. What's greater is they stay in compliance with Housing Laws by performing quarterly inspections and upgrades. The community is very respective of one another and always enjoy a good round of water volleyball game in the community pool. I absolutely love it here.

St. Mary's Square changed management companies in September 2018.   

Continental raised the rent and starting cutting services.  Trash is piling up, elevators do not function, and the property is not maintained.  Printers, wifi, coffee machines simply do not work.  Hallways are filthy.  This is becoming a terrible place to live.  You will regret moving here.

I moved into St Marys about 8 months ago and have lived in many other apartments around Raleigh. I love living here, the amenities are great, maintenance is fast, their floor plan options are very open and warm, and the location is ideal! Would highly recommend!

I’ve lived here for about 7 months now. Started at a 1 bedroom and just recently upgraded to a 2BR. I absolutely love the staff and all the amenities. I have a dog and she loves the dog park here! Transferring to a bigger apartment was so easy as well. I can’t wait for summertime so I can hang out by the pool again!

I lived in this apartment just over two years and only left because of a job relocation. The apartment was beautiful and in a great location. The staff was definitely a selling point as well. They were super friendly and very helpful. Maintenance was great and I never waited on anything. I would recommend if you are looking for a place downtown this is the place.
I've lived here for 2 years and I love it. Amenities are great, great location, friendly people.

I like everything here 
clean, good maintained, good location. Peacefull community.

My experience with Creekside only two months in is that they work incredibly hard to make things right for the residents. I worked with Sakina, who has been super helpful and attentive to any concern or questions I might have. The building is so nice, quiet, and the amenities are several steps up from my last residence, which had the same price point. Exceptional location!
Creekside at Crabtree is a well maintained community and the staff is very responsive to any issue brought to their attention.
If you are looking for a secure building with high end finishes that is clean, this is that place.  Also in a really convenient location to mall and restaurants.

Creekside at Crabtree has been a excellent place to live! Management & staff are prompt in answering any concerns. The grounds and buildings are well maintained along with all the amenities! Management and staff have always been kind and friendly!
I appreciate the care Creekside’s staff takes in maintaining the quality of our community.

Daniella is the type of Leasing Consultant who will respond three business days before you even know what your question is. She is always on her A+ game. We assumed that she was an outlier, but wow, the entire staff at The Lincoln has been phenomenal. We have primarily interacted with Daniella, but Cesar, Lani, and Meagan are clearly all on the same wavelength. I’ll be real, I literally only leave positive reviews, but this review is different. There is an energy here. The residents seem happy, the staff seems happy, and if you don’t believe me, just look at the reviews for The Lincoln over the course of the past few years. There are residents who have lived here for over 5 years who continue to rave about this place. Anyways, yeah, I might be hopped up on 9 shots of espresso right now, but this place is awesome. Come see for yourself. Thank you to The Lincoln Team. We are happy to be here.

I lived at the Lincoln for several years and it's been the BEST experience! My neighbors are lovely and the people here are so welcoming! The office staff which is Meagan, Daniella and Lani have been super helpful when it comes to anything I need. The Amenities are wonderful and I enjoy all the resident events each month! They love my fur baby everytime I come in the office, there's always treats when you enter the building. I plan on staying here until I purchase a home in the future. 

-xoxo

The Lincoln has been amazing! From the awesome staff, ideal location downtown, amazing amenities and reasonable pricing. What more can you ask for?  Not to mention how much love is given to my furbaby! I truly love the sense of community and proud to call The Lincoln my home.

Such an amazing property with magnificent staff. I have lived many places and I have not lived anywhere with such proficient communication. It feels like a real home not just somewhere to rent for the time being. I appreciate Meagan, Daniella, and Lani for making my stay so smooth. Maintenance is very responsive as well but there aren't many issues either so that's a plus.

I love my apartment here at The Lincoln! Its so close to everything and it's not in the heart of downtown. I have some peace and quiet here, and yet be able to walk in the city, which is like 2 blocks away. The staff is amazing and so responsive. They always handle everything on time! Such a great place to live, the people here are so friendly, I highly recommend the Lincoln!!

So happy, My husband and I moved to The Lincoln Apartments last month from Michigan. The weather is absolutely wonderful here, love that we are in the city and its calm on this side of downtown. So many places  nearby to eat and have a great time! The Office staff and maintenance are the bomb.com! Everyone seems to know each other here and super friendly! We are so happy about our move here to Raleigh, thanks to The Lincoln (:

Car break-ins in the alleged "secure" parking garage continue to persist. very easy to tailgate into this building and into the parking garage. Cameras not working in the parking garage frequently so for a woman to be walking by herself be aware of your surroundings. Lighting is very dim in the parking garage as well. Police are here frequently and an individual was arrested this past week as well. If I had a young daughter I would never recommend this place to her.  On site manager tries her best.

Best move-in experience I've ever had. My apartment was spotless. Maintenance has always been really responsive and friendly. The leasing office staff are not only kind, but also very approachable, which I feel is not always the case in a lot of apartments so I really appreciate that. And for the location, the price can not be beat!

I really liked The Lincoln... Until the riots.  All the best things to do downtown near The Lincoln got destroyed totally by the rioters.  Just about everything that is worth doing around The Lincoln is totally shut down and boarded up.  For those who aren't familiar, The Lincoln is on the outer fringe of the good parts of downtown and the lower quality parts of downtown so the rent is a tad cheaper than other downtown apartments.  At the end, hearing gun shots being fired often just outside the building was too much, so I left.  I think Raleigh Police have given up on policing the area due to the current climate.

I tried to negotiate a rent reduction because I hate moving, but they wouldn't budge or give me the deal they normally give to new applicants.  So, I decided that I wasn't going to pay high rent with nothing to do that was also located in an area that I consider to be less safe.  Unless you live downtown, you can't believe what a hassle it is to live downtown but have to do all your shopping in outlying suburbs.

While I was there, I enjoyed the pool and the management team was responsive.  I was a bit put off by the nasty carpet in the common areas.  Once an area gets stained (The Lincoln is pet friendly), they never seem to replace the carpet.  I think the carpet cleaning service they use is a joke and the carpet smells worse after it is 'cleaned' than it did before.  The package delivery system is the absolute worst as they have a complex two room solution (spaced far apart) that confuses delivery drivers.  Amazon drivers never seem to figure it out.

But for the riots, I'd give the property a four star review because of the common area stained carpets and package room system (otherwise a five).  Because of the riots, and the general decay of the immediate area, it gets two stars.

I now live in a nearby area with a substantially lower rent bill.  It's safe, and there's good shopping and things to do nearby.

Recently relocated to Raleigh after living in the Greater Boston area for many years. The Lincoln is awesome! Our unit is beautiful and well-laid out, plus we love the amenities it has to offer. The pool, lounge, gym, parking garage, package services, and resident events are just a few that make our life here convenient. The best part is by far the location - you can walk everywhere, but don't feel like the building is squished in with everything else! Highly recommend!

Love living here. I loved that I was able to find a more affordable option downtown. The staff is really nice and helpful. I love how many dogs and dog friendly people there are in the building, including the staff! Love having the coffee machine downstairs (the vanilla latte is my favorite). The gym is simple but has everything you need, plus they have a little fitness studio room as well which is nice. Pool and courtyard are cute and always have friendly residents to talk with. Definitely glad I chose The Lincoln!

Just moved out of the Lincoln after 2 years.  In the beginning it was a great place with awesome staff and neighbors.  Slowly as office staff transitioned the Lincoln became unbearable.  The real kicker was the hiring of an adult babysitter to watch the pool area on weekends.  Its a pool, people are going to want to hang out, have some drinks, play some games and listen to music.  But not at the Lincoln.  Because a couple of people weren't smart enough to realize that living in a poolside apartment would have above average noise, the rest of the community suffers with a miserable summer pool season.  When trying to have a conversation with building manager about the specific rules and regulations concerning noise, I was shut down when I brought up specific decibel numbers and if they had recorded noise above them.  Enough on that, expect rent to increase yearly while you meet new people who get move in specials and free months of rent.  That to me just shows the lack of appreciation for already paying customers.  Also, I noticed the sense of community is being lost over my last few months there.   When I first moved in, people would say hi and small talk at the coffee machine (when it wasn't broke), but now it seems people go out of their way to avoid saying hi.  This is probably due to the lackluster events the staff throw every once in a while.  So in conclusion, new management style sucks and is ruining the community feeling of the first year.

I moved into the Lincoln apartments last year and have absolutely no regrets! The office staff (Christine & Amber) are always pleasant & quick to respond to the questions and concerns of the residents and maintenance is on any issue ASAP. I have never lived in a complex with such friendly and outgoing neighbors who look out for each other and are pets. We are a tight group of professionals who work hard during the week and enjoy the amenities, in particular the pool on the weekends. I am not sure where some of the negative reviews come from about the noise, as I hear nothing other than the occasional noise you would expect living downtown, from emergency services or traffic. 
$imon

This is literally the best place I have ever lived.

The amenities rock and the staff are equally awesome. The apartments are great and the decor is perfect.

Christine and Amber are so quick to help in any instance and really go to the bat for the residents to take care of the place.

The complaints about the noise at the pool are almost entirely due to the buildings design as an enclosed interior and the sound travels. The pool scene on Saturdays is the best and we have a real community of residents that love to work hard during the week and let loose on the weeks.

The residents that complain about the noise, I guess my question is have you have ever come and spoke to anyone with the music or the loud noise on Saturday afternoons or have you just called the police??

I think we both know the answer to that question.

You live downtown. You live in a younger aged building. Get a reality check people.

I LOVE LIVING AT THE LINCOLN.

~The Mayor

PLEASE READ! I have never posted a review about a place I have lived at before. The Lincoln apartments are great as far as the gym, pool, and apartment. The MAIN PROBLEM is that the walls and floors are so thin! You will hear everything! I get woken up around 2-3 am everynight by the person above me walking around. It is not just the noise but you feel the vibrations in bed! It will wake you out of a deep sleep. I would not recommend letting my worst enemy stay in here for a year. Losing sleep is the worst feeling you can have especially if you are paying for the main reason to sleep at night. 5 stars for everything but 0 stars for sleeping and the thin walls. Really please take this advice you can see the amazing place inside and out but you will get tricked when you fall asleep on the first night and realize you are stuck listening to everyone around you during the night. AVOID!!!!

I recently moved from another downtown location that was more frat house than house in the sky but I wanted to stay in the same area. The Lincoln was the perfect answer! Great location, all the same amenities, more space (a lot more space), better parking, safe, and a place I am proud to call home! The staff are great too!

I recently moved from another downtown location that was more frat house than house in the sky but I wanted to stay in the same area. The Lincoln was the perfect answer! Great location, all the same amenities, more space (a lot more space), better parking, safe, and a place I am proud to call home! The staff are great too!

I loved living at the HUE and downtown.  I am not a fan of all things new so the smart lock (think hotel room entrance lock) is a little annoying to me as I do not care about turning my appliances off from my cell phone (I am not a youngster and this does not matter to me!).  LOTS of hidden fees- the base rent is doable but if you are on a tight budget and have to stick to it, do not rent here.  The price can swing $40 or more monthly.  Management is great and any time I needed any repairs, maintenance responded quickly.

The apartments are nice but I wouldn?t go so far as to call them luxury. The hallways are freakishly cold, sometimes moldy and do not look clean. The garage is very nice with an abundance of parking but without clear lanes, cars zoom past in the middle and cause daily close accidents. The key fob system is great for security but is a serious annoyance with guests. There should be a way to unlock the garage or lobby doors from the apartment or an app.

The rooms are spacious enough, the amenities are of reasonable quality (with some minor issues here and there). Worth noting, however, that there are no options for recycling beyond cardboard, so if that's an issue for you then keep it in mind. Management is nice, but the gym and other communal facilities are a bit lacking. Overall, it's a fine place to live.

I enjoyed living there. I was there for 4 years and never had any problems. The apartments were nice, location is great, staff was helpful, and maintenance was quick. I also think you get more apartment for the price compared to a lot of the other luxury apartments downtown.
It's generally been really great. The location is top notch, and the construction of the building is second to none in the downtown Raleigh area.
Convenient location, great staff, good amenities

I must have moved in right after the people who had the bad experiences because there was all new management when I signed. The good: Located in the heart of downtown Raleigh, the Hue offers an optimal location for an area that's quickly revitalizing. The amenities are solid, if unspectacular - there's a decent fitness center, free coffee in the common area, and a salt water pool. The building was originally built to be condos, with poured concrete, not just "sticks," so sound absorption is better than it will be in many of the newer downtown buildings.

The bad: The property is owned by a multi-million dollar real estate company that has zero interest in serving customers. Be prepared to be treated as an entirely expendable source of income, not a resident of a building. The fees will wind up costing you $200-$300 more per month than the listed price, and the terms of leaving early will cost you anywhere between $4000 to $6000. Even if you pay them a buyout fee! 

In sum: It's a decent place to live. You'll pay less than you will at many other downtown sites. You'll also be treated poorly, and if you have to leave for any reason, you will be exorbitantly penalized.

First, the good: the building is clean, well-maintained, and ideally situated in downtown Raleigh. The neighborhood is rapidly evolving, and residents of the Hue will be located amid a bustling revitalization project taking place in Raleigh.

The amenities are solid, if unspectacular. A serviceable little fitness center, a pool, and a secured parking garage. Response time on service requests varies, but the individual staff who supply maintenance are really great.

Now, the bad (and, in my opinion, a good enough reason not to rent here): the terms of the lease border on extortion. You'll notice, off the bat, that you pay for internet connectivity regardless of whether you use it. There's a trash fee, despite the fact that you're walking your own garbage and recycling down to a dumpster. And various other charges. For a building of this sort, these are all fairly standard - but just to be clear: you will be paying a $200-300 a month over sticker price, once everything adds up. 

Worst: if you need to get out of your lease for any reason, you will pay them a 4 month penalty. That's right: multiply your monthly rent by 4, and prepare to hand them $6,000-$10,000 just for the right to walk out the door. What's more: the constant revolving door of leasing agents and property managers (none lasts more than a year or so) are either incapable of explaining this to residents or willfully mislead them. 

Buyer beware: it's a nice building, but there's a very real chance you get exploited financially for living there.

Instead of installing working security cameras and fixing the entrances, management spent money to repaint the building. Because priorities, right? More recently, someone broke into the complex (not hard to do since most of the doors to the building don't close all the way - anyone can walk in here at any time) and destroyed one of the elevators. To people who've had their property broken into or stolen, management tells you that you need to take better care of your belongings and offers absolutely no condolence or reassurance that things are being taken care of. Or they tell you to call the security officer to report things like doors being propped open or suspicious people - guys, reporting all of that would be a full time job. It's absolutely ridiculous. I've never seen more unprofessional management or a more insecure building - especially at this price point. Until massive changes have been made here, I would never recommend the Hue to anyone.

Staff is great, apartment is great... I will renew but I just expected a better atmosphere of tenants. Sometimes I just do not feel safe.
Horrible place to live.You can hear all the noise from outside, smoke free apartments but the smell of weed is very often outside and in the hallways
El personal es muy amable y son bien rápidos en atender cualquier necesidad o problema que se ofrezca en tu apartamento .
Staff made it very easy to apply and sign lease for desired apartment online. Special shout out to Raven and Dodge! Thank you.
This apartment is a dream. The layout is gorgeous and well worth the price. The leasing office made my move in such a smooth & seamless process. Im very excited about my new community.
Apartments need a little more closet space but it is a wonderful community and everyone is extremely friendly and nice and professional. The apartments are very clean and so are the yards.
I have been renting at Everly for 2 weeks now and I am enjoying it. The area is accessible to many stores and highways. I wish the access to the pool and gym were a little sooner.

My overall experience here has been fair. The appliance package and finishings are very nice. The soundproofing is not great, I can hear my neighbors walk upstairs and can occasionally hear them cough. The gym  and pool look very nice but they can get crowded and the pool area is quite noisy with the traffic from Tryon Road. 

The valet trash company is inconsistent with pickup and won’t return calls. If you need to take out your own trash, the compactors are always overflowing (see photo). 

Getting packages here is a pain. Half the time couriers will not put packages in the package room even if it is specified in the delivery instructions. The package room door does not close automatically, is often left open and is easily visible from the main road. I voiced my concern to the property manager who said there would be an automatic door closer installed, but this never happened after several months. 

For the price, I would recommend looking downtown. I personally think this is overpriced for the location/quality of service.

Poorly built property. Excessive noise from other apartments due to the poor design. You dont have to be a contractor to see all the corners they cut in building this place. Management SUCKS!!!!! Wifi is community based which is weird, and it’s ALWAYS going out. They don’t inform you when the water is being turned off. They never power wash the buildings. The fire alarms go off all the time even in the middle of the night. This place is a lemon. Shiny on the outside only.

Enjoy the fake reviews. Built horribly, office staff is garbage, amenities are broken or you're not allowed to use them. Gym equipment must have log ins for them. Useless machines.  You are not allowed access to the clubhouse. Dont depend on them for coffee. Door/Key system is the worst. Lots of car break ins but they wont tell you about it. New buildings built horribly. Moved into a damaged new apartment. Community littered with dog crap everywhere. No dog stations. Fire alarm issues and elevator problems. Package room is never closed. Shared forced internet - goes out every day. The area is homeless heavy now.

Lets see how many fake reviews come after this one to "defend" this crap hole. 

DONT EVEN BOTHER TOURING the fake newly built dumpster fire ninety nine apts.

This is a great place to live and a great area and environment. Very peaceful, quiet, not a lot of loitering, but more so people walking in the area for exercise, not a lot of visible disruptive behavior and a management staff that takes pride in the upkeep Ing of the grounds as well as, the apartments. I highly recommend people that are looking for great place to live to give it a try. The only way that I won’t renew my lease is if I decide to get a home. I look forward to another year and also, they have a lot of great activities for the residence for example resident appreciation week, different activities , that promote a closeness in the community of the residence, and also a great pool party had so much food, fun, fun, music that was very appropriate and easy on the ears, and a great ambience for the residence who had great interaction and fun give it a try and maybe you’ll see me there. **special shout out to Linsey(property manager), and Liliana and Zack that effectively run day to day operations, and last, but not least, the maintenance supervisor, who indeed is awesome. I could go on and on, but I just want corporate to know that if anyone of these individuals were to leave, then there would be a tremendous vacancy to fill…

Sincerely, 
 Kelvin J.
My lease ends tomorrow and I can say I enjoyed my lease term here. Excellent apartment and excellent service.

Nice staff and apartments. Everything is within driving distance. Very clean and well kept. Lilane( think that’s right ) and Reagan was the first two to help me when I first moved in and they are super helpful. Angie is also super nice and helpful. Think I learned everybody name lol but overall great place. Pool and weightroom are my favorites

The apartment itself is very nice, however the message that the leasing department provides “luxury” care and service is incorrect. I lived here for 18 months and upon my arrival it was under a different property management company, which was great from my experience. After Air communities took over, the quality of the environment declined. Now you struggle to get someone on the phone, getting your maintenance needs met which is horrible when dealing with ant infestations. The property is a new build so be aware of bug problems. I once had to throw away everything in my kids room, all of their toys included because ants infested our apartment in a span of 48 hours. I do want to emphasize that the pictures do match what you will get with your apartment, however its not worth much when the leasing office is not up to par. The amenities are nice but beware that the multitude of residents are a lot of younger adults, so forget about the pool and other amenities on weekends if you have kids. They get very rowdy and its uncomfortable being there with family. I have seen police being called for this several times. Lastly, there is a car break in problem in the neighborhood. Get the ring door bell app to stay up to date on those things. There is a parking lot that use to be free, but now you have to pay for parking which is ridiculous for a private lot.

Overall, the apartments are nice and a good distance to a lot of things, but the bad unfortunately outweighs the good and I would not recommend someone move here with kids or a family, or elderly.

The most incompetent staff I’ve ever dealt with. Not only did I refuse to move in because of the lack of professionalism, when I was refunded my deposit, they tried making me re-pay for a “move out” fee. I had to explain that I never moved in. New apartments across the street are much nicer and the staff is competent and reliable. Do not bother with this place.

It's a nice place to live, but it's not enough parking from the start. Then they decided to take some of the parking spots there and make them assigned parking spots...BUT if you want a spot you have to pay $25 extra a month per vehicle. Rent is already high enough.

I have found that it is very difficult to find a community that is both welcoming and beautiful and Raleigh Exchange offers both! All of the apartments are filled with lots of natural light, beautiful finishes, and oversized closets! The community is so beautiful too, I personally really love overlooking the ponds as I watch the sunset from my balcony. Even though we are in the city, this complex offers serenity that is so welcomed! So happy to be home!

I moved in less than a month ago. I’m very happy. Jenifer was very sweet and helpful. The rest of the staff members are equally welcoming. The maintenance man is wonderful. Always available to help. My apartment is beautiful. Very spacious and open for new decor. In less than a week I felt like I was home. There are so many windows and natural lighting that I do not put on any lights until 8 pm. There is a park near by for walking dogs, a children’s playground or just walking the path. It is pretty quiet day and night. Friendly neighbors to chat with if you like.

My experience here so far has not been a great one. So let me explain. When I first moved in, it was amazing... no deposit, top floor, great floor plan with great bathtub/shower. After about a month and a half, I started to smell cigarette smoke inside the building. Management did nothing about it for months. The excuse was we can't know who is doing it... we can't do anything about it. Are you sure it's not coming from the patio/balcony? We do allow people to smoke there. You know when people are smoking inside versus outside. My whole unit reeked. Finally, after the annual fire inspection, the smoking inside stopped. It took 4 months for the smoking inside to stop. On top of that, other residents in the complex must have complained as well because in the news email they send out to remind people not to be smoking cigarettes or Marijuana in common areas or apartment units. Also, beware that something you think that management should cover in repairs may fall to you. Renters beware!

My daughter, her GSD and I have had a mostly positive experience living at Marshall Park. Where there have been issues it's been with other residents not picking up after their dog or being inconsiderate of residents late at night. These issues have improved and the office staff have been supportive in responding to the community needs. I appreciate being able to communicate with our office staff via email or by stopping in to see them.

The only things that would make me hesitant to recommend this community are the inconvenient recycling and call boxes. It is very tedious to have to drive down to the dumpster just to recycle cardboard, and the call boxes, especially for the garage, are too confusing and it is frustrating having to explain it to people every time they use them.
I have recommended this community to friends and family. However, most of them feel it?s too expensive. They don?t see the reason for the expensive rates.
I would recommend the apartment because it feels very inviting and clean.
Maintenance responded quickly and left a note of confirmation detailing work that was done.

Rent is pretty good compared to the rest of Raleigh and the size of the apartments. Close to shopping amenities. However, management is sort of iffy with being on top of things. Have neighbors that work on their cars, I think even running a car repair shop out of their garage at this point creating noise. Management hasn't done anything about it since its been going on a year now. Bug issue but probably coming from other tenants within the building (roaches, house centipedes, etc.). Maintenance is usually pretty good, though have had issues with them not being on top of fixing some stuff but they do end up fixing it and replacing broken appliances.

Recently moved here and absolutely love it!!! Updated and clean apartment!! And all throughout the apartment complex is lovely! Staff stayed after hours to help with a code for door problem and fixed ! Can’t say enough good!!

As required, I submitted a punch list upon moving in and only one thing has been addressed. There are so many issues here.  Management is only concerned about full occupancy; not keeping tenants.  It is impossible to work with them because there is an excuse for everything.  Oh, they also charge you a fee to pay the rent. You are charged extra to just make the rental payment online.  And of course, that is what they want; it’s a scam.  If you are one day late, they also serve an eviction notice and take you to court.  Because they can take more of your money.   You are charged twice the regular amount for cable and internet because they have a contract with Spectrum.   You are required to buy renters insurance and name the apartment complex as beneficiary and the rates are high.  You are charged extra fees for everything.  Water, trash, etc.  and the trash service here is horrible.  One dumpster for hundreds of units and every week you can drive by (it is right up front) and see how nasty the people are.  There is always a lot of trash on the ground and overflowing from the dumpster.  I asked for several items to be repaired and cleaned prior to moving in; not one item was repaired or cleaned. There is mold and mildew and spider webs in windows.  There are large and unsightly holes knocked in the walls where a true drywall contractor would have used the proper tools.  Maintenance has come in once, on a rainy day without wearing shoe coverings.  They never came back to finish the job.  There are so many issues here.  I would never have moved here if I had known, but being new to the area, I did not know anyone.

Place is nice looking aesthetically, but don’t let that fool you... the AC cuts off during the summer season more than twice. It was a trail of ants everywhere in our apartment that we just got rid of an I know we didn’t bring them because we was here a year prior before and had no type of insect problem. The terminix spray they used didn’t work so we used our own little concoction an even that took sometime to help clear the problem up. It’s always something at this complex, smh

If i could rate this place a half a star, I would.. and that's because its the only way I'd be able to inform people to stay as far away from this community as possible. Ive had nothing but issues since I moved into this unit. And before you think this is a personal preference, I'd like to inform you that the entire building I live in also hates this place equally as much. There should be an ad posted in bright red letters "Do you like ants? Rather do you like ants living with you, do you also like living in a unit someone killed themselves in 6 years ago, better yet... do you like paying for a unit thats supposed to have 2 working ethernet ports but only one of them does because we're just too lazy to fix the problem the last 12 months we've known about?! Well come on down to the nastiest community in Raleigh and we'll be sure to have you living in disgust in no time." If that doesn't describe this place im not sure will

Moved in in July.  Apartment was not clean at move in.  Complained nothing done so I hired professional cleaner and paid with my money. Various issues and some handled.  But this month mouse got in somehow and being ignored.  I want to move.  Terrified or rodents.  Mouse got in closet and destroyed clothes and shoes .  Frustrated.  No one seems to care in office

Despite what they might say, these apartments aren’t luxury. They’re just fine. The appliances function, but not well. The oven, for example, heats up to a temperature nowhere near where it’s set and takes way more time to preheat than the indicator says. (Want to bake at 400°F? Set for 450°F or higher!) Maintenance and landscaping show the priorities of this place are all about getting you in, but not keeping you. The landscaping near the leasing office is great, but our old apartment in the back of the complex? The “planter area” outside our building was planted with... unkept grass that was 4 ft high. Along Alm St., there is a firm line near the main entrance where you see the trimming stops becoming a regular priority. When they mulch once a year, 50% is washed away in the next decent rainstorm because they don’t mulch enough and don’t keep up with water drainage. Geez! In one place across from the playground, every time it rains, there is a “mosquito pond” that forms over a blocked drain that sits for weeks. It’s been this way for all of 2019. When something in the playground broke, it took almost 3 months to fix and reopen. Why? There are four office workers to just three maintenance workers responsible for all 350 apartments and all the grounds. So, if you have a maintenance issue, be prepared to wait at least 4 business days for anything that isn’t a major emergency. Then there’s the trash problems. If you care about recycling, you can’t do it here. There are 6 bins for 350 apartments. That’s about 20 bins too few. And the trash compactor, your neighbors will be too stupid or careless to know how to use. People just throw their trash around, never bothering to open the door and put their bags in. The layouts of the apartments work well, but the total package isn’t worth the hassle.

No property is perfect and judging from previous reviews that is what people expect. I have lived here for quite some time and am very happy. No complaints on my end. If you want perfection then you should by a house, because apartment renting is not for you! I love the girls in the office and the maintenance team always greet you with a smile.
I love living here! The property is beautiful, the office staff, and maintenance team are friendly and caring. Best place to live in Brier Creek.

I have lived in this apartment complex for awhile, but sad to say, management and maintenance has gone downhill BAD.

Apartments are beautiful, but maintenance, management, and staff are HORRIBLE.  I will not be renewing my lease as there are plenty of other apartments to choose from in the Brier Creek location.

I lived here for several years....they keep have a rotating staff and management. The staff is very nice but management keeps getting worse...it saddens me because I love the location and the apartments are nice but I don't know how much longer I handle it :(

I have lived at Colonial Grand at Brier Falls for three months now and I am absoutely in love. The apartments come with upgraded amenities, washer and drier and beautiful spacious balconies and well priced. I must also say a beautiful apartment complex is even better with an amazing staff. The Staff members are incredible and pleasant to work with and the maintenance staff is super quick. In all I can see my self living here for a long time to come. Colonial Grand isn't just the apartment complex I live at, it's my home.

We have lived at this community for several years now and have noticed things going downhill. Residents leave their trash in the breezeways or throw it behind a building rather than take it to the dumpsters. Even though we have notified the leasing office about the trash behind the buildings they are slow to clean it up.

Unless you have a simple maintenance request, good luck getting the issue fixed. We had a issue with our heat constantly running but not heating. That took several maintenance requests before it was finally resolved but the issue also caused our power bill to be double for over 2 months.

We have a current issue that we have submitted multiple requests on but has not been resolved. It is going on 4 months now with no resolution in sight.

Other than these issues, the complex is located in a great location close to shopping, restaurants and easy access to the interstate. It is also close to the airport.

This place is an awesome location to brier creek shopping. Restraunts, shopping, parks, whatever you need is close to this complex. Awesome staff in the front thst have always taken care of me and could not be happier with the layout of the apartments. The pool is killer on top of everything else!

The view is beautiful. I have a pond in front of my apartment. The pool is resort style with a waterfall in front of it. My neighborhood is really quiet--I have had zero problems with noise so far. The staff is friendly. All of my friends are amazed about how spacious my place is to be a one bedroom. My only issue is with parking. I usually have to park far if I come home late at night. I wish they would regulate visitor parking because there is not enough room for everyone at my building.

The location is ideal and warranted, clean, & maintenance well. Shopping plazas, grocery stores, & the airport are less than five minutes away. Elementary school is walking distance, yet,school bus system will pick up. Middle and High Schools in Cary are ranked in the top 10 in Wake County.
Great Location, tons of amenities, and a variety of spacious floor plans. Residents make it a fun place to live. Leasing staff address all issues in a timely manner.
Very fast response to my request. Repairs were done quickly and professionally. My second request in 15 months and both handled without delay or any problems.

I have lived here for several years with several building management teams. I would currently recommend not living at SkyHouse.

SkyHouse is best known for its views and its safety. However, it no longer the same luxury standards set by previous building managements. This appears to be in-large part as Greystar changes the strategy held by previous managements.

The management team has struggled with their communication of severe maintenance issues (including the commonly known elevator woes) -- which do not appear to be close to being resolved despite it being a several month issue. The management team also appears to be struggling with the frustration expressed by current residents, incredibly protective rather than being conversational about issues.

It is one thing to be upset, it is another to not be hospitable.

Greystar has also begun to focus on catering to shorter-term stays -- including allowing AirBnb hosting and a new feature of a "guest stay." 

The building is forgo-ing cleaning carpets on floors in pursuit of new non-carpeted flooring and is making changes to the clubroom area that will impact quality of life. The building feels stripped of the qualities that made it a great place to stay, in-lieu for a cheapened approached intent on generating money.


It is evident that Greystar has a vision however that vision does not look out for current residents or residents in the short-term.

The only problem is that the elevators seem to be in constant need of repair. The long wait time for elevators can be annoying at times. Overall, Skyhouse has a great location for activities and restaurants and museums. And as a bus rider it has the best location for me.

As a current resident, I cannot stress enough how far this place has declined. It is way worse than I ever expected it to get, I wish I could give negative stars.

1. The Building is Filthy
The hallways are some of the dirtiest and most disgusting I’ve ever seen and such unsightly stains everywhere you look. It’s embarrassing to have guests over and make them walk through such unclean conditions. There is one cleaning person on staff who is always in the lobby "vacuuming" —but nothing ever looks clean. It seems like she is just pretending to clean, as no area has seen a vacuum or proper cleaning in months.

2. Amenities Are a Joke
Most of the amenities are broken and have been since I moved in. Even the ones that “work” are frustrating to use. For example, the upstairs TVs have about 10 remotes, but none of them actually function with the TVs. Instead of fixing these persistent issues that residents repeatedly raise, management has added a new, completely useless amenity that you have to pay extra for.

3. Guest Parking Was Removed
One of the main reasons we chose to live here was the access to guest parking. Mid-lease, they took it away with no real solution other than telling residents to “contact NC Park.” This shows a complete lack of accountability and disrespect for residents.

4. Broken Elevators and Long Wait Times
Prepare to add an extra 15 minutes to your schedule just to leave the building. One elevator has been broken for ages, and the remaining one is so overburdened that there’s often a line in the lobby. The other day, I had to wait through multiple elevator trips before I could finally get on.

5. Management is Nonexistent
The property management consistently fails to address issues. They don’t fix anything, they take away amenities, and they make false promises about renovations and hallway repainting that never happen. Their disregard for residents’ concerns is beyond frustrating.

Final Thoughts
I, along with several other residents, will definitely be moving out  after our lease due to the poor management and the rapidly deteriorating living conditions. At this rate, I’d be shocked if anyone renews their lease.

To management: Step up and start taking responsibility for your property and your residents’ experiences.
My time here has been the best experience of my life. I can’t wait to Rene my lease again and get 2025 started
Skyhouse has been a breath of fresh air after dealing with so many horrible living situations. The community is nice, people are friendly and I love to get a free view of pets :)

Pro:  beautiful view; love the apartment layout
Cons:  Dirty floors; dirty elevators; dirty loading dock; dirty walls; one elevator is frequently out of order and the service elevator might be locked for move-ins/outs, which means one elevator for the building

This apartment building is in an amazing location, surrounded by excellent restaurants, a square with lots of activities, and walking distance to the Amtrak station. It also has beautiful views and an incredible lobby with excellent concierge service. It is an older building so you can’t expect everything to be perfect and up-to-date as you would see in a new apartment building. But for a downtown city location, it cannot be beat.
Skyhouse is a great community and convenient to so much in Downtown Raleigh
Great staff, great amenities, great location and access to downtown attractions. Love the views I get from sun up to sun down.

I have lived here 1 and 1/2 years.  I love the convenient location and the views from Skyhouse.   We have a lovely Skydeck, with 2 grills and a firepit for winter.

However, the building desperately needs refreshing.  The carpets are disgustingly dirty.  Over the past couple of months, the elevators have had paint dribbled on the floor and walls/doors are scuffed badly.  The TV in the yoga/pilates room has not worked for several months so you cannot stream workouts there.  I could go on, but hopefully you get the picture.

Moore Square used to be a great area and now the homeless and gang population has gotten really unsafe, especially for single females. 

The leasing staff is terrible and rude. There are MUCH better apartment complexes and high-rises in better areas where the staff actually care about the residents.

Overall, I have had considerably mixed feelings about my two years at Skyhouse Raleigh.

The views are great, without a doubt. Concierge and the staff, in general, are all very friendly and helpful for the most part, including the maintenance staff.

However, there are problems with noise pollution. I have had my share of rude neighbors who constantly *slam* their doors and have lead feet. I have heard some horror stories from another resident who ended up having to have the police called on someone who was a constant disturbance despite submitting several complaints beforehand. It should have never gotten to this point for them.

It can be severe in colder climates. The frigid temperatures seem to cause openings in the balcony doors, which lets in a lot of outside noise pollution. That is on top of the elevators which can too be loud at times (to the point you can feel them vibrating the walls).

The portal software which is used to send rent payments and submit maintenance requests is buggy. I have had my share of issues with the software, most recently where I could not log in to send my payment properly and ended up getting stuck with a late fee because of it, then told that I could no longer provide payments using the portal system.

My rent has increased significantly since I first moved in. The first time it increased, I was offered the same free months rent incentive if I signed a lease for another year, or a 6-month lease with no increase in rent. This year, I was told I would not be given the same offer, and on top of that, if I was to opt for a 6-month lease this year my rent would be increased $100/month.

Skyhouse staff have started hosting pool parties and the likes again, which produce noise so loud it is constantly vibrating my walls in every room of my apartment all throughout the day. If this becomes a problem like it was my first year at Skyhouse again, I plan to terminate my lease and seek residency elsewhere.

So overall, very mixed feelings. There are times when I have loved it here, but now it has become incredibly frustrating.

If you're into constant partying and don't mind constant noise and the smell of pot lingering in your apartments occassionally, this could be a great place for you. But if you're a young professional truly trying to go somewhere with your life, I would recommend looking elsewhere. This was NOT the kind of environment I was promised, and I've started to regret moving here again this year.

I love living here. I never want to leave. There is a long list of great things I can share with you about this place after living here for the past six months. Here are a few.

Maintenance requests are always handled with exceptional speed. Same day service is normal. I have not had very many requests, but the ones that I have submitted have 100% been completed as expected and quickly.

To call the rooftop pool amazing is an understatement. It is awesome to float in a clean saltwater pool 250 feet above downtown Raleigh while drinking a cold beer and listening to a first class sound system. They also have TVs on the pool deck, which is an ideal place to watch football. The grills and fireplace on the other side of the roof are also very nice. The exercise room is always clean and they keep the AC at the right temp. Extra points for having wireless Internet in there. I can take my iPad and watch Netflix while doing my cardio.

The apartment itself is my favorite part. I love looking out my floor to ceiling 10 foot windows at the city skyline. The real hardwood floors are super classy. The exposed cement ceiling gives it a modern feel like no place I have seen. The granite countertops and stainless steel appliances are very sophisticated. Everyone that lives here that I have met so far is friendly.

This place is all around the best of the best. I can't wait for next summer to party on the roof again.

We moved to the SkyHouse Raleigh in May 2015 and LOVE IT!
Pros:
* Great office staff especially Kristel, Daniel, and Allyson. I don't know the others 
* The maintenance and the security staff are really good. It is a third party company supplying 24 security.  MOST of them are pleasant and helpful. Selena is very competent, pleasant represents the building with class.  
* The parking is acceptably convenient. It's covered parking and RIGHT next door with covered walkway between. 
* It has smokin' views from many apartments.
* The roof deck views are stunning and are the location of the gym, pool, clubhouse and outdoor kitchen. 
* The selection of local restaurants, parks, museums and concert venues is amazing.
CONS:
* It's a new building with all new staff.  At the beginning there was SOME adjustment period while they figured out how to work together and accommodate the unique challenges of the Raleigh location. It gets better EVERY day.
* Some of the tenants are a little whiny and impatient.  They OBVIOUSLY have never lived in a highrise apt.  It has unique problems but, fantastic benefits.  Relax people you are not that important. 
* They still need to resolve how they deal with visitors. I've lived in several high rises in major cities. The solution is not quite here. I don't mind the level of security.  I rarely even lock my door during the day when home.  
* The compressor for the air conditioner is on your balcony.  Luckily it's not a really loud one.  They did this to avail the rooftop for the amenities.  Also, you don't want to live in a building with shared air of any kind. TRUST ME ON THAT ONE! 

¡MOVE IN IT'S A GAS!

Skyhouse offers luxury amenities, cool modern apartments with amazing views of downtown and beyond, great staff, and the location can't be beat! I absolutely love living here! 4 stars instead of 5 because it's a brand new building and they are still working out the kinks, the units are on the small side, and the price is at the top of the market.

The units inside are great but the property outside is terrible. Everything is broken, gross, and there is trash everywhere. All the pool furniture is broken and has been broken since last year, management won’t replace it. The pool itself is always dirty and never really clean. And there’s all kinds of car breakins but no security improvements.  Wish they’d improve in the exterior of the property because it wouldn’t be a bad place but at this point it’s just dirty and unsafe.

I'm approaching my fifth year at The View and I couldn't be happier. This community is simply a beautiful place to live. Its parklike atmosphere and the friendly interaction among the office staff, the maintenance crew and the residents, many of whom like me have been here for years, makes it a nice place to call home.  In this crazy world we live in these days, it's comforting to live in a lovely safe environment like The View.

I've just signed my sixth lease - needless to say I love living here!  It's a clean, safe, and friendly community.  The staff is great - always cheerful and helpful.  Management is always working to make it an even better place to call home!  If you're looking for a new home - you'll love it here!
Laid back quiet community, nice apartment. Good area for restaurants and stores.

I love my apartment and just signed for a 2nd year! I have so much space and storage and it feels more like I live in a house then an apartment. I really like not having to look at a parking lot when I'm on my balcony. It just feels really good to be home! The staff here is amazing, especially the maintenance guys. They are all so friendly and so quick to take care of my work orders. They have great events every month but because of covid, they are on hold :( I saw some comments about the internet and I only know that I have never had any issues even now having to work from home. I've had to move a lot in the last 15 years and this by far is the happiest I have been in an apartment! Thank you to the staff for everything you do!
The amenities are nice, but there is constant - as in seven days a week, 10 hours a day - noise from construction.

Well it's that time of year. I can't believe it's been a year already, and it's been a wonderful year living here. I LOVE the area! The office and maintenance staff are always friendly with great customer service and helpful when something is needed. We have enjoyed the pool/grill area. I can't wait till it gets cool to enjoy the fire pit!!  A HUGE THANK YOU to my Asst. Apartment Manager Mr. Kristan for assisting me with my upcoming lease renewal. THANK YOU AND I LOOK FORWARD TO ANOTHER YEAR AT AVELLAN SPRINGS!!

If I could say one thing its dont live here. 
The apartments have an old bone structure and as they renovate only so much of it. 
The cockroaches are everywhere in the apartments to the point where “pest control” dont do nothing.

I live at The Enclave at Crossroads and have a 2nd floor 2x2. The apartment is so unique due to the fact I have my own private entrance. Both of my bedrooms and bathrooms are on opposite ends for added privacy. Plus, I have a real wood burning fireplace. This by far is the best bang for your buck!

I lived at Waterstone for 18 months and these are my thoughts on the complex.

The good parts.  The apartments are quite well designed, spacious and with good traffic flow.  They’re fairly quite as far as noise from the other apartments are concerned.  The fitness center is marginally adequate and apt. maintenance is pretty quick and good.  There’s plenty of parking and Brier Creek is very close.

The not-so-good parts.  You’ll never see your actual apartment until you move in.  It’s always “not available yet” and won’t be until your move-in time. So, you’ll be shown the model unit.  This wouldn’t be so bad except that you’re probably not moving in for a month or so yet you need to make a decision as movers will have to be lined up, etc.

Snow removal is a joke.

If you’re unfortunate enough to get a unit near the pool, forget about regular sleep in the spring, summer and fall.  While the pool area is supposed to close at dusk, everyone ignores the rules and there’s never anyone to enforce it.  People will often leave and leave the TV on blaring away at 2:00 in the morning.  What’s particularly annoying is that roughly half of the party goers don’t even live in the complex.  Also, airport noise is not too bad except in the mornings (around 6:00 or so) and there is a constant airport and highway drone all the time.

The fitness center is small but adequate.  However, half the TV’s on the machines don’t work, no towels on the weekends and it’s cleaned about once a year whether it needs it or not.

Beware of the language in the lease.  I almost took a job out of state which would mean needing to break my lease.  Well, there’s a 2-month penalty for breaking the lease and a 2-month penalty because you didn’t give them 60-days’ notice that you were going to break the lease.  So, if your rent is $1,250/month for example, that’s a $5,000 penalty in addition to everything else.  I finally got my security deposit ($200) back about 2 ½ months after I moved out and threatened to go to small claims court.  Of course, it was reduced to about $98 after they got through with every nickel and dime item they could think of.

It’s a bit worse than similar complexes because the management has a “I AM THE LORD THY GOD” attitude.  While they’re pleasant initially, develop an issue and either they don’t know anything about your problem, can’t do anything about your problem or “that’s the way corporate works and it’s your problem. “
Would I live there again?  Nope, not a chance.

We used the gym, pool, laundry room and club house probably more than any other residents to pass through. The community grill and outdoor TV are a great perk to living here as well.
