First and foremost the office staff was fantastic. They took the time to show us our options and gave us all of the information we needed to make an intelligent choice. That was not always the case elsewhere. Very professional and friendly! The apartment itself is all we need. Spacious, well appointed and are quiet. The maintenance staff is responsive and extremely friendly. If you need an apartment look no further. This place deserves the five stars.

After downsizing from a house/yard, been living here for a year and love it.  Quiet community and friendly neighbors.  High ceilings and lots of light.  The grounds are nicely landscaped and well-kept with tree-lined sidewalks close by for walking/running.  Close to trails and not far from James River outdoor spaces. Nice to have restaurants close by when you don’t feel like cooking! The leasing office managers and the maintenance team are friendly and open with an easy smile and hello, responding quickly to requests.  Convenient location to get around town.  Very glad I chose Creek’s Edge community.

The apartments have plenty of natural light, are up-to-date, and have a spacious kitchen. Management and maintenance teams are kind, very friendly, and respond within 24 hours to concerns. Best apartment complex I've lived in!

I’ve here for a number of years, and find this to be a hidden gem.  The staff is friendly and responsive, and the owners have been excellent at being proactive with updates (washers and dryers, appliances, amenities) rather than waiting for stuff to get old and ragged before replacing it. 

The location is great and is really convenient to Stony Point Fashion Park (obviously), Chippenham, the West End, Powhite Parkway, and Carytown.  Because it’s not on a main thoroughfare, traffic noise is minimal.

It’s a great place to live and I highly recommend it.

Being here the past year as we transitioned to our forever home was the best thing we could have every done. The staff is kind and compassionate..and always responsive. The property is beautifully kept and maintained.  I would recommend this over and over again to anyone.  It's a nice quiet place to sojourn as you travel thru.  My hats off to them. They are 5 star!!

Went to see this property today, which is advertised on their website as open until 5pm on Saturdays. Very nice gated community with swimming pool and many amenities. The staff is very friendly and do a great job. The maintenance guys are great and always do a good job. The location is great for getting around Richmond. Pet friendly but I do think the pet deposit could be lower. The charge for each animal plus monthly fee is more than enough to take care of damages.

My family moved into an apartment at Creeks Edge almost 5 years ago and we have loved every minute of it.  The office staff has been nothing but gracious with any questions or concerns we have ever had & the maintenance staff has been absolutely SENSATIONAL!!  I would/have HIGHLY recommend this property to anyone that is looking for a friendly & happy community.

Be sure to check the fine print of the pet policy & get in writing the life expectancy of the carpet before you sign your lease. I verbally lodged my concern about the condition of the carpet before I moved in & was told there was 23 months left on the current carpet before they would replace it. I lived in my apartment for 24 months & unfortunately 3 months before the end of my lease my dog was diagnosed with bladder cancer & had several accidents on the carpet. I kept the front office informed throughout the entire emotionally draining ordeal & also told them about having the carpet professionally cleaned. I was thanked for doing so but informed it was not necessary due to carpet due to be replaced anyway. However after moving out I received a bill for $700 for carpet damages. I challenged this due to the information I received from two of their staff (at move in & move out) that it was now due to be replaced. I was now being told that the carpet STILL had 23 months remaining after I moved out & that no one at Creeks Edge ever provided me with information about my carpets life expectancy. Also, they refused to test the air in my unit because "they just don't do that" even with the presence of mold in the provided dehumidifiers and the concern that it is in the air ventilation.
- Mail Distributers Do Not Have Access/Keys To The Parcel Pending Lockers: Packages get stacked next to it and all over the desk and table in the front. They charge a fee and it is not optional, you are paying for a service that the mail distributers are not using. I've been a tenant at Todd Lofts since 2013 and I used to love it here. The all-inclusive monthly rent simplifies things and the staff are nice. However, Todd Lofts has been making a number of renovations to its units and facility, many of which have been quite invasive and with many of those events happened with little warning. While this would have been worth it for the value of the new improvements if they had grandfathered in current tenants, they opted not to do this and most tenants saw astronomical increases in their rents (mine was a 25-30% monthly increase). Considering the difficulties of the renovations, having to deal with a sudden and substantial rent increase was a slap in the face, and to add further injury they decided to no longer give any rent concessions to renewing tenants. Rule #1 of business: reward good and loyal customers. I renewed my lease only because I was far too busy with other things to go apartment hunting right now. Word to the wise: if you are splitting the rent with someone, this place could still be a good deal. However, don't be surprised when they eventually take you for granted as a tenant and jack up your rates. If this isn't a concern for you, you may enjoy being a tenant here.

I call the office 2 months ago about a rats problem no help went in the off again this month to re report the rats problem and fixing my sink they messed up NOTHING I WENT YESTERDAY TO SHOW PICTURES OF RATS EAT MY FLOOR UP LETS SEE WHAT HAPPENS -100 rates

Cockroaches outnumbered the Richmond city residents. Had a hole in the ceiling of my bathroom for at least a year and black mold. Was never taken care of before I moved out. Lived there three years. Rent kept being raised by more than allowed. Do not recommend at all.

Smoke alarm took a month to be replaced (after move-in) 2 months after it was reported.

Don't mind the mice and cockroaches. They won't fix it, do routine prevention, and according to the lease is 100% your responsibility. Glue traps are the only thing that works, and those are horrific.

Maintenance staff, now that they aren't fixing an entire building, are great. They come quickly, they are respectful and get the job done right. Sometimes things aren't all the way fixed (our dryer was not wanting to dry in a reasonable amount of time) they came back 2 times since the first attempt didn't work.

DON'T! Just DON'T.  If you can afford a little more then DO it and find something better. Maintenance has always been decent and the people in the leasing office are friendly. Appliances in the apartment are nice, I've never had any issues with anything. My biggest complaint is that you HAVE to have Verizon cable/internet, which sucks because they charge a boatload for it. I have to pay like $115 a month, which is ridiculous because this is an INCOME-RESTRICTED place and you would think they would let you have something else a bit cheaper. The property used to have nice landscaping but have since changed companies and dogs trash the grass so it does not look nice anymore. Management does not respond to your emails/concerns, new maintenance guys are ok, community feel is not there, it is a loud complex with dogs barking and loud cars at night. Decent place but poor management and overpriced. Would not recommend this place or any other BH management properties.

Amazing complex, great amenities and location and even better floor plans

I love the area and it's really amazing when you love your apartment too! The staff and neighbors are friendly. Couldn't ask for a better home!

I have lived in three apartments: on VCU's campus, in the fan, and now here in Manchester. I just renewed for my third year here at Terraces, the longest I've stayed anywhere. Really soundproof building, which I greatly appreciate, but I have considerate neighbors on my floor too. Super pet-friendly and has tons of dogs! I wish parking was still included in rent, that is my biggest complaint. They raised rent, pet fee, and added a $60 (indoor) monthly parking fee- with no upgraded amenities. Greedy Thalhimer is the one to complain about- the staff itself here is lovely. Maintenance will come the day of or the next day 95% of the time to resolve any issues, there is an emergency service line if necessary too. I have to guess this is some of the best views in Richmond (depending on where your unit faces.) The building is cleaned almost excessively and is never dirty. Walking distance to the James River trails, footbridge, as well as Brown's Island. Cute local spots around the area and easy access to downtown to eat. I love exploring Manchester and it's definitely an up-and-coming area. Many residents I meet come here from the surrounding buildings, and say they're horrible. I've scoped them out and the rent is not significantly lower enough to be worth a horrible living experience. Terraces is worth the splurge, and I doubt you'll have regrets. I have no complaints about my living experience here.

I’ve lived here 1.5 years in 2 units and could not be happier with the building, residents and staff. Customer service is second to none. The views, amenities and finishes in the apartments are 5 star all around. I love living here!

The views from the entire building are incredible and the beautiful property has exciting upgrades happening all the time, I love the new outdoor dog park! The management team go above and beyond to make residents feel at home and respond to issues quickly and professionally. Manchester is an exciting place to live, close to beautiful trail walks, Browns Island festivals and great places to eat & drink.

Highly recommend this building to anyone looking to live in RVA.

Coming up on the end of my time at the Edison I thought I'd detail the best and worst parts of living in this building in hopes it will help those looking for a Richmond apartment. Overall my experience has been quite positive.

The best:
1. The actual apartment- I absolutely LOVE my apartment itself. The layout is unique (I have a loft bedroom), with high ceilings, lovely features like granite countertops, floor to ceiling windows, and a spacious living area.
2. The amenities- the gym, yoga studio, lounge, common patios, and movie theatre are very nice to have in the building and are always kept clean and in mostly working order.
3. The staff- I've always had positive experiences with the leasing office and the maintenance staff is fantastic. They have fixed any and all issues I have had within 24 hours.

The Worst:
1. The parking garage- To be totally fair, the garage is managed by an outside provider so these issues are not totally the Edison's fault. The garage is full of horribly tight spaces and turns, terrible parking jobs, ONLY has access to the building on the 6th floor, and is $110/month which is rather expensive for Richmond. Additionally, two floors of spaces are "reserved" for a VCU partnership so be prepared to go to the top of the 8 floor garage if you're coming home from work.
2. The location- If you work downtown, you might love the location! However, for myself as a recent college grad I was looking for walking distance to night life and restaurants. There is some of this around, but not a lot so driving and Ubering is your new best friend. If you're looking for what I was in a location, I'd recommend looking in Scott's Addition or the Fan. 
3. Storage space- Within my apartment, the storage is lacking. There is no coat closet, no drawers in the bathroom (only the under the sink cabinet), and the washer/dryer closet has no storage space. In the kitchen, drawers are really tiny. There are quite a few cabinets, but only high up so the configuration of your stuff was bothersome.

Again, overall I really did enjoy my time at the Edison. For me, the positives did outweigh the negatives and I would recommend this building to anyone looking for a reasonably priced and wonderful place to live.

We have lived in Pohlig for 2 years. 

Good Stuff: There is no denying this place has great charm as a renovated industrial space, tall ceilings, wood floors, etc. The location is really great too - only a few blocks from Libby Hill, shopping, restaurants, and other urban amenities. Matt, the property manager, is a good dude and is pretty responsive and helpful.

Bad Stuff: I work in construction and I can say confidently that the quality of the renovation work they did several years ago was not great. We've had leaks in our ceiling from the unit above, faulty refrigerator, and can regularly hear dripping in the walls when faucets are running. The WORST problem, though, is how much noise you can hear from other units. Even normal walking from upstairs neighbors will sound like thundering and creaking on the old floor boards. God forbid your next-door neighbors are loud, because you can hear almost everything that is said and done in adjacent units. After a year of living here, we had new (extremely disruptive) neighbors move in next to us and the noise is so problematic that we will not be renewing our lease. If your neighbors are normal people or don't have pets, it will probably be OK, but otherwise, good luck with the acoustics. - It's hard to understate this problem.

Location is great--easy walking to Shockoe Bottom, downtown, Capital Trail and the river, and smaller parks like Libby a block away. Plus the market and drug store are conveniently outside the back door--literally. While the finishes inside individual units are being upgraded, the community-feel has diminished in the last year under the more corporate management. Long time tenants are leaving monthly probably for this reason. Rent increased exponentially within months of this shift in ownership--around the start of the pandemic of all times, yet common spaces do not reflect the increase as promised; in fact they are less clean. The lower level exit sign now hangs from a wire and those halls have become someone's personal storage, lined with furniture. The clean scent of the lobby from a weekly plug-in: gone; mail scattered all about the lobby desk; discarded items left for charity and never removed; stairwells often in desperate need of sweeping; plants in front of building: dead or on their way there. As the tenants leave, there is near constant construction noise in the various units as they are upgraded for new tenants. Warning, too, the "free" DirectTV doesn't work in storms and heavy rain, the "free" high-speed internet sometimes goes out or slows to a crawl for no apparent reason, and the HVAC is super loud while the walls are scarily thin. You'll hear your neighbors cough (among other things); luckily, most neighbors are quiet and respectful of this feature. Matt and Colin are pretty responsive to maintenance and other issues, so that's good as well.

To be close to downtown, the interstate, the best restaurants, and to feel like you can still get away from it all.  The building is beautiful and the apartments have really nice finishes. There is never a wait long for maintenance work to be done. You can't get any closer to a grocery store or CVS.  Most importantly, Holly is the best property manager I've ever worked with!
