I've been here since May 1st and things couldn't be any better!  This  building is well run.  Everything is aimed at pleasing the residents.  And maintance is excellent!  All staff members do a magnificent job!!

Apartments are very old and outdated. Winters are very cold (building controls heat). Maintenance fixes things but takes along time to do. I’ve had two leaks in my closet the second one took 2 weeks to fix.

Old outdated apartments. Bad water pressure, old plumbing, apartments have been leaking for 3 years with nothing done about it. No routine maintenance in the units only half attempted fixes. Will let you move in prorated, but will not work with you if you need the last month prorated. Break in recently that the property managers did not make residents aware of even though they are capable of email alerts.

1. always wired sound during the night
2. winter is so cold, but no one wants to fix it
3. lots of bugs and flys
4. leak on the ceiling
5. even you clean all, they will not give you the full refund. You have to make sure it is like when you moved in, apparently, it is impossible.

Never have had a problem. Sure it doesn't offer high end amenities as newer modern apartment, but the property is well kept, maintenance is quick to respond when needed, and the community is quiet. People do like to park in the fire lane, which is also the entrance/exit and can be annoying. Some parts of the building could use a little modern renovation. It is conveniently located to many places as well.

Living there had so many ups and downs, it smelled, it was small, and people were always in the fire lane including the manager. But let me tell you, we "upgraded" to a fancier bigger place, and I never realized truly how much PM was my home. I honestly really miss living there. Though they did take forever to clean empty apartments and fix simple things

Very basic apartment. If you only need a roof over your head, then this is the place for you.  I could go on about the bugs, Cigarette smoke in the halls, clutter in the maintenance room (that is also the back exit door), and people parking in the fire hazard lane (including property manager) but instead I'll just leave my rating.
It was okay. It could use a renovation.  It was hard to find parking spot. High turnover in property managers. I did not like package pickup hours which were mostly in daytime.
Madeline was very thorough in her tour and review of the building and room. Knowing every resident and employee that came through is a great endorsement of how they manage the property.

Madeleine, our new leasing lady is absolutely amazing, she goes over and above for our home here at the Oliver House, we love it here and hope not to move want this to b our last move. The building is well maintained, so we r here for the duration. Thank u K&D
Awesome community, friendly residents and staff. The property is always clean and work orders are taken care of in a timely manner.
I have been at the Oliver House for about a month, it is at really nice and clean property. The staff are super friendly and maintience gets things done in a timely manner. I would highly recommend.
The best darn customer service I have experienced and I have live at the Oliver house for 12 years. keep up the great work Oliver house.

The Oliver House is a hidden gem. The staff is very friendly and always so very helpful. The new staff in the office is awesome!!! The buildings are clean, easy access to the bus line and a laundry area on each floor. I love living here!!!!
Madeline was very helpful and super friendly, she made the tour fun and answered all of our questions. The complex was very clean and well kept.  We will definitely be considering living here!

Madeline and Debra are the most
Welcoming, wonderful people! They gave us the best tour and made us feel so welcome!!! We were blown away by our experience and how beautiful the apartments were!!!!

This apartment is more like a home without all the extra responsibilities.  It has ever amenity you want, and the location is in the center of it all. The surroundings are extremely well kept, and the apartment units are very well appointed. You will find the atmosphere serene with esthetic views.
If you are empty nesting or just want an uncomplicated life style, this is the place for you!
You have to see it for your self to believe it!

Lived here 9 1/2 years; large suites, quick maintenance request response, accommodating office hours, friendly neighbors, outstanding staff from office, housekeeping, and maintenance, manicured grounds, pool and courtyard available, centrally and conveniently located for public transportation, travel, shopping, and socializing. Love my space!
Nice apartment with great friendly people  They take care of the grounds very well.

Not worth the rental price.. especially for a 1 bedroom apartment. Everything looks outdated.
The corridor and kitchen looks outdated.
Not familiar with maintenance. I only visited.

I would have say that after living in Kensington Club for a year that apartments are average and no noise complaints.Parking passes can be hard to find!Everybody pretty friendly.They do spray for bugs and have air conditioners built in Apts.

When we moved out and our "Statement of Account" came in, we were asked to pay for an additional month (May) even though we haven't lived there since April 30th. This place claims to be Luxury. But, it's just over priced. Security doors choose to lock at will. Buzzer system works in only half the buildings. Roaches. Washer/Dryers smell like mildew. Outdated shag carpets.

Overall, despite the negatives it is a really good living experience. Relatively cheap considering all the square footage that I receive and the close proximity to some really nice events and businesses.

Management is awful. They entered my unit on more than one occasion with absolutely no notice. Denied that they entered despite leaving equipment in the unit and being caught on my security camera. I called the owner after seeing almost a dozen apartments that were marked “available” but told me he didn’t have any until October but left all the units marked “available” to keep the photos up and people calling. HORRIBLE liar.

Great location. Large apartments. Maintenance is always up to date. Landlord is responsive and fair. He will always try and help and goes out of his way to be accommodating. Building is quiet with a large percentage of long time residents. Always peaceful after dark. Neighbors are friendly. Overall, a great place to live. I’ve lived here for nearly 4 years.
Landlord does not keep up with building or his responsibilities. He will try to blame you and then keep your security deposit for issues from before you moved in that you dealt with the whole time.
I lived here for a year a I really enjoyed it. The landlord is nice, the property is well kept, and my unit was updated and clean.

My experience at Norwood place was great from the very beginning. Love the fact that they have an app where you can submit any tenant request and also easily set up automatic payments. 
The apartments are just beautiful and spacious and the area is perfect! Very conveniently located near a lot of restaurants, supermarkets and walkable areas which are a must for me. Would definitely love to live again there without hesitation.

The apartments at Norwood are lovely, with updated appliances, no pest issues, and friendly neighbors. However, the lack of responsiveness from management is a significant drawback that would make me reconsider renting here.

Upon moving in, I immediately noticed several issues, including chipped paint, missing light bulbs, a missing shower rod, cut cable lines, and no mailbox key. Internet connectivity was initially hindered due to cut cables, requiring multiple technician visits. Additionally, there is no secure place for packages despite assurances otherwise.

The window wasn’t replaced for two months, during which it was sealed shut, preventing me from opening it. Once replaced, the caulking around the windows took another month to complete, finally being finished in the fall after repeated rescheduling and reminders.

While there were moments of prompt service, the overall maintenance responsiveness at Norwood Apartments was inconsistent, often requiring persistent follow-up. Despite the nice space, the lack of reliable and responsive management is a significant issue. Many problems in my apartment went unresolved for too long, which is a non-negotiable for me.

Let's start with the radiators—they seem to have a mind of their own, emitting a cacophony of clanks and hisses that echo throughout the apartment. It's impossible to find peace or rest with such a disruptive soundtrack constantly playing in the background.

Speaking of disruption, the walls might as well be made of tissue paper. Conversations from neighboring units are as clear as if they were happening right in my living room, leaving no semblance of privacy or tranquility.

As if the structural integrity weren't already in question, the ceiling has decided to join the fray, with cracks and leaks appearing as if on cue. Waking up to find bits of plaster on the floor has become an unwelcome routine.

And then there are the bugs. They seem to have taken up permanent residence, infiltrating every corner of the apartment despite all efforts to keep them at bay.

Adding insult to injury, the lack of air conditioning during the sweltering summer months is nothing short of unbearable. Residents are left to swelter in the heat, with no relief in sight.

To top it all off, the pervasive smell of smoke lingers in the air, making it impossible to escape the acrid odor of burnt offerings.

In short, Clifton Lake Apartments is a far cry from the peaceful sanctuary one expects from a place called home. Between the noisy radiators, thin walls, crumbling ceilings, unwelcome guests, lack of air conditioning, and the smell of smoke, it's safe to say that this is one living situation best avoided.
My apartment constantly smelled like smoke and management never did anything about it. Even though I sent countless messages.

review: Awful management, I don’t know why it says they offer internet access on here because they do not, they aren’t upfront with their prices, terrible plumbing, it’s hot as hell in here and the ac has never been turned on in my apartment even though maintenance requests have been put in, when I moved in the ceiling was falling apart which they never told me about until they were moving me in, I’ve lived here for 8 months now it’s still never been fixed, the microwave stopped working and hasn’t worked in forever, one of my toilets is no longer working, I have a room that is supposed to have a glass window it overlooks the living room, if you aren’t careful you can definitely fall out of the window and get seriously hurt, they scam you out of money, they started charging 45+ for parking in the surface lot that was previously free, it’s always dirty and the laundry room is in the depths of the building, my apartment got broken into back in March and they said they would put a bracket on my door and never did, they’re constantly renovating stuff but can’t fix anything inside the actual apartments, and even when they renovate they never finish what they started

review: The location is great! You’re near major highways, Ohio City, Downtown, Lakewood and major store plazas. Units are roomy and they have free parking lot.

review: The apartments are spacious and the staff are very friendly! The maintenance works usually get job orders done within a day or 2. There are the occasional bad tennants that clog the trash shoot/ not picking up after their dog poop due to no doggie bags being provided.

review: This is the worst place to live. It is very dirty with trash everywhere, management is awful, there is no security during the day to run the drug addicts off, the electric bills are out of control, they nickel and dime you for everything such as trash, water, sewer, and a bogus admin fee. review: Love the unique character of the apartments. Apartments have exposed brick and oversized windows which I love. Also nice to find a place that is clean and pet friendly. apartmentName: The Brick Lofts at Historic West Tech
review: I currently live in a three bedroom three bathroom. While the structure is nice ( 1 bathroom, laundry room, kitchen, and 1 bedroom on the first floor; 1 bedroom living room bathroom on 2nd floor; master bedroom master bath on 3rd) the utilities plays a big role in one of the many cons of this building. The building is brick, making it hard too keep the apartment heated. As a tenant you are only required to pay electric, however everything is ran off of you lights. Heat, cooking is electricalmaking an average light bill of 350/month. They offer the option of renting a washing machine for 60/month on top of paying a 75/month for underground parking. While underground parking doesn't seem like a necessity, parking is very limited. If you get off after 4, you can forget about it. All of this glory for 1285/month. The walls are so thin that I can hear my neighbors alarm clock. Need I go on?

apartmentName: The Brick Lofts at Historic West Tech
review:
I've lived at West Tech for almost two years, and I can't say I'm happy with my choice. I chose West Tech for the reasonable prices and large space. But unfortunately that's all they have to offer. The pet friendly apartment has a yard that is constantly littered with dog feces and trash. The halls are regularly littered with trash after hours and on weekends when the cleaning lady isn't working. The fire alarms go off at least once a month without notice, and that doesn't include the regular fire alarm testing that they do. The hallways regularly smell of pot. Our neighbors smoke both pot and cigarettes causing our upstairs bedroom to smell of them as all. The maintenance requests can take weeks to be completed as long as you keep on them about it. Otherwise it may not get done at all. Lastly before i move onto the apartment itself, is the parking lot and security. The parking lot is consistently littered with vehicles in disrepair, despite the warnings displayed that threatening towing. Several vehicles stolen out of the parking lot and parking garage due to lack of security and the constant foot traffic by non residents on the property. 
     The apartment itself is spaceous. The walk in closet and huge master bath with his and her sinks is awesome. However apon moving in, I was very disappointed what I saw. The carpet was stained, the cupboards needed a significant amount of touch up painting done. 2 of the light globs were broken, walls still needed painted and the some of the appliances were usable but in disrepair. 
      In summary, I would not recommend this place. There are better units around Cleveland for around the same price.

If I were moving into the stockbridge now these are the things I would want someone to tell me:
-Take pictures of everything on move in day.  A week after I moved out of my apartment I received an email saying that I had damaged the floor and bathroom door.  Both were in the same condition they were when i moved in.  Thank god I take an obnoxious amount of photos of my cat because I only had evidence of the existing damage in the background of cat pics.
-The neighborhood is no good.  Carry mace and don't wear headphones ever.  Trust me.
-Put your mattress in a bedbug proof cover.  The only time I've come across bedbugs was in this building.  
-The police will probably bang on the front door to arrest one of your neighbors at some point.  Let them in and take the elevator, they'll use the stairs. 
-Get acquainted with your local tenants rights group and know what you need to do to put your rent into escrow if repairs go unaddressed.  
This is hands down the worst building I've ever lived in.  Competent and helpful building management does exist-just not here.

Stockbridge is very affordable with rent that includes utilities and a close location to the highway. There are some grocery stores near by, but the 15 minute walk to Heinen's is worth it. You will have to pay monthly for parking. There are the garage spots which are  in the building's basement, or the back lot with a gate. The back lot has issues with cars being damaged or broken into, and has happened multiple times in the time I have lived here. The gate also occasionally breaks. The building is very sound proof, and I have had no issues with my neighbors. Most of them are very nice or keep to themselves. Either way I was happy with the people I lived around. The heating can be a bit much at times and it is not controlled in unit, so you will have to email them about the settings. The kitchen feels like it was just placed into the apartment. It is very small and fits one person, and the lack of ventilation above the stove is somewhat bothersome to me. I haven't had a maintenance issue so I am unsure as to how responsive they are in that regard. I will say that I wish that they had a better way of communicating with tenants. There was maintenance on piping so they shut the water off without any notification. I emailed and they were responsive to letting me know what was going on, but I feel that prior communication would have been better. Overall it has been an average experience with some experiences being better than others.

Loved living here. Place is older, but well maintained. If I ever had a problem, it was taken care of by the maintenance guy. I only moved, because I bought a home.

First i'll start with when we first moved in the carpet was disgusting, tub wasn't clean, and they had paint all over everything. I was in the apartment closest to the woods, BAD IDEA! We got ants terribly and then after we got the ants to go here come the MICE. Come to find out this is a normal thing you could literally hear them in the walls or see them dart across the floor in the evening. Last thing  is the parking they were having an issue with visitors parking in resident parking so they started going crazy with the tow truck. You would go to bed just to wake up to your car gone. I knew several residents including myself that got wrongfully towed and they could have cared less about reimbursing. Just save yourself the trouble you could find a better apartment for the price they're asking for this dump. WORST YEAR EVER!

First..They have mice annually as the weather starts to get nice. It doesn’t matter if you’re clean or not because they will come into your apartment and make themselves at home. 
Second...they said there were no dogs allowed but I’ve seen residents sneaking dogs on the property. Third...we’ve called the landlord several times about our garbage disposal because it was broken and nobody came to fix it.
Lastly...they didn’t clean the apartment before we moved in. The tub was dirty and there was dust and dirt everywhere.

The layout on the inside of the Townhouses are nicely spacious for a couple or small family! We did get very dirty carpet and mold within the bathroom when we first moved in.... Although the noise barrier and parking situation is a little irritating...youre only given 2 spots to park and it is VERY tight parking so be prepared to get bumps and scrapes. The walls are thin and you can hear neighbors doing unspeakable things. The neighbors on our side love to argue and scream and on top of that you are next to train tracks that can be loud sometimes unless you are used to that. If you have your windows open you can hear everything going on outside even if there are people hanging outside talking. Goodluck if you decide to move in!
The office staff was very helpful when I moved in. They are very responsive to any matters that you would have.  Would recommend them to friends.

If you want to live the maintenance free life of apartment living, Tabor Ridge Apartments IS NOT FOR YOU! This is the second Christmas in a row where Management (property manager and maintenance manager)  left for the holidays only to leave us residents with no snow removal, no driveway plowing or even throwing down some salt so stoops, sidewalks and the parking lot were safe for our guests arriving on Christmas day.  After a heavy snowfall,  tenants have to perform their own snow removal if they want to leave the apartments or wait days until Management finds the time or hires personnel to clear the snow. The individual unit maintenance performed here is a joke. Repairs are done by using rubber bands, glue and duct tape only when they (Management) deem it absolutely necessary.   The Management team at Tabor Ridge is rude, condescending and downright nasty to the tenants.   Tenant turnover is high, hmm…. I wonder why?
I toured with Gina! She was awesome and the unit she showed me was darling! Just right for me and my kitty.

Poorly managed. The property manager  doesn't seem to care that most of the outdoor lights are non working. Makes it real inviting that the whole complex is completely dark, including the lights that light up the sign and the flag.

I've lived here several years and this place is getting worse by the year.

Pros: Large sized bedrooms, lots of storage, washer/dryer hook ups, quiet neighbors
Cons: Takes a month to get repairs, serious ant problem, dead trees leaning over parking lot, pot holes, disorganized and unfriendly manager, constant rent/water bill increase (4 times in 2 years)

I would not rent here if you have children, but for a single person who doesn't care much about how things look, it's suitable for a temporary place.
Appearance not as presented, tiny space, management takes every opportunity to squeeze out addl.fees whenever possible

apartmentName: 202 E. Green St by Bankier Apartments
review: 202 E Green has been my home for the last year and we've just renewed our lease. Initially we shopped around for a better deal, but its hard to beat the location and quality of service that Bankier provides. Their maintenance team has been very responsive to all of our requests and I highly recommend signing with them!

I've been with Town and Country for a while now and very much enjoy my unit! The staff here is friendly, maintenance is timely and efficient, the overall atmosphere of my complex building is quiet, which I share with equally cordial neighbors!
The apartment I had when I lived there had everything I needed for a great price. Leasing office staff and maintenance was always attentive and helpful. 5/5
Good place to live staff is friendly and willing to help

Clean area 
Very nice and respectful property management 
Maintenance get on things right away 
Highly recommend

I went in to tour this property today and was honestly impressed. The staff was knowledgeable and kind, and you could tell they took pride in the community.

The apartment building looked and smelled clean and the show rooms were beautiful and inviting.
Since I moved here it has been amazing they have been very understanding when I go to them with questions never had any issues.i love it here and the staff are wonderful.
Looking for a place to live is not easy, and finding a place you enjoy to live at is harder yet. I moved in Aug of 2018 and have not looked back.
Loved working with management and excited to move in! The apartments are great and a deal at the price.

Parkland Point is a one of a kind of place live that centrally located and affordable within the Champaign-Urbana area. Staff is very helpful, caring and level of care is provided to each resident on a personal basis.
Pretty good for it's price. The apartment has all utilities included, and it's very convenient to pay rent and bills.
Very helpful and friendly staff, with a great environment. The apartments are nice with plenty of room.

Parkland Point is a safe, fun, and clean place to live. Its’s super close to Parkland College which makes it so easy to get to class. The property is well maintained and maintenance is always willing to help. Friendly staff and great people!
The apartments are quality for the price you pay and the closeness to Parkland College is a godsend. The pros are only compounded by a kind and efficient staff, which makes living here easier.
Beautiful place, always kind and hospitable and available for any problem. I am a student at Parkland College, and my college is 2 minutes from the apartment, this is perfect for me.
Very clean and safe. I love living here. Walls are really thin and neighbors are loud but if you don’t mind that then it’s a great place to live!

Parkland Point does a great job of making residents feel safe! The friendly staff make it easy to put in maintenance requests, get new parking stickers, etc. Being right next to Parkland College is also a plus!
A great place to live, very spacious, and very modern apartments!
Great location, lot of space, great maintenance! Love how the area is gated, perfect walking space in park next to apartment, and no problem for parking!
Parkland Point is super well maintained on the inside and outside. If you have any questions the office is super quick to respond and do everything they can to maintain a safe and clean environment.
Parkland Point provides a safe place to love. The clubhouse always has fun things going on and are very helpful!!

BEDBUG RIDDEN. My roommates and I suffered numerous bites, blood spotting and stains from having to live with bedbugs while treatment was being conducted after we found them during move in. Very dirty. Poor spotty internet. Extremely high utility overages due to horrible apartment insulation. Management will withhold security deposit. Friends apartment in other building was much nicer than mine even though we paid the same rent.
I paid rent on time each and every month and had to fight management constantly for a clean apartment with all utilities/amenities promised upon lease signing. 
Stay at your own risk…

The apartment itself is fine except that it is kinda pricy for its location (really far from campus). However, the management office can basically do nothing for you but charging you fees. I live on the first floor and mold came out of nowhere in a bathroom that I had never used. (I live in a 2b2b and use the other one because that's where all the shampoos and stuffs are). It was  so obvious because there  was not a single towel/bottle/whatever in the bathroom. The manager insisted it was my fault due to my misuse of the bathroom(srsly?)and took away the showerhead, which I don't really care because I don't use it anyway. But I still have to pay for the ridiculous "mold damage".

Would give zero stars if I could. The apartment itself is not terrible. The location is good. The amenities are kind of nice sometimes. But management is terrible. I was forced to move apartments because they were renovating the unit I was originally leasing. No big deal. That's in the terms of the lease. But then they charged my rent to the wrong unit. So I got a notice of unpaid rent and threat of eviction because they messed something up. I went to the office and got it all taken care of. Didn't get evicted. After my lease was up, not only did I not get my security deposit back, but they charged me $400 for cleaning fees. Turns out, they didn't switch my security deposit over when they forced me to move apartments. Then, after multiple phone calls and multiple emails, none of which received any reply, they sent my bill to a collection agency. If you move here, you will have to keep management accountable with your money.
Management is terrible. So many issues with requesting for maintenance, Miscommunication, and Mischarging. I highly recommend to not live here.
If I could give this place a zero I would. Too many hidden fees and they have terrible management. They don’t communicate at all.

Anyone looking to rent here should carefully consider 2 things. Condition of units vary greatly because units are not inspected or cleaned before tenants move in. Do not rely on your stated roommate preferences. You are better off finding your own. Maintenance crew is great. Units are pet friendly and completely furnished.

My apartment was very clean and organized when I moved in, and this is a big thing for me. I really liked the staff and complex overall. I definitely recommend living here if you are looking for a quiet place to live.

I loved my apartment at The Place, as well as the staff. The apartment was clean and organized when I first moved in, which is a big deal for me. I definitely recommend this place if you're looking for a quiet area to live.

DO NOT LIVE HERE

If I could rate this place one stars I would. First the management is HORRIBLE! They will lie to you every chance you get and try to extract any type of money from you. Second the units are not up kept. You will have to clean it yourself. My unit was dirty upon arrival, it had mold, broken and dirty toilet seats, pee stains on the mattress, chipped paint, dirty everywhere… and a host of other problems. I would recommend no one stay here, it is uncleanly. Not to mention the place stinks of the farm next to it. I’d recommend finding somewhere closer on campus and save yourself the hassle of dealing with a horrible unit and horrible management who doesn’t look to resolve anything. This place should be shut down

Working here must be just as miserable as living here- the turnover rate is extremely high with new people in and out all the time, making it hard for anything to get resolved through one person. The people who work in the leasing office are rarely of any help & are often rude as they just assume the residents are stupid young college students. You are better off paying more to live on campus because half the time they cancel the shuttle anyways. Would give a zero if I could.

There are squirrels and birds living in the attic. The linoleum tile is cracked and split on the floors. There is water damage everywhere: on the vents, the attic, the ceilings. There is dark mold in the pantry and in the bathroom. The wind shifts during the day and the complex smells like the pig farm it's built next to. The people who work for the leasing office are checked out, because literally all of the units have so many problems they can't keep up. Do not move here.

It's one of the few places that I've lived however I have noticed very noisy and very nosey neighbors. The office doesn't seem concerned with noise complaints especially concerning animals and there is a minor bug problem mail delivery is a bit of a hassle and if you get packages delivered they will not deliver them to your door you have to go to the office to pick them up

Now they are calling it Place@117. 

This place sucks more than you can imagine.

First, they charged me a late fee for twice, it was 50 dollars each time, while the contract says it is 5% of monthly rent, which is way more lower. And they blame me for paying the late fee in the first place, after my moving out and asking for a refund. I tried to reason them with several times, their manager, only agreed to refund me part of it, and deducts the amount of money in the final statement from it. Of which I am seeking legal explanations to see if it is legal or not, cause I think it is not a deposit, no money should be deducted from it.

So who ever has been charged a late fee for 50 dollars, pls refer to your contract, Article 4, it is after 4th of that month, and only 5% of your monthly rent. Argue with them to see if you can get a refund.

Second, it seems like they can take advantage of every loopholes in the contract to charge you. Especially the move-in and move-out inspection. Be careful to ask for a move-in inspection, cause it was not mentioned when I moved in. And when you move out, require a move-out inspection together. If you do not do that, they will do it on their own, and charge you with the damages which may later result in a dispute.

Third, avoid the Room C in the 3*3 apartment, cause you will receive no heating from your outlet, cause it is the last one in the apartment, and gets least or none heating. That's is how their air conditioner works, according to their maintenance staff. He is a nice guy, I wonder if he still works there or not. Anyway, the maintenance team is good, it is just they are not in charge.

Fourth, be prepared they will shut the shuttle down for any excuse, especially in winter.

Fifth, it used to be a quiet place, but not for the summer. 

If you can settle with all of these, and their sometimes poor management which treats you like an idiot, I think you will enjoy living there.

I LOVE The Place!...It is very clean and well maintained property, with nice neighbors and it's pet friendly. The common areas are pristine; a sparkling pool in the outdoor area, a basketball court, and indoor fitness center. You couldn't ask for a better staff! They are very friendly and helpful. The staff makes an extra effort to match perspective roommates together based on age, common interests, pets, and maturity. I also love the international flair of tenants; of all races and ages. If you come by for a visit, you will not be disappointed! I love the ease of the shuttle and public transportation. All necessities and conveniences are close by as well. The Place IS the place to be; what a beautiful property, both inside and out!
Too cramped. Neighbors are nosey and rude! Not a good area to raise a family.

Try to save your money and do not sign a lease with Smile.

A group of 4 of us roommates signed a lease with them in 2022 and paid a one time 1000$ cleaning / admin fee, instead of the security deposit. At the end of our lease in 2023, not only did we leave the house with zero damages, but also cleaned the apartment before moving out, which we have proof for. At the end of the lease period, we were charged for multiple cleaning charges as well as a broken closet door, which had been damaged by their maintenance team on a weekend when we were all away. We were expected to pay these charges with them setting a deadline, with them not even responding to our emails until that deadline for any clarification.

Pathetic customer service, poor maintenance, no response to our heating and cooling not working efficiently during peak months are some of the highlights of our time with Smile.

The apartment buildings are extremely unsafe, structurally and with respect to security - as anyone can access the floors whether they are a resident or not.

The office staff is extremely unprofessional and has no answers to most of your questions regarding maintenance, billing and lease terms.

Definitely do not sign a lease with them. This is one of the many experiences that we have heard from our others as well.

Smile Student Living you need to start making money the right way and not by looting students. And if you do have an answer for where the initial 1000$ was put towards, that would be great.
I like the apartment and surroundings and new neighbors. I had a couple of maintenance requests which were completed quickly and effectively.
the apartment space is nice but maintenance takes a long time and usually we need maintenance to come multiple times before the issue is solved
I have had a good experience so far in my apartment with Smile. The resident portal makes it very easy to request maintenance which is very handy and they are typically quick to resolve the issue.
Apartment is good, but maintenance is very VERY slow. When I talked to the office, the man there was very condescending. Felt very disrespectful when I’m just trying to get my dishwasher fixed.

So far Smile has been a great place to live at. The maintenance comes when requested and everyone I’ve interacted with has been nice. My only complaint is that you can hear your neighbors if they walk with their shoes on in their apartment.

I love the staff and management!
Chris has been great through the whole leasing process! I'm very thankful to call Lancaster home ??

I decided to live here my junior year with my three other friends. This place was perfect for us. The apartment came fully furnished. In the bedroom, the closets are huge, with mirror sliding doors. Under the bed, there are dressers and storage as well. I kept my suitcases, boxes, and other stuff under there. I really enjoyed how big the bathrooms were too. I would 100% recommend students to live here. The top of the apartment was my favorite part. It's like a sky deck where you can see all of Champaign. Most importantly, the staff is very nice and caring. They always act fast when you need them.

This apartment has given me some of the best times I’ve had at college. It’s close to campus, great location for bars and restaurants, and it’s amenities are perfect for college cookouts as well as studying.

This property has been an excellent place to live this past year! Despite living with four other people, I felt like the living arrangments of the rooms let me have my own space when it was needed. The location of the facility is close enough to campus, green street, and the ARC so you never feel like its a chore to walk there. The staff is always friendly when I run into them. I would recommend that anyone give this place a shot and live here!

My roommates and I were struggling to find an apartment to live in this year, and we luckily came across Lancaster! It came with everything we wanted: a washer and dryer in unit, a TV, and modern finishes at a reasonable price. They also have a great maintenance staff that comes to fix whatever needed in a timely manner. There's a lobby where you can get water and make coffee, and the staff is really nice and provides us with snacks and treats during finals and holidays. There's also a nice rooftop to hangout on, and I enjoyed having our own balcony too. I like how secure the building is as well. It’s a great location near Green Street and multiple bus stops, and it is not a far walking distance from the quad. It’s difficult to find an apartment that has all these qualities, and I’m glad to have lived here this year!

The management team is very friendly and generous to tenants. I have lived in the apartments under this company for two years now and already resigned for next year! The apartments are clean and modern, with balconies and lots of space.

I would highly recommend Lancaster. It is a prime location, excellent price, and has exceptional staff, like Chris, that are there to support her tenants! If you want a comfortable, social, and happy experience at UIUC, I would suggest choosing Lancaster.

I am currently living in Lancaster while i'm getting my masters and it is perfect. It comes fully furnished and is a great size for me and my two roommates. Rent is super affordable for the location. I would definitely recommend Lancaster to anyone looking for a clean, updated, place close to campus!

The location of this apartment is outstanding. It was my first time living in an apartment and I’ve had a great experience. Maintenance completed requests very quickly and management is always there to help. Chris is great and always was so accommodating to my friends when they came to visit as well. I love having our own balcony and we really wanted an unit washer and dryer with storage space so this apartment was 10/10.
I’ve lived here for a while and have had a wonderful time. The rooftop is great for bbq’s, the staff are absolutely amazing and helpful, and the location is perfect for college students
I live at this apartment currently and have never had any real issues with the management or apartment itself! All of my maintenance requests have been met and the customer service is great too.
This apartment has a good location and great service! The rooftop is a huge plus along with your own balcony and in-unit washer/dryer.

this is a great property. The management is wonderful any time you have a problem they will be on it right away and they are always willing to help out if anything comes up. Great living space, close to everything. secure .  Lower parking entrance not so great tho.

They took months to give me back my security deposit and my roommate still hasn't gotten his. Know plenty of people having the same issues currently and in the past with these guys. They'll act all nice and fake to you but do not let it fool you their only interest is money and taking 2 hour lunch breaks during work hours.

I stayed at 51 E John St. for 2 months over this summer, taking over a lease from someone else. I stayed in a 4-bedroom apartment, with two other housemates that I didn’t know. I had the luxury of getting there first, so I didn’t have to share one of the two bathrooms.

The kitchen is spacious, with two refrigerators, and tons of counter space. The bathroom is similarly large. the washer and dryer are extremely effective and easily accessible. The hallways in the building are open to the outside, which means that there is excellent ventilation in the entire apartment and smells from cooking do not stick around. The water quality is very good.

In terms of the management, they were absolutely wonderful; when I was moving out, they let me have my pick of the items that had been left behind when people left - I got a vacuum :) they were extremely helpful and friendly people at every opportunity!

My very very minor nitpicks: the TV in the apartment is a large android TV, which is mounted somewhat too high on the wall. The back of the device is almost completely inaccessible, and it took getting help from friends to take it down to get an HDMI cable into it. This was the essentially the only annoyance I had the entire time.

In a review of a furnished apartment, I think it’s useful to list the additional furniture I bought. I got a table and chairs for on the balcony, a small table for next to the bathtub, and a large trash can for in the kitchen.

 I also had to buy a wifi router, but the internet there was already taken care of- not sure if by the previous tenant or by the building.

All in all, this is an excellent property which I would have happily stayed in if I had not had another place lined up!

The management is second to none at the Maywood. Anytime you need something or have questions, they're more than happy to help. Courtyard and balconies provide plenty of fresh air and you have to love when management provides you with complementary breakfast or lunch. I would totally recommend living here.
The staff is very friendly and helpful! Pet-friendly apartments, and very convenient/close to campus! Amenities are great, staff frequently provides food/snacks in the lobby! Great place overall!

This is a fantastic apartment building! The gym is great, the people are a respectable and the pets my neighbors have really brighten up the day. Management is really involved in everything regarding the apartment since the leasing office is in the lobby of the building so they are very attentive to the upkeep and activities the tenants have going on. In that regard,  they always have awesome events or lunch for the tenants on special occasions. Great Apartment, out of the 4 apartments I've had, Maywood has been the best by far. My apartment was outstanding.

Really spacious rooms to begin with. The employees here are fast with helping fix things in the apartment and very understanding to any issues experienced. They also leave snacks out everyday as well as special treats on certain days. The contests for holidays are also fun. Most importantly my neighbors are great. No loud noises, minus the weekend and often help with packages and things like that. Great place to live.

The rent is reasonable, maintenance is very responsive, and the leasing staff are friendly and professional. The 5 Green is close and makes frequent trips to campus if passive commute is your thing. The neighbors can be a nuisance, but everything about the property is good.
It is an okay property. They don't always come on time if you put an order. They keep changing leasing specialists almost every year.

My only complaint is that the air conditioning is not central air and there is only one unit in the living room so the far bedroom gets pretty hot. Other than that this is a great place to live and the staff is very friendly and quick to help with whatever you may need. I would definitely recommend living here.

I love these apartments. It's pet friendly and super close to the university and only 7 min drive to the vet hospital. There is a gas station right around the corner and Meijers is like 5 min away. The apartments are very well taken care off and the staff is amazing. They always answer my emails with questions and concerns very quickly. They are super nice! As a student I think the price is great especially for the amount of space I get. 
The only thing is sometimes getting deliveries from amazon might be difficult because of the locked front door in every building. With that being said, I think this is a very safe place to live in. I definitely recommend it.
Have lived here almost a year, so far very quiet and the staff is wonderful to work with. If I ever have a question they are very quick to respond.

The staff at Parkside is very helpful including the office and maintenance staff. When we moved in our apartment was very clean and the grounds have been nicely maintained year-round. It is very pet friendly and conveniently located. After looking at many apartments around Champbana I don’t think you can find a better value.
Staff were always super nice. Apartments are very big. Gym equipment is not the best and I wished they opened the pool earlier not on May.

I have had such a wonderful experience living at Seven07, I lived here the past 2 years and just renewed my lease for another year! The leasing office is great, the apartment complex is always clean and well put together. The amenities are the best in town as well, so happy to call Seven07 home.

Consistently expect appliances to break or cease working. Complex will mark your work orders as complete and no one will ever show up to conduct maintenance. Front office very rude and won't even acknowledge you once your lease is signed. Security guard with the beard is unbelievably rude and has sworn and been aggressive with myself and other residents.
This place is going to be so cool, the amenities look insane!
Can’t wait to use the basketball court and pool next year! Also a fantastic staff in the leasing office!

When looking at apartments for the upcoming school year I passed 707's leasing trailer and was kindly greeted by a girl right away.  She made me feel super comfortable and got me hooked with all the amenities.  I even got a snacks and a drink.  It was nice to see what the kitchen and living room would look like in person since they're still building the apartment.  After a couple a days I decided to sign for a 2 bed with my friend and they were super helpful during the process. I cannot wait to live here next year!

Don’t live here. I can’t wait until my lease is up in march, living here is a joke. The office staff is not helpful. My apartment was given to me with stains on the carpet, dust on the baseboards, & ceiling fans. Didn’t even bother to clean before letting me rent probably. 2 weeks ago i had to witness and hear the landlord fighting and arguing with 2 ameren employees in the foyer for 10 minutes before they finally went outside and shut up. People smoke in their units and the smell comes in through the air vents and all the staff did was put a sign up that you can’t smoke on the units. My breaker trips almost every time the air conditioner turns on. & then to top it off today I am sitting in my apartment and 2 of the maintenance men are standing out between my back patio & the pond just looking in the windows to my home like it’s no big deal. Issues and issues and issues. Price is NOT it for what you get.

The unit itself is fine. Plenty of space and reasonably priced. The office staff are of little help to you once you sign your lease, however. They do not enforce lease policy at all. 

Floors/ceilings are very thin, so if you have upstairs neighbors be ready to feel like you are a part of their conversations. Be prepared to be woken up in the middle of the night from excessive noise.

The “landscaping” is just a handful of dying shrubs in a rock garden outside each building. Some siding is broken or missing on some buildings, vent caps and grates blown away that have never been replaced. Many buildings appear to be falling into disrepair from the outside.

They finally installed a fountain in one of the ponds, but the noise from the motor is so loud you can’t sit on your “private balcony” to enjoy it. Further, all grass clippings are thrown into the ponds as well as discarded trash. Unsure what “beautiful pond views” they are referring to in their discription.

All in all Hunters Pond is not a well ran apartment community and you would be better off continuing your hunt for a home. They are only after your money and have zero regard for their residents.
Friendly staff and anything needed is done in a quick and timely manner..we have been here over a year and all our needs have been met.  The office staff and maintenance crew are all excellent

We used to love living here. It was quiet, safe, and reliable but recently management has let the complex go. Lived here because the reviews were good but old reviews no longer apply. The constant music, yelling, and parties both inside the complex and in the parking lot might be fine for some but if you’re looking for a safe quiet place to live, this is not it. I have reached out to management and nothing has been done for 7 months.

In an age where more and more people are working from home and need high speed, reliable cable internet, ie xfinity, why would they not give their tenants the option to choose?  Seems like a nice place, but that will be a deal breaker for many.  I'm gladly paying more at another place since I need high speed internet for my job.  They should reconsider their policy and I would definitely move when my lease ends.

There have been several issues that could have been handled if they just provided what I would consider good customer service. Nothing above and beyond or extraordinary. 1. No hot water for 3 days....could have given discount on rent for the inconvenience. 2. Credit was ran more than once...could have at least looked into the issue or apologize if unable to fix. 3.Went to the office because a package was delivered. Staff claimed it was not there. I received a notification less than 2 minutes after leaving that it was there. I asked if they could bring it to me and was told no at first.....hello if you make the mistake you should correct it. While there are some things I like about Hunter's Pond, like the usually quiet atmosphere and the clean, safe area, the internet monopoly makes this a very difficult place to live. There are things I need to do for class on the computer that I just can't because the internet is so bad. If you need access to reliable internet and aren't looking to pay $70 a month, this is not the apartment for you.

We lived here for 2 years, apartments are quite specious, common area is very well maintained. Office staff is also very helpful and location is great. 
But the main problem is internet& it sucks big time. You have no option without getting their internet & tv channels. In 2016, we had rationing on Internet.. I can't believe this. Rent is also on high side & they keep increasing every year. In the same price you'll probably get better places in town.

The apartments themselves are nice, I lived on the 3rd floor and never heard anyone unless someone was in the stairwell or had an 808 going (which was rare.) My only complaint with the apartment itself is the carpeting, it's not soft and shows any trace of dirt/marks up easily. Other than that, the apartments are pretty great. The 3rd floor has vaulted ceilings and a great view of the pond, though it is slightly more expensive. The internet is another thing to consider if you are planning on moving here, as someone else mentioned you can only get it through Bloom Broadband, which is incredibly overpriced (i.e. for 12 Mbps I paid $50/month and it was as slow as 6 Mbps at times.) I never felt unsafe living there, though there was a shooting at the complex up the street and there were a string of car break ins. Overall, it was the best place I lived in while in Champaign.

The staff here are really kind the the property is well maintained.  That being said, people considering living here should be aware of management's anti-competitive policies regarding the internet.  The complex insists that you use their parent company's (Edward Rose) wholly owned subsidiary (Bloom Broadband) for TV and internet service.  Bloom's broadband is more expensive than other alternatives in the area.  Likewise, buying Dish service through Bloom is more expensive than contracting with Dish directly.

The worse part by far is that Bloom imposes an arbitrary and unnecessary data cap on internet usage.  The most expensive plan is capped at 350 GB per month.  For context, that works out to 3.9 hours of HD video per day or 1.8 hours of UHD video per day.  Their motive for this is obvious, as they want to discourage streaming video delivery so people are forced to buy into their overpriced Dish TV, which also has monopoly standing.  There are no overages allowed at any price.  You don't have to be doing P2P or running a server farm, simple Netflix is enough to get you in trouble.

If you live alone and you like to read or buy DVD's, this place is probably fine.  If you intend to stream video content, play online games, download any games or software, or live with anyone under the age of 40, I would look elsewhere.  I plan to.

This complex transitioned to new ownership last year and they have invested a lot of money and effort in superficial changes (such as painting it blue and grey) but little to nothing has been done that substantially improves living conditions for tenants.

Living here now. It's okay. Just beware that if you live on the first floor, you do not get a private balcony. We are in one of the two bedroom apartments and we are right next to an apartment building next to ours, so we get absolutely no sunlight in our room and since it faces the apartment side where people come in and out, we have people constantly walking by our windows and looking in at us, so I have to have the blinds closed at all times. We have people drop stuff from the second and third floor onto our balcony and people walk through it all the time to reach their apartments. When I called to switch units when our lease was up, you have to pay ALL your fees all over again. They weren't willing to work with us on that, which was frustrating. We've been good tenants, I like to think, we pay our rent on time and if we are going to be a few days late, we pay the late fee and we call ahead of time to let them know and make sure it's okay. Doesn't really seem like they care enough to have us here to work with us on that. The fees to move in here were astronomical (at least for us) and can't afford to pay those all over again, just to get into another unit. I'm not saying it's terrible, but it could be better. The maintenance people are nice, the office people are nice, the area is nice, but I think i'll save up this year and maybe move to a different complex next year.

The apartment complex is quiet. But as far as maintenance goes for the hallways and lawn care they lack. The apartment is actual spacious and would be good for roommates or a young couple like me and my boyfriend.

I lived here for 4 years, and only left because I moved out of the area. From move in to move out, I had an overall great experience here. Maintenance and management was always incredibly friendly and responsive, and my few maintenance requests were taken care of within hours. The walls are thick, and I rarely heard anything from my neighbors. Overall a great place to live!
I enjoyed my time here. The apartments are nice and spacious. The office staff is very friendly and gets back to you quickly with any questions or concerns.

I have nothing but good things to say about my experiences at Garden Court Apartments. I rented a 2 bedroom for a year while I was in grad school and I am so happy I chose to live here - it was quiet and clean. The neighborhood surrounding the complex looks a little shabby, however, I never felt unsafe. The complex is surrounded by a gate, which further ensures safety. I lived on the top floor and I loved the privacy the beautiful trees outside of each window provided. The premises of the complex in general are beautiful and well kept as well - especially the coy pond! Every encounter I had with Penny and Stan, the landlords, was positive. They are kind, considerate, fair and pleasant people to encounter. Any time I had a question, Penny would be VERY quick to respond. Rick, the groundskeeper/handyman, lives in the complex and therefore is nearby and quick to help if anything comes up. I was by myself and moving to a new area and Penny helped make me feel comfortable and welcomed, I can't thank her enough! The way I found out about this apartment was through my research on Google and I was reassured by the numerous positive reviews it had. Looking for them today and I wasn't able to find them - I just see several recent reviews instead. This is unfortunate because I found those previous reviews from way back very helpful during my searching. This location is solid too - close to bus lines, the mall area and the highway! Once my lease was over I moved to another city to be with my significant other but I appreciate the quiet, safe, beautiful and comfortable environment I had at Garden Court while going through stressful grad school!
I have lived here for 2 years. The owner Bryan is real nice. We have water damage every time it rains . It never gets fixed. I have 2 other neighbors with the same problem.

I gave my  apartment four stars because of the tenents and management. I've lived here for 20 yrs. and have seen many changes. But the management has always been very kind to me and my children. There are also a few tenants that have been there for awhile as well. I like where it's located and it's affordable!

The appliance maintenance is shoddy, often times waiting weeks to get to requests - I have an outstanding request from at least two months ago that has yet to be addressed. The walls are paper thin and your neighbors are inconsiderate jerks who will yell and blast music at all hours of the day and night. And don't even get me started on the three times I found POOP in the laundry room and stairwells. Don't move here until they clean up their act.

I am not going to lie...the studio apartment was FILTHY upon move in. I swear the amount of dirty I swept and mopped up is disgusting. Let alone the old food dried on the walls in the kitchen....For the most part the apartment complex is quiet, but you can still hear people talking especially in the hallways. Overall, I am happy with the apartment. The rent is cheap, once you clean it up it is very nice, and Marsha has made it EXTREMELY easy to move in. If you are looking for a little fixer-upper for an apartment that is super cheap, this is the place to go.

The new management company here has made a huge positive impact on my experience. The grounds are cleaner and taken care of, the office staff is friendly and actually helpful, and when I've had a work order it's been taken care of by the next day. The rent is extremely affordable and I never have an issue finding parking, plus I love being so close to the downtown area and right down the street from the mall.

Office personnel has always been kindhearted and understandable to our needs. They have always worked very hard on trying to get things in the apartment that are broken, fixed and are very professional in their work at Windcrest.

I am a happy tenant of windcrest Apartments. I have been living here for almost 2 years with my daughter. I have no complaints and i am very satisfied tenant. The people are very polite, professional and caring. And do whatever they can to work with you and keep the tenants happy.! Also if you ever need maintenance they have a amazing maintenance crew... this is a great place to live.!

I HAVE BEEN STAYING HERE FOR TWO YEARS I HAVE SEEM A CHANGE...kids are actually able to play outside n peace..maintenance actually comes out and fix the problems you have (no half work jobs)...the management and worker are very resspectful
And understandable..they residence is they number one priority...the crime rate have drop since I been living here am very happy with the changes thy have made and continue to make come in check it out..

They lose your payments and require you to pay more , they do nothing about harassment , rude and make you pay 2 months of rent if you don't let them know you don't want to resign 2 months in advance don't move out there !!!!!

The apartment itself is actually really nice (mine had brand new carpet) but the staff and leasing problems were the biggest issue for me. The manager shows up unannounced and maintenance enters your apartment without your consent even if a maintenance request wasn't submitted. Their reasoning is that it's "in the lease" but they could at least inform you before they just show up and enter your bedroom while you're sleeping. They also have a policy that they don't mention until after you've signed that says you have to renew your lease by March if you signed before labor day (even if you signed your lease all the way up until the end of August). Otherwise your apartment goes back up on the market. So if you don't know your plans 6 months in advance, I wouldn't bother.

I lived here for almost a year. Overall, I had a great experience. The area is quiet, and there are multiple parks within a few miles as well as a high school/middle school and a nice gym within walking distance. Sound isolation is good through the walls and floors of the apartments, but wasn't so good through our front door. Staff at the leasing office was always a pleasure to work with, and the repair people were always timely and courteous. Apartment was nice and spacious for the price (I was in the Granite). Each apartment has central air and its own water heater. Plenty of parking right outside the building. I wish I could find an apartment like this in the area I live in now!

This is one of the best apartments I have ever lived in. The staff are friendly and very helpful. Any problems/repairs  are solved fast and, done with excellent results. I would recommend this apartment to anyone.

I was scheduled to have a tour, I arranged a tour saturday morning. It took me two hours to drive to the tour. Meantime, unbenown to me, the realtor sent me an email during the time I was driving to the tour, requiring that I return the email or the tour would be cancelled. Needless to say, I waited 25 minutes for a realtor that never showed.

I lived here for a year and loved it. I would have stayed longer but we decided to purchase a home this year. Other than a faulty shower curtain rod that they refused to replace, maintenance has always been prompt and often one of the owners would come out himself to check out the problem. Most issues I had were related to the apartment being brand new and certain features unfinished or missing, but those were handled usually the same day. As the other reviewer mentioned, this winter we had an issue with water flow. In my apartment it was due to the meter being frozen and not allowing water to flow through to the rest of the apartment. Very early the next morning Antonio was in my building with a space heater thawing it out.
I also loved that these apartments are new, and in a quiet condo community. Get an upstairs unit if possible, as those have more room due to the entryway, staircase and balcony.

My son and his roommate have lived in these apartments since summer and the maintenance is very poor.
Today is the third day they have called about not having water and still no one has come to fix the issue. When I called today I was told they are lucky their pipes did not burst like another lady and damage all their belongings. I think they have an issue with insulation in these buildings because several apartments have had problems with the frozen pipes or not water.
If you own a complex, you need to make sure you fix issues of water or plumbing within 24 hours or call someone to fix it.

I lived in the Alcove my sophomore year until graduation (3 years), and overall had a great experience. It’s an older building than some of the high rises on campus, and doesn’t have any amenities (pool, etc.) but those didn’t matter to me. 

The price and location of the building is amazing, it’s basically right next to everything (classes, nightlife, and restaurants). The leasing company is smaller, so the staff are way more attentive to the tenets. All of my maintenance requests were completed under 24 hours, which was great. 

The property managers are super nice and friendly, and actually care about the tenets, unlike some of the bigger leasing companies on campus. Overall, if you want an affordable place with a great location, then I’d 100% recommend the alcove.

I woke up with vomit outside of my front door. So I assume it's not safe to stay here. Also, I complained it to the property management. They probably sent a cleaner who just vacuumed the place without wiping it with any cleaning agent, so there was still gross stain and intolerable odor. I reported it to the property management again and they said "it's the inherent nature of vomit to stink". I lived in a 6 bedroom unit in this complex. The rooms in this unit are very disproportionate (some are very large while others are small). There were a few problems when we moved in such as a bad window/blinds and bad mattresses but the landlord came through and fixed them albeit it did take awhile for them to get around to doing it.  It is basic college living no frills while on a budget. A plus is the large walk in closets and the high ceilings on the second floor.

My apartment is 2 bedroom 2 bath very comfortable apartment it's close to everything I need being disabled it's very comfortable to get around in. The apartment I live in was taken over by a property management team called Team Kay a couple of years ago. They have provided excellent care and upkeep since taking over. Dont waste your time here. Most of the units are not updated like the pictures at all. Ramshaw is such a hassle to work with, and the property manager doesn’t care about helping you with anything. Everything was clean and brand new it was just screaming for me to apply and call it home. And that I did. I’m very satisfied with my decision.
We love living here. It's so nice and close to everything. The gym, sauna, rooftop deck and in unit laundry are a dream. Renewing my lease for the 3rd year.

I moved in back in August and have loved my experience here. The management has been extremely friendly and helpful and quick to respond to service issues (which are rare since it’s a new building). I also love the amenities, keyless entry, package lockers, bike garage, and gym. No complaints other and noisy neighbors, which is to be expected from time to time in a large building.
Not a terrible place to live but the walls are VERY thin so be prepared to hear loud neighbors and base reverberating through your walls. Drywall cracks everywhere.
Like most I was not able to get in contact with someone. I wasted my time on more than one occasion trying to tour. If I know anything about downtown, if they don't answer don't bother!

My partner scheduled a tour via email, and when we showed up, no one was there for our appointment. We walked around outside for a while looking for sign of life, and found a guy who said “oh, sorry, your name wasn’t on the list” and closed the gate. 
I submitted a request for another tour and have no received a single response back to date.
Don’t waste your time trying to get a response here. It’s very telling of how unreliable management is.

This place has great views but you don't get enjoy them when you are battling roaches all day. They come from every opening to a wall. It doesn't matter if your unit is spotless! The elevators are always broken. The property management team does not follow through with their claims of improvement. I would advise you to stay away unless you have no other place to go!
DO not live here. Parking lot pot wholes everywhere. ROACHES.....Management horrible. Only thing about this apartment was the reasonable rent. DO NOT MOVE HERE.

Fire alarm goes off for hours in the middle of the night.  Tenants disregard all alarms.

When I first came for a tour I thought this apartment was too good to be true. It's in a great location, nice staff and tenants, and very clean appearing apartments. Unfortunately, I was wrong. My first week at the apartment there was an odor in the hallways and in the apartment, the parking lot gets packed by 5 PM and people will park around your car so you can't get out of the lot, my mailbox was completely filled of the previous tenants mail and continued to get the previous tenants mail, and I only had one package delivered and the front desk lost it. I’ve been living her for almost 2 months & I can’t wait to move into another place.

So I moved to Detroit in October, and city place admin made me feel super welcome. My dog actually did not do well with the apartment environment so I had to leave. This was a bummer because of how close this place is to the city, the river and eastern market! Either way the management was super understanding and willing to come to an agreement that made us both happy. Its a diverse crowd at this place but everyone is friendly! Plus its a great price for the location :)

This apartment complex was recently taken over by a Canadian company, who dumped a bunch of money into it.  I had a few minor problems early on, but the staff did everything and more to solve them. The staff improved significantly over the time I was there from changes in the office and hiring/firing in the security staff, which is true for the majority of other things that needed attention.  I found the real advantage of this place was the low rent with everything included.  Also, you didn’t have to pay more to live on the higher floors, which was awesome because I had a great view of the city.  The location is great if you enjoy the Eastern Market, Dequindre Cut, or going to the sports arenas.

I'm not from Detroit so I was a little unsure of what to expect, but I really think this is a great place to live downtown.  There is a lot of young professionals living here working in a variety of fields, especially at Quicken. I thought people were generally friendly and a lot of people had dogs.  I moved out because I found a really cheap place outside of Detroit to live, but I think this place was on the up and up when I left. I would definitely recommend for those looking to locate downtown.

I moved in over the summertime and I have loved it here.  Yes, they are still finishing up renovations but they should be done by December and the place is looking immaculate.  Every single unit has been completely renovated with top notch fixtures and appliances.  On top of that, the staff is very friendly, personable, and professional.  If you are looking for a place to live, I would highly recommend you consider City Place!

I have in City Place for quite some time, and agree with all of the negative reviews that it was very difficult/impossible to get anything fixed, among other things.  

But since the new ownership has taken over it's like living in a brand new building.  They have put a lot of work into fixing up deficiencies, and it's obvious they really care about making it a great building again.  

It's true that under the old ownership it was questionable whether living in such a great location justified all of the issues.  But since the change, I have to say I love where I live and plan on staying here for a long time.  

Amazing views, close to so much, clean and a great price.
Very good space for a single working person.  A/C cuts out every now and then but not a huge deal. great views, cheap rent, nice living areas, very affordable due to the fact they pay for utilities.

I moved to what is now called City Place Detroit apartments September 2014. The beginning was a little rough mainly due to poor communication and follow through on behalf of the office staff, maintenance and some problems with security not doing their jobs (to busy flirting with residents). However they have turned a new leaf, all new staff security included and things are getting done. I see a huge increase in " professional" residents and the once tolerated nuisance tenants are being evicted. The new and improved staffing is able to keep up with the high demands and expectations of a higher caliber resident. The workout room is complete, the new lobby is almost finished and its already beautiful,and the elevators are all working. Unlike other complexes the laundry rooms don't look like a horror scene out of a Freddy Kruger movie, additionally the hallways are clean, carpeted and smell fresher and the store is stocking more and more products daily. The new staffing changes have put a breath of fresh air in a once stagnant building and the owners are viciously attacking improvements all the way around. I'm looking forward to the new parking lot and getting to know my new neighbors that just moved in across the hall. This is a great place to live.

P.S the city and river views are breath taking, Lafayette Park is our back yard.  I regularly enjoy concerts and riverfront fireworks from the comfort of my apartment on the 17th floor which is worth its weight in gold. If you love the city as I do, you cannot ask for more...price convenience and location it has it all.....Tell them Lawyer Girl Michelle sent you....

Wonderful sight of the river and all of what downtown has to offer and a another plus is that its all close by, great food, bars and the football and baseball stadium. They even include all utilities and there's hardwood floors, but i'd be fooling you if I didn't tell you the cons. only 2 of the 3 elevators work, at times the water will be cold, and they give about a 2 days notice when extreme maintenance has to be done. Recently with all the move-ins because of renovations the parking lot is overfilling and if you don't get a spot you've gotta park on the street, but we have security that patrols. It has its problems, what place doesn't? Its nice, affordable and close to everything, just be patient with them as they work out their kinks.

I've lived here for a year now and I cannot wait to leave. The apartments are renovated and look nice on the surface. The location is great and the dog policy is nice. The security guys are great as well. I signed a lease stating that the units had central air. I'm still waiting on that. Some units report having cold air coming from the units, but the majority report the same musty warm air that's readily flowing in my unit. Report issues to maintenance as you will, and they may or may not get around to addressing it. When they do attempt to work on your complaint, they enter your unit without prior notice. The office staff communicates with residents via passive aggressive letters under the door. Though it seems to have stopped in the past 2 months or so, the water was often shut off due to leaks or scheduled repair without 24 hour and often without 12 hour notice. The office staff is very nice while they lie to you, so don't believe what they sell you up front. The lobby is still half-done (as it has been for months)and the central air remains to be seen. Also beware that they do not have snow removal service contracted. So, if there's a winter storm plan on a day or two without your vehicle since the plow trucks are busy clearing their contract clients. There is Aldo a nice permeating aroma of marijuana and stale food throughout the building. Air fresheners don't stand a chance against the awful smells coming from the vents. I would not recommend anyone fall into the trap I did by leasing from this company. The owner resides in Canada, so you have no ability to raise concerns beyond the lovely office staff when your issues go unanswered. I sincerely hope that the conditions improve for future renters and those being suckered into leases now.

BUYER BEWARE. It's interesting that the description of this place is almost identical to the description it had a year ago - the last time they changed owners. Promises, promises. I lived here for 9 months; through construction, broken elevators, absent security, absent management, snow-filled parking lot, water shut-offs, construction crews entering my apartment, exposed pipes. Obviously, I did not renew my lease. And, here I am, 3 months later, still trying to get my security deposit back. I will end up in court, I'm sure. It seems the new owners, in Canada, have to personally write a check to return my security deposit and apparently, they have to be in Detroit to do that. Oh, and they celebrate July 4th for a week...in Canada. They don't have a name or contact information. Stephanie speaks for them. If you are speaking to Stephanie, keep in mind that she is telling you whatever she has to tell you to make you go away.

Do not listen to the promises. I can promise you that they will not be honored. Several months from now, another new owner will come in and Stephanie will have the same story she's giving you now.

Detroit is coming back. There are other properties out there that are contributing to that comeback. Give those companies your business. Don't reward these weasels with your cash.

Well I was very hesitant to rent an apartment here due to the numerous bad reviews, I am happy with my choice. The new owners are taking pride in the building and making it beautiful. Yes, some of the units are still under construction as is the main area, but if you see what they are doing, you will understand. They are completely renovating the entire building and it now looks beautiful.

Not only have I noticed a difference in the quality of the apartment building, the new managers are much friendlier and approachable. I've only had positive interaction with them. When something is wrong, they fix it right away. If I am unhappy they are willing to work with what I need to make me happy.

This is a great property only minutes to downtown but without the downtown price. Great views, great restaurants nearby and right next to the Eastern Market.

All utilities are included, they have a few laundry rooms, pet friendly, appliances are all new as well. The park right outside is beautiful and great for dogs to run around in. I'm very happy with my decision to give these apartments a try. Only downside right now is the noise from all the construction but in time that will be done.
