The lease on my former place of residence ran out. Deciding not to renew, I found myself looking for another place to reside. I contemplated moving to Downtown Detroit, where a colleague had recently moved, and also looked at suburban communities. Having lived in Oakland County for over 30 years, I contemplated moving back. I also looked at a large, recently constructed apartment complex in Macomb County.

In hindsight, my decision to move to Sherwood Heights Apartments and Townhomes was sealed with a simple phone call. The decision was made even though I had never seen a model apartment or set foot on the premises. 

After doing a cursory review of Sherwood Heights on the internet, I called the office and spoke with Gina. In this age of “I’m busy, and I don’t have time to talk with you” I was impressed with the kindness extended to me, and the interest shown in helping me decide if Sherwood Heights would be the right fit for my lifestyle. I got off the phone asking myself, “Could this really be true?  Here is a person working with the public, and seemingly happy in providing service.”

Yes, it was true, and as the manager of the complex Gina’s spirit of excellence and service permeates  the facility. The grounds of the complex are spotless. In my four months of first touring Sherwood Heights, and later moving there, I had to deliberately look before spotting a single piece of paper on the grounds. Upon moving in, I observed that my apartment was cleaned spotless. Even the basement was cleaned to perfection.

I am happy to report that as a tenant “bound” by a lease, Gina’s professionalism has not diminished in the least. While she is diligent to protect (manage) the interests of the property owner, she has been equally diligent in her efforts to ensure that my rental experience is a pleasurable one. Gina seems acutely aware that whether one is buying or renting, “home” is “home”.

Regarding my actual apartment unit, the square footage is excellent. The degree of storage is amazing. The complex is very quiet. I have yet to hear loud music “bumping” out of a person’s car, or loud noise of any kind. My neighbors are friendly, but are not in any way intrusive. 

I have found Sherwood Heights Apartments and Townhomes to be a quiet oasis in the heart of the city. Without equivocation, I highly recommend the complex.
This apartment is great new everything it's clean n bug free nice people and environment

I love my new apartment. It was cleaned spotless before I moved in. The complex is very quiet and peaceful. I have a beautiful  courtyard to look at. There's a storage area and nice clean washer and dryers. Sherwin Heights is wonderful.

I have been living here since the end of October 2012 and I honestly love staying here. The grounds are well kept, community wash room always clean, and everyone who stays here is typically friendly. If you don't have an assigned parking space, parking can be hard on a Friday/Saturday night. Maintenance usually responds to calls within a few hours (less than 24hrs) of your request. Price is great for the one bedroom unity! I do wish that there were community washing on each floor instead of in the basement...clothes are very heavy! A true gem!!!
We are enjoying the stay here. Very pleased with the services.
Pleasant spacious apartment. Good amenities, very pleasant and helpful staff

The boulevard apartments staff is friendly and problem solvers. The apartment building its self is clean and filled with friendly residents. In my personally opinion it’s the best place to live in the area.
An amazing place to live! Office staff is the best!
My apartment is great the Staffing is awesome maintenance is awesome my whole experience living at the Boulevard is has been good so far.

The Boulavard is an amazing complex that feels safe, and clean, and provides a "homey" feeling of Detroit. Kassem is the best! The office staff is always great to talk with and the Amazon hub in the lobby is extremely convenient. The building is very diverse so everyone will definitely feel welcome.

Don’t expect to have a relaxing weekend or a good nights sleep. It’s an event space and restaurant area too so at night there’s really music and random people strolling your area. I live here now and can’t wait to move out

Super impressed with these downtown apartments. Walkable to all my favorite restaurants like Cannelle, Leila and Sy Thai. Plus, there's new restaurants opening soon in the lobby! 

The finishes, views and amenities make it this the perfect place to call home. The terrace views are amazing and the gym is AMAZING. I can't wait to work from The Study, too.

I really like the space. The bathrooms are an excellent size, the closet is GREAT, and the neighborhood is very up-and-coming. I love that I can easily walk to several bars and restaurants. The 24-hour security that patrols the neighborhood made me super comfortable moving to a new city.  I also love how many dogs are around! I surprisingly do not hear any of them barking or anything. 
Sadly, there are several downfalls. They must have skimped on sound-proofing between floors because I hear every step my upstairs neighbor takes. I also hear their music through the vents as if it were playing in my apartment. When I moved in, I was instructed to contact the security company that patrols the community anytime there were noise complaints during quiet hours. The first time I called, the security team told me they didn’t handle that type of thing. When I reached out to the property manager, it took three emails to get a response. Subsequent followup emails have either been ignored or I’ve gotten a one sentence response. 
If you go to sleep before midnight, beware that you might get a young college student that lives above you who does not know apartment etiquette and blasts their music or rearranges/thoroughly cleans their apartment beyond quiet hours. Invest in some ear plugs and a white noise machine, as you’re on your own. Sadly, I can’t wait to get out of here because I can’t sleep.

Lived here for a year before moving out of town. 

Paige the property manager is great at running this building! Him and his staff are rockstars. 

Apartments have a great luxurious feel, maintenance responds very very quickly, your issue won’t go unresolved for long!

Would rent from this management staff again no matter the property.
Have tried contacting them and left voice mails with my info and never got back to me. It all starts with communication and they can't even do that well.
great place to live , safe and good neighbors , good location management is very helpful
Just moved in here and management is doing an amazing job. Neighbors are nice, place is undergoing major improvements which should brings this to AAA rating.

The new management is doing a wonderful job,
I feel very comfortable here in Warren Manor.

Rebranding, Changing the name to "North Park Towers" this place has done absolutely nothing the old "Sapphire" is still out of date no washer and dryers in unit, no self control AC OR Heat in unit, Ac Breaks and leaks all the time and the Management is terrible and Unprofessional. They charge you for the littlest things, 10% of your rent if you late because of emergencies they don't work with you at all even if its not your fault. this place thinks they can just change there name and get away with the same stuff. everything break around here I'm telling you if you are thinking about moving in here don't do it. i will never in my life recommend this place to anyone. This was the worst place i ever lived and iv only been here 8 months. please do me a favor and don't live here

I had a terrible experience with Fairlane Meadows. I scheduled a tour with my local guide and drove for 5 hours to reach the complex, only to have them cancel the tour last minute, citing construction as the reason. They could have informed us earlier in the morning or even before, but they didn't bother. When we expressed our frustration about the long drive wasted, they were incredibly rude and showed zero respect for their clients. I strongly advise against considering this place for renting; they have no regard for their future residents. Stay away!

My son lives here while going to school and he loves it. Office is SUPER helpful and maintenance fast! I love that there is open land and is so quiet but close enough to not be an inconvenience for my son who doesn't have a car.

Management is horrible never can get a whole of them and maintenance people never fix anything at all. Then we have to pay for trash removal when they never come get the trash the trash be sitting outside for days rats and squirrels be all in the trash eating the trash. Rent too expensive for these small apartments I’m glad I’m not staying here anymore it’s horrible.

I regret renting here, it’s far from luxurious and poorly maintained. Serious pest reoccurring problems and LOUD OBNOXIOUS DISRESPECTFUL NEIGHBORS. Trash valet doesn’t pick up trash in a timely manner rendering the service obsolete, it’s better you take your own trash out unless you want to invite critters and bugs into it to end up with a ripped bag that valet can’t pick up by then. Apartment is equipped with awful appliances, not energy efficient so your bill will not disappoint. Musty apartment. I will never rent again with this company.

I must say I really hate living here I have had problems with this place from the very beginning! And then when they transferred me over to another unit I am still not satisfied! The rent here is absolutely RIDICULOUS that we have to pay to hear big rats running in the walls all night the trash people some times can take days to collect rats chew they the bags because there are some neighbors over here who are careless and do not use the trash bins at all! I have complained multiple times about the noise and nothing is done about it a woman in the office told me there is nothing they can do if the rats are not inside the unit! The quality of these apartments are just very low I hate taking showers in my tub because it’s just coats and coats of paint over it after each resident and it’s just horrible and I am so ready to leave this place I never considered this place my home at all I have been very uncomfortable living here since I moved in when I had the chance before transferring I should have just said never mind about this place ! I feel  like this management definitely owes a lot if us refunds or rent adjustments due to the fact it’s rat infested as we can see it’s rat traps all over this place !

I don’t normally write reviews for anything but this apartment sucks. The rent is way to high to having the problems that I’m experiencing. There’s a spider AND an ant problem and the only thing they do is come in and spray the apartment and it’s half done. I also see mice running around outside at night. I won’t be renewing my lease!

The apartment used to be a great place in a great location. However the management has gone downhill over the past several years. General upkeep has suffered, amenities have been removed and maintenance issues are far more frequent. There's often issues with the elevators being non functional, building wide fire alarms are common, there's been several water leaks in the building, general cleaning has been reduced in common areas, laundry machines are out of service often, the management is harder to reach and security has been more lax.

The place used to have a 24 hour concierge and full time office staff that made sure things were handled properly and maintained well. That was cut during COVID and since then it's clear that the property is no longer a focus for the management team. It's not horrible but it's way overpriced for what it offers. You're better off looking at one of the newer buildings in the area that haven't given up.
I tried reaching out to schedule a tour several times and have yet to be reached out to. Such a shame, the place looks nice.

The Albert is one of the best places you could live in the city. The location is excellent, especially in the summer when Capitol Park is always bustling and beautiful green space is right outside your door and easy to access. It's super close to great restaurants and amenities downtown - I don't even own a car because I don't need to living here. 

The apartments are spacious, you can't hear your neighbors, and the appliances are all modern. If you're used to apartment living, you'll likely be happy with your unit. The only downside is hearing trash pickup in the morning if you're on the alley side. As another review said, the rent is high but I think it's definitely worth it (especially if you compare it to apartments in the heart of downtown in almost any other US city). 

To round it out, the staff here is super nice and helpful. Marcus at the front desk is extremely helpful and always willing to help out if you have an issue with packages or anything else. Emily from the leasing office is also great - she is super responsive and very helpful in answering any questions or issues that may arise.

The building is really nice.  The staff is super friendly.  The place is full of dogs (which I love) and the staff loves them too. The have a doggy bathing station too which is awesome. There is also free coffee and pop all day every day. The location is awesome; super close walk to the Compuware Building. However, not everyone is happy up the changes in Detroit, especially the bums at Capitol Park, who play cards, smoke pot and get drunk, which is all fine and dandy, until they start harassing the residents and making it uncomfortable for us to walk our pets and be outside. The area is up and coming but some folks aren’t ready for this change. 

Also, they don’t have in-unit laundry machines so you have to take it to the basement. The laundry machines take 2 or 3 washes to get them clean and most are covered in dog hair.  The credit card machines on the washers also break a lot. There was 3 weeks straight where we could not do our laundry because none of the machines were reading our cards. 

There are also lot of old building problems. The elevators are always broken; the windows were never updated so it's either really hot in the summer or FREEZING cold in the winter.  I literally never slept in my bedroom all winter because we could not get it warmer that 60 degrees in there. We even tried space heaters but that just made my electric bill sky rocket.  I was paying about $150 a month to DTE in the winter.

The other major issue is that they do not have a loading dock.  So  when you return from the grocery store you need to find a spot on the street or bring all your stuff from the garage.  If you try putting on your hazards, the cops will ticket you (been there; done that).

All in all, if (and only if) the windows get replaced; they added washer and dryers to each unit; and we had a loading dock, I would have probably stayed a few more years, happily paying $1,700 in rent.  But at the end of the day, it’s harder to live at the Albert, next door to my office, then drive 30 minutes from outside the city.

The good: location

The bad: thin walls, thin doors (you will hear everything in the halls), paint falling off, terrible windows in non-updated units (you can feel the wind through the cracks in the frame), no parking during game days/events because non-residents sneak in, loud heating/cooling unit (lots of random clanging), only able to either heat or cool unit at once (apartment decides when to switch over to heat), and make sure you ask for a document to write down the issues with the apartment when moving in; otherwise, they likely won't give you one, and you'll be liable for any damages occuring prior to you moving in

I have never written an apartment review before, but I felt compelled to after another sleepless night of hearing furniture being moved around in the apartment above me. Nice views, though
Ever since January the heaters been having problems. They said they are working on it but it’s been over two months. The temperature gets to 50 degrees in rooms. I don’t know what to do anymore

A horrible place to live and management is terrible! I did not have heat all winter and still had to pay my rent in full. I sent a letter certified mail indicating I would break my lease due to the situation and still gave 60 days' notice! Later I received a letter demanding I pay my rent in full. I reached out 5 times via phone, email, and the Briggs website to discuss the situation and did not hear back. 4 months later, I receive another letter demanding payment. I am only paying because I do not want to have to interact with this property ever again!!!! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Currently living at Briggs Houze. The location is fantastic- walking distance to everything downtown has to offer and easy access to the QLINE to go to midtown. 

The management company is fantastic. Managers and employees working at this building are courteous, friendly, professional, and eager to help and solve any problems you might come across. Taela and Catherine are especially great. The community is great too- plenty of friendly residents to make you feel right at home. Highly recommend it.

Had no heat the entire winter, barely got any discounts from it. Original management company quit partway through winter, new company came in. The thermostats in the apartments never have accurate temperature readings. Slowest elevators in the city of Detroit, that you cannot fit any items into. Overpriced for where it is. You have to deal with a club potential he being opened in your building. Parking is expensive.

The Briggs Houze is the best community in Downtown Detroit. The management team always goes out of their way to solve any issues you might have. Both Catherine and Taela are so caring, and always give my puppy treats when we come in after a walk. They also set up happy hours and breakfasts for the building, and do a fabulous job communicating with the residents via email. They make you feel like you are part of a Briggs Houze family, and we really appreciate that since we are both from out of state. 

The finishes at the Briggs are right up my alley. I love the fact that the owner kept the vintage charm, but featured a beautiful renovation. Another reason we chose the Briggs was because of their awesome gym space. The gym is quite spacious, unlike many communities downtown. Another perk is the awesome people that live at Briggs. We haven't met once person we didn't enjoy. Basically, Briggs is the best choice of apartments in Detroit. We don't see ourselves anywhere else but here.
Unsafe, overpriced, things stolen and multiple problem tenants getting evicted as my neighbors.

Seems as though Broder & Sachse is too busy building new complexes to care about The Scott. What was once an exceptional experience, completely turned to the exact opposite of "luxury living" there. I lived there for 15-months and the decline of cleanliness, common courtesy, safety, and overall functionality and accessibility of amenities were a prominent issue.

Not to mention my move-out day (this past Saturday) was completely forgotten about. I scheduled it and of course confirmed for a 10:00am move-out. There are two elevators - one was broken this day and the one they were supposed to lock down for me was not locked and NO EMPLOYEE WAS THERE per usual so my movers took ten times as long to move me out (I was being charged hourly). There was no one to be found to help me.

I called the emergency line (they never answer it) and I emailed the Assistant Property Manager at Broder & Sachse Real Estate and copied two of the Leasing Consultants that day urgently (and a few times) and they STILL have not responded to even just simply apologize (it's Wednesday now and I'm sure they've seen it in the past five days). They blatantly ignored me. My movers were waiting for several minutes each time they had to take something to the truck. It's like they especially didn't care about me because I was moving out instead of in.

This place is a mess. There is basically no security and they took away the 24/7 concierge at the front door so anyone can just walk in most of the time. Also took away the free coffee. There is always something broken (specifically the pool). The only reason I gave it one star at all is because of the community aspect. I met a lot of great people here and they threw a lot of events for us.

ALSO the walls are so paper thin here that the whole building hears EVERYTHING. I lost so much sleep here. I heard my neighbors cough or sneeze and their full phone conversations all the time. Not to mention the neighbor that lives above me - I even heard footsteps vividly.

If you want to be ignored as a resident when you pay for an overpriced apartment then The Scott is the place for you.

The Scott used to live up to all it claimed to be and used to be a fantastic place to live. At the start of 2021, management laid off nearly the entire staff and left only a few employees who’s only job are to sign new leases. We haven’t seen a single maintenance person since 12/2020 and the amenities are trashed. Both grills have not worked in 6 months, 5 out of the 6 treadmills in the gym have not worked for the past 4 months, and the hot tub works about half the time. We have a bug/centipede issue in our apartment due to a construction defect and management continues to ignore us. Broder & Sachse has completely abandoned this place to focus on their new projects. Save yourself a lot of money and even more headache, don't subject yourself to living here.

The apartments and the facilities are all really nice looking, but unfortunately, not the greatest quality (pretty cheap flooring, plumbing issues, appliances). With the pandemic, many of the amenities were also unavailable for the majority of my 10 months here thus far, which is totally understandable. However, when things started to open up many of the amenities were taken away without warning, and without a refund (now you need to pay for the once free coffee, and NO CONCIERGE service), the pool/hot tub rarely cleaned, and gym was not being monitored at all to maintain physical distance/covid-19 standards(supposed to be 2 people at a time with masks on, and that's clearly not happening).  Without a concierge, you cannot guarantee someone is there to receive packages or groceries, or help when you have noisy neighbors at 1 am (which sadly happens ALL THE TIME despite a Global Pandemic). The majority of the residents here seem to be in college or recent grads, and don't take the pandemic seriously nor have any respect for their neighbors. The walls are paper thin, and the bedroom doors are sliding barn doors which don't shut or lock (not sure how that works for roommates, its fine for couples using second bedroom as a guestroom/office). If you have the money, and want to re-live your glory Frat days, than this place is for you. Ultimately, great location, love the covered parking, For the Love of Sugar and Grey Ghost nearby, but not worth the cost. Also, the garbage trash chutes are disgusting and always overflowing. Pro tip: Do not get an apartment near the stairwells or trash chutes, and advise against a unit over looking the pool in less you are really into partying.

The only thing that should be known about this place is the awful sound proofing. Nothing else really matters. It's comically bad. They literally did not put any money or thought into the sound proofing. HORRID.

You do not want to live here.  My friends cars have been stolen or vandalized right out front of the building.  It is not the Scott's fault but they are suppose to have security? If you park in the building be ready for flat tires, I have had 3 in 9 months ($600), the building didn't care.  The concierge is there 50% of the time, they are helpful when you move in and when they are present.  Brian is amazing and should run the entire building.  The Scott is like living in a frat house.  You will receive bi-weekly emails enforcing the rules, I understand why but just another reason to not live here. Went in the hot tub once and had a full body rash for a week.  If you are a working professional or over the age of 25 do not move in!

I am on my second year of living here and came across roaches in the hallway and when I went down to report it they said multiple people had already reported seeing them. I’ve had “pest control” which is the same dude who comes in a pretends to spray your apartment for 5 mins come out 3-4 times and I am still seeing roaches if not more since he sprayed. We have also had to get last minute sprayed for bedbugs because of other residents as well as bedbugs in the community center. I honestly gave up on telling them about the roaches because they do the same thing every time. With no solution

The building is modern, and my view of the Griswold parking deck is so amazing....

Foreword: As a new resident of this property, this review is subject to change throughout the duration of my stay.

Do… 

... Move here if you are looking for a modern feeling building with younger residents and management, and lots of nice amenities*
... Expect a service and building geared toward a urban / younger audience
... Be ready for a friendly community and neighbours, as well as amiable management
... Take advantage of the perks* of this building, should you move in

Do not...

... Expect a cheap stay in a large or even generally average-sized unit
... Move here looking for a home-style unit, expecting the nights to always to be silent 

OVERALL

28 Grand is a smart, well-marketed property, geared toward a very specific audience. The location is great, central to everything but in my opinion this is a property meant for ppl w/ a millennial/gen z mindset. The units have a hotel / barracks / dorm feel but minus the books and class. 

You live with a full spectrum of residents, most are working, educated... everyone so far seems to get along. 

The walls are concrete, so you rarely hear other tenants occasionally there’s a dog bark off. (Most noises are from bar crawls and street traffic) If you’re moving to a downtown Detroit apartment these details shouldn’t be surprising.  

Location

Capitol park is just outside the door and there are plenty of places to eat on the block. (Canelle, IGGY’s) other than space vs cost its everything you can ask for. Capitol Park also has a dog park.

UNITS
The units are furnished but small (260 sq ft), so think Tokyo apt small. Everything is brand new, practical, & well thought out. Also in comparison to overall size the apt has a huge window seat & large double bed. Also notable the hd tv, full fridge, microwave, in room HVAC , sizeable shower, rocket fibre, electric & hot water INC.

No issues... staff go above and beyond for residents. Maintenance staff seem to always be ready, available and around. The move in process was very smooth. Cleaners come through once a day. 

LOBBY /RECEPTION AREA / SEC
The lobby is modern with a secure key fob entrance with a call buzzer system. There is a 24/7 Security / Concierge desk in the lobby they’re awesome. 

My only complaints so far

* While the amenities look amazing when touring, they aren’t operational due to COVID (Fitness Center, Outdoor Terrace, Community  Lounge, Kitchen)

Document all communications with management. Most importantly, always communicate by email (may not help much). If you receive any written correspondence from them, it is likely incorrect information, so it’s best to call and confirm that they did their job properly. They do not communicate well with their tenants or each other. I recently vacated and received a letter indicating what the amount of my refund for my secuirty deposit would be. It stated I was entitled to a full refund. Well, they decided to send a check that wasnt reflective of what was stated in the letter without any communication explaining the discrepancy. 

Communication is very important, especially when dealing with someone’s money, even if it’s $1.

I went in for a tour, and I have to say, I was astonished by the quality of these apartments for their price. Gorgeous Community Lounge and cozy, modern apartments. All amenities included. Put my app in, wish me luck!
I was really impressed at the cozyness ofthe studios, also the multi- purpose room is setup for multiple events. The terrance is great also with a fire pit and two gas grills.
This place is a mess. Nonstop issues that never seem to be fully fixed.  Don't step foot in here if you don't like water and mold. There is much better out there for comparable pricing.

I enjoyed the following living here from 2016 to 2019:

1) The best location in Detroit - Walk to work and goodbye to your commute and the wasted hours each week in traffic. Want to go to Canada? Just take the Tunnel Bus down the street. Greektown, Campus Martius, the Riverwalk, Hart Plaza and the Cobo Center are right at your doorstep! I also felt safe here.
2) Great amenities - The best amenity is having the Millender Center People Mover stop right in the building. The Sky Club is amazing with gorgeous views. The indoor lap and gym are both very nice. The City Market is very beneficial. The rooftop has one of the best views in Detroit.
3) Excellent service - In my experience, this is ultimately the factor that makes or breaks the living experience in any community. Caitlin in the leasing office is a phenomenal professional. We had layoffs at my company and by my planning in advance of my renewal, she helped me with a month-to-month option. One summer my central AC unit died. Within a few hours, they brought temporary window units to my apartment until they could get it fixed. The other huge asset to their team is Roger, one of the front desk concierges. This man is an expert on Detroit and he gave me a lot of advice on safety in the city and things going on.
4) Transportation and parking benefits - I mentioned the People Mover access above, but the new SMART express buses pick up within a block on Jefferson. The QLine is only a few blocks away. If you working for some preferred employers downtown, they will even pay for your parking at Renaissance City. 
5) Community events - There is a great sense of community at RCA and it's pretty diverse in ages and backgrounds. The management also do a great job creating changes to mingle with movie nights, card games, Monday Night Football on the big screen on the rooftop, July 4th fireworks and the monthly events in the Sky Club.

Is Renaissance City perfect? No. But it's pretty close to it and it's the best place I have ever lived. Yes, it's on the expensive side but you get what you pay for from a location and amenities perspective. That's the cost of living in a booming downtown Detroit and not having to spend 2 hours of your day in traffic. If you like urban living and want the best community in the CBD, you will not find a better community.

Can't ask for anything more.   Greatest location in the city.  The people mover will drop you off at your buildign.  The QLine is a block away.  Quick walk across the street to St Andrews Hall.  Ren Cen is a tunnel walk through away.  Hart Plaza.  Campus Martius.  Move here and you'll never leave the city again.

I LOVE THIS APARTMENT! First and foremost, you can't beat the price for a good-sized downtown high-rise unit. I'm renewing my lease for the first time after 12 months and my rent did not even go up. I also have an AMAZING view of Comerica Park. There is a market downstairs  that is a life saver. If I ever forget something at the grocery store I can count on finding it downstairs. They also have fresh made meals throughout the day. The maintenance is always timely and efficient. The gym, which is shared with the Courtyard Marriott, is huge. I do not have to bother with getting a gym membership so I'm saving extra money. There is 24 hour concierge, so this building is more than safe. There is an attached garage so you don't have to worry about parking in an open lot during the winter time. I can't say enough about how much I love RCA. If you're moving to downtown Detroit, move here!
This is not a place you should live if you value your dollar. The apartment is very cheaply made. My car was stolen 8 days into living here. Walls are paper thin and floor carpet doesnt have padding.

I have lived at Ducharme place for almost 2 years now. I have referred a lot of other residents to this complex also. Ducharme is great. What stole my heart initially was the open floor plan and the amazing kitchen. You know a girl loves her kitchen.  The floor to ceiling windows are also a plus. From my apartment I receive a great view of the sun rise and fall. It is very close to a lot of the happenings but far enough to not be effected by crazy noise or street traffic. I have literally walked from my place to Comerica Park or Little Ceasars arena. Also, the spot is pet friendly with dog parts 5-10 minutes away for them to let loose or an open park right next door for a nice walk.

I just moved to the area from the west coast and I was a little hesitant about moving to Detroit for work, however I am so happy that I picked DuCharme Place to live.  The staff has made the transition super easy for me.  I have had so many questions and requests and they have always promptly responded to me and helped me every step of the way.  The property is super clean, smells very nice, and I absolutely love the workout room.  For a place this size they have an awesome work out area.  You really should come check them out, especially if this is your first time in Detroit!

I have been living at DuCharme Place for 2 years now. I love so many things about this apartment complex! The location is ideal with easy access to the highway, about a couple minutes away. I love the hardwood floors and modern look to my apartment too. Lots of natural sunlight with plenty of windows, which is such a place. The staff is very friendly and quick to respond for maintenance too. I would recommend DuCharme Place to anyone moving to Detroit!

I am new to the city of Detroit and spent a lot of time picking out an apartment. I made the right decision with Ducharme place! I love the inclusion within the community. There is a community of outgoing nice individuals who are welcoming. On top of that, the building itself is brand new with amazing ammentities. I have used the grills outside in the beautiful terrace many times, and the appliances within the apartment are brand new and amazing. Great staff, overall a 5/5 experience for me.

My family loves being close to the action of downtown Detroit without being inconvenienced by it. We're a close walk to most of the places we love and avoid the heavy traffic that comes with sporting events, festivals, etc. Furthermore, the property is clean, well-maintained, and offers all the amenities we were looking for (secure parking, in-unit laundry, pool, fitness room, beautiful grounds, pet-friendly). The property management team has been responsive to any concerns we've raised, and maintenance issues are fixed promptly. Of course there are challenges, like any other apartment community; however, the staff here have a track record of swift action. I have a toddler and would never live anywhere that was too loud or didn't feel safe. I've been here for over a year and proudly recommend DuCharme as your next place to live. Come check us out!

Since 2023 June, everything went from good to bad and this year with new management of J went from bad to worse. 
No trash pickup but 25$ monthly payments are mandatory 
Garage must be free but heard that new tenants been asked to pay 50$. Don’t! It is always open. Strangers well welcomed here.
No maintenance but immediate closure of your requests in residence app.
Unknown insurance company that no one send you the details of it.

a great place to call "home". The entire staff always greet you with a smile and are very helpful to our needs, and are quick to attend to any problems that arise . The grounds and facilities are kept clean every day by friendly courteous workers. The workout rooms are open 24//7 are rarely crowded and the pool area is lovely. I love the convenience of the elevator and four story covered parking garage. . I live alone here and could not feel safer anywhere else....a beautiful neighborhood with parks and trails."

Buildings are nice that’s about it. Walls are paper thin, you hear everything.  
They don’t tell you that your neighbors are air bnb guests, really anyone walks in and out of the buildings. Security is a joke. Gates are broken and open on most days of the year. Management is unresponsive. For your safety and comfort I would look elsewhere.

Orleans Landing is a safe and friendly environment.  A walkable community, with several near by enjoyable sites to visit. I love the OL management & maintenance team because they are always eager to respond with a timely resolutions to questions and concerns. The OL staff is considerate and they work together like family to meet the needs of their residents.  I’m happy that I choose the Orleans Landing community to call home.

The apartment is in a great location, everything is very up to date and clean. There‘s always some activity going on down here either set up by the staff or the city and the staff are very friendly and available if any problems should arise.
I have been a resident since 2017. I have witnessed many improvements over the years. Nice amenities and great location!
I am a returning resident. I love the location and the community amenities are amazing. The staff is so friendly and knowledgeable. I would 100% recommend Orleans Landing to anyone.

We love our Orleans Landing apartment. The inside is clean with up to date appliances. Parking is way cheaper than it would be downtown. The ORL staff and local police officers  have done a great job addressing the noise/traffic issues in the summer.

Location is great, right by Atwater Brewery, Chene Park and the Cut. Gym is really nice comparatively. Appliances are much nicer than most apartments. It’s pricey, but you get a great place, well made, and a very helpful staff.

If you’re looking for a clean, safe, updated apartment building located in the heart of downtown Detroit, look no further!
Orleans Landing has been a great experience so far. Their management is quick and responsive with repairs, neighbors are all friendly, and the move in process was easy. Not to mention, the pool, hot tub, and full gym are wonderful amenities. 
I see a lot of negative reviews online but those are all from the old management company. Village Green has definitely turned this place around.
Highly recommend Orleans Landing if you’re a student downtown!

This is a beautiful community, with great management staff and amenities. However, the walls are paper thin. I could hear my neighbors sneeze and snore. I lived on the second floor and it felt like my upstairs neighbor and her dog were going to fall through the floor just from walking. It’s not worth price.

As a current tenant, I have seen some negative reviews about Orleans, but can't stress enough that these were from when the old management team was in place. The new management at Orleans Landing has been nothing less than excellent.  They truly care about your needs and have made living here a dream. From the monthly activities they put on, their responsiveness and many updates for your convenience, this is hands down one of the best places to live in Detroit. 

Did I mention they have a pool/hot tub and no weight limits on dogs? If looking to live in a very safe and upscale place in downtown Detroit, I would highly recommend at least coming in for a tour.

Orleans landing is a wonderful place to stay in Detroit. The amenities are great. The staff respond to your  issues in a timely professional manner. Andre, Jen, and Zack  are always willing to lend  a helping hand to residents when needed. I am very pleased to live in this community.

Joan Nash

This place was truly horrible. We had all our doors and appliances breaking down and nobody came to fix it. Management is horrible and they donnot care about you. All our neighbors moved out because of how bad this place is. The gates are always broken so people can break into your cars and the pool is always dirty, no upkeep in this place. Save your money and find something else for better price. Everything is cheap and they lie to you when they say "luxury living". Stay anywhere but here its def not even worth it.

Be smart and do your homework. Nice building, but considering the noise levels on the streets around the complex, you may as well live in another place for half the price. The police have pretty much given up on this place and the management won't tell you that.

There are so many things wrong with this development that I’ll start off with the positive things: Location, views from unit & neighbors

That’s about it. Now I’ll get into why if you’re considering this place you should run away as fast as possible.

Street noise/racing/loitering – This has been well documented and still continues to this day on a nightly basis (https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/detroit-riverfront-residents-fed-up-with-drag-races-loud-music-marijuana-at-night). Almost every night along Atwater and other surrounding streets, people from all over the city come down to the riverfront outside your door to street race, loiter, drink and play music so loud it shakes your floors and walls. If management or the Detroit Police try to tell you anything different, they are lying. I have dozens of videos showing all the above and more happening as recently as last night (8/20/2017). So unless you like being kept awake until 2-3am every night, there’s your first reason not to live here.

I could go on about sub-standard building materials, numerous maintenance issues that take months to resolve, resident facilities delayed months or still not open, unresponsive and two-faced management, etc., etc., but I only have so many characters I can use for my review.

To summarize, management makes it seem like a great development and pretend like they aren’t aware of the outside problems that have been going on for years. In reality, it’s an overpriced, under-achieving apartment complex that you’ll regret having ever signed a lease for. I know we do.

Just don't live here and thank me later.

As a current resident, I'm rather disappointed in the unresponsive management of the property. The location is fantastic, and the buildings are nice, but management and noise levels are frustrating. Over six months after move in and we still do not have access to ANY amenities, despite the promises of management. There are issues with mail delivery, electronic keys functioning correctly, and no enforcement of the no smoking policy. We receive little to no warning prior to maintenance needing to be done in the rooms, and management often leaves during business hours, also without warning. Noise levels are excessive, more than just city noise, but drag racing and partying in the streets is a frequent occurrence (police have upped patrols since the issue made local news and this has improved quite a bit). It's a great property situated in a fantastic location - it has the potential to be an incredible place to live! However, I am not looking to renew my lease at this point - what I'm receiving just isn't worth the price.

Water turned off for 9 hours at a time multiple occasions since I've been here. At times it is turned off and the apt mgt doesn't even notify residents til after it's off. Whole building didn't get AC until well after they said it would be on. City inspector even came out & was speaking to residents. After the AC was "fixed" it still never worked. Just blew air around the apt but was never cold. 85° in here despite the temp being set to 60. 
Upon talking to mgt in the office & about 6 work requests (some of which they deleted out of the system) they said they would send someone out. 
The issue was still never resolved. The thermostats blow nonstop wasting residents' $ The thermostats here STILL don't work so you will come home to a 90° apt if you don't turn it off by cutting it via the breaker.
Every time I've spoken to someone in the office, I've been gaslit and lied to like this is how things are normally supposed to operate. The front gate breaks alot.
What breaks most is the elevators. Expect to either take the stairs or wait 15 minutes for the elevator. Both have broken at the same time as well. Maintenance does not fulfill quickly. I went a month with a leaky sink, no disposal, no dishwasher. I had no choice but to wash dishes in the bathroom. 4 of my packages that were supposed to be secured in the mail room were lost. Was told to contact the delivery provider but addresses were entered correctly & documented as delivered accurately. Only 1 occasion did I go down for something & then it magically appeared after they couldn't find it. It was days after delivery so they had time to sort things. Let's me know it's disorganized & they did temporarily lose it. The other things are just missing & I'm out of my money. 
This place is undergoing renovations. Hammering & drilling starting at 8/9 am. I understand that it is necessary for renovations. What isn't is listening to their workers yell down hallways, cuss, rap, slam doors & blast music. It's sounded like the construction was in the same room as me. I've gone to work many days tired because I could not find comfort in my home. The washers & dryers break often and when they are working, they're not great. This, honestly, is so far at the bottom of the totem pole of issues. The gym. No sanitizer. Unsanitary. No air flow. 80° all the time. 9 out of the 12 workout machines are broken. Cords cut off!

I’m currently living here and I’m not recommending this place for living, they’re charging a lot of money for utilities and the maintenance in this building is ridiculous. Air conditioning is not working properly and the building is so dirty!!!

This use to be an upscale well respected building not anymore they let amuone in now management has changed so many times it's ridiculous the current management team never answers the phone they talk about residents the building has roaches bed bugs dirty common areas and elevators a dirty pool no screens for your balcony the grounds are not kept up security nor the concierge never does anything they literally let anyone in the building the walls are paper thin you'll smell weed in the hallways your car will be broken into or stolen I'm told they took away valet parking which was very dumb because the parking structure is a crumbling nightmare the fact that they still call the complex "Luxury" is laughable.  Management is a joke again they talk about tenants never answer the phone and the and the one lady always has an attitude while the guy with the bald head acts like he's above everybody there is zero respect for the residents

I subleased from this place in the summer of 2019 and it was so bad that I’m still upset and thought I should warn others. It had roaches and a big leak in my ceiling that never got fixed. I fully cleaned the place after I left and didn’t get my security deposit back, and the worst of it was that they towed my car all the way downriver after giving me full access to the parking garage right when I moved in and somehow “forgot” to give me key information. Towed my car at 3 am and it costed me $700. Bad management and constantly was issuing late fees even though I was always on time.

It would not be a good idea to move into this building right now. There are issues with the elevators, laundry rooms, unfair and suspicious car towing, and cleanliness. The building is filthy and the hallways have not been vacuumed at all this year. They stopped mid construction and have not resumed. Many of the hallways and floors are in an extreme state of disrepair. There is no parking in front of the building for guests, and they have to walk a ridiculously long way to get to the building from the garage. Meanwhile, the parking spaces in front of the building are reserved for a pharmacy that rarely has any customers. There are issues with roaches and other pests. There is no way for your guests to call upstairs and be buzzed in, and you have to come downstairs in order for them to be allowed to come in. You are not allowed to receive packages with refrigerated food, such as Hello Fresh. If you do not collect your packages within four days, they are returned to sender. It is very disappointing to live here at this time, as I have lived here for over a decade. The building is currently in receivership and we have had more than 5 management companies in the past 4 years, each worse than the last company. This building has enormous potential, and I have not moved because I absolutely love my view and the size of my apartment. However, the second I step out of my door into the unpainted halls with mildew filled carpet that fills the air with a really foul smell, I hate it here. We are hanging on in hopes that just maybe, the next management company will actually restore this building to way it used to be when it was still a really great place to live.

I’ve been here over a year and I honestly only stayed for a second year because the office was so unorganized that I couldn’t find a place and move in time. 

My apartment is absolutely infested with bugs they’re in my fridge, freezer, EVERYWHERE. I wish I could post pictures because every bug trap I have is loaded with more gnats and roaches than I’ve ever seen in my life. It makes matters worst that I’m a frequent cleaner and neat freak. My wall is literally crumbling and there are cracks in my living room with water that attract bugs coming from an unknown sources. Cars are broken into frequently even though we have gated parking. Today the front door handle literally fell off in my hand. Each floor looks absolutely unkept and Filthy. I know because I took the time to check each one. There is no onsite laundry that is in working condition— it literally works 6 months out of the year if you’re lucky. It looks so pretty from the pictures with the promise that they’re working on your hallway but they haven’t touched my floor in a year and it looks like it’s fit for a crack house. This place is falling apart— it’s definitely a sinking ship.

Two years ago on Christmas, the sprinkler system froze, burst, and caused severe water damage to the entire building. There was mold on the walls in the hallways for weeks untreated. In my apartment there was hardly and heat and you couldn't control the temperature. It's crazy, I thought the building was condemned...should be. There was always a roach carcass at the front door to greet you though!

When I first moved here it was great. Then they switched leasing ladies and ever since I have only had issues. She does not communicate when anything is happening in the apartments. There are 2 elevators but one is almost always out of commission with no notice from management letting us know when it will be back in commission. If you want to live somewhere where you can never get ahold of the leasing office this is the place to live. Although the maintenance man Mark is a life saver and the best one I have ever had and is great at his job.

I lived here for a year and I absolutely loved it but they won't give me my deposit back (even though the resident portal says they approved a full refund) and are impossible to get ahold of. They ignore my calls and emails, whether I send them directly or through the website. The only time they picked up a call is when I blocked my caller ID info but I never heard back. They had a management change just a couple months before I left and there is a noticeable difference in service. Super disappointing because the staff before was amazing.

If I were going to live downtown longer, I'd be very likely to stay at the Kales building.  The property manager just changed so I can't speak for the future, but in my year here everything has been handled quickly which I'm thankful for.  The building itself is incredibly well built, there's something like two foot of concrete between floors so I've never heard my neighbors unless they're having a seriously loud party.  The apartments themselves are relatively well laid out and everything is good quality.

Downsides, it's expensive and living in downtown can be a serious headache.  Parking is $175 a person on top of rent for underground parking and you've got to go through a long hallway and up an elevator every time you get groceries or whatever.  There's constant loud engine revving and party bar cars on Woodward and the nearby streets so I had to start wearing earplugs every night.  There's also a nightclub near Kales that blasts music until about two AM that makes me have to wear earplugs also.

So all the problems downtown are pretty much downtown issues, not Kales issues.  I'm moving out, but if I were to stay in downtown Kales is where I'd want to be.

I have been looking for a decent size loft style/condo for some time now.  This apartment has everything I could imagine and it is in a great location.  Fox Theater, Hockey Town, Comerica Park AND Ford Field are within a two minute walking distance.  Not to mention once the rail system is complete on Woodward and the new Red Wings facility is complete, this area will be the prime location to work,sleep and play!

I stayed in a 550sqft studio for a year here. For location, building history, natural light, and amount of space for what you pay, it's great.

No control for heat or air, it's essentially just a box with fans and a switch for low-high. None of the vents around the unit actually blew air at any point. The building sets the temp, but there’s always issues with the air control. It's reached 90º in my apartment with the air running on high non stop and the windows and blinds shut. I lived on the lowest floor and had no direct sun in my unit.

Oven never went past 250º, and only 1 burner on the stove worked. All of the dial markings and temp controls were scrubbed off before I moved in.

Constant issues with the water pressure; After a 5 minute shower, the tub fills up completely and takes about 25 minutes to drain. Tap water in the sink comes out cloudy and slightly yellow.

Elevators are almost always broken. One is down for weeks at a time and it takes about 10 minutes to catch the other one. 

Maintenance takes over 2 months to fill a maintenance request, half the time they just mark it as complete without even coming to fix it. I spent 30+ days without a running air system in the middle of July. Called and filed multiple maintenance reports. Finally got a hold of someone in the leasing office when my apartment was 96º and they asked me if I filed a report before sending someone up “immediately”. Waited 3 hours before anyone showed up and then was told they must've forgotten to do routine maintenance on my unit. 

Management lacks organization; no one knows what's going on in the building. Its like talking to a stranger every time you need to deal with them.

Pool is great but there’s always issues with it being closed randomly, not opening for hours, or closing early with no reasoning or warning.

Cars are broken into constantly, both on the street next to the building and in the “secure” parking lot. 

Laundry room is always broken. At one point they had 10 working washers and 3  dryers that ran but took 3-4 cycles to get your clothes dry. People would literally dump your clothes out of the dryer on the floor if you didn't stay to watch. Most of the washers that did work smelled nasty like mildew and would make your clothes smell. 

No system for letting people into the building remotely. You have to go down and get them from the little concierge room.

I stayed here in a studio and then 1 bedroom apartment. View is the best thing place has to offer. Then elevators don't work, laundry has never been working for 20 days straight. There may be just 1-2 machine for 330 apartments. No covered parking. A very small bathroom. It seems worth in the beginning but you realize it later that you are stressed for unnecessary daily routines. Not worth.

They don’t care to fix anything. Heat and Ac don’t work, and the elevators are always down. The laundry room is down and has been for the past year. Don’t move here do yourself a favor and move somewhere else.

My husband and I lived here for about a year and a half. We had a two bedroom due to us having a ridiculous amount of stuff. The apartment was enormous, so much so that when we were looking for houses, we were constantly comparing the space to our apartment! Not many people can say that. The views of Canada and downtown Detroit from our window were fantastic. It was great for entertaining, watching fireworks, and so much more. The apartment recently renovated the laundry facilities, brought in new appliances, and re-did the parking lots. They also created a new system for visitor parking, which was much needed due to people parking illegally. They are very attentive to the needs of the residents. Management, I found, was quite excellent. Pat was always available to chat about any concerns, rectified any issues, and went above and beyond to compensate us when our refrigerator died unexpectedly. Lisa and LaTricia in the office were also both always friendly and helpful. The door attendees were always greeting us with a smile, scanned us in if our hands were full and even held the door open for us. They also were attentive if we received a package that needed to be picked up as well. The apartment was clean, we never heard our neighbors due to the concrete walls, and any maintenance requests we had were filled within 24 hours at the longest. I would highly recommend this apartment complex.

This is probably the worst living experience I've ever had. Cops have been called multiple times, cars have been broken into in the supposed "secure" parking lot, apathetic security guards, and an unprofessional management. Please stay far away.

The management of this building is not great. The washers are dryers are ALL BROKEN, all the time. They talk about fixing them, but they never do. You will waste so much money and time doing laundry, and it will all still be dirty. 

Also, the elevators are not reliable. One has been completely shut down for months, and the other two are regularly broken. And when you take the stairs, you will see that they never bother cleaning the stairwells that people are smoking and leaving cigarette ash in. It's disgusting. 

Also, when you need your air and heater fixed, it can take 4 - 6 weeks because they can't get parts. They won't tell you it's going to take a while, but it will.

Worst Place Ever ! Wish I could rate it no stars. Terrible place all around, management, maintenance .. EVERYTHING. They’re rude and not helpful, we had a ton of problems from the start. Save yourselves and avoid this place at all costs !

The leasing office doesn’t respond to emails and the maintenance workers NEVER come! I put in a maintenance request to get my blinds fixed in June of 2021 and didn’t hear a response back until nearly October 2021, despite putting in multiple requests throughout the months. The staff themselves are very nice, but lack professionalism and communication skills. The amount of problems I’ve had living here are too many to count on one hand, I’m so excited to leave. These apartments are way overpriced for giving residents the bare minimum.

River Place has no active security in place. If something happens you will be brushed off and treated like you’re a burden to their free time. None of the security cameras are utilized even though they are aimed directly at the locations crimes take place and clearly record everything. Cars are broken into and robbed on a weekly basis. Securities response, “you shouldn’t park there”. Packages are stolen daily. Securities response is to hang a sign that says cameras are monitoring. 
Security will NOT check cameras and investigate crimes. They have taken down resident letters hung on walls above where packages are stolen. 
If you are looking for somewhere in Detroit to live where security makes you feel supported and takes active measures, look elsewhere.

I’ve been living here for a little over a year now and honestly can’t complain about one thing. Management has been very friendly and professional. My neighbors have been extremely helpful and outgoing. The property itself is beautiful and very clean.

This place should not be marketed as a "luxury apartment" at all. The building and neighborhood is very charming, but the apartments have many issues. I lived in two different brownstone units over a 2 year period, and both were riddled with maintenance issues. These concerns were always met with reluctance and slow reaction time from management and maintenance teams. We ended up relocating out of our first unit into a different unit due to a seemingly never ending string of leaks in the ceiling. Every time they fixed one leak, another one would sprout, it was like they did not know what they were doing when fixing them. Also, in our first unit we noted a broken window hinge in our move-in checklist and notified the managers about it, and after over a year, the window was still not repaired. 

Both units were insanely HOT, year round, to the point of having to have windows open in the middle of the winter just to not be burning hot. The air conditioning was also pretty sub-par, it would run on high nonstop, but the unit was always 74 degrees or higher.

After awhile, we complained and complained to the managers about our unit, and they finally offered to let us move into a new unit, promising that "this type of thing does not happen in all of our units, we assure you." The second unit seemed okay, until about 4 months in, when we began experiencing more uncontrollable leaks. We had enough when there was a full 1 month period of some sort of maintenance personnel in our unit each and every day. We had drywall guys, painters, plumbers, carpet guys all in and out of our unit and we were tired of living in a construction zone. When we asked for a rent reduction, the management refused, and said there was nothing wrong with our unit, and that we were already receiving a price below market value. We finally had enough of it and pushed really hard to get them to let us out of our lease early.

If the building was properly maintained and did not have such bad infrastructure issues with plumbing and HVAC, we would probably still live here.

The "free air and heat" is a joke the apartment will be a constant 80 in the summer and winter... if you're cool with that, awesome! Also the parking structure is so unorganized, they rent out almost the entire structure to quicken loans and you will have to park on the 6th floor, not to mention the elevators are constantly down in the garage yet you aren't "allowed to walk to ramp" the insanely rude security guards will literally chase you! Spend your money elsewhere
I have lived here twice! Incredible staff and beautiful view

My apartment is beautiful. I wouldn't have thought I'd care for a studio, but I'm in love with mine. Management is great and Doug at the front desk is wonderful.  Only been here 2 weeks and have been so happy

DO NOT MOVE HERE!!! If you enjoy your peace and quiet, cleanliness, and just all around want the space you are paying for to be at least halfway decent please save a few extra bucks and move elsewhere it is not worth it!! For starters they will fool you, that building is definitely not up to code, the fire alarm goes off frequently, the water pressure sucks/the smell, the roaches, the laundry room is filthy & filled with roaches! The elevator does not work that often imagine walking down more than 8 flights of stairs when you have to go to work or coming home from work. Not to mention there is a nightclub every weekend on the top floor they do not tell you that upon move in, they do not control they guest they will be as loud as they want, litter in front of your unit, throw up on the carpet, knock on your door it is HORRIBLE! I DO NOT RECOMMEND this place to anyone Leasing office people are in on it as well so just save yourself the headache. Let’s not forget that construction people will walk in your apartment at any time and they will say “contact your leasing office they supposed to keep you updated not us.” If you are young & like to party buy all means move here but for those mature peaceful adults with real responsibilities or kids do not move in

AVOID THIS PLACE AT ALL COST.

Constant water issues. No pressure. Sediment in water. Just turned off altogether.

I've been here for 3.5 years - way too long. It's noisy. Everything is noisy. The walls are paper thin. If you can't hear someone's TV or music, you hear construction. Don't work from home here.

Oh yeah, and plenty of roaches.

We're repetitively assured contractors will follow Covid guidelines. They don't.

DO NOT move here if you work from home or enjoy restful sleep.

Town Residences could be great but it falls short on every measure.  I have had 2 floods in the past 6 months due to pipes that clearly needed to be fixed 10 years ago.  Their management has put work orders in to fix the issue but left the tenants with three huge holes in their walls (and have not communicated when they're going to get fixed).  To add to that, the repairmen take no consideration that they're walking into a home.  They have trapesed through my apartment with muddy feet leaving me with the mess. As well as removed shelving without my knowledge and did not care to put it back.

Not to mention the several dead roaches I have found in this place.

Also, in lieu of COVID, apparently it does not exist at Town Residences because no one - not even management - enforces a mandatory face mask policy (WTF?!?!).

So unless you like your apartment to be flooded, filled with roaches, and also contract COVID I would look elsewhere. Can't wait to move.

TO TOP IT ALL OFF THREE DAYS AFTER THIS REVIEW: my garbage disposal exploded....EXPLODED. Called the emergency line with a half inch of standing, disgusting water in my cabinet - only for them to tell me I would have to wait until tomorrow for it to get fixed.

I hate it here, I hate everything about this place. Do not move here, do not give them your money - you'd have better service living in a cardboard box.

Absolutely terrible place to live. Spare yourself and look elsewhere. There are serious plumbing and electrical problems in the complex. The elevators go out every other week, and for days on end. The light bulbs need replacing every 3 weeks. The water pressure goes in and out, and there are constant issues with the hot water tank. As of recently, residents have been without water for 5 days and all we got as a response, was an email (every other day) to "bare with them". Also, it took the complex 24 hours to send residences a notice about the water being off. Not to forget to mention, there has been serious flooding within several units. The fire alarms go off at all hours of the night. Lastly, there is construction going on in the parking garage behind the unit (has been going on all year long) and the jack hammer will wake you up at 6am sharp. 

The management team is incredibly incompetent. They lack basic human being compassion and take no responsibly when things go wrong (which is almost daily).
Nothing but problems from leaking ceilings to sewage erupting in the shower

I regret to say that my experience at CBD Detroit has been extremely disappointing. Firstly, the hallways are consistently littered with pet waste, making it unpleasant and unhygienic to navigate through. Additionally, the amenities are frequently out of order, rendering them inaccessible for use. For an entire year, the hot tub remained non-functional, despite numerous complaints.

What's more frustrating is the lack of accountability when it comes to security deposits. Despite repeated attempts to retrieve mine, I've been met with unhelpful responses, being told to contact the "corporate office" without any resolution in sight.

Overall, if you're considering moving here, I would strongly advise against it. The lack of cleanliness, maintenance, and responsiveness from management make it an untenable living situation.

I had a chance to take a virtual tour and view everything from the layouts to the finishes. Xavier was efficient and knowledgeable. He was also able to make what’s often a time consuming and draining experience light and fun!
First apartment and they gave me the blues! Leasing manager is rude/ has the worst attitude. No one communicates or tells the truth. Worst first experience.

This place is the worst! I wet to tour the apartment the other day really liked the place. I was excited to know I was getting an apartment. Went online to fill out the application they asked for $255 deposit which included the application fee. I hit the submit button as I'm waiting on my payment confirmation they had already sent a decline letter to me. How is that when I just submitted my payment and application. Not Evan two minutes ago. So I called the manager and said they don't make the decision which was a lie. I asked for my money to be refunded back to me she said it will take seven to thirty days. How when you took my money in two seconds. What is the point of me giving you two hundred if I was going to get turned down why was I not provided a screening criteria list before I applied and you took my money. I got played they will take your money

The staff was so friendly and helpful, and the building was absolutely beautiful. Angelica was my leasing consultant and she provided outstanding service. This building really has it all. Gorgeous views, great amenities, and historical charm. Not mad about it!

I’ve lived here for a little over a year now, and I still love it. There are some drawbacks, as with any old building. There are some pests, but as long as you keep your apartment clean and have some Raid spray on hand, it’s really not a big deal (I see a bug maybe once every few months in my apartment). 
The maintenance staff is amazing and works very quickly. The leasing office staff is also very friendly and helpful. 
They also have a cleaning crew that comes in a few days a week and cleans all of the common areas. 
Everyone in the building is really friendly and it’s a great community. 
They recently replaced all the doors so they are not propped open anymore and there is a security guard on duty when the office is closed. I’ve never felt unsafe living here. 
I have never had an issue with laundry, there are always machines open and they clean it regularly. 
I live in a 1 bedroom and it’s very spacious, and the vintage details in the apartments are beautiful. 
It’s not right downtown, but it is a great location near Belle Isle, Indian Village, and about a 10 minute drive to downtown. If it were anywhere closer to downtown, it would probably be double the price. 
Overall, it’s a great place to live and I would definitely recommend it!

Been trying to get a response for a week and a half. Their phones route directly to voice-mail and their mailbox is full. it's also pretty clear they don't check their emails either. Guess they don't want our money?

I lived here for a year. If location is your first priority, this is a good option. I lived in a studio and it was very small and cozy. The bathroom often had problems. I experienced multiple leaks from the ceiling, issues with the plumbing, and poor water pressure. The complex is lacking in safety measures as well, often the side doors were propped and people would walk the halls, such as food delivery and others. The water was shut off for an entire day more than once a month.

Many of the 5 star reviews are from people who obviously do not live at Waters Edge-- they were left before complex was actually leasing apartments. I have lived here for several months and am disappointed in multiple areas:
-Design and finishes:  The finishes (Carpentry, appliances, light fixtures, paint, etc.) are on the cheaper end and the execution is poor.  The choices made during construction keep Waters Edge from being a true "luxury" apartment.  From the vinyl floors, cheap washer/dryer, unfinished carpentry and more, Waters Edge is average. 
-Management:  While new constructions are notorious for having "kinks", I have had an issue with almost every appliance in the residence.  What makes matters worse is the delay in having these issues addressed or corrected.  The people working in the front office are very nice, but overall the office lacks structure and organization.  Many of my complaints are met with a shoulder shrug...
-Amenities:  Any "luxury" complex should come with basic amenities-- a pool, gym, covered parking and community room at least.  I was assured that all of these features were under construction and would be available within months .  Now that I am a resident and my balcony overlooks the proposed site for the pool/gym, I can see that NO PROGRESS has been made in the past 2 months-- not luxury

My experience at the Lofts of Merchants Row has been overwhelmingly disappointing. Where do I even begin?

Firstly, the elevators seem to have a mind of their own, and it's never in sync with the residents' needs. They are consistently out of service, leaving tenants to trek up numerous flights of stairs just to get home. For a modern building, this is simply unacceptable.

Secondly, the issue of drug use throughout the building is a serious concern. The management's lax approach to security and oversight has allowed this problem to persist, making many residents feel unsafe and uncomfortable in their own homes.

Trash pickup is another sore point. It's shocking that a supposedly upscale establishment fails to organize regular weekend trash collections. The overflowing bins become a breeding ground for pests, creating a health hazard for everyone living here.

Speaking of management, their incompetence knows no bounds. They're slow to respond to complaints, if they bother to respond at all. Maintenance requests are often mishandled or completely forgotten, leaving residents to live with unresolved issues for weeks on end.

The repair personnel they send are no better. It seems they lack the skills or motivation to fix anything properly. Many residents resort to paying out of pocket for basic repairs just to get things done right.

Access control is another headache. The key fobs and security systems work sporadically at best, leaving our safety and privacy compromised. It's absurd to pay premium rent and yet have such unreliable security measures.

As for the windows, they are so grimy and poorly maintained that we can barely see through them. It's like living in a perpetual fog, which adds to the overall dismal atmosphere of this place.

In conclusion, the Lofts of Merchants Row have proven to be a regrettable choice. Between the constant elevator failures, rampant drug issues, inadequate trash pickup, incompetent management and maintenance, unreliable security, and filthy windows, it's abundantly clear that this place does not live up to its promises of luxury living. Save yourself the frustration and look elsewhere for a residence that values its tenants' comfort and safety.

I lived here for approximately 15 months and am now moving out and I absolutely loved it while I was here. While I will go into further detail below, overall, you can't find a better value for money than these apartments if you are looking to be in the heart of downtown.

Pros:

Location!

Within a ten minute walk there are dozens of bars and restaurants that are all fantastic and each provide their own unique vibe. If you like eating/going out a lot, this is definitely the place to be. Additionally, for the sports fans, you're no more than a 10 minute walk from all the stadiums!

The Staff

I have yet to find an apartment with better staff than LOMR. Everyone is always so responsive and maintenance requests are almost always handled within the same day. Additionally, I had some circumstances around my work that required me to make multiple lease changes and Bre and Armand were always so helpful with that.

Space!

Have lofted cielings just makes everything feel so open! I absolutely loved it. While it could be a con for some people, having no windows in the bedroom was an absolute win for me

Cons:

Noise

If you are hyper sensitive to noise, I would find a different place. You are in the heart of downtown so especially on weekends, it can get loud and there's not a lot of noise isolation from the street. For me this was part of the allure but it's not for everyone

Washer/Dryer

Unfortunately in a lot of the units they use combined washer dryers. I found these to be harsher on my clothing and to take 2-3 times as long at a minimum. That being said, they do have full size units in the basement but you do have to pay for those.

Electricity Bill

With being ceilings comes lots of extra heating costs in the winter. Be prepared for electricity bills around the 150 - 160 mark for a 800 square foot 1 bedroom.

Summary:
No apartment is without flaws but if you love being in the heart of the city, you won't find a better place than this one.

While not as ornate as the Art Deco buildings downtown, Detroit City Apartments (DCA) is one of the more affordable locations downtown that still has a ton of amenities. There is also a very good gym and business center that is common for all residents. 

The parking is fairly expensive, but it is attached to the building and monitored 24/7 so definitely worth it.  It's also connected to a people mover station and across the street from the main bus terminal so public transport is the best in the city.  Everything downtown is no more than a 15 minute walk (Greektwon, Waterfront, Fox Theater, MGM, etc.).  

The staff has been super friendly thus far and there is a 24 hour concierge, another great thing for safety.  I only wish that I had in unit laundry and that the maintenance was a bit faster is responding but some of that is me not being proactive.  The community is very young too - seems like mid 20's to early 30's is most common.  

Overall I think this is a great option for anyone looking at Downtown to live without overpaying to live right near Campus Martius.
