The staff was so friendly and helpful, and the building was absolutely beautiful. Angelica was my leasing consultant and she provided outstanding service. This building really has it all. Gorgeous views, great amenities, and historical charm. Not mad about it!

I’ve lived here for a little over a year now, and I still love it. There are some drawbacks, as with any old building. There are some pests, but as long as you keep your apartment clean and have some Raid spray on hand, it’s really not a big deal (I see a bug maybe once every few months in my apartment). 
The maintenance staff is amazing and works very quickly. The leasing office staff is also very friendly and helpful. 
They also have a cleaning crew that comes in a few days a week and cleans all of the common areas. 
Everyone in the building is really friendly and it’s a great community. 
They recently replaced all the doors so they are not propped open anymore and there is a security guard on duty when the office is closed. I’ve never felt unsafe living here. 
I have never had an issue with laundry, there are always machines open and they clean it regularly. 
I live in a 1 bedroom and it’s very spacious, and the vintage details in the apartments are beautiful. 
It’s not right downtown, but it is a great location near Belle Isle, Indian Village, and about a 10 minute drive to downtown. If it were anywhere closer to downtown, it would probably be double the price. 
Overall, it’s a great place to live and I would definitely recommend it!

Been trying to get a response for a week and a half. Their phones route directly to voice-mail and their mailbox is full. it's also pretty clear they don't check their emails either. Guess they don't want our money?

I lived here for a year. If location is your first priority, this is a good option. I lived in a studio and it was very small and cozy. The bathroom often had problems. I experienced multiple leaks from the ceiling, issues with the plumbing, and poor water pressure. The complex is lacking in safety measures as well, often the side doors were propped and people would walk the halls, such as food delivery and others. The water was shut off for an entire day more than once a month.

Many of the 5 star reviews are from people who obviously do not live at Waters Edge-- they were left before complex was actually leasing apartments. I have lived here for several months and am disappointed in multiple areas:
-Design and finishes:  The finishes (Carpentry, appliances, light fixtures, paint, etc.) are on the cheaper end and the execution is poor.  The choices made during construction keep Waters Edge from being a true "luxury" apartment.  From the vinyl floors, cheap washer/dryer, unfinished carpentry and more, Waters Edge is average. 
-Management:  While new constructions are notorious for having "kinks", I have had an issue with almost every appliance in the residence.  What makes matters worse is the delay in having these issues addressed or corrected.  The people working in the front office are very nice, but overall the office lacks structure and organization.  Many of my complaints are met with a shoulder shrug...
-Amenities:  Any "luxury" complex should come with basic amenities-- a pool, gym, covered parking and community room at least.  I was assured that all of these features were under construction and would be available within months .  Now that I am a resident and my balcony overlooks the proposed site for the pool/gym, I can see that NO PROGRESS has been made in the past 2 months-- not luxury

Waters Edge is billed as "urban luxury riverfront residences", but the truth is that it leaves a lot to be desired...

I was looking to move into this community from out of state (the northeast specifically). The staff was 45 minutes late to our leasing appointment and acted as if it were no big deal. The finishes are not as high end as portrayed. The apartments are supposed to be brand-new and yet the cabinets in the kitchen were already chipping in one of units we saw. The doors are definitely thick because we couldn't hear the loud music that was playing from a unit across the hall 11 am in the morning. While waiting for the leasing staff to arrive we ran into a resident who had lived in the community for 6 months and had some unfortunate reviews for Waters edge. His anecdotes coupled with the tardiness of the staff was disappointing. When I saw Water's edge online, it was the number one place where I wanted to live and I flew to Detroit specifically to see the units and begin the leasing process. I am so glad I saw the community in person and didn't reserve a unit beforehand. It should not be branded as a luxury community because it is far from it. As a former real estate agent having worked with many landlords and leasing offices across the spectrum of caliber, this was beyond unimpressive.

Where in the world can you go to experience such views?  From the changing views of the Detroit Skyline to Belle Isle with the changing seasons.  Let's not forget our neighbor to the south, Canada.  Whether you want to watch the waves, the barges or the seagulls making the daily runs, you can see it all on the Waters Edge Detroit!  I would like to "thank" the management team for bringing this wonderful community to my backyard.  I am looking forward to selling my home and becoming an active member of this community.

It's a golden dream to live off the water,with a window view,watching fire works, boat races, looking at the waves at night dancing in the moon light, counting the stars while you make a wish at night

This is a dream come true for people that loves the water
the building is well kept,you can look out at the water and watch the waves dance , we call it the river walk where people from different back ground's that ride their bikes or jog ,the view is so beautiful better than you ever dream, of near down town shops

There was a fire in the building and damages have gone unfixed for almost 5 months now. Add on the unfinished updates that required repairs and the lack of communication and this place is barely worth it. Lower prices but lower standard of care.

I had a great experience moving into The Lofts of Merchants Row. From the start, Alex, the leasing agent, was incredibly helpful throughout the approval process, making everything smooth and stress-free. Janeen, the property manager, has been so welcoming and friendly—she went out of her way to introduce me to other residents around my age, which really made me feel at home.

Matthew and Vernie from the maintenance department have been fantastic. They made sure my apartment was ready before move-in, and anytime I’ve had an issue, they've been quick to respond and fix things without delay.

As for the property itself, it’s in a great location right on Woodward, so everything is super accessible. My apartment is beautiful with high ceilings and a modern feel, which I absolutely love. Overall, I’m very happy with my decision to move here!

My experience at the Lofts of Merchants Row has been overwhelmingly disappointing. Where do I even begin?

Firstly, the elevators seem to have a mind of their own, and it's never in sync with the residents' needs. They are consistently out of service, leaving tenants to trek up numerous flights of stairs just to get home. For a modern building, this is simply unacceptable.

Secondly, the issue of drug use throughout the building is a serious concern. The management's lax approach to security and oversight has allowed this problem to persist, making many residents feel unsafe and uncomfortable in their own homes.

Trash pickup is another sore point. It's shocking that a supposedly upscale establishment fails to organize regular weekend trash collections. The overflowing bins become a breeding ground for pests, creating a health hazard for everyone living here.

Speaking of management, their incompetence knows no bounds. They're slow to respond to complaints, if they bother to respond at all. Maintenance requests are often mishandled or completely forgotten, leaving residents to live with unresolved issues for weeks on end.

The repair personnel they send are no better. It seems they lack the skills or motivation to fix anything properly. Many residents resort to paying out of pocket for basic repairs just to get things done right.

Access control is another headache. The key fobs and security systems work sporadically at best, leaving our safety and privacy compromised. It's absurd to pay premium rent and yet have such unreliable security measures.

As for the windows, they are so grimy and poorly maintained that we can barely see through them. It's like living in a perpetual fog, which adds to the overall dismal atmosphere of this place.

In conclusion, the Lofts of Merchants Row have proven to be a regrettable choice. Between the constant elevator failures, rampant drug issues, inadequate trash pickup, incompetent management and maintenance, unreliable security, and filthy windows, it's abundantly clear that this place does not live up to its promises of luxury living. Save yourself the frustration and look elsewhere for a residence that values its tenants' comfort and safety.
Ive called and left several messages, and contacted throught this website.Wnet there during business hours, and nobody answered the phonebell. I can only imagine if i had a maintenance issue

I lived here for approximately 15 months and am now moving out and I absolutely loved it while I was here. While I will go into further detail below, overall, you can't find a better value for money than these apartments if you are looking to be in the heart of downtown.

Pros:

Location!

Within a ten minute walk there are dozens of bars and restaurants that are all fantastic and each provide their own unique vibe. If you like eating/going out a lot, this is definitely the place to be. Additionally, for the sports fans, you're no more than a 10 minute walk from all the stadiums!

The Staff

I have yet to find an apartment with better staff than LOMR. Everyone is always so responsive and maintenance requests are almost always handled within the same day. Additionally, I had some circumstances around my work that required me to make multiple lease changes and Bre and Armand were always so helpful with that.

Space!

Have lofted cielings just makes everything feel so open! I absolutely loved it. While it could be a con for some people, having no windows in the bedroom was an absolute win for me

Cons:

Noise

If you are hyper sensitive to noise, I would find a different place. You are in the heart of downtown so especially on weekends, it can get loud and there's not a lot of noise isolation from the street. For me this was part of the allure but it's not for everyone

Washer/Dryer

Unfortunately in a lot of the units they use combined washer dryers. I found these to be harsher on my clothing and to take 2-3 times as long at a minimum. That being said, they do have full size units in the basement but you do have to pay for those.

Electricity Bill

With being ceilings comes lots of extra heating costs in the winter. Be prepared for electricity bills around the 150 - 160 mark for a 800 square foot 1 bedroom.

Summary:
No apartment is without flaws but if you love being in the heart of the city, you won't find a better place than this one.

We were right next to the service elevator and it was too loud at all times.  Then you had the HVAC for the retail units up the spiral staircase where the bedroom was and that was extreme loud in the winter.  Was told nothing could be done. They could put in new windows. Office staff didn’t care.  Maintenance was great and always nice and prompt.

I lived in the Checker building at EP for a year. The unit was amazing and we didn’t have any major maintenance issues. Janet (management) was super kind and helpful when we needed her.

They also retained $250 of the security deposit for some small holes left from pictures/mirrors. It’s not worth the time to fight it, so instead they get this candid review. I see this as a pretty crappy way of recouping vacancy costs.

I recently moved in, and the staff has been really helpful, particularly Janet. Lots of restaurants within walking distance, and super quiet. Easy to walk right across the street to Ottava Via.  I love living here and was lucky to get in before this unique community filled up!”

Having lived in Corktown for almost six months, I am extremely satisfied with the experience.  The area provides a wealth of entertainment and dining options, and the location of Elton Park is perfect. 

The leasing/management team has been extremely responsive and helpful in getting me settled into my new home.  The Checker building complex provides secure, convenient parking and very comfortable living spaces.

I would give them minus 5 stars if I could. Apartment itself is nice. Maintenance/leasing office sucks. They just ignore you for any concerns/requests. Cons:

-elevators were broken almost the whole year we were there (2021-2022) The day we moved out the freight elevator was acting up and at any given time 1-2 elevators of 4 would be down, making wait times very long

-found out 9 months in the entire maintenance staff had been fired for negligence which explained why none of our tickets were answered despite weekly visits to the office 

-filthy property: the hallways had trash despite housekeeping being on the premises all the time, the elevator frames had missing metal, tenants very disrespectful to property 

-office staff would smile and act nice but did nothing to help. The property manager left a few months after we moved in and that’s when things started to turn.

-fire alarms went off at any time of the night so frequently we just stopped going down

Zero communication from management. None of the amenities work. Alarm goes off several times a week and at all times of the day and night. Elevators are always down. I have been staying at DCA for a year now and its one of the best decisions I have made. I love it here especially the concierge team they staying keeping my day going well and I feel safe knowing its some one downstairs 24/7. Very convenient if you work or go to school within the Downtown/Midtown area everything seems within walking distance. I have recommended most of my friends and family to move here because of the great prices for rent and the amazing view! Thank you DETROIT CITY CLUB I am a proud resident!!!!!!!!

While not as ornate as the Art Deco buildings downtown, Detroit City Apartments (DCA) is one of the more affordable locations downtown that still has a ton of amenities.  All rooms are a good size and are equipped with modern options (cable etc.).  The best draw of the place is having an outdoor rooftop pool and barbecue area - major pluses for entertaining.  There is also a very good gym and business center that is common for all residents. 

The parking is fairly expensive, but it is attached to the building and monitored 24/7 so definitely worth it.  It's also connected to a people mover station and across the street from the main bus terminal so public transport is the best in the city.  Everything downtown is no more than a 15 minute walk (Greektwon, Waterfront, Fox Theater, MGM, etc.).  

The staff has been super friendly thus far and there is a 24 hour concierge, another great thing for safety.  I only wish that I had in unit laundry and that the maintenance was a bit faster is responding but some of that is me not being proactive.  The community is very young too - seems like mid 20's to early 30's is most common.  

Overall I think this is a great option for anyone looking at Downtown to live without overpaying to live right near Campus Martius.

I recently moved my parents into Allegria Village Senior Living Community and have found their sales team and overall onboarding process into the community to be spectacular. My parents have lived in the same home for 40+ years, so this is a big move for them as I'm sure it is for all new residents. I appreciate knowing that they will have much less home maintenance to tend to and that the Allegria staff and residents welcomed them from day 1. On top of the warm welcome, my parents are taking full advantage of the amenities available to them (indoor pool,  a remodeled gym, and healthy meals from the cafe, the convenience of Comerica Bank at their fingertips, as well as grabbing small items from the convenience store.  They are also anxiously awaiting the opening of the dog park - fencing just went up - for when their grand-fur-babies visit. 

The sales team did a fantastic job helping us explore options, learn about the community, and generally feel comfortable considering Allegria. 1000% recommend this location if you or seniors in your life are considering a retirement community!

This place is a wild mess… if you gone move here please request the first or second floor because the elevators here never work and people get stuck all the time.. oh and a roach problem they will meet you at the front door if you think I’m lying

The Leasing Team at the Heights are “Amazing”. I came for a tour, Cherita was very personable and courtesy. We viewed the available units. She was very informative to the point she had answered the questions before I had to ask. I applied for the apartment and notify of my approval fairly quickly. I’m excited to moving to a community where management really cares about their residents and if they are happy! I would definitely recommend the Heights!! Valencia

As an employee of the hospital up the street, this place is absolutely perfect. They have been steadily improving every aspect of this place since I moved in and we all appreciate the people in the office.

This place is so horrible. I regret moving here. There is a roach issue that they don’t address before you move in and act as through they never it was a roach issue. In addition, the power is always going out! Even if the weather is not bad, the power just goes out for no reason. Also, everything in here is low quality and cheap. Everything is always coming apart or breaking. Nothing this place has to offer with ever match with how much you have to pay a monthly.

I would recommend the heights of Southfield to anytwhos looking for a place to stay and call home , the property is well kept and the staff is very professional and friendly and willing to work with you on any issues you may have which I had none but they wanted to know any suggestions I may have had to improve their already outstanding service

Do not move here! If I could give zero stars I would. It’s dirty, it has a roach infestation and the leasing agents lie to get you to sign your lease. They clean the hallways during tours so you don’t know they have bugs. Please DO NOT MOVE HERE. They were previously named THE TOWERS OF SOUTHFIELD. They changed their names to avoid bad reviews.

So many issues in a beautiful building. Most noteworthy are the unmaintained pet areas (seriously they don’t even supply poop bags and the relief area has never been chemically treated so it is ?? ), the significant number of AirBnB type units, the smell of tobacco in the elevators, the lack of recycling, the faulty fire alarm systems, a roof deck with zero shade & cheap furniture, and the revolving management teams (6 different property managers & 2  companies in less than 2 yrs). 
The apartments are beautiful and the neighborhood is great but ultimately they charge way too much for the lack of services.

If you're looking for a superb place to live in Detroit, look no further than The Kahn. One month in and I can honestly say I'm blissfully happy here. The building is immaculate and the decor is stunning, making it a joy to live here. Each of the apartments is renovated, too, which is just so nice to come home to. The attention to detail is hard to top and there are three lounges to escape to if need be. I highly recommend moving into The Kahn. It is downright killer.

The Kahn is very delicate and seductive feeling . It makes me feel like I’m apart of something special . I feel secure and important . Which all tenants should feel when renting out a place of such great history .

The leasing managers and staff office was extremely welcoming and forthcoming when helping me with the move-in process. They answered any and all questions that I had, and always replied promptly. They made the daunting process of moving very easy, which was especially great as I was moving on my own for the first time. The maintenance team has also been phenomenal in reaching out regarding any requests. The amenities are always sparkling clean and well-kept, and the general living space and aesthetics of the Kahn have exceeded my expectations. In all, my experience with moving in as well as living at the Kahn has been nothing but positive and I'm just so grateful for the kind staff and wonderful environment.

I started my apartment search & I saw the Kahn the first day. Everyday until I made my decision, I compared every other place I considered to the Kahn. I loved this place the most. It was more convenient for me as far as location, price, amenities & a few other things. I am very pleased with my decision as well as my family. I appreciate the staff for being prompt when I do need them, I haven’t had any bad encounters & I enjoy how close I am to a lot of my favorite places that are within walking distance. I feel safe, fulfilled & welcomed by all.
Great place to stay, nice apartment and appliances. However the apartment itself is a bit too small for the high rent prices.

I highly recommend this rental building. Special thank you to Kara, property manager, who was always there for me. She was very easy to reach and tried to solve my problems and addressed my concerns. She is very professional, friendly and sympathetic human being. I was happy to be a resident there.

I’ve lived here a few months and it’s the best decision I’ve ever made.   Excellent location for everything.    Very happy with everything.    Management is great to deal with.   Highly recommended to anyone looking in this area!
Great Property Manager, upcoming amenities amazing, beach front to relax, great location, love that they are pet friendly and best of all Geo Thermal and Camera Security system.
This historical property is in a great location and right on the river. New property manager is amazing.

I have experienced every kind of roach both inside my apartment and in the halls. Management does not treat infestations with any urgency. Please please please beware!!!!! Do not be fooled by the price, it's not worth it. I want to escape as soon as I can.
Location perfect , all utilities included .. but it’s a chance you will see roaches in your unit
No parking for residences, huge bug problem, outdated appliances
This place is just going down hill fast. I would recommend spending a little more money and go elsewhere.

Building manager doesn't manage anything well, seems to have no contacts with the city, and doesn't vet the staff. The hallways are dim and smell bad because they are never cleaned. The building has been infested with bed bugs three times in the past five years that I know of. There's been a city work crew violating nighttime noise limits for a month righto outsider the building, but because the manager doesn't live here he doesn't care. The building recently got fiber optic internet, which is the only thing recommending it at this point. Staff has walked into my apartment multiple times without letting me know, which is illegal. One time, they saw me naked. The dryers in the laundry room stained all my white clothes with yellow oily splotches, and now I have to do my laundry off site. What a huge mistake moving into this building. Pay a little more for a better place nearby.

I've been here for a few years now and it has worked out very well. These apartments are one of the best values you'll find downtown. With that said, don't expect a luxury loft. Most of the units aren't extremely updated, and the ones that are don't use premium finishes. For the price you pay, everything is adequate. My unit is spacious with a great layout. The floors are concrete (under the carpet), so you don't hear the neighbors above or below. Unfortunately, the thick plaster walls absorb a disappointing amount of sound from the apartments next to you, so hopefully you're neighbors aren't too loud. I can hear every word of conversations at normal volume. My description of the units carries over to the building itself, meaning you get what you pay for. It is well kept with nice historic details, but it is nothing fancy. The fitness room is a nice touch, but you'll want an external gym membership if you're into serious workouts. It has the basic cardio equipment and a multi-station machine. There are mats, benches, and free weights, but the dumbbells only go up to 25 lbs. The laundry room is conveniently located in the basement and has plenty of machines available when you avoid peak hours (Sundays). Unfortunately, there is no dedicated outdoor space for grilling or relaxing, but the grassy park area across the street is good for pets. The parking lot is attended throughout the day and gated with electronic access at night. The lot is managed by a different company, so you have to pay the monthly fee separate from your rent. A big downside is that the parking spaces are not assigned, so it can be difficult to find parking at times and there are frequently cars that block you in. Luckily, there are plenty of things nearby when you don't want to use a car. Bars, restaurants, Greektown, the ballparks, Campus Martius, you name it. Many places within quick walking distance. Overall, I would recommend this place to anyone who asks because the location cannot be beat and many of the units have awesome views.

Make sure you note the fact that you need a 60 day notice to leave your lease. Not 30 like the state of Michigan says. We didn’t even live there for a month and we still had to pay for everything. When we turned in our keys they said we were good and didn’t owe anything else. Nothing showed in our rent portal that I checked for another month and a half after we turned the keys in we also attempted to call twice to make sure we didn’t owe anything. But they never answer their phones. Front desk staff was constantly on their personal phones whenever we went in person as well. 4 months later I get a letter from a collection agency stating we owed over a grand. Never received anything from River Oaks themselves stating we owed anything. Not in an email or mail box. But they did call us twice to ask if we were renewing our lease after we gave notice and they came to check out our apartment. Even in those phone calls they mentioned nothing. And then they are trying to charge us for fees from 2 months prior; and the kicker? I can’t get into the rent portal to get my past payments to show that I did pay the past months. Idiots all of them. Set clear and save your self the time and money. We didn’t even have a working dish washer for 6 months and there were literal holes in the wall near the windows and lastly the front door to the unit never locked. Not a great look

We've lived here for 3 years now, and will be moving soon due to job changes. The apartments are modest (some appliances are older, some sloppy baseboard and tile work in the kitchen and bathrooms) but are well maintained, and while we've lived here the windows and refrigerators have been updated throughout the entire complex. Maintenance has been excellent in their response times and considerate when entering our apartment. We had no issues with water leakage or insects. The grounds are well maintained as well.

The apartment design overall is a little awkward to fully utilize. The cubby in the living room has the cable jack, but won't fit modern entertainment centers. There are few to no lighting fixtures in the common areas. The One Bedroom model has an irregularly shaped bedroom. However, these are minor concerns.

The location is excellent. There's a corner grocery store and a gas station within walking distance (that's it), and downtown Dearborn and the Fairlane shopping mall are both a very short drive away. The complex sits on Ford Road, which is basically always noisy, so be aware if your living room or bedroom windows directly face the street. Also be aware that the police often idle in the complex's parking lots to set up speed traps.

Our only major complaint was laundry. Each building has hookups for private machines, which we did not have, and the "laundry facilities" are 3 washers and 3 dryers attached to the lease office, which was a long walk away from us. Those machines service the entire complex, so they are very worn and are usually taken. There are a number of coin laundry places on Warren and Ford road, and we ended up utilizing them heavily.

Overall, I would highly recommend this complex to students or families. It is not top of the line, but it is great for the price point!

This place is incredible. I cannot speak highly enough of the building, management, and community at The Ashley.  If you are already living in Detroit or thinking about moving to Detroit you need to have this building at the top of your list as a place to live. The team at The Ashley is kind, attentive, and friendly, and they truly go out of their way to make the building feel like home from the second you walk in the door to check it out for the first time. I knew pretty much immediately after my tour that I wanted to live here and the team made my transition into the building seamless and every moment living there an absolute joy.  10/10 - LIVE HERE!!!

This is the first apartment I moved into out of college. The location is perfect as it is in the heart of the downtown scene and a few steps to both the people mover and the Qline which take you most places you will need to go. Over the span of my lease I had several service requests that were performed quickly by one of the staff named Jason, very professional and friendly. Apartment was great quality, rent was unbeatable, and the security of the building helped me ease into the transition of living in a big city. The wine bar downstairs is a huge perk if you enjoy the events etc that they have or just want to stop and grab a quick glass of wine or cocktail. Great property!

The Ashley completed a full renovation in February of 2015, and the flatiron-style building is in the heart of downtown Detroit. 

The common facilities are clean, appliances are state of the art and there is plenty of natural night throughout the building. There is also a wine bar opening soon in the basement, retail next door and a number of concerts in Harmonie park. It's the ideal location for someone interested in soaking up all that the city has to offer. 

Rent is extremely reasonable for this location, and on the whole management is attentive. Building security is a bit confusing to me and I still question whether it's effective; there is a code to get in the door of the building and a unique keystroke to get onto each floor using the elevator. Since it's a ten-story building with no security to get into the stairwell, it seems as though an elevator code would not be a deterrent to even the most lazy of intruders. I moved from an apartment from across town with a doorman, and i think that was a more effective security management option. 

The building was once a historic hotel and the redo keeps the integrity of the original architecture. This gives the building a lot of character but also means the rooms can be a bit cramped and storage is lacking. For example, my closet is large but almost half  of it is taken up by a hot water heater. In the bathroom, the sink did not include anywhere to put towels, medicine, etc. we are also unable to hang things on the walls without command hooks, which is limiting and kind of expensive but not a deal breaker. 

Overall, this apartment comes recommended. I look forward to a number of years in this unit.

Horrible rude management doesn’t care about residence at all. Apartments are dirty and infested with bugs and management will not respond to emails and plays dirty tricks to keep extending your lease. Avoid at all costs too many other options in the area to settle for this dump.
Run! Management/Maintenance is unprofessional and rude. Neighbors loud and inconsiderate. Horrible place to live.

Terrible service, difficult to work with the staff, complete disregard and disrespect for students. Never in the office even during working hours. Atrocious at communicating and will never work with the residents unless it benefits the office.

The management is horrible and take it out on its tenants. The complex is very old and outdated. The building I’m staying in has a ton of roaches. I would definitely go somewhere else if I had a choice.
Lived here for years. Staff is great has been helpful. Manager is understanding and very responsive when I needed help. Would recommend to live here.

This is an excellent apartment to reside in for many reasons. First, the new management  is responsive and concerned with the concerns of its tenants. In addition, its a wonderful place to raise my 12 year old son. Lastly, the complex is located near some excellent schools and retail stores.

I currently live here and try to keep to myself, but am constantly running into issues with management over them over charging me and not repairing issues in the unit. Just this year, I have been over charged with unlabeled "fees" that management has no explanation for, my unit did not have heat for 2 weeks, the entire building did not have elevators multiple times for days at a time, the entire building also did not have hot water for a full week, and management does nothing about it. Most recently, they emailed to let us know that our pool is out of order due to them not making the payments on it. If you choose to live here, good luck and keep an eye on your bills.

The building itself is nice but it is not maintained. Heating in apartments periodically goes out in the winter and units are too cold to stay in, the elevators are frequently not working, the property manager(s) have high turn over and don't seem to care, laundry is expensive and also frequently broken, and the garbage backs up a lot. You can tell the staff and property manager all you want but they don't seem to care. When I first moved in here, the property manager was amazing and cared about the residents, since then we have had maybe 5 different property managers and the management has been terrible. This place is too expensive to have such terrible conditions and inconsiderate staff. I cannot wait until my lease ends and I can find somewhere that actually maintains their building.

I am counting down the days until my lease is up here, which unfortunately isn't soon enough.

I'll start with the good: the concierge and maintenance staff are wonderful people, better than you'll find elsewhere.  The couple of stars I'd give this place fully is because of them.

I'm writing this review at almost 2am because I have neighbors who have been screaming at each other for the last few hours.  This isn't the first time and won't be the last.  Even though the trash chute wasn't clogged today, my floor still smelled like garbage because whether the chute is clogged or not, there's an out of control problem with people just dumping their trash on the trash room floor.  Whether this is limited to my floor or a building-wide issue, I can't say, but it's pretty frequent.
Finally, my bills have been substantially higher than I was told they would be.  The leasing agent said that utilities never got higher than an additional $150 per month, which was only the case for the first couple of months I lived here and has been untrue ever since.  In spite of paying more money than originally intended, I am already looking for a new place and intend on using my savings to pay double rent for a few months just to get out of here early if possible.  I don't have extra money to spare, but I will jump at any opportunity to get out of here early if that's any indication of how things have been.  For the amount it costs to live here you can do much, much better - or at least might have a chance at a single good night's sleep.

Management is friendly and attentive. There are no pest issues, only cleanliness issues from individuals. It's truly shameful what people will do to try and get some free rent.  What you get vs what you pay for, is tremendous. Gated parking, electric, low cost utilities, and we're 5 minutes to downtown! The renovations are going to be super nice, and I can't wait to move into mine! Tracey the concierge has consistently been a delight. The building is also mostly concrete so the noise level for an apartment is really good!

I've enjoyed my time with ECP. The staff has been great and responsive to any questions or concerns that have come up.

Ashley has really done a lot since she first came on to improve the building, including a lot of preventative maintenance, communications about events planned or resident reminders to help ensure a secure building, pest control, and swift action if an issue arises in the building. I know if there's anything needed or actioned she'll make sure it's addressed.

There is a lot of coverage from the office and concierges to maintain a large level of building management and address resident needs. The primary concierge, Tracy, has been fantastic through the time I've spent in ECP and under Ashley and the previous property manager.

This place has a great proximity to downtown, making ventures for events, dining, concerts, or passage to Canada a short trip away. If you work in the downtown area the commute is short and void of slow-moving highway traffic jams, which I think anyone would rather avoid.

This place is all and more than I want in a new home! Appointment is tomorrow! I only gave 4 stars bc I am yet to be a resident! WILL update if I make it! Sure it'll be great..perfection for my teens!

We are IN LOVE with our apartment. It is renovated and stunning. The area is quiet and safe and is surrounded by the best things Midtown has to offer. The team is kind and helpful, and we are so grateful to be living in such a great place.

Do not move here! The people in the leasing office do not care about residents. My car broken into along with several other resident cars and they do not care. They take zero action. Much of the staff has been consistently disrespectful to myself as a tenant and my guests.

Gym- always very clean 

Package pick up- has always been safe and smooth for me.

This place has the absolute worst and most obnoxious management. They are rude and so unreliable. They continuously were difficult about the terms of my lease and made me so frustrated. CONS: Management is not kind or helpful. Apartments and hallways often smell like smoke. When it was anything above 30 degrees outside and sunny, my apartment was unbearably hot (even with the blinds closed). At least one elevator is usually broken. Security is usually on their phone or just not at the desk and during my time at the Towers, multiple cars in the guest parking lot were broken into (which is alarming since security sits in that lot). 

Overall, I would not recommend living here to anyone.

They don't have good security. I've only been living there for a year and I've already had 2 friends who's cars have been broken into in the guest lot. While I understand that crime can happen anywhere there's no reason that break-ins should be so frequent. If they just had a security guard posted at night there's no way anyone would break-into cars so this is totally preventable but management doesn't care.
I love this place it’s so clean neat and was ready for me unfortunately I couldn’t bring my dog and he had to stay with my sister in her apartment but other than that it’s great

Great view, very secure and safe, friendly staff. Although most amenities are included in the rent, you have to pay additional for parking, electrical and Wi-fi (even though they offer internet - the signal is poor)

I love my place and the people I stay with, however, there comes a time for    loving a place all your own...I love my space, especially the closet space, tall, wide, and deep just right. There are two cabinets above that fits all of my art supplies and a drawer beneath for personal care products. Now what I love even more about this place is the second closet that helps organize all my colors. Now the bathroom is nice. It has a slender old fashioned sink and nice size tub. My kitchen has all the space and dark carameled cabinets you could want. I just sit down sometimes and ease into a book that's usually cheesy and  romantic. I could go on and on about my place but the important note to take copy and paste to memory is to no matter where you go or who you live with. Make your space your place,  Make it your home.

This place is just a walk from Greektown!  I've been living downtown for 4 years now and this area is definitely a contender for the hottest spot in Detroit.  The place itself was built in the 60's and designed by world renowned modern architect Mies van der Rohe.  My first two years there were slightly less than satisfactory, with the heating during the winter not working all the time.  But the buildings were bought by new developers and in the last few months there have been many great improvements such as pool, elevators, and lobby refurbishments and geo-thermal heating.  A couple of the negatives that I have for Lafayette Towers is that my AC unit is hilariously outdated and loud and that after 3 years there they are still increasing my rent when I renew my lease.  It's one of the best places in the area, I would recommend it for someone who is taking their first step of moving into the area.

Overlooking the great city of Detroit. Great staff, and security. I feel safer than ever. The updated kitchen, fitness center and laundry room sold me. Great place to live. I would recommend it to anyone looking to live downtown.

Staff is nice until you get in.  Then you'll need to HOUND them to fix anything that goes wrong (which won't happen all the time, but does happen occasionally).  View is absolutely spectacular, location is fantastic, building and area is well-kept.  Pool is phenomenal.  Kitchen is very small (and we are in a larger unit).  Overall, it's great for about a year, but then you'll be ready to move.

I live on the thirteenth floor in a corner apartment.I
enjoy peace and tranquility daily. My visitors enjoy visiting me. Everyone is extremely friendly.

I'm thinking about moving in soon so I visited the area and the apt couple of times and it was not as bas as i thought it would be for Detroit.
Great place, worth checking out!

We moved into our apartment at the end of summer 2019. Despite repeatedly reporting a multitude of issues (mostly construction-related) to management, most of them were still not fixed over a year later. The building has zero amenities, including a proper mailroom. Common spaces are not well cleaned or cared for; the carpet in the hallways is already stained with dog urine and there is always trash in the stairwells and entryways. Don't waste your time or money.

I love Philip Houze! The location is prime and apartments are gorgeous. The only thing better than the spaces and where it’s located is the incredible service. The staff is phenomenal. Philip Houze is first-rate.
I love Philip Houze. The apartments are gorgeous. The only thing better than the spaces and location is the staff. They are phenomenal. I made an excellent choice.

I’ve only lived at Philip Houze for 7 months, but I’ve lived in Downtown Detroit for 15 years.

The staff here are extremely friendly and very easy to get a hold of. All questions are answered very promptly (and to my satisfaction), usually in person, since the staff is always available, one way or the other. Communication is handled so well, that my questions are answered before I even ask.

Maintenance issues are resolved in a timely (and friendly) manner. I never feel like I’m “putting anyone out”. The maintenance team goes above and beyond to ensure our safety by making sure everything is running properly.

Our cleaning guy is amazing! He begins early each morning to keep the building sparkling clean! Even my hallway is vacuumed regularly, and the stairwells are maintained. The building is very old, but it always smells and looks clean. This is a big plus in my book! 

Management plans lovely, regularly scheduled events that accommodate all different types of residents (including the dogs!). Nicely printed flyers are posted in advance so that we know what’s going on and can plan to attend. It’s such a nice way to meet my neighbors!

We have a secure, organized room where we can pick up our packages at our own convenience. If we know we have a delivery and would like it placed in our apartment, we just email management and they take care of it!

I love the fact that we have a secure bike room conveniently located in the basement. They’ve even installed a “bike station” with every tool necessary to do simple bike repairs. A heavy-duty tire pump has also been installed. It is securely bolted to the concrete floor, so you don’t have to hold it down with your foot. This may not seem important but, if you have a bike, it really means a lot to have these items available.

All in all, as you can tell, I think that Philip Houze is a great place to call home and I highly recommend it!

I have been in my unit for 5 months now and everyone has been so helpful and courteous when it comes to our concerns. We have had a shift in management and I was leery at first, but the new management is equally eager to accommodate the residents. It’s a great spot to live as it is placed right near a lot of the “happenings” downtown as well as the apartments have a really nice industrial design. The other residents are friendly and make living here the least bit better. I plan to renew! Being that this building was renovated in the fall/winter months, I’m excited for the fire pit/patio to come in the summer!

I have lived here for seven months & loved every second.  The staff is friendly and accommodating, the apartment has quality finishes, our lobby has a pool table, there is fitness room, a pickup dry cleaning service, a trash chute for convenience, and the location is unparalleled.  The entire city of Detroit is at your fingertips.  The Tigers, Lions, RedWings, and Pistons all play within walking distance, not to mention the Opera House, Fox Theatre, multiple other performance venues, and Detroit has an amazing bar and foodies scene.  I can ride my moped to Eastern Market, walk to Corktown for brunch (kinda far, but walkable) and hop on the QLINE in two blocks if I want to go to Midtown.  

I’m not sure about the review below as the call box does work, we have a package room, & when my heat went off for an hour during the freak of nature  Polar Vortex, the friendly staff had it back on within an hour.  Yes, there will be eventually be an outdoor space that hasn’t been completed yet, but when you open in October and have a Polar Vortex kinda winter, when does one expect that work to be completed??? You can’t run gas lines in the winter months for supposed outdoor fireplaces.

The Remodeling of the building is VERY nice and Great Staff, they will work with ALL your needs.

The only thing I don't like is paying for Parking (LOL).

I enjoy staying here!!
Cathedral tower has been good to me so far pleasant folks for the most part and the construction turned out beautifully.  Happy to call Cathedral Tower my home.

Management has no respect or consideration for the tenants. You could complain about a stolen item and they won’t care. Parking is a mess. Office staff are lazy and extremely slow about resolving issues. This place is not secure. Any and everyone can come and go as they please, so be sure to lock your door and car. The laundry room is pitiful. Elevators need to be replaced.

i lived there for only 3 months and immediately broke the lease after my home was broken into, as well as the next door apartment. Crack dealer on the top floor that attracts bad crowds. Also soooo many roaches it doesn’t matter what you do, THEY WILL NOT GO AWAY. please read all the reviews, people are not lying this apartment is a nightmare.

This is the worst resident I have ever paid to live in. Management is super rude. Everyone in the office always seem to have an attitude or don't know what they're doing except for one person. There are extreme bug problems no matter how much you clean roaches bed bugs and other creatures that don't pay rent. Walls are super thin you can hear everything your neighbors are doing. if you put a service order in it will take about two months for them to get back with you let alone resolve an issue you may be having. Very unprofessional building always smell bad roaches in the hallway and on the walls. The fitness room does not work. The trash chutes do not work have not worked or been in use since September you have to take your own trash outside. Did I mention there are bugs here.? Maintenance is overworked. New management is rude kmg rude. Elevators go out of order every other week. They shut the water off every month to fix water problems that they have had since May of 2019.  lighting system is poor your lights will flicker a lot when your air conditioner is on. Do not move here if you are looking for a peaceful living environment

The staffs of KMG are just rude. Don't expect they help you. KMG is the new manager, not like previous ones. 
Don't trust the photos here. The gym is very old. There is no piano or foosball table. You will smell smoke and the fire alarm rings all the time.
Be careful with paperwork. I returned the keys, they said everything is set. I shouldn't have trusted them. Later, they charged me for leaving the apartment without telling them! I wrote to KMG but no answer.
There are bedbugs and fly will get in your apartment in the summer!
Try to avoid!

I’ve message/ emailed/ called this property multiple times over the past 2 weeks called 4 times this morning NOTHING. I’ve SIMPLY wanted to schedule a tour; if I can’t get in touch with anyone to simply take a tour I don’t want to live there any issues or concerns I have won’t ever be solved because they can’t even pick up the phone

I stop by earlier this week to check out Hidden Valley Apartments and was surprised at how lovely the model version of the 1 bedroom looked (it even smelled nice). 

I’ve been to numerous apartments on a search to find a new home and was put off by how rude the staff were or the look of their model apartments with old furniture and bedding (it is 2019 and not 1980) Lol

I spoke with the leasing agent at Hidden Valley and was pleasantly surprised at how accommodating she was, I can tell she was extremely busy (Bless Her), but she put everything to the side to help answer any and all of my questions.

I work near by and lucked up and checked out this place after reading the reviews I was quite skeptical. I had the pleasure of speaking to the staff members there and to my surprise I didn't encounter the rude service or agent. The leasing agent was very nice, she made me feel comfortable and answered all my questions I believe she said her name was Donna, I maybe wrong but it start with a D. She offered me water and some treats she just made me feel real comfortable and at ease. I look forward to hopefully becoming a tenant here. Keep up the excellent work!

I find the apartments to be very convenient as far as a nice complex with friendly neighbors and pretty much close to a lot of shopping businesses.  I've been here for 3 going on 4 years.  I try to avoid calling the office as much as possible unless I really need something.  The lady at the front desk as a bit of a smart attitude, curt, sarcastic, and mainly condescending at times.  The property manager is almost the same I've spoke to her one time where she wouldn't even allow me to speak she just kept interrupting me.  The guys who work maintenance are nice.  They have a pool but takes time to open during the start of summer because they have to find someone to work there.  Mainly I would say make those leasing agents change their "attitude" and sound caring to their tenants.  I hate hate hate calling their office, they never answer, they don't  call back and one time I believe the lady at the front desk hung up on me.  They do have security ride around at night which is a good thing.  Good Luck.

I am staying in Hidden Valley for 4 years now. I got an apartment facing the woods which is what I love the most. It is a very private and quiet apartment. Management so far has been good to me and they respond well to emergency and non emergency requests. One disadvantage is they do not have 2 Bed 2 bath apartments.
Very ran down and outdated!! Don’t waste your time! This place needs new everything eeeeewwww
This apartment complex has rats. They send out pest control just to set traps without tackling the actual problem. Beware!

I hate living here. I’ve had trouble from no intercom system or working dishwasher as stated in my lease, didn’t have my bathroom sink for days because water was backing up into it, took them weeks to repaint my bathroom to get rid of the mold where I bathe my 2 year old. You call the office manager and she giggles at your frustrations. Also I’ve missed days of work because the building is so poorly maintained squirrels were chewing through my lines due to the whole up there in the attic . So hopefully they fix it before they chew threw the new line .

Noisy, falling apart property, and they never come in to fix ANYTHING!! Don't live here this place is a hell hole and we cannot wait to move out to someplace where we can actually get some sleep at night and not worry about the ceiling caving in!

I have lived here for 8 months and my overall experience is a -1. My neighbors car tires were stolen and left sitting on bricks and my apartment was burglarized 2 days before the new year during the day, due to the main entry doors ALWAYS being broken and open to anybody. Kids and teenagers run up and down the stairs and play on people doors and sit in the hallway all day. the property manager has no concern for residents safety. I can not wait till my lease is up in a few months. If you can please avoid this place with ALL measures. It's not safe and not worth your hard earned money "Everything that's cheap ain't good"

Riverstone Apartments is not a safe place to live. My friend spent the night and woke up to all 4 tires being stolen from their car. When I informed the staff, they said there are no cameras and there is no telling when a security system will be put in place. She told me to fill out an incident report and that could help. How?! 2 years before that my roommates car was completely stolen. On top of that, the door is always broken from being kicked in. Don't move here if you want to feel safe.

Windows need replacing… old buildings…old appliances…they spray paint everything to give a new appearance to the renter…but as time wears on you can see how old and in need of replacement things are… kitchen counters included… the rent is too high for what they provide…when I moved in three years ago the rent was reasonable for the quality of the apartment… there has been a $250 increase in two years but no new windows, appliances, carpets, or counter tops. Some windows I’m afraid will fall out when I open them .., many units put plastic to the windows to minimize the cold wind in winter… the property manager and service staff are nice but nice doesn’t provide needed upgrades… if I wasn’t ill I’d look  for a more reasonably priced property with upgraded features… it’s not the amount of rent but what you get for it… those who own their units don’t have these concerns but those who rent from legacy place Be aware!!

Only gave 2 stars because it’s cute and extremely spacious for a 1 bedroom, (although the closet is super small )and the location is cool. We pay entirely too much in rent to be experiencing the problems we have . There is only 1 maintenance man for 9 properties, so it will take forever for your issues to be addressed. Birds are nesting in the wooden frame of my front window which is causing it to essentially bust at the seems which now allows for flies and insects to enter . I have brought this to the property manager and maintenance attention and am still waiting for this to be addressed by a contractor . 

Good luck living here with all of the construction RIGHT  off  the balcony of 3 of these units , which i have been hearing for the past 4-5 months of my 6 month residency, so far. No one wants to live next to the construction of a wedding venue with a rooftop lounge / bar or continue to live here once the space is open and accepting bookings
This was a great place to stay! I enjoyed being in the heart of downtown. The management is quick and helpful. It’s spacious and well kept. It gets cold in the winters so be prepared.

I've lived here for 6 months and can say the rent is not worth the hassle.  The hallway constantly smells like garbage because there is no ventilation in the building.  I had bugs crawling out from behind the toilet and had to do my own pest control because all property management did was set out traps.  The drains have constantly been an issue backing up and smelling awful.  Now my toilet is backing up and has not flushed for a week while I wait for property management to do something.  Beware that this building has many issues and the condition of units, while they look good in walk through, is poor.  In my opinion it is not worth the rent I am being charged.  There are dilapidated buildings elsewhere downtown charging half the rent with fewer issues and more amenities.

First off, forget the pool. It hasn't worked in years, they worked on it for a month this summer, but it won't be up for years.
The maintenance crew is awful. Never once was anything actually fixed.
The floors are uneven and ugly. Every was redone cheaply.
Jeanette doesn't respond to phone calls or emails.
Not worth the extravagant price.

I have lived at Central Park Apartments for two years  (I am in the process of moving back home due to personal reasons) and it has nothing been nothing less than a wonderful living experience!
I lived in the 631 building overlooking Lafayette Park, and the views were just breathtaking. Imagine waking up in the morning and drawing the curtails of your living room open, to see the morning sun lighting up the Detroit skyline in the summer, the trees ablaze with color in the fall, a holiday scene straight out from a Christmas card in the winter and the trees in bloom during the spring. The views are unmatched!

The apartments are situated close enough to the city center  (walking distance) but removed far enough to have a peaceful space to yourself or your family. I loved walking into the city for work and dinner and having the Dequindre cut as a path way to the Eastern Market or the Riverfront. The complexes are in an excellent area for students, professionals and families alike since all the city's must see places are just right out the door.

As a young professional, the apartments has all the amenities that I could have asked for and more! All the appliances (stainless) were shiny new when I moved in, the bathroom was just redone in a crisp modern style and the rest of the apartment retained its mid century modern aesthetic which was a dream. The complex boats a mini gym, ample laundry machines that were load card operated (which was such a convenience), a pool, in-complex letter boxes and a new parcel system that was so convenient and secure. If you needed further motivation to move in, your neighbours are some of the best that you will have! I will miss my two neighbours because we truly were a little Central Park family: getting together for holidays, exchanging holiday gifts and just enjoying the park from our balcony on a summer evening with a laugh and a drink or two.
The maintenance team is the absolute best! They respond quickly to any work requests and make sure that  you are satisfied and comfortable.

I can go on and on singing the praises of Central Park apartments but this review will be chapters long. You will not regret living at this place. Please schedule a visit and I assure you that you will feel at home once you enter the gate and are welcomed by the Central Park Family.

I moved to Central Park Apts a couple months ago and there were some unforeseen circumstances that delayed our move-in. The staff were very kind and accommodating during this time. They did everything in their power to help us move in at the time we needed. The apartment is beautiful and VERY spacious. It is the best you can get in Detroit for the given price. The surrounding areas are safe and there is a parking lot with affordable parking fees. They newly renovated the apartments and are continuing to make changes, and giving it a modern touch. The maintenance team works really hard to make sure all requests are completed at a reasonable time. I just love these apartments, the staff, and the area. I plan to live here as long as I can!

I've lived at Kirby Manor for a few years now and my experience has been exceptional! The building is located in a nice part of Midtown Detroit that has more of a residential type feel to it. But it is still within walking distance of the DIA, the Q-Line, and Wayne State University. I used to love my morning walk to class when I attended Wayne State. I would recommend living at Kirby Manor to anyone!

I lived here for a little bit, it got progressively worse. Elevator is always broken, packages are lost, laundry is always broken, and they will raise your rent $200 every year. It’s also totally impossible to contact management, even though they live in the building.

Total upgrade from my last place. No leaks, heat works, hardwood floors were redone and I have a beautiful kitchen. The halls get dirty from the workers sometimes but its usually cleaned up by the next day.

Been living in the “Midtown” area for several years. This is by far my favorite building. (A lot of slum lords own apartment buildings in the cass corridor, if you find a really cheap apartment theres probably like a thousand things wrong with it). Dont have to worry about anything here, and everyone in the building hangs on the porch on the weekends, which is nice.  Huge lot next door for my dogs. Rent is reasonable, and theres no crazy fees for parking. I pay $40 a month. Not sure what “property manager is not license” means? Ali is seriously the best!

If you value you're time and money don't move in here. If you want to be respected by management look elsewhere. 

I put down a security deposit on a unit and told it would be ready in mid July. The move in date continued to be pushed back. Once mid September rolled around and the unit was still not ready for move in I demanded to have my security deposit refunded. I was given a hard time about and again was told the unit would be ready in 2 weeks.

After waiting 3 months and the unit was still not completed, I again asked for my deposit back and was told it would be 3 weeks to get it. I had to call and attorney and threaten the management with legal action. 

The place is run by 21 year old kid who doesn't know what he is doing. They do not respect your time.

Move on, there are better spaces for a much better price.

This apartment complex is definitely not ready to rent any apartments. I don't believe they understand what all goes into  leasing real estate. There are to many issues that need to be resolved. First, there are a lot of safety issues, secondly they have a big plumbing issue, and the apartments are extremely small. There are some small showers stalls in some apartments and bathtubs in others.  I do not believe they realized when they bought this property what they where inheriting. They have fixed up a few apartments to go up on the rent, but there are no amenities included except for a laundry room. The building is old and really should have been torn down and rebuilt from the ground up. What I have experience is that they continue to patch things up and ignore the real issues that they are having in this building. I like to see anyone succeed in any endeavors of their choosing, but be cognitive of your actions and be fair and honest with people.  Had I known or read the reviews before moving in here I would not have considered moving in at all.

I have been living here for four years. The owners live on site and they were having trouble keeping everything together. 

A few months ago, they hired a new property manager named Ali. His presence has had a huge impact for us here. He is kind, answers his phone immediately and I haven't had to wait more than a day or two for any maintenance issues since he started working here.  Unlike before, where it would take several days to even get someone to return our call.

Quiet neighborhood, people in the building are chill and street parking is free.

Terrible managent and owner. Cutting corners will only leave you with a full circle of endless problems. Might as well knock the entire building and start from scratch. DONT MOVE IN to this property. You can't keep putting a bandage on things that need more serious attention.
DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE! the management is terrible, apartment is overpriced and half of your stuff will end up missing

This apartment building has all the makings of a top notch rehabbed industrial building, and the price tag to come with it.

However, we were not made aware of the long construction project currently happening in front of the building that will last a long while to complete.  Additionally, parking is managed by a third party, to which they charge a whopping $250/month.  You'll want the parking though, as there is a rehabilitation center across the street that puts you near some interesting characters when on the street.  This area and location will probably be nice in 5 years or so, but as of 2019 I would NOT rent here. Additionally, the heating/HVAC system is not set up for residential units correctly, you're either freezing because it's out, or getting directly blasted with heat to the point that it's tough to be in the room. Whoever put up the walls made them paper thin and not-flush with the ground, noise/light from the neighboring unit frequently comes in.  Water and heat have been consistent issues. Again, I highly recommend you do not live in this building at this price point. It's just not worth the price point for the issues you deal with.

Has really bad roaches and water leaks. Terrible place to live. The only good thing about this place is the location. It is over priced for what it is. Has a lot of potential but has roaches the size of 50 cent pieces in the basement. Then the heat is constantly going out.

Was fine for the first half, but had lots of leaks that got worse as it was left unaddressed by maintenance despite multiple calls from me and my roommate. Roach issue just got worse over time and was also unaddressed save for leaving a few sticky roach traps.

I moved into a studio in July 2020 and had so many issues my entire time there. The building was infested with mice, I caught 15 mice in my apartment and had to move out & stay somewhere else and the building did nothing to  help or compensate. All my neighbors also had issues with mice and or roaches. I broke my lease in  after threatening legal action for the disgusting living conditions and I had to wait 5 months to get my security deposit back. Terrible management please stay away from essential management company and any of their buildings in midtown.

Maintenance here is a big problem, but management above maintenance is not doing their job either.
The apartment manager is unreliable and unresponsive.
No one here cares about living conditions.

Rooms are overcharged for what they are. 
Personally, I am a good tenant and would like more than anything to not deal with maintenance. But the problems occuring here, are beyond my reach. 
If you don’t like headaches, don’t rent here.

Rooms are live-able. Some bedrooms might not have a heater in them. Noise from people are quite loud but I personally think it is ok. Do not surprise if washing machines sometimes do not work and are not fixed for a month. The biggest problem experienced living here was the maintenance. On the third month of living, some part of the bathroom ceiling fell down. I asked for maintenance twice and did not even get anything fixed. Two months later, there were people coming in and  COMPLETELY TEARING DOWN the bathroom and kitchen for renovation. The apartment was completely ruined by dust... I was not even informed that there would be a maintenance. Even though I email to the manager, I did not receive any reaponse until I called via phone. Apart from its location near to WSU and safe neighborhood, there is nothing left.

I've been living here almost 5 years. I never had any problems what so ever. I leave and go to work come back home and it's the same as I left it. My neighbors are awesome, we all mind our own business but look out for one another. Management could be a little more to up keeping the apartments, I put in an work order almost a month ago and still no one has come to fix the things that needs to be fixed here, that's my only complaint about this place.

Pros: The price, location and people in the building. Everything else sucks. Our windows are chalked shut due to lead. The front lobby if you can call it that floods every year and smells of mold. We have gone weeks with out air... every single year and always on the hottest days of the year. We also have gone days with out hot water. But the worst part of living here is the club Anxex next door. If you are looking at a 01 or 02 on floors 2-6  you will be able to feel the club in your apartment. It gets so bad my hanging glasses clink together. This isnt just the weekend but also random week days. The best part is stepping over the club goers vomit in the morning to get out of building.

The number isn't even connected. Don't even bother calling because no one will talk to you. For people who are trying to make money off of apartments; they really have zero interest in talking to anyone.

I have called everyday at different times, left voicemails several time leaving my contact information, and sent multiple emails. None of them were answered or returned. I stopped at the apartment several times to speak with someone and nobody is there. It looks closed every time i stop by. Very unprofessional.

Set up an appointment for a tour. Arrived at building, waited 20 minutes and no one showed up. Communication was through email. Never answered their phone. Called and emailed again before we left. It has been 2 weeks and neither was returned. Cannot comment on apartment itself because we never were able to see it. 
Based on the comment below mine and my experience, even if the apartment is nice, not worth it if you can never get in touch with management.

I promise if I did not work near this building I would think it was closed you can call any week day at any time and near get there or a call back. I have even tried with multiple number not once have I spoken to anyone.

Management is the worst thing about this place I understand things happen but when they do management doesn’t care. If you have a maintenance requests look forward to not getting any updates or hearing from them until you personally go into the office.

Roaches, Nets, Flies, Mice. Only cosmetic work completed LITERALLY! All reviews are and will be true. I truly believe everyone here regrets moving here. They only take care of things that are literally important. Management appears to be so reassuring but they aren’t. I moved here for a temporary reason  and this is the worst decision of my life. Ceilings falling in, washers and dryers  stolen, management doesn’t communicate with tenants at all. They own other places in royal oak and Dearborn as well. There’s other reviews out there as well regarding their other properties. The reviews on the companies website are FAKE. Notice they’re all 4 stars. There’s also rusty water here. I could go on and on. Stay away!

When i moved in everything seemed perfect. They raise rent without notice. No utilities are included with rent wifi doesn’t work well in all units. All units have problems with water pipes my unit; personally my son room leaks during rain and my bathroom leaks from the unit above me. I don’t recommend anyone moved it any of the location

My costumer service experience was super fast!! The leasing agents were so quick even with COVID19 going on :) ive called the office over 20 times since applying and tori made sure she returned every call with every question answered! Im so happy with the team you guys have! Kyle is amazing at doing his job as well!! Stay blessed

This is an older building but you can tell the management is really trying their best to make updates. Renovations to units, a new elevator, updates to electric/water all within the last year.

Building common areas are clean and the neighbors and friendly/quiet. Staff is responsive too if you have questions. 

I've loved staying in this building, it's a great distance between midtown and downtown. I'm glad the prices are somewhat affordable for the city. Parking is a bit of a struggle but otherwise no complaints. Laundry is located in the basement.  I'd recommend checking this building out.

Extremely friendly neighbors and staff. Convenient location in terms of the arenas and downtown area. Kitchen area had brand new fridge and convention microwave.  Was only able to stay here a few months due to work/covid situation but would highly recommend!!

Bad (REALLY bad) communication from management, bed bug outbreaks were a serious concern, and the elevator was constantly broken (my friend even got stuck on it once and had to be rescued by myself and another tenant). There was one manager who was really nice and genuine, and they fired her pretty quick because she was actually trying to help people. I’ve seen the new guy maybe once in 6 months. Don’t live here. It ain’t worth the utilities.

Been here since August and it’s awful. We just got new management but nothing has really changed. The ‘gated’ parking lot isn’t gated, lights outside don’t turn on until like 10pm so it’s super dark out front for the longest time. Not a single floor has a working washer AND dryer. I do laundry on 10 and dry on 2, and each load is $1.75 for the nastiest machines, plus the elevators feel like they’re gonna drop any second, it’s horrifying.

I’ve lived here for multiple years and one thing keeps me: relatively affordable rent. I try to keep an open mind and recognize that this is a large apartment complex. That being said, there are many things I wish I could change  Cigarette smoke is SO heavy in this building that I’ve considered getting an air purifier. My hair and clothes still smell like smoke when I leave town. Marijuana smell is almost always present as well which I wouldn’t have an issue with except for the fact that it’s nearly constant. The elevators are only both in operation 50% of the time, and they are filled with trash and unknown sticky substances frequently. The building is “secure” but there are ways to get in without a key. Parking is included which is a plus, however, the parking gate also only functions 50% of the time so anybody has access. Residents (or non residents, who knows) park in non parking spots which ends up blocking cars in when there are plenty of spaces to go around they are just further away from the building entrance. There are frequently issues with the hot water which I want to have sympathy about, but also I shouldn’t be without hot water for 5 days multiple times in a year. Unlike others, I don’t have complaints about the office staff. They want to work a 9-5 just like anyone else and the office has been better about being staffed during posted hours in the recent months. They have responded promptly to my requests, there are just many things I understand as a resident probably can’t be changed.

It has been hell Living at Pallister since the new landlord. At least with the last one I could call her to get things done. Not with this one though. She is Never available and when there is a fire, smoke concern, gas issue or any issues with the water, which happens a lot...the voicemail is full on the emergency line. You would think that if a payment declined that it would show up on the bank statement as well.  Initially, they said that I did not pay my rent and later on after getting my lawyer involved they said they found the payment but it did not go through. They also claimed that I left my room a mess and took my security deposit, which was a lie. I should have taken pictures of everything before I left AND did a walk through with the staff! When I called to ask about it, the woman I spoke to was very short and rude to me. The only office member I remember who was very kind was Katie. She was awesome!

Overall, I would not recommend anyone to move here, especially if rent increased. My overall experience was poor and it definitely was not worth it.

I just helped my son move into Pasadena Apartments.  I cannot say enough about the wonderful assistance that we received from Tawanna and Tony.  Tawanna is a lovely, hard working professional who takes her work seriously.  She takes care of the tenants at the Pasadena, and is very attentive to their needs. Her interpersonal skills are extraordinary. Her value to the company is immeasurable, and I look forward to seeing her the next time I visit my son there. Tony is in charge of security there and helps tenants with all sorts of things.  He made sure that we had easy access to the freight elevator when we were moving in.  He helped my son unload and carry everything into his apartment on the seventh floor. He is a very nice man, and it is clear that he really cares about the tenants. The Pasadena is an historic building that dates back to the turn of the 20th century.  Vestiges of its former grandness are still there, including high ceilings, great original wood floors, beautiful tiled hallways, and some great old fixtures.  In recent years, they have been making a great effort to reclaim this wonderful old building.  My son's studio was exceedingly clean the day he moved in.  He loves the old bathroom fixtures, and the kitchen with granite countertops, double stainless sink, and clean appliances.  He is a chef, so he knows a clean oven when he sees one.  He has a stunning and uninterrupted view of the beautiful Detroit skyline to the west.  He could walk to the GM building in under 20 minutes, and public transportation is right at the front door 24/7.  He rides his bicycle anywhere he wants to go on well defined and maintained bike lanes. If he wanted a car, he could park it in secure parking for a mere 40/month! But a person can actually live well without a car from this location.  In short, The Pasadena is a great option for folks wanting downtown at a reasonable price.
