We absolutely enjoyed our time here. Knowing what we know now, we would absolutely sign on again with them if we were staying in the Dearborn area. 

1.) They are highly proactive with pre-winter maintenance. Prior to last winter, they inspected every single apartment. For our apartment, they replaced our furnace and repaired the downstairs heater. I’m glad they found it when they did, because winter would have been quite cold without their proactive approach. 

2.) They are very responsive with maintenance needs. We asked for someone twice for non-emergency, basic issues. Within 24 hours the problems were resolved. 

3.) One of the reasons we chose here was because of the subdivision’s beauty. We love to run, and it’s been incredibly nice to run on quiet streets without having to drive to a park. Plus, the ponds have ducks and geese pretty much year round. In the early spring, you get to see the year’s new babies. They’ve done an incredible job at keeping the natural beauty of this area.

4.) The staff inside the office are always nice and very attentive. Even more, I will say that, due to my interactions especially with two people in the office, that they are also just good people, not just helpful landlords.

5.) The pool is wonderful, as is the club house and gym. The gym provides excellent variety in work outs, from yoga to cycling, weights to treadmills, etc…

6.) They foster a wonderful environment for anyone, regardless of family type. Our building has elderly (including a handicapped individual), college students, and families with young children. We have never had a problem, nor have I heard of anyone else having an issue. It’s quite remarkable, especially since we’re right next door to a college and have college student neighbors.

If we were staying in Dearborn, we would stay here until we purchased a home. Unfortunately, life’s taking us elsewhere. This is the first time where I’ll actually be sad to part ways with my landlord and management. This was truly a wonderful experience, and I highly recommend it to anyone considering moving to the Dearborn area.

I have been living in my apartment since the opening of the building! I love my space it is so inviting. I can look out and see the birds and the squirrels and people walking by.  The people in my building are friendly and we have had good times here. I would like to think that I will stay here for as long as I can. My Samoyed dog loves sitting on the patio watching everyone go by and loves to sleep outside at night. Being on the 3rd floor really makes it safe for her and myself. Hope I will have many more years here.
Not much going on at this property.  No get togethers.  Little communication from Management. People moving out and not seeing many coming in. Reputation is not getting better. Many rumors.

The community of Town Park Villas is okay, it is centrally located and quiet and has a small town feel to living here.
The rent and additional fees being charged are way too high for what you are receiving, but that seems to be the new norm in San Diego.
Great place to live. Very quiet. Great management and maintenance is good too. Very safe neighborhood. I would recommend to anyone 55 . Close to freeways.

The management is the best. I enjoy living here and plan to continue here my home. I live in a quiet end of the block other than my neighbors barking dogs. My other neighbors are great, respect full, kind and we cooperate with each other. Except the barking dogs
I love town park community. The neighbors are really nice. I love to see them walking running while in the bike. I love the gym in the movie theater. Thank Town Park for everything. God bless you.
We love the people here, they're so friendly and kind.  Apartments are a generous size and meet all of our needs.  The outside landscaping is well kept and is pleasant to look at.

Prices continue to raise. This is a 55  community and the majority are retired older people. A lot of people mo ING out ( more than moving in) because we are now spending  much more money for less services and activities. The pools remain unheated so we lose use around 6-7 months even though we are paying for the use. Maintenance takes it's time responding because they share staff with other owned properties.  New staff are in place and HOPEFULLY they might care about the people that they are hired to work for ( Customers)

The neighbors around here are very nice. They speak to you every time they see you the dogs are nice. And friendly. I love this community. I like the maintenance guys. They are very nice. Parking is nice gym is nice. Thank the staff for everything that they do here.

I lived there for 1.5 to 2 years. I can't recall now.  I liked the location a lot.  I lived in the older units and they were alright.  I think that they were actually bigger than the new ones.  One thing I really disliked was that they didn't have assigned parking.  Some times I would come home and the parking lot would be full.  That would indicate that someone had someone visiting and they parked there.  No way to find out where they were so you end up parking on the street.   I talked with management about this at the time I was signing my lease.  A lady showed me the apartment. I ask about parking when we pulled into the parking lot.  The lady showing me the apartment told me that they were in the middle of assigning a parking space to each unit and they would have it finished shortly.  I would ask about it frequently and get some lame excuse.  It was really irritating to me.  I would come home in the evening, especially on the weekend, and there would be no place to park.  Sometimes even the on-street parking was really busy and I might have to park a block away.  Great.  The other issue I had was about the water bill.  The way they figure it is screwy.  I lived there alone.  But they would divide the water bill by the number of apartments, not the number of inhabitants.  So fo course if you live alone you get the shaft.  It's not just $3 or $4 either.  It was just annoying.  I guess the fact that I'm an accountant didn't help with that issue.  Lastly, they had just completed building a new large pool with a recreation center and office.  That was good.  But, the problem was that they closed it all down when the office closed.  Think about how convenient that would be for you as a renter there.  So, it's a great location, but management sucked.
Reasonably priced. Outdated kitchen and bathroom.  Garden style and very private
Not worth the price. With rare exception, it seems like they don’t care about us and that we are a nuisance.
I would like to live here a bit longer before leaving a review. Thank you.

My move in experience at Diega has been excellent. The facility is clean, well maintained and has great amenities that provides me with all the life style options on the premises for easy access and no need for extra gym or club memberships.

The best community I could imagine - I feel so lucky to be here. Not only is it a welcoming staff, the amenities are top notch, the location is unbeatable, and the events are always so well done. I believe objectively the best community to live in in Downtown San Diego!

I love living at Diega. Sure the maintenance needs to be quicker, but they don’t allow short term rentals and do a lot to make sure this is a safe and friendly community. I wouldn’t live anywhere else downtown.

Living at Diega has been a great experience.  I've lived in the community for the last 34 months and have found the staff to be extremely friendly and professional.  The convenience of living downtown is a plus by being able to walk to many restaurants and Petco Park.  The facilities and grounds are very well kept.  My wife and I could see ourselves living at Diega for a very long time.

I lived at Bella Posta for over three years, during which there were some positives (close to downtown, Amazon Hub, and quick maintenance turn-around), but mostly negative. However, I was sticking it out. Yet, after asking the status of my lease renewal that was up in less than seven weeks, I received a notice stating that they would not extend me another lease option instead giving me the option of moving into one of their remodeled apartments. Based upon seeing the remodels through windows, they look nice, but the units are horribly overpriced already given the issues with the complex. So, in the middle of a pandemic, they want me to move from my home into another one so they can charge me more. That gives you some insight into the mindset of the property managers.

If you don't mind any of the following, you should love living here: the hall and your apartment smelling like cigarette and marijuana smoke due to air circulation issues; people parking in your assigned parking spot with no way to tow them; frequent water shut-offs and poor water quality that have been going on for years, with no notice; people breaking into garages and stealing your stuff; complex changes that are sold as "improvements" but really are major inconveniences like moving one building's mailboxes to another building; no visitor parking; charges designed to circumvent the house increase law (charges are about $80 a month in addition to your rent, up from about $50 in 2017); secured buildings that are left unlocked; unreturned messages to the site manager and assistant manager; poor security; routine elevator maintenance that takes over eight months to complete; air conditioners breaking in summer with slow repair time; and massive freeway noise from I-8 and I-15.

This is all on top of the normal things you see in apartments: bugs, low-quality appliances and carpeting, and loud neighbors and barking dogs.

This place is an utter mess. As other reviewers have mentioned, they've been undergoing renovations. I get it, that can be messy. But it's been so poorly managed, it was a constant joke with my friends. 

I lived in the front building, where the leasing office is. They decided they needed to tear up the tile in the entryway, which also meant they closed off the stairs closest to my apartment, the way I normally get out of the building. An email went out saying it would start on Wednesday and end on Friday (which I thought was crazy ambitious). It didn't finish until a week from that Friday. I had to walk through a maze of the complex to get to my car because they decided they needed ivory tile instead of saffron. 

I was given 60 days to leave the apartment because they decided they absolutely needed to renovate my apartment (so they could charge more money). The last two weeks or so I lived there, I had basically no hot water. The water was constantly being shut off, sometimes with no notice, but even when it was on I couldn't take a hot shower.

I don't think any new residents will be kicked out, since they've renovated all of the apartments now. But be prepared for the most incompetent management you'll ever experience!

For the past 11 months this apt complex has been a war zone. They are far more concerned about luring future residents than helping current residents. This complex is located next to a major highway but the good news is you wont hear it over the constant day in and day out construction. Jack hammers, tearing down siding right outside your apt, ripping up carpet outside your apt, painting inside and outside (fumes leaking into your apt), update your tetanus shot because I have stepped on nails twice! They gave us 3 days notice and told us we had to leave out apt for an entire week for interior construction. Our water has been shut off dozens of times in the past 6 months. They have limited parking and will only give each apt one space and street parking is a nightmare. Worse they are constants closing off sections of the parking lot - they will give a few days notice then TOW all the vehicles in that section. So if your out of town you may come back to an apt with people inside and your car towed. They are ripping up and completely remodeling apartments on all sides of us. Our pictures fall as the walls shake, constantly denied access to our front door by construction workers, and it's so loud you'll need the TV on full volume to hear anything. I wish someone would have warned me about this complex.

I lived there for a year, first few months were nice. Then, once we started having to talk to them a lot or confront them with a issue, they were either on their 3 hour lunch break, or no one to be found in general. Nice people at front desk, but a bit TOO care free for my living standards. Some people also living there are nice, but a lot are mean that act like they're better than everyone. Maintenance people were my favorite overall. The parking is absolutely ridiculous, even as a resident. My boyfriend and I couldn't wait to get out by the time our lease was up. Lots of bugs, lots of issues that last days. For the cost, which they raised, you're pretty much paying for the location. Only.

My husband and I have been living here for about a year now. We absolutely love the customer service here. The people that work in the front office are genuine and make you feel right at home. If there are any maintenance issues, the maintenance guys tend to it in a very timely manner, and are very respectful. It's located in a perfect place. There is a small shopping center next door that has everything from a laid back bar for relaxing and good restaurants with diverse palettes, to salons and dry cleaners for your convinience.  The grocery store isn't far. In fact there are 3 that takes less than 5 min to get to. Since you're in mission valley, it's a breeze traveling anywhere in San Diego. It's perfect for bouncing from home to chores and back. 

Physically, it is very humble, but realistic for the lower prices. We currently live in a one bedroom for 1351$ monthly and it is much larger than what most apartments offer. The apartments are well insulated, and noise has never been an issue. Central AC is wonderful in the summer. Laundry rooms are available on each floor and take a laundry card that can be reloaded. The gym that's included has very few and basic equipment, but it's nice to have a treadmill on location. There are two pools available, that are maintained regularly. There is a hot tub and sauna as well. The parking seems to be the biggest issue, as you are alloted one parking permit per unit and they tow regularly. It is helpful though to regulate those who frequent qualcomm stadium events. Street parking is available for first come, first serve. All in all, it's competitive and military friendly for someone with realisticly economic expections.

Great price for a good area! Apartments are nice, not amazing but nice. Area is kept clean, which is nice, but there are lots of bugs, which is normal... This is San Diego. A lot of partiers live here, so there is a lot of noise on the weekends. The staff here is nice, and they are quick to take care of issues. 2 of my biggest complaints would be they are always shutting the water off and working on it, and if you get home too late at night there usually aren't any spots near the building, and you have to park way in the back, but thats still not too bad. So, yeah, move here, unless you can afford something nicer.

I recently moved here and cant wait to leave. Pay attention to the parking. If you live near the front, you're screwed and end up parking at the end of the lot. Plus the spaces are so small that the car mirrors barely touch and you need to squeeze yoyrself out of the car. Walls were painted with strands of hair stuck to it. Issues that need to be fixed take over a week or aren't even addressed. I keep finding ants crawling all over the walls, kitchen counter and cabinets. 
Originally I was told water and trash are included. However I get a bill and I'm being charged for it and other fees.

We have been a resident at Villas of Rancho Bernardo going 8 years. We like the school district, and had no plans of moving out. Two small kids 4 years old and 10 years old. We have enjoyed our stay here till recently. All of a sudden we had two new neighbors moving in and both smokers: cigarettes and marijuana. Our life has become un-bearable. 
Neighbors are nice people but that does not help us. One Next door and one Below. Smoking starts at 5.30 am, when everybody enjoys fresh morning air we are breathing fresh smoked cigarettes. And then they smoke till 12 midnight. 
My 4 year old is severely allergic. We contacted our leasing office right away on September 5th, 2017. Manager said that he will talk to legal counsel and get back, no word. 
October 21st, 22nd, 23rd, we had a week over a 100F, we were sweating in our apartment. My daughter broke out in rash. On Wednesday, October 25th, 2017 I approached the Manager again and handed him a written request to find a way, because we cannot be expected to breath cigarette smoke in our own home. I told him we understand that we have 4 more month on the lease, but it even when we close doors and windows it comes through the AC because its right next to the neighbors patio. Manager asked us what did we want to do?-Transfer, or move? Transfer did not guarantee that there will be no smokers. So we said we will move. He said ok we will help you "Let me call legal and I will call you back tomorrow". So we start looking for a new place because it unbearable leaving in an apartment that you cannot air out. It takes a week for Manager to call back on  November 2nd, to say "Sorry its not against the law to smoke cigarettes and marijuana" so you cannot break the lease. "They can smoke as close to the building as they want, ITS LEGAL". I am not breaking the lease, I am asking to be able to live freely in my home that I am paying for. 
He says just close your windows and doors. I said it's coming through the AC: No it's not possible! Can't do nothing about that. 
Really!?

I just moved into these apartments a little over a week ago and I've never been so happy!  I have lived at several apartments over my lifetime and these far exceed most of them.  Upon looking at a model unit I was told i could have my apartment custom painted, any walls and color of my choice, the first wall free.  I have never been offered a custom paint job!  So of course my apartments was professionally painted prior to moving in.  In addition to this I got brand new carpet! They gave me the choice to have wood floors or carpet, I chose carpet (yes, I'm old school, lol). I've never been given a choice like that.  They gave us a new shower, bathtub, new toilets, new windows, new fridge, new kitchen cabinets, and possibly the granite countertops might be new. I'm not sure if some of these things were here before with the last tenants but it seems new. We got tile floors and beautiful granite countertops!  Most apartments care more about your money than providing you with nice things. My last apartment was a dump so to come here was a huge change. I got a poolside view apartment which is literally right there and i love looking through my new windows at night. My last apartment had old rotted windows full of mildew so I get excited about these windows lol.  They gave us a beautiful fairly new washer and dryer, full size!  The washer and dryer at my last place looked about 20 years old, and one finally stopped working right before we moved out. So to come here and get such a beautiful washer and dryer was a real treat!  This place is so grand looking as you enter with the tall well kept palm trees and landscaping. The tennis courts are lit up with people actually using it and an AMAZING gym.  It has a LOT of machines and even free weights. They provide clean white rolled up towels for us! They have a beautiful large gated dog park. This place is immaculate which surprises me because it's pet friendly. Upon moving in I was given a welcome bag filled with lots of popcorn, cookies, sodas, paper towels, toilet paper, water, and hot chocolate. Who does that!?  I could go on and on but my poor hand hurts lol. The office staff is FANTASTIC and the maintenance crew is friendly too. I LOVE it here!  A special shout out to all of you at the office and to the maintenance crew for making my experience so great!  A big hug to you all.  If I could give you ten stars I would. Your happy tenant, Steph!

We just recently renewed our rent here for the 3rd time. I've been very happy with our apartment. The granite countertops, in-unit washer and dryer, nice appliances (including dishwasher). We're downstairs and have gone through three sets of neighbors upstairs. No matter who was up there, only rarely do you hear them (vacuuming, loud music, etc.). Since we moved in, they fenced off an area for a small dog park, which has been awesome. We've never had any major maintenance issues, but even small issues (replace lightbulbs, laundry doors off the tracks) have been taken care of same day (usually within a couple hours). Plenty of guest parking.

The cons: Very small parking spaces. Management has messed up something with our lease at each renewal (although they eventually fix it). Back pool can get kind of dirty and cold (front pool is cleaner, but more crowded). Depending on where your unit is, you might get some freeway noise.

Overall, we've been happy here. No apartment is perfect, but this one has been fine for us. As long as you don't have to deal with management, there's little to complain about. Unless something dramatic changes, we'll be staying here until we need to move into something larger.

These people think it's ok to vandalize my property! They gave me 4 warnings to move my car in one day and got upset that I didn't call them that day. They put two stickers on my car that are non-removable and told me to remove it with a knife that they didn't care. I explained to them that I have moved the car and I would like them to remove the adhesive that was not being removed. I think for the top management to not care at all was weak and they should be more sensitive about what materials they use on your car. I also had issues with my balcony getting trashed after they clean the roofs. It's was horrible to clean up and wash my furniture. I just think they could do a better job of taking care of their current customers and not just prospects. That's all they care about not the people who actually live in the apartment complex.

Love the area, love my neighbors, not a fan of the staff.

They are not professional & refuse to take ownership of mistakes that were made. Basically, told us too bad so sad, without an apology.

Too bad, we really wanted to renew here.

This apartment complex is exceptional, with its well-maintained surroundings and top-notch amenities. The staff, from the office to the maintenance team, are amazing and always ready to assist. The apartment is a warm and inviting home in a vibrant and welcoming community. Special recognition goes to Diana for her wonderful activity organization, enhancing the sense of camaraderie. Living here has been an absolute pleasure, making it one of the best places I've ever lived in.

Pros:
Management team (leasing office)- every time that I have had to call the office, you all have been very helpful and completed whatever request or answered any question that I have had in a very timely and professional manner.
Maintenance team - very quick, safe, friendly, and efficient whenever I have required assistance.
Cleanliness - hallways, parking garage, and other community areas are always very clean. The exterior portion of the complex also appears to be very well taken care of.
Units - Very nice and modern. This would include the appliances, floors, cabinets, countertops, etc.
Security - Considering that the Mobil 1 gas station right across the street appears to be a breading ground for homeless people, drug addicts, etc, I have not seen any of that type of behavior within the complex. It feels very well isolated from the common by-product of homelessness that haunts almost every portion of San Diego.
Pet friendly - although I don’t have a dog, this would be a very easy complex to reside in if I did. Whoever thought of including a dog wash station deserves a pat on the back.

Cons:
Parking garage - The parking garage is an absolute nightmare, especially for people that reside on the higher floors. Going around 18 turns and 9 speed bumps to get to/from my parking spot everyday is a huge pain. While there is no legitimate solution to solve this, maybe an incentive for residents that live on higher floors could be discussed. Whoever designed that portion of the complex should not be designing any more parking garages. Something else that could be resolved would be having the gate open up automatically for cars exiting the parking garage. Not sure how this impacts security of the overall complex, but waiting to exit the parking garage when my girlfriend is borrowing the fob is an unnecessary hassle. The sad truth is that people wait on either side of the parking garage all the time for whatever reason, I know that I’m not the only one.
No card fobs available - The previous complex that I lived at had an option to purchase a card fob for 35$ and then returning it when your lease is up. Incase you are not aware, they did not open up the parking garage, only the doors. Management dropped the ball on this one. Huge pain for me and my girlfriend who was not on the lease for irrelevant reasons, and had to utilize street parking. Do parents whose children that are not on the lease get an extra fob? If not, watch out when that elementary school opens u

I've lived here for 2 years. Yes, it looks nice, it has a lot of amenities and yes, it is close to malls, restaurants and grocery stores but all of that means nothing next to the money you pay and the actual experience of living here:

- Most residents constantly break the rules that they agreed upon by signing the lease to rent: Being in the pool area after 10pm, smoking cigarettes, dogs without leashes, trash next to the trash shoot, dog poop in "no pets allowed" areas, to name a few.
- Residents obnoxiously mark up the whole complex with their overwhelming cologne smell and speed up in the neighborhood with no regards for pedestrians.
- Next door neighbors are disrespectful, I can't study, read a book, meditate nor sleep in without being disturbed by thumping noises and kids screaming, the walls are incredibly porous. 
- People love invading your reading space if you try to read a book somewhere outside in the complex (walking really close to your chair that your books gets brushed by every time.)
- You feel almost forced to be in your apartment because of the residents violating rules everywhere right in your face.
- Residents are incredibly inconsiderate about thumping noises, door slamming and loud echoing noises in the courtyard. They also let kids horseplay in the hallways and occasionally dogs running and playing fetch without leashes in the hallways inside.
- Hot water takes 10 to 20 min to come out early in the mornings or early evening, which is the times you need it the most.
- Pools and hot tubs are a nice feature, however, people make it gross by being occasionally obscene in the jacuzzi, letting kids play in it unsupervised and bringing dogs into the pool area (which they're not allowed), so I hardly use any of them.
- The leasing office does NOTHING to enforce the rules nor address complaints but they will charge a fee for something they noticed without giving the resident a notice.
- The security services never shows up about any issues I've reported.
- Daily fire alarms going off and every other month there is a power outage in the middle of the night.
- Residents put up un-allowed propaganda and tend to steal packages, break into cars inside of the "private parking garage" and vandalized the building itself by breaking glass doors and leaving trash bags in random places of the building.

From the outside it looks amazing, looks can be deceiving!!!! I could hear my upstairs neighbors conversations, my apartment smelt like pot, staff was super rude!!!! My favorite were multiple cars and motorcycles were stolden out of the parking garages. Security does nothing but walk around smoke and eat. Staff was super rude after receiving my keys. It is not as secure place at all cause most of the time the outside doors aren’t locked and homeless people come in. If you can live with all of that and the super loud fast and the furious drag shows that happen ever evening by all means enjoy your non peaceful home! 
Make sure you unit has cell phone signal, I had to go outside for an entire year to use my phone.

Ignore the ' perfect ' reviews, this apartment home has got to be one of the worst apartment homes in San Diego, despite their fine floor plans, their customer service is very obnoxious, their responses to their calls and emails are very inadequate. From a personal experience, I had a 16 hour flight back home, where I had to bring my bank statements to lease an apartment. However, I was surprised when I returned to see them being declined as they claimed it didn't include my full name, even though they didn't notify when I was back there. To sum up, I don't recommend such a place.

They will tow your car with minimal notice. I came to visit my friend who lives here. We went into the leasing office to get a guest parking pass. The guy inside said there was nobody available who could print us a pass and to come back in an hour. When I asked him what I was supposed to do since I had already been in the two hour parking spots for two hours and did not want to get a ticket, his reply was "well we aren't responsible if you get a ticket". So with that helpful information, my friend decided we would park my car on the roof where the guest parking is and leave a note explaining what happened. 1.5 hours later, we notice a missed phone call and text on my friends phone from security. We immediately go to check the car and it is gone. Towed. In one and a half hours the car was gone!!!! $370 to get my car back, bc I had to leave it overnight at the tow place since even if we picked it up,THERE WAS NO PLACE FOR ME TO PARK IT. By that time the leasing office was closed and I did not want to run the risk of them towing it once again. Live somewhere else. Or only live here if you don't plan on ever having visitors.

I put a $150 deposit down to reserve an apartment and was led to believe everything was good and had everything switched over to the new address (what Travis told me to do) and then just out of the blue 3 days before I got to see my new apartment they denied me for something unreasonable and kept my $150!! I'm glad tho. That place is garbage now that I have seen other apartments! Do yourself a favor and avoid this dump.

Management at this place is extremely disrespectful and avoidant. They do not care about accommodation when it comes to the residents who live here and they don’t even work out of the office at pinnacle. They’re rarely available and trying to schedule an appointment is difficult as if they only make time for future residents. In BOTH spire and pinnacle there are so many water issues, elevator issues, garage gate issues and also parking fees are $180+ at the moment AND INCREASES yearly. People are constantly in and out of living here and I don’t blame them IM NEXT!

We've lived here for 12 months and the entire time have been waiting to leave. Every day the elevators are broken, everyday you will step in dog pee or at the very least be kept up all night because of dogs barking in the park. Every weekend the screams from the pool echo through the buildings. There are absolutely no rules when it comes to the common spaces- toddlers run around the gym, men workout without shoes on, it's hell.

The amount of packages we've had lost from Amazon, UPS, and USPS is staggering. Right now we've launched an investigation with USPS for an international package that somehow made it to Pinnacle (and was scanned in by USPS) but never made it to our mailbox. This happens pretty frequently and luckily we always get refunded by the sender- but WHERE do the packages go? The front desk staff is a constant rotation of temps, so your guess is as good as mine.

This place is far too overpriced for what it is- you WILL have your packages stolen, you WILL step in dog poo in an elevator, and you WILL be harassed by homeless people the second you leave the front door. Oh! Also, pretty much all the time there is random trash scattered around hallways, etc. So get used to that!
The management is horrendous. Constantly waiting 10+ minutes on elevators and complex is always covered in trash and dog urine. This complex is more of a headache than a place to live.

Save your time and don’t even bother living here. Although the two months free is great up front don’t let it fool you. Property is horribly managed from management to the amenities. The garage doors and elevators go down numerous times a month, management takes forever to get back to you regardless of urgency, front desk staff is horrible. And the cherry on top is I got my own car towed out of my parking spot. Definitely the worst peppery I’ve ever stayed at

Update—————
Things are getting worse day by day. Management doesn't give a rats back on what's happening in the building. People are attacked by homeless in the parking lot. They've increased parking to a whopping $180 per month. Car's are broken into on a daily basis. Motorcycles are stolen from the "secured" garage, storage lockers are broken into. Do your self a favor and find another place to live. DONT PUT YOUR LIFE AT RISK.
Worst customer service. The front desk staff is rude, acts pricey and ignorant. It's impossible to get a ahold of the leasing agent if you're in problem. The maintenance service is super slow and annoying. Had a broken bathroom, took them 15 days to respond. They don't attend to your request for weeks even if it's an emergency. The security here is a JOKE, anyone can walk in get to any floor.
Don't believe these 5 star reviews, they all have been bought, none of them live here. Living here is worst than a motel. It's no where close to a 'luxury apartment'.
Do yourself a favor and rent somewhere else.

The community is great! Slick, urban design. Location by Little Italy, Old Town, and minutes away from downtown. The modern architecture on this building is unmatched. Where else can you find Lofts like these in the city.  Dog friendly community!

First off, the actual location is unbeatable for the price of rent. However, the area around the building is not so great. It's sort of cut off from the neighborhoods around it (old town, mission hills, little italy) The units themselves are very modern and well built, with the exception of the lower level units which lack windows. The bedrooms do have doors rather then windows but lack door screens so good luck leaving the door open for more than 5 minutes without finding a spider or a lizard inside the apartment afterwards. The noise from the neighbors upstairs is not so much a problem unless they stomp on the ground or stairs. The back area which is basically a shared backyard is great if you have dogs, not so much for hanging out or relaxing due to the loud train noise every couple of minutes. Oh yeah going back to the area, i forgot to mention the train tracks which run right behind the building. Parking is great since there is plenty of space and a parking space comes with each unit. also storage units are avaliable inside the garage. So overall if you are looking for a modern well sized apartment in a great location and look past the area and the lack of windows and train noise, this place is perfect for you.
The building, the staff, the community of people, the security, everything here at ALX is the best!

What a magnificent and fastidiously well-maintained property!
Great vibe and is, in close walking proximity, to all the best that downtown San Diego offers!

I was looking for an apartment on a very short notice and inquired about ALX online. Shelby reached out and was super helpful in scheduling a tour of the building the same day and was extremely knowledgeable about everything. She helped me have a quick and easy move in and I’ve been enjoying living here ever since. It’s clean and well taken care of and it’s conveniently located close to where I work and the excitement of downtown is in my backyard.

Just moved in and the leasing experience was extremely smooth. Shelby and Kaii were super helpful and timely when responding to inquiries. The building is in great shape, the gym is solid and the people are friendly. Overall a really positive experience.
ALX is a great community. Well managed, stocked with great residents and friendly staff.

Beautiful building with friendly management, great location with easy access to the harbor walk. If only they could prevent loud parties in the middle of the night, and keep the elevator fresh thought the weekend.

Went to view the apartment, however  the  unit we would be  moving into was not available to be seen for another few months. The property was asking for $1400 non-refundable holding deposit, which doesn't guarantee you will like the unit you move into or that  it will look the same as the one you viewed. This $1400 holding fee doesn't even include your security deposit or application fee you will have to pay at the time of renting.

Don’t even bother, I called made an appointment and when I arrived the apartments looked amazing. However, I was devastated that I couldn’t even look at them! Nobody was there and no one answered the phone the 6 times I called throughout the day. Terribly sad, I was the most excited about these apartments in my search.

I’ve lived here on and off for 15 years and owned property nearby. I find the staff extremely helpful and the maintenance staff are angels and fix things quickly. The apartments are beautiful and well-maintained and it’s a quiet place to live. I wouldn’t live anywhere else.
Made an appointment to tour. When I arrived not one answered the phone and the doors were locked.

It looks nice, and the property is appealing. However, the staff and experience make me regret ever moving here. It doesn't feel like a home. They never let you forget that you don't own your space. Susan is the most condescending person I've ever encountered with the most fake facade. 

Just save yourself the horrid experience. SD has so many wonderful properties. Don't move here.

I scheduled a move out inspection which they did not show up to. They admitted this was a mistake. Then after move out I was billed $1,250, for damage that was not there. I filed a dispute and was in contact for 8 months. They would say they would respond in a few days and the next thing I’d hear was a debt collection notice a month later. They eventually took off $600 of fees since they realized it was already damaged as noted in my move in form and there was no evidence. I am still not happy with the bill I had to pay.

They respond to work orders quickly and have very nice amenities.

The only benefit of this apartment complex is its proximity to campus.  Otherwise, it is awful.  The apartments are infested with ants.  Other bugs come in through the vents.  It is noisy and the amenities constantly break down.  While living there, my storage unit was burglarized, and the complex disclaimed any responsibility and did not even notify the policy of the crime.  I have heard of other residents having disputes and suing the company that owns the complex repeatedly.  And don't expect any help from the staff -- they are remote and incompetent.

We had the BEST experience with Alexis!  She went above and beyond to be very accommodating, helpful and kind!  The property is gorgeous with grounds immaculate and very well appointed.  Our unit was spotless at move in and everything is kept so clean and beautiful!  Thank you!!

PLEASE READ!!  I do not normally write reviews, but this review is well deserved. My brother lived at Pacific Ridge for several years while in Law School and every time I would visit him, I felt like I was at a beautiful resort. The complex is extremely clean, the people that I encountered who lived there were very nice and the amenities are stunning. I have always thought about living at Pacific Ridge but wanted to do my fair share of research before applying to Pacific Ridge. I looked at over 20 different apartments online and somehow, I always found myself ending up on the Pacific Ridge Website. The location of Pacific Ridge is prime, safe and the complex has everything I desire when calling a place home, especially an amazing pool and jacuzzi. Through my research of different apartments, Pacific Ridge by far had the best amenities, the most spacious apartments for the price and most importantly, I noticed through my research that Pacific Ridge has a security gate which made me feel even more comfortable with wanting to apply. Finally, after being tired of not finding an apartment that fits all my needs like Pacific Ridge does, I decided to reach out. I took a tour with a lady by the name of Alexis who showed me the entire complex and let me be the first to tell you that when you tour Pacific Ridge in person, you are going to fall in love!!
When you walk into these apartments, you will immediately notice that they are clean, very spacious, includes a washer and dryer and the appliances are all updated!!  Alexis went above and beyond by showing me several units and honestly, I could live in any of them because each of them were unique and each one had everything, I was looking for in making this new apartment my home. 

Before I started the application process, I had so many questions and Alexis replied to every single question in no time. I could tell that they cared about their residence which is a big plus for me when applying to a new apartment complex. Having a good and responsive management team is key in keeping your residence happy and satisfied. Alexis, thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the time you have spent in answering my questions so that I be satisfied and comfortable with my decision in applying to Pacific Ridge.

Finally, I applied and was guided through the entire application process. Once I was approved, I was informed of how to efficiently start the moving-in process! Thank you for all your help Nicole and Alexis!

I have been very impressed at the professionalism of the leasing office- with special mention to Nicole Liverpool! She has been very helpful from start to finish. I must have emailed her a ton, and each time she has responded on a timely basis and provided us with straightforward answers. She made the whole leasing process seamless.
 Thank you very much. My daughter is looking forward to her second year staying at Pacific Ridge!

We just recently moved in and at first we noticed some minor things that needing fixing. After being in the unit for a day or so, we realized our young children could get out of the front door very easily - even when we "locked" the door. My husband went down to the office to ask that they add an additional lock chain on the door for the safety of our children. Nicole understood the urgency needed to get this fixed ASAP, submitted the service request on our behalf and ensured the maintenance team got it taken care of immediately. Thank you Nicole and Rick for taking care of everything so quickly!

No apartment complex compares to Pacific Ridge Apartments in terms of style, design and exclusivity. 
While there are many college students who live here and live as college students do. I have not had issues with noise or behavior. 
This is my second time living here, I have been at both ends of this complex and both have stunning views, exciting open floor plans and ease of access to amenities. 
Thank you Pacific Ridge staff for being on top of all of my concerns and issues. I look forward to another wonderful stay.

Best apartment complex in San Diego! I lived at Pacific Ridge for 5 years, then moved to PB. After 6 months, I had to come back to Pacific Ridge! There is no place as luxurious, convenient, and loaded with amenities including A/C, in-unit laundry, garage parking, great security, gym, snack room, pools, etc.. for such a reasonable price! The staff is great, maintenance is quick and efficient, and it is an overall great living experience!
Awesome facilities and management is very helpful. Minor issues with the apartment which maintenance fixed within the same day. Great for students because of prime location. Highly recommend!

From the beginning the leasing staff, specifically Nicole, was so incredibly helpful in all aspects regarding my prospective apartment. Nicole was very prompt and helped me troubleshoot any problem I had in a timely and efficient manner. The move in process was extremely easy and it was lovely to talk to such a nice leasing office who clearly put a lot of passion and hard work into Pacific Ridge and its residents. Highly recommend Pacific Ridge! They make you feel right at home! And the sunset views can’t be beat!

I am about to sign my second lease at Pacific Ridge. I have really enjoyed living here. As a young woman, I always feel safe and protected. The amenities are amazing and so well kept. I highly recommend it. Nicole is also very helpful and always answers my questions!

I am not one to write reviews as I feel that my own opinion is what matters most.  Choosing to live here was based on reviewing websites as our home is in Hawaii.  This apartment was for my son who was attending USD.  The location was the closest (across the street) that I could find.  The underground parking assured me that my son was secure in entering and leaving his vehicle.  The security guard entrance gave me comfort with this additional effort in keeping the complex/grounds secure.  Any issues that the apartment needed were promptly and professionally taken care of.  I liked that he had the gym and pools and were just steps away from his front door.  There were so many other amenities that I thought were great but he did not take the time to use them so I cannot comment on everything.  Security was very strict on the 10pm quiet time.  Trust me!  I received calls the next day that my son's apartment violated this curfew!  Mountains for the winter sports, beaches for the sunny days, and numerous hiking places convinced my son that he wants to stay in San Diego. Overall as a parent who wants the best for their child, knowing that they are close to school, safe, having amenities right there for them to use, and most of all he had many friends from campus that also lived there so much of his social and study life were all at USD & Pacific Ridge :)

From the very moment we drove onto this property we felt right at home... The Security staff were very polite and professional in directing us to the parking space and Leasing Office. The Leasing Office staff were courteous and answered all our questions and gave us a tour of the property right away!

We didn't even have to think about it... We signed the lease agreement the next day and moved into our apartment that weekend!

The place is clean, and kept that way by the housekeeping staff. Any maintenance issues are quickly resolved by the on property uniformed maintenance personnel.

The luxurious amenities are fantastic... Gym, Pools, Coffee, Conference and Game rooms, are all tastefully decorated and furnished with the upmost comfort to the residents in mind.

Once you see this place first hand, you'll want to call it home, too!

I love this apartment,very good and helpful leasing office employees,very good security guards,every time i go to p2 to park my car,i see them that check every where,any time i needed to fix something in my unite ,handy mans coming on time and they do their job perfect,i love coffee room and swimming pool,very lauxury and the bbq area is super clean,i never seen bbq be dirty.their apps helps alot to pay rent very easily and order handy man or getting parking permit.i love you guys.
The property is beautiful and the staff are extremely kind and willing to help you with anything you need. It is very accessible and well managed and taken care of. It truly feels like a second home.

This place screws over its residence. They make the decor and outside look super nice but little do they know that the little things are cheap. Elevators suck, hot tubs never work, walls are thin, college students are everywhere. Then they screw you over with your security deposit when nothing is broken. Make sure to read the fine print because they charge you to repaint when the walls aren't marked at all.

This apartment complex looks really nice from the outside, however, the entire infrastructure is cheap. One elevator per building and on top of that they break every other week and are the slowest elevators I have ever seen. I would normally just use the stairs but they even messed up the stair locations. Also, terrible sound proofing and customer service.

Absolutely loved this complex but it's fairly expensive. I would keep staying here if the rent doesn't raise. But it most certainly a dream complex straight out of a magazine. Just going to the pool makes you feel like royalty. I have lived at a bunch of complexes, I have never lived at one amazing as this!

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review:
The living experience here is terrible…don’t live here if it’s possible. 

We’ve only been here for about 5 months but we’ve already lost more than 10 packages…the package system has big problem, my package can be put anywhere , always hard to find it, and  always being stolen. 

The EV charging fee is ridiculous too. Charging the car from 20 to 100% needs more than $20 for only energy fee, even more expensive than public chargers. 

The valet garbage service is useless, but we have to pay for it. Usually, there are many conditions to collect the garbage. It is much more convenient to throw away the garbage by myself.

They always building something unnecessary to upgrade the rent, but they don't consider what the residents really need.

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review: It is truly impressive how bad this place got with the new management that it should be studied.

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review: Forcing us to pay for trash service without an opt out yet the trash is missed at least once a week. No free community events anymore. Used to have free kombucha on the 3rd floor but now it costs. Parking used to be included for the first car and now has a monthly cost with the second car price going up too. Parking around the complex used to be free for visitors and again is now paid for at a rate of $4 an hour. Then we received an email that “management heard our feedback” and said in an effort to free up spots they will just tow cars who don’t pay. That is ridiculous considering the parking wasn’t full from paid visitors because no one wanted to pay to park there. It just seems like greystar nickel and dimes you for every little thing and residents are absolutely unhappy about it.

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review: Lack of interest from greystar to resolve resident maintenance issues . Worse place to live

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review: Friendly people, safe place, all the bells and whistles of amenities. There isn't anything not to like.

apartmentName: The Vive on the Park at The Vive Collection
review: I loved living at Vive. The location is as central as it gets in San Diego. The amenities are great and the staff is amazing!

apartmentName: Casa Aldea at University City Village
review:
I have just renewed my lease after being at Casa Aldea for a year.  I can promise you, I am as picky as they come and I cannot find a single thing to complain about!
The leasing agent (Marcia) The activities director (Kelly) and the entire staff for maintenance is amazing.  I love my unit so much, but I was worried being in SD that the lease rate would go way up.  It went up some, but didn't everything?  I have the perfect, private unit and my neighbors are gracious and so quiet.  I still work full-time, so I am not able to do all the activities, but they have so many and look like fun!  Someday!  There is always a wait list to get into Casa Aldea, and I know why.  It is perfect!!!  Shawn

apartmentName: Casa Aldea at University City Village
review: Casa Aldea University City is the best move my parents could have made! They couldn’t be happier. After enduring subpar living, care & staff at 2 previous facilities (1 independent living & 1 assisted living), they decided a 3rd move was eminent. Casa Aldea UC has exceeded their and my expectations! Clean, spacious, apts with huge accessible bathrooms. Compassionate and caring staff who ensure your needs are met promptly. Always greet you with a smile and time for a conversation. The grounds for a leisurely walk are beautifully landscaped. I couldn’t be happier for my parents. Knowing they’re safe, content and in good hands take a load of worry off of me. Casa Aldea is #1 for senior living. Have a look for yourself...you’ll agree.

Stay away from this apartment complex! There is ongoing constructions so it's very noisy and wakes you up at 7am in the morning every day. And there is very limited parking space. The office doesn't provide enough parking for the residents and we had to park on the street of which they said it was ok, but then suddenly one day my car was towed away. I had to pay a lot to get my car back, and the office is not doing anything to resolve this issue to our satisfaction. I'm very disappointed with their customer service and management office. Worst experience ever. I'm sharing my experience here so hopefully you don't have to deal with this awful place
Square footage and garage parking are nice. Management is busy, however will always address the issues.
Overrall great location and great spacious apartments. A few hiccups here and there but now settling in nicely.
A BEAUTIFUL COMMUNITY!!! Very well maintained, convenient, and the staff and residents are all very friendly.

I’ve lived here for over a year and Do Not recommend it. 

In fairness, let me share the pros : the layouts utilize the space very well with natural lighting, high ceilings, balconies, washer/dryers and garages. 

So why have I given the property a low rating? 

I have come to learn that this may be a tax scam and the ownership deceitful. They are taking in higher rents than warranted for a concept that is more smoke and mirrors than truth.  

With new leases, they are no longer including electricity, rents are being raised during economic uncertainty (at the time of writing this, the world is gripped with corona virus anxiety), no pool or community center is forthcoming. 

The tenants I have spoken with are furious and many of us want to move out rather than renew our leases. Would I recommend this place? Not anymore - it’s renter beware at this time and that makes me sad.

Would not recommend this property to friends , family nor peers . Definitely a nice property with visually pleasing perks . But the leasing is very misleading . They never answer the phone and not up front with information

I recently moved to the Townsend and have been very happy living here thus far.

Management was genuinely cordial and accommodating throughout the leasing process. The apartment complex itself exudes classiness with the newest amenities and modern apartment features. Parking is easy with a 5-story garage down the hall, and the building feels quite secure with the courtesy patrol and access control system.

It is true that the Townsend (along with neighboring apartment complexes) are located next to the 8 and 163 freeways. However, I can barely hear the noise through the soundproof windows. And, the upside of living next to the freeways is being centrally located, with all of San Diego within reach.

You want to pay huuuge rent and live next to the pollution and noise of the 8 fwy? Go right ahead. We who have lived here for a long time are laughing at you.... and this building has the car park in the middle so yeah... you'll hear the cars coming and going. NO THANKS
Been paying rent for 4 months now. AC has NEVER worked. It's 80 degrees every day. Management does nothing to help

I am moving from Northern California to San Diego and Marissa helped me every step of the way! She made my lease signing and move planning such an easy process. This experience has made me so excited to live at the Simone and start off my new life in San Diego on a good note. Thank you, Marissa!
dreamy and one of a kind. Not just an apartment building but a place for gathering and meeting new people.

I have been living here for a few months now and I have to say I'm so glad I rented here. My one-bedroom apartment is so modern and updated. The amenities are gorgeous, and the community seems really friendly. Although there have been minor issues here and there, it is to be expected when living in an apartment complex as opposed to a home. Overall, I am so proud to have company over and to be in this community! The maintenance staff is so helpful and friendly, and the office staff are so pleasant. A huge thank you to Rafael, the assistant manager for helping me through the process of renting and moving in, he was just a genuinely cool and smooth guy. A great welcome.

It's a really good idea that's been horribly executed. Construction was rushed, promised amenities were not completed and others  have yet to be delivered.  Security is non-existant (see other reviews) and management would rather save face and virtue signal than take any meaningful action on issues. If a break-in and  double homicide in a common area can't drive any change, I don't know what will.

Seriously,  LOOK ELSEWHERE for student housing.

I have had my fair share of apartments since 2018. This is by far the absolute worst apartment complex I have ever lived in. Whether it be no coffee in the coffee machine or dead bodies in the staircases. There is no limit to what Union Grantville and it’s poor security team, Security first company, will do to disappoint it’s residents and compromise the safety of said residents, who might I add are just 18 years old. 
What I expect from a property that I am renting from, is secure entrance in and out of the building, and the feeling of safety when I come home. Union Grantville Apartments goes above and beyond to avoid providing any stability and safety for their residents, despite MULTIPLE comments and complaints from this living here. 
I sincerely URGE you to NOT let your children rent here nor advertise it to ANYONE you know. Stay FAR AWAY from Union Grantville and ANY greystar owned properties!!!
Do not live here. You will never feel safe as there is always homeless or more recently, a DOUBLE HOMICIDE in the building. Find another place to live.
I would not recommend this place, they totally ignore everything you put in your application. It is also very challenging to get out of your lease even though they have violated the lease agreement
The staff at the leasing office is amazing! Came in to visit 2 months ago with my daughter and she is so excited to move in!

the team was amazing and i’m super excited to live there. The staff helped me with the process of filling out my application and found me the best apartment for a reasonable price. I wanna shout out Lisa for helping me find a place for next semester.

We move a lot and I've never really liked living in complexes because of the noisiness/dirtiness/usually unresponsive management... but my partner was in love with the unit and I gave in. The manager, who is new herself to the building, has been wonderful -- understanding / attentive / responsive -- just a total rock star. We came along right before she came on board and I've seen a huge transition in the attention to detail for its residents. Anytime something breaks both in the common spaces and my apartment, its addressed and repaired promptly. Excellent communication, quiet neighborhood (apart from a few screamers on occasion but thats Hillcrest for you), a hiking trail nearby, and just a general sense of community and friendliness here. I think we will be here a while!

This building is filled with problems. I have lived here for 6 months and there hasn't been a month where there hasn't been problems. 

There is a broken fire alarm system that goes off in the middle of the night. It happens so often that people have stopped going out and the fire department has stopped responding. It's a tragedy waiting to happen. 

At Christmas, the hot water tank broke and it took nearly a week for it be fixed. The only solution for tenants was to take ice cold showers or boil water. 

And on top of the constant maintenance issues, the building is noisy. There's construction behind the building that starts weekdays at 7am. In my case, the apartment above my unit hosts parties nightly that often go until 5am. Management is aware of this and has not responded to complaints or done anything to address it except to tell me to deal with it myself and call the police. 

The units might be updated and look nice, but there are a ton of issues behind the scenes that will come up soon as you move in. If you choose to live here, don't expect ConAm to help in any way. Once you've signed a lease, they have no interest in helping you.

This apartment is TOO EXPENSIVE for what it's worth! There's really no "amenities" here. The jacuzzi is super old and very small. The gym is tiny like only 2 people can work out there together comfortably! A gym at a Holiday Inn hotel would be so much nicer than the gym at this apartment. The apartment manager, Ericka, is HORRIBLE! She looks like she hates her job so much and she's very defensive at everything and not approachable at all! 

More importantly, the elevator in this building breaks almost every week! So one could only imagine that taking ALL the groceries up by stairs is horrible! 

Last thing, there was a burglary in this building where at least five cars got broken into in the garage that happened September 2019.

I love everything about this apartment and neighborhood. The 1-bedroom apartment I have is well appointed; I can't believe that I actually have a fireplace and my own washer/dryer in the apartment! I love the flooring and carpeting, as well as the marble countertops. The balcony gives me a treetop view of the sunset...it's like being on vacation! The neighbors are friendly and I love that so many have sweet little dogs; I love the convenience of the garbage shoots and the recycle on my floor; I love having a 24/7 exercise room with modern equipment; I love being able to soak in the hot tub; I love having my own parking spot in the covered, access controlled garage and then being able to take the elevator up to my floor; and I love the property manager, Desiraye as well as Mr. Arturo, the full time maintenance man. I can't believe how helpful they are in making me feel like this really is HOME!

And the neighborhood is amazing...peaceful, quiet, well-maintained single family homes and apartment/condo homes. It seems as safe to be walking at night as during the day...we are a couple blocks from all of the fun (and yummy) businesses and restaurants in Hillcrest and Mission Hills (Washington and University streets). Sunday mornings, it's a straight shot (12 minutes) down 4th Street to the Gaslamp, where the parking is free and it's not so crowded. Life is good at Montecito Point!

No one ever answers the phone...if they are ever in the office at all. 

New mgmt taking over has obliterated all hope for current and prospective residence to reach anyone there.

Wow I can  not believe the cost of rent it's amazing especially in California let alone san dieho, I love Hillcrest  area  very posh and live scene  type of style  thank you ....
Mandi Kamyli Itani
The young man who showed us around was easy to talk to and made us feel comfortable the entire time while going through the entire lease agreement!

We recently move Cresta Bella luxury community and we are so happy with this magnificent place. We had find everything that we need around here. Excellent schools near to us and best qualify in California State. We are so close 15 Highway and we can move any place north to south. landscaping is great and long green areas and all time is well maintained. We can enjoy with my child and wife all common community areas as Club House, salt pool, Gym, court, kids area, etc.
If you want live as your dreams, come here, my family is fascinated.
Just live it.

great quiet location. Parking is close to unit can be hard sometimes. Management is very helpful. Candace especially has been helpful. I really enjoy living here and I have enjoyed the 2 bed layout and single bedroom layout.

Cresta Bella is amazing. I searched apartments before I moved back to the states that was beautiful and in a safe neighborhood. Cresta Bella offers everything I needed with a friendly staff. Everything I need is a walk away, shopping, theater, restaurants, and great school. I couldn't ask for more.

Cresta Bella luxury apartments is convienlently located next to a major highway-the I15. From here you can easily commute to work within minutes of downtown and access top-notch schools within the area as well. These apartments are reasonably priced for the gorgeous area of Carmel mountain. There are many styles to choose from that will fit your needs and each unit offers central A/C, gas stove and dryer, ceiling fans, new appliances and even hardwood flooring. The units offer garages as well. Electricity, gas, and water is cheap and the maintenance service is very good as well. The complex offers a pool, gym, tennis court, grill area and social area as well as pet friendly. The staff are very knowledgable with any needs you may encounter and friendly to boot!  One of the only downsides, if this bothers you, is noise from neighbors which is typical of multi-unit sharing.  Come see what the beautiful Creat Bella can offer you and your family!!
Everytime you shower brown water drips all down your walls and your studio is suddenly damp! Roaches everywhere. Trust me don’t rent here.
They do not respect their tenants. Anytime you ask the leasing office for help the staff acts dismissive towards you.
The community is clean, modern, and has friendly office employees that are easy to get ahold of.
I really love the location. Right near Petco and tons of restaurants and bars nearby as well. The staff is really great even when they hire new folks.
pretty good price considering the location and amenities.
Location is nearby all major attractions in downtown SD. Amenities are also great!

I lived here for 6 years, and while I had a great experience for the first 4 years, the new management and owner are horrible. Since Greystar has taken over, they've increased rent on tenants every year, added additional charges on top of your rent that used to be free (such as parking and storage), and then on top of that, they withheld my security deposit after move out and made false claims of damages to my apartment to try and withhold it. If you look at other reviews, other tenants say the same thing.

The building responds to these messages saying that they care and they take the feedback to heart, but the reality is they don't care at all. They try to nickel and dime you for everything and you should think twice before renting here.
1810 feels like a small community in the heart of Little Italy. It's really a hidden gem with everything walking distance. No noise at all and very relaxing to live.

I moved out of 1810 State St. for three reasons: Increased homeless population, significant increases in rent and utilities by Greystar, and the new Greystar property management staff. Also, Greystar did not return my security deposit within the legal timeframe which is 21 days. Do not rent here because you will regret it. The new Greystar property manager does not communicate with residents and does not resolve issues.
The staff at 1810 are excellent. It's a wonderful place to live in the Little Italy area.

After looking at dozens of places in little Italy, Eighteen Ten was by far the best choice! Great location, wonderfully designed units with large windows that block out sound, under crowded roof top and lounge, and hands down the best staff. Jarret is the man.
Walking distance to the best restaurants and coffee in San Diego! I feel safe going home and parking every night. I appreciate the community of management team and residents.

I lived here for 18 months and found more than 30 issues. Each of them would be enough to have a count down for my lease to end. 
The biggest issue with this place is that it seems the place, facility, staffs etc. were designed for a much smaller community. Maybe for 100 units instead of 900. 
Here I will only talk about two main deal breaker issues:
1. The parking: The parking has 2 gates. More than 95% of the times the gates were broken. The parking had no security camera and there was barely any security guard there. Besides, East village is one of the sketchiest neighborhoods in SD.  All these make the massive 5 level parking the heaven of thieves and hobos. I was lucky that only my bike got stolen in the parking. I witnessed over 20 robberies, especially from storage units. I asked many times why at least they don't add camera to the parking and as usual they did not care. 
2. Elevators: In my 18 months of residency, I think there were less than 10 days that all elevators worked. There were 4 elevators, usually one or two of them broken and one reserved for move. So there was only one or two elevators for 50 levels. On average it took me 10-15 minutes to catch the elevator. Many times it took much longer. One time I missed my flight because of the elevator. Also because of poor parking design, you should add another 5-7 minutes of drive from your car to street. So on average I should have included an extra 20-25 minutes to all my drives. And this was for the times that I was lucky!
Because they are significantly understaff, you barely will receive reasonable responses from the staffs. The best that you can get is: "talk to the management". And the management never respond. 
I would say this place is only suitable for people who are extremely obsessed with the view. Other than that I don't see any value. And you should keep in mind that only around 30% of the units have good view. You should do your own research and pick the units with good location. In most cases they do not show you the actual unit, so it can be misleading. Also, in my 18 month of residency, they never cleaned the windows. So your nice view is going to be compromised with the filthy window. 
The only positive experience that I had was during the move out process. The procedure was surprisingly smooth and relatively fair.

This place is awful, don’t let the makeup on the pig fool you it’s still a pig. The management team is terrible. They took away the elevator for the floors up to the fifth floor. You can never get ahold of management if you have a question or concern. If an appliance breaks good luck you won’t be getting it fixed. Actually anything in general will not be fixed. I moved in and my found my window was broken and wouldn’t close, 4 months later it’s still broken and won’t close.

Broadway Towers is run by Spire.  
They will swipe your card and take the hold out for an apartment, but they won’t return it to your card if your not approved or denied. THEY mail it in like a month.  It’s been 4 months now and no check. accounting  department at spire insisted they mailed the check (regular mail) and because i never received it.  Not their fault. So they want to charge me $35 to stop payment on a check i doubt they ever mailed. 
Spire tell people who put deposits down, they will be mailed ou, MAYBE in a few months and if you don’t get the check, they will be charged to issue a new one. 
ANY place who does business like this is not worth moving into.  Imagine they can’t figure out how to return money to your card. ONLy take it. 
Spire needs the $250 this bad, SO cheap.

First off, our apartment was gorgeous and the views are spectacular. However, the appliances break easily and are poorly installed. Management is unresponsive at best, and denies you access to amenities or spends over half of your security deposit to "paint the bathroom ceilings" at their worst. While CA had difficult restrictions for everyone, Pinnacle International really went out of their way to make sure home felt as much like jail as possible. Despite employing a small army of security guards, they still did not manage to stop any of the three robberies we were victims of. Please do not live here. They do not care about you as soon as you sign your lease.

The leasing agents and door people are great, but the management is awful, especially Chad, who rudely walked away from me when I bought him trash from inside the pool today. The parking levels are dirty and unsafe. The police is onsite regularly. I have opened service requests and nobody has showed up or contacted me to get them resolved. Mask wearing is not enforced, not even in the elevators. The pool is always filthy, I'm not sure it's safe to swim in it.

My wife and I moved in a year ago when the building was brand new and since then our experience has been great, staff is accessible and super friendly! There's 24 hours of security and concierge to make your experience even better. Now the views you get! Nothing can beat the view from Spire looking towards harbor drive and coronado bridge! The city of SD is all under you to watch its beauty at every hour that changes! Sunsets are breathtaking and I would def recommend people to move in here

Lived here 2 years and hands down the worst management I’ve ever experienced. 

Unacceptably slow to respond to emails, if at all, no communication regarding broken elevators which are a frequent problem. Stolen packages happened twice within a year due to no package lockers just open shelving, and management refuses to do anything to remedy the situation. No amenities other than a rooftop deck that has been neglected and has a fire pit that works half of the time. With all of that said, rent was raised $300 our first year and $100 our second. Better managed buildings with more amenities and cheaper rents in the area. Don’t recommend.
Perfect location. The facilities are great. did not have any complains for the 1 year I lived there.

I have been a resident at this building for over 8 months and have been very satisfied with the building's management. The apartment is really nice, with wonderful views of San Diego, and the area is also very convenient because of its easy connection to all major freeways so I can get to many areas in San Diego relatively quickly. The area has a lot of nearby local services and shops to visit when my roommate and I need something. Balboa Park is nearby and can always enjoy that on nice days.

Management is attentive and responsive and the buildings location is very convenient for us.

Well designed and well constructed with minimal transmission of noise between apartments likely because of the glass, concrete and steel construction.  My apartment #603 was one of the best places I have ever lived, with views south to Tijuana and daily sunsets to the west--2 walls of glass with a balcony open on 2 sides.  Easy walking distance to Sprout's, all the University Heights and Hillcrest nightlife and restaurants....The manager Yeshi is warm and responsive and lives onsite.  Good management and the building has high standards for cleanliness and repair.

Had to give a review to this place. I am a new resident been here about 2 months now. I love this building! It's beautiful,new, its modern and everything works! They have a gated garage and everywhere you go you need your key fob (helps to deter break-ins)to get into the building and the garage. The on-site manager is very nice, easy to work with and always wants to help. This place is also dog friendly which is a plus. 

Your walking distance to Sprouts Groceries.

I give this place 5 stars.

Gracie has made our move in experience absolutely wonderful. She is incredibly thorough, kind and responsive. Our initial tour was smooth and she went over EVERYTHING. All 101 of my questions. 
Gracie, the property, the location, the floor plan and finishes of the units made our decision easy to start the application process. We did a cross country move from Jacksonville FL so being able to do everything remotely and still have top notch customer service/communication from Gracie meant so much. They are a gated community, they are pet friendly, everything is near by (and I mean everything), so far the few residents I have encountered with are extremely nice. I truly love being able to access the parking garage from each floor level which makes heading home after a long day easy. I love that the parking garage is above ground so you don’t lose cell service. Placing work orders is easy through the resident portal and Todd came same day to change our light bulb. Very great level of customer service! Great job Greystar, you have a great team running Vora. We are happy to be here for 15 months!

I would recommend this apartment community because its at a reasonable price point compared to other comparable communities in the area. The staff members I have interacted with were all pleasant and the community overall seems like a great place for peace and solace after the hustle and bustle of work.
I would recommend it because it?s a clean community with responsive staff.
I was looking for my sister and it was to small. I answered questions as if i was going to be renter.. Brian did a great job of showing us around.
Too expensive, smells like marijuana all the time, loud parties even into the night past quiet hours.

I stayed in this apartment community because of my excellent experience moving into apartment 527. It has been nothing but the opposite experience moving into 420. the lack of compensation for such poor and damaged apartment would not make me recommend this apartment complex to anyone.

The experience moving and settling into Cielo has been a breeze and above expectation. My Fiance and I are in love with the space, building location, and access to so many great amenities. Management is extremely friendly and easy to work with as well as security. We’re loving this new chapter in Little Italy and it’s hugely in part of loving where we live in Cielo.
Clean, friendly, safe, and by far the best location.
Absolutely incredible! A dream! Such a fun exciting experience!

Have live in Cielo for about a month and I truly can’t complain! The staff is friendly, the community is very well maintained, and the rooftop has probably one of the best views of the water in all of San Diego. My apartment was very clean and the layout makes it feel very spacious.

I have been a resident of Cielo for three months and it has been an overall great living experience. The units are spacious with great light from large floor to ceiling windows. The rooftop area is comfortable and provides a great place for daytime sun and sunset views of the Harbor. The walkability to restaurants and nightlife is perfect and having Waterfront Park across the street is clutch for my dog. I do live near the train but it is not bothersome at all.
