The staff is excellent and answers any questions I have along with maintenance needs in a timely manner. The gym has the essentials for working out (lifting or cardio) with many free weights, expectant smith machine, and a few cardio machines including spin bikes. The little Italy farmers market is only two blocks away and provides a great way to buy local fresh produce and products. Cielo is a great place to call home and highly recommended for anyone interested in living in Little Italy.
Cielo is a wonderful place to live. Incredible staff, unbelievable location for walking to the harbor, restaurants and all that Little Italy has to offer.

Since day one when we just toured this apartment we have been in love with it! The leasing staff, specifically Taylor, Freshte, and Riqa, are so sweet and helpful with all of my (excessive) questions. The maintenance staff has been so kind and so quick with fixing our chirping fire alarm and keeps the property looking freaking spectacular!! They have seriously been the best and made sure our move-in was incredibly easy- even on the rainiest day San Diego has seen in awhile haha! On top of all of that, the community is so incredibly beautiful. Moving from downtown, it’s nice to be in a place that feels so serene and secure! It’s seriously like a resort vibe. It’s walkable, has incredible amenities, gorgeous apartments, and great staff. I really don’t know what else you could ask for!
If you value your time, energy, and money, stay away. Prolonged construction and awful management.

Living here has been fantastic! This place, a converted hotel, has everything you need—AC, a pool, and laundry centers in each building. The location is unbeatable; you can walk to shops, restaurants, and more in minutes.

What really makes this place special is the management. They're on top of everything and genuinely care about the residents. Any issues? They handle them quickly. 

Yes, the neighborhood has its quirks, with some questionable characters around, but the residents here are super chill and respectful. It’s a peaceful community despite what’s happening outside.

Overall, it's a great spot with solid amenities, a prime location, and management that truly makes you feel at home.

This place is a joke!! Stay away at all cost they lie about everything an constantly have to deal with the meth an crack heads that Occasionally try to break into your apartment. If I could give this zero stars I would.

This great apartment complex has amazing management that makes it worth living here. I really enjoy the little things they do like the coffee and snacks they put in the management office. The maintenance guys also are fast and friendly. They keep the gym and gym bathroom really clean. I love living here!

The maintenance team at IDEA1 completes work orders in a timely manner. However, communication needs improvement, as staff members are not always responsive when greeted and lack professionalism. The maintenance manager is relatively new, which may contribute to the current communication gaps.

If you're choosing to live downtown, there are always going to be noises and community around the area that are different from a neighborhood. Avoid staying in certain units here though. Specifically the ones that have plumbing pipes on the ceiling. Due to the "industrial design" of the property, everything is open ceiling and plumbing pipes line a lot of the ceilings of the units. Every time someone flushes a toilet, takes a shower, it rains, or scheduled draining, you hear water through them. It's not quiet either; it is a very distracting and annoying sound when trying to enjoy living or sleeping.

Its literally built in skid row. The trolley thunders past the building every 15 minutes from 4:30 am until 1:30 am. There are homeless drug addicts on the sidewalk around the he building and many of them sneak in and break into cars, rooms, storages, or sleep on the roof or in stairwells. To name a few things. If you want to pay the premium prices for the Lousy housing this is the place for you!

The people in this community are not held to any sort of standard. The management team does little to nothing to address the issues brought to their attention. I have been here for two months and have had to start looking for a new place. The conditions are unlivable and the only recourse is to leave.

If I could give zero stars, I would. We moved into K1 three weeks ago, and from day one, it has been nothing but problems. Our unit had a laundry list of issues, including graffiti throughout the apartment due to a previous break-in—something that should have never been overlooked before handing over the keys. Instead of moving into a clean and properly maintained unit, we were left to deal with the aftermath.

Beyond our unit, the overall maintenance of the building is severely lacking. The gym has been closed the entire time we’ve lived here, and the trash chute is locked about 75% of the time, forcing tenants to find other ways to dispose of their trash. On top of that, the interior of the building is dirty, and it’s clear that they let in questionable tenants who don’t have basic hygiene. In just three weeks, we’ve already seen dog poop in the elevator once and dog urine multiple times. For what we’re paying in rent, there should be a higher standard for cleanliness and upkeep—especially considering this is supposed to be ‘luxury living.’

To be fair, the maintenance staff is very nice and does their best, but the real issue is the complete lack of organization and leadership from management. They are polite but extremely unprofessional, and from what I’ve gathered, when the previous manager left, the transition was handled poorly, leaving the new manager either underprepared or simply not equipped to run the building properly.

Repairs aren’t just delayed—they’re often done incorrectly when we’re not there to oversee them, which forces us to repeatedly submit maintenance requests for the same issues. Instead of ensuring repairs are completed properly the first time, we have to deal with a frustrating cycle of poor workmanship, follow-ups, and redoing work that should have been fixed initially. The fact that tenants have to constantly re-input maintenance requests just to get things done correctly is unacceptable. Meanwhile, management conveniently ignores more serious concerns, like our request for compensation for the continuous inconvenience we’ve experienced.

Looking at other reviews, it’s clear that this isn’t an isolated experience. If you’re considering moving here, save yourself the frustration—this building is completely mismanaged, and you won’t get the level of service you’re paying for.

K1 San Diego is a fantastic place to live in the east village neighborhood. It’s close to everything you want and has great views of the city from the Horizon Lounge. Neighbors are friendly, and the building is quiet which is uncommon for a high rise building. The fitness center is adequate especially for an apartment building, there’s TVs everywhere that actually work. The pool is a nice place to spend time and you really can’t beat a billiards table on the 22nd floor with a view. The management staff is one of the best I’ve ever seen personally. K1 is a great place to call home.

From beginning to end, exceptional service. Sonia assisted me all the way through leasing process, answered all my questions and was extremely helpful. The whole K1 leading Team is excellent and very professional. The building is well maintained and the community is excellent. Thank you!
Staff are very responsive and mindful of your needs!
Friendly attentive staff. Beautiful, quiet, clean building.
Overall, I've enjoyed my stay here and would recommend it to those interested in living in a convenient location downtown.

We been going on a month of constant hot water outages, garage repairs and other building repairs. Went weeks without being contacted for open maintenance requests, the office seems to never enforce having dogs on a leash, constantly running into people who think the building belongs to them and their dogs. Take your money and go elsewhere. It’s not worth it.

It takes 3-4 weeks for service to come after waiting for a service request. The app is always broken and can’t schedule time for the gym. The leasing office has very high turn over with the managers and front desk for a reason clearly. They up charge you for every little thing.

This building is so great and clean. The leasing office staff are super responsive with such a high level of customer service. The amenities just add to a vacation like atmosphere. Would definitely recommend.
Super responsive staff! Received quick replies to all my questions to help a short notice move. Shoutout to Larissa for all her help!

The first weeks of living at EV lofts are amazing. Also our dog love the place a lot. The apartment got everything you need and the staff is amazing Samantha helped us with the apartment, she friendly and her response time is so fast. Amazing!
EV Lofts is a great community; friendly staff, clean building, great amenities. Would recommend checking this place out if youre wanting a downtown San Diego living experience :)
Ev Lofts is a good place, especially for staying less than 5 years in San Diego. It beats the other massive apartment buildings. parking is better and the people are better.
I've lived here for over a year and love it! The community is safe and amenities are great. Very dog-friendly and the rooftop dog park is a great place to meet others in your building.

This building is not ideal to be living at for the price you pay. I would suggest looking elsewhere. For awareness some units deviate from unit schematics they post online for dimensions mainly - especially for units near elevators.  Elevators and garage door were constantly not working and very slow which was a pain and water maintenance was constant. The points of access for getting into the building can be very inconvenient depending on what unit you are in. Getting ahold of management in person is usually a battle as they lock the office doors and you have to "text" everything to their main phone number. During my stay there was extended maintenance on the pool area for months which was very noisy and disturbing for work from home.  Receiving packages which we pay for each month is also terrible as the lockers always fill up and your packages are dispersed in the mailroom for anyone to see or potentially take. The amenities such as Grills on the roof were not kept in great state and sometimes didn't work or heat up - for these rent prices they should be working! Additionally, after move out they tried to take my full deposit of $550 and had to fight to get it reduced even after deep cleaning (however this is common among most places). This was a battle with their main UDR team which isn't even out of the San Diego so had to deal with email which added additional frustration.

This place is freaking trash!! Rent increases of course year after year but last year by over $550 meanwhile the garage door or elevator is broken every week and the pool is under construction.. the management can’t possibly care less about anyone who lives here as they still lock themselves in the office while we deal with safety issues inside and outside the complex.. My unit has flooded before and they did little to nothing to help despite the entire issue being their fault and only saying to ask my insurance to help.

Leasing office doesn't return calls or messages. They never have great service. Ignore you and your requests. The common areas are always dirty and smell. The elevators are always broken. The water systems are always being repaired. Garage door is always out of service. Go someplace else if you're looking in East Village.

I love this place. The amenities are so nice. The gym, rooftop, pool/ courtyard, and the downstairs lounge area are all so nice. They keep things nice and clean and updated. The staff is so nice. They know me by name and remember pretty much every conversation I've had with them. Honestly no complaints. It's a bit pricey living here but in my opinion you get what you pay for. I'd rather pay a bit more for thick walls, nice staff, lots of amenities than pay less for a hole in the wall.

The building is overpriced for the area they need to come down a bit. Lived in the building 2 years. I wanted to stay and upgrade units. They really gave no incentive to stay. Although they had my deposit they wanted me to pay another? It was very silly I've lived here 2 years? They don't seem to care once you move in so busy trying to sell new tenants. Maybe if you had incentives to keep tenants you wouldn't need to hard sell everyone?

When I started searching which I had no intention of doing until the inconvenience of paying a 2nd deposit. I realized for what I was getting I was paying more. If you want to charge more than everyone else you need to offer more. How about concierge or something like that?

It's a good building and staff is great just following policy of the company. Yet value for price doesn't match. Again if you charge more than other new buildings next to you what are you offering different?

Definately above average, but falls far short of luxury. My partner and I moved in with high expectations. After all, it says "Luxury Living" on the outside and was overpriced enough that one would assume the extra rent went towards customer service, a great management team and maintenance?? It was under a year old when we moved in...

PROS
-Boutique hotel feel in lobby, common areas and hallways
-VERY modern and beautiful apartments
-Quality fixtures, flooring and appliances
-Quiet neighbors, especially for downtown. A mix of young professionals, military and work from home tech feel.
-Small gym but well equipped, especially for the size
-Very nice, small saline pool. Temp varies so you have to check before you know if it's right to go in.
-Great free coffee maker in lobby when they remember to refill the beans
-Email for new packages. Screen in mailroom too but they never turn it on.

CONS
So keep in mind, we were looking for 1) good customer service 2) hotel type building i.e. always clean and well maintained and 3) a good management team that really fixes something when problems do come up.
-Leasing agents are ALWAYS busy selling new tenants existing tenants have to wait. Sometimes 5 min or more. Leasing office is understaffed.
-Poor management - When there is a problem, getting it fixed quickly and correctly is not their strong suit. Fire alarms, broken garage door, broken front doors, water alarms in the garage. The same issues happen too often to be able to blame the vendor every time. At some point it becomes poor management and oversight.
-Maint projects start too late and, once they start, are usually abandoned before finishing. We had our hallway taped for painting for over 2 months before any painting was done. Dirty hallway carpets are constant. Garage never washed. Dust and soot gets tracked into your car, house and forget about ever washing your car again. It won't last a day. I have to carry the dog across the garage to the car.

So in summary, great building, poor management and
AREA? East village isn't quite there yet but it's coming along quickly and has a fun quirky style to it. Homeless are a real issue and local businesses have not yet opened on the surrounding blocks so you'll end up using the neighborhoods next door like the Gaslamp.
Genesee park is a nice and quiet facility. I love the property and office staff

This place is really awful, everything is old and filthy and stinky. hallways carpets and stained and disgusting. kitchen cabinets are smelly and stinky. Appliances are really old and inefficient. pool is always closed, I mean for the last three years it's been always closed. stay away from this place.

I highly recommend these apartments. The tenants are friendly and quiet. I was in a 2 master bedroom and it was very spacious. Parking is very convenient. Mariann the manager and Scott were very pleasant and if you needed maintenance, they took care of it right away. Check this place out!
I came in not a happy customer left feeling like I found my family a safe home. Beyond Satisfied!!

Genesee Park Apartments has been my home for the last 11 years, I am so thankful I found this Oasis. I have absolutely no complaints with central air, dishwasher and security in the evening who would :-). The apartments are quiet and give you a sense of home. Moving here was the best thing I did being a single woman. The neighbors are friendly, and I absolutely love and appreciate how there is always parking aside from the parking place you receive when you move in as a tenant. The maintenance man (Juan) is literally a gem. Juan comes in and fix’s anything that need to be fixed and does it with a positive attitude and in record time. I have to say… I have absolutely nothing negative to say about Genesee Park, the staff is the best, professional and courteous and always greeting me with warmth and a smile. If you are looking for a place to call home, this is the place! FYI I moved here because I needed central air conditioning… The day I moved in it was so hot and I knew I made the right choice when I walked into my apartment.

Needed a place fast. Nicole and Sandy in the office made our application and move in process quick and easy. Timely manner to respond to maintenance calls. Parking is easy!! There is covered parking and plenty of guest parking. Nice quiet location with friendly people. Plenty of good food and shopping within walking distance! Glad I picked Genesee Park to call Home!

A constant shutdown of water several times a week. Often non-working washing machines and dryers. All equipments in the gym are broken. Very noisy neighbors and very thin walls, it is impossible to sleep here at night. Terrible parking. Management will ignore your complaints and requests. Very old appliance. Maintenance is almost non-existent, we submit requests for water leaks, and they were not fulfilled in 3 months. Nobody even contacted us.

This is an old building that gets re-painted and cleaned for new residents to move into. So, it's really a patch up job. Don't expect a modern home or appliances. I'm assuming the pictures on the website are pictures from when the building was first built. There was water leaking from my bathroom ceiling due to my up stair neighbors taking a bath. Water was leaking from the ceiling where the lights are. I'm not sure if this has to do with the foundation of the building and not even sure how that was possible.  But I had to get a bucket to hold the water until my neighbors cleaned up their spilled up upstairs. My hubcaps were stolen from my car and both license plates were stolen as well (different incidents). I was told by the leasing office that cars parked under the building is not a good location and that this happens a lot. So if you move here, make sure to choose the parking spots that are not covered/ under the building. Police reports have been made and no other assistance. They use to have a security patrol. but the complex has gone through 3 different companies so far and none have lasted. I'm unsure what the reason is. The laundry machines are always broken and you will have to call to report it. Clothes are always wet from the washers or your clothes won't dry on the first round. The facility updated how they want your renters insurance policy. You need to add the Property name/ address (Conam/ PO Box #) and upload it to a certain website only. (For residents that are not tech savvy - you're in for a run) I had the apt name but was missing the address so I ended up uploading it after the "deadline".  The complex charged me a $25 fee. I pay for my renters insurance annually so it wasn't because I relapse on my policy. It was because I didn't have the PO Box number. I called the leasing office to have it waive since I am a long term resident and always pay rent on time or even before the 1st of the month. But she told me there's nothing she can do about it and charge is valid. I honestly think that's not right. Charge me if I am late or charge me if my policy relapse or I don't have a renters insurance policy. But don't charge me if my renter's insurance was missing Conam's PO Box # which caused the first set of documents to get kick back for that reason. Rent keeps going up every year and the place is no longer worth what I am paying now. Location is great and price was reasonable when I first moved in.
This location is definitely at the top of my list, if considering visiting definitely talk to Karina she was awesome, helpful and informative.
Has beautiful courtyard but not inside the apartment unit. and it lacks upgrades of all kinds. It looks pretty in the pictures but beware once you move in. I won't recommend this place

I'm resident of prado home apartment. Here is real experience that I been through. This water sink in my bath room is stucked about 17 days ago. I notice the apartment two weeks ago and now the problem is still, they didn't even send someone to check it. I notice the office several either by email or go to their office. So it can't be that they didn't know. Now it fill with this ugly water with awful smell. So if you plan to live here, keep this in mind.

This complex is perfect for me. Every one has different needs but you can't beat the location. The location is in Mission Valley, close to freeways, grocery stores, EVERYTHING! The courtyard is landscaped well, there is 2 pools to share, the 'gym' is okay, and parking is fine (no guest parking!). Also, the water gets shut off at least twice a month for 'plumbing repairs.' It is a very quiet complex and I have really nice neighbors.

HOWEVER, if you need something from management, do it yourselves. There is so much miscommunication between residents and management that it is ridiculous. Oh and be prepared to be treated like a child and be talked down to by those ladies in the office (Especially Autumn).

This property is adorable and has great amenities I was so excited to move in. However, it has been a mess since day one. Emails and work orders are just ignored. If you want something fixed prepare to stand around in the leasing office and miss time from work. This is the most poorly run complex I have ever dealt with. I really wish I could leave a better review.

Maintenance is really good, they come and fix the problem really quickly. There is a mold problem, it's literally everywhere. Parking is first come first serve and garages are $150 a month if you even get to rent one because of the long waitlist. After 6pm you'll have to park far 5-10 minute walk. Walls are paper thin so I recommend an upstairs unit but be aware neighbors can hear everything. Apartments get really really hot during the summer. There's a gym, pool, basketball and tennis court. Laundry rooms are ok, sometimes there's 1/2 machines out of order and you should go get your clothes a couple minutes before it's actually done because I've had people grab my laundry and move it around without consent before (??). Everyone has a dog here, it's nice if you have one they're very welcome. Blinds are not the best for privacy, if you're downstairs everyone walking by can see inside. This spot is ok but definitely not my forever home.
Great work. The only issue was the worker did not speak English

Never had any major problems here! some of the reviews are a little ridiculous considering this is apartment living! If you want better parking and other things buy a home! Apartment living does come with some complaints but this place has taken care of little things! The office staff is always helpful, and the property manager has personally came and check an issue I’ve had and made sure it was addressed properly! When we moved in everything was clean; and ready to go! No complaints!

I am almost 6 years here and the maintenance staff is wonderful.  Miguel has been here many times over the years and goes above and beyond to complete any requested repairs.  I always know they will be here for me and do a great job.

Unless you want to have your packages stolen constantly don't move here. I just had a $200 textbook stolen from my porch and I have seen mail theft here first hand. The price you pay monthly to live here and not have your own parking spot is not worth it. I have a video of someone hitting my car and the car behind them trying to get out of a parking spot on the street, and that happens all the time. In the laundry room closest to our apartment we had 2 out of 4 washers broken for at least 3 months, and management did nothing about it. If prices in San Diego were affordable I would move literally almost anywhere else. Also, the walls are paper thing and I can hear *all* the activities our downstairs neighbors are engaged in. Do yourself a favor and don't move here.

Do not rent with Terra at Mission Trails. Very unorganized. They rarely are at their office and rarely help you with anything. They upcharge you for multiple things even if you leave them with a brand new looking apartment. Awful management. No parking for guests
They approved for to move in and then told me it was a race to get the deposit. I lost housing because of their unethical practice.

We lived at Terra for almost 2 years. Its a great location and the place is kept really clean.  They also accept dogs, which was really important to me. I lived upstairs near the pool and it was never loud or out of hand. It is a little out of the way to make a U-TURN at Jackson Drive to get back to Mission Valley every day but other than that we really had no complaints while we lived there.
These apartments were decent. Nothing special, nothing terrible. There was water problems a lot but other than that not too many issues.
The community is beautiful and well maintained with great additional amenities (pool, gym, tennis courts, and club house). Also, the staff is very helpful and nice.

We chose The Club Torrey Pines for its amazing location and also because it has the best amenities in Carmel Valley!  The huge heated pool along with the tennis courts are great!  The apartments are nicely renovated and well priced.  All of the staff is very nice as well!

Don’t be fooled by the model home they show. Actual unit is always “not ready.” There is no AC so will be hot in the summer months; regardless how nice the weather is. Unit is outdated. Shared water means you pay same amount living by yourself as four college students. In fact my bill went up the month I was away on business trip. MOLD. There’s mold that’s painted over. You discover it after moving in, because you don’t even get to see your actual unit before signing contract. There’s a reason why they make you sign a Mold Addendum. So they can make you pay for mold treatment even though it was a preexisting issue prior to your move in. Staff is either smoking around front of office or clubhouse area. Secondhand smoke not a good way to start my workout. By the way, having tattoos is not a license to be disrespectful. There is such a thing as customer service when you manage apartments.

In general I love this place, but the noise has gotten really out of control. The gardeners use the loud blowers every morning for hours & then again midday & again in the afternoon - what?! With no A/C and a very hot summer of course you want your windows open. They need to upgrade to electric blowers, or be more reasonable.

The Club Torrey Pines is the perfect location near shopping, food, the beach & freeways! It's spacious rooms are available upgraded for a good price or slightly dated for a great price! The washer & dryer in unit is a huge plus! Highly recommended apartments.

This is a great community for anyone who wants a nice family friendly and quiet place to live. My expectations were not very high for my first apartment and the Club Torrey Pines definitely exceeded mine. The windows are new and the carpet was immaculate when I moved in. All appliances were in good working order and the grounds are kept very nice and clean. The staff is very friendly and responsive and the amenities are great! It is very close to great shopping and only minutes away from the UTC mall. Overall it is a great place to live and I am very happy here!

We have happily lived here for 2 years, but are moving out of state for my husbands job or else we wouldn't leave. Since I was just going through the hassle of apartment hunting in a new city, I've noticed that positive, unbiased reviews are very hard to come by!  

Darlene and the staff have always responded quickly to our maintenance issues, and all work orders were completed within 24 hours. I don't recall any excessive or unnecessary walk throughs, especially not without ample notice. Everyone on staff is very friendly, trustworthy, and really seem to care about the residents. 

The grounds are beautiful, the pools are clean, and as cat parents, we are OBSESSED with the ability to turn our balcony into a screened in "catio" so our floofs can safely use the little sliding window to let themselves outside... and use their litter box in a place where I don't have to smell it lol. 

We LOVED having a garage spot, and the storage unit that comes with it is insanely large. We were able to keep any clutter out of our house and stored away in a safe, clean environment. Finding street parking for our second car is easy, and we have always felt safe with our car on the residential streets. 

Ok the negative-ish: Rent increases? Sure it sucks. But it's so-cal and the economy is up. Literally EVERYONE has raised rent. Even when we thought about downsizing and moving more east, rent has gone up there too. For the space, accessibility, and comfortability we get here, it wasn't worth leaving. 

Overall, we highly recommend this complex! Safe, clean, friendly staff, great location with lots of restaurants, salons, and grocery shopping just a block away, (Hello, Sprouts!) and easy access to the 5 and all the additional shopping in Clairemont.

We just moved in yesterday and these apartments so nice (so far!)!The manager is super friendly. The walls are so soundproof it doesn't feel like apartment living at all. The laundry rooms are super clean and nice, the pools are very clean, neighbors are quiet, the views are awesome, the rent is cheap-ish, what more can you ask for??

Do not stay here. I signed the lease because I received 5 weeks free, but I cannot emphasize enough how much I regret it. The management is horrific. They will go weeks without returning calls and without picking up the phone at all.  When I moved in, the apartment had obviously not been thoroughly cleaned as there were crumbs in the drawers, the oven was filthy, the bedroom smelled like a dog, and there was a cockroach infestation in the kitchen. It took 4 MONTHS to get rid of the roaches completely. I had a broken refrigerator for 2 weeks, and the office did not pick up any of my daily phone calls for that entire two weeks. I finally found an emergency number on the leasing office door, which I called to complain to about not having a working refrigerator for two weeks (on the emergency maintenance issues list was broken refrigerators), but she told me this wasn't an emergency issue (but it was listed as one) and then angrily hung up on me. There has been a revolving door of maintenance workers (who are all great and do the best they can), so there are obviously management issues that are causing them to quit or stop showing up to work. 

Another thing is the leasing agent over the phone told me the apartment had hardwood floor when it is actually a rubber linoleum that looks like wood, so keep that in mind too. There is a broken light in the hallway that apparently is unfixable, and the bathroom outlet only works when the bathroom light is turned on. The final straw is that the water is shut off at least once per month. In December or January the water was shut off three weekends in the month and sometimes for multiple days at a time. Do not stay here unless you literally cannot afford anywhere else.

Also, this is probably obvious to San Diego natives, but this complex is not in La Jolla. It is in University City, an ugly industrial-like neighborhood outside UCSD. La Jolla is only a couple miles west, but it is like night and day. All the reviews here saying that this is the best apartment complex in La Jolla are obviously fake because La Jolla is one of the most beautiful cities in California, and this place is a dump.

I lived at Gold Coast Apartments for 3 years.  The staff at Gold Coast is really nice. They have  AC and large 2 bedrooms 2 bath apartments.  I have told a lot of friends to move there and they were happy as well.

Gold Coast Apartments is a great place to live. I give it 5 stars lots of open space, beautiful pool area, private patios and more. Dan the maintenance guy can fix anything and Lee the onsite manager is terrific at handing any issues in a timely manner.

I love how quiet the neighborhood is. Really nice to come home and not be disturbed by loud neighbors. I am impressed at how well maintained the property is and the staff is very nice. I definitely recommend this place to others

Before I rented an apartment at Gold Coast I was concerned about pest that might be in the apartment.  Lee mentioned that each apartment is inspected after the last tenant moves out by a licensed Pest Control Company and if any pests are found the unit is treated.  I have had some bad experiences in other apartment communities and wanted to be sure this would not happen again. I just moved out after 2.5 years and I was very satisfied with the apartment.  The only issue I had at the property was my refrigerator stopped working and the maintenance person brought in another one the same day to use until the new one arrived.  I also liked having my own parking space and not having to always hunt for some where to park. Good place to live.

This is the second time I have rented  at Gold Coast Apartments. I rented again because the staff does an excellent job of managing the property. I was able to get a fully remodeled apartment with a garage and everything was new. Lee really takes care of her tenants and when I had a maintenance request it was taken care of the next day. I was also able to make some extra cash by referring a couple of friends. I would highly recommend Gold Coast.
5 stars….

Apartment is nice being so close to school being a full time student but building itself is old and hear your neighbors talking or walking above you. Can't afford to move to nice apartments but wish I could!! Please help me!!

Maintenance requests can take weeks to be addressed. Pools are filthy, pool area not maintained. Right now the pools have algae and the Paseo pool gates have been chained shut for a week with no note or explanation.

Upon moving in, there was a list of problems that were not evident until the first week we started using items: dishwasher doesn't work (still not working 2 weeks in), light did not work, ants all over kitchen (we took care of this, not wanting poison sprayed), kitchen water was not clear, kitchen faucet had to be replaced, blinds wouldn't come down, rattling in air conditioning vent (still not fixed), sink not draining in the bathroom. We were told the carpet was brand new, it is not; the old tenant popped her head in and introduced herself and said, no, this is old carpet.
The maintenance folks are super friendly, I think they have too many orders and it takes forever to get to us, but bottom line, these should have been addressed BEFORE renting it out to us.
Plusses: friendly neighbors and staff, pretty good sound proof in walls, great area.

We have been living here for many years. Really like the community and very grateful to be here.  I have a lot of respect for the great staff, very pleasant, helpful, sincere and they do care very much about the tenants and the community. Great resident neighbors. I recommend this great 55+ seniors living to family and friends.  I wouldn't like to live anywhere else! Thank you for your fine work and help.

Have lived here 1.5 years & a current resident. Location is close to everything, good neighbors, & fast maintenance team.  You will want a unit with at least one assigned parking space. Overall good. only concern is the growing crime in the area:  not really the apartment complex fault, specifically vehicle break in’s, maybe Loma Palisades can get security to patrol at night, or install security cams, or invest in gates for parking lots

This is my second year living at this complex. I  love the layout and how it feels like a home. The patio space is very large and the maintenance are always so quick to our place. Some of the apartment is outdated - like most.

BUT... every unit is different and the model unit you get to view for showing is nicer and bigger LOL. The pool has been closed all summer. I had to pretty much yell at the property owner to keep the laundry areas clean (they are always clean now, funny how that works). They just finished putting in windows and were in our homes for 8 days with no compensation. We started renting 2 years ago and we looked and our place is 2x the price we are paying now --beware!

I lived here in an apt/townhouse for over a year. I moved in believing that the location would be great for my little family. I couldn’t have been more wrong! It was loud, smelly, busy, rickety, moldy, often “2am drunk-fights in the street” type, awful parking, the laundromat machines were very small and didn’t work well, things were made cheaply and fell apart easily, and there is a big homeless population in the area so It was often that we would wake up to people camped out sleeping on our porch walkway, guys stumbling through trying to open our door, or ask for money. Normally that wouldn’t be a “big deal” to me- but I have small kids, so trying to navigate them through that felt really unsafe. It’s dog friendly, which we loved, but the walkways often smelled strongly of pee, or uncaring owners often left poop behind (even though there’s plenty of dog bags offered). We had a hill behind our place where guys often camped out in the brush, and if we left our windows open - we would see little red lights flash or would see a camera flash, as if they were taking pics. It was just an offense on ALL senses and systems.  By the time I got the opportunity to move out - I just didn’t care and left as fast as I could. It was well over-priced for what you get.

Told us 2 DAYS before we were slated to move into an apartment we had been approved for and paid money for that it wouldn't be ready for WEEKS.  We were literally homeless for 2 weeks until we found a new apartment to rent.  Already changed our utilities over (their requirement), changed our address, etc.  Had packages en route to new apartment, the office didn't even have the decency to decline and return to sender.  Mailed back holding deposit as a money order paid to LOMA PALISADES so we couldn't cash it back.  AVOID

When my dog died, I let the office know so that they could remove the pet rent from the next month's invoice. They said they required a 30 day notice that the dog would no longer be living there, and that I had to pay for my dead dog's rent for 1 more month! I also had to submit a letter in writing, and provide them with proof that the dog died! These people are sick.

I've lived at Loma Palisades for three years now and my experience so far has been amazing! The staff in the office are so nice and helpful, any issues I have had they are taken care of in a timely matter.  I would highly recommend Loma Palisades to anyone looking for a place to live. Their community is well maintained and the best part is I'm so close to the beaches and the stores are close as well, which is very convenient for me since I have three needy children. :) Thanks Loma Palisades for being the best place to call home!
Amazing customer service and I was given all the information I needed to make a decision,
The staff is very helpful and overall it was a great experience. Thank you.

I am grateful to be living at the casas Ruiz apartments I'm grateful to have a place I can call home finally I feel safe and secure no worries at all neighbors are friendly I have no complaints whatsoever I recommend these apartments to anyone that is looking for a place to go home for themselves

My wife and I are happy in our new and cozy home.
Thank you very much for the service and customer care
Sorry nothing for this year. Everything is diminishing especially this year. Year ago alteast there a response may be few days or few months later but no more. They don't care.
Renting with them for almost 5yrs and we love the place, the amenities are always clean as well as they do immediate actions with regards to maintenance.

I lived here from 2018 until 2020 and I had a good experience living in my apartment in the 9085 building. Maintenance was quick whenever there was a problem and the unit was well maintained. Management was fair with the security deposit when I moved out.

One complaint I have is that it does not seem like the pool amenities were maintained as well as you would expect. Cushions on the furniture would not be cleaned. The gym was nice though.

I highly recommend not to lease in these apartments. All the appliances are really old and never work properly. Even if you raise many maintenance requests , they will offer you some quick fixes never permanent solution. Our air conditioner is not working. Almost 3 weeks now.. no one is bothered to fix it… I have couple of raised maintenance requests and followed up with leasing office, no use…. All in all, any future resident considering this apartments my words for you are: if you are looking for a wonky stove top, with noisy washer, no air conditioned house and with occasional leaked ceiling and most of all if you enjoy raising maintenance request every fortnight and following up on them you will enjoy your residence here.

I've been a resident of La Jolla Crossoroads for a year. We enjoy the peaceful atmosphere and taking our daughter to the playground. I know there's been a lot of positive changes at this property. The clubhouse is being renovated and such delightful staff. All of our works orders have been taken care of in a timely matter. Thank you for always taking care of our community Crossroads, the landscaping and grounds are always cleaned! Looking forward to renewing our lease.

Sincerely,

Our family

I've lived in this community for over 6 years and love it. The location is perfect with a short walk or a free shuttle ride to the nearby Westfield UTC Mall and quick access to the 805 and 5 freeways; plus metro transit access on Judicial Drive. A beautiful and very large park is only a block away from the complex (soccer, baseball,basketball, picnic areas, library, kids playground, and dog park). The buildings and common areas are well maintained  (art sculptures, multiple pools, grilling areas, and play ares for the kids). If you like quite, then choose a building away from Golden Haven Drive or overlooking a courtyard as the buildings amplify the sound. The apartments are roomy, nice size balconies to enjoy the great weather year round and each unit includes full size washer/dryer. Plenty of underground gated garage parking with assigned spaces. Multiple elevators in each building making getting around easier, but you can take the stairs if you prefer.

This place is beautiful! The management is so nice and they are very helpful. The atmosphere is lovely and I love living here. It's very clean and the cleaning staff is very friendly. The rent is a little pricey but that is because of the location and scenery. Its right across from the mall and so close to pizza hut and which wich. It is perfect!
in terms of p/sf to value as a tenant, you can't find a better comparable deal. downsides are that sinks and grinder break down near expiration, and smoke alarms go off at random times.
Great place to live on the edge of downtown SD. Great facilities. Great staff. Clean and sustainable.
I love the community and have enjoyed living here for 3 years now

Love the property so far. The community is friendly with doggos to complement. The amenities are beautiful and the move towards smart home technology is a plus, not to mention the availability of fiber. You will get mild street noise (but you are near downtown). I’m a huge fan of how beautiful the dark interiors are and how elegant the newer finishes are. I do wish the construction was more dense or thicker carpet, as I can feel my upstairs neighbor’s heavy footing and get rattled anytime something heavy is dropped. The property staff is extremely friendly and have been the biggest reason I enjoy staying here so far. I just can’t wait for the new construction across the street to be finished.

Everything is maintained so well, everything is so clean and all of the staff are so friendly!  It really makes for a pleasant living experience! Even the cleaning crew are so genuine and nice! So appreciated!
Amazing location, amenities, and quarters. Absolutely would recommend anyone staying here.
Poorly managed. Residents are disregarded. Complete lack of quality control and upkeep.

I only lived here for a year, but this is genuinely the best apartment complex I've ever lived at. It felt more like a home than an apartment, and the only reason I left was because of a job promotion that took me 90 miles away.

Where do I start? First off, there's absolutely a difference in a place like this that's got a single owner as opposed to these other places owned by Realty companies, etc. Every single day I saw the maintenance crew working on something to maintain the property. Any time I had a maintenance issue, it was resolved within a day.

The neighborhood is SO quiet. I never had issues with loud neighbors. This is a nice little secluded section that's very close to the freeway, but you wouldn't know it walking around.

The layout is great - I was in a one bedroom, and the way the apartment is broken up helps to make it feel more like a small home/flat. Having the kitchen separate from the living room unlike most apartments was a big deal for me.

Some realities of the area:
- RB is near a canyon, so there will be bugs around during Summer. However, this is nothing I couldn't fix with a small bug light! Also, I NEVER saw a single cockroach. For me, roaches are non-negotiable.
- There is an elementary school right next to the complex, which is great if your kid goes there, but kind of annoying if you're trying to get to work. If you plan for it, it's no big deal.
- This is a GREAT area for night walks, VERY safe. However, not a ton within walking distance. You do have a great Starbucks within walking distance, as well as a CVS, Marco's Pizza, and some other good things. Outside of that, you'll need a bike or car.

The office staff is great - Caryn was amazing the entire process of me moving in to me moving out. I really, really miss this place, but at least I know where to go if I end up in San Diego again. Do yourself a favor and check out this hidden gem - you get every pennies worth out of it!

The best place to live in Rancho Bernardo for families with elementary school age kids. School is just across the street and kids have many their friends living here. Kids play outside year around. Very safe and brings great feeling of community. Green area is lifted above street level, so kids can’t accidentally run into the road. 
Maintenance service is alway very prompt and staff is very friendly. A lot of storage in 2brs apts. Love living here!
Beautiful  complex...HORRIBLE  lease consultant!!!  She needs more people skills training...was not friendly at all!!!

La Terraza is a gem in north county San Diego just off the 15 freeway. 
The community is very well kept, the staff is great.
La Terraza is located in a in a quite family neighborhood. 
The apartment are nice with washer / dryers, fireplace, garages...

Beautiful complex with very nice landscaping in a very quiet neighborhood. Apartments come with some of the biggest kitchens in the area and have more square footage than most other apartments while still having an affordable monthly rent. A very important amenity when we were searching for an apartment was a washer and dryer included in the unit, La Terraza goes above and beyond with all amenities. One of the best in the area.

This is the perfect place for entertaining, large party room available, olympic sized swimming pool, beautiful landscaping, and always a friendly staff keeping the grounds and units well maintained. Vaulted ceilings, huge kitchen, with laundry facilities in each unit. Large balconies, and your own garage with storage. Minutes from the freeways, you wouldn't know it when you come home to a nice quiet parklike setting. Great barbecue area in a tropical setting. It's like living in paradise.

I lived here for three years, and I loved it. The building is beautiful: it’s architecturally interesting, and there are plants and flowers throughout the common areas. Also, the location is perfect for anyone working downtown. Most importantly, the staff is amazing; in addition to being friendly and professional, they made this building a great community. I highly recommend it.

The area is great, we chose this place because of how close it is to downtown Issaquah and hiking trails. We like to walk places and we can walk right into town on the trail that is directly behind the apartment complex. The unit itself is newly renovated which is very nice, beautiful marble counter tops, great fireplace. The rooms are spacious and cozy at the same time, not sure how they do that but it's awesome. The only complaint I have is that the renovations on the other apartments in the building aren't done yet so we get to listen to that, kinda getting used to it though. Overall very in love with the apartment!
I have had my apartment for 5 years & I LOVE it, but every year they raise my rent at least $50.00 a month. This will make me start looking around for a cheaper apt. this year!

The apartment Is in avery desirable location. It's close to Gaslamp and the seashore to take evening strolls. and there are less bums in this area. there is even a park close by. the windows need major major overhaul. they are thin and heavy to slide. in these days all windows should be dual paneI. This would cut down the noise from the fire trucks coming down Front St. and the freight train noise coming down harbor blvd.
And during the harsh temperature changes insulate the interiors better. The management staff are very professional but need to explain the basics of rental a little better for those who never rented before. There is no 24 hr emergency staff to call in event of troubles like toilets. When certain things break like garbage disposal they will have their repair staff immediately work on it during normal working hours. Parking is good if you pay for the $100 spots which is still cheap compared to outside parking lots which charge $25 a day. There are no electric outlets for any electric vehicles. Overall it's a very good place to live with an oversize jacuzzi and a small lap pool. I wished they would put a BBQ pit next to the pool or in the courtyard so we could entertain more friends in the summer.

I love this place. I've been living here for a year and I have to say that this is the best location to live downtown. You're close to everything! A block from Horton Plaza and 24 hr Ralphs Grocery. Two blocks from Seaport Village, 4 blocks from the Gaslamp, around the corner from the Convention Center. Everything is within walking distance that you could ask for. Being located in the Marina district is a plus also because you don't have to worry about so many bums hanging out around the building like you would in the East Village. The only problems I have with the place is that the windows are thin and you can hear everything outside, especially if the neighbors come in late from the club and want to talk loud. Also, parking can be a problem if you get a $65 a month spot. I'm paying $100 a month for a spot to not get my doors dinged. But there is a security person on duty every night with a post in the parking lot so you feel safe. Overall I love the location and think this is one of the best places to live downtown!

The apartments are old and rundown. There is no security and solicitors knock on my door all the time. I have had my laundry stolen twice since anyone can access the buildings. The new management company by FPI management is just terrible. The only plus side is they are pet friendly.

We just moved in! I like the size of our one bedroom. It’s just enough for us two and our pup (oh yes they are definitely dog friendly) we live close to the parking lot so we don’t walk around as much but we do take the dog for walks around and the amenities are really great; especially for what you pay here. Cannot go wrong. Lief really helped us move in SO fast!

My girlfriend and I moved into Baypoint in August 2018, and the leasing agent was an angel to us, she found the perfect spot with a bay view on 3rd story, unfortunately she is not here anymore (Jennifer, I wish you the best and thank you). 

We have been impressed by the amenities and events that the complex has. I use the gym, sauna, business area, pool, jacuzzi and more. Yes, the complex is old and some gym equipment is dated but it works. 

If you have any issues where you need maintenance, they usually respond fairly quickly and will call your phone number directly to address the issue as soon as possible. The only downside to maintenance is water being shut off. This happens completely unexpectedly without notice, and I have addressed this with management and they are working for a system. I am hoping some sort of notification system is rolled out in 2018. 

The only issue that I have had is when my bike was mistaken for being abandoned and it was disposed of. At the time I was furious, but after speaking with management they were very understanding and allowed me to blow off my steam, and then eventually compensated me for the mistake. 

Overall, I love the complex. The units are large and open and allow for a bunch of sunlight through. Then in general it kind of seems like you’re living at a hotel and always on vacation when walking around, it is really nice. 

The management has changed recently and the new manager is really working to improve things with all of the residents. After speaking with her, it made me feel good that it seemed like we have a manager on duty that understands her residents and will work for US to make us happy. Thank you.
They raised my rent $300 a month!  I'm a tenant that has paid on time for over 2 years.  I'm out!
Honestly, just read the yelp reviews. Everything you need to know is in those reviews.

The management staff is rude and condescending and unwilling to help you resolve issues with your apartment. My apartment flooded twice while living there. Cockroaches everywhere all over the complex. Parking is horrible if you come home anytime after 5pm. Many other apartments that are in better shape for a better price and location with better managers/landlords.

Maintenance: The maintenance staff are great—responsive and efficient. Unfortunately, the office staff aren’t as effective.

Grounds: The complex looks nice from afar, but inside, it's littered with trash, dog waste, and dirty areas. The pool is hit or miss, often unclean and unheated. There’s frequent dumping of large items, and we all end up paying for the cleanup.

Safety: The garage gate often malfunctions, making it easy for unauthorized people to enter. The security staff are rarely seen, and parking enforcement is lax.

Neighborhood: Located by the noisy freeway, with limited nearby amenities. The bus stop is convenient, but there are noisy pool parties and occasional issues with homeless individuals near the west entrance.

Noise: Expect noise from the freeway and loud garbage pickup, especially if you’re near the west garage. Noisy neighbors are also a problem, with the inept office staff failing to address complaints.

Office Staff: They’re friendly but ineffective. The focus seems to be on appearances rather than solving real problems.

Overall: If you can’t find a better place, this complex might work, but be aware of its many issues. Avoid the west gate area and consider a top-floor unit to minimize potential noise problems from your neighbors.

I recently toured Griffis Mission Valley and had to leave a review based on my experience. The property itself is wonderful, but the people I met really made the experience a stand out one! Zoe, the leasing agent that I toured with, was personable and charismatic. She made me feel so welcome and made me want to be a part of the community. She showed me their recent upgrades to the apartment homes and, WOW, they look amazing! 

10/10 experience and a 10/10 apartment community. I can’t wait to move in!

Beyond absurd. My car was towed inside the garage by leasing at 1am. My car was registered in the system and I paid parking every single month. Their reason was simply "my sticker was not visible" and "for security". For what security????????? They can clearly contacted me beforehand but no, simply towed away,
No communication or help from the leasing at all, I had to call the towing company myself and pay over 300 dollars to get it back in a weekday morning and missing school/work.
For all my neighbors here, just watch out. I was still lost of words for what happened.

This is the worst place I've lived at. Been under 3 different management in less than 1 year I've been here. Griffis is the worst of them all. This is what you're looking at for paying luxury apartments pricing, which also is getting increased:
1) constant water shut off, at least few times a month, sometimes even once or twice a week
2) we haven't had access to our mailbox in OVER a month and mails and packages are being stolen
3) their parcel locker is constantly not working either, more lost packages
4) there are flies and bugs everywhere, it's just nasty
5) security is a joke here, not sure I've even seen one lol
6) cars getting broken into all the time, but now we are being charged more for parking too....but obviously without any of the current issues being resolved
7) also, they LOVE to ignore your concerns and complaints. Sure they have a community wall, but it is all monitored so they reject all your complaints and concerns. Not only that, they don't even bother to reach out to you to resolve these issues. 

So if that's what you're looking for as your next home at a premium price, then maybe you'll love it here. Otherwise, just do yourself a favor and look somewhere else.
My apartment is beautiful, and the staff here is very friendly and helpful!

Vehicle was broken into 5 times, 2 times in the same month.  Caught a burglar one time.  When i asked management about it, they stated that they are not responsible for your safety.  So if you or your family is attacked by a thief or homeless person, they are not responsible, even though it can happen on their property.

Packages get stolen on a daily basis because of no security.  Trash rooms get full because property management doesn't take out the trash, and water gets shut off once a month.

Look elsewhere.

Look elsewhere! Terrible maintenance management! Read 1 star review before choosing this place! I should’ve believed it.
Lived here for a year and all I get are empty promises. Got my bike stolen twice. Asked them to provide me a video of the garage and they said they will and followed up and waited multiple times and got nothing. SECURITY is a major issue even with the gate!! Multiple water heaters were busted in my area including ours that required our water to be turned off multiple times and have to deal with a flooded non livable bedroom for days. Now I got back from vacation and arrived to a water heater and no hot water for a week now!! A WEEK! And they have 1 maintenance person for the whole complex. Then, now their parcel where you get your packages is down for a whole pick and presidio view and parcel pending are doing the blame game and not getting it fixed for a week now. This place is just falling apart. Terrible management! Paying premium price for a substandard service. I will not be recommending this place and would not renew my Lease. Look elsewhere. There are a lot better apartment nearby.
Can't wait to move out. Few more days!
I have lived at Presidio going on 6 years. Overall I have very much enjoyed my time here. When I have friends over they invariably comment on how nice the complex is.

I love my apartment! It has all the amenities, the location is great, and it feels like I live in a resort or spa with the bamboo and stream outside. Management is cool and maintenance is quick to respond, too.
wonderful environment,  friendly neighbors, and inviting to pet parents.

The apartment looks nice from afar and may seem like a luxury complex, but the experience of living here is subpar. Managements poor communication has made handling any apartment issues extremely difficult. Our apartment was not ready for move in even with several weeks between the date of the last tenants move out and our move in. Ive tried my best to be patient and understanding through all of this but it feels like all of these problems have gone unheard and/or ignored by management. After giving them the benefit of the doubt time and time again, I am incredibly disappointed with how we have been treated as new residents.
I enjoy the amenities and location and quality of the apartments at Presidio. However I do not enjoy the the overflowing amounts of garbage/trash in the parking garage. That is my only complaint.

I walked in with a newly acquired voucher for rental assistance and was told by the mgr. they don't accept voucher. Not updated on current laws. They missed out on a good tenant with great credit and rental history.
Adriana at Sola is outstanding in her service with leasing matters. I absolutely love my new apartment , the location and amenities are awesome.

I love the amenities, a great jacuzzi and pool, many high end BBQ grilling areas, clean and well appointed club room as well as a modern and well equipped gym. We also have areas to study and take business calls that are semi private making this a never needing to leave home. The proximity to nearly every shop and business just a few steps away makes it a winner.
My family and I have living happily at SOLA for almost 3 years, we totally recommend the service, the property team always do an incredible job to creates a sense of community and responsiveness.
The plan of the house and the apartment complex is very useful. We feel comfortable and safe.
Living at Sola is an excellent all-inclusive experience and a great environment for families of all ages.

Just a horrific place to live. Whatever you do, do not move here. I'll outline some of the cons below and why I would never choose to live here again:

-They assured me that a $800 increase in my monthly rent was 'below market value'.

-I only receive about 50% of my packages. The rest are stolen by people that walk and stalk the halls at Sola.

-Parking is a complete nightmare. People park sideways, in incorrect spots, and on the wrong floors. Yet, nothing is done about it.

-You pay $45 per month for trash. $45!!!! How is that even possible? The only service you have is large places to dump trash bags.

-You are not living alone because you can hear EVERYTHING that your neighbors beside and above you are doing. Other residents have told me the same thing. Literally, I can hear every footstep that my upstairs neighbor takes and can hear personal conversations from my neighbors.

Another downside is no central A/C, but our unit's orientation (windows north and south)and height (15028 #E) really kept that from being a problem. That unit has great views and great breezes.

This limited timeframe makes it extremely difficult to prepare and manage essential tasks that rely on running water. Moreover, the duration of these shutoffs can range from 1-2 hours to an astonishing 5-6 hours

Furthermore, there have been instances where no advance notifications were provided, leaving me unaware of the water's unavailability until I discovered it firsthand in my apartment. This lack of communication adds to the frustration and inconvenience.

Additionally, it is disappointing that the leasing office does not offer alternative options for convenience during these water shutoffs, such as mobile toilets or drinking water bottles. As paying residents, we deserve better treatment and consideration when faced with such situations, especially since we are responsible for paying our water bills.

To compound the problem, these water shutoffs often occur during the morning hours, around 10 am, which is a peak time for engaging in daily activities that heavily rely on water. This timing clash disrupts my morning routine and creates unnecessary stress.

For individuals considering renting this property, I strongly urge you to weigh the consequences of these frequent water shutoffs before making a final decision. It is crucial to contemplate how you would manage in situations where water is unavailable for extended periods, particularly during peak hours. While the apartment may possess other positive aspects, this recurring issue presents a significant inconvenience that should not be overlooked.

In conclusion, I sincerely hope that the management takes these concerns into serious consideration and endeavors to find a more reasonable solution to minimize the impact of these water shutoffs.
