The apartments may look decent on the outside and convenient, but not worth it !

management is very unprofessional and rude. Maintenance issue constantly. Do not rely on having running water that is cold and hit because the piping is on the roof and not insulated, so you don't get hot and cold water. There are bugs, spiders, roaches etc. 
People steal from your open patios, vandalize your cars and there is no security patrol. The laundry rooms are crammed and tight. No space to do your laundry.
Quiet area, nice neighbors.. Down the street from a dog park. Parking is kind of hard at certain times, but that's most of area. Shopping center is one block away to make up for the parking..

Let me just start off by saying this place is cheaply done for the price that I’m having to pay. When I first moved in, not a week went by and I was already having plumbing issues and a couple things were broken like the sink handle and the shower door. When we asked if we could have someone check it out, they didn’t seem to really care about our situation. Same goes with the noise!!! The walls are paper thin, you’re able to hear everything! Whether it be arguing, people having sex, babies crying, etc. I made a complaint and nothing was done about it. Also, the ongoing construction is ridiculous. I understand you guys are trying to make this a better looking place but being woken up 7am just to hear drilling being done & other things is annoying. & for some reason they’re raising the rent up that’s why I’m planning to move out of here as soon as possible. Don’t waste your money on these apartments!

I have lived in these units for the last year and love them. They are one of the most spacious units I have seen in San Diego. The building is dated but well kept. Management is attentive and does a good job at keeping the buildings clean.

I stumbled across these apartments and was interested, so I wanted to call just for more general information. I called a couple times over the span of few days because there was always no answer, sending me to voicemail every time times. I then found their website with another number and called that one. Someone finally answered, although it wasn't a pleasant interaction at all. 

I politely introduced myself and began explaining how I found the available listed unit, was interested, etc. To make it short, the woman who answered (I didn't hear her name clearly, Jenny I think it was or something like that) was very rude and had an bad attitude for no reason. She gave me no information at all, and just sounded like it was a hassle to speak on the phone. Anyway, any interest I had in renting here is completely gone from the horrible customer service alone. If that phone call reflects what the office management is like here, then I don't see how anybody would want to live here at all.

Is a really nice place to live at, however they are always feeling you that they have to fix the plumbing and the water is always out. They also fix the pool every once and a while but they decide to fix it during the summer! Who does that?! The manager is really rude and they take forever to fix the maintaince requests.

Management is more interested in charging you then supporting you in an over priced apartment.

Don’t let the sleight of hand technique on photos of the interior-only take away from the army of homeless who loot patios and vehicles of which hang out steps from the exterior property line.

Little efforts for security or safety lighting.

The staff are extremely unreasonable and clearly interested solely in having 0 vacancies. They take advantage of the lack of vacancies in Point Loma to give no consideration to customers.
I applied there and I was extremely clear that my current lease was not coming up for three weeks and that was my desired move in date. Imagine my surprise when they decide that, no, what I actually meant was less than a week in the future. That's basically demanding that people either wait til literally the last minute to find a place to live or they pay two rents for several weeks.
But, I was willing to do that since there are no other options in the area. Then, they decided I needed to provide a cashier's check as a holding fee, in person, despite quite clearly having no issue accepting digital payment for the application fee. This is late Saturday. What's not open on Sunday? Banks, that's what. So, after asking them politely to wait until I get off work on Monday, they decide to give the apartment away
Do these seem like the kind of people that will approach any issue that comes up with stellar customer service?

NOT WORTH THE PRICE!!You cannot have curtains up for extra privacy or anything on your walls, without a written consent from the landlord prior to lease being issued. They will not tell you this. They give notice of entry same day and mark it as if it was given out a week ago. Cops are called on kids for playing outside. Parking spaces are not big enough for you to comfortably to get out of the vehicle let alone enough space to pull in and out without scraping your car against a pole or someone elses car. You would be lucky to find parking in the afternoon if you do not have a spot under the car port. You will have to park on the street just outside the apartment complex. The leasing office is rarely open. Pest control is supposed to come every Wednesday and they never show up. Fire alarm and Gas detectors are supposed to be checked and batteries are supposed to be replaced they do not ever come and do that like they say. Walls are thin, so everybody can hear you and you can hear them. People here are extremely nosey so be prepared for people looking through your windows and up through the crack in the balcony. Heads up if you do rent here during the summer the apartments get to about 100 degrees inside even with the dining room fan on and windows open. At nights it 10x worse.

This complex is horrible! No maintenance, no security. Cockroaches and spiders everywhere. Too pricey for old-as-a-dinosaur cabinets. The manager ladies are the worst too. They don't care about you, just your money and their friends they have living there!
There are bedbugs and winter green does not take action on the matter and my room was flooded with the rains in December.
Several stolen motorcycles from the "secure" parking garage. Cameras are somehow all "corrupted" afterwards. Avoid at all costs unless you like your property being stolen.

Be aware.
I have leased here 6 months (Sept-Feb) and actually lived in the unit for 4. This is a list of things I found unacceptable for a place this expensive:

- Throughout my stay, the gate code never changed (they said they change it monthly). That meant homeless people knowing it, sleeping or hanging out, almost all delivery guys enter and I find them at my doorstep.

- Fire alarms drill is illogically lengthy and goes on during working hours, while working remotely, and has gone to 4 straight hours on and off.

- Hot water stopped twice for over 6 hours, complete water shutdown happened once for 5 hours, within 4 months.

-  A neighbor disrupted my optic fiber internet and because the unit did not have cellular coverage (AT&T and Tmobile) I was not able to work on the site. Refused to allow me to work in the business center while the internet was scheduled to be fixed (4 total days until the issue was resolved). No cooperation.

- They did not consider travel ban when I was trying to come back to the US in the pandemic for my last month, and required a 60 days notice and I was forced to pay full March lease (an additional month not on the contract despite the fact that the issue was from border control).

- Upon moving out I thoroughly cleaned my unit, pictures attached. 15 days later, I receive a statement for carpet cleaning ($75) which was used for only 4 months, another $145 for touch up paint throughout, patio deck, and exterior front door & frame. and then another $160 for cleaning my apartment, which I paid a cleaner $170 to do for me before leaving.

Not referring nor advising anyone to stay here, I should have taken other reviews on the property management in consideration.

Two years at Regents Court is a nightmare. Four years in University City, I NEVER HATED ANY COMMUNITY LIKE THIS. I am glad I moved out and ended this madness. Although I loved my first two months here with the old leasing team led by Christian, everything went downhill rapidly after they started the renovation of the leasing office, changing multiple managers and a dozen employees.

IT IS NOT A SAFE PLACE! Some stranger approached my two female suitemates in the garage while they were loading equipment off of their car. The stranger accosted and tailed them while they were carrying the cameras and walking back to our unit, they had to knock on our neighbor's door pretending it's our unit and call me to pick them up at the other side of the building and call the police. The stranger ran off from the stairway and exited to the street after hearing my roommate calling the police. We emailed the property management about this, and they claimed they would do a gate code change, which never happened. And this is not the only scary thing that happened here. You can get people going door-to-door trying to make you donate money late night or asking if you want to buy some candy???

THE NOISE LEVEL IS RIDICULOUS. I stayed in a unit close to the basketball court in Doyle Community Park for my first year here. Almost every day, people play basketball at 2 am, 6 am, 11 pm, and 12 pm. Teenagers and homeless are the frequent visitors to the park; the former blasts out music and parties through the night, the latter screams and harasses morning runners and attracts multiple police cars. There were sports events every night till 11 pm during summer and fall; movie nights in the field once a month. You can hear all that, and noise-canceling headphones are not useful. I suffered from severe anxiety and insomnia while living in that unit, which was not cheap. The management told me to deal with it myself. I send countless emails to the park manager, but no resolution.
Great experience living here. The staff was was really on it! and I absolutely loved the amenities this place offers!

I never write reviews but I have to this time because you all deserve to know what happened to me to make informed decisions. 

I  stayed here for one night to visit my friend. Guess what, if all four guest parking spaces and street parking are taken and you have no choice but to park inside their residential parking structure, your car will be towed within 24 hours. I had to pay $352 to get my car back. 

So basically, if you live here you probably want to think twice about accommodating guests. The people at leasing office were very unprofessional. When the question to them is "Don't you think you should make sure that your residents are aware of the choice of getting a visitor parking permit for their visitors?", their answer is a big careless "No." Getting visitor parking permit for is not written in the contract either. 

So they don't care about making your living experience easy. You have to go out and ask them and fight for it, and you don't get what you need. 

By the way the gate of the parking structure is very narrow. You have to be extremely slow and careful when you enter so that you don't scratch your car to the iron gate. 

Rate is also higher than other apts in the same area. 

Make wise choices.

I've lived at Regents Court for 2  years and the one word with which I can describe this place is quality. Many of my friends live in other apartments/townhouses nearby and none can live up to the quality of Regents Court. The complex is very clean and the amenities are always in good shape. This complex likes to upgrade communal areas/amenities which shows that they care for their residents; they just renovated the hallways and recently repainted. The leasing office associates are very nice and the maintenance team responds to service requests in a timely manner. This is the perfect place for UCSD students as the first shuttle stop is directly across the street. It's also walking distance to McDonald's, Costa Verde Center, and the Westfield UTC mall. Overall, it's a great place to live.

I set an appointment for a tour through their website online and it was confirmed. When I arrive I’m told by a security guard that happened to show up that they’re on break for an hour, the entire duration of my tour… Imagine traveling from a far location for an appointment that was CONFIRMED with no one showing up…

Everything in apartments and outside are really old like all the appliances, doors, windows and so on. Gazillions of seagulls are everywhere in pools and on the roofs. 

Management really reluctant to do any fixes - if you use app to make a request you can forget about it immediately if you go to the leasing center and demand something probably will happen. 

You can forget about deposit the next day you paid it. Doesn't matter how big it was they always find enough dirty stains and scratches somewhere under a sink to keep it all.

The management is absolutely horrible. They are rude and do not respond half the time. The water is almost always going through an 'emergency shut off'. The apartment we live in is out not updated which is fine, except we pay the same price as those in an updated apartment. They recently raised our rent 7%. Food trucks taking up handicap parking spots and parked with loud generators right outside your windows are a weekly occurrence. Loud music coming from the pool is a daily occurrence and goes on for hours on end. Want to spend a nice sunday studying? Sorry. Want to chill by the pool and listen to your own music or read? Sorry. Bottom line, they have set up this complex like a freshman dorm when many of the residents are working people or families. For the price we pay, a little respect would be lovely. 

p.s,
Whose genius idea was it to put a dog kennel right next to apartments and mailboxes...It smells.

Poor management skills... I get a letter 24 hr before tell me no parking in any complex spot for the next 2 days because of re-striping or YOU WILL BE TOWED!!
There is about 10 street spots. When does a place do this? How about a roller so no one has to move or one area at a time. Completely ridiculous

Lived there for 4 years since it was called Trieste apartment. I really love the location and the setting of those apartments. I mostly like the settings where a door from living room and bed room both go to balcony which gives you much more light. But I want to stress the amazing management especially Giselle and Nik they have been so great with addressing my issues and work with me on anything I throw at them!! when I decided to move out, the apartment I was moving to had renovation issues and and pushed its' availability by 9 day. My apartment at Axiom was already rented to another applicant. I was in big trouble as I didn't have place to go for 8 days!! well Giselle and Nik actually worked with me and made the contractor that is going to renovate my apartment shorten his time to accommodate me for the extra days until my next apartment becomes available. And they did this for someone who is leaving their community!! I 
5 starts for this community. You will never regret moving there

I love it here! The management team is great and always accessible(monday-friday)in case any issues arise and to make sure things are going well. Its been a fantastic experience. There is a sense of community here. They hold occasional events for tenants, and the food cart comes by once a week, where renters congregate. I have met a number of very nice people while living here. The maine pool is like a weekend in Cabo San Lucas; with plush greenery and cabana style seating, it is an amazingly relaxing experience. The work out area saves me money on a monthly gym membership, they have everything I need. Also, maintenance is always on call incase of an emergency. Overall it has been an amazing experience and I look forward to renewing my lease and enjoying another year here :)

Apartment was not ready for move in. I have lived at Valentia for nearly 3 months now and when I tell you it is NOT worth the rent cost, trust me on this. I moved into the apartment with a termite infestation and am still dealing with this nightmare. I requested one month free rent in return for the extensive troubles (moving in with a corroded/leaking faucet, termite infestation, unreachable attic door open letting bugs in, damaged mirror, dry rotted bedroom door to patio, being told via email the wrong mailbox at move in, and the list goes on and on), and I have only been compensated $500, despite moving into the unlivable conditions, and rent is more than 6x that for a 1br apartment. Termite droppings literally come out of my vent and I need to clean them up daily. At move in, I let them know that the termite infested door and frame to my bedroom needed to be replaced ASAP and it still has yet to get done. The vendor came today, but had not been informed that the entire door frame would need to be replaced due to the extensive termite damage, so they’ll have to come back tomorrow. I find that lack of communication interesting. I have had to miss work over this, and people are constantly coming in and out of my apartment to fix things or treat termites. Shea Properties, please do better. The amount of stress this causes is truly unjust.

My husband and I have lived at Valentia for almost a year. Hands down these are the nicest and largest apartments in the area that allow dogs. I believe every apartment has vaulted ceilings and a huge patio. Plus having a full size washer and dryer in the unit is amazing. I really wish the kitchen and bathroom were a bit larger and had more storage. We are also on the second floor of a building facing west so we don't get a lot of light in the apartment. Other than that these apartments are great.

Staff in the office is very attentive and any issues we've had, be that with residents or maintenance, have been resolved quickly. The community is quiet and people tend to keep to themselves, but are still friendly. Lots of college kids and young families here, but even with college kids parties are rarely an issue.The community has 2 pools, 3 hot tubs, and plenty of seating outdoors. 

I would definitely recommend Valentia to anyone looking for an apartment. These apartments are a great size and the price isn't terrible for the area.

Living here has been a pleasure! Not only are the apartments beautiful and not typical apartments more like condos, the staff is friendly and attentive. Grounds are always well kept. Security at night.

Ideally situated in La Jolla/UTC between the I-5fwy and I-805fwy; less than 4.5mi from the beach,  is a beautiful neighborhood called Reinnessance La Jolla. In this lush tree-lined community,  right across from a sprawling park, recreation center, and library,  are Valentia Apartments.  Units are spacious, with thoughtful layouts and descent sound proofing. The property has high-end amenities throughought and is well-maintained.

Pros? Safe, auiet, beautiful,  spacious, good location, friendly staff.

Cons? Crammped guest parking, shared water/sewer/trash bill, crazy high rent with huge annual increases.

I've been a resident for 4  years and love it here. The neighbors are friendly and you see many of them regularly at the pool or grill or at the beach. The best feature is of course the beach just across the street! Some neighbors have been here more than a decade and some have left and come back. Great place to live.

Great place to live. It's extremely close to the beach and within walking distance of downtown Del Mar. The neighbors are pleasant and friendly. The complex itself is very well maintained with the staff being on call and the manager is very friendly. Overall a great place to live.

For all you beach lovers out there, this one is for you!!  Situated across the street from prestigious Del Mar beach, there are ocean views available (one of which I have from my second story studio) Pool on premises. Safe. Walking distance to the beach , city of Del Mar, dog beach,Del Mar  racetrack, , restaurants and parks. A true "find".
This place is absolutely the worst place we have ever lived.Everything about it is awful.We could not wait for our move and are so happy in our new place.DO NOT MOVE HERE.
Regents La Jolla has an excellent maintenance team. They are quick to respond when something needs to be repaired. We appreciate their friendliness, too.

Many persons own their appartment here. It might indicate that the place is good for long term staying. There are many oversensitive ears and watching eyes here, that is sometimes good, sometimes annoying. The two beautiful pools are the most desserted pools in the area. I dont know why....
I love living here.  It’s beautiful, clean, carefully maintained, and friendly.  Going on my seventh happy year here at Regents La Jolla.

This place is my personal heaven since my hubby and I arrived 2017 from Chicago.  Spacious layout, top appliances, delightful patio looking down on lushly-landscaped courtyard, super maintenance, responsive management.  Even great neighbors!  Manager Julian effective and accessible; office staff Bianca, Faith, Dane, Angela so professional.  Did I mention superb maintenance?  Love it here!
Regents La Jolla continues to be my happy place, beautiful apartment, lovely grounds, responsive management, even great neighbors.  Six years here and counting!
This place is a delight.  Excellent and responsive maintenance and management, beautifully kept up, quiet, clean, safe—a real pleasure to live here.
Garbage service and overpriced. Waited weeks to address the mold in our apartment then left the job unfinished. Please don’t move here.

Please avoid this place management is awful and service is really bad nothing gets fixed or works the only good thing about this place is the girl who actually did the tour. Equipment is awful my clothes got destroyed from using the dryer and still not functional but nobody is willing to fix it or address the issue . This place is nothing but a headache

Overall it is a nice community with great club house and fitness center. The apartment is spacious, repair is generally quick and the people in leasing office are nice. However, the soundproof of the apartment is poor.

You can put lipstick on a pig, but it is still a pig beneath the surface. Think twice before leasing here. 

I have been a resident for nearly two years and had more inconveniences during this period than 10  years in a rental up north. 

Get used to FREQUENT water shutoffs (that's NO WATER, no toilet, no showers, NO WATER) "emergency" inspections in your apartment unit, structural and alarm testings, garage leaks that damage your auto, etc. A summer long of power washing and painting noise, jackhammering fountains, mandatory car movement in the garage to accommodate workers. 

The latest? A gas leak on the property 3/29/19 - residents in at least 3 buildings without hot water/heat for 5-7 days. 

Lipstick on a pig - you've been warned.

The management at this place is horrible. They don’t follow the rules and regulations. They give you trouble all the time and sometimes they enter your apartment without notice and create a mess in your apartment and on the top of that they never call or inform you that maintenance ever enter in your apartment. When you call the office they will say yes we allowed them and sorry not to inform you and just hang up. Be careful with the management at this property

Regents La Jolla is a fantastic apartment complex to live in. The complex is situated close to the Westfield UTC mall and only a 10 minute drive from the beach making it a convenient but also relaxing place to live in. Regents comes with great amenities such as a gym, two poolside cabanas, a lounge, sports club, movie theater, and dance studio--all of which (except the gym) can be reserved for private use with a fee. Not to mention that the movie theater plays movies that are not in theaters BUT not yet released on DVD (it's that in-between sweet spot). The complex itself is very clean and held to a high standard of luxury that only La Jolla can offer. 

I'm docking off 1 star due to the leasing office being difficult to work with every now and then. Some days the Concierge gives off the vibe that he/she does not want to talk to you. Additionally, I've also emailed Regents Operations managers regarding issues and have never heard back. 

Despite the staff being sometimes difficult to work with, Regents is a fantastic place to live in.

Management is unorganized and rude!  They had no record of our moveout notice and moveout date.   I had to show them the email they had sent to me confirming our moveout date. The entire time she was looking she was condescending and talked down to us.   Not until she found our notice and had to eat her words, did she try to recover and apologize.  Amongst getting things fixed which was a pain as a tenant, I would say Management is the worst.

Great compared to the apartments nearby. We moved here my third year at SDSU and stayed for the rest of our degrees because it was spacious, offered 2 parking spaces, has AC, and was so quiet compared to the surrounding area. It was a sad day when we moved out.

Signed my lease at a decent rate at the time and now they want to increase it to the maximum allowable. Claims it’s below market and it’s not. I can - and have - found better places for the rate they’re asking. Not even offering a re-sign rate lower than going month to month. The unit was not clean when I moved in and had to clean it myself and repairs had to still be made after I had moved in. There’s no security patrol. Security is off-site and won’t get to you until hours later. The complex is not gated either. That said, I haven’t had an issue with vandalism or theft so at least the neighborhood is safe on its own. There’s no guest parking. I do have to give credit to the maintenance staff - they’re great.

We love that our apartment is in a great location, so commute time is easier for work and even for university.  This apartment complex's location makes this place the ideal apartment to live in!  For instance, there's a Vons, Walmart, PetSmart, Banfield Pet Hospital, and Fry's just a mere hop, skip, and throw away -- many folks just walk to them since they're all less than a mile away.  Moreover, within a 5-mile radius are the public library, numerous eateries, wonderful employment opportunities, various universities, an airport to earn your private pilot's license, a hospital, and some cool places to visit.  Another highlight of our apartment is the wonderful pet policy -- no breed restrictions and no weight restrictions, plus you can have two pets per apartment!  Besides that, there are a number of community events in our apartment complex, like free pizza night and free sundae weekends.  Amenities include a fitness center, a pool, a tennis court, as well as a movie theater you can rent to host events for guests.  There are many families in our apartment complex, and the neighborhood is great for trick-or-treating.  We're also a military family, so this apartment complex is situated close to military family communities (like Murphy Canyon, Serra Mesa, and Linda Vista military housing areas), which is lovely because living in our civilian apartment complex enables us to get to be away from the base and yet still be close to other military families and friends nearby.  Yet another positive aspect about this apartment complex is that they provide cash prizes or bonuses for referrals.  Plus, there are opportunities to buy and sell items and/or services via the apartment complex's community board.  Our apartment complex is also very good about maintenance and upkeep of the common and public grounds -- for example, they just refurbished all the exterior lights in all the apartment buildings and facades, which thereby makes all the common passageways very well-lit for safety.  The only downside to our apartment is that because it's such an AWESOME place (this apartment's the best-kept secret to apartment living in San Diego!), rent continually climbs each year making it very, very difficult to set any funds aside for any contingencies or even emergencies.  Sooner or later folks are pushed out because of the ever-increasing rent, and you'll be forced to relocate to a cheaper place that could never ever hold a candle to this AWESOMELY wonderful apartment complex.

I lived in Cambridge Park for two years. At first, the apartment was middle of the pack in pricing at 1875 for a two bedroom. 

With its beautiful crown molding, high ceilings, and walk-in closets, it was amazing for its price. The wooden floors were easy to maintain, the cherry cabinets and stainless steel appliances beautiful. Its pull and barbecques were exquisitely maintained and its plentiful dog waste stations made walking our hound so much better.

The winter was a bit cold and the summers hot, thanks to the shoddily fit windows and the the door's lack of a breeze guard. 

When renewing, they raised my price 110 dollars. This put it near the top for its area, but still under the largest competitors. Come renewal this year, however, the price was raised 150 dollars, putting it on par with its most expensive competitors -- and the price of renting an actual house. 

Thus, we have regrettably decided to save money and move. Cambridge Park remains an amazing place -- if you can afford it.

Apartment is great! Especially for only being 700 square feet, the layout of the 1/1 is perfect! The only down fall to this community is PARKING! Long wait list for an additional spot, and no guest parking. You have to park outside of the complex. Also alot of the assigned parking spots are extremely small.

I love living in the Cambridge Park Apartments. They are located in the center of San Diego but up the hill above Qualcomm Stadium in a well maintained quite neighborhood. They offer large apartments with lots of amenities. The complex has tennis courts, pool, jacuzzi, business center, putting green and a theater. The units have washer and dryers and are pet friendly. I'm so happy I decided to move to this complex. Anytime I have company over they always love where I live. Some of my friends are thinking about moving here too. I am planning on living here for a long time.

DO NOT move in here... Worst place i have lived in San Diego to date.
Here are some details of all of the negative experiences we experienced:
- BUGS: One week into our lease when we encountered 2 cockroaches, one of them being a 3 inch flying "waterbug" in my bedroom. Huge spiders. Silverfish everywhere.
- WATER SMELLS LIKE ROTTEN EGGS, clearly sulfur in their pipes.
- THIN WALLS & DISRESPECTFUL NEIGHBORS: To sum up 6  months of how miserable we were, our upstairs neighbors were disrespectful, rude, and threatening. There were easily 4  people living in the apt above us. They continuously blasted music that would shake the walls of our place from 5pm til 11pm or later. I had called the overnight patrol, they did nothing. You could also hear their engine revving shaking your bedroom wall at 5am. Hard to enjoy living life or getting any sleep. Only got worse when upstairs neighbors got 2 husky puppies who continuously scratched at the floor and barked. They proceeded to park blocking our driveway and when we were kind enough to ask them to move, they refused to move the car and threatened to find out where we live and were very aggressive. When we expressed our concerns to the leasing office, they said they would reach out to them and that we should call to get the car towed next time we have someone blocking our spot. We felt very unsafe. Austin did not provide us any solution rather than offering us to pay hefty fees to terminate our lease or move apartments. Very unfortunate that we were the tenants being punished for our neighbors unruly behavior. 
-PARKING: Horrendous. Neighbors are disrespectful and will park 3 cars in a one person driveway. 
-CONSTRUCTION: It basically never ends in this community. Water pipes, tree trimming, patio replacements, painting the exteriors, replacing toilets. Also, construction equipment parked there for months on end take up the few available street spots or the no parking signs.
-APARTMENT ISSUES: Broken dryer. Leak in the bathroom ceiling. Leaking water heater and gas leak. Fire detectors fall off ceiling.  
-DEPOSIT: Do not expect anything back. Put aside a few hundred to pay hefty fees to replace entire carpet. Even though during our 2 move out inspections the maintenance guy shared that only 2 out of our 3 bedrooms needed to be replaced. But guess they went ahead and did all 3 even though it was "new" upon our move in.
Nice and quiet, close to freeways and downtown,....

We have lived in this community for going on four years. The management has always been helpful. The maintenance crew respond quickly and do very well with dogs (they give them treats and a card saying they did a good job). The main issue with this community is the parking. The street parking is near impossible and could do well with a different system, I.e. parking lot style spaces rather than parallel parking. 
We live in one of the older buildings so some fixtures aren't as substantial as others. Overall the safety and atmosphere of the community trumps all else. For the price - you can't do much better and still get to live with your furry friends.

The location of this apartment complex is really great. It's right by multiple freeway entrances, hospitals, and very close the Mesa community college. The community is really nice and you don't hear loud neighbors or blasting music, mostly the sounds of kids playing. The people who work here are always friendly and the neighborhood is safe. You can actually have pets unlike a lot of other apartments. And you can do your laundry in your unit, which is a big plus!

I have lived here for 4 months now, the staff here are always friendly and helpful. The surrounding area is quiet considering the hospital almost next door and the common areas are well maintained. Nice family style apartments.
The apartment is like a palace and huge. Bathroom is like a bedroom. Kitchen is so huge that I love it.
Friendly front desk and maintenance team, prompt responses to requests, surrounding area is pretty and well maintained, they also have fun contests for the residents to win gift cards

Have lived here for almost two years and intend to stay.  My one bedroom is spacious and comfortable.  The large patio area and separate laundry room complete an ideal living space.  The lovely grounds are continuously manicured by the landscape team.  If a maintenance call is necessary, the response is prompt and professional.

Our experience at La Serena has been outstanding. The complex is situated in a beautiful, quiet and safe location.  The controlled access (gated) and convenient parking is a plus! Ground maintenance crews are on site consistently to ensure the outdoor area is neat and presentable. La Serena management and maintenance staff is incredibly friendly. Suggestions and issues are dealt with quickly and courteously. We frequent the pool, hot tub, tennis court, and workout facility; wonderful community amenities that most complexes do not offer. You will not find a better place in RB to call home! 

Other noteworthy features: in-unit washer and dryer, large patio, suburban feel, beautiful landscape

The apartment is very spacious with a larger kitchen than most apartment complexes. The units have a large patio with two different doors. Overall the apartment is very nice. The downside is that there is a lot of spiders... It feels like I'm killing one three times a week. My unit is on the first story which might explain that problem.

excellent customer service, quite and clean area, nice and quite neighbor. I think its safe for children and its a cross street from med-hi school.   
less than a mile to super market and shopping area, 2 mile to shopping mall.

The Pacific at Mission Bay is by far my favorite apartment I've lived in. This is my third apartment in San Diego and I couldn't have better things to say. Cassandra and Sara are wonderful, the apartments are HUGE, and the pool is always clean. Work orders are filled quickly and I never feel unsafe (since they have patrol officers at night!). Thanks Pacific at Mission Bay!

Straight shot to Pacific Ocean and freeways leading to various local and out-of-town destinations -- mountains, desert, Mexico. Walk to Mission Bay, golf, tennis, schools. Gated; pool; Jacuzzi; parking; small pets allowed; onsite, multimachine laundry rooms; weight and cardio rooms; computer-equipped office space; very well-kept grounds; caring, responsive staff.

Everything here is wonderful! The apartments are huge and constantly updated, the grounds are beautiful, the staff treats you like family, they are pet friendly...even large breed dogs, and they have q fantastic location to everything!!!! Would highly recommend living here!!!!

It's a good apartment with a friendly staff and a pretty good location. Right across the street from a basketball court, a golf course, and about a mile from the beach. One negative is no a/c in a lot of the units its very hot in san diego and with no a/c it makes it very uncomfortable sometimes. They say they have a weight room but its not a weight room no bench press or really anything and the highest dumb bell is one 25lb dumb bell. The pool is very nice and refreshing and the rose creek bike path is right outside with some awesome views.

Overall a pretty great place to live. The rooms are pretty spacious and the living room is huge. Lots of great facilities, including a pool, hot tub, barbecues, party room, and a gym. There's also a paid laundry room, though I would prefer to have laundry in the apartment itself. The place feels very safe, the scenery is beautiful, and it's overall just a nice place to live. It's also very clean and the community is friendly.

There are a few drawbacks. Parking can be a hassle because unless you pay for a garage, you only get one space per apartment regardless of whether it's a one or two bedroom, and parking on the street can be extremely difficult at times (and expensive if you forget about the street sweeping, which is every week on Grand for some reason). Maintenance is often very slow - the one elevator on the South side of the building was broken down for months before it was finally fixed, and we waited over a month for certain small things to be fixed within our apartment. They also charge a $50 "pet rent" every month on TOP of the pet deposit, which I think is absurd, and makes it just that much more expensive living in San Diego.

Please save your money and headache with a different apartment complex. Had termites issue during my one year tenant. There is a lot of noise due to a busy street but it's worse because there is no security overseering the loud noises from neighbors even though they said they would have 24 hour surveillance. In addition, it is very easy for strangers to come and open the window to unlock the door. There was one incident where a homeless person went upstairs and slept the night on the end of the apartments. I would not even bother reviewing this apartment but after not being able to get my security deposit back and charging me on top of the deposit for bogus reasons, I had enough of them using petty ways to gain money. Do no bother with the pre-inspection appointment to avoid getting charged on any damages. They will not give you any results. Thus, they will ignore you and not give you an explanation.

I moved in May of 2016. Within a few days I started seeing cockroaches everywhere which I've never had in my life. Management had Terminix spray and they said they would die and be gone for at least a couple months. I started seeing dead and dying cockroaches everywhere the next day which I grossly had to pick up with paper towels and throw away. Less than a week later they were back. The office had Terminix spray again and they promised they would be gone for good, same thing within 5 days they were back. Now 7 months later they have to spray every week and I am constantly picking up dead cockroaches.... Laundry machines are often broken..... Now that we are in December I see that the apartments actually don't have heat and its an igloo in my place at night... I tried to get out of the lease and they refused to let me out.... I think the property manager was incompetent and slow to reply before now we just got a new property manager and she is even worse. I can not wait for May of 2017 so I can get out of here!
I live here now and can't leave because of my lease but there are cockroaches everywhere. Do not live here! It is horrible they are everywhere.

We've been living here for about five months now.  It is a great place to live.  The staff is super courteous, even with just general morning greetings.  It was very easy to apply and move in, we moved from Florida and had to communicate via email and phone, the process couldn't have been made any smoother.  The apartment itself is very spacious for a studio with a building plan that makes sense, making it very cozy.  The outside aesthetic is nicely painted, and each building has a very unique gathering area (one pool area, one grilling area, and one nice fountain / Adirondack chair gathering area).  I love the Orange and Grey building colors, and plants that habitat the ground floor.  The staff is great!  Any issues that did pop up were resolved quickly and easily, and any upgrades made were well notified.  It's close to my, now favorite, Ramen (!!!) restaurant (literally across the street), and a bunch of other great markets and restaurants down the street.  Can't say enough nice things about the place, did I mention the staff was awesome?

First, I'll say the staff is excellent. Very friendly and responsive to tenant needs. Michell was very helpful throughout the entire process and the move in was quick and simple.

The remodel is what sold me. Nice hardwood floors, cabinetry and paint. Windows seem to be brand new and the blinds are also very clean. Appliances are super clean and work as expected. The interior will not disappoint.

Mailbox and parking are in a convenient location. The exterior is freshly painted and adds some color to the surrounding neighborhood.

I also like that the staff has even more improvements planned. Pool renovation, community grills, re-striping the parking lot, new washer dryers, and more.

Surprisingly there's also a lot of stuff in walking distance including a grocery store, gas station, dry cleaners, and your choice of walk-able nearby restaurants are sushi, ramen, Thai, Chinese, Korean BBQ, Indian, and an awesome taco shop. 

In my opinion there are no cons to this place, but worth noting the below for future potential tenants:
- The community is right on Clairemont Mesa Blvd. So if you're sensitive to street noise it's worth thinking about. I've noticed traffic dies down by 10PM and is almost non-existent by midnight
- Studios are decently sized, but the door/window locations force you to get creative with the floor plan

I recently visited a townhome that was just perfect. The design was modern yet cozy, with a great kitchen and a comfortable living area. The bedrooms were peaceful and the master suite was luxurious, especially the bathroom.

The outdoor patio was a lovely spot to relax, and the location was convenient for shopping and dining. The community was welcoming, and the townhome had beautiful details everywhere.

Overall, this place is fantastic and I highly recommend it for a top-notch living experience.

We have lived here almost 9 years.  Management and Ownership was okay
 in the past.  HOWEVER, Greystar is making everyone miserable.  Massive rent increases.  Management won’t even provide light bubs.  They recently raised garbage rates and now charge extra for pest control.  These units are MASSIVELY overpriced.  They also don’t care about their tenants.  We will be moving out.  This place is NOT worth what they are charging.

We’ve lived at Ocean Air for almost a year and we’ve had a great experience. New property management came in shortly after we moved in and they’ve been phenomenal ever since! Quickly responsive to any needs we have, friendly and caring. The complex is quiet, safe and the grounds are kept very clean. Maintenance is quick to jump on any repairs ever needed. It definitely feels like a community here with everyone enjoying and taking care of the nice amenities Ocean Air offers.  The pool, gym and outdoor gas grills are our favorites. Would highly recommend these apartments & townhomes! (March 2024)

We moved to Ocean Air in November 2014. Our apartment is nice, but our experience here has been ruined by the property management. 

Since we moved in, our next door neighbor has used her garage as a living space, which violates the lease. She leaves her 2 young kids in the garage for hours at a time, which is right below our living room, so we constantly hear them screaming, crying, and arguing. 

We made a complaint to our manager, and after the neighbor ignored the manager several times, she was given an eviction notice. She was not evicted and the noise continued. Prior to renewing our lease, we wanted to make sure our neighbor was moving out.  The Regional Manager of Pinnacle Property Management said that because the eviction process takes so long, they were going to send the neighbor a non-renewal notice instead. Based what she said, we renewed our lease for another year. 

Guess what? Pinnacle never sent the non-renewal notice, and they allowed the neighbor to renew her lease. When I asked why, the Regional Manager stated that she never told me that the neighbor was being given a non-renewal notice. This was a lie. I talked to Pinnacle’s Regional Vice President, who asked us to send him our complaint in writing, and he would try to help. 

Before we had a chance to respond, we received a letter from Pinnacle’s eviction attorney. It said that our complaints were disruptive to management staff and to other tenants, and that any future contacts regarding our tenancy must be in writing and through the attorney’s office only. The letter said that this action is being taken to protect the quiet enjoyment of all the residents of Ocean Air. Apparently, our quiet enjoyment hasn’t been a concern to Pinnacle.

We pay $2,500 a month for a 1-bedroom apartment and no amenities. We pay our rent on time and keep to ourselves. We expected upscale treatment for the price, but instead, the management took extreme and unnecessary measures against us for asking them to perform normal management duties.
Good job!!!! good job) Amazing property and a great location.
Great staff and the place felt like home. I enjoy the pool area with family waiting for our laundry to be done. 10/10 would recommend anyone to live here. Best place in San Diego!

New management has taken over and done nothing to fix the preexisting problems. They were, however, successful at increasing the rent substantially. As I type this, there is currently another problem that has been brought to the attention of management that is outside of my window. A gang of teenaged potheads turned a porch that was once used as the mail box location into a bong and brew head quarters. They are found here at all hours of the day since school is out. You come home from work, and there they are. You hear a loud noise that wakes you up at 12:30 a.m., and there they are. Bongs in plain sight as the smoke blows right into your child's room, forcing you to close the windows in the hot summer since the air conditioning unit does reach back there. The other morning I left my apartment to go to work and saw a masked teenager with a hoodie checking car doors inside the apartment parking lot. The time was 5:00 a.m. in the morning! I reported this to the front office, and they said that they would increase security, but of course that didn't happen. My neighbor has moved out, and I'm on my way as well. I hope this helps you make a decision.

This apartment complex is pretty nice. Plenty of light. Everything inside the apartments are pretty new and good condition. It's located below a catholic school playground so u can hear the kids during recess if u don't mind kids screaming. No need for clock inside the house because the church bell is loud enough. One assigned parking and tenant pays for water, gas and electric bill.

The apartment is amazing and beautiful and the staff is outstanding.... The areas of the apartment is clean and well maintained .... Also can see great view of the pool from your apartment and has beautiful backyard with tall palm tress....
Mission Pacific Apartments have an great staff, they are friendly and hard working. From the apartment you can see an great view of the pool and the nice clean area.

The staff is great but the residents need to learn how to pick up after their dogs!!

I especially love the maintenance staff!  They are always out there making the place look nicer and are always so friendly!

DO. NOT. LIVE. HERE. The complex is full of snake employees waiting in the grass. Lied to us about our move out inspection. The maintenance guy came in to do the pre check inspection and said “you’ve lived here almost 2 years, we’re not going to charge you for paint”..Over $300 later for paint on our deposit refund. 

Maintenance is beyond unreliable. Put in multiple request to fix a broken dishwasher that leaked onto the floor. About 4 or 5 days went by before they sent a confirmation of the job to be completed and it wasn’t. Then we repeated the process, more days went by and got a refurbished dishwasher that the maintenance guy put together and shot water all over our apartment and made the girlfriend hold the hose spraying water while he left to figure out how to shut it off. People drive through the complex like it’s nascar. DO NOT let you’re kids play in the street.

Overall this community is just really bad. The quality of life you’re going to experience here is terrible for what you’re going to pay. If you made it to the end of this review, please look somewhere else. This complex and this company is not it.

Since the day I’ve moved in I’ve had complaints that have went unsolved for months. Pest in apartment since day one, refrigerator doesn’t work and took weeks for them to even come out still doesnt work properly, paper thin walls I hear my neighbors cellphone ring and 5am alarm EVERYDAY! Heat is on 80 just to feel it. Ac is on 60 to cool down and you can feel the air the air coming through the windows up to 3 ft away. SDGE will be hundreds. They just will falsely complete or just delete out the system to clear. Bathroom smells like mold and mildew. Packages get stolen often and office doesn’t care. Parcel container is a joke and you have to pay to protect packages that still get stolen and delivered in wrong box!
No property manger on site let alone on property because they don’t have one. All temp employees and very rude. Will talk to a new person everyday!

This is the Shashkov Family from apartment 3324. We are tired of living here because in the span of two months of living here our apartment smells like marijuana and cigarettes (this is a smoking free community). When we turn on the air conditioner the vents fill the apartment with this smell, and when we open the windows for fresh air it fills our apartment. We have a newborn daughter and this has been a problem since my wife was pregnant. We call and arrive in the main office everyday, and still nothing has been done to fix our issue. My apartment is nice. Its just a little small. You can hear outside noise a lot but it's not too bad. The pool and gym are really nice. But parking late at night if you have more than one car is hectic.

The pools are reminiscent of resort-style pools surrounded by palm trees and jacuzzi to unwind after work.  The on-site gym includes a sauna and inspiration to get back into the gym when getting there is no hassle.  The staff is extremely helpful, professional and responsive. Ample restaurants and stores within walking-distance in a centralized location.  Everything you would appreciate on vacation becomes everything you have at home.  You and your friends will love where you live!

Liliana has been amazing with my application process and has had the best customer service.She has gone over and beyond to make sure I got everything that I needed to submitted. She has helped me every step of the way in the process. I am very excited to move in to my apartment.

I recommend you check other sites for reviews regarding this place it's nice but management tries to force you out once they can raise the rent there are numerous issues and they're not willing to work with you even the property manager has it listed that she specializes in effect turn over for profit on her linkin

Torrey villa was renovated 2 years ago. The property looks nice on the surface, but has many issues due to low grade materials. For example, the dryer doesn’t dry clothes well. I lived in TV my first year in San Diego. I figured I'd give downtown a try - so moved into east village (wish I hadn't). I recently moved out of Montierra Apartments after two years, and the move-out process was disappointing.

During the pre-move-out walkthrough, the team promoted their $150 worry-free cleaning service, assuring me it would cover all necessary cleaning. Trusting their recommendation, I agreed. However, after moving out, I was provided with photos showing dust on the walls and baseboards, but instead of cleaning them as promised, the management decided to repaint the entire apartment at my expense.

Their reasoning was that cleaning walls and baseboards is “usually not sufficient." In our case, the apartment was well-maintained, and a simple vacuum or wipe-down would have resolved the dust issue.

This excuse feels both arbitrary and unfair. If their cleaning service doesn’t cover cleaning walls or baseboards—this should have been communicated upfront. Instead, it feels like a convenient decision was made to proceed with a full repaint and pass the costs onto us, without sufficient justification.

Efforts to clarify this decision were met with vague responses, and my follow-up inquiries were ignored entirely. The lack of transparency and misleading promotion of their services leaves me feeling exploited.

If you’re considering renting here, be cautious. Their move-out process and charges may not align with the promises they make during your tenancy.

While living here one of the residents crashed their car into mine totaling out my car. They did not leave a note.   I notified the office of what had happened giving them a clear description of the red Kia optima that witnesses saw hit my car but did not get a license plate.  I asked them if they would mind to send a simple email to the community asking if anyone had information to please contact me or the San Diego police department. The office refused and offered no assistance in helping me.  They refused to look up their list of registered vehicles matching description.  If you move here beware.  This place is very unprofessional.

The property conveniently located close to the freeway, shopping, dining.  The property has a lot of landscaping that requires routine service.  This goes on practically nonstop and the noise echoes throughout the property which made working from home impossible for me.  The basketball court, volleyball court, tennis court are in high use by the residents so if you need quiet to make calls, concentrate on work, even watch television you will have plenty background noise. The sound pierced the walls.  This is something to think about before choosing this place.  The maintenance requests were filled 75% of the time.  My apartment wasn't very energy efficient and bills can be higher than usual most of the year.  The USPS delivery person a left note in our box stating she has Arthritis so if you live upstairs you will have to drive to the post office to collect your packages as she is unable to climb stairs.  Be careful leaving at night and early morning often times I saw coyotes wandering the property as the property is next to the canyon.  We were left without heat in the winter which was not fun.  They never resolved the broken heater even until we moved out a month later.

Montierra is a good place to call home if you are:
1.) Looking for a dog friendly (large dog included) complex. Dog complexes are pretty hard to come by and LARGE dog complexes are near impossible! This is one of them and they love their pets here. 
2.) Looking to have your apartment close to the freeway. I-15 is literally your neighbor. 
3.) Someone who likes to be away from the busy city but close to shops and strips. 
4.) Someone who is looking for assigned parking so that you don't have to walk 5 blocks back and forth to your car. I visit friends who live closer to the city and have 1 spot for three roommates! You'll have space here. 
5.) A bicyclist who likes to enjoy long bike rides with scenery. The mountains are picturesque. And I have heard from bicyclists that RP/Mira Mesa are prime cycling routes. 
Montierra may not be your home if you are:
1.) Someone who is allergic to animals. The complex holds a lot of dogs and plenty of felines. You'll be buying a lot of anti-allergy medicine if you come here. 
2.) Someone who wants to be in a walk-able community, where you can walk to the grocery stores, the post office, etc. Montierra is convenient located near the 15 but not much else. You'll need some wheels. 
Overall, I would say that it is a great place for families, young professionals and fur babies alike.

Poor Communication – There have been countless times that Esplanade has given us little to no notice about things going on around the complex that effect residences. Managers advised us to make a claim through our renters insurance.

Stay away from this place.
