-Dog urine in elevators almost daily 

For what this company charges for rent there should be so much more responsible management and tangible value.

My family recently visited Del Mar Ridge apartments and was very pleased with the assistance we received from the community manager, Christie. She was patient, helpful, and articulate in explaining the leasing terms and conditions of the apartment.  Most importantly, she would address your concerns that you may have regarding your application either via email or phone in a timely manner. On our self-guided tour, we found an apartment that was very beautiful, clean, and comfortable. The application process was quick and easy. My family and I highly recommend the Del Mar Ridge apartments.

I lived here for a little over a year. From the day I moved in till the day I moved out (Almost 2 years), I had violent men on drugs knocking and banging very hard on my door,  trying to open it, threatening me looking for the previous tenant. I was informed by police that this complex is hot for drugs and violence. This company did absolutely nothing for my safety. 
A Nightmare on Catoctin Dr

There has been 4 deaths in these apartments already and the maintenance is horrible. Leaky sinks, broken heaters, and roaches everywhere. A couple years ago termites came from the cracks in the ceiling during the summer and completely infested our room… do not trust these apartments

I've been to San Diego numerous times and found it to be the place I want to move. My cousin lives in the Corinthian Apts and I foud it very nice, I love what the complex has to offer, beautiful scenery as well. So with that being said, hopefully when I arrive in April, they will still have suites available.

The lady in the office is very nice and maintenance issues inside the apartments get fixed quickly. Unfortunately there are huge water cockroaches both outside and inside. It's not an issue of being messy, as I am a very clean person. Also, there is no a/c unless you buy your own window unit. It has been insanely hot during the summer. The parking lot is "gated" but the gate has been broken countless times since I've lived here a year. The gate to enter the complex from the parking was very difficult to unlock. It also took several months to get this fixed. Overall not recommended.

My name is Sharon and I had been waiting over 9 years for my section 8 and when I was finally given the voucher I was given a 2 page list of available units in San Diego.  Those names were given to every one and therefore the units were full up or they no longer participated in the government program.  But I went thru this website and found the unit that would take my voucher soon after I was given the ok to find a place.
They saved me by taking me as a tenent as well as accepting my small dog and it was ideal for me for the location but for the amentities that went with it such has pool, beautiful landscape, running water fountain near my front door, offstreet parking, walking distance to stores, library and park for my dog...
Management was wonderful and understanding to my needs.
Love it and want to stay forever.

Thank you Apartments.com for having this apartment building listed.
Very spacious for a 1 bedroom..quiet and nice area.

Rent increases every year exceeding $500+. Amenities are ALWAYS broken- treadmills down for months, this is a 4 story complex- ALL elevators are down, homeless are found everywhere- in our parking garages+in the hot tub bathing. It’s disgusting!! The place is not unkept well- stains and scuffs line the hallways. The apartment itself is missing a wine cooler(even if it shows on the website)+ trash can pullout bin is broken in my cabinet and management won’t fix it. Honestly for the high rent prices you don’t get ANY amentities and the apartment itself is JUNK. Save your money and go somewhere else!

This place absolutely sucks. Their management is poor. They’ve had all 3 elevators in a non working status for DAYS and are doing NOTHING to fix it. They literally using the RAIN as an excuse for not doing anything about it after countless residents complained already. Not to mention the place is COMPLETELY unsecured and unsafe, their entrance to the complex doors are always unlocked, all you have to do is give it a little tug. The walls are PAPER thin. Constantly hear doors slamming. The location is also terrible and very dangerous being right off of a major highway. There’s so many better places to live around here than this overpriced joke of an apartment. Save yourself the time and money! My biggest regret was signing a lease here, never again.

I have lived at the Jefferson Pacific Beach for going on 2 years and I can’t really complain! There’s usually security, so I feel safe.  I have a (SPACIOUS) 1 bedroom; the amenities are wonderful, and being right next to the 5 doesn’t hurt, either! Any time there is a Maintenance issue, they are ONNNN it, and always in constant contact. If you have questions, emails are responded to fairly quickly! Even With Pandemic, I could not have asked for a better place to have moved in to!
Complex is clean , friendly with numerous amenities!
I would not recommend this place. Too expensive. Garbage is too expensive. Always stressed out about the parking situation. Mail has been stolen on several occasions from the mail room. Deliveries.
I hear the conversations of my neighbors and every footstep from above. Paper thin walls. Everyone talks about it here. Nice furnishings. Sssllllllow elevators. GREAT leasing agents.
I feel so happy and grateful to live in such a secure and safe condominium complex. The amenities are wonderful and the entire staff could not be more helpful. I love it here!

Awesome community. Great management team, really friendly and helpful. The pool area is amazing and everyone here is down-to-earth, fun, professionals. The cost of rent is pretty high but in comparison to any other complexes in area its well worth it!

This is a fabulous condo complex:
Secure: 1. packages delivered to parcel lockers
2. Resident parking behind coded iron gate
3. Elevators require key fobs to operate
4. After hours security patrol, on call.
5. Leasing office, with staff, onsite during business hours 
The amenities are great, with a large gym, saltwater pool/jacuzzi, large community room, and a dog washing area. Love it here!

Ive lived at the Jefferson for a bit over a year, and it has been amazing. Between Kelsey and her office team, and Brad and Daniel with maintenance, it made this crazy Pandemic so much less of a stresser! Work ethic and attitudes are always great - and its nice bumping in to any/all of them on the grounds! Thanks again, Jefferson PB!

I feel incredibly lucky to live in such a secure, safe and well-maintained condominium complex. The staff is wonderful, very responsive. We have an after-hours security patrol, which adds to our safety!
Leasing staff is awesome!  Made us feel like family.  We love our new home!
Jefferson Pacific Beach is a beautiful, upscale property with great amenities and conveniently located. Management is outstanding and we enjoy living in a resort-like type of community.
Im so fortunate to live here, as its close to shopping, freeways, the park, golf course, biking trails, all the wonderful complex amenities and very secure. I love it!

I have recently moved in to the gardens apartments, and my move-in experience was nothing but exceptional. Zoe and Vladimir were of great help and they made sure everything went smooth. The apartment itself was recently renovated. The rent is very reasonable compared to the average rent in SD.

The decoration of the house, the noisy neighbors, the dog barking, the most important thing is the construction team across the road every morning, the garbage truck at 5:55 in the morning, and the weeding at 8 o'clock. In the evening, you can hear the super loud grunt of the neighbor. You can't have a high-quality sleep at all. The quality of the neighbors in this community is particularly poor. The neighbors scratched the car without leaving a note, a terrible leasing office. The only thing worth a star is that the repair staff will quickly help you repair any problems. But overall, it's a bad community!
ABSOLUTE WORST LIVING EXPERIENCE!!! They break CA Renter's Laws, provide cheap renovations, and HORRIBLE customer service. Don't waste your money here.

My experience here at La Jolla Colony is great, the front office staff is very helpful in answering questions and concerns.  Very professional,  as far as the apartments itself they are in a great location, close to shopping, beaches, great schools. I would definitely recommend these apartments for anyone who is looking for a relaxing environment.

I have been living here for about 3 months.. It’s definitely a cozy little apartment.. it’s definitely do able.. but the price is definitely not worth it.. everything in my apartment is really old or really cheap. I wasn’t told before moving in that the apartment is next to a very busy road so traffic is extremely busy all day and all night. It’s way to hot to keep the windows closed there is no air and no good air flow.. neighbors smoke outside there door and all the smoke comes in my apartment the apartment complex behind my unit has many people outside partying all hours of the night…  you can’t do anything here no BBQs, kids can’t even play outside… they do keep up on the property which is nice location is great… but if you want a home to come home to where you can relax after work this is not the place … your paying for location and that’s it

I spent weeks searching and narrowed it down to Point Loma Bay Apartments being a perfect spot! I did my personal unscheduled tour of the area and then scheduled a viewing of the apartment. Viewed the apartment, got all the information I needed.  5 minutes after I left, they called me and said it was no longer available!

This app keeps saying they have a two bedroom available now, but they don't , they never do, six months ago was the same thing , the app say is available , I come here and they say is not available , is very frustrating , and annoying, and irritating

My one-bedroom apartment is located about a mile's walk from the beach and the neighborhood is quiet despite the few homeless persons wandering near a small ravine. 
The kitchen is small, but the space is ample for me to cook comfortably, if I am the only one in the kitchen. The two only windows in the apartment do not allow for sufficient airflow on hot days, and there is not AC in the apartment, so I am considering purchasing an AC unit. The washers/dryers (located in community area) are outdated (like all of the appliances in my apartment) and have often left marks on my clothing. 
The parking usually plentiful, I have only had to park on the street a handful of times for the 6 months I have been living here.

I toured with my partner this past Saturday and just want to shout out Brittany. We arrived to our appt a little late due to some traffic and she was very patient and still accommodating in helping us see the unit we were interested. We simply loved the amenities, and the balcony was insanely huge from what we have been seeing.
We love living here at Windsor Rancho PQ. It’s a quiet and clean place.
New apartment with good looking facilities. Management and maintenance  need improvement.
Hailey n Brittany are a great team in the leasing office great attitude and happy to assist!
I’m in shock. This place has been amazing. The manger cris and his team have done such a good job with the property. I love this property and the management. It has everything. 5 stars all around!!!

Unfortunately after our experience here we do not recommend this place. Our issue of our neighbor smoking has been constant and we cannot get this resolved. Since our move in date we let the staff know. We have submitted reports. We can't use the patio. We can't leave the windows open. There are times when they spend a longer amount of time smoking and smell of cigarettes begins to seep into our apartment with everything closed. We bring this up in emails and in person. The staff has seen the pictures and videos. We just want some help. We don't want anyone evicted. But it seems that nothing is being done. Either the staff is not doing their part to help us on this issue or the neighbor just doesn't care. Either way you put it, how does that sound? There is no follow up on ensuring the issue is getting resolved, we have to constantly deal with this and inform the staff but there is no change. The solution that we were given, to put it bluntly, was to move out. If we move out, then YOU may be the one who possibly has to deal with this if you are considering moving here. Whether it's this unit or a different building with a smoker.

If this review gave you something to think about before scheduling an appointment here please give this a thumbs up. If you are a neighbor, please give this a thumbs up. Issues are something to be taken seriously and attended to no matter what the situation.

I've lived here about a year now. 

Pros: The units are decent and the management office is pretty good at responding to maintenance requests. The people in the management office are nice and do their best to make the building better. The cleaning staff are nice and do a good job. The amenities are nice when they are functional. 

Cons: Both me and my roommate have had lots of plumbing issues. I've had a few cockroaches in my apartment and I know multiple other tenants who have varying degrees of the same problem. I have had items stolen out of the laundry room. I forgot to lock my car one time and everything was stolen out of it, while it was in the parking garage. The mail room was broken into this year resulting in months of having to retrieve mail at the post office, causing considerable inconvenience. The building is constantly being vandalized by disgruntled tenants. The security cameras in the building are useless because none of the persons committing the offenses are ever caught. The pool and hot tub heaters were out of commission for a couple months this year, and both are generally dirty. Tenants are constantly throwing broken glass, trash, food, etc, onto the basketball and tennis courts and it takes a long time to get cleaned up. The outdoor grills don't work well. The equipment in the fitness center is all falling apart. There is a bathroom in the fitness center which lots of tenants and employees use and causes the fitness center to stink. The elevators are constantly breaking down (on average only 2 of 3 are operational). Tenants consistently leave trash in the stairwells and other areas of the building. There was a week this year where the trash chutes were having work done and tenants stacked trash in the elevators and lobbys. The stairwells and all the entrances and exits to the building reek of dog pee and poop (at least half the tenants have dogs). The trash shoots are located in the elevator lobbys which causes the lobbys to smell bad. Homeless people hangout around the perimeter of the building (on building grounds) and are seldomly removed (and occasionally get in the building). The building security generally look like they're not doing they're jobs (with the exception of a couple individuals). The building is by a freeway exit so traffic noise is high.

Location is great, remodeled apartments are very nice practically a brand new apartment. Management is friendly and open, staff is friendly and helpful, everyone who works here is very personable and approachable even the lady who cleans the lobby she is very nice. The residents are pretty nice foe the most part very friendly Elevator rides. Also this property has fantastic amenities for being right in the middle of San Diego. How many apartments have a basketball court and a tennis court? Also the views are pretty good as well!

Lived in this apartment for three years, and the last year was solely because of the fact my roommate and I were too lazy to move (huge mistake). Would never recommend it to anyone I know (or don't know honestly). The windows in the rooms seem like they were installed in the 1820s. Not only does closing them block out absolutely no noise (in a very busy part of the city), but if it's the slightest bit windy it will sound like your apartment is falling apart. The building has fifteen floors and three elevators, and you should consider yourself lucky if two of them are working leading to nearly ten minute waits to just get to your car quite often. Beyond that, the people who work in the leasing office couldn't be more unhelpful or unprofessional. When we first moved in we were told we would be given a free carpet replacement before moving out, and despite me bringing this up multiple times before moving out, they charged us for a carpet replacement when returning our security deposit. Anytime we called them because our neighbors were playing music loudly in the middle of the night, they did absolutely nothing to rectify the situation despite knowing exactly which apartments were responsible. Not only that but they just wouldn't return messages or emails left to their office (on more than one occasion). During COVID, absolutely none of the amenities were open (understandably), yet when it came time to renew our rent for the coming year, it didn't decrease or stay the same. It went up by over $100/month. For reference, when we first moved in our rent was $2200 a month, and by the time we moved out they wanted $2700 a month (3 years later). That's before throwing in whatever other miscellaneous charges they tack on like parking ($125 a month). Meanwhile, while they were trying to squeeze us for $500 more a month than when we first moved in, they were leasing the exact same apartment as ours for that same $2200 price. They would hold their yearly fire drill inspections multiple times a year which means they would run the fire alarms in every apartment for an entire day. One month went by where construction crews with jackhammers would start work outside our apartment at 7AM or earlier, and when we tried to speak to the leasing office about this, they would just shrug their shoulders and do nothing. Hope this helps at least one person avoid this place.

This place is a good place to start your apartment living from ground zero because they offer credit check and not 3 or 4 times rent. They have great amenities and a great community around the units. Dog friendly and offer 24/7 fitness center. This is a great place wether you are first time renter or not!!
Terrible customer experience with the leasing office.

I have been living at Ariel for 1 year now and just renewed my lease for another year. I live on the 22nd floor in a 1br/1ba with about 670 SF. I face south, so I get a 180 degree view that includes downtown, Coronado, and the bay. Ariel is by far the nicest complex I have ever lived in. All of the units have tile floors in the living and bathing areas, stainless steel appliances, in-unit W/D, and the largest balcony with incredible views. I also have 2 huge closets--one in the entry way and 1 in my bedroom. I honestly have zero complaints about the unit and the complex.

One thing that might turn some people off is the noise from the train tracks. I'm used to it by now, but the only train noise that was bothersome at first was the freight train that runs a few times a day. When my windows and balcony door are shut, it's muffled and I barely hear it. The trolley and commuter trains are so quick and don't make much noise. I wouldn't let this deter me from living here at all, but I suggest getting a listen before renting. 

The property management team is always very friendly and quick to respond. Jackie, the property manager, is the best one I've ever had. She's always helpful and on top of things.

One of the best things about this place is the location. It's so convenient to all of Little Italy, but also easy to get to all other downtown locations and the freeway. We are right across from the trolley stop, but a lot is walkable too.

I plan to stay at Ariel as long as I'm living downtown. It has everything I'm looking for at a very competitive rate.

Brand new building and yet everything is broken - elevators, hot tub, fountain in lobby. Rent increases nearly 7 percent a year - has been raised $400/month in less than 3 years. Inexperienced management - communication with residents is limited to fliers taped to your door - which is completely ineffective if you travel a lot. 

You have much better options in Little Italy with more competent and professional building management, newer apartments with parking included and buildings with functioning elevators. Incidentally, for the last 3 years they have charged $50 every time you use the grill in the pool area - yet boast a plethora of “amenities.” You can do better than Ariel - and Ariel can do much better by its residents.

Unfortunately at this point I feel obligated to leave a review. I work in customer service and understand the impact of a negative review, but I’ve had enough and need to share. I’ve lived there on 2 separate occasions. Each for 1 year. I recently moved out on January 8th. A few days after moving out I was notified that the elevator was allegedly damaged by the movers I hired. (During the move the fire alarm went off rendering the elevator useless) I notified the leasing office and the corporate office to pursue the moving company directly if they could in fact prove the damage was caused by my movers. My deposit was supposed to be returned in full as my apartment was in excellent condition. I received a letter in the mail stating I would not be getting my deposit back and in turn I owe $750 on top. 2 of the charges were for heavy carpet staining and drywall damage. I lived alone with no pets and never had shoes on the carpet. There were no stains. I asked for pictures/video proof of the damages. They weren’t able to provide either and ended up responding “we’re sorry for the oversight, we’ve reversed the charges”. I would be careful, it looks like their “oversight” is an attempt to charge people who don’t read their deposit paperwork at the end of the lease. The bill still included the alleged damage to the elevator. Which now after 4 attempts to retrieve the video evidence ( I have email proof where they stated they had video evidence ), they are not willing to share it with me. Imagine being in a courtroom where the plaintiff states they have video evidence on the grounds of “just trust us we do”. This is how I’m being treated. I have refused to pay the bill until they share the video. I need to share the video with the moving company so I can be reimbursed by the moving company. Unfortunately nobody in their corporate office understands that the quicker I have the video the quicker I can pay and pursue the moving company. Unfortunately the leasing office manager seems unsure of how to handle situations like this. When asked for someone’s phone number I can contact at their corporate office (a few exits down in La Jolla), there is suddenly no human that works at the office. The leasing manager stated “they’re not a call center”. A charming way to handle a situation like this. Try to avoid living here unless it’s absolutely necessary, and pray you never have an issue that needs to be resolved with any ounce of critical thinking on management’s end.

If you want help from management, a nice place to live, elevators to work, parking don’t live here. It’s awful management never answers to emails, calls, pool closes extremely early most people aren’t off of work till 5 it closes at 4:30 here. Gym is awful small and not very much equipment. You can rarely find guest parking and worst of all did I mention management it’s terrible! Only person I liked was the maintenance guy.

I moved to Torrey Gardens 3 years ago and i loved every bit of thos community. The apartment is very new looking and the amenities are amazing. The office staff really made me feel like i was important and they cared about me. Dan in the office was always so kind to me as well as the manager Stella and Sherry. Im really going to miss this place and i recommend it to anyone who is looking for a great place to live with a warm staff to take of you.
Torrey Gardens is a luxury apartment.  The pool is like a hotel and the gym is state of the art.  The management is on top of everything.  Love this place and could see myself living here forever!

This complex is brand new, which is why we chose it since just having had a new born, we wanted something new and clean. All the appliances are new, and quite, except for the AC, we can't even hear the tv in our living room as it is so loud. The complex is gorgeous, amazing gym, nice pool, we are located up high too, we have view on the very loud freeway, we can also hear it from our apartment. There is also an army base less than 10 miles away so we constantly hear the loud airplanes, day and night. The location is great, we're in the middle of everything, so all and all I am rating this a 3 because it's not so fun hearing the freeway and army planes everyday.

We moved into Torrey Gardens in January and love our apartment! First off, the apartment is beautiful and spacious. The location of the apartment is ideal with being close to the 805, 5, and 56 freeways. Right in between La Jolla and Del Mar, about 25 minutes to downtown. Maintenance is efficient. We had an issue with our refrigerator a few weeks back. I went online to inform them about the issue and 20 minutes later someone was at our apartment to check it out. I went out for a few hours to run some errands and came back to a whole new refrigerator! The leasing office staff is super friendly & helpful as well. We are sad to be breaking our lease early to move out of state or else we would be staying here for a couple years!

I am comfortable I feel safe I'm at peace my home  all the neighbors have some nice around the neighborhood this is the only year that I've been thinking about moving to another place because our rent went up for real going to give up some things and we're still going to be sticking around cuz we're comfortable

The walls are insanely thin, the property is a mess, management is disorganized and hostile, and neighbors leave a lot to be desired. Management will gaslight you and deny any criticisms you have on the complex as an ex-resident. A 2 year lease turned into only a 6 month stay because of all the issues here.

The only plus to this complex is the location. Otherwise, don't be fooled by the low prices & spacious apartments.

I am three months into living at Summit Park and I can't even tell you how many issues I have had with this property management company, including charging twice for utilities, gaslighting, having everything broken into the apartment when I moved in, leaking walls, and more. It makes sense why all of their good reviews are about maintenance and the tour day, aka not very good reviews. The office is insanely unhelpful and gaslights you when you clearly have receipts of payment and know they are playing a game. On top of all of the lead paint coming off in the rain (which is dangerous and not in the agreement we signed, as it states that lead paint is only dangerous when it is coming off (like it is here). I'm already counting down the days until I can leave them, they are the least trustworthy company I have ever worked with for living this far, and that's saying a lot. Stay far away. The only good thing is apartment size and that's probably not worth it. The maintenance guys are nice, but that's the only saving grace here so far.

In the 16 months I have lived here I have experienced 4 shootings all involving the same unit across the street from me. Management ignores it and won’t acknowledge the problem with their residents at all. The drive by shooting on May 8th was at 5:20 in the afternoon, in broad daylight, near where children were playing. There is no security, no cameras, and no accountability. Furthermore, the unit I rented was dirty when I moved in with broken windows, a broken stove, broken cabinets, and holes in the walls.  It was infested with both German roaches and large American cockroaches. Do not move here. It’s not good for your health and it’s not safe.

I wish someone had warned us before choosing to live here. The long list of problems we have had (in only a few weeks) are too many to number from filthy carpets, filthy apartment overall, buckled bathroom floors and shower. It’s as if they waited for a tenant to move in and then address all the problems. The refrigerator has to be at least 20 plus years old but it also was full of mold.

I just moved out after 1 year of living at summit park village. The actual apartment was a decent space. However, I have issues with how the complex is run. Rent is too expensive for what you get, and there are crimes too frequent in the complex that are not mentioned by the staff. There was a man who got stabbed in the parking lot a few months ago outside of where my roommates and I lived. Instead of owning up to the lack of security and attempting to make the residents feel safer, the complex raised their prices significantly for "improved security." There was never an apology letter, so I lost all of my trust in the staff. I am very disappointed with my experience at summit park, and I hope you consider all of your options before renting at summit park village.

The apartment itself is decent sized, and an older building so it gets very warm, and there is only a wall AC unit to cool the whole place. It has some positives in the two balconies or patios (If you're first or second floor, of course). There are issues in the general outdoor appearance. Things like the common laundries are not treated with respect by other tenants, and even when management tries to fix something it's broken the next day. We first moved here and things were ok. We had a broken garbage disposal, a room to room wall fan that sounded like it had a wrench in it, and other issues like a subfloor that creaked like a coffin in a horror movie. MOST of that was fixed. Two stars rather than one only for the size of the place and the balconies. Oh, and you can have a barbecue. Yay.

Horrible military housing. No amenities, security is horrible, break ins into cars almost every night, packages stolen daily. You can’t even move your furniture on your cheap laminate flooring without tearing up the floors as well as our dining room table left dents in it which I’m sure we will get charged for. We are extremely clean people and we still have cockroaches and mice in our home even after getting it sprayed, it’s disgusting.

Lived here for years, many plumbing issues, and somebody broke into the mailbox a few years ago and I had to go to the post office for over a month to collect my mail. They have ZERO cameras in the common areas, would not recommend for the price they are asking.

Living here is a pleasure, Great views of Mission Bay and nearby shopping is a dream. Love the pools, gym, and the dog run. The grounds are routinely maintained. The staff here is efficient, professional and friendly. I have lived here 7 years and would highly recommend living in Villa Monair.

I've lived in a lot of different apartment complexes and I can say that Villa Monair has by far the best staff I've come across. From the office staff to the maintenance staff, everyone is super friendly and they've addressed any issues I've had right away. It's quiet, well kept and just overall a nice place to live. I've been here for over 3 years and I have no plans to move any time soon

I have lived at Villa Monair for almost two years now and could not be happier. The location, quality of the units, neighbors, maintenance and staff are all great. Definitely one of the better deals available right now too. Looking forward to signing another year lease and continuing my living experience here. Thanks, Villa Monair!

We love living here. The location is conveniently close To the 5 freeway, restaurants, groceries, and under the 10 minutes to PB Pier.  
The amenities are great too; multiple pools, laundry on site, small gym, doggie area that’s fenced in. 
The office & maintenance staff are the real icing on the cake - super friendly!

There's a couple perks to Villa Monair. It's in a good location and it's pet friendly (not without a hefty fee, though)

The cons of Villa Monair are greater. First of all, they have increased their one bedroom prices by over $1k in the last year, literally during pandemic times showing they only care about money. 

If you are active and want an apartment gym, don't even bother here. The gym was cleaned ONCE my entire time in a year I lived there. The floors were dirty all the time and the gym is constantly neglected. Minimal equipment, dirty. 

The barbeques have never been cleaned by maintenance. Constant washers breaking down. Elevator broken. The pools aren't heated. Front desk person LC is condescending, literally asked me "what do you want" instead of a nice hello when I went in to ask a question. Don't recommend this place.

Tried contacting this property many times. When I did talk to someone they would only talk to me over text and when I asked them to call me I never heard from them again. Completely shocked with the costumer service.

The property manager is extremely rude and does not respond to messages about anything. It’s gated but the gates don’t lock or stay closed so many homeless people come in and sleep by the laundry facilities and in the stairwells and the property manager does nothing! Maintenance takes forever to fix anything I’ve had to put 2-3 more requests in to fix something before they actually come to fix it. The floors are so squeaky and you can get a noise complaint just because of the floors that you have no control over. This apartment is extremely over priced it costs $35 for a parking spot and $100 for a garage on top of rent and the water fee Don’t live here!

This place is beautiful and quaint. Property manager is super helpful and respectful she will always get back to you in a timely manner, if anything needs to get fixed they fix it within 1-2 days. Price for what you get is perfect. The landscape is always maintained well and clean, shared community spaces are always clean and maintained. Only downside is parking and in the summer it gets pretty warm since there is no AC.

They have been through five property managers in three years and all give different answers to policy questions. The current manager has said that she cannot deal with any problems that began before she started two months ago and I need to speak to the previous manager. The previous manager has not answered emails and my no longer be employed by the company. The phone line for the corporate office is a voicemail that no one follows up on, and their phone tree to find direct lines is mostly gibberish. Don’t rent here if you can afford anything else at all.

The location is the only thing I still like about the complex! I moved here when it was purchased by a new owner and the rent rates were still good! I don't see the reason for the large increase, overpriced for what you get.  The tight parking lot situation is difficult along with the paper thin walls! Privacy shouldn't be on your wish list!

High crime area. No dog building with dog crap everywhere. All storage cage agreements cancelled, likely because of the high amount of break ins. So you better have a backpack or get the largest apartment. Parking is a nightmare, assigned spots are ignored, no visitor spots. Ancient appliances. Limits on every amenity. Constantly broken elevators that take a week to repair. Penny pinching in every corner. Sweeping views of the coastline? Give me a break. So many half truth claims. Expect noisy neighbors, inconsiderate spoiled party students. 
The location is the only positive.

I have been living here about 4 years. I like my apartment and the maintenance staff is very good. There seem to be a lot more college kids than before. When i first moved in, they were more selecting in who could live here but not lately. Also, notice the no pet policy that id a total joke. Everyone, and i mean EVERYONE has a dog here i guess except me. So you will hear dogs barking on and off.

I have been living here about three years, fed up by regular apartment complexes, poorly built so that you can hear every one walking/stomping around, partying etc. 
I signed on here in a building high-rise even though the rent is more than most Apts in this area, hoping that  there's more of a soundproof wall situation in this type of building. Also the apartment above me is the model, so there was a guarantee no one above anyway. Overall, it's good here worth the extra money. I do hear my neighbor's toddler screeching through the wall at times, but it's not bad. The rent does go up some every year, so I will have to leave at some point, but for now it' s ok.

Awesome place. It is central to multiple schools, shopping, the beach, and food. The maintenance crews are fast and efficient and the doormen are welcoming and even remember your name! The pool is nice and usually fairly vacant so it's a quiet place to go and relax. There is a small gym in between the two high rise towers but an even bigger and better equipped one across the street. It is a little more expensive than some of the other places around the UTC area however for that little extra spent I believe it has been more than worth it based upon the quality and service received. I've been living here for a little under two years now. 
Hope this was helpful!

This is a perfect high rise community in lively neighborhood of UTC/La Jolla. Walking distance to stores, groceries, restaurants.

The amenities are wonderful and the maintenance staff is very quick in responding to the complaints.

Usually I have seen in other apartment the leasing officers are not so friendly but leasing folks here are really friendly.

They have nice pool and jacuzzi along with basketball courts and tennis courts. Really wonderful gym in the community with personal trainer options also available.

All I can say is if you are in San Diego you should experience staying here for once in your lifetime

Also Lajolla beach and UCSD campus is really near by

THIS APARTMENT IS AMAZING.  THERE IS A VALET WHO WILL PARK YOUR CAR OR EVEN HELP CARRY GROCERIES TO YOUR DOOR.  THE BUILDING  FEATURES AMENITIES THAT INCLUDE, A TENNIS COURT, BASKETBALL AND ROOFTOP POOL WITH BARBECUE GRILLS.  THERE ARE LOTS OF RESTAURANTS IN THE BACK OF THE BUILDING AND A SMALL PARK TO SIT AND RELAX.   I HAVE LIVED HERE 4 YEARS AND EACH TIME THERE IS AN INCREASE I THINK ABOUT MOVING BUT IT SEEMS THAT IT SEEMS TO ENTICE YOU INTO STAYING EACH TIME YOU COME HOME AND REALIZE WHAT A GREAT PLACE THIS IS.  I AM NOT THE ONLY ONE WHO FEELS THIS WAY.

Please know your SCRA rights. Tried to deny us from termination of our lease due to new PCS orders and deployment. Provided the correct paperwork. They tried. Nope. We out. Please please know your rights.

These apartments in general have been pretty convenient and affordable to live in. Being a UCSD student, I can easily go to campus on the 41 bus that’s right outside or I can bike it during the rush hour. The apartment is also close to several major freeways such as the 5, 805, and the 52 entrance that is only about a mile away. Having the 2bed and 2bath apartment has been ideal for housing roommates that can accommodate for doubles in each room. We are also thankful to have 2 assigned parking spots, parking available for visitors, and street parking nearby. The apartment is also equipped with amenities such as a dog park, pool, a recently renovated picnic area with grills, and a volleyball court that are always maintained cleaned. Although the on-site laundry is a little pricy and not open after certain hours, I am glad that it has a coin-change machine that makes it easy to get quarters without having to constantly go to the bank. The area is also very safe as I have never had issues like theft of my bike or amazon packages.

As a UCSD student, I have found this place to be ideal for the past 3 years since I moved off-campus. Compared to other apartments in the La Jolla area, this place is definitely one of the more affordable options that can still get you to campus by bus within approx. a 20-minute commute and about 10 minutes by car. The 41 bus stop is also just a 2-minute walk from the apartment complex that takes you straight to campus without the need to transfer buses. Across the street is also a convenient shopping center with a Vons, restaurants, gasoline stations, a Rite Aid, etc. 

As for the apartments themselves, the rooms are very spacious with plenty of space for storage and large furniture. It also comes with appliances that are in good shape like dishwashers, stoves, microwaves, etc. The parking spots vary with some being large while others are covered by roofs, so it really depends on the luck for which one you get assigned. I have never encountered problems like pests infestations, power blackouts, or rowdy neighbors, and the complex is kept clean by the workers. Teresa, the manager, has always responded quickly to any maintenance issues and occasionally sets up fun events for the community.

Overall, my time here has been pleasant and I recommend this place to any student/person looking to rent in the La Jolla community.

La Jolla Park East is a best Community to live in if you love natural beauty.This place is pet friendly as well have children park where your kiddos can enjoy .We have best schools in our neighborhood also.

I have been living here for about 4 years and I never had the chance to complain because the society is so clean and green. Also, we have access to many places and locations like highly rated Schools: curie elementary, university city high, Standley middle school, vons, rite aid, and the library which is very helpful because I can get my books from there easily. We have many places where we can eat like Carl's JR, UC Yogurt, lornarl's Italian kitchen, Subway, and  Ahi Sushi. There are salons and activities for kids to do like taekwondo and little artists, The staff has also been very helpful cause they are always trying to keep the society clean. Playground for kids to play in is also available which has swings, sea saw, a slide, and volleyball court, Barbeque is also there in case you wanna do a party outside and not in your house then you can just do it out there. All this credit goes to the manager Teresa for making this society so wonderful, clean and fun.

Here at La Jolla East Apartments, you have access to many places and locations way easier. Places such as UTC Mall, Curie elementary, Standley Middle, University city High, Vons rite aid and last but not least the UCSD.

Lets start with the good. The place is small as expected but very updated with modern features such as: Stainless steel appliances, bamboo floors, sliding frosted glass doors instead of traditional doors, granite countertops, granite bathroom floors and bathroom fixtures. The pool is nice is size and kept clean on a weekly basis. The location is absolutely superb, you can ride a bike virtually anywhere you need to go including but not limited to: downtown San Diego, Hillcrest, North Park, South Park, University Heights, and even the water (Seaport Village, Coronado Island).

The things I wish to see change, or that may be out of our control are to be expected. Things such as minimal closet space (which is a fairly easy fix with Rubbermaid closet inserts), no central ac/heat, and no dishwasher. There are pets allowed in this complex and because of it's design, you are more likely to hear dogs barking if your window is open throughout the day. There does not seem to be a bug problem, but I will mention that there is a fly problem. Although the outside structures are taken care of to a certain extent there residue from the palm trees leaks onto the pavement and seems to attract flies. Because this complex is on a steep hill, the sun seems to set a few hours early which may not bother you unless you adore your sunshine and pool side lounging for extended hours. Parking is pretty straight forward, you get one parking pass and gate opener for the lot and any additional cars must be parked street side which usually has plenty of open spots. Rent is due via money order/check to the property manager's rent drop box. No online payments. SDGE is responsible for your gas and electric, which you pay separate. Water, sewer, trash is included in the rent.

Overall the things I like about this place outweigh the negative. The location is key because of it's close proximity to Balboa, the Zoo, and other desirable locations such as Downtown and North Park. Great if you have a dog that likes to walk especially because the area is safe. I would recommend this place for anybody willing to pay the price to have these high quality amenities that are both directly and indirectly a part of the living experience in Canyonwood.
Moving here has been a true blessing! Staff is very helpful, and always gets my maintence requests done in a timely matter. I can’t thank them enough!

When I called to schedule a tour the service was outstanding!!! The lady who took my call was very helpful and only took about 10 minutes to set up. The tour its self was amazing and sold me instantly. The living experience has been nothing but blue skys. My unit is in amazing condition and I can’t complain!

I’ve had an amazing experience living in this apartment. The unit itself is well-designed, with a spacious layout and high-quality appliances. The management team is friendly and quick to address any maintenance requests. The building is quiet and secure, making it a comfortable place to live. Plus, the location is unbeatable—close to great dining, shopping, and public transit.
Quick and excellent service. They are so quick to respond to our needs and so knowledgeable and experienced in fixing our issues. Awesome team

The management here is very rude. Every time I’ve called to ask about availability someone acts like they’re doing me a favor instead of doing their actual job. It’s like they can’t wait to get off the phone and sound annoyed. I would not be able to live here dealing with these people.
If I could give this place 0 stars I would. The staff was super rude when asking if there was availability.
Es una excelente comunidad muy pacífica con muy buenas instalaciones amenidades no tiene problemas de vecinos y sobre todo es muy tranquila

I have had a horrible experience with these apartments. I moved out December 25th 2023 and haven’t been able to receive my security deposit. I have multiple attempts to resolve the issue but it is still pending.
Silo is hands down the best apartment complex in San Diego! Great staff who responds quickly and always willing to go the extra mile for you. 10/10!

The leasing team is a dream and made the process effortless, all of the ladies are super nice. Liana and Ingrid were amazing. I feel extremely comfortable, especially knowing my dog is welcomed here and we’re very happy with all of the amenities.
When it comes to facilities and staff professional I believes those things alone make it a good place to live.
It’s a quiet community, but I wish there’s more space for parking.
Beautiful homes. The property is new and all the residents are settling in but it’s very quiet so far. I love my apartment. I feel good coming home and dwelling here.

This apartment complex is affordable, Dog friendly, and very up to date. The interior design of the units are very modern and give spacious areas despite square footage. The flooring is kid and pet friendly, and the smart home features makes you feel very safe to be alone at night. The complex is located perfectly by the highway and away from the city. The nights are quiet and commutes are easy. Highly recommend for military and families.

Silo is a growing community and has very big potential to expand to a very successful community. My time residing in Silo has been amazing especially with the assistance of Fabian. The staff is super friendly and very helpful when the time of need is needed. I will definitely recommend Silo to anyone who is deciding to look for a beautiful home.

Ive been living at Silo for a month but so far so good . The apartment is cery clean and luxury like living with smart home features and lots of lighting . The community is very friendly and peaceful as well .
The architectural design of the buildings are amazing, friendly neighborhood. Easy use of the apps and amenities. Only concern is there being lots of spiders in the area.
Management (Liana and Fabian) are awesome. They made our leasing/move so smooth. The community is very quiet and peaceful.
The architecture is what caught my eye, it has the feel of living by the beach. Peaceful living.

Management is impossible to get a hold of. You will never be able to talk to someone directly. They use a third party maintenance service. Calling to talk to an apartment manager always goes to voice mail. They only return calls 50% of the time. I have had 4 water leaks in the last 12 months. They don’t do preventative maintenance and do shotty jobs on requires repairs

Toured the complex recently and was surprised at how quite it was. The manager was nice,(linda or lindsay), she showed me both sides of the complex, pool, laundry and parking. They have a wall hanger outside the office with all the current opening with prices and what is required which is cool if your hunting late like I do, the managers cell phone is posted on the door which is cool, you wont get an answering service all the time. Clean complex, looks like they are renovating the units and keeping up with the times. Price is reasonable, paying for water, trash and sewer sucks to pay for but i get it, we live in San Diego. 

Thank you for the tour, hope you have availability in June.

While leaving the apartment, the apartment, was very very clean, without any single stain. but still the management took $450 out of $600 security deposit for studio apartment cleaning. 
Even if rent is late by 1 day, they charge $100 as fine - no exceptions, but when you have to call them for any maintenance, they don't respond.

My rent for studio was more than 1 bed room apartment of my neighbors, and there was always loud music from neighbors - and management took no action even after multiple complaints. 

 Avoid this place at any cost.

If you plan on living here just know that the management is very poor. They do not care about their home owners and will try to break your lease as much as possible. No parking areas at all. You have to park down the street or take a Lyft/Uber if u want to live here from blocks away. Always traffic getting into the apartments. Leaving the complex is very dangerous because of a blind spot near the leasing center. VERY BAD APARTMENTS

I just had to leave San Diego and move back to PA. I rented a 1 BR here for almost 4 years. My apt. was right by the pool but I had no issues with noise. The staff (Toni, Joy and Alfredo) are fantastic. Apts. are from the 1970s but they keep renovating and updating. I have never been treated better. Laundry clean and complex clean. Neighbors are friendly. Staff will not tolerate any violations of rules. Maintenance staff does not delay. Absolutely a wonderful place to live. My experience was great. I'm only gone 2 weeks and wish I could move back!!
Great location, near many stores, movies, and shopping.  Don't like having to pay for water.
New management has taken over (2020) and they are extremely knit picky. There are better locations and better places for the price.

Ive been here 3.5 yrs and love it. The view of the airplanes taking off outta Lindberg is a nice amenity  where else you gonna live in San Diego AND have a perfect view of SD Bay and the local airport
Very judgemental and lazy management. Lots of smokers, most windows don't shut properly and loud neighbors... awful

I lived in Willow Glen for a year. My experience here was good. The manager/landlord was super friendly and really showed that she cared for her residents. The appliances are updated and the apartment was in good conditions. If you have a creative mind you can definitely make it your own space. My concern was not having a parking spot but I was able to quickly get one since I was communicating with the landlord for availability, just try to get one on the front side not the back. The street parking is not bad either and never had a bad experience leaving my car out there. I gave it 4 stars because it can get a bit noise at night if you live by the 7eleven side but you eventually get used to it. Overall I would recommend, especially if you are looking for a shorter term(less than 2 years).

By far, the WORST apartment complex I've ever lived in. Trilar in general is trash. They set all these guidelines, but don't enforce when residents don't abide by the rules. The manager is so unorganized and very unprofessional. Apartment had a carpet beetle infestation, mind you there is no carpet. The buildings are just old, I told manager about infestation, she sent Terminix once or twice, but the problem was NEVER solved. When you request maintenance, they do a POOR job at fixing the issue. I wouldn't recommend these apartments to anyone, don't waste your time. Look for a place that is worth your money, because Willow Glen isn't it.

This Property Is so Great. Me, My parents and little brother was living here, and didnt had no problems and got free Internet Services, no one was arguing. This property was just perfect and thinkin about movin back to live here once more and again.

I lived at Willow Glen for 2 years during grad school at SDSU and LOVED it! I cannot speak highly enough about the quality of the apartment, mangers, staff, etc. My one bdrm was the perfect size and affordable pricing and I loved the color accent wall. If I ever had a maintenance request they fixed it right away. Parking is right in front and always available. I felt super safe here and the other tenants were always chill and nice. I got lucky and lived on the upper floor in the far left building that is more open and could see the sunset everyday! Arthur and Joanna the owners are seriously so kind and helpful, whenever I needed any help they would always work with me. Ever since I moved in, they have always been doing things to make the property better, like landscaping (I love the succulents and palm trees they planted) and they installed a mail box locker so you never miss a package. I'm so lucky I got to live here and am very grateful for Willow Glen.

I took a chance on this place because it was newly renovated and management appeared like they were really working on the property. Totally wrong. Since day one I have had nothing but issues. Access doors don't work so anyone can come in, parking is awful, the washer and dryers are always dirty or out of order, the grass up front in disgusting and smells. The management doesn't care and lies about every little thing. Homeless people dig through trash regularly and thugs hang out back by parking area which really sucks when you have to walk down the alley to get inside.

I would give this complex ZERO star if I could! This is the worst complex I've ever lived in. DON'T LET THE PICTURES FOOL YOU. When I first moved in, the apartment was full of dust and garbage from the last tenant. Broken doorknob, dead bugs and crooked closet door, you name it. There are animal excrements and urine everywhere and no one bother to clean the mess up, if you like the nasty smell and crazy party people around you every day, be my guess. DON'T EXPECT the landlord to resolve issues for you! Someone was trying to steal my vehicle, and the security can't care less about it! Some homeless people constantly go to the garbage bin to dig your stuff out and make a mess, lots of thug hanging out, smoking pot in public area, and guess what, the landlord never cares. People are fighting over limited washers and dryers because the broken washer and dryer were NEVER repaired for over 6 months!! If none the above bothers you and don't matter to your kids' safety, welcome to the complex!

AMAZING place to live! Management is super helpful. Blessed to be a tenant for more than 4+ years. Excited to see the new changes with the new manager Irma. Now is the time to move if you are looking to lease, Irma is super helpful and will answer any inquiries. Overall 5 stars.

Moved into Doriana Apartments in 1989 and have recently moved out on Sept. 30, 2022.  Recent improvements are amazing, including buildings painted in different colors, much better numbering of buildings & units, landscaping, way better lighting at night for better safety and vacated units are beautifully rehabbed (see photos and I do think that’s my old place, which looks absolutely marvelous).  Made lifelong friends here and we wouldn’t have stayed here this long if we didn’t like it.

I am a College student a single mother and I'm glad my daughter and I have a roof over our heads.  My apartment is not the best but it's better than nothing.  The management raised up the rent, they don't do any upgrade,  dogs do their business on the grounds, the grass no one comes to clean it.  I needed some fixing my bathroom it tooks almost 6 months or more before the maintenance guy come fix it. I also need some fixing in the kitchen it been more than 5 months since no one comes to fix it until my friend came over and fix it for me. I live here for 3 years now. I'm paying $900 for one bedroom apartment. I wish I could afford to live in a much better looking apartment, with better and more caring management.  I love living in apartment,  it's less to deal with than owning a house although I would love to have my own house in the future.  I love nice and clean apartments with beautiful views. I wish I was living in a great apartment to give great reviews.

The apartments look good on the inside, a little worn on the outside but for the area its really one of the nicer places available. Parking looked like it needed some touch up, numbers are a little faded, but overall seems to be clean. Office was hard to locate due to it being on the second level of the property but there was parking in front and main area looked well taken cared of. The manager, Tre, was very helpful and informative. He gave me a tour of the apartment, pool and laundry room, all of which were in good condition and clean. I verified all of the info was accurate to what I searched up and it was spot on so I applied and now just waiting to hear back from them. I don't know what the living experience is like here yet but if it's anything like the initial meeting, it should be OK.

Pulling into the place I had reasonably high hopes, the outside looked clean and the grounds well maintained. Stepping foot into the office was a different story. I walked in to one employee sitting behind a desk. She looked up for a second before going back to whatever she was doing before I got there. No greeting, nothing but a quick glance. I tried to break the awkward silence by asking how she was and she did the same and then she sat there silently again. I told her I was looking for an apartment and she told me they didn't have any available. She offered one that was a little ways out but it was not what I was looking for. Would not come back to rent.

I could say so much about this place so I’ll make it a short as I can. Soon move in we were told that parking spaces were in construction and would be finished within a month or two of moving in so we had to park on the street where MULTIPLE cars have been damaged from other vehicles hitting them and ten months later they lot still wasn’t finished. More construction to the building was started and another apartment had the fan fall from the bed room ceiling. The electricity went out multiple times for days and Managment wouldn’t reimburse certain things. Appliances needed servicing and they said it was our responsibility. An apartment still had personal household items in it and they have construction workers inside of the house to open the wall to make an entrance to a small porch and it’s just blocked with a board and when we got to the house they left the door wide open over the weekend when they gate code(that also got changed with the access to our place with a day notice) will be open along with the back area open for anyone to walk in. This place is definitely somewhere I would NEVER recommend to anyone to live.

This is not for someone who works nights. RUN AWAY! This apartments are underconstruction as well as road. Very loud!!!! Parking space is not available, yet. So, someone stole my sons vehicle (parked on the street) :[ , my apartment does not have window screen in any window :(. Contacted the office & did not care anout this issue. Be prepare not get your mail for months, possible year due to new construction. The post office & the apartments complex blame each other and nothing gets result. Of course, my rent gets pay on time. I can't wait for my contract to end!!!

The complex provides one parking spot per unit and there is plenty of street parking for a second car or guests. The manager and staff are not always easy to reach, so you need to be assertive if you need something. 

There are a couple issues with these apartments. Almost all the bedrooms are placed right next to Clairemont Mesa Blvd., so you will hear a lot of traffic noise if you open your window. There is no air conditioning either so this isn't a great place to live during summer time. 

Overall, not bad for the price but there are less noisy areas for the same price.

Honestly, upon moving in this place was a dream. Great amount of space for the price and a decent location despite the hospital traffic. 
Cons: parking is a nightmare. They’ve promised us parking spaces for over 4 months now but nothing. Reading older reviews it hasn’t changed since 2015, yikes. Obnoxiously noisy neighbors. We had a unit by the pool and oh my god the blasting music and screaming teens till late at night and use of pool after hours during the summer. It feels like none of these people have any respect on each other’s spaces despite asking politely to keep things subtle. Weed and cigarette smokers around the area will leave your car smelling like an old bar.

My group tried continuously to get approved just to find out this corporation does not accept student income which was a large portion of our group's total income. We lost valuable application money and several days of time. At the same time, our application process was difficult, lengthy, and stressful. As an incoming senior this fall, I genuinely just want a place to call home to finish my studies, no bad intentions. I highly advise you to look somewhere else or just consider the rest of the reviews that were left.

The street lights are all off and they won’t get it fixed. Every night many cars and storages  are broken into and they don’t do anything. 
Good luck if the apartment is by the freeway, it’s so noise that you won’t be able to sleep without earplugs.

These apartments were recently taken over by new management and they have been amazing!  It’s hard to find a caring staff but all the praise to this team. They have been nothing but friendly, helpful and have solved any issues I have had right away.  You can’t go wrong moving here!
Horrible people!!! Horrible place to live! No response from nobody!!! No parking!!! No jacuzzi!!! Close to freeway!!! To much noise!!! And  They just taking your money

I lived here for a year in 2013-2014.  When I moved out, I was not told that I owed Agave Ridge any money whatsoever.
In December 2018, I got a call from a collections company saying that I owed Agave Ridge $400 as an "insufficient notice penalty."  I had never heard of this penalty until that call. I called Agave Ridge multiple times and wrote letters and emails, asking for evidence or any proof that I had not given enough notice when I moved out.  I got no response.  Because Agave Ridge had not sent the case to collections until after 4 years after I moved out, they were past the statute of limitations to collect - and I had to send multiple letters to collections getting that point across.
If Agave Ridge truly believed I had given them insufficient notice (to the tune of $400) then they could have easily responded to my calls and letters telling me why they thought I owed them money.  And telling me why it took them 4 years to try to collect.
It was an incredibly frustrating experience for me to deal with collections for a debt that I know I didn't owe, but when any proof was in Agave Ridge's possession - and Agave Ridge wouldn't respond to me in any way.  I would not recommend living here; they clearly don't care about their tenants and were just trying to get $400 from me for some fake penalty.  I gave them so many chances to just help me with the collections case or give me any proof at all that I owed money. They didn't and all I can do is now hope that others don't live here and go through the same experience I did.

They are horrible here! Place is old and anytime u need something fixed it takes weeks to get someone to come. You have to call 3 or 4 times. There customer service at the office is horrible! I wouldn’t move bck here even if they paid for my rent! I wouldn’t moved here if knew this! It will take them weeks to fix your shower but don’t be a day late on rent they will answer those calls and make moves on those situations! Absolutely horrible here.

The Pros:   Close to 805S and 163S, Walking distance are Restaurants, Gas Station, Kearny High, Mesa College,Sharp Hospital. Pet friendly Central Air, Pools, Work Out Room, Laundry.

My choice of this complex was its location and monthly rent. I needed to downsize from a large 3bd/2ba apartment that was outdated and mice infested; and the property management company increased the rent. So I decided to downsize and move when my lease ended. I live in Southern California and the economic standard of supply and demand absolutely applies here. There is a low supply of rentals in San Diego County with a high demand. So owners and property managers can assess rent at higher prices. Lemon Grove is one of the smaller communities east of San Diego so there are opportunities to rent for less. My 2bd/2ba (2 full baths) apartment is 900sq ft; but the layout makes it appear and feel larger. There was an update completed recently so upgraded carpet was installed, new paint throughout, new cabinet doors and fixtures in the bathrooms and kitchen, new flooring in the entry, baths and kitchen and new appliances (black instead of white). There are laundry facilities (two) on the property so the washer/dryer situation is still convenient. I have covered parking that is included in the rent. (There was a monthly fee for covered parking at my former place.) There is a wall unit air conditioner (my former place had center air/heating); but the point is I still have air conditioning. So it was worth the move even though I gave up amenities such as a business center, wi-fi in the business center, a recreation center, a washer/dryer in the unit and central air/heating.

Olea Apartments in Little Italy are beautiful, new, and in a prime location in this neighborhood of San Diego. I moved into to my unit last August after the building finished construction and I truly never want to leave! The design is sleek, contemporary, and easily complemented with different decor styles. The upside of this building is that there aren't excessive amenities that compound the rent. So we pay for what we live in; nothing else. Other communities in the area offer pools, fitness centers, etc. that jack up the rent for the same square footage by at least $1,000 and more. If you don't use those amenities, you're just giving away your money. And realistically, you can pay for a better equipped gym with more on-site amenities for less than actually offered at these other places and for WAY less money. Olea has a coffee shop, beer tasting room, and soon to be open "Raki Raki" sushi and ramen house, dubbed the #1 ramen house in the entire state of California via Zagat. Only a few steps away is Juniper & Ivy, an upscale restaurant curated by chef Richard Blais, Ballast Point brewery, an urban winery, and many more boutiques, restaurants, and specialty stores. Walking distance from the weekly Little Italy farmer's market offers residents fresh vegetables & fruits as well as locally produced food. Little Italy is an up and coming neighborhood of downtown San Diego, and Olea is located in a perfect spot close to the epicenter of its popular spots, but situated conveniently to not be in the middle of it all. This offers privacy, quiet, and ease of access right off the freeway. Although the flight path flies overhead, the double pane windows offer outstanding sound protection. You'd never know we're so close to an airport! I highly recommend the Olea building. I am very satisfied living here, and plan on doing so for years to come!

Basically this place was the best we could find with the most room for the price in a great quiet location, and the only downsides are no air conditioning, loud snot rocketeers, and random long gazes into the eyes of the peeping neighbors. Leaks in the ceiling allowing rain into apartment ceiling - and mold grows. 1980s appliances. Plumbing/sewage problems. Maintenance is super apathetic and slow. New management has ruined these apartments. This place used to be amazing. The grounds were beautifully kept, the staff were helpful and polite, and issues were always addressed in a timely and professional manner. NOW, THINGS ARE ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE, FOR YOUR OWN SANITY DO NOT COME LIVE HERE.

This place has gone so far downhill. Save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.

I have lived at the Reserve for 3 years now and all was going great until management changed a few months ago. 'Corporate office' is referred to (located in Austin) everytime questions are asked. Seems no one in the leasing office can answer questions. The leasing office is short staffed as is the maintenance staff. Their website has no way to report maintenance needs, and there is no maintenance staff available on weekends. The repaving project has been a nightmare for elderly and handicapped. We were told each repaving phase would take 2 days when indeed it took them a week to partially complete phase 1. The painting of the entire complex is another issue. The color scheme of blue, green, orange and ecru leaves a lot to be desired. Why not just refresh the current colors and clean up the weeds and trash bins? New management has introduced 'valet trash pick up' which is an attempt to keep trash in bags instead of residents throwing loose trash in the large bins. This valet trash is not an option for the responsible residents who know how to bag their trash and walk the few feet to the bin.  
If I hadn't already signed a lease, I would be looking elsewhere at this point but I'm hoping the corporate office will fully staff this site soon and take care of the residents with respectful and timely communication and service.

We started our paperwork with the Reserve at the very beginning of June. They took a $350 deposit to hold the apartment, and then dragged out finalizing the lease for 5 weeks, making tons of excuses for their delays and assuring us every step of the way that everything was fine (as it should have been, we have plenty of money, good credit, a great rental history, volunteered to pay the entire lease up front, and had a great co-signer as a backup) - only to tell us we weren't approved, 6 days before our agreed upon move-in day. 

In the end, liquid assets are inadequate as income proof, they don't allow you to pay for the entire lease up-front as a "rule", and they don't allow you to use a co-signer if you're over 28, as another "rule". All of which were concerns we addressed in detail on day one, before we paid the deposit, because as sole proprietor business owners our tax returns reflect a low taxable income due to a mountain of deductions, including initial investment write-offs, which we have detailed logs for. Again, everything was assured to be fine. Had they told us all of these “rules” at the beginning we would have simply left and found a property that had more reasonable terms. 

Needless to say, their bizarre stalling has been catastrophic for both our family and business when combined with the housing crisis in the area, and the fact that our existing lease was up. Good luck finding room for a family of four at the last second anywhere right now, even if you can pay for the entire lease up front. 

Do yourself a favor, stay far away from this place.
I’ve lived here a year now and love it! I feel safe and any problems are taken care of within 24 hours. Staff are very friendly.  Great place to live!
Pretty cool place to live at.  They will work with you if you have any problems.

I moved here about 5 months ago despite the bad reviews. I decided to give them a try, and I cannot regret my choice. Great apartment complex!! Recently changed ownership and service has improved significantly. Maintenance is on top of their game and all apartments have been recently upgraded. Its an okay place to live. The residents are very nice but the apartments have a lot of a/c problem such as water leaking from the ceiling.

Save your money and your sanity. This place is a joke as far as management and maintenance workers. The concrete walkways are dirty and often cluttered with debris.  When I first moved in, there were no noise issues and now I hear late night music thumping for hours. Forget about relaxing by the pool, using the bbq or strolling on the path. The noise is so loud the windows shake. Can't be inside or outside the apartment. You have to leave to get peace. Wish I had paid attention to the review that said this. I don't want this to happen to anyone else.
Definitely best apartments I've lived in, plenty of light, specious closets. Open layout. On the down side the living room was small and couldn't clean the walls with out the paint coming off.
The apartments are nice. They are a little old and things in my apartment keep breaking, but they are being upgraded. They are pricey for what you get, but hopefully the upgrades help.
it's a good community, safe place , clean , good maintenance 24/7 .,

The smell of a dog hit you as soon as you entered the apt. foyer/stairs and study room.
