I have one major issue that I think potential residents should be aware of.

Water Bill: This has been my biggest beef during my time here. So as a refresher; I live on floorplan A1 (the smallest), I live alone, I traveled out of town regularly throughout the month and I have no pets. Now that we’ve established that I have to say some of the water bills I’ve received while living here have been absolutely ludicrous. I’ve received bills as low as $12 and as high as $144. That’s right, a $144 water bill.

The apartment complex does not handle the water billing. They contract that out to a company called NW President.They read the meter and send out the bills. Villas at Mira Loma then collects on the bills sent out by NWP. The first time I went down to the leasing office to speak with them about the excessive water bills they credited me part of the bill. While I appreciated that gesture, it did not resolve the issue of the water bill being so high in the first place. The second time it happened I was told that they could not credit me a second time. When I asked what could be done, I was told to call NWP. When I contacted NWP, they requested that a bucket test be done on the apartment. The bucket test was done and no leak was found. Now it was clear to me that there could not possibly be a leak based on how the bills would fluctuate up and down from month to month.

Over the coming months I would get bounced back and forth between the property staff and NWP with each telling me the other was responsible for the meter. Another bucket test was done which again found no leak. I found this frustrating and poor service as I own neither the meter nor the property itself. As a resident and a customer, I expect to receive help when there is an issue with the unit I currently reside in. Being passed back and forth like a hot potato is not what I expected.

The end result was that I had to contact TriVest McNeil Real Estate directly to reach a resolution. The resolution was that after my water bill is posted to my account I contact the folks in the leasing office and they credit me part of the bill. Even with the credit my bill is still much higher than what I was originally paying the first few months I lived in the complex. My hypothesis is that I am being charged for multiple units in the building but I have no way of proving that without cooperation from NWP and the property staff.

Choose wisely my rental friends!

 used to be a good property. I've been here 24 years. You should begin by reading the reviews of of Honey Hill Apartments written in 2017; there are multiple critically correct writeups. Be advised not to rent anywhere where Catalyst manages. Walk the property and look around the dumpsters, parking lots, etc. Go in the buildings and look at the dirt in the common areas, the unfinished painting around the doors of each unit. You have to get your mail at the post office as they can't get around to installing a security system after many mailboxes were broken into 3 months ago. And how about people being without heat for 1 month because the property manager doesn't have the authority to contract for repairs without corporate approval which obviously takes too long. Oh yes, were on our 7th property manager in 12 months. The system doesn't allow you to pay ahead of time, doesn't know what you owe, so you have to tell the Wal-Mart or HEB worker what the correct amount is. For January there was a mystery charge of $1.75 added on by Catalyst, so all our bills were wrong. And bills come no earlier than the 2nd last business day of the month. When no bill comes you have to go to the office and get a printout from them. In December the system didn't work at all; instead of posting a note on everyone's door telling them to get a money order instead, we know nothing until we go to the store to pay. In conclusion, hang around long enough to catch 2-3 tenants outside and ask them about living here. That save me from writing twice as much as I have already.

STRONG WARNING to any considering renting from these most unprofessional, in-efficient landlords we've ever dealt with!

My time at New England Village Apartment Complex was a living nightmare that still haunts me. They demanded $2000 in unjust fees after I moved out, all because I didn't give written notice, despite fulfilling my entire lease and being the perfect tenant. The horrors I endured during my stay were beyond comprehension.

From the moment I moved in, it felt like the apartment was cursed. Persistent leaks dripped like a slow, torturous water torture, never properly fixed, creating an incessant, maddening rhythm. The air conditioning barely functioned, turning my apartment into a sweltering oven, the oppressive heat suffocating me and driving my energy bills sky-high. No matter how much I begged management for help, my pleas fell on deaf ears.

Water supply disruptions were frequent, occurring almost every other week. One particularly harrowing week, the hot water was off entirely while my mother visited. We were trapped in a hellish routine of cold showers, the air thick with the stench of mold and decay. Cockroaches scurried through the shadows, their numbers growing each day, a creeping infestation that invaded every corner of my existence.

The laundry room was a forsaken place, a graveyard of broken washers and dryers that were never repaired. It was as if the complex thrived on our suffering, each malfunctioning machine a testament to our despair.

Despite my verbal notice to vacate due to my lease ending, the management coldly insisted on a written notice, ignoring my plight and the horrors I had endured. The unjust charges they imposed were the final twist of the knife.

Living there felt like being trapped in a haunted house, every creak and drip a reminder of the malevolent force that seemed to possess the building. I strongly advise against renting here if you value your sanity.

If it’s during the summer, your AC has a good chance of going out and they don’t spend the $$$$$ they make on maintenance. All year long you’ll see roaches. There is a large feral cat colony nearby but despite that there are rats and you’ll probably hear them in your vents. The unit is decades old, and looks its age. Every so often they will paint over the cracks in the walls and do their best to hide the shoddy infrastructure of the HVAC Systems.
I told them my AC was failing two months ago and it’s the dead of summer and it’s the same temperature outside as it is inside (90 degrees).

The apartments are beautiful if you like a vintage feel. However, watch out if you plan to rent in an enclosed building. The cigarette smell will not go away because it comes through the vents from the other apartments. My clothes reeked all the time and it was so annoying. Maintenance is a drag. It took months for them to fix our toilet and running faucet meanwhile racking up a high water bill for everyone in the building. Woman in the office catches an attitude with you when you try to ask simple questions or check the status of your requests that they never seem to get to. It is a great area for cheap price, but the little things start to add up the longer you are there. Honestly, spend a little more for a place that can give better service.

This past year I lived in apartment 2V, a three bedroom two bathroom layout with two other girls. We attended the nearby university, so New England Village was a great location since it was so close by. Our apartment layout was decent – a good deal for college students on a budget. However, proximity to school and cheap rent are the extent of the positive things I have to say about New England Village.

While my roommates and I were gone over winter break, rats moved in to our apartment. We came back to an apartment that had been ransacked. Chewed up carpet, destruction of personal belongings, and rat droppings everywhere. The rats were living in the attic space above our apartment and coming in during the night hours. We continued to deal with this problem for the rest of our time living in the apartment. Management was extremely unhelpful. They initially responded by cleaning and patching the carpet and setting some traps. Over the next few months we killed 21 rats with these traps. It was clearly a problem that needed more attention than a few traps, but management refused to do more. At several points when we demanded they either have a professional come out or relocate us to a different apartment, they pretended to be unaware that we had a rat infestation in the first place. 

Besides the rat infestation, we had other smaller issues with management. They kept changing their email address, making it difficult for us to ensure they were getting our maintenance requests. If we wanted anything to get fixed, we had to call and email them multiple times. We also had problems with our air conditioning, as it broke down at the very least five times during the hotter months. 

Overall, living in this apartment was a traumatic experience. One night I woke up to the sound of a rat gnawing at my bedroom door trying to get in, and all of us came across bodies of dead rats in the apartment at some time or another. We felt uncomfortable in our own apartment. Living at New England Village might be worth it if nothing goes wrong during your stay there. However, I wouldn't recommend taking that risk.

I'm a college student working at the Stinson Municipal Airport, and I've been living in a studio for over a year. 
My experience living at this complex hasn't been terrible, but it hasn't been great. 
You'll have roaches. Accept it or move somewhere else. I keep my apartment extremely clean, but it's no use if the complex is filthy. The treatment doesn't last. I've resigned to just having a can of Raid as a permanent staple in my kitchen. Most of the time it's just the little ones; I'll occasionally find the Texas-sized ones in my apartment. 
The neighborhood isn't normally too loud, but there's always an exception. Maybe 1x/month I'll get woken up by people in the pool or just loitering and being noisy. 
The parking lot frequently has pot-holes. They get fixed, 2 weeks later they come back. Just drive slowly. 
Maintenance requests take a week to be taken care of. That's best-case-scenario; I've had it take over a month in the past. From my experience, the squeaky wheel gets greased.....i.e. -- if you call in and complain enough or show face at the office they'll take care of it more quickly. 
Most of my neighbors are friendly enough or keep to themselves. I've never explicitly felt unsafe. I've had a few (2) strangers approach my door...there's a peephole so I just check and if I don't know who it is I don't answer. Both times they went away. 
My car has been broken into 3x, but I can't really say "broken-in" in the traditional sense of the word. I drive a really old car, so my car doors are typically unlocked. I don't leave anything valuable in my car. Who knows how many times someone has gone through my car, but I only know of 3 occurrences because the offender(s) went through my glove box and left napkins all over the place. It doesn't really bother me; nothing worth taking gets left out there. I would recommend anyone considering moving here to practice the same habit. I've never had someone break-in/tamper with my apartment. 
The laundry facilities are functional, but don't let your clothes sit in there for long. I've had my underwear stolen from the dryer. Yes, specifically underwear. I don't care to know the reason the individual decided to take that specific article of clothing. 
Overall it's not the worst place in the world to live, and the important thing is that the rent's cheap. So if you can put up with those inconveniences, then you can move in. If you're not ok with those standards, look elsewhere.

The downsides to Post Gateway are: visitor parking is extremely limited to the point it practically doesn't exist, not all rooms have a washer/dryer (either have to rent or use the ones downstairs), gyms don't have Wifi, and lease has harsh restrictions on leaving. 5 stars. Great customer service. Great maintenance staff.
Great customer service. Maintenance team was quick to respond. Would recomend.

I would give them zero stars if that were possible!!!!  My husband and I lived here for two years and it was the worst two years ever. This property is excellent feel comfortable and at home
Not treating well ,doesnt listen to us if we have any concerns

Don’t care about residents. Not recommended.

I moved in June of 2024 from out of state the staff was very accommodating.(Francisco and Alex) Apartment is beautiful and modern. (2 bd 2 bath) No Issues. They keep the grounds clean close to lots of shopping and restaurants. I would renew my lease no question.

I woke up covered in bites, only to find the bedbugs crawling up the walls! Company does not care about residents, money hungry. Resident voices do not matter. Will put everyone and everything above the people who pay thousands of dollars a month to be here.
Francisco the leasing agent is very helpful & knowledgable. I definitely would've rented but the space is too small. Awesome community.  Everyone was super friendly on the property.

The apartment did not update their towing company on the parking pass design update that happened months ago. The property manager lacked any empathy and did nothing to help us. Not even an Uber ride. She said the towing company wouldn't make us pay so she didn't see why we were still going back and forth about it.

All of this, and the property manager remained smug and even smiled a few times at my frustration. I'm disgusted. To me, this shows the apartment does not care about its residents.

Shouldn't the apartment accept responsibility for this? They should have let their tow company know months ago about the design change.

I was considering renewing the lease but after this situation, I would be a fool to do so.

My husband paid their deposit upon approval. A day later the assistant manager gave the apartment to one of their current tenants. Didnt tell him anything. He found out once he came to sign paperwork. The manager was dismissive and didnt talk to us. The assistant manager avoided us. They kept his deposit too.  I wouldn't let my dog move there after that encounter. It ended up being a blessing because we heard they have constant car break-ins. I recommend do not move here.
I moved into an apartment and it was crawling with roaches.  Here are the pictures of proof!  I also have a video!

Be very careful with this place, the people in the office will look for many ways to get your money, I left my apartment spotless and they even charged me for the coffee in the office. Be very careful, this is not a place I would recommend.

Been working with Tiffany at IMT. Communication via phone and email has been consistent and timely. Very thorough with information and the property is very well maintained/clean. I have not currently moved (will be in Jan), but so far it has been an excellent experience and I look forward to moving.

Just relocated to Charlotte and living in IMT Ballantyne. Nothing but a positive experience every step of the way. From before I moved thru the application process to move in, office staff were available, helpful, and pleasant. Every aspect of my move was like clockwork. My apartment was spotless upon move in. I had a minor repair issue and maintenance is great. Timely response. Went above and beyond to fix the issue. Awesome place to live.
Sharon

I do love this location. The staff is amazing and always there if there is an issue. My only complaint is the clubhouse closes at 5:30 daily.  This leaves me so disappointed as I am not able to enjoy this amenity unless it’s the weekend.  And even on the weekends, it closes at 5:30 which ruins plans if you want to have people over and enjoy the amenities.  the clubhouse is great. I just wish I was able to enjoy it at all.

7 months in and things are still great at IMT Ballantyne!The maintenance team Gage and Brian are so helpful and so reliable, although my requests were minor you can count on them to get it done. The office staff always greet you with a smile and always willing to help even if it’s just a recommendation on a restaurant. I’ve work with Brittany from day one and been very responsive anytime I’ve reached out and answer all my questions in such a professional and attentive manner. Thanks IMT team for make my stay an enjoyable one!

Thanks 550 for not only providing us with some pretty amazing amenities including the dog parks that my fur babies absolutely love. Also for making this more than just a place to live but somewhere that feels like home, especially with concierge. Jalauni is always there with a smile, warm words that can make the worst days feel better and would even go out his way to assist with carrying groceries or just any questions i have. Concierge Dion is always there to help as well as give me laughs when I come in. Jalauni and Dion have no idea how their amazing energy and willingness to help really changes the trajectory of our day sometimes. This has been an amazing experience!
Awesome amenities, common areas events, and living spaces in a great location.

The reviews written 5/5/20 were during a promotional offer to get a free bottle of tequila to leave a positive review.

This place is awful. The construction is shoddy. The 6th floor and below continually flooded and we had water damage in our ceiling. Our oven was broken for 7+ months and we couldn't get maintenance to fix it. Our water filter needed to be replaced and maintenance said that they didn't have any replacements so just disabled the indicator light. Management didn't enforce any covid precautions and still had their private bar open on the 21st floor. People continually threw things off the balcony. The dog parks are filthy and there were multiple days where there was dog waste in the hallways. Their fire alarms are faulty and went off all the time requiring evacuation. There are only two elevators for the tower so if someone is moving in/out you only have one elevator to service 21 stories; there are times you would wait 10+ minutes for an elevator.

NWR properties are like no other. The amenities are superb, the staff is amazing and the units are beautiful. While this is week one, Uptown 550 is THE address to live. The tower provides a living experience that will change your life. I am so proud to call it home!

We met Alexis at lunch today. She convinced me and my buddies to come by for a tour after we mentioned that we were looking for a new place. She gave the best tour experience. The property and all the amenities were amazing! The rooftop bar was lit! She
took the time to explain all the questions we had, and was very enthusiastic. Highly recommend Uptown 550 and look forward to being future residents.

We didn't provide notice to vacate in the specified time in our lease. Not much of a heads up was provided. We had to pay for an extra month of rent, which is understandable. However, they charged us double for that time. Definitely not market price and unfair during a pandemic in my opinion.

The amenities at this complex seem great when you first tour. But the poor construction of this building far outweighs the benefit of a nice rooftop bar. There are other complexes out there with the same types of services. 

The front line staff in the leasing office are pretty nice but nothing gets addressed to the standards you’d expect in this type of establishment. And upper management could care less about you.

I have loved my time at uptowwn 550! It is always very clean, the staff is super friendly, and the amenities are amazing. My favorite is the sauna! Not to mention the walking distance to uptown and so many restaurants and activities.

I have been living here for 2 months now, and I couldn't be happier that I made the choice to live in Uptown550. The location is absolutely amazing, a 5 minute walk to SouthEnd, or a 2 minute walk to the Spectrum Center - it's everything I could have ever asked for. The apartments themselves are modern, and are a very clean style. The amenities themselves really drive the entire experience as well - beautiful pool, gym, and rooftop bar! Don't think twice - choose to live in Uptown550.
Excellent place to live!!!! Staff is fun and personable.  Always eager to help!

I have been a resident for 2 months at Uptown 550 and couldn't be more pleased with my experience thus far! Being a Charlotte native, living in multiple communities around the area, and having just moved back after 2 years of renting in San Francisco, I can confidently say that living here is a treat! The quality of the interiors is a step above many other rental options in uptown Charlotte. Being a new building, there were a few minor maintenance items early on that were addressed quickly and precisely. With outstanding amenities to offer, the staff has done an incredible job at providing resident events that are creating a true sense of community among residents. They have offered free weekly small group fitness classes, botox and spa facials, trivia nights, and cookouts. Mario, Desmond, Engrid, Erica, and Gamal have been ultra available and accommodating. It's never easy to keep residents happy when you are supporting a property that is still partially under construction, but the leasing and maintenance staff are handling it beautifully and creating a community experience anyone would want to be a part of! Thanks for all you do!

I moved to Uptown 550 two weeks ago and I absolutely love this place. The amenities are incredible and the location is perfect.  I am walking distance from Target, Trader Joe’s and multiple parks.  The prices are extremely competitive and the entire staff, Mario, Erica, Engrid and Desmond are so helpful!

I can't recommend this place enough. Brand new building, staff goes above and beyond and they're so accommodating (Mario and Desmond are both so amazing and helpful and made the move-in process so smooth. They're on top of everything). Maintenance requests are completed very quickly and the maintenance staff is so kind. The apartment itself is absolutely perfect - the floorpan was so well designed, all of the appliances are top quality and I haven't heard any noise from any of my neighbors at all. Floor to ceiling windows provide so much light, and the dimmers in every room are such a nice touch. Tons of kitchen counter space, barn doors, and I have enough room for a sectional and a 4-person dining table. There's also a mud-room area and shelving when you walk in, so you aren't cramped at all. Very reasonably priced as well. One other thing I love is that it's just a 3 minute walk to Whole Foods, a 30 second drive to get on the highway and it is never difficult to get out of the parking garage, even during rush hour traffic. Even though it's still under construction, I don't find it to be an inconvenience at all, and they're making so much progress daily. Excited to see it all finished because the amenities will be the best in Charlotte. They've thought of everything. I could ramble on, but bottom line is I would recommend this to anyone looking to move uptown.

Not even sure where to begin! I recently signed a lease at Uptown 550 and the entire experience- from start to finish- was absolutely amazing! Moving can be super stressful, but Mario, Desmond, Gamal & their whole crew went above and beyond to ensure a seamless & enjoyable process! I am so excited to live here and am proud to call Uptown 550 my home!
I could write a story on why not to live here but just don’t.

This apartment is ok. Cons: The grounds are an eye sore. For being a new building it already looks run down. They need to do some serious power washing of the building and pavement, lay some fake grass or mulch so it’s not just mud everywhere when you step outside. No one picks up after their dogs. Cheapest appliances: I think they have the first ever made dishwasher which is beyond loud and cheap stackable washer and dryer. Neighbors: zero respect for each other. If you want peace and quiet move elsewhere because the walls are made of paper. Parking garage: they don’t have parking passes and people just tailgate in. Zero security so it’s very sketchy.  Pros: gym is nice and they do a good job of cleaning with covid. There’s always workers in the hall cleaning. Maintenance is friendly and quick to respond to issues. Overall way better apartments available in Charlotte for a similar price.

Pros: Convenient to NoDa (walk/scooter) and to uptown via CATS station across the street. Building is new and well appointed with all the amenities you would expect. Pool, resident lounge, onsite gym, etc. Decent value compared to comparable properties.

Cons: Neighborhood is a work in progress and building is surrounded with light industry and vacant lots. 25th street bridge is under construction which will be beautiful when completed, but for now there is construction noise during the week.

Minor complaints are the outdoor grills are electric instead of gas, so little better than using an indoor air-fryer. Haven’t been able to take full advantage of the amenities yet due to Covid, but not the fault of the property. Gym hours and other features are limited during pandemic.

I found about this complex from a resident who moved in when it first opened and after comparing it to other complexes in different neighborhoods, the location/amenities/price of Warp + Weft were unmatched. Great proximity to the LYNX/breweries/Optimist Hall(!!!)/grocery/and everything in NoDa. I moved in Oct and the staff helped me find the exact unit that fit my needs in terms of views/cost. Highly recommend to those moving to the area

good view of the city and the sky. spending a good amount of time indoors recently makes it hard on everyone, but the people and the residents are always so cheerful and nice. nice poolside area and the events are cool too. i like the resident lounge although we cant stay in there too long for obvious reasons. 10/10

My experience was amazing. Me and my boyfriend moved to Charlotte a few months ago and were looking for apartments. When we came across Alta Warp & Weft we had nothing but the best service. Ramatu gave me a tour of the community. They had great amenities such as a pool that looks like it belongs in a 5 star hotel, an incredible gym, resident lounge, and our personal favorite, the community GARDEN. Plus, so much more. On another day, my boyfriend came to tour with Shelsea due to our deferring work schedules and was equally wowed. The rooms are huge and up to date, I have closets that’s as spacious as the bedroom with a washer and dryer in it. The overall community is friendly and peaceful. The Manager Alicia has also been very accommodating. She gave us updates from the application process and what was needed whenever we called with a question in our transition to becoming permanent residents here. Truthfully, the entire staff here work very well together to make us feel at home even through the journey of applying. My boyfriend and I are so happy to come home to our new apartment and to know that there is a staff willing to go above and beyond at any time is refreshing.

I have been living at Providence Row for 3 months and am already looking elsewhere. The staff is extra wonderful UNTIL you move in, and then they completely stop caring about you. (I could write a book about that alone). The apartments were  poorly built. If you need maintenance they will NOT give you any sorts of heads up before coming…they won’t tell you the day or give you a window of time, so good luck planning around that! It was a nightmare for us, and the staff could not care any less, please just trust me. The locks on doors have been broken ever since I moved in. Definitely not safe. I moved here for the coffee shop, but there’s been no barista for almost a month now. The concierge quit so good luck dealing with getting your packages. Even the lobby has an alarm that’s been broken for a month now and beeps so loud all day every day, literally every second. Just hate it here so much that I wanted to warn people. Their good reviews I’ve noticed are people who just finished their tour and are excited to live here, just like I was.

Do not be fooled by the nice amenities at Providence Row.. the construction is cheap and the overall quality assurance/oversight is an abstract failure. This places an undue burden on leasing management focused on occupancy and profit beholden to the company and shareholders vice the paying customers. The leasing staff are not trained properly for quality assurance tasking, problem identification and process efficiency when it comes to new construction. Essentially, you are living in a construction work zone without proper management. Several residents have discussed their move in issues. They range from:
Hot water heater not connected to power
HVAC system not working
Laminate flooring peeling up
Refrigerator water disconnected
Uneven flooring
Washing machine and plumbing connections are reversed.
Residents are burdened by conducting quality assurance on a level in which the contractor should be accountable for and the leading staff/company should require.
Construction- 0 stars

Property Management/Leasing
Overwhelmed and Under Staffed. Concerns:
No Concierge- Package delivery is an Easter egg hunt. No process in place that assists residents or delivery drivers
Building cleanliness is not maintained on a daily basis to include trash left in garage and laminate flooring dirty.
Constant fire alarm panel beeping in lobby.
Response time is lacking due to focus on occupancy rather than designated staff members to assist with tenants issues.
No designated process to QA apartments prior to renting
Property Management-0 stars

Maintenance- response time has been excellent. They are responsible for two buildings.. one with old problems and one with new construction issues. They should have more staffing to address construction issues.
Maintenance- 3 stars due to response time

Cleaning-1 star

Amenities-unfinished
Not Rated..

Summary- Providence Row Phase II is NOT READY for occupancy. Talk to residents. Take time to thoroughly look at the property while touring. Do not get enamored with the glitter of the amenity spaces. There are numerous places more cost effective, better quality and properly maintained.
Overall-1 star

If you wish you pay the extra to live in a 'luxury' apartment community WITHOUT the 'luxury' experience, this place is it for you.
This place is not managed well.  Very weak security, new building/units poorly built; already falling apart.  They moved residents in way too early without proper timeline of making sure the it is ready.  Fire marshall inspections are still going on every week, almost everything gets broken, and all the doors are open 24/7.  NOT SAFE.

Providence row is a beautiful community, that’s well maintained and has great leasing professionals. I worked with Bre to find the right apartment for me and she helped me get all my concerns/questions promptly addressed at move in. 10/10 would recommend!

Just moved in to the luxury condos at Providence Row and could not be happier. A good demographic mix, amazing amenities - my kids are already using the hot tub, it is quiet and everyone is so nice. Oh and the barista in the morning is an added bonus to get my day started. Let’s be honest though the staff is top notch especially Bre! She helped me through everything and gave an awesome tour to my kids and I when we first stopped by! Thanks Bre!
I have been in Providence Row for just over a month now and can't describe how happy I am here.  The staff and facilities are second to none and there is everything you could want on tap.

I am surprised at some of these reviews. I have a great experience and the staff have been so friendly and helpful (especially, Patrick my lease agent) I work from home and I don’t hear much day or night. I would recommend, in my personal experience!

This apartment complex isn’t worth half of what they charge for rent. I’ve lived in dorms, and college apartments that are more adequate at 8 metro’s price point. Poor quality built apartments, nasty and inconsiderate tenants, and something is always out service. If you move here, make SURE you look at the actual unit on the lease before you sign. The building they show you is the best building here, and sets up awfully high expectations, that the other incomplete and dirty buildings just can’t reach. I was rather embarrassed to bring my parents here, but that’s my own fault for not taking my own advice. Currently a student, my hands were tied and I needed to extend my lease for a while, and I still get upset when I think about how much time I have left. The staff is nice though!

Don't pay attention to reviews before the beginning of 2022. This place USED to be great. 8 metro station horrible. Do not move here! I lived here for over 2 years. Since then a new property manager took over and the quality of these apartments in every aspect as has gone down significantly. It has gotten so bad, that this morning I woke up and my car was gone. They had the car towed of a resident who lived here for years and when I brought it too their attention they basically told me I just have to pay. So not only was money lost due to being late to work and having to reschedule clients, but a $300 tow fee on top of that. Months ago when they first took over, I asked them about the new stickers, and they "said don't worry about, we are not towing right now." 8 metro station is not only incompetent, but they do not care about the residents that live here.

Please learn from my mistake, this is NOT a quiet community and I would not recommend this complex to anyone looking to work from home or students that need to focus/study. If loud environments disrupt your well-being, I highly recommend paying a little more to live elsewhere.

I’ve found that if I need to concentrate, I have to commute into Uptown and go into the office. Considering the cost of gas and parking, I’d probably break even living somewhere else while also enjoying the comforts of working from home.

We’ve talked to management multiple times about  the vibrations we FEEL from our downstairs neighbor’s bass music while sitting in our living room. I’ve lived in apartments for over 10 years and I understand that it’s not uncommon to hear moderate levels of sound from other units. But I have NEVER experienced vibrations coming through the floor.

The community manager told me that they “can’t tell people to not play music in their apartment”. I tried to explain that it’s more than music, but she didn’t seem to care. All I wanted was a courtesy reminder to keep their bass at reasonable levels. We’ve called the courtesy officer on multiple occasions and that did not seem to help either. I’ve invested in noise-canceling earphones but that doesn’t stop the vibrations.

The problem doesn’t seem to be unique to our unit either. I’d consider this a party complex as we’ve heard parties on many occasions while walking throughout the community. I would recommend requesting a copy of the community rules before paying the $200/person application fee so you’re able to see what your protections are as a resident. Most communities have quiet hours or guidelines around noise control but the verbiage in the contract is very loose and they don’t seem to enforce anything.

We did not visit in person before moving here because we were not local to Charlotte at the time. If I had seen the level of cleanliness and security (or lack thereof) of the property, I would have kept looking for other communities. I can look past the condition of the property, but I can’t get past the noise.

The community was bought out last summer and it’s so unorganized but their are heavy rules being wrongly enforced. Elevator never works, not enough visitor parking, leasing office has a nasty attitude

Hanna did an awesome job on getting me and my kids in an apartment. She was very proficient and got the job done immediately. So far so good. Complex looks exactly how it does on pictures. Would recommend if you’re looking for a nice, safe place.

Amazing amenities and I love my apartment view! I would recommend the Ellis to anyone looking to live in a high rise apartment. 

The events are well planned and thought out as well.

Apartment itself is nice but the large amount of homelessness and noise in the area is almost not worth renewing my lease. 1BD has no balcony. 

Amenities are great. I would consider this location for a 2BD and up.

Just go elsewhere! I'm sure you can afford it and so could I. Trying to even reserve an apt at this place was a headache and the staff lacked empathy and actual reasons for why they wanted more information than mortgage lenders. This building is in an unsafe area with homeless lined up just on the adjacent street. There's also a loud hookah bar across the street and it stays open late. Choose peace not this place.

I toured the high-rise studio and 1-bedroom apartment homes and they are beautiful with concrete construction between the ceilings and floors. The 33rd floor clubhouse with pool and commons areas is breathtaking. I also toured the mid-rise 1-bedroom apartment homes and I was impressed with the size of the unit. All in all I am excited to move-in and experience all this community has to offer on a daily basis.

These people literally took my money and made it seem like I was moving into a place. Communication SUCKS! I moved out of my apartment in Columbia only to be told I was unable to move here after she was aware that I had no where else to go. Leasing management sucks at communicating. I wish I would have never trusted these people. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME!
This entire process has been very questionable at best. Poor communication and lack of follow up are two of my pet peeves in any leasing staff and The Ellis represented both well in my experience.

Multiple cars have been broken into..including mine. Hallways smell like trash. Doors going into the building sometimes don’t lock behind you -meaning anyone can get in. Homeless people sleep in the stairwells and elevator works 3 months out of a year.

I tried to be as patient as possible and give them the benefit of the doubt. I’ve been patient and gave them every chance possible to change my opinion, but all I have to say is read all the reviews since September of 2022. It’s all consistent. It’s all true.

I had a water leak that led to extensive damage below the floors, baseboards, door casing, behind the walls, and under the carpet all right before Thanksgiving, and it took two weeks of me constantly following up every day desperately begging for action… which resulted in them finally settling on moving me to a new unit.

Rhonda and Curtis are nice people, but that’s about the only positive I have since MAA took over. Exterior doors don’t lock, so you don’t even “get what you pay for” when it comes to security. Car break-ins, and all we are told from management is “we can not and do not guarantee your safety and security” basically telling us good luck on staying safe, but make sure your rent isn’t late!!!!

If you’re looking here, don’t. Turn around and go in the opposite direction as fast as possible & prioritize your health and safety over the bold cover up of pretty pictures.

This was decent with Novel, it had its quirks and wasn’t perfect but it has not been peaches and cream since MAA took it over, nice team, but the new
Ownership was/is NOT prepared and it has been a bad experience ever since. They don’t even have a maintenance team.
TL;DR
- Apartment is next to HVAC Closet.
- HVAC is leaking into our closet and our bathroom.
- Something like this should be fixed immediately, our clothes in our laundry basket is soaked and we’re using our towels to soak up the water.

This happened once earlier this month but Sully came and fixed it immediately. I spoke the the MAA team this morning at around 9:30am and nothing has happened. It’s gotten so bad that the water has leaked through the floor and damaged the paint/drywall of the mailroom. Mold has grown as well but I suspect thats from the last time this happened. Also mentioned and usually once mold is concerned property management companies bend over backwards to rectify and remediate…..still waiting.
In general it’s a great place to live. Excellent Staff and very convenient to commute
Great amenities and helpful staff available even on weekends!

It’s been the absolute best living here! Very friendly neighborhood and great events! My apartment feels like a home. The amenities are phenomenal, I doubt you could get this experience anywhere else in an apartment complex in Charlotte.
Great location, amenities, and resident events. Definitely worth considering.

Everyone that works in the Novel LoSo community I've encountered thus far has been great! Communication from the team has been positive, prompt, efficient, and made for a smooth move-in for me! I am excited to live here!
This apartment is great! Love the location, amenities, and modern touch. Awesome all around.
Move in was smooth. Staff are super friendly. Great location near Scaley Bark station, perfect for commuting to uptown. Looking forward to enjoying all the amenities!

Moving from out of state I had to do my apartment hunt online and I couldnt be more satisfied than how I feel right now. I truly feel like my apartment is a home and its just so beautiful. The property staff, specifically Amanda and Dallas are truly wonderful and kind. Maintenance and the coffee shop staff are wonderful as well! I have no complaints and the property has exceeded my expectations. Even the ongoing construction doesnt pose a problem because I cant hear it when Im home! I would highly recommend this building (and Im not being paid or receiving an incentive to say this)! 5 stars!

Such a UNIQUE spot in South End near all the breweries and restaurants!! I fell in love with the open co-working space and the LTH coffee shop in the building. My roommate and I decided to stop looking at other complexes after viewing here last week. So impressed with the interiors, amenities and how tall the ceilings are! We really enjoyed the leasing staff and how helpful Amanda, Dallas and Christian have been. We even had the manager, Roger, help us by calling to follow up after the tour. We felt right at home and cannot wait to move in to take advantage of all the amenities! I would definitely recommend to anyone looking for a new apartment in Charlotte's South End area!!

The finishes in the units are so beautiful. They've thought of everything! The staff is super friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable which helped make our decision easier. I've very excited about this location as well because it is so close to everything.

If I could give The Edge over 5 stars I absolutely would. My partner and I moved into the building in February of 2024 after relocating states and cannot say enough good things. We looked at over 15+ properties in South End with a super demanding list of needs and this place was totally the winner. Location is within walking distance to all the fun without being right on top of the action (so it’s so peaceful at night), the leasing team (shout out to Audrey C) is so helpful, the facilities are spotless and well kept, the amenities are excellent, resident events are always fun, and maintenance is extremely responsive. We look forward to re-signing next year! We love The Edge!

I love my apartment at The Edge! The floor plan is very spacious, amenities are great, and the staff members are so nice and helpful. It’s a great post grad location, but good for people who enjoy a more quiet living environment compared to some other areas of South End.

I absolutely fell in love with this place. Incredible amenities, perfect location, extremely attentive office staff, and all around very welcoming environment. Anyone looking to move to Charlotte would be lucky to live here!

Marsh properties have started construction right across the street of another apartments. Constructions works start at 5-6 am. So all those who want to live at construction site are welcome! 
Company doesnt care about people living around OR their own renters!

I have resided at The Leo Loso for several months, and while the experience has had its positives, there are substantial issues that overshadow the benefits

Pros:
Communicative and Approachable Staff: The office staff at The Leo Loso is consistently communicative and approachable. Especially on the weekends thanks Bria!

Cons:
Facility Door Issues: A critical concern is that all facility doors do not close adequately. This is a major security flaw and poses a risk to residents' safety. Also, on holidays when the leasing office is closed; the office entry doors remain open, until the "operational hours" come to an end. The automatic system should match leasing office hours, even on holidays, to avoid any unwanted guess.

Emergency Exit Problems: Some emergency exit doors in the stairwells do not open properly when the unlocking mechanism is pushed. This is a severe fire hazard that needs immediate attention.

Non-Operational Amenities: Several advertised amenities, including the car wash, grills, and fire pit, are not operational. This is disappointing and diminishes the value of living here.

Pool Area Maintenance: The sink area near the pool has a wooden part that is detached from where it belongs. Additionally, the pool doors are set to be unlocked from 10am to 8pm, which is a significant safety concern as it allows unauthorized access.

Faulty Delivery System: The latch system for deliveries is non-functional, making it difficult to receive packages securely and reliably.

Inadequate Security: The security personnel smoke on the property, despite it being a non-smoking facility, and they dispose of their ashes in the parking lot. Security measures are generally subpar, leading to several break-ins. These incidents are exacerbated by the malfunctioning facility doors. Including homeless individuals breaking into several apartments, that were both occupied and unoccupied.

Unreliable Security Contact: Calling the security number provided by the leasing office connects you to various promotional offers instead of actual security assistance, which is highly frustrating and unhelpful in emergencies.

Air Conditioning Issues: The sky lounge and several floor areas do not have air conditioning. This is a serious health concern, especially when outside temperatures exceed 90 degrees and inside temperatures in the sky lounge can surpass 100 degrees.

The numerous safety & security issues at The Leo Loso significantly detract from the overall living experience.

I regret to say that my experience at Trailside Noda has been quite disappointing due to an ongoing pest issue that has severely impacted my quality of life. I have been a tenant here for a little under 2 months and was satisfied for the most part up until now.

 For over two weeks, I have been plagued by an infestation of phorid flies in my apartment. Despite a visit from pest control, who treated the drains, the problem remains unresolved. The pest control service was not only ineffective but also misidentified the pest as fruit flies—something I had to correct myself after seeking a second opinion.  These are not pests I have ever encountered living in apartments over the past 3 years.

Every day, I see around 20 of these flies, particularly in the kitchen where they create a significant nuisance. Preparing meals has become impossible as I am constantly swarmed by flies, and any food or drinks left unattended are at risk of becoming infested. This is very inconvenient and unsanitary as I work from home and have found myself eating meals in my car to avoid the bugs.
The issue is not limited to the kitchen, as I have also found flies in the bathroom. Despite taking numerous steps to address the problem myself—such as treating the drains, sealing them at night, using a Zevo pest lamp, and maintaining a pristine space—the infestation persists. I have spent over $75 in supplies between Amazon and Walmart to help control this infestation, none of which have worked.

I reached out to the leasing office as well as a regional contact to express my ongoing frustration and request further help, but unfortunately, each time my emails were ignored. According to the office this has been a complaint from multiple tenants as some neighbors have also experienced a bug issue in their units. When I went in person, I was met with vague assurances that the problem would be addressed—yet no effective follow-up or response has been provided. This should not be surprising to me as communication was an issue within the application process as well.

In all, I am truly disappointed with my experience here at Trailside as it looked as if it would be the perfect place to start roots in Charlotte. Writing a review on this community was the last route I wanted to take in this situation, however, when someone is paying to live in a safe, clean space you would expect your concerns to be taken seriously.

I enjoy the amenities and my space. I am dissatisfied with the residents upkeep of the area, not cleaning up the trash or dog poop. I am dissatisfied with the residents loudness and inconsideration of other residents.
The tenants are friendly. The office staff is very professional and always helpful. Maintenance has gone above and beyond to get things done in a timely manner. I enjoy the peace and quiet.

I love my apartment. Its smaller than my last home, but its clean and cozy. If only i wasnt afraid of spiders... no other critters...just spiders.

Lived in one bedroom, great little space. Nice pool and equipment room, two gated entrances. Plenty of room for a one bedroom apartment. Great location. Many restaurants and shopping nearby. Access to interstate is close by. Post Ballantyne grounds are kept up well. Plenty of parking and parking spaces are wider than normal. Quiet. No issues with any tenants. Office personnel are professional and helpful with any issues. Maintenance requests are taken care of promptly and done the right way the first time.

Very good...front parking is an issue sometimes with customers from restaurant across the street taking up spaces meant for residents..rent getting way to expensive considering the apts are no longer new..but enjoy living here..

Great facilities, great support, great location. If something breaks or needs attention you just put it into their app and it?s fixed in one business day, and you don?t have to be home to let them in.

The complex is in walking distance to a variety of stores, great restaurants, entertainment and still close to the freeways - just 20 minutes away from the airport or downtown and still surrounded by beautiful landscape, ponds with fountains, which invite to walks and wonderful relaxation after work as do the pool and the gym.

Post Ballantyne has a beautiful property, is a quick walk from grocery shopping and restaurants, and is a very calm and pleasant place to live.  They are dog friendly and provide plenty of areas to walk your dogs.  The neighbors are polite and everyone really keeps the grounds clean.  All in all, it is a great place!

Awesome manicured grounds with lots of beautiful trees and landscaping.
Excellent office staff and service staff.
Good size apartments, with walkin closets, a lot of windows for bright rooms. Close to restaurants and grocery stores.

I love the location and the staff Nick is awesome, just make sure your car doors are locked, its a comfortable place to live and a good place to call home, if you are wondering to live here you cant go wrong, give it a try its quiet here to, i love it.

Nice apartments to stay in. Love the pool. Staff are nice as well. They hold quite a few things for residents. Definitely check them out.

The amenities are great! Having a pool, gym and dog park within the complex is awesome. 
The parking is first come first serve but I have never had a problem with parking 'far' away from my apartment building. 
Maintenance keeps the grounds very clean and is very receptive for anything that goes wrong in the apartment, things usually get fixed same day!
My only complaint would be some of the neighbors are extremely loud, especially when they live above you and some of the dog owners do not clean up after their dogs, but you find that anywhere you go! 
Overall, great place to live

these apartments are actually really nice. Great spacious floor plan. Roommate style with own bathrooms. I like this place because I feel safe and secure. The community is rather quiet.  So far no issues. I would recommend anyone stay here.
I love my complex, very well kept...the pool and the gym are wonderful. A new electric grill was put out by the pool...is like heaven.

The location is great, but the apartments need updating and is far from luxury. The also aren't very accessible the office, after hours, and emergency maintenance number is all the same and doesn't work at all. 

And there is a $33 service fee to make a rent payment online and they don't accept any other method of payment. So they are forcing you to pay an extra $33 every time you pay rent.

If you're looking for a place that close to everything, Colonial Village, Timber Crest is a must see. The staff for the most part are helpful and very responsive to maintenance request. It's a great community where you get to know your neighbors. 

The pool and other amenities are at time not accessible for resident use, which can be inconvenient to say the least.
Heather and Daisy are very nice! They really make you feel at home!

Overall the apartment is okay. The staff is great and helpful. The only thing is I wish the extra $50 added to the rent for cable each month was something that's optional and not mandatory. The apartment units could use a little upgrading.

This place is awful. How the heck! Did anyone could give it five stars. The apartment HVAC system is gross. Kitchen was falling apart. Bugs Galore, Big ones. And they will rip you off when you move. DO NOT RENT THERE!! I warned you. there's to much to list.

Honest Review. It's July 2022. I moved here in 2019. I needed a quick apartment that I could find last minute. This was cheap and spacious.. but what I didn't realize was how terrible the upkeep to keep the ROACHES out of our apartments. I've literally dealt with this for 3 years. I'm so tired of this and will be moving out. I have no idea how they keep getting in. They need to do better. There's a reason they are so low priced relative to everywhere else. BECAUSE THEY ARE TERRIBLE.

the price may be lower then some.. but you get nothing for it and they are raising prices way too high each year.  

 pools have never opened on time in 5 years.. and they have 2 pools (again neither are open at this time), there is trash all over the walkways and yards and they dont clean it up just run it over with mowers. the "gym" is outdated and only open very short hours when most people are at work -which makes it useless.    maintenance takes forever to come  (currently waiting 2 weeks for 4 items) complaining does nothing.  Their "dog park" is useless and actually is unsafe for animals.  They have dog poop everywhere because they rarely take the trash out of the bins and they almost never replace the dog poop bags   (its been at least 2 months since ive seen them in numerous holders)    Buildings are older which is fine, but inside is not being updated unless you want to pay super high new monthly amount .    

In order to keep up and try to be a contender in the area... they need to improve the gym to be open at least until 10 or 11pm with updated equipment (currently only open when the front office is open) , they need to improve their prices for the current residents,  they need to make sure the pool opens by memorial day every single year and they need to do more cleaning up to improve the look.  

and, Btw, complaining does nothing they just get defensive and still do not do anything about it.

The pros of living here are its a good price and the apartments are fairly spacious. For the most part the people living around the neighborhood are nice and the surrounding area is also a plus. The front office people are all cool too.

The Cons: There is a bug problem. Waterbugs of all sizes  will pop up outside and inside your apartment too. Maintenance didn’t spray unless you ask personally and even then whatever they spray doesn’t help. 

Another con is the upkeep of the buildings. I cant speak for every building but the exterior of my building was filthy for several months and no one came to clean. There were also plenty of times trash was everywhere at the dumpster. I had a few maintenance requests that also took very long to be handled.

I have been here for just over a year. I have only stayed this long because I like the apartment style and location but that has worn thin because of the continual maintenance issues. I have had poor responses, if any when I call or am forced to leave messages during normal working hours. When I first moved in neither shower was working and the emergency line outright refused to fix at minimum one of the two so I can get clean after moving. I called the office when they opened the next day. I was met with a lackadaisical attitude that it might get fixed over the next several days and it took me screaming at them and making the manager get involved on her day off to get it fixed. I had a laundry list of problems in addition to the showers that I had to talk to the manager before they took me seriously.  It still took them several weeks to get them all fixed. Multiple times they came in with a work order for something that needed to be fixed and it was something that had been done days before or they had the wrong item listed that needed to be fixed. After a year of living here things have barely improved. It still takes weeks before something is fixed and when I complain- if they answer the phone I get the same they they are a large place with a lot of things to fix, blah, blah, blah. I have talked to other residents who agree that the best can be said of the office staff are most are polite. There are a few that shouldn’t be working with residents as they immediately get defensive and argumentative if you have a simple issue that needs addressed. I have called the maintenance emergency line a couple of times and left messages each time but have never gotten a call back. Run away from this apartment complex if you like working equipment and staff who can get things done.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review: This is an excellent apartment complex. The staff is very friendly and helpful. I had been looking for a place for six months and moved in in six days. I’m glad I didn’t listen to some of the reviews stated online, otherwise I would have missed an opportunity for an excellent apartment. I encourage you to see for yourself what an excellent place to live. I’ve never been happier to find a great place to live.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review:
Outside landscaping, the property is mostly quiet which was important to me as a person that works odd hours.  No issues with law enforcement outside one of their waiting spots at the end of the road.  Convenient to all shopping essentials within 5 mins or less, and rents are more than fair for the value.  

Office staff are exceptionally helpful and empathetic to issues.  Maintenance takes great care of the property.  Currently about to sign my third lease here.  Highly recommend.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review: Do not move here unless there is no other option.  While the location seems nice and secluded and the apartments are decent, the management is horrible. The you call the office for an issue, they do not respond for weeks.  Email gives the same lack of response.  Contacting the management company, Westdale, is impossible as they will not give out emails and the phone number goes to voicemail that is not returned.  The safety of residents is of no matter to them.  Parking is by permit, however there is constantly people without permits parked taking up all the spots for residents forcing residents to park on the unlit road and walk in a dimly lit area to there apartment or be towed.  The police are here at least twice a week.  I have lived here for a few years and very much enjoyed it, but with the new management team, I can not get out of here fast enough.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review: I have lived here for 2 years. The staff sucks. They always have an attitude when there's an issue & never follow back up if they're supposed to do something or find out more information then get back to you. My rent has increased drastically but the amenities aren't any better than they were when I first moved and this is outside the inner city if Charlotte.  This will be my last year here. If they didn't take so long to let me know what my rent would be to renew my lease I would've moved somewhere else. Car breakins are bad. Someone just had all 4 tires stolen off their vehicle among 4 other car break ins. Don't move here, you'll regret it.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review: My family and I were looking for a place. The community manager, Jessica, was very helpful and courteous and patient. Unfortunately we couldn't move forward with moving here because they didn't have availability but I definitely would consider it in the future if the need arises again.

apartmentName: The Village at Brierfield Apartment Homes
review: Been a resident here for about 3 years and it has not been the best experience. The apartments are old, and the appliances are cheap and old. There is hardly any closet space.  The fitness center is the size of a closet and the equipment barely works. It's constantly mold that forms in the windows and bathrooms. The management has not been the best or most pleasant but I'll leave it at that. If you find something else do so. Don't recommend at all.

The absolute WORST neighborhood I have EVER lived with my kids! It was a bit better when it was BRAEMAR, once THE MURRAY took over everything went downhill! Do NOT MOVE HERE! I swear to you, this is no place to live & to be truthful, it’s best they just tear these apartments down! The apartments are NASTY! They’ll want you to take your own trash to the dumpster or keep it inside until after 5pm! Your trash can that THEY provided isn’t even allowed to stay outside. They rather you bring a nasty trash bin in and out of your home. They never fix anything and IF they do it’s NEVER done correctly! You’ll think maintenance has come because they’ll reply on your ledger but reality no one even comes. To the point the maintenance manager had to come do the work himself! There was mold all through out my apartment and NOTHING HAS BEEN DONE ABOUT IT! Houses and cars get broken into and stolen. 

I HIGHLY HIGHLY HIGHLY REGRET RENEWING MY LEASE HERE !!!

I moved from NY to Residence at Braemar in July 2015. It is so nice and quiet here, I feel like I live in a Senior community. The staff here are so friendly and pleasant to deal with. All your needs are tended to in a swift and timely manner. The grounds are very clean and well maintained. Daily the staff makes sure all areas are clean and free of litter. 
I have three bedrooms and love the space and layout. The patio and storage space are to of my favorite features. The pool and club house are nice get aways. They have community get togethers with different themes, the latest was Cup Cakes and Canvas, which was well attended and enjoyed by all as they painted and ate cup cakes and socialized with one another. The Braemar staff and Maintance are very attentive to the residents and community.
I love living here.

The beautiful well kept grounds, the great office  staff, and maintenance crew have made living here a joy. The community is situated in a quiet area with lots of trees and there is  plenty of shopping, restaurants, businesses, and medical facilities near by. The city’s Blue Line Railway is less than 3 miles away which gives you access to many areas of the city including Uptown all the way to University City.
 
Living here thus far has been a great experience. 
 
We love the monthly resident events which creates a sense of community where you get to meet and spend time with your neighbor.

But during hot weather, I have seen house centipedes enter from the cracks in the restroom and also all sorts of bugs creeping inside and outside the house. That has been a very unpleasant experience. The maintenance could be better. Well sealing of the cracks is necessary and something regarding the bugs needs to be done.

When I contacted after 30 days are over, I got an answer that check was mailed and It was lost. Can you buy that? Even after that, he said new check is issued and its in transit for more than 10 days and still not received it. There was no proactive communication and information from their end. Manager sounds totally helpless and blame everything on corporate which has no face and no name. I have been just asked to wait endlessly on their mercy to get by refund.
Very pathetic. STAY AWAY... There are many other options in same area

Overall the experience was good but there are roaches in the halls and if you sign a lease make sure you’re not planning on breaking it because they charge you two times your rent to break. Also, they will find every reason to take your deposit so don’t have any intentions on getting it back.
Horrible neighborhood and horrible customer service. Cars broken into almost weekly, roof has been leaking for months and they refuse to do anything about it.

This place is horrible!!! The staff is rude and everything in the apartment is old and broken. I constantly have to call maintenance  to fix the  same problems because they never fix it properly the first time. I would not even suggest for my enemies to move here. Also make sure they don't put you facing the trees because you will never get natural light. The $50 cable fee is a rip off because you have to pay for it even if you don't want it.

Great place to live in the heart of Charlotte! Lived here for over a year and have 0 complaints. The leasing office is so friendly and accommodating to their tenets. The concierge staff is extremely helpful and always willing to assist in any questions you might have. Their gym is a decent size and has basic equipment. Their pool is lovely and a great place to spend the hotter days in Charlotte. Their elevators do get crowded during certain times of the day but nothing major. Loved living here and would recommend their 2 bedroom apartment for roommates, couples, or a small family.

Big increase in rent but amenities, maintenance, and services remain below subpar. Age old amenities, recently kitchen sink supported by wood planks literally fell off, filthy old hallway carpets- last renovated probably decade ago. Very poor management, no empathy towards residents (see other resident reviews) . Recently they towed my brand new car registered by their leasing agent as a second car with an RFID tag yet management towed it from an empty parking floor in 'non' reserved space cause it took up another space. AGM Chrissy (very rude) knew it's a resident's car by the RFID tag yet towed it w/out even a courtesy call - let that just sync in. Absolutely not recommended, they thrive making your life miserable- terrible management and unsafe environment.

The apartment and location hands down is great.
Lack of empathy though. Here is a case  Due to a technical issue on the app my auto pay got cancelled which I didn’t get notified. Coz if this not at my fault the rent was paid 4 days later than the cutoff and I was charged $ 75.
They had sent an email on the last day of cut off directly stating you are now gonna be charged late fee. 
Basically without my fault but issue on their rental app I was fined. 
When I brought this to managements notice there was no consideration.
I would have agreed with them if I missed to pay rent at my mistake but this is absolutely taking advantage.

Catalyst is a wonderful place to stay during my client visit to charlotte for bank of america. The front service lady "Domanique" is a wonderful person i have ever met in my life. She is helpful generous and a real time helping friend of mine.  She understands people very well about diff culture diff customs. She is a true friend and a generous person i have ever met in charlotte. Whenever i need of any help no matter what the one person i could approach is Domanique. She tries all her means with her sweet kind and pleasant awesome behaviour that she is ever ready to help us. I hope my stay in charlotte will be smooth for another 5 weeks as i had for past 2 weeks.
