(Over $200 more in rent every month, $70 more for parking, an extra $100 in common area utilities that we are now required to pay, and it sounds like another $100 for their internet package.) Maintenance issues do not seem like a priority to them considering it took 4 months for them just to fix the hot water in my apartment. They struggle to keep common areas clean and the trash cans outside will be overflowing with dog poop before they are noticed and changed. Needless to say, I will not be resigning my lease.

Funny how most of the five star reviews are just commenting on the tour of the property and not actually living here…. Seems suspicious. Not claiming they are fake, but are they real? I know I don’t typically review an apartment tour….

I'm going to start by saying the apartments itself is lovely and the area is great.  We made a lot of great memories living there.  The management, on the other hand, is absolutely horrible.  We tried to resign but couldn't get ahold of anyone for over a month and all of us worked during their office hours.

upon moving out - they tried saying we had over $2,000 of damage which was so far from the truth.  They had originally told us they repaint the walls after every move in and to not worry about the walls, apparently they wanted to charge us anyways.  We had cats so they tried to say our cats peed on the carpets when they have always been extremely well trained and have never had any accidents.  (if you're a cat owner - you know that you would notice if your cats peed on ANYTHING that'd not the litter box)

After fighting this bill for about 6 months they finally had their attorney call us to settle for $1,360 - we ended up paying it to be done with them but upon that conversation, he said this is a known thing this company does to almost every tenant they have.

They charge an absurd amount, if you fight it - they'll lower it but it's still completely out of line.

PLEASE NOTE - by signing a lease here, you will not get your deposit back, they will stick you with a huge bill at the end.  They will not listen to what you have to say and they do not care about you.  They care about money and that's it.

“Amenities” are fall below the standards set by apartments downtown, the leasing agent asks overly personal questions about your whereabouts, and good luck getting a straight answer from management on procedures that are listed in your lease. It will take at least two weeks and 6 follow up emails to get one reply and even then the reply is in explicit ignorance and violation of lease paragraphs. Not to mention the CONSTANT break ins and theft, lack of 24 hour security that was originally boasted when signing our lease, and full blast noise from the light rail when we were confirmed that our apartment was “sound proof”.  Actual amenities like the pool and gym were closed when the staff wasn’t even wearing masks while speaking closely to tenants....Avoid.

So many things wrong with this place. First off the management is anything but helpful. They genuinely do not care about the tennants there. We have had a ton of issues. The most recent one was the water out of our faucets sputtered brown water randomly for a good chunk of a day. The place and common areas do not get cleaned. The common bathrooms I have seen poop built up and plugged more than a few times. The laundry room actually makes your clothes smell worse and are covered in gunk and mold. Do not live here whatever you do.

The management here is awful and can really make your life difficult at times. The employees are always on different pages and give you all different answers. They never follow through with issues they say they are going to solve. Do not recommend living here!

If I could give this place 0 stars I would. I have seen this apartment building change in management from Doran to East Bank Communities and the results have been disastrous. I continue to be more and more disappointed, and just when I think it can't get any worse it does. There used to be security onsite during the night and on the weekends, and east bank communities management took this away. This was helpful, especially on the weekends, but now if there is any trouble with noise the only option is to go through the police. The garage door breaks down very often and there is no compensation for these down times. Just $150 per month to park in the garage and you might still have to pay to park it somewhere else when the garage breaks! Let me reiterate that the staff is not helpful. You will end up feeling like you are doing their jobs for them for simple things like following up on rent payments or coming home to an incorrect eviction notice because they made a mistake.

The management also does not care whether you have lived here one month or six years, so if you're planning on staying in a location for awhile choose somewhere that will properly reward you for the money you are spending as a consumer. 



Also, if you plan to sublet the fees are astronomical. Each subletter has to pay $190 per person, in addition to the vacating residents paying $300. In my case, it cost $680 for what should be a simple summer sublet. This cost all goes towards "processing paperwork."



With the ongoing boom in the apartment industry, please do yourself a favor and spend your hard earned money elsewhere.

Avoid any properties managed by East Bank Communities. They're nice buildings in good locations, however the property management is absolutely appalling. At my current building, exterior doors are constantly broken, with the door handle unattached, or locking mechanism not working. Garage door has shut on top of my vehicle, and the elevators routinely malfunction (state inspection certificates are expired). The list goes on and on. Recently, they didn't give reasonable notice before entering my apartment unit. Also, my roommate transferred her lease, and East Bank Communities refuses to furnish the unit properly, despite the fact they advertise as "Fully Furnished".

Avoid East Bank Communities. If you choose to lease with them, read all binding documents carefully, and be prepared for the management.

The Dinkydome building has great ceiling heights... The laundry room smells and is never cleaned. They claim the cleaning crew comes around every day, but this is a lie. You need to walk far to throw out trash. You can get better amenities at all the other buildings on campus. Also management is never here and terrible at fixing problems and responding.

I lived at the Edge on Oak the year that management shifted from Doran to East Bank Communities.  The building is nice, and the location is great.  Doran's management wasn't great, as they're a big company with a lot of power, but they were at least responsive and fairly reliable.  When East Bank Communities took over, it was noticeably worse. Thankfully I am no longer living there, but it is now April 2016 and I STILL haven't received my CRP from 2015 (which by law should be sent no later than end of January).  Despite filling out a forwarding address form when I moved out, I haven't received a single thing that was mailed to the Edge after I moved, and multiple times had to contact senders and have them resend to my new address. When reaching out to East Bank Communities about this they are unresponsive, and on the off chance they do respond, are unhelpful. All I can say is DO NOT LIVE HERE. You may think, "The worse that can happen is bad management for a year," but I moved out over 7 months ago and still am haunted by needing to deal with their poor management.
Whoever answered my call was super rude. Please work on your customer interaction skills. Thanks!

Very affordable. Friendly staff. I’ve lived in two different buildings with Stevens. There are different types of units so I would definitely look into Stevens for a showing because 1) the photos don’t do justice for the other apartments they don’t have photos for and 2) they seem to be renovating more! 
Also, I really enjoy the staff. They’re attentive/quick to help and they’re always nice.

If you are looking for an apartment with hardwood floors and historic character with affordable prices Stevens is the best option for you. The staff are very friendly and attentive. Ask for Amy or Emily when touring they are both great!

I SiVonne Gamble love my first apartment. Its close to my job and my school. Me being a full time student I can'can't afford bus far half the time. So I can walk to school and back in the matter of twenty-five minutes. I have only been living there for seven months. It also close to the bus line. Just a block away for my apartment! My apartment builting also have gatherings in the park. We have meet and greets every month. I plan on stay more then a year thats how much i love steven community.

I would suggest renting from Stevens Community Apartments to anyone who is looking for a first place of their own or to someone looking for an affordable place close to a lot of attractions! 

Stevens Community Apartments has been a really great first place to have on my own! Moving from Iowa, they were really helpful with the whole application, leasing, and moving in process! The rent is reasonable and the location is close to a lot of entertaining things. The maintenance is in the bottom of my building and everyone who works in that department is so kind. They are also very quick to respond to any problems I have had, are efficient, and do not leave behind a mess. 

The neighborhood consists of a lot of apartment buildings making it a pretty busy area, and if you do not pay for a parking spot, off street parking is the other option. 
It can sometimes be hard finding a spot and I have to drive around the block a few times but I have never parked too far away. 

Moving from a quiet neighborhood I wasn't used to having the noise of a city and a lot of neighbors, and it hasn't been bad or distracting but you do hear noise from the park that is right outside the building and just outdoor life.

Hope this is helpful to anyone who may read it!
If you want to be close to downtown, AND have affordable rent, Stevens is your place. Cute buildings, amazing staff, and even better location.

This apartment isn’t the best, it was my first apartment since moving on my own so I wasn’t expecting much. The maintenance overall is kind of shabby, my bathroom has mold, the wall is falling apart because it’s painted water damage. Sometimes the heater works, but only on a certain setting. Even then you only get the option to turn it on or off. 

There are cockroaches that come from somewhere on the kitchen walls from another apartment when it’s dark or cold out. I often come into the kitchen for a drink or snack in the night and see them scurry across the counter and underneath its edge. Though I put traps around and it’s always clean they still like to wander to the farther corners of my apartment, just to die. 

The neighborhood is not bad, but it has gotten a little more active than it was when I moved in. There are two new shot spotters within a few blocks. The fire alarm and police sirens are always coming to visit at random times throughout the days as well. My floor is a main contributor to this and it tends to get very loud on holidays or weekends. 

There has been new property management since I started my lease and there has been some improvements such as the elevators and stairs being so dirty. The elevators on the south side of the building are usually operable, if not there is another on the north side and there are a few staircases. There are no entryway cameras as people have destroyed or stolen them, packages constantly go missing and get stolen. So I would not recommend sending your packages to this address, unless you will be there when it arrives. The maintenance man is very attentive, but I believe that there is a maintenance fee each time you put in a work order now.  

Aside from all that’s listed above as long as you keep your space clean, set out some traps and maybe cover wall openings you should be fine. I would not live here if you would like a peaceful, cleanly, and quiet building however.

Affordable and great location.
But there are several security issues.

Overall still satisfied with building, location, amenities etc. My first maintenance request (kitchen sink) was completed quickly and efficiently! However, recently making requests take a ridiculous amount of time to be completed (mail key, bathroom ceiling, etc.) No reciprocated communication with staff ever. Anytime I wish to speak to someone I'm forced to show up at the leasing office unannounced.
Property management does not care about the residents. You sign the lease and pay your rent. Management won't talk to you again regardless of the importance of your situation.

I can’t wait to move out of this place. Everything below is true. Stairwells constantly have pet pee, crap, and puke all the time. The entry glass door has been shattered 3 times and the package room was broken into several times over 6 months ago. It hasn’t been fixed since and there isn’t a package room for this building. People constantly smoke weed on every floor and the radiators will click and wake you up at night. There’s sirens and gunshots constantly and people sell drugs in the parking lot.

I can't stress enough how much you should NOT live here. It only took a week for me to realize how much I screwed up by signing a lease here. The apartment complex itself is disgusting. The first floor constantly smells of cigarette smoke and pee. The elevators rarely work and if they do, there is a good chance they will be dirty or filled with pee (human or dog??). The place gets dirty almost as soon as it is clean. There have been multiple times when the lobby has blood on the floor or vomit in the entry ways. People steal things out of the laundry room all the time. When the homeless aren't living in the vacant rooms or utility closets, they can be found in the entry ways and tend to leave their belongings there once they leave for the day.  They also threaten to harm tenants when begging for money. BUT DONT BOTHER NOTIFYING MANAGEMENT. It took three days and multiple calls from many residents for them to come do anything about the homeless people who were living in the utility closet next to my door  and empty apartment down the hall. When management came, they came without law enforcement and left before the people exited the complex because they were scared. 

Besides handling  on site problems poorly, management also doesn't know how to handle money, send an email, or make a phone call. When I gave them my money order, they ended up depositing my $1000 order for the incorrect amount, never notified me of their screw up, and assessed me late fees. When I reached out to inquire about the problem, none of the staff could tell me what was wrong and kept referring me to one staff member. I was told multiple times this person would call me but rarely were those calls received. Most of the emails I sent about the issue were not answered until I visited the office in person (during a pandemic and when it was supposed to be closed to the public) and when a response was made they said they would have the issue fixed by the afternoon.  It wasn't. 0/10. DO NOT RECOMMEND
Great move-in Cat was very helpful for our move-in and we are excited to be residents.
Great place to live! Wonderful and friendly staff. An excellent location near lakes, trails, shopping, and restaurants.

I’ve lived in a lot of apt buildings and this is by far my favorite one. Great, friendly, helpful management. Really nice maintenance person. The building is well taken care of. Fun community events. Respectful neighbors and it’s close to so many things so it’s a very convenient location. Definitely recommend!

Everything about the Foundry Lake Street is amazing due to the great location, quality, amenities, and staff. The location is wonderful because it's right across from the lakes, so you can be outside on a beautiful day enjoying the weather. I like this area too because it's not congested like the downtown area. It's only minutes from Uptown, so you can enjoy the shops and bars there as well. It's also steps from food, yoga, and shops. Another plus is that the building is close to the Greenway, so if you are a biker, or runner, you will love it here. The Foundry has wonderful amenities as well. There is a rooftop pool and bar, many well-designed community spaces, and a state of the art workout center. The apartments are done beautifully with nice quartz countertops and beautiful floors. The apartments are spacious and even the hallways are beautiful. This building even comes with underground heated parking. Lastly, the staff is amazing. They made me feel welcome from the start and were full of enthusiasm and energy. I have nothing, but positive things to say about the Foundry.

Very good price for the area, but the apartment is not good. Very messy common areas that never get cleaned, packages get stolen, and some of the residents make things uncomfortable. It is a great location, with free parking but you definitely get what you pay for.

Management is pretty responsive, a huge plus is the parking spot included in the rent. That's pretty unheard for the uptown area. Lived here for a year and loved the ability to walk everywhere and a lot of the buses were a quick walk away. The walls are a bit thin so I could often hear conversations my neighbor was having while in my bedroom. Rent is a bit high considering there aren't really any amenities but that's just because of the location.

I moved here from Sioux Falls, SD in December 2014, I thought Minneapolis was going to be super crazy in comparison to Sioux Falls SD, its affordable, its quiet, safe, and close to everything. I wouldn't want to move .

The best part of these apartments is definitely the location. The apartments surrounding it are very expensive (1500  for one bedroom). There is a grocery store right across the street, plenty of bars within walking distance, shopping, and a lot of nice restaurants. The apartments themselves were renovated recently so they are pretty nice. The kitchen isn't huge but it is new which makes up for that. Neighbors aren't too loud which is nice and there is also free off street parking which is rare for uptown.
Better price than the apartments in the area. However, some of the apartments have very little natural light and thin walls.

I have lived in Seven Corners for 3+ years now, and absolutely love it. There is a reason there's a waiting list every year! The units and building are well maintained. Management is very friendly and quick to respond to inquires or maintenance concerns. Super convenient location with Trader Joes and many restaurants in walking distance. Easy to get to the lightrail and bus stop. They deliver packages to your apartment. Small security concerns from time to time (it is in Minneapolis after all), but I have never felt unsafe and management is always quick to respond to any issues.
It’s wheelchair accessible and allows service animal’s, I think god sent me in the right direction.

This place is nothing to write home about.  The management is very friendly and quick to act when there are any problems.  The building does allow smoking in the rooms, which is a bit of a disappointment, the smoke does leach into the halls and into living spaces of adjacent apartments.  

The complex is dated but for the price it is to be expected.  The neighborhood is wonderful, close to the University of Minnesota, bars and restaurants, and trails for biking and running.  

Overall living at Seven Corners Apartments is a positive experience.

This apartment is right where all the action is. I'm a Big Viking Fan and the Metrodome is minutes away. There are Great Resurants and a Theater is just around the corner.The Staff at Seven Corners is a great support team. And three times a year Staff do a community dinner for the residents. It's a very quiet building which is shocking with 90% of the resident are college students, its a great place to live. The building is always improving. And if your anything like me and don't like the ideal of family staying at your home when visiting from out of town there's the Court Yard across the street. Perfection!!!!


Go Vikings!!!
Stephanie W, Minneapolis MN

This is the perfect balance between living comfortably and living within your price range. Other options in the same area may cost twice as much for a similar space. It is in a perfect location near the University of Minnesota and only a short walk to the light rial. Seven Corners offers everything one needs to live comfortably yet sensibly.

This apartment community is the one you are looking for which contains all you need and the place is just great!
I would like to suggest this to my friends.

Absolutely terrible communication, they put us on a waitlist that required $500 non refundable after 3 days and then petitioned us for info multiple times that ran over the 3 day limit. They are only here for your money. The apts themselves are fine but the process is exhausting and building management is incompetent overall, whatever you do I HIGHLY urge you to look elsewhere, these folks are not worth it.
They won't return your deposit. The management team is not responsive and have take a lot of time to process smaller things

Looks nice on the surface but really quality cheap plumbing and amenities.  Also once you’re living here you’re no longer valued. Any request or work order takes forever and management acts like you’re the biggest burden for wanting things fixed. They say they have security and concierge though dropped those services, I at least didnt seen any for the better part of a year before moving.

If you’re applying for an apartment or showing any interest in renting, don’t expect nearly as much response as a resident. When I first toured, they showed me an apartment that was A) Not the unit they ended up giving me B) A different floor plan, C) on a different floor than the actual apartment. I didn’t get to see my actual apartment since move in day. The management takes weeks or even months to reply if at all. The mail room is a mess. There is absolutely no order to their system, they just put it on whatever shelf it fits on. Some of the hallways smell bad pretty often due to the dumpster in the loading dock that half of the time has the door wide open. Despite what may be insinuated, there’s no concierge. My apartment has quarter walls all throughout, it just looks like an oversight. I really wouldn’t go with them, I’ve had a terrible experience here. Look for other apartments around the area that are more reasonably priced for the quality and with decent reviews. Seems like almost everyone here has had a bad experience. :/

If I could rate this organization at 0 stars, I would. My husband and I had a bad experience with Eitel Apartments from the very beginning. Management consistently overlooks important details, has poor communication (it either takes them days to respond or you have to do significant follow up to get answers and it's rare that someone is available in the office or answers the phone) and is snarky or rude when communicated with. They will tell you that there's on-site security and concierge when you move in - we moved out mid May and hadn't seen a security guard for months and hadn't seen a concierge for even longer. Even when they had the concierge, the concierge doesn't do anything. They will tell you whatever you want to hear and offer you move-in deals to get you in the door but they do not value the tenants that they currently have. If you decide to move in despite this warning, take photos of EVERYTHING before you move in and when you move out because in more ways than one, management tries to nickel and dime their tenants for everything that they can. I could give a million examples of the ways that living here was extremely frustrating and/or unsafe. Save your money and move to literally any of the other apartment buildings in the area.

Management turnover is high, with each new batch somehow managing to be worse than the previous group. Maintenance doesn't view the ticketing system, have to call and complain to get air conditioning or heating fixed in a vaguely timely manner. Even then they will try to drag their feet
Affordable and quite! I love it is near the mall and bus stop. Very friendly and responsible management and maintenance team!
Just moved here im lookin for a great neighborhood to move in to call my home and this looks gud the area & everything I will love it

The staff here is very accommodating, they take your privacy into great consideration (they never do walk-throughs, etc). The value is very good as well. and the units are well kept.

My only problem (and why we are moving out) is the noise, if you cannot deal with children in the neighborhood, do not move here. I don't mean kids off and on, I mean kids at all hours of the day (past midnight) who will not stop yelling at the top of their lungs. I have had friends ask NOT to come over because the noise is so excessive.

Shame, great otherwise.
I love this place! It has all the amenities I need. I hope there is one available when I am ready to move in March. Early searching!

Been here 2 years now and its one of the best places ive lived. The property manager Timm is the best guy. Everything is well maintained in a timely manger, very professional, communication is good. People in the apartments are chill, and parking is never horrible. The only con is YES the trash is loud and picks up a lot (which is standard for downtown) but it fills up quickly, the one day they dont come it because crazy full. You get use to hearing the trash and its nice to know that the whole place is clean and doesn't smell like old garbage.
The garbage trucks are scheduled to come way too early and often and wake up the entire apartment complex four days a week at 6 am. Hard to get good sleep due to this.

The worst part about living here is that for some reason the private trash pickup is scheduled to come 4 days a week in the middle of the complex and wakes the entire apartment block up at 6 AM with very loud noises. Otherwise it's nice.
Great management- cheap finishes but well maintained

I love living here.  The rent is affordable, and the amenities are a huge bonus. Gas and water included. When I moved in my apartment it had new carpet and a brand new refrigerator. Every unit has a unique design and feel to it. The location is awesome too, a 4 minute walk to all downtown has to offer. I plan on being here for a long time.

I can not express how Thankful I am of Drexel apartments. Because I have over 15 years of customer service this is where I would like to focus.  The office manager Tim, is a one of a kind guy! He's super helpful, ALWAYS available,  ALWAYS in a great mood and has an AWESOME attitude! 
I was at my wits end looking for my apartment. Tim welcomed me and my sister in, showed me the 1st studio apartment. Didn't like that one at all. Tim suggested another apartment, let me know upfront it was slightly out of my price range which is why he didn't mention it, and OMG! When I saw it, and the view that It had, I had to have it!!! Put my deposit down right away and glad I did! I absolutely LOVE my new apartment!
Thanks Drexel Apartments! You Guys ROCK!

The front office has consistently failed to address ongoing complaints about the inadequately sized parking spot for my vehicle. That i pay for. Additionally, there is a cement beam protruding out from the cement wall, and the vehicle parked to the left is a larger SUV, making it nearly impossible to maneuver into this spot effectively. As a result, i have incurred damage to my car from scraping against the beam, which has diminished its resale value. This spot would be more adequate for a compact car or appt equipment. Despite my repeated requests for a different parking space and numerous follow-ups, the front office continues to respond with generic, scripted replies from management instead of taking meaningful action. Only interested in getting your money.

I initially had a really good experience with this apartment. Halfway into my 3 month lease I had an unexpected leak. I totally understand it takes time to get them fixed, but what happened with my situation is ridiculous. I had my oven and dishwasher pulled out in the middle of my kitchen for 4 days without a timeline of it being put back. I had holes cut above my cabinets. I had maintenance entering all day throughout the day for a week without knocking before entering. On the 4th day, my appliances were put back, but I was left without a kitchen ceiling. A hole so large was cut that I did not have a ceiling in my kitchen. I was left with no electricity in my kitchen or living room. My shower had little to no water pressure, nor did it get hot. My apartment was left barely liveable and I was not offered another unit or hotel. When I mentioned I was left without electricity and just spent money on groceries I was now unable to cook, I was told "Your refrigerator and microwave should still work." When I mentioned not having water for a day and a half I was told "There is a community bathroom downstairs to brush your teeth and give your dog water." I asked about compensation for this disaster and was told I am expected to pay my rent on the first or with an 8% late fee by the 6th. This is absolutely ridiculous and the least helpful someone could be. 10/10 do NOT recommend living here.

False sales and promises. Promised one month free on my 3 month lease. 2 days before when they sent lease I asked where the deal was written and James in the leasing office apologized and sent me an addended lease with this deal. That same day she said they could not honor this deal; leading me to have to find a long term stay 2 days before moving to a new city from out of state. Poor business tactics and customer service. By the way, James never got back to me or apologized for her mistake. Neither did Chris the manager.

I had an excellent experience with my tour and leasing process at the Paxon! Nate greeted us right away and was able to show us multiple units that met our needs and rest of the amenities at this property! I would recommend this apartment to others as it is in a GREAT location and the staff is very accommodating. We were able to tour and secure our apartment the same day and were given an additional parking spot at VELO to help with our needs! Great experience and excited to becoming a resident soon!
The Paxon seems like it would be a really great place to live and I can't wait to move in. I would definitely recommend this apartment community and as a matter of face I already have.

The apartment itself was great. Some of the finishes are cheap (floors coming up, cabinets askew) but I loved the view and the size. However the common areas were not as great, the pool was often dirty, very few engagement opportunities, the parking area was unsecured (I had my car broken into twice). The 2 biggest reasons I left were 1. the rent was way too high for the value, and 2. there were too many rules(i.e # of guests allowed at the pool) instead of dealing with the specific tenants causing problems, blanket rules were made. Jake at the front desk is very helpful and friendly, the other desk staff are snotty and not helpful at all.
The neighborhood has potential to be fun and there are lots of things to do within walking distance.

I had high hopes when I decided to sign a lease at the Walkway. I was unable to tour due to Covid restrictions, so management sent me a floorplan of the unit and a video of a unit with similar finishes. I packed according to the floorplan I was given, and when I opened the door to my new apartment, the floorplan was completely different. I had to call maintenance for issues with my appliances at least four or five times. On top of that, the common areas were poorly kept. People’s pets would roam the halls, and I would find anything from dead plants and dirty underwear to food and animal vomit in the hallways. The wallpaper in the hallways was peeling, so they had a loud fan and big trash can sitting in the hallway for a week. The parking garage had a large puddle of dried animal (or human?) pee that hadn’t been cleaned in weeks, and oftentimes the garage smelled like cigarette smoke. The location has started to feel unsafe whether it’s a shooting a block away or a homeless man sleeping in the front entrance so I am unable to leave my apartment. Further, there have been issues with stolen bikes and people breaking into cars in the garage and stealing valuable items. I have never written a review in my life, but I wanted to share my experience to save others from feeling like they spent a boatload of money to live somewhere they regret.
I would recommend The Walkway for its prompt management and maintainence team but ultimately I cannot recommend the apartment for the price, amenities or age of the building.
Great residents, nice friendly staff, great location and great amenities.

It depends on what stage in life the individual is in.  There are a few residents who do not respect the common areas or are still living the "college life".  This is somewhat annoying from time to time.  Especially due to the fact that they do not know how to pick up after themselves or stop trashing the place.
Great building and management in a convenient location. However if you're looking for a fun and social building there are other buildings now better suited for that,

I  currently live here in two bed room, yes the building is new but the management and the office staff are not welcoming  you always going to come back from the office unhappy. Parking is $80 and No visitor parking I feel I pay my rent where it is not appreciated. The night security guard is bad he will not let you in if you forget your keys upstairs and your phone is dead. even though you everything to proof  you live here.
not renewing my lease and not recommending any one.

I currently live here in a 3BR apt, the building is brand new but was built terribly, everything in the units are cheap and flimsy. The surrounding area is un-safe and always very loud at night. The units are all very bright at night and the building does not let you put your own blinds on the windows. The security of the building is also very bad. The building is always dirty and the residents spit in the halls and on the floors. You can easily find better, cheaper apts a few blocks away. I would never renew a lease here or sign one knowing the information I know now.

Beautiful lauxery apartment with a gym and a baeutiful balcony there's a park near them for kids and the community center .it has big bedrooms and bathroom so it has alot of smace for stuff and there is baeutiful court yard .it has heating.it has cable for tv and wheelchair Accessible (Rooms) and really a beautiful aparments for family's and students

There was a recent change of management and the new company doesn't seem to know what they are doing or care about the residents. The service offered has seen a HUGE downgrade. I would've recommended this building so highly before, but it's not worth the outrageous rent for the lackluster service.

Blue is a wonderful place to live in Uptown! The location is perfect, right next to Lake and Lyndale with plenty of shops and restaurants to explore and right on the greenway for biking and walking. The management was always friendly and very accommodating going the extra mile to make sure requests were met and any issue was handled in a timely and professional manner. The apartments themselves are very spacious with beautiful big windows that allow for natural light to pour in every morning. All of the amenities were always clean and accessible, my favorite was the pool in the summer! Overall highly recommend this building if you are looking for an affordable but beautiful building in Uptown.

A building with great amenities and within walking distance to a grocery stores, convenience/gas stations, restaurants, bars, coffee shops, clothes/home goods and fitness centers. 

The amenities in the building are well worth it too. I was sold on the dog park for my puppy and the chance to meet other dog owners and make puppy playmates! Also, a pool, a gym (cardio, weights, studio and sauna), daily coffee, courtyards/fireplaces and weekly community events to attend. Another nice perk is the free coffee every morning and breakfast on Wednesdays. 

A few things to watch out for is the commute to/from work. Spending summer days by the lakes makes getting to uptown with construction a hassle somedays. The price can be prohibitive to living there without a rental incentive. Parking is extra too and not guaranteed for every resident who signs a lease (waiting list).

Recently moved into Blue a few months ago and it was my first "newer / luxury" apartment experience. Honestly, I'm pretty blown away by how nice everyone is and the apartment. My 2 story loft is amazing and the location cannot be beat in Uptown. The only reason I took off one star is because some of the amenities are showing it's age like standard coffee makers in the lounge instead of an expresso machine and there isn't WiFi in all the common areas like the pool or courtyards, only in the lounge. For a top-notch building, I expect community WiFi everywhere.

If you are looking for a hassle free place to live in Uptown Blue is perfect. Gym and common areas are always clean. In unit washer and dryer. The rooms are a little small but you don't live in the area to sit inside all day. Right down the street from uptown bars and perfect places for Sunday brunch!

I loved living at Blue! Underground parking, in unit washer/dryer, AMAZING concierge staff, 24 hour FULLY EQUIPPED workout room.. I could go on, but my point is it's like living in a hotel. Our apartment wasn't huge, but the open layout was nice and open. The only reason we are moving is because I started grad school and you don't get all I mentioned above for a price that can be afforded by student loans :)If you're a young professional with a little extra money to spend for all the comforts, this is your place.

Looking for a modern, fully furnished 2 bedroom apartment in Minneapolis? This is it. It is quiet,clean, excellent staff. Excellent view of Mississippi,off street parking. So glad we found this place to reside while receiving care at U of M.
They did a great job of meeting our needs during a stressful time.

I have lived in this building since 2 months after it opened, and I struggle to find anything to complain about. I’ll try to keep this brief.

The staff are all friendly, welcoming, and pleasant. If you like to chat and get to know them, they’ll know your name within weeks. If you don’t want to, that’s fine - they’ll still be so kind every time you interact with them.

And the amenities ... first of all, free champagne Monday-Friday at 5pm? Is this a hotel? The champagne hour sometimes attracts a lively group but even if you choose to have a glass and be antisocial, no prob.

There’s a coffee machine. There is complimentary breakfast snacks (not sure what time, I’m usually at work before or after it would be put out). The gym has pretty much everything I need, personally, and is always kept clean and taken care of. In fact, everything from the common areas to maintenance in the apartment is taken care of efficiently and well.

There’s a movie room. There are two business centers (I don’t own a laptop or printer so this has come in handy!). The rooftop is beautiful, perfect for a party or bbq. I’ve had a small party on the roof at the same time as multiple other groups, and it’s never been a problem.

The trash chute rooms smell like SKITTLES. Constantly.

I really can’t say enough. Emma at the front desk is ESPECIALLY charming and kind, as well as Dee (a member of the cleaning staff) and Will in leasing - they’re all great.

This place is not worth it. Great location but I have been to many other cheaper apartments in NL that don't have to deal with the shoddy management. This month they drafted rent out of our bank accounts twice due to a technical error. I have lived here for 6 months, and the garage door has malfunctioned and not let me in or out twice. It is constantly down for maintenance and then you have to plan your day around it and park outside. I have been locked out of my apartment at midnight due to a malfunctioning key FOB resulting from them changing management companies and received no apology. The coffee machine works ~60% of the time. Rent another place in NL.

So far my experience at variant has been awful.

I live on the 4th floor. When I moved in I immediately heard pounding noises and could not figure out which neighbor it was coming from. After many mornings of waking up consistently at 4:45am, I figured out it was coming from the boxing gym below. After 4, yes 4, months it had been *sort of* resolved. I continue to wake up 3 out of 7 mornings of the week. Management originally told me it wasn't the gym because they had soundproofed the building for it, but after other residents complained they confirmed it was in fact the gym.

Aside from this, I would describe this building a frat house. It's filled with people who just want to party. If this is your lifestyle, this is the building for you. If it isn't, and you appreciate sleeping through the night on the weekends, I would stay far away from this building. 

The building is poorly soundproofed in general. I can hear my neighbors talking, bass from speakers, footsteps, people closing doors (your whole apartment will shake especially around 2am when everyone gets home from the bar) overall.. if you enjoy peace, this is not the building for you.

Solves for these problem via management: move your bed away from the wall, get a sound maker, a fan, call the police.

After months of giving management updates, they have basically told me that I can kick rocks if I want to transfer to a different unit or get out of my lease.

Overall very disappointed in my experience here so far.

My wife and I moved to Variant almost a year ago now, and our time here so far has been a delight. We love the location, the apartment layout (we have a 1 bedroom), the community spaces, and so on. We also really appreciate the management team. Matt and Kevin are great to work with and they go above and beyond for the residents. We appreciate all the work everyone at Excelsior does to keep this apartment running smoothly!

Recently moved in as empty nesters from a 3,000 sq ft home. Nice to get rid of all the stuff we had and get back to basics. Freeway noise is there but tolerable, and amazing sliding door completely shut it out. Place is very clean and residents are nice. Also the free happy hour is a great place to meet your neighbors.

The place looks nothing like the pictures. I GOT CATFISHED. I got a tent for an apartment, and I live with four other people all elderly dudes. The outdoor lounge is actually a piece of gum off the floor, re chewed and spit back out. I hate this whole place, but the pools nice!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I have lived on the 4th floor over 2 years.  Given that it’s an average apartment building, I think your experience really depends on how good/bad your neighbors are.

Apartment community:  1 star

I’m practically surrounded by neighbors who slam their doors dozens of times a day and bang against a shared wall at all hours of the day and night.  It could be midnight, 2:30am, 4:30am, 6:00am, it really doesn’t matter—if a door opens, it’s slamming shut.  I have to wear earplugs to sleep and still get woken up 5+ nights a week.  I know it’s terrible living next to them and I’m sure it sucks living below them, too.

The smell of other people’s weed and sometimes cigarette smoke also fills my unit every day in the cold months and every other day in the warmer months.  Sometimes it comes in from the hallway and sometimes from the vents in the kitchen and bathroom.

Management seems unable/unwilling to address either issue.

Units:  3 stars

The units are Ikea-nice:  a clean, modern look, but nothing special.  Lots of natural and artificial light.  Seems designed for tall people—big bathtub and high microwave and cupboards.

There’s a mirror set into the wall near the windows that makes the place look a little bigger, but it also cuts the thickness of the wall in half.  Unsurprisingly, that’s exactly where vocal and TV noise will pass from unit to unit.  This poor design choice really is too bad because the rest of the walls are fairly soundproof when it comes to that type of noise.

Parking:  3 stars

The open-air lot is accessible to the public.  Several cars have been broken into and even stolen during my time.  The new management company added some fencing to discourage non-residents from transiting the property.

Street parking is usually available.

Neighborhood:  4 stars

What you’d expect from a residential South Minneapolis neighborhood:  a couple parks, a lake, and several restaurants and shops within walking distance (including 2 smokehouse and BBQ places within a block that often fill the neighborhood with the smell of smoke and smoked meat).  The proximity to the light rail is nice for going downtown or to the airport.

Safety and security:  2 stars

Several cars have been broken into and a few stolen from the open-air parking lot during my time here.  Many, many packages have been stolen from the entry area by non-residents who were let into the building.

I previously wrote the review "Quiet, comfortable place to live." I recently moved out for a few different reasons. A new property management group took over. They were not responsive to issues (it often took many requests through many channels over many weeks or months). Very rarely was notice given well in advance of anything. The cleanliness of the building has declined - still relatively clean, but it used to be spotless. The finishes on the apartment did not withstand the test of time/general wear and tear (the trim crumbles when you so much as stub your toe on it). Also, with a BBQ joint down the block and a smokehouse across the street, it's very difficult to have your windows open. Smoke was blown into my apartment at least 3 days a week. Overall, it's an okay apartment with management that leaves much to be desired. Frankly, it's not worth the trouble.

This is a great apartment building, and well taken care of. Things seem to be built quite well, but the huge windows are the main feature of each apartment. The management company takes care of concerns very quickly and deals with maintenance requests with surprising speed. The building is really quiet and the neighbors are respectful. Everyone mostly keeps to themselves. The neighborhood is mostly mid 20s and 30s folks and has a nice balance of feeling fairly hip without being busy. While you can hear the light rail, ambulances, and a little traffic on 55, the sound is overall pretty minimal for how conveniently located the building is. As a woman, I have always felt very safe in the area right around the apartment and on public transportation. No grocery stores for a good distance, but I'm willing to overlook that for all the other benefits of living here. This review might sound redundant to the other one, but that's just because it's really all true - the apartment's great.

We've been living at 3828 apartments for about a year now, and it's honestly the best place we've lived in. The apartments are beautiful and get great natural light, and are very spacious and open. The building itself is extremely quiet, very rarely do you hear your neighbors. We've only had one time where we had to call maintenance for a small fix on something, and they arrived within the hour. The management company is also extremely friendly and attentive. They have a great rooftop deck with grills, it's just a quick walk to the lightrail station, and there is a coffee shop and great brew pub right across the street!

My experience at the Aberdeen has been completely stellar. To start, the staff has been off-the- charts amazing. There’s a reason Nicole is mentioned so frequently in the reviews of this place. She responds to emails quickly and effectively, and is always willing to go the extra mile to make sure all of your problems are taken care of in a timely manner. The cleaning staff is very friendly; the building is always tidy, clean and fresh. It’s a relatively quiet building; though, it is right next to the highway, so ambulances and cars can certainly be loud at night. People outside can occasionally be loud, but when you live towards downtown, that can be expected. I would 10/10 recommend living here.

I've been living here for a year now and can say that Nicole is just as great as the other reviewers say. The whole building is very clean and quiet. I'd love to talk about maintenance requests, but I've never had an issue that required one. I say its a hidden gem because it's on the edge of downtown, but close enough to walk right into it. 35 and 94 are right here which makes commuting a breeze.

Its been only 1.5 months since I moved in these apartments and it already feels like home. Nicole, the property manager is super helpful and resolves any kind of issues at utmost priority. The apartments are brand new and have almost every amenity that one can think of. The rooftop view is nothing less than awesome. I'd love to recommend this place to anybody who is looking for a place to live in the heart of downtown!

I really want to like this place but every step of the neighbor walking above you can be heard and it gets tiring. My doors will even rattle sometimes; it's a constant banging sound. The complex is maintained very well, and Nicole the property manager is really nice. The rooftop has wonderful views and the community here is safe. Overall for a brand new building, it's disappointing more quality wasn't put into the floors like it was for the rest of the building.

I've only been living here for a few weeks, but Nicole is the best! She's been helpful, patient and easy to communicate with. I love that every unit has a washer/dryer. The rooftop deck is fantastic and has an awesome view of downtown. It's still early, but I really think I'm going to enjoy living here. :)

The Modi apartments are a great place to live! I moved to Minneapolis last year from the east coast right before winter hit so I was very specific in what I needed from an apartment building and Modi checked all the boxes for me. 

The apartment unit was very spacious with huge windows all across the living room and bedroom. I was definitely glad I had a lot of sunlight during the winter and then during quarantine when I was working from home. The building has a gym, a rooftop deck with a grill and firepit, and package lockers to keep packages safe! Also, with The Wedge Co-Op right across the parking lot, popping out for groceries whenever you need them is very convenient! 

Jessica, the property manager, is also super responsive and attentive of all the resident's needs! She is always available to answer questions and address anything that might come up on the property! The residents are all super down to earth and the community is very respectful of one another. I really recommend living here if you are looking in the area!

If you are sensitive to noise, don’t live facing Washington Ave. The ambulances and fire trucks and overall car noise from trucks and loud motorcycles is just awful. It never ended. You’ll hear a siren drive by at least 2-3 times per hour. No amount of fans or noise makers could help me sleep. I dealt with it for a year and got out and feel compelled to warn people. I had a friend who faced the other way and said they heard the light rail bell chiming constantly, so maybe there’s no escaping it. The inside of the building is super quiet, but man those windows were thin.

Location, location, location! Great to be so close to US Bank Stadium as well as the train line. Across the street from Trader Joe's? Can't be beat. The building makes it very easy to get on and off the highway - downtown living without the downtown fuss. The quality of the build has shown itself - I have never heard a neighbor to the side or above me. Having the option to park in the covered garage or in heated underground at different prices has been a great option. The amenity deck was vacation-worthy last summer, I am anxiously awaiting warmer weather to enjoy the sunshine and the pool again. 
The staff is helpful and friendly. They are led by an incredible building manager: Jessie. She is considerate, efficient and so obviously cares about her job and the tenants. I have been so impressed with her work ethic! An apartment may be luxurious but without great management it isn't worth the frustration. Fear not at Ironclad! Jessie has you covered.

Henley was my first apartment living on my own. It was a great experience, management was very quickly to respond and easy to work with. I had no major issues living at the apartment and it was well designed and a perfect studio to live in. The location was great and sometime you got free entertainment from the auditorium next to Richfield lake. It was a great first apartment and I would have loved to stay if I didn’t decide to go to graduate school!

i am living at a studio now. I wasn't able to connect anything with my Alexa. is it smart apartment? i don't think so and power outage often occurs and we have to set up the light and the air-conditioning every time because WIFI disconnects the devices. it doesn't use gas, heater. only electricity. The cost is so expensive. Last February, the electricity per month was about 120 USD for a studio. that's crazy.

The neighborhood is bad, loud residents, and worst of all, Shane and office people are the worst. They seem to be very lazy and can't solve issues happening in the apt. Very glad that I am leaving. Find a different place. 0 star not even worth 1 star
I love living here! The office staff is nice and attentive. They are always on top of everything! Nothing compared to where I used to live. This place is great! And they have free coffee ??

This review is coming from a late career professional. The management team are professional,  accommodating and welcoming.  Platform747 is safe, quiet and convenient - close to University of Minnesota campus, next to light rail and 280. You can get to virtually anything you need or want in 10 minutes!

If you are looking for a good dog-friendly place, I highly recommend Platform. The property managers are very helpful and responsive. The amenities are great. It is close to everything. Great location and good management.

I just moved into Platform Apartments and have been amazed by the welcoming leasing agents, beautiful building, and spacious apartments! The amenities are incredible with a pool, hot tub, solarium, gym, garage parking, and working from home spaces. The rent is very reasonable for all of the amenities and space in the apartment. Appliances are all new and in excellent condition. Great access to public transportation for both Minneapolis and St. Paul. Excellent apartment and would highly recommend renting from here!

Sound travels up the windows in the front of the building….so a dog barking for hours could be coming from above me, where the stomper lives(oh yes….stomping….not walking ever) or below me.  Back to the stomper….things from their deck ends up on mine…and before they moved in management had the deck cleaned up there and all the dirt went onto my deck….so I’ve never been able to have anything on My deck.  My dog was caught peeing somewhere besides the undersized dog park and I got a pretty serious warning.  NEVERMIND the fact that other people let their dogs pee all over the place….but this is a see something say something building…so people tattle if they think it will benefit them.  People barbecue on their decks…don’t clean up their dog poop, and invade your space without asking if it’s okay.  I could go on but I think you get the point.

It has been 2 months since I've moved in and it has met all my expectations. The management team of Robin and Theresa is exceptional. They are always there when needed with a smile every time. If they are not there, building manager Dubei is there if you need him (embarrassingly, I had some really stupid questions but he smiled throughout. He's that awesome!) The area has been amazing with Edina being 2 minutes away and the Richfield part is sweet too. You are only a walk or short drive away from Southdale Mall, great restaurants, nail salons, grocery stores, and Super Target. As far as the building, it is beautiful with great amenities. The dog park and heated indoor garage is everything. Plus the gym is all new. The neighbors are cool. Soundproofing is #1 as well as far as we have experience. Super happy to be part of this neighborhood and in Novo Apartments.
This campus is immaculate, the living space is gorgeous, friendly management, clean, cozy, unbeatable!

If you're considering Ruby Apartments, I recommend proceeding with caution. While the property might look appealing at first, there are several concerns you should be aware of based on my experience.

The biggest issue is the lack of soundproofing. You can hear noises through the walls and ceilings, making it hard to enjoy a quiet living space. If you value peace and privacy, this might not be the best choice for you.

Additionally, I found the move-out process frustrating. Despite raising concerns about the unit’s condition when I moved in, I was charged for what I believe were pre-existing issues. Make sure to document everything carefully before signing the lease and during your stay.

While the location might be convenient, the overall experience left much to be desired. I would recommend looking into other options to ensure you get a fair and enjoyable living arrangement.

This is just my honest opinion based on my personal experience—hopefully, it helps someone make an informed decision

Honest review: SAVE YOUR MONEY and look for a FINISHED and well established, well rated building (don’t be fooled by the exterior, or the reviews of people who just moved in two weeks ago). Lots of deep issues here that you’ll discover only AFTER living here awhile.

Main thing to keep in mind is that the bldg is NOT FINISHED & coming construction will be unlivable for many units and unpleasant for all (common areas and pool will be radically affected by the noise and dirt for years to come!). The (surprise!!) pre-construction to prepare the lot last winter was incredibly disruptive. RENTER BEWARE.
The Ruby is a nice apartment building. The staff are friendly and responsive. I was able to move in quickly. I'm happy to call The Ruby my home!

I really love my new apartment, I'm someone who is very picky and loves to live in a nice apartment. So, when it was time for me to move from my old apartment, I was looking for something similar. Luckily for me, I found  Midline apartment which had an extra touch of modern design. I usually love white kitchen cabinets, but when I found the color and the background design of my new kitchen at Midline, it was so beautiful, and didn't think twice. Moreover, the pricing is, affordable compared to surrounding Apartments which have brown kitchen cabinets and doors, which was something I wasn't looking out for. If you are looking for modern style and design, don't look elsewhere other than Midline Apartments. Also, the management of Midline especially Bryanna and Steven made my move-in so smooth, Steven was very polite and answered all my questions right from the beginning of my search, whiles Bryanna was very flexible with me when I had to change my move-in date a couple of times due to unforeseen circumstances and she was even awake around 10 pm to answer my questions during the day of my move in. The only thing I wish I had with my new apartment was a patio or balcony since other rooms have it, other than that everything looks great!
I love the process with applying with them they had made it easy an painless they answer all my questions an was flexible with my move in dates. can’t wait to move in

I have yet to move in, but I will say that the leasing process was absolutely flawless and fast. It took less than 48 hours to get approval and sign my lease!! The staff was very friendly and promptly answered all my questions (and as a first time leaser, I greatly appreciated it). I cannot wait to move into my new home!!

I love my new apartment at Landsby on Penn. The staff have been wonderful, prompt and professional. The shared spaces are beautifully designed. Roof top deck is awesome. Workout room fully appointed. I'm used to city living but this apartment is surprisingly quiet. Looking forward to using the makers space for some DIY projects for my home. I highly recommend checking out Landsby on Penn! Also, Lund's and Byerly's across the parking lot is so convenient.

Went for a tour and found the apartment really nice. 

Only caveat is they are not transparent with their rent prices 
The month rent shown online is the price you pay after all the monthly saving. The truth is, the free month rent is prorated and your monthly is $200-300 more.

They also hike the base rent when they have promotions and bring it down a couple days after the promotion.

All other apartments we toured showed actual price and the discount is on top of that.

Management is great! The lobby is always clean. The roof top lounge and pool area are great places to relax. The apartments are energy efficient and a great size. As an extra plus this apartment is also dog and cat friendly.

I have been here for almost a year now. I give Corsa a 2.5/5.

I'll start with the pros of this building:
- Location. It is amazing being so close to the walking path and Excelsior Blvd. Very convenient.
- Low noise, to a degree. The exterior door is not great at keeping noise out. I know you can't expect a noise-free environment in an apartment, but I also believe you shouldn't hear the jingle of someone's keys as they walk by your door (which I do). I do not regularly hear noise from the surrounding apartments. The pickleball court is a unique feature, but caution: even the fourth-floor apartments facing the courtyard get the pickleball noise quite clearly.
- Gym. It's updated with a lot of different machines. Yoga rooms are a plus too.
- Unique community nights.
- Overall stylish apartment.

Cons:
- The parking garage. It's small and cramped. Also.. open air at a steep $150 a month. This winter wasn't even abnormally cold for a Minnesota winter, yet a pipe burst in the garage, and the garage door seemingly can't work if it's below 15 degrees (I mean.. c'mon, it's MN). The garage was left open for about a week in February alone due to cold temperatures. As of most recent, residents became aware of vehicle break-ins and bike theft in the garage, not from management, but because of the resident community bulletin board. Instead, management sent out a notice about driving speed in the garage with no mention of the break-ins.
- Water quality. I know this is no fault of the apartment building itself, but there is extremely hard water here. A shower head filter is not effective enough, so if you're a bottle blonde like me, just be prepared.
- Lack of appropriate information being shared from management. Since I have been here, there has been a new management staff since the other management staff received many poor reviews (see below). The new management continues to leave more to be desired. Management has not been communicative about building-wide fire alarms. Each time it has happened since living here (at least 3x), I have received no updates. My partner emailed Corsa management asking why it went off, and the response was uninformative. Also, as mentioned above, even when it comes to vehicle break-ins and bike theft, Corsa management still does not provide residents with information about what is being done and what happened.

Just want to warn people, the studio and one bedroom units here have electric heating, so my energy bill was $215 in December, $250 in January, and now $225 in February. That is with me being as energy conscious as possible and keeping the temperature in my 700 square foot apartment at 65 degrees. So budget accordingly for the winter months. I felt misled by this as my lease specifically stated each unit had a gas meter.

Other cons: the garage door malfunctions quite often, my boyfriend and my mountain bikes were stolen due to someone being able to walk with a saw and cut our locks off. The hot tub closes when the pool closes in late August - we were told during our tour it would be open year round.

Pros: the best apartment gym I’ve ever had (brand new treadmills, two squat racks, etc.) great location, love the private pickleball court

Furthermore, I should add that the influx of positive reviews over the last month is because Corsa offered the chance to win $1500 in rent credit if we leave a review in February :’) so take these recent reviews with a grain of salt.

I’ve been living in this apartment for 8 months and I couldn’t be happier with my choice. The unit itself is spacious, clean, and well-maintained, with modern appliances and plenty of natural light. The floor plan is very functional, and I love the ample storage space.

The management team has been incredibly responsive and professional. They’re always quick to address any concerns or maintenance requests, and the building is consistently clean and quiet.
One of the biggest highlights for me is the location – it’s so convenient! Located near the lakes, Excelsior&Grand, and the West End.
I also feel very safe here. The building has great security, and I’ve never had any issues with noise or disturbances.

Overall, I highly recommend this apartment to anyone looking for a comfortable, convenient, and hassle-free place to live. It’s been a great experience for me!

My dog and I moved in September, and it’s perfect! The dog run is nice for quick potty breaks and being right across the street from a trail has been fantastic. All of the other amenities are great too. Looking forward to using the pool in the summer!
I’ve lived here a year now and I absolutely love Corsa! They are very communicative, the amenities are amazing and the apartments themselves are awesome. It’s also such a great location!
My girlfriend and I just moved in and absolutely love it. The front desk service is first class and the amenities are top notch. So happy with our decision to move here!

Just moved into the best building in town bar none. Great location. Best set of amenities ever! Theater room, swimming pool, hot tub, sauna, and tanning booth, etc. Then I go to the website. A million dollars in renovations. Awesome! Then I find out those exciting renovations are getting rid of the theater room, sauna and tanning booth. All the cold weather amenities that make this building so a step above the rest. Who would rather have a co-working space instead of a theater room with surround sound? If tenants wanted that they would just go in the community rec room. Also, they forgot that most people who work from home need a landline phone to do their job. So it will likely just sit empty and attract no new tenants...at least far less than a theater room would. They don't realize how great those things make it her.  . 

Once the renovations are done this will just be an ordinary old building. Not really even luxury anymore. Honestly no new building could compete with this place because of all the great amenities. But unless  they plan on lowering the rent when they get rid of everyone's favorite amenities, it kind of won't be worth the high price anymore. There won't be anything to do in the winter here. Am writing this review to ask, before doing the expensive renovations, ask the tenants how they feel about it.  It will likely be worth it to keep our favorite amenities and invest the money in other things or just save the money.  We love it just the way it is!

THE DOOR LOCK SAGA: I get an email at 3pm that they changed my locks back to the standard electrical fob, which I previously had a dead bolt. I left work earlier then expected and came back to the apartment trying to get access to my keys so that I didn’t get locked out. The woman in the office at 5pm was in the process of trying to reprogram my keys. It didn’t work. They called maintenance and he had to use a special key to get into my apartment… one hour later I am in my apartment. Catch is I had somewhere to be at 5 and was now hour late, and the door was just propped open. I had to get the maintenance guy to come back to lock apartment before I could leave.. and he assured me someone was coming to change the lock back to the dead bolt that I had previously had so I could get in when I returned in a few hours, crying out of frustration I left not wanting to be stuck in an unlocked apartment or risk leaving it unlocked if I had to go somewhere. I come back at 8:30pm and the same electronic lock they assured me would be changed is on the door and I don’t have a key for it. My phone is about to die but I call the emergency maintenance number there times and leave massages each time. I call a friend and am staying on her couch now because I can’t get into my own apartment. No answer or call back from emergency maintenance over an hour later. I have a cat and a lizard that both need fed and was planning on being at work at 8am but I have none of my stuff and the office doesn’t “open” until 9am and staff are regularly late. I will have to spend more time off work dealing with this tmw to make sure I can get in, get access to my clothes and work laptop.

Update: after leaving me locked out of my residence for the whole night the emergency maintenance  never responded. They offer me $150. My rent is $46 a day and the $100 remaining wouldn’t even get me a trash hotel for the night they left me on the street! Not to mention loss of sleep, work time, no medications, unfed pets and stress!! Absolutely criminal!

don’t rent here! It is really not worth it!

I have lived here a while and have made many friends here. Although this community is large, the happy hours (on hold for the pandemic) would bring us together Yesterday, for example, a neighbor stopped by with Chocolate Ice Cream as a thank you to me for looking after his packages. The day before, another neighbor stopped with a "just because" gift.  While this sheds a light on those of us who have made this our forever home, of course, the younger people have a vibrant lifestyle and the layout of this complex allows for freedom and autonomy; but also the opportunity to connect.

808 Berry has big, beautiful town home style apartments with very attentive, helpful staff. It's not the best location for the price considering you're about a mile away from the Midway neighborhood of University Ave./Snelling. I would recommend this place for college students who are looking for a place close to the campus and downtown.

Right off 280 and university/ 94 allows for easy access to MPLS and St. Paul, but constant construction immediately adjacent gets a little tedious and annoying. Beautiful apartments and building, big garage below, and lovely pool area and courtyard. Street parking gets full on weekend nights and only cats on upper levels, unfortunately. Management and maintenance staff are helpful and friendly, but losing a key or garage door opener will cost you $100 each.

We have been living at Berry Place for over 2 years now, and if there is anything to know about this place we know. 

The apartment building is great, the staff working here is fabulous. They provide great service. Monthly HH is a good way to connect with other residents. They deliver packages to your home...LOVE IT!!! The location cannot be better. Easy access to major freeways, light rail station and buses. Everything is close. 

There are a few negatives that I would like to point for which, I'm only knocking off a star!!!
1. Underground parking - only one spot included, not matter what apartment size you're in. Not fair
2. Garage hasn't been power washed in over a year now...It's dusty and filthy! 
3. When everything in the apartment is nicely finished (stainless steel appliances, great plumbing, etc...), the blinds are cheap and give no protection from light.
4. Rent increases have been very high from what I have heard from other renters.
5. This is my biggest issue... THIN WALLS. Can hear everything. Literally everything around you. NOT COOL!

We love living here due to convenience and ease of access. But we are not happy with some of the things I mentioned above.

Recently our power went out for the better part of two days.  On the 2nd day, the back up generator blew - so there was NO power.  No elevators.  Nothing.  Took them almost 10 hours to get a back up for the back up.  This is typical for this building.  They do not fix anything until a catastrophe happens.  Then the management staff acts like you shouldn't be irritated.  BTW-they have been thru about 7 property managers in less than 3 years.  The grounds are not kept up, the parking lot is a mine field of pot holes, the dog park becomes a lake when it rains, the pool is never opened on time, constant water leaks, belongings are stolen w/no response from management, the elevators are consistently not working, should I continue because I could...oh! don't plan on sleeping well because the windows rattle with the wind and the a/c units barely work.  Any review that says management is great has to be them writing because they don't care.  The owner doesn't care.  Don't live here.

I have lived here for a little over a year.  In this time frame:  no hot water several times, the elevators are down constantly, multiple water leaks, repairs never get done, my shower took three months to work properly, the building air doesn’t work, been out of electricity (due to a water leak) for two days, and my apartment is so hot-it never gets below 75.  

Poorly ran, poorly managed, poor maintained.  Do NOT recommend.

I love this place!  The apts have walls of windows, views you can never get sick up and cozy neighborhood to walk around. We're within blocks of a grocery store, drug store, restaurants and a movie theater.  The office folks are really nice too.  There are plenty of amenities, i.e. driver during day hours, continental breakfast, pool, underground parking.  I keep looking elsewhere for something cheaper and newer, but haven't found something awesome enough to make the move.  So glad to have found this apartment here!  Good luck and have fun in your searching!

I was looking for places in Minneapolis, but after I toured park trails and met Helen it was a wrap.  I wasn't impressed with the unit but my needs as a tenant are number 1 priority and after meeting Helen with her great  energy and no non sense approach to the lease agreement I signed with no questions asked as I am sure all my needs will be met with the great Management and attitude of the office Manager Helen.

Have had a great experience here! Manager very responsive, very kind & helpful. Maintenence responsive w/i a day. Updated apartments with new balconies on trail side.  Great location by Trader Joe's, Target, Steel Toe Brewery, and walking trails to name a few places. Highly recommend!

I lived here for several years because I couldn't afford a good place to live. Property management sucks. Loss of water, loss of power, lots of bugs and a decent bit of mold. This place really sucks. Don't live here.

I've had someone with keys coming in and out of my apartment, without notice, the whole time I lived here. I suspect it was the management, but don't know for sure. I had several items stolen, as well. I also noticed they like to get people's car towed, again.... suspect that's management-super shady practices. The place is overall, really dumpy. The hornet nest was never taken care of even AFTER bringing it to their attention and I was almost swarmed by em. The washer has been broken for over a YEAR, and they never bothered fixing it. The apartments ARE in a good area, though.

I lived at these apartments for 2.5 years which was 2.5 years too long.
•	These apartments are under the flight path of MSP airport, so you will hear loud, low flying, airplanes non-stop.
•	My building had an extremely loud entry door, which my bedroom was directly above. Every time someone went in/out, I’d hear the door slam, loud enough to wake me up and hear in other parts of my unit.
•	There were endless water issues at these apartments, either I had no hot water or no water at all. The repairs to the water heater and pipes seemed to be merely bandaids on the real problem. Not only that, but my shower would randomly get scalding hot for no reason.
•	Outside noise and hallways noise is definitely an issue, especially when they started allowing dogs, which when I moved in they didn’t allow.
•	I’m not sure if neighbors were smoking in the building, or if the smell of cigarettes just carried that far from the smoking area by the dumpsters and into the building, but my unit often smelled like cigarettes.
•	Management doesn’t stick around. There were four different property managers during my stay. They also do not provide backups when they’re on vacation and do not communicate when they’re out or when they are no longer with the company.
•	Snow plowing is slow in the winter and therefore the snow gets packed down and then becomes ice.  The parking lot in general is a bit of a potholed mess with puddles when it rains or snow melts.
•	Lastly, guests are required to have guest parking passes which the property manager issues (which are a pain to get when there's no manager). My boyfriend’s car was towed due to the carelessness on the property manager’s part while filling out the pass.  This cost $200 to release the car and then 2.5 weeks of working with the towing company and Park Trails to get a refund.

Every unit in my building turned over while I was living there except one unit, maybe two.  People do not stay here long term.  I would look somewhere else especially if you enjoy quiet and running (hot) water.

Apart from the good location and relatively low price, there are very few pros. I’ve been here almost three years, every year thinking it will get better. (Spoiler, it hasn’t...) Terrible management with fast turnover, maintenance issues constantly, and no hot water frequently. The water was shut off completely several times in 2020 alone. Noise travels a lot, as the building is very poorly constructed with cheap materials and not maintained well.

These apartments are poorly built and the property managers and parent company (Soderberg Apartments) do not appear to care about their tenants. The property manager, Max, was great when we moved in, but he left soon after and we’ve gone through several property managers since then. Soderberg Apartments never communicates these changes to the Park Trails residents, so we’ve gone weeks at a time without a property manager to handle issues and maintenance requests. We have gone hours without running water on several occasions with no warning, and my building also has an issue with the hot water going out frequently. My apartment has cracks that have let hornets inside three times, and we also have pest issues with silverfish and house centipedes.
