The pipes have had several issues in my time here, and the water has so much mineral content that it leaves residue in the tub, sinks, and on dishes and laundry. Our apartment wall also has a bad smell when the sun hits it, which makes me suspect mold in the building materials. The only redeeming qualities are the somewhat low cost, free parking, and the friendly maintenance person. The updated kitchens are nice but not the best quality appliances, and the “maple” floors are laminate panels.. not actual wood.

Don't move here if you like hot water. In fact, don't move here if you need running water in general. Don't move here if you want maintenance to follow up on maintenance requests. Don't move here if you want management that cares about you, your unit, the property, or even their own company. Maybe just don't move here at all.

The apartment itself is nice.  The maple floors and granite counter tops are a nice touch.  Overall the area is quiet and the neighbors are very kind.  General spaces are kept clean and maintenance is quick and respectful in responding to work orders.

What they won't tell you...

- Air Conditioning: the wall units are very old and not efficient.  They do not cool the whole apartment and the dials often do not work 100%.

- BBQ Area: This is non-existing.  There are three picnic tables total on the property and one grill which is never clean and tucked in a corner.

-  On-Site Property Manager: They tend to have a 3 month shelf life and sadly leave or get let go, leaving the residents to have to hunt for someone at another property to get assistance.

- Package Receiving: Inconsistent due to the common lack of an On-Site Property Manager.

- Vaulted Ceilings: They are standard height.

- Walk-In Closets: You can walk in and then immediately hit the wall, these are not walk-in at all.

- Laundry Facilities: Not enough per building.  The dryers do not fully dry items, even when only 1/3 full.  Tried reaching out to maintenance and the company that owns the machines and was told it wasn't their issue.

- Courtyard/Picnic Area: Do not exist.

- Business Center: This is the Property Managers office, but since there is more often not a Property Manager on site, the office/Business Center is not accessible.

- Smoking Free: Not true.  Many residents smoke on their balconies, Friday and Saturday nights in the summer the air is so stinky with cigarette smoke.

Storage Units: These are incredibly small.

- Rent Increases: a $100 increase is common.  There is no explanation when you ask why.  

- Property: There are three shipping containers, two in the yard area and one in the parking lot (taking up spaces) that showed up in the spring.  We were told they were new bathroom vanities for all the apartments.  No one has received new bathroom vanities, in fact the containers have not been accessed since arriving.  They are unsightly and suspicious.

Lived her for a year. The buildings look run down inside because maintenance, while very timely and quick, does sloppy repairs. (For example, not trimming and nailing in wall bases properly or sealing in all areas with caulk properly. They put a brand new wood floor in before I moved in and scratched it up with appliances before I even saw it.) However, management has been good. Stacy was always timely and polite in responses, and Ana has been great so far. The location is really what makes this apartment so great. Trails that lead right to Lake Calhoun and close to shopping and hwy 100. The 1 bedroom units were worth the price last year, but now you could rent a nicer place for the same price.

I have been living in Park Trail Apartments for about 3 months. The apartment itself is very affordable, clean and has a very nice layout. The community is very quiet and respectable. The neighbors are friendly and welcoming. The maintenance staff is incredibly responsive and is more than willing to show up during off hours to address a need. Now for the best part about this apartment ... The LOCATION. This complex is located very close to the uptown area. There are plenty of shops and restaurant within walking distance. Plus you have plenty of access to parks and trails. One of the coolest features is that there is a large park and a trader joes across the street. My wife and I have been thrilled with our apartment.

I have been living at Park Trails for a year and love it!  The location is great - you are close to uptown, walking distance to Trader Joe's, can easily hop on the bike path, and there is a park and rec center right across the street (ahem Pokemon Go people).  Being a recent college grad and living on a tight budget, I was having a hard time initially looking for apartments in the area.  Although Park Trails may not have super fancy amenities found in upscale and luxurious apartments, the units are renovated with newer appliances and the location itself definitely makes up for it.

I've lived at Park Trails now for about 6 months and would recommend living here. The location and renovated apartments make this property feel newer than it really is. 

Pros: Remodeled apartments, friendly management, and walking distance to the grocery store! 
Cons: No garages and not dog friendly 

All in all if you are looking for an apartment in the St. Louis Park area this property is the best value around.

I moved in about a month ago, and I couldn't be happier!  Onsite property management and maintenance staff has been incredibly responsive, efficient, and friendly.  My unit is beautiful, well laid out, and has tons of storage/closet space.  And the location is amazing!  I am no more than a 5-10 minute drive (and sometimes a 5 minute walk) from anything I want: restaurants, grocery stores, shopping, lakes, parks, post office, bank, yoga, gym, EVERYTHING.  I am extremely happy with my experience so far and would recommend Park Trails to anyone.

My roommate and I just moved into Park Trails Apartments in September, and so far our experience has been great. The location is absolutely amazing, right off excelsior by Highway 100 and only about a mile from lake Calhoun. The staff here has also been exceptional. Lydia is always very sweet and friendly and quick to respond to emails and questions. Eric, with maintenance, has been so helpful since we've been here as well. We had a few initial but minor problems and Eric and Lydia were always so quick to respond and persistent on ensuring the problem was fixed and that we were happy. Free parking for residents is a huge bonus, as is the newly updated apartment units and appliances!

Park Trails is perfectly situated in an area that makes Uptown and Minneapolis accessible, and yet outside of the area enough to get a quieter suburban feel. Many of the people in the area/residents are young professionals. Trader Joes and the Civic Center (Hockey Rinks & Outdoor Water Park) are within walking distance. Insofar as the building, the outside appearance really fools you. If anything, that alone needs work. Once inside the rooms have very nice looking wood floors and great appliance and countertops. The rooms can be a little dark and the bathrooms are super retro, but they aren't large issues and the space is very nice. The management staff is onsite and very responsive/friendly. No problems there, and the online rent payment makes the rent (One of the cheaper in the area) that much easier to take care of. St. Louis Park does not allow grills on decks, so they are rather pointless... But the pool is a nice touch in summer (It has been "broken" for a portion of this summer but they quickly fixed it. Very satisfied with my choice to live here after leaving Uptown and the sirens!
I had to give written notice 3 times that I was not renewing my lease. I got a call months after I moved from the office and they still didn't know.

I lived here for three years right after college. It is an excellent price for the location and amenities. The area was kept clean. There was always parking available right outside my building. Great place for the price.

Motel 6 and Velo… what’s the difference? Not much. To start, there are homeless people wandering around or sleeping in common areas on a reoccurring basis, and cars getting broken into all the time. This place has absolutely zero security and management does nothing to boost security. Instead, they will tell you to call the police or to avoid using the main door so that no one sneaks in. Your apartment unit is breaking down every month and maintenance will apply bandaid fixes so good luck with that. You can pay a similar amount elsewhere in north loop for way more amenities, safety, and a better quality of life. Management cares about one thing and it’s money; they will gouge you every chance they can. If some random throws a couch in your dumpster, guess what, you’ll pay for the removal. I had my apartment professionally cleaned after I moved out, but I still got charged a “cleaning fee”. The place was insanely clean. Your apartment will be very cold in the winters so bundle up, and you’ll pay insane energy bills all year round as these units are not sealed. I could go on and on but I’ll leave it at that. I rarely write reviews, but this is warranted, especially if it helps you not make a bad decision.

VÈLO, located in the North Loop, is a modern building with nice amenities and comparable pricing. Unfortunately, all of these positives are irreparably marred by a management team that can only be described as wholly incompetent and expressly disinterested in resolving even the simplest day-to-day issues of apartment building life.

The issues themselves are numerous: Poor ventilation and installation in the bathrooms causes recurring mold and mildew problems. Public areas are plagued by insects, shoddy cleaning, and supply issues. Dog owners refuse to pick up waste in front of the building and on the 2nd floor deck (from the gym you get to enjoy a direct view of dogs pissing on the deck’s astro turf bocce ball court) and are not reprimanded. HVAC systems are underserved. Rent checks are cashed unpredictably. And the entire building seems to be in a continuous state of mild chaos.

Individually, any one of these issues is to be expected in apartment living. The crux of the problem, and what makes it impossible to recommend VÈLO as a home, is the management's complete unwillingness to even try to do their job. Correspondence with management is unreliable at absolute best - we had to personally stop by the office every single day for over two weeks just to make sure that progress was being made on our bathroom’s mold removal (and they still did such a half-assed job that the mold has already returned). Maintenance will often cancel requests from the app with no explanation. And when they do bother to stop by your unit, they do so without warning and their work is so poor that the problem always returns. 

No building is perfect. But the building management team of VÈLO should be humiliated at the rate at which extremely simple issues repeatedly exceed their abilities to address. How difficult is it to instruct the custodial team to clean common areas? How difficult is it to resolve a mold issue, or to clean HVAC units? Challenges that tens of thousands of buildings swiftly and easily resolve every single day across the country leave the VÈLO team dumbfounded. And the result is a deep and persistent dissatisfaction from a growing host of residents.

Until sweeping personnel and policy changes are implemented property-wide, we cannot recommend VÈLO. Look elsewhere for North Loop living.
yes
The office staff have been super helpful and very friendly. I enjoy living somewhere where the office knows the residents.

One negative is the recent change to charge residents for water trash and sewer. I am rarely home and yet I have a bill every month for $35 for other people's use. One wonderful selling point of Vélo was that all services were included in rent. Now it's just another building.
Jay and Marriah do a marvelous job keeping the apartment building clean, near, quiet, and friendly. I would highly and DO highly recommend it.

I have lived at The Abbey since its opening in 2022. The apartments, leasing staff, and the view of the city are unmatched. The close proximity to Loring Park is a huge perk! It's flooded with a variety of birds and friendly people from the community.

You're within 15-20 minutes of the Warehouse District as well so you can enjoy all that downtown Minneapolis has to offer from Twins games, concerts at First Ave., or whatever strikes your fancy!

I'd give The Abbey 10 stars if I could!

I absolutely LOVE living here.  The Abbey is amazing and the the beautiful and historic mansion coupled with fabulous apartments (very well appointed) make this THE. BEST.  place to live. Close to so many great Minneapolis places and events. 
Nolan is so kind and professional and keeps us posted with everything we need to know.   The amenities we have in the mansion and throughout are top notch!  Love it here!!

Moved into this property recently and while the staff has been great and the building looks nice, the walls separating the apartments are way to thin.  I have been kept awake and woken up on multiple occasions in my short time living here by noise i can hear from other adjoining apartments. This has been highly disappointing as i expected better building quality.

1) The walls are thin, and I can hear my neighbors all day. Management is reluctant to resolve this issue.

2) The garage is disorganized

3)  The units are unfinished

Horrible apartment building. Do not live here. Walls are paper thin. Unstable neighbor threatened to kill me for a noise issue. Had a drunk apartment mate walk into my apartment at 1am on a Thurday scaring the crap out of my girlfriend and I. They're letting just about anyone live here. Horrible apartment building, regret the day that I signed at this god forsaken place. DO NOT live here, you will regret it. The apartment is also filled with the most unfriendly people you will ever meet in your life.

Do yourself a favor and literally live anywhere else. I'm in the process of terminating my lease.

The Abbey is amazing and the combination of the historic mansion alongside the modern apartments sets it apart from any other place we saw. Jack and Nolan are kind, professional and left us space to ask questions and really find the right place for us. Experiences matter when it comes to shopping for a new place and this experience drew us in further! Cannot recommend this place enough!

I have lived here almost 2 years now and only have good things to say about living here! The buildings are older, but they are well-cared for and feel cozy. Management has always been very understanding and willing to work with the tenants for their needs. Any maintenance requests I have put in have been attended to in a timely manner. Keep up the great work, team!

I've been living at East River Terrace for a couple of years now and I love it! The location is ideal as it's next to the Mississippi River and not far from great restaurants, coffee shops, and grocery stores. There's a great sense of community and comfort. The property managers are really nice and helpful. Maintenance is responsive and knowledgeable. Special thanks to Jake for helping with my repair. He was very friendly and respectful. Highly recommend living here!

We just love, love, LOVE our new rental townhouse.  We were looking for a bigger place, and boy did we get it!  3 floors & 2 bedrooms and 2x the sqft of our last place! (wow)
The basement isn't finished, but its clean and has a dry concrete floor. Its the perfect play area for kids and adults.   (we are putting a music studio in!) There is also a washer & dryer in the basement which is such a convenience.

The townhouse is right off of East River Road which gives  us spectacular views of the Mississippi National River and Recreation Area:  In the middle of a bustling urban setting, this 72-mile river-park offers quiet stretches for fishing, boating and canoeing.  Other spots are excellent for birdwatching, bicycling and hiking.

50   restaurants in the area, including the Seward Co-op, which is just a mile and a half away.

Apartment is very close to The Shriners Hospital for Kids; University of Minnesota, Minneapolis; and The Ronald McDonald house.

Garage space is available, and the nearest bus lines are very close.

Kolo has been fantastic to live at and the management staff is always very professional with communication.  Highly recommend living here if you're looking for a modern feel just a few blocks off of Bde Maka Ska!

Kolo is such a great place to live. Clean community areas, great location and great management. You can tell they really care for the safety and well-being of the residents. My unit was clean upon move in, maintenance requests are fulfilled in a day of/ in a timely manner,  and the property manager, Jimmy, has been so helpful during my move in and is very accommodating and friendly. Anthony was also really helpful in helping me get information on my unit/leasing. I love living at Kolo and would recommend it to anyone :)

I have loved living at Kolo. From touring, to lease signing (on a convenient app), to having work orders fulfilled day-of, to the beautiful finishes in the apartment, and the proximity to the lakes, I had a great experience. Management is extremely responsive to emails and flexible with lease start and end dates. I did not take advantage of the lower level parking garage, but it was always easy to find street parking right outside of the building. All of my neighbors have been friendly, and the common spaces in the building are always clean. I recommend Kolo to anyone!

I don’t know why this place got good reviews. I moved in last week and my experience so far is TERRIBLE!!!!! The day I moved in I found out that the AC in my bedroom is not working. And the next day the AC in my living room also stop working. It is 95F outside and my room is facing west so it become super hot during the day. I called the “24hr emergency maintenance “ and I was told that it is not emergency, the maintenance won’t come until maybe 3-4 days later. I have no choice but to live in hotel instead. It’s July 4th weekend and it cost me $150 per day for it. The maintenance can’t be worse. The rooms are also very dirty and have some stinky smell, stains everywhere, looks like not cleaned at all before I move in.
I thoroughly enjoy the community within the building and the surrounding area. I feel apart of a great community.

I never lived on this property, but I did apply in spring 2023. Our leasing agent was perfectly lovely, but know that there are some financial catches that come with applying. The application costs the usual $55 or so to submit. Then, before you even sign the lease, they take $150 from your card for "administrative fees" and the $300 security deposit. If you change your mind and decide not to sign the lease, as my friend and I did, you do NOT get any of that money back. This information is buried deep in the application agreement, so make sure you keep an eye out for it.

I had an amazing experience living at the Calhoun Greenway, where I lived for almost 5 years (spent at least a year in each of the three CG buildings: East, West and Be). Maintenance requests were dealt with quickly - via an online portal, so it was easy to submit them whenever - and communication with residents was great. Rent was a little high, but it is Minneapolis, after all! And as other reviewers have mentioned, buildings are definitely a little old, but renovations help them feel newer. Location was perfect-- very close to the lakes, Whole Foods/Chipotle/Noodles/Caribou/Wakame, and the 12 & 17 bus lines. I moved out because I needed a little more space at a little lower rent, but will miss it tremendously.

I was suckered in a year ago by its amazing location and the amenities that were shown to me during the tour.  For the price, the amenities are actually pretty nice.  The location is phenomenal and parking is easy enough to come by, even during the winter.  The pool (indoor & outdoor) are nice and usually available.  And the gym has just enough equipment. 

My negative experience has much to do with the age of the flooring in between floors in this apartment.  It is an older complex that has been painted over time and time again to look nice.  You can tell they have put significant effort into making this place appear nice, but I assure that it is all cosmetic. I suspect the flooring in between units is quite old, nailed down instead of screwed.  Thus, EVERY TIME somebody so much as tip toes upstairs, you WILL hear an ear piercing creak.  Go ahead and try ear plugs, loud fans, pillows over your head.... Nothing will dampen it enough.   

I have attempted to contact management on several occasions about the noise, and they are generally unresponsive, perhaps issuing a warning to my upstairs tenant.  And what really can they do?  It's not like they are going to tear the floor apart and make an upgrade like that, it is not even my upstairs tenants fault, they pay the same price I do and have the right to be a night owl.  It is my fault that I did not test to see what the flooring would be like above my head.  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND going upstairs and walking around, you will immediately notice how creaky the flooring is.  

The apartment itself is quite spacious for the price.  Those white cabinets look so nice when you are doing a quick tour, but upon further inspection you can easily see that they are old cabinets that have just been painted, i'm surprised mine are still hanging on the wall.  There is dust everywhere.  If you have any sort of allergy, look out.  No amount of vacuuming seems to remedy the allergies I have obtained since moving in.  Also be wary of the air conditioning units on the walls.  I do not know the last time mine was cleaned, but when I peered into the vents I was alarmed by the coating of black mold.  I recommend cleaning that ASAP.

All in all, if you love the location then maybe it is worth it to you.  But I am now convinced more than ever, that I will have to sacrifice either location or price in order to get a good night sleep, remain allergy free, and have at least some resemblance of a peaceful living situation.

Calhoun Greenway is a nice residence for someone looking to be in near Uptown and enjoy the fun of Lake Calhoun. The apartment buildings are a little old (40-50 yrs or so), and they show some wear tear, but the apartments have been renovated so everything still feels new. Management is receptive to maintenance issues, but slow to react. The rent here is a little cheaper than similar places in the Calhoun area, so all in all the pros definitely outweigh the few cons.

I found this apartment on apartments.com before traveling out to Minnesota.  The staff was very helpful and nice when I came for my tour and I immediately knew this was the place for me.  You cannot beat the amenities or prices you have at this complex nor can you beat the location with a mix of city and suburban lifestyles.  Great restaurants and shopping are literally across the street and uptown is a quick 3 minute drive.  At the same time the greenway is tucked away to give that nice quite suburban feel.  I highly recommend this complex!

I’ve been here for a few years and I love it! I’ve seen some negative reviews. There were a few bad tenants that are gone now. Also new management. Dalton is making some great changes. Fun people and location!!!

The apartments themselves are pretty nice, and amenities, when working, are good. However, the management company doesn't put a shred of effort into the property in any facet.

Just to list a few issues, the hottub has been down for over a year and is showing no signs of working soon, the gym has been out of wipes for months and now smells like a bacteria petri dish. There is garbage overflowing everywhere in the parking structures, grills dont work, and there are slurs all over the elevators. If you need to get in touch with management - too bad. It's not possible. Calling them yields a full mailbox, there is no email that can be reliably reached, and the front desk is often empty during working hours. 

I've been owed a referral bonus for 10 months and have asked multiple times just to be told they'll send it soon and I never receive it.

Overall, just a company that wants to do less than the bare minimum and try to hoard as much as they can

I lived here before the most recent management company took over and enjoyed the space. 

Living here 2022/2023 was not enjoyable. Multiple exterior doors/gates broken for months on end, leaving entry open to anyone. Requests to management go unanswered. 

I have since moved out, finally, and now management ignores my requests for my deposit back. 

Just know what you’re getting into.

We moved in Nov 2022.....the process was smooth and the office is very responsive here. Yes things break down here and there but that will be anywhere you go. They email as soon as anything happens and don't ignore problems. Maintenance is on point and get right to it! Walls are not thin here like I've read. Management does not play about people smoking or stealing or being loud since this is their home as well. I love Flux just wish it was in a different area. the area as a whole is a little to poppin for me!

Since I've moved in there has been multiple property managers and no communication between them. My move in day was a terrible experience. I've had to give my car info multiple times and been threatened to be towed when I pay for a spot. The package room is a hit or miss if it's working, loud neighbors thanks to thin walls, barley any response or care from the management group, elevator decides to stop working here and there, gym getting broken into and weights stolen and rude dog owners. I also do not feel safe once I leave my apartment. All of this is disappointing since I do love my actual apartment space and the maintenance staff.

Branded as a "luxury" apartment complex Flux does not meet that standard. The Units themselves are nice, I do like having a gas stove and the building is still new enough that the carpets and cabinets are not too worn. However, the amenities need updating. The gym is missing half of the dumbbells, the felt on the pool table is lean, and the delivery package room often doesn't work. But the main reason I can't recommend Flux is Simpson Property Management. Their staff are often negligent or unresponsive. For example, they originally scheduled me to move in on a Sunday, when the office is closed. I caught this and had it rescheduled to a Monday. Showed up in the morning, day off of work, family members to help me move, and no staff was working to give me the key or even open the door. I spent the entire day making calls and trying to get in touch with someone with no response. It was only in the evening, after a wasted day someone finally returned my call.

When I first moved here, I loved it. The location was convenient and decent. Now, it’s a cesspool of a constant stench of weed EVERYWHERE you go, even in your unit. People wait outside and piggyback when you’re leaving or coming in, and the floors stay sticky, Every weekend, someone manages to spill fast food by the elevators and who knows when it gets clean. It’s a shame that it’s a nice building, but it’s going downhill fast.

 I can’t wait until I move.

I lived here for many years.  Only moved because I got married and combined families so bigger space was needed.  It was a great experience.  I was unsure about apartment living after having a house for several years.  But the people who work there made me very comfortable.  I made many friends and it was an awesome location.  My kids loved it too.

I've lived at Lake Harriet Commons for many years and I love it.  The staff are super friendly and professional.  The maintenance guy always remembers a treat for my dog and the manager couple is awesome.  My apartment is cute and has so many closets.  I can walk to either lake and to so many great places to eat and shop.  There's a lot of green space and a parking lot that I appreciate in the winter.  Nothing not to love about living here!

I lived at Lake Harriet Commons for several years.  The apartments are very nice, clean, and tons of closet space.  You cannot beat the location, especially at that price, an easy walk to Lake Harriet and there are a few city parks within blocks of the apartment buildings.  The management was wonderful, they are friendly and took care of any problems that came up promptly.  If I ever move back to Minneapolis, I wouldn't live anywhere else!

This is the absolute worst management I have ever experienced. They gave completely false advertisement. The entire place was dirty upon moving in. Nothing was even dusted,there was paint still on the walls from the previous renter, and it smelt like wet dog. The closest smelt like cigarette smoke in a nonsmoking apartment. The pipes in the stove had holes in them which caused a dangerous gas leak in our apartment. Needless to say it was also completely dirty underneath the stove with caked grease. Our fridge was literally duck taped together on the inside and when they sent someone to fix it, the person came a week and a half after our complaint of it. The person who came to fix it came unannounced, did not leave a note, and it turned out to be the husband of someone who worked for management.. aka a random stranger they gave the keys to our apartment to. DO NOT LIVE HERE! Please take my advise.

If I could give zero stars I would. This place only continues to go downhill every year. Neighbors being loud all hours or the night blasting music, no security, no communication skills in the office. Used to be a fairly nice place to live but not in the past 2 years.

Management seemed to go out of its way NOT to respond to tenant concerns. The maintenance office never answered the phone, never returned voicemails. A water leak once went unaddressed for three days before anyone did anything. The office staff never answer the phone or return calls. They’re kind when you’re considering Uptown Lake, but lose any interest in you once you sign the lease. They leave work early, ignore problems, and fail to communicate when large issues in the building are afoot (including safety and health code issues). I often wonder if Cushman Wakefield uses ULA as a dumping ground for underperforming or incompetent staff.
Accessibility, friendly neighbors, staff, comfortable rooms
I love the location and the staff is very nice. There are three grocery stores near by so that’s great. A ton of rewards programs. Highly recommend.
So far it is nice no problems very easy to go to the store it’s down the street pharmacy as well plus restaurants very convenient for anyone

Just moved in and so far so good. Clean hallways and a clean gym! The heater/AC has been working well. Shawmen from the leasing office has been very communicative and very responsive when I have a problem or question.

City place lofts is incredibly clean, convenient and classy! Concrete floors, 13 ft ceilings and windows with great views of the Downtown skyline. Walking distance to anything you desire and you can hop on the light rail or bus and be anywhere else. Joe the manager is always friendly and you can usually find him tidying something up in the common areas. Now if I could just get them to validate my parking

I moved in here with my daughter less than a month ago and upon move-in we discovered that there was a problem with the fuse box for the air conditioner unit in my apartment. Zach, the go to maintenance guy here, had it taken care of within two days. There have been a couple other miscellaneous issues that needed to be addressed and both of them were taken care of literally the same day. So far I’m very happy with the customer service here as well as the location. My daughter is thriving and I am very satisfied with the decision to move here!

I have lived here for a year and the price is good compared to the other apartments if you are wanting to live here for location - walkable to bars, restraints, target, cub. If the nightlife isn’t your main attraction then live somewhere else - overpriced for no amenities (“workout” place is a joke) and parking, as well as loud neighbors and creaky floors if not carpeted. Management is a little bit of a curve ball but they always eventually respond and good about resolving issues.

Good luck getting ahold of anyone at this place. I cannot wait until my lease it up and regret renewing it. I have lived here 1.5 years, first year was great, but it has gone way down hill. Trash EVERYWHERE. You many not be able to get in the front door but all other doors are broken and wide open for everyone to get into. Glass is broken on the doors. Kids running around all the tine, music blaring at 2AM, yippy dogs barking all night. No one cares about their neighbors and management doesn’t care either. The phone number doesn’t go directly to the ‘on-site’ team, and there is no email, not like anyone is ever here anyways. Place is a joke.

In addition to the laundry list of issues in previous reviews (most of which I've already experienced in my first two months), you are completely on your own when something goes wrong.

I'm currently writing this review in a completely dark apartment as my power just went completely out. The circuit breaker is unresponsive. I called the mgmt office who "took a message" about me being completely out of power , with no ETA or steps for resolution. Who knows how long it will take but this is about as bad as you can possibly get for emergency maintenance or maintenance response.

For the money, you can get a decent looking apartment, but literally everything else is there to remind you that you live in a poor managed dump.  I'm the type of person who can look beyond that, as I stay home almost 24/7 -- until anything goes wrong and you're left in the dark, literally.

Stay away.

To be honest, when I moved in there were absolutely no reviews for this place, so as I prepare to move out I want to ensure there is a review for future tenants. First, I personally have not seen the pest issues, but that is terrifying as reading below. It's also not surprising. The building and the grounds are kept in awful condition. There is no management on site and so nothing is taken care of in any sort of timely manner. Garbage is left literally all over the grounds and is never removed. There are "amenities" such as a gym that is not in working order and an elevator that has not worked since I moved in. Residents allow their children to play in the halls as if it is their own personal playroom. I have complained numerous times and nothing has been done. Management does not call you back. I was never contacted about renewing my lease, now as I'm moving out I can't get a hold of anyone to schedule a time to give my keys back. God only knows if I'll actually get my deposit back. The apartments have no sound proofing. They are renovating apartments, which is what sold me, but they are not worth it. I recommend avoiding this place at all costs.

Beware of the low rent prices. This apartment has so many issues including management not answering or responding to calls or maintenance requests, not keeping up with the grounds, not fixing amenities that were advertised, dogs that constantly bark, police are constantly here, super loud neighbors, violence, no parking, pests, and just all around terrible living conditions. We are counting down the days until we can move.

If you would like to live in a building where the management company is slow to respond on maintenance issues, does not reinforce rules of the complex for select tenants, has a roach infestation that they clearly cannot get control of and falsely advertises amenities that are not available & never intend to fix making them available then this is the apartment for you!

No parking for guests only. It is taken by residents who do not get permits for their vehicles & New Hope tickets anyone on the street from 2am-6am. 
Elevator hasn't been operating for more than 18 months.
building entry doors that don't lock leaving the building exposed to anyone who wants to enter.
None of the equipment in fitness center works that needs power.
Rental rates are increasing. I don't know why. They haven't improved conditions.

Feel free to take the risk. I’ve noticed they’ve raised rent on units online but haven’t done anything to improve conditions other than make the units look pretty. Beware of the shiny surface here. Under it are layers of grime you do not want to deal with.

Heat, AC doesn't work. Cockroaches, mice and pest problem. Homeless found sleeping in public spaces often with no security. Amenities constantly not working and mismanaged priorities of management. 
Posting this 10/17/2023. I promise that the negative reviews are not being fixed and they are telling the truth. Please be wary of fake reviews that management has posted.
Pictures are inaccurate. It is not that nice. The property management is bad and has horrible response time and your maintenance request rarely gets done. Good luck!!!!

First off , the pictures of the apartment’s that they offer on here do not look like that in person! The management does not fix anything, the hot water is always having issues the utility bill is always high, the elevators always have issues, the pool has been closed for months, the laundry room looks like the ceiling could cave in any minute, homeless people are always roaming the halls and this “Onsite Security” is here maybe once every two weeks! Not safe for your car either the parking garage is a high theft zone . The rent is also not worth your buck.

DON'T MOVE IN BOLERO IF YOU LOVE YOUR HARD EARNED MONEY - 
1- High Utility bill, They have changed our Lease without any prior notice as per lease it should be Flat rate. Earlier total bill used to be below $100 and now its more than $300+ every month , including Electricity and Internet it will go $500+
2- Trash charges are $50+, which is more higher than other apartments whereas most trash chute doors and handles are broken.
2- Onsite management doesn't care about residents, Not ready to hear us.
3- Be ready to wait for weeks , if you have raised any maintenance complaint.
4- Room window is having leakage, Raised complaint multiple times in past 2 years but no one is here to hear us.
5- Today I saw attached letter at my door, So I came to know HIGH UTILITY BILL issue is bothering entire apartment residents.

They need to update their information on apartments.com because pool is not 24/7, hours are 10 am-10pm and their is not washer dryer in any units. They apparently took them out so residents wouldn’t have to wait on delayed parts. I would rather have one in unit and wait for a part then have to use the 90° laundry room. Some of these things are what I want in a apartment and wasted my time touring.

The new management is terrible. I have lived her 4 years and they do nothing. You never know when someone will be in, they won’t see tenants (expect you to make an appointment a week out because they don’t want to deal with anything), won’t answer emails, don’t respond to maintenance, and then threaten to make you pay for it when it was there negligence on upkeep and failure to complete a 3 week old maintenance request l that mentions water leaking. If you want the headache and stress and being buckled and dimed then move in. I fully expect they probably find every excuse to keep security deposits upon move out.

Great building, location, community and communication. Could not speak more highly of my time at Wakpada. Van was especially great and attentive on the rare occasion I needed to speak with a property manager. 10/10 all the way around.

Anthony made it easy for me from start to finish. He was prompt and professional. He thoroughly answered questions I inquired about and provided me with detailed information about the area. I am excited about moving to my new apartment.

Can’t wait to move in! Anthony was very knowledgeable and made the leasing process a breeze! At no point did I feel pressured or rushed. Everything was upfront, even saw a few apartment floor plans. So I know I made the right choice. Can’t wait for my first BBQ on the rooftop patio!
The entire application process was quick and painless. Anthony was attentive, responsive, and made sure all my questions were answered.

Anthony was great! Was very quick with responses, and made the whole process a breeze for my girlfriend and I. I had reached out to another property to schedule a showing, and before they got back to me, Anthony has answered all of my questions, gotten us approved, and gotten a lease signed. I still haven't heard back from that other company. Definitely looking forward to living at Wakpada. Will update with my experience living there!

Confirmed a date and time to tour their available apartments but got stood up. Waited in the cold for 10 minutes buzzing, calling, and emailing, but clearly they didn’t bother to show up to their job.

They don’t respond, I called them several time during there said working hours it goes straight to voicemail, I scheduled a showing to see if they’d respond, I sent them 4 emails and they do a security deposit that is supposed to be refundable if you cancel within 3 days but the issue is they don’t respond to anything. I promise you this isn’t worth your time and I’m still waiting for my money

Tenants smoking, ceiling has collapsed twice since i’ve lived here in less than 2 months.  Maintenance does not respond to water pouring from the ceiling.  Trash buildup for over a month.  Very poor experience!
I moved in a couple months ago and things have gone so smooth! Management has been great at responding and addressing the very few issues I’ve had. Love it here already!!

Fees, Fees, Fees and more fees. I paid more in hidden fees to KMS than I do for my Verizon and Wells Fargo bills (Lets not forget Wells Fargo is the company that was creating fake accounts just to charge more fees). Also, management lacks the ability to communicate why they are charging these fees.

To put it simply, upper-management is terrible. Before signing my lease, as I was previewing my room, I quickly noticed a considerably unpleasant smell. I was told not to worry about the smell, it was probably just the glue from the new flooring. I figured the smell would go away, needless to say it never did (the smell was so bad my 5-year old nephew held his nose when he came to visit). I asked management to investigate further into the smell, nothing came of it. I asked to move rooms, they just ignored my request. Over time, I pinpointed where the smell was coming from, the gas stove, leading me to believe the smell was gas. I even tested my theory that the foul smell in my room was gas from the stove. I barely turned the gas on (didn't ignite it) and smelled near the burner. Sure enough, nearly identical smells… Recommendation: don't rent any rooms that smell like gas, and cross your fingers the apartment complex doesn't blow up. 

It doesn't get any better. My lease ended October 31st. In mid-September, I switched my lease to month-to-month, as I was uncertain where I would be working. At the time, I had my rent paid through October 31st. On October 9th, I received a note on my door saying, If I didn't pay rent by the following day they would take me to court and possibly evict me… Unbeknownst to me, they reallocated my October payment to the following month. I never received any notice, nor is there any indication in the lease agreement of any such reallocation policy. I asked for an explanation, they just told me I had to pay it or else.… Also, if you switch to a month-to-month lease during the winter, if they don't find a new renter when you leave, you lose your deposit (to their credit that policy is in their rental agreement).

After having moved out nearly a month ago, I am still being charge for the utilities and have yet to receive any of my mail. Management told me they would take care of the utilities and the forwarding address…. Still waiting.

Also, on multiple occasions, someone tried to break into my apartment. Always keep your door locked.

Please take caution in renting from KMS Loring Park.  I reside on the 3rd floor of the building (36 Spruce Place) and there are cockroaches --- there have been attempts to solve the problem but it continues to exist.   The property management team has created a false narrative around treating my apartment which has caused the problem to worsen.  There is also a lack of communication from the rental office in general.  If you are looking for a positive downtown living experience, please look elsewhere.

I moved into the apartments because the location was great and the rent was very reasonable.  It wasn't until the second year at the apartments that I started to notice the negatives about this apartment.  The apartments increases rent every year to a point where I could move to nicer apartment for the same price.  Which is what I did.  If you're looking for a cheap apartment close to downtown and don't care about amenities then this is a great start.

I have lived here for a year and just renewed my lease.  The building and staff are fantastic.  Great amenities (including pool), extremely responsive on maintenance issues, and great location.  I love living here and would recommend it.

Living at Central Park West has been a great experience! The staff is friendly and always willing to help. The amenity spaces are great and the building is well maintained. When I place a work order, our maintenance supervisor Jon completes it quickly and proficiently. The resident VIP program has been a great perk to have. It allows residents to get discounts at Crave, The Loop, and even the Reveal rooftop bar at the AC Marriott Hotel. The golf simulator is an amazing feature of the community that I did not see anywhere else while touring the area. I love the Central Park West app that allows me to create service requests, communicate with the office staff members, post on the community board, and even reserve rent-able spaces. The two bedroom guest suite is a great perk especially having family coming into town to visit. It is well furnished and I get to have my guests close by without having to sacrifice my own space.

I recently moved into the apartment complex and the whole process was very smooth. The on staff was very accommodating to my requests for modifications to the walk in closet shelves and even assisted me with removing garbage from my apartment during my move in. 
Joe and Kathryn who work at the front desk are really nice and courteous. 
Both of them have fulfilled our requests that ranged from moving our parking stalls  to one that had a bike rack to removing heavy garbage from our apartment unit.

There are various amenities that I have taken advantage of which ranged from printers, conference room for my meetings, free wifi to get me by until I had my own internet set up. 

It has been a wonderful experience so far thanks to the wonderful staff who have been very responsive, friendly and a pleasure to know.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review:
I have been living here since last August.
It's very user-friendly and safe neighborhood.
The facility manager and staff are always helpful and professional.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review: We have lived here a little over a year and truly feel at home. The staff know us by name and always ask us how we are. Maintenance comes within hours of putting in the request and the amenities make it feel like we live at a resort, especially with the pool.  It’s close to shops and very accessible from anywhere. We love it here.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review: I loved living at the landings at the beginning but new management has taken over and they are the absolute worst. Lisa and the front desk staff are very unprofessional, incredibly unhelpful, rude, unfriendly, and they lose important information you give them.  The staff is the reason why I left.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review:
The staff is pretty helpful, and the maintenance is very quick.  I've called at 8pm with emergency situations are they are there within half an hour.  The apartments are incredibly quiet, which was something that worried me.  Dogs are allowed in the building though, so I do hear some barking occasionally.

I currently rent the 1A style apartment, and I really love it.  However, rent is increasing by $75 if I resign my lease, and I'm not sure if I want to do that.  Just an FYI, they often list the 1-bedroom apartments at $1100 - $1300, but that is not true.  If I choose to resign my lease I will be paying $1320/mo.  Also, none of the utilities are covered.  That is something worth thinking about.  In my 808 sq foot apartment I pay between $100 - $200 a month depending on the season.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review: I'm enjoying the wonderful amenities: heated outdoor pool and hot tub, fitness center with well-maintained equipment, sauna, movie screening room, clubhouse with kitchen, bar, pool table, and pinball, heated underground parking, great security,  plus many others.  What I enjoy even more are the people who live here.  It really is a community, where others hold the door for you and even hold the elevator if they see you are coming.  The building management encourages us to get to know our neighbors  with once a month 'wet your whistle Wednesday' where we have a wine/beer happy hour.  They throw a pool party each summer for families in the building as well as a Halloween costume party. I also appreciate the quick response to maintenance requests. Pets are also welcomed here. I've been here for about 2 years, and I will most likely stay a while longer.

apartmentName: The Landings at Silver Lake Village
review: Beautiful views convenient to shopping and staff that is always looking for ways to make our home a better place to live.  Have been here for 3 years and can't think of a better place to call home.

This property is absolutely stunning! There are so many amenities from free underground parking to a free coffee bar. the staff are excellent. They're always on top of everything and you can tell they really care about the property and take pride in it. They just opened July 2021 so the units are brand new and never lived in! If you want to live in a place where you can get upscale AND friendly then I recommend PSF.

I just moved in this month, and I love it here so far. The staffs at Parker Station Flats are so pleasant. Aja and Anton made me feel so welcomed and were very patient with me during the whole application of approval phase. This is truly an awesome management team. This complex have some amazing amenities that I love so so much. I feel so safe and at home here already. Keep up the good work guys :)
The apartments are new, very nice and the staff was very friendly. They helped us through the process and I would recommend PSF

Don’t waste your money on this apartment. This is the worst money am spending in my life right now. As a first experience renting on my own I’m glad it was a bad one. That’s the only good thing out of this apartment. 

The management here is terrible and neighbors a very disrespectful of other peoples space. Noisy neighbors; apartment walls are so thin that it feels like monsters at living above you and around you. Management would not address concerns of tenants. You have no control over heating and air conditioning at this building. During summer, you’re so screwed if you don’t have a fan… during winter you’re in for a deadly surprise. Weed smokers everywhere even though apartment says smoke free. Laundry machine still uses coin and oh your clothes will not get washed so don’t bother using it. 

Don’t waste your money I promise you your life is better somewhere else. I’m stuck here for the next 4months after this I will make sure no one with respect for their hard earned income ever stay at this dungeon. Or any other apartments managed by Sela Investments.

Love my new home!  Brand new everything.  Lot of cupboards and storage places, great common areas inside and out, beautiful neighborhood.  Maintenance walked me through on how to use/maintain everything such as air cond, wsh/dryer, disposal, outlets with breakers, just about everything. Dog friendly with beautiful walking neighborhoods.  Even has "doggy stations" on several street corners around the building.  Friendly helpful staff.

I’ve been here for over 3 years now and have been relatively satisfied! Great area and close to pretty much everything. The units are clean and remodeled to give nice modern look! The only issue I have is that you’re not supposed to have pets. Yet, I’d say roughly 50% of the other renters have pets. Definitely would love to have an pet of some sort and wish management would consider making it pet friendly! The amount of prospective renters would probably increase quite a bit!

Advice to management: become a pet friendly complex! You can charge a pet deposit and do monthly pet rent!

If you read a negative review about Greenway village apartments (like I did last year when I was searching) it is 100% only because of the old property manager. She never got back to people, was not on top of her job AT all, and was always chatting with a staff member in her office. About 2ish months ago she was replaced. The new property manager is wonderful, helpful, and want to make sure residence feel cared for This apartment has been everything I wanted and more. It has about a year now since I moved in and it’s been great. When searching for an apartment a concern for me was having thick walls where I can’t hear my neighbors, as this has been a problem in my past apartments. I have never heard a neighbor and majority of the time not even hear my roommate when our doors are closed. It’s amazing. Additionally if you need maintenance, you just submit it on the online portal and someone will come the next day. I know some apartments charge to fix things, but I have never been charged. My boyfriend pays $150 a month to pay for parking at his apartment and it is FREE here. Water and gas are also included in rent, which is on the lower end for other apartments around the cities. Love being so close to the city (12 minutes to downtown) while still having woods, a yard, and trails in the back. Wonderful. Won’t be moving anytime soon.

The management here has been recently replaced and the new management is great! The management has demonstrated excellent communication for its residents. The apartments are cozy, modern, and generally quiet. There is no covered parking. The location is exceptionally convenient, the stairwells are always kept clean, the fitness center is clean and has the basic equipment. The maintenance is helpful and punctual, they replace your air filters every few months. There is one main building, which is older, and several detached newer buildings on the property. The older building has elevators, but the new buildings do not. The appliances are all high-end and the wooden paneling on the buildings has been recently restained, they look nice. The apartments are warm and I love the large windows in the newer buildings! The complex is also right next to a bus stop, very convenient for students to commute to the University, which is also nearby. Overall, wonderful place to live.

Like many other long-term residents, I recently moved out of the Vue because of ongoing maintenance, management, and security issues. 

The Vue is 10 years old and it shows. Unit interiors are dark and dated. Appliances in most units are a decade old. The common areas aren't any better. The gym is barebones - think 1 elliptical, 1 bike, 2 treadmills, and some weights. The rooftop is small with grills that need to be replaced and a broken fire pit. The parking lot is filthy and next to dumpsters that overflow. The carpet throughout the building is stained and the trash chutes in the hallways make every floor smell, especially by the elevator banks.  

The neighborhood has gone downhill - period. Despite this, management has not meaningfully invested in security. Packages are stolen because there is no package room and management allows deliveries to accumulate in the lobby. Bikes are stolen from the garage and cars are broken into. "Piggy-backing" occurs at the front entrance. 

Simple maintenance requests take 1-2+ weeks to fulfill. Getting action from the after-hours maintenance emergency staff usually required multiple follow up calls over hours to the call center. Last winter, a significant portion of the building experienced issues with hot water; this summer residents are going without AC. Residents are denied compensation in the form of rent or parking credits for these ongoing disruptions. Building management is inexperienced and understaffed, with only one Community Director serving 100+ units. Calls to the front desk go to voicemail, sometimes immediately. 

Despite these deficiencies in value, safety, and community, the Vue bills itself as luxury living and consistently hikes rent by hundreds of dollars per month when residents renew leases. For what the Vue charges, your money can go much further in a newer, nicer building that prioritizes residents' comfort and takes safety seriously.

DO NOT LIVE HERE!
3 months ago I met with the director of housing to let them know I would not be renewing my lease. They assured me that they had made note and that we were good to go on our end. Now they are pretending like our conversation never happened, in attempt to charge us more money. Management will lie to you and manipulate you.
The management team is very unprofessional and have been known to misguide tenants.

I moved to Minneapolis four years ago and lived in several places. I have to say that view was by far the best. They have so many awards for customer service on the reception desk and I must say they are well deserved. 

From my first tour from Rick, the wonderful maintenance man, Norm, that always took time to have a chat, to the awesome community events thrown by Josh and Sam, I have been unceasingly impressed by passion this team has for giving there residence a place to call home. Everyone is willing to drop everything to help the residents. 

This property is beautiful and in a beautiful nook of Minneapolis. Great park for my dog, beautiful sunsets from the roof and a awesome place to host parties and events. This is the best place to live in MN.

I have lived at the Vue for over a year now, and I'm so glad I made the decision to move here. The location has great access to both downtown and the freeway, the shared spaces are clean and well-maintained, the staff is friendly and hard-working, and my experiences with the maintenance team have been stress-free! Management is super good at communicating with all the tenants in the building, and I always feel very safe and content when I am home. Honestly, I couldn't ask for more!
VUE is in the perfect location with great, quality apartment homes, welcoming and friendly office team! I love living here!

Honestly, for this price, you'd have a hard time finding a place as nice in this area. You can pay an arm and a leg for the luxury apartments on the block, but seeing as all of those luxury amenities have been shut down for social distancing, you're really just paying twice the price for exactly what you'd get at 333 Oak Grove St. Garage parking is also cheaper, than the luxury apartments, and comes with the same amenities - secure access and a parking stall, with tons of cameras to protect your vehicle. Inside is pretty nice, too, compared to all the other affordable living options in Minneapolis. The walls are almost soundproof, so you barely ever hear neighbors. Whenever there's any type of issue, management contacts you about it, so you can rest assured it'll be taken care of. And, on top of that, everything you'd ever need is within walking g distance. It's a half block from Loring Park, and a short walk from the local college. There are shopping centers, govt resources, banking, and grocery stores just a short walk away. And, on top of that, it's also a short walk from the art center and sculpture gardens, and there are walking trails everywhere. It's seriously a great place.

Great apartment, and new on-site management (since early 2018) has made this place a LOT better, so take that into consideration if you're reading older reviews. The apartment itself was phenomenal and everything worked well, and when it didn't maintenance staff was extremely prompt in fixing any issues. There are great common spaces (deck, gym, party room) which are barely used - it's a building with ~200 residents and I was often able to host parties on the common deck without anyone around, it was great! Really enjoyed my two years here, only left because I bought a home in the area.

I have recently moved into my apartment, and I have loved it ever since. The Leasing Agent is very personable and knows most of the residents by name, the Building Manager is very open about making sure my experience is going well, and the Maintenance worker is kind and respectful. 

A few tidbits that have stood out to me:
1. The Leasing and Management team was willing to help me with paperwork, set up utilities, and was upfront about all of the costs for living here.
2. Within 2 weeks of moving in, we had a new backsplash installed by the Management, free of charge. It is a beautiful White Subway tile.
3. The building is very Pet-Friendly, and I enjoy seeing all of the dogs walking around.

I absolutely love everything about living in Red 20. I moved in a couple months ago and have zero complaints. Our apartment was clean and flawless when we moved in and we have plenty of space in a two bedroom. My roommate and I utilize the community spaces quite a bit which are beautiful; both to play pool and for Bachelor Monday's. The residents here are very nice and respectful. I absolutely love the amount of dogs in the building, I get my puppy love every time I enter the elevator. The new community manager, Shane, is very welcoming, organized, and friendly. The neighborhood itself has tons to do and explore; good entertainment and great restaurants.

Red 20 is a great new building in Northeast Minneapolis. I live with my girllfriend and 2 dogs and we have plenty of space in a 1 bedroom. The amenities are beautiful and top of the line. The staff is very responsive and truly care about getting to know the residents.  Everything you need is walking distance as well; grocery, liquor store, and great bar and restaurants.

Red 20 is in a great location - surrounded by a diverse group of restaurants (casual, fancy, quick, unique, etc.) and easy to get around (close to public transportation plus easy parking).  There are many building amenities and there is a true sense of community with the neighbors!

I have absolutely loved living at Arcata, it truly feels like home. Our maintenance guy Nelson is amazing and always on top of it. As soon as I put in a maintenance request, he knocks on my door with the biggest smile!! He’s fast and efficient!

Arcata apartment has been my amazing home for the past three years. The staff in particular is what makes the building a home! The leasing staff and maintenance man, Nelson, are all so incredibly accommodating and kind!
Hello everyone! I’ve lived here for 7 years and I love it. It’s a good quiet with great service. Maintenance staff Nelson is the best and always so nice!

Great place to live with lots of amenities.
The staff has been very nice.
Highly recommended for people looking for apartment in the area!
Arcata is an excellent apartment community! The employees take the time to truly care about their residents and the property. We love Arcata Apartments!

Just moved in and accidentally dropped my keys down the garbage shoot along with my garbage, like an idiot!! However, I called our on call maintenance and Matt showed up within the half hour and that poor guy dug through the ENTIRE garbage for me to find my key at the bottom of the compact garbage bin, in another bag!!! Matt and his partner did not give up looking and when he knocked on my door with my key, I wanted to hug him!!!! The apartment is great too but as far as service goes, I am so pleased to have staff who would do just about ANYTHING for their residents!!

I have lived here 6 months and really enjoy the excellent management (Jim, Ashley, Ike, and Julia), the upscale facility, great neighbors, and Central location.  The staff were very supportive when I moved here and work to keep the place clean and up to date. They also strive to make it a community and hold monthly events so you can meet your neighbors. They had a 5 year anniversary party that was catered, had enjoyable live music and was well attended. The people, facility, amenities and location all make for an exceptional Big City Lifestyle!

The location is absolutely perfect. 5 min to downtown, yet still able to quickly get out of the city if you are wanting a weekend away. Small, but nice looking apartments. All of the office staff is nice but one of them, Ashley is absolutely incredible, I have never seen a office person vacuuming hallways before, but it shows that they really care about how the place is presented on a day to day basis vs just waiting until the next cleaning crew arrives. Love it here!

I live here for a while and I'm pretty happy with the location and amenities. It is very close to West End and easy commute to downtown. The community room is very nice and you can brew yourself a nice coffee.
I gave 4 stars because there are few points where they could improve.
1. I'll start with my personal pet-peeve- the elevators. They never take down the ugly blue protective padding. I understand the purpose of it during moving in-out, but it is always there, regardless if anyone is moving furniture. I believe that if you put 'luxury' in your name then you should live up to it, and this one is simply not caring in my book and could be easily corrected.

2. Cleaningness - the lobby is always clean but the hallways and elevator areas can be pretty dirty. I can see same trash laying around for couple days before someone vacumes it.

3. The gym- is really nice and a great perk the only downside is equipment is not repaired often e.g. treadmill not working for nearly a month.

I don't know how there are such negative reviews here. The living space, the amenities, and the staff at Arcata are excellent. Emilie is the sweetest. We love it here, the location is perfect, and we have zero complaints.

I would not rent here again. After looking at several apartments I found Arcata to have a great location and amenities but have some serious issues. For instance, I got an email about a month ago saying that there was a homeless person seen walking around our building several times. Now that in itself is not a huge concern, but what if he was dangerous and wasn't just staying warm (stealing, damaging the building, looking for unlocked cars, etc.) So how does he get into a building that costs a lot of money to live in? Easy, the door by the pool is unlocked and ready for anyone to walk into the building from the outside with no key. They say it is a "fire code". For this much money, you can't even be guaranteed your safety. Find a new building to look at. I promise you will be happier and safer.

Go to the Flats at West End. Their are plenty of other apartments that will treat you far better and provide far better customer service than the Arcata. I was lied to, mistreated, & disrespected... and this is suppose to be a luxury apartment. HARDLY! All management can say is "sorry" when they mess up. It's never their fault. No accountability for their mistakes as they continue to make residents past and present pay...I was asked to move out early which worked out perfect in my schedule and then just kidding... that didn't work for them and was charged the entire month. I was told nothing in my apartment was wrong at the walk through and then just kidding, they decided to take the entire deposit plus more. These are just 2 of the many examples I could list when it is just disappointing the Arcata deems itself Luxury living. I know luxury living and it is not here!

Arcata is a new complex, which means everything is beautiful and well-done, but the leasing staff is not very seasoned. Arcata has a heated two-level garage directly underneath the complex. The pool area is very nice, and the units are well-designed and modern. The gym is adequate but much smaller than comparable complexes in the area. The only downside that I have experienced is that the leasing staff have trouble keeping track of e-mails and answering inquiries. They do not seem to communicate among themselves. They seem to be very nice people, but they don't have their act together yet. So far, I'm fairly dissatisfied. There are many other nice complexes in the area, and the rent is quite high considering the relative lack of customer service in the leasing office.

Brand new building which is nice! But also comes with its quirks, random firealarms, gates and stuff not working, waiting for little things to get installed.

Community here is GREAT. Kitchen is awesome. Tad pricey but I think no matter where you live you'd like it cheaper haha

I have never lived somewhere I felt as safe, happy, and Bougie as I do in this apartment. Ideal for young professionals, this building has excellent security, responsive management and maintenance, and the LOCATION! Right near Nicollet Mall and the downtown Target would be a big upside on its own, but during the week, this building is also directly connected to the Skyway system! The ability to access that entire network without ever having to go outside is an INCREDIBLE boon during our tundra-esque winters. Not to mention assigned garage parking in the heart of downtown, again a huge plus during snowy times. The apartments themselves are gorgeous, the amenities nice (though the driers are weird), and the views outstanding. I have never lived anywhere better.

Property management is amazing. Staff are some of the friendliest people I've met. 

I lived there for three years, apartment was in great condition. Had only one maintenance request in the three years I had been there - they take really good care of the building and units. 

I looked at a lot of places downtown - you can't beat the metro.

We moved in a few months ago and have had the best experience living here. The apartments are high quality and have been well taken care of. It is extremely quiet and we never hear our neighbors or the noises of downtown. The location and helpful staff can’t be beat! The only downside to the building is that small dogs are not allowed, that’s the only thing that might keep us from renewing our lease for another year. If the pet policy changed, we would renew in a heartbeat because everything else is perfect. Great place overall!

The Metro Apartments are fantastic. You can live and work downtown while still having access to a quiet home at night. The staff here are so kind, responsive, and helpful. I did a lot of research before leasing my studio and honestly this place is so great compared to other units in the community. The units here are affordable and super well-maintained too. There is a small gym and a beautiful terrace to enjoy in the summertime. The attached parking garage is also great. Everyone who lives here is friendly and professional. I have not had one issue while living here for one year. I would definitely recommend this place and it makes sense now why people stay here for a long time.

My wife and I moved to Minneapolis and spent our first year in the area living in the Metro Apartments.  We were very pleased with the quality and condition of our apartment when we moved in (recently updated so it felt like it was brand new) and had an overall great experience with the building management.  In the year we spent there we never had any urgent maintenance needs.  On the occasions that we had minor needs management was always available and very responsive to our needs.  We also greatly appreciated the location of the apartment and it's direct connection to the Minneapolis Skyway, which is ideal for anyone who works downtown (especially in winter).

The location is quite good. Being skyway connected makes a huge difference. Management is very responsive and friendly. Common areas are kept clean, and the building seems quite safe. Noise is minimal from above and below, but the walls, on the other hand, are rather thin and noise travels easily between apartments.

Hiawatha Flats is a newer complex. We have lived here for several years and couldn't be any happier! Each unit has their own washer and dryer! The utilities are extremely low because of excellent insulation and newer central heat and air. Each unit has their own HVAC! Hiawatha Flats has wonderful amenities! (Swimming pool, sauna, exercise room, and more!) The location is absolutely outstanding! You will love it! The garage is safe and secure! Most importantly, Hiawatha Flats has outstanding management and staff! If you have maintenance needs, action will be taken ASAP! If you have larger packages that might come in, they will be signed for when you are gone. We have never lived in an apartment setting with better management than this! You will love Hiawatha Flats, Minneapolis!

We have lived here for 3 years and have had enough.  When we first moved in, things were great. Now 3 years later things have really gone downhill.  You will wait days for emails to be returned, you will find the office randomly closing early, the PM will lie straight to your face when you have in writing what she has previously said (many residence we have talked to say the same thing, she is a compulsive liar) maintenance will say they have fixed something, then find out it was not fixed.  We have had issues with cracked walls, only to be painted over and re-cracked.  The painter to come "fix them" and not repaint, so you will have white splotches on the walls for days, or weeks in our case waiting for them to come back and fix them.  You will be notified the day of that someone is coming to fix something.  We have had bug issues for the pasts 6 months and when they come to check they say "oh we didn't see any so we didn't do anything" (even though we had pictures) zero preventative pest control in units.  This apartments.com ad states "modern luxury apartments".  No.  The counter tops are old laminate with scratches and are peeling and it has old carpet.  It also says "brand new stainless appliances"...they have been the same ones since we moved in 3 years ago, how is that "brand new"? "Resort style indoor pool"?  It's the smallest indoor pool I've ever seen in an apartment building and is ice cold.  They "fix" it randomly and its warm for about 3 days then goes right back to ice cold.  They raised garage parking by $10 for some reason, we are not getting anything else in the garage so I'm not sure why they upped the price and I, and other residence, are pretty sure they are no longer heating the garage as it's always cold.  Rent keeps going up and the quality keeps going down, with the building and the staff.   We have moved into a brand new building with more amenities, quartz counters, hard wood floors, stunning, for the same price, and it's not very far from this location.   Look elsewhere!

Hiawatha Flats is the best place I have ever lived. The property is beautiful, rent is reasonable, and the property manager cares so much. Even the hallways and pool area are cleaned on a daily basis. 

For the Longfellow neighborhood, there isn't a better value. I am steps away from public transit, delicious restaurants, beautiful parks, and sparkling lakes.

If you are looking for a place to live long term in the twin cities, this is definitely the place for you.

These apartments are fairly new, with great interior appeal.  The buildings have multiple community rooms, including a movie theater, fitness centers, game room, and indoor pool.  Staff is exceptionally friendly and goes out of their way to make your life easier, from posting the weekly weather in the elevators to dropping off packages and watering your plants. Just a block from the metro, it's a perfect place for the working class.  The neighborhood is quiet and close to the beautiful trails of Minnehaha Falls.  Overall, I love everything about it!

Has an easy in and out bike room, great location. soothing interriors

Very quite, well run, they could add more outdoor seating in grilling area

The location cannot be beat. It's practically between the Lake of the Isles and the Bde Maka Ska. There is green space on most sides. It's situated next to the midtown greenway and 'The Mall' park, which hosts a regular Farmers Market. Walking distance of two grocery stores and several restaurants and bars. Its kept warm during the winter and the view is great. The floor plans are well sized and the management is very personable.

Where to begin? 
Personable, amazing office folks who will help with literally anything, great gatherings with residents, nice views, care taker can do pet sitting whenever you need, and convenient for every type of food from Barbette to Brim to Stellas Fish Cafe. 

This building will always hold a special place in our hearts. Sidenote: it's much more social at a lower price point than "luxury buildings" up the street. So if you're budget conscious like we were, this place is tremendous value.

Thanks for making Uptown so special and no doubt new residents will love it too! Cheers, Greg and Christa
So bad !!! Scheduled an appointment to go check it out and I was there on time and called nobody answered ...

I lived here a couple of years ago, the place was infested with bed bugs. I had to throw out everything I owned. 

From what I hear, that hasn't changed.

I lived here a couple of years ago and this place is infested with bed bugs. Management was incredibly shady about the whole thing. I came to find out they had major issues for years. After moving out, I saw the same exterminator there almost every week. It was a disaster. I had to throw out everything I owned. Ask yourself, this building has been here for 30-40 years and there are 5 reviews? This place is infested. You’ve been warned.

Pros: good location/rooftop view, management is quick to respond to requests, the people are friendly and will give you a tour when management forgets your scheduled time

Cons: the kitchen water in certain units can take 10 minutes to get hot, certain units don’t have outlets in the bathroom, the internet port is in the bedroom closet so if a device requires a Ethernet connection you’ll need an extra long cable

The management does not make the smartest decision. The 24/7 gym and lounge are now unavailable at night with a time limit. There's never communication between the management and the residents besides that one meeting which led to nothing. Residents get their lease terminated with no logical reason but a vague statement on the letter. Do not recommend.

East End Apartments has been a horrible apartment complex to live at.
