They bill themselves as a luxurious community yet they lack amenities most other downtown apartments have, including no hot tub, no sauna, a small fitness center and no rooftop club room. The staff has been a mess, the current manager Hayden is rude and unhelpful, when it comes to lease agreements on concessions they are not fulfilled until a complaint is logged, there have been huge issues with security including a unit that was burglarized in the middle of the day, homeless sleeping inside lobby doors and a massive issue with parking. If you park your car in the lot beware that you may not be able to get it back out, there are constant breakdowns with the gate access and huge backups due to these issues that don't seem to be getting fixed. The supposed concierge is nonexistent, in the last few months the desk has been empty roughly 90% of the time a concierge staff member is supposed to be present and when they are present they are rude and don't have any desire to communicate to the residents. Currently East End is also renting out 15 apartments in an Airbnb style so there is a constant flow of people who trash the complex and create huge amounts of noise, nothing is being done to handle this issue. In my opinion it has been the worst apartment I have ever lived in, any other complex in the area would be a much better choice. I will avoid Sherman Associates properties if possible since they manage this property.

The location of this apartment is what immediately drew us in to renting and we couldn’t wait to get moved in. Upon moving in the blinds were not even put up and were on the floor in the living room, and patches of the wall that had clearly just been repaired had not been repainted yet. At this point we were so excited to move in that we just accepted it and sent in a service request that was responded to fairly quickly. 

It went downhill fairly quickly from here. We have had cockroaches to the point of having our apartment fumigated, water leaks that required tearing up carpet, constant issues with the elevators (multiple people have also been stuck in elevators for extended time periods), and having to deal with 1 laundry room for 30+ floors of tenants. 

This is touted as a “luxury” apartment but it certainly is not that. And do not fall for the free parking gimmick. There is a very small surface lot that they market as free parking but it is constantly full and you’ll be stuck either paying for street parking, waiting long periods of time for a spot, or paying for a garage parking spot. 

With all that said, the maintenance team has always been awesome but they clearly have their hands full.

Moving from TN to MN, Churchill apartment was a wonderful place to stay. Specifically their 2 patio apartments having both city view and the river side view at the same time. The apartments have lots of closet space and good enough space to set all your furniture in. It a     wonderful view from the apartment while you sip a nice cup of coffee or enjoy the snow. Kitchen is very spacious and lots of cabinets.  The Churchill management are very welcoming and lovely people. Special thanks to Jamie to help in a seamless transition to our new home here. Trevor and Jamie make a great team providing best tenant services and organizes lot of events for the tenants. The apt maintenance services are prompt and diligent and well managed through their property manager app. I have lived here for almost 2 years and had a great experience. They managed the COVID situation very well. The apt has good security and feels safe compared to other apt in Minneapolis downtown. Less noise pollution of the city as it’s closer to the river. Only once I had a an experience of bike theft. Apart from that it’s great place to live in.

I’ve lived in the Churchill now for about 1.5 years.  I have obnoxious neighbors that play their music extremely loud.  I’ve reported these people many times to management.  They were quiet the last couple of weeks, but then started up again today.  Security told me that they can’t do anything, and to call the police.  Why should I call the police to an apartment that states it is a luxury building?  My bathroom on the other side continuously smells like smoke, despite having residents sign a non-smoking agreement.

I was faced with the challenge of abruptly moving from Boston to Minneapolis during a national pandemic.  Needless to say, the timing was less than desirable; however, the Churchill staff made this as literally painless as moving could be.  They were incredibly prompt and communicated well, had so much patience with my questions, concerns and virtual touring.  Once moved in, they were so incredibly hospitable - really went above and beyond (while displaying proper social distancing recommendations) to give me everything I needed to make the move in as stress free as possible.  I would do it all over again - the staff is incredible and my apartment view is just breathtaking :)

Let me start off by saying that The Churchill is actually one of the few tallest residential buildings left in Downtown Minneapolis. It has many great amenities and luxury renovations despite its age. I have been here for over a year and I can say with confidence that you would love calling The Churchill your home as you have connected skyways, shops and breathtaking views. People complain about Management but I feel that anywhere you live, you’ll complain or find something to complain about. I have had issues but I never let that get in the way of the actual living experience here. Work orders were always done fast, packages are secure, security is on point and Staff is always helpful. This building is about 33 stories high with 370+ units, so I think Management is doing the best they can for a residence this large. You cannot judge a residence, restaurant or anything based on one issue or moment, you should look at the experience as a whole. Overall, I am making a review based on my living experience and I would recommend it to anyone looking for their new home.
Very horrible management.Best place to live but management is the worst thing in churchil
Friendly  Curtis is nice and friendly. And he does an awesome job when it comes to our request ??
Perfect  The apartment is well managed and everyone is friendly and nice.
Awesome! Excellent; theyre proving they keep their promises

Great place, Great space Love the vibe and energy from the leasing team. Always happy to help always available. Love the unit warm in the winter cool in the summer just the way I like it.  Been living here for a good minute and I still and enjoying it.

I had an issue with my scheduled move in date and last minute needed to push it back and Brandyn was able to help me with a good attitude and a quick response, definitely one of the best leasing agents i’ve ever encountered.

Mice infestation. I wish I could upload my camera footage I put on floor to see how bad the mice really are. Camera has been going off all night cause the mice keep running across it. Pest control has been here 4 times in two months but it gets worse each time. Deep cleaned my home cleared out clutter yet two mice are on my camera . Safe to say there is an infestation in this building and it needs to be condemned. To top it off the new lease they sent out was raising my rent lol I’m out of here! DO NOT Move HERE U HAVE BEEN WARNED !

Last Spring (2023), the apt had a large fire. 30 apt were lost due to the fire. The managers told us they would keep residents informed about what was going on and share details post the fire chiefs investigation, but didn’t. Their lack of communication post the fire is very upsetting and shows their lack of care towards their residents.

When  Centerspace bought the building they began requiring pet rent- this wasn’t ever the case for the first five years of me living here. They did this due to allowing dogs in the apt and due to their desire to earn more money than the apt is worth. If I owned a dog, I wouldn’t live here as there’s no where to walk them and people have allowed their dogs to crap in the stairways and in the trash shoot area-which is extremely disgusting. 

Currently there are only 8 washers and dryers in the entire apt and over 200 people in the building. 

Centerspace is focuses projects that aren’t even worth completing at this time rather than focusing on tasks that should be complete. Since the fire, the garage has been used to store all of the fridges and ovens and toilets from the apt damaged. This is causing the garage to be less appealing and trashy. 

Surrounding area of the building is very dirty. The apt below me has trash outside their back door and this wasn’t cleaned up for months and now is filled with trash again as the current residents in the apt are tossing all their trash out back.

I have informed the management of things to help them and received no thanks or follow up emails. In my eyes this allows me to know they don’t care about the building or my efforts to help them make this a better apt.

Lack of timely notice when they need to enter my apt. I have received notices with the wrong dates. Tasks that they’re doing in the apts have multiple steps meaning i have to be home from work multiple days when things could be done in one day rather than multiple days. For example, this summer the county was coming to look at the building (which requires them to set this up months in advance- I worked for the county so know their methods of these type of visits), but we get a days notice.

Center Space Homes!
They bought this building last year and have done nothing but raise the rent by $100's. You will live next to a cement factory and the planes will drive you nuts! They will raise your rent next year. KEEP LOOKING!

I've lived here since 2017 and I have really enjoyed the apt. I think the best aspect of it is the heated garage. They give you your own parking space, its priced well, and is super safe for your car. Apt layout wise I think my only complaint would be that they got rid of two floors worth of dryers and washers and there are only 6 of each in the total building. I think that was one of their mistakes as we pay for water and they had space for them, just frustrated that they did that. Other than that building is super safe, clean, pet friendly, and management is willing to work with you when needed. Also super good distance to the highway, target, Walmart, and other needed stores.

This place is a pretty average apartment building. It does not have the wow factor of all the 'modern, one-syllable' named complexes popping up in gentrified areas, but it is fairly well kept and comfortable. Some of the pros include: some updates to fixtures in kitchen and bathroom, as well as flooring. The rent is fairly affordable for the metro, and the location is great! Very close to suburban shopping, and city-life all in one. The staff are friendly and pleasant to work with. There are, however, many cons. The halls sometimes smell like 1950's Las Vegas (smokey and cheap perfume). The balconies are creepy and in need of repair. Ceilings in the halls are somewhat low and not well lit. Renovations take forever, they have been in the process of replacing the door numbers for at least six months (not sure what the hold up is), and they underutilize modern technology. Laundry will be replaced with card-machines (currently coin) and they underuse email communications. The neighborhood is in need of gentrification. Very industrial with poor sidewalks, with a very creepy cemetery a half block away. Would I move here again? Probably not. Will I renew my lease? No. But for now, its alright.

Aside from having a heated garage, woodhaven ‘s staff are super friendly, the building is fully secured, staff live on site and can assist when needed, and the neighbors  are great. Although rent is a little high for a one bedroom, I don’t mind paying it considering what I get out of the complex.

Do not waste your time with this place. The cleanliness is very bad. The windows in the common areas, exit doors and other locations are rarely ever cleaned. If you look real close you will dust on the carpet along the edges of the walls, around the pipes in the stair wells dating back several years. the cleaning person sprays soo much scented deoderizer to mask the smells. Falsely advertising a Billiards room, when it has been removed for months now. A sauna that takes hours to heat up before you can use it. State of the art excercise room, REALLY!!! Loose stairwell handrails you would think maintenance would have observed in the past two years. The back parking lot stairwell has been falling apart for a few years. When it snows, forget about it getting shoveled. The maintenance guy does not drive so why would he clear it for the tenants.  It took a year for maintenance to replace a closet door. But they keep raising the rent because they need to remodel instead of fixing or replacing things as they break. I guess their moto is, "let things get to a disgusting state to justify uping the rent" 

Staff will pass by apartments with "POT" smoke billowing out of apartments and never say a word. So if your a drug user this is the place to be. If you don't want Maintenance snooping around your apartment, make sure your there when something need to be fixed.

The mail carrier for this building has left the mail boxes unlocked for anyone to steal your mail. Has also left stacks of mail on top of the pop machine. Will leave your packages laying in the hallway for anyone to steal. 

OHHH, and above all do not trust the property manager Alexsandra. Very incompetant and Lies very well with a smile.

Indoor pool is great. But when winter comes you cannot use it because they do not keep it heated enough. Do you wanna be a human icecube?

I made a mistake signing a lease and then staying. I'll pay more for a better environment.

New, cabinets and counter tops have been installed in most apartments but the appliances and flooring are severely dated with no plans to update.  Hallways and laundry rooms are clean, but dated.  Management is pleasant but makes outrageous claims to get renters in the door.  However, maintenance staff is knowledgeable, efficient and friendly.  Indoor pool and exercise room are clean and enjoyable.  Common shower, bathroom and pool table room are dated and unpleasant.  Sauna does not work and advertised tanning bed is non-existent.  Off-street parking is at a premium and not guaranteed.  

Overall, I like the location, the size of the apartments are good but it is not luxurious in the least.  I would recommend for transitional living at best.

Relatively small, well priced apartments. New cabinets and counters make the apartments very appealing. Pool and "gym" amenities included in the rent. Parking seems to be a problem, as the lot can fill up before 11pm. You may have to park on the street late at night.

I went to view an apartment but he manager was in her office so I had to wait in the lobby. First of all the windows in the sitting area facing Lyndale were utterly filthy the order in the building was horrible. Clearly this building needs a complete overhaul. One the manager was done with her business she took me into her office the carpet on the floor was filthy. I told her that I was looking for an apartment with a balcony but none was available to see. She setup an appointment for me to come back the next day - I hated to do it but I had no intention of going back. I could not get over what I had just witnessed I certainly could not live there regardless of what the apartment looked. This complex needs some serious, serious upkeep...I hate to be so critical but it is what it is...I could not wait to leave there.

I’ve lived in two different different units in 1907 Colfax and have enjoyed both of them. Maintenance is quick to respond and the manager is easy to talk to. Pretty clean building and friendly neighbors. It’s also in a nice location where I can walk to parks or good restaurants. Rent is comparable to other nearby buildings too. I liked that I could pay for laundry using an app.

My apartment has flooded over 4 times while living here. First 2 months ago. Still waiting for it to be fixed while i get more water damage. Had to throw away rugs and some furniture. Theres holes in my celling that leak dirty water from the upstairs neighbor. My home feels unsafe and gross from the damage. Waiting for maintenance to fix the leaks and the water damage. Very upset about how slowly this is getting fixed as well as how the company has handled this so far.

Lived here a year, the liquor store parking lot right next door is always full of screaming people and loud cars blasting music. Upstairs neighbors would scream and fight until 3am. Every maintenance request someone would stop by but if i wasn’t home nothing would get fixed. My kitchen floor flooded overnight 4 times and they claimed there was no leak. The property manager is really nice however and very understanding. Apartments and building need major renovations and repairs.

The walls are so thin you can hear full conversations in other apartments. The front doors have no sound proofing so if someone opens a door, jingles their keys, walks, coughs, speaks, breathes...you will hear to it.

There are a couple people in the building that play their music LOUD past 3AM so often that I’ve invested in quality earplugs or I would never wake up for work in the morning. 

If they would just sound proof the front doors and set/enforce a noise curfew, that would make a HUGE difference but I’m not sure the owner actually cares enough to do that. 

Pros: Near transit and you can walk to a lot of places and parking is priced reasonably compared to other places in the area. The team is actually pretty responsive when you have requests or need maintenance. Also, the online payment system is super easy to use and you can access all your info (including your lease and maintenance) in one area, cat friendly, mostly nice neighbors (except for the 2-3 loud ones).

You won't regret renting here! Especially if you appreciate:
1. A friendly, helpful staff
2. Beautiful scenery / courtyard (with a picnic table & grilling area) -- feels like a small, ivy-covered college campus -- very well-maintained
3. Great location...Very convenient to both downtown & Uptown (along the #18 bus route between downtown & not sure where!)
4. Great location...Very convenient to both I-94 and I-35W
5. Parks nearby
******
Not everything is perfect! Here are the only drawbacks:
1. Parking can sometimes be difficult on Friday eves, Saturdays & Sundays (due to the museum and children's theater)...The most I've had to walk is about a block...So, still not a big deal. Annoying when you have groceries, though.
1.5.....Garage parking has a long waiting list (the last I knew)....and the spaces are TIGHT! Hasn't been an issue for me to not have a parking space, though...
2. Cell reception is not very good (I've had both AT&T and Verizon and sometimes calls get dropped. Guests who've been over, though, haven't had issues, so maybe it's just me!)
.....Can't think of anything else!
OH...MORE GOOD....
** Laundry areas always clean and typically available (Sunday nights can be tricky, as anywhere!)
** Storage locker area is clean & well-kept (All were taken in my building, so had to find one in the next building over...no big deal...it's storage, after all!)
ALL-IN-ALL...
A great place to live! It's quiet and respectful. My neighbors (after many years) have all been nice (except one, years ago, who didn't last long...)
You'll like it here!
** AGAIN...THE STAFF IS AMAZING!! **

The building is old with some windows that don't open and AC which needs to be installed but this is easily a place to fall in love with. Staff and maintenance are responsive and kind and there is so much to fall in love with here. The red brick ivy is inviting and something I like showing off to friends. I'll take walks to spot rabbits and butterflies with them in the courtyard. When I work out, Arnold Schwarzenegger posters motivate me to keep going as well. Can't recommend enough!

I lived in fair oaks apartments for more than one year is a beautiful place and the staff is a 10. 
the pictures that you can see are the real pictures and you can have underground parking wich is very convenient in winter time.
do not hesitate to look this place is a 10.

Fair Oaks has it all, classic old buildings, close to downtown and uptown, and quiet even though it's in the heart of the city. There are tons of restaurants in the neighborhood, you don't even have to drive. The building managers, maintenance crew, and office staff and absolutely wonderful and always helpful. I have loved living here and have for over two years.

Couldn't be happier with our apartment in the Fair Oaks complex. Lots of windows, hardwood floors, and beautiful architecture. The courtyard, in particular, is spectacular. The staff is very nice and responsive. The complex is right across the street from the Minneapolis Institute of the Arts, near numerous bus lines, three blocks from "Eat Street" and several blocks south of of downtown. The neighborhood--based on my personal experience--is pleasant and quite safe.

Only a couple caveats: no dishwashers, no pets (understandable, given the hardwood floors), and the buildings are quite old with the attendant "old apartment" problems (clanking radiators, peeling paint, etc.). Again, however, the staff is incredibly responsive and will address such problems efficiently and expeditiously.

This classic collection of six pre war buildings is located close to downtown and across the street from the art institute. The vine covered walls are topped with terracotta french tiles and create a gated inner courtyard. Residents are encouraged to create garden spaces and join, at their option, the gardening group. Each unique floorplan has original hardwood floors, deep nine inch window sils, and 8.5 foot ceilings. The boyfriend, not included, loves the wonderful water pressure in the shower, which is amazing given that the apartment is located on the top floor. Don't miss this gem!

Moving day was not pleasant, but the new leasor was super professional and super understanding. Got me the help I needed it. Kept me updated on my situation. Also property management was able to work with me and my situation! Really awesome team!
Very  noisy and unsafe place with neglectful management

The building itself is a great community, great location and truly a great place to live. But if anything becomes broken, don’t expect it to be fixed quickly. We still have washers/dryers that have been out of use for months.

This is a terrible place to live, they are terrible at taking maintenance requests and never fix anything-just cover it up for now. Water is always getting shut off. Cockroaches are a constant. The management is rude when you call them and packages get stolen regularly. To talk to someone you have to go through the large office and rarely gets anything done at the local building office.
I appreciate the apartments, the clean environment, but the maintenance services are very slow, not on time.
Courtyard apartments are great! They have good spacious layouts and maintenance is very responsive. Office staff are amazing!

I signed a lease for this apartment before viewing the property in person. Once I viewed my new apartment in person I realized it was absolutely beautiful but way too tiny for my liking. It honestly made me feel claustrophobic and panicked. I would advise anyone who is thinking about leasing to please view the apartments in person before signing a contract. While the property team has been kind to work with, they have unfortunately not been able to accommodate my situation. My lease has yet to start, but my only options are either to upgrade to another unit which is still quite small, or buy myself out of the lease. It would be really great if they could have been more accommodating to this situation.

A friend and I applied separately to live at the Bryn, but we were both shocked by all the hidden fees. After talking through potential leases, my rent would have been over 300 dollars more per month than the listed value. Also, although each apartment is listed as about 450 square feet, it feels more like a micro apartment due to the poor layout. I'm just posting so people are more aware of issues I didn't know about until later in the application process.

Very clean and good apartment. My main problem is that they take way too long to answer and follow up on maintenance requests. But otherwise the gym and lobby seems nice. in unit washing and dryer works well.

After the first couple weeks living here I have noticed how the apartment looks to be very cheaply made. Last night the door opened without using my fob which raises safety concerns. One of the treadmills broke while using it. Overpriced.

the website has false advertising, stating that parking is included in the base rent. When I asked the tour guide about this, they stated it was an extra $150 a month and they had brought it to managements attention around a month ago, but nothing has been changed. The fact that it has not been changed is a big red flag in my opinion. I highly suggest you update that information, as that could mean the difference of someone choosing to live in your building or having to look elsewhere due to affordability.
The new management obviously cares more about the residents than the previous one. They set up a bunch of events to create communiy vibes. It's just the building itself is a bit too old.

I’ve had a positive experience at Solhaus in Minnesota, and would give it 4 out of 5 stars. The community here is friendly and welcoming, making it easy to feel at home. The location is fantastic—close to restaurants, shops, and the University of Minnesota, which adds a lot of convenience. Maintenance has been a standout aspect; they respond very quickly to requests and handle repairs efficiently, which is a huge plus. The apartments themselves are modern and well-maintained, with spacious layouts and a good range of amenities. While there are occasional noise levels from nearby streets, it’s nothing major and is to be expected given the central location. Overall, Solhaus is a solid choice for anyone looking to live in a lively, well-maintained, and convenient area in Minnesota.

Good luck trying to get your CRP if you move out before tax season starts. Call all you want about a problem you're having no one will answer and when you come by to talk to someone in person no one will be there. If you're lucky you may be transferred to an "emergency line" and a person will take your message, but you'll never hear back from anyone.They'll say they're understaffed or the manager was out on the property it's not true. The front office sat empty while I lived there. And two weeks ago when I went in person to once again ask for my CRP. As for the apartment themselves I guess you'll be housed. But I recommend you rent any other apartment in that area. There were a lot of little and major problems that popped up while I lived there. Though I will say the maintenance man was very responsive. A lot of moisture on the windows leading to mold. The only room that gets warm is the living room because the HVAC faces the window, and there are no vents to any other room.

Genuinely awful experience. The building is situated right next to a set of train tracks and it's very loud. I stayed in a one-bedroom and the bedroom area has no windows, meaning if you close the door to avoid the train noises, it's pitch black. Someone's dog defecated in the stairwell and it took four days for it to be taken care of. Package theft was rampant the entire year I was there. I have had several packages slashed or stolen. For a time, people's cars were also being broken into inside the building's garages. There are many similarly priced apartments in this area, pick a different one.

The loft style studios are different than your typical studios in that there is a dividing wall separating the living and sleeping areas. I really like this, and it makes the apartment seem more like a 1 bed than a studio. Some parts of the building are a little dated, but I kind of like this, as it gives it a sort of "vintage" feel. The building is quiet and so far the management has been great and maintenance requests get done in a timely manner. Great location also! Would recommend.

I love this apartment, its super close to the lake and has been kept up very well by the owners.  They truly take pride in the outdoor appearance of the apartment and I think it is the best looking place on the block.  It's in close proximity to the popular uptown area- which has many dining and shopping options!
I have lived at Southsider for 2 years and it has been a great place. The maintenance crew was always quick and responsive and management has great communication. Good price too.
The building is always clean and sanitized. The maintenance team is great. Modesto is very friendly  and always takes care of any request we have had quickly and thoroughly.

I took a tour with a charming and helpful manager named Willie. He provided me with great information on the apartment and local restaurants in the area. It was a beautiful building with updated appliances and a great view from the community clubhouse. I can't wait to join this fantastic apartment! I put my appreciation in today!

The people at southsider apts are great. The application process was made very easy and if there is an issue they can help with they do.  We love our apt. I have only been here a week but I would recommend that anyone looking should try it.
The building is gorgeous and brand new, but the manager is terrible and bad at communication! The building also has a major water leak problem

Actual units are fine. Setting up a tour and getting through the application process was awful. Lots of fees and you constantly have to follow up with management or they won’t reply. Really expensive for the location and amenities which are only open half the time. Only good thing is the maintenance team who are quick and professional. Would not recommend Deco overall

The building itself is fine, some of the advertised amenities are not actually present.  As far as I can tell there is no dog run or secure bike storage in the building yet. 
 
My real issue was the application process.  It was a nightmare and took over 1 month to get approved.  For starters you are charged both an application fee and an admin fee totaling $300 together. Then there is the pet fee and pet deposit fee.  They don't list the security deposit, but its the full rent amount for one month.  This is fine, but the application initially has you put down a 1/3 of the deposit without letting you know that there is more deposit required.  
I found all of this out the afternoon before I moved in.  Adding all the fees and deposits up I was out $2k before ever paying rent.  I also had to figure out how to get that money together the night before moving in and also being able to pay rent for the month.  I was also told the day before move in that I needed to switch my renters insurance or face an additional fee that would be on my first months rent statement. I ended up paying the first months rent plus fees and deposit with a credit card so you guessed it another $100 fee.

Having paid nearly $500 in fees just to get into the door, I would have expected a better application experience.  It should not have taken several weeks to get approved.  I tried contacting the management company about this, but I never heard back. 

Give yourself plenty of time and keep your options open.  Prepare to pay fees that provide you zero value.

Living here for about a year now. Discouraged every time I go get a package from the leasing office because it’s nice! It smells good, the lights are bright and working. 

Then I go back to my building to a dingy smell, stains on the carpets, writing on the walls, lights not working in so many parts of the building. - 1st floor, 3rd floor stairwell, laundry rooms. And the barely usable gym. Then I look on here and am reminded of the beautiful gym I toured. And every time I go to the leasing office for anything. 

They have an unused pool room here that could be turned into a beautiful community room for this buildings ease of access. 

Really wish they would bring the other building up to the same living standard as the one they advertise. Currently on apartments.com looking for one that does.

I been living here for 7 months and I’m enjoying it the laundry room is amazing I love the work out room this building does a lot of activities which is really good for the kids I would definitely recommend this apartment to others…

I have a family member that lives at this property. Please be advised that you can't have vistors due to their parking guidelines. Schmitt Towing told a vistor that they can tow their car any time of the day if they do not have a parking permit. They were visiting and their car was towed before 10PM. If you plan on having visitors the Windsor Gates is not where you want to stay.

After being a resident at The Marshall apartments for the past 3 years, there are so many great things to rave about. Recently the whole clubhouse and office area were remodeled. As a student I love this because there us an abundance of sitting space for studying. They also have a computer lab that is available for residents to use 24/7. The whole ambience of the space is warm and inviting. I would recommend this propety!
The staff here is great and super helpful! Libby gave us a tour and the property was so nice, really love the amenities, especially the big private courtyards.
We did a tour with our son and loved the amenities and appreciated the safety. Our tour rep, Libby, was able to answer all questions. Thank you

I have spent the last 2 years living in one of the 2 floor Townhomes and it has been a great experience. If there is ever any issues, Libby and another CA (cannot remember their name off the top of my head) have went above and beyond to assist.

I have lived at the Marshall for the past two years and it has been a great experience! I feel safe at all times and the staff here is very helpful and always kind to people that come in. I wouldn't want to live anywhere else

The newly updated clubhouse is super nice and has a ton of seating. Also, the apartments have a lot of space and have nice updated appliances. Overall, the staff and building as a whole are super nice!

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: Confirmed a date and time to tour their available apartments but got stood up. Waited in the cold for 10 minutes buzzing in and trying to contact them, but there was no one in the office. It’s been a week and they have not apologized or even followed up.

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: I have lived here for nine years and have enjoyed it.  The building is well maintained and the staff is responsive to requests.  The location is another plus.  I highly recommend it!

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: Beautiful looking property that they are continually doing small renovation projects to keep it pretty, but its all surface level. In my apartment the bathtubs water has been constantly running for the past 4 months with no one doing anything about it. I have tryed leaving many service requests and emailing the property manager with 0 action. It has gotten so bad mold has started growing on multiple surfaces around the bathroom. Another issue we have had is the baseboard heater in the main part of the unit has not work ever since i moved in, it has gotten down to -40 degree temps this winter so we were forced to use a space heater which costed us an extra $80 a month to run when Heating is supposedly payed for already having to rack up my electrical bill for their issues seems unlawful.

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: This is not the nicest but not the worst neighborhood in Minneapolis.  I have lived here three years and definitely recommend living at Buckingham Apartments. Our neighborhood and the city of Minneapolis has had civil unrest this past year, and we  are making a fast and recognizable recovery.  I REALLY like my apartment.  I have lived here 3 years.  The first year my owners were great but not interested in updating the building.  Then there was a difficult transition year two when we were between management companies.   Fortunately, we have a great new management team and they are very responsive and pleasant to work with.  They communicate well and are transparent with us about all construction and improvement projects happening in the building.  There is a nice gym and a mod pool/hot tub common room in our basement.  It is safe and secure all around the building.  We live by a fire station on a street where cars are exiting from downtown, so if you haven't lived in a big city before this could be an adjustment.  But I endure the nightlife and busy street, because I have a good view of downtown (on the north side of the building) and I am saving a lot of money living here rather than finding an overpriced apartment in North Loop or even near me in Loring Park.  Since this was a hotel in the 1920's, there are many small  units that are great for students, twenty-somethings, or anyone who needs a small space near downtown.  There are some larger apartments for families too.

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: Unfortunately from the moment my daughter and I went to take a tour, this has been a terrible experience. We were extremely clear from the very beginning regarding the price range she could afford. They still proceed to show us 3 apartments that were over her budget. When I pointed that out and asked to see one within her budget, he said he didn't have one ready to show us. Once she was finally able to see the apartment, there were repairs that needed to be made. We were told they would be done before she moved in but almost 3 months later they are still not fixed. You can never get a hold of the property manager and it takes him a few weeks to return phone calls.

apartmentName: The Buckingham / The Commodore / The Parkw...
review: When I first moved into The Commodore Apartments it was not a great experience at all. Granted, I was moving to a different state in COVID, but it was still a horrible experience. I couldn't see the apartment before I locked in on it, didn't get a tour of the facilities, there were issues with the paperwork I sent in, so all in all, not a great first impression. With that being said, there has been a change in management and the new manager is very helpful when you can get ahold of him (not his fault they are very understaffed), and he will do anything in his power to resolve any issue you have and assist you where he can. Other than that, I lived there for 6 months and don't have too much to complain about. They renovated the buildings, fixed up the patio and pool, I felt as safe as I could have living there, and you can't really beat the price for rent and the location is not bad.

I went to go check out this apartment and the lady showed me two different apartments. They were really small and when I left I started to feel itchy. I get home and while I am taking off my shoes I notice that I have a bite on my foot. DO NOT RENT FROM THIS APARTMENT !!!!!!!!!

3/30/2024: I moved into my apartment in September of 2022 and have had a great experience with them! Maintenance was very quick and they even offer help with window A/C unit installation and removal. They also send notice of important things for residents to know in a timely manner. I recently requested to terminate my lease early and they were very clear about what steps I need to take and their move out expectations were very clear. Their apartments aren’t high end but it was perfect for me! No rodent, insect or other vermin issues either which I REALLY appreciate! I’d say this is a great place for someone moving out on their own for the first time. Really walkable area and easy to get to the suburbs (from the location I rented).

Good maintenance team. Simple affordable living. 

Only downside is a lot of pets.

The apartment itself and the company were both great. However, on-street parking was a bit iffy, crime around the area was a bit of a problem, and the area around the buildings in the city was a bit dirty. That said, there is off-street parking available for a fee. The management was courteous and responsive, I didn't have any problems, and the apartment was very nice.

I'll try to capture the experience of residing at Highland Village Apartments. At the time of this review, I've lived at HVA for about 15 years. Some residents have lived here much longer. My wonderful neighbor below me has lived here for about 10 years. Half of my family has lived at HVA at some point in time. Much of the staff lives on the premises. Apartments are charming and functional. With windows on three sides, they are filled with light and good air flow. There are trade offs where ever you live. Laundry in the basement is less convenient than in-home, but I don't go to the gym, so a little exercise on the stairs is good for me. Between the parking lot in the back, street parking, and a garage option, parking is adequate. You could also get by without a car. The neighborhood has about everything you need in walking distance, and there are several bus stops within a block. The premises are beautiful in every season. In the spring and summer, when you walk past flowering hedges, bushes, or trees, the breeze is fragrant. Fall is gorgeous with the changing leaves. And winter is cozy and bright with holiday lights and wreathes. I love the radiant heat in the winter. The staff is uber responsive. For example, after many years, my fridge went out late on a Friday night. By Saturday morning, I had a new fridge in my apartment. Management is continually re-investing in the property. They're always doing something to maintain (like replacing stretches of sidewalk) or upgrade (like creating gardening plots for residents and an outdoor grill/patio area for communal use). Over the years, office staff have gone above and beyond to help me out in different unforeseen circumstances. I'm a single female. I feel 100% comfortable and safe with all of the maintenance staff. By and large, it's quiet and peaceful, although I sleep with white noise regardless. It's very rare that I turn on the radio to mask noise/conversations from the street or within the apartment. Maybe if someone's moving in or out it's a little noisier, but that rarely happens, because most people don't move out.  Every friend or guest I have over says the same thing, "I love your apartment!" I can't say enough good things about HVA.

I've lived in a Highland Village apartment for 3 years and have had a great experience! The apartments are really charming and well-kept. The few times I've needed something fixed (from normal wear and tear), there's always been someone out to fix it the same day. My experience with the management has been really positive, and I've found them to be helpful, friendly, and flexible. The location is fantastic- within walking distance of Target Express, Starbucks, Chipotle, Lunds & Byerly's, Patina, Haskell's, the Highland Grill...the list goes on. Plus, Minnehaha Falls and all its trails are a 20 minute walk. Highly recommend!

This place is a pretty great place to live if you're looking for something that feels homey and cozy.  There is tons of natural light and the kitchen is awesome (center island and tons of space to cook!).  On the surface it looks perfect, but after living there minor quirks begin to show up.  Things like a small wine-rack above the cupboards that falls apart if you put wine in it, or a built-in shelf that we chose not to use because it didn't feel attached well enough to hold anything of much weight.  However all these quirks have proven to be minor, and usually negligible, as they don't really affect the way you feel when you're living in the space.  There's also a shared courtyard and our neighbor has it looking great with all the gardening she does.  My roommates and I have really enjoyed living here.

For three years I have been very pleased living here!  A variety of apartments, easy to decorate, with a nice ivy, vintage vibe.  Garages, laundry and attentive property management on site. Conveintly located to resturaunts, boutiques, a small movie theater, coffee shops, and (recently added) Target Express right next door!  Easily spend a weekend of entertainment all in walking distance.

I absolutely love this apartment. The staff are so helpful, SAME DAY maintenance requests, every time, they are so helpful. The apartments are well kept with beautiful hardwood floors and the location is so god, I don't think I'll ever have to drive again! Definitely recommend this apartment.

Drive off Cleveland Ave, you know the southern end where there are a ton of restaurants, a theatre, grocery stores, etc. and down Inner Drive to a long courtyard lined with red brick buildings covered in vines. The atmosphere feels like the setting of a little English neighborhood. The base of each building is lined with gardens that the residents can sink their hands into, and out towards the street there is parking a-plenty. In your apartment is a great layout that my boyfriend and I tailored to our taste with ease, and they even put in a new kitchen in per my request. The maintenance is on site, so the one problem we had with the sink leaking, it was fixed that day.  Overall, its a great price, the right location, and a beautiful home.

Just moved in for 2 weeks and already love the place. Had a great experience dealing with the management. Don, helped me work through the lease paperwork quickly and easily even though I wasn't in state at that time. The apartment area is not noisy and has easy access to light rail. I must mention the security level here, so good. Overall happy to stay here. Thanks---Thamina

As a young woman, safety is of the utmost importance to me. The Ray has tight security. There are several fob readers, and you have to scan your fob several times to get anywhere in the building, including each apartment. This is a great place for young people to live safely and comfortably.

I've lived at Ray for a little over a year now and just absolutely love it! The units are modern, fresh, light, and efficient.  The balcony's are spacious and the nest thermostat is clutch when you're in and out of your unit all day.  I've had great experiences with the management team, they are warm, welcoming, and professional.  The location is so convenient as well, with it's adjacency to the train line, its central location between Minneapolis and Saint Paul, and its proximity to the U of M campus.  I've lived in 4 different apartment buildings in the twin cities and none of the others compare to Ray!  Highly recommend this spot!

I have been living in this location since 4//4/2021, so I have been living here for just over a week. 

I had checked out a variety of different apartments before choosing RAY. Many of them offered awesome services and locations, but I chose RAY for a variety of reasons. 

When I first pulled up to visit the location, I felt noticeably comfortable in the area. Additionally, of the apartments I checked out, none had better parking than RAY. As far as parking goes, I had the option of a nice parkin garage, parking lot adjacent to the building, or a $25/month parking lot about 2 blocks from the building. I chose the $25/month option, and I am very happy with the choice. The light rail stop is directly between the apartment building and the additional parking, and the extra crosswalks make that lot easily accessible.  Additionally, there is so much nearby public parking that I almost decided to not even choose the $25/month parking. 

I have had a great experience dealing with the management. Britney, the residence manger, helped me work through the lease paperwork quickly and easily. I have also had the opportunity to meet two of the residence maintenance crew, Dewey, and Chris (Dewey if I mis-spelled your name, I am sincerely sorry!). Both individuals are fantastic people, and I know that if I have any issue that one of the maintenance crew will kindly come and help me out. 

One thing which was especially important to me was overall noise levels in my studio apartment. I have been here for a week, and I can say that I do not think I have heard one of my neighbors in their apartment a single time. Occasionally you hear a few footsteps in the hallway, but they are transient and the noise is gone within a few seconds. I am sure they are all great people who I would love to meet, but I am profoundly happy that in this concrete walled apartment, I do not have to hear anybody else. 

To reiterate; I have been here for a week so far, and I had a great experience moving in, as well as living here so far.

Thanks!
-Jim Swenson

I moved from out of the state and the management team made everything easy. I got pictures of the apartment before I signed the lease. Move in was quick and easy and I have not had any issues since moving in August 2019. It Is close to the green and blue lines and there are fun restaurants in the area.

Only 39 underground parking provided. I am on the 8th place on the waitlist of underground parking, as I moved in Mid-August. I didn't know before I sign the lease. Basically, if no one moves out, you won't get the parking spot. It drives me crazy, especially, it's Minnesota. I would not recommend this place if you cannot make sure you have reserved parking.
Declawing cats is a barbaric process. Requiring cats to be declawed to live here is unacceptable.

Heating bills in the 3 and 5 story buildings are astronomical. Mine for a two bedroom kept at 62 degrees was over $160/month in the winter. One neighbor in a studio had bills over $180, and others in two bedrooms were over $300. One neighbor, who was out of town in December, had her highest usage day when she was gone, despite thermostats set very low. It makes one wonder how individual units are metered. Incidentally, tenants have no access to their electric meters, so one cannot turn the circuit breakers off and determine that there is no current flowing. Occasionally wind was felt coming from the furnace closet, and the furnace sounded like a jet taking off. Floors in first floor units, over the heated garage, were ice-cold in the winter.

Noise from other units was unbelievable, with every footstep heard from overhead. Low-flying planes sometimes shook the building, and stereos and TVs from neighboring units tended to be shared, willingly or not.

Bedrooms are 10.5 feet wide, and are barely big enough for a full-size bed, even in the "luxury" units on the 10th floor of the tower. Incidentally, the tower is built with post-tensioned concrete, as compared to the other two buildings, which are stick built, so it is probably quieter, although I don't believe there are masonry walls between units there.

The 24-hour concierge is an excellent idea, and the personnel at the front desk are fantastic. However, they are not empowered to do anything, such as about noisy parties in the community room, misbehavior in the courtyard, etc.

Living here felt like living in an airport hotel at O'Hare.

The design is exactly how I would want my home! Every thing was thought out at this apartment complex.. the excessive storage, the sun facing pool deck, natural light filling every room and a staff that makes you feel at home.  The location was what really sold it for us - Southdale Mall, grocery store, unlimited restaurants all in walking distance; and quick access to 494 and 62!  We love our home here and would recommend anyone considering this apartment.

We came here right before the management change, Two nice, professional people greeted us and sold us instantly. Later on we came back to sign the lease and the new manager messed up on the time leased and price. Fair enough, being a new manager sucks we figured. Little did we know it was an omen of how awful this manager was. Maintenance requests are ignored, water is turned off without warning and package theifs run rampant. At one point a homeless guy lived in the laundry rooms because the locks didn't work. We got a letter saying they were raising the rent 300 dollars from what it originally was, nope. Do yourself a favor and just don't.

Pros: location is great, neighbors are quiet, fitness room is decent
Cons: old building, ceilings leak all the time, maintenance takes forever- have been taking cold showers for 2 weeks after coming home to a flooded bathroom, hallways always smell, stairwells are disgusting, washing machines are horrible and don’t get clothes clean, company is unresponsive when it comes to incorrect charges

Really wish I would have spent $100-200 extra per month on a different place. Although I appreciate the deal I was given when I moved in, this place is not worth it.
The current property manager does not do his job and no repairs ever get done. Get ready to get ignored.

I rented here from 2021-2023 and during my time here I generally liked The Edge of Uptown, had decent amenities and was in a convenient location. Unfortunately, in early 2023 there was a management change and things started to rapidly fall apart.

While living at the Edge Of Uptown there were several maintenance issues which took weeks if not months to fix, constant water outages and problems in the building. There were frequent security issues with doors broken and packages being stolen, most of the amenities became unusable, people would park in your assigned garage spot multiple times, the surface parking lot was never plowed on time and worst of all the office staff treated you like dirt.

Nobody in this building has a clue what they are doing, they don’t seem to care about their residents, they will straight up lie and gaslight to your face even when you want to look at other units in the building they become difficult and are not willing to work with you. If you are lucky you will get someone who answers the phone but most of the time nobody can be found in the office and they won’t answer your emails either. 

I would look elsewhere until management can get their act together, but don’t be surprised when they continue to raise your rent even though they make no effort to improve the building.

This place used to be great, but a new manager took over and now nothing is getting done. I have had a plumbing issue in my kitchen for months and no one has done anything about it. The ticket was placed in April and a follow up ticket was placed mid June and it's now July and nothing. The main office also doesn't respond to emails or messages from the resident portal so your only hope is to catch the manager in the office. Half the time the office is empty and the other half there is already someone there and you have to wait. I've been trying to turn in my 60 day notice for a week now and have gotten nowhere. Called corporate about it and Corp has been very helpful, but nothing is getting done in the office.

I feel like upkeep and improvements have been stagnant for awhile and I'm not sure if after my lease is up next year if I'll want to stick around if nothing changes. The rents keep going up but nothing more is getting done. So basically I'm just paying more into someone else's pocket instead of it going into community improvements. The carpets are so ugly and gross looking. It makes the new paint job kind of pointless since everything still looks scrubby. I'm genuinely embarrased to have people visit with how it looks right now. There are frequent issues with the washing machines that take weeks to months to get fixed. The garbage chute rooms don't ever seem to be cleaned. Those are my biggest issues but I just wish there was more care put in to my home. I know there's been a recent change in who works here so we'll see if that improves anything or not.
I lived here for one year and moved out in July 2023. This company will charge fees you do not owe and then threaten you with collections. I would never live here again.

Good place to live excellent location.  Close to restaurants, lakes and centrally located.  Something for every enthusiasts.  Walking trails local shopping, dinning, concerts, bus line, access to lakes kayaking and fishing biking.
Excellent access to lakes and nature.  Easy access to shopping and grocery stores.  Close to uptown and downtown.  Great restaurant on ground level.
Ellipse and E2 offer a great living experience with clean and spacious amenities and above-average, friendly staff.
Our experience at the Ellipse on Excelsior has been excellent in all repects.  The building is great.  The staff are excellent.  The neighborhood has many interesting amenities.
I love living here. Location is perfect and the staff is always friendly and very responsive. Highly recommend!

I want to warn everyone about the terrible building conditions at Park Point Apartments. The place is falling apart! The walls have cracks, and the ceilings leak when it rains. The heating and cooling systems don't work properly, making it unbearable in extreme weather.
Plain and simple. This was sold to me as a smoke free building but people smoke and the manager doesn’t care and will just deny it
My experience at Parkpoint Apartments has been overshadowed by security issues and rampant vandalism in the parking lot. The lack of proactive measures to address these concerns is disheartening.

This is supposed to be smoke free, but management doesn't enforce it.  Neighbor vapes and/or smokes weed several times per day.  I've tried many times to get mgmt to do something about it but they won't.  They don't even respond to my emails anymore.

There has been a lot of turn over with the maintenance staff and it takes a long time to get anything fixed. Management has to be contacted multiple times for any issue as they seem disorganized and likely spread too thin. Overall building maintenance has declined significantly over the last two years.

UPDATE 11/27/23: The new property manager, Nancy, is amazing!! She called me and talked over some stuff. She was so apologetic of her predecessors behavior and even though none of it was her fault it still felt very good to be heard and have that apology. She definitely seems very promising to turn this place around. Excited to see what she accomplishes in the last month of me living here. and tbh a little sad I'm leaving now.

I really enjoyed living here and with the new manager I think its gonna be a great place to live again.

11/24/23: I've lived here for a little over two years now and I'm so glad it's not gonna be a third year. The first two years were really good. Communication from property manager was very prompt, maintenance issues were dealt with fast, and the halls were pretty clean. Over the last few months there has been a change in management and this is now a terrible place to live.

I will be honest I did try to go for a third year, got a quote for a new lease and everything but then they ghosted me and never got a new lease over to me. FYI for anyone out there apartments don't legally have to give you a new lease no matter how many times you reach out and they say they'll send one. The communication is horrible. I don't think I've gotten a single email response since the new management took over and phone calls aren't much better. The halls are dirty and haven't been vacuumed in months. There's an emergency maintenance issue today in the laundry room and I can't get ahold of anyone. I'll be moving next week and I truly can't wait to get out.
They don’t answer they’re phone or email back I’ve been calling and emailing for weeks to try to schedule a showing. This is crazy.

I have lived at Liv Apartments for about seven months now. I couldn't be happier with my studio apartment. It is incredibly spacious and the floor plan is laid out in a smart way. It really feels more like a one bedroom with an open floor plan than a cramped studio that one thinks of at first. The kitchen space is huge with an island counter. There's plenty of room to do work on my laptop there, and on the other side, I have more counter space than any other apartment I have ever rented before. 
The property is the perfect distance from Uptown, quiet, but a few minutes away from Calhoun Square and the rest of the restaurants and shops in Uptown. 
I don't personally own any pets, but they allow both cats and dogs. Even with dogs in the building, you rarely hear any of them, and never at when trying to get to sleep. 
All in all, the price is comparable to anything else in the area. I feel quite fortunate to have stumbled upon this property.

I have lived at Liv for 9 years - perhaps only 8 - I forget the year as it was a stressful time. The area is great. Close to Minneapolis and near Hwy 100 for convenience of traveling the cities. There is a beautiful park/nature walk located next to a Rec center across Monterrey from the building and another great walking trail across 36 1/2. Our current office manager, Mandy, is great. She replies to questions/issues promptly and even sometimes during her off hours. She understand the nature of people and tries to help out when she can.

I have lived here for a year and a half and have been very pleased with the apartment complex.  Very quiet and they do a fantastic job of keeping it clean. They do allow dogs which is great since many properties are choosing to ban dogs (I'm not a cat person). The best part is that you are very close to downtown minneapolis and also close to shops/restaurants.

I have been living here for about 6 months. The unit I am in is absolutely beautiful and the building in general is very clean and seems to be well maintained. The building itself is not brand new so there have been some internal problems (pipes breaking, heat going out, etc.), but they have all been dealt with swiftly. Management and maintenance staff have been friendly and helpful in my experience here so far. I really enjoy living here!

apartmentName: The Legends at Silver Lake Village 55+ Apa...
review: We just moved in a week ago and love our specious 2 bd. and 2 bath apt. The manager Elizabeth and her assistant Dee were very welcoming, informative and helpful in setting up and qualifying !!!. We are really enjoying our new life here. We highly recommend checking out this place and it's staff.  Harriet and Daryl.

apartmentName: The Legends at Silver Lake Village 55+ Apa...
review: Everything you ever need is close by. Amenities are terrific - 24/7 gym, washer/dryer in unit, pets allowed - that's huge. Tenants have a committee and are striving to get feedback and suggestions from everyone to make the residence as good as possible.

I rarely leave reviews, but my experience with this apartment complex was so terrible that I feel compelled to share. From the outset, the entire rental process was a disaster. We were only shown a renovated showroom, which was in stark contrast to the unkempt, dirty apartment we were actually given. The carpets were stained, and it was clear that the apartment had not been properly cleaned or maintained.

To make matters worse, we faced constant issues with water. It was regularly shut off, making daily life incredibly inconvenient. Adding insult to injury, we had a mice infestation that was never adequately addressed despite our complaints.

The office staff were unhelpful and dishonest throughout our time there. They were evasive about the apartment’s condition during our tour and offered no solutions or compensation when issues arose. Our microwave and dishwasher were non-functional, and despite numerous requests for compensation, nothing was done.

Overall, the lack of proper maintenance, the misleading initial tour, and the poor customer service made this one of the worst renting experiences I’ve ever had. Save yourself the trouble and look elsewhere. This place is not worth the hassle.

For the mouse infestation, we have requested 2 times a full revamp of the apartment to Review all apart sides, walls, and doors for holes.  First time was on December 7-2023 Sadly we had only received assistance with a mouse trap , and the manger hanged the phone on my face while I told her this is an important and they had to solve this problem ASAP , her answer was when they gonna come to do tour they will check our apartment but when they came they gave us a mousepad trap. Second time it was on January 5-2024 I called them sadly as usual we have to wait tell they clean tour they should  check but tell now no one shows up  today is January 16-2024 because it is freezing out side yesterday I turned on the heater but sadly I have mouse in my apartment now , I can’t not sleep I left the apartment at night I have a kidney infection and I am sick I am so tired off this I don’t sleep at night I can’t use the bathroom I was in the Emergency Room and I came home to get rest but I couldn’t sleep or use the bathroom because of this issue. Most of the time I leave the apartment this is unaccepted and I will seek legal action for all that. ( my apartment not the only one has this issue my neighbors have the same issue too). Jun 5. 2024 I have the same issue but what they just gave us mousepad traps, this is the fifth time we have this problem but tell now they did not give us a solution about this the mouse still there the whole night I couldn’t sleep , they kept saying it because of the heat but now we are summer we don’t even open the heat . The worst apartment ever I advise you guys stay away from this apartment.

My wife and I have lived here for 3 years and have had minimal issues with the management staff...all have been very friendly. The location and outside of the complex is very nice, however, the inside is a bit less than hoped for, but still fairly nice for the price. They have raised the price on us over the last couple of years, causing us to look elsewhere. All in all, they were a great starter place for us.

The Equinox properties are nice and our apartment is great and came clean. For being carpeted, it is VERY clean with no smells when we moved in. The space in the apartment, along with the location, make the price a GREAT deal! We walk to Cub and Caribou all of the time. It is so nice to have a garage included as well! 
The staff is very attentive; we had a work order on a faucet in the bathroom and it was fixed within 48 hours, which was very nice. The pools are great and we use them regularly along with grills around the property. Our building is quiet and without noise outside. The ONLY real downside is that the bedroom is facing all of the stores, like Cub, so the lights shine in at night. We bought blackout curtains and the problem was fixed. Overall, I'd recommend Equinox as your next home.

I lived at this property until June 3, 2016 at which time there was a major fire that made the apartment uninhabitable.  While the fire was traumatic, the treatment from Bigos (the company that manages/owns Beach South at the Lake) made the experience exponentially worse for my wife, dog, and I.  Aside from fairly blatant lies that were told to us regarding the demolition date of the building, access to the unit, status of our property in the unit, etc... Bigos then took it upon themselves to determine - without any form of consent - that they would demolish the structure without providing us with any access to salvage any of our property.  The treatment from Bigos was so horrendous that I didn't feel comfortable making the move across country that we already had planned without hiring a lawyer first.  I can't/won't tell you what you should/shouldn't do, but can tell you that I will never do any business with this company again.

I think it's really rude that only one car per household is allowed to park near the apartment while the other person has to walk from a non secure lot. If you don't have a sticker in your windshield, you'll most likely be towed. That's really inconsiderate because both me and my boyfriend pay equal rent and we deserve equal comforts from the company. 
Last night by boyfriend bought a large tv and parked in front of our building (no permit sticker). in the time it took for him to lug it up the stairs, get into our building and set it down and unwrap it, his car had already been towed. I wish the company footed some of the bill since it's not the residents' fault there are so few parking spaces. Now he gets to pay a towing company because he needed to park in front of his own house for a little bit instead of walking a tv across the property or leaving it in his car until I could help.
I also find it very odd that we don't have a garbage disposal. Isn't that kind of basic now a days? Anyway, the parking situation needs to change. All residents should be given the same amenities.

I have lived in several apartment complexes, so I know what I am rating.  First, the staff at Beach South are friendly and accessible before, during, and after the leasing process.  Second, the maintenance team is skilled, efficient, and accessible. Third, the location can't be beat.  You can be in downtown Minneapolis in a matter of minutes.  If you prefer suburban shopping and activities, Maple Grove is also quite close.  The complex is set back away from the noise, but right off of highway 100.  The lake on property is beautiful, and great for boating!  The amenities on site are fabulous-- indoor pool is well-cared for, fitness room is clean, party room is great for get-togethers with friends, and easy to book.  Finally, our home is really nice.  When we moved in, the paint and carpet were all new.  Everything else had been deep cleaned, and when we arrived, there was a gift bag waiting for us.  We felt so welcomed, and now feel so at home here-- we may never leave.

The building has decided that they will turn off the air-conditioning in early October regardless off the weather. For a top-floor south facing apartment you are left no options, but to endure a truly uncomfortable living space. Reaching out to the building manager resulted in a non-sensical response about the HVAC settings and the instruction to 'open your windows'. Such a condescending answer was particularly frustrating given that my windows and balcony door were wide open (and a fan was pushing in cold air) and the apartment was still in excess of 80 degrees.

I have lived in this complex for 2 years and just signed my lease for a third time so obviously I do like it here. The building is up to date and repairs are done fast. Paying rent is easy online. Depending on the unit be prepared to pay a nice sum every month but it is comparable to other units in the area. I do love how the river is a mile away for biking and running.

The Lyric is a great place to make your home if you love exploring both St Paul and Minneapolis. The building is well maintained with open, light-filled apartments. The people who work here are friendly and responsive.

But the true advantage of life at The Lyric is its location. South St Anthony Park has a variety of housing options, so the neighborhood is diverse. Being part of the Creative Enterprise Zone means there are colorful murals to be discovered around every corner. Hampden Park Coop is walking distance for delicious soups and groceries.

When you feel like exploring the world, there are nearby bike routes that will take you into St Paul or Minneapolis. Not feeling like walking or biking? The Green Line can get you close to bus routes that take you anywhere. And, if you must, 94 and 280 are easily accessed by car. 

This is the place to live if you want a comfortable home that makes it easy to explore the world. I've lived here 2 years and still am happily making new discoveries every day.
I love the apartment, for what you pay you can’t beat it. However the location isn’t great.
Quiet, clean and beautiful apartments. Supportive staff that responds quickly! Love living here!

I've been residing at The Lyric at Carleton Place for over a year now and have been really pleased with the upkeep and maintenance of the public areas and attention given to residents whenever an issue arises.

Management is excellent! They care about those who reside on their property and make a point to stress the rules to keep everyone in order all the while engaging the tenants in fun. Various activities are available for mingling if that's your thing, and they are kind enough to acknowledge tenants personally on major holidays and birthdays; what apartment do you know in the area that does that?!

If you're looking for a safe, clean and fun place to live, look no further. I highly suggest you check out this property and see if it's a great fit for you!

When I first visited The Lyric, I was very impressed with the lobby and the leasing women were friendly. There was a recently vacated room that had yet to be cleaned, but I was fine with seeing the room in a less than perfect state. The leasing agent agreed and reminded me numerous times it would be clean which was nice. We got to the room and I was extremely impressed. Nice appliances, granite counter tops, great looking floors and spacious rooms. I called my future roommates and said we need to sign the lease now. We went the next day and signed the lease. It is quiet on the weekends and you almost never heard neighbor noise or the people above you (if you're not on the top floor). Also, you don't use a key to lock your door, but rather a magnetic sensor type thing. Hold the sensor near the door and when it turns green you can lock it. That's really nice.

There are a few things that almost prevented me from giving 5 stars. You can't bring your dogs in the elevator which I don't really understand. Also, there's a paper processing plant a few blocks away that produces an interesting smell. It's not bad or gross or anything, it just smells like, well, paper. The bedroom doors are barn style so they don't close in a door frame resulting in no sound insulation and they don't lock. Not a deal breaker, but an interesting style choice.

The underground parking is wonderful, the in unit washer and dryer is a huge plus and there is adequate area to take out your dog in a secured area. If there were more things in the area, this apartment would be perfect. Overall, the small things I dislike about The Lyric are far outnumbered by the positive things. I would definitely recommend this apartment to others.

I've lived at The Lyric since June of 2011 and I have loved every minute of it. The apartments themselves are gorgeous and the building is well constructed. I rarely hear a neighbor. Great amenities, too, with a washer and dryer in every apartment. I love the ladies that work in the rental office, they are practically family and have been nothing but accommodating and friendly to me. When I have a maintenance request, it's fixed RIGHT away. They really do a great job here. Absolutely, without a single doubt in my mind, the BEST apartment complex I've ever lived in. It's like living in a 5 star resort!

I have lived at The Lyric since August of 2010, which was shortly after they began leasing units. I have loved my time at the building and continue to renew my lease because I can rely on great service, value, helpful staff and maintenance, and a top-of-the-line apartment. I can't say anything negative about my experience so far and plan to stay!

I love the Lyric. It is an awesome place. It's very centrally located, close to the highways, bus stops, and the light rail. The amenities are great. I'm lucky enough to live on the 6th floor, near the outdoor theater, the solarium, the sauna, and the grilles. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They have truly gone above and beyond to help me have a great experience at the Lyric. I have thoroughly enjoyed my 1.5 years here and hope to live here for a long time. Sincerely, Frederic

I have lived at "The Lyric" since August 2012 and I love it! The staff here is really polite and welcoming. If something is malfunctioning it gets taken care of quickly! The Maintenance Staff are very helpful and efficient! I live on the top floor (6th), so I am not troubled by noise. The building was built in 2010, which means a very modern style with very nice-looking apartments. In the title I refer to the Light Rail currently under construction. With a station being built right outside the building, going to Downtown will be easy! "The Lyric" is located between Downtown Minneapolis and Downtown St. Paul in an Industrial neighborhood. There is a liquor store one block from the apartment complex, with McDonalds and Subway close by. It is located close to both University of Minnesota and University of St. Thomas, making this a nice place for students to live!
I believe you will have difficulty finding a better place to live than here!

My significant other and I searched for a long while to find the perfect apartment in the city. The Lyric has exceeded our expectations in all areas. We have both experienced apartment living prior to The Lyric. We were impressed during our very first point of contact with the office staff. They were attentive and not at all pushy to get us to rent. Once we saw the property, it sold itself. It is beautiful, very well-managed and extremely clean. We had zero complaints when we first visited and have been happy renters, 18 months and counting.
The Lyric holds themselves to very high standards. They aim to keep their renters satisfied with the level of service they provide. I have lived in other apartment buildings where the office staff is non-existent or very hard to get a hold of and where maintenance takes days to respond to anything..even urgent matters. At The Lyric, the office staff holds regular hours, makes sure that they are accessible and are both friendly and warm. Maintenance responds to requests on usually a daily basis, but from our experience it's normally within a short time of our request for help. The staff at The Lyric, alone, is one of the main reasons we wanted to sign another lease. They are phenomenal. Some other positives: spacious beautiful apartments with large floor to ceiling windows, unique amenities like a roof-top outdoor movie theater, a generously sized workout room with a variety of equipment open 24 hrs, several community rooms to hang out in including a party room where large events can be held, yoga/hip hop and other onsite classes offered as well as community art shows regularly scheduled on the first floor. Lastly, of any place we have ever lived, the community here at The Lyric is the most pleasantly diverse group of people. The range runs from small children of families to elderly and from all walks. My family and I enjoy this diversity and the friendly, inviting community we call our home at The Lyric.

Nothing comes closer to a perfect living space then the Lyric.
