Very personable and responsive staff; professional and respectful maintenance; beautifully designed eco-friendly apartments; amenities unmatched by any apartment community I have seen (amazing selection and versatility in uses); gorgeous views of the Twin Cities on the south side of the complex; ample storage in the apartment and a storage unit in the heated underground garage; a compassion for the arts in the decor, the architecture, the staff and the fact that they built a theater with a reception area in the building.

Located 10 mins from both downtowns the Lyric will be one of the most convenient location in the Twin Cities by 2014, as it will be half block from a newly completed light rail station and a block from a Nice Ride location. (looking forward to saving on the gas)

The rent is appreciable but with all of the amenities mentioned prior it is well worth the budgeting. Along with a pretty low stress environment. (did I mention the hot tub available about 7 months out of the year... Heaven!)

Lastly, on a more specific personal note... I am a professional performer working through out the Twin Cities and I have found that the space fosters a wonderfully creative environment. I feel inspired and productive when I am home and that's been a true asset to my career; to live in a place that I can create in.

I love coming home!

The Lyric is modern in style and amenities. A great mix of people live here and a sense of community is deliberately fostered by the management team. As a dog lover I especially enjoy all the happy dogs who live here. The social spaces are really great and host weddings, parties, art sales and concerts. Yet my own apartment is remarkably quiet and private. Everyone who lives here is eagerly awaiting the launch of the Green Line light rail with the Raymond Avenue Station right out front. Note that all the light rail construction near the Lyric is completely done. In the meantime the Metro Transit bus service is excellent. The neighborhood is known for its population of artists and seems to be drawing new and interesting shops and restaurants. I think it's a great place to live!

I have been at the Lyric almost 2 years and I love it. The apartments are spacious with quality amenities. I have a huge closet which easily fits my clothes and sewing stuff. I love having my own washer and dryer. Appliances are top quality and the living area is beautiful with lots of large windows. This is the best value in town for size and amenities. Anything else comparable is much more costly. Maintenance is terrific with immediate response and well skilled. I have found the office staff to be extremely pleasant, responsive and helpful. The building is beautifully maintained, and quiet. The exercise room is great and there are several beautiful common rooms for meetings or gatherings. It will also be exciting when light rail starts up with a station a block away. Easy access here to just about every where in the Twin Cities.
Management is not helpful, many clauses in the lease, came home to a man sleeping in the front door one night. Rooms are nice, hot tub is always dirty, workout room is commonly broken.

The only good thing about the apartment is the Location.
Most units are old and floor squeak when walking,Insufficient heating system,and  new management doesn't seem very keen on Work order requests.
My apartment got flooded with bad management. Stay away from this crazy apartment and save yourself the stress.

Lived here for 2 years and enjoyed it. Perfect for a quiet place to live in an excellent location and the price is amazing. I toured all the apartments around this place and settled here since it was the cleanest (stay away from the 2 across the street!). The walls are thinner so you can hear the floors creak or slight noises, but I haven't lived in an apartment where you can't hear your neighbors. I would highly recommend if this place meets your needs.
A quiet community. Cozy but functional apatments. Attentive staff. Laundry machines either dont work or double charge you frequently. Otherwise no real complaints.

I and my family lived in Rose Hill apartments several times for short and long terms. I should say the fact is that the officer Tony treated me and my family respectfully. She tried to help us by any means. So, I and my family are grateful to her forever. For this reason I also recommended some of my friends who were graduate students to live in Rose Hill apartment. The other staff that I do not recall his name was also helful. In general, Rose Hill is a good and quiet place to live.

This is the first apartment I ever lived in. I loved it. Toni basically became my aunt. And I can't remember the name of the maintenance man but he was always available, very consistent about keeping the place clean and his smile was always welcoming. The neighbors were either college/graduate students, or young parents. Which I loved. It's like 10 minutes from EVERYTHING. I think I woke up to drunk people outside my window twice in the year I lived there which is saying a lot. And the rent is perfect.

This place has a wonderful maintenance man. Fast to respond and friendly. The apartments are upkept well and pretty modern looking. The parking is hard in the winter because you can't park on the street and there is not enough parking in the lot. All of the common areas are nice, but there are really no amenities besides the fitness center.

We had a house and because of my health we had to sale our home.
My sister, her husband and puppy said move here!!! We did. It's handicap accessible. The management has be wonderful in helping with my needs.

At Lyndale plaza Apts you not only get very well thought out apt homes with the very best of living spaces and beautiful appliances and crown molding and the feel of living in a home but the grounds are very well kept and lovely to look at all year round. The neighbor hood is growing with new eateries and stores schools lake and nature center walking paths and handycap friendly everywhere ! I can truly say "there's no place like home!!

The location is ideal for anyone looking to live or work in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area as it is right off both 35W and 62 and just a mile from 494. Just minutes to downtown Minneapolis or out to more rural suburbs, its the perfect in between. Within easy walking distance are several delicious restaurants, a gym and grocery stores.  

Not only is the building ideal, but the people who keep it going are great. From the leasing agent to the maintenance personel everyone is there to help and make living at Lyndale Plaze a breeze.

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review: Good Dwelling is a great place to live.  Beautiful modern building and amazing staff!

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review:
Ever since management switched to Level 10 Management, my experience at Good Dwelling has been terrible.

Packages get stolen regularly, management is unresponsive and unhelpful with any situation, public spaces are not taken care of, absolutely no sense of community and taking care of shared things in this place. Even the carts to bring in groceries get stolen.
 
I’ve talked to other residents who’ve had their cars broken into and hit, and unsurprisingly management does not do anything. 

Spend a little more money and go elsewhere. I have never been happier to move out of a place.

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review: Set up an in person tour, just to wait around for 2 1/2 hours and not be shown anything. Called and emailed multiple times, and no response. This happened about 4 days ago, and I still haven’t gotten any type of email or call or text back about the missed tour on their part. Was hoping this was going to be a great place to move in and was very excited but now I see staff are very unprofessional.

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review: Everyone in Minneapolis knows about Eat Street, but people need to know of Good Dwelling, a brand new building. The staff is super friendly and the updated units are a really good deal $/sq foot when compared to other units around town. Can’t beat the location!

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review: Now with renovations mostly completed, Good Dwelling is perfect. It has the best views on Eat Street of downtown Minneapolis, wonderful sized balconies, new appliances, floors, granite counters, etc. I like the location in Whittier close proximity to everything including highways a well equipped fitness center. Management and staff so far are friendly and responsive. I think anyone interested in an apartment in Whittier, Uptown, or Downtown should check out Good Dwelling!

apartmentName: Good Dwelling: Live Your Best Life!
review: Moving from the East Coast. Been searching far & wide for an apartment complex with a little bit of customer service. Ethan (the manager from what I understand) was so easy to deal with and answered every single question. He was really in the know about the happenings in Minneapolis. Flew up, met him, and he gave me a detailed layout of the area surrounding this property. After several months of getting treated like just another tenant, Ethan talked to me in a kind and welcoming manner. I am eager for my move in day later this year!
The new management, Redtail Residential, is pretty bad. Ignores maintenance requests. Don't recommend renting here.
New management that took over in fall 2022 is extremely careless and lazy. Doesn't respond to emails, takes over a month to deal with a maintenance request, doesn't clean the building... Avoid.

Red Tail has taken over. There is no response from management or VERY rarely. The whole acquisition has been horrendous. Homeless sleep in the entry way and stairwell. Snow removal is not done. The maintenance team tries to work with what they have but get no support and the "fixes" are done with super glue and jerry rigging. I highly recommend you look elsewhere.

As a warning, every picture you'll find online for this building is for the largest, nicest apartment they have. Due to early COVID restrictions, we weren't able to view the apartment in person. Upon asking for pictures of the apartment, we were sent to their website where we looked at what was described as the apartment we thought we'd get (the same pictures they have everywhere else). Low and behold on moving day we have signed for the smallest, dingiest apartment I've ever been in. Should I have done more due diligence? Absolutely. Was it underhanded how this apartment was presented before we signed it? In my mind, absolutely. 

I can't walk into the kitchen without shimmying past the refrigerator which blocks the doorway. This apartment hasn't been updated in a long time and it is showing. The apartment clearly gets a new coat of paint after every resident, since the poor job they did sealed all windows shut (this was in the summer and there's no A/C mind you, we were told to use a screwdriver to open it), sealed several cabinets shut, sealed a doorway shut every time it was closed if it was warm out, and is peeling and bubbles up everywhere. The plumbing is a disaster as both sinks and the tub have had to be repaired in the first 9 months. The electrical outlets are few and far between, with almost no available outlets in the apartment, and none of them are three-prong so good luck using an extender. The bathroom has the ugliest blue fixtures and its radiator takes up a quarter of the floor space. The building has a new gang tag spray painted on it all the time. I could go on and on about how much stress and anger this building has cost me, but instead I think I'll just move out. 

2/5 for everything above, although for positives I'll note that the location would be nice (if it wasn't for COVID shutting around it down), the price is great, and the maintenance team was always helpful. I just wish I didn't have to meet them as many times as I did.
It does not provide security for your packages, I have had 3 packages stolen in less than 6 months and nobody answers for that!
This is a new building complex. Very excited to move in. The staff has been wonderful working with me to make my transition easier.

They allow outside contractors to enter apts without supervision, Just given the keys to come in. Don't tell you they have been in the apt, you just kind of find out when you see something has been done.

Terrible management. They are extemely irresponsible, rude, worst customer service. They do not contact you to let you know the status of your application, they’re always closed, they never answer the phone. Would not recommend to anybody.

No garage parking since September of 2018.
No walk-in closets.
No manager onsite. 
No clubhouse in the building. 
No dishwashers.
Onsite laundry is not sufficient for building size – 2 washers and 2 dryers for 36 units. Laundry room is not accessible by the elevator due to parking garage being closed. Often machines are broken, so you have to take laundry to a laundromat. 
The entry ways are not controlled. People often block doors open for hours at a time, including people who work for the management company. Door entry system at the front door does not work. 
Elevator often breaks down. It also stops on every floor, no matter what button you push. 
Management will not renew leases. After the first 1 year lease, they will insist you stay on a month to month lease. This is so that they can raise rent prices frequently. 
When you call for a repair in your apartment, you will not be given notice of when the repair will take place. Repair people, even if they are from an outside company, will be given the keys to your apartment and will enter your apartment without supervision from management or notification.
The area in the back of the building does not get cleared of snow and ice in the winter – this makes it treacherous just to take out the trash. 
Heat is supplied by a boiler. It will often reach 80 degrees or warmer in the winter months, even though you set the thermostat at 72. Windows ice over and freeze shut.

My rental experience at Verso Apartments was the worst I’ve ever had.  This is a privately owned building that is managed by Minnesota Apartments LLC. The utilities are not included in the rental price, and averaged above $200/month for a 411sq foot studio. The monthly cost for both utilities and rent exceeded the price of comparable units in apartment buildings with nice amenities— this building has absolutely no common space.

Because the building was under construction last spring, and I was moving from out of town- I regrettably signed the lease without viewing the unit.

First, they initially misrepresented the size of appliances as full sized, when they are miniature. The management stated they were given incorrect information by the owners and provided a parking space for half-price to make-up for the mistake. When I moved in everything was dusty from the construction, and painting tape was still up in some areas. I didn’t complain, because the apartment was brand new.

Secondly, the brand new temperature control unit began to malfunction within the first month. My air conditioner would drip excessively and short circuit— sometimes switching to heat unprompted. After numerous maintenance requests, the problem was never fixed. Each time I was told they couldn’t tell what was wrong. I had to live in constant anxiety that the AC would switch to heat while not at home because I have an assistance animal.

Lastly, upon moving out I clean the apartment exceptionally well,  leaving it more clean than when I moved in. I had art up on my walls, and filled the holes with patch & paint. Regardless, they took my entire deposit for a cleaning fee, and then charged me an additional $720 to paint.

As a person with a disability I am used to life being unfair— but this place functions outside of normal business ethics.

I lived here for two years. The price for the area and amenities was fantastic. Management was quick to get back to me with a response. The biggest reason I left was safety. I know they are making adjustments. My car had been broken into multiple times. I had packages stolen as well. The gas station across the street unfortunately can get a little interesting at nighttime. Overall, it was a great place to live.

Where to start…I’ll start this with the construction in the building that is ongoing for a majority of the lease I signed for. The construction is so loud, I can’t even sit in the apartment with loud music on, so many days I have to leave my apartment for hours on end just because of the renovations. I got the room next to the renovations, you think they would let me know it remodeled and will be under construction. On top of the issues, which these are few of many, the biggest is anytime that I’ve tried to figure out solutions with this company, maybe to move rooms or terminate the contract, they won’t do anything to help, besides say the noise will go away(it’s gotten worse) or I can pay for two months and the $1300 fee to break a lease. Shady

This has been my home for the past 2 years and I can honestly say it is one of the best you’ll get for the price you pay. Sitting on the edge of the North Loop literally surrounded by Breweries and Cider Halls I never had to worry about ubering. Just 2 blocks from Target Field station I was able to take the train to work everyday and basically be dropped off at my front door. I was bummed the Pandemic shut down the Fillmore before I could see a show. With it being across the street it made for a perfect opportunity to maybe pre-game with friends then walk over. Awesome skyline view from the rooftop for night caps. I loved hearing the fireworks from the Bomba Squad hit home runs from my couch while I watched on TV. Street parking is super cheap! Like $3 let you park all day.  My only gripe would be the Holiday across the street. I know it sounds convenient to have but honestly it was swarmed with Homeless and beggars and the occasional Drug addict tweaking in the bathroom. The door system up front could be better executed  to allow guests in to use the call box. I’m told that is in the works. Overall it’s a pretty decent place to live if you want the City life  experience without paying the Price for the City Life. Enjoy!

My husband and I have loved living at District 600 for the past 3 years. Location cannot be beat. Price is excellent for the area.  Staff is always very attentive to cleanliness & safety --something we came to truly appreciate in 2020. Would definitely recommended to a friend!

I've lived here for 3 years and I love it. It's in a great location, just 1 block away from Target Field & Target Center, & the light rail train. Just a couple blocks away from some great restaurants in the North Loop. Breweries basically surround the place, if you're into good craft beer/seltzer/cider. A few blocks away from concert venues like First Avenue & 7th Street Entry and Fine Line. Plenty of things to do very close by. There's a Holiday gas station across the street which is a nice convenience. The building itself is 3/4 years old so everything is nice and new. The residents I've known the last 3 years have all been friendly. They have a nice rooftop room with tvs, couches, a fireplace and kitchen that any resident can use to throw parties or events, with a nice outdoor roof deck with lounge chairs and bbqs, all for free. There's a workout center, which is small but hey, it's there if you need it. The staff has been nice to me the whole time, I'm not sure why there are reviews saying otherwise, because that definitely has not been my experience. Very friendly and attentive. I even referred my co worker to move in (you also get a $500 reference fee for referrals). Overall, I enjoy living here, and it's very reasonably priced especially downtown and in the North Loop. Love it!

I throughly enjoyed my experience living here, the staff was always super helpful and friendly and handled my requests and questions in a polite and timely manner. It was a convenient place that was close to everything I needed, which was nice because I didn’t need or have a car while I lived there. 

The building was always kept clean and super tidy and if there was a spill or an odor, it would be gone within the next day. 

I would recommend for young people/couples that enjoy the DT/north loop night life. Oh they also had some really cute puppies living there with residents, so that was a plus to always see them around as well!

The buildings here are very old and have been in need of a face lift for a while. However, rent is cheap and the new management has been courteous and doing all they can to improve things. They have been slowly implementing changes and are investing in updating basic safety of the apartments (recently they have been installing sprinklers and fire alarms). 

However, these new improvements do come at a cost. As someone that primarily studies in and is in a graduate program where instruction is mainly over Zoom/online, the amount of noise and interruptions from construction has been very disruptive. Understandably, construction takes time and doesn't always follow a communicated schedule, but there have been times where I have had to rearrange my apartment to accommodate construction that gets delayed, sometimes up to the following week. Additionally, though the walls are decent, the doors are metal doors that don't completely fit the doorframe, and therefore allow excessive noise from the hallway/the apartment across from me to creep in. When my neighbor across the hall decides to play his music, I can clearly hear every note and beat. Additionally, since these apartments are old and dilapidated, it takes maintenance quite some time to get around to fixing things because of the sheer volume of things that need to be fixed that the previous management did not address.

Overall, the management is nice and I appreciate their sincere efforts to improve the apartments. Additionally, they kept rent the same for this year. However, the noise from these improvements is incompatible with my lifestyle described above. If you are someone who uses an apartment as just a place to sleep, go ahead and rent; however, if you are someone who spends most of their time inside their living space, wait a few years to rent, once major construction issues have been fixed.

Lived here for a year.

As you can find, the rents in here are relatively cheap compared to the others. Just think of a cheap hotel you can imagine.

So the general conditions of the apartment are below the average:
1) Plumb issues.
2) Out of order washing machines that nobody cares.
3) No ventilation at all.
4) Water outage, power outage happen sometimes and it took a time to fix it. 
5) Some bugs.
6) Sometimes you can see the brown waters.

I am not lying anything about the issues above.
Good location close to downtown.  Close to bus and free off street parking.  Clean and fresh apartments. Lots of places to eat and coffee shops are a close walk.
clean and quiet with a nice layout.  Close to downtown Minneapolis and freeways.  Shopping steps away and places to eat.

Have been living at the Marie Antoinette for three years. It is a beautiful building and the management company has been attentive. Street parking is never an issue. There are less amenities than other luxury apartments in the neighborhood but the units are spacious and pretty.

The Stinson Apartments in Saint Anthony offers a comfortable and stylish living experience with a thoughtful design that maximizes space and creates a luxurious atmosphere. The open floor plans allow for seamless flow between the living areas, while the large windows provide stunning views and ample natural light. The finishes and fixtures are of the highest quality, from the well-appointed kitchens to the spa-like bathrooms.

My cat absolutely loved the large windows in our apartment. It was the perfect spot for her to lounge and watch the world go by. We were lucky enough to always enjoy golden hour in our unit. The large windows allowed for stunning views of the sunset that bathed our living space in warm, inviting light.

The apartments are immaculately clean and well-maintained, and the management team is friendly, kind, responsive, and committed to quality. Maintenance requests are fulfilled promptly, ensuring that the apartments remain in excellent condition. The convenient and vibrant neighborhood offers plenty of amenities, making it easy to explore and enjoy the surrounding area.

As one of the first tenants to move into the apartment, we were fortunate to experience the pristine condition of this new construction. It was first available in March of 2022.

The only reason we are leaving is due to a job relocation, and we sincerely wish we could have stayed longer. This place even left our cat pondering why we left... she's definitely purr-plexed. Looks like she's feline pretty betrayed! Extra treats will be given until further notice.

Overall, we appreciated how the management team was always welcoming and went above and beyond to ensure our stay was enjoyable. We valued how maintenance requests were fulfilled promptly, and how the apartment complex remained immaculately clean. We highly recommend the 3725 Stinson Apartments to anyone seeking a well-designed, convenient, and luxurious living space.

The office lady is rude and isn't willing to work with you. They lost my rent check and I still had to pay all the extra fees, and get a mark on my rental history. The maintenance guys either complain about having to come fix something, take forever to even do it. And/or Jerry rig all of it. Inside of the Apt. isn't worth the money. Raise rent every year. Your paying for location. But the neighbors mind their own business. That's a perk.

Lived here for a year and outside of little nitpicky things we enjoyed the building and mostly the people in it.  You WILL hear people above you milling about and you WILL hear music from neighbors from time to time.  But mostly tolerable.

The on-site staff and the on-call maintenance guys are absolutely terrific.  They're friendly and always keep the place as clean and functioning as possible and any issues are usually dealt with within a day.

Laundry room is pretty mediocre as some of the machines just don't work very well and/or are dirty. $1.25 to wash, $1.00 to dry.  It's not completely terrible and it's functional but most of the time just easier to go to the laundromat.

Don't bother with the extra money for off-street parking (unless you can get lucky enough to snag a garage).  It's on an upper tier and so you have to walk all the way to the end of the building, around the dumpsters and fencing and then all the way back to your car.  You're not much safer back there but it might be slightly better in the winter (since Minneapolis doesn't care about side street plowing or maintenance).  If you live in the front, you might prefer to park on the street where you can always have an eye on your car.

The biggest problem with this place is across the street.  It's cheap rent and already furnished units so the people there are... less than respectful.  Talking and loud gatherings go on all night.  Every single car has bass thumping at any point during the day or night. They love to use the turnabout in our building for temporary parking.  The level of noise and yelling is intolerable and seemingly constant. To top it off, they "remodeled" the outside last fall and painted the building bright pink with giant (and I mean GIANT) white numbers.  It's really an eyesore.

This apartment is the worst place I have ever lived. The walls are incredibly thin - I could hear EVERYTHING that happened in my neighbors apartment. I knew more about some person I had never seen than my own family. The washers/dryers are constantly broken and not fixed for weeks at a time. The elevator was out for over a month at one point. They also changed the parking lot from free surface parking to $50 a month and parking on the street isn't easy especially in the winter. My move out experience was the worst experience I've ever had.
This apartment is poorly soundproofed. Not recommended.

Rent is way too high for what they offer and supervisor provides incorrect information and is not alway available when she should be.
The appliances in the apartment are dated and break down very often.

They have nice management who swift to update you on the happenings in and around the facility. Maintenance is fast and prompt and its nearness to the light rail makes communication easy and comfortable.
Maintenance is great and fast and you get a lot of room for the price. There's street parking if you opt of a parking contract and the light rail is super close. Overall, I really like living here.

Can it get better than this? Stephanie in the office made things so simple and understandable for our,out of state move here to the twin cities. We were shown many apartments in our price range byt none quite fit the image we had in our mind. She listened to our wants and needs as we toured and we ended up at our current unit which fit our lifestyle to the T and wasn't that much more than what we'd wanted to spend originally. The Loring grove apartment building has its own Majesty and I cant wait to see how she helps to develop the neighborhood.
Close to schools, parks, & grocery stores. Great starter place.
I absolutely love this place! It’s central to just about everything and the price is just right. With friendly staff and maintenance you can’t go wrong. Give these guys a call!
Over the pandemic, Stephanie has worked with me with different payment programs and options. I am now going on my third year living in the community and don't plan on leaving anytime soon!

I love Oak Grove Downtown! I just renewed for my 4th year and am very happy with my apartment. The management (Stephanie & Khari) and maintenance (Tony) are very friendly and willing to go above and beyond to ensure every resident is happy from timely email responses to 24/7 accessibility for maintenance to upgrades/renovations upon request. The location is perfectly central for city living and the layouts are unique. The management recently changed - so any bad reviews should be given another shot!

10/10 recommend.

Deeply regret living here. My friend had a good experience so I did not listen to the negative reviews or the C- Better Business Bureau rating. Don't make the same mistake.
This company never missed a chance to charge for anything, meaning I paid way more over the course of my time there then my actual monthly rent. I am certain my deposit will never make it to my forwarding address. They were 100% out for my money and nothing else.
The nice location is not worth dealing with shitty office employees and hidden fees. Live somewhere with a good reputation and don't give these people any more money.
**Edit: Never received my deposit and am currently going through the Dept of Revenue since they never sent my CRP.

Instead of working with me when I lost my job they excited me! I had their money they just wouldn’t tell me how I could pay it! Instead they ignored me!!! I even Explained my situation early in the month and about 2 weeks later I was Served with eviction papers! This place doesn’t care about their residents they just want your money!

Moved in only a couple months ago but it has been great. Lots of great amenities, friendly residents, fantastic staff. Jenna, the building manager, seems to know every resident by name. Very good location, close to pretty much anything you would need.

Only drawback so far is they just started the process of replacing both elevators. One at a time over the course of the next 6 months or so. Though it has so far surprisingly been essentially a non-issue.

I absolutely would recommend the Edina Towers to anyone looking to move.

I have been at the Edina Towers for 7 years and I just love it. It is conveniently located, has beautiful amenities, and my apartment is the quietest home I have ever had in my life.

The maintenance manager is the best, and the manager is highly professional, friendly, and helpful.

If you are looking for apartment living in the Southwest Metro, please visit the Edina Towers!

I tried to schedule a tour from out of town and they would not respond to my emails and are not open on Satudays or Sundays. If there management does want to accommodate a visit, I can only imagine how poor they treat their residents.

This apartment is great. the amenities which includes free movie rental, free tanning beds, Underground park, pool, party room, great views from balcony, ect... all in which singles or families can enjoy.

Way too overpriced! Moved into a dirty apartment. WAY too much theft in this area! “Free” WiFi is SLOW and always out of service!!! The new door system they had installed never works! And you have to email them telling them it’s out of service, no one is proactive here. Bedrooms are small and the walls are paper thin (you can hear every conversation and the people walking above you!) Don’t let their “new” amenities trick you!

Want to live in a place under continuous construction? A place where management gives you less than 18 hour notice telling you to move all your furniture so they can put in an A/C (and then never shows up and makes you do it over again 5 days in a row)? Want a place where they will do construction on the evenings and weekends without warning you in advance? Want a place where they take away your use of the laundry room for months on end and make you take it out? Then this is the place for you!! Management won't answer questions. They just don't care. Gotta get those renovations in to suck more $$$ from future residents. Don't fall for it - their A/C isn't enough to cool the entire apartment. Go somewhere else while you can.

Park Glen is a wonderful place to live. I love everything about it. Chris, Payton,
Olivia and Tobias can not be beat. Everything is well kept up and clean.. couldn’t be happier here
Responsive front desk staff. My only complaint is how hot the 1st floor units get due to the heated garage and hallways. That and there are never poop bags at the dog park

Safe, quiet, good location. Annoyances include rent getting jacked up with new ownership. Overall probably competitively priced for what it offers, and location really is great. Generally have had good experiences with office as well, though not always.

The location is great, the walking trail is amazing, management is nice, and maintenance fixes requests in a timely manner. Only downside is how warm the apartment has been in the winter. Can solve it by opening windows but it’s a little annoying. Overall nice place to live!

We have lived here almost 6 months now and it has been a great apartment. Good location, safe, and maintenance is fast to respond. As long as they don’t raise our rate we will be staying here a long time.

The apartment community has some great amenities. Spacious apartments, plenty of layout options, and some are renovated if you want a more current look. There is unfortunately little insulation between above and below apartments, so you should expect to hear your upstairs neighbors - especially if they have heavy feet. You can also unfortunately hear TV noise through the floor/ceiling, as well as dogs barking at all times. In general, it is a decent apartment and the management and staff are great, it's just noisy.

Kenwood Gables was built over 25 years ago, however, with the updates and the location (which is superb) it can't be beat!  We have washers and dryers (in unit),  three major bus lines right outside our door, underground parking, air-conditioning.  What more could a renter ask.  Did I mention workout room and parties?!

Apartments here are so nice! They keep everything so well maintained and the office staff are just the best, just two women who I have become really good friends with. My apartment is huge and the location is perfect, I even have a great view of the city and just one mile to lake of the isles. It even comes with high end whirlpool appliances. I couldn't have asked for a better apartment here in Minneapolis!

As usual, Solhem knocked it out of the park with the design, layouts, and amenities for this building. I am not an employee, but rather a long-term renter, and I want to say something about management, too: you will never find kinder people. The policies are, like all policies, in place to define the community parameters, keep peace, and preserve the quality of the apartments. Sometimes, people only respond to consequences to their wallet, hence fees. I do not mind them because I try to be responsible to the community, and at all times in life, I understand that when I screw up, that's my responsibility. If you enjoy walkability, cheery people, stunning views, and well-maintained apartments, then welcome home!

I moved in in June 2021 and have only had positive experiences at Borealis. Management is awesome and on top of their stuff, they do have strict rules about some things but it's to keep the building clean and safe for everyone (e.g., clean up your indoor pet messes, clean up broken glass, break down boxes appropriately). to me, it's basic "living with other people" stuff.  Through the quarterly events and weekly yoga classes I have met many of my neighbors and we get together a couple times a month for drinks! my apartment itself is gorgeous and the only complaint I have is most of my windows don't open, but otherwise i have extremely happy!

Don’t move in, I’m glad I left that building!! There is a reason why this apartment has such a fast turn-over rate and no one stays for long. You’ll feel like you’re living in a dorm again, and management is the RA. They will nickel and dime you with hidden fees and add arbitrary tack on’s to your bill. This is not a good deal, there are better, bigger apartments everywhere for cheaper. Management sends out angry emails and post signs everywhere. No candles are allowed, so they sent out an email. If you leave anything out in the hallway they will essentially cite you. There was a passive aggressive post saying if you didn’t break down boxes in recycling they will charge you a fee. If your items are too big for the trash, they will also bill you. If you take your dog on the roof and it pees, they said they will monitor cameras and then also fine you $250. They sit and watch security cameras to big brother all the residents, and yet the building has had multiple break-ins and thefts!  Just don’t live here, it will only get worse... if there are a lot of openings, that’s because people left.

Rooftop is a great spot, has good lounge chairs and fire pits and grills.  There is a $175 charge for garage parking, $125 for all utility flat rate, and also an extra charge for large item garbage disposal. Apartment management seems uptight about residents hanging up any items, and they inspected my place too closely when I moved out for every little scratch. Be aware they'll try to tack on as many charges as possible when you move out. The building was mostly quiet while I lived here, but became too expensive so I left.

I've moved four straight years from apt to apt and I think I finally found a place to stay. The area is wonderful and getting better. The location is close enough to downtown to feel the energy of the city but far enough away for when rest and relaxation is wanted. The building has wonderful amenities that are kept clean and in fine working condition. The community and the people are very open and make the complex feel homely. Very pet friendly, I almost feel outnumbered because I don't have a dog. Simply put, this will be home for a few years at least.

Great place to live! Great people, perfect location. We love living here at Oaks Station Place. Any time we have a question, Jess is available with an answer. Nicole addresses any issue we may have with speed and efficiency. We love it here. Plus, the Venn Brewery is a nice draw!
Nice apartment,Nice people  Very clean,quite and best staff and I life this place almost 6 years i really like it
Thank You We were pleased with the prompt response to our maintenance request.  Requesting assistance is easy online. The work was done quickly and efficently.
Amazing as usual Quick and thorough fix as usual, even if it was New Year’s eve day :) Thank you all!

Great Place to live! We have been living in Oak Station Place for five years!  We love the location and its easy access to downtown, the Light Rail, and so much more.  The people who share the building with us are pleasant and good company. The staff here are easy to relate to and respond quickly to concerns when raised.

Great team makes a great place to live! The Oaks team has always been responsive to any issues. The common areas are kept clean and the landscaping is lovely. My dog is welcomed at the office for a quick hello and a treat. Jess and Savanah are super friendly and easy to work with.
I love to live here! The management is awesome, the neighbors are kind & warm. It feels like home :)))
Great service Very happy with it as always. Helpful and quick service!

I lived here for 4 years and overall it’s a good place to live
Pros:
- Service requests are handled quickly and usually fixed the first time
- Safe - they have a security guard nights and weekends
- Convenient for buses and light rail
- Great neighborhood - close to lakes, parks, Minnehaha falls, and trails
- Great neighbors
- Manager is nice and good too - the one who is manager as of this review - overall willing to work with you if you have issues
- Amenities are great - Theater room, community car, fitness center, community room and patio area that can be rented for events, Luxer System for package delivery, underground parking (if you can get in, there’s usually a waitlist)
- It’s pretty quiet there - I hardly ever heard anything from my next door neighbors nor those above me (I know others have left a review that you can hear everything….I don’t know where they got that, because I’ve never had an issue, see below for my one exception to this)
Cons:
- A fellow resident’s apartment was flooded and I don’t think they handled it well as they could’ve
- Limited parking in the parking lot - and some spots are taken from Venn customers that don’t read that it’s permit parking only
- I was originally told that utilities are just my apartment - but they are actually split (gas, water, and sewer) between all units depending on square footage. This is a minus regardless…but especially when you move out - when I hadn’t lived in the apartment for a month, I was still responsible for utilities which came out of my security deposit. So despite not living in the apartment, I still had a bill since it was split between all units
- Speaking of noise - complaints about a very loud barking dog never appeared to be taken seriously and that was really frustrating 
- If you break your lease early, you have to pay for it. Not only do you give 60 days notice and have to pay for that 60 days - that part I understand. But you also have to pay an additional 2 months of rent as a penalty. A company like this is big enough that they don’t need my money for an extra 2 months. That’s 4 months of rent, which is a lot and ridiculous in my opinion. Life happens and sometimes people need to leave earlier than expected (my lease was up in December and I couldn’t wait that long and when it was coming due the previous December, I wasn’t thinking I’d move anytime soon). This is the main reason it lost 2 stars. I wanted to try to email the owner, so I hope he reads this
Place is a joke. Residents have no priority for parking here they just keep reducing parking.
No Parking ever, place is a joke for the amount you pay a month

S Schuch

in the last week
Oaks Station Was a fantastic place to live. It was quiet, clean, and had a great community of people. It is incredibly pet friendly and dogs will have no shortage of friends. The amenities are very nice, particularly the community room and patio. The location is perfect with the transit center for easy commuting and the gorgeous biking/walking trails nearby. It was my favorite place I have lived and I would not have left if work had not taken us away from Minneapolis.

This is the perfect complex if you want a quick walk or bike to parkways & trails. Complex is close to public transit as well as stores, restaurants and has outdoor space with barbecue grill for personal or community events as well as community room & theatre room and your furry friends are allowed. The building is well maintained and staff are very friendly and helpful. Each unit comes with washer & dryer, dishwasher, central air/heat. My unit has huge walk-in closets. I call it my little Park Place in the city.

My first reaction when viewing my apartment unit was how small it was for a one bedroom and not too happy about the dark colored paint on walls which makes unit look smaller, but I have grown to love my little space. 

Positives:
The apartment complex is close to several parkways, trails, public transit, stores, restaurants, etc. Each unit has washer & dryer, central air/heat, building is pet friendly to all size dogs & cats, most of my neighbors are very friendly and courteous. Maintenance staff are very friendly and hard working. New leasing manager is friendly and so far seems to be a big plus to the complex. 

Complex has exercise room, community room, media room as well as wifi if you are in the right area of the building. Tenants pay for all utilities, water, sewer, trash, heat, electric.

Negatives:
The building for the most part is quiet but with every complex there are always a handful of people that make apartment living negative. 
Living by the parkway and public traffic also has it's negatives with a lot of people traffic that frequently hang out in complex front entrance. Rent goes up every year which is the norm now-a-days but I wasn't happy about the huge rent increase I received this year. Unit & Hallways need a good coat of new paint hopefully lighter colors so the complex doesn't look so dark & small. Apartment units carpets as well as hallway carpets need to be shampooed and front entrance needs to be converted where people cannot access the front entrance.

Oaks Station Place is the perfect place for me! The modern amenities and the VERY CLOSE proximity to the light rail only enhanced my pleasure in living at this community.  From the spacious apartments, to the very well decorated Community Room and Theater Room, the 2 (TWO!) dog runs and the great staff sets this place apart from other apartment complexes.  The staff knows you and makes you feel right at home!

I think for my first year living here, I could not BELIEVE that I lived here....lol

This place is a hidden gem in the south Minneapolis area. It's literally right off the light rail and bus transfer station, making it very nice for a work commute if a car isn't an option. The staff is great and very helpful. It's always so clean and any service requests are fulfilled in a day. It's pet friendly and they're always hosting events to meet your neighbors.

I have lived in the building a while. I really love it! The building does allow dogs which comes with the good and the bad. The bad, the landscaping and grass can suffer from so much urination. the good, you have a dog! I haven't noticed lots of noise from the dogs, but I have heard them. I mean... this is an apartment so you will sometimes hear your neighbors. The management seems to be trying hard to make the apartment very comfortable. Most people generally keep to themselves, but the outgoing neighbors are friendly. The maintenance of the building is taken care of by a husband and wife couple that are wonderful. They are super friendly and I look forward to seeing their smiling faces and helpful attitudes. The neighborhood is generally safe and I do not know of any incidents involving crime since I have lived here. The lightrail can bring some “undesirables” to the area, but keeping alert and aware will keep you safe. Speaking of the lightrail, this is a wonderful feature of the location of this property and the main reason I chose to live here. The lightrail is literally a couple of dozen steps from the front door. When I first moved to the area I thought the lightrail would be loud. I couldn't have been more wrong. If you are VERY quite in your apartment you might be able to hear the bell of the train, but generally I never hear the train. I'm trying to think of the bad parts of the building and if I had to pick one it would be the parking. Parking is only bad if you don't have a spot. Parking outside is very limited.

Overall, I would highly recommend this apartment complex to anyone working on or near the lightrail.

Visited complex. Overpriced units. TERRIBLE parking - no parking essentially other than long wait list. Soundproofing for outside noise was successful, but soundproofing should have been addressed inside. Lots of yapping dogs as we walked the corridors. Office staff does not answer telephone on weekends, and no one has returned my call three days later. Not worth it just to be on the light rail line.

Be @ axon is one of the worst apartments I have ever lived at. The actual apartment itself is great but the unit to unit noise is unbelievable. You hear neighbors from each side (music, conversations) and EVERY. SINGLE. STEP. the upstairs neighbor takes. I can even hear them sometimes opening/closing cupboards. For the rent we're paying I can't believe the insulation can be this bad. Staff is beyond unhelpful. An actual quote from an email I received from them: "sounds like regular apartment living!" And it might be. But even apartments I've been in that were less than half this price had better insulation. If sound is an issue for you PLEASE look elsewhere.

Terrible place to rent. The Greenway is gone with the light rail construction and they won’t reduce rent because of it. The grills haven’t been working for years. The garage keeps getting broken into. The building has been literally shaking from the construction. They promised community events every month when we moved in several years ago and that hasn’t happened.

I live in the divine alcove floor plan which is perfect size for 1 person.  Location is 2 blocks from lake calhoun and is on the greenway bike path.  I love that the apartment feels a bit secluded and overlook the trees and pool yet is minutes from Uptown.  Staff are always friendly and residents are great.  Only negative I have to say is the 10 pm close time for the pool and grilling area.  Other than that I have had a great experience at Be and would recommend the apartment.

In the 'be' building I walk down the hallways and it reads 'be' Dynamic, 'be' Amazing! When I enter the elevator it says 'be' Uplifted or in the party room 'be' social, in the fitness room 'be' fit! Our concierge can make any day sunny!  My beautiful studio apartment is walking distance to gorgeous lakes, a Whole Foods and restaurants.  My apartment has high ceilings, stainless steel appliances,and a stacked washer and dryer, like other many other places but I know you cannot find a more fun-loving community housed in an uplifting complex which makes this apartment my home.

When I first moved to Minneapolis I lived Downtown near the convention centre.  I had no idea where to go before moving up here from the south and found the first available reasonably (by my post college student standards) priced apartment.  I was miserable.  For the longest time when I rode my bike along Cedar Lake trail and the Midtown Greenway I would see this apartment building and think it was way to upscale and out of my price range.  
Fast-forward to a year later when I wanted to move into the Uptown area to be near more people near my age and this was one of the apartments I happened upon  while searching, never making the connection of it being the building I passed on the trail behind the building.  My roommate and I had multiple tours set-up for the day, but this was our first viewing, and we instantly  loved it.  The building itself is very new and feels alive.  Do you want amenities? Because this place has them like crazy.  While having access to all the areas like the gym and pool for this building (as well as free 'rentable' party rooms), you also gain access to the amenities over at the Calhoun Greenway building, including an indoor pool and sauna as well as multiple other rentable party rooms.  
The apartments themselves are very upscale.  With granite counter tops as well as kitchen islands and tons of cabinet space, you can make full use of the kitchen.  The bathrooms are nicer than any hotel I've been in with a very large soaking tub.  The closets are nearly as large as the dorms I had back in school.  
While not being in full-blown Uptown, I have actually found this to be much better than I thought.  Not only is rent significantly cheaper and more affordable, we have a much more peaceful area without being in the more suburban St. Louis Park.   Instead of having to deal with the terrible traffic near Lake street, we have easy access to our building with minimal traffic.  Whenever we want to go out, we can either hop on the greenway and ride into Uptown or walk if we're inclined.  With Lake Calhoun right there within sight, I have never had problems getting out and having a good time.  This is seriously the best area I've ever lived in, and I look forward to my continued residence.

Be@Calhoun is the place to be. Be@Calhoun is in a great location, it's near the chain of lakes, lots of great restaurants to walk. Although you are next door neighbors to uptown, you get the feel of a neighborhood. It is located right on the bike trail which provides easy access to downtown and most suburbs. They have lost of amenities. You have access to 3 pools, one of them is indoors you can enjoy all year round along with a hot tub and sauna. They also have a theater, tanning and several community areas which one of them is located on sixth floor giving you a great view! They are pet friendly. If you like pets but want to not be so close, they do offer on floor pet free. The staff is helpful and friendly. They take pride in making sure all the common areas are clean. Oh I almost forgot, for the days you don't want to jump on the trails to do your daily workout, they have 3 gyms. The equipment is new and they have  several different cardio machine, strength training machines and a great range of weights!  I have lived in several apartments, and i recommend this is the place to come see. You wont regret it!

Unbelievable!!! I've never seen management like this in my whole life! I moved in one of their studios at Minnehaha Ave two weeks ago, and my studio is full of cockroaches!!! Cockroach kingdom! I called them immediately (it was in the middle of the week) and they told me that they can't do anything before next Monday!!!! Heeey, next Monday!!!
That Monday is today, and guess what?! Nobody even showed up at my place to treat cockroaches!
As soon as I start to thinking that this can't be any worse, I called them again, and the girl who is working in the office, with some heavy Spanish accent, told me to come at 4pm, to speak with the owner about that. I was in front of their office at 3:55pm, and guess what, OFFICE DOORS ARE LOCKED!!!!
I read my lease, and it's clearly written that cockroaches should be treaten in 24 hours of notice! It's been all week, nobody even called or showed, or did anything!! 
And the worst of all of this that cockroaches are in my bed and clothes, and I personally tried to do everything to get rid of them, and there is nothing that works. 
I'm going straight to health department tommorow.

At first I was extremely excited to move in! The apartments were beautiful and new. I had let them know the date I was looking to move in but they didn’t notify me that the process was going to take longer. They provided misleading information during the process and once I was approved and about to sign they decided to more than double the deposit that was originally agreed upon. I was willing to work with them on the additional money for the deposit but they then informed me they would not be giving me the rent special anymore. All of this occurred after I paid the application fee and after they told me I was accepted. Overall they were very unprofessional to work with and I would not recommend anyone to work with them.

I lucked out when I found this location.  I came from out of state and I rented it without seeing it in person.  I was nervous about renting a place I hadn't seen and also just generally renting after owning a home for a long time.  These apartments are better than the apartments I remembered having in my youth.  I was worried about the noise from adjacent apartments.  But after living here for several years I will tell you that it's a pretty quiet building.  I very rarely notice my neighbors.  The top floor sky deck is beautiful.  I love it when I have people visit me from my home state.  They are always enamored with the sky deck and the amazing views of Lake Bde Maka Ska as well as the city views.

This is a great spot to live during the spring/summer months as it is located right across from lake calhoun. However, the current management of this property should be a big red flag if you are considering this location. The property management is virtually non-existant, with no feedback taken from the current residents and notices of any ongoing projects are only posted with flyers (typically only a day or so in advance) and they always come with delays. When looking at pricing, the property manager will make broad promises (that management is looking into allowing personal grills, that the laundry room will accept cards instead of coins only, that renovations to apartments will be minimally disruptive) however none of these are ever executed on and when talking to people at Kleinman, they are very unresponsive. They have priced out a number of current occupants without any regard to the community and the property manager never solicits recommendations or comments about noise disruptions.

Again, this place is great, and with the right price it can be a good value. however, be cautious when you are shown any apartment as what is promised on can be expected to have no execution or delivery.

You can't reach the manager via email or phone. Does not respond to either. 2 weeks in and still can't get her to add name for door access. I like the walk down from the 4th floor. Other requests are acknowledged and then nothing. 

I used to live here about 10 years ago with great management. Now, it's beyond bad.

REALLY regret moving here.

Also would like my packages but because NO ONE is ever in the office it's tough. I might have to call the emergency number just to see if anyone actually works here.

My wife and I lived at Oaks Hiawatha for 4 years and have just recently moved out as we purchased a home due to our growing family. We enjoyed living there! Friendly staff, respectful neighbors, large and like-new apartments, clean building and priced just right for what you get. There are not many amenities in the building, but that seems to be normal for city living. One thing that we will never forget.. a couple of months back our neighborhood was hit hard by storms and our building was without electricity for almost a full week. The staff kept a close communication with all residents, making sure everyone was okay and comfortable. They even gave every unit $200.00 cash to help stock our refrigerators again once the electricity was back up and running! Now, if that isn't awesome customer service, I don't know what is. The only downfall is there is a Snap Fitness attached to the building. We were on the 2nd floor and could hear when people would slam their weights down at any given time of the day or night. Other than that, we have absolutely no issues and we enjoyed living there and will continue to recommend Oaks Hiawatha to our friends and family. Thank you Oaks!

Be very careful with this one. Although, the location is outstanding and the building looks nice from a distance, there are many hassles here. First of all, be thorough when you read the lease as property managers have not been honest during discussion. Three property managers have come and gone in the last five months, and they all have been difficult. They also are frequently absent and don't answer the phone. Once you do reach a property manager, you'll have to ask two or three times before they follow through on sending someone to resolve a maintenance issue. Utilities are much more expensive here than other places of similar size in Minneapolis...especially air conditioning because they use wall units that aren't very effective, and you'll find that it is uncomfortably warm in the interior hallways during summer. The only option for high-speed internet access is CenturyLink. If you do move here, make sure to get a unit on the first floor as the elevator is a solid test for even the most patient souls. I remember a time when I was so excited to be calling this place home because of the location, and now I wish it never happened and can't wait till my lease is over.
Nice location. But very dated building. Dirty hallways, dirty grounds. Looks like it doesn't get vacuumed or swept ever. Only 1 elevator and laundry room. Friendly staff.

The apartments are quite dated, with ancient cabinets, ancient stoves, fridges that need to be repaired multiple times, knockdown style walls that are not even, and scratchy old carpet that is not pleasant to walk on.  The entire complex isn't level and leans slightly towards the east, which can make cooking things interesting as sometimes the pots do not want to stay centered on the stove. The windows leak to the point of freezing over during the winter.  

These are "smoke free" apartments, yet my apartment smells like cigarettes almost every single day.  Management has been made aware multiple times, and always "addresses" the issue, but it always comes back.  The range hoods and bathroom exhaust vents for various apartments are connected, so when someone cooks something awful, or is blowing cigarette smoke into their range you, you can bet it will end up in your apartment.
Laundry Room: There are times where for hours you will be unable to get a washer or dryer.  People leave them absolutely disgusting, as it is regular to find them filled with the previous person's hair, dirt, you name it. 

There are multiple issues with the apartment complex that cannot be overlooked.  The parking situation in the lot is dreadful.  They allow visitors to park there, even though there aren't enough spots for everyone who lives here to begin with. They advertise underground parking, but do not expect to get one of those spaces anytime soon.  (It took me 11 and 1/2 months to get one).  

Next is the trash chute.  It jams up for multiple days at a time, multiple times a month. The hallways and entry-ways will regularly smell like garbage due to these issues.  Another fairly common issue is plumbing problems.  At least once a month since we've moved in, we've personally encountered a plumbing problem, or have received notice from the building that water will be shut off to repair the pipes.  We had black water come out of the kitchen drains and pour all over the floor, carpet, etc due to these issues.  

Management has been fairly responsive to react to issues, although I've only had them fixed in a few situations.  It took almost 4 months of living here to get my toilet replaced when I had first moved in last April. 

Positives:  They are conveniently located, the bike room downstairs that was recently redone turned out very nice, and the apartments are very quiet due to the amount of concrete between each floor (although you will hear planes fairly regularly).

518E dishwasher I had a great experience recently. I work from home and was on a call when the maintenance guy came, and he quietly entered the apartment, fixed the dishwasher promptly, and now it works great. I didn’t get a chance to thank him, but it’s the guy with long hair, roughly 5 ft 5 inches. Very helpful, will thank him the next time I see him around the building.

Didn’t know anyone was in my apartment  It is nice that they came to fix things, but if I didn’t have a camera I would have no idea that anyone was in my apartment which makes me feel uncomfortable. The last maintenance person left a note saying they were there and what they fixed/di!

Every time I see an email come in from management I shudder....must be new rules. For instance, the pool used to be open 24/7 and now closes at sunset or 8:30 PM. The rooftop used to be open 24/7 and now strictly closes at 10 PM. They suddenly took away the paper cups from the PUBLIC coffee machine so you now have to bring your own and can't get any for your guests. You will pay $120+/month for a parking spot and then they will do garage cleaning that takes 3-4 days and they don't have any back-up option for you to park during that time....It is a beautiful building but this management company is ruining it. Advice to management: Stop making us feel like we live in a college dorm with all these rules. Everyone is fed up. We're all adults here!!!

My husband and I recently moved back to the Twin Cities and had a very short timeline in finding a place to live. We were so lucky to find Talo, especially because it crossed off all of the items on our wish list: spacious apartment (large kitchens!), heated garage, large fitness center (you won’t need an additional gym membership), close to downtown and highways (easy to get around), and most importantly a respectful, helpful and kind property management staff!!! There are so many more amazing amenities, that you have to see for yourself, and the decor is absolutely beautiful. We love it here! We toured all of the newer buildings in the area, and this one was the best by far!
The move was very quick and we didn’t have a lot of time to plan in advance, but everyone in the office was so responsive, helpful and attentive in helping us resolve any issues and answer all of our last-minute questions. Since we moved in, we have had to make a couple of minor maintenance requests, and the maintenance team is also fantastic and so efficient! 
I love the events that they organize for the community as well. It makes the place feel like a true home (apparently Talo means Home in Finnish)!
Just moved to this building and I have been so impressed by the amenities and staff! Clean , friendly and inviting building! High impressed!
It’s great, don’t see anyone, don’t hear anyone!  No one bothers you,   If you like peace and quiet this is the place
Flickering light The day after I submitted a work order the wall switch was discovered to be the cause and was quickly replaced the next day.

Excellent I’ve lived here for over a year and it’s lovely and mostly quiet.  The couple of times I’ve needed something fixed, they get it done, like, immediately.  Maybe the best responsiveness of any management ever.
Terrible management that is invasive. Owner as zero intent of recognition of any accountability.
Rachel is Amazing! The building is beautiful. The vibe was great. And Rachel is so so friendly and bubbly! Thank you!
Kitchen light fixed! Repair was swift, apartment was undisturbed, prompt helpful notifications on progress were delivered online, great service!
Staying here was such a good decision. The management team and the event coordinators are incredible

I have lived here for over two years now. 
While it seems value for money based on lower rents as compared to other properties around it, there is a good reason for it. The building smells of weed all the time. 
The apartments are often rented for Airbnb or through third party renters. The management claims no responsibility for the misbehaviour, noise or other issues with these kind of tenants. Mask policy is not enforced. Smoking and weed odit are ignored by management unless a tenant reports it (nothing done even then). Additionally, the management takes no responsibility for lost and stolen packages.

I would not recommend living here. I have been here for the 10 months, and there are many issues with the property. 
The price is cheap, but it is not worth it.

I was issued the wrong apartment unit. I have had my bike tires and lights stolen from a secured garage. There is a door handle to outdoor access in the back of the apartment that has been broken for at least 3 months without fix. Unacceptable.

Pros: the maintenance staff is fast, there is a nice green space upstairs with good study spaces as well, and management is friendly and quick to respond to issues.

The two bedroom apartment we stayed in was incredible! It was nice having a washer/dryer and great space in the bathrooms for a closet. The workout room was a bonus with a variety of equipment with the perfect view to outside. The location was very convenient with a short walk to campus and restaurants. The windows let the perfect amount of natural light in allowing us to relax and enjoy the day. I was VERY impressed with the management and staff. They were attentive to our needs and very accommodating! I would recommend The Arrow apartments to anyone looking for a single or double room!

I signed lease on march 2017. I was supposed to move in early September, however they notified resident a week before move-in date that they will have to postpone the move in for two weeks. they delayed another week. after that they delayed another week. Delayed 4 weeks of move in and when i moved-in, the apartment was filled with dust. took me two days to clean my place. They said that they would provide hotel when they announced the delay. They still took the rent money for September when people weren't able to move-in. homeless sleeps at lobby-they don't care. resident's car broke into multiple time-they don't care. Packages were stolen multiple times-they don't care. What they care is make people sign the lease and make sure they can't get out for a year. Make sure you ask resident what it is like to live here and you will get your honest answer.

Not only is the management incompetent but the quality of construction is appalling!  Hardware missing or falling off, exterior door does not lock! My father says the quality of the finish work is honestly the worst he has ever seen and he has been a contractor for 30 yers.  Forgot to mention that we could not move in when promised, twice.  One worker during business hours asked if i wanted to buy dope in the building!  Another stopped to ask if i had a smoke and sat smoking with a tenants for 20 min. Another worker was in the hall fixing ceiling and I could not walk by and he was rude about moving and then dropped Sheetrock all over me.
If you decide to rent with them, good luck.
prime place is an apartment that is located in prospect park which is near the university campus

I personally was treated with the utmost respect and patience by the Management. I was impressed by how professional and informational the tour was along with how well the management was able to maintain organization and remain efficient, despite their high demand and work load. Dispite slanderous outbursts and endless character defemation by media and the disgruntled.  I can see Prime Place will be a great place to call home.

To summarize the pre-move-in scenario, they lied to us about the finish date on three separate occasions bumping back the expected date by one week each time so we wouldn't sign a lease somewhere else and put us in a horrible position for the start of the school year.

About the apartments themselves-- with the furnished option, the "wardrobe" provided is about enough to store your socks and underwear but not much more. The two beds do not fit under each other, so most of the bedroom is simply unusable space. The finishing job is terrible-- as the first tennants, we have a chunk out of our kitchen vanity, multiple pieces of trim hanging off, paint smears on cabinets, and half-loose vent covers. The mattresses are so hard that we legitimately thought they were box springs and that the mattresses hadn't been delivered yet until we were told by the managers that they are in fact mattresses. The place has no full-time staff and no parcel delivery service, so your packages are stacked unceremoniously in the lobby where anyone could just pick them up and take them.

The general managers, Michael in particular, has been very apologetic and understanding of our grievances-- but there are many things he just can't change. The management company needs to buy new bed-frames, mattresses, and wardrobes. The building needs to have a dedicated mailroom to receive packages and a front desk at least during the daytime. 

In all, I would sincerely reccomend leasing somewhere else-- there are plenty of good apartments on campus.

Was told a week and a half before move-in that my room wouldn't be ready until "at most" 2 weeks after class starts. Then, I get an email saying we will get another notification whether it'll even be ready then. Some of my friends won't be able to move in until December. I can excuse the slow communication, there's one guy in charge of dealing with hundreds of angry people. Regardless, spent a month in a hotel, paying for an aprtment I couldn't live in.

Have a lawyer look over your contract if you're actually looking to live here for some reason.

Plugged in our coffee percolator that has worked fine everywhere else it has been used. Breaker tripped and smoke alarms went off, no smoke coming from the percolator but we could smell burning rubber. This has happened a couple times now, even without the percolator. As an electrical engineer the whole thing reeks of faulty wiring. We talked to Michael and he was super friendly, he had an electrician come in. Electrician looked at the breaker box, said "eh, it's fine" and left. The problem has persisted.

There is nowhere for package carriers to put your boxes. There is a pile of people's packages on the floor in the lobby, easily accessible by anyone because the doors aren't locked.

Calling the finishing job abysmal would be a compliment. Our countertop is out of alignment, so the trim above the cabinets hangs out the side. There's a paint smear on one of the drawers. The trim throughout the apartment is practically falling off. The bunkbeds provided don't fit under each other so a third of the bedroom is just unusable space. Provided drawer space is enough for your socks and underwear, good luck with the rest because the closet rack looks like it's going to collapse without any weight on it. There's a chunk of wood missing from the vanity in one of the bathrooms. The light fixture in one of the bathrooms is missing its cover. The matresses are so hard we're pretty sure they're box springs that the company is calling mattresses.

IF YOU ARE OVER 5'10" DO NOT LIVE HERE. PERIOD. I am 6'2" and these showers are so low that simply washing my hair is going to turn me into an Olympic gymnast by the end of this lease.

In conclusion, if you are a midget who doesn't care about severe risk of electrical fires, likes having your amazon boxes stolen, enjoys holes in your trim, and likes being sweet-talked to but doesn't care if customer service actually does anything, then this is the place for you.

The apartments are not ready. The lease was supposed to start on Sept.2 and after a month, my apartment is still not ready (most of the apartments are still not ready - they are in construction). Some friends could move in after a month, to realize that their AC unit cannot be controlled from the apartment... Their thermostat doesn't work and they cannot turn off the AC unit, which is really loud. Horrible management.

My review is similar to others who were angered at the fact that construction was delayed forcing the hundreds of students who signed leases with Prime Place to not know their living situation for the fall semester just weeks before it begins. However, I think you all need to know more about exactly what happened leading up to this decision. So I called Prime Place a week before the email was sent out to me and asked, is my apartment specifically going to be ready for move in on the correct date. They said yes, Mike, your specific apartment will be ready, although others will not be. This was in late July, around July 30th. On August 1st, the send me an email saying that that was not true, and that I needed to chose between 3 options. I won't bore you with all of them in full, but the first correspondence said this for option 2, the option I selected. "You can choose to have Prime Place find a place for you to live until your apartment is ready...". Seems to suggest that they would find a place for you to live for two months and then you get to move into Prime Place, right? Nope. Their second correspondence omits certain parts of the option that were in the first correspondence and essentially all it was is a termination of the lease. You might be think here, read things carefully before you give a response, but considering the fact that they lied to me about my apartment being ready, told me my specific unit which they knew was not going to be ready, was in fact ready, and then sent an email saying that option two would mean we would move back into Prime Place after two months, they deceived me. I know that by the time you're reading this construction is probably done. You don't have to worry about that. But what you will have to worry about is dealing with liars as property managers. You'll have to know that anything that they say has to be taken with a grain of salt. Maybe two grains. Management has proven to be unreliable and willing to sacrifice the security of its patrons when it is convenient to them. They didn't care about me as a lease holder, so just be careful before assuming they will do any different to you. 
Best of luck,
-Mike

I signed a lease with Prime Place at March 2017 and planned on moving in at 2nd September 2017 right before school starts. And now they just sent me an email told me I can't move into my apt until December, which means I will have no place to live for the whole semester. They only gave me two choices, I can either move in at December and they will give me 1500$ for the inconvenience, or I can just cancel my lease....After two days searching for places, I decided to choose the first option,  but all the sudden I received another email from them said they decided to cancel my lease because my contract doesn't have a guarantor which none ever requested me to provide in the first place. Overall, I think Prime place is an extremely dishonest company, which took advantage of students and parents.

I lived in Karinsplass Apartments for almost two years and very much enjoyed my stay there. I only moved out after finishing up a graduate program and searching for new work, else I would have stayed.

The location is exceptional for anyone studying or working in a nearby university or business. It's on a major bus line and close to the Seward Co-op. The immediate area is pretty safe, though a few blocks west (outside of the university area) is less-so. 

Management was, by and large, professional and reliable to work with. Maintenance and move-in/out procedures were seamless.
