The only logistical difficulty I had was with package delivery: delivery may not occur if attempted outside the limited office hours. I once had to bus to the post office to retrieve a package that failed delivery too often. 

My unit was spacious and in great condition, just like you can see in the profile photos. A great value for the reasonable rent back then (2009-2011).
Since there has been new management for the Park and Franklin Lofts I’be been enjoying living here. They really make it safe and communicating with management is easy and they are super kind!

Under the new management, the building has undergone impressive improvements. It's consistently tidy and secure for residents. Navigating the hallways and stairs is now enjoyable, as they're clear of debris. The management team is responsive and thoughtful, swiftly addressing any issues to ensure the tenants' comfort.

It's been nothing short of a nightmare since I moved into this place. It took three months for the property manager to finally respond to the many phone calls and emails I sent to get set up in the utility management system just to pay my water and gas bill. 

The grounds are constantly littered with trash. So much trash that I am constantly worried what my dog might get into if I'm not vigilant when I take him outside. Enough trash to pose a risk to cars coming in and out of the garage.

They don't return phone calls. About anything. Someone broke into our car and management won't pull the security footage to give to the police. After speaking with some neighbors, apparently, this isn't the first time something like this has happened. Avoid this building and any property managed by Level 10 Management.
Clean apartments with charachter. Walk across the street to Lake Calhoun, bike/walk/running trails. Reasonable rent.

I lived it...
And thank god I made it..

Literally a joke, i called over ten times, emailed them over 5 times and attempted to physically stop in over a period of 2-3 weeks! Worst process Ive EVER seen in a housing scenario. Thanks for nothing
I would recommend StoneArch II to anyone seeking a lovely neighborhood.

I'm very comfortable where I live. At times I would rather stay where I am than move to a different property. There is always someone to listen to concerns, big or small. That's very nice and it isn't available everywhere in the community.
I'd recommend this apartment community because it's in a great location, walkable to everything I need to access. The staff are great. It's a great place to live.
It suppose to be smoke free, but people are still smoking and only thing that can be done is wait till lease is up for renew.
Price is the biggest factor -- if apartments were more affordable, I have several friends looking for a place to rent.

Building is nice and taken care of. Also the other residents seem respectful of one another. The building is not very loud, unlike other places I habe lived and visited.

Heating is a big deal...having it work properly is essential. it's been over a week and it's still not resolved...

There is no support to change this that i can see.  Also wonder if property management gives a darn about the ckeanliness of the property. The rugs in hallways, on all floors at SA2 havent been cleaned since we opened. They did a pathetic cleaning one morning last year. All floors wet and smelling like bleach. Did all floors in a couple hours. Very bad job. Our windows were not washed either. Last year they attempted. That was first time they attemted to clean since opening. And the vendor did a horrible job. Our complaints stopped at the office. So not sure id highly recommend the place. Or id recommend with them knowing what they are getting into.
I have recommended to two friends and one is moving in on may 10, 2018!
Parking is terrible in this area. The design of the 1 BR unit, especially the bedroom, is very small and linear.

Great neighborhood, complex is well-maintained and cleaned often, and the office staff is always helpful. Some fellow residents aren?t the most respectful to the property which is sad to see, but that happens almost everywhere.
the fact that SA2 so easily slips into not enforcing the contract (for the renters), Im not sure I would highly recommend living here, but I would encourage someone to look at their options.

Santa has been a joy she loves people and understands that this is our homes and always make sure that we have a Pleasant and comfortable life in our homes she always welcome us with a smile she's awesome.

This property manager gets, and stays on top of things! My moving process became stalled, but once she stepped in everything moved smoothly. Not only that shes always smiling and has a positive attitude. If you come to her with a question or concern, she will get to it right away. I love my apartment, it's perfect for my daughter and I. It was clean and move in ready. My building is quiet as well. I'm so thankful to Santa and City Limits. We plan to be here for awhile. Thanks Santa if your reading this.

Me and my two daughters live in this two bedroom unit that too small. We are nestled between the airport, a highway and a grocery store...we deal with mice, ugh! Doors that are not stable and unsavory neighbors. Please help, lol!

I do like these apartments the only problem is the neighbors living in it. Everything about these apartments is very organized. Security is provided at night parking and its convenient with the gas station and cub foods next door to it. As well that the bus rout is right around the corner. Anything else is that its located at a nice environment.
I lived here for two years before I bought my house.  The management was very thoughtful and kind.  He was understanding and fixed thinks very promptly. HIGHLY recommend.

Resident for almost 2 years. The location of this apartment complex is one of the best in the twin cities. A perfect mix of nature/city feel at the same time with a park and Lake Bde Maka Ska a crossed the street! Plenty of great food and a Whole Foods within walking distance. Staff is very nice and helpful.
All of the new updates have made these great apartments!

I moved to Minneapolis a little less than a year ago and for me it was all about location, and I found it. West Calhoun is located across the street from not only a great little shopping center but also one of the most vivacious lakes in the Cities, Lake Calhoun. The apartment itself is small but as a single person it is the perfect size and even includes a spacious bedroom. You're also allowed cats and small dogs. My only complaint is that there are some issue's within the apartment that have been looked at, they are usually extremely prompt, but have yet to be fixed. Overall I highly recommend this location especially if you are living single and don't necessarily hang out in your apartment a lot which when your right on Lake Calhoun and minutes from Uptown, why would you?!

With the proximity to Saint Louis park and Lake Bde, one would assume it is a safe area.  That is far from the case. There is no security despite the numerous car jackings and break ins. Management has been “working” on finding a security company for the past 10 months. The surface level (free) parking lot is also located around a blind turn causing accidents in the winter. The apartment itself is decent. There is decent living space but the kitchen is quite small. The building is also OLD. We have had several things break that required maintenance to fix. The heat doesn’t get warm enough in the winter and we relied heavily on a space heater. The AC works in the living room but doesn’t spread to the bedroom. The amenities are only open during business hours so don’t expect to be able to hit the gym or take the kids to the pool after work. For the price point of this apartment, I wasn’t expecting anything luxurious but I at least expected to feel safe (which I do not).

For the cost of rent (around 600$ a month for a 2 bedroom) this apartment is definitely just "Okay."  First of all its location is a couple of blocks from Lake Calhoun which is really nice when it's nice out but its not exactly walking distance to uptown unless you have plenty of time to kill. You can use the gym and pool in the main building but only during office hours which can be a little bit of a set back for some people. On another note it was a little off putting to see how lackluster they were about cleaning out our apartment after the old tenants moved out. Upon moving in we found dirty dishes in the oven and a full medicine cabinet in the bathroom. This doesn't make the apartment worse but it illustrates how efficient management must be. Overall, for a 2 bedroom apartment in the basement you get what you pay for.

You can't beat the location of this apartment. It is within walking distance to some really great restaurants, grocery stores, and convenience  stores. Lake Calhoun is less than half a mile away and only a mile or so into the heart of Uptown. The staff is great, professional and handle any issues right away.
Great price- even better management. I would highly recommend to anyone looking to live in the area. I have truly loved living here.

I just moved in from another apartment that was also in Marcy Holmes and I can say with 100% confidence that these apartments are high quality. Not only does St. Anthony Village offer spacious apartments but ones that are clean and renovated. They are super fast with maintenance calls and I love that they have a rental office where packages are dropped off. I am a cat owner and they also have extremely reasonable pet fees. The area is generally quiet as well with residents that are mostly past the college scene. I would recommend St. Anthony to anyone looking for a spacious apartment in a great location that is close to the U of M but also close to the food/bar scene in Northeast as well as downtown!
While we've had a few problems with our apartment, the staff has been overwhelmingly helpful. The buildings are clean and well maintained, as well as the landscaping.

I LOVED this apartment! It has prime location - in walking distance to so many awesome northeast restaurants and an easy bike or bus ride to the U of M. It is a good value for your money in the area - clean apartments with great management. Any issue we had with our apartment was fixed within 24 hours of placing a maintenance request. There is SO much storage for a one bedroom -- HUGE closets! And the open layouts are fantastic,  it definitely makes the room feel bigger. I loved this place & am sad to be leaving!

The building is fairly quiet and the staff is great at addressing concerns or if anything in the apartment that needs to be looked at. There is limited parking in back of the building. There are quite a few dumpster divers and quite a few drifters that walk thru the parking lot. Overall, it is a pleasant place to live and convenient to many different places near by.

I really enjoy my apartment. The bedrooms are very large, the kitchen has all new stuff (dishwasher, cabinets, etc.), and it's clean/easy to take care of. The location is great, really close to the bus stop and to bars/restaurants. Once it starts to get a little warmer outside it gets noisier with people walking around and kids playing, but that's true anywhere in the city. The building itself is very quiet. My only complaint is that I wish the kitchen had a little bit more storage space as I have a lot of cookware. The staff is helpful and quick with repairs. Safety has never been a concern. Overall the best apartment I've had in Minneapolis and DEFINITELY the best value.

I moved into this apartment while completing my last year of training as a physician at the University of MN. The building is nice and relatively new. Apartments small but nicely furnished and reasonably priced.
There was a change in management halfway through my lease, but I didn't note any big issues at the time. The problems started when I moved out. During the last month I was there, I found other people parked in the parking spot I was paying $125/month for multiple times.  Phone calls to the office about this were not returned. In the one case where there was actually someone in the office to speak to about this, it turned out SHE was parked in the spot, though she was kind enough to tell me that she'd be leaving in about 45 minutes and the parking spot I WAS PAYING FOR would be available then. I ended up getting to load my belongings into my car in the rain, while paying for street parking, multiple times.
Then I moved out. Less than a month after I'd moved out, I started getting repeated calls from an unrecognized phone number. I eventually answered to tell them to stop calling me, and discovered it was a debt collection agency. Rather than calling, e-mailing, or snail mailing me the final month's utilities (all methods of contact they had), the management company sent $177 to a collection agency less than a month after I moved out.
I called the office multiple times, listened to their cheerful message indicating that "Village Green has been number one in resident satisfaction six years running," left multiple messages, and did not receive a call back. Eventually, I apparently called at the magical time and spoke with a human being, who confirmed that the collections call was not a scam. She informed me that they had “had an issue” with the previous property manager, that the debt had been sent to a collection agency automatically (again, less than a month after I moved out and with NO attempt to contact me). She offered an apology, but nothing else.  Unfortunately the apology will not repair the damage to my credit rating.
I am absolutely furious. The amount of money in question is frankly negligible for me, but I have never in my life had a debt sent to a collections agency, and level of personal disrespect on display here is breathtaking. I would strongly recommend avoiding this complex and this management company.
