Close to downtown and great amenities and community with in the building.

My apt is great smells good and is clean to my liking. The building however ALWAYS smells like hot trash in the front entrance, halls, elevator and there is alot of trash in and around the building always like many dont knownhow to use a trash can.

I lived here for four years during medical school. It was a wonderful experience overall.

Some things I liked about living here:
- LOCATION: Downtown is a short walk, including the stadium. The U of MN east bank is one train stop away. Many hospitals are on the light rail so it was great to be so close to the West Bank Station. You can also take the light rail to airport which is great. the  There's a chipotle very close as well.
- SAFETY: I felt very safe living here. Never had any issues with safety in this area or the building. The building is locked which is nice. I also like that the first floor is the lobby so even if you live on the first floor of apartments you aren't on ground level. 
- AMENITIES: great to have an elevator. I think in four years only once did it break and was fixed quickly. There's also heated assigned garage parking which is amazing in the winter and one of the selling points for me. They have a secure package room which keeps packages from being stolen. There's a pool and gym as well. 
- APARTMENT: Big closet with lots of storage place. Bathroom well lit. Lots of kitchen storage. Reliable appliances. For apartments facing the light rail, the sun is amazing. I have never had happier house plants than I did when living here (see below). It also helps your mood in winters to get lots of natural light. Most apartments have a spacious deck which I used a ton. It's big enough to have plants/a small garden on it. I also had a patio chair and table and loved sitting out there and studying when the weather was nice. Because it has a screen door, you get a ton of natural light because your whole wall is a big window.
- UTILITIES: I don't think I ever turned on heating when I lived here because the apartments around me kept my apartment pretty warm. Additionally, in the summer you can get away without the AC on many days. This is in part because the deck means there's a sliding door with a screen which allowed a lot of fresh air. Additionally, a large tree provided shade in the afternoon. 
- COMMUNITY: most people in the building are professionals or graduate students going to school nearby. There were not tons of younger college kids. Because it's all studios, there weren't large families or lots of kids and thus the building was very quiet.
- STAFF: I interacted with many staff in four years, and they were all responsive and very reasonable. Zach and Sydney were especially great!

I've lived in these apartments for almost 4 years now and I really like it. I like the landlords, and how they make sure that residents are safe, informed and get things fixed promptly. The apartments feel huge and are perfect for a bachelor like myself. I think that the area is quiet and close to everything. I highly recommend these.

The landlords are very nice and easy to bring any questions to. The building is very quiet (it’s mostly grad/law students and professionals) and it feels safe in the building. Ive never had issues finding parking in the parking lot. I’ve had a great experience here.

The apartments are located in a very good area. Close to campus and the West Bank lightrail stop. Management gets back to you in a timely manner whenever there is a problem. There is some street parking for guests though it fills up pretty quickly. It's really nice having a pool too and there is a great view of the new football stadium.
The property is dirty in common areas especially the hallways. It is not cleaned regularly. It smells and has trash on the floor. The hallways are dirty and trash everywhere.
it has playground game fitness also excellent for transportation also like it the kitchen it’s beautiful apartment

Management is great! very helpful in letting me know what to expect and followed through with everything! Apartment is very beautiful ! staff is friendly and helpful!
Virginia

I've lived here since 01/2020. With our new management and new security teams I'm feeling much safer and secure here. They're putting a lot of effort and assets into making our homes a great place to live. They're planning a full renovation. I'm satisfied.

Hands down the best experience I have had renting an apartment. As a previous homeowner, it was important to me that there was a level of service that came along with the beautiful complex. Liz was the most professional, accommodating Manager I have worked with. She was helpful and answered all of the questions I had. Moving into the Finn was flawless because of her help. This feels like home! Highly recommend Liz and The Finn.

Even registered cars are towed without notice. I liked the place until they changed the property manager. They will not inform you about the plowing dates well. They will put up a sign somewhere in the building back door where you are unlikely to ever see it. Then they will tow your car for not moving it. They used to send email about plowing so we all thought they were going to do the same thing but the new property manager is lazy and doesn’t inform the residents about it. They will just tow your car and try to make you pay for it. DONOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE.
I recommended 3 people to this apartment thinking it was good but they have clearly done downhill within a year. Save yourself a lot if headaches and look at other places.

We’ve been here a couple months and have absolutely nothing negative to say about it. It is a great living space and it’s super clean and has wonderful helpful management. Don’t see myself moving anytime soon

I moved into Aria two months ago, shortly after it opened, and couldn't be happier. It is the epitome of a luxury apartment building--location, design, amenities, staff. The location is convenient to tons of shopping, library, parks/lakes/trails, and highways. The design is contemporary and elegant with sophisticated details. It has beautiful community spaces, well equipped gym, gorgeous pool, bocce court, putting green, spa, grills, fire pits, etc. And ALL the staff members, from leasing to maintenance,  are extremely professional and friendly. They make living here even more enjoyable.

I lived at the Shoreham for 7 years. I once considered it my home. When I moved in, it was wonderful! The apartments are nice. The property is so run down. AND, the security is crap!!! They have no caretakers on staff, only a "vender" you can call. People who do not live there can easily walk in. Not only me, but other residents have found people who do not live there, sleeping in various areas. When I brought this up to the manager, her response was to call 911. When I brought up they need better security, I was informed that it is not in the budget. When a car is stolen in the heated underground garage, the responsibility is put back on the residents that if we don't know who is in the car behind us pulling in, that we need to confront them. If we don't recognize a person coming in the building, confront them. They seldom update or CLEAN! The location, maintenance people, the actual units are great. The management is lazy!!! It WAS a great place, as I did, move on.

This place is overpriced for the units they are offering. You can't control when the AC heat is turned on, you can hear your neighbors through the walls and current management recently got rid of the utility packages so that they could charge based on usage (which is impossible for a high-rise without individual meters). If you sign here be prepared to pay more for less.

My favorite place I've rented from In the Twin Cities. Close enough to the action, but not too far removed!

Beautifully put together complex with great amenities to complement! The apartments themselves are elegantly styled and have the BIGGEST walk in closets in any rental I've seen.

But above all, the management team of Heidi and Landon put this place above all. Their care for the residents goes above and beyond you'd expect of someone in their position. They made living here, especially during the pandemic, an absolute joy.

I have lived in The Shoreham since it first opened and have watched the management steadily decline. The original management team was amazing (Kathy & Nathan) - friendly, personable, and went out of their way to make you feel welcomed. Since their new team started, I have had nothing but bad experiences. Firstly, they made a mistake on my lease and have been less than helpful getting it sorted out. Good luck EVER getting a hold of the property manager, Heidi. She is impossible to reach by phone or email. Most recently, I had a leasing agent unlock and walk into my apartment home to show it to a stranger while I was home WITHOUT notifying me of a showing, and have yet to hear back from Heidi after notifying her of the intrusion. There is a clear lack of communication between management and staff, and I would highly recommend living elsewhere. Not to mention, the construction was done poorly and the finishing touches inside of the units are very cheap and fall apart more every day. I am not one to write negative reviews but feel as though potential leasers need to be warned. I am eagerly awaiting the end of my lease.

The apartments themselves are nice. The building claims "dog friendly" but makes it difficult for dog owners to let their dogs out with signs stating "NO DOGS ON THE GRASS" surrounding the building. The pet stations are inconveniently placed and far away from entrances, so the idea that dogs can mindfully hold it until in a "designated pet area" while outside, is unrealistic. 

The old management was very personable and inviting, and planned community events for the building that had great turn outs. In January the management team turned over and the new management is insincere and rude. They have come in trying to overhaul everything that was done before, including the things that were done well. We loved it here before the management switched over, and now we are looking to move out when our lease is up. 

I would not recommend moving here, it is not worth the money for a place that inconveniences residents and doesn't even know your name.

Made a terrible mistake of choosing The Shoreham.  The apartments themselves are nice but that is about it.  For the price they are charging you can do much better elsewhere.  Can't wait until our lease is up.

As residents of our building, we have recently witnessed a distressing increase in package thefts. This ongoing issue has become a source of significant concern for all of us who rely on safe and secure delivery of our online purchases. Despite numerous complaints and requests for action, the building management has yet to implement effective measures to combat this problem.

I don't recommend living here. I subleased this apartment without touring it, and after I moved in, I understood why the previous tenant moved after only 4 months. I lived on the first floor, which was easy for moving. The apartment was very very spacious...but old. When I first moved in,  had cracks on the bottom of all my doors in the apartment. They never bothered to fixed that., It was like someone literally took a hammer and was taking apart the wood one by one. The refrigerator was somehow really short and old. The oven heats up really quickly and really hot, and you can see smoke coming out of the very top when it's at 350 degrees for more than 10 minutes. The dishwasher was FILTHY! As in old and needed to be switched out, it could not get cleaned, AT ALL. 

One day, I had my kitchen sink backed up with water overflowing onto the floor. They came and fixed it right away, so they thought, the next day, a Easter Sunday, it happened again and as I waited for them to come fix it again I had to use the dishwasher to wash my dishes. The one time I ran the dishwasher, water piled to the floor, so much dirt came out of the dishwasher. Ick. But again, they came and fixed it right away. 

My bathroom was also a problem on it's on. There was no drain stopper in the tub when I moved in, and there was always some stench coming from that drain. Aslo, tub was small but I didn't mind. My toilet had a rusted ring in it that never went away, and the part that holds tons of water was solid black liquid. I noted all these when I moved in and nothing at all was done about it. I was not comfortable using my own bathroom or bathtub due to these things.

My heat never worked. There's literally no cell service unless you're outside, especially at night. All my friends that came over had to rely on my wifi, no mater what cell tower they were using. 

Management wasn't bad. Kari is really responsive through email and when packages started getting stolen in the apartment (not just my packages, but neighbors too), she offered to take some directly in her office when she's here. As I'm moving out in three days, there's new management that's coming in. This new management is alright. My old apartment was ran by them and they were bad at getting things done, but good at communicating. Hopefully things get better here. I just wish, I trusted the reviews I read from years ago instead of believing that it has truly changed in three years.

My husband and I have been very happy at Joppa Lane! It's super conveniently located, easy to get to uptown, Shops at West End, and Edina/Southdale. The two bedroom we've been in was huge, with tons of closets for storage. The fitness center and pool were great amenities. Management and maintenance were very responsive to requests. I highly recommend this complex for the price and location!

It looks like a great place at first glace--the area is nice, there is parking, a pool, and the prices for rent are great for the area. 

There are however so many things wrong with this complex:

-The elevator is CONSTANTLY out of order
-The washing machines/dryers are CONSTANTLY breaking. They straight up just don't work, or they wont drain, the leave reside or stains on your clothing, the dryers wont get hot and therefore wont dry your clothes. Parts of the dryer breaks off leaving exposed screws that rip open and ruin your clothing. Also, the laundry is coin operated only. Get ready to be constantly getting quarters for the $1.75 cost to wash, and another $1.75 to dry
-The appliances need updating but instead get "quick fixes." Despite asking, my dishwasher was only really used to hide dirty dishes or to sanitize. No matter what rinse agent, there were always water marks. My fridge often goes off and is "fixed" by taping the electrical cord upwards 
-Management threatens to close the pool each summer multiple times
-There is often no parking because people from neighboring apartments park in the lots. Management tried to enforce parking passes and threatened towing, but one of the lots is inaccessible to large vehicles like a tow truck...so pointless.
-They claim that the concrete construction is a good thing, but it is horrible. You will get absolutely no cell phone reception. It is impossible to hang things on the walls. It does not actually make it quieter. I can hear all the things my neighbor says when he plays video games or has friends over. You can also hear the water running anytime your neighbor or the person above you flushes the toilet, runs the sink or runs the shower. 
-The heat FREQUENTLY goes out when it is cold outside. I once did not have heat for three days over Christmas and there was no one to address the issue. My apartment dropped down to 50 degrees.
-I once waited over 4 months for one of the closet doors in my apartment to be fixed. FOUR. MONTHS. 

This apartment looks great, but nobody deserves to pay money and have to live this way.

I lived in this place for almost 5 years and I loved it.

Pros:
- The location is awesome. Close to everything - uptown, downtown, lakes etc.
- Price is very reasonable. 
- Rent went up only 2 times within 5 years and the increase was only $20.
- Very quiet, nice neighbors.
- Concrete walls!
- Very very warm in winter and you do not need to pay for the heat. 
- Underground garage which is connected to the building (you do not need to go outside in the winter!)
- The best management, all requests were resolved within the reasonable time frame. Communication by email is perfect. We never had any issues with management.
- FREE party room (very good room).
- Swimming pool, gym.
- Very clean building.
- We were not charged any cleaning fee. The manager is very reasonable on this question.
- FREE storage unit, big elevator.
- Many units have updated appliances (we had a brand new stove and almost new refrigerator; newer conditioner in the leaving room). 

Cons:
--- Laundry room needs some updates but it is still ok since the price is low.

I can't agree more with the previous reviewers:
1. You can absolutely hear everything you neighbor was doing. I share the living room wall with my neighbor, and I woke up by their loud music while I was sleeping in the bedroom! I can even Shazam their music in the living room. I can hear ppl talking while sitting in the living room trying to watch TV. Such a bad place to stay.
2. If you live by the Minnetonka BLVD side, then good luck. It is sooo noisy. I just can't stand it. the traffic is so loud.
3. Absolutely no signal, I was using ATT, 1 bar in my apartment, 0 bars in hall way, in laundry room, in elevator, garage, NO THING
4. Children running in the hallway almost all weekend.... they opened and closed stairway door so loud and chasing each other while shouting in the hall way. 
5. Bad applicants, everything is so old and junk.
6. water... just prepare for water rings. 
7. Laundry room is horrible, way too many times the washer was out of services and full of dirty smelly water, and NO BODY took care of it, many ppl called maintainance, well, perhaps they didn't get the message. 
8. Poor services, I'm glad I don't have to deal with the rent office anymore. And their tone in the notice is just bad, very unpleasant to read anything they slip under the door. 
9. Air condition is in a hole in the wall.... prepare for the cold windy days.

This is the perfect location for a U of M student. It is right next to the 3 bus route to get to campus or go to both Downtown Saint Paul and Minneapolis to enjoy the night life. The management is great! They are friendly and have always been prompt to getting back to me for my maintenance needs. The apartment itself is small and has limited closet space, kitchen storage is especially lacking. There are storage rooms in the basement if you really need them. This is a great place for one person or maybe a couple if they are adept at utilizing the space they have. The area is generally quiet and I have never had any problems.

The price per square footage is quite good for the area. Leasing agent and solo repair man are nice and quick to respond but lack attention to detail (maybe understaffed). General care of the unit was somewhat questionable, water pooled underneath the tub, someone grouted over shims to level the toilet, and the tub knobs were stripped. It could be worse. The building is old so issues come with the territory, for instance I went a month without AC and had two leaks in my ceiling. Water hardness is horrible. Never had issues with any residents or noise.

If you’re fine with an older building and good enough maintenance I think this is a fine option for the area.

Lived here almost two years now-property is kept very clean, there is always parking, and maintenance is quick to fix things.  We are in the smallest 1BR 1BA that they offer, it is just right for two people plus a pet.  I like the community of people that live here, I have met many cool people doing lots of different things.  Residents are also helpful-holding doors, helping carry stuff, turning in lost money or credit cards, moving each others packages behind the locked door so there aren't thefts.  We will be here until we buy a house.  Management is very friendly and we appreciate them!

Lived at Park Embassy for 2 years and loved every minute of it. Plenty of space in the apartment and for parking. Loved the nature- we saw so many deer on the property! Steve is simply the best and cares for his tenants. Do yourself the favor and come in to meet Steve and see for yourself.

I lived here for a year and it's one of the best apartments I have ever lived at. The apartment manager Steve was always on top of everything and was nice to all the tenants. The apartments are huge and inexpensive. I would recommend people.

Great location; management is great to work with. We got a remodel while living there and they didn't skyrocket rent. Parking lot was plowed in a timely manner and with plenty of notice. I lived here for three years. I lived in other apartments throughout the years and this was definitely the best one.

I just started to rent at park embassy. It's a great place! 
I'm 25 years old and loved this area.
Steve is the property manager he made sure that I got everything I wanted for my upcoming enrollment. Brand new furniture and appliances, wooden floor and brand  new carpet! And all that for a great price. I love this place. The people living around are respectful and nice. 
I made an emergency call at 5 am and Steve was there to answer my questions ASAP and reassured me. The operation crew are hard working people and always greet you with a smile. 
I did my research and park embassy is the best bang for the buck in St-Louis park/Up town area. It's located right next to a few beautiful lakes and summer over here is super hot!

Have fun shopping around!
Jonathan ;)

Do not rent at this apartment building, it is not a smoke free building/environment as advertised. I would also not recommend renting at any Halverson Blaiser property. Management takes no accountability and lacks the willingness to do anything about the smoking in the building beyond sending notices. This action is a step up from the previous manager who claimed he could not do anything about the smoking in the building. It is not only an issue in an individual apartment, you can smell it in the halls particularly around individual units where there is smoking inside. Again, management is not concerned with the health of renters who are exposed and will not assist you. There are apparently residents who were grandfathered in when this building changed from smoking to non-smoking which was never disclosed. Most of the tenants do the right thing and are good people, but it only takes one. Do yourself a favor and avoid the potential headaches by finding a better environment.

I have a neighbor that makes loud noise in the middle of the night. I cannot sleep in my bedroom. I sleep on a very uncomfortable cot in another area of the apartment. I have been complaining to management for 9 months and it has not been resolved.

My fiancé and I moved into this complex from out of state 2 years ago and this is the first place where we have felt at home. The caretakers and office staff are incredibly helpful and even left us a welcome basket when we moved in. Everything was in perfect shape and if it ever isn’t it is responded to so quickly. But we have only had 1 maintenance problem the entire we have lived here, and it was fixed within 1 hour. We couldn’t be happier with the complex itself and its amenities. It is unparalleled and the grounds are a dream and so well maintained with walking paths and a sculpture garden! We can’t recommend it enough and will stay here until we are ready to buy a house. The people who move here stay here so long bc it’s is a great location with great staff and amenities!

I have lived at the Oaks since the day it opened 
and I'm still very happy here....Great comfortable apartments... fun programs that
bring residents together...caring management 
people that keep the Oaks clean and work hard to meet everyones needs.
Also a pool, fitness center, business center and underground parking accessible to all residents.
That's why I call this place my home !

I have lived at the Oaks on Pleasant for 10 years. It is truly a place one can call home. It is beautifully kept , well managed and has everything you could want in a home. The residents are great and fun activities are an added plus.

I live in a great and well diversified community of 3 brm town homes and apts along with 2brm and 1 brm apartments as well. The building has be recently refurbished outside and re-landscaped with new grass, trees and flowers and is really quite beautiful and is a very attractive place to come home to. My floor plan which includes a second floor loft and a second floor bedroom is an ideal combination of open space and unique architecture to give a comfortable flow to the many rooms and closets. i really enjoy the indoor pool and spa as well as the workout room that is adjacent to the fully furnished community room and it's separate kitchen. Management is very friendly and cooperative and i never worry about delays in getting any repair or maintenance issue completed. This is a nice calming oasis of comfortable living in a city on the move.

Yesterday evening the property manager called me to reschedule my tour of the apartments for today. I was set up to see three apartments. I get to the appointment early, only to find all three units two in a different location are gone. She told me they were filled yesterday before she called me, but didn't advise me. Then told me to pay the application fee and put my application in, but again the units are already gone.

I have lived here since January 2016. I love the affordable price of living here and how close it is to Uptown and how easy it is to get to St. Paul or anywhere in Minneapolis quickly. A well-lit parking lot with lots of extra places to park make it easy to have guests over. Problems are taken care of promptly and in all it is a great place to live!      - McKenzie Hohlen

I enjoy living in these apartments. It is mostly quiet and the neighbors are pleasant and keep to themselves. The management is kind and always returns messages promptly. I especially love that the walls are painted warm shades of brown so I don't feel like I'm living in a white box.


-Natalie King

I had an apartment showing scheduled 4 days prior to the showing date. I even received a confirmation text and call from them about 2 hours before the showing. I left work an hour early because they refused to agree to a showing time after 5pm. Anyway, I drive 40 mins in peak traffic and arrive at the apartment and there is No one at the leasing office. No one answered my calls, I must have called 3 different numbers atleast. How unprofessional can anyone get? It doesn't matter how good an apartment looks if the property management treats a future resident like this. Unacceptable!!

Management refuses to answer questions and has zero respect for tenants.  Maintenance never comes, and if work is done, it's shoddy - Just look at the parking lot, if you drive by - they covered the cracked broken driveway in tar to try to color match the redone parking area .. which has no traction and is very dangerous in winter.  Tenant quality is up and down, but police visits to the property are not uncommon.  Noisy neighbours up late.  Dirty hallways.  "Secure" doors constantly propped open or have coins jammed into the locking mechanism.  The *only* positive about Lyndale Garden Apartments is the location - and there are other apartments in the area.
No amenities, rent is way too high, no heat (doesn't work). If you are a busy individual, accommodation in this property is very poor, they will charge you, for their act on laziness.

I've lived in this apartment complex for more than a few years and have decided to end my lease due to managements lack of action towards noise complaints I've issued. I've issued multiple noise complaints about noisy neighbors over the last year. Management has acknowledged the complaints but has not acted upon the information I've provided. As a result, the excessive noise persists. I have trouble sleeping, I have trouble reading a book, and I  can only exist in my apartment when I wear noise cancelling headphones. In my experience, management has not done what I believe they should do in order to keep me here. As a result, I have let my lease expire and have moved somewhere else. From my experience, I would not recommend renting a lower floor unit until management can show that they have a good noise complaint policy that effectively addresses tenant's concerns.

I've lived here about 4 years. It's a pretty basic place with no amenities but the price is decent for the area. 
Theres few parking spaces and street parking is pretty limited especially in the summer. I pay for a garage for this reason. This year they have been HORRIBLE about plowing the alley where the garages are after snow. I've seen several people get their car stuck because it doesn't get plowed until late afternoon following snow. Several times this year I've had to beg people to give me a ride to work because I've been snowed into the garage I pay monthly for.

This is a perfect apartment with good ventilation and excellent community.Unlike other apartments it has full security as there is a police academy in the area.It's like having a touch of county right in the middle of the city as we have all restaurants,groceries,saloons,hospitals in the nearby area.The area is well maintained by the apartment manager and is always accessible for any repair.

The staff is very very friendly, Becky at the woodhaven office is so helpful and kind. And Mo is a great handyman, the buildings are always kept in such good condition because of him. Whenever something is out of order they are on top of it, and the issue is fixed ASAP! I’m very content with where I am, it’s a good place to be. :)

I have lived at Southdale Parc Apartments for almost a year. It is a nice apartment complex and my unit overlooks the local parK which I love. My apartment is nothing fancy but for what I pay  it is clean and in good condition. Also the closets are big which is a plus. The staff is friendly and the location is great for anyone wanting to use public transportation as a means of travel. I can easily get to work, the store, the mall,the gym, and Uptown by bus. I don't think I will live in this complex for years but for right now it is the perfect fit and I am happy to live here.

Southdale Parc is a quiet complex with great accessibility to shopping, entertainment, and the different highways to get through or out of the cities. Some amenities could be better but it's a decent enough for what your paying in rent. Good place for one person/couple just getting used to the area or starting out on their own.

Living in the Southdale Parc apartments isn't an amazing experience but it's decent enough. The managers are honest and want to be as helpful as possible in all situations. From moving into the buildings for the first time to if you're try to put in a repair request, the managers want to help as best they can. The interior/common area's are kept in decent shape by in-house staff but you or your neighbors' personal habits lead into how well everything is kept clean and fresh in the building.

The main negatives about the complex comes down to building amenities. This is just a review of my building (2720) in general so things may be different in the other two buildings. There is supposed to be extra storage on the first floor of each building but there is no way to regulate who uses how much of the extra storage. The other major negative is that there is supposed to be a picnic area on the property but all we have is an old campground grill and a picnic table on a narrow strip of land. 

You really can't beat the location to entertainment, dining, and shopping you get for the price of rent though. Everything from major shops to convenience stores are within a short walk/drive and there's highway access on all sides within 3 blocks. 

Don't choose the complex if you're expecting to build/house a family, it's not really spacious enough for that situation. If you're on your own or have a partner you could do a lot worse than Southdale Parc Apartments.

My first week here the leasing agent used his master key to enter my unit (no knock or notice) and catch me in my underwear. My car has been broken into inside the parking garage, windows smashed on other cars. I asked multiple times for them to review the camera and have heard nothing even after filing police report. My bike has been stolen, packages stolen, all mail sent to a house down the street due to this being a new building and they haven't registered the address. I cant even get my DL renewed because they haven't properly identified this building as a valid address. The gym equipment has been broken for months. The list goes on...

Very unhappy with this apartments parking situation. The surface parking lot (which you have to pay for monthly) is a block away, across the railroad tracks and out of view from the apartments. On top of it being a hassle to carry things into your apartment and walking in the cold, it’s also unsafe. My car was broken into and almost stolen 3 times while living here. They have no cameras in the lot outside and people leave the gate open constantly. Recently the gate looked like it was ripped off altogether. The garage they have has limited parking spots (about 40) so there is no guarantee you will get a spot inside if you move here. If you park in the alleyway because you don’t want your car broken into you will be towed. I can’t have company over because i’m afraid that their car will be damaged because there is no where to safely park. Management makes it clear they are not liable for your safety here, they will not show you footage if something happens to you or your property.
I live in a studio apartment at Yale Place. It's a beautiful old building. I have a walk in closet, that is huge. Claw foot tub. The kitchen is a little small. I enjoy living here.

there are people smoking in their apartments that gets into the hallways and into other apartments. nothing is being done to stop it. 
the pool hasn't been opened, and maintance is hard to find if there is a clog in your bath.

I have lived at the Carrington Drive properties for about 3 years.  During approximately the first half of my time there, my experience was great.  Then, Aeon Management took over the property, and the results have been abysmal. They are unwilling to address maintenance needs in even a remotely timely manner.  

My tub drain back-flows and fills the tub with disgusting sludge.  This is an ongoing problem that has gotten worse recently.  This is currently the 4th day that I have been unable to use my tub, and my apartment is filled with a really terrible smell. 

This isn't the only problem with the plumbing in the building that I live in.  Recently, my sink began to back fill with the same greasy disgusting water that is in my tub right now.  I bailed over 50 gallons of water out of it while waiting for maintenance, who took 2 hours to arrive despite me telling them how urgent the situation was.  

The laundry room has overflowed twice since I have been living here, soaking a large area of the carpet on the basement floor.  Today, something similar happened again, although I think it was the boiler that flooded rather than the tub.  I suspect this is a mold risk.

These types of problems mean that I currently live in an apartment where I do not know if my belongings will be water damaged when I come home from work.  That's horrible. 

Also, parts of the parking lot turn into a lake after heavy rains since the drainage is so poor.  I would estimate they accumulate around a foot of standing water during these times.

The worst part is how difficult it is to get in touch with anyone at my apartment leasing office or Aeon management, and how apathetic they were when I finally did reach them.  It is not an exaggeration to say that I have called and e-mailed Aeon and the leasing office 10 times in the past week and left several messages in an attempt to get my problems addressed, and my tub is still full of gross waste.

I strongly recommend against renting here now, but I do want to make it clear that prior to the Aeon takeover, the staff in the leasing and the maintenance staff were really great, and I appreciate everything they did.
Alright place to live. Most neighbors are very nice. Management and other staff are great....

I have lived here for one year two months today. I love it here, very nice and quiet place to live. The staff here are all nice and provide good costumer service to the resident(s)/tenant(s). Maintenance personnel always show up promptly when there's a need. The management always listen to tenants needs/concern, and work with them in a satisfactory way. I  would recommend anybody who's looking for apartment in the Brooklyn-Center area to rent here at Carrington Drive Apartment.  Over all the property manager is awesome!!
cant say enough about the staff the apartment are the best lookin ones that i have seen and the office staff was just really helpful
I have lived here going on 2 years now and love my apartment and location. Staff is very nice and accommodating. I would recommend this apartment to anyone looking for an apartment in the area.

I moved into my apartment, because it's a great location for me,it's close to my doctors office,  as well as being close to the stores, be it grocery or food. And walgreens is across the street, and all this is helpful for me because I don't drive.  The bus is just out my door,not even a half a block. That way I can visit my daughters and grandkids, cause their not too far. And it keeps me active.    Thank you.

I was interested in the area, and got terrible vibes when I did a walkthrough. The building is falling apart and reeks. The unit I looked at was an abandoned mess and looked like somebody left without taking their stuff, much less cleaning. After I left, the manager (who gave me a tour) proceeded to call and text me 5-6 times to see if I was interested, so I blocked his number. No thanks.

I used to live here 6 years ago. I just came across this while looking. On move in day, the apartment was a wreck and disgustingly dirty. I called them immediately and offered to clean, but stipulated that I wanted to be compensated in some way and the management went nuts on me. I was younger and a bit naive, so I just took the verbal abuse. The sink wasn’t properly working the entire time I was living there and they did nothing. I also replaced the toilet seat on my own and a few other things. He also went to my apartment when I wasn’t home, without notification. Lastly, he took money out of my security deposit at the end of the lease and I left the apartment cleaner and nicer than when I moved in. run!

When I first moved in everything seems good, but the second I had a problem they were nowhere to be found. I have water damage from the apartment upstairs, and the landlord has not talked to my insurance company. Also it is now march 20th and my ceiling has not been repaired since the damage has happened and been reported February 2nd.

I rented some years ago, after this management took over; I gave them the 60 day notice, cleaned and returned keys as outlined in the move out letter. I had bought a home and after moving out, they sent me a letter demanding over 1,000 stating I had not returned the keys, had not cleaned(note they had not painted for years or fixed the bathroom); they refused to return my 365 damage deposit. Even the prior mgmt. stated they were unethical. Stay clear.

I agree with all other reviews listed here. The landlords did no walk through or check list upon move in. I cleaned the apartment for hours when I moved in to make it clean enough to be tolerable. I insisted on a walk through when I moved out. They did come, mentioned to dust the ceiling fan, which I did. Then they sent me a bill instead of my deposit with all kinds of made up charges. As also mentioned before, no one came or called back when called for having no heat or needing a repair. The names I was given of the man and woman apparently are not their real names. Why would people have to lie to their tenants about their names? Halls were gross. I mentioned that upon moving in and they said the caretaker would take care of it. Thee is no caretaker. The halls are never cleaned. If there is a working light and working machines in the laundry room you lucked out. DO NOT MOVE IN TO ANY OF THESE PEOPLE'S BUILDINGS. They are the worst landlords, greedy, selfish, do not care about their tenants. They will do everything they can to rip you off.

I am thankful I did not end up renting from this rental company. The landlords informed me I was the first to view the apartment and consequently I filled out an application and paid the $40 fee. I did not hear from management for two weeks, so after a few attempts I got a hold of "Mary," who showed me the unit. She obviously had no intention of calling me and already rented the unit. When I pressed her about the $40 application fee she got flustered, said she would look into it, and hung up. Do not waste your time or money on this place.

The best part of this place is that the units have some really great amenities (dishwasher, new stoves, etc) and there are some really nice people that live here. But there has been a huge problem in the past couple of years with multiple managers coming through and not getting much done. It’s hard to have a maintenance request filled for example. There’s also been some safety concerns with people getting into the building who don’t live here and vandalizing the property, and unfortunately some tenants just don’t treat the building with care either. Would not recommend moving here.

We blinding signed a lease all the way from PA and it was seamless! Our time at Abbott has been amazing! Great management, prime location and CLEAN facility. Sad to go but we just needed more space! Or we'd be staying! HIGHLY recommended!
I have lived here for almost 3 years and just agreed to stay another year. It’s a great place to live. Amazing location, great management, and friendly neighbors.

We have lived here for about six months now and love it. We we're worried about the area when we moved in because we are not familiar with Minneapolis, but it has proven to be safe. Lock cars, don't leave them running unlocked in the winter, and we had some graffiti but it was taken care of quickly and not returned. We have a dog and the park is awesome for her and they are allowed to go in the front of the building and side which is nice for the winter. The managers are great and very helpful. Things get fixed within a day for us (light out and clogged tub fixed that day) and when we were out of town and got food delivery by mistake they put it in our fridge for us and saw a light was out so got it changed. The gym is nothing special but gets the job done (more suitable for runners and only dumbbells for weights. Parking is a average price for around here and we haven't had to worry about moving much this winter for snow. We are very happy we choose this place. Close drive to everything we need and only 7$ cab to most places around.

Abbott apartments are located near downtown Minneapolis in Steven Square neighborhood occupying a newly renovated hospital building. I have stayed in Abbott for the last 3 years first in a 2 bedroom apartment (new appliances, hardwood cabinetry, dishwasher etc) and then in a 1 bedroom unit (same quality and spacious!). My neighbors here have been kind and helpful and so has maintenance and office management - they are very good about holding and signing for important packages when I'm away! There are lots of events at our building including scheduled breakfasts, barbecues, food and used clothing drives by management throughout the year to bring together the people of Abbott. I would definitely recommend Abbott!

The first thing I tell my friends is "Yea, I live in a 100-year old hospital." Their reactions are always the best from "Dude, that must be haunted or creepy as all get out!" to "Oh, you're sick?" And then I explain to them that no, I'm not sick, I just live in a historic building that was converted into beautiful apartments (and totally not creepy). This is the longest I have stayed in one apartment; I love it that much. The staff is amazing, super friendly, and despite having a ton of residents, I'm pretty sure they know everyone by name. Maintenance fixes anything super quick. They pay for heat AND central air (you seriously can't beat that) and the campus is just gorgeous. The layouts are beautiful and unique with a modern design and up-to-date appliances. This is my favorite apartment I've ever had.

Quadrel , a company out of Chicago, manages these buildings. Or I should say are responsible for managing them but literally do nothing to provide good customer service. They do not respond to maintenance requests, take weeks if not months to respond to phone calls, have had multiple local property or leasing agents who leave and are not reliable, the people in the Chicago office are Even less responsive. The maintenance issues are ridiculous: water damage from months ago, broken sinks, broken windows, no shelves in kitchen cupboards, cupboards falling off wall in kitchen….

Now managed by Quadrel, this property doesn't get the upkeep it used to.  All the maintenence staff have been let go, except for a single revolving door pairing for all the area buildings. They lapse payments for the crews that have been working on remodeling for over a year now, which get pushed into maintenance calls. They can't even keep the grass watered anymore, the fire alarm is faulty, and the utility payments have been an inconsistent mess. Be prepared to follow up multiple times if you have any issues.

Used to be good place to live than taken over by 10th Floor Properties. Everyday maintenance went way down hill. No heat. Bugs. And supposed to be smoke free but I guess you can smoke pot.
Live here since 2008 & ordered to vacate so they can jack up the rent for next poor sap. Good Luck if you rent here.
It's kind of a boring building, but great location!

The building is very old and everything is falling apart. 2 of my rooms do not have ceiling lights. Pipes break from rust and they charge you for it. I was without a shower for a week and left several messages for the maintenance guy and he didn't show until over a week later. I have woken up to the maintenance guy in my bathroom without notice. I was about to take a shower!! He does not knock, just comes in whenever he feels like it. Laundry takes 14 quarters. There is no elevator and it is horrible going to the top floor every day. I have to keep my apartment showroom ready for my last two months of my lease or else I get charged a month's rent (and they say they can come in without notice). The only things I like are that the walls are thick, lots of space for the money here, and great views.

I was a resident of The Haverhill Apartments from 2010 until 2013. My partner and I loved our apartment and it felt like home. Lonnie, who works at the front office was a pleasure to work with. He is such a genuinely nice and honest individual who truely cares about the residents and property. The maintenance team was also exceptional. During winter, they would venture out early in the morning to clear the sidewalks in an effort to make the morning walk easier for the residents. They were just as nice and caring as the office staff. The building has its quirks, but that just comes along with a building that is 100 years old. It's character is something that cannot easily be replicated by some of these luxury apartments that are popping up around the city.

The Fern is a nice building with lovely apartments. I especially love having an in-unit, full size washer and dryer, and access to an underground garage. 

Lauderdale has a quiet, small town atmosphere while being in the midst of the Twin Cities. A great location on the.border of where Minneapolis and St Paul meet, just off Hwy 280. Close to shopping and restaurants. There is an active healthy seniors’ group in the neighborhood, and its just a few blocks from the charming St Anthony Park neighborhood.
Older building but close to campus and the river parkway. Management is very friendly and responsive. Relatively affordable for the area; ideal for a UofM student.

We have been living here for 2 years and this is great experience so far! Location is great and the price is reasonable. Property manager Tracy and maintenance team have done a fabulous job. They are very responsive and professional and always helpful. I appreciate the great job!
My friend and I lived here for 1.5 years and loved it! Being able to walk to lunch/dinner, getting a tan on one of the many beaches all around you and you can’t beat those sunsets over the lake!

I recently moved into 2920 Dean Parkway and I'm very happy with my experience so far. Roxanne the property manager has been very professional and made the moving in process a breeze. The location is fantastic and my apartment was very clean when I moved in. Would high recommend these apartments and this management group.

I have moved to MN from another state knowing no one nor the place. Roxane who is the part of the Management team made my moving experience more than anyone could have asked for. She kindly and patiently showed me the apartment, educated me about the area and all that it has to offer. And now I am proud to call this place my new home! I wish for everyone to have such an excellent moving experience as I did-thanks to Roxane!

I have lived here for over a year and had a great experience. If anything needs attention in my unit, management prioritizes it. The building is situated right off the Greenway and is flanked by Lakes Bde Maka Ska, Isles & Cedar Lake, which makes it perfect for people who are active. My unit is carpeted (others I understand are hard wood) and has been kept in good condition. I have found this a friendly place to be, with good management and in a prime location.

They allow pets, have garage parking, and a $/sq. ft. that is hard to beat in Uptown. With the lakes, the Greenway, a bus stop and a bunch of shops and restaurants nearby, it's a great location. Also, the owners have been good about updating the place, keeping things tidy, and hearing any inquiries from residents (at least in my experience). Highly recommend.

The units here are recently re-done and they look great. I love my granite countertops and the appliances aren't half-bad either. Pair that with how spacious these units are, along with a practical common room, a brilliant location in Uptown, and a great rate and you've got an awesome place to live!
Love the place look like a little garden. Very clean and quiet, friendly people. Lot's of stores around too. Love it.

My mother-in-law lives here and pays an exorbitant rate for a one-bedroom apartment although her rent just about breaks even with her monthly income. Why are they labeled as affordable senior housing? And, be aware that the units do not have bathtubs, only showers. There is only one shared bathtub on one of the floors that no one wants to use. Who designed a senior building that's unaffordable and excludes bathtubs? I gave 5 stars due to the nice appearance, but subtracted 3 due to the issues I noted above.

My parent lives here. I work as a home nurse and visited multiple senior homes. My family and I wanted our parent to live here because it's a senior home. Biggest con is there is no furniture in the family room lounge, no senior events, workouts, Bingo, senior gatherings. Biggest concern the workout room only has a bike and treadmill ( Where are the weights,, TV, and it's freezing)This is very concerning. Nice place but definitely an after thought for seniors. If it doesn't change we will not renew lease. I'm sure at this rate the building is going down hill already.

This is the best apartment I have ever lived in.  Sr living is the best! It's so nice and quiet and clean plus my neighbors are ALL very nice. Big beautiful windows in my living room that overlook the garden area and a small playground and the best is watching the beautiful skies. This place is truly a blessing.

I would advise you after living there for 9 years that you should not rent from Cora or Gerald Rygh. It takes forever to get a simple thing fixed if needed, and likely that they will not call you back ever about the situation possibly would just randomly show up to take care of it without any word. If there are ever mad at you or you let them know that you're moving out, they will basically just pretend that you don't exist to them at that point. The parking lot is a destroyed concrete pit basically and over crowded. Will show up to your apartment days before end of month with no word to try and show apartment. A pain to deal with in general, and a nightmare to deal with this last month.

Just moved in a couple of months ago, already frustrated with the management and the building and all the noise from out side. Roch,mouse and their drain system stinks. Can't wait to finish the lease and move out. I should have trusted my gut when I did the tour.

I called 6 times to know about the availability dates for 2 bedroom apartment but they only disconnect the line and finally when they recieve they again hang up the call. The workers are not so helpful. No more in my favourite list.

This complex has a great location for anyone who finds themselves in the Seward neighborhood of Minneapolis often. This is in the center of theater arts, colleges, and a great community atmosphere. Located right by several freeways and great views of Minneapolis with no extra view charge! Privately owned and the staff listens to you. I would recommend to anyone in their 20s-30s.

This apartment is not perfect by any means, But I love it here, My 2 bedroom has a mind blowing view of the Minneapolis skyline. This is my first apartment and so far I am very satisfied with the facilities here including but not limited to the cheap laundry, a beautiful new sundeck, a pool and a fully loaded work out room. also with in walking distance of the light rail and many restaurants.

lots of character in this smaller apartment building. tall ceilings, huge windows, lots of natural light, the balcony is HUGE! and you cant beat the view from every window. looks right at the city skyline. gorgeous at nigt
Tall Ceilings, huge balconys, lots of character, lots of natural light. The view from every window is breathtaking! looks right at the city!

I've had nothing but great conversations with our land lord company. The building is in great shape and out 4th floor apartment has a beautiful view of minneapolis! The only downside is parking, they have off street parking but not enough spaces for everyone.

Unfortunately, everything you’ve read about this place is true. I've never lived in an apartment building that I hated every second of. The units are incredibly small, barely accommodating a queen-size bed in the bedrooms. When I first moved in, the units were listed on the website with smaller square footage, but somehow, the same floor plans are now listed as 95 square feet larger. For instance, the "Helena" floor plan was listed at 515 square feet but is now listed at 610 square feet. Predictably, the price has increased to reflect this "larger" unit. Don't believe the website listings; they're misleading everyone. There are about 6 or 7 Airbnbs in the complex, possibly more, so strangers are constantly coming and going. This was not shared when I was moving in, otherwise this would’ve been an immediate no for me.

When they sent me the terms for renewing my lease, they, of course, increased the rent. I declined, and now I see my unit listed for less than what I had been paying all year. They will find a way to screw you over one way or another.

The noise is unbearable. There's no insulation between units, making it feel like you have unwanted roommates. This was my first time living alone, and it felt like I was back in a college house. You can hear everything from your neighbors, including barking dogs. If you work from home, you’ll need excellent noise-canceling headphones because it’s miserable. The upstairs neighbors sound like elephants (likely due to the poor construction amplifying every sound). If you have a dog living above you, be prepared to hear it scraping across the floor day and night.

Living here is not worth the money; it’s all for show. This is the cheapest apartment I’ve ever lived in, yet it’s supposed to be "luxury." The front always smells like pee, and the key pad hasn’t worked for months. This has been the most miserable year of my life, and I can’t wait to find a new place to call home.

This was my first apartment rental in 25 years.  Mark is beyond the best person to ever own/run an apartment building!  He is beyond fair.  He treated us so well.  I can not thank him or his staff enough!  We loved our apartment and the fellow tenants there.  They had a Christmas Tree decorating party that was so fun!  Such a feeling of family in this building.  I miss Mark and the friends we made at 230 Oak Grove Street.  I would move to this building again!

I am a long time resident and can recommend the Oak Grove Hotel as a decent place to live.  

I stay because I have always found the place to be so centrally located that I can get anywhere in about 20 minutes, city or suburb.  Parking is an issue but that is the nature of living in the city.  You need to pay to park. I will say the snow removal for the building has so vastly improved I never worry that I cannot get out of a parking spot.  And if I do have an issue, the building mgmt will come and help.

The apts are old school, but are being updated with granite and new cabinets but still have that old time feel of space.  The staff has always been quick in helping when there has been a problem: leaky faucet, clogged drain.  The building is pretty quiet but any issue is dealt with promptly.

  People are friendly, there are holiday parties in the lobby for anyone wishing to attend.  People look out for their neighbors. People  live here a long time so something must be done right here.
If you're looking for yoga classes, dry cleaning, you"re on your own. There is a small grocery store next door  If you're looking for a quiet, decent place to live check it out.

I have lived here for almost 5 years now. The apartments all have that great old time charm while still be clean and kept up. I very rarely ever hear my neighbors which is a huge perk living in the city. Huge updated laundry room is a big plus too. Great location with super easy access to public transportation. Close to the downtown area, eat street and most of the stadiums. Beautiful park just around the corner that hosts tons of fun events and a cute little convenience store right next door. Great for those that don’t want a car, although off street parking is available. Everyone is super friendly and easy going with lots of dogs to pet in the lobby.

I moved to the oak grove apartment hotel because of it central downtown location .I do not have a car and still get around town easy whit my bike. I have lived in the building for over 10 years and highly recommend it .

I never thought I would be in one place so long. I’ve lived here for 20 years and it’s been great. The building is clean and safe. Management has been very accommodating and easy to work with. We love the neighborhood. It’s so easy to walk to most things. Most people know each other in the neighborhood. There is a nice feeling of community. It’s home.

This company wasted my time! The application process took two months only for them to send me a generic email saying I was denied due to being over income. They gave me the run around and had me believing that I would be approved just to be denied after two months. There wasn’t even an apology to the time they wasted. They are heartless and very unprofessional. I know countless other people that they did the exact same thing too!
Very cute but small and hot as hades in the humid MN summer!!

Finally, a management team that is truly concerned with the quality of life, safety and comfort of all residents 
I’ve lived here for nearly 3 years and I’ve never been more impressed with management. Toobay,Mary Ann and Lavell are a force to be reckoned with! They are responsive and genuinely concerned about all issues a resident might face.
 I wholeheartedly recommend anyone looking to live downtown to seriously consider East Village . It’s affordable and the management and amenities make it a very nice place to call home!

If you’re looking for a place to call home, do not rent here. The place is filled with BUGS, they constantly ask you to pack up your entire apartment to have pest control spray. Right before I moved out, they were checking apartments for RODENTS. They do not send emails to communicate with tenants, hoping that important information will be read via paper notes they put in front of all the doors. The common spaces are constantly filled with trash and aren’t maintained on the weekends. Fire alarms go off in the middle of the night frequently - they take hours to get it to stop. I had many other issues while living here but I’ll leave it at that.

I strongly advise against living here. The management staff are not responsive, give out incorrect information, and do not do what they say they will do. The building often smells and is not well maintained. There is also significant security concerns that management claims to be addressing, however, they have not followed through with many of their claims. We have experienced theft and have been negatively impacted by drug use by other residents in the building, issues that were not addressed by management. When we needed assistance and had questions about our residency, we were required to email management and would often need to physically go to the office to get a response to our concerns and answers to our questions. They are very difficult to work with. Other notable problems include the courtyard littered with trash and dog poop and unauthorized people gaining access to the building. There has been literal poop in the stairwells and people sleeping there overnight.  The fire alarms are also bound to go off in the middle of the night.  Do not live here.

Decent place to live. Pros: in unit washer dryer hookup is huge and works really well, stove, fridge and dishwasher are all great, very dog friendly with a nice park and dog run out back, good location. Cons: terrible plumbing, AC is a crappy wall mounted thing that's only in the bedroom and doesn't affect the rest of the apartment, sinks clog very easily, very bad security, very bad package management system, and understaffed management.

The security is particularly bad. There are often people who 'piggy back' off of others to get into the building. As in they wait outside the door until someone comes by and unlocks it so they can slide in behind. I've seen people sleeping in the hallways and stairwells multiples times. Once I was even forced to call the cops because the dude had like 4 handles of vodka on him and refused to leave. It's super dark at night, they turn off all the lampposts, and they only have one lone security guard patrolling around. Very unsafe for downtown.

There's also something very messed up with the plumbing in the bathrooms. My sink has been clogged 3 times in a year, my toilet doesn't flush or refill randomly, and the shower keeps getting backed up with disgusting dirty sewage water. It's gotten to the point where i don't feel comfortable showering at home, even with shower shoes.

Welcoming staff that becomes a family to their residents. The building is well-kept and the fellow residents are friendly. Great for anyone looking for their first apartment or for starting or relocating their family.

The East Village Apartments are spacious, visually pleasing, comfortable and very affordable. The building and parking garage are very secure, utilizing a key fab entry system. The staff is very helpful and ready to solve problems.The proximity to downtown Minneapolis makes it a great choice for anyone that wants to experience big city living.

This is a fun quiet complex of three buildings.  Heated garage space available -  storage, exercise room, pool and whirlpool available.  Third floor can be rented for parties and there are a lot of fun things to do during the week for retired people. 
Miss some of it as still working but have gone to plenty of their dinners and parties love living here.

This was the worst experience I’ve ever had at an apartment. Jets fly over the property constantly making it so loud that you can barely spend anytime in your apartment and you will never be able to sleep. It truly ruined a year of my life.

This apartment is directly under a flight path and has non stop low flying jets going over it all day starting at five in the morning. And the building is not sound proofed at all. This has been a terrible experience living here.

You will hear non stop very low flying jets go over your apartment all day starting at five in the morning and doesn’t stop until midnight. The apartment is located directly under a flight path and is very close to the Minneapolis airport. This has been the worst time of my life living here.
just viewed the apartment this past week nice new marble counter tops and bathroom sink counter top. clean and well kept.
I love this place like I told the assistant manager I'm claiming this apartment. I enjoyed the tour that I had

Good location and fair price in comparison to other single bedroom and studio apartments in the area. However, there have been many problems including water damage, insects, rodents, plumbing and just the fact that it is an old building in need of major renovations.  Also, the apartment claims to be "smoke free", but many residents freely smoke cigarettes and recreational drugs in the building without any repercussions.

I rent in a Studio apartment and i must say I do like it. The rent is fair for the location, size and Quality of the Apartment. Although, the building is older and the it shows. This apartment is great for some one living on there own going to school.

To anyone applying to JEK properties, don't waste your time applying to their complex. After applying and paying their fee. My wife and I thought we would meet their application requirement. My wife will be a student and myself had a job lined up in Madison. Of course being out of towners, our jobs meets their requirement as wells as our credit score, but moving into Madison seems to be more difficult then expected. After e-mailing back and forth they seemed unhappy with our application and requested more information like rent history, job offers, as well as other information which they stated they needed 4 times the income to rent if you didn't have rent history, which we didn't meet the requirement. JEK properties stated we needed an outside co-signer to meet their requirement under both our names. Mind you my wife and I aren't some teens to twenties individuals applying for housing. Maybe being a minorities may not be the case but it doesn't look that way. Don't was the time unless you know for sure you can get the apartment then pay for the application fee. We applied at the Ridge which the unites had some redone and renovated but the facility isn't all the great.

I am currently on a 1-year lease, I am disappointed by the property manager's lie about the noise level. I live on one of the top floors and you can hear EVERY SINGLE VEHICLE on the road. To make it worse, this complex is near many hospitals, so there are ambulance sirens even at 1 am in the morning. I am giving 2 stars because the in-house amenities are nice and so is the sky-deck for hosting guests, but these are very scarcely used and are supposed to be in good condition as the apartments are fairly new. The windows have very bad condensation every single day and staff asked us to wipe them to avoid mold, saying that is common. The heating/cooling is also quite uneven between rooms, so for people viewing apartments virtually DO NOT TRUST what you are told. Some corners have been cut in the name of luxury apartment.

Unfortunately, I have had a very bad experience with Peloton. When looking for an apartment in Madison, I informed the owners that I was looking for something with parking, close to downtown, and that was within walking distance of businesses. They had reassured me that all of this was possible with their apartment complex. When I visited this last weekend, I was very disappointed. Downtown was 2 miles from the apartment and was not walkable. Parking was not available at the complex as all spots were full, but I was encouraged to park on the street.  I noticed quickly that the parking was very limited within certain hours or days of the week that would make it impossible to park on a daily basis near the apartment. There was also nothing open within a block of the apartment as most stores were closed or boarded up. I felt as though seeing the apartment complex did not match what the owners described to me at all and now I am forced to choose between losing my deposit and renting for 18 months or living somewhere unsafe and without parking for 18 months. I am very disappointed and was not contacted to discuss further although they said they would call me within 24 hours. Instead, I was given an email and no one returned my call. I would not recommend this area, this apartment complex, or the people that run it.

I have continuously written to management about how the residents in this building play loud base music that shakes this whole apartment, but NO ONE HAS STOPPED THIS NUISANCE. It is extremely aggravating. The walls here are paper thin made of cheap materials and the residents need some sound control. I wake up at 4AM during the weekend, but it is so loud here that I can't get any sleep. 

Better go elsewhere if you want some peace

I would give a NEGATIVE ?? if I could. The "manager" Kimberly is extremely rude and unprofessional. She did not return our messages or emails and seemed annoyed when we discussed our application status. Despite requesting all application information within 48 hours and taking a $50 application fee, she admitted several days later that she hadn't even looked at the applications or emails. 

While I understand that Madison apartments are busy with applicants, Kimberly could have informed us if she was overwhelmed and placed us on a waitlist like other apartments did. This would have allowed us to choose whether to apply, look elsewhere, or join a waitlist. Instead, our calls were ignored, and I was even hung up on. I had to call from an unknown number to request a refund of our application fee, as we no longer wanted to proceed. 

Kimberly and her assistant Jennifer are not the people you want to rent from. If their application process is any indication, I can't imagine how they would handle maintenance issues. Please read reviews before deciding to apply here. I've never left a negative review before, as I usually speak directly to companies about issues, but this experience pushed me beyond that point. I want to warn future renters.

I've lived here for several years, and every year the complex goes downhill, management is not pleasant especially after you get your keys. Also the landscaping never gets taken care of. The hedges have been taken care 1 in 4 years, you can't even sit on the patio because everything is so over grown. Also, there's a infestation of nates due to the trash and recycle shoot . There in the hallways and especially when you open your door they get into your unit. Lastly the amount they raise the rent when your lease is up is way over done. The rent you pay here is not worth living here. There's plenty of other apartments in the area and there new builds. I would advise going that route then living here.

I toured here and the staff was quite unpleasant, not even taking me to the apartment but instead handing me keys and pointing in the direction of the building the model was in. The exteriors look like a prison? Interiors are poorly updated. Unimpressed.

I lived in this complex for 1 year. Something that they did not tell us before we moved in was that tenants can smoke in their apartments. We had downstairs and side neighbors that smoked and so we could never open the windows or balcony. It also smelled of smoke in the hallways and laundry room. We did not have central AC and the box unit that is in the living room didn't cool down anywhere else in the apartment so we ended up sleeping in the living room for multiple months. There are a lot of families with young children who tend to play in the parking lot without supervision. The walls were very thin and we could hear all of our neighbors, even multiple apartments away. We also witnessed a fist fight in the parking lot. The only reason I didn't give it a 1 star review is because the staff was very nice (besides not telling us about smoking) and because it was a cheep place to live for a year.

I lived at Green Briar 2 different times but moved for work . I would give Green Briar 5 stars because I loved my place when I lived there and the management was always helpful and there for my needs. . I felt at home living there and if I ever move back the first place I will go to is Green Briar.The location is great and the pool was nice and relaxing.The apartments are a little out dated but still nice .This is a great place to live.

My house was Robbed on 10/3/16 at around 7.30 pm in the Evening , I live in  building 234, My house is facing the woods,. the theif took all 2 laptops, watches, camera ,'CLOTHES' and lot of valuable personal items.  for all those who think green briar is safe - NO IT IS NOT, there are Break In's which happen regularly for once every four months (according to cops) .. If your lease is expiring i strongly recommend to moving to a secure community which has more lights and good play area for kid's.
