Another issue occurred when the maintenance staff lit the pilot light in my fireplace (as I requested) but didn't turn off the switch so my apartment was 96 degrees when I got home from work.  I contacted the leasing office to let them know what happened, and I never heard anything back.  Those were just a few of the issues I had in my last year living at Autumn Creek.  After the last year, I cannot recommend these apartments.

This was my first apt after graduating university. It was really lovely, maintenance was quick to respond to any issues that arose and appliances worked excellently. Community events were something to look forward to and my neighbors were very polite.

I’ve lived here in a 2nd floor unit for three years. Great tenant. Always paid rent in time. One time I asked to transfer to empty unit on 3rd floor because of excessive noise both above and below my unit. Was told no with no reason given. Had issues with drugs in the building and was told to deal with it myself. Am moving now and asked to extend my lease one month mid summer and was denied, despite the many vacant units already in the complex. Not accommodating at all, not smart business and very unprofessional as far as I’m concerned

If I had known about the disastrous parking situation, I would never have moved here. Since moving in just a few weeks ago, I have spoken to the property manager twice and was told that each unit is allowed two vehicles, but only one space. Okay... so where is MY space? Visitor parking at the back is usually full meaning that I have to park in front of the first building and walk across a dark, grassy hill at 2 am after returning from work. This is not just inconvenient, but dangerous. Both Castleberg Properties and the HOA board should be ashamed about this mess and especially when a simple solution is within reach. Am already planning on my next move OUT of this 'amazing condo community.'

I lived in a 2nd floor unit on this property. It is spacious enough to accommodate a small family, with lofted ceilings which add  an expansive feeling to the environment. Maintenance is responsive, friendly, and quick to service requests. The property manager is friendly and works as much as she can in the best interest of the resident.

The neighborhood is mostly populated by families; on any given day in the summer, you're likely to find young children playing around with each other, giving off a neighborly, residential vibe. There is a bike path right near the property which leads to the UW Arboretum. Just down the road there is an elotero and various food truck vendors selling their wares near the elementary school, adding to the charm of the neighborhood. Lastly, there is a pool, which is restricted to the residents of Whispering Pines and their guests. This is a cozy, affordable place to live.

Just before I moved out of my condo (for reasons unrelated to the quality of the place,) the property began making renovations to the buildings, replacing the siding and front doors of each unit only adding to the value of the place and communicating an investment in the people who live there. It was a pleasure to have lived there as long as I did.

I currently live in a 2 bedroom and I've enjoyed my stay at Whispering Pines. James the property manager has always be really flexible and accommodating for my roommate and I. We didn't have to call maintenance often but when we did it our issues were resolved promptly. I love that the biking trail is right next to the complex and easy to access. Neighbors are pretty quiet and you get a lot of fresh air as the area is close to some woods. The grounds are pretty and kept clean. The apartment itself is spacious and I loved the lofted ceilings for the 2nd floor. I'll really miss this place!

I lived here for three years, in two different units.

Overall, the place is great. The property is well maintained, I liked the peacefulness of the neighborhood, and the management has been good.

When I lived on the Fish Hatch side of the building, I decided to switch to the other side of the building because Fish Hatch was a very loud street. Especially because it seems to be a preferred ambulance route into Madison.

Also, I like the neighborhood, but it is not improving in a way that’s good for general public. Meaning, no new restaurants / businesses / bars / etc. Only new medical facilities and luxury apartment buildings.

These apartments are in a great central location, with a nice coffee shop and great places within easy walking or biking distance. There are lots of nice perks, including a great bbq patio in back with plenty of seating, two reservable community rooms, and a rooftop deck with views of the lake and capitol. The landscaping and common areas are very well maintained and staff is friendly.

I am approaching my one year anniversary and have extended my lease at Wingra Point.   Competitive in cost with other buildings of its kind, it has many extras that give it a sense of home and enjoyment...a lovely outdoor patio and rooftop exterior, a game room, a gym, free coffee in the morning. The blond exterior with floral landscaping makes it very attractive.   This midsize community, located in a residential neighborhood centrally located with easy access to the entire city, is a gem.  It is convenient to medical, educational and social venues with a great coffee house across the street and walking distance to a local grocery.  I appreciate how the courtesy and responsiveness of the staff. Everyone feels welcome.

The 1BR apartments at 518 are small-ish but having all utilities included and an overall low rent makes smaller living worthwhile. Being right downtown has great perks too. Pretty much everything Madison has to offer is walk-able from the University events, to the Farmer's Market and both lakes. McBride is very responsive when it comes to maintenance requests as well.

I have been living here for 7 years and have nothing but good things to say about the property and the property management company. The apartments are lovely, and everything is very well maintained. It's also in a prime location next to Waldorf Park, and just down the street from the Jeffy Trail. I feel at home here!

Located in a nice, quiet residential area.  Great for walking or riding bikes.  Some parks and trails nearby but shops, restaurants or other retail is too far to walk.  For a fairly new building, I was disappointed in the quality (drawers and cabinets coming apart...management said they were working with the builder/having issues), wall cracks and mismatched paint from repairs.  The apartment was turned over in filthy condition so make sure you inspect immediately upon receiving keys in case additional work needs to be completed.  So much hassle trying to get things done after move-in!  Also, for the price there are absolutely no amenities except parking, courtyard and doggie clean up stations.  But overall decent place to live with a great floorplan.

Ive been renting a studio apartment here for the last year and it's really nice. My friends all live on the east side and wonder why I live so far away but I really enjoy this building. It's the most quiet apartment I've ever lived in even with a lot of dogs in the building. The cons consist of: the floors are hard to keep clean, there are some aggressive dogs (not aggressive breeds, they would benefit from pet interviews), and we had some trouble with maintanence clearing snow with a leaf blower at 3 or 4 am in the winter. But having a washer and dryer in my unit is worth any con I had to deal with here.

The location is great, the apartments are quite nice, and the price isn't bad either! Much more reasonable than some of the neighboring buildings, with better appliances, more space, and great parking! They do lack some ammenities, and the repair services were a little slow. Other than that, we have had no issues here. 

The building is quiet, the neighbors keep to themselves (sometimes too much so), and the common areas are always kept clean. Finally, underground parking included in the rent is a HUGE plus!

This is the building I have been waiting for. I am currently on the mailing list for this property. I am very excited about the location and the upscale features. Close to downtown, restaurants, parks, and Vilas Zoo. Finally an affordable building with great location! So excited!!

It's been over six months living in this apartments after selling our house, we did felt like our home. Maintenance is great (takes care of any problems immediately and the service is really good). Wexford Place Apartments are spacious and located in the west side of Madison near to hospitals, restaurants, and shopping malls. This apartment also features clubhouse to throw some parties, 24x7 gym for tenants, and swimming pool. Management is top class!

Before moving to Wexford we were looking for a safe, well maintained and reasonably priced place. If you are looking for the same thing, this is the place. I would recommend 100%. There’s a pool, gym and a shared room that you can book for a day for FREE. Everything is cleaned and well maintained at all times.

The units are nice, and spacious, prices are competitive.  I think pound for pound it’s the nicest place to live in the city of Madison.  Surrounded by good restaurants and beautiful shopping centers you’re not far from something to do, but is also a quiet, residential neighborhood.  Home buyers program is useful.
Great apartments. So fast at replying to emails and very on top of it all around!

Quite Neighborhood, Friendly Management, Spacious Apts, Well Maintained and budget friendly with many amenities. Located right where you have all that you need (restaurants, groceries, Malls etc.) in just couple mile radious.
Do check them first if you are looking for one.

We’ve lived here for 2 years and we have not had any reasons to complain. The staff and management respond promptly to our needs; the neighbors are friendly and the grounds are conducive for my little one to run around. Recommend Wexford 100%.
Since moving in our pets are happier and so are we. It's beautiful with the dark flooring with granite  countertops through out!! A   rating!  It's the best place to live!
This is a gorgeous new apartment building with open floor plans and top notch fixtures and appliances.

I’ve been trying to call the office for days and at different times, but no one, ever picked up the phone to set an appointment to handle my application. When I finally got it at the time of my interview the lady in the office said she was in a 45 minutes long virtual meeting and that I should wait until it was over. Why did I bother setting an appointment? Bad service, non-existing way of communicating with them

I love my current apartment--it's a good spot if you're not super interested in being all the way downtown or too far into the suburbs. It's a 15-20 minute drive to just about anywhere in town, and walking distance to a few need-to-go places as well (Copps, Starbucks, Great Dane, Anytime Fitness, Walgreens, etc). I love the heated garage and the size/layout of the apartment, plus it's pet friendly for those people who care about that. 

HOWEVER, there is not central heat/air. It just has the wall-unit, which would probably be okay except that in the apartments which have a lofted design, I have found it to be nearly impossible to get the upstairs at a good temperature when it is the dead of winter or the height of summer. No matter how many fans I use or how much I blast the cold air, the upstairs is always significantly hotter in the summer. At least in winter it can be handled a little more since heat rises, but as someone who doesn't just leave the unit on all day while I'm gone, it's pretty brutal at first.

Also, this complex doesn't have any sort of pool/workout center/clubhouse or anything, but that wasn't super important to me. There is a courtyard type area where people can run their dogs around though! 

Other than that, I love the apartment and I would recommend the location for anyone who wants the nice middle-ground location in Madison/Fitchburg.

My husband and I lived at this apartment community for a little over a year and I can honestly say it was a very nice experience. We moved from Texas to Wisconsin bc of a job transfer and even though ppl might think it's crazy I was mostly only worried about crime/safety. We never had any problems. It was very nice and quiet. Management was always on top of everything. The only thing I would've wanted was a pool! Definitely recommend this place.
I should have viewed property during daylight hours. I only saw area around apartment at night. Big mistake.

Very awesome place Maitenance is a little bad but other than that the place is phenomenal it's a fancy apartment for a great cost compared to the last two apartments I lived in this is like high class very welcoming and quiet neighborhood very home like highly recommended love it here

I have been very pleased with this property. It is quiet with friendly neighbors and the property manager responds within a day. The ladies in the office are always pleasant. I highly recommend this clean, quiet and well kept apartment complex.

I have lived here now for nine years and just love it.  Friendly people which includes all the personnel who work here to keep it up and looking nice.
Things get fixed the same day in most cases....unless its something major where they have to order the appliance.
Rent is very reasonable. the pool is large and maintained as well as the grounds.....Its is kept up like you would if you had a home.

I haven't even moved into the West End Apartment Complex's yet and I am having an amazing experience. The staff and landlord made me feel reassured in my decision to move forward with the apartment and have pathed a walkway for my with ease the whole process. I am a first-time renter and it has been a stressless process, also with visiting they had shown me respect and dignity. The location is incredible and the look of the property outside and inside is breath-taking. Easily one of, if not the best, places to live in Verona!

I enjoyed my time at West End. The 1 bedroom apartment has plenty of living and closet space. The trash and recycling is located inside a room within the parking garage -- a huge plus in the winter! And the staff is helpful; they are quick to respond to questions and are easy to work with. 

I'm going to miss being so close to Epic. The longest part of my commute was driving through campus! On days I wanted to hit the snooze multiple times, it was nice knowing that I could go from lounging in my bed to getting ready to sitting in front of my desk within 15 minutes.

Quiet building. Friendly staff and maintenance on time. 
Beautiful designed apartments with granite counters, ceiling fans, central air. Your lucky if you can get in too one of these apartments. Pet friendly. I’m happy I moved here. That’s saying a lot since construction has been ongoing for the past year across the way but speciality shoppes will be added as well. Cisco is down the street and Middleton is called “The good neighbor city.”
Happy Camper
Very accommodating pleasant decent neighbors quiet a place you can call home

The management is terrible. This fix nothing. The have a mice problem and never addressed it. Garbage is everywhere. When they changed to a new management company the whole place went to hell and the tenants are trashy and the children have no supervision. Management never fixed anything work orders 2 years old. Everyone started to move out. DO NOT rent from them. You will also find charges that are false. There books are not kept up properly. They don't care about the property at all or the safety of people.
The outside looks nothing like the photos. Garbage is everywhere & the siding is damaged &fading. 4or 5 units moved in the last months &we are trying to as well.

From 6/1/21-5/31/22 we were tenants at The Revere at Smith Crossing. In order to have pets a $1530 deposit was collected, and we paid $20 extra for each pet per month for a total of $1570 per month.  We received an invoice charging $1453.84 which was for cleaning and carpet replacement and no return of deposit when we moved out. 
The replacement of the carpet was ordered on 05/11/2022 when the Property Manager submitted a work order to "Pull Carpet".  This was a full 20 days before the lease was up and prior to any final inspection.  When asked about this, the decision was justified in an email from the property manager of stating:
"The carpet replacement was scheduled early as a precautionary measure after my pre-inspection in which I noticed a heavy pet odor and likely damage.  This is standard practice in order to secure an installer as they get very busy towards the end of each month”
Photos taken during check out show the state of the carpet and that there were no visible surface stains which leads one to the conclusion that changing the carpet of ANYONE with pets is indeed "precautionary" "standard procedure" not based on actual visible damage noted. We own two cats which are litter box trained. The litter boxes were located in the front hallway right when you entered. This is the source of the smell. Once the litter boxes were scooped and changed the odor also dissipated.   The Revere stated that the presence of 3-4 stains, under the carpet on the pad but not visible on the surface necessitated total carpet replacement. 
We were billed for $1453.84 which is $2375.28 minus the for new carpet/pads. They even provided an invoice for the carpet, where the installer clearly wrote "No new pad needed"
The official check out checklist provided to us states: "We will attempt to have it cleaned at your cost" No record of this being attempted or a submitted work order is given on the final receipt.

I've lived here for almost 3 years now and really have enjoyed it. By far some of the best apartments I've lived at. Never had a bad experience with the staff here or with other residents. The review on here saying the hallways and such are always dirty and full of debris is entirely incorrect. They are cleaned at least weekly. Rent is easy to pay online, underground parking is nice, elevator is modern and works great.

I called to set up a tour to see one of the apartments when my daughter is visiting from out of town.  The person who answered the phone (a male) said that he didn't have time to show us any apartments.  He said that they don't have any available apartments to show that are not occupied.  I told him that it states on the website that they have over 10 apartments available for rent.  I said that we would look at a 2 bedroom if that was easier for him.  He said no, that he would not show us a 2 bedroom unless we were interested in renting it in the next 60 days.

I told him that we are visiting from out of town, and we would like to see the facilities.  He said that I should tell my daughter to look at the website photos.  He said that I should call back 60 days prior to the move in date.  I told him that he was forcing us to visit other apartments, and he said that sounds good to him.  

Not sure why I received such rude treatment when I was calling to schedule a viewing to move in on June 1st, but I'm not going to visit now.

For the amount of $$ this place charges, everything should be cleaned and hallways vacuumed.

* Hallways and inside of apartment complex is NEVER KEPT UP. smells, dirt, and debris left all over.

Apartment is NOT worth the money

I love living at The Revere! The quality of the finishes is better than any other apartment that I have lived in and are the kinds of finishes I would want when I build a home. The on-site management is always friendly and available to answer questions. With the fitness center I was able to stop paying a gym membership and actually save money! Its extremely close to grocery stores and all sorts of restaurants!
Decent amount of room, landlord is awesome, love having assigned parking,   it's great area close to everything i need  to get to.

Beautiful building but management doesn’t care about tenants or their well-being. Requested to meet several times and was not given the opportunity. Management too busy to meet with tenant. Police are called to the building on several occasions, feel free to check with the police station to see how many times they have had to come for calls. They are quick to non renew your lease for small in fractions even if your rent is paid on time.
This place is disgusting. Dog pee in the hallways, trash constantly piles, management never responds.

The staff here are the absolute best we’ve ever dealt with! The property managers Conyunn and Julie were heaven sent! This development is HUGE and to get personalized service is unheard of, even with smaller properties! Their energy, attitude and conduct is professional and caring! Love to call this place home and recommend it to anyone seeking new, quiet and convenient location!

Avoid this place at all costs

Living at Society Orlando has been one of the most unpleasant and embarrassing experiences we’ve had as residents. Before you move in, they treat you wonderfully, promising exceptional service and efficient management. But once you sign the lease, they stop caring about you completely.

The management and leasing staff have no idea what they are doing. They are not qualified for their positions, and all they do is waste your time. If you have an issue or need help, they send you from one person to another without giving you any explanation, as if they don’t even know how to do their job. The information they provide is inconsistent, depending on who you talk to, creating complete chaos with payments and any actions you need to take as a resident.

Even worse, their incompetence forces you to pay unnecessary charges that you never get refunded. They give you incorrect payment information, making you overpay for things, and even charging you twice without any justification. When you try to dispute it, they simply ignore you or keep giving you vague responses that don’t solve anything.

In particular, the management team, including Nicky and Cherry, is extremely unprofessional. Not only are they incompetent, but they also show a complete lack of interest in helping residents. Their attitude is indifferent, unprofessional, and completely unacceptable for a place that is supposed to provide a good living experience.

The leasing team, including Angela and the rest, is no better. Instead of providing clear and precise assistance, they confuse residents even more with contradicting information, causing frustration and unnecessary issues.

It’s a shame because the building itself is beautiful, but the poor management and terrible treatment of residents completely ruin the living experience. There is no real service, no assistance—just indifference, disorganization, and a complete lack of knowledge from the staff.

If you’re considering moving here, think twice. Don’t make the same mistake we did.

Gabbi was amazing! Starting with her excellent service made my initial impression positive. The place itself is undeniably beautiful, and I appreciate the vision behind it. However, given the high rent, I would have preferred more spacious accommodations. Better promotional offers and a lower deposit, perhaps, would have made me more inclined to lease here.

Stay away from this property. They think it’s suitable to collect full rent on a unit that has had black mold for over 60 days. I’ll save the details regarding the 3 manager changes in the last 18 months and the deterioration of the complex for another post. To be continued… 2/17/25 I thought I would update this to say that they were committed to resolving this issue but that was not the case. They felt it was only sufficient to pull up a small portion of the floor to check for mold and only offer about a 15% discount on January’s rent that included compensation for my damaged items. Since then, other leaks have occurred in this unit. Please avoid renting from this property at all costs.

Long time resident that has seen the complex go downhill dramatically with the current property owners. The front office provides cookie-cutter responses while smiling but there seems to be no concentrated effort to resolve serious issues with our apartments or the grounds. Management will rarely get back to you in a timely manner when there is a serious issue (ie, plumbing, fire risk, hazards on the ground) but are very quick to write a response when a negative review is left online. 

Trash is littered on the floors of every building thanks to the 'trash pickup' service we were forced to agree to, essentially making tenants leave their trash outside in bins that are rarely emptied and almost always improperly kept. The water is shut off every 1-2 months without notice on average and the dumpsters where trash is collected are almost always overflowing and pouring into the street. All of these issues continue with no actions taken while we receive daily texts announcing the arrival of a cheap food truck or that the office has closed early. 

They simply do not care. 

Save yourself the anxiety and stress and do not fall for the "luxury" they offer.

First of all, this place was originally called Heather Glen apartments and then was sold. The new owners changed it to the Glenn to escape the negative previous reviews. Now a few years after that, Spring of 2022, it was sold to a management company in Seattle that changed the name to Phoenix. If it was such a quality apartment, why change the owners and name 3 times?? 

Appliances do not work at all. The awkward layout includes a freaking fireplace! Who needs a fireplace in Orlando, FL?  They do not include a microwave either so I had to go buy one of those. I've had to have my washer, dryer, fridge and oven fixed so many times. They never actually fix something completely. It's just a "duct tape" fix until it breaks again 5 hours later.

I moved in with mold in my a/c ducts, an empty fire extinguisher, a carbon dioxide monitor that wasn't turned on and didn't even have batteries in it and lights not working over the stove and one of the bathrooms. 

They frequently turned the water off via text message saying it would be off in one building for 45 minutes but it would be the entire complex for about 6 hours. It's wonderful not to be able to use the bathroom, shower, or clean your kids for 6 hours.

The complex started getting updated in the units near the leasing office so we went to tour the model and it was beautiful! Hardwood floors, brand new appliances, more space, walk in closets, double sinks, no weird fireplace layout in the living room and being close to the pool, office and mail center sounded remarkable. We signed for the upgrade and the increase in price after being promised an upgraded unit in 2 months. That was 6 months ago and my family still lives in the old 2/2 with carpet, broken appliances, the sink drains smell like raw sewage, and no space. 

We do get the pleasure of now paying over $300 more in rent for the upgraded unit we are not in. We keep asking for an update on when we can move so we can hire movers, switch mail, internet and cable, lights, etc to the new unit. We were told every month for the last 6 months but there is a waitlist. Now there's signs all over that there is no wait list and immediate occupancy is available. We had friends we asked to call from their phones to ask about availability for an upgraded 2/2 to be told there is no wait and those units are available now.

I've already downloaded copies of my lease, found a new apartment and hired a lawyer

I’ve lived at The Glenn now called The Phoenix for almost 4 years. It has switched owner twice in the time I’ve lived here so I’ve seen the good, the bad and the ugly. If your a college student and in your 20s this place is great for you. Residents partying all the time at the pools, loud cars and people hanging out in the parking lot most of the time. If you own a car plan on it getting bumped by people trying to park their cars at 2am after a night out. Will threaten to remove you & any guests out of the property  if they feel you are not obliging their rules. The level of unprofessionalism of the staff is unbelievable. Save yourself a headache don’t bother, I can’t wait to leave this prison.

Did my research and schedules a tour in April. Loved everything about the complex and apartment and signed my lease 3 days later. Moved in end of April and it is now August and I’m so happy I chose this place. Kendra at the front office is great as well as the other staff and nothing but good things to say about the maintenance team. Work orders are completed within 24hrs and bonus (for me anyway), it’s literally right by the airport. I never really here the planes which is surprising. Can’t wait to look into a 2 bedroom when my lease is up
I placed a work order. Immediately that same day, they solved my problem. I am very pleased, thank you.

The apartment itself was nice enough, however I can not say the same for the front office staff. Make sure EVERYTHING is done in writing with the office. We would not recommend this apartment complex.

Great place to live with sound security. Office staff, Andrea offers great customer service.  Always attentive and quick responses to any concerns or problems. Awesome place to live with great amenities.

I arrived in Orlando from Denver, Colorado almost two years ago. After searching and touring luxury apartments throughout the city, The Yard was the one we liked the most because it had the best features. Excellent location, Extremely clean and maintained, friendly staff. It has the best pool area in the city. I definitely recommend the Yard for people looking for the best in town.
After 3 years I still love living at The Yard.  I can walk to shops and restaurants.  The gym is outstanding.  Maintenance is always quick and helpful.
I enjoy the community but guest parking is a big issue
I genuinely love living here. There’s a nice sense of community, the staff is incredibly kind, the amenities are beautiful and the surrounding neighborhood is lovely.

I have lived at The Yard for more than 2 years and the maintenance team have always been prompt, professional and friendly each time I have reported an issue.  All my issues have been minor in nature. Love living at The Yard!
The Yard is a great place to live, with fantastic amenities. The Ivanhoe area is perfect for working professionals, and has numerous restaurants and bars in walking distance. Highly recommended.

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review: Moving into The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park was an amazing experience! The leasing team made the entire process seamless, special shoutout to Jamie. The apartments are beautiful, spacious, and great views. The amenities are top-notch, including a great pool and fitness center. The location is unbeatable—right in the heart of Baldwin Park, with easy access to great dining, shopping, and parks. I couldn’t be happier with my decision to live here and highly recommend The Majestic to anyone looking for luxury, convenience, and a great community!

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review:
I’ve been a resident at The Majestic for the past two years, and I’ve had a great experience. The property has an overall welcoming atmosphere. The management team is always professional and responsive to any questions or maintenance requests. I also appreciate the convenience of the location—it's just a walk to shops, restaurants, and public transport.

The community here is fantastic; my neighbors are friendly, and there are regular social events that really foster a sense of connection. Overall, I’m very happy with my living experience, and I would highly recommend The Majestic to anyone looking for a great place to call home.

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review: The location is incredibly convenient, with easy access to shopping, and dining options. The customer service, maintenance responsiveness, pools & gyms and overall environment have been an excellent addition to my lifestyle.

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review: Challenging place to live. No trash service must take garbage down the elevator to dumpster. Elevator broken often. Upon moving out refuse to return deposit chasing it for six months already.

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review: Horrible place to live. Would not recommend to anyone. My ceiling leaked for 9 months before it was fixed (only due to it caving in). There was mold for the longest time and when asked about rent reduction due to the literal hole in my ceiling I was told to contact my renters insurance. Wish I had never moved in.

apartmentName: The Majestic at Downtown Baldwin Park
review: I have lived here for a month, and I'm loving it!! But the best part has to be the location everything  is downstairs on the main floor of the building!! Lake Baldwin is perfect to exercise and unwind after work super friendly  neighbors

The staffing and management is terrible. I live here for about 2 months and then I move out due to a job transfer. Every unit here has a smart lock but my unit doesn't (the excuse was that it was on back order and none was available, I never receive a smart lock for the door from day of moving in until day of moving out). 

I put down a deposit to rent the unit and then I was told it could be void if you applied for their services. In which I did sign up to void the deposit but that didn't happen, I still have to pay for the services and the full deposit which is a bummer when they lied to you about it. I never receive the deposit back as they say it was put toward fixing the unit upon my department and nothing was damage when I left, so basically I lose the deposit I put down. 

Overall I don't recommend renting here since there are a lot of fee you have to pay for. From parking, to mailbox fees, among other housing utilities fee. You'll end up wasting more than you would think for renting their unit out. I give this place a 1 star.
Apartments are terrible, roach infested refrigerators terrible appliances save your time, energy and piece of mind this place is a dump!

The appliances in my apartment are old and in bad conditions and management has been informed several times. Nothing has been done. They promised to take care of the appliances for me and that was never completed. No security-a trespasser entered the complex and starting shooting. These are only some of the highlights. I would’ve wished that someone would’ve advised me about this place before I moved here. DO NOT RENT HERE!

Roaches, mold, ants and holes in the wall. Said unit was ready for move in and it was a mess. Also doors have no keys, it’s a keypad lock, not very safe to me. And the office, goodluck reaching them! They are always closed or no help at all!

I lived here for as short amount of time as possible. The place was covered in garbage. I had fleas in my apartment when I moved in. They never fixed any maintenance requests that I submitted. And when they DID fix anything, they left a mess which stained my carpets and then they had the gall to take that out of my security deposit. The walls were literally rotting away. There was grey slime dripping from the ceiling (Can't make this up). This was by far the worst place I've ever lived in. I'm still waiting for them to return my security deposit. It's been over a year. They claim I'm somehow responsible for the disgusting state of the place, but that was all due to their inability to maintain their property. Whatever you're thinking, this place isn't worth it. Save your money and take your business elsewhere.

shoddily built, can hear EVERYTHING upstairs and toilets.

management refused to fix dryer, or lets just say, I told them about it being broken from the 12th to the 26th and then just fixed it myself.

they admitted they are too lazy or incompetent to fix things by saying...."well, we have over 60 other maintenance things and its first come first serve.

you advertise as being a luxury apartment complex, if you can't even address 1/4 of all the apartments having maintenance issues, then you are just a slum.  don't rent here.  trust me, its only been 19 days and can't wait to leave.

I just wanted to take a moment to express my gratitude for the exceptional service provided by the staff at our apartment complex. From the friendly and attentive management team to the diligent maintenance staff, everyone goes above and beyond to ensure that residents feel valued and well taken care of. In addition to the safety measures they took to keep us safe all day everyday. It's truly a pleasure to call this place home, thanks to the hard work and dedication of the entire team. Keep up the fantastic work!

Flashy but cheaply built with some unique issues. Focusing on the problems you won't notice on a tour. AVOID SIXTH FLOOR, ESPECIALLY THE CORNERS!


Location:
Lots of noise on the southwest side with construction, loud trains / announcements, and buses.

With those transit hubs, the 7/11, and the abandoned building on Amelia it's a magnet for homeless folks (it adds to noise).

When this stretch of Orange is closed for parades and events several times a year it's hard to get in or out of the building.


Quality:
The building itself is cheap wooden construction. 

Our unit was at the top southwest corner and sags causing cracks throughout and the floors to sink so far that you can feel elevation shifts and get big vibrations as you walk. The hallway AC unit on the roof directly above the office gushes water and causes severe leaks.

When a hurricane created new damage there were so many leaks from so many things in the building (ACs, sprinkler issues, the roof, the hurricane) that ours weren't fixed from 9/22 until 1/23. There're still damaged ceilings in the hallways and I've heard from management that there're roof leaks that travel down to the second floor and they have leaks in their own units.

Pipes already make weird noises, at least one elevator goes out every few months, the package lockers are damaged, and the garage gates get stuck open or shut often (most recently one was stuck shut for 1.5 months endangering everyone by forcing incoming and outgoing traffic to share one tight gate with blind corners). 


Design:
Shared space decor is really hit or miss.

The hallways are in bad shape from lack of repairs, painting, or care.


Management:
American Landmark took over in 2021.

Renovations have come slow and are poor quality, sometimes even being abandoned or undone.

The office is unwilling to budge on policy to help you yet don't make enough effort to enforce policies like not leaving trash in the hallways.

The maintenance team is very nice and seem to be doing their best with what they inherited. Unfortunately, whoever is allocating funding for their fixes isn't providing them with enough money to get the work done right. Fixes for anything that takes over a day are slow.


Safety:
The building has security but residents and even homeless folks outsmart it. I've heard of them getting into hallways, stairwells, and vacant units. There was a video posted by a woman who came home to find a homeless woman going through her stuff.

I have been a resident here since August of 2022 and this review is definitely long overdue. Central Station on Orange was my first apartment living in downtown Orlando and this team has added to my experience in every way possible. Nakia and Reneil (the property managers) are hands down the best leasing team I have ever had in my years of renting. They set up weekly classes (art, cooking, etc.) in the downstairs cafe that is free to every resident. For Valentines day they hosted a “dinner under the stars” on the rooftop with a DJ, drinks, amazing food, and (the best part) the maintenance team serving the entire night with amazing dance moves, smiles and jokes. After the valentines event, they personally came to our door with a gift bag including a framed picture of my roommate and I and some goodies. Every single person from the maintenance team has done everything possible to help my roommate and I set up an amazing home and feel as safe as possible considering it is two women in the apartment. Walking around the property everyday really makes it feel like home and a big family all because of the bright smiles and care from Nakia, Reneil, the entire maintenance team, Victoria, Alex and Angie (previous leasing agent).
Plus they have free snacks and coffee every single day in the office and who doesn’t love that?

The worst rental experience ever. I lived here for two years and never had a late payment. Upon move out, they had a final payment notice of $145 but did not send it to my new address I gave them upon move out, they sent it to my old apartment address in the building... AFTER moving out. I was only notified of this after I received my credit report and a collections notice hurting my credit score. I was never contacted by phone, mail, or email, and their portal never showed the amount balance. This is the most incompetent Real Estate Management company I have ever dealt with.

The apartments themselves are nice and spacious on the inside. The amenities are about average. But please be aware before signing a lease: There is almost non-stop construction right next to the apartments of a new high rise. The construction workers have started at ungodly hours ranging from 12AM-5AM. The property management company says there is nothing they can do about it. If you are looking for an apartment here and it’s on the side of construction I would advise DON’T do it.

The apartment complex is one I hope to never leave. It is secure and safe! The office staff call you by name and are always able to assist! The floor plans are spacious and livable. Communication is important and they are on it!

The positive reviews are inaccurate and probably written by the office staff. The parking situation here is an absolute joke! There is literally no parking for visitors whatsoever! My babysitter circled the parking lot for over 20 minutes hoping one of the very few visitors spots would open up, no such luck! I told her just to park in the way back of the complex because it was going to be impossible to find a visitors spot. Unfortunately, her car was towed last night! When I spoke to the office, their suggestion was to “park down the street at Publix.” Are you F’ Kidding me?! Park a mile away and hope that your car doesn’t get broken into or towed. People are barely getting by and these people are making money off towing your car because they don’t provide adequate parking. I do not recommend this property unless you never want to have family or friends over. This is just another headache from an over priced and over rated apartment complex.
A tow truck is every night making money out of people who paid rent and is no parking available

I moved into  my apartment about 2 months ago and i can honestly say i love it here! I moved from Miami so it's been a pretty big change for me. My boyfriend & I have absolutely no complaints whatsoever besides the overflow of parking but this is actually something they are currently resolving so we are excited to see what happens now. Kimberly was the one who initially showed us the apartment and helped us through the application process and she was great!! Anna on the other hand was the one who moved us in, did the walk around in the apartment and she's also been the one to deal with my 1 million questions lol. She's honestly so amazing and extremely helpful! Coming from a city where everyone is so fast paced, rude and lacking in customer service, moving here with a great office staff is a breath of fresh air. Every time i call the office whoever picks up the phone sounds "ready to help!" which is great! I definitely recommend The Oasis at Moss Park for anyone looking to move in the Lake Nona area :)

I am the first tenant in my apartment, have lived here for a year, and I will not be renewing my lease. Here's why:
1.) Parking is miserable, if you work late nights (like I do) you won't get a parking spot anywhere close to your apartment
2.) It's not very well lit out at night
3.) They do yard work outside apartments at 7am
4.) I can hear EVERYTHING from my upstairs neighbors : Fights/yelling, walking around in heels, music (I could sing along if I wanted to), and they always wake my husband and I up around 5:45am. Noise complaints have yet to solve this issue.
5.)The apartments are very dim/dark once furniture is moved in.
6.) You can hear everything that goes on in the hallways outside of your apartment
Pros:
1.)Can pay rent online
2.)Close to 417
3.)Pet friendly (even has a puppy park that no one takes their dogs to) 

For the money you're spending, it's best to just rent out a house instead. I got pulled in by everything being shiny and brand new, but the past year living here has been pretty miserable. The little things add up and slowly will get on your nerves.

Cons - The parking is AWFUL. If you are not there by 9pm sometimes 8:30 you can forget about having a spot anywhere close to your apartment. The apartments are dark...hardly any natural light. The air quality is poor and it often smells bad especially now this time of year. They left dead love bugs all over the sidewalks and in front of the apartments. The air conditioning does not flow well in the apartments. Will get coolest in the living room while the bedrooms are still very stuffy and warm.
Pros - It is quiet. I can hear foot steps from other apartments but that is to be expected. I can not hear anyone talking or being loud. It is close to 417 for convenience.
This place looks amazing! Would love to live here in a few months! Compared to where I live this place is beautiful!
We've been here close to two months now and really like the apartment. It suits all our needs well, and is well maintained.

It was an easy decision deciding on Dover Gardens. We have been here just one year, will be renewing and hopefully more.. The property is always kept safe & clean, the staff in the office is extremely friendly. The maintenance are quick & efficient. My children are safe and happy. Thank you Lulu & staff for all your hard work. It is truly appreciated.

Nice place, good community.
Maintenance is top notch, and getting in was easy
Es un lugar donde se respira paz, tranquilidad. Siempre esta limpio, las personas son muy amables. En un lugar centrico cerca de todo. Lo recomiendo.

Beautiful property great spacious apartments with a very nice set up. Pool area is beautiful quiet neighborhood and friendly staff. Especially the maintenance team. Great job Dover staff! You make this place worth calling home!
Son excelentes profesionales, desde mantenimiento hasta los de la oficina. Vivi por 7 años y el servicio fue de excelencia. Gracias y nunca cambien.

Landon House has been a premier complex for our stay thus far. The location is awesome. The complex is beautiful. It has safe surroundings. The office staff has been attentive. The maintenance crew cares about the grounds. Great job Landon House????

Don't get me wrong I love our apartment.  But the Managers are not doing a good job maintaining the building.  The Managers also need to work on their people skills.  I just wish the quality of the building was like it was on the day we moved in.  I hope in the new year we will see a change in the management staff as well as the building.

This used to be an amazing property. It was kept nice and clean.  Now the amenities are falling apart the hallway carpets are torn and dirty.  The pool furniture is filthy.  The Manager Kim doesn't care at all.  Its really sad because we used to love living here. We live on the first floor and see worms all the time inside the building.

The single best apartment experience of my lifetime. The staff is classy and polite and responsive. The property is gorgeous and the construction is high quality. The infinity pool is gorgeous, as are the added amenities: ping pong tables, hammocks, grill, and putting green. The fitness room is spacious and offers a wide range of equipment. I will have to ask them to add an arc machine. Overall, the property sports high quality fittings. The layouts are smart, efficient and attractive. The appliances, floor surfaces and available storage are better than any apartment I have seen. 

Very happy to rent at Landon House.

The staff is amazing, big shout out to Tony. This place is fairly priced in my opinion. The pool area is fantastic and lively but not too lively you can’t sleep. People are respectful here. I had lived in two different units and loved both of them. I hate that I moved away from work because it’s been a nightmare finding places for where I’m at now, but believe me this is a great choice. Oh, and every week they schedule quality food trucks to come by. I loved coming home from work and trying them out!

I absolutely love living here! The amenities are a great addition to the beautiful floor plans, awesome office staff and very kind and respectful tenants around the building. These apartments are also very secure with gates all around and the only way to enter is with a key fob (only residents have) or by entry allowed by a resident.
WOULD be a 5/5 if maintenance and leasing office was a little less lazy
This place was alright pre-COVID. Now it is a rip-off.

My experience with Coda apartments has been great from top to bottom. The leasing staff were very helpful with the move in process. The maintenance staff are thorough, skilled and prompt. I have no complaints. I'm very happy!
The apartment was clean upon move-in & everything was ready. If there were any issues, maintenance handled it within 24 hours. I cant wait for the rest of the lease term.
Very modern community, great amenities especially with the amazon hub!!

Since it is located right next to the Valencia College/UCF downtown campus, the building has that college dorm vibe. I've seen adolescents walk around shirtless in gym shorts/flip flops and kids running around. There is constant noise pollution from the hallways and doors slamming, especially during the evening. There have been numerous times of people screaming and cussing at each other late into the night. (Huge negative.)

The amenities are ok. Half of the EV chargers are always out of service. They only limit 2 hours of charging every 24 hours. The gym is ok as well. I do give props to the facilities team. The one's I have interacted with have been super nice and professional.
Lots of amenities, close to everything, excellent location.

The building itself is one of the worst pop up covid apartments! It is far from luxury. It’s fruit fly infested, pipes have bursted multiple times ruining apartments and belongings, the fire alarm gets set off which might not be annoying but if you work early in the morning it’s a huge inconvenience especially when it happens about twice a month. People wait at the door to try to sneak in behind you, there’s no guest parking they will tow your friends car from the hours of 6pm-8am. If you want to have friends over they have to pay per hour. And you have to go get your friends. Once they fix the garage (not sure if it’ll ever work it’s been broken for 6 months) how will my guests get in? They don’t have fobs so not only do they have to park on the 7th floor I have to go all of the way there just to open a door. We pay $25 to park in the garage and for what? There’s no security watching the garage and no security on property period. I wouldn’t mind paying if that money was actually going somewhere. There’s one security guard on property and that’s only because the gate is broken. There isn’t any pantry space for food, the cabinets are extremely small, there aren’t any storage closets for towels or blankets, there aren’t any light fixtures except for the kitchen, and the ac is the cheapest thing I’ve ever seen. I miss my old apartment in Kissimmee that I paid $600 less a month for. I cancelled a lease to live here and they truly offered luxury amenities. I was offered two months free but I’d pay the two months to GET OUT.

New management came less than a year ago and they’ve already turned this complex into a complete s***show. In the past 2 months, we have cars getting broken into almost weekly, refusing to fix the garage door. They allow fire alarms to go off weekly, many times in the middle of the night. They tried to sneak 2 extra charges onto my rent thinking I wouldn’t see it, had to dispute both times. Implemented new parking and threatened to tow anyone who didn’t pick up their tag within a week. Some other extremely poor aspects are them not keeping their pet relief area sanitary and forcing me to run a dehumidifier (which is basically as loud as the fire alarm) on 24/7 because someone flooded their apartment 8 floors above me. Terrible experience, would not recommend this apartment complex to anybody unless it’s their last resort.

Flooding, elevator broken, maintenance walking in without knocking, 0 guest parking, and other issues have been a huge problem at The Julian. I’ve been here 2 months and I am ready to break my lease and move on. I’ve stayed in a lot of high end places over the years and this is by far the worst experience I’ve had. I do not recommend living here at all.

Staff is super helpful, knowledgeable and polite. A variety of activities are offered for the residents. The amenities are spectacular and the units and common areas around the complex are beautiful. I love it here!

The Julian is overpriced, poorly managed, and offers a poor living experience behind the illusion of luxury. Do not move here.

I am a graduate student on a budget, but seeing as I only needed the apartment for a year or so, I decided to splurge on the Julian. The last apartment I lived in costed a quarter of what the Julian does, so I expected a significantly nicer standard of living. Other than the gym and pool, which are nice enough, that is not what I got. 

For a building that is less than two years old, there are a shocking number of infrastructure issues at the Julian. At least one of the building's elevators is broken at all times, often stranding residents in the process (myself included). If any of the smoke detectors in any of the units go off, the entire building is evacuated by deafening sirens and flashing lights. This is going to sound like an exaggeration, but sadly it is not - this has happened roughly twenty times over the course of my year-long stay here, all but one a false alarm. At one point we had evacuations on four straight days, two of them during Hurricane Ian, forcing residents and their pets outside and into the storm. 

On the subject of management, the Julian's is the worst I've ever experienced. The day I moved into the Julian, I had an appointment scheduled by management to be given my keys. Nobody showed for several hours, and I had to wait in the lobby for most of the day. That management team was far better than the two that have since replaced it. Current management is incompetent, rude, predatory, and completely unwilling to address even the smallest request without acting as though you are inconveniencing them. When I tried to go month-to-month to extend my lease for a short period, I could not get a straight answer as to what I'd be paying and how the transition to month-to-month would work.

Finally, let's talk about the other tenants. For whatever reason, the Julian is a magnet for inconsiderate people. Obviously there are plenty of residents who are nice and normal - but they are not the ones who affect your living experience. The tenants who play music at nightclub volumes after midnight, do hard drugs at the pool, go swerving around the tight corners in the parking garage, and leave dog poop and urine in the hallways and elevators are the ones who do affect your experience.

There is even more to take issue with that I won't go into, but if you have read this far, you get the picture. Don't move to the Julian.

I've only lived here for one month and my experience with management has been mostly unpleasant. They assigned me an apartment that they knew had a broken AC unit. It took 14 days after I moved in to get it fixed even though they told me when I moved in that the parts were on order. On top of that, I paid them the initial deposit they required but their online account showed I still owed $329. Then I didn't get the second month free I was supposed to get for moving in before July 31st. They said they found the error and it would be fixed by Friday 22nd. Then the following Monday, they said they had put in a request to see if they could fix it. I waited all week for any news on the fix. Then they ignore my messages this weekend when I try to get an update while out of town. You literally have to go down to the office and harass them to get an answer and its usually vague. They run The Julian less like a luxury apartment and more like a time share. If you do decide to move here, I highly recommend legal representation before signing the lease.

They’re constantly changing management, since Altman took over things got worse. All the good people left ( Brianna, Catherine , etc) and they put really bad staff that are not knowledgeable and do not care for residents. There is no internal communication regarding management changes.
They do not answer the phone, front gate is broken for a week now and I’m really concerned for all the money I’m paying here
They’re abandoning the building

They will do anything to get new residents however when it comes to renewing your lease, you'll see prices skyrocketing and no specials whatsoever 

you will be stuck with Hotwire that has a terrible service  
Had issues with water leak and mold and smells really bad

The Julian is a roach infested ghetto off Parramore. The ac constantly breaks. Bathrub and plumbing issues. Constant management changes. Garage and security doors breaks. Urine and trash in common areas. My dog was attacked and by an off leash dog on property and the Julian reviewed to cooperate with Animal Services. I do not feel safe. If you want to pretend you live in Downtown, feel free to apply. If you want peace and a safe neighborhood...RUN!!!

I've been living at the Julian for about 10 months and I still love it here, like the first day! Lately, I've really enjoying the community events like yoga, the food trucks, and the social media contest. Also, the amazing leasing staff always wants to make sure the residents are comfortable and they take care of any request immediately. I love it here!
We love our sunset views, the resident events and getting to know all of our neighbors here! It’s been a blast so far!

The absolute best! This apartment complex is so relaxing. It’s so quiet and I never feel like there’s nothing I can’t do. Also, they have the best events for the residents - working out, food,  wine nights, etc. The amount of work they put in to ensure we have these fun things going means a lot. Thanks Julian team for all that you do!

Save your time and money, don’t rent here. You’ll pay an insane amount to live in the middle of a construction zone and can’t walk one block west without being in the hood. I had to take an alternate route to the property because I would not drive through the neighborhood the gps wanted me to drive through.
It’s nowhere near market value and it’s in parramore! Google that street I’ll save you the trouble

I just moved out. Good riddance. Any interaction with the leasing/management office is unpleasant. They treat you like an insect and try to swat you away. 

My chief complaint is that the windows do not open. And the door to the balcony has no screen. No alternative but having AC on 24/7. While the summers are disgusting, no way to take advantage of nice weather when things cool off. No fresh air. And bad for the climate. And if the AC is broken (as recently happened as a result of Hurricane Milton), the apartment is rendered unlivable. 

Kitchen hood is not vented. Just blows the cooking fumes right back into the kitchen. And no way to open a window! 

Alarm incidents happen every few weeks and ALWAYS in the middle of the night. 

Valet trash service renders the hallways into an odorous  back alleyway full of trash containers everywhere. This concept saves the owner from having to put in adequate trash infrastructure like multiple trash chutes, while at the same time charging and profiting from the “valet” service. 

 And s finally, very large palmetto bugs, as well as fruit flies are always lurking about. 

These slipshod developers do anything to cut corners and enrich themselves, taking full advantage of inept building codes to the detriment  of the occupants.

I’ve been living at Deseo Grande Apartments for the past six months, and I can honestly say it has been a fantastic experience! From the moment I moved in, I felt right at home. The staff here is incredibly welcoming and always available to help with any questions or concerns. It's clear they care about creating a great community.

The apartment itself is spacious and well-designed, with a modern kitchen and comfortable living space. I love having a large pool area where I can relax in one of the pool lounges, enjoy my morning coffee, and soak up the Florida sun. The in-unit laundry is a huge plus as well, making life so much easier!

One of my favorite things about living here is the amenities. The pool area is absolutely gorgeous and perfect for relaxing on hot days. I also appreciate the fitness center, which is well-equipped and rarely crowded. Plus, the location is ideal—just a short drive from all the major attractions, shopping, and restaurants, yet it still feels like a quiet retreat.

I’ve enjoyed getting to know my neighbors and the sense of community here. Everyone is friendly, and there are often social events that make it easy to connect with others. 

Overall, I couldn't be happier with my decision to call Deseo Grande home. If you’re considering moving here, I highly recommend it! It’s truly a wonderful place to live.

I have since removed a review I wrote a week ago but this time, I will not be removing it! On Monday, the management team said some people were going to come out from 9-6pm to test out the building's ridiculous alarm system as it goes off at least 4-5 times a month or more. I don't know if anyone came out to check the alarm system as it never sounded that day, like they warned the residents. But it definitely went on at around 330am last night. I am sure it woke up the whole building. Like others have said, if there was a real fire, it would definitely be catastropihic as there have been many false alarms that almost everyone ignores at this time.

The leasing team/management cannot simply tell us they cannot legally remove them from our units. These alarms only cause stress for a lot of people, they do not serve their purpose. Management needs to remove these alarms and install better ones. For the $$$ they charge, they should! Plus, if they are truly concerned about our safety, action would have been taken and we shouldn't be having the same issues over and over again. Their action clearly shows, residents'' safely is NOT their #1 priority. It is not a surprise that some residents try to disconnect them. I have been a resident here for 3-4 years. When I first moved in, rent was lower than it is now. It made sense that the amenities that I paid for to the ones that I actually used ratio was good. To clarify, the laundromat was terrible. It required a card system that required you to go into the office,  a minimum of $5 per card (which is reloadable), and the washers were small. I would go to the laundromat in a shopping plaza. Since the rent was cheap I didn’t feel anyway about going a distance to wash my clothes. 
Now, my rent has been raised and my apartment hasn’t been updated. The outside of the complex and the aforementioned on-campus laundromat have been updated. They added storm doors to what used to be open air walkways to dark stairs. They painted the parking lot, planted some pretty flowers, took down the torn and tattered American flag, and laid some multch. I believe the roofs and the gray paint came before the new management. 
When comparing the price of my apartment to other appartments I have to say I am being robbed. The bathroom, laminate flooring is coming up, shower pressure is completely off, instead of redoing the tile I believe the painted it, the vent fan doesn’t work. HVAC system does well. The ventilation of the apartment is another thing in itself. This apartment was built in 1975, I’m assuming they didn't think central air all the way through. Each room has a one single vent. Depending on which way your apartment and room face, sunrise/sunset is going to be hotter than two slabs of bacon on a frying pan. The AC will not be able to keep up with this and you don’t have ceiling fans. 
Maintenance is now handled via an app.. That app is terrible. When they are complete you don’t get a notification nor do the leave a work order. It might be me but I like to know if a stranger I requested to come into my home tells me he was there so I don’t leave a million VMs waiting for service. 
The front office, It would be nice on weekends maybe a 9-12 or something once a month. When I do go into the office the office is aesthetically pleasing but the people that work there service is not. The people that worked here before felt like a mom and pop almost. Current management is a corporation and they treat it as such.
