Alot of people in and out your home isnt safe to me. The kids have a curfew but never go by it.

This place is really nice! All the appliances, tile wood floors, and granite counter tops are super nice. Everything is in great working condition. Been here for about 4 months now and have had no issues. Also if you’re a pilot and want to live close to the airport I’d choose this place. Really cheap and no more than a 15 minute drive to the airport.

I have currently been a resident here at Suncrest for three years I hate to move but unfortunately the rent is going up and the good news is I have found a home was actually to rent a home there is an apartment but I would recommend Suncrest to anyone looking for a good place to live with your family it was just me and my son and it was great for the three years that was here but it’s time to move on to bigger and better things Stacey and the Suncrest team is great!!!!!!??Kim Jones

Moved in several months ago and several things that I listed as not working on my move in list have still not been fixed. For instance, there is a random cable that is cut in several places runs across the whole apartment and the doors(finally just removed this one myself), the washer and dryer are broken, and the closet doesn't have anything to hang clothes on. You can hear EVERYTHING in the main hallway but can't hear much in the actual room. The staff changes frequently and has difficulty keeping anyone other then one person. The street lights are usually not working, only a few work that I've notice and they are mostly by the main office. The fence that is between this complex and another is broken and there renters walk through this complex all the time. The complex next to this one is very disruptive and police and ambulances are called often. You can not get pizza delivered due to the complex next to suncrest. If your unit does come with a washer and dryer it is ridiculously small, as in 3 pairs of pants if your lucky. The shower was dirty when I moved in.  there is an ORANGE wall in the dinning room.  Thought that was accident but nope, it's on purpose. I don't necisarily regret living here but I wouldn't do it again.

Our cars have been broken into 2 times in the last 3 months - this place has grounds light everywhere but that has not stopped anything. Clover Leaf people are super low class housing with matched people. We have lived here less than year and can't wait to get out! People are always leaving, never see anyone move in. Gun shots 2-3 times a week and crime in area is super high (check IMPD crime map.) The area has gone downhill. The USPS REFUSES to leave anything at the door - b/c we had items stolen and so did 2 of my neighbors (asking if we got their package by chance - that is how we found out.) We can't get a pizza delivered any longer. Papa John's guy was beat up and robbed - by the club house (in the spring.) There was no Trick or Treating this year, in the complex, due to the crime rate in the area. I would not recommend this place based on reasons above and many others.

Renting at Suncrest Apartments has been one of my best rental experiences yet. It is one of the most affordable Indianapolis communities that provides a washer and dryer in the unit. The walls are thick enough to keep the neighbors' noise to a minimum. The maintenance team responded very quickly to all of the items we noted on our move-in checklist. 

The property itself was purchased by a leasing company earlier this year, and they put millions of dollars worth of renovations into the community. This is obvious when you tour, as all of the kitchen appliances are new and the carpet and laminate flooring are very clean.

Most importantly, the front office staff is incredibly friendly. In the past, I experienced leasing agents that were friendly up until the moment the lease was signed. Suncrest's front office staff has continued to greet us kindly and be helpful long after lease-signing. They are invested in their community and are excellent representatives of the company.

There are only a few reasons I did not rate this community a full five stars. The first is that it is close to the airport, and the thin windows do not keep airplane noise out very well. Also, since this is a converted retirement community, there are not very many parking spaces. The leasing agent told us that there is only one parking spot for each unit (and you can imagine that several units have multiple people with multiple cars). Additionally, there are breaks in the fence that surrounds the property so that people can walk in; I personally do not feel unsafe because of this, but I can definitely understand why some people would be concerned about this.

The cons that I listed are only minor issues. Overall, I would rate this as a very good rental choice, especially if you work in Plainfield or Avon, but want to be close to the city.

Wow I can't believe how much this place has changed. This one of the most  unfriendly environments I have ever lived in. We moved here from another city. And the reason why I returned to this location is at one time this was a very beautiful location and affordable housing. This community is run down and the staff handles daily maintenance and support concerns as if you are asking them to go out of their way to provide what their own advertisement claims. The security is horrid because maintenance comes in your apartment when you're not home anytime they desire. The neighbors are juvenile delinquents that live like hoarders leaving trash all over the property. All of this filth attracts pest. My apartment building has an infestation of crickets , spiders and water bugs. I have been experiencing extremely incompetent and rude staff who have been harassing me with letters of nothing but false allegations from racist neighbors. I will give you a full warning of buyer beware. Do your homework please before coming here. You must view ever inch of this place before coming. Do not I repeat do not waste your valuable time speaking with management over the telephone. This is a must see with your own eyes experience. The online version of the property is how it used to look. You will have to visit and see for yourself. My building , I wish I could upload photos.

ROACHES!!! Absolutely nasty. For 6 months out of the year, they swarm the entrance after dark and the stairwell is littered with them, dead and alive. It's impossible to keep them out. The apartments won't do anything about it nor do they care. Not to mention the construction of the apartment building next door, homeless people sleeping in the stairwell, thin walls,no parking on Friday and Saturday nights and attitude from the office manager. This is a horrible place to live. You'd be better off burning your money for warmth next to a dumpster. There would definitely be less roaches!

I have been living in Temple Lofts for going on two years now and love it. Staff is very nice and helpful with service requests. The location is great, rather not right in the heart of downtown but only a five minute drive to the heart of downtown with ease. Neighborhood is pretty quiet outside of sirens. I would recommend anyone to live here.

The apartment itself is very nice. Granite counters, hard woods floors, etc. 
However, the management is awful. They do not respond to e-mails, they post important notices outside on the doors, they charge unexpected fees. They will be kind until you sign the lease, then you’re on your own. 
Our callbox has been broken since December. Despite (6 complaints, from different people), it still remains unfixed. This is just one example of the poor management. 
I would not recommend. The apartment may be nice but you will spend thousands in extra fees for it, not to mention the extra stress. In the end, it just is not worth it.

Moved in last May, everything has been great! Maintenance guys are always throwing salt down and taking care of the place. Everyone is very friendly. The managing team is on top of everything and easy to contact! It's very close to the canal and IUPUI. It's relatively easy for guests to find parking, too. Definitely would recommend.

I read a few reviews before moving here, I saw a couple of them stating that there’s random gunshots. I’ve been here for almost 3 weeks & so far I’ve heard random gunshots twice, I have one on audio recording from my camera. I asked the front office about the gunshots before I moved in but they said it wasn’t an issue. Lots of kids running around but they don’t usually cause trouble, landscape is maintained well, very loud vehicles and loud stereo’s blaring, you can hear people’s conversations in the hallways of the complexes, & the trash gets filled up extremely quickly. Office staff is never there but they are pretty helpful when they are there. I don’t see too much of an issue with living here but I think it’s a personal preference, I’ve seen lots of things. I’d give it an average rating, it’s not too terrible.

I lived here since 2016 and i can say it’s gotten relatively worse. Constant gunshot sounds, people have been shot/murdered and the police are always here. Office staff never mentions anything.

On top of crime, Exterior is not kept up well, can hear raccoons walking in the roof in the hallways. I recently seen one crawling in an opening on the roof in the daytime. Geese are everywhere and so is their poop. 

It has potential to be a good place because of the proximity to downtown/broad ripple.

I lived here for 2 years. My 1st year here was very pleasant. My second year here not so much, random gun shots happen pretty often. I no longer feel safe. If you move here ask about that. Ask your leasing office about gun fire before signing a lease.

I moved to the area and had to rent sight unseen; they worked with me pretty well in my whirlwind move. You have to pay everything with money order before you move in, then you can pay with personal check. Kind've a hassle, but not a huge deal. I moved in, then things started to go downhill.
Pros: 
-Affordable
-Water/trash included in rent
-Huge bedrooms and closets
-Walls are painted with color (not white!)
-The front office will sign for packages (there's a lot of package stealing here)
-Lots of trees on the property
Cons:
-Kitchen and bathrooms are very small
-Very old fixtures and appliances, some of which aren't kept up well
-Had a problem with my water heater (hot would turn cold every so often; maintenance just turned up the heat which didn't work)
-Walls/ceiling are super thin--I had to wear earplugs because of people walking and laughing upstairs. I could hear someone talking in the apartment across the hallway--two doors away!
-Not the greatest location. Gunshots, drugs.
-No sidewalks to the complex, so you have to drive everywhere
-Can't get food delivery here (poor location!)
-THIS PROPERTY IS NOT SMOKE FREE. This site says it is, it is not. Plus, the air vents are connected throughout the building, so if one person smokes, it gets pumped throughout the building. Plus, the entry ways are indoor, and people smoke in the hallways. I had a poor closing door and smoke, cigarette and pot, just flowed into my living room. I ended up using my patio door as my main entrance and taped off the front door to limit the smoke filtering into the apartment.
-Leasing office staff are kind, but they are hardly ever there. I estimate that 75% of the times I went to the office I had to return because they weren't in the office, and 1) didn't come back at the time stated on the door and 2) many times for several hours. There are three people in the office M-F; one person should be in the office at all times. I talked with several residents who also complained about this.

Ended up breaking my lease because I didn't feel safe and my upstairs neighbor wasn't courteous. They left trash on their patio that leaked onto mine and dumped a pot of water/kitchen grease on their patio (super smelly). They weren't responding to calls from the front office and the front office didn't do much more. The grease spot was still on the porch (even though I requested it be cleaned) when I moved out, 2 1/2 months after it appeared.

Summary: if you can afford it, look elsewhere.
Mold, Poor Maintenance, Disrespectful Staff And Getting Your Deposit Back Is Nearly Impossible!

The apartments are poorly maintained. They paint over mold and have no integrity with their maintenance. When I moved out I could barely breath because of the mold and saw spots coming through all over the unit. They moved someone in the unit less than a month after me. 

Staff is also very rude and unprofessional

I currently live here and love it! Its quiet and close to everything I need and close to highway access!!
I love how all the apartments are single story and it's not a huge community so it's quiet all the time!
Exterior has chipping paint & rotting wood. Wind blows thru windows. Maintenance theory is fix after broken with no routine upkeep.
my husband and i have been here a year and we love the management and maintenance they're very nice place to live for what all you get and the people are nice great Neighbors

I lived in a one bedroom apartment at Jade North in Broad Ripple for a year before relocating out of state. If I hadn’t needed to relocate, I would have lived in that apartment for years. It’s a wonderful location at a very reasonable price for that location. 
The entire year I lived there I had someone above me and someone next to me and I never heard any sound through the walls at all. Which is almost unheard of in newly built and over priced apartments nearby.
Other people that live here are very friendly, and the staff is very kind and genuinely cares about your experience living there. It was always easy to reach someone when I had questions or issues. I think what I valued most about this place was their refusal to price gouge their tenants. Which is the opposite of what most apartment buildings are doing right now. You never had to pay any nonsense trash fees, you could just go take your trash out yourself to the easily accessible cans. You do not have to pay to park outside your own apartment and pet fees are very reasonable.
All in all, it is a great place to live if you’re on your own or with a small family. It’s an apartment feels like a community and other apartment buildings surrounding it should take notes. Because the people at Jade North are actually doing it right.

There's a few quirks to the place but for the price I have been very pleased.  The location is fantastic.  While a little older, the kitchen/bathrooms have worked well.  Before moving in there was new carpet and blinds installed, as well as some bathroom touch-ups.  There's a great community around the courtyard and pool which means some music playing and people having fun during summer, but no noise problems in my opinion per se.  Would recommend.

I was nervous about moving to Jade North.  I lived in a secure locked lobby apartment for 16 years & was concerned about my feeling of security.  I've lived here six months & I feel very safe.  The apartment is spacious and the appliances are nearly new.  The courtyard view from my balcony is lovely, especially on summer nights when the lanterns line the balconies.  The courtyard is beautifully landscaped, as is the rest of the property  with mature pine trees.  The property managers are friendly and very responsive to requests.  Sarah & Jeff, in the office, are great and Terri showed great kindness & consideration when I moved in.  I've lived in apts 40 years, and Lance & Mike are the best maintenance team I've known.  Mike lives on-site and he's there anytime you call. They are all wonderful.  I encourage everyone to check out Jade North. It is really a well kept Broad Ripple secret worthy of your attention.
This property is run-down, poorly maintained and has significant water damage that has not been properly remediated. Be aware of what living in a water-damaged building can do to your health.

I have lived at Jade North for over a year now and I can say it is probably the best value this close to Broad Ripple. The best feature of the complex is the maintenance - so prompt. If it’s a small request it will usually be taken care of within a few business hours. 

Jade North also offers a lot of amenities for the price. Covered parking is a great deal. 

Drawbacks are: 1. The washing machines are down pretty frequently; 2. Dishwasher is so old it really doesn’t do anything - dishes must be clean going in; 3. My apartment had a bug problem when I moved in, was able to resolve it within 3-4 month. 4. Gas heat - extremely expensive in the winter. 

Office staff has always been helpful and friendly enough. Overall the drawbacks are pretty minor when compared with the price and location. Great community.

I moved here from Texas hesitant cause of the previous reviews. Don’t let those review fool you they are old reviews nothing current. This place is quiet and the price is right for the space . I am glad I took the leap and choose this apartment complex.

Me encanta el lugar es muy tranquilo muy comodo ,la escuela y gasolinera muy cerca me gusto mucho

My husband and I have lived a lot of places and left a lot of places due to noise levels, animals, unsafe, dirty etc. we have lived here since Feb and we LOVE it here. Eric is wonderful and so easy to work with and our place is beautiful and quiet. We are in NO hurry to leave! We love our home. ??

These apartments are nicely built not too old, and up to date on appliances etc. Amenities are nice, valet trash services, open gym and secure mail room for packages however, the leasing office is never open, leasing agent does not know a thing about professionalism. If you want maintenance to walk into your apartment without any notice or by “mistake” like they help you pay rent then this is the place for you. It’s no way these nice apartments should be having a poor unprofessional team behind it. Ring cameras on your door is highly suggested before leasing.

I absolutely love living here. This property is a true gem here in Indianapolis. Thank you to the staff for working so hard to making sure the residents are comfortable and well taken care of. The safety, location, amenities, and quality of the apartments are unbeatable! I am truly cherishing my time here! Thank you team!

This spot is brand new and I'm glad I discovered it. I'm the first tenant in my particular unit and have only been an Alpine Studios resident since June 2021. When the first year of my lease ended, I had zero hesitation in signing another agreement because I love the place. The location is literally right outside of the 465 loop with downtown nearby, offering modern, stylish living spaces and operated by genuinely friendly, thoughtful people. Contemporary but nothing too flashy — every guest that's visited has had nothing but compliments. As of this review, looking up the location on Google Maps produces an image of an empty lot, just to speak to how new these apartments are to the area.

I just moved into Alpine Studios about a week ago and since applying, I can't say enough good things about the staff and maintenance! Through my endless calls and questions, the staff is always more than happy and able to help. Since I've moved in, maintenance has addressed any/all concerns with shocking speed. I really look forward to the rest of my experience living here!

Currently have lived here since they opened. The apartments are beautiful and the area is quiet. The leasing office and maintenance is amazing! I love living at Alpine Studios in my beautiful apartment!

Beautiful, new, clean apartments. Super friendly staff. Maintenance is quick and efficient. I had a late night emergency, and he came right away. Great area with many stores and restaurants around as well as downtown being very close by.  No complaints

I’ve lived in St. Agnes Apartments for a little over a year now and I really love it. It's in a great location, 20-30 minute walk to most things downtown (5 minutes drive).The area feels safe, and is located across the street from a beautiful Cathedral. No package concierge system, so you'll just wanted to be careful with deliveries (p.o is nearby though).  Megan is very responsive and pleasant to deal with. The building has a lot of history (it used to be a girl's catholic schoolhouse) and I adore the charm of the building and my floor plan. Inexpensive and safe off street parking is always a big plus downtown as well!  I viewed quite a few places before falling in love with this one, definitely worth checking out!

List of issues I've had in 1.5 years here:
-No idea who the property manger is, never met or spoken to them
-I had mice
-Power randomly going out in the building, multiple times
-hot water going out in the building, multiple times
-paper thin walls
-anything maintenance fixes is barley rigged together
-entire building smells of cigs
-packages get stolen from inside the building
-people write on the walls and in the elevators
-never know when the elevators are working or not
-4 washers and dryers for the entire building....half of which never work
-2/3 windows did not latch...didnt even come close
-their online portal and your lease do no have the same information & will end up costing you money. And management is 100% aware. They do not care, they just want their payment. 

Even for the location and the price, this DEFINITELY was not worth it. Living in a run down building is no fun, trust me. This place is in the same shape as a halfway house & no one seemed to care.

I'm a current resident of St Agnes. Overall my experience has been good. Not great. But good. 
PROS- No bugs, no rodents. The parking is gated off and so far been very secure. Maintenance is above average and is usually pretty fast to fix whatever problem you are having. Big tall ceilings, and massive windows makes for great natural light. I feel pretty safe in the area too (knock on wood). No gunshots. The occasional crackhead walking down the alley yelling but you'll get that anywhere downtown. Walls are pretty thick unless my neighbors just don't make noise. Very nice front lawn. WIFI is super speedy. 
CONS- don't leave your packages out in the front lobby. Left mine for one day too long and it was stolen just like that. In the winter expect a VERY pricey eclectic bill. For one person living here in a small apartment who is not home half the time the bill was HUGE. More than 200 a month for 400 sq. feet. thermostat set at no more than 68 degrees. I talked to other rooms who were also having the same problem. Management had nothing to say about the manner. Absolutely ridiculous. 
If you don't order online and don't mind massive bills in the colder months, this is good place to live, for the price and location.

I’m a current resident at St. Agnes, and, although it seems some of the management kinks have been worked out, there are cockroaches that crawl from the hallway into my apartment, it seems maintenance is quite literally power washing my wall/window every day. The paper-thin walls make every conversation maintenance (loudly) has outside of my window wake me up. The paper-thin walls of the apartments make every noise my neighbors make wake me up. The neighborhood is decent as far as how close it is to everything but it is also pretty sketchy. Cars still get broken into, people still approach me for random sketchy things, etc. I tried to contact management about how consistent (for approximately 4 months - who power washes a building for 4 months?!) and loud the maintenance work was outside of my apartment but they promptly ignored my email. I don’t know, I was excited to live here given how close it was to things downtown for the price, but I see why the price is the way it is. There are still many kinks to work out before this is a decent place to live.

Always there for me if I ever had an issue. Rick even gave me a lift back to my car once! Responsive, courteous, and always available. Rick is a very direct guy, which might rub some the wrong way, but I loved his style. Got to appreciate a straight shooter. Affordable rent and well maintained property!

I and my wife have lived in this apartment for 5 years now. We love everything about this place. There's a safe, reserved parking spot in a gated compound. The building itself has a beautiful architecture. Rooms have higher ceiling making them comfortable during the hot season. Downtown indy is a bare 1.4 mile drive. Ramps to  I-65 and I-70 are two blocks away from home on Meridian Street. Maintenance needs can be reported through online portal and the team takes care of issues the same day almost always. The property manager (Rick) is such a great person. In the 5 years we spent at St.Agnes, he has gone above and beyond to help us pretty much with everything we asked for and always made us feel at home. The ability to pay rent online is another great feature. I believe this is the ideal place for a much reasonably priced apartment close to downtown indy.

I have been here for a few years now. I love my studio apartment with high ceilings and windows. It's close enough to the canal and monument circle yet in a quieter space. The residents are friendly as is the management.

I work at the medical school and don't own a car. From St. Agnes, it's a 15 minute walk to the People Mover station at Methodist Hospital, which goes to Fairbanks Hall and Riley Hospital. It's also about a 20-25 minute walk to the downtown/Mass Ave area, which is convenient. As a walker, I do try not to get caught outside after dark for safety reasons, but that's an Indianapolis problem and not a St. Agnes problem; the immediate area around the building is decent. I did a lot of searching, and St. Agnes is the best value I've found. It is not the newest property, but it is maintained well and maintenance requests (which are not often required) are promptly attended to. For anything newer or closer to campus or downtown, the rent skyrockets. Some other properties in the area that I looked at, which were comparable in terms of rent, were totally sketchy or downright slummy. St. Agnes is a clean, well-maintained, and secure building.
Lived at the Devonshire property and loved it. Great location next to Mass Ave and my room had just been furnished with new carpets, stove, cabinets and refrigerator. 0 complaints in 2 years.

I first moved to St Agnes in 2011 when I was working downtown and wanted to live in downtown Indy. Though I have been working in Carmel for some time I continue to live at St Agnes due to my satisfaction with the facility. For the location the price is unbeatable. You're six blocks from the canal and ten blocks from Mass Ave. There is secured parking for the very reasonable cost of $20 a month. The apartments are always in great condition, fresh paint and carpet. Routine maintenance is done and there is a rapid turnaround time for requests.   The landlord is on site, very friendly and accomadating to your individual situations. I would recommend this place for anyone looking for downtown living.

Long time resident of St Agnes ('06). Super convenient to everything downtown- events, shopping, bicycling routes, walking convenience. The building is secure and the gated parking is a big plus. The property manager, Rick, is extremely responsive to the residents. Any maintenance concerns (very few over the years) are addressed very quickly and followed up on by a very competent staff (Scott). Stallard and Associates office staff are courteous and helpful. Compared to other downtown offerings you can't beat being here.
Kevin D

I've lived in my one bedroom apartment in St. Agnes for a little over a year now and have decided to renew my lease. Rick, the apartment manager, has handled all my issues/concerns/questions promptly and is great at communicating any maintenance or repairs ahead of time via email. I also think the price is incredible for what you get - a spacious one bedroom apartment with high ceilings in a location that is approximately a 5 min. drive to anywhere worth going downtown. I recommend to anyone looking for a great deal in downtown Indy.

I am an international graduate student working at IUPUI.
I and my wife have been living in St. Agnes apartment, one of Stallard and Associates’ properties for more than 2 years. 
Reasons we chose this place were the distance from the school, secured entrance doors, and a fair rent.
Most of all, this room has a high ceiling which makes us feel unstuffy, and comfortable. 
We, honestly, tried to find other rooms cheaper than here one year ago, but those were less safe, and shabby we felt although $ 100 cheaper, so we were able to be pleased with this apartment more than before.  
The only problem we went through was a water leak from the ceiling this month, and the apartment manager immediately respond to my maintenance request next day.  
I would like to recommend this St. Agnes apartment to anyone looking for a place to move.

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review: Front office does their jobs well. If the community abides by the standards set forth in the lease it would be even better. Maintenance is always fast and efficient and we have never had any bugs other than the occasional spider. The location is very convenient and our church is in walking distance from our apartment. We feel safe at Dawson village and will continue to rent here.

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review:
Pests: The first day I moved into my unit there were roaches in my kitchen. They have pest control every month but that does not help. There are large holes under the sinks which allow mice and much more into the unit. When I left I had to throw away multiple pairs of shoes that mice had pooped in without my knowledge. 
Inconvenience: They schedule the lawn care company for 9 am on Saturday mornings so if you plan on sleeping past 9 on a Saturday you won't be able to. The laundry room is gross. All of the laundry and dryers have a dirty smell to them and the laundry room itself is dirty.
Office Staff: The two women in the office are rude. They will yell at you on the phone and they also threatened me with charges to my account upon leaving.
Charges: They charge $60 an hour for PATCHED holes. They charge $50 for blinds that they need to replace anyways because they are now considered a safety hazard and are not sold in stores. They charge $20 per item in the unit that is not cleaned to their standard once you move out. I had my mom come help me clean the unit and they said the sink and toilet were dirty and I was charged $20 a pop for items I had cleaned.

The only good thing I would say is that the maintenance will do their job. Other than that the units are poorly maintained, the office staff is mean, and there are PESTS!

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review: The office staff and maintenance are super easy to work with. Nice comfy home!!

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review: My apartment at Dawson was one of my favorites!! Yes it's an older community but it's got so much charm. You can't beat the price for what you get. Living in a flat I never had to deal with anyone over or under me. The maintenance staff are responsive and knowledgeable and the office staff take good care of the tenants!!!

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review: This apartment has a great deal on a 2 bedroom! Maintenance is quick, front office people are nice, and this is a good neighborhood. 10/10 recommend

apartmentName: Welcome to Dawson Village – Welcome Home!
review: I have lived at dawson village for 7 years and i love it here the maintenance guys r awesome and the leasing office employees are so amazing and amber is just so amazing at what she does and does her job very very well amazing lady
I chose an apartment without looking at the apartment first & I can say I am pleased ! New carpet fresh paint very clean & any issues you may have they will definitely take care of them !
This community has really cool lakes and pool!  Also, the staff is so nice and friendly!
I absolutely loved my stay here!! Recommend strongly

I had file my application I got approved that was on Monday and my moving date was supposed to be on Friday. They really have no type of communication I’m the one that have to keep calling to ask if I’m really qualified to move in mind you today is Wednesday . She gunna tell me that the manager still reviewing my case . Not to be selfish but It don’t take 2 day to reviewing something.

AT&T U-verse internet and Dish is provided through a third party and is very slow to help if there are any issues. There are no other options even if you wanted to switch. I've just been told there is an outage and technicians are "working on it."

I've been living at Scarborough Lakes for almost a year now.  Let's start with the big things I wish I knew:  There ARE cockroaches, packages delivered to my door get stolen (delivered to leasing office is OK), and neighbors are loud. 

I initially was really excited with my 1 bedroom apartment -- it really is a great price for the amount of space you get.  The kitchen is outdated, but everything works perfectly.  I have had multiple problems with cockroaches in the apartment.  I call to report this to the office.  Except, you have to call in every single week to let them know you want your apartment treated on Thursdays.  I've had multiple treatments, and not seen any improvement. I'm not even notified with a confirmation that someone indeed came to spray/ treat my apartment, or that anyone entered at all. I'm on the 2nd floor, so it's not a "ground floor" issue.  I've also had problems with very noisy neighbors (playing music so loud I can hear every word clearly, anywhere from 12 midnight to 4am).  I let the office know, and multiple "notices" were sent to the neighbors... but it was a very long time (2 months) before they were not playing loud music anymore.  Walls seem generally thin -- especially the ceiling where you can hear your upstairs neighbors.  I've lived in other apartments and never had as bad of an issue with upstairs neighbor noise as in this apartment. The laundry unit in my apartment has not worked completely since I've been here, either washer or dryer is broken.  There is one washer/dryer for 10-12 apartment residences.  I just pay for a laundromat.  Neighbors in my unit dump junkmail from mailboxes right on the sidewalk/ stairwell at the entrance of the apartment, instead of throwing it out in the dumpster or their own garbage.  People throw garbage into the bushes and strip of grass in the front of the apartments. 

Aside from that, the office staff are very nice, especially answering all of my questions as a new resident.  The fitness center is very small, but does have a treadmill and some weights.  I like the balcony designs, which seem to give you a bit of privacy while sitting out on a summer evening.  I only have to drive a mile down the road for any groceries or other shopping to do, and only minutes away to I-65 or 465 for easy commute anywhere.  Overall, could be worse, but also could be better.  If there were no cockroaches or neighbor problems, I'd say this place is great.

I’ve been a resident of Rosewood Commons for a year. We’ve had 2 leasing agents and 2  maintenance crews .
But the problem is still here! The property Manager!
She is rude and very negative. Is is the reason that the maintenance quit and I wouldn’t be surprised if the leasing agent doesn’t leave. When things don’t get done, the manager will throw the staff under the bus.
I’ve had issues with my ledger and she informed me it was my fault and I owe it and better pay or they will take action against me. I had to go over her head and get it corrected. Which was done with no problem.
I hope that Elon and Rachelle figure out that she’s the problem before it’s too late and more people leave along with the office staff.
It’s a bad place to live, just move here and my freezer stop working it’s been 3 day and I still have not gotten it fix or a response from management. Can’t wait to move already.
i live here now great!! place to live you should come join the family lol seriously!!
I have lived at Rosewood now for 4 years! I love the office staff, they are so sweet and kind. The maintenance staff is GREAT AND FAST!!!
This is a small complex with awesome staff! Maintenance very fast in responding, well maintained property! Best apartments in area for price and location!

Moved here in September 2019. Staff is friendly. Maintenance is fast to respond. Seems to be a lot of retired persons and those on disability live. With a mix of working people. So, it quite and everyone knows everyone. Not crazy about the water/misc fees, but it clean and quite.

Had family move in recently.  Everything has been fine until Mgmt tries to find ways to nickel and dime you to death.  Especially, hurtful to folks who are barely making ends meet and the extra fees have actually nothing to do with the any damage or issue with the apartment itself.  It was something outside of that that was no big deal and was an inadvertent error.  Mgmt really needs to chill on ridiculous fees and stop hurting people.  Understand if it was damage or something related to that but it wasn't.  Very unfair and hurtful financially to those that as I mentioned are barely making it and also, having health issues.   Very hurtful and causes emotional distress.
We've only been here a couple of weeks but it's clean, quiet and very friendly.

Drive this property from entry to the end, you will see overgrown bushes, paint chipping from patio fences,
building lights outs, water drainage issues, large bare grass spots and more. No Curb Appeal. Talk with some of the residents- maintenance issues- repairs not performed correctly. Old carpeting and old appliances. However,
the building structures are in good standing.
I've been here for a few years now and the manager Aisha has been exceeded my expectations. She's been very helpful. I would recommend her service and this community to anyone.
Aisha is great! Love the location and single story units! awesome place to call “home”

The office staff makes this place the place to live. Aisha wow what a great down to earth manager. She always goes over and beyond her job title. If you aren’t qualified for her community she always has suggestions of what may work for you. Now that’s over and beyond l. She’s so sweet. Thanks for all you and going out of your way to provide hosing for so many!

This community is awesome I'm glad to be apart of it. What I love about this community is that its quiet, you dont hear people kids, people mind their own business, if you have anything that need to be done in your apartment trust me they go to extreme measures. They also make sure your happy and satisfied with your repairs.The women in the office are nice and kind but my favorite is Aisha, she is amazing, professional, kind, and she make sure all issues are addressed that anyone could possibly have. Another thing you can live comfortably out here meaning the rent not super high, you dont have to rob Peter to pay paul. I highly recommend this place, trust me you will love it here.
Aisha is a great manager, that has all the patients in the world. I definitely live here because of the staff.
The apartment is infested with roaches and bed bugs and too expensive for a building like this I would not recommend nobody to move here

The building is infested with bed bugs, roaches and mice. if you are sensitive to smoking so don't rent from here. I had neighbors that smoked in their apartments on both sides so I always smelled it. Im a very clean person and my cabinets were crawling with roaches. My cat caught 2 mice while i lived there. the bed bug problem is horrible!!! They are in the laundry room. Management refused to do anything about it. DO NOT RENT FROM HERE!

I only lived in this aren’t for a few months. At first it was fine, as a student trying to get in as little more debt as possible, the cheap price and close distance to campus was great. 
There were always homeless people on the corner. I would get cat called by them and the employees of the shops behind the building. I didn’t leave after dusk because I was too scared. 
The apartment building is old and kinda grimy, but for that price a little grime is expected. But I hit my breaking point. 
I woke up one morning COVERED IN BITES. I didn’t know what they were but after it happened again I washed my sheets (in their gross washer dryers) and sprayed some stuff. 
The next morning I had more bites but I different type. Instead of being small and itchy these bites swelled up into giant red splotches. That night I found a cockroach. I immediately let management know about this and they said they would send someone. I waited all day so I would know that they came through and no one did. Then it was the weekend so I got absolutely no response. This getting bit every night went on for like 2 weeks until I emailed the guy and said I’m moving out. I will say they didn’t charge me anything to break the lease but that was literally the least they could do. I washed literally everything I owned before I took it out of there and my new mattress ended up by the dumpster WITH LIKE 3 OTHERS. 
PLEASE DO NOT MOVE HERE you’re much better off either increasing your budget or looking further from the city. 
(Also it’s non smoking but my apartment smelt like Cigarettes every night)
I lived here and found the management to be slow to non existent, bugs found in the apartment in the summer. Also, get responses from the sales guy in writing and check up.

I waited for several months to get some maintenance issues addressed. After writing the "Thin Walls" review, suddenly they contact me the next day and want to schedule a time for maintenance to come out.. Go figure. So we eventually schedule it for a Monday. Monday came and went. No one showed up or called to reschedule. Same thing Tuesday. Wednesday I happened to see the maintenance supervisor outside, I explained my frustrations and showed him inside my apt what needed done. He said he would be out the next day after lunch. No one showed up or called! Great service and communication guys!-sarcastically.. I called Friday and they finally sent someone at the end of the day... Not enough time to address all the issues in this shotty apt. Said guy was quite nice and stated he would be back next week to finish the other issues. Well, it's Friday again and no one came or called... I don't doubt he was pulled aside to do other projects. There are soooo many things wrong at this place, it never ends!! People have overflowing toilets and it's NOT considered a priority. DO NOT LIVE HERE OR MOVE HERE! Let's see how long it takes them to call me now. ????

I've lived at Cambridge Commons for over a year and can't wait to move. You can hear your neighbors on every side of you, especially behind you. I smell marijuana often, have dealt with roaches, ants, and stink bugs. Maintenance doesn't want to fix anything. The office staff will act concerned but then never do anything about it. I literally have ants coming out of my wall and they won't come and try to find where they're getting in. They just keep sending Gold Seal to spray... The neighbors enjoy playing their music loud, and every few minutes a car with loud bass drives by.. Hate it here!!
Very nice and quite the reason my visit i am looking for a apartment. Staff were very courteous, how i learn of your property online
Its a decent price for a decent apartment but terrible management
Property is well lit and secure with gated parking lot.  Lots of surrounding schools with easy access to both work and bars downtown. Love the wooden floors as well. Can't beat it for the price!
Great place to live! Quite, nice neighbors, with friendly staff that always response within a short time frame. I definitely recommend living here.

Our apartment is about what you'd expect in its price range; $600/mo for a 2-bedroom, 1 bath 2nd floor apartment. The staff keeps the place clean and reasonably well-maintained, though the repairs done to the floor a few months ago weren't done properly and the tile will have to be replaced again. Who ignores a leaky toilet? These guys, that's who.

Maple Court Apartments, a gated community in the Mapleton-Fall Creek neighborhood of Indianapolis, looks like a nice enough place. Stallard and Associates' maintenance staff keep up with the lawn, though the rose bushes are pretty sad. They keep up with the gates, except for the missing knobs on 2 out of 3 pedestrian entryways. They're "family friendly," though there's no playground. They keep up with pest control, except for occasional plagues of bed bugs and roaches. Their response time is good, except when it's not. The ad we answered said, "Utilities included in rent," but "included" means "tacked onto," so you pay a different amount each month. In short, it's not a *terrible* place to live (hey, we've never been carjacked or burgled.) There are much nicer places for rent, but Stallard and Associates keep prices down with their zero-tolerance corporate policies. Whether it's worth it depends on your specific needs.

I moved into this place a little over a year ago. They have just approved me to move into a larger unit... it is not because it is my desire, but because an illness will require 24/7 health care. They could not have been more accommodating. My current apartment is in great shape. Clearly the new management has cleaned things up.  I love my neighbors...I even refer to them as my community. And that is just exactly how it feels. A community. It is clean, well kept, and very spacious with well kept apartments. My studio has served me very well. Bella...the person on duty in the office, is just wonderful. I consider her a friend due to her kindness. And Luz, the district manager, has proven to be friendly and gracious and so helpful. The maintenance workers, James and James are incredible. The gym and theater room on the top floor are something out of a major city magazine.  Please consider this place. It is a diamond in a fast changing, progressive part of town.

I moved in here eleven months ago at the end of July 2017. I have had  a wonderful experience here from the very start. I am given a hundred dollar discount for being a student. That allows me to afford a one bedroom instead of the studio I originally had come to see the model of. The staff is very friendly and curtious. I enjoy the lounge access and always available laundry here on site. There is plenty of parking especially since the opening of the overflow lot. The place is kept very clean. It is also a very calm and quiet atmosphere  here in the hallways and lobby. The building is very secure and gives me a good sense of security. There is a grocery store, convienence store, gas station, church, and multiple restaurants within walking distance of a block. I decide to renew my lease and spend another year hear at the MTA. The place I love to call home.


Bryan

I have been living in the Shorelands since April of this year. the building have an  Bed Bug Infestation. the leasing team is unprofessional and non understanding. I have to now break my lease  because no one will take action and try to get there multiple issues under control. People stay loitering around the building and my guest feel uncomfortable visiting. There is always a strong stench in the air of the apartments hallway. I would not not recommend this apartment for no one.

I have lived here four months and I it is completely infested with baby and adult and cockroaches of every species and kind. I have never seen a live cockroach in my life but I have became very versed on them in my short time here. The ceiling in my bathroom leaks urine from the upstairs toilet on my toilet, floor and it has leaked on me so I am hoping no one upstairs has a communicable disease. I have called them, told them in person, called again and they really just don't care at all. My stove was on in my kitchen when I came home one day and would not shut off so I've had to unplug my stove. My refrigerator is not working properly so of course ice cream won't freeze. I guess in 110 degree weather on the fourth floor with no heat or ventilation I didn't need the ice cream or ice in my freezer! I have cellulitis on my ankle from bug bites and my ankle is swollen and I clean full-time for a living 50+ hours a week so that's awesome. I have an online store which I can't make anything now because I don't want to have to possibilty of giving cockroach infestations to my customers. I am totally exhausted from working, coming home and having to completely bleach and clean my belongings and just trying to protect my belongings and my health, forget about being comfortable at home. It's been the longest, exhausting fight of my life to live like this. I can't believe that people live this way. I get no response of course on the phone and when after working a 10 hour day, walking to the office which btw, they switch names from Indy flats, midtown flats and Northside flats to act as though they are different when they get so many complaints and to act like they lost money people gave them but luckily I keep all my receipts. I hope this helps anyone make an educated decision. It is really a struggle and exhausting and I feel really gross everytime Im in my apartment. Thank you and good luck on your apartment search!

Some leasing office staff are nice, some not so much, but overall they aren’t good about reporting issues to maintenance that need fixing.

Maintenance is a horror. Water emergencies causing damage are not a priority and expect to have giant hole in the drywall for over 2 months while they look for a contractor to fix it. There are a lot of unfinished projects like unpainted moldings, half way done light fixtures, mismatched paint in the hallways.

Cleanliness in the buildings doesn’t exist. Someone comes to sweep and vacuum the halls about once every 6 months. Cigarettes, trash, everywhere inside and out. Whatever ends up getting cleaned is by neighbors. Any maintenance done in public areas isn’t cleaned up, just chunks of plaster and wood everywhere.

There are definitely fire and safety violations like unlit EXIT signs, cracked off steps on the stairs that you can barely fit a foot on, unlit completely blacked out hallways and stairways...that won’t get fixed for at least a week if ever. 

I personally haven’t had issues with pests, but clearly it’s a problem in some units because they had people come treat every unit weekly and the hallways daily for a few months. 

Why do I put up with this nonsense? I really love the neighborhood, my utilities are bundled into my rent, I like my apartment (not the landlord lol), and I’ve taken to doing some repairs myself. I also have finally learned how much to nag the leasing office to get things fixed.

If I could give zero stars I would. I lived in the Rotherwood for over a year and it was disaster after disaster. 
They gave me the run around for 4 weeks about my move in date before finally telling me when I can move in. So I pack my things and load up the uhaul truck and head to the Indy Flats to pick up my keys and move in. They tell me, "oh I thought someone called you, the tenant decided not to move out after all so we don't have an apartment for you." This left me homeless, with all of my items in a UHaul truck. They tell me they can give me a studio instead of the one bedroom I was supposed to move in to, but it'll be dirty and won't be available for two days. At this point I'm just desperate to have some where to live so I take it and give them $600 upfront so that I can have the keys. So I move into a studio instead of the two bedroom that I was supposed to have. 
And then it goes downhill from there. I live on the first floor but my windows don't lock so it's easy for anyone to just climb into windows and this neighbourhood has a really bad junkie and homeless problem because of the methadone clinic that isn't even one block away. 
The lock to the front door is also terrible so the lobby was always filled with junkies and homeless people looking for a place to hang out. 
If you want to feel safe, this is not the place to live. 
Also everything is peeling and the bathrooms are molding and everything is dirty. If you can imagine something being badly maintained and disgusting then you can imagine one of their apartments.
But hey the rent is decent, until you have your car towed even when you have a parking sticker and have to pay $200 to get it back. Or having to kill roaches constantly. Or constantly being afraid of being mugged or having someone steel the rims off your car like one of my neighbours. 
The building is so bad that someone from the city housing unit came by and left their card at the door asking tenants to call them about what's going on in the building. 
Also, there was no outlet in the bedroom portion so imagine the heat of summer and not being able to have a window unit. 
And all of the maintenance requests I ever put in were marked complete but none of them were ever complete. Hmmm. 
But when the maintenance guys ever did come to my apartment they spent the whole time flirting with me and making me feel uncomfortable. Great.

Probably one of the worst living experiences I've ever had. I ignored all of the bad reviews online, don't be like me ! People rate this apartment complex horribly for a reason. I can deal with the building looking old and torn, I knew that going in. But the disturbing amount of roaches and bed bugs, it's been a nightmare. I never want to be home because I'm always killing roaches. I'm constantly afraid of being bitten when I'm asleep. I'm trying to move out as soon as I can. Unless they manage to seriously renovate these buildings, don't move in here.
That's the best I can say about my apartment. The office isn't always friendly or helpful.  The grounds are kept up that great.

Having lived here since the facility just opened, we have watched the growth and struggles.  With a total of five different managers, there have been issues.
Parking is one issue.  Trash pickup has been another issue.  Statistically Canyon Club at Metropolis is the only luxury apartment home option for Plainfield Indiana. Unfortunately, the ownership changed over the last few weeks, and so too did the allure of this once nice facility. One would assume that the new owners of the most costly facility in the city would have prepared to have the day-to-day operations of the complex managed appropriately. However, the idea of managing the complex appears to have been an afterthought. First, no website was, or is, in place for prospective or current tenants to have access to any information regarding the facility. Second, the clubhouse/office, pool area, and gym are looking as though no one is in charge of maintaining them, and the bathrooms are quite dirty including the floors, toilets, mirrors, and walls. Third, the office staff are not only lacking in personality, but they appear unprepared with regards to managing a pretty nice complex. In addition to the poor office management staff, a lone maintenance gentleman has been seen trying to do the job that three full-time maintenance workers used to do. This maintenance persons struggle is evident by the mounting maintenance complaints and the deterioration of the complex appearance. Fortunately, new options for nice apartment living have been built near Plainfield over the last few years, and the new apartment homes are ready to pick up where Canyon Club left their tenants who expect more. Sadly it seems as though Towne Properties (new managers) will hurt this once nice apartment complex. Cons: Leaks, mold, bugs, faulty appliances, lack of parking, dog poop everywhere, awful management/maintenance and questionable leasing practices.

When we moved in to a "new" unit, it was filthy and both bathroom ceilings had water leaking through from the toilets in the units upstairs. This (like anything else) took weeks to fix.

Next, there was water leaking through the wall into the master bedroom's walk-in closet. This was due to the tub being installed incorrectly. Multiple items we had in the closet were damaged. Not even an apology from management.

Had no water for days due to emergency maintenance (aka, more consequences of poor construction). After water was turned back on, our unit and 3 units above us flooded. Thousands of dollars in personal possessions damaged. Management refused to move us to another unit and forced us to spend weeks in an unlivable apartment with dozens of unannounced (illegal) maintenance visits, including instances of them entering while we were in the shower, etc. Unit still has mold from this incident, which was months ago.

Windows need re-caulking on a regular basis to prevent dust and cold air from blowing in.

You pay for pest control monthly, but bugs litter the halls and often make it into your apartment.

Appliances that broke or became loud/unusable within a year: Refrigerator, Heater, Microwave, Washer.

There is no guest parking and garage parking isn't enforced. This effectively makes Blackwelder a one-way street that is difficult to navigate.

Gates are usually propped open and/or can be opened without a fob. Random non-residents wander around at all hours.

Lazy dog owners leave dog poop everywhere, even in halls and in front of other residents' doors. Using the bags Argon provides isn't hard.

Management feels no need to apologize for issues and no urgency to fix them, and maintenance staff don't know how to schedule or keep appointments, let alone announce their visits/presence.

Despite expressing my intent to terminate the lease months in advance, they claimed I hadn't submitted whatever form they needed for me to move out on my lease end date. They threatened to send me to collections if I didn't stay for an additional 60 days at an inflated month-to-month rate.

They advertise being keyless-entry as if that's more convenient than having a key. The truth is, it's worse not better. You still have to hold your electronic key up to the door, exactly the same as a standard lock. However, if you step out of your apartment to check the mail, grab a package, or meet a delivery driver, you better have your electronic key. Otherwise, you are automatically locked out of your apartment and they will charge $50 to have someone drive from 20 minutes away to let you back in to your own home. It's ridiculous that forgetting to grab your key will cost you $50. I would rather have a standard lock. It's a rip-off for the apartment's convenience.

We have been in Downtown OKC for ten years: this has been our favorite. The staff have been awesome, they are there for you to make your experience great. The amenities are great and community events bring a nice touch of appreciation for tenants.  Back to the people: management, leasing agents, concierge service, and maintenance are all great. They have made this property easy to stay with for many years and many more to come.

Unlike most of the downtown OKC apartment complexes located in the Deep Deuce and Bricktown area, the Park Harvey Apartments offer a quieter, more secluded feel while offering a perfect location for those looking to walk to work, museums, gardens, Thunder games, and more.  Other nice amenities that the Park Harvey can boast over other OKC communities are a large and fully-capable 24 hour access gym, partnerships with 3 other local apartment complexes for joint fitness and social events, skyline views of the metro, key fob access to the front doors and elevators which are manned 24/7 by the nicest attendants in town.  Also, the PH is one of the only complexes in town that does not charge separately for utilities - so your housing expenses are stable each month.  Square footage also seems to be a little more generous at the PH and pets are welcome (although there is probably an up-charge).  All that being said, no apartment is perfect; drawbacks include communal laundry on the 2nd floor (although some are happy with not having personal units knowing that the communal laundry is free and multiple loads can be done simultaneously), challenging parking (no designated 24/7 parking for residents - during the week you have access to a nearby garage, but you have to be out by 7:30am and can't return until 5:00pm.  So residents who don't drive to work end up forking over an extra $100/month to rent a 24/7 spot at a garage 2 blocks away).  Overall, if you can find a way to get comfortable with the parking challenges, the PH is a great spot in downtown OKC.

I am a young professional.  These apartments have everything you need to live comfortably.  There is a 24-hour concierge staff. There is dry cleaning that will pick up your clothes and return them to your apartment.  The staff is very friendly and will help accommodate you in any way they can.
