Moral of the story don’t move here. The gate you also pay to park in is constantly broken
They will take your money and decline your application without any real reason I wouldn't apply here at all.

We have lived at Holden Heights for almost a year and plan on resigning. The property is very nice with high ceilings, updated appliances and decor, and quick maintenance. The location is walking distance to HEB while being nestled in a quaint heights neighborhood with plenty of street parking (a rare find). 
The only complaints I have about living here are the lack of security and enforcing community guidelines around trash. While there are badge only entries and a night security guard, there are absolutely no cameras throughout the property and the parking gate is constantly broken or left open. Earlier this year there was a break in to several units, but the lack of video equipment was definitely frustrating. Additionally, the valet trash is a nice perk, but the complex does not enforce the rules around trash pick up, making the hallways smell constantly.
I would definitely recommend this complex to a friend but encourage the management to fix some of the issues above.

Can hear everything from other residents around your unit, whether they are next to you, above you or next to your neighbors; there are inconsiderate rude residents walking, running around the house on these hardwood floors during middle of the night will cause you no proper sleep, yet the management is not solving these problems.

I first moved to Houston from San Antonio 2.5 years ago and my entire stay has been at the Holden apartments.  I love it here and I plan on renewing my lease for another year.  The pool is lovely, pets (including large dogs) are allowed, and there are plenty of free events for residents.  The area is safe, and I can walk to so many places nearby - the new HEB is literally right next door!   If I need help with anything, I always go to my favorite staff member, Armando.  He is always available to assist and answers all of my questions.  I would highly recommend living here, it has made living in Houston an amazing experience :).

I dont know where to begin... my last 2 years living at holden heights is exactly what I needed as a new houstonite! The staff is extremely freindly and they make a point to get to know every person. Armondo, specifically, made it a point to be friendly to me and remind me of resident events. Such a great place to meet people with the monthly events and great social area/busy pool in the summer. The only reason I'm leaving is because my roommate bought a house. If I ever need an apartment again, this will definitely be my first place to look! Thank you for all you and your staff have done! Keep it up:)

I have been a resident of Holden Heights for almost a year now and absolutely have enjoyed it! and so has my little Lola :)  The location is great!  We walk just about everywhere even for groceries at HEB now!  The complex is maintained very well and my work orders for filters/light bulbs changes are fulfilled within 24 hours.  Management also hosts fun events about once a month.  Armando in the front office is always so friendly and eager to assist residents.  This is definitely the best apartment living I've experienced.

I’ve lived at Holden for about 2 years now. The first year was fine really, management was good and dealt with issues, Rodrigo was very helpful. The second year has been a complete nightmare, new management hasn’t lived up to the same standards which is often the case when these properties change ownership. It doesn't feel like the same place anymore.

The good: The location is great, the maintenance crew is very good too, no issues there, and honestly the apartments are nice inside. Pool is nice, they are pretty strict with the number of guests which is fair enough.

The bad: The noise is unbearable. Constant barking from dogs left by inconsiderate owners on balconies. There’s a royal rumble dog barking match every day in my courtyard. Residents will have party’s outside in the courtyards until gone 2am on the weekends and you can hear everything even from the top floor and there’s nothing you can do about it. Other times people will sit and shout at each other on their balcony until the early hours. We ask them to keep it down after 11.00pm and they shout abuse back as they are almost always drunk. Then they leave trash all over the place, that's the kind of people who will be living next to you.
                
Management don't enforce the noise complaints, or people letting their dogs run freely through the grounds. From my balcony I saw one woman recently trying to leave for work one morning that had to turn back as there was a huge black poodle bounding towards her, the dog's owner nowhere to be seen.

The air conditioner will cut out at random so you return home to a 80  degree home, it's an easy reset on the system but shame it happens so much. Dog wash is really good, when it works. The car gate is almost always broken.

Recently my dog was bitten by another dog on the grounds since the owner couldn’t control her dog and it got off its leash. I like dogs, but this place is ridiculous. It's non-stop, so if you are in anyway sensitive to noise don't move here. If you enjoy sleeping in past 7am on a Sunday, don't move here. You will be woken by some clown letting their dog bark. Now the construction noise is a different level, but this isn't Holden's fault so I can't hold them accountable but it all adds to an uncomfortable please to live.

There are simply too many properties out there to take a risk on this place, do yourself a favor and look elsewhere.

Horrible and they don't care. Water is off every week, literally. They will leave you over the weekend without water. Maintenance is very very poor. you will be sorry and regret every day living here. My lease is up soon. I can't wait to move!! horrible

The crossing Sedona apartment were built in the 1980's. Despite the age of the apartment complex, the management is doing a good job at ensuring that the compound is clean and tidy and that the residents needs are met.

This is my first apartment. I moved here in June,2015. I have not had any problems and if I need something inside the apartment fixed, the maintainance personell are sent out to my apartment at a timely manner. 

I actually was able to find this apartment with the help of apartments.com. I'm very grateful for the good job that you are doing to help people around this country to find their ideal apartment. Thank you

The hallway smells due to animal waste and refuse. The management is very hostile and always looking for ways to exploit tenants. Security is poor and interior is too basic for a supposed luxury apartments. I regret moving in to the apartments.

Roach infested, unorganized and dirty. No one sweeps or maintains the building. You have request pest, or it’s not done. Summers are filled with roaches and gnats. I had a leak in my ceiling for months with no resolution until I called and emailed videos. This has been the worst experience of my life.

The leasing office is the worst I have ever  experienced in my entire life. I have ROACHES AND ANTS ALL ACROSS MY APARTMENT! For which they refuse to fix despite my paying pest control every month. I have never experienced such a terrible place to live. The leasing office is dishonest and rude. They have lied to me several times about fumigating my apartment then email me after an angry voicemail I left notifying me that the unit was NEVER SPRAYED. This is following several guarantees that it was as though I was the problem. The worst apartment complex and facility staff I have ever met in my  life. The air condition was broken for two weeks of which I notified them of as a MAINTENANCE EMERGENCY and they did nothing. I am brand new to Texas from South Carolina and never experienced such terrible service, I am extremely frustrated with H6 and do not recommend them to anyone.

Overall, it's meh. Based on my tours and looking around otherwise, I expected a lot better for apartments in the area. I'll list my pros and cons. Pros: 1) Maintenance is very good! Things get fixed pretty quickly, so I'm happy about that. 2) Apartment itself is very nice. I like the cabinetry, the tub, the kitchen island, and the granite countertops very much. Cons: 1) Courtesy officer never shows up when necessary. We've reported this multiple times and nothing is done. 2) Security of the building in general is ehhhhhh. Broken gate, broken doors on the upper floors. It's not great. 3) No parking permits, and no difference between residential and guest parking. People bring dozens of guests into their single units all the time, and it's very difficult to find parking on your given floor. You can pay $50 for a reserved spot with no extra perks PER MONTH, and some idiot will park in it anyway half the time. 4) There's a large amount of dog owners here that seem to let their dogs take a dump in the hallways or on the stairs and just leave it there. A lot of the residents have zero regard for others, and the management does not care despite making platitudes to your face about solving these issues. 5) The hallways, the stairwells, and the parking garage are smelly, grimy, and full of gnats, fruit flies, and roaches. Roaches are not so much of a problem in my unit, but the gnats get in all the time, and even with an electric fly catcher, it is never enough. 6) Management is nice, I've experienced no rude behavior, but I feel like they don't even do their job half the time. People go to them to help resolve issues with other residents, and half the time they seemingly don't do anything. If they do, there isn't a lot of communication, so my trust in them has waned. 7) Fairly sure someone lit off fireworks on the fourth of july and lit the top of the building on fire. HFD had to come to put it out. No official word from the complex or GPI. Lack of communication, again on this one, and it's sorely disappointing. This doesn't even cover everything. I've only lived here for a season, and we will be moving out at the end of our lease.

Run while you can, the worst option to live, dirty corridors and parking lots, smell of marijuana everywhere, there is no security, someone broke the windows of my car and they stole my belongings and nobody does anything.

We moved here because it looks like luxury, but it was the worst decision, The people at the leasin center are the worst, they never solve anything, they take more than two weeks to solve the problem (they haven't fixed it yet), the hallway smells bad,  there is no space in the garage, there is never a place or visitors or residents, it‘s horrible, DO NOT MOVE HERE you will regret

Save yourself the trouble and look elsewhere. Yes the apartments look nice, but it is not worth it. They look very luxury but once you start staying, it only goes down hill. To start off, the apartment complex always smells. There is trash everywhere all the time. Maintenance is a great guy only upside of this place. The garage gate was always broken and at one point someone got in and crashed 4 parked cars. They will charge you quickly for late fees but if you need something resolved, will take their time. Also do not forget to put your TV volume really low because they will fine you for disturbance. A fellow renter whom I am friends with was charged with this as well at the same time but we live on different floors. Do not even try to go to dispute it because they will not listen. The office staff is simply terrible. As stated by another user the office staff is not worth paying your money to. They will hang up on you if you try to call and resolve an issue. Garbage pickup is timely and consistent, maintenance is responsive, office staff are kind, gracious, and attentive, the two pools are lovely, the complex is very dog friendly, and accessibility to the highway and all major grocery stores, restaurants, and Katy Mills Mall adds to the convenience of residing here.  Of course, no place is absolutely perfect without fault – the issue of parking can sometimes be a struggle for folks but the office as been working toward navigating different solutions which I appreciate as a tenant.

Do not get me wrong - it is a lovely place to live....and also a place that will give you a lot of headaches because of some...major inconveniences...

CONS:
1. My car has been towed twice. There was a system error which deleted my parking permit on file leaving me without transportation to bring my grandmother to the hospital in an emergency. I'm awaiting to hear back from the complex to see how or if they will reimburse me for all of this. 

2. Meanwhile, there are other vehicles on the property which are not registered that have not been towed. There is a disconnect between the front office and their answering service. 

3. They either don't receive messages for them or they just don't check messages from them. Whenever I try to follow up on concerns left with the answering service, they usually have no idea what I'm talking about. 

4. They say they've made efforts to fix parking issues but there is no improvement. If you do the math, there is literally not enough parking spaces to accommodate all the tenants in the first building for spaces to be within reasonable walking distance. It's just something you'll have to accept. 

5. The main building is the only building that has elevators. 

6. The North gate has been out of service for some months now. 

7. The gym doesn't have as much equipment as I've seen in other apartments. 

8. The system for package lockers has been malfunctioning for months. You'll have to enter it manually vs electronically. 

PROS: 
1. Garbage pickup is always on time and they are consistent with that. 
2. Maintenance is typically responsive - I hardly any complaints about that. 
3. The office staff are pretty nice despite all that they deal with. I can't recall a single bad interaction. 
4. Two beautiful pools. 
5. Very dog friendly. 
6. Very comfortable environment/atmosphere. 
7. Clean halls. 
8. Accessibility: the highway and all major grocery stores and restaurants you'll need are nearby. Katy Mills Mall is less than 10 min drive without traffic. 

BOTTOM LINE: Can you be happy here, yes. But...you could be happier somewhere else. Get into someplace that has parking. The distress parking causes...is just....more distressing than you'd ever expect. I underestimated it and ***unfortunately*** this? outweighs any pros for me. It shouldn't be this terrible to ask for the basics....like...reasonable access to my own vehicle.

I was stuck at this location after COVID struck and it suddenly became the only place I could afford near the med center. That is no longer the case. After several unfortunate years here in multiple units, here is my review:

Pros: 
-Relatively close to the med center.
-Uncovered parking is free, and I haven’t had my car broken into.
-Packages are most often easily received and delivered.
-Can at first be an affordable choice, but you will never be able to afford renewal.
-Tenants, while noisy, seem to be mostly kind people, and it’s a diverse and welcoming demographic.

Cons:
-It’s a roach hotel. The “Valet Living” trash “service” they make you pay for (no opting out) will skip days without warning, leaving hallways packed with trash.
-During a particularly hot summer, they seemed to have lapsed in their pest control (all the outside roach bait boxes were collected and didn’t come back). Roaches of both major types swamped the apartments for the hottest part of the summer. Also, ants and spiders are a permanent nuisance, and they leave the hallways absolutely festooned with spiderwebs.
-Lazy cleaning crew. The hallways are left consistently uncleaned for weeks at a time. The hallways, trash rooms, elevators, and even newly cleaned apartments will be filthy. See how many boogers you can see wiped on the elevator walls if you visit.
-Loud tenants. There are no enforced noise rules, and all the units are in the same building. If you’re in a courtyard facing unit, I hope you’re not nightshift.
-Rude staff. They shuffled staff through at a rapid clip over the last year, and none of the good staff or managers who used to be here remain. They will be overtly aggressive in some cases, and mockingly dismissive in others.
-Unwilling to negotiate leases or renewals, even when better apartments nearby are cheaper (as is the case now, thankfully).
-Gun crime. There are gunshots in the back parking lot every other weekend. Consider yourselves warned. “Courtesy officers” seem to ignore it.
-Stray and abandoned pets. Abandoned dogs were living in the back lot and attacking residents for weeks during February of 2022.

Do not live here. Management is horrendous.

Would NOT recommend staying here unless you have the time and energy to deal with delayed repairs, poor communication, and inadequate timely compensation for any problems on behalf of the Alta apartment complex or Wood Residential company. And moldy walls. 

In August, there was apparently a leak in my water heater that caused extensive damage to the unit below me and the unit below that one. Alta hired outside contractors to begin repairs. For the first week, I lived and slept with this loud noise in my unit from the fans drying out the space. Alta bought me noise cancelling headphones to help make the space livable (just imagine sleeping with that on.) When I asked the technician how long the repairs should take, he said my unit had the least amount of damage so it should take a maximum of 2 weeks. They needed to cut my water off so I couldn’t stay there. 

Well it took 4 weeks and 1 day from then for me to get back into my apartment. The repairs to my unit itself took perhaps a week but the company wanted to be “cost efficient” and do all the repairs at one time instead of fixing my unit (the least damaged one) first so I could be back in there in a timely manner. For the first 2 weeks of this, I was staying at a friend’s because I kept getting told “the repairs should be done soon.” For the last 2 weeks of this, I stayed at a hotel that Alta at least agreed to pay for. The rest of the compensation for my time, great inconvenience, and mental toll included one month of free rent….. when I was already not staying there AND I still had to pay my utility and internet bills for that month???? 

Fast forward to November now, and I finally JUST got the reimbursement check for my hotels… which is OVER A $1,000 SHORT! And to top it off, there’s evidence of a water leak in the same area now. I’ve notified the front office about it nearly two weeks ago and I still haven’t heard about when they’re going to fix it. Meanwhile, the water damage and MOLD gets worse and worse. Seriously, I can’t believe this is what I get for how much I pay for rent. Take your money elsewhere and don’t stay here!!

apartmentName: Smart Living on Cullen Apartment Homes
review:
I am absolutely appalled by my experience at Smart Living On Cullen. From the moment I moved in, it has been a nightmare. The management is unresponsive and rude, treating tenants with complete disregard. Maintenance requests take forever to be addressed, and when they finally are, the work is shoddy at best.

The apartments themselves are poorly maintained and falling apart. I’ve had issues with leaky pipes, broken appliances, and pest infestations. The walls are paper-thin, so you can hear every noise from your neighbors, making it impossible to get a good night’s sleep.

The complex is filthy, with trash constantly overflowing and common areas never cleaned. The grounds are neglected, and it’s clear that the owners do not care about the property or the residents. I never feel safe walking around at night.

The rent is exorbitant for the quality (or lack thereof) you receive. Save yourself the stress, money, and frustration – do not move into SMART LIVING ON CULLEN. It’s the worst decision I’ve ever made.

apartmentName: Smart Living on Cullen Apartment Homes
review: Great place to live I’ve moved here when they were still doing construction. I recently moved out of Domain Heights, unfortunately, the property did not live up to the expectations. During my time there, the complex consistently struggled with maintenance issues. The hot water supply was unreliable, often leaving residents without hot water for extended periods. Additionally, many of the advertised amenities (golf simulator/sauna) were frequently out of service, which was extremely disappointing.

One of the most significant inconveniences was the elevator service; the elevator was out of order for nearly two months, causing considerable distress especially having to carry an elderly dog up 4 flights of stairs multiple times a day!

Moreover, after my lease ended and my family vacated the apartment, I was surprised to be charged additional fees without any valid reason or information from the management. $200 for water which made no sense since our water bill each month was nearly $20-$30. We were also charged for replacing carpets...This was after the manager mentioned on final walk through that the carpets looked great and would not have any issues. The same manager did let me know that the original carpets put in the apartment were cheap and would most likely need replaced, but each customer should not foot the bill for a poor choice in product.

I have tried to reach the property on the phone for months and in person, yet the management continues to duck the conversation and will not return phone calls or emails.

Things I love:
* Everything is clean and looks good. Hallways are cleaned regularly, no smell
* Everything is fairly new and works. I've only had two issues and they were fixed pretty quickly by maintenance.
* Staff are friendly and helpful, and amenities are good. The gym is never too crowded.
* The view from the La Branch-facing apartments isn't perfect, but if you angle your couch right, you can make it so you only see the pretty skyline
* Price relative to location. There are far worse located apartments for the same or worse prices, which ties into...
* Proximity to everything. There's no downtown HEB, but it and Target are a short drive away, and the Red Line rail is an easy 7 minute walk away, which gets you to the Texans stadium/Rodeo, midtown, Herman park, and the museum district. Discovery green is a cute little park that's also a 7 minute walk, and Phoenicia market, an adorable little grocery store with a great bakery, is right next to that. Downtown is not like other major metropolis downtowns, so it's not the most happening and  you won't have everything you need in walking distance / open late, but it's about as good as it gets in Houston for walkability.

What to be aware of:
* You're choosing to live next to the Astros stadium. If you don't go to more than a handful of games, this is exclusively a downside. Traffic on gamedays / concert nights is centered around this building, and some people blast their music after games often, so baseball season is generally fairly loud for my apartment on the La Branch side.
* Other noise: You can't hear the main street clubs or anything, but a few times a week there will be a loud car ripping its engine, someone absolutely blasting Wanna Be A Baller by Lil Troy (yes, that song specifically), or a group of people riding quads. These last from 2 seconds to 2 minutes, and even with your doors and windows properly shut, it's very loud, but this is the case with a lot of places in the loop so it's only specific to this apartment on gameday. The median volume, though, is very quiet for what you'd expect from a downtown.
* Parking pass system is strict at 24 hours. You have to re-create their guest pass as soon as the old one lapses, otherwise your friend's car will be towed without mercy. This is the one thing staff wouldn't help me out on.

You get a standard, basic washer\dryer in each unit which is also all most people need.

It is with heavy hearts that we have left The Inverness, after four memorable years, for the "suburbs" in another city.  I continue to believe that The Inverness is the best apartment community in Houston, and it is the consequence of several things that make it so.  As an example, during almost two years of lockdown resulting from the pandemic, we did not have one single maintenance issue arise.  The property is maintained so well, nothing seems to break down, everything works as it is supposed to, and if any concerns do arise or need attention, the staff is on it and---problem solved immediately.  Much praise is due to Juan, Margot, Jose and Leo for their unfailing ability to keep everything running well; to be free to never question their expertise and knowledge is a luxury in and of itself---and that kind of confidence affords a comfort level little else can match, when the subject is the place you call home.  Krysten, Luciano, and Alisia run the leasing office at The Inverness.  Once again, in four years residing there, we did not have a single complaint or issue arise. I have e-mailed the leasing office for one reason or another during non-business hours, and then received an informative, proactive response before the office is even open the next morning. I've called when everyone else in Houston seems to be working from home, and found that my call gets answered/action is taken/my questions resolved by Krysten, Luciano or Alisia--- who are actually in the leasing office, working, there on-site for the purpose of assisting us, the residents. These administrative tasks are accomplished in a professional and effective way, absolutely, but what makes all the difference is that Krysten and her staff are supportive, warm, and basically the kind of people you'd be inclined to say are your friends, too---and they happen to be running The Inverness.  No matter how much I may like the "suburbs," where I have moved to, I'll miss living at The Inverness, and I'll miss the wonderful people that make it the truly exceptional community that it is.

Sometime between this ticket and the last, they had me remove everything from my cabinets and countertops to let their pest control do a deep treatment. I had to be away for 3-4 hours. I waited two weeks since they said expect to see more roaches directly after since they’re trying to escape the chemicals. Today is 9/12 and the issue is not any better. I am even seeing roaches crawl up from my shower drain while I shower. Yes, you read that correctly. I have a video of a roach simply appearing at my feet in the shower. 

9/12/2022 I asked the property manager about my options to terminate my lease. She said I have to pay 75% of the remaining contract which would be over $4k. I refused, citing pest issues. She said I could be moved to a new unit on the property. I refused, citing pest issues. She said they could move me to another one of their properties, I would rather not, because I don’t feel valued as a resident with this company. I requested her supervisor’s contact info. I’m awaiting their call back. 

The property manager said I have no grounds for legal termination since I do not technically have an “infestation.” She says the gaps between my reports were too large to suggest a real issue. She says the roaches in my fridge were not alive (well how do you think they got there?). She insists that she has personally walked my unit and didn’t see any roaches. Well of course not, they come out at night. Her assistant manager has personally seen roaches in my ice maker and fridge. The issue they took over a month to fix. They eventually gave me a fridge from another unit. If anyone would like proof, I have pictures and videos of all of these things. If you don’t mind roaches it’s really not a bad place. Otherwise, the staff is friendly and usually responsive. But this pest issue has been wildly mishandled. For that reason, I cannot in good faith recommend this complex to anyone.

My experience at this apartment community has been extremely frustrating. Despite trying to give them the benefit of the doubt, I've encountered numerous issues in my nearly six months of residency. Can you believe I've had to submit nineteen service requests already? What's even more astounding is that half of these were for hot water alone, with the first instance occurring within my first month here. Talk about a less-than-stellar first impression!

Furthermore, another one of the ongoing problems I've reported is a continuously running toilet in my master bedroom. Despite being assured in November that it would be replaced, I'm still stuck with the same issue in February. It's incredibly disappointing and frustrating to be promised a resolution and then see no action taken.

As a full-time student juggling two jobs, the lack of hot water is particularly challenging. There have been instances where I've gone without it for over three days, forcing me to resort to boiling water on the stove for basic hygiene needs. It's an incredibly inconvenient and uncomfortable situation to be in.

I've tried addressing these issues with the office, and while they initially seemed willing to help, the lack of progress is disheartening. It's reached a point where it's becoming ridiculous, and I can't ignore the truth in the negative reviews I've read about this community.

Overall, my experience has been far from satisfactory, and I hope that management takes these concerns seriously and works towards resolving them promptly.

It's even more frustrating to note that despite always paying my rent ahead of time, I still face constant inconveniences. Adding insult to injury, my rent is over $100 more, primarily due the water billing. It's a situation that's so absurd, I can't help but laugh to avoid sinking into frustration.

The fact that I'm paying for a service that's consistently unreliable is disheartening. It's clear that the management needs to prioritize fixing these issues rather than burdening residents with additional costs for subpar amenities.

In conclusion, while I maintain a sense of humor to cope with the situation, it's crucial for management to address these concerns promptly and fairly. Residents shouldn't have to endure such inconveniences, especially when they're already paying for a comfortable living environment.

Pros
A clean, well maintained environment. Very friendly and helpful maintenance staff and close proximity to shopping, restaurants, pharmacies and grocery stores. Nice amenities and a true sense of security.


Cons
1. Office Staff.
We have been living here for a while and had the pleasure of working with Vincent and other office staff. They were very friendly, helpful and always willing and attentive to concerns that we had. The community hosted events regularly and this allowed neighbors to meet each other and also for management to develop a closer relationship with residents. There was a really close sense of community. It is quite obvious that this is NOT the case with the new office staff. They rarely address concerns, their attitude is definitely NOT customer oriented and they do not seem bothered by the issues that affect residents. 
2. Noise
If you are living on a lower level apartment, you will be forced to be subject to jumping, stomping and running from tenants living on the upper units. I really don't know how people with babies and small children can sleep with this constant noise. If you live close to the gates, you will also be interrupted by the slamming of manual gates and the loud chatter of people on entry and exit. The same is true for people living close to the pool and club house. You will be subject to constant noise from events, parties and weekend fun.
3. Rising Cost
If you do your comparisons, you will see that the cost of living here is considerably astronomical as compared to living in other apartments. You will get more square footage and the same amenities for less if you do your research. In the past, very attractive incentives were offered to new and existing customers. These offers no longer exist.

Though they're doing it all at once instead of spreading it out evenly with time. Maintenance here was always quick and super nice, though now they have their hands full with full scale renovations. My maintenance request was made last December and now its February... the renovations were necessary, but they threw the current leasers under the bus to do it. They refused to stop and can only make empty promises as to when your apartment may get looked at.

Did I also mention they keep changing websites to pay your rent? Each website is riddled with bugs and this month's bug is that you can accidentally overpay your rent. Management has told me they can't do anything about this. If you made a maintenance request on the last website, they will also fail to tell you it was deleted. There won't be a follow up email or phone call about it. You have to figure these things out on your own and be on their case about it. Not that they'll look at apartments anyway. Its full steam ahead with renovations.

The entire staff was also out sick with covid last December and came back better in January, but still maskless. They refuse to wear any as well. So good luck if you're doing a walk in and have pre existing conditions. Health is not a priority here.

The office staff is so amazing and very helpful. Yaniri helped me out and is a very sweet young lady. Karina, the leasing manager is always on point with helping me in my needs.

Apartments do not look like in the pictures. Cabinets are water logged, roach infested, fought roaches for over five weeks. Due to the conditions I couldn’t keep food outside the refrigerator. I had roaches in my bedding, I’m my clothes, in my food. The place is gross. If I could give zero stars I would.

The experience here has been the worst. Employee  was actually very helpful . Got us a beautiful apartment. However , theres roaches everywhere. NONE STOP. To make matters worst your own neighbors will criminally trespass your home. We are able to get out however we need to pay back 800$ out of our pockets for leaving since we got a month “free” . lived here for about a year, amazing staff, everyone is friendly and helpful, complex is clean and well kept, area is so-so but that just means prices are decent, would recommend!

I have lived at Post Midtown Square for a year. I toured 25 different apartment communities prior to moving here, and honestly, selected this community because of the leasing/property staff. The staff is usually the people you call with problems, and this staff seemed friendly, efficient and competent. In addition, they were very knowledgeable about the area. Marsean, Sandra and Chanel are very helpful and extremely easy to talk with. Even if there is a problem, they are quick to address it. I don't know how they remember everyone, but they do. Also, they send emails to keep residents up-to-date with anything happening in the community.

There are several buildings, with a variety of floorplans, and you can transfer to another unit, after you've lived in yours for at least 6 months. We have pools, a gym, package room, and each building has its own set of mailboxes. The office also hosts pool parties and food trucks.

Maintenance is SUPER fast to address issues. They even showed up the day of the hurricane (which I did not expect). They are always friendly, fast, and they clean up after themselves. If they are not able to make the repair, they explain the reason and give a timeline for when they'll return.

Probably the first thing I should have mentioned, is the unbeatable location. (Without the other things, however, location wouldn't matter, lol). It is very walkable --groceries, restaurants, CVS, bars--a cool little tequila stand, downtown, etc. Also close to 69 and 45.

The only negative is that traffic is occasionally loud; however, that's a side effect of living in the middle of everything.

I spent 2 great years of my life here. The best possible location, the only real walkable area of Houston. Restaurants and bars nearby. Only issue is the noise on Friday and Saturday nights, you will not sleep much if you face Gray.

Stay far away from this place. I literally beg you not to live here. It's been nothing short of a nightmare. We had no working elevator for months at a time and the office didn't even care enough to let anyone know what was going on or when it would be fixed. My window has been broken since I moved in and I have let them know countless times via email and maintenance requests and nothing was done for 10 months. The entire winter I was freezing and my electricity bill was outrageous ($300!!) and I live on the loudest side closest to the bar so I literally had to sleep with earplugs, but the entire office completely dropped the ball and ignored me until the month before I am moving out it just got fixed. No one was apologetic or took responsibility for this major fumble. I have had 6 stolen packages since November, again, with no apology and they simple blamed the delivery person every time. I emailed corporate because they responded to my other review asking me to reach out, and all they did was forward my email to the complex. I work in customer service myself and have never seen such disrespect toward the people who literally pay to live here. The pool was closed during the summer due to failing inspections and codes. The gates are broken. The outside area is constantly covered in trash and garbage and it's not ideal for walking dogs. This place is a little cheaper than surrounding complexes for a reason. Please save yourself the headache and pay a little more somewhere else.

We were suppose to recieve a half month free for the first month if we signed up that day, but never received it. Getting in was an easy process and the apartment is located in a great spot, but can't get into parking garage and cannot get the situation rectified.

The elevator was out of service for months. The pools failed inspections and were closed. My packages disappear. My roommate’s car was towed with the parking permit in the vehicle. Homeless people everywhere and they pee on the building and it smells bad all the time. Trash everywhere outside. My roof is leaking. It’s incredibly loud and I have to wear earplugs to sleep. Do not live here, save yourself the headache.

Positives: OK price for location, and maintenance USUALLY comes quickly (not always and I was once forced out of my apartment for a week due to broken A/C). Negatives outweigh the decent pricing. 

Negatives: 
1) NO FREE GUEST PARKING. They will lie to you and tell you there is free guest parking on the 5th floor of the garage so that you move here. Not true and you’ll end up paying ~20-30 dollars a day if you have anyone staying throughout the day/night. 
 -there is a building you can pay a monthly fee to park in, but the clicker regularly malfunctions and there’s one person who can fix it and they are conveniently never there. 
2) random fire alarms are still going off which is doubly annoying in the time of working from home due to Covid. 
3) be wary of which building you’re in because it can get extremely loud
4) Pool is out of service regularly for maintenance, which makes me wonder if it’s ever actually clean? No pull should be shut down 1+ weeks out of every month randomly. 
5) extraordinary fees to move out 
6) old A/C temperature control system so your apartment will be cooled unevenly. Example: my bedroom is always freezing but the living room is hot. 

All in all, I am counting down the days until I finally get to move out of this place. I have lived in multiple apartments with no complaints and this is by far the worst one I’ve ever experienced.

As a satisfied long time resident I’ve seen quite a few improvements in the security and maintenance with the new team this year.  The property is showing it’s age and the owners should invest in the appearance more. That being said it’s the best location in Midtown. Restaurants, coffee shops, and pubs are all downstairs and parks and grocery stores are an easy walk nearby.  Great front office staff. Kaitlyn, Veronica and Brittany are always happy to help with residents requests.

Honestly, I rarely give or even write reviews in general, but I think my voice need to be heard of some sort since it was not heard at the store. 

Location of the apartment is great, everything else is pretty much horrible. Leasing managers are rude and inconsiderate. (The agents are nice, but I could tell that there is a huge turnover there.) No securities or camera around the apartment, homeless are peeing everywhere. I was scared for my safety at times, due to the gates being broken and anyone could enter the building. Maintenance response time is decent and they are nice. Laundry room was down for a month, so couldn’t do laundry then, I had to take it to a friend’s place. Mail room is a mess and packages are left on the ground. Honestly, I did not get what I paid for, and I am happy I moved. Last but not least PLEASE READ LEASE AGREEMENT because they are slick with some wordings and overcharges you. 

 DO NOT RECOMMEND, IT IS A TRAP. Pictures on the internet is not the same IRL.

I moved here from out of state and wasn't able to visit the property before moving in. 
In order of least annoying to most;
- I am 28 and the location is VERY loud being that you're right above the street and in the middle of lots of bars. You pay a premium price for the location and they use that to justify not keeping up with the property itself.
- Everything is always broken. The gym is not well kept, the parking structure gate, pools...Often out of order.
- Communication from leasing office. It often times took me MULTIPLE emails to get a response from anyone in the leasing office. They are very difficult to communicate with and it's hard to get in touch with anyone outside of physically walking into the office.
- Security (or lack there of). They claim to have security guards always patrolling but what they really are, are young guys in blue security shirts roaming around on their cell phones not paying attention to anything. The doors in the parking structure are supposed to only be accessible via the key fab they give you, but the doors are always broken so you can just push it open without using a key. Anyone can park in the structure without paying or get into it with ease.
To sum up, I had a terrible experience here and they still told me they were increasing my rent if I would've signed another lease. Very poor.

Yes the location is nice but that's all they have.
Apartments are not great, lots of roaches problem (and other resident friends have had them also).
The worse is the service, management will try EVERYTHING to get more of your money (won't give deposit back, will charge you for any parking issues, will try to make you pay late fees when their IT/banking is to blame...)

Dont be fooled by the location, other nearby properties have slightly more expensive rent but LOT better service/apartments.

Things get stolen in the premises, hallways dirty and smelly, pools dirty, gates and doors broken often. Staff is really not helpful and they even lose the renters' delivery packages. Not a good option!

Do not move into this Apartment Complex.  They have minimum security and cars are broken into constantly.  Management is not obligated to increase security or take the necessary steps to prevent these crimes.  You are on your own.  Make sure to read the entire lease specifically the security section.

Pros:
-Great location (more on the Montrose side of Midtown)
-Great restaurants nearby (within walking distance)
-Two dog parks within walking distance
-Good value
-Variety of options (w/d hookup, w/d in unit, upgrades, various floor plans, etc.).
-Some of the associates in the office are very helpful (Oscar is the best)
- 3 pools

Cons:
- Your guests will be required to pay for parking (even in the parking garages) or they will be towed. Also, every morning around 5:30am a tow truck enters the gated garage and tows residents who don't have a parking decal (be aware of your company cars).  I've never heard of an apartment who tows residents every morning from a secured gate. 
- There are 5 buildings. Not all of them have attached parking. You may be walking your groceries across the street to get to your apartment.
- Certain buildings do not have an elevator on either side of the building. So, if you are disabled or don't want to walk the stairs, you'll have to walk through the parking garage just to get to an elevator (not convenient if you're walking a dog).
- Packages (FedEx and Amazon) are often not delivered because the buildings are secure and the leasing office is down the street. Expect to have issues with deliveries.
-Maintenance will enter your apartment without notice (and will not leave a note). This happened on multiple occasions; even after bringing it to management's attention. 
-Fire alarms go off in the middle of the night (in halls and every room of the apartment). The fire dept has been dispatched. This seems to be an issue for Camden and Post apartments.
-When the power goes out, you lose water. The apartment leasing office told me to call back at 10am (we lost water at 7pm)...really the answer is "call back tomorrow during leasing office hours?"
-The pet fee of $500 and leasing fee of $150 will not transfer if you move apartments within this complex. They will make you pay again. Seems excessive; especially if you want to retain customers. 
- The hallways and stairwells are open air; they are hot during the summers and are not frequently cleaned. 
- Not all buildings have upgraded features or patios. Make sure you know about the amenities before you sign a lease.

I have lived in the complex (2 different apartments) for over a year and it has been a pleasant experience. The staff is nice and helpful and the maintenance team has been responsive. The finishes of most of the apartments aren't as nice as you will find in newer complexes but the location is hard to beat. Noise can be an issue depending on which building you are in and which side of the street you face but it is to be expected when living in a downtown area. Being closer to Gray is definitely louder than if you are facing a smaller street like Webster.
When I was visiting the leasing office I had a difficult time finding parking. However the staff was very fined,y and even sent me follow up emails.
Since we moved in, they have made improvements. They keep up with the place and it's a safe place to live. It's also conveniently located near the freeway, parks and schools.

The staff is very nice . Clean environment ! Has two pools available including a spa , and is pet friendly

Maintenance is always responsive and accommodating. This place is a gem and we have been so happy with our experience. It’s also pretty affordable for the location. No complaints from us!

Nice community with nice amenities for a fair price. I absolutely love the location . I'm very close to the freeway and very close to some awesome entertainment venues . Staff is always very nice and helpful . Pool's and gym are wonderful and overall maintenance is fantastic!

My daughter loves the huge pool there too. This is a great gated community and only minutes from shopping. Oh and as much as I shop online I never have to worry about being home to accept packages, there take of that as well.

Id highly recommend anyone to this apartment.
We love living at Siena Memorial Heights. The grounds are always maintained. The staff is helpful and friendly. The location is excellent for us.
A great place to live with great location and layout of spaces. The response times for my A/C request were attended by Reinaldo who was very professional and efficiently solved the problem. Thanks.

Since our move in early 2020, MST has devolved from a vibrant, secure community into a disappointment masquerading as luxury living. What was once a haven of fun and safety has become a playground for petty criminals, with car break-ins now a regular occurrence.

Want to hit the gym after hours? Prepare for your personal security escort, because heaven forbid a paying resident use an amenity unsupervised.

The nickel-and-diming is relentless. The theatre room, once a seldom used but casual hangout spot, now comes with a $150 price tag. Brace yourself for an onslaught of arbitrary fees – trash, water, and who knows what they'll dream up next. It's as if they're determined to squeeze every last cent from our wallets while the building crumbles around us.

Speaking of which, enjoy your surprise cold showers courtesy of the increasingly frequent water leaks. Nothing says luxury like unpredictable basic utilities, right?

The Fourth of July "celebration" was a sad reflection of MST's decline. In a misguided attempt to create exclusivity, they managed to throw the most depressing pool party in history. Nothing says "Independence Day" quite like an empty pool and a DJ who apparently fears sunlight.

Maintenance? What maintenance? The gym looks like it's been through a war, doorknobs remain broken for years, and the wallpaper in the building is peeling faster than residents' patience. Essential amenities like the sauna, steam room, and golf simulator were out of commission for months on end, all while we continued to pay premium rates for phantom services.

The saving grace? The ground-level staff. Concierge, valet, and others, who soldier on admirably despite upper management's best efforts to run this place into the ground.

In short, unless you enjoy paying exorbitant fees for deteriorating amenities and the privilege of being treated like a delinquent teenager, I'd advise you to look elsewhere. MST has become a masterclass in how to alienate residents and destroy a once-thriving community.
