With my  daughter who is 4years old now . She loves  the playroom which is available on the 2nd floor. Plus rooftop is awesome as well ! Concierge is always on point and so is management .
Manager unavailable most of the time. Staff can't do anything to help because of corporate policies. DON'T LIVE HERE. THEY DON'T CARE ABOUT THERE OWN PEOPLE.

It's a nice apartment in comparison for the area. The staff were my only complaint. When I called to set up a appointment I had to persuade the tour guide to schedule a time. When I did arrive, traveling from out of state to view this apartment, the tour guide looked at me from behind the glass wall, continued to work, and once she realized I wasn't leave decided to yell "give me a second" still from behind the wall. She didn't seem very interested in my business during our tour, so I did not rent. But pretty building though!

I have lived at MODA for 2 years after coming to NYC from Chicago. 2 blocks to E,F, and J train, less than 10 minutes to LIRR and AirTrain direct to airport. The building is quiet (at least, has been for me) and I feel it's well-insulated.
The price, for the area, is high. They are charging for the convenience & amenities, versus neighborhood. You could get a 1 bedroom in Jamaica (elsewhere) for probably $300-$500/month less. It comes down to the quality of life you're looking for. If Jamaica is a neighborhood you'd consider, you should check it out. But be forewarned, prices may surprise you for being so far out of Manhattan.

One of the most impressive luxury building(s) in Manhattan with gorgeous units/finishes and amenities. Beyond that, I have been shown service that has gone above and beyond. The leasing agent and general manager created a small miracle in finding a dream ideal unit at a fantastic price point for exactly my move in window. This is the first time that I have lived in NY that I have not had to sacrifice a major desire/need (the classic price, space, location... add luxury) when looking for a place to live. I am elated.
Lovely building, horrible dangerous tenants. Do not come here.

Not very favorable at this time. Overall attractiveness has definitely fallen. Lots of drama among some occupants. Noise, drunkenness etc. the premium nature of the place, in my opinion, is threatened.
World-class building, staff and amenities in a great location. Honestly did not think properties like these existed!

I’ve been living at Waterline Square for a while now, and honestly, it’s amazing! The apartments are beautiful with floor-to-ceiling windows and stunning views of the river. The amenities are next level—gym, pool, tennis court, you name it. There’s even a soccer field... I mean wow.

The location is perfect, right between the Upper West Side and Midtown, with lots of great spots nearby. Plus, the waterfront park is a huge bonus. If you’re looking for luxury living with everything you could possibly want, this place is it. Highly recommend!

We absolutely love living in our building and couldn't be happier with the incredible amenities and outstanding administration. As parents of a toddler, we've found this place to be exceptionally convenient and family-friendly. 
First and foremost, the variety of amenities available is truly unparalleled. Our little one enjoys spending time in the children’s room, which is perfectly designed for kids to play and explore safely. The pool area is fantastic, providing a great way for our family to stay active and have fun together. The music room, equipped with drums and a piano, is a wonderful space that encourages creativity and provides a fun outlet for musical exploration. The garden is another highlight, filled with fresh greens and herbs, that allows us to enjoy organic goods on our tables. This thoughtful touch adds a unique and healthful benefit to living here. 
The administration team is exceptional. They are always responsive, friendly, and go above and beyond to ensure that the building is well-maintained and that residents’ needs are met. Their dedication to creating a welcoming and comfortable living environment is evident in every detail.
Overall, our building offers a perfect blend of convenience, luxury, and family-friendly amenities. We are grateful to call this place home and highly recommend it to anyone, especially those with children. It’s truly a wonderful place to raise a family! 
And last but not least, the location is simply unbeatable. We are just a few blocks away from Central Park on one side, and on the other side, we can enjoy peaceful walks by the Hudson River. This ideal location provides the perfect balance between vibrant city life and serene natural beauty.
There are cockroaches in the basement and regularly on the first floor. The elevators were under construction multiple times.

Worst place I've ever lived..... And I've lived in basements. The construction inside is endless. They are still very early in the process of turning old apartments into "luxury".  ...definitely NOT luxury.
The toilets, tile, and flooring is the finest CRAPmanship I've ever seen! Lol ...two of my toilets are 7" taller than a standard toilet. My feet do not even touch the ground when I sit on them. The appliances were all wrapped in plastics and not setup whe. I moved it. I had to setup the ice maker and shelves in the fridge. The stove was also not set up. They had floor plans, manuals and plastic stored inside the stove and microwave. The tile does not lay flat on the kitchen backsplash. And flooring was laid with huge gaps. It is done by people that really don't care and don't know what they are doing. Everywhere I look there is a problem. My balcony door finally shuts properly after three months of issues. It was never installed right.

So the construction.... It started at 8am the first day, and when I complained they only changed it to start at 8:30am. 
It has been going on since I moved in in September. They are redoing the apartments both above and below me at the same time. It honestly feels like an earthquake. I had to take the paintings and mirrors off my wall because they were shaking so badly. 
The vibration was so bad that a pipe in my bathroom broke and the toilet is now leaking! 
They have not decreased my rent at all. Even when they are working on the apartment 2 doors away from mine I hear it clearly since the walls are paper thin.
To the icing on the cake is the dust! It seems to somehow make it into my apartment and now is covered in white concrete dust. The smell tickles my nose and is noticeable. 

I can't wait to move

If you have any problems while living here, you can be sure that they will not help you at all.

Lot of improvements going on in the building, but it is starting to come together. Great location! Huge balcony in many apts. close to 4/5/6 and will be stop for 2nd ace subway. Equidistance to Central Park or Carl Shurz park on east river. Pet friendly. Great restaurants and bar all over the neighborhood.

This is the perfect place for you, if you like: jackhammers in the apartment above you, someone occasionally sawing through the ceiling above your bed while you're in it, scalding water pouring over your balcony, and 90% of your building under construction with no end in sight. They tell you none of this upfront, so please be forewarned. It's a great neighborhood, but you may (will) end up living in a *very* active construction site. All of this has personally happened to me in my apartment in the course of less than a year living here, and there are days I want to cry as I work from home. :-(

My family has lived here for decades. it hasn't been easy, especially since they are seniors. Yes, it hasn't been easy for myself as well,  however they can't afford to move. My father's boss doesn't pay him regularly. Still it's our home. Please consider them.

I been living here twenty five years with my husband, he recently passed and it’s a struggle for me every day, there are owners living above me and for the last several months they have been doing some kind of construction hammering and it’s becoming very hard for me to live with, I have called Parkchester security many times and they come and go talk with them but to no avail it keeps happening, always after five o’clock after business hours the constant hammering and it’s causing me problems with my health, if your looking for somewhere to live I think you should consider finding somewhere else because you won’t find the help you need here, don’t get me wrong I am grateful for a place to live but this is won’t help your peace of mind, I am also looking forward to finding somewhere else to live I’ve had enough.
Parkchester is about money not your safety or your health if you see this don't move here.

I have been living in my Parkchester apartment since 2007. I loved the area and space the apartment provided for the cost. it was really great for NYC. Loved having everything you could possibly need in this little area (grocery store, cleaners, Laundry, even use to have a movie theater here) granted with time everything changes but it saddens me to say that the area has been on a downhill slope.  The Parkchester Ownership does not response to tenant/owners needs as quickly or efficiently as they use to. It is now 2022 and I would not suggest the area to anyone looking to move now where as I once was a constant advocate for the area.  I stayed in the area because I felt it was a safe place for my family. Now I feel like Parkchester has the ability to still be a great place to live however the new Management that has taken over a few years ago clearly does not provide the same level of service to its residents. The  truth is you get a good size apartment, however this new management has taken over with sizable increase every time you renew your lease. (and this started before the Pandemic) Forced some people out just because of the increase and the area is not as clean as it once was, however still better then a lot of other NYC neighborhoods.  as of 2022 I would tell you to keep looking because if you come here you will be looking for a new place to live shortly thereafter. I hope this helps.
I was shown these apartment and they had dead roaches and they want too much paper work for these project looking apartments. Don’t waste your money and time.

So the refrigerator that they gave me just broke. Ruining hundreds of dollars worth of food as well as my diabetic medication. There is a ton of issues here. Don't even bother coming here.

I have been living at Parkchester for two years. I contemplated moving, but other places want twice as much rent for half as much space! Not only will I continue to live here, I want to transfer to a two bedroom.

I love my apartment, I love the staff, the building is always super clean!

They are caring, hard-working, and honestly, feel like family!  Cheers to Phil, Solomon, Carlos, Charlie, and the rest of the amazing team!
I love living in this building the entire experience is exponential! We have such a great and supportive staff. I highly recommend this building as a place of residence.
The apartment is well maintenance. All the staffs here are super helpful and nice. I'm so glad that I choose MHM.
The on-site staff are extremely professional, friendly and efficient. I feel very safe knowing they are here and am confident that service requests will get completed in a timely manner.
Living at Murray Hill Marquis has been a great experience thus far.
I love living at MHM. The staff is all very friendly and responsive to any requests that you might have. The move-in process was seamless and the amenities here are great. Love having the gym.
Nice building, very good layouts, very nice people working here. So far so good, I've been here only for 6 months, but hope to stay here much longer.
I love living at Murray Hill Marquis. The process from beginning to move-in day was seamless. The staff and doormen are excellent and I am very happy.
Its a wonderful place to live with a great staff and cleanly environment.

Murray Hill Marquis is an excellent community! The building is in excellent condition and amenities are great. Its centrally located, and I feel absolutely safe living here. The best thing about it though is the staff, hands down! They are exceptional and a lot of the reason why I will stay here.

Management is not good. They do not fix the issues in my apartment and the entire apartment was built in a cheap manner. The floors are not level, appliances continue to break, and maintenance leaves a complete mess every time they come to do work. Management/Superintendent also do not send out emails for general notices to tenants, they put papers under each door or post by the elevators, which is no good if I am not home.
The Murray Hill Marquis in amazing, both the building and staff!  I highly recommend putting it on your top lists of luxury rentals to come see.
The upgraded amenities that we were promised are still unfinished. This is unacceptable.
Have had a great experience at Murray Hill Marquis - from moving in to solving any issues I’ve had, the process has been seamless. Everyone has been really helpful and attentive!
I love living at Murray Hill Marquis. The apartment is brand new and beautiful. It truly serves as the best midtown location. Everyone working in the building is friendly and attentive.

The Murray Hill Marquis is the place to be in Manhattan.  The location is perfect being located on 34St between 3rd and Lex.  Everything in the building is brand new or in the process of becoming brand new.  We have a laundry room and gym for use by everyone in our building and there is no membership fee for the gym.  The lobby is very nice and we have a 24 hour doorman.  The guys at the front desk are absolutely the best in NYC.  They are so accommodating and so helpful.  They greet our guests cheerfully, they handle our packages diligently, they provide a great safety and security for everyone. The maintenance staff is very nice too.  Our building Super is available for any questions or problems that may arise, you call and they are on it immediately, you know they care about us.   We have a few luggage carts in the lobby to help move large items up to your apartment, a huge benefit for all.  The elevators are new, we have four of them.  They are large, fast, reliable and have camera’s inside.

I have a studio on a lower floor.  The apartment is bright and cheery and everything, I mean everything inside is brand new.  New bathroom, new kitchen, new appliances, new flooring new a/c and heat and new track lighting.  My apartment is quiet too. It is more than enough space for me and I don’t feel crowded.  I have been meeting my neighbors day by day and everyone seem to be very friendly.  I am very happy with my decision to rent at the Murray Hill Marquis.  The rent is certainly affordable for this great location and the condition of the building, the outstanding staff and our building amenities make this a sought after location in midtown.

I have been a tenant for an year from Dec 1 2020 thru Dec 1 2021. I a writing a review because it's a nightmare to get hold off them. I have recently relocated from NYC to Miami and hence I had to send the keys via mail when my lease terminated (in time). I received a security deposit which is about 900$ less (some deduction is justified) and the break down they have given me is ridiculous. I wish they had taken pictures of these damages to show me what exactly they were referring to and I could've told them how it was when I started to rent the apartment.

So my point is, I absolutely do NOT recommend dealing with this building management or maintenance as this isn't the best in terms of service. It is incredibly frustrating to go through this. The only reason they were able to do this is because I wasn't physically there during the inspection. I have lived in NYC for 12yrs and I have never had this kind of experience ever before.

Used to love this building but as another reviewer (in July) put it, the constant construction and things just not working is making this a terrible place to live. They have no desire to do anything about it but weak offers of "you can use another space for work" and "we have no schedule on our construction."

I came back home to find that the air conditioner had leaked all over my bedroom floor and mold was growing on the wall. "We cleaned up!" was the answer. A little Clorox on the wall was all that was done.

Don't move in. Just don't

Do not live here if you ever want to talk to anyone in management. I’ve been having an issue for weeks about extremely loud construction noise while trying to work from home. I’ve called and emailed more times than I can count and have received any help on the situation. Save your money and live somewhere else
I love staying within these historic walls. The amenities are fantastic and friendly staff
Quiet, well-maintained building in a great location with terrific views of Manhattan.

The Octagon has quickly become our new home. We feel so relaxed the second we walk through the doors. From the gym to the pool to the huge windows with fantastic views, the Octagon has truly become our oasis.

Living in an 200 year old castle with great amenities, tourists attractions, nature, UN and corporate executives is a dream come true.  Affordable and super competitive rates.  The leasing team is state of the art, top professionals, genuine, kind, and want you to be happy to stay long term.  Always with a smile and love for humanity.

I’d highly recommend The Octagon to anyone looking for a luxury, pet-friendly apartment in NYC. The building staff is exceptional, the premises are beautiful, and it’s such a great community for people in all life stages.
The Octagon is one of the most beautiful places to live in Manhattan. It is peaceful, safe and enchanting. The Octagon is truly an Oasis in the middle of the East River.
This is wonderful and warm place to live full of so many great people and families. You could see and hear the joy of each child that live here as they enjoy many of the amenities for kids.
Recently I am very unhappy with the maintenance. They do not take me seriously.  They come whenever they want. I do not understand why they can’t coordinate a time to come and see the problem
We are having a great time at this apartment. We are on our first year. We just renewed a two year lease and honestly will continue to live here as long as possible. Everyone is great and wonderful.
Since I’ve been here, I’d like it a lot. The neighborhood is good nice people around clean building. They’re on point on everything in the building, loving people around.and my kids love it

You are mostly dependent on the Q train if not having a car, which means if commuting will need to transfer to the subway and takes around 45 min to get to most places. Usually things get done in 1-2 days when requested through the built app. Gym is ok, might need more equipment. Rooftop grill cleaning is on the residents. All the ice makers in the buildings don't make ice. I wasn't told this until I moved in. Other than that not a bad place to live. A very quiet neighborhood.
Lots of pets! Very nice. Beautiful outside and great amenities. The doormen are great too. The neighborhood has some nice stores around too for needs.
Just started living here but I can already tell the community is beautiful. The amenities enable us to communicate and socialize amongst each other. Plenty of dog friends and cat owners!
I love the building. My kids are happy to live here. A lot of fun stuff and events to do here clean nice people. and my kids love the playground

Love this residence and management are always available to help. Clean and quiet building . Will sign another two year lease 
Very family friendly environment
The building is beautiful and staff is pleasant. The apartment is super lovely and spacious, and viewing of the courtyard make it feel like oasis. Love my neighbor. Love it here:)
Very clean, loving people in the building. i’m so happy and excited my kids are happy and comfortable. very fun events, they having in the building

All the concerns and issues are being simply igrnored or their reply would be ‘get the door pillows!’  The elevators make a very annoying sound and stop on every single floor every weekend and holiday. The elevator broke with us inside of it yesterday, and we were trapped with no air for 25 minutes until the fire department showed up. As you can see... the list goes on. It’s a very promising building that does not deliver, we are extremely disappointed.
Lived on middle floor and had 6 mice. Also hallways smell of garbage frequently. Staff is nosey and cause drama.

I would not recommend living there.

For over 8 months now they have been doing mind-numbing construction on the facade.  Management does the absolute bare minimum to minimize the impact on tenants. I've met people who have recently moved in and they were not informed of the noise. If you work from home, have small children, or just want to be able to reasonably use the apartment you pay for, do not move here.

This building in this neighborhood have both really gone downhill in the past couple of years. The rents have risen dramatically and yet the service has declined severely. Was formerly mostly young people but seems to be leaning more towards those in their 30's and families. Not much of a community as people keep to themselves but overall friendly and well maintained.

Service calls to your apartment are usually taken care of within 24 hours and the staff is pleasant. They will try to raise your rent every year but negotiating is possible. Great for those looking for shares or those that can afford 3K plus for their own place.
Great building, gym, pool, package room, newly renovated elevators. Won't have AC in living room if you flex. Same apt in midtown is $900 more. Only drawback is relying on the 4-5-6 trains.

Reception staff is rude and upon viewing their units can't say many positive things about their maintenance team.

For the next year, this will be a four star apartment. Big windows, uninterrupted views of the west side down to Jersey City, nothing in the way of sunsets or the Hudson. But three big buildings are going up South, West, and North and it'll all be gone by 2017. And constant construction sounds.  

Staff great, roof nice, free shuttle to subway.

The house is well-maintained and offers excellent amenities. Highly recommended for anyone who loves nature and city living.

As a recent Columbia graduate, living at Central Park Manhattan House has been a breath of fresh air. I love that I can still enjoy the academic energy of the Upper West Side while being so close to Central Park for outdoor study sessions. The washer/dryer and private bathroom are luxuries I never had during undergrad!

I enjoyed my stay with Outpost Club. The apartment was well-kept and in a great neighborhood. The move-in process was straightforward, and the customer service team was always responsive to any issues.

The location is unbeatable, with Central Park just a few blocks away and a host of great local spots nearby. The apartment is comfortable and well-maintained, and having easy access to popular attractions like the Museum of Natural History and Barney Greengrass adds a lot of value. It’s a top-notch place for anyone who wants to be close to the park and enjoy the UWS.

My stay at the Central Park Manhattan House has been fantastic. The location is ideal for anyone who loves being near Central Park, and having so many attractions within walking distance is a huge advantage. The apartment itself is comfortable, and the proximity to famous spots like Absolute Bagels and the Museum of Natural History is a real bonus. My only critique is that the building’s amenities are a bit dated, but overall, it’s a great place to stay in NYC.

The exposed brick, modern furnishings, and clean shared spaces make it feel luxurious yet cozy. Having a private bathroom was such a treat, and the neighborhood is fantastic. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a stylish and comfortable home.

It is one of the best co-living spaces I’ve ever stayed in. My private bathroom was a lifesaver. The location in Brooklyn is ideal for both work and leisure. I couldn’t be happier with my decision to live here.

The apartment is fully furnished, professionally cleaned, and in a convenient location. Plus, the community here is welcoming—I’ve met some amazing people. My only hesitation is the price once the short-term lease promo ends, but overall, it’s been a solid choice for an easy move to NYC.
A beautiful house in a central location. It’s been a quiet place to come home to after work, and the rooms are nicely furnished. A few minor maintenance issues, though.

The bedroom is spacious with plenty of storage, making it easy to keep things organized. The bathroom feels fresh and modern, and the abundance of natural light throughout the space creates a warm and inviting atmosphere. It’s a comfortable and functional setup that feels like home.

After months of searching, I finally found a room with Outpost that fit both my budget and needs perfectly. Their professionalism stood out from the start, and their customer service has been outstanding. From getting the room ready to addressing small issues, everything was handled efficiently. I'm extremely satisfied with my stay and would highly recommend them to anyone struggling to find a quality place in the city.

The room is small and it’s pretty expensive for just a small room rent splits on every week payment. Bathroom is nice. First floor is very beautiful. Scary elevators. They have kitchen downstairs. They have nice rooftop

I liked it a lot. My stay was 95 nights long. I was there from the beginning, there was a lot of renovation going on at the time, the staff was always very friendly and completed tasks quickly, I never had to wait long for anything. The whole team was like family to me. Every day they try to give their best and are very eager. The location is the best in NY. Everything is within easy reach and you are in the heart of the city. I will definitely come back.

When I first moved in in 2019, the building was super nice and clean and well taken care of. Once COVID hit this place became an absolute dump. Bed bugs and roaches everywhere (yup they had someone spray numerous times but the entire floor had a problem) and the laundry room is disgusting. I moved out ASAP once the bed bugs took over. Worth mentioning the pool is owned by an outside company and WAY too expensive to actually use.

I have been in my apartment since Oct 2021 and so far so good. I love the building, the convenience of parking near the entrance, and esp the laundry area. There is someone who will pick up & deliver my laundry for a resonable fee. I also like that they deliver Amazon packages to my door. I love the sunset view from my 3rd floor. Now some negatives are the super is not that great, however, certain things got done, like they fixed my terrace door, changed a light bulb in a timely manner. The people in the office can get edgy, you have to know how to deal with that. I suggest just be nice. The shopping is great in Bay Terrace shopping center and I love the Stop&Shop there. Overall, very happy. And it is auiet where I live and not one roach, which could be because I have a cat. I do recommend this building.

I lived in this building for 20 years. Moved to Fla. last year. This used to be a very nice place. But management doesn't want to hear anything, except for you to pay your rent. For two years I had to put up a tenant above me that stomped around, dropped heavy items, etc. Management paid no attention to my complaints. After 20 years, I had no respect. And they no longer vetted new renters.

You don’t want to live here. The maintenance is non existent. The bathroom overflows constantly and nothing is done. You either pay for a private plumber or live with it. At best you’ll get a kid to sneak your toilet now and then but it doesn’t solve the problem of the systemic level.  DON'T DO IT!

Williamsburg House is decent but not perfect. The rooms are a bit smaller than expected, and the laundry facilities could use an upgrade. That said, the location is amazing, and I’ve enjoyed exploring the area. The street art and weekend markets nearby are definite highlights.

The Williamsburg House was my first home in NYC, and it set the bar high. I stayed for three months, drawn by the in-unit laundry and modern kitchen. The neighborhood was lively, with Smorgasburg and waterfront views just a short walk away. The roommates were respectful, and the management team was incredibly responsive.
The location and nearby spots make it unique, and the amazing atmosphere adds to the charm. Plus, I’ve met so many great people here—it’s been a fantastic experience!

Outpost Club has been very professional and responsive since day one. Their rates are pretty competitive, which is important for someone like me balancing school and rent. It seems like the apartments are managed by the landlords, but Outpost acts as the go-between, making everything easier. I’ve never had an issue they didn’t address quickly, and their local maintenance team is on it when it comes to fixing things. The short-term lease flexibility was a big factor for me, as my schedule changes frequently. Highly recommend, especially in a fast-moving rental market.

I moved here right before starting a new job in Manhattan, and it was such a relief to find a place so close to the L train. My commute was less than 10 minutes, which is wild for NYC. The apartment was clean, and my roommates were all super laid-back. The only thing I wish was different was that the common areas were a bit bigger — it gets crowded sometimes. But overall, a good spot in a dope neighborhood. Definitely recommend!

Williamsburg House Williamsburg House is in a great spot if you like the artsy vibe of Brooklyn. I’m from Chicago, so I wasn’t sure what to expect, but the location won me over. It’s right by the Bedford Ave L stop, which made getting into Manhattan quick and easy. The apartment, however, had its issues. It’s a bit cramped, and there was a problem with the A/C when I moved in, but once that got sorted out, things improved. I’d say it’s decent, but maybe a little overpriced for what you get.

I had a great experience over 4 years there:
-The rare time I needed maintenance, the turn around was markedly quick.
-After snow storms the parking lot was cleared quickly
-Parking lot is a huge plus
-Washer/Dryer huge plus
-Nice apartment
-Good privacy between upstairs/downstairs room
-Convenient location
-Very helpful, pleasant management office

It couldn't have been better. I would recommend without hesitation.

Roach infestation ! Roach infestation , building is full of big roaches and small ones

Lefrak is the worst possible apartment you can rent. The tenants are mostly there because they have nowhere else to go. 
Their Maintnance office is never open *during* business hours. They are unreachable by phone calls, and they take lunch break from 11AM-2 PM 
They also leave the premises before 4PM (the stated time). 
Their leasing office/management offices are also very non-accommodating. 
They will try to abuse your rights as tenants and bank on the fact that you’re not familiar with all the nitty gritty NYC laws to take away your rights from you. 
The management office lied, and in one case told us that lease resignation is at landlord’s discretion, where it’s the tenants right by law. 
The management also advised another tenant on evacuating, only to use that as a tool against him in a court case. That case fell through. 
When I was helping the other tenant in his case, their lawyer tried bullying us out of the case and subject us into paying thousands of dollars wrongfully charged. 
They are never responsive via email, they will respond weeks later after multiple reminders and follow up emails, *on time sensitive matters* 
They will never look out for the tenants, instead will use them only as source of unfair profiting. 
Because they are so large, you may not be able to watch out for yourself as much. 
Their apartments are infested with roaches, mice and water leaks are a constant affair. 
Their hallways are dark, smelly and full of disgusting stains 
The lobby is equally dirty and not well maintained 
It’s hard to get in to the apartment, even if you’re a tenant of many years if you forgot your key fob with you. They have no way to check your information and open the door for you. 

And NOISE is the worst, of the 6 years I lived there 3 of them was unbearable with Jackhammering and construction noise right on the building, you could not sleep with that noise, and no compensation was made for it, instead added charge was imposed to your rent for building reformation. 
If you haven’t experienced the worst of New York City, you definitely will with Lefrak City.

Ideally located close to mass transit and shopping malls. Not a totally negative review, except for dogs pooping and peeing and their owners/walkers not cleaning up after them. Especially in elevators. If you're transferring from one apartment or building to another do your own research more than 90 days about availability and procedures.  KNOW BEFORE YOU GO. Your personal and financial information must be uploaded via PDF. Years of living in the complex, even with stellar on-time rent payments, do not translate into you being treated like a 'loyal customer'; you're just another candidate for residency with a hit or miss system for getting an apartment. Timing also plays a role. Again, KNOW BEFORE YOU GO!

The Bali building in my opinion is one of the best buildings in Lefrak City. Not only does it have a great maintenance team led by Superintendent Sandy and Neker, but the manager Jennifer is such a sweetheart as well as the RPA Angelica. Bali building is near all the amentias such as the park, library, and pool. The laundry room is always open so you can go in no matter what day or time which is convenient. There is always a guard patrolling which always makes me feel safe and secure. I just loving living here, moving to Bali was a great move on my end. Thank you again :)
Mes gusta por las seguridades que nos proporciona tanto a mí cómo mis familias y vecinos.
Staff is great, always courteous. Building  is always clean including the elevators.
The Hancock House offered me a clean, modern living environment with thoughtful amenities like monthly cleaning. I felt safe and connected to the city’s culture while staying here.

The building is structurally sound, and I live in an apartment where there are quite a number of 1 bed/1 bathroom suites.  No one one has a wait to use a restroom and most tenants have their own private bathrooms--this alone, makes the moderate room pricing enviable.  The weekly cleaning is a great asset to living here and is done fairly well.  Also, whenever there have been any issues with maintenance or apartment needs member support service agent, Jolene, has been amazing.  She takes tenants' requests seriously and responds to emails in timely and professional fashion.  Jolene believes in member support and respecting all tenants.
It's an nice size and enough room for kids and younger family members can run around

This is the worst building I've ever been in my life, the problem they have with mice and rats is completely exasperating. all the units are riddled with mice and the ciampa organization does absolutely nothing but blame the tenants for the rat problem, claiming that the responsible are the tenants for not being clean enough, can you believe it? , besides this, that building is always dirty, the super who lives there, its as if he does not exist, never responds to complaints that may arise due to problems. and if that were not enough, the ciampa organization charges you an extra monthly commission in addition to the payment of the rent for alleged charges of late payments even if you pay on time !. I only lived one year there because it is full of rats And mices! It is a nightmare living there specially if you have baby or kids, DONT EVER MOVE TO THAT PLACE! Ever!!!!

This building is managed poorly and employs a part time super who doesn't maintain the property up to the neighborhood standard. Work orders take weeks or even months to be completed.

This is the first place I have ever rented, and I definitely...learned some lessons. It was very difficult to contact the property manager to get a tour and fill out an application, and maybe I should have taken that as a sign that something was off, but I ended up renting anyway.
Maintenance has either dragged their feet or neglected to help at all for every single issue I had, from unsafe electrical outlets to broken washing machines (they claimed it "wasn't their problem" despite the machines being for the entire building's use). Management doesn’t get back to you about anything

This has been the worst management company I have ever lived in.  Have not been able to get a hold of anyone in Fairfield for 9 months.  Great location but that is about it. This is by far the worst but most expensive apartment building I have ever lived in (I've lived in a total of 5).  Management is AWFUL and no one in the office returns phone calls. Tenants constantly write in the elevator "WORST BUILDING EVER" and "RUN" in Sharpie if that's any indication.  It's like being in prison or a psych ward until you can move.  Can't wait for my least to be up in a month.  Spend your hard earned money elsewhere. RUN!!!!

Would give 0 stars if I could. Nothing but a nightmare ever since we moved in a month ago. Drain flies, mold, leaks, absolutely zero concern or communication from management. I mean radio silence. Stay far away.

I must say they tried to fix up this place but with all the deadbeats that live here brings this place down and its sad. I have a three room apartment for me and my five kid . it a nice apartment .needs miner work done to it .the apartment is a nice size for me and the kids.
The apartments are ok but some of the people are terrible. As another reviewer said when you call this specific  lady is very nasty and she is the one takeing care of the apartments.

I am presently living in one of their apartments barely 3months and the experience is disappointing. Management is rude as well as so called security. I drove past these apartments and omg I really wanted to live there. So updated and pretty. Close to a small shopping center and the train.

The only criticism I have is the customer service. The number that is on this app is not a good number. I had to find a different number after googling arverne view apts. Then when I finally got in contact with someone, she was rude. She also told me that she would contact me back, took down my information, and never called me back for a follow up. I can only imagine how they treat their residents!!!!

the area is perfect.i've lived in rockaway for 4 years.i watched the construction.the improvements are incrediable.clean and friendly
Beautiful, elegant and modern NYC living for out of state prices.
The apartments at Arverne are very nice; however I was not qualified because of my income. My salary was above the amount necessary for a one bedroom.

I did not agree eith the price and the application process good credit really no credit they have to do better for ppl looking for apartment ppl who sre just starting out...when u call they are very nasty......why will u want to live some where and the ppl dont care.

My husband and I went here to view an apartment. On our way to the management office, we had to pass people loitering. This was on a cold rainy day so we could only imagine how the development looks when it's nice weather. We were disappointed and felt that we waisted our time.I gave two stars and not one because the property has potential if they address people standing around with nothing to do.

The team at the management office is okay. The boss is terrible. Really nasty attitude. As I was speaking to a broker he overheard the conversation and rudely commented his opinion on my conversation. Very bad taste of management.

The management company is unresponsive. 

The community room has been closed for over 2 years and the property manager refuses to give residents an update. 

The community here isn't what you think it would be. The building isn't that big, but folks don't take care of the space and it's really unfortunate.

worst place ever to live. the landlords do not turn the heat on until far too late and they also turn the heat off ASAP. tried turning the heat off literally just because it was 70 degrees one day in february. theres a team of landlords but yet they never respond to the emails and they take half of your deposit for some "building charge". every single tenant i spoke to was extremely dissatisfied with the team of landlords and the building itself.
Hallways get vacuumed every 2 weeks. Garbage rooms never moped and cleaned. The paint on doors are scratched up and scuffed. The maintenance on this building has gone down severely.

Alcove studio that is extremely spacious with more closet space than any NY apartment I have seen.  There is a separate area by the bathroom for storage and "dressing table".  Updated kitchen and bathroom.  Building has few amenities but is fulltime doorman building with excellent super who fixes any issues within 24 hours.
This is the perfect location with great doormen.  Close to the best shopping, bars and restaurants it is the perfect New York experience.

This building said we could apply with 3 people on a lease, so we went forward with it only to find out after giving them everything they asked for, that they would only allow 2 people on the lease. We would never have applied (all 3 of us giving $100) if they had told us that upfront. Now, they refuse to refund us on THEIR misinformation.

This prewar apartment is advertised as a full service building but the doormen don't really do much. Anyone can walk into the building. Literally anyone. Doesn't really feel safe. The building is extremely overpriced for what you get. No gym in the building which is an inconvenience. You are paying park avenue prices without reaping the benefits.

My wife and I were looking for a pet-friendly 1BR within walking distance to Grand Central (and within our budget). This building fit all those criteria, as well as some of our secondary requirements.

Building has 24-hour doorman and a live-in super. Staff were all very nice and helpful if issues arose (we had no maintenance issues in our unit in 2 years). Building has a small gym, which is free for residents. Building also has a laundry room and elevator.

Building is located at 36th and 2nd, which lends to some traffic noise due to tunnel entrance, but it wasn't overpowering. Flip side of that is you're walking distance to many bars, restaurants, grocery stores, drug stores, subways, etc. There's a big park right across 2nd (basketball courts, large blacktop area, squash courts, large playground) as well.

Our unit had two in-wall A/C units (bedroom and main room). Unit had been updated with granite countertops and stainless steel appliances in kitchen, marble tile in bathroom. Quality of work was a little shoddy, but everything looked/worked just fine.

Overall, building is in a convenient location with decent amenities. It's nothing fantastic, but you could do a lot worse on the east side.

Do not live here. Do not waste your money/time Horrible building management. Only two elevators, which are constantly out of service needing repairs. Currently both are broken leaving residents trapped. Zero accountability from building manager

Pros: Relatively renovated units (W/D, dishwasher, etc.), elevator building, relatively clean trash room on every floor, safe area

Cons: Old looking hallways, not very convenient to any major subways, extremely slow response times/lack of care from management, lots of maintenance issues (both with elevators, gym equipment, and in-unit), saw 2 cockroaches on the 11th floor, some of the doormen are not that friendly 

Overall,  I didn't stay longer than a year and wouldn't recommend. You can pay less and get nicer places in the city.

We moved into a newly renovated apartment. Every aspect of the building was immaculate and the apartment seemed to match. As the weeks went on, we did discover a number of things that didn't work properly. Although it was slightly annoying, management was very quick to fix anything that was below our standards. The doormen are great. They are really friendly and personable, but also give you space. The gym is nice, but a little small. The only downside that I can think of is the fact that there isn't a roof deck. Overall, I highly recommend this building!

We had no broker fee which is a rarity in the city (we contacted the apartment directly).  We converted a 3 bedroom to a 5 bedroom and have had no problems with neighbors.  Doormen know us and are very frinedly.  The gym/lounge area is never busy and has two televisions to watch sports/shows.  Definitely recommend living here.  The only downside is that the elevators have small issues sometimes (they were closed down the week we moved in).

Below are reasons to consider before moving into the Ambassador East, 330 E 46th Street. (Note: we've been residents here for ~2 years):

1. Cockroaches. We have consistently had cockroaches in our unit (as you can see in the pictures) DESPITE being incredibly clean and paying thousands of dollars for a cleaning service monthly (think Maidsailors, Myclean, etc). We have raised this issue with management multiple times but they send us a temporary exterminator who spends 5 minutes in the unit just to put down paper traps and spray. This is an issue with the building itself.

2. Loud noise and toxic fumes from constant construction. Due to a lot of construction held at the site, it's very loud in the unit during the day. So if you ever work from home or do any activities during the day, it will be incredibly disruptive for meetings or calls. The units are also being repainted and there is a toxic smell which lingers throughout the units, which is certainly a health hazard.

3. Poor communication from the management. We reached out to the management (property manager named Walter) regarding incessant construction noise and toxic fumes. They took over 2 months to get back to us and only replied because we followed up. They then raised our rent by $200 and refused to provide any compensation for the loud noise, vermin, and toxic fumes caused by construction for MONTHS. They provided ZERO notice to residents about this and when asked about this issue, they replied over email: "We don't have to ask or get permission from tenants for work we feel needs to be done."

Positives: the doormen are very nice and friendly. However, the above reasons are all things to consider before moving here.

I’ve had a great experience living at 207 East 37th Street. The building is well-maintained, and the management is responsive. The apartments are spacious and bright with modern finishes, and the amenities like the elevator, laundry room, and on-site superintendent add convenience to daily life. The location is fantastic, with easy access to public transportation, shops, and restaurants. Overall, I highly recommend 207 East 37th Street for anyone looking for a comfortable, well-located place to live.
wonderful management. super responsive and helpful throughout my entire time living in this building

Do you love the sound of cab horns and Midtown Tunnel traffic 24 hours a day?  Then this is the building for you.  37th street between 2nd and 3rd avenue is nothing but traffic, and probably shouldn't be zoned residential.  Some units in this building are nicely renovated - mine is not.  Old appliances, fuses constantly blowing, floors and countertops that never seem to come clean.  Also, there's a real lack of ventilation.  No hood for the stove means that you better be a good cook, because you'll smell your meal for a while.

This apartment is cozy, has washer and dryer in the apt stainless steel appliances and a full length private terrace. 

YOU CANT BEAT THAT!

50 North 5th is about 1 1/2 years old and a wonderful building. The staff is incredibly friendly, helpful and very detail oriented. The building and grounds are very well maintained. We also have a wonderful apartment with beautiful countertops, dishwasher and washer and dryer. The location is great, close to the subway, water, ferry and bars and restaurants. We have a beautiful roof deck with grills and lounge chairs which weve used throughout the entire summer. I can't think of a better building in Brooklyn. Our only complaint is as a new resident, we found flaws in the apartment we moved into. The paint job was not well done, a few door knobs didn't work properly, a small leak under the kitchen sink. Other than that the apartment is absolutely perfect.

BlueSky, the managing company for this building (and many other properties) is about as inept as any company could be. The property manager does not care about any of the issues in this "newly renovated" building. We moved into the building while construction was still going on, even though we were promised that construction would be done by August 15th. They were late to finish the work, and it really shows if you just look closely at everything. Furnishings and appliances are cheap, white paint spots (and scratch marks!) on the "brand new" wooden floors, poor electrical work (seriously, we only have one outlet in the "living room"). Not to mention, the wifi has been cutting on and off for months, in-unit washer/driers flat out don't work in the majority of the units, there's barely any water pressure in the sink and shower, and the best part? Management simply doesn't seem to care! I've been lied to by management saying that they were "working on fixing the issues in the building" but it took management three months to send a technician to replace one part in my drier. For the price you're paying for this place, you might as well flush that money down the drain because you are NOT getting what you pay for here. Stay far away from any BlueSky building and take your business elsewhere where management actually cares about its tenants.
Enjoyed living here.   Would love to live there again if I move back.

The two overpriced, glorified housing projects that sit on Victory Boulevard have seen better days. And, speaking of the staff at Silver Lake, the property manager, assistant property manager, and head of maintenance are incredibly rude and condescending. look elsewhwere!
