This place has rats, mice, and cockroaches.  The water is green and tests high for bromine.  There is no pool as advertised.  Terrible security

I agree with the review that tells you to check everything out. The air conditioning system I can say if you live in a studio (can not speak for other units) does not work well it is on the side you put the couch and aims straight forward it has no way to move the air so the bed area is always hot and muggy the kitchen hot and muggy and the bathroom it also does not help that they do not heat or ac the hallways just the lobby so your electric bill will be through the roof for a 350 sq foot studio my electric bill has not once been below $130 and when I spoke to conedison they told me it was common for this building of similar sized units but not for other buildings near by. Parking I was promised when I signed my lease has never been available my lease is now up in two months and the pool has never been opened. Like I said both these amenities are half the reasons I moved from Manhattan to Jamaica the train ride is more of an hour to Manhattan and the area is not safe at all. The management company has done nothing to offer compensation for these amenities that were promised that they fell short on for the entirety of the lease. Also be careful the doors lock behind you they will not tell you this and the lock out fee is $150 each time.

New building, so the look could fool you. Pool still not available and management team is keeping it closed for their own reasons. The response from management is always a negative response and they do not address issues. please save your money and time

Also, there have been instances where employees have entered tenants’ apartments unannounced. For a new building that proclaims to be luxury, the garbage was not collected from Christmas Eve (Thursday 24) to Monday 28; the refuse was disgusting and nasty; two of the 4 main elevators is always out of service; and one of main entrance door has been broken since forever. The building is pet friendly, however many of the tenants do not clean up after their dog - nasty individuals. The park is decent, but last August or September 2020 someone was shot, and the choppers were roaming the area (very loud). My advice is to look beyond the "newness" of the building (it was once a hospital). Turn on the water faucet to see if its leaking, turn on the ac/heating unit and check the pressure; open the window and see what flies in; ask if the apartments are soundproofed (they aren't); try the washing machine (is it working); check out the refuse (A&B) to see the cleanliness; listen out to noise level (music playing, tv; furniture moving; chatter); ask which apartments have pets. Ask about the pool, ask to see the pool (it was to be completed months ago) and lastly, speak to current tenants and get their opinion/feedback (I wish I had done that).

This building is a star from floor plans to appliances, all very functional and working exceptionally well. Don't think twice about renting an apartment in the Bronx, a great neighborhood, very close to public transportation, and much more; St George Crescent is the right place. I am planning to stay here for a long time.

Warm and friendly neighbors, living at St. George has been a great experience, and I can say that I am 100%
satisfied with my accommodation. The appliances and wood floors make all the difference when renting an apartment, and I can say the company that built this building put a lot of care and effort into finishing this with high quality. I would recommend renters don't miss the chance to become part of the St. George family!

The good aspects of this building is the location(close to parks and zoo), the cleanness of the building(the management company often look for ways to improve the location), 
and the fitness center located in the building(I can work out downstairs and quickly go home and relax) love it!

Excellent management team and prompt response to calls. A month ago I placed an order requested to do some repairs, and the management team quickly address this matter and made sure that I would be satisfied with the job provided. I love the aspect that they follow up with me after the job was done, showing great care and attention to my case. Well  done management team!

I was hesitant in writing a review but realized it will help future applicants. I was excited to move into a new building & close to my job but was short lived days into moving in. I had a bathroom toilet leak & kitchen faucet leak. Management did quickly address the matter. At the time of signing the lease I was happy to hear the rules & regulations of considering other tenants as well commit signing off to-the no noise / loud music after 8pm , maintaining laundry machinery, etc; thought to myself wow this will be a great building to live in. Not at all since the quality of tenants (some) which they’ve consider in renting don't match such.  A couple of months into moving in I had a ceiling leak coming from the light fixture landing in my bed, courtesy of the tenant above. A month into that I had 2 bathroom leaks again courtesy of the despicable tenant above. Have not even made a year & encounter so many issue. It’s been an unlivable environment & very much disappointing. There’s not much ventilation or windows in the hallways & either tenants don’t know how to turn on the vents in there kitchen or refuse to but the smell from their cooking penetrates these walls where your clothes & household smell too, you can only imagine when seafood is being cooked.  A studio apartment the rent is nothing cheap & living here is not great at all! If your looking for quite neighborhood/ building, this is not the place for you. I would not recommend this place.
The management is helpful they reply to emails for everything very quickly. The buildings are always clean and quiet. I love it here. A gem in the Bronx !

Its so hard to get in contact with people who are responsible to show these  apartments , i have been trying to contact, the office for weeks, no response, or the real estate agent, who takes 3,4 days to respond to a message. And and tell you the last day , that the apartment is rented, one day before showing it . Very unprofessional.!

It is excellent to rent at The Park and grow in this part of the Bronx. Also, there are plenty of grocery stores, deli, and much more around the block. Easy access to the MTA transportation and across a nice park area. The commodity that you find in this building makes all effort worth when you consider all the benefits that come when living at The Park. Great choice!

Love the building and the area! Living at the park is a great deal for those who have a family and enjoy walks in the park with their dog. On weekends I take my son to play at the park across the building, and I love this area. Also, I want to thank Mariana, who helped me get a great deal on my two-bedroom apartment. Great Job!

Best deal in town, don't miss the opportunity to living in this excellent building located close to the Riverdale park. When I first moved here, I was a bit unsure If this building would offer the experience that I want, and I can say I was surprise how responsive the management company is with this building. 
They make sure to follow-up my requests and schedule services that works with my schedule. Well Done!
I have ben living in this neighborhood for a couple months and I can say that the location of this building is great. Living in here it has made easy my morning commute to work. It is worth the shot!

I've lived here for a couple months now. The residents are friendly, building is clean, apartments are well built. I worked with Lighthouse Living Realty's agent, Joe, he was great! Very responsive! Management here is great too. Has quickly and politely answered all my qu's. Definitely Recommend. Loving it.

Living here has been a frustrating experience. The unreliable HVAC system makes the apartment uncomfortably hot, and management doesn’t seem eager to address it. Neighbor noise is a constant issue; despite complaints, management has done little to ensure a peaceful living environment. For the rent price, I expected a higher standard of comfort and responsiveness, but this place fell short. Wouldn't call it luxury although the price is definitely for luxury.

Staying at 180 North Jefferson was a delight! The luxury boutique apartments are beautifully designed and offer fantastic amenities. The location in the West Loop is perfect, just steps away from great dining and entertainment. Highly recommend for a stylish and comfortable stay!

Elevator has been broke since I moved in, making me miss the train and be late to work several times. Asked them for a replacement key and they never responded. The location/amenities are great, the admin is just not great.

Fantastic, apartment’s in great shape and move-in was seamless! 

180 N Jefferson is a great location in a safe, clean area and the front desk was heavily involved and extremely helpful throughout my move-in process!

Easy to move in and everyone is so friendly. Front desk workers are also so nice and welcoming when first moved in. Elevators being limited is kind of on the downside but that is the only thing I would change!
This is our first apartment so we were nervous about the move in process, but Danielle and Marvin have been such great help with our move in. We’re so excited to call this place our new home!
We love going to the movie theater and restaurants in 5 minutes.  Marianos is across an indoor parking lot.  Convenience!
New City Residence offers amazing quality and a full service. It is absolutely worth considering if you work in town or in the Lincoln Park neighborhood!
Wonderful building, great staff, amazing access to amenities and shops in the area! Would rent here again.
Too many issues with noisy neighbors and management inaction to enjoy anymore. Was a nice place at first but has gone drastically downhill since covid.

I have been living here for several years and think it's the best apartment building in Chicago. Very convenient with easy access to Mariano, pharmacies and other necessities, which is especially important during this pandemic time.

The building is amazing, great amenities and very clean. It is not all 20somethings partying at all hours and is geared towards working adults or families which is what I wanted. I hope it contintues to be a real community.

The views are incredible, amenities are beautiful, and the staff is super friendly and always helpful! Becca in the office has been great! Everything here feels high-end and well-maintained. Definitely recommend if you’re looking for a great place to call home!

The amenities are on point, you can’t get a better Chicago skyline view, and the staff has been great - Shout out to Becca in the office for being so helpful & patient! 808 feels like a high-end resort that still feels super laid-back. If you’re after a cool spot with all the perks, you’ve gotta check this out!

The views from my apartment are unbeatable! The co working lounge has been so amazing for switching up my work from home routine and the staff has been so incredibly nice -  Brad and Becca in the office have been so helpful, you can tell they truly care about their residents!

I just moved into this awesome apartment in a beautiful area of Chicago! The apartment is super modern and has all new appliances. I love the big windows that let in so much natural light. The amenities are top-notch, and the staff is super friendly. It’s also within walking distance of so many restaurants, parks, and bars, and it's a quick walk to the subway station! Everyone here seems really welcoming. Would highly recommend!

Don’t move here. I moved in March 2024 and feels like a bait and switch. If you’re reading the reviews the 5 stars are from folks who took the tour, and the one stars are from people who live here.

One thing I wasn’t told when I moved in is that there are third-party rentals in this building. Something called Home2Suites and also Airbnbs. The building also have apartments where each room is rented out individual which causes more inconsistency of folks.

I was also told you can’t hear your upstairs neighbor because the ceilings are cement. That’s a lie - I hear my neighbor walking all the time and I can hear the person on the other side of the wall opening their door, closing their drawers and sometimes talking.

Overall - this building is not well managed. There is only one building manager. The building has been through 2 assistant managers in the 3 months I’ve been here. Every support person is outsourced so maintenance leaves at 3pm. I’ve only seen one cleaning person and it feels that way because the common areas are half-cleaned, the outside areas are never cleaned. The TV room doesn’t have a trash can.

No one cleans on the weekend, so if there’s a mess - it just sits there until Monday.

Outside the grills are sticky. No one resets the areas and trash just stays around. People bring their pets outside and it ruins the area for people to lay out. Quiet hours are supposed to start at 11pm, but they don’t lock the outside area so people are out there all night and I can hear them all the way on the 13th floor.

The pool was delayed opening due to broken pieces and now that’s it’s open the water is murky. Pools have to be cleaned every morning and there’s no one to do it. And the hot tub in is cold with dead bugs floating in it.

The gym is visibly dirty - it’s gross to do stretching next to strands of hair. The wipes are dried out and no one replaces them.

I’m in an ADA apartment and the shower door was improperly placed so there’s a pool of water whenever I shower and if I try to clean the shower door while it’s closed, my bathroom is flooded. Been waiting on a fix since I moved in.

Packages - wild Wild West. Sometimes the delivery people will place in a locker and sometimes they won’t. There’s also a package room for larger items but your code won’t tell you it’s there and if you try to input the code, it will come up inactive. The front desk folks keep rotating so they are no help.

If I could go back and not move here at all I would.

This place is a total disaster. The low-income buildings across the street are always blasting music, and right now, it's almost midnight, and my windows are vibrating from the noise. Seriously, if you're thinking about renting here, don't do it! You'll regret it big time. Save yourself the trouble and find a quieter spot to call home.

NEMA is the epitome of an experience. Their team worked extremely hard to make the building an all encompassing mood. 
So thankful for the amazing team of professionals that worked hard to make NEMA home. From Mark in management to Mallory/Nate in resident experience to the entire door staff. Everything felt designed for my own personal enjoyment. Even through covid the staff managed some level of keeping us connected and feeling welcomed. Their covid protocol is outstanding.
It has been a crazy year for downtown residents. Crescent should feel proud of how well they worked to treat us well, it’s been hard. 
My best description there is for an apartment in NEMA of my size(around 600sqft). It was like living in a world class hotel, and who wouldn’t want to live in the Four Seasons. But eventually you want to go home. Get a unit of a bigger size and you’ll never leave. Anyone that tells you otherwise is likely insufferable. I’m sad to not have been able to negotiate something that would have worked for me.
My only real complaint is Ive heard my neighbor whistling. Carry that through to the other possible noises. Also the shower water is NOT HOT. It’s warm at best lol.
Pool has been broken for 2 months and is still not fixed Management has not responded to tenant requests

They made the garage private. So your guest can no longer park in the attached garage. So if your family and friends want to come over and stay they have to park somewhere else. But they still let Gibson restaurant use the garage for valet. But paying residence cant have guest parking its a shame. Also they don’t let delivery people such as DoorDash drop off food at your door.

If you seek a prime location in the heart of the city of Chicago surrounded by museums, 5-star hotels, luxury brands, fine dining restaurants with a walking score of 100, and a walking distance to major supermarkets like Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s, Jewel-Osco and Aldi, easy access to a garage or access to RED and Brown lines. Then “The Chicagoan” at 750 N Rush St is a good value compared to other competitors in River North.

Adriana, the building manager, is super professional and gets things done quickly, and she is an excellent representative to Planned Property Management “PPM Apartments.”

Engineers and maintenance staff are very skillful and always on time. They care for everything and keep everything in place daily, from the GYM to the Sundeck/Pool/Grill area. In addition, the Front Desk and Receiving/Mailing/Dry Clean staff are friendly and kind.

The apartment is nice and updated but it is small. You are paying for location. The walls are a bit thin in places. Planned Property Managements is the worst company I have ever worked with. It sometimes takes them a whole month to cash our rent checks. They are also very rude when you call inquiring if your check/payment has been received.

Hi everyone, my name is Craig. I have lived at the Chicagoan for over four years now. My wife is a shop-a-holic, so she only has to walk three blocks to Water Tower Place. I love to get my grocery shopping done at Whole Foods which is two blocks away. Ever since ppm took over management at my building, Mary and I have been pleased with their work ethic.

My roommate and I have lived here about 6 months. The surroundng area can be really scary bc of homeless people everywhere all around the building. The shared areas are not very clean. I like the people who work here.

Have been living here since 2018. Thank you Lisa, Babara, Sekina, and Triston (sorry if I made any typo here), and many more supporting staff. Thank you for always taking care of us and helping to resolve any issue and problem.

Lisa M. and Barbara A are wonderful Concierge employees! Both women are attentive and happy to assist residents with any and all issues. I have lived here for two years going on three and I highly recommend the building to all people searching for a place to live.

The people who work at the Conceirge desk are absolutely wonderful, especially Lisa and Trent. 

I have lived here for over for years and they were extremely accommodating. 

The apartments are new feeling and clean, though the street noise can be a bit much. 

Management is fairly flexible, when you can get a hold of them.

This is a glamorous historic property. Unfortunately, the building was sold to an insurance conglomerate. Since then, a two bedroom apartment is now $3700 per month. We have, with regret, decided to move. They have priced themselves out of the market.

The Belden Stratford has been a great place to live and I can't imagine renting anywhere else. The staff is wonderful and extremely helpful. The building is pet friendly and the staff is beyond considerate of pets, which so hard to find in Lincoln Park. Between the staff, rooftop and gym this building has been the perfect home. They also quoted me much higher for my utility bills before signing my lease. I thought I would be paying $75-$120 more a month, but have yet to have a bill that high! I could not have made a better decision to live here.
Dysfunctional elevators, horrible communication from management, and a recent forceful break-in to four units that was not communicated to other residents. Definitely do not move here!

I've been living here for some time, and I strongly advise against choosing this place as your residence. I'm sharing this anonymously because of the differential treatment residents receive from management and maintenance when expressing concerns, whether in person or online. Contacting management is nearly impossible, and the elevators consistently experience problems.

Absolutely disgraceful management and communication. We have not had both working elevators in over a year. I would never recommend living here to anyone. Cleanliness is a problem and exposed walls and electrical make this building a safety hazard. The building manager is awful and no help whatsoever.

It is December 2023 and I have lived here for four months.  This is easily the worst place I have ever lived in my adult life.  There have been multiple days where NO ONE ELEVATORS WORKED and I live on the 18th floor.  No rent adjustments.  By the way, the lease no early termination clause.  You have to stay until the lease ends.  This place is garbage.  In the entire four months I've lived here, both elevators worked maybe for 6 days total.  Aside from that, there are so many other issues.

I have been living in the building for three months now and I’m really happy with the management and staff! Taylor the property manager is super helpful and responsive - he made moving in so easy! The gym is so nice and has every machine you could need for a full workout. The in unit washer and dryer has been so great. Overall I love how new and clean the building/apartments are. The sliding glass doors for the bedroom are so unique and let in so much natural light. I plan on living here for a long time!

My husband and I love it here! We use the Fitness Center at least 4 times a week, we love the interaction exercise screen with numerous programs to choose from. Our friends love the grilling deck. The neighborhood is awesome, everything is in walking distance. We are close to work in the downtown area as well. My husband travels a lot, so I love the secured entrance doors and the concierge are great. We have an phenomenal view of Chicago!

been living here for almost 2 years place is great location to downtown and boystown. what makes this feel like home is that everyone greets each other. simon and edgar are truly amazing. any concerns. i had with my previous units they make sure it gets done and they take pride in helping there tenants. covington would be the same without them. concierge staff is nice especially barbara. she greets you with open arms . morissa our new P.M has truly showed how passionate she is . always on the run. very understanding.

The building has 3 elevators that are constantly breaking and getting people stuck in for 30+ minutes. If you want to get to work on time and not wait forever for elevators, do not move here. The concierge are nice, but the building manager does not know how to manage time properly and can only help by calling maintenance when you need.

Broken down elevators, washing machines and dryers. Elevators smell terrible. People don’t clean up after their pets. Took them less than one year to raise rent $150 despite there being no improvements to the property

The amenities in the apartments keep breaking down, I'm constantly having them fix stuff in the place, which defies the term 'luxury' they use to advertise their building.
They also raised rent by over $500 with only a 20 day notice and they threatened to evict me over a false $15 charge.

Yup, they don't care about your wellbeing in this building and will screw you over ALOT.

-1/10 strongly don't recommend.

I had the worst experience of my life by living here. Worst staff, worst services, worst management. Don’t make a mistake of moving in here even if that is for a short while. They all are mean and rude and will make your life hell. Better live on streets than living here!

I moved in an apartment here in 2012 but I still have nightmares. I was shown a fabulous apartment that appeared clean and perfect. However, upon moving in I realized my apartment was infested with roaches. Infested! The manager, Darla, kept telling me it was because of a woman living upstairs from me. However, there was never a time while I lived there that I did NOT see roaches. Because I signed a lease, she wouldn't let me leave so I had to live there for a year. I moved out one month prior to my lease expiring and on the day the movers came, no one was at the gate to let us in. It was a horrible experience. I bought a ton of insect repellent, packed all of my belongings into plastic bags and sealed them to prevent transferring the roaches to my new home. I've never seen so many roaches in my life.
Beautiful Lobby! The building appears to be well-maintained. Entrance is quite elegant. The apartments themselves were small. I thought the rent was high for the square footage.

Apartment Tour Miss Megan was fantastic help with our apartment tour! She showed us a simple 2-bedroom apartment along with the amenities and had a wonderful personality all the while. Our experience with a different agent at a different location was the complete opposite from Miss Megan’s bright and sunny attitude. We had a good time here and we are hoping that there is availability for us when the time comes for when we move in!

Beautiful building and nice rooms, nice gym, nice roof and common areas.

Unfortunately, it is the loudest building in the entire city of Chicago. Spent a year trying to sleep with trains every 15 seconds to 1 minute. Clark and Lake Station houses multiple El trains (not just 1!) so it is relentless. Bought earplugs, noise cancelling headphones, etc but it is just exhausting. They will not tell you this until you move in and experience it for yourself.
Nice building, nice staff inside, terrible management that does not care.

Avoid living here or it will be a Start of nightmare for you. You will regret if you go with this place. You won’t realize until you move in. A tour doesn’t show you everything. It’s like you are paying for living in a construction site. This place is like a joke.

I’ve lived here for 2 years now & have loved it. Right in the loop so you’re near everything & you can’t beat the price for the location. I’ve never had a problem with management, maintenance was great, & yes, Will is incredible. Very sad that I have to move but would recommend this place to anyone!

The leasing office will tell you that only certain floors allow pets.  However, if you are dishonest you can get away with a pet and not have to pay.

I’m on a floor that doesn’t allow pets.  My loud neighbor has a barking dog.  “And how can this be?” you ask.  Well,  after I asked why he’s allowed a barking dog, I found out (after contacting the office many times) that he has an “emotional support” dog.  No proof needs to be provided.

So, bring your pets to any floor, lie to management because they wont check and you won’t pay the pet fees.  If you get caught, just claim the dog was a gift from a family member and is an emotional support animal.  My loud neighbor gets away with it.

The office has no interest is supporting the honest tenants.

Have been a resident for six years and enjoy everything about the place.  Excellent downtown location, fantastic amenities, connected to the led way system and well managed.  Add a local public/private park, a high-end Mariano's supermarket and restaurants and it has to be amongst the best locations in Chicago.  High cost per square footage but includes basic cable, electricity, water and gas and all the pluses.  Can't go wrong.  Can look for availability through rental management company and local condo owners.
This is a very nice building, location is well suited for downtown work. Good value for money

I lived at Prairie Shores for quite some time and, unfortunately, my experience ended on a very disappointing note. After moving out, I received a charge for door repair, which I believe was mistakenly applied. I reached out to request detailed documentation supporting this charge. While Prairie Shores initially responded and assured me they would follow up, I never received the requested information despite sending multiple follow-up emails. Rather than addressing my concerns or providing clarification, the charge was forwarded to a collections agency.

The collection agency, IQ Data International, contacted me with what they called a "courtesy call" before proceeding with collections. During this call, I explained the situation and the reason for the delayed payment. However, their representative informed me that my only option was to "pay in protest." To make matters worse, I was pressured to make the payment immediately during that call, without being afforded even a single day to review the matter or seek further clarification.

I am incredibly disappointed with Prairie Shores’ lack of transparency, communication, and accountability in handling this issue. Additionally, the high-pressure tactics employed by the collection agency felt unfair and unprofessional. This experience has been both frustrating and distressing, and I strongly urge Prairie Shores to improve their processes for addressing tenant concerns and disputes.

By far the worst place I have ever lived in 40 years! Cockroaches, low water pressure, laundry is hit or miss if the machines work, security it practically worthless, and the leasing staff is rude, incompetent, and lazy. 9 months in and I still don't have all the services that I'm required to pay for. DO NOT MOVE HERE!

You literally have to beg them to pay attention to you. I don’t understand what the leasing agent’s job here is. Don’t waste your time here. 

I had an appointment which I was late to, due to being new to the city. An agent still attended me and sent me a virtual tour, and also told me to email her back so she could put me into her tour schedule the next day. I did so. She didn’t answer until the next day, then proceeded to simply ask me the same question she had already previously asked me. Finally, she asked what day would work for a tour. I suggested the next day again. She emails back saying it’s full, and if the next day would work. I said yes! Whatever times works for you, I’m in…
No answer. Next day comes, I follow up. No answer. 
Next day comes. Email her and the leasing office. No answer. Called the leasing office 3 different days, over 5 different times, all at different times. No answer. I mean… just exactly what do you do at work?
They turned off the heat for a few days in one of the most coldest days of this past winter. Poor management service.

I have lived here since early 2023, and have had relatives here in the past. I currently live in one of their "renovated" units.

-Heating issues are terrible here. WGN came out on 1/16/24 due to the excessive complaints of no heat, my own unit is barely 50 degrees currently. Golub/Prairie Shores wasted a ton of money on the "Hub" building instead of replacing these windows that are from the 1950s.

-I constantly see ants and tiny bugs in my apartment. My building had a whole building pest control happen 2 months after moving in as roaches kept getting seen everywhere. I still see them maybe once or twice a month.

-Ground floor units suffer from plumbing issues it seems. My kitchen sink would constantly back up from the sewer. The explanation given was that it just happens to the ground floor units due to all the units above it, which is just not an acceptable answer.

-Bathroom faucet constantly leaks out rusty water when it's first turned on.

-Freezer would constantly have issues going into a defrost cycle and ruining my food. It was swapped with a new unit, and that new one developed the same defrost issue within 2 months.

-Parking is atrocious, and Contract Tow should be ashamed for raising the annual $125 parking fee to $25 flat fee every month (now it's 300 total). You get no guest passes. Winter parking is terrible for guests as King Dr has a winter overnight parking ban. 

-People here are inconsiderate in general. Laundry machines are communal in the basement (10 washers, 10 dryers) as most units do not have their own laundry units. People will take up more than 3 washers/dryers at a time, and then leave their clothes in there for hours on end. If you don't do your laundry in the early morning or late at night, get ready to have to move peoples laundry out and deal with them crying about it.

-Lease renewal is a joke. They jacked my rates up over $150 for a studio. I am moving out shortly, and checked that they listed my studio for the original rent I was paying instead of the lease increase. That is just ridiculous.

Sent in my application never got a call, text email from anyone at the leasing office. I called multiple times and never got an answer. Sent an email on Saturday which according to their website, and on the application form, both leasing and management office are open:


OFFICE HOURS
Monday-Friday10AM-6PM
Saturday10AM-5PM
Sunday12PM-5PM
 
Please note, above are the Leasing Office hours. The Management Office will be opened Monday through Saturday.



Spoke with somenamed Demisha who said no one was in the office Thursday, Friday, Sat or Sunday. So essentially 3 out of the 4 days that they have posted as open. 

Again, I was the one who had to constantly call without a response. 

And after all that ordeal, she tells me that my admin fee will be refunded in the form of a check in 30 days. Ridiculous, how can I be sure that I am going to get a response or even get my $425 if they are very difficult to get a hold of. I also find it extremely frustrating that I was the one that had to chase them down for a response. 

Please be careful when filing out application to live here as they lack basic business etiquette such as communication and basic customer service skills. 

If this was the awful experience applying I cant even begin to imagine how awful it must be to address any issues living there.

If you are looking at places to live in Chicago, you should seriously consider Parkview Apartments. The staff are what makes this place special--Lauren, Howard, and the Maintenance crew (just a few that I have met so far)--go above and beyond for the tenants here, and truly care for them and their experience. In my short time of being here (a little under a month), the building has gone through improvements-whether it is adding fire pits to the rooftop area, or renovating the gym in the basement-it is apparent that the management of this place cares about the facilities and pursues improvement. However, I believe that the greatest example of the amount of care that the management has for the property and its tenants happened this past Air and Water show, where the property hosts a gathering on the rooftop for the tenants to view the planes fly overhead. While it was a well organized event, the thing that took me aback was to see the entire management group--property manager, leasing agents, doormen, and maintenance staff--come together with their families and interact with the tenants. At that moment, I knew that there
was something special about this place--where you are not treated like a customer or a tenant-- but you are treated as a friend.

I moved here 3 months ago and absolutely love it! Lauren and all the other front desk people are super friendly and have no problems answering any questions I’ve had so far. My apartment itself is well remodeled and the building is in a perfect location. If you’re considering moving to Chicago I would highly recommend considering this place!
The management team is AWESOME! So helpful, and fun to talk to. :)

This is a great building. The staff is extremely helpful and friendly. It's close to tons of public transportation options and restaurants and is right across the street from the park. Couldn't ask for a better location.

I would never rent from Mode Logan Square the way the building is managed and operated. It's detoriating, gets cleaned once a week, trash outside the apartment. There used to even be scents when you walked in. Now there's just empty glass bottles with sticks in it that say "Westin Hotel" 

The oddest thing to me is that there were new lights put in the gym and mail room. There's so many issues that seem to need to be addressed.

Many prior reviews were made during Christina's time as building manager and Nick's time as a building engineer--- they have both since left and the building has completely gone downhill. New management is abysmal in comparison.

My apartment faces east with an abdundance of daytime sun for my plants to feed on. I'll start by stating the location is great! I love how my windows look over a lot of trees and I can see pretty far out and watch amazing sunsets. Strongly Do NOT recommend this place as a result.  This is unreasonable under any circumstance.

These apartments are overpriced, poorly run, and management doesn’t care about the tenants. Management doesn't allow you to store your bike in your apartment and you have to store it in their "secure" room. Do not move here. It outrageous for the price they are asking.

I am utterly disgusted with the state of affairs at Astoria Tower Apartments. Our experience has been nothing short of a nightmare from day one.

Initially charmed by their smiles, we soon realized their friendliness was a facade. Within the first week, we faced numerous issues, each requiring multiple repair requests. Though they addressed these problems efficiently, the frustration of moving into such a problematic apartment cannot be understated.

The ongoing saga with the elevators is beyond frustrating. It seems like there's a maintenance sign hanging up every week, and the fact that these elevators are shared with the public garage only adds onto the issue. The constant breakdowns have created a logistical nightmare, resulting in unbearable traffic flow when even just one elevator is out of service.

To make matters worse, the security of the building has been compromised for months due to the broken key fob entrance. This negligence poses a significant risk to residents, as anyone can enter the building freely and access our floors. The liability this presents is absolutely unacceptable and should have been addressed with the utmost urgency.

On top of these ongoing issues, the chronic malfunctioning of the AC during the summer months is intolerable. And despite the building's supposed non-smoking policy, the persistent odor of marijuana lingers into our apartment and causes an unhealthy living environment, especially with someone who has asthma. Despite numerous complaints, management has turned a blind eye, offering nothing but empty promises and ineffectual emails.
Management from Astoria Tower(Francy) and even upper management (Josh) from 3L Living has yet to respond.

It's abundantly clear that management's sole priority is rent collection, with no regard for the well-being or satisfaction of their tenants. Living here has been nothing short of a nightmare. Astoria Tower Apartments is a prime example of a management team that is utterly negligent and incompetent. Avoid at all costs.

extremely satisfied. 1. The location is fantastic. 2. Views from nearly every unit are gorgeous and they allow Dogs at the building ! 3. Safe, conveniently located and the staff is amazing. The building itself is beautiful. I couldn’t speak highly enough of this place. It’s wonderful. Any issue with the apt and they fix it the same day. Highly recommend.

I've been living at the streeter with my boyfriend and I love it here. The pool on the 13th floor is my favorite part about spending my summer here. Although we are moving in November, it's been a fun year at the streeter.

Location - About a block away from the Green Line CTA, which provides easy access to downtown. Walkable distance to Chinatown & Red Line CTA. Bus Line 3 & 4 run along Michigan.

The Shelby is located conveniently in South Loop area where it it not too crowded, yet the excitement of the City Life is only a 5 minute ride or 15 minute walk away.  The building is very clean and maintenance is very good.

Absolutely love this place. The community is amazing, it’s clean, and pet friendly. The neighbors are extremely nice, and the property management team is amazing and always there to help immediately. Absolutely would recommend! If you’re looking for a place, definitely choose The Shelby!

I moved here a few months back and I love it here! The location is ideal. The apartments are a great size for the price. The gym is my favorite, they have a great variety of equipment to choose from. And the staff are all great! Always so friendly.

I'm blessed to live in a building w/ my Mom- available to help @ moments notice. Our home is centrally located- close to downtown, public transportation (bus/ train), airport, lakefront, Museums & the President.

The most luxurious apartment ever we are on the 32ND floor we have beautiful view of the lakefront our bedrooms are a nice size we have a modern kitchen we have a nice modern shower made like a spa,shower a nice healthy living room and a separate dining area ...I love my apartment so much I miss it so when I am gone to work.

Management is constantly changing, and they never keep track of anything, police show up about 2-3 times a month, no one picks up their dog poop in the dog area, valet sucks, no parking otherwise in the neighborhood, packages get stolen, expensive and constantly increasing rent prices, just a horrible experience

It might look amazing at first glance, but construction and loud noise was happening during our whole lease 2022-2023. That’s not temporary. Construction is temporary. Nobody likes it but it is necessary in order to keep the place updated. I’d rather live in a well maintained dwelling than a run down building.

Only reason I gave a 1 start is because it's a pretty good location; not great, but pretty good - close to Jewel, walking distance to good restaurants/ bars in Fulton Market and West Loop.

The amenities are pretty poor. Only bright spot is the pool that you can use for around two months of the year.

Literally the day we were moving in, we were met with issues. Started with management not having a freight elevator reserved for us.

We’ve dealt with our heat not working for all of January and most of February. Maintenance came and “fixed” it 2-3 times before having to replace the whole unit in March. It’s June 2021 and the AC Unit is leaking again. 

I think the folks at Echelon has largely misunderstood what “luxury” means. Having basic heat and AC is not a luxury. The best part about the apartment is the location. My advice to anyone considering moving here - don’t. It’s not worth the waiver admin fees or first month off rent.

This is my first time living in a "professionally" managed building. From my experience here, I would never pay for something like this again.

My fiance and I have had issues since day 1. To name a few:
-The Resident lounge is actually an employee lounge throughout the day as that is the only space the employees have to go to.
-The grills have been broken since day 1. You have to bring down your own lighter, pick up the metal grates with your hands, and then light it to actually get it to work.
-Once snow started in Chicago, the management team would not have the snow removed from common spaces making the grills, etc. inaccessible.
-The key FOBs don't actually give you access to anything. I don't even know why they give them to all the residents when they don't work to get you into any of the common spaces.
-They will randomly do renovations on a floor without providing any of the surrounding apartments a notice. This is very frustrating especially during a GLOBAL PANDEMIC when everyone is working from home.

When you speak to the management team about these issues, they make you feel like you are the only one with problems and that everything is great about the building. That is not true as I have spoken to several residents who are frustrated with all the same issues.

This experience has made me think twice about paying to live in a managed high rise building.

Living here has been a mixed experience. On the pros:
The apartment is beautiful and the layout is well thought out. The location couldn't be better and the service staff is quick and kind.

Cons: There are CONSTANTLY issues with the management team:

1. Our building fabs don't work for anything. The business center, resident lounge, backyard etc. You have to track down the front desk who is absolutely swamped with amazon packages and visitors to try to get you in anywhere.
2. The resident lounge is also the employee lounge. This is literally what the management team told me AFTER we moved in. The employees eat and watch TV in the lounge without headphones in every day during their working breaks. It's not a resident lounge, be warned.
3. They do construction on apartments and don't notify us in advance. The power drills, hammering and music is super annoying when everyone is trying to work from home.
4. The management team is only available during working hours. So if you have an issue, you need to keep running down until you find someone. And when you do have an issue, they make you feel like you're the only person who has ever said a single negative thing about the building or your experience living here.
5. Snow removal. The grills and common space areas are not shoveled or maintained. In fact, the grills are all broken. You need to bring your own lighters and equipment to get them started.
6. When you have packages that arrive, it can be several hours before you're able to pick them up from the front desk. They have a sign that says come pick them up later and sometimes that sign is up all morning and afternoon.

Had many service calls with both throughout our time here. We paid for an upgraded internet package and still had issues/outages multiple times a week. It is in a good location for public transportation, close to both the green line and blue line and also very close to the highway. Parking is $200  a month but they gave us 6 months free when we moved in. Pool is billed as rooftop, but it is really on top of the parking garage, which is the 4th floor, which is the main entrance level (1-3 is the parking garage). Walkable to downtown/the loop and also river north and great restaurants off Randolph street.
Best complex in the city!!!! Staff is great!!!  Jewel across the street

Amazing staff and perfect if you want to stay in Hyde park around everything but still want to commute to school/work. I love the people, the neighborhood, the safety, and how the building has its own community!

nope not worth is. felt unsafe and cluttered, security concerns, environmental concerns, sanitation and just old filth.
