Certainly shop around for the best option for you, but keep this one on the short list.

We just re-signed for our 3rd year! 

Awesome location in the heart of the Gold Coast within walking distance of the CTA Red Line, grocery stores, restaurants, bars, shopping— you name it! I moved here from Florida and didn’t know much about Chicago neighborhoods, but I LOVE this area!

Although the building itself is a bit older, it is very well kept and always super clean. Renovations were recently done on the elevators and there have been virtually no problems since. Between the key fob operated front doors and doorman on duty every evening, the building always feels safe. Awesome rooftop area with lounge chairs, grills, and a beautiful view of the city and lake! Really nice fitness room in the basement with a great variety of equipment (even a new Peloton!). While I do wish there was in-unit laundry, there is a large laundry room in the basement as well. I love our 2 bedroom/2 bathroom unit; the perfect size, no maintenance problems, always nice and warm in the winter (again, Florida, so that’s a big deal!), and an amazing view of the city/John Hancock building outside our window.

 Everyone from the leasing office to the doorman to the maintenance staff to the cleaning team are super nice and always greet you with a smile. We definitely feel at home here :)

There were no unpleasant surprises when I moved in.  If you live on a lower floor you can hear the bars next door, but that is to be expected when you live on a lower floor next to a bar.  The heating system is older and knocks and there is no AC, but again I knew this before I moved in and those are the biggest issues.  
The location is awesome.  You can easily walk along Michigan Ave, the beach front, the river walk and so many other places are in easy walking distance.  It's also right next to a Jewel and a CVS, so it is easy to get groceries and other necessities.  It's also close to the Clark and Division red line stop which makes commuting easy.  
The maintenance have quickly fixed all the issues that came up in my apartment and all the office staff and doorman are nice people.  
Overall if you are looking for a place in a great location with a nice staff, it's the place to be.  Just know that there are nicer apartments in this area of the city, but they all cost a lot more.
Very helpful and friendly staff, nice units and common areas, prime location and a great value. No complaints after living here for a year.

As a first time apartment renter, I couldn’t have asked for a better place. The apartment itself (2 bed 1 bath) is spacious yet cozy, has a decent amount of storage space, and has character with an archway into the living area and an alcove in the wall to decorate. The staff are all SO friendly, very responsive, and helpful. The maintenance crew also has a great response rate and has always fixed any issues. The gym is a great amenity and the laundromat area is very clean. The location can not be beat!! Overall it’s been a great place to live.

I have lived in this building for the past 3 years and I have to say that this is one of my most favorite apartments that I have ever rented in Chicago. Located near the corner of the arterial roads of Division and State st, this building is in the perfect location of the city. Whether you are looking for nightlife, restaurants, bars, groceries, lakefront, or park, everything (from Streeterville to the Gold Coast to Lincoln Park) are within a 10min walking radius. 

The units themselves are very fantastic as well. My unit was a clean and classic one with a bay window and radiator and it was everything I could ask for and more. Maintenance was quick (1 day or less), the management office was very helpful and quick with responses, and the doormen were very friendly as well.

Highly recommended!

My overall sentiments over the last 4 years here can be summed up as:
2018 - "I love living here!"
2019 - "Still great, I don't mind the bump in rent"
2020 - "Some familiar faces disappeared, and yikes with the rent, but still worth"
2021 - "Had some uncomfortable incidents, but I'll give it one more shot"
2022 - "I absolutely regret renewing my lease, get me out of here"

Starting 2021, I suddenly started having more experiences with rude and inconsiderate neighbors that made living very uncomfortable (loud noise and music late night/early morning, aggressive domestic arguing, leaving trash outside).

Please note, I never had a single bad neighbor experience from 2018 - 2020.

In the worst instance, I had the police mistakenly come to my door due to a suspected domestic violence (the noise was actually from my neighbor).

I feel very bad for the families here.  I've seen a few of them on my floor only stay a few months, thinking that this is family-friendly place (it is not).

I am willing to update this review, but I believe this is a fair summary of my overall feelings right now
Moved in a month ago, so far so good! Love the vibes

With the high rent prices that Luxe charges, you can find better apartment options elsewhere in West Loop. Building management has been consistently poor, and maintenance of the property has declined over the course of the year. I have serious concerns about security because key fob devices have been non-functional periodically, sometimes for several weeks at a time.

Two months into living at Luxe, and after much reflection on how I feel, I must say that I am disappointed in Luxe's services. Let me provide some examples. I was assigned a parking space that was already assigned to someone else, and the error was not noticed for weeks. If you receive a next-day package on Friday afternoon, you may not be able to retrieve it from the mail room until it is processed by office staff on Monday (or even Tuesday if staff are busy); if you really need that package, plan ahead. On-call maintenance over the weekend may ignore a work order, even when it is a pressing situation. The dog run is large BUT needs maintenance; the turf is sinking, seams are showing, and nails are increasingly visible (one dog has already been injured). There are, inarguably, problems at Luxe, backed up by countless stories I have heard from tenants. Services just don't seem to align with the high amount of rent charged for apartments, especially considering that the building does not have that many amenities compared to other buildings in the area. Before you choose to live here, do your research on other properties in West Loop, and be certain to avoid any Greystar-owned properties. Greystar sends out surveys to tenants, yet issues that I hear from other tenants and experience myself are seldom, if ever, addressed. And once you move in, communication with management and staff will become extremely difficult. They will court you to sign a lease, and then the relationship changes. You will hear the excuse that they are busy. This means you may have to email, call, and attempt to drop by the office (if it is open) multiple times to get a response.

I've only lived here for 3 weeks. I love the building, it is well maintained, seems like the maintenance staff is great and works hard. The location is awesome and the dog run is a big plus. The downside would be that getting packages is difficult on the weekends when no one is here, and the building does not help residents if they are locked out of their units. I've lived in several high rises and never once has this not been provided, even though there is usually a fee. This put a bad taste in my mouth, but I am optimistic that management will resolve it.
Although a great location, the building is not kept clean and suspicious activities have been noted. Recommend you look elsewhere.

The Luxe on Madison is well maintained, has a very professional staff. The staff are also very kind and helpful in all matters. My neighbors seem very kind and considerate. I could not be happier living here. Also, location, location, location!
Great location. Wonderful building. Happy to call this home!
Amazing quality for an incredible rate! Love the staff and location!
Although I love my apartment, I am very disappointed in the lack of responsiveness to service requests particularly pertaining to the dog area.
We love our new apartment and the space. Functional floor plan with tons of natural lighting.
Great location and friendly management office staff. It would be better if the management office staff can respond to emails faster.

Luxe on Madison is in an ideal location in the West Loop. Minutes away from Target, exercise studios, shops and restaurants. I've had a few maintenance issues since moving in, but the management team and maintenance staff have been on top of everything, working to quickly fix the issues. Would recommend living here!

Located in hot West Loop, these reasonably priced apartments are a steal. Huge windows with skyline views, great amenities, and excellent service from management. Pet friendly too! Only con is expensive  parking.
Maintenance Team A    It's hard to get better or more attentive than the maintenance team at two West delaware! They never disappoint and are always so friendly! Kudos to the entire team.
Great tour The tour was informative and pleasant . Nice building and amenities
Everyone was professional and timely. The big difference compared to the last five times we have placed a request to fix our refrigerator is this time it seems to be fixed.
Nice building - move-in was a little messy as we did not receive a fob right away and the apartment had some minor issues. Other than that, love it so far!

We're a recent move in and initial impressions include 1) unit continues to overall meet expectations 2) repairs are needed and uncertain how simple, quick 3) most staff are overly communicative and seems to be trying hard.

Building has gone significantly downhill. 2 W Delaware has been fo sale since the fall 2023.  The owners have decided to put the least amount of maintenance investment possible so things are literally falling apart. We have not have a functioning garage door or lobby entry door for 7 months. The other night ALL the elevators were down. I have heard from former maintenance engineers that we don’t adequately keep up with elevator maintenance.  Scary. Also, they used to clean our windows  2x a year. Hasn’t happened in a year and I bet they skip spring cleaning.  Mean while, they keep increasing the rents for people that live here and offering deals that are 20% lower to new renters.  I can just hope new owners are better.
i love my building, the area, the neighborhood, the pool and the gym, even coffee machine on the 15th floor, concierges, leasing office crew  and maintenance team, everything is perfect.
A lovely place to call home! The staff is supportive and kind. The amenities are cozy and spacious for fun gatherings. And the pool i area is nice and relaxing.
The apartment is beautiful, including the lobby, clubhouse area, pool, and rooftop deck. Also, the units themselves are so nice! They are very spacious and have beautiful finishings.

Recommend this building to anyone that is looking. I've had an incredible time living here. It has everything you could possibly need from an apartment building. The unparalleled views and great staff are the icing on the cake.

I love living in North Water. It’s the perfect distance from my work (about 20 minute walk) not to mention it has everything you need in a 2 block radius. Sushi restaurant or Robert’s pizza, liquor store, Target, Walgreens and everything you need within walking distance. Front desk provides extra security. Upscale apartment complex. 10/10
Northwater is a great place to live.  I have lived here for over 6 years and the staff are wonderful.  The views are amazing and for the most part, it is quiet.
Best Apartment Ever My Dream Place Never Want 2 Move Very Satisfied  And Very Happy At Xavier
I enjoy living at Xavier. I like that the building is fully equipped with all the amenities needed to live in the city.

I have been living at the Xavier for about 2 weeks and it has been great- awesome staff who is super great with communication and great community spaces that are well maintained. My apartment is great and functional with a great layout.

A beautiful well maintained and managed property with good community areas. The studios are spacious with modern appliances. East facing apartments have amazing views, it is dog friendly and the location is perfect.

Xavier is a wonderful community to be apart of, I couldn't recommend it more. I have loved living here over the past two years, it has become my home away from home. The staff from leasing to front office and maintenance go above and beyond to making this place a safe and inviting environment for residents.
I love Xavier and I have been living here for 5 years. I love our amenities especially the rooftop.

My daughter recently filled an application to rent an apartment at Marquee Block 37.  She was asked for a guarantor. I completed the guarantor application, including income info etc. However, then their system asked me to link my bank account electronically for "income verification." I proposed that since such electronic linking is a security concern, can I provide copies of paystubs to confirm income.  This was not accepted by the management office and they proceeded to cancel the application. On top of that they refused to refund the application fee. BE VERY CAREFUL WITH SUCH BUSINESS PRACTICE WHERE A BUSINESS ASKS YOU TO LINK YOUR BANK ACCOUNT TO THEIR SYSTEM. In this day and age of cyber security breaches, this is an awful business practice. I encourage Marquee Block 37 management to wake up and reconsider this business practice.  In the meantime, we will not touch their apartment consideration with a ten foot pole.

In the first few weeks we moved into Marquee block 37, we had several times experiencing a strong smell of Marijuana coming out of our bathroom.  We've discussed multiple times with the property manager Wendy, with each time Wendy telling us we need to report instantly when this smell happens so they can catch the smoking in the action, thus they can issue a proper stop-smoking or evict notice. However, though we did as we were told, every time the maintenance crew came confirming that there were such smells, they did not take any actions to knock on the around apartment doors to future investigate as Wendy told us. We realize the property management does not have the capacity to resolve this issue, thus propose we move out of the building without any penalty. However, though Wendy agrees our proposal was valid and reasonable, she still denies our proposal. I have no other options but to post this experience here so everyone knows better about what is happening with Marquee Block 37 management. DO NOT COME TO THIS PLACE! (unless you are a marijuana lover of course)

The building's amenities are standard for the area and price point, but Marquee really struggles with it's management. Unclear communication, inflexibility and money grabbing are very prevalent and make dealing with the management a nightmare.

Moved in after being sold on the convenience.

I’ve lived in high rises for quite some time and this one by far is the poorest quality.

1. Excessive amount of people who are AirBnB’g. Had I known this I would have never moved in. They don’t respect the building as much as some of the residents.

2. It’s severely understaffed given the size of the building. 

3. Absolutely no community activities with the exception of the AT&T soliciting their horrible cable and internet. Also, there were only 50 bagels for the breakfast the building found itself hosting with well over 700 residents.

4. Office staff barely know the residents (knowing my dog doesn’t count) and are too busy trying to sucker some poor couple into living in this pseudo luxury high rise.

5. In the summer time the dog run radiates a putrid smell all the way to the pool. Also, fellow residents are bums when it comes to cleaning up after their dog.

What’s saving this building is it’s location. If you are new to the city and looking for a place to stay until you transition it works but after that you’ll find some nicer buildings.

My wife and I have been here for over 2 years (moved in March 11, 2017) and it was great for the first year or so.  Management was awesome and so was the staff.  Since within the last year, things have gone down hill.  Management changed basically for the worst.  They state this as a non-smoking community where you will be in trouble if caught and can't be within 10-20 ft of the main door.  We now have college kids (after they made an agreement with certain schools) that will smoke pot in the units and we have to keep informing the front desk to check it.  People literally smoke right around the corner of the front door and my wife or I inform the front desk staff that have to inform them to go out to a certain area to smoke.

I've spoke to the office staff about offering my ability to create signs and print them at work since I work at a printing supply reseller.  No update from them what so ever.  I would have done this at no charge and so we can have "signs" around the front and per floor regarding these restrictions, but get no word back from management.  With having a 7 month old and apparently they DON'T care about those that smoke, it makes my wife and I want to get out of this building quicker than our lease is over.  Keep sending emails out and most of the residents don't give a crap or read it.  What's the point of rules that benefit the community if they don't implement them properly.

The pool area has rules of no glass and residents must wear a certain color band while guest where another color and MINIMUM # of people per unit is so many that they don't even care.  There can be a party at the pool with glasses of booze and management emails residents about it not being acceptable.

Lastly, a unit next to ours (on the other side of the stairwell) had apparently college students in it with their music blasting and we could hear it pretty well.  With our baby around 2 months old at that time and us trying to get sleep, we had to inform them it was too loud for being 11pm at night on a weeknight.

I rarely write revies like this, but when being at a place for this long and things gradually change for the worst, others should be aware if they are like my wife and I where you do your best to obey rules and that basically goes out the window to create a crap environment.  A few of our friend/neighbors feel the same way about this place now and we all can't wait to move out.

Hope this helps with your decision

As the review says you can hear everything. Bathrooms are especially bad. 
Staffs are unresponsive. No smile. 
Amenities are broken for a long time and not fixed. 
Rooftop jacuzzi has been broken forever. 
Steam room has been out of order forever.

Management company needs serious improvement - mishandling of several safety related concerns and their response was garbage. Had garden window kicked in during week of polar vortex and was a fight to get bars on the windows; they would not reimburse for astronomical heat bill due to us cranking the heat as a result of having a broken window...No reimbursement for when we had to live somewhere else because we couldn't keep the apt warm enough. Other issue -man on our back porch that cut a hole through the window screen of bedroom window - no action taken by CLK Managment. They have us the runaround and lied to our neighbors about "having this under control." Took months to get even a light installed (we ended up buying one ourselves). Honestly avoid at all costs - beware.  Disappointed with the experience and hope they start caring for their tenants' safety and wellbeing. Apt itself is decent quality, maintenance is relatively responsive.

The rent is a little high; but in-unit laundry, dish washer, exposed brick, great location.  sounds worth it. In Chicago it's kind of hard to find for a reasonable price, and we got 1 month free.  A few months into living here, my new neighbor's dog starts barking all night.  We have a dog too, so I was reasonable the first couple of nights and sleep in the living room, because the dog is probably just adjusting to the new home.  NOPE. Dog barked all night and management did nothing after I complained. A couple months into the barking, we get a notice that they are raising rent by 10% and my roommate and I had a good hardy chuckle and moved. I now get a full nights sleep :)

It would take me forever to list out all the negative things that have happened to us at this place, so I will just say this. Do your research, all the reviews have the same themes.... they don't address resident concerns, they provide different information to different residents, I have felt seriously unsafe a number of times living here, they just installed cameras a few months ago after residents begged them, after not one but two cars had been set fire in the last year. This place is a magnet for bad things happening, and it doesn't help that management has zero competence in addressing those bad things.

They held a contest to have people write positive reviews on this site...7 months ago....This company is the worst.  Everything you read below is true.  They are the cheapest.  All you have to do is look at the landscaping and the blinds in the windows.  They don't take care of the property.  Check out all the packages sitting in the mud at the gate.  I have had multiple packages stolen because the company refuses to accept packages.  This place is terrible.  DO NOT RENT HERE!!!

I have never had so many issues with a management company! The number of maintenance issues I experienced, along with the horrible treatment by management staff were the main reasons I ended my lease early. I thought once I left, the stress of dealing with CLK would be over. I was wrong! Less than a week after leaving, I received a notification from the online company that CLK uses to allow residents to pay their rent online. This company informed me that CLK never deleted my account, but instead added my sublet to my account, which gave them access to pay rent using my bank account and credit card that were on file. I had to reach out to CLK multiple times for them to give this company permission to cancel my account. CLK NEVER APOLOGIZED for giving another individual access to my banking information without my knowledge or consent. Instead, they blamed the outside company and denied refunding me the ridiculous $400 fee I had to pay to be dropped from the lease. Not refunding the fee is one thing, but to not offer an apology is terrible customer service. At the end of the day, CLK is responsible for the vendors they hire, yet they show no accountability for errors made that have serious consequences for their residents. I would hate to see this happen to someone else, so if you still live at CLK, do yourself a favor and stop using their online system.

We've lived at The Maynard at Elaine Place for over a year, and have not had one good experience with the management company (and we've been here for the management change, so the responses saying that will make it better have not).  They continuously ignore maintenance requests and provide shoddy repairs when they have to because the maintenance workers don't know what they're doing.  We've stopped even reporting problems to them because we can't deal with the frustration of fighting to get them out here.  The building is old, so it's freezing in certain areas of the apartment and burning hot in others during the winter.  The courtyard gets "beautified" once a year and the rest of the year it's either swamped with rain or filled with dog poop.  The management staff is unresponsive to logic, and any reasonable suggestions at improving the facility are ignored for no other reason than laziness.  I have nothing good to say about CLK, the location is lovely but if asked I would say it was not worth dealing with these incompetent people.  Would not recommend to anyone that values their comfort and sanity.

This property has had terrible issues with ventilation and heating.  The property management does the bare minimum that they are required to do, and if you want a good living space I would avoid this complex at all costs.

Please save your money. I could go into so much detail but it’s really that bad. Suspicious way to getting tenants to pay their rent (money orders/cashiers checks) that they claim they don’t receive when tenant clearly dropped to their desk and or gave to the property office. Elevator smells like dog pee. Amenities barely work. They have a group chat for concerns and what not and they consistently delete complaints and try to cover things up. Overall, just super suspicious.. corrupt company. Also, if you look it up they are the only luxury building but the management owns multiple other buildings that are very low income or section 8 which explains how suspicious and inefficient they are with handling problems. Spend your money elsewhere & listen to these reviews because I wish I would’ve it would’ve saved me so much money and time and legal fees.
Constantly smells like weed everywhere past the leasing office. You and all your stuff will smell like weed even if you don't smoke. Constantly loud.

The services are there but usually never available. Maintenance requests take weeks to get resolved. The rules they have in the building are laughable. The door person changes every 2 weeks which speaks so much about the building. You feel like you’re walking into someone’s place everytime you walk in the door.  I do not recommend this place. There are much better managed buildings for the same price.

Everything about the Logan had been wonderful until new management took over just over a month ago. I would stand clear of moving here until they get their bearings together. So many folks in the community have had the same issues with lack of communication, amenities being neglected with maintenance, no real guidance of what changes are happening, and even the new property sending a petty email regarding the last management who was nothing but wonderful to us. Some people have even had their rent checks lost which is a HUGE security issue. The excuse seems to always be "we are new, so we don't know" I understand there are growing pains with transition, but these are issues where the entire community suffers.  I would save yourself the headache of living here and look elsewhere. It's truly sad to see such a lovely place to live take a negative turn.

I love living at Logan Apartments, everyone from the concierge, to the maintenance team and cleaning staff are so kind and helpful. If I ever have a concern or request, it is addressed promptly and thoroughly. I feel lucky to live here!
Team is very friendly and building is clean and secure

Love it here! It's not just a place to stay, it's a place to call home. Everything you need and most of what you want is here and in the surrounding neighborhood. Professional, responsive management, great amenities and a sun-filled apartment AND a Target store beneath the building. It's GREAT!
Living at Logan feels like living in a hotel! The amenities are unmatched and the common areas are constantly being cleaned. The building is very secure and the staff is very friendly and helpful.
Logan is clean and homey, has wonderful amenities, and is pleasantly located near fun places to eat and hang out!

Prior to moving to Upshore Chapter, I was reluctant, because there seemed to be so much turnover and confusion with the Property Management team per online reviews. It was very difficult to even contact the leasing office to try schedule a tour. Even now, communication is difficult, with there being limited office hours and nobody available Saturdays, Sundays, and Mondays. It is my hope that additional office staff or a night security guard could be hired in the future. On a positive note, Hector has been exceptional since day one, going beyond his maintenance duties by assisting with my move-in on his day off and consistently supporting residents with various issues. 

Despite the difficulty in reaching the leasing office, the maintenance and cleanliness of the building have been exceptional. Coming from a Property Management background, I understand that complaints are common, so I wanted to commend the maintenance team and the upkeep of the building. I am genuinely happy to be living here!

Initially, I had concerns about leasing at Upshore. I had two tours - one was conducted the day before I moved in so that I could see the actual unit I would be moving into. The building itself is beautiful and I loved the units I toured. I was mostly concerned about safety. However, the property agent I spoke with answered all of my questions and provided much clarity. I felt comfortable after working with him and was glad to move into Upshore Chapter, concern-free. I definitely recommend this property.
Upshore Management and Maintenance are completely incompetent

It is a great place to live, there are so many great things about the amenities. location can be scary at times but the safety at the building is very good. located in a convenient place with grocery and train lines near by and you have the lake in walking distance.

Gas/hot water has been unavailable since 5/17, and it won’t be on until 5/21 (or so they’re claiming; but they’d said it would be on 5/20 too and it’s not). People’s Gas confirmed it’s not an outage, that they stopped service to the address. What we all guess happened is Upshore Chapter didn’t pay the bill.

Updates from management have been insulting. They lie, through admission and obfuscation. They won’t admit they messed up and take responsibility.

My experience at the very beginning of my move at Upshore Chapter was not the best. I moved into a dirty apartment and had to sent several emails to management to get the apartment cleaned. I was given a credit towards my rent for the inconvenience but since then everything has been ok so far. I like how the apartments are very modern and energy efficient here.
The units are beautiful but the building management is subpar. Amenities are broken or missing. AC isn’t turned on despite my unit reaching over 80 degrees.
Worst managed apartment I have ever lived in during the ten years I’ve been in Chicago. This is an absolutely joke.

My friend had moved in about a month ago and I helped her for the 1st few days to move/unpack/etc. The community itself is a hidden gem. Residents are friendly; some had invited us to socialize with them and their friends in the building. Where do you ever see that in Chicago? There's a maintenance guy named Ray that helped make the moving process smoother. It's so helpful to have that dog spa and dog walk; nobody wants to go for a long walk on a cold day so this is useful. Razia is so sweet at the office. She was a huge help. You can't find that level of professionalism that she has and genuine care to go out of her way to help, anywhere. The sunrises on the rooftop are breathtaking. I visit my friend at this building often and I'm jelly that I don't live here... yet. The people here from the office, maintenance, and resident's really make this place special.

The elevator is completely out constantly for days at a time, dog urine on the elevator and lobby floor mats daily and often left for days, lots of dog poop daily in the dog run and left there for a week, the community coffee maker and printer don't work for months, SOOOO many people smoking pot in the building and on the rooftop daily, large parties allowed at all hours of the night without any action taken to prevent them or figure out who is having them, won't get a door man even though our packages are stolen A LOT, the front door locks and parking lot gates malfunction CONSTANTLY, leaving the building wide open to anyone and everyone off the street, and management that is completely unresponsive to these issues and your concerns. The maintenance and cleaning crew all take off for essentially 2-3 weeks straight during the holidays while trash, dog poop and recycling is left to literally pile up to the ceilings and nothing gets cleaned or taken care of during that time. I hope you like the sound of fire and ambulance sirens because you'll hear them LOUDLY! ALL. THE. TIME. I mean, ALL day and ALL night long on their way to the hospital two blocks away. That's just off the top of my head.

Don't let a Greystar comment saying that these issues aren't happening well after they took over, because they're happening right now, well into them having taken responsibility for the building.

Look elsewhere to pay this kind of money for an actual "luxury" experience, because it definitely isn't at Upshore Chapter Apartments.

Not worth the outrageous rent for this area, especially this corner. Shootings and drive bys happen frequently. When I moved in, parking was quoted at $150, but after a drive by damaged cars in the lot, they jacked it up to $250…zero increased security. There are still bullet holes in the gate.
If you look past the initial appearance of a new building, you’ll see lots of cut corners.
My first closet system collapsed and initially, management tried to charge me for a contractor to come repair it. I had to pull up the manufacturer’s installation guide to show them it was installed incorrectly.
Flat ceiling paint is used on all of the walls inside each unit, which means they cannot be cleaned without leaving marks. Then they’ll charge you to repaint the unit.
One of the windows in my unit randomly shattered. Coincidentally, there was a contractor on-site for the same thing in another unit. Management said that it’s a known issue in the building and it’s likely because the building is settling. They sent a maintenance person to come out packing tape on my window until it can be replaced. I’ve spent the last month vacuuming up shards of glass as it fell on the floor where it could hurt my animals. I requested a rent adjustment for the month because I have to keep my blind shut and vacuum the area daily. Management got back to me a month later stating there would be no adjustment because a vendor was onsite to measure the glass when it happened.
The HVAC system works well once a year, during summer. Fall and spring, the units get super hot and their solution is the let you borrow a portable AC unit. Winter is hit or miss, sometimes it’s fine and you don’t need the HVAC on at all, other times it’s too warm.
The landscaping our front consists of weed, broken glass, bullet casings, trash, and mud. The landscaping our back is overgrown weeds growing into the generator full of rats. It’s gotten so tall that it lifted the sprinkler system off of the ground.
The mail area and package system are awful. The mail carrier once left a bundle of mail for the whole apartment complex rubber-banded on the floor near the mailboxes. FedEx, UPS, and Amazon almost never use the luxer system and packages are thrown haphazardly in various places on the floor. Pretty decent for the first few months, but with property management rarely on property, it declined quickly.

There is a reason they want you to sign a lease within 24 hours. Ask questions to current residents to understand how the building is managed.

1. Shootings almost every other week due to gang violence. 
2. The garage door is sometimes broken in this unsafe area, this means that your car is exposed to theft
3. Property Manager is always in his office, door closed. Sometimes it is hard to know if there is anyone on site to talk to.
4. There is no doorman and homeless ppl enters the building and sleeps on the lobby couches
5. Package get lost a LOT because carriers dont have easy access to the building so they leave your package outside or in between the front doors. 

As much as this seems like a luxury building, it is not worth the price at all.

Agent seemed responsive at first to my inquiry, so I submitted my application for a unit. Didn't hear anything for  3 days, so I followed up with the agent. He said he didn't know I had applied, that I was suppose to message him to let him know I applied (which he never told me). He said he would look for my application and get back to me. I called him back a day later to find out the status of my app, and he said the unit was no longer available, but he might have another unit available and would get back to me later that day. Didn't hear from him, so I called the next day and he said the new unit had already been sublet by the resident. He also mentioned that the person that got the original unit i applied for applied after I did, but because the contract was already signed there wasn't anything he could do other than refund my app fee. 
The part that bothers me the most is that the apartment should have been mine, and when I first contacted the agent to follow up on my app he didn't mention that the unit had been rented or that someone else was applying for it. Maybe I could have still got the unit if he had acted quickly when I told him about the app, instead of wasting more of my time (did I mention my move in date was in 2 weeks?).

Imprint is beautiful and the staff is kind. The space is luxurious, well kept and all people are friendly. The views are amazing and the neighborhood has so much to access no matter your lifestyle. Food, friends and solitude are easily accessible.

My wife picked this community, finding it online and speaking with Don, Amber and Darian prior to our move to Chicago. We were swayed by their sincerity, the architecture, and the proximity to the sights and culinary standouts. Imprint was OUTSTANDING in every way! The security and maintenance teams are also exceptional. We loved it here.

Yes, it can be tough to find a place to live downtown where the renovations, over the years, have been competent enough to not leave problems with water, heat, windows, and other important aspects.  Solution?  IMPRINT!  Loving the simple elegance of my apartment, the views, amenities, and especially the friendliness of the staff.

So far, I have found Imprint to have friendly and helpful staff (maintenance, property management office, and front desk/concierge) which makes a positive difference on a managed building apartment living experience!
The Imprint staff is the best! They really look out and care about their residents!
This apartment is nice clean and organized. I love my view and how quiet it is. The people are friendly and it’s in a great location!

Love, Cascade and LSE this neighborhood is safe and simply peaceful. From the management to the staff who has now become family is why I continue to call Cascade home. The professionalism from management is top tier (which shocks me to see other reviews) they make living at Cascade enjoyable. The front desk/staff is always friendly on top of being helpful to accommodate residents 24/7. The buildings, amenities, and common areas are always clean as if the building has just been built. The residents are friend & respectful and do not over utilize amenities which is a plus. And lastly I love the app and activities for our community that is constantly being elevated month-after-month. After work I run home to engage in activities. The peace and tranquility is unparalleled as you walk on the lake and go into the park that is huge and also have movies in the park in the summer ^_^. 5 star restaurants in the St. Regis and we are only a walk away from the river. Can't beat it. So come visit and see for yourself.

We specifically asked if we would hear the upstairs neighbors, that is, how effective between-floor soundproofing is in this building. Marco in the leasing office told us there were no issues whatsoever. However, there was constant noise from upstairs, making it difficult to sleep, and sounding like a troop of restless elephants. It's hard to understand how designers of such a new building could have failed to adequately engineer sound proofing between floors when the technology to do so has been around for a long time. Some apartments have good views, though overall it feels more like living in an office building than a home. Best attribute is nearby parks/lake front, but other buildings have that too.
Great amenities! The area is beautiful with the parks/dog parks. The staff is always friendly. The apartments are modern. Good place to live at.

I cant get on the basic app for building services, and to find out things like how to get my mail or events or announcements. I can only get on the rent cafe  portal to pay 

The orientation link was broken.  I have been here two weeks.  

Everyone in the office says they do not know anything about it.  Really stressful!!!   I give up.   Not the best experience.

Amenities are good, but that's all they'll emphasize if you get a tour. The prices are way too expensive compared to other buildings, rooms are too small, walls are thin so you can hear loud neighbors, and lack of transparency from management i.e. regarding stolen items.

This building is absurdly poorly run and poorly constructed. It lived up to absolutely none of the leasing agent's promises. And despite that it's brand new, something new breaks in my unit on an almost weekly basis. Bottom line, unless you want to pay an obscene amount for a loud, janky building that's poorly run and unpleasant as hell, rent someplace else.
Poor communication - they changed management and it is really tough to get to talk to them
Building location is excellent, middle of everything. Staff is super friendly and helpful. Rooftop Pool is awesome. Parking is limited but easy to access, EV charging available!

Location is decent but driving to the garage is a hassle and the parking is on lower wacker making it super confusing to find and park in the TINY garage spaces that cost $400/month (which is significantly higher than the other apartments I searched in the same zip code). The leasing office does not care about current residents and only wants to attract new customers. For instance, we had some delivery food stolen from the front lobby desk (in the few minutes before we could get downstairs). My husband went to the lobby to check what happened- the leasing lady told him “I’m not letting you in” - so she didn’t ask or realize he is a resident and needed office assistance because he was dressed casually. The dog run has no grass or turf (and is mid-way up the building) so my dog won’t even pee up there which makes it useless; there is a pet bath which is handy. The apartment finishes are decent but there is very little closet/storage space so our items end up cluttered; the lay out says “walk-in closet” which is an exaggeration- it’s a small step-in closet and not enough space for 2 people’s clothing. Do not plan on extending my lease.

I applied for an apartment and during the application process, I found out that it was an ADA accessible apartment and was not disclosed online. Once Siearra informed me of this, I choose to withdraw my application. Although this was an error on their end, they refused to refund my $550 application fee. Such a shame that what should be a beautiful, new property is ran so horribly. There are plenty of other great properties that are ran well- go elsewhere.

Run away don’t rent here. I moved here 2 weeks ago, since I moved in there is strong smell of something I thought it could be from painting or new apartment smell but that was not the case. I had 2 friends came over and they all said there was some kind of moldish smell so I went ahead and ordered a testing kit. 48 hours later it’s positive for mold in my closet which is in the living room closet and kitchen. Back and forth and management they came over and said they can’t smell anything since I had instances there to get rid of the smell. Spoke with corporation they won’t break the lease and trying to find a professional company to come test for mold based on my request. I have a pretty bad asthma so does my kids and this is absolutely a very terrible experience for me, it cost me to re clean everything that I had put away in the closet and now I have to re do that again moving anywhere else. Safe yourself the headache and rent somewhere else even if you have to spend some extra money this place isn’t worth it at all. I had a very bad headache and dizziness and had to go sit in the lobby in case anything happens to me yet they don’t care.
Attached is a picture of my test and will be taking legal action.

The apartments and the building are nice. However, my unit is facing west and it's unbearable staying inside. The AC in the units is extremely useless and is not nearly enough to cool down the place, not even a bit. The administration won't upgrade them for better ones either, so I'm stuck in this annoyingly hot apartment until my lease end. I would not recommend living here.

Honestly, my advice is don't even bother touring this place. It is a great looking apartment building with lots of amenities, but the management is horrible. And you're going to sit there and contemplate whether the apartment is worth dealing with the management. They were great until something went wrong and then after that they were extremely rude, despite the fact that it was 100% due to their incompetence. If nothing had gone wrong I would have been writing a good review. If they had handled it maturely I would have been writing a better review. But their inability to solve their own problems without placing blame on the rentors is astonishing.  If you choose to live here, I pray nothing goes wrong for you guys. If something does go wrong, then good luck.

The front desk people are nice, as are the maintenance and cleaning staff, but Horizon Realty is the only rental company/landlord I have ever had an issue with. My unit and hallway have smelled like cigarette smoke all day and night for two months now even though lease says it is a smoke-free building, even after 120+ phone calls and 80+ emails from tenants on our floor alone. Management claimed that they could not locate where the smoke was coming from after two months of multiple complaints daily. Half of laundry machines are routinely broken, printer broken, continual water issues. Frequent broken elevators. These units cost the same as other comparable units in the city but come with many less amenities and zero customer service mindset from company at the higher levels.

I can not say enough positive things about Park Michigan! 
The front office staff is so accommodating and friendly--Kristian and Evan are honestly the BEST!! They have been super helpful, professional, and always efficient! 
The concierge staff is also exceptional; T, Patrice, and Jasmine always greet me with a smile and even have treats for my dog, Kodiak. They make me feel like so welcomed! 
I never hear my neighbors and the building is so quiet! 
The ONLY negative--is the laundry room. The washer/dryers don't always work and sometimes leave soap on my clothes :( But, they have Tide Cleaner Lockers, so I just have been using those! This small issue doesn't over shine all the positives that Park Michigan offers!! 
I highly recommend!

Park Michigan location is amazing. Right next to the Roosevelt stop and walking distance to grocery stores, restaurants, museums, parks, and key sightseeing spots in downtown Chicago. 
The maintenance crew is great. Put a work order in and they will fix it within a day or two.

New management is barely better than the last company, constantly fighting them on hidden fees and increased random utility charges. Manager unresponsive and often rude, "improvements" are always promised, rarely delivered

I lived here for a year, and couldn't wait to get out.  It was just such an unpleasant atmosphere. 

Management almost never responds to repair requests (or anything else.)

The dog park is always COVERED IN EXCREMENT.  Some of the common facilities are shut-down entirely.  Much of the gym equipment was broken.  They didn't even bother keeping wipes in stock for the machines.

One or more elevators are frequently broken.  They also had not been recently inspected while I lived here.  

They don't turn the heat on til almost December.  

The main lobby is deceptively nice, but everything else is decrepit.  

One redeeming factor:  The door staff and maintenance people are extremely nice and always do their best.

I am so happy I found I found MDA apartments. I have been here for over a year and never had one issue, except maybe when my garbage disposal went out.  They had someone here within 24 hours, and as with all my state of the art appliance's it was as simple as hitting the reset switch. The Front desk people are great, the management is stellar, the other tenant's are cool and all I have to say it's a great vibe at 63 Lake.

They will never respond to you. They won't answer your calls or emails. They will avoid it at all costs, unless of course you are telling them something positive in the email. I have been waiting for weeks to address so many issues, and I am so glad I am moving out of this awful building. The concierge and maintenance staff are wonderful and should be given a raise considering how awfully this building is run. Do not move here.

My roommate and I had some kind of extensive maintenance issues, but the team was so helpful and kind once we let them know what was going on! The building is old so there is some general issues but overall really love the building and the people!

The property management team at MDA is one of the best I have ever encountered, working always in a professional and friendly manner. I worked with Pat and he tackled any issues that came up without any delay. The maintenance crew and concierge at this property is also wonderful. The amenities are well kept and very, very nice.

Incredibly disappointed in my experience with Coast throughout the almost year I have lived here. The location is amazing and Lakeshore East is a great neighborhood. HOWEVER that does not make up for how bad this building and its management is. The apartments have super dated appliances that are constantly breaking, the window insulation is so bad that your floors are dripping wet in the winter time and you have no control over when the building turns on the AC so in the Spring, Summer and sometimes Fall the apartments get up to 80+ degrees inside. The leasing office staff is USELESS and unhelpful, there are constantly cars getting broken into in the garage and there are not enough elevators for how many people live in this building. The bright points of the building are the wonderful front desk and maintenance staff and the view. For how much you pay it is not worth it. AVOID COAST AT ALL COSTS

I just moved in a couple of months ago, and I find this place a great fit to live in the heart of the City - Chicago. Following are the reasons why:
1. The building offers some amazing views (Lake facing and South side parks) and plenty of apartment options to pick and choose the best one that fits our budget and expectations.
2. Great services provided from end to end - From start of the application till the date you move in to the apartment. Special thanks to Karim, Sarah, Sheila and team for their assistance
3. Building amenities and others (Gym, lobby, reception services, Mail and Parcel room, library, resident lounge) are of great quality. They tend to maintain it nice and clean. The reception staff always makes you feel warm and welcome and do assists around often.
4. The apartment structure is nicely built, decent size - 1 bed in my case. Mix of wooden and Carpet flooring available. GE electrical appliance are in great shape as well
5. Maintenance and repair works - That's something inevitable with every apartment buildings, but Coast team does a fantastic job when it comes to assisting residents with fixing things and getting things back to working. Timely and professional.
6. Amazing public parks available in the vicinity which seems like a great fit for the summers.

Overall a great apartment building in the downtown Chicago area in terms of pricing and availability.  Definitely worth moving in.

5 stars! The Coast management staff and the front door staff are always personable, pleasant and accommodating. The location is excellent, the residents are respectful and polite, and the amenities are also top grade. The management team is very responsive and keeps the residents informed on activities. This is a well-run organization with a focus on Customer Service. I'm confident that you will be as delighted in Coast as I am.

i am so regret i rent the apartment. it appears nice at first. however, when you move in, you will find problems here and there. the kitchen closet door fall off only after two months i moved in. there are always spiders on the balcony. However, beside all of these kind of problems. the maintenance is the worst. i was forced to pay lots of money for the damage that is not cost by me. And they said to me that they are the boss, if you argue, i will charge more. Don't choose the apartment and let yourself regret.

The actual  apartments are not is represented in the models.
The kitchen sink is so shallow, that a large pot or pitcher won't  fit under the faucet. 
The medicine cabinet in the bathroom, is placed opposite the toilet. Seriously! 
The microwave is not mounted above the stove. This leaves three options; (1) place the microwave next to the stove-which leaves no counter space, (2) place on top the refrigerator-which means you can't see in without a step-stool and your dangerously pulling hot items over your head, (3) or place on top the combination washer dryer unit. 
The stove does not have a thermostat. There's no way to tell  when preheating has reached the needed temperature. 
The  combination washer-dryer unit takes forever to dry a load of clothes. A small load of light to medium weight items takes about two hours.
Coast apartments are well designed and have great layouts - form and function! Pair that with a fantastic staff, million dollar views, and the perfect location and you have a great place to live.

As the other negative reviews have stated otherwise nice building ruined by management.

Touring staff said that if I applied within 48 hours there would be no admin fee. Applied and still got hit with the 600$ (!) fee which they refused to remove/honor.

*Maintenance* staff is quite good but at least one elevator is usually broken. In a building with 40 floors 3 working elevators means you're waiting 5-10min near rush hour.

Parking is fine if expensive. It's public parking also so regularly get stuck exiting by someone who can't get their app to work for 5 to 10 minutes.

Packages stolen from the mailroom and management is no help.

Overall nice physical building. Gym is fine. Pool was closed well past Memorial day which was annoying. Views are quite good and location is accessible to several trains.

The 5th floor amenities have been closed since December and the rooftop has been closed since new year's eve (it is leap day 2/29 today) and no answer has been given regarding them re opening. To give context, the media room, shown to us during our walkthrough (apartment rented in 2020), was closed first for covid, then "to be remodeled." It not has yet reopened. 
   Also, on the factually coldest day of the year, they allowed the heating to go out on a Friday during the day, until 11am the next day. e-mail contact was the usually run around of no answers, until after a staff member ran to each apartment to reset each heater the next morning around 11am. 
  Underneath the carpet is a line from the second redoing of the floors after someone walked through it the first time, leaving foot prints in the ground for some time. Perhaps you could optimistically call it artistic, but that was not the case. Also, the elevators run with a touch screen that was out of order for some time, instilling confidence while riding.
   Front desk, maintenance, and co. are great! Leasing office lost their last quality employee a couple years ago, possibly when the building changed ownership. Only a handful of staff have remained constant, which is a bummer when it comes to the very friendly desk team.

We really enjoyed our stay here at 1001 although it was kinda short lived.  It's bittersweet to leave, but Life goes on and Change is inevitable.  The staff was awesome ?? (Leasing and Concierge).  I highly recommend 1001 to live, work and play!  
Sincerely, Veronica

First off, before anyone from management responds with the canned "we care...please reach out to discuss your concerns..."  we have reached out.  Multiple times.  And are far from satisfied with the responses.

Upon receiving our keys, we went to do the move-in inspection, and discovered several issues.  Most notably being massive damage to the floors in almost every single room.  Their initial solution to fixing the 7-inch gash in the living room floor was to literally paint the floor with grey paint.  It obviously looks like trash.  When we expressed our displeasure, they said they'd schedule the flooring vendor to get a quote to repair the floors for us, and would follow up in a week.  Six weeks later (and several emails requesting more information from him), we were told that there had been a "miscommunication" and that they would not be repairing our floors.  But, they'd allow us to go through their vendor and repair the floors ourselves.

They want us to pay to repair the floors for damage caused before we moved in.

In addition to this, the bathrooms constantly smell like cigarettes from other residents smoking in their unit, and the smell comes straight through the vents.  If we try to open the windows, they get stuck and maintenance needs to come in with a block of wood to bang on the windows to temporarily fix them so they will shut (until I want to open them again...) 

There were chunks of food, garbage, and hair throughout the kitchen and bathrooms upon move in.  The washing machine's hot water setting doesn't work.  

The parking garage cost has gone up twice since we moved in.  The office announced a $75 lock-out fee because they do not want the inconvenience of helping their residents (and refuse to give us a spare key; there's no way to make spare keys with the lock system in place here).

The majority of the front desk staff don't wear a mask, and nobody is enforcing mask wearing in elevators or other common areas.

Yeah, the view's nice.  But before anybody gets too excited about that- looks like the view is about to be blocked once 1000 Michigan goes up.

The management company is the worst we’ve ever had to deal with at any luxury apartment. Hardly any monitoring of guests coming in and out, probably why there was a shooting in a unit last year. Not to mention the constant smell of drugs and cigarettes accompanied by loud obnoxious partying consistently. The management company doesn’t care about the safety of the residents and only cares about rent being paid. Too many issues with cars getting broken into in the parking garage or stolen and the management staff doing absolutely nothing. There’s a list of issues with this place and the management that goes far beyond this review. Don’t waste your time or money renting at this location, the amenities aren’t as great as they appear nor the excessively high amount of rent they are trying to charge in an area that is unsafe.

We have just moved into this wonderful apartment. Besides the wonderful views of the skyline and lake, I'm really impressed by the staff from the leasing office. Yesterday we had some unusual requests regarding the apartment, which we weren't expecting any work-around, but resolved in just hours (should have taken days) with the help of Bobby and other staff  in the leasing office. Thank you guys very much!

I booked a tour exactly one month in advance, immediately upon calling to book the tour the women made it sound like booking the tour was a chore for her on the phone. A month goes by and we show up for the tour at the specified time and no one comes out.. so I call the building and the women answers and says there was a "emergency" and no one would be in the building till 4 days later. We found it very unprofessional that no one bothered to reach out to let us know they were going to cancel the tour. Which was disappointing because we are from out of town. Would not recommend trying to visit this place unless you want a unprofessional and low customer service experience .

Been a resident for ten years. Maintenance staff is prompt and efficient. The building is kept very clean. 
If you like the smell of weed, this is the place for you! It’s prominent on nearly every floor and comes into your unit all day and night through the vents. Nothing is done about it and you will just get snarky responses from the management office. 
Rent has gone up astronomically (10% the last two years) and for the older building and what you get it’s just not worth that kind of money.
Air conditioning is horrendous. Unit will not get below 70 degrees at any given time.
The building leases out several hundred units to Kasa which is Airbnb’s. This presents its own set of problems. 
Elevators are out of date and the fire department had to come and rescue someone off of one of the elevators earlier this year.
This used to be a great building but there are much better options in Chicago.

Living at One Superior Place is a dream come true. Management's ongoing commitment to cleanliness, speedy response to resident issues and overall genuine care and concern for its residents is at the highest level of service expectations. The good Lord will I hope to spend my remaining years right here at OSP. They will definitely "leave the light on for you!"
So far, the amenities stand up to par. The amazing views of the apartment is what got us and definitely still amazes me when I walk in to my place. Love how dog friendly this place is!

If you enjoy leaving your apartment then this is not the place for you. The fact that all 3 elevators servicing my floor have gone out of service more than once while I've been living here for the past 6 months is absurd. 1 of the elevators hasn't been functional since I've lived here, so even when the other 2 are operational they are often packed, and take forever.

One Superior Place has excellent management, security, and maintenance. One Superior Place is excellent as there respective staff noted above are professional, knowledgeable, and courteous to the me. I truly recommend One Superior Place to anyone looking for a fabulous apartment building to live at. In conjunction with One Superior Place’s staff. The building is near all modes of public transportation. Not to mention One Superior Place’s close proximity to excellent restaurants.

Building is nice. Views and balcony are top notch. Location is great. It's very convenient to have Whole Foods right across the street, as well as other grocery stores and restaurants very close by. Layouts are fantastic compared to similar properties. While it is nice to have doggy daycare in the building, my experience thus far has been that this is not a dog friendly community. The dog run is a joke. It's unkept, outside, in a parking garage. I can't think of anything worse. It's dangerous for the residents and you have to take two elevators just to get there. It's usually not even worth it to use. Also disappointed that we are not allowed to use certain entrances when coming and going with pets. It makes no sense. Last, many of the units really need an upgrade. Having carpet is embarrassing to the renter and reflects poorly on the building as a whole. The cabinets are also dingy and old and the tile in the kitchen/bathroom is way outdated.
Amli Lofts is a great apartment building.  Great finishes and amenities. Staff very friendly!  Also a lot of pups :)

My time overall at Amli Lofts has exceeded my expectations. I moved here from across the country and they were very accommodating to that. Since I have been here I have not had many issues. One time I had an issue with my sink, I put in a maintenance request and the issue was resolved within a hour. I was impressed lol.
I love it here! Super close to grocery stores and great restaurants. All the amenities are amazing and the staff is super friendly!

The living experience at AMLI is one of the best that Printer's Row has to offer. You simply can't beat the amenities, the hospitality of its staff, and the community itself. Its a convenient walk away from anything you could want or need, and the living space is so comfortable. We're so excited to start a life here at AMLI!
Excellent location, amenities, events, apartments and a true sense of community.

Great place to live. Pricing is better than most similar luxury apartments around the area. Pool, courtyard, and gym are a big plus. All modern appliances and the biggest plus by far is the balcony. Good mix of young professionals and families. Biggest drawback is only two elevators, which can often be only one on the weekends if someone is moving into/out of their apartment.

This location has totally dropped in value. Management, customer service, unit insulation, plumbing etc makes this building and RELATED a terrible option amongst their competitors in the centralized downtown chicago area.

Management is extremely unprofessional. They are rude and will harass their tenants. They've tried turning off my fob because I had my mask down while alone in the gym. Now I have to use my neighbors fob to go to the gym or knock on the doors to be let in. Who turns off your fob without notifying you? Especially during your last month for a clear misunderstanding?

This building needs to train their employees on unconscious biases and blatant inconsistencies. I say that because when I was working out in the gym, my mask was down on a cardio machine and there was someone else who later walked in with no mask and wasn't addressed. How does that make sense? How would that make anyone feel?

Please save yourself the OVERPRICED rent and move somewhere else downtown. Their "app" and rentcafe platform is glitchy and their customer service is often abhorrent. It is not worth it! MOVE ANYWHERE ELSE DOWNTOWN. Not here!

They turned my rent on autopay without my permission and made charges to my accounts without my permission. Again, who does that?

I will be updating with photos and more detail. There is just too much to address before I leave... but I want to give it a wholistic analysis.

LOOK ELSEWHERE!
Management sucks. Dont move here. they will hit you with bills and rent increases even in the pandemic. They are greedy and intrusive

I work in Real Estate and I have seen almost all of Chicago's luxury rental apartments. I would say that, hands down, the finishes in these units surpass any other I have seen! We love living here. There's something about this place that makes you feel at home the moment you walk in. The staff is very friendly and helpful and the concierge service is a nice added plus.
When it comes to the amenities, they really knew what they were doing. You do not need a gym membership anywhere else as there is an Equinox gym ion site! The pool area is spectacular and you can see the fireworks clearly each week.
There's isn't enough I can say about this place. I would recommend this building above all others!

I applied at The Row after touring a few units, and discussing my financials with a leasing agent, to make sure I qualify. After being assured that I the assets to qualify, I applied, paid $50, and they checked my credit. I sent over my financials. Now, after all that, I am being asked to provide proof that I have liquid assets totaling 40 TIMES the rental amount, to qualify. AFTER they took my application, the application fee, AND checked my credit, they mentioned a new requirment that was never mentioned before.

Also, 40X the rental amount? Lol. No. 

Related Properies practices are shady, and will bring you nothing but confusion, stress, shock and disppoinent.  Not worth it. Better to save yourself the trouble and apply somewhere honest and professional.

We had a wonderful experience with Nicolette at the Row. The finishes in the pre-leasing center are beautiful, and Nicolette was incredibly thorough in her presentation. I'm very much looking forward to touring the building in person!

My family and I went on a tour with Group Fox and had the most unpleasant experience I’ve ever encountered during apartment tours in my 17 years of living in Chicago. Ann Cort was rude throughout the tour, responding to our questions with annoyance and irritation. Initially, we thought Ann Cort might just not be a friendly person and tried to continue with the tour. However, Ann Cort was just racist and being rude to us. We are Asians, and out of the blue, Ann Cort commented that we ‘smelled like garlic.’ We were too shocked to respond and tried to laugh it off. Yet, Ann Cort persisted, repeatedly asking who had eaten garlic and where the smell was coming from. Not knowing how to respond, we just said that none of us had eaten garlic or anything at all yet today before coming to the tour and asked if it might be her. Ann became offended and responded that she ‘never eats such a thing’ in a degrading tone as if garlic was something ‘her people’ would not eat. It was clear that she was not asking the question with a good intention when she became offended when we asked her back. I have not experienced much racism in real life and certainly did not expect to encounter it during an apartment tour. I should have read the reviews before going on the tour. I would not recommend this place, especially if you are Asian.
Our AC has been broken since February 2023 and they never fixed it. The management office claimed that "being too hot is never an emergency."

I moved in March of 2016 and I am very happy with my decision. It is hard to find actual loft apartments in Chicago, most of the new buildings although spectacular look relatively the same. I appreciate that my apartment is unique.  Every encounter I have had with the management team has been positive, I do wish they had more bike storage on  in the building, but the rest of the amenities are spacious and well designed.

I’ve lived here for several months now (since the beginning of April) and overall have had a very positive experience! If you’re at all like me, I DEFINITELY look through and appreciate reviews when considering if I want to live somewhere. So, here we go…
Pros
Staff -- The Staff is great. They’re friendly and they go out of their way to be accommodating, but fair to all residents.
Building -- The building is BEAUTIFUL! The units are gorgeous and the amenities are top notch.
Location -- The location is AMAZING. 
Cons
Parking – Parking is expensive and unassigned ($250 a month). 
Overall, The Lofts are a great place to live and I would definitely recommend it to others! ?

We were in awe the minute we walked in.  Even my mother who has been trying to get us back to the burbs!   This building is so super cool.  Seriously could not believe the size of the units.  And I don't know who designed this building but we cannot believe how different (in a good way) it is.  It's not like any other building.  The hallways are HUGE.  But the lower level where all the amenities are really blew us away.
Um... about as cool as it gets.  this building looks nothing like the hundreds of other buildings.  we rented a 2 bed here.  the minute we walked in we knew.
Excellent service, move in experience, amenities. First time signing a lease where I was truly looking forward to the living experience
Quality of the apartment finishes and the location are why we chose this building

I’ll start with pests. I can count 3 different species of spiders that I find and kill nearly daily that regular sprays do not stop. Spiders have been found in my bathroom, closet, kitchen, BED - you name it. I also have the joy of finding earthworms (yes, you read that right), rollie pollies, and now centipedes. Additionally, I’ve had to invest hundreds of dollars in heaters, fans, and humidifiers due to a horribly inefficient and outdated HVAC system. Think: 80 upstairs and barely 65 downstairs with no air circulation. Brick falls apart if you touch certain areas in the unit due to negligence, and management’s fix is a temporary sealer that looks like whitewash painted on the bricks. Other building perks include hearing your neighbors’ every conversation, smelling their dinner or when they decide to smoke, and oh! I also don’t think they’ve ever cleaned the gym. I have just wrapped up my first month living at Lake Shore Plaza and have found the experience to be remarkably... neutral.

Here's your pros:
1) Location, location, location. Lake Shore Plaza is well located in the south part of Streeterville, and is a comfortable walk from Michigan Ave., the loop, and about 2 minutes from Ohio St. Beach and Lake Michigan.

2) Easy leasing experience. My leasing agent, Cody, was very helpful and a definite 5/5. Took me less than 30 minutes to apply online and was approved quickly. Nice if you need a fast move like I did.

3) The views are great, particularly if you get a north, east, or south facing view and live on the eastern side of the building.

Now the cons:
1) The elevators. What is an elevator to a great living experience? Everything. LSP's elevators are 30+ years old and completely dysfunctional. The rattle, jump, shake, and take forever to get to you. I have actually written much of this review waiting for an elevator. Living on the 40th floor the elevators are the bain of my existence at LSP.

2) Things start crumbling. When I toured my convertible, all seemed well--and largely still is--but some maintainence issues surfaced quickly after moving in. Closet rods sheared off, my dishwasher consistently suds over and fills with water, and the space had been less than well cleaned upon my move in. Maintainence is generally quick to fix these issues as they arise, but should I have to fill out a work order every week?

3) Things operate for weird hours. Management office generally closes at 5, except Tuesday and Thursday when it stays open until 7, but if you work a sporadically scheduled job like me it can be difficult to make it in with much ease. The dry cleaner in the building takes delivery of your packages and you have to get back by the time they close to get your things which can also be irritating if you're expecting the most incredible package ever only to realize you arrived five minutes late. Also laundry isn't quite 24 hour... Why not? These sort of things just get on people's nerves and could be easily resolved if management tried.

Again, LSP is fine--it is relatovely cheap compared to other nearby options, well located, and has a friendly enough staff to keep you pleased.
