It is one of the best located apartment communities in the Bucktown area - a two-minute walk to the Blue Line, within four blocks of two good grocery stores, conveniently located medical services, a bike ride to the best gym in Chicago, close to the 606 Bike Trail, and a short walk to many bars and restaurants.  The location is hard to beat.

For only being a couple years old, this building is a mess. The elevators are out almost every weekend and expect broken dishwashers. The construction of the building is very poor, you can hear everything your neighbors above and below are doing. 

This building was built the cheapest way possible and the units are priced too high. There are plenty of options in the area so not sure why anyone would pick this one.

I have loved living here so far. The maintenance and other staff have been so kind to me, as has Brianna from the office. The community is very secure and clean. I appreciate the opportunity to live here and want to recognize everyone’s efforts to make this home for me.
It's a good place to be, and the neighborhood is decent.
It's a great place to live, pretty near to the lake!
The facilities are always clean, the manager and the assistant are very nice people, and they are attentive to any concerns.

This place has gone down hill year after year! 
Don’t bother pay a little more and live better

I would never recommend anyone to move here.
Below standard unacceptable for the money being charged

If you like being lied to while being accused of lying, this is the place for you! If you like people banging on your door with eviction notices when you've paid rent every single month, this is the place for you!
The people an office. Are really helpful an nice to talk too. It's easy going no stress. Love it here.
Times square have the best people to work on apartment.

My wife and I love the building. There is a nice environment in the building, the staff is really super attentive and professional, from the leasing office agents to the security guards and maintenance staff. The response time for maintenance requests is surprisingly fast for how large the building is, and communication with staff is easy and accessible.
Great building with very friendly and attentive staff and excellent value units!
My experience with Times Square has been great so far. The property managers and staff and very tuned in and always working to make it a great place to live!
I would not recommend, I found my experience to have been awful and the amenities do not match what is offered nor the price listed.

If you are looking for a little place to call home, look no further. With studios and one-bedrooms in a variety of layouts - something is sure to fit what you are looking for. It's right on a few bus routes and close to the train.  And there is some of the best pizza in Chicago within walking distance.

The management at this property never responds, things are often broken, and infested with mice and roaches. The communal living spaces are filthy, and unsafe conditions were never addressed, including other tenants stalking women in the building, breaking windows, and setting fires.

overall living here is not bad, with communal showers. For the most part the girls bathroom is always clean . HOWEVER the kitchen is always nasty ! and this is a bug/rodent invested building!!! no matter how many inspections they give you. a bug or a mice could literally crawl under you doorspace at anytime. with that being said i wish i could end my lease rn so DONT DO IT.

This building is not ideal for someone working from home. There are people constantly in the hallway making noise and shouting during the day. As for the ventilation, random smells were constantly coming into the apartment vents, especially if someone cooked or even smoked marijuana. Plus, the MONTHLY BED BUG AND PEST INSPECTIONS AND SPRAY, was normalized by management in order to “prevent the problem from happening”. I don’t know about you…..I’ve lived in my fair share of  apartments. I’ve NEVER HAD TO HAVE MONTHLY BED BUG/PEST INSPECTION AND SPRAYING to “prevent the problem from happening”, especially in a new building. Usually, that doesn’t need to happen unless there’s a problem…but what do I know.The place is absolute circus! As for the management office and leasing office, the lack of professionalism is TRULY ASTONISHING AND ATROCIOUS! There is absolutely no solid communication with management and the residents. The only time we usually hear from them is when they slip a sheet of paper under your door to tell you something. If you try to email or call, especially maintenance requests the likelihood of getting a response is EXTREMELY UNLIKELY! When they do respond, they mention that either they didn’t receive it, didn’t see it, or have been busy! Nevertheless, “despite being so busy”….they’re able to CLOCK OUT EARLY ON FRIDAY AT NOON/1:00 PM with so much stuff to do! (Sarcasm). When we decided to get out of our lease due to us no longer feeling safe at the building, we had to THREATEN THEM WITH LEGAL ACTION SIMPLY TO GET OUR SECURITY DEPOSIT BACK AFTER REPEATED ATTEMPTS TO CONTACT THEM WITH NO RESPONSE. If I did any of these actions (like the management  and leasing offices), I would’ve been fired from my job. I guess they don’t work in the real world. Honestly, the ONLY EMPLOYEE THAT HAD ANY PROFESSIONALISM AND CLASS at that place is the custodian. He was always very friendly and accommodating. That is the only positive thing I have to say about this place.If you want to still live here, well……. enjoy the crazy. I agree 100% with everything the December 2023 poster says here!!

Where do I start. The front doors do not work with your key fob. Imagine not being able to access your front door. The back door stays open all night because it doesn’t latch right. Imagine having a back door open all night in Chicago. The elevator beeping has been happening for months with no fix in sight. The management is the island of misfit toys. They don’t respond to calls or emails and they lie. The leasing office acts like they have the knowledge of never knowing anything about the building. They are in code violation here and I’ve told them that. I’ve talked to several tenants trying to get out of their leases. If you want to never hear from management please move here.

Absolutely love living here. I was one of the first to move in. Secure building, secure package lockers, simple gym for when it starts to snow. Units are spacious and have a clean look. Right down the street from the Diversey L stop. Ebony was great during the tour/signing process and was beyond helpful. 10/10.
Great place to live, close to CTA transportation, shooping, restaurants, entertainment, schools, hospital, lake, bike and jogging trails. What more can you ask for.
The community and amenities have exceeded our expectations, the building is always clean, the staff are friendly and welcoming, and any maintenance request is handled promptly.
It is nice, and is a good location in terms of airport, highways, and the city.   But the price is not always reflective of the experience.
Great location. Quiet. Friendly and considerate neighbors.

We rented this apartment without ever having physically seen it as we were moving here with very little notice from Texas.  We used Apartments.com and searched for 4/5 star apartments in the area and quickly found Park 205.  The apartment community is VERY well maintained, it's in a great location with a great little downtown area with lots of little shops and local eats.  The maintenance response rate is crazy fast and the office staff are friendly and efficient.  Not only that, but our apartment is incredibly quiet and RIGHT next door to Whole Foods so grocery shopping is easy.  The only reason we didn't rate this place a perfect 5 stars is due to a few minor things (I would have rated it 4.5 stars if that was an option).  We have a 2 bedroom and 2 bathroom unit and there is no pantry...and not a ton of kitchen storage. I was actually super surprised there was no pantry and we had to do some creative storage things as we came here from a home in Texas.  Among the small things that kept it from being a 5:  The refrigerator door was all scratched up (minor scratches, no big deal) and the master bedroom is pretty small.  Once our bed was in, there was almost no room for the dresser.  It fits, but you can't open the drawers all the way because it's too close to the bed.  A weird design thing was that the sprinklers and alarms and vents are all installed in the walls instead of the ceiling and at weird places so it's really hard to hang pictures because there is always something in the way.  Other than those minor things, the place is really very very nice.
The environment around apartment is good and it is easy to access to restaurant, bank, supermarket, and train station by walk.
Staff is great and there is a sense of community here. Feels like tenants look out for each other a bit. I just moved from an elevator building in the city and am not used to that LOL
Jorge Clean, fast, deligent and friendly!  He is an asset to have working at One East Delaware - Stephen & Sylwia - 32G

One of the nicer buildings in all of Chicago Building is beautiful, amenities are awesome. This building is perfectly located and well maintained. Ended up being a bit above my budget but with GREAT reason. 

Will look at these apartments as my budget rises.
The issue was solved in less than a day - quick response and effective & clean work! Thank you!!
Dishwasher  Thanks for replacing the dishwasher. It was becoming a chronic problem. ????
Quick Response in Maintenance Requests My maintenance requests were handled same day as request. The men who assisted with these requests were great and efficient. Both my issues were fixed. Thanks!

Happy with the Wednesday morning bagels. Monthly events with free food. But really did not appreciate the cover up about the construction when signing the lease. It’s Monday- Friday 8:00 AM -4:00 PM. It’s horrible no headphones or ear plugs can prevent you from hearing the noise. Beware!!!

The building carefully concealed the fact there will be construction with excessive noise. This was not mentioned during the tour or anything and within a month my life was a living hell. I was forced to break lease and the building only cared about extracting more and more money from me. I would not recommend anyone moving here.

Do not move here!!!! Construction has been awful. If you work from home, you will not be able to work in peace or have meetings without disruption. When we resigned our lease they forgot to mention this conveniently. Everyone in the building has been moving out every week and we wish we could do the same. Management does not offer ANY concessions and has continued to raise the rent prices. Friends in similar buildings in the Gold Coast have better amenities and are not subjected to construction for hours on end.

Do not move here! Currently repairing building facade and jackhammering balconies for the past 4 months and until 2023!! It is MISERABLE!! Management even increased rents during this period for existing tenants who are affected before work was underway on their unit. Refuse to reimburse for costs of noise canceling headphones, WeWorks, or rent concessions. Whatever you do don’t move here in the next 12mo.
You won't live without intense construction if you live here for the next three years. Avoid at all costs.

Major construction, awful management. You won't be able to live in peace for 5 out of 7 days for the majority of the day. No communication from the office, just horrible. Construction lasting more than 3 years. Over priced. Do not rent here.
There is major construction for the next three years, making work from home impossible. Do not rent from here if you want peace and quiet during the week.

Do not rent at One East Delaware!  Jack hammering from Concrete restoration project is relentless from 8 am-4 pm each day.  Forget working from home!  Management underplays extent of construction.  You will not be able to use your balcony due to noise and dust.  Construction is on 3 of 4 sides of the building so no apartment is unaffected. Construction project will take 3-4 years.  Many balconies have to be demolished and rebuilt due to extensive concrete integrity failures.  There are many better rental options in the neighborhood.  Choose them!

Careful when looking here. Seems like a great place at first. Other buildings in the same price range have far better amenities for the price. Fitness center is very minimal. There is only one small "meeting room" you can reserve if you want to work from home, which gets booked up quickly. The "water feature" on the patio has been under construction since I got here. The apartment doors automatically lock, so if you step out into the hallway (i.e. to take the trash to the chute) remember your keys or you get locked out. Getting locked out wouldn't be a big deal but the doorman will not let you into your apartment until you agree to pay 50 dollars. Consider before renting here.

One East Delaware closed its package room and stopped accepting all resident packages. Instead, they added $15 per month to everyone’s lease and rerouted all packages to an offsite fulfillment services. We then have to use an app to have our packages delivered to us after they’ve been delivered offsite. That’s right: we have to pay to have our packages delayed and rerouted. Other buildings in the neighborhood do not do this, so why move here?
Good property with really nice remodel. Friendly, helpful and responsive staff.

There are as many apartments as their are restaurants to choose from in Chicago.  As a service industry professional, I understand that most products are the same; every apartment can have a pool/patio/gym ect.  What separates fantastic places to live is the service, and 1 east delivers on that.  The people that work here are simply the best, and the reason why tenants are happy!

I have lived at 1000 S. Clark for 3 years, and it is a great place to live! The amenities are amazing. I love the full-floor gym and very nice public spaces.  The management group plans guest events and provides free food, drinks, and a fun time.

On March 11, I applied for an apartment and disclosed my credit situation upfront. Underwriting assured me it wouldn't be an issue, yet I was denied on March 13. I paid $515, expecting a $450 refund for the admin fee, but it hasn't arrived after 17 days. Despite multiple calls, promises of reimbursement, and filling out online forms, there's been no response. Despite assurances of callbacks, including from the manager, nothing has materialized. This experience has been frustrating, and I advise against engaging with this organization. A denial should trigger an immediate refund, and the lack of organization suggests possible malpractice.
I have really enjoyed my time with Mondial River West. I have found the staff to be very welcoming and quick to help me with anything that I need.
kelsey made the whole process very easy & as stress free as possible. super friendly staff & all together so happy with our decision to move in.

It’s been great here and we’ve only moved in a week ago. Love the vibes here, everyone is friendly and there are a lot of adorable dogs. The staff are awesome which I feel makes this place ten times better.
We love everyone at Mondial, it really feels like home. Everytime we have an issue, maintenance is very quick to help. Every time we need Lizette she is there and willing to help with a smile.
It’s the best building I have stayed in Chicago yet. The management team is amazing and same with everyone who lives here. Hopefully I will be able to resign!

Once upon a time, it was a great building, but it deteriorated within the last year or so. Problems includes, stolen packages constantly, stolen bikes, 8-5 water shut downs for days in a month, electricity issue for an entire floor, unauthorized parties thrown by non-resident selling alcohol and shooting off fireworks, no front doorman/security, unable to access garage multiple days, not even one moving cart, unorganized package room, almost never cleaned dog run, missing gym equipment (while they claimed they are replacing with new stuff), the "we sincerely apologize... I'm taking this super seriously... I'll personally oversee it..." but do nothing management, the list goes on and on. For the price you are paying, you can go any building in River North and get better than this. The only person that's keeping this place together is the maintenance guy Burim who's super friendly, responsible, and actually get things done!

The promoted rooftop parties with a cover, DJ, and liquor are completely out of hand. Summertime at the Ardus is like living in a hotel with a club. You will see random strangers coming in and out. It’s not a safe environment. There is no doorman and nobody regulates any of this. Packages are stolen. I’ve seen homeless people trying to get in and ask me to let them in because they have gotten away with staying in the lobby overnight. I’ve seen people sleep all night in the lobby. Management is unresponsive at all times. The only thing that they are responsive about is maintenance issues and that’s because the maintenance guy is amazing.

Apathetic ownership. Unsafe conditions. There is no doorman on first floor and front door as well as elevator/stairwell requires key fob. Sounds fine, but there was a fire a few weeks back and the fire dept. had to break the front door, break mailroom door, break maint closet door to get in. The fire alarms on other floors also did not go off. 

A maintenance person attacked our dog when they came in the unit. Tried swinging at our dog with a hammer. Flats apologized and attempted to resolve the situation, but their logo is a DOG! You think they would have training and procedures from the get-go. 

All of the outlets in the entire building and in every single unit are upside down. That is a great example of the lack of attention to detail and care. 

Location is fantastic. Price was at/below market- you get what you pay for!

Poor Service, Misinformation, and too many unfulfilled promises. 

Location is perfect but is overshadowed by several problems:
- H-VAC system is controlled by management who switches the system from heating to AC every 6 months. You cannot decide for yourself. 
- One elevator is always not operational and the only other elevator is a hit or miss. So you have to use stairs. 
- Packaged are kept in a locked room that only management has they key. Good luck getting packages when you want them. 
- Internet only works with certain routers (which management won't tell you) because the modem is centrally controlled by management.
- Units do not have exhaust vents above the stove, only a circulator fan which, depending on what you're cooking, will set off the Fire Alarm.
- Management rarely responds to emails, is unreliable, and seemingly inexperienced. 

OVERALL: for the price of these units, there are way too many unfulfilled promises.
I just moved in two weeks ago, and I am so happy! Aside from my fabulous apartment, the community is fantastic and I already feel at home!

This building is wonderful. The entire team is friendly and helpful. The building itself is well maintained and has a ton of great amenities. I love working from home in the WFH office spaces and hitting the fitness center.

1225 is arguably the best building in Old Town, Chicago. The amenities are clean and wonderful to use, the staff is friendly and consistent, and the location is unbeatable! Community events happen frequently, allowing residents to connect and chat. Both residents and staff members are friendly. This building is exceptionally dog-friendly, and my pup has made plenty of friends here!

I've been a resident at 1225 for almost two years and absolutely loved my time here. The combination of location, amenities, and quality of units makes this the best in-class apartment complex in Old Town. My favorite part of living here is staff who create a true sense of community.

From the time I came to take a tour to the time that I moved in, the leasing team has been exceptional and made my move super easy. They are easy to get a hold of and quick to respond with any questions. The apartment was immaculate when I moved in, it is quiet and the amenities are a nice plus.

1225 Old Town is a great residence and an oasis in a chaotic city. I’ve lived in a few different apartments in this building and have enjoyed my time in each. I’ve also very much enjoyed watching the building evolve as management is constantly evolving and updating both the aesthetics and functionality. The staff is very friendly and helpful as well.

This building tries to market themselves as a luxury building but it is far from it. From poor design, poor management, and lack of amenities it’s not worth it. The actual units are nice if you get one with a balcony. 
On example of the pain of living here is that packages are consistently left outside because the stupid digital door intercom system never seems to work. So without a door person or way for delivery people to get in, your package might be left next to the door for anyone to take. 
Also, this building markets having a bike room which it absolutely does not.
It's an amazing location. Staff is friendly. Leasing is attentive. Building has great amenities, epically the rooftop pool!

There’s no care or thought at this property. The amenities are dirty, the sense of community / events are nearly non-existent since every event is hosted mid-day when everyone is at work. 

The lobby is constantly in shambles and the front desk concierge sit and watch TV on their phones and ignore you when you need help. Just look around you walk in… the plastic shield between the lobby in the front desk is covered in filth. There’s paper signs scotch-taped up that are brown and needed to be replaced ages ago. They can’t even put their dog treats from the box from the store into something that looks somewhat presentable.

Even looking past the details, while the apartments are nice, the way the front desk concierge and the management treat their people is enough of a reason to not renew my lease or even remotely recommend it to anyone wanting to live in a high-rise downtown.

Overall 805 is a decent building with friendly and helpful staff but there have been several major issues with the building itself that create cause for concern. On several occasions glass from the windows/balconies have shattered/fallen 10  stories onto the the street below, the rooftop pool (while a great amenity) started leaking one night and flooded water down on the entire building causing the elevators to be down for an extended period of time and required significant work in many of the apartments. There have also been heating issues on the 4th floor that have led to a closure of the dog run at times when a dog owner would want it to be available most. On your average day it is a great building to be in but there seem to be major issues that shouldn't happen in such a new building and make you question what will happen next.

The property management team at Eight O Five is one of the best I have ever encountered, working always in a professional and friendly manner. I worked with Theresa and she tackled any issues that came up without any delay. The maintenance crew and concierge at this property is also wonderful. The amenities are well kept and very, very nice. This is by far the best rooftop in all of Chicago!

You pretty much can't beat living in a new building. The 1 bedrooms have floor to ceiling windows and if you are higher than the 14th floor - the views are incredible. There is a large patio on each 1 bedroom unit that can fit plenty of furniture (a glass wall on the side is cool but almost scary if you're on a higher floor). The bedroom is large and has a huge closet. The only way it could be better is if they installed more high tech appliances - they are pretty standard. 

The location also can't be beat - you're next to two different types of trains and plenty of bus lines and walkable to different neighborhoods with bars, restaurants, shopping, etc. The rooftop views are also amazing - but as people move in, the roof gets a little crowded and the pool is on the small side. There is a gym that has new equipment and plenty of hang out/work space. The street is a little loud but since the building is new  - you don't have to worry about hearing neighbors. 

Overall this is an awesome building and well worth the price.

I just moved in a week ago but already love my place.  The views are fantastic, floor to ceiling windows, huge balcony, w/d, just all around beautiful.  The only downside is the price - renting in Chicago is SO expensive!

I've been in this building for a little over a year and have moved from an older apartment into one of their newly renovated units. The new apartments have very nice finishes and are fairly affordable given the awesome downtown location.  My apartment is big, great closet space and I have a view of the lake and downtown chicago.  The maintenance people are always very quick and responsive, I would recommend this place highly,

I have been living at Chestnut Place for over four years now, and recently moved from a "classic" unit to one of the renovated units.  To begin, the location of this building is unbeatable.  Being two blocks from the Mag Mile, a five minute walk from Oak Street Beach and a two minute walk from the red line train is amazing! I can literally walk to anywhere I need to go -- there are six grocery stores within a half a mile (Potash Brothers, Whole Foods, Trader Joes, Treasure Island, two Jewels) as well as plenty of shopping and dining options, not to mention like five Starbucks within a two block radius.  

Apart from the location, the building itself for the most part has been great.  About a year and a half ago, the building came under new management which has brought about a number of changes.  The new management company, Golub, has been working on slowly renovating the building unit by unit as people move out.  The unit that I lived in for four years was definitely "retro"... it has wall to wall carpet and appliances from 1982 (literally!).  The unit I recently moved into (as well as all the newly updated units) are gorgeous -- dark wood cabinets, stainless steel appliances, marble counter tops, and really nice distressed greyish laminate wood floors.  I see this as a HUGE upgrade from what the older units look like.  I know they also have big plans for renovated the lobby and communal areas to be completed over the next year.  The building as a big laundry room, a shared outdoor patio with two grills, and an adequate gym.  The building is also dog friendly as of about year ago (!!). The door staff and maintenance team (old faces and new) are all awesome. 

There are a couple of things that residents are not super thrilled about.  There is a parking garage attached to the building, and when Golub took over they sold the garage to Standard Parking.  As a result, monthly parking rates went up a LOT -- $170.00 per month to $245.00 per month ($330.00 if you want a reserved spot).  They also dedicated a bunch of spots on the first and second level to Enterprise Rent-a-Car, so residents typically have to park on the third or fourth floor which is a pain.  Also, storage units used to be included in the rent and now cost an additional $20.00 a month :(.  

Overall, I would say good outweighs the bad!  Amazing location and reasonable rent for the area.

Helped my daughter move across the country to Chicago. 1000 miles and a smooth move. Nice building and amenities with an easy move-in. Woke up the first day of lease with a flood in unit from next door neighbors AC unit. Had to move out for several days. At least 4 apartments flooded and it's been a nightmare since. Rug damage, picture frame damage from restoration company along with bed frame damage. Ugh. I understand from neighbors other units have had issues also. No help from management, no response to emails, totally ghosted. Challenging once your in to get out whole.

Lived here for 2 years. Extremely quiet and safe. Attentive staff and front desk and front door man 24/7 on staff. Clean, extremely fast maintenance requests (within 60 minutes!) Tremendous walkability score. Been very happy here, highly recommend to a single woman.

The building is the only building that charges for EV charging on top of its super expensive garage fee. Leasing staff bully the residents. Major smoking problem, the building always smells of weed. Terrible appliances. Look somewhere else!!!!

It's been two months since I moved in here, someone on the same floor keeps smoking and smell comes into my unit. I requested the leasing office multiple times to fix the issues, still not fixed. If you do not smoke and you are little sensitive about smells then you might need to reconsider to move in here.

Decorated like a 5 star hotel, yet offering 1 star service. The leasing office obviously have difficulty in presenting professionalism: either reply customer email without salutation or no reply at all, treat customer with arrogance from nowhere, not at all supportive during application process, etc. A kind reminder - you’re paid to offer a high-quality service at a branded luxury building, your pay check, in the end, comes from customers.

The Porte staff is completely useless. They don't respond in a timely manner, when they do they're super unprofessional and they're just looking for your money.

Save yourself a long application process and lease somewhere else else in the area that is going to be worth your buck in every category.

The welcome meeting was really good. Lizette took me around the building, provided me all the necessary stuff and answered my hundreds of questions. The building almost feels like a neighborhood because almost every time you get in the elevator there will be a dog with you which automatically makes everyone more friendly. The amenities are nice and even the shared spaces are clean and well taken care of. The front desk workers are incredibly kind and willing to answer all your questions with a smile.

I’ve loved living at Niche 905! Management and building staff are always very friendly and helpful, and the community activities are always a nice way to connect with neighbors and learn about new local businesses!

I love niche 905! I use their gym everyday and I’m starting to see a difference. Their elevators work fast. The dog park is sensational! Everything in this building is so convenient and management has been so nice!
I’m impressed with the building! So new so clean and such a nice smell.! The gym is awesome. And yes the best part is coffee machine in the lobby
The concierge staff are wonderful and all the amenities are spotless! I would highly recommend living here and taking advantage of all they have to offer
Staff is friendly and helpful! Lobby is always clean and smells amazing. Packages are easily accessible and handled with care. The area has a lot to offer.
I've had a great experience here with RW terrace. They're really accommodating and work hard to ensure that you're stay is a good time.
The apartments have a great layout, the community is nice, pretty and peaceful. Neighbors are great people and everyone looks out for each other. Great place to live!
Great and efficient work. They resolved my AC issues within the first 24 hours.

Always looking forward to coming home from a long day of work where there's always peaceful, quiet and clean community! And on off days or holidays being able to grill or relax on the rooftop or patio it's just serene. And the planned community events by our property manager is always engaging and something to look forward to. Can't forget our maintenance team they do attend to all requests within decent turn around time including off hours that require emergency handling. I'm happy and content with RAVENSWOOD TERRACE!
Great community, great apartments, great common areas, great customer service, great location and safe. Honestly is a great place to live!
It is a great place to live for a small family, young couple or individual. Great location, security, close down units, clean and safe environment and neighborhood.
Maintenance always comes quickly for anything that  is wrong, love the building team! The amenities are always clean and smell good. I can’t hear out her tenants in my apartment.
Great facility and staff! The front desk concierge is very friendly. Any questions that I have they are available to assist. I would highly recommend staying here.
I love living in this building. Our new property management company is lovely. The ultimate luxury mid-rise experience in South Loop! I would prefer if the social room had longer open hours though.
Living here has been nice, the amenities and the building residents are amazing. Location is a plus as well. Parking tends to be a bit difficult.
I had an anmazing experience from the beginning; touring the unit and building to signing a lease. Good staff from the leasing office to concierge.
I love the atmosphere, the kind neighbors. The building overall feels like home. My apartment is perfect for me. I love the amenities and the neighborhood

Living at 1407 S Michigan Ave has been an exceptional experience, thanks largely to the outstanding new management team. They’ve truly gone above and beyond to enhance every aspect of the building. The recent improvements are noticeable and appreciated—from the carpets to the windows and overall cleanliness.

The pool area is meticulously maintained, making it a perfect spot to relax, and the upgraded grills have made summer BBQs even better. Elevator maintenance is top-notch and the addition of a new TV station in the lobby has added a nice touch to the common areas.

One of the standout features is the new concierge service, which has been a game-changer for convenience. On top of that, the management has introduced a fantastic resident app that is not only functional but packed with perks that make daily living easier and more enjoyable.

Overall, the new management has transformed 1407 S Michigan Ave into a modern, well-maintained, and community-focused place to live.
10/10 recommend for the downtown feel but quieter area. I love this location . Concierge team is amazing as well, Robert was super helpful during my move in!
I love 1407 on Michigan! The staff and the amenities are excellent. The area is very quiet but yet very close to all the fun stuff in the downtown area.

Everyone here are very nice and friendly. The building is always clean. Very pleased so far.i loved the fact that they’ve been upgrading and making sure that the tenants can enjoy the amenities for the summer.
The staff are very sweet and attentive here. When you enter the building they greet you. If you have any maintenance request they are right on it. I would highly recommend living here.
1407 is a GREAT place to live.  The community has beautiful amenities and in the idea neighborhood.  The building is close to public transportation, restaurants, grocery stores, and a park.
The neighborhood is great close to down town and public transportation. The staff is nice, The amenities are nice and well maintained. In the units the features are updated.

Rented an apartment for a year and it was a decent place to live, however, we have never gotten our $500 deposit back from moving in.  They sent me an expired check and refuse to answer my calls.  Tried to call the onsite manager as well as corporate offices.   Very frustrating!!!
There is absolutely no better deal in this area. The building and the staff are both extremely welcoming and friendly. Highly recommend!
You won’t find a better building or a better deal in the area. Highly recommend!

Be prepared for constant construction noise and dogs barking through the night. This building is cockroach infested and management does nothing. Work Order My issue was resolved quickly and efficiently. Thank you, Juan!
Kitchen light over sink  Done in record time from work order submission thank you

I'm with you again I have lived in these apartments for two and a half years and this year I extended the lease for another year. I especially love it here, and I must say it has been a great experience. The apartments are equipped with all the necessary amenities for a comfortable stay, and I would particularly highlight the presence of a washing machine and a dryer. The location of the building is also ideal, offering both convenience and tranquility. The River City condo building has owner and renter units throughout the building.  The location is convenient, which is really where it shines.  My unit is a bit outdated but in good shape.  The view of the river is nice and the facilities work.  The price is good for what you get, particularly in a part of the city that is very expensive.
It in printers row by river side hence river city,it is very good condo style building.The rental apartment goes like hot cakes here.Its has it own sun deck and grand atrium.

River City Condos is an iconic building located on the Chicago River. Its the perfect location for young professionals working in the Loop. Although you're living downtown, the areas is very quiet other than the occasional noise from the boat tours and boat partiers.  The security staff is amazing! The building has a beautiful rooftop patio, the only downside is that it is often crowded with families having barbecues and other gatherings. Stay far away from this building and property management company!

Would give 0 stars if possible. ZERO. 

I have lived here for 4 years, across 2 different apartment units. If it were not for Covid I would’ve moved out after one year. 

In my 4 years living at Buena Terrace, we’ve had 3 property managers- this much turnover tells you just how poorly Horizon Realty corporate management is. 

ONLY live here if your other option is welfare. 

Water leaking in units, verbal promises made my management that went unkept, horrible laundry room, and elevators that malfunction weekly. 

You can find better apartments locally for cheaper.

I think there are nicer and better-managed buildings in the area at the same price point. Just moved in and loving it so far. Everyone has been super helpful during the move in process. The outdoor space is really nice to have in the summer.
Love living here! Clean apartment, great management team, and great neighbors! Awesome rooftop and balcony spaces. Highly recommend to anyone who is looking!

For the most part, everything is almost perfect. The package room is a mess if you aren’t using fetch and if you are using fetch sometimes the scheduling doesn’t always work. It’s been good so far, but they did leave my strings to my shades a tangled mess. I’m excited to start living in such a wonderful area and be walking distances from everything I need.
Have loved living at the Hensley great tenants and management. Ever since this new management team took over things have been running smoothly!

We’ve enjoyed living at the Hensley. The location is great, and we enjoy our large balcony and the awesome city views from it. The floor plan has been great and exactly what we need

Management is very responsive, the building is always clean, and the neighborhood is great. 10/10 would recommend!

Have lived here for several years, very easy to get down to the lakefront path and other surrounding neighborhoods. Building is fairly new and only 5 years old- I would recommend

I love my apartment, everything is always so well taken care of here. Everyone working here and neighbors are extremely helpful and nice. This is a great location and building! The management is very responsive and the rooftop is pretty sweet with pano views!

Management could not be worse if they tried. It was nice that they asked their agents to make fake reviews about the building. I have lived here at The Belmont for 3 years now and I still love it! It has everything you want in an apartment building. Prime location on the lake and direct access to multiple bus lines, amazing rooftop, attentive maintenance and upkeep, brand new gym (with free classes!), market/Dentist/dry cleaning/nail salon all attached to the building, and incredible staff. 
From the leasing agents to the concierge, they all feel like family now! Every time we’ve switched apartments, Brittany and the leasing agents have made the transition seamless.  I know that for as long as my husband and I stay in Chicago, we will be living at The Belmont by Reside!

The Belmont by Reside is a well maintained building that boasts any/all amenities a renter could ask for, with a great location, and rooms.  We just re-signed for our fourth year in this building, which is a testament to the units, building, staff, and location.

Pros:
Beautiful building - converted hotel that has a welcoming lobby, old hotel detailing combined with modern touches.
Great staff - the maintenance staff and front desk staff are all attentive, friendly, and we have never had to wait on a maintenance request in our three plus years of renting (including a plumbing issue in our shower requiring removal of dry wall, which was addressed and repainted the same weekend).
Rooftop - great view overlooking the Belmont Harbor, multiple direct feed gas grills, a fire pit, and herb gardens for tenant use.
Others - good storage in-unit, additional storage available, very pet friendly including a common pet bath/grooming area for tenant use, bike maintenance space and tools available for tenant use, very well maintained gym, common rec room spaces, and yoga/workout studio attached to the gym.

Cons:
Older bones of the past hotel, so the old concrete/brick walls diminish wi-fi signals to rooms further away from your wireless router (But this can be made a pro, because you don't hear your neighbors).
Bathrooms are a little on the small side.
No laundry in-unit, but plenty of machines are available in their laundry room.

Finally, the location is great.  The broadway strip only continues to increase in restaurants and shops, a Mariano's in going in at Broadway and Wellington, and your access to the lake front and express buses makes for easy commuting.

- Fixed utility package (does not fluctuate)
- Concierge 
- Great rooftop
- Local deals for being a Reside resident
- Resident activities
- Lobby is nice

Cons: 
- The free internet is terrible (they tell you it is free)
- Noise isn't bad (From the bedroom) but you can definitely hear your neighbors from the living room
- Emails from management are VERY annoying
- Fuse keeps getting blown (though they are quick to fix it)

The champagne of apartment life...The Belmont offers sparkling renovated interiors from the lobby to the roof top. Residents are bubbling with joy and views of the harbor and the iconic Chicago skyline.
Very pleasant team. Very courteous and informative.

 Based on my experience here -   The "luxury" amenities are 2 treadmills and an elliptical in a room with no ventilation, the "dog run" is a 10x10 turf in the back with lights that go off every 3 minutes at night. We absolutely love living at 3450! Our quiet, spacious, one bedroom apartment has a highly functional floorplan with plenty of storage. The amenities are incredible at the building! The views from the sundeck, pool, and hospitality suite are unmatched. It's the perfect place to simply relax or entertain! The building is up to date and meets all of our needs. The property is also in a wonderful location. There is easy access to the Lakefront Trail, a short walk to N Broadway or Wrigley Field, and several public transportation options! Finally, the management and staff are always kind and helpful when we need anything!

I have lived at Hawthorne House for two and a half years and would recommend it to anyone looking for an apartment in Chicago. The amenities, including a rooftop pool, rooftop sundeck, and gym are clean, convenient and incredible to have access to. Even though it’s an apartment in Chicago, the bedrooms are surprisingly large as the building was built in the 60s. Enhancement to communal areas are done often, for example the redesign of the sundeck happened less than two years ago. My absolute favorite part of living here is the people, both tenants and staff. The building has a diverse group of people living here and the staff create multiple events a year to provide social opportunities. The staff also helped me put on a proposal for friends which goes to show how supportive they are of the tenants. Lakeview East is one of the top neighborhoods to live in Chicago, and I found the best place to live in East Lakeview. Highly recommend!

I moved to 3450 N Lake Shore Drive a little over a month ago and couldn't be happier. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. They make you feel like you're really part of a community. The building is very well kept. The pool and sundeck on the roof can't be beat. My apartment is spacious with tons of storage space, and the view is spectacular. The few maintenance issues I've had have been taken care of quickly. I would highly recommend this property.

I've lived at 3450 for a year and I love it. The views may be the best in the city — and that's saying something; its location is primo — in a great neighborhood that has multiples of everything and all of it within easy walking distance; it's literally just across the street from the lake and Chicago's sprawling lakefront park system which includes 18 miles of continuous car-free trails; and there's every mode of public transit including a bus stop just a stone's throw from the front door. We've got a sprawling, tricked out roof deck and a pool. (Alas it isn't a saline pool and there is no hot tub or sauna.) There's a fine workout area that includes a separate room with wood floors for yoga, etc; and a lounge. And everything is clean & very well maintained by a friendly & attentive staff. (I think a good measure of a building's quality is how long its staff stays employed there and the crew here sticks around for, sometimes, decades, making their careers and helping build a sense of community.) The units are spacious with good floor plans and, as I said, amazing views. If Chicago's long dark winters get you down, choose a south-facing apartment and drink in the abundant light. (That's what I did & it's made all the difference.) As for the tenants, they span every age cohort. I recommend it to young people just starting out on their own who want a safe building in a vibrant neighborhood. There are families here too. And there are older professionals & retirees. It's a good mix; everyone seems friendly and to be on their best behavior. The building hosts numerous activities including brunches and barbecues, which is a nice touch. I should also note that buildings like this one are way more energy efficient than single-family units and smaller structures. Before moving back here, I lived in a house in a warmer state and my monthly heating and cooling bills were literally 6 to 8 times more than they are here!
What do I wish was different? Like many buildings from this era and earlier, there are fewer garage spaces than tenants with cars, so there's a waiting list and you'll need to park elsewhere while you wait. And the HVAC system is centralized and has just 3 modes: heat, cool, and off. Tenants control just how much warm or cool air they get. With October still warm &  the sun pouring in all day, I wish I could turn on the AC.

But these are small gripes. I love living here!!

When writing a review for a particular place – it is hard knowing where to start and the same goes for this review of (for) Hawthorne House Apartments. If this were a hotel, I would give it an unofficial 7-star rating. Being right on Lake Shore Dr. you are blessed with an outstanding sunrise view over Lake Michigan (facing East) and a beautiful sunset (facing West) – the unique placement allows for views in all 4 directions (depending upon your unit number – mine happens to be a Southwest sunset view). Another incredible bonus is the ease of public transportation; there is a bus stop less than 200 ft away, another one 1.5blks North, and one more 1blk West (all major streets) – there are 2 different train stations less than a 15-minute walk (Northwest and Southwest). Oh, and I forgot that this area is surrounded by incredible food, boutique shops, and a major grocery store within a 5 to 7-minute walk.

When friends have asked me about the building amenities – they are truly is second-to-none. Besides the standard washer/dryers available – there is a small lounge with free wifi off of the laundry area. On the top floor is a gym, sundeck, and pool (both brand new) – another lounge (much bigger and completely new and can be rented for business or parties) – plus free wifi. An outdoor seating area with a fabulous 360-degree view (brand new as well) of the entire city and lake. Also, when you talk about service – most people ask about the building personnel. Well, the staff is another reason why I give it an unofficial 7-star rating. The office staff is world-class. They solve issues in a timely manner, always greet you by name when they see you, and best of all, they see you as family and not a tenant. The security staff is one of the most professional yet personable and the maintenance crew is always there whenever needed regardless of the time. 

There is more that I can go on about, but I am confident that you will see from what I have written that this location is the best in the City of Chicago. If you are looking for safety, peace of mind, a pleasant neighborhood, ease of movement, and more, then Hawthorne House is the recommendation that I would make.

Thank you,

HH Tenant

Management truly only cares if they're legally required to do so. They tried to promote this massive construction project as "a benefit to all residents" and were extremely deceptive about it up front. They scheduled construction in my unit at 8am ON A HOLIDAY and threatened to fine me $13,000-15,000 when I asked if they could not work in my unit that day in observance of the holiday. They refused to provide any rent reductions, despite my bathroom being half-functional for almost two months (removed vanity, lights, mirror, and all personal items).

Over priced. Appliances are over 30 years old. Charge you for common area utilities in addition to your own utility bill. So if you travel alot or away for a month still expect to pay $60-100 in utilities you didn't use.  Who does that? Its not a condo association . Charge you for every package you receive.  Manager and Assistant manager has lost the understanding of customer service.  No parking available.

This place sucks too many oldies and over priced!!! Appliances are way outdated do your self a favor and go somewhere else!!! Trust, I regret moving here!!! This place sucks, always something wrong, and rude.

Way overpriced, outdated, poor amenities, heavy restrictions on pool with rude staffing. Very deceitful practices on move out for illegitimate charges and poor communication trying to hassle me 4  months after move out.  Not worth moving here nor would recommend to anyone- you can do better!

Do not live here!!! Living here was tolerable, until I got a job across the country and needed to move. They charge you for absolutely everything they can find. To start, this complex is already overpriced for what you get. The view and location is great but the appliances and units are very outdated. They raise the rent a ridiculous amount every year but use the money for mundane things like chandeliers in the lobby. They are slowly renovating the units but the bathrooms are still terrible with old sinks and bathtubs. They don't even have thermostats in the units! There are many other buildings for similar prices that are more up to date and have much better management. They took every opportunity of us leaving to make it as difficult and expensive as possible. I lived there less than 2 years, am an extremely clean person, and they charged me over $700 in cleaning fees when I moved out. I had HIRED people to clean the unit and they still did this. I would not recommend anyone live in this apartment complex!

This is great apartment building for enjoying Chicago summer - rooftop pool and sundeck/grills, close to Lake Shore path, parks, and beaches, and amazing SE views of city skyline and Lake Michigan.  Great amenities with onsite gym, laundry, package receiving room, and valet parking garage. Also great location for busses and many restaurants, shops, grocery stores, nightlife, etc. The 1 bedroom apartments are decent size with good closet space, but upgrades to kitchens, and bathrooms would be nice.  Very friendly and helpful staff and overall great community feel.

Love Hawthorne House!  The apartments are really nice and well maintained. There's security/doorman, receiving room, valet parking, zipcars and friendly management staff. The rooftop pool on the 41st floor is the best for summer in Chicago. They also have a party room and fitness room for use. 
All in all, it's a great place to live. And the views are fantastic.

Great view. Prefect location. Awesome amenities from rooftop pool to gym overlooking Wrigley Field. Quiet building. Friendly and respectful tenants. And last but not least, highly attentive staff. Best housing decision. Ever.

I took a sublease for two months in a 1 bedroom apartment. The tower is gorgeous and the location is great, close to public transportation, to the loop and to the highway, one block from a Jewel-Osco and great bars and restaurants around. The apartment is pretty nice, new kitchen appliances and huge bathroom. The downside is that the windows are not sound proof and you can hear the trains of Olgivie and the Bloomers factory all day long. Another downside is the water pressure in the shower or the tap; sometimes it just cuts off or runs out of water. It seems that if your neighbor is taking a shower at the same time it doesn't work. Great location and nice apartment but too pricey considering the problem of the noise and the water pressure.

Searching for an apartment in Chicago can be a dreadful process, looking from building to biulding for your dream location, that also fits your budget. Yet this wasn't the case for myself, I hit the jackpot with Alta K Station. You move into a family when you move to Alta, from the amazing staff that makes five star resorts look bad, to the residents that immediately welcome you like family, and make eveyday fun and enjoyable. Moreover, you dont just move into a biulding because of the residents you move in for the location, amenities, and of course your living space. Alta is located right on the edge of River North Chicago in a growing safe neighborhood where you have an  abundant amount of things to do, from having the world famous merchandise mart down the street, to being able to eat at some of Chicago's best restaurants just a block away, oh and the fact that Chicago's best night life scene is just a short walk away on hubbard street, so location with Alta is an easy 10/10. Furthermore, the amenities at Alta are the best this amazing city has to offer, from the georgous out door pool with sweeping views of the city  and spa area, to the basketball, and movie theater, not to mention the assoment of amazing complimentry progarms they offer, from yoga to personal and group fitness classes, proving Alta does not cut corners with their amenities. Last, but not least the aparments at Alta are something striaght from a luxury dream magazine, from the updated kitchens with flawless appliances , to the large spacious living rooms that really give you the freedom to   Piece together your dream design, and to top it all off Alta right on the edge of the city gives you jaw dropping views from every unit in the biulding, from the amazing poster like views of the sears tower, to the fantastic dream like views of the handcock over looking beautiful lake michigan. All in all, if your looking for an affordable luxury lifestyle in Chicago , you will not be cheating yourself by moving into the perfect 10/10 Alta building, take it from someone who knows :)

Alta at K Station is a modern, feature-packed building with a very young, motivated, and attractive group of people. Between the gym, fitness classes, theater, and pool with margarita bar, you may even find yourself looking for a reason to leave the building.

The staff is helpful and polite. All of my requests for repairs or battery changes in detectors have been addressed immediately. Not that you'll be needing to call often though. The appliances are new, and work great.

The only negatives I would say are that the crowd can be a bit rowdy at times, and that it can be very intimidating to actually swim in the pool  when so many fit people are just sitting around it enjoying margaritas. As far as typical tenant complaints go though, I don't really hear them.

The yuppie palace comes highly recommended.

At 1600sqft, we have more than enough space.  A pluthera of windows on three sides of the apartment and a door on the fourth, create an amazing cross-breeze on cooler days and nights.  Central Heat and A/C that we control is a major plus.  We are less than a 5 minute walk to Target, Aldi and Jewel, so shopping couldn't be more convenient.  As for transportation, we have the #151 and #36 bus at our door and are a block from the Red Line 'L'.  Our friends that drive never have issues finding parking either.

We didn't move into an apartment we moved into a home in a community.

All I can say is, "Wow!" Such an amazing place to live and management is outstanding. 
Beyond the great building and location, what really makes it such a great place to live is the fantastic team of people who work here including, the team in the management/leasing office, everyone at the front desk, including maintenance team. The amenities such as the gym, business center and newly built rooftop deck are wonderful and always clean. I highly recommend Webster House.

I typically find myself in a crunch when talking about managment as a tenant but here it is the opposite of that case. They are incredibly easy to get in touch with, they meet building requests very soon and they respect our privacy. The building of itself is beautiful and the history is rich. Living here and being surrounded with so much to do is something I will truly miss.
I really enjoyed it. There was definitely a great atmosphere. You don’t feel too far from anything. I’d definitely stay here again

I have lived in Webster House for many years.  The building has seen better days, and is outdated in many respects.  Instead of making major costly renovations, in an effort to attract new tenants management recently began replacing the apartments' carpeting with wood floors.  When this was done to the apartment above mine, my apartment became very noisy, with banging from the sound of the tenants above walking, and their child running, on the bare floors.  When the manager came to my apartment, she agreed that the noise was excessive, and promised to fix the problem.  But she did not.  When I again called to complain several weeks later, a different manager simply told me to get over it.  Management is now committed to the new wood floors, and I am looking for a new place to live.  So a warning to prospective tenants: if you rent in Webster House, your apartment may be very noisy.  And if it is, don't expect management to care.

This is a fantastic building to live in if you are looking for a central location in the Chicago neighborhoods. Webster House is just a short distance from Wrigley Field, the lake, and Michigan Avenue. It is less than a block to a few prominent bus stops and right across the street from the free zoo! There is a new daycare attached to the building and a school across the street as well. The building staff are extremely friendly and there is a 24/hour doorman which makes the building feel even more safe and secure. The decor in the lobby is that of an old hotel and the high vaulted ceilings make each apartment very special and unique. I have been here 2 years and plan on staying a while. You feel as though you are surrounded by winding paths through the park, yet you are simultaneously just on the edge of an infinite number of city-like things to explore!

The most unprofessional management company I’ve ever dealt with and I’ve lived in many properties in my 16 years of living in Chicago. Every week something goes wrong. This is not an exaggeration. Elevators not working (multiple occasions) Fob system not working. Hot water not working. A/C not working. Heat not working. They don’t not keep up with the appearance and cleanliness of the building. Trust me. There are way better buildings in the area.

Elevators are always broken (at most 2 of 3 are active, 1 being a very old and very very slow service elevator). People always getting stuck in elevators. Apartments get hot in winter since the building is either in heat mode or cool mode. I've had my unit up to 80 deg at some point, even with my heat off in the unit (no way to cool down in heat mode besides window cracking). Walls are very thin, so you constantly hear your neighbors. Building always threatens to shut down weight room due to weights dropping. High fee for laundry. Appliances are old, issues with dish washer working. Long story short: great location, terrible building. The rent is extremely high in general, but especially for the quality of the building.

Living in the Gold Coast was an important factor as I work just a few blocks from here. There is a pool on the roof deck which I love to hang out and get a tan after work in the summer. We just had a really fun pool party PPM put on for FREE for all residents. The people are really friendly here and you really get this feeling of safety with a 24 hour doorman. I really do love living here and hope to stay here a few years more!

It is such an improvement from my roommate and I's last place. The staff is so friendly and accomidating, the maintenance is helpful and always available. The view from our window is beautiful each night and the space we have is incredible as well as the vast closet space! The area is wonderful for exploring and going out at night. Can't picturing living anywhere else

It had everything my roommate and I could possibly need to live a great life here. It's just far enough away from the city and is surrounded by beautiful buildings! The leasing staff was beyond helpful when we first toured. Couldn't imagine living anywhere else
The apartments are spacious, airy and nicely updated. Management is courteous and helpful. Come for those amenities but stay for the rooftop pool!
Lived here for 2 years, overall I’ve enjoyed it, the facility is nice and I like area. Great access to blue line and 66 and 56 buses, also a 20 min walk to west loop and wicker park.

Maintenance has been doing a terrific job with all needed repairs.  Everything is going well at Linkt.  And although initially skeptical, I like the addition of Fetch to the building's services.  Packages are delivered much more reliably now thanks to Fetch.

I have really enjoyed living here. My 3 bed/2 bath has been very spacious for my roommates and I. It’s super close to public transit. It’s a safe area that I feel comfortable walking in. The amenities are small, but they’re nice to have. I like the in-unit laundry too.
Great location great units, amenities are a bit lacking, grill area could be better. no major complaints about noise or cleanliness from other neighbors!

I’m halfway through my lease and have really enjoyed my time here. Great amenities, spacious units and a safe environment. It’s close to the blue line stop and several bus stops too. Great coffee shops nearby and only 2 stops from the Loop.

It’s okay. 
 Expensive parking and lots of issues with utilities. Microwave didn’t work, lights don’t work in any room and laundry room. When something breaks it takes forever to be fixed

If you’re nostalgic for the college dorm experience, this might be the place for you. I lived here for seven years and witnessed a noticeable decline in the overall atmosphere and caliber of tenants. What was once a building of mature, responsible residents gradually became home to a mix of young tenants with questionable standards of behavior. There were frequent disturbances—slamming doors, loud parties, and the sound of people running through the hallways at all hours. While affordable rent in a desirable area often attracts a diverse range of people, it unfortunately led to a drop in the building’s overall quality. The rooftop deck, once a nice place to relax with friends, became less enjoyable after an encounter with a disrespectful young bro who bummed a $20 cigar, took 2 puffs then set it down and walked away. Overall, while the location and amenities offered potential, the shift in the building’s atmosphere ultimately made it hard to fully enjoy the experience.

Very Charming 1 bd. apartment right in the heart of the Gold Coast. Good Value, off the beaten path, so no excessive street noise, and most importantly is has a charming Cafe/Wine bar right in the building that has been there for 30 years. It has an AMAZING roof top deck, exercise room, laundry, bike storage, and the staff is very friendly and helpful. Apartments.com made it easy for me to find this place.

Lived here 2+ years. It was a dumpster fire when I first moved in but did get a bit better with building improvements over the years. However, some significant issues such as my roof leaking for nearly 6 months (over my bed no less) and my balcony fence enclosure (paid extra...) not being built for 6 months were unacceptable.

Given the area (okay at best), the place is grossly overpriced and a lot of the "amenities" were unavailable during most of my tenure.

The cherry on top was my car getting towed by the apartment when I was trying to move out. There are ZERO authorized areas to park for cars for moving in/out. The apartment agreed to pay half the towing fee but never followed through despite multiple emails.

Avoid. If I wasn't in grad school and short on free time/cash, I would have moved out after the first lease...

Bedbugs EVERYWHERE!!! All my belongings were destroyed and had to live out of my car and move back in with my parents because I had NOTHING.  Meanwhile, I still had to pay off the rest of my lease.   I lost all my clothes, electronics, literally everything I owned was riddled with bedbugs.  I'm still traumatized by it and it happened 10 years ago.  The management did nothing to help other than notify me that there had been a massive infestation in the building and all tenants were notified.  Lucky me lived next door to the people that brought them into the building.  Management paid for professional treatments for them but did nothing for me.  I lost my belongings, my job, and my life for a bit because of this.   Never ever live here!!!

8 washers 8 dryers
90% of the time, only 1 or 2 are working.
188 units
Do the math
Complain til you are blue in the face. Does not change, ever. You will be forced to go to the laundromat out of necessity. Uber cost..laundromat prices…crowds…waiting.

We lived here for 3 years (2017-2020), and had a great experience. The apartment was capacious with a nice view. The best thing about the apartment is the management staff, and they are very professional and prompt in service. During our 3 years stay, we cannot recall any delay in the service whenever we needed. Excellent neighborhood in the city with stone throw distance from the lake, lots of good restaurants and grocery stores at the Broadway St, proximity to the bus stop, Addison red line make this place just perfect.

I have lived at Grace Street Towers (GST) for 12 years. It is truly a great place to live. The apartments are clean, well maintained, very quiet and safe. The pictures shown are very accurate. Wifi, cable and gas are included. You only pay electric. There is an exercise room, laundry, large patio with a BBQ and parking. The community at GST is diverse in age, race, religion, culture, sexual orientation and ability. The building hosts a community breakfast one Sunday a month, as well as several events/celebrations throughout the year for all of the residents. GST really has a community feel to it. The residents and apartment staff are welcoming and enjoyable to interact with. The apartment staff (Chembe, Cristina, Albert, Rajif and Isabel) are the best. They are all onsite Monday through Friday (and many Saturday mornings). They have an open door policy and are always very accommodating, professional and nice. Service requests are taken care of very quickly. In all my years living here I do not think I have ever waited more than a day (usually a few hours) for something to be taken care of/fixed. The management/apartment staff take pride in making GST a great place to live and an enjoyable home for all who live here. The location is perfect. Several bus lines  are about a 1 minute walk out the front door and 2 "L" stops (Addison and Sheridan)are just up the street. Whole Foods, Jewel, Treasure Island and Walgreens are all within walking distance. The best part-the beautiful lakefront is right across the street. Breathtaking views and miles of walking, biking and running. Great neighborhood, excellent restaurants, lots of shopping. I highly recommend GST if you are looking for a great apartment.

These are run down old apartments.  The carpets are terrible and the kitchens are nasty.  Some of the people who live their are nice but it is only a few.  The one saving "Grace" is Cristina in the office.  She is amazing.  If you have any issues make sure you talk to her and ONLY her in the office.  If I would not have been in such a hurry to find a place I NEVER would have moved in here.

I moved in 4 months ago and can't break my lease.

I've moved in this building recently. And it is perfect place to name it home. Very clean and cozy building. The management is very helpful and highly professional.  There are no problem with hot water, noisy neighbors, heating or something else. Location is also perfect: walk distance from the lake, 10 minutes by car to downtown, bus stop and metro station are nearly. I would absolutely recommend Grace street towers for choosing.

I hate that I'm leaving a 1 star review but the 40 East Oak building management truly deserve it. In my two years of residence they have been consistently rude, unwilling to address issues and disruptive to my living experience. I've had to have my bathroom redone 4x this year because of a leak that they won't fix - and they won't give any reduction in rent or admit the issue exists.

Other management issues:
- Rent rates are not consistent - do not sign here without pushing back. My friend lives in a significantly larger unit and pays $150 less per month than me.
- They increase rent for residents who want to resign but keep open units at lower rent rates (my rent increased $75 monthly but the open identical unit on my floor was offered at lower than my previous rate).
- Elevators are often down - particularly the freight elevator which is the only one that leads to the laundry room and gym.  

Door staff is wonderful - they are the only upside!

Best location in the Gold Coast. Lake access is a half a block and the rooftop gives a great view of the city and lake. Any service issue or apartment touch up has been responded to and complete within 24 hours. They want you to feel like this is your home.

The staff is great but the management is terrible.  I live here for 3 years but ever since I moved in, I was disturbed by the neighbor who shares a wall with me.  The wall is very thin, I can hear all sorts of noise from the next door.  I complained to the management numerous times, no one can do anything about it.  I end up moving my bed to the living room so I can sleep.  By the way, the management raises the rent every year by $50 per month.

The apartment units are updated and appear very nice, but everything is installed/made cheaply. The kitchen cabinets, bathroom racks, and kitchen sink handles fall off on a regular basis.
I am a very clean person, but I continue to have bugs in my apartment. I have sprayed my unit to get rid of the bugs, but they seem to be inevitable. I have reached out to the staff for assistance several times without a response.
There is also always a smoke smell in my unit coming from others on my floor smoking indoors (not allowed). It comes in from the windows, vents, and hallway. I have reached out to the staff for assistance several times and do not get a response on this issue either. 
Overall, I would definitely not recommend Belmont Tower.

No issues with the apparrment.
The building is old and was built in the 70s as affordable housing. 
250 units with a small laundry room, most of the time half of the machines do not work.
Management does not care about retaining tenants that are invested in having a safe and clean living environment. So don't be surprised if the 5 roommates living in the apartment next to you have a party and end up vomiting or urinating under your door.
Don't be shocked if your unit smells like weed because people smoke in the stairwell and later decide to sleep there.
But hey location is great!

My sister lived in this building for a year with a different roommate before I moved in, and we don't ever want to move! Our apartment is HUGE and the price is incredible for Lakeview East. We both bought large bedroom furniture and we have so much floor space  in each of our rooms. Our kitchen is set up a little weird with only so much counter space but we've been in other apartments and they're set up a little differently, so it really depends on the apartment. If something needs to get fixed, a quick email and the guys come as soon as they can - they snake our drain once a month -usually during the same day we request. It's also great that there's full time office workers too so you can always stop in there if you need anything. Downsides: laundry room - currently only 5 washers are working - and with 24 floors of apartments it can be difficult if you go at a busy hour but they're promising to fix them soon. No central air - each apartment comes with 2 units and we have ours in our rooms- we can cool the whole apartment if we open our bedroom doors though. Best part: parking!!! on site!!! and only 95 bucks even for the covered spots. Cannot beat that in Lakeview! Other best part: Half a block to all the buses that go into the city and half a mile or so to the train. Cannot beat the location!

Location is everything in the city of Chicago I give the building 5 stars for placement and 3 for the actual living space. Walk just one block East from the front steps and you hit Belmont Harbor and the Lakeshore running path, one block in the other direction and you'll discover unique restaurants and fun bars.  Perfect location for the work commute downtown. Just hop on the express bus and you're on Michigan Ave within 10 minutes! The building itself is old, but well kept. White walls and tan carpet..fairly "vanilla", but your personal decor can go a long way. No modern appliances and minimal amenities... The upper floors have awesome views looking south at the city skyline!
RAT INFESTED! Rats living in the walls climbing out your filters! Broken elevators, Passive Aggressive property manager. And the list continues! All the tenants are crying out for help right now

Mouse infestations, broken elevators, flooding, and the management is passive-aggressive.

As others have stated in other reviews there are ongoing roach and mice issues dating back to 2019 and they're still present today. Check the reviews, and talk to residents before going any further.

Where do I start? I’ve lived here a little over a year and it’s been a journey. 

Horizon’s management took the building down a major turn for the worse. The building flooded over the holidays and they did not communicate and passive aggressively left tenants high and dry. Construction is cheap and disruptive. They have a “concierge” that is clearly not there to help residents but to scrutinize us. 

Worst of all, there are MICE!!! And the building’s response was to put duct tape over people’s vents. It’s such a mess. A psychologically scarring experience for a crazy price. Any positive reviews are fake - they keep trying to bribe people with gift cards

Once you sign your lease the management does not care about you or any of your problems. There has been a leak in my hallway for nearly 2 years. They send a maintenance person up who says they cant figure it out, then they forget about it until I message them months later. Wash rinse and repeat. Our "secured package room" has been broken into a raided TWICE this month alone. Has management done anything to remedy this issue or secure our building? Nope. Because it doesn't involve new tenants signing new leases. There are numerous other issues that have gone untended to, because they hire the laziest building managers who put in minimal (if any) effort to solve your problems. Look for another apartment. Any apartment that is NOT managed by Horizon Realty Group. I have emailed all the way up the chain to the Vice President of the company and NOBODY cares about you once your lease is signed.
I have been living here for a month and haven't been able to use the AC in one of the bedrooms, I have submitted several maintenance requests and so far no one has been able to fix this issue.

I’ve been living here for a year now, I absolutely love this building. Apartment layout is awesome the floor to sealing windows!  
All amenities are new, the patio area, grills, and wifi, the fire pit, very nice layout of patio. The lobby has smart food kiosk with fresh food and produce, fitness is 24/7 open witch is cool. Management is very nice and friendly!
Booked a Tour and nobody showed up. We called and they said they saw my appointment that I made a month in advance and would send someone down. No one ever came down.

It’s an old building. If you complain about the lack of water (hot or cold) they will tell you the building is old and that you shouldn’t shower, cook, etc during busy times of the day. Busy times are apparently all day sometimes. Heat and water were out for over a week in Jan due to pipes  and management just told people to buy heaters. Gets extremely hot in the summer (100+) until the air is on. Management just tells you to get a fan. That’s if management responds at all to emails and calls.

Pros: I originally liked the layout of my studio. That's where the good stops. It's not worth the price AT ALL. 

Cons: 
- VERY inconsistent water (sometimes doesn't run) from the kitchen to the shower
- they have 3 elevators and you can end up waiting up to 5+ minutes on one
- the apartment gets extremely hot like a greenhouse with no way to cool it down aside from being able to open a window ~4 inches
- the gym and its equipment are trash, 
- the lobby always smells like garbage especially on warmer days
- management communication is terrible taking long times to respond to requests

Unless your goal is to live in hell AVOID this place.

If I could leave 0 stars I would. First as mentioned before the AC situation in the summer is AWFUL.
