The actual vent is so full of dust and dirtiness that id you are even slightly asthmatic this would be an issue. The package situation has gotten worse with new rules implemented at the whim of the staff without any prior warning. Laundry room is DISGUSTING. The machines are either broken or dirty beyond use. The dryers same situation, with some just NOT heating UP. The elevator situation is awful, if you are unfortunate enough to try to get to your apartment when someone is moving in or out the wait times for an elevator can go up to half an hour of you just waiting for an empty one.

My building is pretty nice I live on the 15th floor and my building has a pool & a tech center! It's close to my school and has free wifi it's honestly great! Only problems are the small bedrooms and the elevators are really small and take so long! Also I don't like paying for laundry.

I walk through the front doors and enter the lobby, there awaiting to sign in our 4 pretty girls, I tip my cap to them as I proceed through another door towards the elevators.  It is a quick shot to the 14th floor where I arrive to my door and enter my home.  It is slightly hot and these AC blares from the wall behind me.  My place is kept clean with a crumb or two here or there on a table but always ready to host an event.  I live alone which is peaceful being able to do whatever I want at any time of the day.  I've really enjoyed this room and wish I could stay longer.

I spent about five months apartment searching before I moved into the Regal Apartments. I toured quite a few properties and this building provided by far the best value in terms of square footage and appearance in this very conveniently located neighborhood. The building has a great deal of vintage charm with the high timbered ceilings with the modern amenities you could want, but not all the unnecessary frills no one really uses in some of these overpriced buildings nearby. The staff is friendly and responsive.

The Regal “CAN” be a nice place to live, but unfortunately bad tenants puts a damper on community living. The good tenants like myself pay too much rent to be dealing with bad tenants. It’s exhausting. I wish the higher up gather the good tenants up and hear us out on how The Regal can and should be a better place to live.

Ever since I first got a tour of the Regal Apartments, I was drawn in by the gorgeous building and interior and the warmth of the community here. We have a beautiful apartment, and any issues are fixed quickly and professionally.
We have loved living at Regal so far. The apartment is beautiful and the location is fantastic.
The regal has a great staff great location and the residents are friendly and quiet….
We’ve been here a month and we love it. Everyone we’ve met is so sweet(including all of the dogs) and it really feels like home.

Apartments are close together, resulting in frequent noise complaints. We’ve encountered issues with neighbors, including excessive partying and disruptive behavior. This isn’t limited to festive days; people get carried away and endanger themselves and others. 
Contractors have consistently delayed projects, often taking over six or more months to complete them, even if they’re finished at all. They disregard any residents who live there. They work during weekends and after hours, causing excessive noise with drilling and hammering that has worsened over the years. Some of this is due to the building itself, which fails to inform anyone when it’s going to make a lot of noise to fix pipes and other issues. They constantly use the service elevator. 
Elevators are perpetually malfunctioning, with jarring stops between floors and loud doors that give the impression of being on a roller coaster. Even during holidays like St. Patrick’s Day, the rules seem to be disregarded, allowing an excessive number of people to fit inside.
Laundry on the 20th floor is a major issue. People disregard the common areas and the machines with your clothes inside. They take your belongings, leave their clothes hanging for hours, and even steal valuables. To make matters worse, the machines are frequently broken. 
Marina City Valet Parking has significantly deteriorated. We pay $280 per month to endure a 30-minute wait to retrieve our car, only to be subjected to another 10-minute wait to exit the chaotic traffic that forms in the combined parking lot of the House of Blues and Marina City whenever there’s an event, such as a Marathon, St. Patrick’s Day, or any other event. Valet employees expect a tip, or they will retaliate against you.
Balconies are a significant problem. They lack a proper drainage system, causing large puddles of dirty water to form after every snowfall and rainstorm. Every balcony requires maintenance every two years, and it’s advisable to bring your belongings inside, even if it’s not your floor, as maintenance workers may carelessly spread dirt and debris. Residents constantly have a mess on their balconies, despite the beautiful view some apartments have, which is ruined by their mess. 
Security guards can become complacent in their duties, especially when things are quiet, which can lead to a lack of vigilance.

Moving in or out of Marina Towers is fairly miserable. I'm posting this review to save people some grief.  It is a mess in the Marina level area of Marina City so it's a must for you to go down and see for yourself how to drive the truck in, where to park it(no designated place) and how far it is to move your stuff.  Neither condo management or Alto realty took me downstairs and showed me where to park the truck or other tips.  
Plan on being interrupted at least twice for workmen to use the elevator. They are rude and think they should have priority over your move.   If you want to be nice then empty the elevator load into the hallway so they can move their tools and materials.  It's a 50 year old building and seems to have work going on all day.  They could at least limit work around month end when people are moving in and out.
You will probably have to move the truck a couple of times to let other trucks get by.  
They have hotel cart available but you have to know to ask for it and also leave an ID.  They could have it ready and provide more carts.  
Be aware of the clearance height downstairs. I hired 2 Men and a Truck and they brought this massive truck for 4 bedroom house and it didn't fit under the clearance so they had to park far away and lug my stuff farther which cost me more money because it took longer.

I just moved to a studio apartment at Marina City and so far it has been a pretty fantastic experience. Living in the corncobs is a dream. The location cannot be beat and I have a balcony that is almost half the size of my boyfriend's old place (I'm not kidding!) I have a clear view of the Sear's Tower and the River and can even see the Lake on the other side! Waking up to my view takes my breath away every single day--I can't believe I live here! 

I do the reverse commute and the walk to the Metra is not terrible (~20 mins), but when it gets colder I will have a plethora of other options due to the high-demand River North location. I can access every L line in under 10 minutes, and several buses pick up just outside the apartment. My place is near anything and everything you might need (grocery stores, home stores, restaurants, bars, you name it) and there is even a dryer cleaner and market that carries everything from deli meat to Ben & Jerry's in the lobby of the place! 

Security guards are stationed at the entrances 24/7 and I have felt completely safe living here. I was concerned about closet space but after moving in I realized how silly it was--my closets (there are THREE of them!!) are probably less than 50% occupied. 

Bottom line is, for what you get here (amazing location, breath-taking views, a balcony of its size, safety, and many conveniences most places simply do not have), Marina City is the most affordable option there is. Plus, it doesn't hurt that the building is a landmark in Chicago (it's pretty cool to be watching a movie from the 80's, 90's or present and see your building featured..it's truly an icon)!

I adore my apartment in Marina City, a two tower complex affectionately referred to as "the corn cobs."  These are iconic buildings I have known and admired since childhood, and I sometimes can't believe how lucky I am to be living in such an architectural gem.  

My unit is on one of the highest floors (of 60 total) and I face directly north, providing me a majestic overview of the city, with the river streaming by on my left, and glimpses of the lake to my right.  The balcony is gigantic, fitting a large patio table with seating for six, plus several large flower pots, and still plenty of room to walk around.  And that's just the main balcony off the living room.  There's also a half-balcony off the bedroom affording me even more outdoor space.  They don't build them like this anymore!  

Inside the unit, there's a spacious living room/dining room, a super fun retro kitchen (retro in that it has barely been updated since it was built in the early 60s, and I wouldn't have it any other way), a great sized bedroom with room enough for a queen bed and large dresser with tons of space remaining, a nice shower/tub bathroom with separate vanity/sink area, and a walk-in closet!  There are also huge closets in the entry hallway, plus each unit has a storage locker on the 20th floor.  The 20th floor also houses a small gym with some basic equipment and a laundry room.  

The location is right in the heart of the city.  River North bars, restaurants, and shopping surround me, and I can easily walk or take public transportation to any other neighborhood.  

I have never been so thrilled with an apartment, and I hope to enjoy Marina City for many more years to come.

Fantastic river front, 1 bedroom apartment off of a 250 square-foot covered balcony. This apartment is located on the 37th floor directly across the river from Chicago's new riverfront development. I watch sightseeing boats, private vessels of many sizes, kayakers, and rental boats directly off my balcony. The apartment has been recently renovated with hardwood floors and GE appliances. Unit is located in the iconic, round, Marina City development. I am steps away from restaurants, bars, downtown shopping, and Chicago's
Magnificent Mile! Spectacular views day and night! I Love my apartment!
Beautiful views and big patio! Nice building and friendly neighbors. The gym is a bit small, but never too crowded. The little market downstairs has a great beer and wine selection.
I think this is a really excellent place for single people or people with a kid or two..
Things  are  progressive  and getting  much better, with maintenance ??

Museum Walk Apartments has been my home since 2001, and even though it’s  been many different managers, almost every single one of them made me feel like I belong here. 
My last maintenance request was to let me back into my unit after I locked myself out after hours on Friday, February 7, 2025. I was mortified because I didn’t want to make anyone have to come out on a Friday just to let me into my apartment unit, plus I was trying to not feel lonely and sad on my birthday. But when I called the maintenance emergency hotline, every person I spoke with when I called  was so kind and patient and helpful, I didn’t feel embarrassed. I especially appreciate Dario coming out to museum walk to let me into my apartment unit. The kindness and professionalism of TLC’s response makes the lockout fee worth it. Thank you, Museum Walk and TLC!

Three years later and it's just not worth it, they arbitrarily raise your rent by huge margins, force fees on you for services you didn't ask for or have when you first moved in, no way to opt out. It's not worth the hassle at this point.
Nice area, right off Lakeshore. Building is kept clean. Very quiet.
Museum Walk provides A-1 services hands down, no doubt about it.

Elena and the whole property management team at Dearborn North Apartments are incredibly friendly, thoughtful, and responsive when you need them. Whenever I had a question or filed a maintenance request, Elena responded to my message very promptly and courteously. Additionally, the square footage you get for the price is vastly superior to anything else in the area -- not even close. If you want to live in Gold Coast, a block away from Butch McGuire's and Gibson's Steakhouse, and you want a friendly, reliable place to live but also have a budget, Dearborn North Apts should be your first stop.

I have been at 1117 N Dearborn for 13 years. The maintenance/management team is the best! Any time I had a request, even if it wasn’t urgent, they would be to my apartment within the hour. If I wasn’t at home, I felt safe and secure to give my permission for them to enter my apartment if need be. Elena, the manager always checked in with me making sure everything was good with the apartment. The rent is the most reasonable in the city of Chicago for a great location in the Gold Coast.

Lived there for 2.5 years and loved it. Only moved to switch up neighborhoods. Elena and the whole maintenance team - so nice, so professional, and wanted me to have a good experience. Definitely look in to moving here, especially if you're on a tight budget

So I had the chance to tour the apartment and it was okay, and I decided to apply. But the application process was emotionally draining. Elena, property manager (I think), was very very rude. Communication was extremely bad and she kept demanding documents without communicating the reason. In the end, I decided to withdraw my application because of the negative attitude I was getting. Although this is a fairly decent place, I don't think living with that for 1 year is worth it

Elena is by far the best landlord I’ve had to date living in Chicago. She is so incredibly kind, caring, and trustworthy. She knows all her tenants and greets you kindly whenever she sees you. She always tried to make everyone feel safe and at home in this little community. Before the pandemic she would throw community events in the summer and winter that were so much fun! All shared spaces are kept clean and Elena and maintenance crew are incredibly responsive. When I was locked out of my apartment at an incredibly late hour, there was a system in place to have someone there within minutes to led me to my door to unlock it after verifying I lived there. The location is amazing!!!

I have lived at 1117 North Dearborn for about a year now and have had a great experience. The landlord Elena is very friendly and always available to answer questions. The maintenance staff is professional and complete work orders very quickly. The apartments are relatively cheap for the area and are a good value. The building is a good location 1 block away from the Clark/ Division Red Line stop. I cannot think of any negative experiences so far while renting here.

The Property Manager, Elena, is amazing. She is helpful and diligent. I have not had any issues since I moved in and just re-signed my lease because I do not want to live anywhere else. The appliances and condition of the apartments are immaculate, and nothing like other gold coast buildings that have gross carpets and cockroaches. The building staff is always working and provided assistance to me when I was unable to walk (injuries). Obviously, the location is great being so close to bars, restaurants, the city and public transportation that will take you anywhere you need to go. There are always building-warming parties and lobby events to meet other residents and create a sense of community/warmth in the building. I highly recommend living here to anyone who is considering.

I lived at Dearborn North for one year and was sad to leave! The location is amazing - right by the red line and in the heart of the beautiful Gold Coast. The building manager, Elena, was wonderful! Always smiling, knows her residents by name and she and the maintenance staff take great care of the building. Would highly recommend!

I lived at 1117 for two years and it was the best. The building manager Elena is wonderful. She is always smiling, as sweet as can be, and gets the job done! Whenever there was anything I might have needed she was always on top of it and had her staff fixing the issue immediately. 
I toured several buildings in the neighborhood and would absolutely recommend this one!
I never would have left if I wasn't leaving the city. I miss it there!
Dishonest manager. Says one thing then denies it later when it's profitable for her to do so. If you make the mistake of living here, make sure to get every single interaction with her in a document.

Well at the time I moved in I would give it a nearly perfect rating. Having lived in this building for 1 year now, sadly have to lower it to 1 out of 5. 

First of all the woman manage the building is unfriendly. she just want to get the thing done, shows 0 courtesy, never say please or thank you. When signing up the apartment she's literally the sweetest person I met but after I signed she's totally a different person. You don't want to put down 1500/mo to someone with a poker face. 

Second the building is old and smelly. And the water system is terrible. If my neighbor is using water, then water from my tap will instantly become burning hot. Happened to my several times I have to turn water off to avoid burning, when I'm ...um naked and covered by soap bubbles 

Third this place is not well maintained. Fitness room has equipment that are so closely packed, maybe from the 80s that I'm afraid the treadmill will break into pieces when I run on it (I'm 110lbs). Computer/printer was broken - told poker face lady and she said 'ok' - 3 months later it didn't get fixed. Package was all piled up in the computer room where everyone has access to - I lost a package here once. 

Anyway - not recommended. And they raise rent every year by $100/mo.

I lived here two years and can't say enough good things about this building and it's staff

Elena is the building manager and is great and very on top of things and super nice 

Her building staff are so nice and fix everything on time when needed 

Units are in great shape and well maintained 

Very quiet building and kept clean

I had to move for work reasons and I will miss this building and it's people!

I just resigned for a second year at Dearborn North. It was not a hard decision because it has been such a great experience thus far. The staff are super friendly and helpful. They go the extra effort by bringing packages to your apartment (a huge pro for me because I travel during the week and don't need to worry about it) and then coming back later to retrieve your empty boxes. They do a great job with the upkeep of the building-- there are always fresh flowers and festive decorations. My apartment has updated appliances and lots of storage. Even though it is small there is plenty of room for all of my stuff. Not to mention it's a great location! It's the best bang for your buck in the Gold Coast!

I’ve been a resident of Dearborn North since mid 2011 and I’ve rented two different apartments, sizes and on different floors.

The overall building is a charming vintage building with radiator heating, a small gym, bike storage, business room, laundry room, and an outdoor courtyard. There’s no central air but you can either rent from the building or use your own window A/C unit for the summer months. The elevators are small so if you have any large size furniture it will have to be carried up the stairs. I managed to fit a queen size mattress and separately a 3-seat couch in the elevator.
 
The building staff is very pleasant and accommodating. If there are any maintenance issues in the apartment it’s been taken care of that day or the next.

Twice a year the building has a resident appreciation party. It’s a small thing but to me it goes a long way.

The first apartment I rented and lived in for 4 ½ years was an east-facing 400 sq. ft. studio on one of the upper floors. The apartment received great natural lighting and I had a nice view towards the lake. The layout of the apartment is interesting with an old Murphy bed space converted to bookshelves and a big walk-in closet that leads to the bathroom. The bathroom is what you would expect from a studio apartment but also has a full size bathtub/shower. The actual size of the apartment is very accommodating once you figure out a layout with your furniture. I easily fit a queen size bed, 3-seat couch, TV plus stand and a desk. The kitchen is fairly small with no counter space but was recently renovated and upgraded to stainless steel appliances just before I switched to a larger apartment. 

The other and current apartment I’m in is one of the 600 sq. ft. convertible one bedrooms facing south on a lower level. The natural lighting isn’t as plentiful as the previous but the apartment still gets enough light during the day and has plenty of ceiling lighting. The layout is nice and has two closets. One is a walk-in by the front door and the other is connected to the bathroom. This unit has a large renovated kitchen plus the upgraded stainless steel appliances along with a dishwasher. The bathroom is similar to the studio unit but slightly more spacious. 

Overall, my experience living here has been really positive. I would recommend this building to anyone that is looking for an affordable, quiet, well taken care of building and residents and for someone who is looking to live in a good lively neighborhood.
Friendly tenets and stellar Management. Axis is in the amazing Streeterville neighborhood close to the Mag mile, Navy Pier and mass transit.
Great staff, beautiful building, awesome amenities, overall great place to live!

I have lived in this building for 2 years now. I love the location and the views are great. The apartment is nice however, the building does have a few issues. The elevators can be very slow and tend to breakdown which slows them down even more. Aside from that, I love my apartment and am very happy with the location!
I like the building and the neighborhood. It's convenient to everything.

Just before this request there was an absolutely horrible maintenance issue. It took this team seven months to repair the living room heating and cooling fan. It stopped in January during a cold snap, my apartment was only 60 degrees, Chicago ordinance is a min. of 68. Still not fixed as summer approached and there was NO A/C....several days it was 80 deg with 82% humidity!!! Shameful...no I'm sorry, we'll get this fixed ASAP....nothing. And Mgmt STILL raised my rent!
Great location, love the deck. Nice size rooms and a very bright, modern look.

The building is a nice place to live. That is why i have been here for over 20 years. With the last Management things were great. Management is not good @ all any more with Avanath. There is so much room for improvement here. What a shame.
The building seems unsafe.  There are non residents and homeless members of the community wandering common spaces, and trying to break into each apartment.
I would not recommend LPP to anyone. The building is gross and unkept. The leasing office is dismissive, poor at communicating, unorganized, and condescending.

I recently had the pleasure of living at Sheridan Gunnison Apartments, and I must say, it has been an exceptional experience, largely due to the outstanding management team. Virginia and Maria, in particular, deserve special recognition for their exemplary service.
From the moment I moved in, Virginia was incredibly welcoming and made sure that the transition was as smooth as possible. They were always available to assist with any concerns, no matter how small. Whether it was helping with maintenance requests or providing information about the local area, their dedication to resident satisfaction was evident.
Their attention to detail and genuine care for the residents create a warm and friendly community atmosphere. It’s clear that they go above and beyond to ensure that Sheridan Gunnison Apartments remains a top choice for anyone looking for a place to call home.
I highly recommend Sheridan Gunnison Apartments, not only for its great facilities and convenient location but also for the exceptional management team led by Virginia and Maria. Their commitment to excellence truly sets this place apart.

We lived there for about 6 years  and recently moved out due to job relocation. Had a great time. Management team is amazing. If you have issues, send out email to manager or call, if it is major, resolve within few hours. Never lost a package. Utilities are included in rental fee except electricity. If you are budget oriented, this is the place you need to look for first. Parking fee is very reasonable. Location is great. Lawrence statin is 7 mins distance by walking. If I have to come back to the Chicago, I will definitely rent here again.
This Property is dirty and washers and dryers never work

When we first moved into Sheridan-Gunnison apartment, we were not sure if we made the right choice because there's few review online about it, but after living here for one year, we are so glad we moved in.
The staff here is fantastic. Virginia the manager is always friendly and willing to help. Andrew is like a family to us and always makes sure we get our packages. The maintenance team is quick to response. Altogether we were very happy to live here.
The apartment itself is great. We have a wonderful view of the lake without any blockage. The apartment is clean and spacy, refrigerator and microvan is newly installed.

The Vivian is filed with roaches, bedbugs, homeless people, and mice. It’s absolutely nauseating. Management ignores any issues brought to their attention. There are tons of homeless people and criminals that hang out in the entry way , and there is often no hot water in the winter. The radiators also stop working a lot in the winter months. Management refuses to do anything about it.

Do not trust the pictures and floor plans. This is an old building and many of the units are super unique (in a good and bad way). I was sold a unit that was "just like the model studio but with a city view" only to move half way across the country to a totally different floor plan that was wayyyy smaller and facing a brick wall. Eventually I got into a better unit after weeks of living in boxes. There seems to be a new manger every few months so they don't know what the unit they're selling looks like. The appliances are nice but there are still radiators so its hard to place furniture and regulate temperatures. If you live on the top floor like me, prepare to have scorching hot sink water so hot it burns your hands without warning and 0 shower water pressure unless you get up to shower at 5 am. My only complaint about the people is they cant seem to follow the simple instructions to place their trash bags in the trash shoot- they leave it in the room for others to smell all week until maintenance gets around to removing it. Other than that, the people in the building are nice and you never have to worry about thieves. Although the managers change a lot, they are always nice and helpful and the maintenance engineer is a doll. 2.5/5 so I'll round up to 3.

I've had the opportunity to experience numerous transitions with the property as I've lived in this location for two+ years.  The management company works hard to build a sense of community and connection.  I've been a Chicago renter for many years.  This apartment is the first place I have had that's modern.  The management and maintenance team are always responsive.  I'm genuinely proud to call this place my home.

An update on my previous review: The new manager on site, Jenn, truly has been so helpful. This building upon me moving in had its fair share of issues as a result of remodeling and other major transitions, but credit is due to Jenn for keeping her word and doing her best to make sure everything is done to address and resolve the concerns expressed.

Im genuinely impressed by the dramatic change I’ve noticed since her arrival. Every morning when I walk my dog, I witness a cleaning crew cleaning the common area. Pest control has been consistent and aggressively addressing pest issues, and Jenn has followed through with ensuring I am satisfied with her service. The new staff are also much more pleasant. Im very grateful and as a result, I do recommend the Vivian.
Stunning views of Lake Michigan, close proximity to the redline and great restaurant scene in the neighborhood.

Been here for 5 years. Rent increased $400 and residents (many who are disabled) are being forced to move out because of the recent price increases. Ownership of this building has changed so many times over the years that many ongoing issues are never resolved. The leasing agents are trying to sell the idea that this is a luxury apartment but that is far from the case. Many of the washers and dryers have been out of order -- the elevator has been broken 20  times in the last few months. When the elevator is broken, everyone is stuck walking flights of stairs while waiting for management to hire someone to run the maintenance elevator. When they hire someone to run the maintenance elevator, it is only in service from 7am-10pm which means if you're disabled, you are left in the dark. The management is horrible and the fact that they're pricing people out is disgusting.

I love this building, which I've now lived in for more than a year. Very well designed (great use of every inch of space) and very well built (pretty much sound resistant). Management is responsive, maintainance is excellent and staff are very friendly and responsive. Friendly neighbors with great low-key vibe. Terraces and public spaces are awesome. Inside garage a plus.

Overall a great community. Management has really stepped up and taken the lead with issues in the building and has hosted community events. Great place to live and very convenient to public transit, grocery stores, and nightlife!
I been a Resident for over 10  years and it's a nice place to live and in a great location close to downtown.
I was told I had no appointment when I arrived. I was assumed to be low income and I am not. I never got a tour or an apology for getting a wealth of incorrect information.

DO NOT RENT HERE!! I’ve been living here over two years and let me tell you.. this place horrible. The front door to the building does not lock, so anyone on the street can walk right in. Our garage door was broken for MONTHS and what did the management team do? JUST LEFT IT OPEN TO THE STREET. Cars were broken into, packages are constantly stolen, and it’s just unsafe. Don’t bother submitting a maintenance request because no one will come to fix anything. I can’t wait to leave this dump.

I have been a resident here for over 20 years trying to move out  now the building is under new management from the time I moved here the old company was good which was Renaissance north. this new company Avanath do not care about our safety nor our concerns. Doors be wide open to where anyone can walk right in come to the floors and twist our door and check to see who is door is open. I have had packages stolen from me which management seems to not care about as well. I have had my car broken into because the garage door was broken for months on in. The building have went straight down hill and is not clean like it use to be. The up keep of the building is not what it use to be. Run and save yourself the headache you do not what so ever want to rent from these people. And last but not least. The machine that we use to add money to our card was stolen and ripped right from the wall and management has not yet replaced it we have to wait for the office to be open to even add money to our cards so we can wash. Like I feel like I went to living in heaven to hell.

I’ve lived in this building for 15 years. The original company that owned it was so great. The building was sold to Avanath a few years ago and they are terrible. They don’t care at all. One example of many is that the garage doors were broken for months. So naturally they were left open for anyone to come in. And people did come in to check out the cars in the parking lot,  Try to open residents doors. Thankfully nothing bad happened. If you do chose to live here LOCK YOUR DOOR, BE SMART, and BE SAFE.

Classic Chicago property in Outstanding River North location! 
Princess in the Front Office is always a pleasure. As well as our Maintenance on site. Proud to call Gramercy Row Apartments home!
This is a very old building and the administration is very ineffective when it comes to solving problems.

Only positive thing to say is the location is prime.
Management is lazy and poor quality.  They dont really care about tenants issues. 

Huge cockroach infestation.
I really appreciate that the apartments are so close to transportation and downtown
Great location for reasonable rates.  Friendly staff.  Recommended apartments.
What I love the most about Gramercy Row Apartments is the location, it is so close to downtown, so it is close to restaurants and shops!
Visited the place for viewing the apartment that was pre-scheduled. The manager was very rude. Her behavior was so bad that I left the place without even looking at the apartments.

I moved to Sheridan Tower for its elegance, emenities, and -- most of all -- it was CHILL.  The vibe changed the instant the new manager arrived:  Immature, disorganized, and petty.  

They installed cameras on the terrific rooftop deck because of ONE incident, so I stopped going.  I understand the need to schedule gym time because of COVID but I've stopped going because I just can't deal with management.  I send my laundry out now.  

Sheridan Tower is an excellent place to be a homebody; however, outside of your apartment, the property is becoming a trashy daycare center.  It's a shame, and a sad end to my otherwise fantastic experience at Sheridan Tower.

Unfortunately I strongly advise not renting from Horizon here right now. The current property manager at the 5650 North Sheridan building has really ruined the atmosphere here. It's become a stressful, hostile environment and managed more like a college dorm. We receive constant emails (an average of one every other day in the month of August). Some have told us literally how to do laundry and take out trash...ridiculous! There are increased unnecessary restrictions however rent only increases as the living environment promoted has drastically declined. The behaviors of a few notoriously violent and nasty neighbors are promoted and not handled professionally by property manager. Many residents who have lived here for several years are stressed, frustrated and exhausted by current property manager including myself. It’s sad because it was once a great place to live and most tenants are really friendly, kind and fun. Current management has really ruined it here.
Nice place great location nice people in the building as well.

I’ve been living here for the past four months. The units are small, but if you make the most of your space it’s honestly fine. The ladies is the management office are extremely nice and helpful. If I ever put in a maintenance request they are there to fix it ASAP. The rooftop is beautiful and there’s another patio space on the first floor that’s nice too. Gym is pretty small too but still has decent equipment. My only issue since living here was that I found a dead roach in my apartment one day. I’m a clean freak so I blame it on the heat wave we were in at the time. the next day the maintenance sprayed my apartment & I haven’t had any issues since. 10 minute walk away from the beach and it’s a great place for a young person to live. Lots to do in the area. There’s no central AC but they allow you to rent a window unit for the season which works fine for me and keeps my place cool. I feel safe living here too for the most part being a woman.

I lived in floor 14/16 and got one of the best unobstructed views of the Gold Coast Area. My apartment was also recently renovated and was definitely worth the price. Location is prime, only steps away from the Mag Mile and so many public transport options. The best option for anyone new to Chicago.

I moved into my beautiful studio apartment in early September, I was moving from Philadelphia for work and I was nervous about the daunting task of finding an affordable place close enough to my job downtown in River North. I feel so blessed and lucky to have found Dearborn Plaza apartments. I worked in real estate/helping people get apartments for over a year and I can tell you that this is a great find!

The office employees are extremely kind and friendly, my tour was very easy to schedule and I was approved in a day or two. My apartment has an extremely competitive and fair rent price (especially for the view), the unit had brand new floors/a very clean and updated bathroom/a great little kitchen with very clean and fully functional appliances when I moved in. My apartment also had two large closets so I have never felt short on storage. Management made moving in easy by scheduling you time with a freight elevator big enough to move anything I could imagine in, and the only utility you pay for is electricity! The building has a very unique and cute build, constructed in the 20s as a luxury hotel for women, the studios are about the size of a large extended stay hotel room. If you are looking for w quaint and updated space you have found it! Dearborn Plaza's maintenance team is second to none, they helped me hang all of my pictures and shelves/lamps within days of me moving in. Between my move-in and December they have replaced every window screen and cleaned the windows of every unit, as well as fully repainted the hallway trims. I hear them vacuuming the hallways on my floor and cleaning a few times every week which is great, they really care about the upkeep of the building and it shows. I haven't seen a single bug in my apartment or otherwise in the building which is great. I recently got a cat and they don't even charge a fee for having one, which is very kind-hearted compared to a lot of other units I've seen.

I plan to live in this quiet and well kept space for years to come and I highly recommend this building if you are looking for a studio like I was.

3 stars for the amazing rooftop deck however it get closed off most the of the year. The units are TINY, smaller than the micro-studio I lived. Only 1 unit I viewed had updated appliances. Don’t believe the “updated” photos on this listing.

Units are about 150-200 square feet.  Some units are nicer than others and it's the luck of the draw. 
Charge you $125.00 to "rent" a  window A/C unit for the season.  They remove it and reinstall it in the summer.  During this past heatwave allegedly someone almost died because the rooms were so hot.  The hallways were hot.  There is no central A/C.  But it was nice and cool downstairs in their office. 

No common spaces inside the building.  This place used to be a hotel many years ago and that's the layout. What brings you here is the location! location! location!  If you are 25 years or older you will be miserable.  These are dorm rooms and it's not for adults.  The location and price will make you chose it but just don't. 

There is not parking on site.  There won't be any street parking here at all.   You'll have to pay 100s to park in a lot or a garage.

The building has a roach problem. They’ve had to come and spray multiple times and I still see I keep my space very clean but I’ll get up in the middle of the night and see one. It’s not just my apartment either- I know that they’ve sprayed other tenants’ on my floors apartments as well

I've lived at Dearborn Plaza Apartments for more than 2 years now, and it has been a great experience. I'm a recent graduate who was lucky enough to start renting in the Gold Coast neighborhood at a reasonable price. Though the studio spaces are a bit small, I think the neighborhood, rooftop deck and indoor laundry facilities make up for it. The staff is very helpful, and my landlord is very reasonable. The only downside is the occasional bug problem that occurs with some vintage buildings. They do spray for the bugs, but they return every spring and summer. Other than that, I've enjoyed my stay here!

Are you an aspiring actor/artist/dancer/musician? Have a profession downtown Chicago that you commute to from the suburbs by car/train? Prefer to be within walking distance of the Magnificent Mile, John Hancock Building, Oak St. Beach & the Loop? Meet Dearborn Plaza in the Gold Coast! Rent is under $900 a month with HEAT INCLUDED! Hardwood floors. Unbeatable view of the skyline. Charming. Cultured. Vintage. Very safe. IN THE CENTER OF EVERYTHING!  For the right person, a move to this area could change your life & place you in the epicenter of your "downtown dreams!"

I knew very little of Chicago when I moved here about a year ago, and totally lucked out with my choice to live at Dearborn Plaza. 

Pros:
1. The staff is so friendly and efficient. They respond to emails and concerns quickly, communicate when maintenance work is happening, and are overall helpful. The maintenance staff is so kind as well and any issues I have (which are very few) are resolved immediately. 
2. The location is amazing--great, safe neighborhood. Close to downtown, Wicker Park, Lincoln Park, Oak Street Beach, Lincoln Park Zoo, Michigan Ave shopping, etc. Public transport is super accessible as are grocery stores, banks, Starbucks, and drugstores. 
3. Aside from electricity, all utilities are covered with rent. I know heat can be very expensive in Chicago winters, so I'm glad I don't have to pay extra for it. They aren't stingy either-- I never felt like my apartment was too cold. 
4. The building is well-maintained. 
5. They host BBQs, holiday parties, etc for the residents which is very sweet. There is a cute rooftop where you can hang out as well. 

Cons:
The apartments are tiny, as is the kitchen space. But for the price, neighborhood, and peace of mind, it's more than a fair trade-off.

The management rocks socks.  The laundry machines eat them but not without reimbursement and assistance.  The vintage lobby beckons to be painted by a Venetian painter and the location.  Holy Smokestacks it's great especially in the midst of Chiberia because 2 blocks North is Treasure Island and across the street is a Blue Agave to warm you up with authentic Mexican.  The places are cozy and the radiator blasts.  I selected this place thinking I'd be here a year and going on five.  Sweet and sophisticated spot with Lincoln Park and North Ave Beach a lovely 10 minute walk away.

I have been living here for a few months now,the management is friendly, helping and courteous. The building is kept clean and well maintained, the place is in downtown and close to red line metro, oak street beach, state street which has tons of restaurants, rush and division bars for nightlife, Jewel Osco in walking distance, a 7-11 grocery store just outside the building, Walgreens (all these mentioned places are within one mile radius). Only cons about this place is some people might find the room space small(they only have studios) and they don't have air conditioning on site( for which you can rent window AC from the management) apart from that I would recommend this place because of the affordable price and location.

This apartment is everything I wanted, needed and more.  It is two blocks from the greatest grocery store, CVS, a beautiful park, restaurants, shopping and parking lots.  If there is ever something needed to be done maintenance wise, it is handled within 2 days no questions asked.  The laundry is in the building and the machines are new and all in working order.  This apartment was one of four I looked at and I couldn't picture myself anywhere else.

Getting ahold of floor plans and square footage will be really helpful in making your decision. The studios I looked at were very very small and the kitchen appliances were toy sized! That said I wouldn't have minded living here, I just found someplace better in my price range.

The staff is always willing to accommodate and work around your schedule. The apartment was exactly what I was looking for. Just down the street from Starbucks and next door to 7-11 and all the local bars and night life.

I will recommend to all my friends
Just moved in and have an amazing view of the lake. I'm also right across the street from Mariano's. Super convenient for me. Management is very kind and helpful. Gym is huge!
no complaints! staff is great. location is great. apartment is updated

Since I moved in, there have been multiple fires, a broken fire alarm system, multiple burst pipes, mold in the stairwells & hallways, common areas with leaks almost every single day, broken washers/dryers, rodent problems, elevators that are repeatedly broken for long periods of time, maintenance staff that marks items complete without doing any work, and management staff that is frequently out of the office. And the “new” management is mostly just the same people from before.

I've been here about 4 months and will be leaving soon, but here are all of my experiences thus far:

This month, a few days ago, there was a fire in the building on the 6th floor. Not a single fire alarm sounded. My boyfriend happened to be in a group chat of about 70 people, and THAT is how we were informally told to evacuate. We're grateful for those folks in that chat.

3 months into living here we got a knock on our door and we were informed the building had been in foreclosure status and would be sold that upcoming weekend, which we never knew, as we came from out of state, nor were we ever informed. On Thanksgiving weekend, that Friday night, I mistaking tripped our electrical breaker, and after informing their 24/7 desk downstairs they told us we would have to be without power for the whole weekend and that there's nothing they could do and no one they could call. I reported the building, as that's a clear violation of the Chicago electrical ordinance, but Sunday night, it was resolved, and it seems that the employee may have been fired after that incident. Needless to say, we still went almost the entire weekend without power, with a fridge full of Thanksgiving food. We were VERY unhappy. 

Homeless people are let into the building most nights. They're harmless, and it gives me mixed feelings. I'm just hoping none of the homeless take advantage of the kindness of whoever is letting them in and do something awful. It's just something to be aware of. 

Parking doesn't exist here. There's a wait list to be added to one of maybe 6-8 parking spots, which are also in use by the employees, so realistically, there are about 4 spots for the entire building. Needless to say, I've been paying for parking separately - a whopping $200 per month for a spothero parking spot. 

The washers and dryers are on premises, but half of the driers are broken. 

The rooms are stuffy with little to no air circulation. Luckily, we're here in the winter,  I would hate to experience a summer here. 

I've never been more disappointed in an apartment complex. I'm hoping someone sues the hell out of them for the fire incident. Fortunately, my partner and I were not injured, but we most definitely took note of all the issues we found here.

New ownership is coming soon, but for now BEWARE!

The place looks beautiful but there are mice everywhere for the second time I see a nice inside my apartment. Management told me last time they covered all the wholes and I wouldn’t see it again.  24 hours maintenance is a job and staff is not very polite and professional. Move somewhere else.

This is a vintage building with an interesting history as a 1920s residential hotel.
The lobby is large, beautiful and well- appointed. Gym and laundry room are inconsistently maintained.
Apartments are on the small side, but have several large closets. Kitchens have built-in dishwasher and microwave, and plenty of cabinets.
It's an elevator building and apartments have an open-kitchen layout, which makes it partially accessible. It accommodates wheelchair users who have some ambulation.
The neighborhood is diverse and lively, with abundant public  transportation.
Management changes often, bringing periods of chaos and confusion.
Entry is via keyfob. The intercom system has been broken for months; visitors and deliveries have to call on their phones and wait outside while the resident comes down to open the door.
There is a front desk, which is occasionally staffed, but more often desserted.
Response to maintenance requests is inconsistent and largely ineffectual.
There is regular pest control with nontoxic spraying.
Pets are allowed, with some size restrictions and an additional monthly fee.

Strongest pro: location/neighborhood
Strongest con: poor management

I’ve been living in the Rosie for a few months. When I first moved in, things were ok, but then I noticed when I went in our community app, neighbors were always posting about their packages being stolen. Then it happened to me. Apparently, this has been dating back before my time living; however management doesn’t see fit to fix it. 

The property manager has left (as he should have), but we haven’t received any new emails from new management introducing themselves or letting us know what they plan to do about all the thefts in the building. 

Because their are so many thefts, the building is very unsafe. There have also been altercations in the building between neighbors. 

Move to other buildings where there is a doorman, management answers concerns and there is a real package/delivery mail system. There are plenty of places in West loop that cost less or about the same but offers more.

Current resident. Do not lease here. Management is unresponsive, absent and largely apathetic. The building is littered with trash and pet excrement on a near daily basis. Packages and personal belongings are stolen and management refuses to support residents or communicate with them regarding these issues. Hallways smell of marijuana and tobacco. Central HVAC has south facing apartments sitting at 80+ degrees during the day without AC availability or proper air circulation from windows. Walls are paper thin and neighbors are disrespectful at best. FLATS advertises this building and charges residents for "luxury apartment living" but the building and atmosphere are far from it. I wholeheartedly recommend AGAINST living here.

The finishes are lovely, but the rest is in shambles, nowhere CLOSE to luxurious…

The HVAC system is controlled/monitored remotely by a 3rd party and is a DISASTER—multiple complaints have been filed with the city. Many tenants are freezing and unable to turn on their heat, battling with intermittent cold air that blows automatically—even when a thermostat has been turned off. Others are boiling hot and unable to keep the heat off; it will also turn on automatically. We’ve been lucky enough to alternate between BOTH miserable scenarios in our unit.

The mass email sent in response asks that we email management to notify them of issues in our individual units so that they can in turn contact the HVAC 3rd party to ask them to…monitor a unit’s system….? Which they’re already supposed to be doing? Irritating, given the fact that most emails to management go unacknowledged.

The mail room and package closet is utter chaos, costing a ridiculous amount of time and effort to find packages on unmarked shelves (which no one is responsible for organizing).

Cherry on top; you can only create a maintenance ticket on their app as a means to communicate with the building (regardless of whether your matter is even related to maintenance), as there is no onsite management. I’ve completely given up trying to reach anyone via phone or email.

You have no control over the ac or heat… I have submitted a 311 service request but will most likely be leaving because of the lack of care from management. If you don’t mind freezing or burning up depending on the unit and the time of year then this place is decent.

3L Living is HORRIFIC, just like their properties. Roaches EVERYWHERE. Noise ALL DAY AND NIGHT. Broken doors that are NEVER PROPERLY FIXED. Violence is CONSTANT. I could truly go on forever with all the problems of 3L Living.

Please save yourself -- do NOT rent from 3L Living, and NOT live at 5540 S Hyde Park.

In the past 2 days I have probably done more to kill Roach infestations in this building than management has done in 2 years that I've lived here. I've tried being patient, but having one exterminator come once every few months is NOT sufficient to handle this infestation level. the whole building needs to be shut down for a time and fumigated at this point, but obviously that's not a realistic expectation. So all I can do is encourage you to look somewhere else.

The roaches have gotten significantly worse as time has gone on, and the property managers are not only rude but frankly negligent of the situation. This was a nice building but has progressively gotten more disgusting due to negligence.

Do not move here.

The first unit I lived in, I had a neighbor blasting music 5-10 hours a day, at any time of day or night. When he was doing that, he was threatening or beating his girlfriend. Management told me they had given him a warning but nothing changed. Then it was offered that IIIIIIII move into an apartment two floors up to get away from it. So I had to pack up and move all of my things because someone else was violating their lease agreement.

About a month into this new unit, I discovered a bad bedbug infestation. So I had to pack up all of my thing again so they could send up exterminators to treat it. It takes longer than a month for bedbugs to become adults and to be large enough in population that you find them so this was a preexisting problem and I was moved into the unit anyway. For the last year, I have been living out of trash bags, never fully being able to unpack because the bedbugs are an ongoing problem. Bedbugs are life-disruptive in general but the treatment process is even more life-disruptive and it appears that you will have to go through it a lot if you live here. You don't live here. You exist here.

The units have no individual kitchen. There is a community kitchen on the ground floor which is absolutely disgusting in normal times but just downright dangerous in a pandemic. Maintenance has damaged my personal property while dealing with a drain fly issue in my first bathroom and I was never reimbursed.

For my incredibly stressful time here, the price is laughably high. Not worth it. Avoid avoid avoid.
Management is unresponsive. Looks great on the outside but everything is old and run down.

Our Maintenance man is awesome ! 
But the office lady is unhelpful and the lobby needs security

I'm a happy two year resident at beach walk apt. The studio is a perfect size for me and updated so nice. The location is amazing walking to the zoo and beach and all the shops and restaurants so close by. The management and staff are so helpful and friendly. It's also quiet safe no mail issues and no bugs or rodents. So happy I found this place.

Beachwalk is located in a vibrant location full of restaurants, bars, and the beach. A 10-15 minute walk isn't too bad especially since Fullerton (the closest stop) has 3 different lines to get around the city. 

For the apartments, I've got to say what wins me over is both Ms. Kennedy and Scott. They've been so helpful and quick with helping me out whenever a problem arises. I love them.

DO NOT MOVE TO BEACHWALK APARTMENTS. I promise you will regret it. The entryway may look like the place has had a fresh coat of paint, but there are so many disgusting and unacceptable issues with this apartment that building management should be ashamed. From an ever-presence putrid smell in every hallway, to cockroaches, drain flies, and other assorted bugs crawling around, to other tenants that clearly smoke in their apartments and get drunk in the lobby and harass you, to an incompetent leasing office, the list of issues is never ending. Do not give these people a dollar of your hard earned money.

I’ve been living at Beachwalk for 4 years now. Granted it’s a very old building so there is always work to do but with Scott as our maintenance guy, he’s been very helpful whenever I submit an inquiry or have a question. Love the location!

I like to start off and say I have a balcony and you look and see Lake Michigan very pretty view . Secondly we have parking garage under our building and also have Landry room . The inside our apartment have two bathrooms ,our rooms are very spacious and we also can have pets . I just love my apartment.

I've lived in this apartment over six years now and it's mainly due to the view of Lake Michigan out my front windows. This building is literally steps to the beach (it's across the street) and each unit has some sort of view of the lake. I happen to live in one of the front units which has an amazing view. 

The rest of the apartment is well sized for a 2 bedroom 2 bath. The bedrooms are large, especially by Chicago standards. One bedroom has a king size bed with no problem (and that's the small room) while the master bedroom has a queen (could fit a king easily), two desks, a dresser and around five book shelves. Oh - and a comfy chair. Each apartment also has a fairly large balcony that easily fits a table and chairs - each also with a view of the lake.

The building itself is a bit run down in the hallways and a bit dated however the building was recently sold so maybe the new owners will spruce things up a bit. But it's really nothing horrible.

There are washer and dryers (five of each) on the main floor. None of the units (that I know of) have in unit laundry.

Parking is relatively easy out front but the building does offer garage parking and lot parking for an additional cost.

I am here from another city, and this will be my home until I go back. I love my apartment, it’s up to date with a loft feel. The building is always nice and clean, there is plenty of parking, the buildings are under surveillance and key entry secured. There’s laundry right down the hallway which is always a plus. There is plenty of parking, and as a single woman I feel really safe here. The location is great with a huge pond right across the street with a walking path. Everyone is peaceful and family oriented. 
But the best part about these buildings is the management. They are so helpful and accommodating. Move in was so easy and fast, and every issue I’ve had they’ve worked through it and have been extremely helpful. It feels like a community here, not just living in an apartment. I’ve lived in a few apartments, I’m glad I chose here. They by far are the best.

As a single woman I feel safe! Camera's everywhere, onsite management and well lit parking lots just to start. My unit was spotless when I moved in, even had brand new carpet! They told me all units get new carpet and they delivered.

I was transferred to the area for a year and needed a quiet clean place to live. I found this place after looking at several different apartments in the area. Immediately I could tell a difference. The office woman Jackie was great and made sure I had my deposit check back in two weeks after I moved out!

Great job Brentwood

The place is great. My husband and I lived here for a little over a year.  Leaving was the problem. When you sign the lease, you will see alot of fees they can charge you, believe it when I tell you, they will charge as many fees as they can. If you dont clean the carpet, you will pay for a new one, and that new one is $899. Keep in mind this is 1 room 1 bath. I did my best to leave the apartment clean, but they still charged us for them cleaning the bathroom, a very exagerrated fee, and a seperate fee for cleaning the stove. I obviously defended myself, as I was the one that cleaned, and they told me "it wasnt up to our standards". They even tried charging us for a "Couch disposal", which was never even ours. We took our couches. We never received our deposit back, instead received a huge invoice for "move out fees". With the experience we had, we truly recommend you read the lease and expect to pay all those exaggerated fees that are there. Dont believe the lady that gives you the contract and tells you "you wont have to pay that, is for extreme cases". I am in peace because I know how I left the apartment and is just sad that these thing have to happen. You will end up getting a huge bill, and no deposit back. This is our experience living in these apartments for 13 months. Hope it helps.

I moved in two weeks ago.  It could not of been a smoother process.  The guys in the office showed me the exact unit that I would be renting prior to me signing my lease.  I found this tremendously helpful and I was not able to do that at several other complexes that I visited.  The application process was quick  and easy.
 The kitchen and bathroom are brand new!!!!
 I cannot say enough good words about Brentwood Apartments!!!!!

I signed the lease on Saturday and by Sunday I was sleeping in my new home. The move in process couldn't have been easier. 

The apartment is beautiful, the unit is shiny and new. Couldn't have asked for a better place especially for such an affordable price.

Great management and maintenance crew …. Very attentive.
Love my view…

I've definitely had my hiccups while living here, I've been here for a few years now. Rent is astronomical for an average studio in not the best location. As a woman I don't feel safe going outside after dark in the slightest and everything you want to go to is a bit away. It's conveniently placed next to the Howard stop but the red line is a bit of a mess and with the new construction it's really unreliable. It's also not the safest of the stops and I've personally been mugged at knifepoint once there and I've been hesitant to use it since. Management is okay, not the best I've ever dealt with but not horrific. Maintenance crew is very kind but I've had mold in my bathroom on the ceiling since moving in and I've put in requests countless times but I've been repeatedly told it's just the paint and I need to have my fan on. I always have my fan on and it's very much black mold. It's just frustrating being gaslit when I know what black mold looks like and it's putting my health at risk. They're just putting a bandaid on a really serious issue. But other than that the maintence crew is good. The sound proofing is awful, I can hear my neighbors dog barking early in the morning and I always hear someone's kid down the hallway screaming at various hours. Security is a joke. They're never there. I have no idea what we're paying for because they're never downstairs, I last saw someone months ago and they always have a really nasty attitude. If you order food it will probably be left out in the street because there's no way for tenants to let anyone into the lobby unless if you race down using the very slow elevators (which one is always reserved so you can't use it) and try to meet your delivery driver. And packages have become a mess. No one monitors it anymore and packages are just chucked into the mail room that's kept open 24/7 for anyone to go into (super secure), I've had packages stepped on and stolen which is really frustrating because they set up this fancy package system that I assume my increased rent is paying for. It's just so frustrating. It's not all bad living here, the view is fantastic and i do like the size of my studio and my in unit washer/dryer. Just use caution moving in.

1) Packages are often left strewn about the lobby. When I contacted management, they told me it was the mail carriers' fault - when old management was here, this literally never happened.

Not only that, but they don't tell you when you receive a package. You'd better hope no one sends you anything important, or if they do, that they tell you when it was delivered. Because they don't log packages, many people lately have been complaining about stolen or lost packages. If you tell management about this, they will tell you it's the mail carrier's fault. How convenient.

2) Security guards refuse to give you your package if they can't immediately find it. The package room is a disaster and they hate looking for your package, so they tell you "come back tomorrow" when you know your package is in there.

3) New management changed the parking policies. Fair enough. Except for the fact that they threatened to tow us (their own residents!) instead of sending a polite email about it.

4) You are no longer allowed to get guest parking unless you get it during office hours. Want to invite a friend over after 5 pm? Tough luck, they're forced to park outside on not-the-safest street in Evanston.

5) Residents were not warned about roof construction in the early morning. Once enough residents called to complain, an email went out that afternoon, warning us that roof construction would be starting...earlier that day.

6) When doing unit inspections, they did not thank us or apologize for the inconvenience. They said "This is mandatory and will not be rescheduled."

All in all a nice place to live aside from management, but save yourself the hassle and the headache and live somewhere else.

Decent building, but key services have been lower quality since the change in ownership. Building entry, parking, and now package delivery have all been outsourced to not very reliable apps with no alternative. Secure doors are often either left unlocked or the electronic keys don't work, leaving you locked out. Front desk staff has high turnover, instead of the fewer, familiar faces of the old staff. Many seem to be checked out during their shift--making personal calls and appearing reluctant to sort incoming packages. The new package system has many poor reviews online from other buildings, and requires a payment method on-file to automatically charge residents for late pickup (or system errors).

Maintenance continues to be excellent, but also appears to be the only staff that were retained during the changeover.

I saw a shooting at the corner of Milwaukee and Howard during my stay at 415 few months ago. Many homeless hangout in the building lobby on several occasions and felt insecure. The building went downhill. Packages are delivered but not sorted in the mail room. Door system changed and not working. Recently moved along with many others because it's no longer safe to live at 415.

All in all a nice place to live aside from management, but save yourself the hassle and the headache and live somewhere else.

I have lived here for two years and have enjoyed every second of it! Management is very responsive and will resolve maintenance issues promptly. The walls are solid and will block out most of the peripheral noise from within the building. Overall the people who run the building are kind and take care of the property and it’s tenants.
I really enjoy my apartment complex. The managers are very friendly and accommodating. Maintenance is very prompt and reliable. The apartment complex is clean and looks new, I have no complaints.

I love the management here, they are so responsive and helpful. Maintenance is on-site, so they fix everything very quickly. There are parties every couple months, which is a great way to meet your neighbors. Everyone in the building is nice and friendly as well. The apartment has a very efficient layout, nice appliances, and is a great place to call home.

Lived here for a year, just moved out yesterday. The apartment is great, it’s beautiful and it feels like a hotel you get to live in. The hallway is beautiful I love the blue led lights, the have people clean the hallways and gym and amenities area every afternoon. I’ve never encountered a dirty area in the whole year I’ve lived here. Whenever anything breaks down Pete and Ardy gets on top of it and sends someone to fix it immediately. The rooftop is beautiful. Loved staying here unfortunately I’m moving out of state but if I ever move back around here I’d definitely be back!

Expect at least a 300 dollar rent increase after your first renewal.  Property management inconsiderate of your time in the apartment and wanting to schedule viewings while still living in your apartment not even giving adequate notification.  It doesn’t matter if you work overnight, they’ll still want you to jump thru hoops to do a showing in the morning.  

Property management loves to hit you with fines without even considering other alternatives and taking into consideration that a non pet deposit. Also, threatening to coming in and out of your apartment without notice.  

I don’t recommend living here.

RUN! Oak Park Residence Corporation is NOT what it use to be and has hit an all-time low.   Expect a 4% or more annual increase in your rent.  They are overly priced for what you receive.  The one thing they do well is try to put that “used car salesman” spin on “upgrades”.  A “remodeled” laundry room that consisted of the same dented 10+ year old machines that constantly break, freshly painted dirty walls/floors, and water dripping from ceilings.  Please keep in mind, when machines break, you (the tenant) are responsible to contact the company they are leased from and schedule them to come work on the machine.  Every spring/summer, the decks and units are overrun with spiders, including those that drop down on your face while you are sleeping.  All contractors outside of maintenance are bottom barrel hires.  This includes the company they hired to prepare the building for the “new windows” they installed a several years ago.  Ever since these “upgrades”, you will experience a real nature feel with the constant ceiling/wall water leaks that they will “fix” and a few months later paint over.  Fear not, they will be back within a few more months, including the those they delay fixing due to “weather” and then ignore for months.  Bathroom walls bow and have such internal water damage that they crumble under the weight of a single empty shelf. Due to the lack of bathroom ventilation, black mold will grow from the ceiling and walls.  The solution I was given was to shower with the bathroom door or window open.  Nothing beats a hot shower with a fresh artic wind blowing in during the 9 months of winter.  They claim to treat all tenants fairly.  There are individuals living within units that are not on leases (even though this is “required” for background checks and safety).  These residents vocally brag about getting away with it as OPRC won’t do anything about it.   Long term residents who abide by the rules have quickly bailed and left due to the condition of the properties and lack of attention from property management.  Electronic tracking key locks were installed on all doors/units, so privacy is a thing of the past.  It’s hard to reach property managers as they clearly screen phone calls.  Additional bonuses include ~$1,000/year in village parking fees (if you drive), an area with extremely high crime including break-ins (units and vehicles), shootings almost daily (day and night), high speed chases/crashes, assaults, robberies, hit and runs, and more!

The property where I live is very dirty and people leave their trash everywhere. I've had mice before and water damage that they took way too long to fix. The laundry room has not been updated probably since the machines have been installed. The machines are in very poor condition and all they do is take money. We have complained and nothing has happened. I have been told that the machines will be updated back in 2021 but nothing. The dishwasher in the unit is in very poor condition too. Do not rent using this "service".

It's been a few years since I lived here, however, I loved this apartment.  The rooms are a good size, it has a separate dining area, which I totally loved.  It could have had more closet space, but I made a way.  They kept the garden area and laundry area clean.  Whenever I needed something done in my apartment, they were prompt.  The corporation and my property manager was very helpful.  When I am ready to move again, I will most likely consider OPRC in my search.

This place is great in theory. It looks nice, has some nice amenities but there are kinks that keep it from really being luxury. The plumbing backs up (often), they don't enforce the pet policy (dogs bark all day and night despite complaints from neighboring units). Because of the staff turnover the door people don't know the residents despite being a small building and projects seem to start but never quite get done. The location is great and people inside are very nice but you're paying more than its probably worth.

When I first moved in 2020 it was an ok place, the floors/ ceiling are very thin, so you will hear your upstairs neighbor very easily! In summer/ fall 2023 someone in the 4th floor get bed bugs very very badly, they did not report this on time! I unfortunately got them as well and I  have been dealing with this issue since November 2023-July 2024! The management office hears you, but also questions if they are really in my apartment. I do not recommend moving into apartments in the 80-82 range of each floor!
There is a maintenance person onsite and thankfully he is the only one that gets things done, most of the time! The washers and dryer also suck!

I have had the tremendous fortune to live here for the past two years and can't say enough about how much I enjoyed my time here.

Especially as the owner of a dog some places consider "too high risk" (she's a Belgian Malinois, very similar to a German Shepherd) by many places in the city- Legend Group stands out.  

The Lakeview East neighborhood is amazing, there is a ton to do, and you're a 15 minute walk to the Red Line (and Wrigley for that matter).  

The Building Supervisor, Orlando, is one of the nicest guys you'll ever meet and the management group is attentive and has always treated me like a person (especially in these wild times).

If I was not moving out of the city for my new job I'd 100% be renewing my lease!

Mac properties is a decent company to rent an apartment though. It's fairly expensive in my opinion for the maintenance and care of the building however and the communication from department to department isn't good. I would like to renew my lease once it's up, however I would like to see some improvements.

Ever need maintance? They're always Right there. It's great im such a clutz running into doors and clogging drains with my hair! These 
Studios are big enough for any lifestyle.

The staff is always on top of things and I always feel like they're keeping us updated with everything. I like living here a lot and the amenities are nice. Gym is small but if you find the right time you're golden.
nothing but positive things to say about my living experience at Wave Lakeview! cannot wait to enjoy another summer on the rooftop or right along the lake.

I have lived here for a few years, and it has been a very positive experience, but there needs to be an upgrade to the older central heating system now that is too hot in the warmer winter days. Everything else is modern amenities and works very nice. The management and staff here are very accommodating and friendly.   The view is amazing from the top because the location is prime in Lakeview. All in all, I enjoy living here.
The hot water is not hot. You're lucky to have a hot shower. Maintenance says they increase the boiler temperature, but it helps for the day or two, and then water is cold again.
Good place to live. It is right by the lake. Nic me restaurants. Good location to public transportation   Good upgrades for kitchen and bathroom. Wash and dryer
Nice place , good location , comfortable apartment, great view from the balcony, love it so much, kids enjoy gym and pool, also pet friendly, my dogs are exited to be here

I am writing this review in January, one of the coldest months in Chicago and my room is currently 58 degrees. The city requires the temperature to always be above 69+.I have filled numerous work orders, even reported to the city but they no action has been taken. It is very cold and they are not heating the units. BE WARNED!

After residing in this apartment building for 3 years, my experience has been riddled with frustration and disappointment. The promised amenities, such as the rooftop deck, have remained inaccessible throughout my entire tenure. The service elevator has repeatedly malfunctioned, leaving me (and almost every other tenant I’ve talked to) stranded on multiple occasions. I had one instance where I was stuck in the service elevator late at night, frantically pressing the emergency buttons and alarms to no avail. Despite reaching out to management about this incident, I received no response. The lack of action from management only added to the sense of helplessness and vulnerability.

The presence of cockroaches in both my living space and the parking garage has been a constant source of distress. Despite countless complaints, management allows this issue to persist.

The laundry room is barely functional. It's perpetually in a state of disrepair, with malfunctioning machines and unsanitary conditions.

The management of this building is abysmal, to say the least. Their consistent failure to address critical issues speaks volumes about their incompetence and lack of regard for resident well-being. Basic amenities are routinely neglected, with repairs taking months (if YEARS) to be addressed, if they're addressed at all. The communication is virtually nonexistent, with management ignoring emails and requests for assistance.

Their disregard for tenant safety is alarming. The non-functional emergency features in the service elevator, coupled with the lack of response to maintenance requests, create a hazardous living environment. It's clear that management prioritizes cost-cutting over resident safety/satisfaction.

A particularly egregious aspect of management's conduct is their propensity to issue excessive fines for minor infractions. Residents are bombarded with threats of fines for the most trivial of matters, creating an atmosphere of fear and distrust. I recall one instance where the property manager sent 7 separate emails in a single day, each threatening a fine for a different perceived transgression. Don’t breathe too loudly here - it could cost you $500. 

In conclusion, the issues plaguing this apartment building go far beyond mere inconvenience; they pose a serious threat to resident safety and well-being. Unless drastic changes are made, I cannot in good conscience recommend this building to anyone seeking a safe and comfortable living environment.

Mail room door broken and left unlocked. If it is locked, good luck getting your key fob to work to open it. Laundry room floods, washers and dryers broken. The “gym” is a joke. This was a day or two after they called my mom (only listed on the lease as my emergency contact) who told them the same thing I did- I had the apartment for the whole month and was taking that time to move out!! They still came in and trashed the place (and left the door unlocked). Terrible management and a subpar place to live for the amount they charge for rent. The location's great but definitely not worth it. I'd recommend checking out any of the nearby buildings before this one
