Save your money and time by looking somewhere else if you can. Any 5-star reviews are due to management offering money for them, not because the building deserves it at all.

I've lived at 4241 N. Kenmore for 5 years now and I am overall extremely satisfied with the experience. I lived in one of the 375 Sq Ft Studio apartments during this time and it was perfect for me while I was attending school downtown. The building is well maintained and the building manager Kalia and her husband do a wonderful job taking care of things including decorating the public areas and signing for/collecting packages to prevent the wrong people from taking them.

The space itself is great. A large square to maximize space with a little inlet for the kitchen and the bathroom. Water pressure is good and the maintenance is timely and do a wonderful job in fixing the few problems that cropped up. The view is nothing special. I get to stare at the lovely brick wall at the building next to this one, but for the price it was well worth the sacrifice of scenery. One potential negative is that the walls/floors/ceilings are pretty thin, so if you are sensitive to noise like me you will hear other people's television and music on occasion. Fortunately, the building manager is very good at handling noise complaints.

Buena Park is a beautiful neighborhood with easy access to the Red Line with buses that will take you to the Brown and Blue lines as well. A super Target is very close by along with a Jewel-Osco for all of your shopping needs. There are a few bars and family owned restaurants that are absolute must trys and it's a nice walk to some nice beaches including the Wilson Dog beach if that's your thing.
This is a great building. Lots of amenities for a good price. The area is pretty quiet but a close walk to grocery shopping, restaurants, and more! It is spacious with excellent appliances.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: Dirty units, dirty buildings, poor amenities, dirty wash machines and dryers, trash shoot is always clogged making the floors smell crazy, i can go on and on, bottoms line, it’s worse than student housing …don’t waste your money

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review:
I wish I could give 0 stars to Letterman Chicago because even 1 star feels too generous. My experience at this apartment has been nothing short of a nightmare. From the day I moved in, I faced constant issues, including water damage, leaking toilets, wet carpeting, and a foul odor that made the unit completely uninhabitable. Despite reporting these problems multiple times, management failed to provide any meaningful resolutions.

The situation escalated when my unit experienced sink regurgitation, soaking the carpet, damaging my personal belongings, and attracting bugs. The smell of sewage was so unbearable that it caused me physical distress. To make matters worse, smoking and odors from neighboring units infiltrated my apartment every single day, making it impossible to find peace or comfort at home.

When I asked to terminate my lease due to these unacceptable conditions, management refused and forced me to stay in the unit, despite the ongoing problems. This lack of care and basic decency from the management is completely unacceptable.

Living here was a nightmare physically, mentally, and emotionally. The stress and anxiety caused by this apartment have taken a serious toll on my well-being. I don’t even want to give a single star. If you’re looking for a safe, clean, and livable apartment, avoid Letterman Chicago at all costs. Don’t waste your money, health, or sanity on this place.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: Amenities are a joke. Its unclean, maintenance doesn’t like doing their jobs, they’re disrespectful when entering the apartments and complain in front of tenants. On top of that this dumpster of a place wants to increase rent. Management also has an extremely poor attitude towards tenants nor do they respect them. Along with the disgusting lobby and embarrassing hallways and unruly service. It would be incredibly idiotic to even so much as think to live in a dump such as The Letterman. This place makes me sick.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: I lived here for during Summer 2022. I paid $150 move-in fee and they only cleaned the bedroom and not the common areas were in terrible condition. And when I moved out they forced me to $170 cleaning fee for the areas I was not responsible for. Terrible management, terrible staff. I don’t recommend this place at all.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: Omg automatic lofts are amazing. The people are so nice I would love to stay for a long time this place is for me. So close to the subway and easy for to get it I fell in love with it all.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: I really like the apartment and I wish to live there for the rest of the days.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review:
This is the perfect building for students attending college in downtown Chicago who desire to live in close proximity to class, shopping centers, and the nightlife of Chicago. The rooms have fully furnished units that are modern, have up to date furniture, and just about every television channel you would want to watch. Unlike other student complexes in the loop, the wifi is extremely reliable. The unit is very cognizant of residents without cars, specifically with UIC college and Target located within walking distance roughly a block away. Also, with the blue line train system and freeway located directly across the street, getting to and from the complex is made easy. Pool tables, a large TV room, and KISS FM playing throughout the first floor lounge creates a great atmosphere for residents to have fun, interact, and stay upbeat. 
Oh, and it's probably worth mentioning the free Starbucks served every morning for sleep-deprived college students. If you're attending college in or near downtown Chicago and love the city feel and bright lights, the decision to live here should be automatic.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: I love the location! It's close to all the major highways and right off the blue line. Making it easy to get anywhere in the city. I recently sold my car because everything I need is within walking distance. Along with a plethora of bars, restaurants and nightlife to choose form. Great staff whom are always willing to help.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: The automatic loft is an extremely nice place to live because of the people, environment, price, and it is just a pleasure to be here. As a professional student with a busy schedule and not much time for social events at school I'm able to enjoy a convenient social life here because they host so many fun events.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: This apartment offers many benefits, including fully furnished spaces, clean and appealing living spaces, beautiful city views, extremely friendly and helpful staff, and much more. Although it is more than 10  minutes walking distance from the Chicago Loop, it is conveniently located just minutes from a CTA station that drops off nearly anywhere in the city. On a crime distribution map, the building passes  perfectly as it rests in a location with minimal to no crime reports. The staff has many events planned to create opportunities for the residence to meet. The living spaces have large windows to accommodate those that do not receive a window room. All together, Automatic Lofts is run very well and is a highly acceptable place to live.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: The Automatic Lofts are great for students. They're right across the road from UIC and the blue line, and within easy walking distance to Mariano's (grocery store), Target, and Greektown (a great area to get food or go hang out with friends. They even have parking available under the apartments! Great location with security and they have options to match you with roommates so you don't have to worry about finding people to lease with, although you could if you and a friend wanted to live together. There's a gym on the first floor, and they have community events so you can bond with your roommates and get to know other people in the building. The apartments have a great feel to them too. They come furnished and there are exposed brick walls and wood beam ceilings giving the place an old Chicago vibe. I would definitely suggest this place to any student looking for an affordable, but awesome place to live.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: The Automatic Lofts is the perfect place for beginners. It's right across the street from UIC, super close to the blue line, and right by Greek Town and Little Italy. It's reasonably priced and fully furnished! The staff and residents friendly and welcoming, and the wooden beams and brick walls give it an urban, yet cozy, feel.

apartmentName: The Letterman Chicago - West Loop Apartments
review: Automatic lofts is a great place to live. Very convenient location, minutes from downtown. Everyone on the staff is nice & always willing to help.

The first week I moved in, I was forced to undergo not one, but *two* bedbug treatment plans because of my neighbor. I had to put everything I had in the bathroom while my unit was heated to a couple-some hundred degrees to kill these bugs that had been there on a recurring basis before I even moved in. No one told me that when I arrived, but they had to treat my unit, too.  While it got off to a horrible start, I was still optimistic –– until I walked in the bathroom one morning to find a cockroach, at least two inches in length. I lived on one of the highest floors, and was/am a relatively tidy tenant, and while I moved out of the Sovereign a year ago, I killed approximately 45 cockroaches in the time I was there. Often found them in the halls, sometimes dead and sometimes alive, too. Pest control did absolutely nothing. I took it upon myself to use every kind of sealant possible, yet nothing. Please don't live here, I'm so glad I no longer do. 

45 cockroaches. I wish I were kidding.

You’d think with it being such an old building that the walls would at least be made out of concrete or something thicker but I swear they’re plywood. I can clearly hear my neighbor talking on the phone from 8pm to 2am nightly for the past 3 years I’ve lived here. Who could she possibly be talking to for that long? Also forget about taking a decent shower as the water pressure/temperature is god awful. Do yourself a favor and look for somewhere else to live.

I lived here for 6 months, and I wish I could forget my time here. Everything is very cheaply made/finished. The tile has been painted over multiple times in the shower. What? why would someone even do that? I have found cockroaches in the apartment a few times. They "fixed" my door and now I have to shove my body weight against it to get it to open or close. The management seems to not care all that much. It's insanely cheap, but you get what you pay for. My whole hallway smelt like cigarettes because one tenant is a chain smoker. I  reported it multiple times and they did nothing about it. It got so bad that i put a scarf under my door to try to get the smell to go away. I feel gross even being in the building. I wish I had taken more time in looking for an apartment. The only good thing is you can't hear your neighbors.

There's a Thai restaurant downstairs and an excellent coffee shop across the street, which are my favorite features of my current location. The staff here is always helpful and on-site, as well as friendly. They change the carpets every time a new move-in occurs, apparently, so it was nice and clean when we moved in over a year ago. The overall area around this apartment also has a low crime-rate (especially for Chicago) and is generally friendly and relaxing. It's very convenient if you're a Loyola student or you wish to commute via Red Line (like we do.) We can see the Red Line from our Living Room window but it's far enough away the noise won't bother you. Some apartments in this building also have a view of the lake, as I'm told... You can see just a sliver of it from one of our windows, haha. There's also a gym in our building, but you'll have to purchase a membership.
  Anyway, on to the negatives... Our kitchen is tiny. It came with a full-size fridge and an oven/stove, so that was nice, but there's hardly any room to do anything in there. Our counter space is so small it's difficult to even do dishes, and we can't fit more than our toaster on there if we're going to use a drying rack for our drying dishes. I feel as if our kitchen was a closet previously. I'd be happier if they knocked out the wall between the living room closet and the kitchen and made the whole thing a kitchen. Our bathroom is very small too, but it's not as noticeable. 
The other thing that bothers me is the laundry situation. Maybe we are cursed, but the washing/drying machines on our floor break down pretty often. There's just two washing machines and two drying, and they are constantly being used when we need them by other residents. I guess the building can't have much control over these factors, but it's something to think about when considering moving into this building. I very often have to do my laundry on a different floor.
All-in-all, the pros outweigh the cons in this building, but it feels a tad expensive for its features. Compared to other buildings in the area, the price is steep for its quality. It's always good to keep in mind that living close to the loop will raise the price a great deal. You aren't taking much risk living here, it really is a great building, all-in-all.

My wife and I have been at this apartment for nearly two years now. Great local coffee shop right across the street for those early bird coffee runs. Located in a quiet college neighbor 200 yards from Lake Michigan. Formerly a hotel, the outer walls of each apartment are solid concrete so you get great privacy and separation from other tenants and the inevitable noises. Utilites included!! Trash shoot and laundry on every floor! Highly recommend this apartment!

The carpeted halls are a bit dingy and could be improved. Also, they are doing construction which can be a bit noisy. I love love love this place only moving because I need a dog friendly building.

Parc Huron has been an amazing place to live! I moved pretty last minute from many states away and they were super accommodating and helpful. Gave me a virtual tour, and was very up-front about the whole process, which made it so smooth to move.

Flair Tower is more than an apartment building it is a home.  The entire staff and care taken of the property make it feel so.

Moving from Florida to Chicago was the biggest move I've ever made- emotionally and physically. The second I applied to live at Flair Tower has been nothing but high class all the way. My unit is a great size, updated appliances, updated counters, updated flooring, in unit W/D. My rent is more than fair for the size and quality of the apartment.
