The management company will respond to your requests very fast and the common areas are kept very clean.  The apartment itself is very large for a one-bedroom in the area.  Most of the apartments have a step down living room and a full size kitchen.   Arguably this apartment is one of the best one-bedroom apartments in the city for the money.

I lived here for 3 years and had a good experience, but there is definitely room for improvement and potential to make it even better.

Pros:
Good location, dog friendly, washer and dryer in unit, dishwasher, responsive maintenance, rooftop

Cons:
Only one elevator which is challenging when someone's moving or it's broken, no garbage disposals, limited community space, few events, tiny gym, can be noisy (door slams, parties, people gathering at elevator late at night), trash and dog poop on west side of building, no poop bags or bins, no package security, drafty windows, aggressive dog incidents

Suggestions for management:
- Don't increase the rent for existing tenants by ~$400+ per month. They proposed a hefty increase for me and some of my neighbors when it came time to renew in the past few months. It's more expensive to find new customers than keep existing ones, and some units remained vacant for several months after they raised rates.

If you're increasing the rent, instead of resting on your laurels (location), give people a reason to stay by making improvements to the property and/or units. I proposed some of the ideas below to the property manager while I lived there.
- Open up the area behind the gym for community events vs. only using it for occasional staff meetings. The rooftop is great, but you can only use it a few months out of the year. Also, more events would have been nice versus just once or twice a year.
- Install package lockers in the lobby for security and to keep that area tidy. I got frustrated having to sift through a sea of (sometimes heavy) packages to find mine, and it is all out in the open.
- Install better lighting in the hallways for security reasons and to make the place feel more cheerful. Current lighting is very dim.
- Regularly clean up the trash, dog poop, and broken glass in the grassy areas on the west side of the building off N Honore. While that's technically not part of the property (per management), it's right next to it, so it is a reflection on the property. I cleaned things up a few times because I didn't want my dog to step in it, but I shouldn't have had to. If it's the city's responsibility, management should call the city to take care of it.

All in all, though, not a bad place to call home if you're new to Chicago.

I lived in one of the South/West facing corner units for three years and truly loved my experience. 

Tina, the building/leasing manager and Doug, the building engineer, are both wonderful, very responsive if you need help, and they're always looking to make the building a fantastic place to live. For example, based on feedback from the tenants, they put in a gym on the first floor with a treadmill, hand weights, weight machine and a Peloton, which was perfect. They also recently added a coffee machine to the lobby, which was a great touch. 

The units are beautiful and the appliances are fantastic. I loved the KitchenAid appliances so much that I am planning to buy the same pieces when I purchase a home soon. 

The only reason I moved out was due to a relocation but I would highly recommend this building.
This building has been a horrible experience and I would strongly advise people not live here. Most people I speak to are unhappy. Just don't do it.

My experience here has been extremely disappointing and I would strongly recommend people avoid this building. While the location and amenities are attractive, I have had numerous issues since moving in (including bugs in my unit and common areas, repeat Wi-Fi crashes, my dishwasher flooding repeatedly, my washing machine breaking down repeatedly, and a moldy ceiling from a leaking pipe that was missed before my move-in). Other residents have also shared with me that they are looking into terminating their leases early due to poor experiences.

The biggest issue has been that my apartment has had an ongoing problem with sewer gas since October 2023. The sewer gas comes out of multiple rooms in my apartment at multiple times throughout the day and night. I have also smelled it in the common hallway, basement, and other units on the north/east side of the building (the 11/13/14 unit corner).

Despite the situation being ongoing since October 2023 and inspectors confirming the sewer gas in May 2024, the situation has yet to be resolved.

All in all, save yourself the trouble (and literal headache from sewer gas) and find somewhere else to live.
There are many other high-rises you can move into for the same or less money that offer more. The apartments are outdated.

Love the building but over the past year the front desk team has been wedeled down to a group of people who were caring and welcoming to a group of people who are indifferent to providing service. Also, the self-service package room is a mess. There is no inventory done and there is no way to know if you have a delivery other than checking the room each and every day -- and that is even if the boxes are put on the right shelves. It really is a great building, but they need to get their act together with their staffing and package handling.

Lived here for ~3 years with my husband and our dog. Cannot recommend the building more. Great apartments and finishes, awesome location, incredible amenities and the BEST staff. The management team is extremely responsive and easy to work with and the concierge is friendly, attentive, and are like family. Jeremy, Ralph, and Jonathan are especially amazing - we’re going to miss them so much! If we were staying in Chicago we 100% would have continued to live at State & Chestnut!

I've lived in Chicago all of my life, and since I was young I dreamed of living somewhere downtown. Seeing how beautiful and affordable it is really embodies the vision I've had since I was young. With its prime location and amazing view, I can't wait to live here!

I have been living at 3000 N Sheridan for nearly 5 years. I have also lived in another Wirtz property on Melrose before living here. The first thing I have to say about Wirtz Residential is that they know what they're doing and are very thorough and "legit" in their practices and they treat good tenants VERY well. The application process may seem excessive, but you want to go through with it because once you're a tenant here life is grand. 

3000 is a particularly nice building - the area is great and you live in one of the nicest residential properties (and that goes for ones you can buy) in  Lakeview. The staff is helpful and maintenance is generally pretty attentive and will fix things right away when needed. 

The bang for your buck is unprecedented. Do the cost per square footage calculation and compare it to other apartments - you will be amazed at how great a value this building is. Best of all, I get stellar compliments on my apartment from each guest that I have over. The apartments are beautiful, well maintained, and are very, very large.

I have lived here for a little over two years. When I first got here, I very much enjoyed it and the property did not have many issues. The neighborhood is great and the facilities, including the gym, are pretty solid. However recently, every week either the power or the water go out. Management and maintenance is slow to react to anything and are generally unhelpful/incompetent with any individual issues. Upkeep around the apartment has suffered. Rent increased this year about 5% higher than the Chicago average and the building has only gotten worse.

My wife and I lived here for three years and have nothing but good things to say about the property.  It's great value for the area, the appliances are great, the apartment is beautiful and well maintained, and the management team and staff are responsive, respectful, and kind. We are leaving Chicago but otherwise we would have stayed here for many more years.  Highly recommend!

My girlfriend and I chose a one bedroom in this property for several reasons:

1) They allowed a 6mo lease with option to renew, perfect for our work situation that has us moving to California at the end of the year

2) Location: in Lakeview, two blocks from the lake, with two small grocery stores a block away, a dry cleaner in the building and plenty of restaurants and other stores less than a 15 min block away

3) No deposit (!!!)

4) Amenities: The apartment itself is spacious, with open concept living room and kitchen, great upkeep and appliances. Plenty of closet space too - the bathroom is a bit small but it works. There's laundry in the building, a gym and a huge deck with sun loungers, eating spaces, chilling out spaces and grills. Awesome to have people over.

5) No doorman but door staff during the day and maintenance 24/7. This means that when you invite people over it's not too much of a hassle having to go through door people to allow them up. Personally this is a bonus. 

6) Price. I think it was fair for the apartment and building amenities and especially considering there is no need for deposit and they allowed short leases

Beautiful updated apartments! I have a pretty good view of the lake. The deck is nice and has grills  and furniture so you can hang out and meet people in the building. We also have a gym in the building which is what finally got me to start working out. Great place.

The only units with views are the "penthouses" they rent out for 3-4x a regular montage. Parking is an additional 250/mo. Expect annual 4% rent hikes - no negotiating.

Their "award winning remodel" won the award for getting the most done with the least amount of money - and it's showing its wear. They tout that they're in west loop, but they're in Fulton river district and you'll have to walk across the 8-lane highway to get to west loop.

The condo units face each other, the lower level units have no views, expect to hear the metra go by according to schedule daily. The higher level units used to be great but there's so much construction you don't see anything but the residential units looking into your apartment now.

For a "luxury" apartment building, the road it's on is decrepit. Located next to an unmaintained underpass and behind a restaurant. People recently had their cars stolen from the garage.

This is a great building, centrally located in Chicago's West Loop neighborhood.  Walking distance to Union station and CTA bus and train spots makes it easy to get around the city and to other destinations outside of the state.  The building itself is very well maintained and you're always greeted by a friendly face.  Walking distance from Chicago's famous Randolph St restaurant district, Jewel Osco, Whole Foods and the French Market, this location is hard to beat!

I have lived her for only 8 mts..   I have  battle cockroaches and the tenants above me smoke - a violation of their lease. I have submitted 2 incident reports.  Just this week mold appeared in my bedroom - near my bed... so now I  have to sleep and breathe in mold every night...  Management refuses to do anything about the smoking - even while other tenants have complained and the tenants have even  to smoking in their unit.  The washing machines are filthy and the laundry room has flooded a number of times.
The new management is crap. Stay away from this property.

-Terrible management. They ignore emails and never seem to be on your side if you have an issue. 
-Parking is so tight good luck not getting your car hit.
-During the winter, cold air seeps through the windows. Management tried to fix it, but didn't, and told me this building had old windows and that's just how it is. This raised my bill so high and I was freezing all winter.
-A dog has been barking since the day I got here and has been going unresolved for months even though a doorman confirmed the barking and I sent a video of the barking at the beginning of my lease. They keep saying I need another doorman to hear it and more videos.

This building is far from what it may seem.
We loved the leasing office and thought that the apartment was in a great location. All of the tenants seemed friendly and happy.

Price is a little high compared to some options in the area. Plus some of the amenities that would add value are a little below average. For example, the gym is a little small, the laundry is very expensive and we've barely been able to use the rooftop because of all the building construction...which is very loud and annoying
I would definitely recommend this building to friends. The staff is helpful and the building is in really good shape. No one wants to live in an old and tired building.
The only problem I have is with all the noise with the works. It has started up again and it?;s so loud I can't think during the day. This makes it hard to study.
This apartment has a fantastic location with first class amenities.
Great bustle in the neighborhood but feels quiet and comfy inside. Everyone is very nice.
love my new apartment. The distance to the lake is really convenient for taking my dog on walks. The new management renovated the place and it looks nice and modern.

Where do I start? At first glance a person who's desperate for a place to stay might think they hit the jackpot by finding This place. The move in special is what first gets your attention, half off first months rent would be a life saver for anyone. But after the landlords had our $100 non-refundable application fee it seemed like even with good credit that offer wasnt on the table anymore. Either way we needed a place to stay, so we went ahead and signed a one year lease, but that was only after pulling the landlords teeth to get them to tell you that you dont have to sign the 36 month lease that they will push on you ever so relentlessly. Moments after the lease was signed and filed away they precede to tell me that there is one problem apartment on our floor and the tenant is dirty so there may be a little bug problem for the first month but after that person is evicted it will be back to like before, bug free. LIES! Were now 6 months in and we've found hundreds of B. germanica (German roach) and P. americana (American roach) <--- which are huge and fast and they bring my poor girlfriend to tears. After speaking with some of the neighbors its very clear that everyone gets the same story. "Youll love it here! The last person who lived in your apartment lived here for 17 years." "Its a brand new apartment!" Theyre all lies, they just paint over every square inch of the place and call it "new". There are even roach legs clearly stuck to the wall from a lethal blow, and then painted over. Its despicable. RUN. Run as fast as you can away from 5036 n sheridan in chicago. Youll never be desperate enough to live here happily. Ive had so many roach encounters and I honestly believe they're running away, just like we are.

The place is full with roaches they claim that they spray it every 3 Months but I never seen anyone come in.i had to but products and try to fix the problem myself.as soon as I moved in it didn't take me long to realize it,as I spoke to the neighbors everybody has the same problem. No one lives there more than the lease term. They also got me to sign a year and half term which is odd, but I totally understand why know.The lady and man in the apartment are super rude and it's really hard to communicate with them especially the man.I would tell anybody that wants to move here don't make the same mistake I did.I also found a lot of bad reviews about the building after I moved in wish I did my research before.

Pros: My unit was near the top floor and facing the southeast so my view was mind blowing. If you have a southern facing corner unit and it’s high up, you will love the apartment. Other than that, Laundry room is well-maintained and always open. Maintenance is great. Location is fantastic (especially if you use public transportation). Very safe building - didn’t see anything sketchy or ever feel in danger. Right by a dog park which is nice for some people. Never had any issues with bugs or anything of that nature.

Cons: Elevators are slow and the building isn’t brand new but you get over both of those quickly in my opinion. 

Summary: I lived there for a year and only moved because of a new job. Otherwise, I would’ve renewed my lease. It really is a great apartment and I’m happy I picked it… And for that reason, I felt like I should share my experience. Hopefully it helped!
I have lived there for few years. Great building. Amazing area . Beautiful view

If you are looking to live in the Gold Coast/River North area, this is probably the best priced building in that part of the city. Management is nice, prompt, and helpful. When my husband and I first signed the lease, management was able to accommodate our requests at no additional cost, specifically installing laminate flooring in the living room and bedroom, as well as installing a dishwasher. We would have renewed our lease if we weren't moving. Living here made our year in Chicago especially wonderful!

I lived here for 3 years. This is a great building - apparently, it is not one of those newest buildings, but property management has been upgrading over the years. We've got new tiles, lobbies, fitness centers and party room this year. The amenity is well maintained. I never had to wait for the washer/dryers, gym is great and clean, and there is a huge sun deck that definitely adds a great value. The building's location is unbeatable, very close to train and bus station, Michigan Ave, and walkable to River North and Gold Coast neighborhoods. 

The thing I like the most is definitely the staff. Everyone is very friendly and very helpful. The building manager, Laura, makes everything incredibly easy. I have made all kinds of requests during my time here, such as switching units, temporary parking and etc. Laura really went above and beyond to accommodate my requests and provided a lot of flexibility for many of my very last minute requests. I am very thankful for all the help I've got.

I had to move out of this building due to work relocation, but I will always recommend this building to anyone.

I have been living here for one and a half year and have to say, the staff here are very responsible, tenants are easy to get quick responses from the manager. The doorman and maintenance personnel treat their work very carefully and seriously. The highlight of the building should be its location, close to Loyola University water tower campus, Ogden International School, 22 Bus and Chicago/State station of red line. The rooms of 7 and 8 have a good view to see the Washington Square Park and Lake of Michigan.

55 West Chestnut is a great place to live.  The building staff are all so friendly.  I was very happy with my apartment!!  The building manager, Laura, was on top of everything there.  She was quick to respond to any questions and always willing to help out.  The location is awesome also...very close to the lake, shopping and restaurants.  So very convenient!!  I would highly recommend 55 West Chestnut!!!

I'm so happy we found this building! My daughter moved to Chicago for work and was blessed to find such a great apartment. Laura was very helpful and made sure everything was always smooth, from move in to move out! The unit and amenities fit our needs perfectly and were appropriate. Location is especially amazing! The door person added security and peace of mind (especially for parents). Highly recommended!

I lived here for 2 years and had a wonderful experience. I was very happy with my unit, the building amenities, location, and the building staff are all so friendly and helpful. Laura was always on top of whatever I needed! Would recommend!!

I love living here! Everyone is so friendly. The manager, Laura, is so awesome and helpful. The bulding is very well-kept and modern.  It is also in the best location in Chicago! It’s close to the lake and a bunch of great restaraunts and shops. It’s a great place to live!

I have nothing but good things to say about this building. The staff is very accommodating and friendly. The manager, Laura, is very helpful and truly cares for the residents. I LOVE the big patio, there are grills and plenty of tables to sit at—great for entertaining guests! Renovations to the lobby and party room are just finishing up and so far they look great! There is also a business center with computers and a printer—ink and paper is provided. The location is one of the bests in Chicago. Close to the mag mile, grocery stores, restaurants, bars, and the beach! Safety was a top priority in my apartment searching. I feel very safe in this building with the front door security. I plan on staying in the building for many years to come.

Being new to Chicago, I was very happy to find 55 W Chestnut - my home for the past 2 years. The location is perfect - very close to both the Red and the Brown CTA lines, and walking distance to many choices for markets, restaurants, and nightlight. The building is very well taken care of by the staff, who also happen to be very nice people. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking to live closer to downtown while still looking for more of a neighborhood feel when you walk out the front door.

Loved living at 55 W. Chestnut! Amazing location, very close to grocery stores, shops, restaurants, night life... as well as the beach! Public transportation is very accessible from here as well. This is one of Chicago's prime locations!! Very safe building, very friendly staff, very pleasant building manager! Questions and concerns are handled efficiently and quickly. Apartments are spacious and confortable. Esther is amazing: she's thoughtful, sweet, kind, and caring. Laura, the manager, is excellent! Make sure to get in touch with her and secure an awesome apartment at 55 W. Chestnut! Don't miss out!!

I absolutely loved living at 55 W Chestnut. I lived in a 2 bedroom, 1 bathroom apartment with another roommate. Spacious area, great location-- in the vicinity of Old Town, Gold Coast, and River North. Shopping, grocery stores, and restaurants all walking distance away. The landlord, Laura, was very helpful -- answered emails on time and no matter what was going on, she was always willing to help out and respond in a timely manner. There is also a doorman/ security right before entering the building, which definitely made it safer. Esther was excellent as well. She was very helpful and always would go out of her way to say hello and help others. 

Really recommend this building! If you have any questions, make sure to reach out to Laura!

I have been trapped in my apartment since yesterday because both of the elevators are not working - there has been zero communication from the property management.  Only one elevator was working for weeks and now there are none.  If you need elevators for health reasons - do not ever move here!         Some of the front door staff make you feel uncomfortable asking for anything, one was sitting up there with her shoes off!  They frequently walk the hallways talking to their friends on the phone.  There has been a shooting in this building - no communication from property staff.  All my work clothes have been destroyed in the washing machines, they look like they were tie dyed now.  And that is when you can actually find one, be prepared to fight to try to do one load of laundry.

This apartment complex is great if you want to live in a walkable area. The apartment amenities are reasonable provided the location and price. The staff are also helpful and friendly. Maintenance requests are always completed within a few hours, and the management team and door staff are polite and responsive.

Terrible place to live.  I would not recommend living here to anyone.  The elevators are terrible and usually do not work.  The door staff is constantly rude and super unprofessional.  You feel guilty asking the door staff to help with anything because they make it seem like you are inconveniencing their life so much.  Not to mention, the worst heat/AC situation I could ever imagine living in.  The AC does not turn on until mid May - June, so this means you get to spend all of April/May sweating in your own apartment because it is 80 degrees.  There are also only 7 or 8 washer/dryers for the entire building, so good luck trying to find a time where there are multiple open, especially on a weekend.

I live in a 1bd, and although the living room and bedroom are nice, the walls/floors/ceilings in this building are questionable to say the least. There is a part of my apartment which physically slopes down a noticeable amount, and in fact, I've noticed the entire apartment is actually slightly uneven. The sound bleed from doors and walls/ceiling are immense; I can hear people talking upstairs/ watching tv through the ceiling often over my own conversations/ tv (same goes for next door). The elevators are concerningly broken (no buttons light, it goes up instead of down, the doors will shutter, etc). I have found only a small portion of the apartment that doesn't squeak when even I walk (I'm only 120lbs). The electrical is a danger, several switches and outlets have sparked or simply no longer work. THE BEST: there is a fist-sized hole above my shower, and maintenance shrugged it off saying "they fill it when you move out anyways," so for going on 6mos now drywall and water from upstairs (and rain) have been leaking into my shower. Icing: the kitchen has space, but it is closed off meaning it is walled in with no access to natural light and it gets HOT and LOUD; and the gas stove is "iffy" to say the least.

Currently live in a 1 bedroom apartment on the top floor.  Bedroom is large with a wall length closet space (plenty of room for 2 people).  Kitchen has a decent amount of counter space and to side is plenty of room for a table and 4 chairs.  The living room area is very large (enough room for 2 couches, rocking chair, TV, and coffee table).  There are two air conditioners (one in the bedroom and one in the living room space, so temperature control is not an issue).  The building manager is very nice and quicker than Jimmy Johns to respond to your questions, concerns, maintenance issues, etc.  Overall, it has been a great experience living in this building!

At 350 W Oakdale, you are paying for the prime location and excellent views. Aside from that, it is hard to justify why they are charging luxury building prices with none of the services or amenities to go with it. The fitness center is adequate but poorly maintained - machines are frequently broken, and there was once a cockroach on the floor for days before anyone noticed. The water is shut off at least once a month, and residents are only sometimes notified ahead of time. The walls are THIN - I can hear every word of my neighbors' music and video games, and can hear coughing and burping because the sound travels so far. Management is hard to track down, and are not always responses to maintenance requests, let alone emergencies. Once, my key got stuck in the external door and I was unable to get in touch with anyone from the property team. In all, if you are willing to pay the prices that PPM charges, I would advise looking at any of the other high rises in the area where your rent prices will actually be justified. Similarly, if you are willing to settle for a building with less services, save your money and look elsewhere.

-Management is either lazy or stupid. There’s so many simple solutions to many of the problems that I’ll list here but nobody does anything about it. I imagine these problems have been happening for years.
-paper thin walls (yes, you will hear everything neighbors do, elevators, and literally every door slams)
-email communication doesn’t exist.
-your service requests are routed to an agent who then calls the building and communication there always falls thru
-no inventory checklist upon move in, big concern there
-air filter was black when I moved in
-cockroaches
-CONSTANT lost mail
-paint peels
Elevators are always broken and repairs are lasting months, not weeks (like they told us) to fix. Water bugs are present.

This is a beautiful, well kept building just steps from the lake. The maintenance staff does a wonderful job replying to work orders as well as keeping up the lobby, common areas, and all hallways. The studio apartments are large and wonderfully designed, it almost does not feel like a studio. Every room has a wall of windows with a breathtaking view of Chicago, no matter what direction you face.

Living at Elevate apartments gives me the peace of mind knowing that the environment is safe, clean, and professionally run. When I travel, I can leave the premises with the knowledge that all will be well upon my return.  The staff is extremely courteous and professional.

My stay at Elevate was nothing short of amazing. The apartments are stylish, well-equipped, and in a great location, making it easy to explore the city. The WiFi was fast and reliable, which made gaming a seamless experience. I spent hours playing roblox downloaded from deltaexcutor.com without any lag, making my downtime even more enjoyable. Whether you’re looking for a place to unwind, work, or game, Elevate is a fantastic choice!

We have been very pleased with our Elevate experience. The staff is excellent and the building is well maintained. Most importantly we feel welcomed and a real sense of care and community from the staff.

I've lived here 4 years and  management has gone over and above to help with all issues which have been few. Love living here
JOAN E
Elevate is an amazing place to live! The staff are amazing and we love the updated features of our unit.

An exquisite staff, from the front desk, to the leasing office, to the maintenance and nighttime staff.  Beautiful tall ceilings everywhere, incredible location, fast internet(with hookups in every room).

I lived in this building for 3 years and the elevators were constantly broken for days at a time and sometimes weeks. Worst is when they are broken at the same time. Management company is also not very attentive in remedying the issue, unfortunately. If you do end up living here, I’d avoid the higher floors.

I just signed my lease about a month ago. I was really struggling finding the right place with a company that wasn’t shady because I have run into that quite a bit. They really were helpful and the agent was patient and kind. My place is really clean and exactly what I needed, really enjoying it so far. I would highly recommend PPM and 441 to anyone.
Spacious street facing one bedroom apartment with multiple closets and open floor plan. The building engineer is very responsive and helpful.

Terrible management team. On the day that I moved in, they messed up the elevator schedule, and I had to wait for a long time before being able to use the elevator that I reserved two weeks ago. I hired a truck and three movers who were charging by the minute, yet the management was not at all helpful. Since I moved in, there has been noisy construction going on in the building every single day. Why scheduling such noisy constructions when you know that everyone is working at home due to the pandemic? The construction starts at 8am every morning, and management team refuses to let me know when it will end.

PS. Since I moved in a month ago, the laundry room has been shut down three times for repairment, water has been shut down twice, and there has also been two internet outages. The current internet outage has lasted more than 30 hours and is still ongoing. Seriously, what the hell is wrong with this place???

Since I last wrote this review, my bedroom and bathroom got flooded 6 times, including one case where my ceiling literally fell off, no one ever fixed the issue despite my repeated complaints. An old laptop of mine got ruined due to this flooding, but the management team literally told me "this is to be expected for an apartment building" and refused to compensate me for this loss.

Something is ALWAYS broken in this building. Laundry room is down every other week, water gets shutdown every other week, elevator needs repairing every month, the gym got shut down for a whole month due to flooding. The garbage system also was out of service for weeks. Internet outage also frequent. Noisy construction happened in the building for months and the management team would not even announce a schedule. My deliveries get stolen regularly and the front desk does nothing about it, nor would they share with me the video footage.

Plus several members of the management team is both rude and incompetent. WORST building every, definitely avoid at all costs.

I’ve been eyeing this apartment building for a few years now and done my research before applying! For starters, I love that I have a sky line view in my apartment! The area is very quiet and peaceful when walking at night. The apartment process was quick and efficient! No long delays! No runarounds and the best part is they respond back to phone calls/emails in a timely manner! I love how they have community events every month with amazing prizes for residents! I love how they have a car service, free coffee, two storage rooms for packages (both are secured and don’t have to worry about missing packages) and the best part is there are two large laundry rooms! I’m a UChicago Medicine employee so getting to work is very efficient for me because there’s a shuttle bus top around the corner, the 172 bus is 1 min away and the 6 bus is 2 mins away! U can’t beat that! Plus the prices.. need I say more! I love living here and you will too :) I hope this review helps you!

By far the Worst Management staff ever! The Manager is never on site or available for questions and concerns. My floor and the building smells like weed. Loud music or police sirens constantly wakes me up on a daily basis because of all the drug dealers management allowed to move-in. There has not been any communication from the Manager on what is being done for the safety of the Residents and Staff in light of the break-ins and murders that took place next door. I'm a long time resident and no longer feel safe at Twin Towers. As soon as my lease is up I'm leavening. Unsatisfied!

Terrible management staff, clueless and unhelpful. Very noisy construction frequently going on in the building from 8 am, the management wouldn't even inform the residents in advance. Water shuts down every week. Laundry room breaks every week. Internet shuts down as well from time to time. This place is simply ridiculous, avoid at all cost.

The building itself is beautiful. The management team is extremely unprofessional and lack knowledge. They are super gossipy and are not to be trusted. I was a tenant here before, and "your quality of life" really depends on who is running the building. The management prior to this when I lived here were excellent. Older and professional. You have a bunch young people in the management office that are not qualified and lack knowledge of HOW to run a business/building. I've had several instances of unprofessional behavior. I finally had enough and got a new place because my peace of mind is worth quite a bit. The only reason I wanted to possibly stay is because, moving itself is stressful. But look around Hyde Park before choosing this building. There are alot of reasonably priced apartments with excellent management choices in Hyde Park. The decline of the building is because of office management period. Many tenants complain, but nothing is done. Also there retention/turnover rate is nuts. People tend to not stay. City Hyde Park is a excellent choice for Luxury Apartments. Try Mac Properties, they have reasonable prices, up to date apartments, better management. They seem to be more professional and hire people that understand how to run a building and not young inexperience individuals.

I moved to Chicago last year and have not regretted my choice of apartments. The buildings and common areas are very well maintained and the majority of the staff is friendly and helpful. My apartment is not fancy but it is clean and comfortable at a decent price.  The location is wonderful with a beautiful view of Lake Michigan. The staff provide extras that help make this feel like home like a summer bbq and winter holiday party for residents. I would not hesitate to recommend Twin Towers to others.

Writing this because I wish there had been a recent review before I signed a lease here. If you're considering moving in (especially if you fear bugs), read this:

The only thing I can truly speak to is the cockroach problem I experienced.
Before signing, I searched everywhere for reviews mentioning pests but found only old ones, so I thought it was under control. I asked Bry, the property manager, about pests, and she said they had no issues, which I now doubt. I even hired my own pest control service biweekly.

When I did a walkthrough, the maintenance guy was scraping caulk from the baseboards, likely used by the previous tenant to fill gaps. I noticed a tiny bug near an outlet covered with tape, presumably to stop cockroaches. My stomach dropped as I realized they had been dealing with cockroaches.

I had already signed the lease, so I had the apartment cleaned and pest control come before moving in, hoping the baby cockroach I saw was a one-off. It wasn't.

My first night, I saw a cockroach with no food in the apartment. After that, they appeared everywhere: in the bathroom, on kitchen cabinets, walls, clothes, and even an empty fridge. Centipedes followed, attracted to the cockroaches. I was terrified and barely living in an apartment I paid for, constantly spraying insecticides and using peppermint oil to deter them. I even showered at the gym daily to avoid attracting them with water.

I wish I had seen a review like this before signing the lease and hope it helps someone else!

For the first ten months or so, we had no issues. The apartment was loud since it is right on Sheridan, but that was minor. Then the roaches started. The roaches are living in the walls, but the management company thinks that spraying is enough to treat the issue. Well, it isn’t. They always blame certain apartments, but refuse to take responsibility, even though the maintenance people always leave the back door open (also a major security issue). 
The washers and dryers are almost always in a state of disrepair, and one of the washers constantly rips holes in clothes. Every winter, during the coldest days, the radiator pipes freeze up, forcing us to have a space heater to stay warm. There has also been constant issues with packages being stolen, which again, not great security here. On a couple of occasions, the garage and first floor have flooded. 
Horizon does the bare minimum, and is just not a good management company. Sure, these apartments are inexpensive, but you can find better apartments elsewhere in Edgewater.

I flew into Chicago from New York to house hunt. I had a very pleasant phone conversation and scheduled a showing at Sheridan Glen, when I arrived the leasing office told me they had no record of an appointment and hung up on me. After I called back they said again that there was no appointment and they had no vacancies during the time I’d be moving despite telling me the opposite when I scheduled the appointment. With managment that bad, I feel like I dodged a bullet

If you want to know what your life will be like moving into 2500 N Clybourn please watch the movie money pit. The leasing office promises the moon, but sadly they don't deliver. The leasing team is like the island of misfit toys. No one ever signs their name to the email so you don't know who you are emailing with. The maintenance team doesn't know how to fix anything and you have to beg for things to attempt to be fixed in the first place. I would check all the doors and locks before signing a lease. I would also check to make sure you don't have any plumbing issues. My advice would be run for the hills.

My husband and I have put in our notice to vacate after just THREE -FOUR MONTHS  living here. While the apartment maybe nicely set up with space, the skeleton/foundation of the building is absolutely HORRIBLE!  Unfortunately, I agree with the August  2023 poster, maintenance will come to fix things, but it never gets truly resolved. A few examples include our shower getting backed up twice that a plumber needs to come in to fix it, and is unable to tell us why it’s happening. The first time it backed up, we were without a shower for 60 hours (yes we started counting).  Our ceiling has leaked that we once again called the maintenance. We've also heard from neighbors about the same issue. We also found out that they had to caulk the 4th floor for it. We’ve also had to put in multiple maintenance requests for other issues, including but not limited to: leaky dishwasher, electrical sockets not working, etc. As for the security of the building, once again, I agree with the August 2023 poster about the locks on the access doors that you have to jiggle your key. I also agree with the August 2023 poster that packages definitely get stolen here! I took a picture of my package from UPS showing that it was delivered into the building. I brought it to their attention, and was told that a new amazon locker and mural design on the front entry door would be done in the next month or so. Not only is there no mural design on the front entry door, their “new amazon locker” is a closet metal wire storage rack that you can get for around $40 at Amazon!! They simply placed packages on it, and moved it slightly out of the way!!! Plus, on our ring doorbell we’ve seen a man who we don’t recognize from our floor, walking past it in the early morning (like after midnight early morning).  We put in a request to Chicago 311 (along with our plumbing problem)because one of the stairway access doors to the garage was constantly jammed, without resolution from maintenance. Currently, it remains propped open.  As for the surrounding area, while this apartment may be within walking distance to the shopping center, you’re encountering homeless people who camp under that bridge, and will start trying to talk to you. Overall, it has been a terrible experience living here, and we’re counting the days down till we get out!! Honestly, there are other apartment buildings with MUCH BETTER quality for the same exact price they’re charging, if not less!! The nice space hasn’t been worth it!!

Units are good so far as space. You can definitely hear neighbors and the building is not truly secure. Packages stolen because they’re just thrown on the floor right inside the door and anybody walking by can break in-which did happen. Maintenance attempts to fix things but most don’t know what they’re doing. Management is pretty nice but issues don’t really get resolved.Like cmon-locks on access doors can’t be fixed for two years??!! And the elevator is another story-that thing moves as slow as ever….

Leasing team is knowledgeable and kind, John who is the admin was so helpful in setting up an apt with such short notice. I met with the leasing agent Jacky who was GREAT, just a wonderful experience! Great place to call home!

This property is where it's at! Great walking distance to whatever you need! Whether its food, drinks or your daily groceries, nothing beats the convenience.
As for the units themselves, it's all updated! You get new floors and new kitchen appliances. 
Really enjoying my time here.

I'm sure by the end of 2022 the apartment building will be nice and renovated but right now the entire thing is under construction making wfh impossible. The hallways are filthy and the air is full of dust from all the construction and water is constantly being shut off all day long. I lived here for three years and was never notified that the construction was even happening in the first place.  When I asked if there was anything they could do since I was having severe allergy reactions from the dust and couldn't take meetings during the day from the drilling they told me I could try working from Starbucks or break my lease and move out. Besides the construction the apartment is constantly smokey from the restaurants next door, the parking garage is difficult to maneuver and janky, and packages are frequently being stolen from the mailroom. Basically, look elsewhere.

I finally got hardwood floors, I know that sounds crazy but I have been looking for an affordable place that had them. Not only that, but they even upgraded my kitchen for me, so I got brand new appliances. The price fit my budget and the building fit my personality. It’s close to whatever you think you would need and the L is just down the street. Clean, friendly, and a great location, that’s a win in my book.

The building manager is great, the neighborhood is pretty nice and the rent is reasonable. However, the top floors tend to get really hot during the summer and the AC units have a hard time keeping up, and it can get pretty expensive. The elevators also seldom work properly.

I had an amazing experience moving into the sally ! I was assisted by brooklynn throughout my entire application and moving process, she was very helpful and informative of the property. Move in day was a breeze.  I love the neighborhood and the amenities included ! 10/10 recommend

I couldn't be happier with my new apartment! From the moment I moved in, it was clear that this place is special. The cleanliness was impeccable, making the transition incredibly smooth and stress-free.
One of the standout features has to be the top-notch appliances. They're not only great looking, but also incredibly efficient, making daily tasks so easy. 
And let's talk about Tyler, our leasing guy. He's been an absolute pleasure to interact with. He always greets me with a warm smile and takes the time to pet my dog, who adores him. Tyler goes above and beyond; he even helped me move my couch into the building when it arrived.   His friendly demeanor lights the Sally up! 

Overall, I couldn't have asked for a better living experience. Five stars all the way!

I've been a tenant for several years and have seen Managers come and go due to the lack of unprofessional demeanor.  It has been a challenge for them to keep a good office manager.  The current office manager is one of the most in sensitive, unprofessional, rude and demeaning manager I've seen so far.  The manager exploits other tenants personal information.

We wanted change last year and current office manager was brought aboard due to the high volume of complaints due to last office manager.  Corporate definitely should be more tactful of choosing there manager.  If there was a more diversity office setting in the building it would make a change for the better.    People are afraid to come forward due to the fear of some type of retaliation treatment.

Over all it is a decent building to live in and great location and views of the lake.   When you have a good building but bad management it doesn't make a great presentation for the Lake Village East apartment building.
They are under renovation and will not lease until Nov. or Dec...so the price on here will go up dramatically.
I came here to visit a friend for a couple days and it was pretty a good place to live and location was wonderful

Hi; My name is Victoria Clark, I have lived on both property Lake Village East and Greenwood Park Apartment. I have had a wonderful experience living on both property. The staff on the property really care about your needs. The property is well maintain, all you have to do is walk or drive by and you will see the beautiful up keep of the property. The bedrooms are very spacious and closet space is to dye for. I have never an any issues when it came to repairs even thought they were very small, the maintenance are the best group of hard working people you will ever find, when it comes to repairs which are very small if any at all, they treat it as if it was a very big issue to make sure the problem don't return. The office staff are very supportive and nice to their tenants, and treat them as if they were their own family. A great place to live.
I have been calling every month for over a year inquiring as to obtaining a 3 bedroom. They to date have not had any three bedroom available.
I love the design of the building. the rooms are spacious too, with a touch of class. I am too searching for a 2B apt and with a little luck...I believe that I have found it.
Terrible application process, don’t believe the requirement thresholds to apply, they’re false and deny according to personal judgement rather than if you meet requirements.

Recently moved to Chicago and was looking for a place in Lakeview, by Wrigley field. Also needed to be close to public transportation to get downtown. After a lot of research I checked out 430 Diversey. Glad I did, close to the bus stop and the 151, brown line is a few blocks west. Not to mention they put in hardwood floors in my one bedroom. It’s a great location and easily accessible to get to and from.
The best part of my apartment is defiantly living on the border of Lincoln Park and Lakeview. There's so many places to go to and downtown is just a train ride away!

Everyhing was fairly easy from start to finish. Laundry and bike onsite and bright, clean internet room for when working from home and wanting to get out of the room for a bit. Love having the attached dog park. Elevator is outdated, but haven't experienced issues with it so far.
The elevator has not been inspected by the Dept of Buildings in years and breaks down constantly.
The associate I dealt with was extremely rude and liar. The quality of service they deliver is dreadful and their attitudes are disgusting! AVOID THIS PLACE AT ANY COST!

What can I say, it’s Lakeview and its dog friendly. Two very important things I needed in a place which Briar does and does well. They have this cute little dog park which is super convenient. They have a business center right next to the dog park where I can get free wifi as he runs around and plays with the other resident’s dogs. If you have a dog, love Lakeview, you should definitely check out 515, I love it!

There is no parking. My lease outlines it, yet management refuses to offer it, and they continue to deflect my concerns. I emailed my leasing agent about this, but he forwarded my email to multiple other employees for them to all berate me over this. Avoid at all costs.

Currently here and so ready to move! Firstly, during our tour we were stressed the fact we wouldn't be able to hear the trains, but we can. The huge windows are gorgeous, but other than that it's blah.

I do not recommend The Winnie. I have been here three months and i'm already looking to move. The elevator is currently broken with no ETA for repair. The key fobs only work on certain doors, parking is a nightmare as there is only street permit parking, even though there is a parking garage in the building no one is allowed to use. If you have packages delivered, good luck finding them as the carriers leave them in various parts of the building...sometimes outside!

Close to the action.
Far enough from the crazy.
Safe and secure with local fun fests just blocks from the front door.
Parking always available.
Hardwood floors and well kept unit.
Large enough for a family or to get away from friends when needed. 
Plenty of room for get-togethers.

Perfect for anyone in any situation!

Pros: Location. This is what you are paying for. Great neighborhood, quiet residential street. Close to grocery store, restaurants, Wrigley Field, and bus stops (not super close to L stations, though). Chris (building manager) is very responsive and helpful. Quiet community - people generally keep to themselves. Laundry machines rarely break. Some units have updated kitchenettes (I would not categorize it as a full kitchen).

Cons: Cheap building and shoddy construction - plaster walls with layers of white paint to cover up (literally) the fact that the building is old and needs serious updating. No air conditioning. 250 sq ft Studios. Vacant businesses in the lower levels leads to some issues with spiders, centipedes and roaches. No dedicated package room – packages are occasionally stolen as it’s easy to get in the front door. Call box never worked during the year that I lived here. No amenities. Two maintenance requests went unanswered (one relating to my bathroom sink detaching from the wall, the other relating to roaches). HEFTY utility bills – the building is metered so that each tenant pays a portion of the building’s entire usage based on their apartment’s square footage (so even if you keep your individual use low, you get hit with $100+ utility bills every month for a 250 sq ft studio). 

I would put the price in the “Pro” section, but, honestly, after you pay rent + utilities + Internet + electricity, you pay more (or at least equivalent) to other units in nicer nearby buildings. A decent first apartment if you are trying to establish yourself in the city or explore a new neighborhood, but I left after a year.

Been here since early 2020. Nice doormen and management, but I cannot recommend this facility to people who prefer non-smoking apartments. Marijuana smoking is prevalent here despite being declared a non-smoking facility. Smoke is sometimes seeping into my apartment on a daily basis despite all the times I've reported it to the doormen and all the emails and in-person interactions with management.

Walking distance to oak street beach, water tower place, food and bars, red line and buses. Quiet building and clean apartments. Pool, small workout room, good size laundry room, and doorman. On site maintenance and staff are great, always willing to help even for the smallest problem. Not updated kitchen, white cabinets and appliances, but everything works and is clean. Probably the best bang for your buck for Gold Coast area. Only con is the heating bill. Windows are not 100% insulated properly which can cause the heating bill (electric) to be pretty high, especially for a studio.

I love this building. I have lived here for a year now, and here's what you need to know:

The neighborhood is quiet but still walking distance to both River North (more downtown), Old Town (bars, food, comedy) and Lincoln park (zoo, food). Beach access is across the street, and if you get a "C" unit in the building, you get a lake view.

The apartments are clean and comfortable. White carpet means less entertaining, but it looks crisp with floor to ceiling windows and makes the overall feel of the apartment more like home than a bar. If I am entertaining friends, it's normally at the beach or local establishments.

The biggest pro is the rent - about 300/month under market value for what you get. Amenities include a pool, workout room, on-site laundry, and the best staff I have seen anywhere. Most of the staff has worked here for 30 or more years, and they are all very friendly and helpful. 

My only complaint is that they charge $10/person for visitors at the pool. It really makes that amenity less fun, and other buildings in the area don't charge guest fees for the pool. I'm staying another year, and rent only increased $30/month.

Pros: large apartments, pool deck, maintenance staff is great, good rent for the area. Close to Chipotle.
Cons: Outdated with smaller kitchens and bathrooms. Insulation is not great, so heating bills are very high. No in-unit laundry or garbage disposals. Parking spots are a tight squeeze.

This building is awesome. The location is perfect I can see the park from my apartment and it’s across from Target. There’s a nice gym on the roof that’s never busy and the sun deck is cool in the summer. No there isn’t a doorman or pool but it’s way better priced than Lincoln Commons and my unit is bigger than the ones I saw there. I prefer a quiet building anyway. Management has responded to all my requests and they leave me a note when I have a package on my mailbox. The value is good with the move in specials.

The high rent you pay for this building does not equal the lack of service and lack of amenities. Go to the new twin tower apartments down the street at Lincoln Commons. Webster Apartments has ZERO apartment maintenance for this building. Good luck having Nancy the Manager return a call. The security guard sits in his car in front of the building smoking. Beware, the security guard leaves at 1am, the local bars when not in COVID times closes at 4am. In non-COVID times, there are fights, broken beer bottles and police called every night Thursday-Sunday after 1:00am. Expect to be woken up every night Thursday-Sunday between 2am-4am by drunk and disorderly drinkers leaving the bars on Lincoln. The windows do not open more then 2 inches. And make sure you know people from the streets can see into your windows at night. There is something weird with how you are charged for electricity, everyone in building no matter size of the apartment has approximately the same bill each month. The washers are tiny, only 2 towels can fit in them and do not fill up with water. The common areas are suppose to have free wi-fi, but that is never working. The business center is a desks with a printer that does not work because there is no wi-fi and the internet cable also does not work. The workout room is on the top floor, the connect from the exercise machine and the tvs also has poor to no audio connection. (Bring your own music.) The gas grills on the roof top need servicing, they do not start without a match or lighter. The gas fire-pit does not work.

Pros: locations, spacious apartments, great view from roofdeck

Cons: almost everything else. The management here is almost nonexistent, which is really absurd for the prices. There is no doorman. There is a "security guard" who comes from 5-1am (not exactly sure why they think 1am is an acceptable stop time?) who sometimes is at the front but usually is off "monitoring" the rest of the apartments. There are tons of children and young women in the building and it is crazy to me that they don't have at least two security staff, ideally full time or at the very least 4pm-6am.

Package management: also non exist. There is one room where everyone's packages go and anyone can get in there. Which means, of course, that stuff is taken all the time.  I've probably had at least 10 packages stolen. The management company couldn't care less - they don't pick up the phone or return calls. I was so excited about this apartment building but I will never rent here again once our lease is up (we got here in September) and I'll certainly never rent anywhere that is connected to RBI Sandz.

I've been a tenant at 1940 N Lincoln for a little over 2 years, and while I've appreciated the building's charm and location, I've had my fair share of maintenance issues. As someone who knew going in that the building is nearly 100 years old, I expected the occasional spider or centipede, and I was not surprised seeing the elevators out of order, or seeing cracks in the plaster walls, or the floors being uneven.

However, over time, some more significant problems have arisen. During my first winter in the building, the hot water was inconsistent at best, and the radiator had a drip that the plumber didn't fix, he just told me to reach out again only if it got worse. Packages would go missing all of the time, and all management would do about it was to send an email to all tenants explaining that PPM legally has no responsibility for it. More recently, I've experienced issues with roof leaks. After the sixth time the roof leaked into my apartment, PPM sent out a roofing company to tuckpoint the brick above my window. The roofers laughed at how simple the fix was, and assured me that the roof wouldn't leak again, but it's happened 3 more times since.

I want to acknowledge that the new building engineer has made efforts to address some of these problems. He has been responsive in general. They installed a new boiler, which has fixed with the hot water issue. The elevators have been functioning more or less consistently for around a year now, and I haven't had a package go missing since then as well.

The location is good, and I generally have felt safe in the building and surrounding area. The building is brick and concrete, so I used to rarely hear my neighbors. Recently though, some people moved in who talk loudly in the hallway. There was also someone screaming and slamming their door at midnight on like a Tuesday a few weeks ago. It's really amazing how just one or two new neighbors can really shift the vibe.

As someone who values honesty and transparency, I feel compelled to share my experiences with potential renters. For me, the location and affordability initially outweighed its drawbacks. However, as time has gone on, the cumulative effect of these issues has made it clear that this building isn't the best fit for me. If you're considering renting here, I encourage you to weigh the pros and cons and ask plenty of questions before signing a lease.

I have been living here for a little over a year, I just renewed this summer! 1940 has become home for me, it’s great, close to public trans, great restaurants and they have a roof deck! PPM even threw us a roof deck party. They seem to really care and if you have any issues you can call, they have always been helpful to me. I highly recommend this building.
I have lived here for 2 years and I just renewed for a 3rd - love it!  Great neighborhood, Nick keeps everything super clean and I have the best roof in Lincoln Park!

I lived in a 3 bedroom here and it was a blast! It is a great location, with a lot of stores, restaurants, places to go out nearby and 7-11 right across the street. Door staff is super friendly! Loved the floor to ceiling windows in the apartments and I think it was a good price for what you get. Great to have a roof and pool for the summer time. Overall great place to live, I would definitely do it again!

This building is amazing. Best locatin in the Chicago right in the middle of the action. Kelly works there and she is the best if you need to rent a condo. Super friendly and was a pleasure to work with.

Gold Coast living, high-rise, and amazing places to go out. Not to mention the redline is just a few blocks. Myself and two of my buddies have been living here for about 6 months and so far so good. The three bedroom is huge and plenty of room for us. The best part is the roof deck pool, which has been awesome for my friends and I this summer in having it. The property company even puts on a pool party for us with music, food, everything. Great place, been having a blast!

1111 has been a great place to live for the past 5 months. The maintenance and management teams are very responsive, and the amenities are exactly what I need -- basic fitness equipment for when I'm too lazy to go outside to the gym, a rooftop pool for relaxing (okay, "need" may be strong here), a business center with free wifi, a laundry center, door attendants 24/7, and on-site receiving room and dry cleaning. 
I live in a studio that's about 450-500 square feet, with floor-to-ceiling windows. I think my particular apartment hasn't been updated or renovated recently, so my kitchen and bathroom have seen better days... That said, I have other friends who live in the building, and their newly-updated kitchens and bathrooms are great! If you're looking to move in (which can I recommend), definitely make sure you see the particular unit you're moving into, because there is a fairly large difference between older and updated units. I didn't know there were updated options until my friends moved in, so I was in the dark until recently, but I'd definitely prefer to be living in a more-recently-renovated apartment.

Aside from that, I think rent is more than fair for the area and the amenities in the building, and they have good resident referral bonuses, as well.
Everything is ok, except the price a little high. And administration fee is very high... I don't know why
Just moved in, so far so good. Pool is awesome and the staff is great!

Worst management company I have ever had to deal with. Frequently dealt with issues such as cockroaches, finding crack pipes in common areas, and the elevator breaking down. When I brought up these concerns I was threatened with legal action for saying I wanted an elevator inspector to come out.

I went to a scheduled viewing and while I was waiting for my appointment time another man who had an appointment one hour before me had to come on our tour because the dude forgot about him or something I guess. As soon as he walked in he was running around frantically and his secretary told me he was in a rush to leave even though I had scheduled this a week in advance anyways he was like practically making me and this other guy run just to keep up with him which I was here to potentially see about a home which is not a rushed decision. While going to see the units i had some difficulty trying to turn on the shower due to me not being strong enough because it wouldn’t budge and I made a note that it was not working, of course he goes in and it turns on when he does it the water turns on and then was pretty rude about it saying “oh it doesn’t work now does it?” It was weird, he was also like shouting and chomping gum the whole time. Anyways not even like 30 seconds after we shut the door he flat asked me “do you want it or not?” Anyways the place isn’t ugly but it’s pretty small but I just got bad vibes all around my gut just told me to stay away.

I liked it when I first moved in but now the staff and the residents don’t seem to care. Residents act entitled, like they can leave their garbage wherever they want and someone else will clean it. There are so many drug addicts, running up and down the fire escapes, blasting their music late at night. Someone got 25 noise complaints and the police called on them many, many times and no eviction and the first floor smells awful. As for my apartment, it’s a nice studio, but the plumbing is awful. The ceiling in my bathroom caved in because of water a leak, caused by a mistake made by maintenance and now it’s doing the same thing and the management is making me wait a full day until anyone will even look at it. Do they want their building to literally fall apart? Our current property manager doesn’t care and it shows. I want to like this person, but after my first interaction, I can tell they’re just collecting a check and phoning it in. It’s location is it’s only saving grace at this point, but there are better options for cheaper.

Let me start this review off by saying, Roberto, the property manager, is fantastic. I have never had a property manager that cares so much about the tenants. I am new to Chicago, and Roberto helped me a lot with moving in, and getting settled. The building is an older style, with a beautiful interior. I really feel at home here. If there is ever an issue, management fixes it. Highly recommend that you check it out!
the bathroom in the picture is filthy so what do you think the  bathrooms actually look like...gross!

Just got off the phone with the property management company, Calibrate, as we are looking for our first studio/1 bedroom apartment in Chicago. I understand it is 4:30pm on a Saturday and they close at 5pm, but seriously WHY the attitude and rudeness. 

As we navigate this process this is a red flag if you cannot even be nice on the phone as this is our first time renting a place out of college and we have questions about the process and timing. HOW on earth would they respond if we had apartment issues? 

Stay away.
Please just don’t bother unless you want your belongings crawling with roaches. Oh and the bed bugs are still here.

Do not move in here! Bed bugs & Roach infested! 
Terrible Management! Do not let the photos fool you! People in the building steal packages! Water is turned off once a week. Elevator barely works. Laundry room is just for show because it makes your clothes even more dirty. Just say no!
mice infested, do not move here. you can literally hear them playing in the walls
I love being a TLC resident! Both the management office and maintenance staff are professional, friendly, and promptly responsive.
I am glad about my decision to move into The Ella Apartments. Ms. Veronica and Jerome were nice and attentive.  The residents are respectful.  The building is quiet secure and clean.
From the moment I moved in over a years ago everything has been flawless. Maintenance has been very attentive and friendly anytime I needed something addressed.

Lack of communication from management and maintenance person. I have done what I needed to as a renter via reporting things directly to management and the resident portal and still have not received the help needed even a week later.
I love living here at The Ella Apts. and would recommend to anyone!

I have been a satisfied resident of The Ella Apts. for 2 years and it's been a wonderful experience! I'm proud to be living here and I hope to continue for many years to come here in this beautiful, warm & cozy apartment complex! Keep up the great work!
Any requests I have had maintenance has been serviced quickly and professionally.
I enjoy the environment at The Ella Apartments because everyone is friendly, and the building is always clean and quiet.
I feel valued as a resident of The Ella Apartments. Maintenance is superb!
The Ella Apartments is a very quiet and clean building which makes my time as a resident very peaceful.
Even though Ella has new management every 2 months, each PM has been exceptional. They have helped me enjoy living at Ella and I am considering leasing for another term.

I have found the current property manager and maintenance responsive and helpful, the building itself is nice and the apartment has no serious problems. Occasionally there are problems with some of the machines in the laundry facilities, or a fumigator must be called, but those being the only problems I have had after a year make this one of the better buildings in the area for the price.

I haven't even moved in yet and this has already been a nightmare. After signing my lease, I didn't hear from anyone for weeks. After many many calls and emails, I finally heard back from someone three days before I was supposed to move in with all of the items I had to sort out before moving in. Then, the night before I move I get an email changing my move in time by several hours with no explanation. It's been a very unprofessional experience so far.

I lived here for a year. The property managers are incompetent, unorganized, and lazy. On my move out day, neither of the two showed up to do my walkthrough. Refused to do repairs and when they did the problem came back in less than a week later.

They appear unorganized and unaware of the daily function of the property. The website is misleading and there's no follow through with the information provided. The building upgrades are decent, but nothing special. TLC should do themselves a favor and properly hire staff that truly know how to manage residential property.

I’ve lived in Lakeview for about 5 years, bounced around to a few different places. However there was always an issue, either maintnens was a pain or the property managers where a nightmare to work with. Some places were just out right dirty. Then I found 2630 Hampden and I have to say this is one of the cleanness places I have lived in. Our live in maitnece is either cleaning the lobby, sweeping the sidewalks, or in the winter shoveling the snow. My place is quaint and quite just how I like it.

I work at Northwestern and lived in Evanston for awhile.  It's a nice community, but I wanted to experience Chicago city life a little more.  That's why I moved to the Lakeview/ Lincoln Park area.  I didn't really know what to expect at first, but only after a month living here, I can say it is amazing.

I was able to get this apartment at a relatively low monthly rent, given the quality of the area and the apartment itself.  That's all thanks to a really good apartment finding agent, Jeff, who works for Planned Property Management (PPM).  He really knew what he was doing and got us a great price. There's so many places to eat, and I have yet to be disappointed.  I could eat at a different place 2-3 times a week for a year, and I think I wouldn't run out of new places or get bored.

Commuting to Northwestern is a breeze too.  I can easily hop on the "El" train purple line express and be here in 30-40 minutes.  Getting downtown is super easy too; there's a bus stop right outside the door.

If I had one complaint, it would be the parking situation.  It is very hard to find street parking in the city p, this close to Wrigley field.  There are parking spots at the apartment complex, but they are too expensive and too small.  It is too difficult to park the car when other cars are present in adjacent spots.  The solution is to not own a car - you really don't need one living in the city.  I sold mine a week after moving here and it's been a major relief.

I've lived here about 7 months and definitely won't be re-upping my 1 year lease. You need a key fob for the elevators, so really only the lobby (bar, patio, coffee shop) is open to the public which is fine.

A studio here is probably the newest/best amenities you can get for living alone in Chicago at this price. However, here is the weird stuff: building is SUPER humid. The A/C units use water and drip, and because there is just one window that opens a crack and no vent in the bathrooms it is STEAMY. I bought a dehumidifier pretty cheap which works well. In-unit washing machine/dryer combo is the worst. Gets SO hot even if you pick low heat on the dryer setting. Can smell funky too since these units dry by sucking water out and not blowing air in (kinda mildew-y). Takes about 6 hours for one load. I had to buy a clothes-drying rack. I do not dry my clothes in this machine anymore. Ruined so many of my clothes. Kitchen is tiny and was ok at first, but it just gets tiring being so cramped with no counter space, and hand-washing in the tiny sink is such a pain. If you like cooking, maybe consider elsewhere. 

Being super close to the Red line is one of the best perks here. Uptown is Uptown, so you just have to be aware of where you're choosing to live. 

Property management is hit or miss. Some people are great and friendly in responding and some act put out by tenant requests. They do get fixed eventually (there was mold in my bathroom when I moved in) but it can take some constant communication to get them to follow through.

I'd say just get a roommate in a 2 bedroom somewhere else, you'll spend less and have more space.

At first glance, The Lawrence House is a trendy, art-deco building with cool interior design and great amenities. Very early on into my lease here it became clear that there is absolutely NO soundproofing between apartments, and the residents are almost never held accountable for flagrant disruptions or violations of their tenant's contract. While the lobbies and assorted amenities are great, in theory, FLATS management is too concerned with bringing in business from the surrounding area to care at all about their tenants getting what they pay (A LOT!) for. I spent a year surrounded by inconsiderate, horribly loud neighbors who blast music and TV at all hours of the day and night, have drunken get-togethers which involve talking at absurdly loud levels well past 2 or 3am. The floors (and most walls) are all constructed of concrete, so neighbors in apartments above wearing their high heels and pacing endlessly at 5am echo and all sounds from all directions are loud enough to sound like they're in your apartment. On multiple occasions, there have been complaints about dogs left unattended and barking/howling for hours on end, only for management to maybe send an email but ultimately do nothing until confronted again by other tenants. Dogs are not allowed in the lobbies (unless you're in with the staff, in which case they run around off-leash), you're not able to bring your own drinks to the lobby because they want you to have to purchase the $10  cocktails from their pretentious bar. In the year I was there they increasingly opened the lounges and backyard up to the public for obnoxious events, further impeding on residents' access to the amenities they trick you into thinking are worth the absurdly high rent. Like the review mentioned above, the area is also iffy at best, and at MOST, the building security consists of a part-time security employee who is absent from the lobby for long periods of time. There have been calls to police made on domestic violence that resulted in nothing, I had a drunk and aggressive man screaming and throwing trash cans in my hallway, and at one point there was a suspect of some nearby crime hiding in the building. Don't get tricked into supporting this awful, greedy corporation. They do not care about you.
