YOU DONT HEAR ANYONE UPSTAIRS, DOWNSTAIRS OR NEXT DOOR-its wonderful!!!!  Hyde Park is a deverse neighborhood bursting with culture, good food and jazz. This is our third apartment in Hyde Park and I finally feel like Im home.  The neighbors are friendly, there's a bakery and resteraunt downstairs (you dont even have to go outside to get there, its built in) especially when you're not in the mood to cook....I could go on, but look do yourself a favor...take a minute and take a tour its worth it!!!

My studio in Windermere House is everything I could have asked for. The kitchen is beautiful (just refinished), the carpet is beige but spotlessly clean, and the bathroom has a huge bathtub perfect for soaking yourself in on those candle and book reading nights.  Also, even though it's a studio, it has "dressing room" with tons of drawers and shelves. It holds all my clothes with room for more (and I wouldn't consider my wardrobe small). Plus, a huge walk-in closet with built in shelves and bookcases (!) on the front of the doors.  Electricity, gas, and super fast wifi (slow wifi is free) not included in rent, which is pricey but it's worth it, because you're right next to a bus stop that gets you to downtown in 20 minutes and you live in Hyde Park, a lovely neighborhood with awesome cultural diversity and TWO used bookstores. Highly recommend. One caveat (and the reason for a four star rating): I did not have a good experience with the leasing company, MAC Apartments, during the lease signing process. Make sure all your expectations are clearly stated and not ignored, and please communicate over the phone with them if possible, NOT through email. Lesson learned on my part.
It has the charm that comes with the old buildings and the company is always making improvements.
The views are amazing and the high ceilings make the apartments feel spacious!

The onsight staff are great. 

However public ammenities that need replaced with new products (like our treadmills which have been broken for 7 months and cannot turn on) are ignored. When paying for a building with ammenities you would expect they woild continue to be offered. 

The management company has not responded to any emails on the subject nor addressed the issue.

There’s are pests, weird smells in the hallways, plumbing neverrrrrrrrr works. People steal packages. I was on the phone with maintenance and they hung up on me about an issue that I’ve been having since the summer.

We have package theft all the time, but management doesn't care. Also, you can see roaches everywhere. The laundry connection is lost for 6 months. There's no one in management office even though the office hour is from 9 to 5. The only great thing here is maintenance team. But you will never be able to contact management team... I'm tired of this situation so ready to move out definitely.

Trust me my friend, if you ever chose to live in 5550, you would be in regret in the rest of your life. Theft, Burglaries, ... you tell me. Never ever rent to live in this place, unless you want endless suffering and insecurity. I even wonder if this place is cursed

Pros:

- Good location with respect to UChicago (they seem to think this is enough to justify the high apartment prices)

- Nice living next to other student peers

Cons:

- When I arrived, there were dead bugs on the floor of my apartment...

- No package sorting at all, good luck finding your stuff in a pile of 14 floors worth of other peoples stuff

- Employees enter your apartment without much notice

- Laundry machine's credit card swiping has been broken the entire time I have lived here, and the normal laundry card machine has a 10% chance of accepting your $5+ bills only (get ready to spam swipe/insert bills just to clean your clothes)

- Management doesn't respond to emails of criticism (0/4 so far)


In summary, proximity to campus barely, barely outweighs all these negatives.

The location is extremely convenient, as it is equidistant from the Metra line, the UChicago campus, and the primary grocery stores (Kimbark and Hyde Park Plazas). The 55 bus to the green or red lines is only a block away, and there are a flurry of restaurants a block south on 57th.

University students comprise a small portion of the total residents and the noise level is typically very low. The maintenance staff is friendly and quick to respond to any needs. The apartments themselves are some of the few in Hyde Park that are carpeted and since most other complexes are only three stories, any room on the fourth floor or above offers an excellent view of the surrounding neighborhood, as well as a glimpse of the downtown skyline. The kitchens are maintained nicely with an array of wall and base cabinets, and the stove is of a brand nicer than those in most other apartments. The laundry room is located in the basement, which can be accessed from the elevator. A garbage chute in the stairwell offers a nice convenience as you can avoid exiting the building to throw bags in a dumpster. The residents are all friendly pleasant.

Most of the reviews here are so old. Here's what you need to know. I recently renewed my lease here. The location is fantastic. Quick access to CTA bus and train with 76, 151, 77 within a 5 minute walk of the apartment. Plenty of good food around too. Building is nothing special, but there is a package room and I have never had a problem with the laundry room. They respond quickly to work calls and have fixed any problems I have had in unit promptly. 

However, you need to know the crowd that lives in this building. It is mostly college students and if you are a light sleeper who sometimes cannot handle college kids being college kids (loud noises, smell of weed) this is not the place for you. I have not had many problems with noise other than Halloween and New Years, but I am a heavy sleeper so it did not bother me. 

Some of the reviews say stuff about cockroaches which if you are living in Chicago and you are staying at a place that is not a luxury apartment you are either going to have centipedes, cockroaches, or rats. Pick your poison. I have seen one cockroach the entire time I've lived here. They have a pest guy come in to spray for them. 

Overall BJB is a tolerable management company that minds their business. No one bothers me and I am allowed to do pretty much whatever I want. Rent is a STEAL for this location. Especially with all utilities included except for electric. If you can deal with the young people that live here and do not mind the occasional pest it is a pretty okay place to live.

I was very interested in renting this property. I called numerous times over the period of a month and left 3 voicemails and no one ever called me back. The last time I called, I mentioned to the front desk that no one had called me back but it didn't make a difference. If their lack of attention translates to current residents, I would never want to live here anyways.

The building itself is a 1920s/1930s renovated hotel, and comes with a small gym and laundry facilities on site. The rent is very low for the area, and transportation down to the loop is easy (you can take the 134 / 143, or the brown line). However, the building does harbor a very young crowd (a combination of college students / recent graduates) so it can get noisy at times. Also, the trash room (located off the lobby on the first floor) overflows almost every Sunday (which can be gross for the faint of heart). 

Overall, though, the apartments are fine, the staff have been very nice, and if you are okay with living with the <=25 it is a good building to consider.

This apartment is close to the lake close to public transportation very friendly neighborhood although I've had some problems in my apartment they have been solved in a timely matter  it is also pet friendly. Overall I love my apartment

The apartment was presentable, clean, and spacious when I saw it. There was no doubt that I would rent here. The 1 BR is great for living and for studying. The best thing about this apartment is the amenities. Electric, heat, and water included in the rent makes this $785 rent more than acceptable. I appreciate Apartments.Com for pointing me in the right direction. A  job!

I have a studio in this building. Its a really quiet building on a pretty main street. The maintenance keeps the building clean and the pangea company always has great promotions like when I first moved in I got $200 off first month rent. When ever I have a maintenance issue they always come fix everything the next day or no later than two days. The only issue I've had with them is that one night I got locked out of my building unit. I called customer service and needed them to send someone to help me he in my apartment unit. They never called me back until the next morning and I ended up locked out of my apartment for more than half the night. Other than that, I love my apartment.

This is an older building with a number of "banks" of apartments located off of a large, sparsely furnished central lobby area. The neighborhood, Uptown, has been "in transition" for 25 years. While the number of families with young children purchasing condos in the neighborhood is growing, it still has its share of gang-related violence. Not ideal, but not unique in the city of Chicago (or most major cities).

The apartments are in good condition, and the one I live in is a 1 bedroom, 2 bathroom (yes, two full baths) with gas forced heat (though no central air; we still rely on a wall unit). Our unit is a little strange, and not sure how common it is in the building, but we're told it used to be two studios. Hence why it has two bathrooms for one bedroom. The upside is that the bedroom is huge -- bigger than the living room, though if you imagine that there may have been a kitchen in there at one point it makes sense.

My biggest gripe is the size of the kitchen. We bought a used waist-high island that goes up against the wall for more space, but it's still very tight. If we leave at the end of our lease, it will be for that reason.

That, and if they raise our rent.

The lobby, mailbox area, and laundry room are all in good condition. The floors and plaster in the apartment itself are in fantastic condition, and the windows are brand new (no leaks during winter!).

The location is also very ideal, within four blocks of the Wilson red line. It also backs into a pedestrianized section of Sunnyside Ave, which makes it very calm traffic-wise, and is frankly quite nice and provides good shade in the summer heat.

All in all, this is a good bang for your buck apartment building.

I have been living in my large studio apartment for 13 years and absolutely love it.  It's so spacious and roomy and perfect for a single person.  The building is kept clean and well maintained for your safety, by a very helpful staff.  The building, is located just north of the city, in a quite cul-de-sac, next to a street park.  Public transportation, area restaurants, shopping, entertainment and the lake are all with in a short walking distance.  I have recommended and confirmed 3 friends to my building as tenants.

I've lived at Sheridan Shores for 13 months now. Like every apartment, it has its pros and cons:
Pros: 
1. Access to the lake, parks, CTA routes, restaurants, and Lake Shore Dr.
2. Quiet and charming street and area
3. Maintenance and cleaning staff are excellent
4, Communication from Group Fox is very good
5. The floors are original real hardwood, the kitchen and bathrooms are still modern,
6. I have A LOT of closet space to hide my stuff
7. I haven't seen insects in my apartment
8. The building is very pet friendly, and I see a lot of cute dogs
9. Neighbors are nice and trustworthy
10. The elevator is always working
11. The lobby had some fairly recent small updates
12. I feel very safe where this apartment is located

Cons:
1. Residents pay all utilities, but Group Fox advertises that heat, water, and trash are covered - they actually incorporate the fees on top of your monthly rent. Fees average from $40-80 for a studio. 
2. The walls and floors are thin. I can smell cigarette smoke from my neighbor's apartment. I had a former neighbor upstairs whose music I could easily hear.
3. The laundry room can be a tad battle at times of trying to share washers - Sundays are generally the busy days. 
4. Two out of five dryers are generally glitching and not working; however, three working ones still seem to be enough for the building.
5. My apartment itself needed several maintenance requests when I moved in - broken dishwasher, oven didn't work, and a few minor problems in the bathroom. But maintenance was quick to respond! 
6. Parking is available but very pricey (in my opinion)
7. My apartment is almost always hot. I rarely had the heating on in the winter, and I would still run the A/C.

I'd give it...3.8/5 stars.
Don’t move here, building is incredibly run down and pictures do not show it. Groupfox is untrustworthy and does not help with requests.

Despite what they advertise on their website and what you may have read online, they do not provide, or even offer, gigabit-speed internet. They only work with one ISP, AWB, and the fastest speed offered is 300 up/down, which will set you back $225/month. They do not even allow other ISPs to service the building, so it's impossible to get what they advertised. This is more or less the theme of Mac properties. Stay away, there are better alternatives for this insanely high rent.

This building used to be a dormitory, but MAC Property Management purchased it and renovated the building to serve as apartments. I moved into Shoreland in early 2014 shortly after it reopened, and at the time I had high hopes for the place despite MAC Property's awful reputation in Hyde Park. Unfortunately, MAC ended up being just as awful as I had heard they were, and so I am moving out of here in a couple of weeks after having lived in Shoreland for over 2 years.

At the time I moved in (in early 2014), there were two dedicated study rooms, a spacious gym with wooden flooring and mirrored walls, and a gaming room with a billiard table and a ping pong table on the 2nd floor. There were also many empty rooms on the 2nd floor, and as I was taking a tour before signing my lease, I asked the agent what they planned on putting in those spaces, to which they responded that perhaps a dry cleaner or a restaurant would go in there. Although the existing amenities were not part of a tenant's contracts, I reasonably assumed I would get to use what I was shown at the time. Fast forward to 2015. MAC decided to replace the brand new gym with office space; they turned the gaming room into a small, awkward gym; and they turned one of the two study rooms into a gaming room. They also filled in all of the empty spaces in the 1st and 2nd floors with office space, so now this building essentially acts as both an apartment and a corporate office for MAC. By doing so, MAC not only eliminated some of their residents' amenities, but they also made it difficult to find parking throughout the day because a lot of the free spots outside are taken up by employees of MAC who are working downstairs. MAC did the same thing at Regents Park just a year before (i.e., told residents that they were "renovating" the gym but downsized it and made more room for their office space).

There are many other examples I would like to write here as to why I would never recommend this property or other properties managed by MAC to a friend, but this website limits the length of entries so I will just say that this building is not worth what they charge for it, and it is poorly managed and continually gets worse (for the tenants, but better for MAC employees) over time.

I moved back to Hyde park area from west loop, because I truly miss the community.  Hyde parkers have some of the most diverse & interesting people in the midwest.  From business professionals, lawyers, students, small business owners to IT Geeks like myself it's a humbled community that takes pride in the area.

apartmentName: Lincoln Square Commons - 4759 N Maplewood Ave
review: Building has been redone, nice size, and safe location. Management office is terrible. They don't call you back, they are never in the office. Also rent is $1450 which is very high for the area.

I have lived at 5252 since August 2019 and I moved out recently due to my job relocation. I was the second resident to move into the apartment and I can tell you that my time at 5252 has been absolutely fantastic!!! It has great amenities including a nice gym, pool, and sky lounge, but most importantly, the staff at 5252 are AMAZING. Dan is a great manager and he always makes sure the property is safe and clean. Kelvin and Ricardo address all maintenance issues at your unit in a prompt and professional manner and Jackie always welcomes you with a big smile at the front desk! I will truly miss this apartment and the nice/friendly staff of 5252. 5252 gave me the best experience possible in Chicago and I have no doubt current residents & future residents will have a similar experience there as well.

Cheyenne, kelvin + Daniel really make this place feel like home, aside from it being a great location (in hyde park). The views of the water, city + town of hyde park are great and it’s right on the metra stop (literally)!

Any problem we’ve had, Daniel and Kevin have quickly and gracefully taken care of . 

Needless to say we’re staying another year!
These folks are so warm and friendly, they make you feel like family. They are helpful, kind, and always professional.
Very nice luxury apartment but too expensive for the size of the apartment. Very limited storage space and very cold in the winter.
I love living here. The neighborhood is quiet and convient. We're modern style large spaces apartments. Great updated kitchens and bathrooms. Only problem is price. It is expensive for south Chicago!

The Algonquin is a wonderful group of apartments. It is managed by MAC Apartments. The building is very clean, and the management staff is friendly. There are only five apartments per floor. Although this may seem small, having a small number of people on each floor cuts down on the noise on each floor. It is really a great environment to live in.

Management will make this place seem great at first. But when you move in, you will experience endless problems. There is rampant theft, including items left in common spaces (bike room, gym, lounge, package room) as well as apartment break-ins. The key system has technical issues often, and getting replacement keys is next to impossible. Bad neighbors plague each floor. I myself have had to call the police on neighbors multiple times. Management will enter your unit without permission or notice. The air conditioning system will act up in the transition seasons. As of writing this review there have been quite a few hot days this year and many people continue to not have AC. Last winter, several people went without heat in the coldest months. If you move into this place, I promise you will soon be searching for excuses to break your lease. Avoid at all costs.
The A/C and heating units rarely work correctly, the management is EXTREMELY shady, there’s a high crime rate within this area and building.

The Wilson is nothing but problems. Management is slow and not helpful. No such thing as Security in the Wilson. Break-ins often. They don’t care about there tenants and your a/c and heat unit will often not work at all.

I moved in a month ago and have been super happy with my apartment! Tons of natural light, laundry & a dishwasher in unit, lots of street parking around, and utilities don’t fluctuate. Their use of tech is really cool too, the front door has remote access where I can let guests in from my phone & even unlock my door with my phone. Lots of great restaurants around too!
I enjoy living here. Management is very quick to respond. Apartments are pretty modern.

I’ve never been so bummed about having to move from anywhere. Because I also knew that I was relocating from a great management team such as this one.RELIABLE management is hard come by these days when renting. I loved my apartment. The updates on the building just goes to show that the new management and Joe are moving in the right direction. Any concerns I had they were taken care of. Communication was always great, and I felt at peace knowing that any concerns I had were being treated with a sense of urgency.

Lived at 7334 N Ridge Blvd from 2017-2020 and loved it! They have been making major improvements to the building which has been nice to see. Neighbors look out for you, maintenance is friendly, and the property management team is great and responsive (Stella is great). I lived in a studio and it was super spacious and updated. Location is great to! Next to markets, food, gym, and transportation. Would definitely recommend.

I recently moved into this apartment building at 7334 N. Ridge. I can honestly say they are doing a great job with improvements on the building and keeping it clean and updated. They prioritize making the building a great atmosphere for their renters.

The new owners  are the best since ive  lived here in the smount of time they have owened the buildind . Very professional  and prompt with their  seevices considerate  about their tenants. More of a  family orientated environment  with management.  Im very  happy with their services snd i lived here 17 yrs.

I have rented in this building for the last 2 years.  The negative reviews of the building are the result  of negligence on the part of the former owners.  I can say without a doubt that Jim and Joe ( the new and current owners) are making real changes in the building for the tenants.  They have invested heavily in monthly pest control visits from Platinum Plus. As a former tenant as of today I can say had my family not been expanding I would have looked forward to continuing my tenancy under this new ownership.  They have also began to modernize and upgrade the building to make it more attractive with plans to make unit locks keyless, install vending machines in common areas, and the package delivery locker to safe guard the packages of tenants. The quality of life in the building is largely dependent on the tenants and Jim has been diligent in reminding tenants to be good neighbors and practice proper garbage disposal and unit cleanliness.  It’s kind of like how a GM takes over a poorly run team.  They inherit all of the bad press and have to dig themselves out of a hole.  Based on the time that Jim has had the building it won’t be long before it’s one of the best and progressive in all of Rogers Park.

This apartment is located in historical building, one block from Water Tower Place and Lake Michigan, yet on the quiet street. The building is very clean and well maintained. Units are large and upgraded. There is a nice restaurant in the building, which adds convenience. The laundry is in the basement and it's free. Dog friendly!

I absolutely love living at Farcroft. I moved in a little while ago and have had amazing experiences. The process of applying was so smooth, even though this was my first time ever applying and to my own apartment! I toured and the leasing agent I worked with within Tawani was amazing and she helped me so much! She even gave me an application that day and told me about a unit as soon as it became available. Moving day was super straightforward and easy! Living here has been amazing, the building is quiet, my neighbors are so nice, and the amenities of the building are also great! I love my unit too, the finishes are so beautiful. This is such a fantastic find in one of the best neighborhoods in Chicago, I love Rogers Park! I also like that they took the time to restore such a historic building! The views from it are seriously gorgeous. I can see Evanston and the lake, and love waking up to the sunrise here!

The units are all updated and beautiful. The staff is friendly and very helpful. I NEVER waited more than a few days for something to be repaired or replaced. Very dog friendly building. Close to the 147, redline, and a ten min walk to Evanston. My advice as someone who lived there for 3 yrs in 3 units is to get one w a view of the lake. You won't regret it. Making Farcroft my home for the last few yeas was the best decision I made when I moved to Chicago.

When I first walked into the building, I felt like I'd entered a luxury hotel as outfitted by Restoration Hardware. Brown leather, dark paneled walls, and sumptuous fixtures greet guests (not to mention a state of the art gym and hidden kitchenette and patio with built-in grills). Units here are spacious, modern, and relatively new, the only quirk being several non-90 degree walls in most units (the architect was superstitious). My kitchen has a giant granite island and a fantastic gas stove, which is great for entertaining. Laundry and a trash chute on every floor is crazy convenient, central heat and air are  included in the price of the unit , and my window overlooks the Frank Lloyd Wright house on Sheridan Road. The building is full of lovely people and the beach is steps away. I never want to move.

Do not live here - don't be fooled by the low prices for the area and spacious units. The building is maintained horribly - things like the AC going out in peak summer, hot water being down and elevators out is a common occurrence. Most recently - the laundry room in our building is permanently closed with 48 hours notice. I have lived here for a few years and while it started out great, the building has rapidly declined. I'm not sure if this is a building management or larger maintenance issue, but you are better off paying to live somewhere else. I sympathize for the landlords in this building as it may be out of their control.

Old crappy deteriorating building. Bad insulation - summers are unbearably hot(with max AC running which doesnt even blow cold air). During the winters - inside is worse than in a freezer (with max heat set at 85F which blows more like 60F "heat"). Electricity bill is always high. No window cleaning service. Also building has never ending water pipes fixing issues, expect entire apartment flood at least once a year as well. Building refuses to add 3rd party cable/internet providers. Only provider is Comcast. Stay away from it. Newly built rental condos are far better and even cheaper than this place.

The Ontario Place Private Residences are a great place to live if your main concern is location. If you work in the loop it is only a 15 minute walk, and the river and lake are only a 10 minute walk away as well (Oak Avenue beach is a 20 minute walk). The building is two blocks away from the nearest red line which is extremely convenient if you work in the loop or want to take a trip to Wrigley field. The building is also only a 5 minute walk east to Michigan avenue.

The building itself is a converted hotel, and it definitely feels like it. The majority of the condos in this building look exactly alike and aren't exactly "nice" but they are completely fine if you are more concerned about location. The fancier condos in the building have been remodeled by the owners and are significantly more expensive than the majority of the other condos. 

In terms of amenities, the one great thing about this building is the massive gym located on the 7th floor. The gym has three full rooms. One room has a large padded floor and is ideal for free weight exercises, yoga, and dance classes (I've seen the room hold a 20 person dance class with ease). The second room has the 10 classic work-out machines that all buildings have. The third workout room is the real selling point for this building. It contains four treadmills, four ellipticals, a couple bikes, and a stairmaster. For those who are more interested in lifting, the room contains a full free weight set with weights up to 100lbs, a bench press (not the machine), two squat racks (both machine and free), a leg press, and a few other machines. This room is large and is rarely crowded. There is absolutely no need to have a gym membership if you live in this building as the gym has everything you would ever need.

The building also has an outdoor area with a large patio and grill area as well as a pool on the 7th floor. The pool can get relatively busy during the summer because it's not that big and is quite popular among the residents. One drawback of the pool is you're only allowed two guests and you're not allowed to bring in alcohol.

The building also has a 24-hour doorman, on-site dry cleaning which is open every day except for Sunday, is connected to a 24/7 711 convenience store, has a hot-tub open until 11pm every day, on-site maintenance and leasing staff, a computer room with a printer, a party room, a connected parking garage, and 24/7 laundry room.

Apartment units are poorly maintained due to lack of cleanliness and broken utilities. 
Management does not respect the privacy of tenants and walks in with random tours even when tenants are home.

Our apartment has a great view of the skyline and a modern feel. The lobby is quite pretty and the gym, lounge, and laundry room are great to have in building. The rent is a bit high for the amount of square footage, though water and Internet are included. We get a great breeze off the lake in summer and a lot of natural light. The building manager is attentive and they once again accept packages at the front desk, but the hours for front desk attendants can be a little sporadic. We love that they allow our pets and let us paint the walls! Our rent goes up yearly, this year by about $150/month, so that is a bummer.  So, there is a mix of good and bad; whether it is the place for you will depend on your priorities.

This building has fantastic maintenance staff. The 1 bedroom I have is a good size, and the kitchen and bathroom were recently updated. Property management is pretty responsive as well. However if you are sensitive to sound though as I am, this is not the building for you. The floors and ceilings and walls are very thin and creaky. If you live below a heavy walker, you will hear their literal every move.

The place is in a great location, the maintenance staff is super friendly! And I like that they clean the building almost every morning, they mop the floors and dust in the entry way and laundry room.

So close to Lake Shore and the red line. Fully renovated with granite countertops, hardwood floors, updated kitchen and bathroom. Great neighborhood with tons of things to do in the area. The management is very helpful. The common areas are always well maintained.

I have a small studio unit. It's exactly enough space to fit everything I need, but not much else. Things are well kept and there are monthly checks for pest control, of which I have never experienced a problem. The place was well kept when I moved in with a few notable Xs. A broken microwave was left for me to throw away, and there was no smoke detector installed. Heat was paid for in the winter, but I left it off because the room was so well insulated it maintained the extreme heat from the hallway nicely. Not a bad apartment by any means, but clearly a classic Chicago over-price.
The complex has seen some days. Things are clean painted to look nice. The elevator interior was recently remodeled but could use an upgrade in the machinery before its cosmetics. Nothing dangerous, but you can't push 4 until the door shuts all the way. There's not easy way to contact a maintenance man aside from through your landlord. Otherwise I'd have mentioned that two of the 6 paid dryers are in need of repairs.
The neighborhood is very friendly and welcoming. At not time does it feel dangerous and there are a lot of things to do, or easy ways to travel. I don't hate this place, but I will not be renewing my lease hoping to find a better place for the same price.

Rented a studio and there was, or still is, a mice problem...with pictures and emails for proof. No matter what was done or so they said was done but the mice were a constant problem.  Hallway smell like dogs and people are careless about their garbage and leave it near their back doors. I only give this place 2 stars because management was nice....that's it. Otherwise avoid unless this is your last option...which is was unfortunately for me.

this place is awful. they really trick you with the tour, there's so many amenities and the apartments look nice enough and the location is okay enough that you move in. the management is a joke, they are disorganized and will change numbers without informing you. there's supposedly help offered at the lawrence house but more often than not they will just put you on extend holds and wait for you to hang up. my unit was never cleaned before i moved in and after two weeks of complaining some one was sent over to paint. a deep clean was never preformed. i broke my ankle while walking down the entry way stairs and durning recovery when i couldn't walk i had an issue with the entry way buzzer and whenever i tried contacting management he would gaslight me or never respond. the only saving grace of this place is the apartments are quite and there's is a lot of amenities but the amount of headaches the management team creates it isn't worth it, keep looking this ain't it.

apartmentName: Luxury Student Housing at Leavitt Place
review: The building looks nice, but I confirmed an appointment twice on back to back days, even receiving confirmation emails. No one showed up, even giving them 30 min both times, and when I emailed the only addresses I had from the confirmation emails, I got no response. I attempted to reach out through their chat bot but they are fixed responses only and no other numbers or methods to contact anyone which also makes me super skeptical that they would actually take care of issues promptly or at all.
I lived at this place for half a year and had to break my lease due to bed bugs and roaches that Fox Group refused to address. I lived in the 8th floor and they never fixed the poor water pressure.

Please read all the reviews on this property. This place is horrible. Horrible living conditions - bugs mice, property management (lack of), stolen mail, stolen property, etc. There is no way to live under the radar here and expect not to get frustrated or disgusted.
DO NOT APPLY!! They lie during the application process, are incredibly rude and aren't helpful what-so-ever. Worst experience with the application process. 10/10 would not recommend
They don't care about the tenants. Apartments is rat infested. No one came to put down rat poison to control the infestations

I had an incident where I came home on a Sunday, when no security is on duty, and a half naked drunk/high fat woman was on the elevator and not leaving. I spent over 40 minutes waiting for an ambulance and trying to talk to her to see what was wrong until she eventually got out of the elevator, gave me very uncomfortable comments and looks, and went up the stairwell to who knows where. Ambulance arrived a little bit later but we don’t know where she went.

Someone also broke into the buildings main doors, broke into the bike room, and managed to steal my $5,000 bike at 5AM. The camera that is supposed to watch the bike room isn’t even operational according to management. I was able to track my bike down because I had AirTags in it but not in time unfortunately. It was completely destroyed and I had no insurance on it. I see why there’s a note saying management isn’t responsible for loss or stolen property because clearly this is something that has happened before. So if you care about security I wouldn’t recommend this building. The main “overnight” (5pm-12am or so) guard is a nice guy, but an incredibly heavy sleeper it’s almost funny. 

Personally I regret living here. Felt some type of reassurance seeing a camera watching the bike room on my initial walk through so to be told it wasn’t even connected to the new system really annoyed me. 

Get a sound proof blanket for your door as well, especially if it’s a studio. You won’t hear anything from anyone else in your apartment but you can hear almost everything in the halls.

I lived here for about six months in 2021. Can’t beat the location of this building. The prices are also very reasonable for rather sizeable units. Don’t be fooled by the cleanliness of the recently updated lobby, however. This place runs rampant with cockroaches and the hallways wreak of cigarette smoke.
Don’t move here if you plan on working from home and need wifi during covid.

I love my apartment.  It is a typical city apartment, i.e. small.  But the space is workable, the neighbors are great, and the building property management company is super helpful and timely.  The only way I'm moving from this apartment is if I find a condo to buy!!

Great location for the price. The fixtures could be nicer as many of the other BJB buildings in the area have been updated with stainless/granite. However, the new property manager has been responsive and made needed changes to the leasing office and landscaping. Maintenance is quick to fix any issues. All in all solid apartment in great area for a great price.

Location - 5 stars.  Near food, transit, and lots of entertainment.  If you're a light sleeper this is not the area for you.  Bldg has decent gym and rent incls everything but electricity.  Neighbors are quiet but if you face the entry walkway and your windows are open, you will be subjected to loud conversations at all hours.  If elevators bother you, avoid apartment 15 on any floor.  14 is next to freight elevator but that isn't used constantly.

We've lived in this apartment for quite a while now, and when we started, it was great. However, since then, there have been two changes in management in the building and amenities have declined. 

The gym is pretty sparse. People did bring their own weights up there to make it a little better, but management put a stop to that. If you want any weight/strength training machines, or really anything besides cardio and a couple free weights, you'll need an outside membership.

There is a laundry room downstairs, but it is frequently full as there aren't enough machines for the size of the building. In addition, the machines really need to be replaced with newer, more functional ones since they seem pretty old. Also, the service they started using for laundry machine operation crashes a decent amount, and it can take a whlie for the card reader to work.

The elevators are extremely slow moving.

The pipes also have had issues that required the water to be shut off multiple times in the past month.

The internet was pretty reliable when we moved it, but it's been going in and out a lot more lately.

I am giving three stars because management is still nice, and they did keep the rent the same last year when renewing the lease, which was a big help. The apartment is pricy for the size. If rent increased at all, we'd have to seriously consider moving.

I'm starting my 3rd year here. Great space with wonderful details. Not your average apartment.  Both the management and maintenance  staff are top of the line.  Easy public transist access. Light and airy rooms with high ceilings and lots of windows.  Closet space galore.  I plan on staying...forever.  Great community here in Roger's Park.  And the best beach and park in Chicago is a block away.

This building is amazing! I love the key card entry. It makes me feel super safe knowing people can't break into my apartment. I live on the 11th floor and the view is breathe taking. It's perfect for college students cause a lot of young people also live here. The managers are really nice and helpful. Everyone should live here!

I recently moved into 1246 w Pratt and I love it! The management does a great job of conpleting service request in a timely manner. The building is clean and well lit. It also doesn't hurt that recently renovated the whole building so everything is new. In addition to a great management staff, the building has onsite laundry, bicycle storage, and a cute little gym on the top floor facing the lake. I would reccome do this building to singles, couples, and students. The resident population is pretty diverse in age range so overall the building is quiet!

My apartment is great!  I have a one-bedroom on the first floor;  the living room, dining area and kitchen are in one big area and it makes the apartment seem very, very large.  The bathroom is newly remodeled. 
It was immaculate when I moved in and the building manager is like the "Jimmy Johns" of managers.  There's an online maintenance request system through the property managers and the 2 times I have had to use it, the problem was resolved that day or the next.
Each apartment has a locked storage area in the basement.  I'd say it's about 6 x 6.  The  common areas are maintained immaculately, including the laundry room.  
The neighborhood is quiet and very safe and the other tenants in this building are quiet, respectful, and friendly.
I've just renewed my lease for the 2nd time and I plan on staying a long time.
I've been in 2 other apartments that are not exactly set up the same as mine, but I'm sure all the apartments are very nice.
Great apartment!

There is mold throughout the bulding. The staff is completely incompetent. They will lie to you, enter your apartment without consent, and endanger your health. Horrible managment and a dangerous environment. There are other crap apartments that will not hurt you. Live anywhere else.

Moved here for my first job out of college and it was great on a budget for a one bedroom. Nice view, cute little apartment, with friendly and responsive property management staff. That being said, dishwasher worked poorly, shower was inconsistent / difficult to use, and the elevators were so slow I would have to leave 5 minutes earlier for everything. Overall, I enjoyed the deal I got living here but am ready to move into something nicer.

I found this apartment on here and couldn’t be happier. My studio is flooded with light, has great space, and has all new appliances. Also, for the price, you get so much included such as free internet and TV! I love BJB!

Those pics are computer generated. I was shown an unkempt run down property; full of weeds, broken windows patched with clear caulk instead of replaced, damaged walls painted over instead of repaired, and heavy mildew odor in the common area. Everyone's windows were open on an 85F day so there's no working AC. In the unit I was shown, the layout did not match the floor plan renders. Kitchen was unusable (could not stand in kitchen and open fridge at same time, could not reach sink around fridge without burning self on stove if it was on), 'closets' were worse. Construction was going on elsewhere in the building. When I asked what was being done, I was told one of their tiers had 'burned down' and the crew was there clearing the damage. Yeah, no wonder. Total lack of proper maintenance (I did not see a single fire extinguisher anywhere- in my current building there is one at every landing along front stairs and they get checked regularly). Save your money and possibly your life. Keep looking.

Sheridan Plaza is over 100 years old, so it’s definitely in need of some more cosmetic updates within the units. However, if anything actually breaks, the maintenance team responds within hours! The building manager is always accessible in person and the lobby has a 24/7 front desk agent which greatly improves the safety factor. While the neighborhood leaves a lot to be desired, it has nothing to do with these apartments and they are priced accordingly. Our two bedroom unit would cost almost 3x more in the Lincoln Park area.
This neighborhood is unsafe. There is recurring violence in the area, and “unsanitary” conditions in front of the building and in the alley.

I’ve been here since the beginning of the year and I love it. 
It’s an older building with modern interior. The staff have been really nice and helpful in my opinion. I like how close I am go everything in the area including the lake. Very happy!

My fiancé and I moved into Sheridan Plaza about two months ago, and we have nothing but good things to say about it. 

The building is a small community. The staff are friendly and so helpful! I truly feel like we are a small neighborhood. When you are friendly and courteous you receive the same back. 

The building itself is beautiful and well kept. They have cleaners and maintenance on duty everyday all day long. 

The property manager has her hands full but she will always work as hard as possible to get things done. Obviously being a building of its size things are done by priorities! 

This place has character and is definitely filled with people of great character!
If you enjoy people lying to your face this place is for you!

Looking to move to Uptown? There are a few mid-rise buildings that stand out. Our of nearly all of them, Sheridan Plaza has the most reasonable rent. The best part is the store conveniently located on the first floor which is accessible 24 hours a day. They carry everything you could need with the exception of alcoholic beverages. 
To the rest of the building: The maintenance staff are awesome, friendly and helpful. There are storage lockers available and on-site, card operated laundry. All of the apartments are recently rehabbed and include completely modern appliances. There is a parking garage attached to the building that is for renters in the building. It is possible to get a parking pass for guests for just $5 a night, which is a steal! There also 24 hour porters, all of whom are friendly and helpful. There is also a gym that is open most hours of the day. They hired a personal trainer that is in 3 days a week that will kick your butt. Group sessions are free and individual sessions are affordable. 

Step outside and you are surrounded by a wide variety of restaurant and entertainment options. Shopping options you are set: there is a Target, Jewel,and Aldi just minutes from the front door. 

So, if you're looking for a great apartment in a fast changing Uptown neighborhood, look no further. I give it 4 / 5 because I think there is always room to make things better..

Moving from over 900 miles away, we had no idea what to expect. My two roommates and I packed up and trekked our way to the south side of Chicago in search of adventure ( and more realistically, college.) 
The South Side of Chicago can be a really mixed basket of fruit. Certain areas are high in crime, while others are clean as a whistle. 
The Sutherland lies on the weird section of 47th street and Drexel Blvd. to the east of us is a lovely morning walk to the Lake Shore Trail. To the west a block is a Walmart grocery center, Burger King, Subway, and a McDonald's for all your late night snack-age. Much further than that, though, and it can get pretty sketchy pretty fast. However I will say we have yet to feel in danger since moving.
The staff of the Sutherland is friendly, kind and assistive when you need help with anything. Th apartments are clean, upon move in, and the security is impeccable. (Cameras, fab only access, and round the clock front desk makes everything feel homie. 
Recently installed new laundry machines work great, though they are $1.50 wash/ dry. The gym is decent, though could use some love. There is very little sound bleed from other apartments near by, sometimes we forget we even live in a complex. 

All in all, a great spot on the South Side. 
If you need to get downtown fast, taking the 47 east right outside your front door will run you to a 6 bus, which runs downtown express. Max commute to downtown by bus is maybe 30-45min on a  busy day.

For the past seven years we have called this place home.  We became husband and wife; then parents here.  Great space. Love our neighborhood so much to offer with the lake near by, Andersonville and Lincoln square so close you can walk to everything!

DO NOT LIVE HERE.

This place is not even worth 1 star. By far the worst property management I have ever experience. 

— I have lived here for 8 months and have been the victim of stolen packages at least 8 times since and have to reach out to management to even learn that they were stolen.
— The building trash shoots and hallways constantly smell and the entire building is usually filthy with only being poorly cleaned once a week.
— The elevators are constantly broken for weeks on end with little to no communication on when they would be back up and running.
— The building is kept way to hot and when asked about the heat was told just to open a window. 
— About a month ago there was a enormous leak affecting 19 apartments, my unit being one of them, and have been living with warped floors ever since with, again, little to no communication on when they will be fixed.

I have asked for my concerns with these very poor living conditions be escalated MULTIPLE times and have been treated with either no response/solution. I would never recommend anyone live in this building and Group Fox should be ashamed of how all of these residents are being treated, including myself.

The elevators are so slow it will change how you live. The people who live here are great but there are bad seeds that affect the mail room and packages. They spray for bugs and have to come into your apartment monthly. They have 100 year old a/cs that don't work and cost a ton in elec. There is no hot water. The water is rusty. There are smokers outside that cough all day and you can hear it in your apartment. NONE of which the building manager cares about.

This place was worth it! The mail room was fixed...and there are NO BUGS. They do a bug check every 6 months or so. Pretty close to a lot of nice locations. There's also a tiny gym.

Staff though, TUH, rude. They are very "keep to themselves" . The neighbors are a little annoying depending on the floor. My floor was filled with kids who kept slamming their doors. The laundry room is awful. The washing and drying doesn't work. They always break and then the building sent an email out claiming that we must wash our blankets/towels/sweaters/ and other heavy stuff in different washers and dryers that were not on property. The elevators are always busted at the worst possible time. Imagine going grocery shopping and you have to wait in a 20 min line to get on the elevator, or my personal favorite, walk up to your apartment. I lived pass the 6th floor.. . The entrance door...busted...still hasn't been fixed as im writing this.  This are all current and present issues as im writing this..  they raised the rent 250$!? After being there for about 2 1/2years, how dare they have the nerve to do that when most of the "amenities" break or are currently broken. They painted the side door of the bulding...I "guess" it gave them that right. But this is ridiculous.  I live in a two bedroom. They raised my rent to 3 bedroom numbers. What a joke. I dont know if it's to push people out so they can sell the unit to another gullible person...but no longer will I be naive about it. Watch...when you are around the property you ALWAYS see a moving van bringing someone out or in. Bad turnover rate.. its so obvious. Maybe find a place either more north or west cause this one was a doozy.

Unless you like camping, look elsewhere. Water leaks from roof when it rains, or burst water pipes in kitchen ceiling. big one, not the little trickle. elevators constantly out of orders. commons are meh, except on first floor to show new prospects.Garage is a stock yard for broken appliances and else, when sewage pipes do not need flushing. you 'd better drive a mini to park, because otherwise you will not be able to. now have a prayer and a sense of humor for management, because they need your support. and maintenance, well ... they need professional help.

i loved my apartment ,it has a very big balcony which is good for my dog
large living space, tons of closets

My experience with BJB started out ok, but ended up being a nightmare. Over the course of months, I had to place dozens of tickets for fixes around the place (as maintenance would regularly do poor work), I went without hot water in my kitchen for months, I went without a toilet that would work without having to flush it 3-4 times for months, I had a front door that would not lock regularly, screen doors that would nearly blow off the balcony, obnoxious neighbors that would make noise until 11-12 at night regularly without proper recompense from management - and more. Management was not proactive in getting things handled (obviously) as they would not be addressed with a sense of urgency, or not be addressed at all.

Do to all of the above I moved out a month early, with proper notice given; I even offered to help show the place and help them re-rent it. That all being said, they failed to re-rent due to poor management of the effort (big surprise) and are now coming after me for that last month’s rent... 

They KNOW they are in the wrong here, it is clearly documented over the course of months and they have been notified of this; but yet they still persist to come after me, rather than just let me walk away? Now I am involving a lawyer and will fight this all the way through. BJB will not be getting a single CENT from me.

It has been a nightmare and wholeheartedly DO NOT recommend living at a BJB property given that you commit to the property management company as much as you do the unit/neighborhood. 

Don't say you haven't been warned!

4100 N Marine has one of the best views in the city of Chicago. It over looks Lake Michigan and other parts of the city. It has a roof top terrace where you are able to enjoy the weather and view with friends. The rooms are spacious and relaxing. I would definitely recommend renting from this building!

This building is probably the best value for its location, but the maintenance is terrible. Exterior windows are never cleaned, indoor pool has a breathtaking south view of Chicago but has a questionable smell and feel. The majority of the building is occupied by college students.
At the price point MPP is pretty good. WIFI can unstable during the evenings but the building is in a great spot and has great views.

Elevator out of service. The apartment is the worst literally you can here everything from the other apartment because of the pool walls they have, it’s like you live with them. Every time someone closes the door it will hit the wall so hard even you gonna feel like your wall moved because of how hard the doors close at this horrible building. The lobby + elevator smell so bad I have sent an email about it no one replied back. 2-3 out of washers don’t work since I moved here. Garbages always full sometime I have to leave the bag next to it because there is no place for it. They have a mailroom but the packages they never take them there. They’d just leave it in lobby! So you have something maybe expensive it’ll be in middle of the stinky lobby. Back elevator at least 150 years old with two doors! Yes two doors one of them like the zipper so if you have something in the hand or moving things in you have to use hands and feet just to get in. The next apartment and you are playing the same movie at the same time? You don’t have to turn the volume on you’ll hear it! Don’t worry! You have white clothes? Put them in the dryer they’ll come out blue!! Not kidding! The bathroom with no ventilator fan!! Taking hot shower? Leave the door opened or the window! First day I moved here the toilet was broken they did fix it so fast! By putting that white glue!! . I hope you can find a better place to call it home. You’ll get windows in the appartment but they’re so dirty from the outside, even you can’t see well because of the dirt!

It will be non-stop headaches if you choose to live here. From constant cockroach problems( despite being reported to management numerous times), to washing machines that are continually broken, rude and unhelpful staff, appliances that don’t work (you won’t be able to get anybody out to fix them either), missing packages, paper thin walls you can hear your neighbors at all times, this place is not worth it at all.

My boyfriend and I have been living in a BJB apartment for almost a year now and its been fabulous. We are very easy going individuals and in order for us to work in Chicago we took a 400sq foot apartment for 975/month in Gold Coast so that we could work our part time jobs and save money. BJB is amazing in that it has all utilities included except for electric. Its super convenient. It also has a little fitness center. The management here is very nice and replies to any questions or inquiry in a very timely manner. They also fix things quickly. The location is perfect; that's what we are basically paying for. Being near to the most hoping places! Shopping & food is what its about. The only downside would be that the apartment we are living is the lack/none of natural light, slow internet, and condensation on the heater in winter. The natural light is definitely something we need when looking for our new apartment this October (:

I just moved in a month ago, but my experience has been positive so far. 
When I first moved in, many of my appliances weren't working, but when I alerted management to the issue, they responded promptly and cheerfully. I was very pleased with their assistance and look forward to the rest of my stay there.

Given the location, the rent is reasonable and maintenance crew is great and issues can be taken care of very quickly. Nice access to #2, #15 buses and some mins walk to Metra. Most rooms come with ceiling fans.

BJB properties is doing everything they can to milk this slum before it caves in as an investment.  I, and many other have written reviews revealing the roach infestation and other problems of this place you get locked into with a year lease.  They will make you sign waivers of lead and asbestos not being visibly present because it is a cover up.  Those are the least of your worries.  No ventilation in the building with the exception that there is no insulation.  This is just the obvious surface problems.  Management is very good, but there is only so much a company can do to support an inhumane building that should be condemned.  The problem is that it is right next to another building which was kept up well, that would also have to be demolished with this building.  You've been warned.

Steps from everything! Michigan Ave. shops, Oak Street beach, Rush and Division nightlife.  Apartments are ample and neighbors are friendly.  Rooftop deck is a big plus!  Many great events also for the building tenants.  Such a great community to live in.  LOVE IT HERE!!!

Smaller apartments perfect for one person and solid price for the location. Great location if you like to be just steps away from Gold Coast night life and a block from the lake (easy walk to Oak Street beach). This is one of the better management companies I've been with. The maintenance and cleaning staff are on it. I've never waited more than a day for issues to get resolved. Building cleaned almost daily. Easy to get quick responses from management. 
One of my favorite places I've stayed. It's cute, fitting a full bed, sofa, dresser, desk and coffee table. Residents are young and friendly.

I called emergency management because I got locked out. They said an engineer will be here in 30-45 minutes. I decided to wait but not one showed up in over an hour and a half. I called again just to be told I had to go to their office at a different location or wait another 1.5 hours. Then they hung up on me and wouldn’t answer my calls. Apartment isn’t good enough to compensate for this lack of assistance for the tenants.

This is a good building for young people in transition. Located in the heart of the Gold Coast area, it is easy to access the "L" (Clark and Division Red Line Stop) as well as a number of different buses. Entertainment is literally only steps away 5-6 bars and clubs all on your street. The studio apartment is on the smaller side and only has a conventional oven, not a standard one. Definitely one of the cheaper apartments in the area and comes with free cable and a access to wifi (you just have to purchase your own router.)

This place is a slum. They will take your money and let you move into an uncleaned, mold-infested apartment. Then they will tell you they cleaned it in a day, when really they just covered all of the disgusting stains and mold with paint (they actually told me this, and expected me to be happy). Do not rent here.

This is a BJB Properties managed building, and my unit is a studio.  It's the nicest studio I've ever lived in.  Kitchen is its own area, through an arched doorway, quite out of sight from the living area.  It's on the small side, but they managed to squeeze in a dishwasher, and there's plenty of cabinet space.  The walk-in closet (you walk through it to get to the bathroom) is very nearly big enough to sleep in as an extra bedroom.  And it has a door.  The living area is standard, with hardwood floors, radiator heat, and window a/c units provided gratis by the building.  Hallways are carpeted, which helps a lot with noise.  And the walls and cielings must be pretty thick, cause I rarely hear anything other than a chair scraping or someone vacuuming.  But then, faintly.  There's a rooftop deck that's open sunrise to sunset that they just refurbished.  It could comfortably fit 10-15 sunbathers, and features a great view of the lake and Lincoln Park, as well as the skyline.  No big buildings obstructing the view pretty much all around the panorama.  Laundry in basement, in a workout room.  Lobby is almost luxurious, and has a doorman till around midnight.  And the location?  Well, it's a shady street that spills out onto the park.  The whole thing smells like trees and flowers.  Several bus lines at one end of the street, several at the other.  Two Starbux within sprinting distance, Clark street shopping and dining a stagger away.  Trader Joes a five minute walk.  Hospital around the corner.  So what's the knock on the place?  I'd kill for an extra foot or two of counterspace in the kitchen.  And if you're on the courtyard side, any noise from the street echoes a bit.  But it's a pretty quiet neighboorhood sidestreet, so it's quite tolerable.  Oh.  And there's free internet and cable (wall tether, plug in your own router -- no sharing of bandwith).  Friends of mine come over and are impressed, but they don't know the half of this place's charm.  Highly recommend.
Great location in Lincoln Park thats steps away from Lake shore trail! Large studio with great amenities. Maintenance on site, and sign for deliveries. Great experience so far.

Very small apartment for decent price and good location, probably cheapest one you can find around this area, not sure about price/sqft. However, depending on your neighbor your unit can be very noisy. I could here people talking over the wall and every footstep from above. Also at my last month of lease, I had to show my unit pretty much once in two days until unit was occupied and sometimes even without 48 hours notice, if showing is cancelled, of course you wont get notified. Last month of my stay really ruined everything.
I made an appointment to look at this apartment. But I was told by the property agent that all of their apartments have been rented right before the appointment day. It was really disappointed.

I have a studio apartment for 3.5 years now. The initial process was painless, the management was very courteous, and they were just as eager to get me in the unit as i wanted to be there. The  location is perfect for public transportation, lake shore drive, the beach, parks, even golfing. The interior and exterior is always kept nice and clean by maintenance. My unit is huge compared to other studio apartments I've seen, and also very affordable. It's real easy and simple to pay rent online. No need to write a check or run out for a money order. The management has proven that they are really focused on taking good care of their property and tenants.
Tiny living but great building with amenities. Well taken care of. Good price, or at least was.

The property comes with internet provided, which is great to not have to deal with setting it up yourself, but it's VERY slow and the company it's through cannot upgrade it, they told me I'd have to order additional internet through another provider. Xfinity, Wow, and Verizon do not provider service in this building so it's impossible to live here and work from home. Otherwise building is okay, mail room is a NIGHTMARE, but the workers (aside from maintenance) are nice enough. Old building with cheap reno, but good location.
This place is uncomfortable and noisy. Not worth your time. I have had laundry and packages stolen from other tenants.

The building itself is nice, and in a super convenient location. The apartment itself is great during fall, and that is pretty much it. Don't be fooled, you do not have full control over the temperature in the apartment. The apartment gets incredibly warm during the winter even with the windows wide open like a heat pocket, and the AC does not get turned on once the weather warms up so prepare for discomfort when humidity sets in and there is no way to cool the apartment aside from investing additional money. You are unable to get an individual ISP and must use the buildings provided internet which is unstable and unresponsive when you attempt to reach their providers for support. So unless you plan to be traveling a lot for work or just not spending a lot of time in the unit, go for it.

I would give zero stars if possible. My experience with this apartment complex has been a nightmare due to bedbugs infestation, and the management's complete incompetence in addressing the issue.

Not only did we discover bedbugs in our unit upon moving in less than a month ago, but we later found out that they've been battling this infestation for over 6 years! Shockingly, the management failed to disclose this crucial information when we signed the lease.

My roommates and neighbors and I have to throw away furniture, clothes and everything and spend hundreds on treatment.

Communication from management is virtually non-existent. They avoid my calls, and when I do manage to get through, they give vague promises with no follow-up. It's clear they do not care about their tenants' well-being or comfort.

Living here has been a nightmare. Us waking up covered in bites every morning, and despite documenting everything with photos and emails, they continue to deny there's a serious problem.

Save yourself the stress and health risks—avoid this apartment complex at all costs!

Here is the list of problems I have encountered: random power outages, front door lock not working so stranger got in and was trying to see if any apartment doors were unlocked, laundry room constantly flooding and extremely moldy, smelly hallways, dysfunctional toilet, dysfunctional shower, extremely drafty windows which was horrible for summer and winter, apartment was filthy when I moved in, most of the winter so far it has been freezing as they have the radiator in the bathroom which is a closet bathroom (horrible), and the windows were not fixed until the 25th email I sent when I started to threaten withholding my rent, they were consistently underneath the legal minimum for winter apartment temperatures in chicago before, very rude and inept property managers and maintenance who do not really care about helping you and will not spend any money to fix your problem. Guy who showed me the place was extremely aggressive about saying someone else wanted it and it was the last one when in reality there were like 4 more apartments left, he was just a sleeze ball

This place has an insane cockroach problem. They will send an exterminator to your individual unit, but have not sent us out to fumigate the entire building. There is nothing being done and zero communication to tenants about the obvious problem (you can see dead roaches littering the basement floor all summer long). Also, there are NEVER two working elevators. They said it would take 6-8 weeks per elevator to replace. They started the first one almost 8 MONTHS ago and I have seen them working on it maybe five times at most. Also the floors are all crooked and I constantly trip on the uneven flooring in my unit and they told me it was too big of a job to fix. Also a large area of the ceiling once caved in onto my bed from water damage, and they said it would take a week for them to fix it because they were "so busy with new people moving in". I had to tarp my own ceiling from their negligence.

This apartment building is perfect for DePaul students. Units are on the larger side for studios and the property management company (BJB Properties) is top notch. The only issue I have/had with the apartment is the smell in the hallway. I'm not sure if it's coming from another unit or something but sometimes I have to physically cover my nose when I leave my apartment. I have air fresheners and candles in my unit so I cannot smell anything from the hallway while I'm inside. Also, the keys to get into the unit and the building itself are like hotel key cards so that's pretty cool too.

I was set up for a virtual showing today at 3pm. When I clicked the link for the virtual tour, I saw the Leasing Agent Lea was with another client. The Leasing Agent informed me she was going a little bit over and would call me back. At around 3:30pm or so(since I wasn't contacted back yet), I e-mailed and texted the Leasing Agent to double check the pricing on the studio units. It took the Leasing Agent 40-45 minutes to call me back(3:40/3:45pm). 

When she called, she asked if I still had time to do a virtual tour and I said that would be fine(although I wasn't happy about her taking 40-45 min to call back). I asked if she got my e-mail or text and she said no. I asked her to verify the monthly rent for the studio units as I was trying to check if they would be the best and affordable options for me.

I lived at Ravenswood Apartments for three years.  I wanted to give the Property Management a five star for such a wonderful experience.  Chris was polite, efficient, and very professional the entire 3 years.  I recommend living here!! 

Take care Chris! And thank you!!!
I had scheduled an appointment to see one of their apartments, but they never showed up. Also make sure to read the reviews before you consider viewing their apartments.

Like the last review I had an appointment to view a studio. I arrived on time only to wait 17 minutes for the leasing agent. It turned out he was assisting a new tenant with signing their lease for the last available studio. I guess it was a blessing in disguise. I provided my feedback to management, but wanted to leave a review here as well.

The guy stood me up after setting up a 3 pm appointment today. He never answered his phone after I waited outside the unit for 30 minutes. I contacted their office and no one answered after 3 calls. This is unacceptable and they should be reported for treating people this way.

The apartments are motel style places. 
I live in a one bedroom apartment and have parking (hard to come by in this city) for under 1000 dollars. I completely appreciate that fact, however, the building is poorly built. I truly have nothing bad to say about this apartment. Georgiana, one of the property managers is absolutely wonderful and is so pleasant to deal with. All my work orders have been completed the same day they're requested. It's quiet, safe, updated, and all utilities are included (even internet!) the area is amazing. I have everything I need in walking distance. Security attendants are friendly and attentive. Only inconvenience is Duffy's on the weekends, of course, that is no problem of BJB. Slightly smaller than most studios, but if you're living alone with minimal things, it's not bad at all.

If you like being steps away from food, shopping, transportation and the beach this is the place for you. The amenities included in this building are also off the charts - wifi included in your rent, a spacious laundry room, a work-out facility on the top floor with views of the city and rooftop access that overlooks Lincoln Park and Lake Michigan, to name a few. Did I mention the entire building is completely re-done? Very modern and clean. Look no further. This is the apartment for you!

Nothing bad particularly to say about this building.  It's just a little too small of a studio to fit a normal lifestyle in.  I could barley fit my full size bed in the room let alone have a dresser, desk and small dinner table.  I think if you're going to be spending 1,000 a month for a studio you should definitely try and look at other places before settling here.  The rooftop is great to entertain people on but it does close at 7:30 PM which is a little early for my tastes.
I love my place. Everyone here from the security to the manager is awesome. Its the perfect teeny place in the best part of Chicago for my cat and me. Nothing but great things to say!

My roommates and I mostly picked this apartment based on location. Edgewater is beautiful. There are tons of shops and restaurants. A Jewel and a Mariano's within walking distance are a huge plus. The building we live in is also great. It's an old building, but it's been mostly renovated. Our kitchen has granite countertops and stainless steal appliances. We have beautiful hardwood floors throughout and a decent size bathroom. While we've lived here, there have been very few problems. Aside from the building currently being sold to another management company, all of our needs have been met to our complete satisfaction.
No one is ever sitting at the front desk and it took them 5 days to fix my kitchen sink that I have been having problems with with since I moved in 2 years ago

I had my viewing of the apartment on the 7th floor. The neighborhood has trash all over it and it seems there isn't any neighborhood cleanup.

But, it does worry me about lack of security and whether people should be accessing the building or not.

The laundry room had trash and was very dirty. The fitness center looks alright cleaner than most of the building.

The studio apartment was looked very nice and was newly renovated. However, because of the location and lack of cleanliness, I am not sure if this location would be a good fit for me. The apartments don't appear to be sound proof as I could hear conversation and people yelling from the hallways so if noise or privacy is a concern, these apartments may not be a good fit.
This property is not right management is Very Unprofessional & to say Rude will be an understatement plus the location is very ruff unsafe

Love the apartment but it has too many mice. I have caught 25 on my bed. They on my counter. They’re on my stove. They run around in the hallway plan. This is disgusting. I have to live like this. I complain. They seem like it’s OK to live like this, this is disgusting and nasty

Upon moving in, the several windows had been painted shut and needed attention before they could be opened. The ceiling in the bathroom and dining room started leaking one spring but was repaired. The walls and molding have been painted over so many times that chunks of paint fell from the ceiling.The hardwood floors are very creaky and nails come up from time to time.

The building is in a very safe, quiet neighborhood with tree lined streets. The South Boulevard CTA and Main St Metra stops, restaurants, shopping, a half-dozen parks, and the lake are all within a 5-10 minute walk.
