Location location location. That's the primary selling point of Garrison Square. The property is located right on the border of South End and Back Bay, two of the most vibrant and sought after neighborhoods in the city. The location puts you within easy walking distance of the best that Boston has to offer. Of course, you pay for the convenience. Garrison Square charges some of the highest rents in the city... high even for pricey Back Bay.

So, what do you get for your money besides location? Garrison Square is small scale, charming, and beautiful. It is a good compromise if you want the character of a brownstone with the updates and services of an apartment complex. There are two beautifully landscaped and maintained courtyards and a very nice roof deck with a grill. The units have lots of amenities that are hard to find in Boston, including central air conditioning, in-unit washer/dryers, and wood-burning fireplaces. All of the apartments have just been renovated with contemporary colors and finishes. Every apartment has a unique floor plan, many with balconies or patios. The property is very pet friendly, and there is a great dog park behind the building.

There are, however, significant concerns. Garrison Square is an older property, and even with renovations it doesn't compete with other luxury communities in terms of amenities. There is no community room, no business center, and no pool. A fitness center is currently under construction. There is no overnight concierge service. Common areas will soon be renovated, but at present they are shabby and poorly maintained. Overall, the property doesn't have the premium feel that the astronomical rents would suggest. 

I enjoy living here, but I do question whether I am getting sufficient value for my money. There are a number of newly constructed luxury apartment complexes in the city that offer state-of-the-art amenities and a more premium feel for less money. But for location and charm, Garrison Square can't be beat.

We lived at Garrison Square for 2.5 years. I never write reviews but feel it's necessary to put the truth out about this building to help others from making the mistake of living here. 

 UDR is abusing the system of short term rentals that is currently unregulated in Boston

 GS is run like a creepy makeshift hotel instead of a residential apartment building. They do not disclose this and they will lie to your face about it. 
       Do a search, you will find GS advertised on Expedia, Kayak, Stay 
      Alfred, etc.
     They keep padlocks on the #30 building gates for "hotel guests" to   
      gain access. 
 
For the amount of rent they charge, the amenities, upkeep of the property, and the management office is a complete joke. 

There have been many incidents with "hotel guests" coming to stay here to party and packing apartments with people, noise violations, police having to come, etc
   
 You will live surrounded by confused tourists asking where they check in, where the trash goes, etc. Their suitcases will crowd the lobby, they will crowd the lobby, the courtyard and the rooftop and it makes a terrible quality of life

 There is no gym

 There are no trash chutes

 You have to collect your own packages from a locker system in the garage. This room isn't even nicely maintained. 

 The concierge isn't 24/7 and is constantly being pulled away by the temporary guests.

 GS doesn't have a grasp on who is coming to stay on property. I once encountered a mother and her three children being evicted from a temporary stay apartment in the #30 building. She said they had come to stay from a homeless shelter and were told without warning they had to get out immediately.

Living in a city can be stressful enough, who wants to overpay to live in a fake "luxury" building surrounded by confused tourists, their garbage, their rudeness and a management office that refuses to take the time and make the necessary financial investments that they could to help improve the quality of life of their residents. 

Many residents don't pay full price here because they know it's such a terrible product they will negotiate rent.

Shame on UDR for running a building in such a beautiful neighborhood in Boston this way. Neighbors notice. They see the padlocks on the gate, they hear the constant rolling of suitcases. I was under the impression there was a housing shortage in Boston. Why can't you fill these apartments with real residents?

Try calling customer support before you decide to live here!! There is nonexistent customer support. Plus every year UDR the company that owns this building WILL jack up your rent so either you have to decide to move or suck it up and pay the extra $700 they increase it by.

I’ve lived in this building for 6 months now. Terrible smelling chemicals in common areas, door ripped off hinges in the public bathrooms, fire alarms sounding every night, $500 rent increases upon lease renewals, unnecessarily complex entry systems that front desk staff are unwilling to unlock. We got called while we were away threatening our lease because of noise, without verifying if it was actually us (let the record show it was not and they later admitted as such). “Luxury”, it is not.

New residents, steer clear -- especially dog owners! My issues fall into 3 main categories:
1. renewal process
2. communication
3. not truly pet friendly

Renewing my lease was a terrible experience and it was nearly impossible to get someone to speak to live. The on-site staff could not discuss any changes (term, monthly cost etc) -- the algorithm dictate everything. A LARGER apartment was listed for less per month but they would not change the price. They told me to pay a transfer fee and move to the other apartment!

Communication here is abrupt, corporate, and often blames tenants for their issues. The trash chutes are constantly not working, the west wing has at least one elevator down a few times per month.

This past week, they sent an email at 12:30am about "new" pet policies - your dog cannot urinate on the entire city block, which UDR owns -  and if they do, you'll be fined and/or evicted!

This building claims to be pet friendly and resident first but that is, unfortunately, not the case.

The property, amenities and location are great, but the staff and property management are terrible. It’s impossible to talk to a person, the leasing staff inside the actual building are unfriendly, and the assigned leasing agents don’t communicate status and are rude when you ask logistical questions. There is a 2.8x rent-to-income requirement, but exclude 2 paychecks from your income if you’re paid bi-weekly. There are plenty of other locations in South End.

Literally there is nothing wrong with this place! Feels like a hotel with 24 hr concierge. Package room and lockers, gym is awesome, plenty of apartment options and even the small apts have plenty of room. Nice finishes and super quiet space. I barely hear my neighbors ever, very dog friendly and my pup loves the paws park on the 4th floor. There is an east and west tower and they look different one is lighter and the other darker themed. I have zero complaints, maintenance helped me with my heater immediately when I put in a ticket and Verizon specialist helped as well, both within first week of moving in. Everyone is super friendly and I love it here. Rent is steep but you get what you pay for and it doesn’t disappoint.

I’ve lived here for just over 3 months and can think of very few cons. Overall, I absolutely love it here and am so happy to be living here. Some minor things that have been less than ideal: potential for barking dogs in nearby units (very dog friendly place. Can be a pro or con, depending on you!), highly fluctuating rents (may just be Boston, I’m not entirely sure as this is the first place I’ve rented in the city), and noisy construction around the building. All in all, highly recommend, though! Tons of pros.

In my opinion, the building management truly does not care about residents or health and safety issues that are raised.  I've experience several repair issues, including one repair issues that directly impacts my health and safety. It is still not fixed despite months of pleas to management to fix.
Dated, horrible management, constant chaos and issues. Furthest thing from luxury. 0/10

For the price there are better options in Seaport. Construction on all sides of the building, except the driveway side and they operate over night frequently. Pedestrians congregate in the lobby and hangout in the lounge. No service elevator so when people are moving in/out elevators take forever. The maintenance staff is nice, building management is not.

I've lived in multiple Seaport buildings and 100 Pier 4 is the worst, by far. The walls are very thin, the air conditioning system is ancient, the construction noise is unbearable, and management is terrible. 

Don (the leasing agent) lied to me about how bad the construction noise would be before I signed my lease and is terrible at responding to emails.

Other buildings in the area worked with their tennats on a compromise during Covid if they wanted / needed to move out - 100 Pier 4 will give you no wiggle room at all on your lease. 

I'm counting down the days until my lease is up and I plan to move to another seaport building ASAP. I will never consider a UDR building again.

Although it is located in the best part of the Seaport, it is not very safe. Anyone can let themselves into Pier 4 and we allow the public to use our main floor bathrooms. Homeless people are often found laying on the furniture in the lobby. The building allows RE agents to let prospective tenants look at staged apartments themselves (without the agent). They wander the building all by themselves, which is not safe. I used to find random people walking the halls often. The building also allows for Air B&B, so again, random people walking throughout the hallways. The building almost felt more like a college dormitory than it did a home. I would definitely recommend looking at other apartment buildings before settling down here.

These simply are not luxury apartments, no matter how badly the ownership wants to convince you it is. 

The harbor walk is great. Then there are some things that seem nice on paper but in practice are either for show or are more trouble than they're worth. Then there are some things that are simply more at home in a Lynn or Salem rooming house.

The a/c doesn't work until mid-summer-- we ended up buying an a/c unit of our own, which runs a minimum of ~$300 because window units are prohibited. The vent fan above the oven will cause the fire department to show up automatically, as an ear-shattering alarm goes off, because there are cracks in the walls and issues with the ventilation that cause the alarm system to believe the main hallway is on fire. You will wake up to a blaring fire alarm a bare minimum of 3x per week. You are likely to have ceiling leaks, shower leaks, sink leaks, amd dishwasher leaks-- the appliances are older than some college students. Light fixtures sometimes randomly fall off the walls. Don't put your bed under one of the sconces otherwise you might be asking for a hospital bill. During the school year, students on athletic scholarships will be partying loudly. I don't hold that against the college students, but it's something that would be more fitting at a much lower price-point. There's a trash management problem, with chutes and dumpsters constantly overflowing, leading to trash around the property working its way into the water. The elevator is constantly trapping my neighbor, which, to my neighbors credit he seems to be a pretty good sport about.

If Harbor Point is on your list, my recommendation to you is very simple: avoid this place at all costs. It is not worth it.

Also beware of the positive reviews-- Harbor Point's management group has an incentive program for tenants that post positive reviews, they offer a couple hundred dollars off rent if you post positive reviews and offer to make yourself available to prospective tenants. They asked me to do this and I politely declined.

The staff and management are very rude and unhelpful. Hidden fees, rude emails, calls that go nowhere; you’re better off without even trying to contact anyone. Never any parking at night, apartments look vastly different, rude security, chaotic neighborhood, the list goes on…

Extremely rude uneducated management team. The lease is full of hidden clauses which they use to force you to pay fee on fee on fee on fee ($2000+ in fees in less than 6 months ), there is a rodent invasion in each and every single apartment as well, and every where around the place. they try to evict you for petty stuff just because they have a problem with your negative reviews. Also they have a marketing “director” whose sole job is to clean up reviews so they all look higher than they actually are. Don’t go here.
Depending on what apartment you get, it can be good or fair. Perfect location for school, but increased rent every year has forced me to live elsewhere.
The apartments are gorgeous, near luxury. And the complex is great too. It's the perfect place for someone young and starting college (like me) especially when the school is right across the street.

Moving from CA to MA is a daunting task.  It costs both time and money to get everything in order.  When I found Harbor Point on the Bay, it felt as if a huge weight was lifted off of my shoulders.  This place is beautiful.  Large park with many walking areas.  Well equipped gym.  Gated 24/7.  
My apartment comes with a lovely balcony and the public transportation is so ample.  As a student, it was the best choice for me.  My only, small complaint is that in my 2 bed 1 bath layout, one bedroom is much smaller than the other; so it was hard to determine between my roommate and I who would get the big room.  Other than that, I love that all the buildings are locked to the outside and that the laundry is in the building! My roommate loves the ample parking and the option to have covered parking as well. Plus, the rent is not too expensive compared to the rest of Boston.  I love it here!

The apartment is well located and has a nice rooftop (though the outdoor area could be furnished better), but they have a cockroach problem... on the rooftop, but even had one appear to my horror in my apartment, though I am very clean.  The view is beautiful from apartments facing Mass. Ave, but the road noise is very loud.  The building does not have and will not install double-pane windows... which feels like a basic for a "luxury apartment".  The staff is generally friendly, but several folks are more helpful than others.  You're ultimately paying a lot for not too much.

We love Church Park and have been very happy with the doormen and staff in general. They really make it feel like home. I'm also very thankful for the people who make the sending and receiving of packages so easy for us.  What I enjoy most about living at Church Park is the convenience. the grocery store, post office, drug store, and hardware store are all right there and in the dead of winter that is really important to us. Also, not having to fix things ourselves and being able to put in a work order online has been great.

Beautiful buildings in a lovely, historic, and safe area of Dorchester. Near trolley and bus routes. Close to supermarket, drugstore, and other shops. Short drive to rt 93. Easy access to a bike path that runs through wooded areas next to the Neponset River.

I am thrilled with the service and facilities thus far. The moving process was clear and staff we so helpful. I adore my little slice of sanctuary.

Lived here for about a month so far. Every maintenance issue I have had the team has responded in a timely manner, Marcus and Corbin are very helpful!

Very well managed luxury building, highly recommend

If you’re looking for high rise luxury housing housing there are many other better priced apartment building with better amenities. Emerson Place is not it. The cost is too high with outdated amenities.
	1.	Inflated Rent: The rental office consistently raises the rents exorbitantly each year, and the rates are significantly higher compared to other apartments with similar offerings in the area. It's frustrating to pay so much more for a subpar living experience. The building doesn’t have any common spaces except for the gym and the gym is pretty outdated.
	2.	Inconvenient Laundry Facilities: Laundry is pretty expensive at $2.50 for washing and another $2.50 for drying. On top of that, you are required to purchase a $5 laundry card. Furthermore machines not only ruin clothes but also fail to dry them properly at times, leading to an added inconvenience and expense.
	3.	Noise Pollution: The proximity to a highway behind the building means residents are subjected to loud noises and disruptive construction activities during nighttime. This constant disturbance severely affects the quality of life and peacefulness within the apartments. You cannot open your windows in the summer without loud noises. Furthermore the windows in the apartment don’t have screens which is both a safety hazard and allows bugs in all the time. 
	4.	Unreliable and Unpleasant Elevators: The elevators in this building are frequently out of order, making it an ongoing inconvenience for residents. Moreover, the odorous smell of dog urine in these elevators is both unpleasant and unsanitary.
	5.	Lingering Odors: The hallways of the building often have an overwhelming stench of marijuana, creating an uncomfortable and undesirable living environment for non-smokers and families.
The only redeeming aspect of this apartment building is the maintenance staff and front desk, who are remarkably helpful and friendly. However, considering the numerous shortcomings, I strongly advise against choosing this apartment building. If you have the budget, I urge you to explore other options that offer better value for your money.

Packages constantly stolen from the main lobby. Maintenance requests going unanswered for extended periods of time. The elevators being out of service at random intervals when there are hundreds of people who live on high floors. 
The place is also falling apart. They have done the typical move of repainting and putting in crappy flooring that looks expensive. But when you look closely the walls are falling apart, the appliances are cheap, they break constantly, and this place will be a much bigger headache than it is worth. And considering they're charging thousands of dollars per month to live there, it is NOT worth it.

The management team is awful, and will ignore all complaints. They keep your heat at 80+ and there’s nothing you can do. You will be plagued with construction noises, wall shaking, and hammering and management won’t lift a finger to help you. 

You do not want to live here, it’s not worth it.

This place seems wonderful when you tour, but don't judge a book by its cover. I have been living here for about seven months now. The concierge staff are all wonderful, no issue there. But when things break, it takes forever to get fixed. As an example, the elevators have been broken for almost a week now, so everyone in this massive building have had to use the freight elevator, meaning you're waiting about ten minutes for it to show up because it is slow and has to stop to pick everyone up, then it fills up. When you live on the 20th floor and have dogs or a suitcase or a big package, you can't exactly take the stairs all the way down.

If you want value, look elsewhere. If you work at the hospital and want to walk to work, sure maybe it is worth it. But otherwise if you're looking for luxury, look elsewhere because you will be very disappointed. Don't let the nice lobby fool you, this building is not luxury and should not cost as much as it does.

Only the location is optimal. The building is old and they’re always doing renovations and causing so much noise. The building is so old that I cannot use my stove and the outlet next to it at the same time! It’s way too overpriced for what it offers because it’s in a nice location

Early is the man, but he's stretched across six different properties. I hope he is paid well and gets great benefits. I'll just say that I was lucky to get in touch with him.

Laundry: There are indeed laundry facilities on each floor: one washer and one dryer ($5 for a laundry card, $3 per wash, $3 per dryer, so you know). Apartment unit: there are outlets that do not work, and the windows look frosted for how dirty they are. The screens need to be re-meshed. Those are my top two complaints. I will also note that because the building is surrounded by tall buildings, the apartments get very little natural light.

Bottom line: the service of this building is non-existent.

Each floor does have a laundry unit that you will need a money card to pay and use, but that saves me time from having to carry my laundry outside the building and back. Been here only a short time, so I will update more as Boston re-opens. 
The only issue I had during this entire process was I wasn't getting the updated lease contract even though I was informed by my retailer that Hamilton Company told her they sent it. That was quickly fixed when my retailer just emailed me the contract herself.

They pretend like they provide luxury living and concierge services but it’s more of a lie. There’s only one concierge who’s never there since they’re always helping other residents and packages always get stolen

I currently live in TROY Boston and have personally had an absolutely terrible experience. If I could give them zero stars I would. 
1- Management is minimally, at best, accommodating to any requests you might have. Whenever you attempt to voice a concern or request a change you are immediately confronted with resistance, denial, and complete unwillingness to work with you. 
2- They send notice of eviction letters, which they tape to resident doors, less than 5 days after a missed payment. I have NEVER experienced such unprofessional behavior in the decade plus that I have rented in Boston. What is worse, is that they are completely unapologetic and do not in any way recognize or acknowledge their unprofessionalism. 
3- The exceptional rooftop with demonstration kitchen, sweeping views of the city, etc is never available. This amenity is allowed to be reserved for the high price of $350- plus a security deposit. As a result, few residents get to utilize this amenity and instead are forced to constantly check the amenity calendar to see if they will be allowed up. 
4- You are not allowed any additional fobs for entry into your unit. That means if one person signed the lease, only one fob is assigned. This might seem like a small problem, but try coordinating childcare, dog walking, or any other sort of service that requires entry into your unit and be prepared for the headache of your life.
5-The purportedly 24 hour concierge is a joke. I see them at the two front desks MAYBE 25% of the time. As a result you are forced to wait around- which for me as been over 30 minutes at times.
6- I have yet to go a week where the building doesn't smell like pot, fire alarms don't go off, or some utility (such as electricity or water) isn't compromised.

This is NOT luxury living. This is a complete misrepresentation of what the property is. I encourage anyone even remotely considering moving here to ask to speak to other residents...and ask how many of them are renewing their leases. I for one am not and cannot wait until my lease is up this spring.

Background: I choose TROY Boston after touring numerous luxury apartments in the Boston, including: Inkblock (no rooftop deck), AVA Theater District (too expensive), AVA North Point (neighborhood is too quiet), and the Kensington (no rooftop deck). I choose TROY Boston because it was one of the cheapest and because it had all the amenities I wanted from a luxury building.

The Building: The amenities for the building are on par if not better than other apartment complexes in the greater Boston area. The building has two roof top decks (one of which aren't open as of July 2015); the rooftop deck on the mid-rise tower has views of South End, Back Bay, Southie, and has two outdoor grills and a kitchen, which is great of entertaining. Also, there is a small swimming pool area, a dog walking area, a community lounge with a pool table, and a small gym, which contains some treadmills, multi-function cable fly machine, and dumbells, which goes up to 60 pounds. 

The units: I would describe the units as industrial modern chic. My studio unit has hardwood floors, exposed concrete ceiling, in-unit washer and dryer, and modern finishes in the the bathroom and kitchen. The only draw back is the refrigerator, which seems smaller compared to normal refrigerator. Also, there is nearly floor to ceiling windows, so units get great light.

The location: This is the only major draw back for the building, as the building is located in a somewhat desolate area and foot traffic dies down significantly after rush hour. I wouldn't describe the area as unsafe, but I would be aware of my surroundings at night. A homeless shelter is located across the street and a housing project is only a block away. Ironically, even though the immediate area is up and coming, the building is only a few blocks away from great bars and restaurants in the South End and Southie. 

Public Transportation: The Orange Line (Tufts Medical Center) is about a 10 min walk, the Red Line (Broadway) is also about a 10 min walk, while the Green Line (Arlington or Chinatown) is about a 15 min walk. The 9 and 11 bus stops a block away and goes to the Back Bay and Downtown Crossing.

At least the front desk attendants were nice, but still avoid this building at all costs! Three other units on our floor moved out the same month as us - clearly people are leaving for a reason!

Awesome experience! I really love this place! I’ve been living here for almost a decade and I am so happy! The safest place ever, the most convenient place, the best staff!

Just moved in, love the apartment so far!!!!
Everything is clean and quiet here.  I like the colors they used for the walls and the island they have foe the kitchen is amazing. Great place  to enjoy breakfast, lunch, and dinner

The only redeeming qualities of this place is the location (close to Central), and the views. I had lived here for 12 months and could not wait to move out. The maintenance nightmares are too many to count. The worst one that comes to mind, was the refusal to patch up a ceiling crack that ran wall to wall. The water pipes had burst on the floor above and the crack was leaking water onto my bed in the bedroom. They said the crack was "to small" to fix. Nearly all my appliances were replaced with smaller, cheaper versions and any floor/ ceiling water damage was never fixed. The circuit breaker couldn't handle running heat/AC in both the bedroom and the living room at the same time. I could go on... 

On move out day the Community Manager almost got in a fist fight with the movers I hired. The professionalism at this place is a joke. The elevators look to be 50 years old and small. It was amazing my furniture was able to fit. The fire department was called in late January to rescue someone stuck in the elevator. Also, when they say "freight elevator", what they mean is, you can reserve one of the two regular elevators. There is no separate "freight elevator". I would urge anyone thinking to move into this place to look for something else. You can find better places for the money.

929 House has been a great place to live.  The apartments are well maintained, and some have amazing views and are full of light.  The management is responsive and helpful.  I have never lived in a more quiet building, and only very rarely can I hear anything from my neighbors.  The building went smoke-free last year, which is a great improvement (before would occassionally smell smoking from neighbors).  Perhaps the best part is the location--an easy walk to central and Harvard square with great access to the red line, and the 1 bus literally at your doorstep.
I love living at 91 Sidney, the location is amazing and the service I receive is exceptional. The concierge staff and maintenance staff are very welcoming and professional.
We really enjoy living here! The community is great, the amenities are amazing, great location, nice layout with a lot of storage space
The community is amazing, amenities are great, maintenance 24 -7 (excellent service), beautiful apartments.
I am very grateful to live in this wonderful community.
Very beautiful apartment in very beautiful bulding, very frendly administration, very helpful reception people and good location.
(1 Sidney street apartment are beautifull, super location , people working hier are very, very friendly. Adminustration is very good organazied. Answer to all problems immediately.
Living here now having constant mouse problems even with cleaning regularly and there so called maintenance is no help along with when I ask for help they are rude and don’t help
The convenient locations in walking distance and public transportation nearby. The amenities and the community center are awesome save me monies on gym membership!

I want to give it 0 stars.
If you plan to live here, please throw away your two months' rent. They do not refund the deposit and last month's rent.

Concierge? Non-existent - they're never there, and if they are, they're watching a movie on their phones with headphones in. No security whatsoever - anyone can walk in without even providing their name. In terms of noise, college students are constantly vomiting in hallways, leaving trash bags (FULL, STINKY trash bags) outside their doors because they're too lazy to walk to the trash shoot. The apartments are fairly sized, but dingy. They also have a recurring rodent problem. I hated living here and urge you to NEVER live here either. The nice location is nowhere near enough to redeem this place.

The building is an superb location.   It has worked out well for me.  The train stop is two blocks away and the train ride is only 20 minutes to Boston.  The building also comes equipped with a gym which suits my needs and a concierge desk that notifies you when my packages have been delivered.

Really nice location and amenities . 
Rent is expensive .Loudly parties  .A lot of students partying late at night .

First of all they’re on a major road so you literally can’t open the windows without blaring car noise, truck horns, loud engines. You feel trapped. 
Since the Walgreens closed down, it’s terribly inconvenient. Can’t walk anywhere without leaving the area first, and it’s in a major intersection so it’s terribly unpleasant 
They say they’re dog friendly but they’re absolutely not. I have a 10lb dog. You can have a dog, but it’s a huge burden 
They raise rents to insane levels. Part of me thinks “wow you guys must really think highly of yourselves if you think can raise prices to that level”
Fire alarms go off constantly
They tow my car even though it’s registered to the garage??? Then charge 150 to get it back. They say “we don’t have to look up your license plate, we can just tow it”. Luckily I don’t “need” my car, but imagine if you had to drive to work and your car was just… gone? This was infuriating and alone should be enough reason not to ever rent here 
The appliances are terrible. Our dishwasher was replaced twice. The washing machine just kind of… stops. Mid load, still full of water. The smoke detector had to have its battery replaced multiple times as well
I have never had any of these problems anywhere else. It’s absurd 
Wouldn’t recommend to anyone. do yourself a favor and avoid this place and go literally anywhere else

They have one of the best maintenance services ...our toilet got clogged and my husband called the maintenance late night and requested it is an emergency service and that  I was in my postpartum , they came night 11.30 to repair it and I am sure no other apartment will do late night services...
Every week they host a fun events like succulent ,pumpkin painting,pet photoshoot,breakfast morning ,smoothies tasting ect...
Station landing always give me a sweet memories ??my baby was born in this house and we bought a house such a lucky place for my family...

Rude and condescending staff, problems receiving packages, very frequent fire alarms at all hours of the day and night which require evacuation of the building.

Rent increases which are so unbelievably large it makes it impossible to stay here very long because you will be priced right out of your apartment. Once you sign that lease and move in they know it's harder for you to move away, so on your renewals you can expect your rent to go up by a very large amount on a regular basis, and if you don't like it you have to leave.

Well, guess what. That's exactly what we're going to do. As soon as our lease is up, we are leaving. We would do it right now, except that the penalties they charge for leaving early amount to many thousands of dollars, so we are stuck here putting up with their rude attitude until our lease is up.

Be smart and find another place to live instead of here. Moving here was a huge mistake.
Being right on the beach is something I never though I would have gotten in the city, plus my view is pretty unbeatable. Solid apartment
Awesome spot, the management company even did some upgrades to my unit. Also, we're getting a bigger fitness center this Summer that I'm super excited to use after my runs on the beach.

DO NOT LIVE HERE! This place is an absolute hellscape to live in. We’ve been here for 2 years and everyday has been a nightmare. Constant loud construction, so forget working from home or having any shred of silence during the day. The units look nice inside, but it’s like a flipped house. Looks nice, but very clearly took the cheapest of the cheap option. For example, I can scratch the paint off with my fingernail. Any small scrape and the wall underneath is exposed. The management and staff literally couldn’t care less about their tenants considering almost half of the units are vacant at the time of this review. People are leaving here so fast and with good reason. Save your money and look elsewhere if you’re planning on living in Boston.

While this property looks nice in photographs, please be mindful that looks can be very deceiving. I lived here for two years, and it was an absolute nightmare. Akelius, the property management company, initiated its major construction effort 
 on the building two years ago, and there is still no end in sight. It is quite obvious that the work that they are doing should be completed while there are NO tenants living in the building because it is so disruptive. If you are planning on working from home or expect to have any hint of silence during the standard workday, look somewhere else. The common areas are dumps. The hallways are unfinished with wires hanging down from the ceilings and holes in the floor.  Management is extremely incompetent and difficult to work with. Collecting rent while the building is in its current state is highway robbery. DO NOT LIVE HERE.

When we moved in the building was STARTING construction and 2 years later they are not even half way done. Imagine loud hammering and drilling all day and it will be in your lease that you must comply with any changes/construction going on in the building. In addition, there are mice. I know all building typically have some mice but since the construction the mice are out of control. The management company doesn't bather to find the holes or source of the mice, instead they put weak little traps that do nothing! Management is also exponentially increasing the rent due to the upgrades taking place. That being said, the apartments and amenities that are new are "pretty" but poorly built and things fall apart quickly. 

Do not live here.
The community it great! Love being near everything!
As a 17 year resident I am happy to live here. The well kept public spaces and the great manners of staff are an lmportant matter to me..

The Village at Brookline has been a wonderful place for me to live. It has many great qualities that make me want to live here. It is a safe space. A very convenient place to live with all of the amenities nearby. The community is open and friendly to all, and goes out of its way to bring people together.
And my neighbors are friendly and helpful.
I feel very lucky to have had Village at Brookline cross my path.

I have lived here since 2002 and there have been many changes but I enjoy it because I have friends whom I can trust and relate;  and the grounds are always well maintained!  I also enjoy attending some events!

I have been here about five months and find the building very clean and well maintained. The maintenance staff and office staff kind and efficient and my neighbors are lovely. I enjoy living here very much.
A 17 year resident I am in general pleased  to live here.. I like the cleanliness and maintenance of grounds as well as the politeness and friendliness of workers.

I enjoyed living there for six months last year. It was a quite nice and pleasant place to live with good amenities. A grocery store and a Starbucks were located on the first level, which made my life convenient. It's about 15 minutes walk to the center of Cambridge, which was also a good exercise.

Sherikaye made my move in smooth. The building is secure, clean and with good amenities. The front desk is always very helpful. Im on upper level so its quiet here. Dont know about people living in lower floors (2-5).
If you like to pay a high price for eternal noise, broken amenities, poor management, and tons of unfriendly people this is the place to be.

I have lived here for almost two years and the ONLY reason we have stayed is the convenience. I am close to school and Trader Joe’s on the first floor is amazing. But the building is terrible - so poorly built - I can hear everything through the walls, from neighbors talking to upstairs neighbors walking around, to the bus noise from outside. The noise is unbearable and I have spent $1000  on headphones, etc to try to enable me to sleep. I have had packages disappear, been locked out of my apartment because the battery on my fob died, among other minor issues that all add up to make living here miserable. Some of the front door attendants are really great and others are terrible, leaving the desk unattended for long periods of time. There are several Airbnb-type temporary units so your neighbors can be changing constantly and you have little control over that. If you are moving to the area, particularly if you’re a student (as most of the residents here are), I would very strongly recommend you look elsewhere. You can find a much better deal in Cambridge.

I just finished a year lease and moved out. We were participating in a Harvard program so the location was ideal for us. Pet friendly, 24 hour concierge, under ground parking and the exercise room were what sold the property for us. They recently opened a Trader Joe's on the ground floor, which is convenient, but we were on the 4th floor above the loading docks. You can hear the trucks and moving crates at 6 am and all through the day. The North building does not have a concierge desk so you have to walk over for a concierge or to get a cart. The exercise room is well equipped. We were able to keep our parking underground when Trader Joe's opened but many lost their spots. Trader Joe's claims most of the spots except for one row against the wall. At the moment there is outdoor parking at the lot next door. I thought the concierge staff was attentive but they can have an "attitude".

I'm a current resident here and I completely agree with the previous review on this place. What attracted me were the shiny new amenities, 24 hour concierge (not really 24 hours since they are mostly not at their desk), and the obvious benefits of a luxury building at a discounted price due to its in the middle of nowhere location. After a few months of living here, the amount I'm paying is really not worth it. There are almost no good restaurants in the area save for The Breakfast Club. They pride themselves on being pet friendly (more like money friendly) with a hefty $75 pet rent per month, and yet if my dog accidentally pees in the lobby (only happened a few times when I first moved in), I get nasty attitude from management telling me to go upstairs, grab a paper towel and wipe it up myself. Management barely replies to me or my roommate's emails. The general manager also spelled my name wrong when emailing me despite my name being in my email address. They've threatened me with eviction even though I didn't violate any lease terms. It is a new apartment with great amenities and apartments, however in my honest opinion it is definitely not worth what I'm paying and I will not be continuing my lease here. Their management needs improvement, especially in the attitude department.

Ongoing rodent problem, extreme dirt and dust from surrounding construction, laundry machines are rarely if ever cleaned, noise 7 days a week. Management ignores resident complaints and is very difficult to reach.

The building is pretty great, 4 connected blocks with a long courtyard in between the two buildings. Units range from small windowed studio's to duplex's with floor to ceiling windows. In addition, there are units suited to all budgets and requirements. Small, but relatively quiet, gym located in the main building with a large laundry room right next to it. Overall great building, and only a few minutes walk to the Kendall/MIT T Station.

I have lived here for about six months and LOVE IT.  My apartment's floor plan is fantastic.  Location of building is SO convenient.  Leasing and maintenance and concierge staff are all top notch.  Will definitely recommend living here.
Neponset Landing is a great place to live.  Its proximity to Boston is an added bonus. The management, maintenance, and janitorial staff are exemplary.
LEASING STAFF! TIMELY AVAILABILITY; PEACEFUL AND EXCELLENT WITH ALL AMENITIES. PREVIOUS COMMENTS IN THIS SURVEY ALSO DESCRIBE OUR EXPERIENCE.

Hello,

As a resident tenant in Neponset Landing, I would say living here meets below standards of the market rental rate!  When there is an issue pretty much a hit/miss response time to evaluate & address.  There are some aspects of being a tenant where I feel are not honored or respected.  Where the tenant just gets dealt the con of the situation.  Alot of the original amenities & values of being a resident here has passed or been discontinued (which is truly sad).

Hi all - We have recently moved into Neponset at 8th Floor. The apartment have a very good layout, separate kitchen and lot of storage space. We have amazing view of Boston skyline. I love this apartment.

The leasing manager Ann was very supportive and helped a lot during booking process. We got a nice deal by leasing team.

The only con is when i open my apartment windows then , i can hear tracks sounds when a train is passing. 

Overall, I liked the community and apartment and recommend this place.
Neponset Landing is a beautiful building with spacious units and a view that over looks the river into Boston. It's conveniently located right outside of Boston with parking for residents and guest.

My daughter and I lived here for a time while she received medical care in Boston.  First, the staff are outstanding, kind, gracious, thoughtful, and want to ensure that everything is top notch. They go above and beyond! 

The apartment itself is amazing!  It's also very quiet--we never heard our neighbors once!  The layout is great and it's very well appointed.  It's very comfortable and spacious.

Whenever we had a question or need, the staff were immediately on top of it.  We loved the rooms, bathrooms, kitchen, and location.  If you're looking for a place to live, this is the place!  We highly recommend!

I do not recommend reservoirs for several reasons: the structure is flashy, the pool is always dirty, it is far from the center and above all the staff is totally inadequate. One night I was left out of my room and had to wait all night outside because no one could open the room, moreover, only once I left the facility I was asked for money for a problem that happened at the beginning of my stay in Boston . 
It's not recommend for teenagers because everything for us is not allowed because Reservoir are appartaments for old people.
totally professional staff. however they could put blinds in the windows and a few benches in the courtyard.

This is by FAR the best apartment community I have lived in. The staff is amazing, my neighbors are so friendly, and there is a great sense of community and you don't get that alot of places in Boston. Maintenance is responsive and very nice.
I never want to leave!! This is truly the best place I’ve lived and will be until we get our forever home. Love the community, staff, and location

Es un lugar seguro y excelente para vivir lo recomendaría  siempre tine una linda vista  además de eso tenemos el transporte que podemos caminar , el supermercado las farmacias y por si no faltará más las tiendas y restaurante excelente para vivir

Boston East is a great place to live! The units are spacious and beautiful. It is truly a gem here in the community! The staff cares about its residents and they've really provided a wonderful sense of community here!

Yo he vivido por mas de 4 años y no he tenido ningún tipo de problema; mi experiencia asido extraordinaria yo recomiendo Boston East a toda persona que ande buscando un lugar tranquilo y sobre todo que quiera tener todos los tipo de servicios asequibles como la Transportacion, las farmacias las tiendas y sobre todos el súper mercado es un privilegio.
The community of Boston East is really good and everyone is helpful.

The apartments are modern and well-designed, if a bit small and short on storage space, and the appliances are way nicer than what you'd find in a normal apartment building in Boston.  However, there is absolutely no insulation between floors.  You will hear every step your upstairs neighbor takes, and each one will sound like a 20-lb weight being dropped on the floor.  It's a shame because the building is otherwise very peaceful, and the neighborhood is really a nice place to live.

Update: After four months of living here, I have to take off a star due to issues with the building services and the finishings in the unit.  Just too many problems for what this place charges in rent.

As far as the building goes:
1) There's not a package room as is advertised on the website, and the package lockers have been down since late September, with no indication as to when they will be fixed.  The building management blames the vendor, but they also haven't found any other solution to the problem.  They just scatter everyone's packages all over the floor of the mail area, unsecured, and don't send any notifications when you receive something.
2) The after-hours maintenance staff isn't responsive.  There's not a number to call if you have an after-hours maintenance issue; you just have to submit a request through the resident app and hope someone sees it.  I had a lock-out issue once, and, after waiting a half-hour for a maintenance person to arrive and then another 40 minutes for the person to try to unlock my door, I finally just went and stayed in a hotel for the night.

As far as the units, the main window in my apartment is without window treatment of any kind.  Management said something about them either ordering or receiving the wrong kind of blinds for that window and then told me I could provide the window treatment on my own.  Not OK for what this place charges.

Update #2: I can now echo one of the other reviews here.  I've had packages go missing as well.  Contrary to what the website says, there is no "24-hour package room".  Management just lets packages be scattered all over the floors by the mailboxes, unsecured and unorganized.  Not even a basic level of competence on display here.
The facilities are all very nice and new but the noise isolation isn't up to par. I can hear upstairs stomping, showering, running taps etc. Just moved in and it's already getting on my nerves
AC broken for 3 weeks for more than 7 apartments during heat waves. Management aware and DID NOT DO A THING. Run, run for your life.

Location of this apartment is pretty awesome, right next to the T stop and in between Southie and south end. 

Now for the bad: the management here is horrible. Turnover for the staff is through the roof, we’ve seen at least 5 people come and go within a year (big red flag). The apartment is pretty expensive since it’s “luxury” but everything is made cheaply. So many issues from day 1, everything breaks constantly. We have had numerous stents of having no hot water. They are horrible with communicating with residents on issues. Will not be staying here much longer.
Overall great experience despitesometimes the household appliances went down.
They claim to have a 24-7 concierge however the concierge cannot open the door for you during off-hours if you get locked out. Why would I need such a concierge at all?

Great leasing experts at The Greenhouse. My 2 roommates and I were really pleased with the quick turnaround of our leasing contract. Kim from the leasing office was really great in helping us and out and making sure we had everything we needed!

Due to the impact of COVID-19, my friend and I conducted Greenhouse rental application online. We had a very pleasant conversation with the rental consultant Kim, and we look forward to living in Greenhouse.

Me and my girlfriend had just finished our Greenhouse rental application completely online this spring due to the COVID. To me it was a brand new experience renting an apartment only by email and website, but our agent Kim was always very helpful and patient, answered all the questions we have, provided us all the information we need, and made our rental process very smooth and easy. When we finally moved in, we saw the unit Kim recommenced us was fairly clean and in a great shape. The other staffs from garage/front desk/maintenance are very very friendly and helpful. We are very happy with our experience at Greenhouse. Absolutely recommend!

This building is both located in one of the best locations in Boston and extremely well kept. The building is right across the street from the Prudential Center and walking distance to numerous other Boston attractions such as Newbury Street, Boston Common and Fenway Park. In addition, the area is safe and I feel comfortable walking around at all hours (something that I can't say for other areas that I had been looking at). The inside of the building is also spectacular, with a person at the concierge desk 24/7, in case you had any doubts about security. Also, the concierge and leasing office people are always willing to help, no matter how small the issue is. When I moved in, the room was beautiful and cleaned extremely well. Lastly, the amenities which include a gym and rooftop pool make you feel like you are living at a 5 star hotel in one of the busiest neighborhoods in the New England. Overall, if you can reserve a spot in this building, I would highly highly recommend it.
We sold our house nearby and moved in a month ago and wish we’d done it years ago!    Fantastic facilities but the real stars are the on-site team:  thoughtful, caring - a real family.
They don't give back deposit on time. Need multiple follow-up! Everytime they tell some reason and never called me back once / gave an update on where my deposit is.

Honestly, the sad part is originally I would have given this place a better review. But with the circumstances as they are, I'm fairly upset with the apartment complex currently and if I had known two years ago this would have been where I was at, I probably would have gone with a different complex.

First and foremost, if you intend on having any unexpected life changes I would suggest a different complex. MetroMark makes you sign a 90 (NINETY) Day Lease Break agreement, and I fairly certain when you are breaking a lease you generally do not know THREE months ahead of time that you are breaking this lease. In my case it is that I was offered a job on the west coast.

Secondly, they also do not allow subletting. So even if you find a suitable person to take over your lease, they won't allow it. You also are not allowed to add a roommate until your lease is over - so couples looking to potentially move in together please be aware of this.

Lastly, they will not work with you on the renewal amounts. This renewal cycle they wanted to raise my rent $450 - and while the potential new renter I had in line was willing to sign the renewal if they met him halfway, I was told that the amounts were as they stand.

Yes, it is a pet friendly community, but most people don't pick up after their dogs (I am a dog owner and while I appreciate the available dog bags people rarely use them).

Do with this review what you will, but please make sure you take a look at your leases before you sign them - especially since this place has shown they're just in it for the money grab. Ask for a lease example for any place you apply to and make sure the terms fit what you are looking for, because frankly if the last three years have taught us anything, you never know what life throws you and I suggest finding a more sympathetic apartment complex.

While the included amenities are nice, and the location makes for an easy commute to the downtown area, it doesn't justify the price. They continue to raise rent prices without including anything else to make it worthwhile. Noisy neighbors as well - not to mention the continued smell of marijuana in the hallways in this supposedly 'smoke-free' property. Don't recommend.

We have tried to reach the property via apartments.com, their website and via a phone call and received no response at all. One of our friends live there and appriate the property. Given the service level, I would not recommend it.

I lived in MM for 3 years and am very torn between my experience here. Overall, any good experiences i did have are far outweighed by the bad. 

Pros: apartments are nice, appliances work well, common spaces and gym are nice to have. Located close to FH for easy commuting. In a nice location of JP ("up and coming"), and close to great food and downtown JP. 

Cons: 
- not a smoke free community as advertised. many residents smoke in their apartment, on the balcony and in the common areas. I first lived in a street level apt in building B for two years. Eventually had to move out to a third floor apartment because residents were constantly smoking outside the window. I could never open my windows. Moving to the 3rd floor did not solve the problem as many residents smoke on their balconies and in the courtyard. I addressed this with management multiple times (over email, face-to-face conversations), and was always assured it would be addressed. Then I would see the same residents smoking on their balcony. MM should not advertise themselves as a smoke free community without being more strict on their policy. 
- mess dog owners! As a dog owner myself, I understand that dogs have to pee and poop. However, we had multiple issues with finding dog poop/pee in the stairway or elevator. Some entrances we stopped using because of the smell of urine. The biggest issue we had was our upstairs neighbor letting their dog pee on their balcony, which would leak down to ours. Again, addressed this directly with management, and the situation never got better. 
- Management has gone down hill over last three years. While we lived there, we saw 4 different property managers come in. The current management is unprofessional, unresponsive, and will say they are addressing things that never actually get addressed. We had multiple issues with property manager right at the end of our time at MM with emailing or calling us back, or missing phone appointments we had set up with him.

Overall, the apartments not built well enough to justify the price, and don't have a responsive enough management to justify the price. 
Expect to smell constant smoke fumes, dog pee (maybe even have to clean it up off your porch), hear the train, overpay for parking and living, and then when you decide it's an issue, don't expect management to be compromising or do anything to resolve it. 

Would not recommend living here.

While the gym is nice, the other amenities don't justify the price in the area. The rooftop deck provided unremarkable views (of trains, a bus lot, and construction), and is not open year-round. The apartments look nice, but are not made with exceptionally sturdy or high quality materials.

The complex is located next to Forest Hills, and the infrastructure doesn't properly block noise. Additionally, early morning fire alarms were frequent. My partner and I found it very difficult to sleep as a result, and were unhappy with the management's response. We found the upper level management (building manager, and VP of the management company) to be very rude and condescending. 

While the staff does host events, there's no real sense of community. Most of the events were for pet-owners and residents with children.

I have not met one resident who is eager to renew their lease one it ends. 

If you can sleep through multiple buses departing at 4:30 am, I'd recommend this complex. Otherwise, there are plenty more sensible residences in the area that provide a better bang for your buck.
Wonderful building and excellent, professional staff!

The location is prime within a walking distance to Target, Star market, Fenway Park, Museum of Fine Arts. Staff are very helpful and friendly including Shiela, Justin, Jeff, John and Victor. The apartment is spacious and well maintained. The roof top over looks Fenway park.

From initial tour to daily service and amenities this property is run with friendliness and professionalism. On the first day we felt at home. The location provides easy access with all modes of transportation. The neighborhood is filled with amenities and living here is convenient and hassle free. The leasing staff and concierge staff make it a joy to walk into the building. We love living here.

As strange as it may sound, 1330 is now one of the "older" buildings in the spate of Samuels & Associates new construction projects.  I feel that things like appliances, infrastructure and overall "feel" of the building is starting to show its age.  As such, it doesn't seem to be as great of a value as it once was.  I'm still paying top rates in rent and other facilities are probably now more competitive.
Incredibly friendly, welcoming, and responsive staff make living at 1330 a thoroughly enjoyable experience.
Timely and Professional work!  Had a plumbing issue and it was taken care of immediately.  Great work by the maintenance team.

1330 is an amazing place to live! Modern and updated apartments with very spacious floor plans paired with a dedicated staff of concierge and maintenance workers makes living here an absolute joy. No request goes unattended and the amenities make this building a no brainer!
Dedicated staff that follow through on your experience.

Nice building and nice apartments - larger then other new buildings in the area but at a reasonable rent. The management and the concierge are good, at least I am very satisfied with them at the moment. The fitness center is small though - may need some improvement on that.

Great location. Can be a pain during Red Sox home games and get dirty and very crowded around the neighborhood because of this. Appliances need an update and the fact I can only get cold or hot water from bathroom sinks in both units Ive lived in is a head scratcher. Working in the city its a great place to live but could use a few upgrades. Staff is amazing however
Ive been here for a number of years and have felt very safe and comfortable. Ive never had any problems with neighbors or being out in the community.
Great quality with great staff but there are small issues that should have been fixed already. Overall good for the money though.

Although I have called 1330 Boylston home for only a short period of time, I could not be happier with my move! From our first meeting with the leasing office, my husband and I knew we wanted to call 1330 home. The location can not be beat within the heart of Fenway- endless restaurants, shops, and bars are right outside the door. The neighborhood becomes even more alive on game nights at Fenway Park. The building is beautifully kept with shared lounges, rooftop pool, and fitness center for residents. The apartments are furnished with modern touches and floor to ceiling views of Fenway Park and Longwood. We have loved getting to know the concierge and leasing staff and feel like they are readily available for any comments, questions or concerns. We would highly recommend 1330 Boylston to anyone!
Concierge and maintenance staff management office and management are very helpful great improvement in last year

Love living here for the most part. The location is great if its where you need to be but the tourists suck. Pool is awesome in the summer albeit a bit crowded. Gym could use work equipment-wise. Very friendly and accommodating staff. Awesome service.
Living at 1330 is absolutely wonderful.  While the amenities and apartments themselves are top notch, the best part of the building is the employees.
I can't say enough good things about my experience living here. The roof deck, pool and views are incredible!

Entirely unprofessional experience unfortunately. They scheduled a specific time and made sure I was there on time, only to make me wait 20 min. I was also told I could tour the unit I’m interested in, but when I drove there, they said I couldn’t see the unit. What.. is this place? I would never rent here, and reading the reviews, it seems renters have issues with the leasing office/management through and through. So glad I dodged a bullet.

I lived here for 18 months and it was bad. The main power went out for 3 months from Nov-Jan, so they had spotted back-up generators that would constantly go out. On multiple occasions all the food in my freezer and fridge rotted. The back up generators they had shut down multiple times every day during those 3 months, so power outages become regular occurrence. They did not reduce our rent when this took place. 

I had multiple packages stolen. They did not take any responsibility for these thefts and were not able to provide any kind of security footage to resolve reoccurring issue. 

Lots of other little things that turned me off of this place such as rude front desk. Though they did just replace almost all their staff (I assume cause they got so many complaints) so I am not as sure about this new group. 

SUCH an amazing roof view, but the living conditions were just terrible terrible and the staff was rude.

You can tell that this was built to be a rental building. The apartments are just junky. Cheap materials, cheap appliances, just… cheap.
I have lived here for a few years and so far the experience has been really good, it is always clean and the apartments are relatively new, moreover, the location is very good.

I have been to this place for 9 months now and I can say this is place is awesome. It’s secured and the staffs and admin are friendly. Everything is systematic and organized.  Plus it’s near to T and Star Market with Starbucks. I soooo love this place.
Live into HUB25 is a greatful experience because we count with good areas and have access to the public transportation (train and bikes). Thanks

Great location with less than 5 min walk to the T station. There is a Star Market right new door that opens until 11 pm. Very convenient for grocery shopping. 

Because the location is close to the T station, the noise from the train and also the highway is not neglectable. I have to close the windows at night for a good sleep.

The hub 25 has been home to so many memories and good times. I have the best neighbors and have made so many good friends whilst living here. Going on 3 years now since I’ve moved in, and the rent prices stay fair!!! I have no gripes. The staff and management have been amazing to say the least and I don’t see myself going anywhere anytime soon.

Love the convenience of public transportation and shopping right at my doorstep. Management and maintenance staff friendly and helpful and great amenities!! Clean common areas within and without the development.

The radian is a great place to live. The location is very convenient, especially being right in the center of Boston with easy access to a lot of things like the Public Garden, Seaport… It’s been a joy living here.
Overall, lovely building to live! Great location, big windows that let in lots of daylight and views and clean community! Concierge needs to be improved though.

Convenient location and a nice gym, but the leasing team is unprofessional and slow to resolve issues. Overall it’s a good deal if you get a well-maintained apartment right away but becomes a nightmare if there’s something that needs to be fixed.

Moving out of the Radian building after 1 year. Decided to move due to high rent increase and the frustrating air conditioning situation this year. It is not luxury living to have the building A/C cooling tower drained too early taking away residents control of a basic living perk (a cool apartment).
Radian is a great community in downtown Boston. I proudly call it home. :)
Radian is conveniently located, modern, safe, and I love the views from my windows! Highly recommended.

This building is a complete disaster… I’ve lived here for 11 months and I cannot wait for my lease to end and move to something decent.
The common areas are dirty, smell like dogs poop. The building is quite new but it already has tons of maintenance issues. Rats have already made their way into the building. Management is so unorganized and not available when you try to contact them outside of 9-4 pm on weekdays. Maintenance is even worse.. lights switch don’t work, your key fob may not work and there is no one to help you get inside your unit. And let’s not talk about the parking… totally inexistent!
They may offer deals when you first move in, but they quickly increase your rent by hundreds each year.  
Do yourself a favor and keep looking elsewhere. I wish I didn’t have to say this, but you will regret moving here within the first month of your residence.

The building is not at all well maintained and the leasing office will do absolutely nothing to help you. It has been four months since I moved out of the apartment due to terribly loud neighbors and rodent issues, and I have yet to receive my security deposit back. They never return their calls and don't respond to emails. Do not move here. Avoid at all cost.

Let me share some experience with the leasing office (HIGHLY NOT RECOMMENDED this place and NOT WORTH IT!!!)

Time line:
Mid Oct. : receive a call from 1550 on the Charles leasing office. 
Mid Dec. : Terminate date, I visited the leasing office.
Definitely follow the 60-days notice rule.

Before my departure, the leasing office contacted me 60 days prior to the termination date of the lease, inquiring about my intention to end the agreement. During this conversation, I explicitly communicated my desire to terminate the lease. The leasing office representative acknowledged my request and provided specific instructions on how to prepare my room for the check-out process. (I have a call history on my phone)

However, upon the designated end date, when I arrived at the office to inform them that I had cleaned my room and removed all my belongings, I was informed by the leasing office representative that there was no record of my lease termination request. As a result, they stated their intention to charge me an additional 2-month rent fee for not providing a 60-day notice.

Furthermore, despite their claim of having a comprehensive record of everything, they surprisingly lacked documentation regarding the call made to me regarding the lease termination. This discrepancy is quite perplexing and raises concerns about the consistency and accuracy of their records.

The management team must take action to prevent such incidents from recurring. It's evident that the representative failed to fulfill their responsibilities by not properly documenting my request, resulting in unforeseen consequences that I now have to bear.

There are RATS under our deck. We see them right outside our window. Management left one trap 3 weeks ago and has failed to communicate about additional remediation efforts. It is 24/7 stress for us and our dogs. We want OUT and can't even get an email response. If you are expecting a peaceful, safe, quality experience - this is not for you.  If you are hoping for competence and responsiveness, DO NOT MOVE HERE.

Trash rooms are truly vile for days on end. Dogs run around the courtyard off-leash at all hours of the day. Children are left unsupervised running through lobby and lounge areas. Cars are constantly parked improperly in the garage and on the street.

RENTERS BEWARE

There is not enough parking available for the community, resulting in a waitlist for the garage parking and thus people getting their cars towed every night. If you plan to bring a car do not expect to be able to park at home.

This building is very overpriced for its location, with no pool or amenities that most buildings include at this price point. It is a 20 minute walk to the commuter rail. You can find more convenient access to Boston with other similarly priced apartments that are just a 5 minute walk to the T. Parking has been a nightmare here and $250 a month is ridiculous for a location that requires a car to live. Apartments in Back Bay charge $300 for parking and this place is in Brighton, a 25 minute walk to Allston and 40 min to the Green Line. 

There is no safe way to cross Soldier’s Field Road, so no access to the River trail as promised on the website. Tons of construction going on on the street as well.
Lovely facility. Feels very safe and secure - quick responses from front desk and maintenance. Noisy area, but to be expected near the hospitals.
Great location, especially for medical professionals- right across from BMC. Good amenities that are kept clean. Apartment is spacious. Upkeep of grounds is good

Generally speaking, James Court is a conveniently located, quiet, peaceful community.  Free coffee in the lobby is and always has been one of the nicest perks of this community.  However, the "business center" was removed from James Court in order to construct the new package room.  Given this, it would be nice if access to the business center in Harrison Court was expanded to 24 hours again.  Additionally, pets have never been allowed in the courtyard.  The courtyard was always intended to be a quite, serene space for humans only, free of pet waste.  There are plenty of parks nearby that allow pets as well as the dedicated space outside the backdoor of Harrison Court.  Unfortunately, there are quite a few residents who ignore this rule.  It would be great if Greystar could address this issue with dog owners as well as maybe post new, more conspicuous signage than the existing signage at the two entrances from the city sidewalks.
Apartments here are very nice! Spacious, modern, high ceilings (top floor), nice gym, very quiet, good front desk service! Can't beat location if you're working at Boston Medical Center!

First- I want to start of by saying if I were to review the support staff, I would give a 10/5 (front desk and maintenance specifically).

Now- let’s review the property (can we give a 0/5?)

We only signed with this property because the leasing staff specifically stated that the management company “works” with their tenants and that the rent is always negotiable. We found this to be completely inaccurate. For example, when it was time to negotiate our lease change, this flexibility was nowhere to be found. Despite, the 5% decline in rental rate in the specific neighborhood. 

Second, don’t be fooled by the amenities. They are only available when the leasing staff is in the office. Spoiler alert it’s from 10am-4pm EST (not Covid related). The new management changed every lock so that no other employee had access to the buildings.

Speaking of new management- it is terrible. They forced/are forcing the support staff out that keeps the building running and that the tenants love. Also- don’t expect to receive one smile from any management once you sign your lease…. It’s a show.

Final straw for us was “the parking garage cleaning”. The parking garage that we paid $275/car/month (for two cars) was going through a “cleaning”. JHCH notified us 3 days prior to the cleaning, which took place mid week. They told us to move our cars for an entire day without a place to park or a stipend to park. Please note that this is in the South End and there is limited - to- no parking during the week (also not sure what the “cleaning” actually was). 

Either way- there are plenty of places near by that we wish we would have signed with instead of here. GOOD LUCK!

Don't bother even looking here.  I'm a current tenant, but won't be after my lease is up.  For the amount they charge for rent, you can find much more for your money.  Harrison Court was recently acquired by a larger company and they're not treating their staff well, which is exemplified by the number of staff that have quit in the past 6 months.  There's now only one maintenance guy (who's quite good), but unable to keep up with all the work that's required.  As for the concierge, they only staff the front desk part time, which is a tremendous hassle when you want to get your package that's locked up in storage.  The only way to get your package is to walk over to James court and pull away their concierge, leaving his desk unmanned for his tenants.  The gym is poorly maintained with a mix of good equipment beside outdated and often broken equipment.  I could go on, but trust me when I say, find somewhere else.

We have had probably more than 10 mice in our apartment in the last 3 months - never experienced this in a luxury, city apartment. We continue to hear scratching sounds and squeaking in parts of the walls after months of the building (I assume) trying their hardest to address this pest situation. Completely unacceptable.

6 months after moving in, a booming sound started to occur multiple times every hour all day and night long from our vents and that we can feel in the floor. Tried to work with the building / maintenance to get them to identify root cause and fix it. 18 months later, they have not been able to do anything about it. Completely unacceptable.

Equity Residential ‘renewal department’ turns a deaf ear to any of this and tries to raise rent by at least 7% every year even with these chronic issues. Absolutely do not rent here and do not rent with Equity Residential anywhere, especially if you intend to stay longer than 1 year.

The building lists a clubhouse and a fitness center that are not accessible to the residents.  

They are just employee perks for a staff that is neither managing nor maintaining the property well enough to be deserving of any perks.

They just raised the rent by $370/month.  There have been no services for several years, but, they keep increasing the rent.

You cannot complain to management because their policies prohibit going to the management office or calling them on the telephone..

Manager doesn't reply to the email and it takes so long to get responses. The manager didn't reply also on my move-out date and I had to postpone the move-out date. The interesting thing is that I still didn't receive any emails about this situation.

The lobby looked great! Unfortunately, when we scheduled a visit to look at some apartments there was not only a line of people but no one was in the office and no one seemed to know what was going on and several came through and didn’t have keys to said office. Might be a good place to live but we’ll never know.

Yes what the other review said is true. I'm living here right now and they forced a roommate on me after I specifically turned them down on the app. They just care about getting another rent check and not whether or not you will get along with a new person moving. 

I even saw a review on another website where the woman who had female roommates that moved out was forced to live with males after they(management) decided to fill the vacant rooms. It's crazy!

If you are in a roommate situation or sharing a 3 bedroom apt be aware that they will select your roommates despite you objecting to the available candidates at the time. They will also request a large fee to switch apartments or rooms. So if you want to pay that fee just be aware
Toured 7Ink and am blown away by the building!  It looks like it is so much fun to live at.  Apartments are so modern and having everything included is really awesome.  Love it!

Live here if you like sub-par amenities, unfriendly low income residents, unsupervised teenagers partying and groping one another in the lounge/rooftop, rotting food in the stairwells, and constant construction noise. OVERPRICED -- Vivo/Aimco will nickel and dime you for EVERYTHING: $500/month to use an empty parking garage; $100/month for electric shades (because the default tan linen shades block no light). Don't pay for the LuxerOne - Amazon/UPS/FedEx/USPS never actually use it; they will just throw your packages on the floor of the mailroom. Don't believe the other reviews on here - the building coerces people into filling them out to enter a "prize giveaway" that is never actually distributed -- these are FALSE REVIEWS. The building is soulless with no community. AVOID!!

I am a current tenant on the 2nd floor. I have been complaining to management for nearly a year about constant noise issues from the Orange Theory Fitness studio on the ground level. I am woken up daily at 6AM to loud music, thumping bass, and yelling fitness instructors on microphones. This continues until 8PM every day.

Nothing has changed after countless emails, phone calls, and in person meetings. The owner of the franchise clearly has no respect for the neighbors who live in the building, and building management will not fine them for noise violations. So the problem continues.

 If you are considering an apartment on the 2nd floor, beware.

Beautiful Apartments in the best location. 
It is  conveniently close to public transportation, shops, and restaurants, making it a great spot for people who want to be close to everything without the hustle of downtown.
Beautiful property in and the location is perfect!

Blvd Bond Apartments offer the perfect mix of luxury, comfort, and convenience. The modern design, high-end finishes, and spacious layouts make it feel like home from day one. The amenities—like the state-of-the-art fitness center, rooftop lounge, and co-working spaces—are top-notch, making everyday living both relaxing and productive. Plus, the location is unbeatable, with easy access to dining, shopping, and entertainment. The management team is also friendly and responsive, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable living experience.
