I’ve loved living here for the last year and am so excited to renew my lease. It’s super convenient and a very nice place. Concerns are addressed quickly.

I lived here for almost 2 years with my dog until it was time to move out to the suburbs, but we loved every minute! Lots of dog friendly areas, and lots of activities put on for kids throughout the seasons.

Our experience living at Blvd & Bond has been great! The staff has been incredibly friendly and supportive, with a special shout-out to Rachel, who has been professional, knowledgeable, and always willing to go the extra mile to assist us. Our apartment is clean, well-maintained, and offers a stunning view of the sunrise, and night city view. We've also enjoyed the warm and welcoming atmosphere from our neighbors. Highly recommend this complex to anyone looking for a comfortable and well-managed place to call home!
It’s all seamless till you get here. Then the property managers ill treat you and genuine requests fall on deaf ears.

I have lived here for a little over 2 years now and could not be happier!! Besides the occasional lightbulb change (which maintenance replaces asap), there's been no other issues in my apartment. Having the washing machine and dryer in the apartment is super convenient and I can give my puppy a bath whenever I want down in the pet washing area. 

Staff is nice, building is new and clean. I should use the roof deck more often.

DO NOT RENT HERE. As great as these units seem, the management company is awful and there will always be construction. They lied to us and said there wouldn't be, but we've been living in a construction zone since we moved in with no end in sight. It's completely covered in trash and dog poop. It is severely overpriced for the condition of the complex and the incompetency of the management office. We've had water shutdown now almost weekly and multiple times a week. When we've reported health and safety issues, we've been ignored for 6+ months. 

We would have never moved here had we known it would always be under construction. Do not trust the leasing office -- they will lie to get you to sign a lease. 0/10 experience. Worst living experience of my life.

Overall, I can’t recommend.

The good news:
1. The front-line team that manages the building is responsive and kind.  They care about their work, and care about resolving issues for tenants.
2. The coworking space is awesome if you WFH.
3. The underground parking is also great.
4. The local elementary school is well-rated & easily walkable.
5. South-facing outdoor community patio is lovely on a sunny day.
6. The gym is well outfitted, but feels a bit like working out in the basement due to a shortage of windows (there are a few at the entrance, but they are largely frosted over.

The bad news:
1. Our apartment has an extremely irritating 24/7 humming/buzzing noise.  We’ve been told it’s the building mechanicals , which are located near our unit.  Instead of fixing the issue, we were told we could move to another unit (which are smaller, and priced higher, and would require us to sign a new lease).
2. The AC unit in our bedroom (1 of 2 in our apartment) sounds like an 18-wheeler grinding its gears when it starts up.  It sounds like a slamming door when it shuts off.  We were told this is normal?!  However our other unit operates quietly.
3.  We’ve smelled pot when our windows were open, several times.  We’ve also heard yelling / fighting. So, we prefer to live with windows shut.
4. The entry foyer, package room, and mailbox areas are small, tight.  So, you and your guests will be wiggling around boxes every time you come home.
5. Our water supply is weak, and takes a long time to heat up.  Our washing machine does not fill up properly.  We have to run our kitchen sink for 30/60 seconds for the water to heat up.  We were told this is normal and will improve as more people move in (the building is new).
6. Connections to mass transit are bad.  20 min walk to Bellevue regional rail station.  There is a tenant-only shuttle that circulates to the T, the driver Chris is awesome, but this is only helpful if you catch the timing just right (so, very hit or miss).
7. We were offered an on-site storage unit in March.  It’s still not ready, not yet built.  So, we’re paying for an off-site unit.

Great location as long as you don’t mind horrible management, the new heat system that costs $300-$400 per month, never working elevators. I’m really surprised to see such a high rating. Most long term tenants are now moving out.

Lived at Barclay House for over 2 years, all in all it is a great place to live.  The apartments are large and the concierge service is a great bonus.  My interactions with management has always been very pleasant and professional and they seem to maintain the building very well.

I have lived in Brookline for about 10 years now. All of the buildings are old in Brookline, so that is expected when living in the neighborhood. The management in the building have always been very nice and professional towards me and my wife. Anytime something has happened with the apartment they have gone out of their way to make us happy. Even during last winter when we had over 100 inches of snow, they were there late at night making sure there were no issues caused by the snow.

The location is perfect! We can walk to Coolidge corner/Washington square in ten minutes. The T is right there!!!

If you're looking for an apartment in Brookline - THIS IS THE LAST PLACE YOU WANT TO LIVE. Management in the office is a scumbag - highly ineffective and one of the least professional young men I've ever met.  LOOK ELSEWHERE.

I lived there for 2yrs. and loved the location, because my son could walk to Driscoll School.  The T is so convenient, literally right outside your door.  There is a large balcony where you can put an electric grill and a table and chairs.  The security is good in the building and overall it's an ok place to live.

Do yourself a favor and do not move into Barclay on Beacon. While it may charm you with a nice view and closeness to the T, the downsides are way too much.
First of all - the management is the most incompetent bunch I have ever seen. Everything is always a problem with them. Completely unresponsive and unwilling to solve anything.
Second, they allow smoking in the building. Who still does that??? The smell of cigarettes, cigars, and weed is constant. And it's in YOUR apartment! It easily goes through ventilation system and spreads everywhere.
Next, windows. Oh, wow. The most drafty apartment I have ever been to. When it's windy outside - it will be windy inside. And I'm not just saying slight breeze. It will be WINDY. Things have been blown off the windowsill on many occasions. In the winter you will be either hot or cold. No middle ground. The thermostats are far off the windows, so by the time the cold propagates to it - you will be frozen. But then the heat will kick in and by the time it propagates to the thermostat - you will be sweating. It's a constant cycle of too hot then too cold then too hot and so on.
Finally, noise. The green line is especially loud, and you will hear it! No matter which floor you're on. So, you will be waking up at 5 with the first T, and you will be woken up after midnight with the last one.
And a final kicker - they raise the rent 10%! I am not kidding - 10%. Spoke to tenants who have been there for more than a year - everyone said they do it yearly.
In summary, as I said in the beginning - do not move in.

This property is stunning, UNFORTUNATELY the office manager Kelyn is extremely unprofessional. I was in an unfortunate roommate situation and during the dissolution of our lease i found out she had been lying to me about the actual circumstances. I have multiple emails with her stating that there were no payments made by my roommates and the eviction process would be starting soon so she needed me to sign a roommate release form. Come to find out, this was an entire charade made up between my two former roommates and her. Thankfully i trusted my gut and did NOT sign anything until my belongings were moved out of the unit. If i had signed that release, i would have legally had no right to that apartment, and my spiteful ex roommates would have not only succeeded in leaving me with no where to live, but also confiscating all my belongings, literally leaving me with nothing. Email after email i was assured that i was to come in and “help me not get any penalties or eviction on my credit”. An office manager literally wrote untruthful emails to me almost costing me everything. Please be aware that if you rent in this building it is run by an extremely unprofessional office manager that may or may not be telling you actual truth, and has no compassion towards knowing someone might be left without anything- because money talks of course. It’s too bad because this building is very clean, amazing Maintence service and beautiful views. Would NEVER recommend to anyone.

First, the property manager is the rudest woman I’ve ever met in my entire life. She should really be fired. Also the way she speaks to residents and the other team members is appalling. Trash rooms are always disgusting the city has been out several times. Maintenance is a joke the grounds are always filled with poop from dogs the lady who cleans the comman Space is great. 
The management stinks and the rents is so over priced. Looking to move when my lease is up. Upper management of greystar I know this isn’t the first time you’ve heard of the managers poor attitude I know for a fact so maybe you should do something about it. If your reading this!

After 7 years of living here, I'm leaving at the end of the lease.   Since Greystar took over the building, management and the quality of life have gone to pot.  Specifically:

Greystar changed security companies, and the new company doesn't respond to calls, nor do they routinely patrol the area or our building.  This is Chelsea after all, we have rude tenants who have no respect for others, and the Chelsea Police are tired of getting complaint calls
Trash rooms filthy
People partying loudly in the courtyard and nothing gets done
Landscaping has deteriorated
Cleaning has been cut back to one person
Notifications of package deliveries have stopped
Concierge and office services are a joke.  It's like everyone is at lunch 8 hours a day 

Bright spot:  the maintenance staff is responsive

Axis Admiral’s Hill is a great building to live at! Luxury, effortless, and convenient living just minutes from the Tobin Bridge. There's lots to see once you get here including a beautiful sun deck and reflecting pool outfitted with gas grills, all overlooking Admiral's Hill Marina. From here, you can even see the Boston fireworks on the 4th of July and New Year's! Additional amenities provided are a state of the art fitness center, wifi cafe, media theater, garage parking included, and more.

Axis Admiral's Hill is an apartment building with a polished exterior, interior, and views of Admiral's Hill Marina and the Boston skyline. There are fabulous amenities and a wonderful staff that make  this a dream oasis with a quick commute to the city. This gem is true to that title, luxurious and valuable.

Beware: high risk of theft. We've lost 10 figures worth of personal property living here.  Don't place your bikes in the bike room that you pay an extra fee to get the access key to - even if you put individual locks on your bikes, the locks will be cut and bikes stolen.  We lost 4.  After this incident, the management has yet to warn other residents or ask them to check their bikes are still there.  

On top of that, when we asked for security footage, we were told they lost the password to the system; no mention of how they'd resolve that - like even an attempt to reset the password.  We'd already asked about footage weeks ago when items were removed from our trunk in the parking garage (which you pay a fee to park in as well); they didn't address the inability to access the system then.

Packages are also stolen and there is no follow-up when that occurs; I've had items removed from a package while the box and receipt are left in the elevator.

Response from the building management team has been in large part "Oh I wish we could do something to help" rather than actioning.

I've really enjoyed my experience at 10 Essex. The maintenance team is extremely quick to respond and Tracy and Troy are both very friendly to deal with. The building is super convenient to MIT's campus and there's a grocery store right downstairs. It's simple and no fuss.

I moved in when 10 Essex was complete and brand new but my experience has been uncomfortable. Aside from general maintenance issues (that you wouldn't expect in a brand new building) this area is really loud. If its not the nearby outdoor concert venue that plays extremely loud music throughout the day and night its trucks loading an unloading nearby

10 Essex is a brand new building in a fantastic location in central square and moving in when it opened in September 2019 seemed like a great decision. My experience with my particular unit started off awful and only got worse. 

While the management has been recently changed, the building as a whole has had so many inherent issues from day 1. There have been leaks in multiple units and throughout the building that have not or cannot be fixed. The basement garage flooded on Christmas and all of the cars in it suffered major damage. The elevator for this 6 floor building was out of service completely for 2 months and communication around this issue was non-existent. There have been multiple malfunctions of the alarm system where the alarm sounded at full volume regularly for multiple days. Everyone I have spoken to in the building has had negative experiences of varying degrees, with multiple other residents attempting to gather the tenants together to take collective action. There aren't really any reviews of this building, I think because when people move out they just want to be done with it.

I've been living at Parkside Commons for 2 years, I was very satisfied, but for the past 6 months I've been having a lot of problems.  Noisy neighbors with children playing ball, running day and night, there seems to be a playground in the apartment above mine.  I've made several complaints at the office and they don't help me resolve the situation with the neighbors, they always say they're going to talk to the neighbors, but so far they haven't resolved anything, I've even proposed to move my apartment so I can sleep in peace.  also many mice have appeared in the last few months.  Well, if you want a nice night's sleep without being woken up by the neighbors, an apartment without a mouse, I don't recommend Parkside Commons.

On multiple occasions I asked to have features and or amenaties fixed, from leveling the poop table, to fixing a circuit breaker that was being leaked on and arcing dangerously, while I was standing next to it. On multiple occasions I was told they would not fix things, or they would drag their feet and take a month to fix safety issues. I inevitably had to contact the board of safety before they got their act together to fix it. While paying rent there, they had flea and mice problems, both in my building and the other (ie: it wasn't me). During the winter Walden Park is / was too cheap to keep up with snow maintenance, so I often heard of people hiring handy men to shovel out their cars (even though they paid Walden Park to use their parking lots). When leaving, I paid for another "feature" they offer, cleaning up the apartment, again was let down by these paid features. They then charged me extra, because they had to clean the apartment. Yes, it's your property! It's your job to maintain it! You own it! If you had kept up with maintenance, there wouldn't have been safety issues with the space you rented to me! 

In short, they have a lot of half-baked "features" that when you go to use, are broken or are with such large drawbacks. You are better off elsewhere. Save your money, save yourself the headaches.
Very good location in Brighton, right next to the T. Christine in the leasing office was super helpful and Tom was very quick to respond to maintenance requests.

As a new resident to the surrounding Boston  area, I will say that Camelot Court Apartments is great for a starter apartment. It's got an elevator, well renovated facilities such as laundry room, game/club room, small gym, nice sized bed rooms and kitchen. The only thing I would complain about is the lack of AC in the hot and humid hallways and elevator and THE CRAZY AMOUNT OF PEOPLE OVER 65. I had no idea I would be one out of 10 people that are under 30. I feel like I always have to be quiet to not wake up the grandmas and grandpas. So all in all, it's great for this first year, but I'm definitely going to save up to move somewhere with similar quality facilities but less elderly people.

I have lived in multiple apartment buildings and this was by far the worst experience I have had with regard to the building's management team. They consistently tried to overcharge our accounts (over half of the 12-month lease we had to contact the office to let them know the amount owed was incorrect), and they are very stringent with the security deposit (they took over half of it for a 30-minute cleaning job). Never have had such a poor experience, would not recommend.

Don't waste your money and rent at Elevate Cambridge
loft. The apartment prices are very steep, the
apartments are terrible (no human should pay to live in
those conditions). The inside looks unfinished and the
space is very very small. In summer it's terribly humid
inside (my clothes and books felt damp all the time), in
winter it is so cold that the heating doesn't warm
enough the apartment, you will end up paying
electricity bill in the amount $200 per month in winter.
Not only apartments are small, but there's no
wardrobe. I had more than few times issues with warm
water and one time the water was dripping from the
ceiling. The shower floor was leaking water, i had to
clean the bathroom floor every time after shower. The
maintenance team didn't get any work done when i
needed it. When i moved out they took fake photos
from somewhere else and misrepresented it as extra
cleaning work in order to make more money. They
dropped one charge when i pressed but i got tired of
one week email back and forth. Yes, they did it. The
most of lease consultants are passive aggressive, they
even don't listen to address your issues. No sunlight
comes inside apartments. It's kinda depressing after
some time. The morning 7 am, trash truck will wake you
up. The dust from construction nearby will pile up in
your apartment regardless how many times you clean
every week. The bathroom is small and isn't well
maintained. If you are willing to spend so much money
to rent an apartment, look somewhere else. You will
regret if you decide to rent here. The photos posted on
website doesn't represent the reality.

I had a mice infestation in my apartment and wanted to terminate the lease however the leasing office refuses to terminate my lease without paying 2 months. Which isn't fair because pest control and leasing office both determined that my apartment was sanitary and it was not my fault that mice were here.
I also saw mice when I was going to the gym!
On top of that, days after the pest control came, I bought mice traps off of amazon and i caught one with my own trap! After pest control came. The problem is still persisting and I want to leave but they are asking me to pay a fortune when it's their fault. Leasing office is ignorant, biased and inconsiderate. They don't care. They are incredibly condescending and won't respect you. A majority of my experiences with management have been rude and I have never felt so demeaned. I don't recommend this building as no one seems to care about this issue or residents concerns. Also, when I first saw the mice, I immediately booked a hotel room and contacted the leasing office however they refuse to compenstate me by lowering my monthly rent or by breaking my lease. It has been 2 weeks since this issue has occured and I can barely sleep at night. I keep trying to contact leasing office but they are ignoring my emails.

Regular issues with other tenets partying until 3 AM during weekdays. No response from management. Regular issues with other tenets smoking marijuana to the point that my laundry smells like it. No response from management. Regular issues with the hot water. No response from management. You get the gist. Cannot recommend you stay away enough. TERRIBLE MANAGEMENT

I've lived here for over 2 years and absolutely would consider living here again if I moved back to the area.  The grounds and premises are well kept.  Pete, the current property manager, accommodated all of our needs and made sure everything was to our expectations during our stay here.  It is comforting to have a property manager like him that really cares about the property he manages.  Walt is a fantastic asset to their team - friendly, knowledgeable, skilled and a fun person to talk to in passing.

The property is in great condition. The location is super convenient, being in close proximity to the Lower Mills village.  This makes for a quick walk to get a bite to eat, grab drinks, or do your grocery shopping, without the need of a car.  In addition there are multiple bus stops and train stations in the area for commuting, also within minutes.

Apartment not as advertised and among the worst experiences. No parking is available and they will lie to say it will be in a month or two. Handicap buttons in garage are not functional. Unresponsive and unhelpful property managers. Stolen packages and trash/clothes frequently left in the lobby.

This was my first studio apartment and I couldn't have asked for a better experience! The apartment is beautiful and modern and with washer and dryer in unit, one of the most affordable options you'll find in Boston. Great location being right across the street from the Ashmont train station with a cute coffee shop across the street, and a park/bike trail a 15 minute walk away. Management is wonderful and has always gotten back to me within 24 hours. I love this place and will most likely renew for a 3rd year!
It is nice, but is really overpriced for the size of the units and the location. Management could use some improvement...
Si necesitas un lugar tranquilo ,limpio y con buenas expectativas para vivir este es el lugar perfecto.

Amazing location, the leasing center has been nothing but nice to us with getting everything situated. They even went as far as to allow our packages to get delivered early because of a mix up with the moving company.
Great place to live in but if you are facing back, you will be bothered by the noises coming from the blue line. Staff is efficient and helpful.
I love the ocean views, the location so close to Boston, but it also feels so far away at the same time .  Can’t wait for beach days this summer.
Above and beyond. Nice staff. Extremely clean. Very very clean community. Safe and surprisingly quiet... office spaces really helps home office days
I have been living here for 7 months and really like it! Is so cool to have the beautiful view of the sea, use the gym and participate in all the Ryders activities

Walls are paper thin. Smells and noise drift all hours of night. It’s supposed to be smoke free but management doesn’t enforce. 2 washers and 2 dryers for entire building, usually at least one is broken or left dirty (last week opened washer to find no lie spaghetti and sauce inside). HUGE rodent problem.

Constant attempts have been made to break in to various different apartment. Packages go missing regularly. Management is rude and intentionally unhelpful. Has a bedbug and rodent infestation. This place was just detrimental to both my physical and mental health.

Lots of insects and spiders. Washers/dryers consistently broken and eat money which management will not refund. Management unresponsive and hard to get a hold of. Mail and packages frequently go missing. Floors/ceilings constantly creak so if your upstairs neighbors have a different schedule than you, you're going to be miserable. Ridiculously overpriced for a building on the outskirts of town that looks and feels like it's been slowly falling apart since the 80's (with some paint and cheaply refinished floors/cabinets thrown up to make things look pretty for the initial showing).
The property itself has issues & they do have a rodent problem due to that. The property management office are nice to your face, but they're not good or trustworthy.

These apartments are overpriced and nasty. There's dead mice in the halls and dead rats by the garbage. They have tenants smoking pot in the stairwells that set off the fire alarms and they do nothing about it. When they finally get around to exterminating, they use vendors that use products that are dangerous to pets instead of vendors that use pet safe products. The office staff, especially Ken, takes tenant complaints and then does absolutely nothing about them. Their website has been down for days. I told him. He's done nothing and that's how I pay rent. They sent another vendor in that made a huge mess and actually locked the door to the closet my cat's litter boxes are in so she couldn't get in. They have no respect for the tenants who pay their ridiculously high rents. You can do so much better than here. Stay away.

I used to live at flats at 22. 3 months after I moved out, I became a victim of identity theft. Some identity thieves have been using my info to apply for credit cards and bank accounts. They have all my info including the place that I worked for. the only way that I can imagine how they would have got a hold of my info is someone from the leasing office has probably sold my info. Beware of living here. The identity thief is using my old address at flats at 22. It amazed me as to what kind of people they attract. I am still trying to resolve the identity theft and its very frustrating.
Everything was clean, quite place and I will definitely recommended

I'm new to the area and struggling to find a place for my kids and I. That is until I walked into Broadway Tower! The entire building is clean and well maintained. The apartments hit ever mark. I can't wait to move in!

Incredible staff, very helpful! 
Maintenance work was done efficiently and on time. Maintenance workers very knowledgeable and professional. 
Thank you!
Very pleased with the professionalism and wouldn't change anything as long as every tenant is direct with management and maintenance of their issues they will be resolved.

Broadway Tower a great community working, and keeping up with the future elements. 
Great place to call home!
Right in the middle of Revere!
Broadway Towers has the best system for submitting maintenance problem and great timing for fixing the problem.

Corporate Greed and unfair practices is the lasting impression we have of this apartment community.  From the on-site manager to the Regional Manager at their Corporate Office, they ignored reasonable points of contention that were brought up, and refused to acknowledge their OWN mistakes.  I will not recommend these apartments as they place profits over student clients.  ??My son and his 3 friends moved into these apartments in January 2021, as their nearby college was not fully opened up for housing.  I co-signed as all were just starting out and did not have a qualifying income on their own.  Because the occupancy at 100 Memorial was low due to Covid-19, they were given a move-in special offer with over a $1,100 discount in total. They all agreed to the terms, which included their intended move-out date. They provided a security deposit to lock in the offer and terms.  They then received an email confirmation from the on-site management.  After we made calls to order rental furniture, utilities, and renter's insurance, 100 Memorial Apartments then rescinded the move-in offer taking the discount away.  The explanation was that the length of lease that was agreed upon did not qualify for the move-in special.  The four room-mates were too far along in the process and had already stopped looking for other apartments, and therefore felt they had to accept this or lose their deposit.  

The four room-mates had a short lease (slightly over 90 days) and believed that at the time of move-in that the on-site management understood their intended move-out date which was the last day of the lease.  The management sent the boys a reminder notice that a 30-day notice to vacate was required, however they never sent me a copy.  I am the one who was financially "on the hook", however I wasn't given the same notices as the boys were.  The management charged the room-mates a pretty substantial "insufficient notice penalty" of more than $1,000 dollars.  Had I been sent the reminder notice, I would certainly have made sure the notice to vacate was submitted on time.

I tried to work out a resolution with both the on-site manager and Regional Manager via email, however both were not understanding nor receptive to a compromise.

Living in Gamma North had a profound impact on me. I dealt with persistent issues like mice infestations and an awful, lingering smell. Additionally, I was constantly fearful of people trying to break into my apartment or steal my car from the parking lot. Eventually, I decided that no amount of money was worth enduring such a situation. I ended up paying a two-month rent termination fee and moved out early.

Pros: The location is convenient, within walking distance to the subway station and grocery stores. Additionally, the apartments are quiet; either my neighbors were considerate, or the sound insulation is effective. And for these, they get the one star.

Cons: Where do I begin? The building itself is old and rundown. It appears that some units may be in worse condition than others in terms of appliances, but overall, maintenance seems lacking.

One issue is the high level of lead in the water, making it unsafe for use. Mold is also a serious problem, particularly for those with allergies. Additionally, residents should be prepared to deal with various bugs and rodents, especially on lower floors.

While I live on the upper floors and haven't encountered mice inside my apartment, I've spotted them in communal areas like the recycle room and entrance. I've even found dead mice in the laundry room and in front of the entrance. So I guess this is a serious issue for people on the lower floors but also shows how non-hygienic the whole building is.

The trash isn't being handled properly, and the ventilation is inadequate, leading to a persistent odor throughout the entire building some of which gets to your own apartment.

The laundry room isn't cleaned frequently enough. While tenants may share some responsibility, the limited number of working machines for the numerous units makes it extremely challenging to find an available one for laundry.

There are homeless people INSIDE the apartment building asking for changes all the time 

The worst of all, is this constant awful smell circulating around all the floors and in the whole building.

Akelius doesn't conduct inspections or thorough cleanings before new tenants move in. You might find yourself moving into an apartment on the exact same day the previous tenant moves out, with any necessary maintenance left for you to handle and at your expense. For example, if the bathroom needs painting, they'll do it after you've moved in, forcing you to vacate due to the smell of chemicals while paying the rent. This lack of consideration reflects their greediness.

There are certainly more negatives to mention, but I'll stop here. Overall, I wouldn't recommend moving here. It's too expensive for what little they offer.

I never do reviews. But I was looking for a place and saw the rating here as 4.8 and I was like, are you freaking joking?! Yes, it is close to the train station. But you know what else is close to the train station? Station itself!

If you are looking for a decent apartment worth living, being respected by the landlord and not fighting all the time with mice and swage smell just go somewhere else. I have lived in 4 stated and rented 10 apartments by myself and this by far is the worst place I have ever lived in!

First of all, the management company's leasing and marketing team,  Jazmary, Tylor, Ali, are extremely rude and disrespectful. The building is old with a serious lead problem. Tenants were officially notified by the mayor's office. Mice are everywhere. Trash are everywhere. Forget about any maintenance request being done at all, let alone in time. Packages are stolen all the time. And when you move out, they do not return your deposit. If you can, try to avoid this place.

Do yourself a favor. If you dislike living in a dirty, full of trash, full of mice apartment complex, do yourself a favor and look for other places. Akelius only answers you until you get the apartment, after that they disappear and you have to live in a condition that you definitely do not deserve.

This is a fantastic building primarily because of its ideal location, being just a 5 min walk from the Red Line in Central Square, and for its dynamite maintenance team. This is an older post-war building with renovated apartments. Hardwood flooring is great (only if next to amenable neighbors) along with very smart renovated kitchens and bathrooms. Un-renovated apartments are still present for those on a budget. All the homes are on the smaller end but normal for the area around Central Square.
Dog-Friendly, Backyard Grills, and Off-Street parking are all icing on the cake for this cozy complex in Cambridge!

The place is good, but recently there have been security concerns. The management increased our rent by 20%. As good as the place is, there are cheaper alternatives near by with equally good, if not better management. The amenities are also not easy to access. To use the gym, for example, you need to reserve 2 days before. So if you feel like using the gym suddenly, there is no way to access it. The premium rent is not worth it.

The apartments are really old with little insulation, even the renovated ones. The walls are thin and you can hear your neighbor even when they don't talk loud. The heater is extremely loud and the appliances are not good. The lease included fitness center facility which has been shut for almost the entire year either due to covid and renovations. There are mice and rats almost everywhere. The apartments say no smoking but so many of the tenants are smoking all the time and the management does nothing about it. The rules say no dogs but a lot of the tenants have dogs and don't clean up after them. Overall for the price you could go to somewhere better.

The apartments have no insulation - I can feel the wind coming through the outer wall in the winter, I breathe in the multiple substances my next door neighbor smokes in the middle of the night, and I hear the children upstairs running and screaming starting at 6am as well as my next door neighbor playing dance music past midnight. Even the treadmills in the gym have lost their tread and are dangerous to run on. Multiple complaints to the management has been met by "call security", and they have now stopped responding at all.
I was fooled by the security booth and nice lawns. These apartments are incredibly overpriced in a mediocre location. For not being able to sleep and being constantly sick from secondhand smoke, I will never live here again, and I wish I had never moved here in the first place. I wish I could give 0 stars so that no one else experiences this.

Pros

Beautiful area
Security on grounds
Quiet neighborhood
Friendly neighbors
Small pet friendly
Nice appliances
Heat/hot water included
Close to the orange line
Free WiFi*
Laundry in area**

*Wifi is really meant the common areas, Not in your home. So be sure to add an internet service provider to the cost if comparing.

**Washer and dryer available for 2  bedroom homes. other units have access to multiple laundromats on grounds $2 per wash & $2 per dry

Cons

Living space to cost ratio*
Electricity not included
Parking is spotty**

* A studio starts around what one would expect for a 2 bedroom elsewhere and it only keeps going up. Trying to pay for this place by yourself is... admirable but trying to keep a family in such a small space isn't feasible.

**There's no assigned parking (which I think is good) however that also means you're not guaranteed a spot close to your home. Outside of bad weather or moving in/out it's not problem, otherwise it's a bit uncomfortable.

Summary
Aside from living space, you really get what you pay for here. I'd advise people just starting out in their careers to look for more affordable homes and families to find more spacious homes.

I'd recommend this place for pairs who are comfortable with their income and savings.

You'll save more money even if you have to pay for utilities and you'll get more space on top of it.

I feel the same way that the rent is to high. I live here now and this is going be my last year. The property is very beautiful. I guess you are paying for a beautiful property through your high rent.
I really enjoy living here but the rent is too high which is the only reason I may leave
Sudbury is a great community. Great location, quiet, safe. The design and quality of this building are awesome. It definite stands out among many modern apartment complexes that I have toured.
The Sudbury apartments is a great place to live. Management is great and very welcoming. Love the location too!

The Sudbury is luxury at its best. A beautiful building in the heart of downtown Boston with incredible views and services. The employees are approachable, warm, and friendly. The proximity to the North End, TD Garden, Downtown Crossing, and so many great places to eat and shop make this a standout option for living. The building is very dog friendly with a pet spa and outdoor area for dogs. There are so many amazing amenities including a professional gym, chef's kitchen, pool, etc. It is a truly excellent experience and my neighbors are so nice and friendly, too!

I've lived at the building for 4 years and have watched it fall apart more and more each year. The building used to be amazing to live in but has become a daily nightmare. I'm looking forward to moving out when my lease expires.

I love living here at The Sudbury> For three years now I have enjoyed the community of neighbors, made friends, and felt cared about by management and staff. 
The amenities are fantastic, including the barbecue area and the dog park and pet spa. Maintenance is timely. And the location! You can't beat the nearness to the MBTA green and orange lines and buses, shopping, the greenway, Boston Public Market, restaurants (including the famous Union Oyster House), Faneuil Hall, medical facilities, museums...I could go on. Did you know we are about 4 blocks from the Boston Gardens...no need to search for parking during sporting events and concerts? Nuff said. You will definitely like it here.
The Sudbury epitomizes urban living and is located very conveniently and is a great community
I appreciate the effort to update the property and engage the residents in a more friendly manner than previous management.
Like everything, there is always room for improvement; however, I have no complaints.

The walkable resources in the area are fantastic, the apartments have a clean and modern look with floor to ceiling windows, great temperature control, strong water pressure, and some excellent views of the city. Jerson, Paul and the leasing staff were fantastic, friendly, and communicative. I had to put in a small maintenance request after moving in and Oscar was quick to help, efficient, friendly, and gave me great suggestions for upkeep. So far, I'm loving it here!
Luka is an amazing community and building. I'd absolutely recommend it to anyone!
I toured this building last week and I loved it. The view from the terrace is amazing! Looking to move in November and can't wait!
Luka's location and amenities are great for the price you are paying. Everything works well, and the team here is quite helpful.
Hate electric stoves but it was reasonably priced…for now

Luka is average at best. Packages are delivered and residents are never notified. Trash accumulates in common areas. Leasing office is difficult to contact and when you do get to talk to someone, they aren't much help. The only good employees here are the building people carried over from Avalon's time owning the building.

Leasing and front desk staff have been highly professional and helpful with every interaction from newly touring the building to arranging for movers, answering questions, and helping with all package deliveries now that I'm a resident. Location has restaurants pretty much right outside the door. Shops, Boston Common, and AMC Cinema are a short walk away.

Luka is a good place for a decent home. It's a little costly but the facilities are in good condition and concierge staff is nice. However, since the management changed I have had a couple of issues like delays in maintenance resolution, one lost package, and annoying parking system. I understand that issues happen, but the transition has been long and troublesome. I am sure they are working on it and they'll improve over time.

The building doesn't fix appliances if/when they are broken. The building staff is impossible to get a hold of.

If you don't believe me, try calling the building number and choose the touch tone dial option saying you are a current resident, and see if you can ever get anybody on the line. Ever.

Ever since COVID started this building has gone completely downhill. The management does not care at all about making this a nice community and instead treats tenants as hostile. The leasing office is argumentative and unwilling to uphold even the most basic community standards outlined in the lease. If it wasn't for the location this building would be empty.

-The walls are paper thin. I've heard so many animals around me throughout the day that I felt like I lived at the vet.
-My neighbor chainsmoked cigarettes in his unit every day but management did NOTHING about it despite me notifying them when he was smoking.
-They tried to force me to pay hundreds of dollars in cleaning fees when I moved out even though I deep cleaned the apartment myself. I literally had to consult my friend who is an attorney to show me the law that forbids them from doing this (but it won't stop them from trying!).
-The on-site parking is a complete mess. My car has been damaged and I've heard countless stories of other accidents. The valet has huge turnover and nobody there takes their job seriously.
-The common areas, hallways, and gym are usually pretty gross (trash being in the halls for days, lack of cleaning equipment in the gym, overall poor upkeep). Don't even get me started on the outside of the building - the area on the LaGrange street side is always disgusting!

I've also lived across the street in the Kensington and had an overwhelmingly positive experience there. AVA may treat their tenants like garbage, but many other "luxury" apartment buildings in the area can actually deliver on their promises.

I would never recommend living in AVA Theater District to anybody.

While the building has package acceptance, they did not always notify residents’ timely of the delivery. There were instances when a package came in before noon but we weren't notified until late evening.
Speaking of concierge/security, it was very inconsistent. The concierge was only at the front door during the day and was often busy with deliveries and other items which took them away from their desk. There was no one at the rear security station until 6pm. This allowed people to enter through the rear door without being noticed by leasing agents or concierge. During the times when concierge was supposed to be stationed at both doors, they were not always at their station. This lead to situations where anyone could walk in behind a resident and go unnoticed or unchecked by concierge. 
While it was convenient having a gym on the 6th floor, the gym equipment deteriorated over time. The equipment padding was ripped on the weight machines. The building used to provide towels but stopped providing them over the course of our time there citing residents’ theft of the towels. 
There were also instances where members of the building were running their own personal training businesses and inviting their clients into the gym to train during popular workout times like after-work hours of 5pm-7pm. 
The common areas are a nice feature. However, the students bring their friends over to hang out especially during warm weather days. Even though each unit has a guest limit, when multiple people from a medical school live in the building and can bring multiple friends over, it sometimes meant large crowds on the roof deck which made it hard to use the grill or hangout in an optimal location with friends.
There are other drawbacks that can’t be controlled by management but you should consider because they might not arise during a tour of the building. Construction is taking place around the building constantly which means loud noises starting as early at 7am, sometimes on weekends in summer. Large populations of homeless people or drug users directly in front or behind the building, especially during night time of warm weather months. Loud music coming from Bijou and loud drunk people from the two strip clubs or various night clubs in the area. This becomes an issue as the police shut down access to the roads around the building on weekends and if you take ride-share or a taxi, will be forced to walk through crowds of drunk people and homeless people late at night.

No place better than a shimmering tower in the heart of Boston.  Next to the greatest nightlife on the East Coast, and the greatest food anywhere, AVA theater district sets itself apart from most any luxury building in Boston.  I can't imagine living anywhere else!

I moved into my new apartment  1 week ago.
The staff is so friendly and helpful I am very impressed .
The common areas are always spotless and smells great !
The apartment is spacious and has lots of cabinets.
The staff very helpful even when unexpected things  presented 
I give the apartment building  a 4 star rating I would refer  anyone and everyone to this apartment complex !
I want it this place because I'm a college student who wants to move out her parents house. And it's kind of hard when you don't know what apartment you want to live at.

I've lived here for the past year, and I'm very pleased with that decision! The landlord is kind, accommodating, and responsive, and the appliances (with regard to the kitchen, bathroom, in-unit washer/dryer) are modern and well-functioning. Access to the building, individual apartments, and mailroom is secure but also easy, and the garage parking is very helpful. The patio is also a great place to spend time in the warmer months and host gatherings. Within walking distance, there is a gym, a small grocery store, some restaurants, and access to public transportation via Nubian Square. BMC itself is only a 20 minute walk away. Overall well worth the price!

Bottom line up front: This is the best landlord I’ve ever had. Responsive, understanding, and present. The unit was gorgeous, an amazing size and quality for the price, and I had no issues the entire time I lived there.

I moved to Boston from Texas, and I had a short time to visit Boston and select an apartment. Joe was the most responsive person out of all of the apartment listings I reached out to. The tour was great, he answered all my questions, and help guide me through the application process. If I remember correctly, I got an approval the same day.

My move into the apartment was seamless. Joe was present, helped my dad with parking our U-Haul, and was communicative with me in the month prior to the move and the day of the move. 

My time at 125 Warren Street was amazing. No problems with the building. The garage parking is a great add. The amenities and common areas were luxurious and well kept – you will often see people cleaning the halls, and always at reasonable times. You’ll even see Joe taking care of the units himself, whether it’s taking out the trash, putting up packages, or replacing your air filter.

I have not, and do not know anyone, who has experienced this level of attentiveness and care from a landlord. If the gorgeous units and amenities don’t convince you the price is worth it, then consider the service and security of having a landlord who cares. This is how apartment living should be.

I lived at 125 Warren for two years and absolutely loved my experience. My apartment had a huge modern kitchen, large bathroom and a full size washer and dryer. The bedroom and living space was the largest for any apartment I’ve ever lived in. Everything was brand new and in perfect condition. The area is also very convenient with many public transportation options. I am really going to miss living here!

This property is an amazing location near the bus station! It was a very nice apartment to live in and I was the first to live in my apartment. It was very clean and everyone in the building is very nice! Joe is an amazing landlord that helped at any time with questions or services. Was very understandable and always was will to help with whatever needed or asked! Would rate this place more than a 5 stars. I will miss it for sure!

Really enjoyed living at 125 Warren. I moved into apt 408 as one of the first tenants when this building was completed. It’s been a great year. Clean, modern and spacious. Not to mention super energy efficient (loved that high tech heating system) 
The best part of living here though, was the fantastic property manager, Joe made it the most stress free rental. He was always a text message away to resolve any issues and made sure that the building was always kept clean and tidy and as new as it continues to look. 
If I ever move back to Boston I’d happily move back in…Maybe one day!

The apartment units are all very modern and clean. I’ve lived here for over a year and really love it, the property manager is incredibly responsive and helpful—-they even decorate the apartment lobby/hallways for holidays, it genuinely puts a smile on my face. The location is very convenient, close to a lot of bus stations. And I even feel relatively safe walking around at nighttime there. There’s also an indoor garage and an outdoor patio where you’re able to use the grill and fire place 7-11pm!  I’d definitely recommend

After an extensive search across Boston, we've found our perfect home at Rozzie and we are thrilled!  We've been here over a month and can say that everything is still exceeding our expectations.  Our apartment is incredible with floor-to-ceiling windows that are truly remarkable and the community continues to feel homey and welcoming!  

The staff here are fantastic.  Tina, the manager, has been incredibly helpful and continues to impress us even offering tips on local spots such as Delfino's  Restaurant - essential for newcomers to the area like us.   Steff, the assistant manager is always pleasant and incredibly helpful even during our most annoying questions.  Even the maintenance supervisor, Luis, proved competent and dedicated from the start.  On our very first night, after realizing we had no hot water, we called for help regretting the late hour.  Yet, he responded within minutes, ready to fix our issue immediately, though we opted to wait until morning.  However, the commitment to service truly stood out to us.

We've enjoyed meeting neighbors in the gym, elevator and while out and about, and so far, everyone has been incredibly friendly. 

If you are considering a move to Boston, Rozzie should definitely be at the very top of your list.  So far, so good - no regrets.
Overpriced and amenities aren’t great. I wish that the complex would update the gym equipment, its both too tall and too short at the same time.
Everyone has been extremely helpful during the move and accommodating. They have been available for any questions, concerns, or issues, and I am very happy to live here.
The apartments are GORGEOUS and they are right next to the Sullivan Sq t stop which makes it so easy to get anywhere! Would highly recommend!

Staff are great. They quickly respond to any inquiries and service requests. 
The amenities are bare-bones and the location doesn't have too much going on for it without having a car.
If living space is more important to you than location then this is a perfect match!
Staff is there for you in any things that may come up very friendly and helpful and very knowledgeable they make living here peaceful and comfortable
Very nice, respectful, quiet, and friendly community. Public spaces are always clean, and i have never felt as though someone is being excessively loud in these areas.

This place used to be nice, but not anymore. The management is lacking - we pay for common area maintenance, but the restaurant uses them more than residents. Parking in front is for the restaurant, which is odd. The basement is also used by the restaurant, with access to our apartments. Management didn't inform us about a restaurant party with over 200 people in the basement. Complaints lead to rude emails. The gym closes without explanation. Residents must handle concierge duties themselves. The garage smells like dead animals, and management does nothing. Maintenance staff are the best thing this place has (they are great), but the carpets are dirty in every floor. Mailboxes have been stolen, with no notification to residents. The place has potential but needs significant improvements (management 101). It's not the same place I moved into.

I recently moved into this apartment. The location provides an easy access to public transportation. The building itself is well-maintained and secure, with friendly and responsive management. My unit is spacious and bright, with modern appliances, but lack of storage and cooking surfaces.

The community amenities, including the gym and rooftop terrace, are a good. Noise levels are minimal, and the neighbors are respectful. Overall, this apartment is good and I can recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable place to live.

The office staff are great here they always greet you with your first name..and whenever I have a question or problem it is taking care of right away… so as I renew my lease I am looking forward to another year of good living thank you Leslie and Olivia
The graphic lofts is amazing, the leasing office is so good, always can solve your problem, the maintenance team is quick and resolve everything.I really enjoy living here
Nice environment and good community with nice amenities. So far so good with the experience and kind staff. Packages are secure and no need to worry about guests finding the place.
It is a very nice place to live and a quiet neighborhood. The modern facilities are another quality. You will find a friendly and thoughtful staff team.
Love it here!! The apartment complex is beautiful and the property managers are so helpful! Im so grateful that I can be a member of this community
I've resided at The Graphic for 2 years and love it here!  The amenities and location are amazing.  Less than a five minute walk to Sullivan Sq and the apartments are beautiful.

Love the location, maintenance and management are very nice. But it seems that the things that brakes stays the same way until someone complains about it. For example the TV in the basement someone broke it, and have been like that for a couple of months now, same with the packages room, things happens and there have been 0 communication about it or when it will be fixed. Also since there’s no concierge is there’s something that will be done, either install Butterfly MX in the second door. The place have a lot of potential

Very nice place! My one gripe is that the fire alarm has gone off a disproportionately amount of times. Other than that the building is well managed, problems are quickly fixed and the amenities are very nice.
Staff and facilities are tops and they always make you feel like you matter like a family atmosphere love it here other tenants who I have met are also very pleasant to meet
Would recommend renting elsewhere. Convenient location, but not worth the hassle of a faulty apartment at brand new luxury prices.

I lived there for one year and this is the worst apartment I have ever lived. There is no security or service before 11am and after 5pm. No one fixed leaking water and broken AC. All they want is money. When you move out they will charge you a lot of cleaning fee even the room is clean. No one answered the email. This is garbage.

The whole building's AC were broken for a week in the summer, but the apartment office did nothing about it except saying they are trying to solve the problem. Can you imagine living in a 96F apartment for a week while paying an 3500$ rent? It feels suck. Take big consideration if you want to live here because your experience here won't match the rent you pay.
30 Dalton is a great residence. Nate is a pleasure :)
The building is pretty quiet and calm, great location in a safe neighborhood, maintenance and concierge services are very efficient.

Best apartment building! I moved here from Houston and have been so pleased with my apartment and the service at the driscoll! Everyone is so friendly and attentive and the building is so well maintained! Highly recommend moving into 30 dalton for anyone looking for a great apartment in boston!

I have lived in 30 dalton for a few months now and everything has been perfect. From move in to getting fully settled, the staff has been extremely helpful and friendly. Amenities are great and it’s the perfect location to get to anywhere in Boston easily

I love 30 dalton! I’ve been living here for about a year and a half and I have never had a negative experience. Everyone who works there is so kind, always smiling and offering help. The amenities are amazing, especially the gym with the amazing view of Boylston and the Charles. Maintenance requests are always responded to quickly and effectively, and communal spaces are always clean. The leasing staff is also so sweet and thankful for their residents. I would 110% recommend 30 Dalton to anyone looking for a place to live in Boston.

It is a good place to live with, as it is close to the downtown of Boston. Different kinds of restaurants are available nearby. The concierge service is quick and helpful. Thanks for the efforts of the 30 Dalton tams.

We loved living at 30 Dalton for a year. It has a very high-end feel and they pay a lot of attention to the small details. The gym is great and the top-floor lounge has an amazing view. Cold brew on tap and concierge 24/7. It is slightly pricey but actually not much more than comparable options in the area. So, overall highly recommended!

I toured 30 Dalton about a month ago.  The application and move in experience was very smooth and I love all of the finishes in my apartment.  Great location right across from the Four Seasons and Pru and a wonderful place to live if you want easy, luxurious city living.

My husband, infant son and I loved our time at 30 Dalton. The entire staff and management team were very professional, kind, and responsive to any requests we had regarding maintenance, dog walking, dry cleaning - you name it. 
The units are well designed with beautiful views as well as great lighting. The building holds some fun resident events from time to to time and works hard to foster a sense of community. It’s also so nice to be walking distance to multiple grocery stores and good local restaurants. We have many fond memories of our time in this building.
The building is clean, inviting, and feels safe. The staff are always nice and so helpful.

My two sons and I have thoroughly enjoyed living here– watching the beautiful sunset across the city and using the incredible gym facilities are just two aspects that make our experience at 30 Dalton very enjoyable. The location, which is so centralized and close to all of our favorite restaurants, is perfect. Everyone, especially the concierge, has been so welcoming and helpful!

We have thoroughly enjoyed living at 30 Dalton! From the friendly and helpful concierge team to the maintenance and management staff, we always feel welcome and at home. The location can't be beat and the views are spectacular!

I can  very recommend to live here in 30 Dalton Apartments.
The employees from the rental office as well as the conciere are very friendly and helpful.
I feel like I'm in really good hands here. 
The apartment and the residential complex is modern and in a great condition. Furthermore, it is quiet here.
Thank you to all who are working for 30 Dalton.
Very modern, safe, comfy place and worth the money

Everything this building offers from the beautiful apartments to the fantastic amenities and stunning views is amazing. I have had the pleasure of living here for almost a year and it has been a wonderful experience. The service is great and timely and the gym/lounge are perfect. I would highly recommend this to anyone looking to live in back bay. Bonus- the location is great as it is right next to the prudential center and dozens of nice restaurants.

If anyone has experienced the frustration of appliances or other items in a rental apartment that need repair only to wait for days to get a resolution, you will appreciate this review of the maintenance team at 30 Dalton.
Usually within an hour or two of submitting a (non emergency) request, one or two of the excellent team is at the door to provide whatever is required. Even when that takes creative solutions, lots of effort and time, they “get it done”.  While yes this residence can be more expensive than  others, there are some things that are priceless.

We love the location (in Back Bay and within walking distance from Downtown) and the shared spaces (Skyline Suite, library, lobby) in our building, and we especially enjoy our floor to ceiling windows and walk-in closet! The concierges are all super friendly and helpful, and they love saying hi to our cat. The main downside is the very high rent (even for Boston), but we know we are paying for the location and convenient services. There’s also a great bakery right downstairs (Flour)!

If you're considering this, or another Buzzuto, property, you may want to be fully aware that if you encounter any challenges on property, you may hear that "amenity spaces are of no cost to you in your rent". Therefore, management takes no accountability or responsibility.  In terms of their legal response to our central issue (noted below), they write the following: 
Pursuant to the “Community Policies and Procedures Addendum” within the lease, Tenants acknowledged and agreed that Management may add or change rules regarding amenities at the community at any time and at it’s sole discretion.  As such, ownership is fully within it’s rights to “modify” it’s policies".  - BE AWARE- your 20+ page lease presents no options on any of these protections they've afforded themselves, know what you're signing. 

After being excellent tenants for 3 years, forgiving significant challenges, from protests at Sheraton, massive construction related issues, frightening life safety concerns with the elevators, missing packages, and many others, there is a complete lack of accommodation in our desire to exit the community when they "change rules regarding amenities". 

If you're considering this property:
1. Valet parking- since Aug 2017 when we moved in, Valet has been plagued with issues. When we inquired about it in January of this year, the manager at that time encouraged us to hold off, citing continued challenges.

2. Elevators- Elevator issues were enormous at this property.  Many excuses were provided, but very little in the way of a preventative approach was adopted.   As recently as a month ago, I had to walk down 21 flights of stairs with our puppy as all elevators were out with no prior notice. 

3. The building touted itself as very dog friendly, even hosting "yappy" hours, etc.  When we moved in, we were told of plans for a dog park to come next door after the construction of One Dalton was complete.  That was even mentioned in our first two leases. But again, "amenity spaces are of no cost to you in your rent", so that's at their discretion to change.  Upon completion of One Dalton, this changed to a grassy area and tree; fine- it served the same purpose.  Then about 3 months ago, signs saying "No Dogs" were posted.  There has been no resolution on this, months later, as we've seen over, and over again...  

Our experience is that everything takes an intolerable amount of time to resolve. There is no urgency in service on the most important factors.

Building is largely filled with students. As parents are paying rent there is not much care amongst residents about the community. Building has had multiple issues with rooftop area since opening requiring alot of closures and follow up construction. Building has changed concierge services multiple times since opening. Front desk doesn’t know residents. Largely anonymous feel. Don’t even know if we currently have a manager after last one left.

I moved in 3 months ago, the people here are exceptionally kind. It’s also a beautiful community and they hand out cookies/breakfast sandwiches/ hold festivities throughout the year. 
It’s also in a  safe neighbourhood. 
All in all 10/10

I have been living at 212 Stuart for the past 1.5 years and it is the best building I’ve ever lived in! Cheikh at the front desk is incredibly helpful and accommodating and Courtney goes above and beyond to put together the best resident events. I couldn’t imagine living anywhere else!

My fiancé, french bulldog, and I just moved to Back Bay from Dallas. 212 Stuart has been so welcoming, accommodating, and efficient from the moment we signed our lease (shoutout to Courtney and Scott). 

That being said, we decided we wanted to move to Boston last spring. After lots of searching, we flew to Boston to tour our top three places that we wanted to live. We toured 212 Stuart, the Harlo, the Metlo. For many reasons (e.g. location, floor plan, smart technology, community, parking, views, etc.), we ended up choosing 212 and are very happy we did!:)

Beautiful architectural building that blends into the traditional and new spirit of Boston. The convenience to parks and downtown is unsurpassed. Safe and trendy community with quick access to dining and shopping.  Residents and staff very pleasant.  Rudy W

Friendly staff, always available for questions/concerns. Superb monthly events that we can bring our friends to as well. No noise in the apartment. Pet friendly. Clean. Apartment is in the best part of town, close to the public garden/Boston Commons, Chinatown, Newbury St, even seaport. Newer building. Can't ask for a better place.

We are extremely happy here at 212 Stuart. Courtney does a great job with community events and has always been helpful whether it’s through local recommendations, or answering any questions we could have about the building she’s been so helpful since we toured. The Concierge Team, especially Raul always go above and beyond expectations we sincerely appreciate it.

Moving into 212 Stuart has been the most positive move-in experience I have had. The leasing staff were beyond accommodating, helpful, and communicative. Overall, I am very pleased with this community so far.

Great location, close to Prudential Center, shopping area, the Public Garden, Chinatown. Building is new with lots of smart technology. Minimal to no noise can be heard from inside the apartment. Management team is always available, very nice and responds in a timely manner.

Beautiful, dog-friendly new building with great views and within walking distance to the Boston Common, Public Garden, Esplanade, Public Library, gyms, grocery stores, restaurants and lots of other locations. Leasing team is helpful and communicative, and maintenance team responds quickly to requests. Team coordinates fun activities like rooftop goat yoga. Enjoying my first month here so far.
Very positive and welcoming community. Would definitely recommend
Great Location, beautiful apartments, and top service! My favorite building in Boston
I’m the first resident living at 212 Stuart! The building is beautiful and the team is great.
Great experience from lease signing to move in. The fit and finish in both my apartment and common areas are excellent and the building is amenity laden. I truly enjoy living here.

In three years we experienced: 

Roaches, ants, constantly broken/non-draining washers and dryers, packages being stolen from the lobby, drain flies, random days of no hot water or water 100% turned off without being given warning, flooding through window frames due to poor construction, dishwasher wouldn't drain, door locks broken. Hamilton Company gets away with what it does because of how many apartments and units around Boston they own. Do not rent here or ANY Hamilton complex!

Whatever the kind of help you need from the staff members from this unit, trust me you’re not going to get it. They will not sort out anything for you and they will ignore you. I had problems with getting my keys the first day I moved in, and the building has package stealing problem, but they ignored it and lied to me that the security cameras don’t work when they do work.
The MM community is very friendly. The grounds are taking good care of.

I’ve lived in Mission Main for close to 20 years maybe more. During these times I have had some rough times as most people do. However I have had very few very few complaints with the Management of Mission Main/Winn Management Inc. They have been always curious and helpful to me.
Mission main is good place to live have excellent management.
I appreciate the time and the great effort managements takes to keep me inform and update of all information I need.

Do not rent particularly if you are a student. May daughter lived here for 3 months, had to call the police for domestic disturbances and over thanksgiving their apartment was broken into. When I went to visit I witnessed drug deals on the block. She moved out ibn December, its March I cant get anyone to call me back and we have still not received our security deposit back despite being told there was no problem. STAY AWAY

Mission Main is awesome- from the amenities to the staff to the location. Only issue is lots of college students and thin walls so it can be noisy at night. If you're a heavy sleeper- this place is a dream.
Elevators never work, your mail gets stolen out of the lobby, trash overflows, and management is clueless/slummy.  PLEASE do not waste your money on this place that lies on its listings.

This is the worst apartment I've ever lived in. The maintenance people never show up. The property manager never replies to your email. Many neighbors smoke weeds in the apartment, making your room also smelly. Finally, the company still hasn't returned my deposit after I checked out for more than a month.

I'm currently a resident at 225 Centre Street Apartments and I loved it during the tour. However, there are several drawbacks that I wish I would've really taken into consideration when conducting my research. The GOOD: Building is basically brand new; Heat and hot water included, saves us about $100/mo; Staff is friendly; Garage parking does feel safe, great for a not-so-safe neighborhood like Roxbury (i'll get to that later); garage parking is actually $175, not $125 as advertised here; Residents are ok, a mix between college kids, hipster professionals, thugs, and senior citizens; Across from Jackson Square T Station; Lots of police in this area (for good reason, last year someone was shot and killed on Centre Street and this building is literally across from the worst project community in JP); Il Panino's is my favorite restaurant in Jamaica Plain and 225 Centre is right across from it! The BAD: Overpriced; Contrary to what's advertised on Apartments.com and 225 Centre's website, 225 Centre Street is NOT in 02130, it's actually in 02119 which is actually in ROXBURY and NOT Jamaica Plain. They won't disclose this to you until you're signing the paperwork; Staff strictly runs on business hours on business days. Very little flexibility for any time convenient for the working professional; They don't sign for packages, they say they don't want to be liable for anything. Every other apartment community offers this as a free service. As a result, I've had a few packages stolen from the mailroom (where they leave your packages). The only upsetting incident happened before Christmas. Amazon reimbursed me all times; Many of the units are designated for affordable housing. My guess is that my packages being stolen are a result of this (no offense intended); Projects located right across from the building. I don't walk around at night here; Cheap floors and high ceilings cause for a lot of noise echo. Can hear college kids partying upstairs and neighbors next door arguing; Really cheap thermostats, impossible to use, tried googling the instruction manuals and just confused me more; Humidity: 0%. The air is very dry, guests that spend the night often complain about runny/bloody noses. I felt this way for the first month, but you get used to it; All payment is handled by physical check. First of every month, write a check and slip it under their door. It's 2015, who doesn't take electronic payments?! CLOSE: I could've paid less for better living. And I should have.

These apartments are beautiful and located right near a very convenient MBTA station-- literally, right on the corner of the T station. Transportation wise, great...also right on a bike path and near the highway. They proved very convenient for getting to my downtown Boston job. 

Convenience is why I moved there. But amenities are why I stay. The apartments are absolutely beautiful and well-maintained. The staff is extremely helpful. Indoor or outdoor parking spots to get your car off the street, a gym, and a bike room. 

Inside, the windows are huge and you have a great view of the Boston skyline. Modern-looking and with great appliances. 

For someone who is just entering the professional world, this place is perfect. To live here it requires a moderate income, which is why you get those nice amenities. But don't worry, if you are still an entry-level career person, the rent will not kill you. Because this complex is in Jackson Square and right next to the city's hugest housing project (Bromley Heath) the rent for a place like this is cheaper than anywhere else in the city. 

Although never unsafe, the location takes the price out of the rent and leaves you with a wonderful place to live! Once this area is fully gentrified though, the rent will probably skyrocket....we're getting there, so you might want to get in soon...there is a waiting list!

Although this is one of the better buildings in the area, that unfortunately isn't saying much.  Students all act as if this is the first time they've been out of mom's house, drunkenly screaming nonsense at all hours.  Nobody has any manners, and the area is flooded with idiotic Red Sox fans haplessly looking for either Fenway Park of their cars.

The landlord outsources the management of the unit to a company. They rarely answer phone calls, emails. When they do, they don't follow through on what they say they will do. Beautiful location, nice building. Just horrendous management.

Landmark Square (75 Peterborough St) was built in 2000 and is conveniently located in the heart of Fenway, steps from three different public transportation options and numerous restaurants, shopping (including Star Market and Target), bars, and nightlife. 

The building features central heating/ air conditioning, in-unit washer/dryers, and dishwashers in all units. Amenities include concierge service, exercise room, enclosed mail room, dry cleaning drop-off, and more. The management company, Abbey Residential, has always been responsive and professional in dealing with any of the very few issues that have arisen during our three years in the building.

Highly recommended! Landmark Square is a wonderful place to live - while being significantly cheaper than the big high-rise luxury complexes being built around it, despite little or no difference in value. If you're looking for luxury living at accessible prices in a stellar location, this is it!

My apartment is always warm in the summer, even long after the sun has gone down. The "advanced central air system" consists of 2 vents and a thermostat that looks like it's from the 70s. Furthermore, tenants get charged by the fan speed and duration used, plus a base fee which is incurred whether you use the system or not for that month. HVAC charges were not made clear prior to leasing.

We were misled by property management, and arrived to a dirty, dark, and disheveled apartment that could not have been further from the photos. Some nice neighbors, many rude and many STRANGE. Shocked that such a building exists in such a nice part of Boston. Looking forward to our lease expiring and getting out.
Best location, safe, Clean, in the middle of everything Boston, very unique units, friendly neighbors, great on site staff, and you can have a pet, but you wouldn’t know they accept pets :)
Only lived here for a few weeks and it’s clear that the property manager is in way over his head. He’s not good at his job and lies to residents to get them off his back.

I know 3 people now who left specifically because the management/property manager is so bad and constantly lies to us. I’ve lived here for 2 years and am not renewing my lease because I can’t handle another year of this manager. The residents have a group chat just to talk about how bad the manager is.
I lived here for the past 8 years since the building was built and loved the location. Management was nice to me the entire time.
Recently moved in and couldn’t be bang happier with my experience! Management has been super helpful and everyone has been super friendly. Exciting to settle in and explore what Fenway has to offer!

Building needs new management. I’m being put in a hotel for a month because someone else’s water pipes broke and I cant get any update from the property manager at all. I have to knock on my neighbors doors and hope they know anything.

The apartment is nice but we moved in and so many things inside the apartment needed maintenance. Management is terrible and ignores emails for weeks. It's not that bad but there's probably some better options out there.

Parker Hill Apartments are conveniently located near Longwood medical area and close to Northeastern University.  Apartments have big closets and there is free off-street parking. Biggest downside is the constant problem with cockroaches and mice without adequate response from management.

The view from my balcony at parker hill is by far the best part of this unit. It looks out over all of Boston and adds a ton of light to the living area!
