That’s right no running water. No water to cook. No water to clean. No water to drink. No water to use the toilet. No water to wash your hands. NO WATER. An INCONVENIENCE is an UNDERSTATEMENT! In addition to all of that, there has been absolutely NO running water in my kitchen sink for going on 3 weeks now. I’d go on but I don’t have enough characters left. This place is a joke. Save yourself the hassle and STEER CLEAR OF THIS AWFUL PLACE!!

I was taking a look at an apartment in the area this past weekend that was less than impressive.  We looked at the building next door and thought "this looks really nice, lets just pop in" and met with Ava who was so sweet and gave us a quick tour despite their schedule being booked up for the day. 

We started on the roof deck which was so stunning and as a work from home person, I could see myself up there on a nice day just to get out of the house to get some stuff done. 

Then we stopped by the gym, business area, and one of the two pools which all were so perfect.

Then we get to the main event, the apartment itself, which was so spacious, gorgeously laid out, brand new appliances, everything you could ask for in a unit.  

It's also so close to a bunch of restaurants, bars, shops, a nail salon. accessible parking and guest parking. 

It really feels too good to be true.  The price isn't unreasonable but may be out of my range for now. I'm hopeful i can make this work. I can't thank Ava enough!

They are very nice, friendly, and responsive only until you sign the lease, but they will start ignoring your emails or requests and won’t be willing to help after you move in because you already signed and would have to live with it anyways.

I have lived here for 3 years now - Management at Marq Uptown is the best. They are always on top of requests and keeping residents in the loop. They are also very friendly, warm, and welcoming - which makes this place all the better !!

I've been living here for a little over a year now. The change in management has really made a difference (happened sometime in Summer of 2017). You might find some bad reviews in the past, but the current management has really made me feel comfortable while living here. They're responsive to needs and constantly improving things. It kind of sucks that they had to clean up another's mess, but I highly recommend this apartment complex now. If you're curious, the population tends to be young professionals or graduate students. Not noisy, and this is important to me since I have odd schedules and work 60-80 hrs/wk as I'm in doing my medical residency -- sleep is important! It also happens to be right in between the HEB and the hospital :)

Do not live here. Overpriced, homeless camps on every side of the building, including 15 feet away from mine. They fine you for not removing your trash can overnight but allow homeless people to steal your electricity and make the entire area disgusting. Management is a joke. The lead manager is overdue to be fired. Live anywhere else.

The units are updated and well maintained. Maintenance staff are on the ball. Front office staff are friendly and professional. The amenities are nice.  The dog park is amazing. While slightly off the beaten path it's very easy to get downtown from this location.

This used to be Falcon ridge apartments but it was recently bought out. New management has been great. Work orders are completed in a timely manner and facilities are kept clean. All units are renovated. Only complaint is parking. Since there are not designated spaces that distinguish visitors from residents, i often have to park in front of a different building and hike over to my building. Visitors tend to get the good parking spots. However, if I get home before 6:00 then it usually isn't a problem.

This complex has a great green belt that it backs up to, a nice sized dog park with plenty of space for dogs to run around. The volleyball courts is a nice addition as well. You will be able to join some pick-up games on Monday afternoon's. The one tip that I will give you is, don't count on using the outside restrooms near the pool. You'll thank me later.

Apartment complex is very nice and well taken care of. Front office staff is always very friendly and answers my questions/concerns in a timely manner. Location is great for those looking to live in South Austin.

Where do I start….I’ve been at Bexley going on 3 years and when I first moved here I had very little issues but now, I don’t know if it’s the new team or what but read this and let me know what you think….
1.  I have been asking why and when our hallways would get pressure washed. It’s been MONTHS! And everytime I ask a leasing agent they tell me it should be done some time soon but it has not. Our hallways ARE DISGUSTING!
2. When I moved in I was getting my filter in my fridge changed but now, they refuse to change my filter unless I purchase one myself! I don’t see anything in our handbook that says that I am responsible for getting a air filter and why would I need to purchase a filter when this was the fridge that was here when I moved in????!
3. I have been in my place 3 years, at ANY other apartment I lived in before I was able to get my carpet cleaned after a year or two. Why do they not do carpet cleaning?
4. There are days when our trash (like last night) just isn’t picked up and sometimes for days. When I ask the leasing office they’re so clueless. We pay for valet trash that barely comes. I’m not understanding.
I see so many vacant apartments and ppl moving out and I know understand why. This is a terrible place to live and I’m so frustrated with not having what I feel like are simple requests met. If you looking for a place this is NOT it. I wish I could give it ZERO stars

Management is polite. Maintenance is responsive. However, Building 24 has a cockroach problem. Never had cockroaches before moving here. Have been dealing with them ever since moving here earlier this year no matter how spotless I keep my place. I can’t be the only one experiencing this. Both types have made multiple appearances in my home. I can’t be the only one experiencing this.

We lived here a little over a year, just recently moved out. We had 3 packages stolen off of our front step, issues with our neighbors blasting music at 3 am on any given night, homeless people coming out of the wooded area and asking for lighters or to bum a cigarette, and a down stairs neighbor who liked to come up and knock on our door because my toddler was playing and “stomping” too much for him.
After moving out we received our move out damage list a month after our move out date with a $75 dollar charge for our carpets having “high traffic and stretching”. Considering we are currently in a pandemic and we’re under NATIONAL stay at home orders which forced me and my boyfriend to have to stay and work from home this charge is completely appalling to me.

Do not rent here.
My apartment has had 5 major leaks. They cannot fix it and are refusing to let me out of my lease. I’ve slipped in my own apartment because of the leaks from heavy rain. Now here are spiders everywhere.

The pool is nasty and the lounge chairs are almost all missing their shade tops.

They never check the hallways for cleanliness. They left a mess in front of my door for over a week. Some kind of slime.

The cabinet doors fall off.

There is dog poo ALL OVER the grounds. I had to ask them to clean it up because of the dangers it poses.

The trails suck. So does the disc golf course.

The gym dumbbells are not secured on the rack properly. One fell on my guests foot while visiting. They did nothing.

They don’t maintain the dog parks.

When they “repaired” the water damaged interior of my apartment they didn’t even match paint.

The location is also horrible.

The trash valet is horrible and they don’t tell you upon lease signing about the unavoidable extra cost.

They are slow at responding to very important issues in a timely manner.

Just be sure you really want to live there. You can't change move in dates for their pricing, and if you choose not to move in, they will NOT give you your money back with 45 days out to moving in. Apparently, when they put your information in the system, even if you don't sign a lease, their FINE print gives them the right to keep it all. If you are on a budget and can't afford to loose $250, be sure! Almost have to wonder why they are giving away the apartments in the first place with so many vacant. Just be careful and sure.

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review: Have to agree with many of the other posters.  The Management here does not care and lacks any form of customer service.  It has progressively gone downhill.  We recently decided to renew our lease with a "Free Month Rent For December" special.  Our fully executed lease was lost and archive by Management.  This somehow triggered our rental portals to be wiped of all information like previous leases and auto pay.  As a result we were sent a Notice to Vacate on December 4 due to non payment of December rent (the rent we were not to be charge pursuant to our renewed lease).  When we alerted Management to the error they acknowledged it but instead of an apology they refused to waive a 10% late fee or the December rent fee at all.  We ended up paying for December and the late fee so our credit would not be wrongfully damaged and cause even more of a headache.  We're still waiting for a refund of these fees.  If you want to feel like a valued customer and don't want to spend hours and hours calling and emailing over any issue you might want to consider the many other apartments in the Domain that are better managed.  Update - We now have duplicate pest fee charge for January

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review:
- Nearby Whole foods (walkable) groceries.
- Lots of coffee, restaurants and shopping areas.
- North side Domains is better than south side.
- Has an awesome pool to swim, billards to shoot, and gym to work out.

Main downside is the weekends can be loud but that's more of the vibe for this area in general.

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review: Everything is broken by default. All appliances are of lowest quality. Hallways and elevators smells the disgusting mix of marijuana and urine. 24/7 noise of  race cars on the streets which you have miserably tolerate due to paper thin walls. Stay away from Domain and at least from Standard Apartments.

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review:
Stay away from The Standard or any properties managed by bh. I was a resident for 3 years and upon move out I was charged over $1K and lost my entire deposit. The biggest issue I had was being charged for missing blinds which were taken out by one of the maintenance workers and being charged to replace the carpet which apparently had "total deterioration" according to Omar one of the managers. First we feel we were unjustly charged for the blinds as their worker took them out after completing a service job! Second, the carpet damage which they claimed was "total deterioration" was a result of furniture staying in place for 2 years (desk and bed). What were we supposed to do to prevent that? To further illustrate the inconsistency and unjust charges to the carpet: when we lived in another unit at the Standard prior to the one we just moved out of, we were not charged for any carpet damage despite the furniture being the exact same! Why were charged now living in a different unit? Upon bringing up this issue with management they claimed that they "do not negotiate move out charges".

Stay away. Horrible move out experience. Be prepared for a hefty bill upon move out.

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review:
It has progressively gotten worse over the last 2 years. The management team doesn't care about anything, and is non-responsive. I sent my notice to vacate 2 times still haven't heard back... We got a new management  company, BH. From the little I have dealt with them, they are a joke. Their "renewal specialist" doesn't know anything about the property and sent me a lease with addendums that are not for the property. She CC the management team and the management team said I was correct. Then she responded to me and told me they didn't have the correct information.  I actually was going to renew, but the lack of professionalism and management was a sign not to resign there.

The best thing about the apartments is the location. It is one of the best locations in the domain. The crime has increased in the 2.5 years I have lived here as well. When I moved in I felt safe and never worried about things. I have seen numerous cars broken into (all at the same time, multiple times), gates and doors do not stay locked and working. My bike was stolen from inside the apartment building and was locked up. I did a police report and called security, they do not care. The security officer was too busy for me as she was trying to find a burning smell in the building. Save your self the hassle and live at a property that management is involved with their residents.

apartmentName: The Standard at Domain Northside Apartments
review:
Honestly, save yourself the trouble & money and move elsewhere. I've been here for a little over a year, and here's why you shouldn't live here.

Property management is a joke. Poor Communication, Poor Customer Service, and bad employees that hate their jobs, and it shows. Don't get me wrong, there are a few good employees there, but the bad ones love to drag everyone else down.

Good luck contacting anyone at the corporate office or management. Live BH care more about you finding their 3rd party property management service than you getting help.

Constant trash everywhere.
Dogs peeing in the elevator is common.
Elevators breaking down is expected.
Security Gates sometimes are just wide open for anyone to come through.
Trash chutes are constantly broken and left open.
Garbage trucks will ruin your morning at least once or twice a week.
Did I mention there's trash everywhere? Employees will see it and walk away.

You should do the same and walk away. It's not worth the stress or money.

Current tenant and I can’t wait to leave. Have been here almost three years. The building has gone downhill drastically in the past year or so. Lots of weed smell in common areas. The pool randomly locked on the weekends. Faulty treadmills in the fitness room that shut off mid-run. Management disappears on weekends and is routinely negligent, and when they do address a problem they drag their feet or assure you everything is working fine. Nothing gets fixed. My air conditioning went out last weekend (100 degrees, early July) and it took them five days to come up, only to poke around for a few minutes and tell me everything was fine because it had temporarily self-corrected. Of course it went out again hours later. But guess what? It’s the weekend again. Gotta sweat it out because they couldn’t be bothered to look deeper. And no, I don’t expect a credit of any sort. “Luxury” apartments, amirite? Not to mention, living on 35 is a nightmare and has gotten exponentially worse with the expansion project. There is one way in and one way out of this complex and it’s the frontage road. That’s not the building’s fault though. 

I don’t anticipate Farmhouse will correct course because I don’t think they care. This is Austin and there will be renters regardless. It’s just disappointing because I used to brag about how nice this place was and now it’s just a facade that you will pay a premium for. Rent at your own risk.

Moved into Farmhouse at the end of October and could not be happier with my decision. The community and staff help affirm my decision every day. Whenever I go on a walk around the property, I get the chance to meet a new dog and owner. The Community Manager, Kallyn, and Assistant Manager, Austin, have been great to work with as well. If I have any question or concern, they ensure it is answered in a timely manner and follow up. Glad they oversee the property.  

Every time I have friends visit, they comment on the amenities and the apartment. Watching the sunrise from the rooftop is a must when you are at Farmhouse, the space allows for you to feel comfortable and relaxed as you start the day. The apartments themselves are wonderful. Could not be happier with the layout of my apartment. It is open and spacious. 

Overall, my experience here has been great. It was an easy decision to rate Farmhouse a 5 out of 5.

It is with great disappointment that I write this review to make potential renters aware of the incredibly callous leadership that exists within Farmhouse Apartments and properties associated with The Tipton Group. 

In mid-March, my apartment was severely impacted by the historic Winter Storms that rocked much of Texas. While true that the unpredictable nature of weather can make recovery difficult, it's now clear to me that Tipton does not have the leadership within its ranks to quickly and meaningfully make the lives of its tenants better. 

It took property management 25 days to restore hot water to my unit. To date, this property still does not have an active fire sprinkler system. I explained my concerns for the delays in response, failure for leadership to communicate, and the many days in which the property was uninhabitable. Despite that experience, leadership was accusatory in nature and claimed no actual issues occurred. My insurance adjustor advised me to not replace any furniture that was damaged in the unit until fire sprinklers are tested because of concern that they'd go off again. This point was shrugged off by regional leadership.

This storm had a devastating impact to many individuals. That said, the constant failures to communicate with residents, lack of empathy for what our experience has been over the course of this month, and the fact that there is still repair work needed to bring this property to full compliance, have led me to share my story within in hopes that you will reconsider living Farmhouse, or any Tipton Group property.

When a resident is accused of making up property damages, and is denied any reparations, it is a demonstrable reflection of the character of leadership within this organization. I urge you to steer clear of any properties managed by this entity.

I've been a resident of Sentral East Austin apartments at 1630 East 6th Street for over a year, and I couldn't be happier with my experience. 

From the moment I stepped into the building, I was impressed by the modern design and the vibrant atmosphere. The location is absolutely perfect, placing me right in the heart of Austin's lively East 6th scene, with easy access to amazing restaurants, shops, and entertainment.

The apartments themselves are stunning, with high-quality finishes and thoughtful layouts. The amenities are fantastic, and the building is well-maintained. It's immediately clear that Sentral prioritizes resident comfort and satisfaction.

However, what truly made my move-in seamless and enjoyable was the exceptional assistance I received from property manager Alexa, who went above and beyond to ensure I had everything I needed, answering all my questions promptly and thoroughly. Her professionalism, warmth, and genuine care were truly remarkable. She made the entire process stress-free, and I felt welcomed and valued as a resident from day one.

Alexa's attention to detail and proactive communication were outstanding. Any concerns or requests I had were addressed immediately, and she consistently demonstrated a commitment to providing top-notch service. Her friendly demeanor and willingness to help made a significant difference in my transition to Sentral.

If you're looking for a stylish, well-managed apartment in an unbeatable location in Austin, I wholeheartedly recommend Sentral Apartments on East 6th. And if you have the pleasure of working with Alexa, you can rest assured that you'll be in excellent hands, as they have truly exceeded my expectations, and I'm thrilled to call this place home!

Been living here for a few years now and highly recommend. Great location and walking distance from anything you’re looking for. Maintenance is helpful and quick to respond and same goes from the front office assistance, shout-out Alexa for all the help!

This has been my first experience moving, and every step of the way Alexa from the leasing office has gone above and beyond to make sure everything was clear and laid out for me. Additionally she has had incredible patience with me as I try to figure out every new thing I need to contend with or figure out and get back to her with. From the renter's insurance to the internet service, she has had a recommendation for everything I could possibly need. I haven't been here long yet but I look forward to my whole time here and first renting year!

I originally booked a short term stay and ended up leasing a long term apartment with MaryHelen! The staff are so helpful and friendly and there are lots of stores and restaurants to walk to! Highly recommend for short and long term.

i’ve been in austin for about 5 months, and i’ve been staying here for about 2 months . this is the first place i’ve truly felt comfortable. the girls downstairs have been more than helpful throughout this experience.

Moved to Austin from Florida, never having visited before, and spent the whole first week here trying to find where my pup and I would call home. What separated this apartment complex from all the others we toured? Karyn and company. Seriously, Karyn and the others who work here are so easy going and personable, that for someone like me (who isn’t usually an apartment guy) I found it very easy to settle in here. Definitely give them a call or request a tour at the very least.

I have lived in Estancia Villas for several years across two buildings in the property. While I once enjoyed living here, the decline in resident experience since UDR (and Property Manager Jennifer) took over has become impossible to ignore.

UDR's focus on maximizing profit is evident in their actions.  Rent prices have increased significantly, yet these increases are not reflected in any meaningful improvements for residents. Instead, funds are invested in superficial cosmetic changes and "smart" upgrades that are often unnecessary, malfunctioning, and inconvenient. Amenities once exclusive to residents are now open to the public for a fee, further diminishing the value proposition for those living here.

Perhaps most concerning is the pattern of poor communication and last-minute demands from management. On three separate occasions in the past year alone, residents have received less than 24-hour notice for disruptive actions like clearing patios, vacating units for extended periods, and allowing entry into apartments.  These actions demonstrate a profound lack of consideration for residents' schedules and well-being.  Furthermore, attempts to address these issues with UDR's "We Care" team and customer service have been met with silence, highlighting a disregard for resident feedback.

Estancia Villas under UDR management is a stark example of how prioritizing profit over resident experience can lead to a significant decline in living standards.  Prospective residents should be aware of these issues before making a decision to live here.

All of the ratings for this place are from the old management. They were great, with the normal hiccups down the road. The new management blames you for you asking for an appt to come fix things when you have a newborn, the send contractors into your home without notifying you, and said contractors steal not only your tv, but almost $1400 in wine and a $500 KitchenAid mixer you’ve had for 10 years! Do not rent here! Stay away!
Grounds are well kept. Office personnel has been helpful as well as maintenance team.
I've live in this community since the construction began and I must say that I love where I live.
This is a great apartment and it is in a decent location.
I've only been here a couple of weeks, but the people are nice, and it's a good neighborhood so far.

Ever since moving into The Clark, I don't have enough good things to say! The staff is super friendly and responsive. Maintenance is super quick to resolve any maintenance requests you may have. They have also taken extra precautions during covid and making sure everything is super clean, which is truly appreciated. I truly feel like this is a community that cares for their residents. Also special shoutout to Ben and Alexia for going above and beyond to help answer all of my questions. Also Kay the new Leasing Consultant is super cool, she has helped me with a few minor package concerns. Trust me if you want a community that actually cares for you, move to The Clark.

I've lived downtown in various properties for the past 7 years, and by far The Clark's management team is the nicest, attentive, and professional that I've come across.

Bethany, Elise, and the team do an excellent job maintaining the property and planning incredibly creative and valuable events for the residents.

The property itself is also beautifully designed, furnished, and well kept.

My fiancé and I have loved our experience here since even before its grand opening. Great place to live!

It’s not worth the money. The last review was spot on. There is zero insulation between floors so you can hear EVERYTHING. I lived in a few different units and it was totally unmanageable. If you don’t have great hearing, it’s a wonderful place. The views can’t be beat.

Some residents were noisy inside and outside the apartment. When there were high winds that blew past the building, it made it very scary and even blew things off the balcony. Some balconies are not private and are right next to your bedroom window so if you want to open your blinds, your neighbor is able to look directly in your bedroom. Or if your neighbor blasts loud music on their balcony at night, it can be heard from bedroom and living room. Left because the rent price doesn't match the quality. The views are nice, but this isn't the only place in the area that offers a view.

Las personas que prestan asistencia, son muy profesional en el manejo del negocio.

Siempre dispuestas a colaborar y a ayudarme.

Son Carismáticos y con un personalidad dispuesta a resolver cualquier situación que se presente.

Estoy muy agradecido por su atención y su colaboración.
The staff were great in providing an exceptional move-in experience. The apartments are clean with great finishes. Very happy.

I would avoid at all costs. We had issues regarding noise throughout the night and it took months for it to be resolved. We had a storm and water started to leak through the window in the bedroom and through one of the smoke alarms which cause all the smoke alarms to go off. We have had issues with pest in the kitchen as well as in the bathrooms. There has been a smoke smell in one of the bathrooms that permeates throughout the apartment. It has been over a month since we reported the smoke smell and management has yet to resolve the issue. We are unable to use the bathroom due to the smell. The manager does not seem to care at all about our experience here.

Run Run! This place is the worst place to ever think of living. The present management is incompetent and clueless. Poor maintenance, everywhere is so dirty. Trash stays for days before being removed causing air pollution within the apartment complex. They keep changing management. Live elsewhere

Pricing is WAAAAYYYY overpriced for poorly made apartments. These are not luxury apartments they’re alright but definitely not luxury. Construction is terrible and you can see all the imperfections on the cabinets, bath tubs, countertops literally everywhere all throughout the apartments. Amenities suck they make it extremely difficult to use anything and their go to line “it’s policy” “it’s policy”. Don’t rent here not worth the money.

The apartment's in person prices are 300$+ dollars from the amount shown on here. and they don't update it on here to keep luring people there thinking its a greatly priced apartment and be surprised by a whole different price when u get at the property.

In the year that I lived here my car was broken into twice in a span of two months. Broken windows and everything swiped from the car. I spoke with multiple residents who also had car break ins - they happen here EXTREMELY often. The gates and pedestrian doors are constantly broken, stopping no one from entering the parking lot. I informed management after every break in I had, and they didn't lift a finger. They essentially said the management company is too big to care/ do anything proactive about it. They gave me some long speech about why it takes them so long to repair the gates and doors - not the resident's problem. Their excuse for why they hadn't sent a community notice alerting other residents about the break ins, was because people complain about them sending too many emails, yet I never saw one email regarding the break ins. Due to all the car windows being smashed, the parking lot is covered in glass making dangerous for kids and dogs. The safety of their residents should be a top concern. I would never recommend this place to anyone.

Bexley Soco offers a beautiful pool and spacious floor plans. The maintenance staff is excellent, prompt, and friendly. Unfortunately, the management office can be unhelpful and provides the bare minimum of customer service for tenants who pay a premium to stay at this property. "Controlled building access" is labeled as an amenity, however for the majority of our time renting here, the gates did not work. This also included the vehicle entry gate, which was stuck in the open position for several weeks. During this time, an attempt to steal my vehicle occurred at 4am (a time when a working gate could have helped). Many others have experienced theft here as well. Pedestrian access gates often do not work as well, creating an unsafe situation given the surrounding area (per Austin Police) during my police report following a vandalism incident. Lastly, management was not helpful during my move out charges and incorrectly attempted to bill me a few extra thousand $$, resulting in a personal audit of the many charges you will experience here. Lastly, one of our bedrooms shared a wall with an exterior pedestrian gate, making this room completely unusable due to the loud slamming of this metal gate at all hours of the night. Bottom line, you expect more when paying the premium charged here.

I have lived in this complex for some months now. When I initially toured my unit I fell in love with it and couldn't believe I had found such a great place. Unfortunately, there is a big noise issue. If you are not on the top floor you will hear every single step the person above you takes; the vents in your ceiling will rattle loud enough to wake you up from a deep sleep and keep you awake for certain. I have not had a full night of rest in months and have contacted the office multiple times only to be told, in short, to get over it. The constant banging is such a bad problem that it scares my pet, who has now made a room for themselves in the closet as it seems to be the quietest part of the apartment. Aside from the constant noise, the parking situation here is not great either. Most of the parking spots are far too small. I drive a very small vehicle and was still hit by another car that was backing out of their spot, and if you drive a larger vehicle you better hope to find one of the few larger parking spots or you will need to squeeze yourself into a compact spot and hope for the best. The apartments do offer a solution to this problem, as you can get a reserved spot in the garage... for an extra $100 a month, this is on top of your already high rent; and if you are worried about your vehicle being broken into, don't, because the complex is gated... however, the gates seem to be broken every other week, thus being left permanently open until someone can come to repair it only for it to be broken again a week later. Aside from this, if you are willing to pay the extra $100/month fee for a reserved spot in the garage to avoid having your vehicle being hit or broken into, you will be thrilled to hear that the garage door is also constantly left open so that anyone who makes it onto the property from the broken main gate can now easily walk into the garage as well. With this being said, this apartment complex is a great choice for anyone who hates sleeping or any kind of peace and quiet in general, as well as anyone who loves to have their vehicle damaged or even broken into.

I've been a professional Realtor and Broker for over 18 years now, and I work with thousands of properties across Texas.  I can say unequivocally that Magellan Management who oversees the Sienna is one of the worst management groups you could ever encounter.

They are highly unethical, dishonest, and borderline fraudulent in their business dealings.  You can read some of the 1 star reviews for yourself from tenants that have lived there, and I've had other clients live there in the past who did not report any positive feedback to me as well.

It gives me zero pleasure to bash anyone.  But out of duty, I feel an obligation to warn people about this property, and would highly encourage you to seek alternative options before electing to live here.  You deserve better.

I wish I knew how many issues this building has before signing a lease here.

We haven’t had hot water for nearly 2 weeks and the water we do have has a bad taste and smell and feels unsafe to drink.

The views are amazing and it’s great being downtown but that doesn’t matter because the corner of 6th Street and Brazos is genuinely terrifying and unsafe. People are openly smoking narcotics and shooting up right in front of the building. My girlfriend has been screamed at and chased just walking to the coffee shop down the street. I’m a 6’1, 200 pound man and even I feel unsafe walking my dog day or night. There is no security…

The building has so much potential but with the issues and negligence plaguing the building, it’s insane that they’re charging that much for rent and not offering any concessions when I’ve had to literally ask a friend if I can shower at their place because my apartment doesn’t have hot water.

This place is expensive and low quality.  I have lived here for years and now looking to move. We have not had hot water for 7 days.  The hot water is ALWAYS compromised.  It is not the fault of the management team, it seems to be the building itself.

Although there are some positive aspects to living at the Sienna, such as the responsive and personable local management team, great onsite restaurants, convenient location, and nice amenities like a rooftop pool, resident's lounge, business center, and gym, my overall experience renting an apartment in this building has been negative.

I will preface that I had a one month trial period where I could’ve gotten out at the beginning of my lease, but I had invested too much time and money and was convinced the “worst” was behind me and the building would only get better. It did not.

I initially leased sight unseen based on the impressive renderings, amenities, and location. Unfortunately, the actual quality of the finishes, appliances, and overall build did not live up to the marketing materials. While pandemic supply chain issues and labor shortages may have contributed to this, the corporate team confirmed that the actual apartments would not match the renderings. However, as of March 2023, they’ve started renting the 15th floor as “luxury lofts” that do actually meet the initially marketed renderings, leaving the “OG” residents feeling a little miffed.

The build quality, finishes, and appliances feel more like a college dorm than a luxury apartment:
* The two-door refrigerators with the freezer on top are barely full-size and have no water filtration system
* Electric stoves only, with no gas range options
* Economy stackable washer & dryer combos
* Missing screws in door hinges since day one
* Plastic baseboards instead of wood
* Cheap, easily-dented vinyl wooden plank-like flooring
* Showers with cheap plastic floors and shower heads with no water pressure

Most floor plans do not have A/C vents in the bedrooms or bathrooms, only in the main living space. The elevators are constantly breaking down, forcing long waits for residents, and to add to the congestion, the building's cleaning staff, engineers, and maintenance teams also use the resident elevators. The noise level from the bars on 6th Street is unbearable, especially for apartments facing north like mine. The pool is too small for both hotel guests and residents, and it feels like the hotel's needs are prioritized over residents.

Overall, I regret renting here, and I feel that the building is overpriced for the quality of what you get. While there are some highlights, the negative aspects far outweigh them, and I would not recommend this building to anyone looking for a luxury apartment.

Never forget you’re sharing an apartment with a hotel - and their priority is the guests paying $500 a night. Mediocre at best in every way. Wax myrtles is a joke too - food sucks and service is nonexistent. Elevators are so slow you could take the stairs up and down 31 floors twice before they come.  Don’t know who the reality/design group was but I will find out and never live somewhere like that again.
The finishes are VERY CHEAP.  The showers only have HALF of the closure.  Many units have BIG columns in the middle of a room!!

First off, it took me over a month to get the paperwork done to be approved for the apartment. Anytime I sent paperwork it took over a week and several phone calls to get anything done. They initially had over-estimated my income by almost 10k. Now I understand that the complex is under construction, but if you are on the waiting list good luck on getting a call back regarding actually moving. I’ve left voicemails and emails that never get responded to. The voicemail they haven’t changed since last year, stating the complex would be opening in the fall. I decided today to stop by the office, no one there, no one answering the phone, but i did see someone leave the office as I was leaving the apartment complex. This seems like a good indicator that the problems once you live here will be even worse. Don’t waste your time here.
Just moved in, seamless experience so far. Things were made simple and clear, very excited to be here! The staff has been great and the amenities and apartment are clean and well taken care of
The team at 1155 are brilliant, accommodating and so kind. Our tour, application and approval process was effortless and enjoyable. We’re excited to call 1155 Barton Springs our new home!

A great place to live. Fantastic location. Friendly and helpful staff. 
We’ve only been here two weeks but we love it!

I wish I could give 1155 a good review because the residents and the location are amazing. Unfortunately, we have had so many problems living here and the management company, Greystar, doesn't care about the residents.

We were promised things from the beginning that we never got or just got after a whole year (concierge, dog run, 2nd BBQ) and to top it off, they cut our security at night, putting safety at risk (we've had several car break-ins and packages stolen). 

The pool seems like a nice thing to have but it constantly has algae.

We had major flooding in our apartment due to their negligence, had construction in our home (along with multiple other homes) for over 3 months, couldn't use our washer and dryer for over 8 weeks and nothing got done until we complained multiple times. 

This is not a luxury apartment complex and is ridiculously overpriced for what we get. All you are paying for is location.
Great location and neighborhood! Contemporary design. Luxury finishes and amenities. Incredible property staff. 1155 Barton Springs is a great community!

The leasing and resident staff at 1155 made it so easy to apply and get situated in the building when I moved in. I really enjoy the amenities and the incredible rooftop terrace that has incredible downtown views. The building feels like living in a hotel, it is well maintained and the residents are super friendly!

My experience living at Reveal has been nothing short of AMAZING. Beatrice helped me tremendously back in January as I transitioned from Florida to Texas. Angela the assistant property manager has been extremely helpful, understanding, and accommodating as well. Moving in was seamless, my apartment is gorgeous, and maintenance is incredibly prompt when fulfilling service requests (most times same day) I was more than happy and eager to renew my lease here and to call Reveal home.

I am a QA professional, and I call it like I see it, so when I write this review, you will know that I am not being “sponsored” or just throwing my two cents in for a bonus or perk.

My experience with Mansions of Onion Creek has been nothing but positive with S class service. The staff in the leasing office is friendly, knowledgeable, and caring. Any questions I have had they are always there to answer and help, no matter how "silly" the question may be. Upon moving in, I had a few problems with the apartment, one of the major components was the AC didn't work (it was about 90 degrees in the apartment) and the water smelled bad. However, despite these "major" issues, I did not get upset because it is natural for things to be a bit rusty when moving into an apartment. That is what inspection lists and work orders are for (and opening windows lol). But what really blew me away was the turnaround time and professionalism of the maintenance team. When I put in a work order to fix the A/C and water heater issue, it took the maintenance team less than 3 hours to come and fix my issue. I believe the Maintenance team is the true MVPs because it seems that they really try to fix any concern within a 24–48-hour window and my fixes only took a few hours. So, kudos to the maintenance team for being BAMF’s and to the leasing office for ensuring everything runs smoothly. 

As far as the complex goes, the complex is in a great location and is conveniently close to all the essentials. If you go 5-10 miles north or south of the complex, you are bound to get anything you need for your daily life. It is right on the edge of South Austin, so getting into the city is rather quick (even with the regular commute traffic), and the people in the complex seem to be friendly and just trying to live their lives the best they can (like the rest of us). 

Now, I will say, the only “problems” with the apartment (and I would not even say they are problems necessarily) is since the complex is relatively new, there is construction going on in the area, some typos on the resident portal, and potentially noisy neighbors. However, the fact that they are doing construction and fixing things around the complex (on top of doing it all in a timely manner) just goes to show the dedication and professionalism of the Mansions of Onion Creek team. As far as noisy neighbors go, that's just natural with apartment living and that's why you go talk to your neighbor and become friends.

I've only been here for a few months and all I can say is Jessica and Tori have gone above and beyond for me. They make sure you feel welcomed, they listen to any concerns or questions you might have. Coming from a community where the office staff was never available, it feels amazing to end up at a place where it truly feels like home!

Avoid buildings 11, 12, 13, 14, or 15 if you move here. To management: give this tenant a violation and fix this problem and I'll come back and delete this review.

I've lived in a community before where management made excuses for barking dogs, so if you like peace and quiet, take this warning seriously before you move here.

I see all the reviews on here and wonder how I did not have the same experience. Guess not everyone gets treated the same at this property.

Don't live here, it's a miserable place. The amenities aren't kept up, the crowd parties constantly, and the people running the place are really unpleasant to deal with. The price isn't worth the way you're treated.

The Marlowe is NOT a resident-friendly apartment complex. The office staff is absolutely rude at times and totally unresponsive. I live here now.Great area to stay ,quiet, neighbors are also good people.My only complaint is parking.and you might say “parking is and everywhere”….no….if you aren’t home by 6pm.you’re NOT getting a parking spot in front of, or close to your apartment.you’d have to walk.other than that..I’m overall satisfied with the apartment complex

Beautiful mid-rise community currently under construction. I cannot wait to see the finished product. Definitely considering for my next home. Keep up the great work Waterford team! You guys are amazing.

Great location, most of the staff is great, maintenance responds quickly, and a good gym. Yes this is a family complex, so if you're ok with children and dogs, this is a good place to live.

i lived at the Lodge at Lake Line for 10 yrs. I would move back in and may do so when my lease ends. It is on my list o top three complexes that I am considering. Not for the gift card. it is the truth really!

After complaining multiple times, when I told them that I am going to call someone from outside to look at it, they send another technician to check who confirmed and replaced it. Ants, spiders and bugs infestation is the worst in these apartments. A few more families established that. I have had 38 requests so far for fixes in the apartment, and I have lived 1.5 years. Overall very nice. We have some issues with residents allowing their dogs off leash with no reminders/reprimands for not following this rule and leash law and not picking up after their pets waste. We understand that this can be somewhat hard to enforce though and are overall very happy here

You may not want to use this for marketing. I have lived here for 8 years and have been very pleased with Silverado. I have had one major complaint for quite a while which has not been resolved which I believe would not be great for marketing--the community garbage/recycling area. It is not only unsightly but I believe a health hazard--it is difficult to find a time when garbage is out everywhere in the area. This issue should really be addressed because otherwise this is a great community.

An overall good living experience, had some minor issues with downstairs neighbors when I first moved in, and if you want to talk to management, you have to go in person because they rarely answer the phone and never return calls or emails.
The reasons I came back to Silverado was because of: 1) Location to major roads and Brushy Creek Park. 2) Floor plan and pricing. 3) The staff is awesome.

I've been in this complex now for 4 months I currently have mixed feelings about this facility. The office staff that I have had experience with have been stellar. I appreciate their friendly nature and for working to take care of the property and the residents. The pool, gym and other amenities are very, very nice and definitely draw you in to the complex. Also the addition of smart home hardware does take it up a notch. 

However the unit I rented is a bit worse for wear and when compared to other units at other properties really could use updating to accommodate the investment. We weren't able to see the unit before it rented but we saw a similar one by self guided tour. The unit we saw and the unit we rented were so far from each other that I dare say it wasn't even a nominal comparison. The bathroom and kitchen being the most disparate due to age and usage. The kitchen fridge is new but the stove top, dishwasher and countertops have seen significant wear and tear to include missing parts in the dishwasher (a utensil basket to name one) that I've replaced myself rather than go through the process of asking due to the delays and issues noted here. The bathroom is the worst of the two which should've marked this unit for a refresh before it was rented again but it most assuredly wasn't. 

When we moved in the A/C did not work and we ended up opening several work orders to get it online which during summer in Texas is saying something. 

Also I had to report a broken dishwasher and kitchen sink several times before they were finally fixed which resulted in having to take a video and show it to the manager as one work order was closed with notes stating "even if you can't hear it running the timer is working." It actually wasn't resulting in yet another return trip to fix the dishwasher again and add parts to the sink and reseal it as it was leaking terribly. 

Recently they had someone come replace the A/C system for the unit which included swapping out the components in the apartment as well. I'm guessing no one from the complex did Q/A for the job as when I came back home I found a number of self tapping sheet metal screws in the carpet that either myself, my kids, or my vacuum have found by running over them. 

Overall the experience is mediocre at best. The staff and the amenities are the main redeeming qualities for the complex while the apartments and the maintenance staff need some work. I hope they can get it figured out in general.

I recommend going else where. I was told during the summer “the reason why inside our apartment is 100 degrees is because it’s 100 degrees outside”. We had to submit multiple request for our air conditioning to be fixed just to be told nothing was wrong with it. After two week of asking over and over for the unit to be fixed finally they fix a part that was broken. Then it broke again a few weeks later. Mind you we had two dog that had to stay in the apartment all day dying from the heat and on the weekends we had to drive over 2 hrs on the weekends to stay with family to get a break from the heat. The biggest lie so far on the reviews is that the staff goes go above and beyond. that could not be father from the truth. If they cared about their residents we would not have had a broke air conditioning for two weeks in the dead of summer. When you move out they will charge you a lot of money. When we moved out the apartment looked better then when we moved in it. When we moved in the bathroom and kitchen was dirty. They did a horrible paint job around the fixtures. The air vent were dirty and looked like mold. When I put in a request for them to be changed maintenance came and just spray painted them.

I don't hate living here, but I feel you should know what you're getting into before you get your hopes up based on the advertised rent, because that's not what you will end up paying.

Add:
 20 per pet.
 40 for a reserved covered spot ( 20 for non-reserved AFAIK)
 5 for package locker access. They will refuse your packages if the shipper will not leave them at your door if you do not pay this.
 15 for REQUIRED basic cable. This used to be included in the rent, but as of this year it is not, even though ,y lease still says it is. All attempts to discuss this have been ignored or put off with "We have to talk to X". Because of this you will not be able to order/change your cable/internet online, and this doesn't count toward a bundle.
 3 for pest control. Pretend you don't see the anthills that the maintenance guys walk past every day.
 5 trash billing fee.

Including the last two fixed fees my water/trash bill is ~$50 for a 2 bedroom.

Your rest will be raised substantially every year unless you try and fight it. I've been successful the last two years of keeping it the same or a minimal ($10) increase.

The building is getting old but it generally isn't in terrible shape yet. Unless you lease one of the recently upgraded apartments with stainless steel appliances then your appliances are likely to be old. The weatherstripping around my front door is basically gone, and the windows are drafty.

There are gates for entry/exit but they are often broken. There was an issue a while back where a former tenant broke some car windows and stole things, but other than that it seems like a fairly safe place.

Lakeline Blvd is very busy during rush hour. There is a back exit to Old Mill Road that is the better way to get out in the morning if you need to turn left.

That said, it's not a terrible place to live. I recently renewed my lease because I was able to keep my base rent the same. It's more than what's advertised for the same floorplan for new folks, but that's partly my fault for not pushing back on the increase the first year. Moving is a pain, and I might end up somewhere worse, so instead I just live with it here.

This Complex is close to shopping and schools and that is the best I can say about it. The traffic around here is bad. I believe the rent for these apartments is too high for their age. The complex has done some landscape work but the sidewalks all lead to nowhere. The gate code has never been changed in the 7 years we have been here and we have seen many former tenants come and go as they please because of this. Many of the tenants that have lived for as long as we have are not going to renew their leases nor are we. The covered parking is free and there are garages but each building has very few. Our garage is across the parking. Maintenance is just ok, many of the people that I have seen do maintenance do not have proper training. You can rent a brand new apartment on the same street for the same amount of money.

I don't know where the other Renters live that gave them good reviews but the Office Staff is unprofessional and incompetent.  The Unit has several problems that have yet to be resolved. There are people washing cars in the parking lot, this is the Hood and not Luxury living, don't sign a lease here.

Overall, the staff is very pleasant, rent and their annual increase seems to be within reason if you take advantage of any early bird renewals.  The property is pet friendly, and have pet stations located on both sides of the property (toward the center - though I wish they would provide a few alone the obscure paths that go around the buildings). Overall, I am a happy, long-term resident of the community and have no major complaints.
great maintenance team that work together to make sure you are satisfied with completing the job
overall a good deal. staff is very pleasent to work with. good parking. close to my job. close to everything i need.

My wife and I have lived at Echo for over two years now and we can say that we have truly enjoyed the experience of this complex. From the timely and courteous staff to the beautiful apartment wood floors, this place is a gem. 

But that’s not to say that there haven’t been some pain points too. After living here (and working from home full time) for a while we have a full perspective of the building and want to share our experience for those thinking of living here.

The bad:
When we first moved in it was super quiet (outside of the Lamar Blvd street noise, which yes, is noticeable from your apartment- shocker) and there were some vacancies which helped make it feel not so busy. But over the years, due to their large success, Echo has reached full capacity. This comes at a doubled edged sword as more people equals more noise in general- noisy neighbors, dogs barking, people in the hallways, loud music/noise from TVs and speakers, etc. It is also now much harder to find a parking spot on a desirable level if you get home late. And lastly the elevators are slow, some of the slowest I’ve ever dealt with, but operable. Just have to exercise some patience with the amount of people that use them. 

The good:
The apartments are beautiful with real wood floors and (if you face outwards) provide amazing views of Austin. We have never had a structural or “bad” problem with the apartment itself. And the staff at Echo goes above and beyond in their communication efforts and maintenance of the building. After the crazy winter weather in early 2021 there was some water damage to the building, but they moved extremely quickly to get vendors in here to start the renovations and repairs. Samah and Jim, in particular, make living here worth it. 

If you are looking for a central Austin luxury apartment, this complex should be at the top of your list.
