To top everything off, when I moved out I not only didn't get my deposit back despite leaving the place in much better condition than I found it (and documenting everything with their move in sheet originally), they charged me cleaning fees. These people wouldn't know what cleanliness was if it bit them in the you know what. While this apartment wasn't technically the worst I've dealt with, the management was for sure.

If they won't show you the unit you'd be renting you don't know for sure what you're signing on for. After a whole year of hell here I'm glad I'm out and never have to deal with them again.
Great apartment complex, could use some better amenity repairs. The staff and management are friendly. About a 20 min walk to main campus but quite enough from West campus parties
Some quirks here and there but maintenance is pretty good and I really enjoy all the little events that we have. Have had a pretty good experience here so far :)

The staff here are terrific, not to mention the property; I really enjoy having access to two properties with this lease; the resort-style pool at the Villas is beautiful but I love the spaciousness of the Venue Gym! As well, the events held at the properties are always fun and endearing, even if I can't attend all of them; the staff and managers here really work to create a sort-of community that you're welcome to participate in if you wish! Finally, if any maintenance or any other kind of issues arise, the staff here are on top of it as soon as it's reported! I think every maintenance request we've made (not that there have been many) is resolved within a few days of it being placed.  Great work y'all, keep it up!

Amazing experience with quick and reliable service! Located just a few blocks away from the university, this apartment complex is an excellent choice for students and young professionals who are looking for convenience and comfort. The complex also offers several amenities that make it a great place to live, including a fitness center, a swimming pool, and a communal lounge area. One of the best things about this apartment complex is its location. It's just a short walk or bike ride away from the university, making it easy to get to classes, libraries, and other campus facilities. Additionally, the neighborhood around the complex has plenty of restaurants, cafes, and shops, making it a vibrant and convenient place to live.

Overall, this apartment complex is an excellent option for anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient living space close to the university.

My very first apartment! Nice floors, big rooms, and really nice bathroom. There's a huge tub, marble counters and lots of counter space too. The kitchen has updated appliances and whenever something has broken the repairmen are out and have it fixed by the next day!! Right next to spiderhouse and a short walk to UT Campus. It's overpriced, but it is west campus area.

I have lived here for a full year, and it has not been spectacular but it certainly is a lot better than other places in West Campus. 

The people are usually nice, but because they hire tenants, people are in and out a lot and very few know what is going on. It takes awhile to learn who knows the ins and outs of the office and who opens an hour late.

The location is pretty great and also pretty iffy. Torchy's is right next door, Kerbey Lane and (my favorite) Fat Sal's down the Drag as well as Wheatsville, Milto's, and of course UT. For Communications students it's REALLY convenient. 7 minute walk to Belo, CMA, and CMB. The Chevron next door has a lot of necessities if you are running low on anything and the people that work there are all sweethearts. Unfortunately, the location is right on Guadalupe which means loud people on the street, car accidents, and greek house parties.

The apartments are really nice. Granite counter tops, giant closets and bathrooms, garden tubs, hard wood floors... The problems usually come up when the apartment complex doesn't want to spend money. The fridge is WAY too small even for two people, there are no fans in the bedrooms even though there is a switch for it, the dryer is workable but only after lots of practice and three runs, and the A/C freezes one room while barely cooling the rest of the apartments. In my room, it is perpetually 85.

Security is hit or miss. There are supposed to be locks on the doors to the complex, locks on the elevators, and a gate at the parking garage. However, they locked the doors with no warning before giving out the proper fobs and many of us got locked out after hours. Since then it has remained unlocked. Packages are supposed to go to the front office and checked out there, but often they are delivered to the door and I have had a couple stolen.

Yes, there is parking. You get an assigned space now which is nice. There are two separate towers with only about 6 rooms on each floor so it's usually pretty quiet. There is a trash shoot which is nice because it never smells like garbage. There is one particular maintenance guy who is super sweet and goes above and beyond. He has even bonded with my cat. They have an exercise room which isn't spectacular and the a/c is usually obnoxiously loud, but it works for casual exercisers like myself. Also a pool, which isn't very big but pretty nice. Overall, not great but a good first apartment, if you can afford living in West Campus.

As I write this we are 15 days into interrupted water service going on 48 hours straight without water. The building hired incompetent plumbers who have not been able to address the issue. The leak has proved to be so bad that the City of Austin turned off water to the building until the leak is completely fixed. All this while it has been 100*+ outside. Unbelievable mismanagement.

My wife and I moved into The Dexter when we relocated to Austin and our 6 month stay was extremely disappointing. 

The first thing that you notice is that the facility is significantly shabbier than you see in pictures. Retaining walls are crumbling, landscaping and walkways are poorly maintained, and there is a constant presence of pet waste. Trash services are also poorly handled as the dumpsters are in high visibility areas and constantly overflowing. 

Upon moving in, we weren’t able to unpack our belongings for over a week because of a significant cockroach infestation. This required multiple treatments to get under control and we had to go into our own pocket to buy additional spray and traps in order to get the situation under control. 

The gym and pool area are both poorly maintained and were frequently closed. The gym has very limited hours and they closed the pool for the season quite early while there was still persistent heat in Texas. 

Our unit has multiple shabby patching jobs where it looks like a previous tenant punched a hole in the wall. These were repaired with little concern for aesthetics. 

Outages in hot water and electricity are regular occurrences. During the latest winter freeze, The Dexter seemed significantly unprepared to provide any sort of support or assistance to residents. I personally cleared several tree branches with the assistance of other residents simply so we could get our cars out of the parking lot. 

Recently the face panel of our central heating system simply fell off the wall, nearly striking my wife who was sitting nearby. Upon inspection, it’s not clear to me that the panel was ever securely fastened to the wall to begin with.  

 Even when pulling up to The Dexter, you’ll notice that the “T” has fallen out of the monument sign that faces William Cannon Drive. This has been the case for months, and it reflects the low quality of care that management provides for the facility. 

Even in attempting to close out our lease, management has been consistently non-responsive to emails.

If you are looking for an apartment in Austin, I’m sure you can do better than The Dexter at the same price point.

They deleted my original review! Do not move here! You’ll get ur car towed, you’ll have roaches everywhere, you’ll be ghosted by management, repairs will never get done, it’s unsafe, there’s homeless everywhere and shootings and i can keep going. do yourself a favor and don’t make my mistake.

The trashiest apartments I’ve ever experienced. I visit my friend frequently who’s locked into a lease at this place. Trash, dirty needles, nails, cockroaches (probably from the trash) all over the parking lot. Management non-existent. Pool is disgusting. Maintenance leaves evicted tenants garbage all over the place for weeks. Don’t do it. Online pics of complex are heavily edited. Just drive by and you’ll understand.

This place has gone under new management (again) and although it all looks pretty and new on the outside - the actual apartments are out of date, the neighbors have not been vetted (porch theft, domestic violence, car damage) and any attempt to get things fixed is laughably always behind. It's been exactly 30 days since the complex has had real and functioning hot water - they "fixed" it with propane tanks and we haven't heard of any updates since. then.

I lived here a year. The leasing office never answered calls. They also close early or randomly. They handed out flyers instead of sending emails. My AC went out in the middle of summer it took them 3 days to even look at it. My light in the kitchen went out it took over 3 weeks for it to get replaced. Try cooking in the dark! The bathroom doesn’t have a vent so it’s the most humid room in the apartment. I wasn’t told about there not being a microwave. My apartment didn’t have a balcony or washer and dryer connections. I been trying to turn in my apartment keys in for 4 days. Called, emailed,left voicemails. NO response. I highly recommend staying away from these apartments. The rating on Roscoe Property’s is 1.2.

This place is beautiful! new management has made the biggest impact on this property - it's amazing. I recommend this place to anyone who is looking up North Austin. From the fantastic amenities to a great staff. The team here is the best team this property has ever had. Location is great, prices are fantastic, and the newly renovated community is worth it!

I have lived here for about 4 years. It was a good place to live before the management changed and has become better since the current company took over! The office personnel are friendly and do everything they can to resolve any issues you may have. Maintenance sometimes may take a bit, but not too long.

The property feels pretty secure and feels safe even at like 3 in the morning. I have never had any problems with noise, but lots of families live on the property so that may be a part of that.

It's conveniently placed right by two major highways and has every store you could need within a couple of minutes. Plus lots of food places deliver here.

Overall a very excellent place to live!

My fiance and I consider ourselves so very lucky to reside in these apartments. We have an amazing view of a pool with waterfalls. Have an enormous outdoor kitchen gazebo perfect for BBQ which has a swim up bar. There are too many gems to count. My fiance always says she feels like we are already living the retirement dream here. Cannot stress how spacious everything is, the kitchen, living rooms, porches, I could go on and on. 

SIDE NOTE: this apartment complex is more fabulous then the VERY PRICEY wedding venue we have contracted haha. So YES IT IS REALLY NICE.

I have lived in building 15, 3rd floor for almost 2 years and have an amazing view that over looks the 3 tiered pool. The apartment is spacious with 3 bedrooms, two full baths and a working fireplace. The amenities are amazing. (Volleyball court, Frisbee golf, full gym, tanning beds and a sauna) It's almost like staying at a resort, but we get to call it home.

--Jocelyn

I have been here 2 years, never had an issue with neighbors, maintenance requests completed quickly, GREAT and very interactive front office staff. The management went out their way to clear up a "towing issue" and have the towing  company refund me and send apology. The pool area (beautiful) is always clean AND almost always empty- there are always plenty of tables to be used and new furniture and a good lounge/BBQ area.  I am only leaving due to work/family obligations close to San Marco and will not commute. When I am transferred back to the Pfugerville or North Austin area I will not hesitate to return to this special oasis of peace!
They are very good about customer service, maintenance calls and just in general shine bright.
Low noise area and nice complex for the price. Welcoming community & staff! Conveniently located spot in north Austin

I have truly enjoyed living at Pebble Creek Apartments these past 3 years. The management staff is very professional. The maintenance crew is very timely and respectful. During the height of the pandemic they adjusted very well to the CDC guidelines, and sent constant updates for changes. It’s very obvious that the staff care about each member of this community. I’m very honored to call Pebble Creek home.

These are the absolute worst managed apartments I have ever lived in. Management does not respond to emails, and there are constantly people partying in the parking lots. When reporting noise issues to management they do nothing to help the residents instead telling you to record your neighbors for proof of noise issues. Or they say to just call security, which you’ll have to do at least 3-4 times a week and sometimes more than once in the same night. I also had my car towed by security for having my parking permit in my back windshield and not the front, they even took a picture of my car that clearly displayed my valid permit.
They are great Nice people and great complex I recommend theses apartment

I love it here. I just renewed my lease after a year. Friendly staff and my neighbors the best. Love love love my apartment it is so spacious and affordable. Plus I feel comfortable walking alone anytime day or night. It's a great place to live I'm happy I found it.

This is a very nice place to live. It is family orientated and feels safe, especially with the gated lots.  The management is very friendly, and the apartment I have is very spacious with a huge closet.  It's also close to UT and would be a nice and quiet environment to study in.  Glad I found the place!

I would like to take this opportunity to recognize Pebble Creek Apartments in Austin, TX and the outstanding efforts of their staff.

I became a resident at Pebble Creek in July 2018. From the moment of my first visit, it became quickly apparent that this was more than a mere apartment complex; this was going to be home. The leasing office is warm, cozy, and inviting, always beckoning with comfortable furniture, a professional appearance, coffee and snacks, well-lit, and a nice view upon the inner complex near the pool. I first met Karina, one of the office managers, who was polished and prepared to cheerfully and fully answer any and all of my questions I had about my new home. The apartment is conveniently located off of I-35 North Frontage, Rundberg, and North Plaza in north Austin. The leasing fees are very reasonable considering rental costs in the Austin area, yet they sacrifice no amenity to make you feel welcome. Pebble Creek takes security very seriously, and in addition to a gated community and on-site courtesy officer, it is well-lit with an open layout, and it truly has the feel of a neighborhood with the apartments fostering appropriate interaction, while allowing privacy for those that require it. The pool area is spacious and clean, with ample room for lounging or spending time entertaining guests by the available grills. There is also a clubhouse that can be reserved by apartment residents for parties and other special events. There is an open play space for the younger residents of the community. And the grounds are impeccably manicured and are adorned with flowers and trees that ripen and bloom with the seasons.

But I would also like to recognize the staff personally. Nowhere in my twenty-plus years of apartment living have I engaged with more friendly, selfless, and motivated staff to ensure your comfort and happiness. I mentioned Karina above, but I would also like to recognize Isabel and Miranda, and in fact the entire management team – all of whom always welcome your visit like you are an old friend. If your apartment requires maintenance they quickly address it and ensure your matter is resolved with promptness and care. The maintenance staff too, is professional, courteous, and truly cares about the community, from those who fix air conditioners, or those who work by manicuring the grounds and ensuring the complex is as spotless as can be.

I've been living here for about four months now. The staff is wonderful. Mrs. Loli will always greet you with big smile and help you out. It's a nice place and more affordable and most apartments in Austin.
i am living in this place for 7 years..very good staffs, and management.

The kitchen closet and cabinets are so tiny ..they charge you just for having more than 2 chairs on the patio and you can't have too many plants either!!! And you are paying for that space alsoo...sooo disagree with this apartments!!

At the end of October 2015, I will have dwelled at this residence for 3 years. My time here was well spent with minimal complaint. Though every year I have been here they raised my rent. By the 3rd year it was raised to a total of 100$ more. The price is moderate, and the rooms fairly sizable for its price. There isn't washer or dryer hookups in the apartments but there are two small laundromat buildings in the complex. They each have about 10 washers and dryers each. Some have broken down a lot but that is to be expected with machines and the maintenance staff are fairly quick to repair anything that needs attending. The office staff is friendly and when I moved in there was new management(who is still here). Since I moved in, there have been changes for the better. They tore down a playground and put up a nice new one. New light posts around, new picnic areas, new bbq pits, new volleyball and tennis courts. The complex is really close to one of the main expressways in Austin, I35. So a quick hop on and you can be downtown in 15 minutes. 
There are two pools and two hot tubs in each. I do wish they had stricter rules about having children in the hot tubs for sanitary purposes. A bit more upkeep would be desired in this area. 
There is a great amount of greenery and trees in the complex so it's not hard on the eyes. Overall, I'd like to say it's a good starter apartment if you just moved to Austin or want to be near the excitement but don't want to pay up the nose for downtown prices.

I rated all 6 categories 4 out of 5. Because 3 is looked at as fair and everything is way better than fair. And Pebble Creek staff really seems to be going for 5s in every category. Here if you'd like I'll go thru the 6 Categories with you:

Location/Neighborhood: I never imagine I'd give Location/Neighborhood out the 6 categories a strong 4 as I moved to 78753 from 78704 but now I'd have as hard of a time moving out of 78753 as I did moving to 78753. The area has noticeable undercover surveillance signs and a noticeable panhandler population still. But I have not noticed a neighbor or I's car being broke into the whole over a year that I've been here. My first year in 78704 and knowing people in the UT areas break-ins happened to me and I hear about it happening at least once bi-monthly on average and seemingly increasing down south.

The panhandlers ... they're just as present in 78704 and the UT Area now as they are in the 78753 area. Of course panhandlings never a fun reality to live so intimately amongst but at worst the 78753 panhandlers are relatively much more chill and at best the local corner (183 and Cameron) Nun-Chuck Master and the (lamar and Runeburg) Rapper are like amongst the 8 Wonders of the World to me. So don't mean to write a book but I'm that excited about the area. Neighbors are very diverse and very classy!!!

Love my running course and 2 local YMCAs!!!

Domain is a modern first class designed/landscaped urban center and always very easy no traffic 10 minute at most drive North East from Pebble Creek. Its less known and its newer and it is at least 20 minutes north of most of Austin's attractions (15 minute at most relatively Low traffic drive south from Pebble Creek) but its got the 2.0 of alot of those attractions such as the Movie Theater, Cafe and Flagship Whole Foods Market and then its got shops and nightlife unlike anywhere in Austin.

Overall Value: The rate of rent still looks $100 lower and utilities still seem 20% lower at least than South Austin. I said still because the city is and people are working and investing intensely to revitalize the area and word is getting out and you've only got a couple years before rates catch up.

I live in the most economical floor plan Pebble Creek offers. If your price range is as low as mine Pebble Creek should be high on your list of places to consider seeing if there is an opening. I hate to share that with you because the areas rate is going up and obviously everything about this property is close enough to first class. And I'd like to live here for close enough to the deal I'm getting another 12 month lease at least. But screening for criminal backround is strict and the culture of the residents and staff is very layed back but respectful and caring of its diversity of ages, races and cultures and I fit pretty well. So ... if theres an apartment available for you congratulations look forward to seeing you around and if you have them; look forward to also seeing your additions to the well behaved happy kids and pets around.

Office Staff: The office staff is the biggest reason I moved here and even more the reason I stay here. They made a better first impression than all the other property's office staffs and whether you're shy like me or one of the diverse outgoing visitors I commonly see when I visit the office; you don't ever wait long for immediate help or service. And they always seem impressively on top of things and caring and professional happy to work with you whoever you are.

Maintenance Service: You will see the Pebble Creeks maintenance team busy around the property from earlier in the morning than you think you should to later at night than you think they should be busy. And I don't know how because the property seems in good shape and it seems like a well staffed quality/quantity wise team. South and East Austin Properties are known for horrible issues with maintenance and crews. I have a problem with Pebble Creek when I put in a maintenance request how fast and well they take care of it. I am not used to that even in my higher price range Dallas days. Yes I'm complaining for me they take care of maintenance request too fast and too well and I'm a little not just kidding. I'm really don't know if I can get used to how good Pebble Creek maintenance is.

Quality of Amenities: I like all the ones you'll see on the tour and in the brochure. I'd like to point out if you're one of what seems like most South Austin apartment neighbors I had who are inconsiderate about never picking up your pets waste. Be ready to change if you move up here because at least at pebble creek here; waste baggie points are always stocked and here everybody is so considerate nobody ever doesn't pickup their pet waste. There's more; more beautiful pets here at Pebble Creek than any apartment complex that I've ever lived at; but absolutely the most spotless grounds. Parking is 4 out of 5 at Pebble Creek. You usually have to really look or really get lucky to get 2 or 3 out of 5 right? And a huge plus of Pebble Creek is bus stops and stuff are a nice very safe and not too long at all walk away. But N. Plaza dr and N. Plaza Cr are the best 5 out of fivest vehicle traffic and surrounding streets for an apartment property you can ask for. Lots of properties in the area have at best vehicle traffic that takes alot of patience and at worst is highly dangerous.

Noise: No train or emergency vehicle or airplane or any traffic like that. As far as neighbors and the youngsters go everybody seems purely chilled out. There's apartment parties and fiestas at the grills and public amenities but they're calm and considerate and just nice to pass when you're walking. There was actually volume/bass vibration complaints against me for my system and my South Austin habits but they were reasonable but of course firm and quick about the warnings. And now everybody is happy.

So on that note ... Pebble Creek is a LEASE IT in my sound opinion.

I never thought that after writing a first letter that a second letter could even be fathomable, yet here we are.
I've never carefully deliberated the intense importance of hot water. I suppose the feeling of hot water entitlement comes from "first world problems", as the kids say these days, or perhaps it's the $69 paid monthly for my outrageously high water bill. However I digress, the issue at hand is for at least two months I have had less that sub-par hot water. The first month summer had not yet left us and cooler showers were important therefore, the water temperature little ill effect. As the winter season made it's debut my water temperature did not increase.
Monday November 11th I called and put a work order in regarding my hot water's temperature as well as the water pressure. A week went by and I patiently waited for either results or a phone call with some kind of explanation. Much to my dismay there was no change.
Monday November 18th I decided to call again, I put in a second work order pertaining to my water's lack of temperature and pressure. By now the weather was changing, for a week it was thirty degrees and rainy out. I was chilled to the bone and my one wish was a hot and steamy shower to wash away the days hard work. As I approached the apartment I noticed the hot tub was on, steam rose up off the water in signaled plumes of warmth. Seeing this excited me perhaps my hot water would be in working order. I rushed in only to be loyally greeted with less than lukewarm water. I had to boil water and draw myself a bath as if this were 18th century England.
Monday November 25th, the week of thanksgiving, I called and this time I spoke with the apartment manager. He informed me that the apartment complex was on a boiler system and there seemed to be an issue with the boiler. He assured me that although they had to wait for the part to come in, they would try and and turn the hot water up so that maybe the water would be warm enough to shower in. Taking him at his word I got off the phone feeling relieved that something would finally be done about this dilemma.
I rushed home from work excited about the hot shower or at least warm shower I would now be able to take, I turned on my water in anticipation, only to be yet again greeted by barely lukewarm water that wouldn't even fog the mirror. Now I was getting frustrated with the entire situation.
Tuesday November 26th I decided to go into the office, thinking if they see my face maybe something would be different. I got to meet with the apartment manager in person. He told me that the boiler would be fixed by the end of the day. The end of the day came and went and still no change. My faith in the apartment manager is now measured by the heat of my water, less than lukewarm.
I called the Wednesday before Thanksgiving this time the girl that answers the phone says, "The boiler people are here right now and it will be fixed by the end of the day." I am beginning to wonder are they all just lying to me or do they honestly have no clue what is going on? I felt they kept telling me the answer they believed I wanted to hear. In reality I just want to know the truth so that I can plan accordingly.
The water was not fixed by by the end of the day meaning the water would not be fixed by Thanksgiving.
I spoke with a few of my neighbors and they were experiencing the same hot water issue. There was even a woman who lived two buildings away, that said she went to a friends house to shower.
Friday November 29th not fixed.
Saturday November 30th comes, disheartened, I call and ask when the water will be fixed and request she not say by the end of the day, at this point I know that answer is complete fabrication. The lack of communication between management and renter sends me spiraling into a sea of what-ifs. What if this is because I owe the apartments $2.40? What if she knew the next day was Sunday and the office would be closed, the employees would be deaf to our problems. Maybe the Pebble Creek crew has never seen your website, and they are completely unaware of your value for basic human amenities? Or maybe those slogans are only available to a certain class. Let's make a deal because I've already paid rent for November, using December's rent I will pay for all of the days I received satisfactory hot water. I believe that was from November 1st to November 15th

Sincerely,
Disgruntled Cold Inhabitant

Unfortunately I had to stay at these apartments for one year before my lease was up. The office was nice enough when they knew I was a potential renter, but once the lease was signed they were rude and uncaring of any issue I had. I was sent photos of a remodeled unit and was promised those photos were the unit I would be moving into, but upon arriving on site my unit was old, not remodeled, and not what was advertised. Other issues I encountered in my one here on site:

-Garbage fires in the dumpsters on a REGULAR basis.

Save yourself and spend your money elsewhere.

A much better manager was hired in the past year, or so, and bringing significant improvements.  This manager, Cristy, has been excellent.  She has been extremely responsive to my requests for repairs, and goes above the call of duty, to see that my needs are being met.

The property itself was built in the 1980's, so I'm giving it an average rating.  The landscaping has always been kept pretty nice.  Once a lease expires, they have begun making upgrades to the interiors, before renting them out again.

The gate code has not been functional for 2 months, the hallway lights were gone for a week and now the web portal doesn't accept payment. The management is completely incompetent and living here is a everyday struggle now. PLEASE STAY AWAY. The older positive reviews no longer represent the current state.

I live here now, and there are some good things about the complex, BUT, they placed us in an ADA accessible unit after showing us a standard unit and saying we'd get one just like it. None of the paperwork says our unit would be ADA accessible. There are real differences that are super annoying (tiny kitchen sink, lost cabinet space, low countertops, etc.). After going back and forth with them trying to get them to make it right, the best they've done is offer covered parking to my roommate and I, which costs them nothing (they have unused spaces), and doesn't solve our problem. Get in writing what kind of unit you are getting or they can do this to you too!!! The way they treated me seems like this may be the way the leasing office gets rid of the ADA units, which is just wrong.
Elevator has been out of service for over FOUR MONTHS. We live on the third floor. Management has been completely dismissive of this as an issue. LOOK ELSEWHERE!!!

Management changed in March 2017 and since then everything has changed to worse. This property management company (Lincoln Property Company) has a clear low-cost way of doing things, which contrasts with the professionalism that we'd been used to and for which we pay for. Quality in maintenance has plummet and is definitely not a primary issue for them, starting by the main gate that hasn't been working for several months. Since it is open 24/7, it has become common to see ppl you don't know walking around in the complex, but this insecurity problem doesn't seem to preocupy management, whose answer is always the same: "we're working on it". Pool is always green and dirty, club house and bbq area are never cleaned, there is never coffee available and the A/C's have stopped blowing cold air because of the poor maintenance of the external condenser units. They are even cutting back on garden watering. Yes, it is that bad and there are no signs of improvement whatsoever. 

Instead of replying to this comment with another polite excuse to justify your incompetence, try to make an assessment of how much you actually need to spend to manage this complex properly. This might help to put things into perspective, since you are disrespecting all the residents with your cheap management.

I lived here for two and a half years and had a wonderful experience...I only moved because I left Austin, but I would have loved to stay longer. The location is great, and I was easily able to bike to work downtown on the hike and bike trail year-round. Also, the complex is not run by a large management company, and the entire staff (especially Marlowe) really take pride in the property and will do anything to make sure every tenant is happy and has an enjoyable experience living there. They really do go above and beyond! The buildings are somewhat older, but they are very well-maintained. Maintenance requests were always completed very quickly, and maintenance is constantly working to maintain and improve the property. One time my dishwasher was not working properly, and they ordered a brand new one for me and installed it within a week. I really do miss living here and definitely recommend it!
It seems owned by some out of state company that cares more about raising the rents than quality remodeling and having substance.

We've lived here for six years an I couldn't be happier. The management has always been thoughtful, proactive, and very responsive whenever there has been an issue. The location is AWESOME and for where it is located the rent is very reasonable. I actually kind of regret written this because now I feel like I'm letting the cat out of the bag. If you are looking for a place near everything but still feel like a neighborhood this is the place for you.

In my personal experience, this property has gone downhill. The security gates can be easily walked around, packages get lost/stolen, amenities are in disrepair or closed down for no reason, management is not friendly and seems not be fulfilling their basic job responsibilities and there is an affordable housing development being built across the street that will change the area.

If I could give zero stars, I would. We wholeheartedly regret moving to Travis at the Lake. Knowing this is in Lakeway (Austin's most peaceful and serene community). I would think we are living off 6th Street DT. The walls are very thin, and you can hear everything and everyone your neighbors are doing. We have a very rude neighbor upstairs that stomps so loudly and plays very loud music the whole day and during holy hours. We have sent numerous complaints to the management about it, and they never replied and resolve the issue, because the noise never stopped since we moved here last September. We might have to move out soon, because we have not gotten any quality sleep, privacy, and peace. DO NOT MOVE HERE IF YOU VALUE YOUR SLEEP, PEACE, AND PRIVACY.

The office staff at Travis At The Lake is one of the best teams I have seen. They always answer your questions fast. They always have a solution to any problems you may have and are always doing the best they can. The maintenance staff is also always on top of it and making sure the property is in perfect condition. The maintenance manager is irreplaceable. He always has his guys moving and working. I have never seen such hard-working people. If you are looking for a family community and not just another apartment complex this is it.
Everything is consistent and in order which I love. I feel safe and I love my 2 bath 1 bed! Yes, they make those. This is my second year here I would recommend.

Do not allow them to tell you that parking has been resolved. This review is as of 3/12/2020. 
There’s never enough parking. When they designed the complex they went with four-story buildings but none of parking. They blame the city for an hour allowing them to have more parking spaces because of impervious coverage. They should I had multi level parking. Parking spaces are used as storage spaces. Ownership will not respond to my emails. I have pictures of lack of parking. Don’t waste your money here the building is a great new partner looks great the clubhouse looks great the pool looks great but what good is it if you have Your wife and kids walk long distances in the rain. If you have to park far away and lug your groceries. Management just does not address emails and concerns. Do yourself a favor and ask the residence before you rent I promise you you will ride somewhere else I am a current resident. Desperately trying to get out of my lease because of the parking issue.

I was recently looking to change apartment communities. I found Travis at the Lake apartments and just took a tour. The facilities, grounds and units are phenomenal. They have amazing amenities such as a beautiful pool, dog park, outdoor patio/grills, fitness center, yoga room, business center and more! They even have an indoor mail center with a package delivery system for frozen meal deliveries. How cool is that?! This property spares no detail with an attention to quality. The units are extremely high end with stunning kitchens and bathrooms. I was pleased to learn that all the units had plank wood flooring (hooray for no more carpet) and full size fridge in the kitchen. They also have two different color schemes available for cabinets. I am so happy to have additional square footage in my new apartment and look forward to adding a desk or kitchen table which i did not previously have the space for. This property also has great views and is well lit, a gated community and has elevators in every building. Despite all these wonderful amenities the real thing that makes Travis at the Lake stand apart is the customer service. Working with Nadia and Monica was amazing and they handled every detail. The team at Travis at the Lake truly values its residents and I look forward to calling this my new home!!!

Alarming Rat Infestation Issue – Do Not Ignore

If you're considering living here, think twice! The rat infestation in this property is absolutely unacceptable and a complete nightmare. My bedroom ceiling has become a rat playground—they run, fight, chew, and make unbearable noise all night long. It’s impossible to get a good night’s sleep!

The problem is even worse in the garage, where the smell is disgusting, and rats are visibly walking over cables. I’ve reported this issue multiple times, yet nothing has been done to resolve it. The situation is only getting worse, and it’s clear management does not take this health and safety hazard seriously.

This is not just an inconvenience—it’s a serious problem affecting my quality of life and safety. If you value peace, hygiene, and management that actually addresses tenant concerns, avoid this place at all costs!

Would you want to live in a place overrun by rats? I certainly wouldn’t recommend it.

The building is kind of difficult to navigate, but it's fine when you get used to it. The pools are okay, gym is silly levels of nice though. The area is also nice, plenty of trails and places to go nearby.

But rats(?) and mice.
I saw one, caught it, released it miles away, rinse and repeat, with the pest control called only after I went into the office in person to basically beg. They put one spring trap down.
I continued and caught 6+ mice, continually updating management and getting little in the way of help. Pest control returned a few times but never really did much. I found the holes and management finally helped plug them up a bit.

When we decided we needed to leave but didn't want to break a lease we asked to move units and they tried to charge us a unit move fee which is I guess fair but seemed like a less than kind act after all that.

It's an older building but not so old that this should happen and the response wasn't great or helpful for a while and then only intermittently.

There's other options so maybe think of them.

Terrible parking situation at this apartment complex. They changed to 3 separate towing companies over 2 years while living here. Each has a completely different registration process and they’ll still tow your car when registered it’s a $300. My car was also stolen out of the parking garage and the apartment refused to provide CCTV to the police without a court order. Turns out their cameras weren’t working during the theft. They’re current tow company will put massive stickers on your window when your parked in your own reserved spot. Horrible experience, management is wholeheartedly unhelpful.

Apartments are really nice , with great appliances.
Management had a difficult time in figuring out how to manage the building when they first took over.
Key issues: 1. if you have a pet, it’s far to take them out if you live on higher floors. 2. Garbage management is still a struggle. 3. Security : there was a murder in 2019 in the garage, bikes , car tires , car parts , and yes even cars are were stolen from the garage, security is awful here, “management is working on it”, but to pay top dollars to live in a luxury complex and have to deal with this is a joke. 4. Parking garage is dangerous to drive in everyday, can’t list all the near misses I’ve had driving up and down.
Mosaic is a very nice and comfortable place to live.  Office and specially maintenance staff are great!! Will definitely recommend!!
Always a very friendly and professional staff!! Love living at Mosaic!

Management has changed hands too many times, and the only "rennovations" they do is to the office. The building I am in has severe foundation issues, as well as absolutely no insulation between walls. This results in all noises being amplified to the downstairs unit. Walking, talking, the pipes of the plumbing, are so loud, you always know what your above neighbor is doing. The poor insulation has also resulting in being able to smell through the outlets, which in my case is smoke. The plumbing and water also needs to be checked/fixed. When a weird film sits in top of your bath water, you start to never take baths again. I wish they cared enough to condemn this unit and actually fix the problems, as these problems are pre quarantine. Read the reviews of people who are unhappy to see how things really are.

DO NOT LIVE HERE. Is zero stars an option? A new management company recently took over and the ladies who work in the office are extremely rude. The AC in my bathroom had a leak for the two years I lived here. I called and had it fixed multiple times but it would start leaking a few months later and ruined the drywall in there. Nobody would fix it properly. They won't work a minute past closing time whether your issue has been resolved or not and tell you she "doesn't get paid overtime". I got kicked out of their office at 5:30 on the dot. I've never met more rude people in my life. They will also charge you for literally everything when you move out. If you think you're getting a good deal on deposits, you're not. They'll charge you more than what you think is fair when you move out. I even asked for a walk-through to go through it with them and they said they didn't do that. There are tons of kids always running around and screaming. I came home one day and my neighbor's door had been kicked in and his stuff stolen. Another neighbor's dog attacked mine and nothing was done about it. It's not worth the cheap rent that they have, you're better off finding somewhere else.

So I  have been  living at these apartments for  a little of a year. Right before  new management  took  over. New management inside the  office  very informative and very helpful from day one. They worked with  us around the first of the month when they took over to make sure no late fees had occurred since a new system was  being put in.  Christmas Eve pajama  party was amazing. Great food and fun games and  drinks of all assortments. They didn't  have to spend it with us, they could have gone home to their families. But they had a party for us. For mother's day made me cry its been  3 years without my mother. The Manager  Ms. Brown  hosted a celebration for mother's I may not be a mother, but I felt the love in the room. I give props to  the women in the office. They even know my name I don't go into the office much but they know my name, not just unit number as some go by.
The apartment complex is amazing these people go above and beyond service!!!

***Perspective Renter***

Property looks poorly managed and outdated, but I didnt want to judge it by the cover. I walked in and the office manager was busy with what I assumed was a current resident. She asked me wait and have a seat for a moment while she assisted the first person. Which that's understandable, but shortly after the current resident started a shouting match with the office manager. Don't think this place is for me.
I know this apartment is not on the fancy side. But I really don't have much to complain. Office staffs are friendly and maintenance guys are very nice.
Leasing team was very friendly and helpful when I moved in. Also the maintenance men are amazing and get to my requests within a day.

Besides the mold they allowed to grow in my unit's kitchen, they also attempted to unlawfully charge me a RENT INCREASE of MORE THAN HALF of the rent. The ONLY reason they refunded and removed the increase was because I had security cameras inside and outside of my unit which showed that NOBODY from the GVA management came to my door to give me notice about an increase on the day they said they did. In regards to the rent increase its-self, its not worth it!
very nice it's near shopping centers and the park is close by the schools are great i just love it here
Love the central location and the amazing pool! Super clean property.

I had toilet water from upstairs leak out of my bathroom light socket from July 4th. It took a month and half to fix plus residual touch up here and there. There a bad mold problem and sparking of the light circuit. 
I moved out earlier I paid an extra month because of the contract. They want to pay an extra 6 days. Instead of the leaded time to pay at the office they sent to Jetty.

When i first moved in in 2021 the rent was affordable. It was newly opened so a lot of the units were empty, meaning it was peaceful. After 2 rent increases, it is no longer affordable. The quality of tenants has gone down as my neighbors are yelling at each other at 3am. Sketchy things happen at night and homeless people shamelessly steal from the patios. Management does nothing about the complaints. The laundry room is nasty, the pool has had poop in it multiple times, no one cleans up after their pets, homeless people play music loud at night outside of the complex, and the tenants here are sketchy as hell. There are some apartments down the street that are better than this and you get more bang for your buck. Thank God my lease ends soon.

The Studio Apartments are the perfect size for me, and I believe for others. Management is extremely proficient at managing and still resolving other issues that need attention. Property is quite at night for the most part with some interruptions from time to time. That being said, I really enjoy the complex, I love the location, and the other transportation options. If you are single or a couple, of two, this would make a splendid place to live...consider....

Current Resident: McCoy

These studio apartments are not as nice or clean as the pictures make it seem they are. After moving in, I sent hours cleaning. Also the neighbors are very noisy and there is no proper way to make a noise complaint on the weekends. Washers and dryer’s in laundry room are nasty and have pet in them. Dog poop is all in the grass and sometimes on the sidewalks
This is an awesome place and location!!! Love the pool!!!

I wish that I would have had a positive experience. It has been a headache, one thing after another. The maintenance team is so friendly and kind and thoughtful. The “management team” on the other hand, is so incredibly disappointing. Be mindful: THERE IS NO OFFICE ONSITE. The phone just rings. There is no way to interface with anyone in person. You are subject to text and email communications only. And, they are capable of answering the phone, just not for their tenants. I have witnessed a team member call and be able to speak to a “management “ person. Yet, our option is to leave a message that is not returned. My only success was to leave a message on the maintenance line. Maintenance showed up. Management did not return the call. I want to move, but have paid so much to move in. Safe yourself. Live somewhere else. Trust the reviews that are imperfect, as they represent more truth than the 5 star reviews, which are allegedly left by management and their family members.
Peaceful place to live, new property management company is very responsive when we have an issue.

Same issue as the other 2019 reviewer. Management changed in August and the new one (particularly Joanie our property manager) is HORRIBLE. Will not respond to emails or calls. We are in the process of going to legal services against them due to the parking issue (see below) and unfair  fees. Only 1 functional washer/dryer in community laundry room and some idiot uses it as his own personal hotbox. Lots of outdoor smoking and partying.

This may be a little long, but if you're considering living here, I recommend you read this message.

I used to think if a place was alright, the quality of property management didn't matter. The past couple months have proven me horribly wrong. While the apartments may seem nice at first, there's a plethora of issues beneath the surface. Being right next to a hospital, sirens will wake you up at a startling frequency unless you're a very heavy sleeper. We've been dealing with a cockroach issue for three months now they have failed to solve and practically ignored(In addition, we've been charged a separate 'pest utility fee' each of these months). A large hole has existed in our kitchen door since we moved in. The large bathroom has a leak through the HVAC system causing the entire bathroom to completely flood whenever it rains. While for the first month our utility bill was pretty high, more recently we've been charged an obscene utility fee, with no breakdown or reason for it. The amount is nearly triple the listed max utility charge on the lease agreement. All attempts to reach out to management have failed. More recently, we have attempted to go through our property manager's superior, but have never received a reply through email. Afterwards, we attempted to communicate through a phone number, but she has never picked up the phone, and after leaving three messages over the course of several weeks, I assume she avoids answering the phone on purpose. It appears we have no nonlegal options left. Lastly, my roommates and I entered this apartment under the agreement we would have four parking spots. It was one of the reasons we chose this location. As of a couple weeks ago, management has removed the parking spots of nearly half the garage to do renovations. While this may not be managements fault, we are currently still being charged $50 per spot, per month. The renovations shall continue till the end of December, during which we are having tremendous issues dealing with the placement of our cars, and with still no sign of any credit to our account for the price of the parking spots. I'm taking one of my hardest semesters at UT, and don't have the time or energy to fight a legal battle with this absolute demon of a property management team. The one upside is I can't argue the benefits of location. Close to campus and some bus stops, transportation is never an issue. Save yourself the time, headache, and health issues. Live somewhere else. I wish I had.

I have lived at Great Oak Apartments for about two years and wanted to leave an updated review as my roommate and I prepare to leave for another complex. While we have not had a positive experience with 512 Realty and this complex, it is also difficult to find comparable apartments for the price in this area of town.

Pros:
- We have never had issues with any pests (cockroaches, ants, rats, etc.) *Note: we don't have a ground floor unit
- Pool is generally very clean and never crowded
- Maintenance staff is pleasant and seems to care about doing a good job
- Location is the real reason to live here -- it's next to campus and 5-10 minutes from downtown, also conveniently placed on I35
- Our unit has all wood flooring and is relatively spacious (walk in closets, large living room, tiny bathrooms)

Cons:
- TERRIBLE move-in experience - unlivable... think filthy/black footprints all around the unit, a towel with literal s**t floating in the toilet, no electricity working (in Austin... in August... moving up flights of stairs with no AC or lighting -- also with no working refrigerator to store food)
- Parking-- not much guest parking and 512 Realty neglects to tell residents the parking policies. $50/month for a parking spot at the building and they do tow you for being in the wrong spot (they neglect to tell people that spots are assigned upon move in... makes for many mishaps)
- Recurring issues in my unit with the power (including AC/heat and lights) going out. It's happened about 5 times in under 2 years.
- Aside from the pool itself, common areas aren't kept very clean. Lots of broken glass around the parking area, random trash that isn't picked up...
- Noise is occasionally an issue. It's not bad from unit to unit, but you can very clearly hear people walking outside and in the pool area. Also some tenants enjoy running around on the roof, which is very loud if you live on the top floor.
- On-site laundry is pretty run-down. There are several broken units at a give time, and they generally don't post which are out of order. Annoying to come back to clothes sitting in a full machine of soapy, cold water or a dryer full of entirely wet clothes.
- They started asking to renew the lease 4 months into a 12 month lease. If you do not renew, they will show your unit for months with very little notice (often 1-2 hours in advance). So you can expect many realtors and strangers going through the apartment.

German roach-infested, no pool for over a year, the ceiling collapsed damaging my washer and dryer, and several items and no credit or apologies were offered. Rude and unprofessional property manager that changed last-minute move out date in spite of having email confirmation and blatantly added charges and hung up on me.  
Loud neighbors, dog waste everywhere, and mold-ridden.
The only positives are location and prompt maintenance staff.
Multiple buildings are known to flood regularly and have mold. They never fix it properly. STAY AWAY
Diane, the aggressive and embittered "property manager" is to be avoided. Lacking any sense of decorum, she shouldn't be allowed to interact with people. But yea location is ok.

The Silver Creek Apartments are located south of downtown Austin, and minutes away from everything an Austin resident would want.  A small complex as  properties go, the Silver Creek Apartments offer many floor plans, from one to three bedrooms, some with spacious patios and washer-dryer connections, others with an enclosed "green room", ideal for an office space or a third bedroom.  The on-site management is experienced and helpful, as are the maintenance crew.  The complex is well-kept and clean.  There are laundry facilities on premises as well as a off-site laundries minutes away. A lovely two-tier pool sparkles in the center of this 78704 gem. Having lived in this complex for almost 20 years, no other property has the amenities and location convenience.  Pet friendly and electronic lease payment are just two of the many features in this awesome complex!
Perfect location. Close to all amenities. Great quality apartments.

Hallways are dirty, bad changes- fetch. Charge you for dumb stuff- trashcans outside after valet trash. Inconsiderate of residence- painting garage making you move your car twice or you get towed. Inconsistent- I have been told for YEARS they are changing to no assigned parking spots when I ask to move my spot to the floor I live on. They just have no idea what is going on and do not care at all about their residence. For example they have “free coffee bar” in the office but the office doesn’t open till 10…

On the day of move-in, our apartment had clearly not been cleaned or inspected. We immediately submitted 10 maintenance requests, about half of which were actually addressed. The service elevator - broken when we toured two months earlier - was still broken at move-in so our movers took 2 hours longer than quoted. That elevator is still frequently out of service.

The parking garage gates are rarely working. This has resulted in unhoused individuals seeking shelter in the parking areas and having direct access to enter the building since there are no additional layers of security. The amenity spaces were closed for months to undergo renovations, however it's clear the majority of the renovation money was put toward the leasing staff's offices. The Building 2 pool is consistently dirty due to unmaintained landscaping around the courtyard and the uneven pavers are a lawsuit waiting to happen (an older resident with hip problems almost fell last week).

The apartments themselves are dated and poorly maintained. The cheap vinyl flooring, "landlord special" paint jobs, broken blinds, and chipped cabinets will be the least of your problems. There is minimal insulation in the apartments and the windows are DRAFTY. Our showers have had grout chipping away since move-in day. Maintenance has refused to properly fix this so we're just dealing with mold and uncomfortable showers (try standing on raw tile edges barefoot) until we move out.

Our AC unit broke twice this summer. The water pressure is inconsistent, we've had no hot water in our kitchen for 6 months, and have many instances where water was shut off for maintenance or construction or other unknown reasons with little or even no notice. Most recently, water is being shut off from 8pm - 5am (so no showers before bed, can't brush teeth, flush a toilet, cook dinner, etc.) The door locks are electronic, so they can die without warning. This happened to us on a Saturday and unsurprisingly the "on-call" maintenance person was not on site. We had to wait 3 hours for him to return to be able to lock our own door - and even then, they had to replace it with a manual lock temporarily because they don't keep certain parts stocked.

The office staff is rude if you're lucky enough to get a reply to your emails - but I'm sure they're tired of fielding complaints about their poor management.

Renewing at Bell South Shore has been a pain. They actively increased my lease when renewing (although rent prices overall have been going down), so I decided to transfer to a different unit (better unit, but cheaper). Then, when they posted my current unit as available on the website, it was $300 a month cheaper than what they had offered to me. This was clearly a way for them to gouge and take advantage of current residents (otherwise, why increase the rent for an existing resident and drastically decrease the rent for a new one?). When I asked them if I could just stay in my current unit at the new lease prices, they refused. Seems like they just want to take advantage of current residents and are clearly not willing to work with their current residents to the betterment of all parties involved. 

It's a shame that management is ran so poorly. I do not feel valued as a current resident at this property.

My resident experience has been disappointing. The management's poor communication, constant water shut-offs, lack of security, and ongoing repairs have created a frustrating living environment. The amenities are often unavailable, contributing to an overall negative atmosphere. The only saving grace is the location, but it's overshadowed by the numerous issues affecting residents' daily lives. Improvement is urgently needed.

Lived here two years - headline is this property is very unsafe due to the nature of the riverside neighborhood but it's made worse by a negligent property ownership and management groups.

Bell (owner) refuses to install security cameras in the garage or fix broken entry ways. You'll have homeless drug addicts passed out in your hallway and your car will be broken into.

Management also constantly closes the amenities rather than keeping them functional. I've never been able to use the grills (always broken), they've kept the gym closed for months on end, pool was closed during peak usage time this summer.

Package room is also unsafe. Not good people running this building, please look elsewhere.
Everything I need in an apartment community. The renovations/upgrades to the carpets, hallways & package room are all greatly appreciated. I can tell there's care & effort put into the building.

The new owners of the complex are working hard to help the residents live comfortably and investing in how the property looks. Still needs some work on major things like water temperature, security, and maintenance requests

I lived in this complex for several years and there were car break-ins nearly every week, homeless people sleeping inside the building, and a management team with a turnover rate unlike any I've ever encountered. Several residents have also experienced black mold and are currently in the process of suing the complex because of it. Don't be fooled by the pictures or any sketchy positive reviews. Join the community Facebook group if you really want to see how terrible this complex is.

Where do I start other than if we hadn't put down a deposit we would have never stayed in this apartment after our experience? 

We haven't even fully moved in yet and this is one of my fiancè and I's absolute worst experience dealing with leasing and moving into an apartment.

Great location with walkability and sweet amenities sold us and we couldn't have more regret sticking with this place.

It's been an uphill battle since day one being told incorrect information and not having our apartment ready on move in day with no follow ups from management. 

It started with trying to lease the apartment. We didn't hear from the office for 3 days and the leasing office failed to fill out important information such as concessions on the lease. We were told these issues were due to a broken phone system and new leasing system. Understandable. However it took us multiple calls to the leasing agent to get him to actually email and updated lease. We naively hoped that would be the end of the problems.

The lease wasn't signed by the leasing office for another few days and it wasn't until we talked to the manager did we even hear what paper work we needed to provide such as utilities confirmation pages and renters insurance. 

We moved from out of state and wanted to order furniture to have everything ready to go right when we got there. Our leasing agent ensured us packages would be accepted as long as they were smaller than a piano. No luck there. All of our packages (over $1,000) in furniture was lost somehow before our arrival. When we get to the office the same leasing agent then tells us they don't accept large packages and we come to find they had LOST our mail keys and NEVER set up our mail even though we signed the lease 2 weeks prior!!!  

We've now been here for about 2 months at this point and nothing has changed. Management continues to struggle with any kind of communication. If you want anything done you will have to go through at least 3 people and it will take 2-3 times longer than expected. We are regularly hearing that bicycles are being stolen from bicycle lockers, water and fire alarms go off randomly in multiple building with little to no notice.

In fact, my building has been without water for almost 10 hours today and while I understand it may be out of their control there has been nothing but an initial update. 

Please also be wary of any positive reviews you read on here. There are incentives to post positive comments about this complex.

I love living in South Shore! This is a wonderful community. The Management staff is wonderful, very professional and Friendly! Ginnie M. at the leasing office was and is a Superstar and her customer service skills strike out! She was not only helpful but super efficient in preparing my move-in. She followed up later on several ocassions to make sure I was all set and comfortable.  I also got a thank you letter-handwritten by Ginnie - and a welcome bag. The thank you letter was a very nice gesture that I have not seen before and speak very highly of the staff and the work they do.The location of south shore is the best too! 100% recommended.

GREAT LOCATION, TERRIBLE UPPER MANAGEMENT!!!We recently moved out of SSD after living there for 3 1/2 years. We loved the location and amenities there, but we consistently ran into issues with the staff while we lived there. 

In our first apartment in building 3, we got a bunch of mold on our carpets, walls, and personal things. After 6 weeks of going back and forth with them and feeling like they weren't taking us seriously, they finally agreed to move us but would not reimburse the over $1500 worth of damage to personal belongings caused by the mold, which was also denied by our renters insurance because the maintenance staff determined that it was from not changing out the air filters. 

We had more water/rain issues in our new apartment that resulted in industrial fans and vacuums running in our apartment for 24/7 and constant repairs for a span of 2-3 months. And even with all of this, we still gave them the benefit of the doubt and were content there because of the location.

Most recently, we moved out in the middle of March. We took very good care of the apartment that we left behind, having lived there for 2 1/2 years. Of course the apartment needed a deep cleaning, but we were told by the staff that we were already getting charged $125 for a deep cleaning of an 800 sq foot apartment, and that we didn't need to do any additional cleaning. So we left the apartment in very fair condition, only to get hit with a bill for an additional $105 for "deep cleaning of microwave, oven, and washer top," as well as an additional rent charge even thought we moved out before the end of our lease date. How does that work!?!? 

They also charged $420 for glass stove stop replacement after I sent over very comparable units for $125 dollars. I reluctantly agreed to pay full price for the for the stove top but told them we would not be paying any additional cleaning fees or rent fees. The difference ended up being around $130 dollars. They replied that they would not accept and payment that wasn't the payment in full. They were absolutely unwilling to work with us after we paid them over $50,000 in rent and lost over $1500 in personal belongings because of mold, as well as having to move all of our stuff to another apartment mid lease.

Buyer beware.  When our lease ended at South Shore District Apartments we cleaned our apartment and left it in meticulous condition. Ten days after we left, we were notified that the stove cook top had been damaged beyond repair and we were being billed $740.

The appliances were all in perfect condition when we moved out.  Any damage to them may have been done by staff working in the apartment or anyone who had a key.  We turned our key in the day we left.

There are a lot of apartments for rent in Austin.  Look elsewhere unless you want to risk being charged for expenses you didn't cause.

I absolutely love it here. It is the best apartment complex I have ever lived in, and the staff always remembers my name and I feel welcome. Candy and Cynthia were helpful when I couldn’t pay online.
My apartment is beautiful. I have the most amazing downtown views . 
The grounds are well kept and I feel safe and happy here. The best part is the rooftop deck. I love going up after work for a glass of wine.
My apartment has access to the lady bird lake trail so my fiancé and I can go for a jog on the weekends! I even cancelled my gym membership.
Great place to live overall.

Love the location. Close to downtown and the boardwalk. Apartments are all upgraded, amenities are great especially the free work out classes yoga, cycling and more. It's still a new property so things are being worked out from the build out but they do a good job at communicating and addressing anything that arises.

South Shore District has tons of different layouts across 3 different buildings. My layout, lavaca, has to be one of the best one bedroom layouts. Huge laundry room, enormous corner bathroom with separate shower and soaking tub. Walk in closet in bedroom. Kitchen island with huge living area. Three big windows and patio door all let in tons of light. You can walk across the street to the river or chipotle and Starbucks. Area has a reputation, but there are locks on everything and security patrolling at night.  Cons: They raise prices every chance they get and they charge tons of fees. And they will only offer you as little as 2 weeks free on SOME layouts.  Elevators can be reserved which they rarely inform us about. Not good when carrying groceries. Leasing office is hard to contact sometimes. Some people will try and pass you on to the next person with little lies. My check was cashed within a day but never made it to my account balance with them for over a month. So keep an eye on your balance. Walls are somewhat thin. Sirens every 20 minutes, but that's riverside for you. If they offered the same rates to renew I would definitely stay. An amazing apartment with a price tag to match.
Ceiling is leaking about to flood the kitchen. Foundation is cracking upstairs. Only 2 of the 8 doors close. Drug addicts in the parking lot have not been addressed. Roaches and beetles everywhere
Move to SJW if you're ok with: rampant  theft, cut and paste template responses to issues, no access to trash chutes, and loitering from the walking dead that convene near by. 0 stars.

Strongly advise anyone reading this to not move to St Johns West.  After car break-ins, noise complaints, and vagrants entering the property at all hours due to lack of PROMISED security, management refused to email/call me back despite multiple attempts at contacting them through email, phone calls, and going to the office in person.  They ONLY communicate when they think you owe them money, and pay absolutely no attention to resident issues and concerns.

With absolutely ZERO move-out communication, I was slapped with a final statement of over $600 worth of move out charges, and my emails questioning the charges were ignored for weeks.  They pretend to care about residents when we are standing in the office, but there is no follow-through or communication EVER.

Again, any other apartment in town is better than this.  I will never live at an Equity Residential property again.

The first year we lived here was awesome. Things have gone downhill since Equity Residential took over. They did away with Fetch and now there is a free for all package room that is stolen from daily. Cars are broken into and stolen. Someone tried to break into our apartment a few months ago as well as neighbors’ apartments. The garage gates and elevators are always broken. Climbing four flights of stairs in the heat is AWFUL.

I lived here from late 2018 - 2022.

Someone was KILLED in the stairwell and management took no action. People that chose to leave after this were forced to break their lease and pay the penalty despite the fact there was a MURDER.

Management changes yearly as new companies buy/sell the building. The most recent (2022) management is awful. They are slow to respond to maintenance issues, questions, and anything that would cost the apartment money.

On move out I was charged with a handful of obviously frivolous cleaning fees for a modest amount and management seems to be avoiding my questions to explain these. It's an obvious small amount that's meant to be easier to pay than go to court about.

Sadly the apartment is nice and the location is convenient, but the management, all the hidden charges, and unprofessionalism is NOT worth the headache.

AVOID and DO NOT LIVE HERE

I moved out June 25,2022 due to a high rent increase. It is now October 2022 and I have yet to receive my deposit and account balance from this property management. I have been told by four different people that payment has been sent to my forwarding address but I have received nothing. Even corporate has been nothing but incompetent. I will most likely be taking legal action at this point because no one has been responding to my calls/emails. THis company is 80 days past the 30 day required deadline for Texas landlords to send security deposits back. Tenants beware and know your rights!

From the outside it looks high end... it's not. If you have an unit facing the street prepare for a lot of noise and not just bus / street noise.  They use metal exhaust / vent covers on the outside which while they may look good will smash against it's metal frame during high wind and bang all night long.  Since it's connect directly to your vents there isn't much you can do do silence it. When brought up to management they say there is nothing that can be done without even trying anything. A rubber / felt lining might reduce the impact noise. 

Someone was killed in the stairwell but they wouldn't release any more info after the police investigation was over.  You're forced to use services like Fetch (packages are now stolen from your door instead of a surveilled mail room, so no camera footage),  valet trash (even if you literally live right next door to the chute) and shared internet service without any instructions on how to set it up (You can see everyone else's smart devices / computers rather easily). 

They don't even enforce the rules they set.  No one is ever towed from the garage for parking in Disabled or EV spots when they aren't disabled / EV vehicles. 

I've been here close to a year and can't wait to get out.

We've been here a few months now and so far it's been great. When I go for my am Starbucks in the office, the workers there seem chill.  They usually say hi and ask if I need anything.  The pool is nice. I wish it was a foot deeper or so, but the temp is pretty steady and it's always clean.
The area is decent too, I'd say below average in noise being so close to the city.
I'm glad we found this place, if things stay like they are we're going to stay.

This is one of the best places I have lived. The management cares about us. The have been doing residents events, the office loves my pet. If you needing a great place to live come check out the Monroe Come see Ryan, Lisa or James. Oh by the way I can get a Starbucks coffee!! Huge plus.

Terrible property! Many car break-ins, homeless people sleeping everywhere in the building stealing things and snatching your door cameras off your door. Dog poop everywhere, management never answers nor responds to tenant's complaints. Apartments are cheaply made falling apart and maintenance is delayed responding to fix things. I'm not sure what is going on with this property, but it needs to be tore down and rebuilt. This is a nightmare on elm street!

If you could avoid leasing here please do. The property has poor management. They aren’t responsive or concerned with resident issues. Secured access is continuously not working or vandalized. If valet living doesn’t show up to take out the trash for days or weeks. We are still expected to pay. There continuous issues in the common areas. No wifi, property damage and no janitorial cleanups. Neighbors dogs poop anywhere even when though they have a designated area. They poorly make ready unit’s upon leasing. From moving in and transferring units. They weren’t in good condition and the expectation is for you to be accepting or not notice. There is a high retention rate in the office open this property opening 2 years ago, which effect residence. Lease amount isn’t consistent or divide as they said in regards to sewer, water etc. management will also delay in responding emails regarding charges or paperwork that may result into you paying additional fees. Residents move out more then they move in. Delivery carriers cannot access the property if leasing isn’t open or they don’t piggy back behind a resident. Business center has no wifi, printer or computer do I was confused by its existence. Club room and pool is beautiful though.

Even though the apartments are spacious and "luxury". The whole complex is very poorly constructed. Management doesn't communicate and try to make up some really weird lies with what's going on in the building. Fire alarms going on A LOT of the time, gate never closes, doors with key fobs never work, fans wobblin and about to fall everywhere. Keep looking for other properties because you will regret it.

Do not sign here, you will regret it. Management does not care about your concerns whatsoever. Even after multiple car breaks ins and theft, they act like it never happened. It is unsafe, dirty, and the complete opposite of luxury. Steer clear of Asset Living.

Some people really like it here and it's in a nice location, but it definitely wasn't the place for me.

Pros:
-Close-ish to downtown
-Great maintenance staff

Cons:
-Super thing walls. If your next door/upstairs neighbors talk at a normal volume, you can fully understand their conversations
-Entrance/exit is a nightmare. You need to wait at a light to leave the apartment and many residents exit through the entrance to avoid the light making it dangerous to get in at times
-Mosquitoes in the laundry. The laundry door is never closed so mosquitoes nest in the washing machines so you get bitten and/or end up with dead mosquitoes in your clean clothes. These were also broken for months before management got new ones
-Expensive for what you get. Nearby apartments in Hyde Park are at least as nice in a better location for similar prices. 
-Amenities aren't great. The gym is basically three cardio machines and like 10 or so dumbbells and 5 or so kettlebells with no bench. If you want to run/elliptical inside then you're good, but don't expect this to replace a gym membership by any stretch. The pool was always cloudy while I was there. Might just be bad timing, but it seemed gross to me

Random Notes:
-Any review complaining about danger might be outdated or unreasonable. I've never felt unsafe here or in the neighborhood and never heard about theft or break-ins
-Many of the reviews come from early 2019 when management changed so there were certain incentives for residents to leave reviews. They aren't necessarily dishonest, but I would take them with a grain of salt

I like it here. Management is friendly and solves every issue really fast.
