They update everything step by step, so laundry situation is halfway solved: new machines with ability to use with an app. Walls are soundproof (or I have really quiet neighbors ??) walkable distance to EVERYTHING: grocery, coffee shops, gym, dog walking areas, really good restaurants and even a big pet store. And 2 bus stops right behind an exit gate. Lots of bushes and blooming trees, the management take care of the areas every day on a weekdays. It’s quiet here and with all birds chirping it even feels like you live in the countryside. Very pet friendly

I love living in the chelsea but the current laundry situation is abysmal. The washers and dryers are nearly constantly breaking or broken down and the higher ups still have not bitten the bullet and gotten new washers. It breaks my heart as i do really love this complex but this situation is abysmal and has been getting worse

When I first called The Chelsea to show a unit, I was invited at 3 p.m. same-day and given a full tour of the grounds. Having toured most apartments from Downtown to the Domain, I was most impressed by the Chelsea’s prices and standard of living. Within a week I had applied for a lease, was approved and moved in. That was July 2018 and I couldn’t be happier with my choice. A couple of months ago I spoke with a friend who previously lived here under different management and the contrast was like night and day. I can honestly say the staff is helpful, friendly and always keeps the grounds clean while quickly responding to any maintanence requests. Also it doesn’t hurt that my dog loves to meet and play with all the other pets here!

The biggest drawback to The Chelsea is the small size of the gym, however I  put the money I’ve saved by staying here towards a gym membership, which is only a few blocks away.

Big thanks to Alice and James and the whole maintanence crew for making my experience great.

-Garrett W.

My roommate and I overlooked this place over and over again on our apartment hunt because we thought the exterior looked a little corny from the photos. When we finally looked, it perfectly fit everything we were looking for! Great price for a central location, perfect amount of space for two, updated rooms (definitely remodeled within the last couple years), and very safe community. Wish we had laundry in unit, but the community laundry room isn’t very far from any apartment. Seriously love living here! - Kelly C

I have lived at The Chelsea for one year now and have just today resigned my lease for an additional year. What initially drew me to The Chelsea over any other apartment around was the community. Living in a space with only two floors keeps everyone close! We all acknowledge and recognize each other and it is never too loud. We have the friendliest neighbors and in a city that is only getting bigger, it makes all the difference in the world. The maintenance team here are quick and efficient. I knew them each by name by the end of the first month living here. I can always count on them to give me a big smile and a wave whenever I see them around. The Chelsea has a great management team whose number one priority is COMMUNICATION! I always feel informed and kept up to date with anything going on around the complex. The pools and community areas are always well kept and easy to enjoy. I HIGHLY recommend The Chelsea to anyone who is looking for a central Austin location with affordable prices! You will get so much more than what you pay for. Resigning my lease was the easiest decision to make. - Kylie S.
The location and aesthetics are nice, but the utilities inside the apartments need to be upgraded especially the cabinets and the refrigerator.
On big thing is that maintenance never comes to fix things - also the amenities closing so early is extremely inconvenient. The staff is cordial and understanding though.
The the lobby and gym are very clean. All the staff memeners are friendly . Maintainance is very fast and they do a job. Overall, this buidling is a great place to live!

I was a resident here for an year. Accommodation was good, except that sometimes the water doesn't come out well due to low water pressure. Staffs were hard to reach out, it normally took a week to get their reply back. The view from my room was so terrible because the other apartment that was under construction right next to my apartment was super close to my room and noisy every single day.
Beautiful complex, dog friendly, but needs improvement on service and communication. Things like rent and fee’s are not something you want changing at the last second.
Broadstone is a great apartment and a good location. Friendly people and good community. Dog friendly.

This place is nestled among the most beautiful parks and trees, close enough to downtown Austin but far enough from main roads and food businesses to feel less crowded. The apartments have nice layouts, and the staff is flexible and tries their best to go the extra mile.

The experience with the management at Broadstone East End has not been good. On several occasions suggestions related to improvement of living conditions were provided to the management but the management has ignored them.

Brand new place with nice amenities and attentive staff, worth a look in a good location on the Walnut Creek trails in East Austin! A few of the bumps that come with managed buildings of course (fees, things breaking) but the staff is very attentive.

The moving stipend and rent bonus provided by Broadstone was a massive help and made the whole process so much easier. It was a game changer for me. This is a new, well-maintained complex and I am so excited to be here.

We love the location and proximity to food and groceries. Our apartment is getting a little outdated because it is a little older, but maintenance has been very quick with any issues that we have. I do not enjoy the Fetch package requirement - it is a nightmare.
Love it here! Love the staff and the amenities are great. Maintenance is always quick to help and respond. Excited to enjoy the pool more as it warms up.

I adore the location; having a yard is uncommon, and the maintenance has always been excellent. The management office is responsive, and communication is great. Overall, I consider the apartment to be a decent value for money. I'm happy here, feel safe and secure, and haven’t had any major problems.

However, since I’ve been here, the extra charges for various services like liability, administrative fees, parking, packages, and so on have gradually increased without any corresponding improvement in service. Additionally, the valet trash service has been subpar. I believe they pick up the trash too early, and there’s no enforcement of leaving it out all day, which results in the hallways being perpetually dirty and run down.

Overall pleased. Somewhat frustrated with garage gate seldom working, especially when an $10 parking charge is being implemented on top of my $50 reserved spot fee. Also still hoping the rodent situation can be improved

Great location, nice apartments, friendly leasing staff! Only complaint is how difficult it is to get to apartment room in the first place.  With the rooms being in the parking garage, it is difficult to figure out how to enter the apartments, but once you get it figured it out, it's a nice space

I just moved in but so far am loving it! You can’t beat the location and everyone is friendly but not overbearing. Love that the gym and other areas are always clean and open! Only complaint is the elevator being out for a few days, but I found easy street parking in the meantime.

As much as I’d like to gatekeep this apartment complex, just can’t do that, because it really is the best! Im from Austin so I’ve lived all over this city in multiple different houses and apartments including more expensive “luxury” complexes, and this is by far my favorite I’ve lived in. The price for what you get is extremely reasonable (especially considering Austin rates), they don’t do crazy annual increases, and the complex and apartments themself are lovely. The area is quiet, right off the highway so easy to get anywhere, with great proximity to HEB and restaurants, bars, and shopping in Southpark Meadows. I also have to give a huge kudos to the absolutely fantastic leasing staff, seriously everyone that works there is so friendly, easy to work, with and quick to help (shoutout my girl Leilani especially!), and the maintenance guys are great as well! Seriously best property management staff I’ve come across. I’ve lived here 2 years and it was an easy choice to renew again. Wish there were more complexes like this in the city! 5 stars, absolutely would recommend!

I've lived here for over 3 years now, and I'm considering moving only because of a hike in rent (which is typical of renting anywhere in Austin, amirite?).

Pros:
Good location- i35 is close, southpark meadows shopping center is minutes away
Dog friendly and relatively clean - they keep the dog stations well stocked with baggies and empty the bins regularly. Maintenance is regularly cleaning up after careless dog owners and picking up litter. Trash is picked up regularly, although people do illegally dump furniture. The complex tries to haul it off as often as they can.
Good maintenance - the guys have been working here forever and are really attentive to calls. Never had a problem.
Great pools, good dog park, decent parking

Cons:
Not gated, but there is a security cart that rides around at night and parking cameras (there have been break-ins, but thr complex responded by beefing up security). 
Can be loud depending on neighbors and location of apartment. LOTS of dogs, so LOTS of barking. 
Appliances are cheeeeaaaapppp. Don't expect high end appliances. 
Plumbing is not the best, but it's okay. 
Flooring in some Apts is laminate "wood" flooring, aka vinyl which means it scratches easily, so beware. 

But overall a good place to live if the cons arent a problem for you.

My wife and I lived here and moved out October 19th. We were under the impression the building was brand new and that everything was energy efficient and we never realized until we moved how much we were spending here... Our electric bill at Old California was around $150 every month and it was just my wife and I, we didn't work from home or anything. We moved to an older building that has older appliances and my electric bill now is $60.00. We were able to get out of our lease after all the horrible situations we endured throughout our 6 months. Our apartment was broken into, our cars were broken into and work equipment was stolen, our upstairs neighbors were FROM HELL. We lived on a first floor then and live on a first floor now and I can totally tell you that Old California was built with cheap materials. People let their dogs swim in the pools. There is never any parking. This place is just all around horrible. We're so thankful that we were able to leave. The cops are literally at the apartments every other day. Just avoid this place in general if you want somewhere to live where you are happy to come home everyday.
Doesn't know how to run a leasing office.  Asked inappropriate questions that have nothing to do with renting an apartment.

Once moved in we found more and more things that did not work and needed repair.  They only have one maintenance person and there are many vacancies.  Then you get robbed by the utility bill.  It's more than my energy bill and car payment combined.  So far it has been disappointing.  We are hoping things improve.

Again, an outrageous utility bill and no hot water.  When you try and contact the management you get no reply.  So far, I am not impressed and should have read the reviews before signing the lease.   Plus, you pay a door side trash pickup that does not exist.

The first week I moved in I found there were (and still are) rats and cockroaches living in the walls. Pest control hasn't helped even though we pay for it. Management seems to avoid emails (guess they don't want anything in writing.) I've called several times and the leasing agent can never get me answers and tells me to wait until a manager gets back. An excuse he used several times over the course of 2 weeks. Does anyone even manage this place? The walls are warped and the doors do not close. Pool was deemed unsafe by an inspector and was under renovation half the time I lived there. Gym is 3 machines and 1 pair of free weights in a small room the size of a cubicle. Only thing I liked about this place was the location.

I lived here for a year long lease and I hope that my review and the multitude of other bad reviews is enough of a red flag to run in the opposite direction of this complex. 
The list of issues I experienced here starts with our A/C unit not working, and not getting repaired for a minimum of 4-6 weeks in the middle of summer, with little to no communication from management or maintenance on when it would be repaired (it ended up needing to be replaced, as well as the other 3 units in the same vicinity as my apartment, who also had a minimum of 4 weeks without A/C). We were offered no rent credit or other accomodations for the additional expenses of having to buy fans and keep cool, nor for the trauma of living in an apartment with an average nighttime temp of 85-90 degrees, for at least 4 weeks.

If you're still reading, I hope it's out of interest in the additional misfortune of living here, and not to see if there's a glimmer of good in my review. 

Another consistent problem I had reported was hearing animals shuffling around in the attic above my bedroom, and plumbing issues that were eventually discovered to be the side effect of rats infiltrating the apartment. This is an issue I consistently reported and asked for assistance with, and received none for months. When it was finally addressed, I was told that apparently this complex has had a long standing issue with rodents, for at least a year, and has not been able to fully stop the infestation.

Other things I experienced:
- random, sometimes unannounced, and rarely with 24 hour warning water shut offs. Sometimes just hot water, sometimes both
- various parts of the apartment degrading, either structurally leaning or wood rotting
- my cat developed an unknown allergy while living here, and has since recovered fully since leaving the residence. 
- loud leaf blowers at least a few times a week, for sometimes literal hours, blowing pollen and leaves down the parking lot - it echoes more than you think
- "trash valet" which you are required to pay for does not consistently pick up trash. This I am mostly indifferent about personally, but if you're paying $25 a month for someone to pick up trash from your door on a consistent schedule it's frustrating when you have hot stinky garbage at your door for days

Rats, roaches, hot water constantly going out and water outages constantly! My boyfriend and I tried to ask for help when we had the never ending roach infestation they said there was pest control but it never got better. There were rats coming into the apartment and surrounding units from what I heard. They just told us it was normal when/if they even reply to us, most the time they don’t even reply to us after phone or email. Lots of theft too - our car and other tenants cars were broken into and our mailboxes two times got broken into and mail stolen! They have a sign that says security camera but told us it doesn’t work! This was the worst renting experience of our lives! Save yourself and don’t move there!

The management is all but useless. The front office was great before the new crew got there and now it's absolutely awful. It takes forever for them to fix anything and good luck getting them to respond to an email. When something is over the head of the front office they tell you to email the regional manager who either doesn't exist or just refuses to check/respond to emails. The parking is awful, you lose hot water once every 2-3 weeks, the outlets are loose, and the AC units barely work and good luck making sure they even installed your heater correctly. Seriously don't move here find anywhere else to live.

I gave this place benefit of the doubt upon move in. The issues started upon moving in (I moved from out of state, without seeing the exact unit I’d be renting).
It was claimed to have been “newly updated.”
“New floors” were put in, laminate that is now peeling up in several places, especially the bathrooms where we consistently have plumbing issues. No hot water, leaking, sinks that are rusting out. The bugs are a constant problem, I hope you don’t mind roaches if you plan on residing here. And lots of them. Mice tend to break into your pantry as well.
On top of regular issues with plumbing, or counters and cabinets are falling apart. By “refurbished,” they mean spray paint everything and call it a day. Most of the bathroom cabinets are rotting out due to water damage.
As if none of that is bad enough, our AC unit has been out for OVER TWO MONTHS now. What a summer in TX. At this point all of my calls and emails about when it will be fixed are being ignored. They sent out the HVAC company last month, and since being told the unit needed to be replaced, they’ve been silent. We’ve left emails, voicemails, and no one is ever in the office. We are frankly being ignored, most likely since they aren’t willing to put the finances into it. (yay new management).
The mailboxes have routinely been broken into, and the pool has been empty since we moved in last November.
Our lease can’t end fast enough. PLEASE save yourself the stress and look elsewhere. There are better deals and places with better staff out there. In the meantime we are looking to file a lawsuit due to mold and bug issues.
This place is a HEALTH HAZARD.

I tend to take one star reviews with a grain of salt, but here I am writing one. I've lived here for one year and I cannot wait to get out. As mentioned in the other reviews, hot water has been a constant problem since I've moved in with it going out for days at a time. I will say it has been a couple of months since this has happened, so there might be hope. My AC has gone out now twice and, as other reviews have mentioned, the fix did seem to be a band-aid one. I'm not even sure what the original fix was because the maintenance gentleman and I had to communicate through Google Translate and the message of the solution wasn't quite clear. The previous manager, Jill, was awesome. However, she is gone now and everything has went downhill super quickly. If you think the office staff will actually be in the office when they say they are open, think again.

I originally chose this apartment complex, despite reading the reviews, because of the proximity to the UT bus stop, my work, and the fact that it was the only one in the area with a washer and dryer in the unit. Soon after moving in, I had so many plumbing issues with my shower where the faucet would break and water would run continuously. Several different plumbing companies were brought out and it was always poor fixes. The last one did hold, but I am super careful when turning the knobs now.  I will say back then maintenance response was quick, now not so much.

I mentioned above that I take one star reviews with a grain of salt. I've learned my lesson and I hope that those that are reading this one approach this apartment with caution.

All of the other 1-star reviews are 100% true. This place is by far the worst apartment I have ever lived in my 15 years of renting. INCESSANT water issues (flooding, leaking, no hot water). Weeks without hot water. Black mold. Puddles of water on the carpet from HVAC leaks. Burst pipes. Flooding. The electrical system is way past its rated useful life and in need of replacement. Response time is awful, and even emergency calls go unanswered. Do not move here!

After living here, it is apparent why the rent is low for the area. As others have mentioned, there are constantly plumbing issues that result in either the water being shut off entirely for hours/days at a time, or hot water being made unavailable for up to week-long stretches. The leasing office has also somehow gotten worse at responding to maintenance requests. I'm currently experiencing an issue with a stream of water pouring out of my AC unit onto the floor, and have yet to receive a single response despite calling and emailing multiple times a day (I hope whoever gets  my unit enjoys the black mold that will inevitably develop in the ceiling and walls). And for the cherry on top, the living room has started to flood every time it rains harder than a drizzle (have yet to receive a response on that issue as well).

Poor management
Never respond 
The units are falling apart 
Riddled with cockroaches, crickets, ants, silverfish 
Leaky faucets 
Faulty appliances 
Single pane windows, horrible in the summer and winter 
Laminate wood flooring coming off 
Hot water is shut off often 
Just don’t do it to yourself 
Live anywhere else but here

Moved out 2021. Served a 15 months term here.

Do you like your water constantly being off or cold? Does getting over 60 email notices of the water in the complex being broken in a single year sound like what you are looking for?

Do you want an organization where the person(s) at the top don't care about the legally binding lease unless it is good for them?

Would you like to pay for valet trash that rarely actually comes, so you can still get the exercise of taking your trash out yourself?

Does being in a complex built 40 years ago, but that feels as if it was never maintained, while paying prices that are very overpriced sound like the place for you?

Do you want lighting that flickers because of the wiring? Totally not a fire hazard, no worries….

Real talk. Having lived in a myriad of apartments across Florida, Illinois, and Texas, I can firmly say this was the absolute worst apartment experience we have ever had. I've lived in 400$, dingy, old, apartments in Florida, but at least there it wasn't stressful just trying to live. At least there the water worked, at least there the lights worked. At least there it was affordable.

Never again. Do yourself a favor, avoid the issues, look elsewhere

This apartment complex has so many issues. The biggest one is the plumbing. Since moving in over 18 months ago, we have had issues with the hot water. The water will get turned off (most times with little notice) for repairs for hours at a time. Management has constant excuses for the lack of hot water. Most recently, they are blaming the lack of available plumbers after the February winter storm. Before that they blamed it on a plumber who was not reputable after all and sold them bad parts. Last spring we didn't have access to hot water for several weeks and we had to rely on nearby friends and family to get a hot shower while waiting for the appropriate replacement parts to arrive to make the hot water repairs. Management repairs everything as cheaply as possible, so no issue is truly resolved. I have had my leaking kitchen sink fixed at least 5 times. Other issues include malfunctioning HVAC, a leaking roof, water damage from the leaking roof (which was "repaired" by their expert in less than 5 minutes), broken mailboxes (finally fixed after 7 months of being broken--management said USPS was responsible for the repairs and not them), and cockroaches. I would have moved sooner if we were not in the middle of a pandemic when my lease was up. The rent is not low enough to deal with all of these issues, and the community amenities are not appealing enough to justify paying this rental rate either.

These are things I have dealt with since I’ve been here the past 10 months:
- No hot water for nearly a month in the middle of winter. Plus at least 5 other hot water outages.
- Flooding inside apartment each time it storms.
- It takes several requests for them to get any maintenance work done.
- I was without blinds (which come with all units) for my first two months, and I called at least every other week. When they finally came, they simply nailed a sheet to a piece of plywood.

Overall, this place is known for frequent switches in management because of how truly awful it is. Save your money and live literally anywhere else.

You’ve been forewarned - do not live here. This apartment has the most incompetent management I’ve ever seen. They’re also crooks. We’ve been without hot water for a total of more than 20 days in the year I’ve lived here, and currently going on a 12 day streak. Management will do nothing to help or provide any time or abatement for your suffering. In fact, they will ignore you and hold you hostage in this hell hole they call livable. Please live anywhere else.

So first and foremost i did just move in about a week ago.  To my knowledge Greystone Flats is under new management and a new landlord (same people) since Oct.2019. Estaphany, Letty, & Bernadette have been sweet, professional, prompt, & have been great to deal with.

Upon moving in, there were some things wrong and/or missing but a quick call to Letty has solved most of the problems. She set up the work orders for us (new tenant , our profile was not yet set) and sent her maintenance team our way to help us.

The lead handyman is mainly a Spanish speaker so we had some miscommunication talking to him about some of our issues with the apartment. He thought it was one thing but we insisted it was definitely  the other. We went back to the office to clear the air about what was going on. Letty was bilingual and was able to translate for us and get to the bottom of it. Next thing we know our problem was solved. Thank you LETTY!!!

There was another pressing need we needed done asap. They did what they could at the time but unfortunately couldn't get it done with the team they had. They sent a specialist on by to our apt., and in the meantime Bernadette (Supervisor) came with a couple of solutions to accommodate us quite swiftly.  (Which solved our current problem).

--There are still some things they will be working on still but they are not pressing needs at the moment and do not hinder our life.--- (quite minor but would be nice)

In our personal experience, by far the management team was very helpful , personable, professional, and compassionate. Estephany really sealed the deal on our decision to rent here and was easy to talk to (some walkthroughs can be boring and awkward), Letty was on it with our repairs and great with communicating status updates, Bernadette was fast to come up with solutions and did her best to make things right.

Some quick advice,... at times when things goes sideways, it's easy to just flare up and automatically hate the world. But when you give others with the same amount of dignity as you would like to receive in return, things usually work out.  This is a new management/landlord  team  and it is about a 30yr old complex, things are bound to be faulty or stop working. But give them a chance to right the wrongs.

I have lived at Greystone Flats for just over a year and have renewed until next February. I really enjoy this location. Northwest Hills/Far West Blvd has what I need. It's quiet and I have HEB right around the corner. The Domain and Downtown are near and I'm right off Mopac just south of 183.

The management team is very polite. Yoly is smart and has always been helpful to me. She takes the time to answer questions quickly, she is approachable, and genuinely cares for the community and residents. I admire her professionalism. 

Many of these apartments are renovated or currently under renovation. My apartment is not renovated, and from time to time I have to put a service request in, but maintenance gets to it so promptly.  The retro design of my two bedroom is neat. I have a bar in my living room :). My office is located in the dining area and I have two large walk-ins in my master bedroom.  Last but not least, this community is one of the few in the area that already has a washer and dryer in them.

We moved to Greyston Flats last week. Obviously because we are new, we have tended to ask many things to the leasing center. And, the answer has been really good and diligent. Jolie as manager is really good. She always takes care of each request that we ask her. In addition, she is too kind and with a good treatment to us.
The maintenance staff (Eduardo and Adrian)is also very diligent and does the job really well.
Thank you for your great reception for us in this new country. Blessings.

I just moved a week ago. my unit is renovated recently with all brand new appliances. 
everything is new and clean. Honestly, the price was over my budget. However, I decided to move in here after I had a conversation with the office manager (I am not sure I can leave her name on the Internet). She is so kind and always tries to listen to me. As a international student, for me, A person who is always trying to listen to me and help me is much important than the facility. I heard some apartments do not care about their renter once they signed the document. However, she is not that person.

Rent increase by $200 3 months into 12 month lease, permissible by extremely vague lease addendum that is not sent with tenant copy of lease but the office has. Pool never been opened. Elevator broken for 2 months

My partner and I have lived here for five years, and have even witnessed changes in leasing management, and we have never once thought about leaving. Management responds pretty quickly, monthly pest control, routine community functions like pool parties and even food drives. The complex is older, and well loved, but well maintained. We’re minutes from downtown, but far away enough that evenings are quiet. 

When we first moved to Austin, we lived in a studio apartment on campus that wanted to raise our rent by half, within the first year of living there. Since living at Magnolia Court, our rent increases annually, but it’s way more accommodating to our income.

We love Magnolia Court for making us feel at home in Austin.

Do you want a VERY affordable place to live 10 minutes from Downtown? This is the place for you! These apartments are a bit older but they have put effort into updating them. The grounds are pleasant and the staff is wonderful. Felicia has gone out of her way to help me on multiple occasions on everything from moving within the complex to accidently overpaying rent. Sometimes maintenance is a little slow getting to things but for the most part, everything is efficient and excellent.

I came to know that someone turned in a notice and a one bedroom apartment became available today. I talked to three leasing agents to see what I should do to get the apartment and was trying to fill in an application online. But, online application keeps complaining missing required fields. I called leasing office and they said put NA for all empty fields but it still keeps complaining missing fields. So, I asked the leasing office if I could scan and email the application but it won't allow me to print without the missing fields. 
Then someone from leasing office called me and said someone had put in a deposit and so it is not available. I just wasted four hours talking to leasing office and trying to get the application put in. It just sucks from start to finish.

I just moved in and am so happy to be here!

I have what has been called "an impossible standard of cleanliness." I am totally aware of this, so I always plan on having to clean any new place prior to moving in. Much to my surprise, I did not have to do that upon moving into my new place here at Magnolia Court! This is the first time that has EVER happened. I was thrilled! 

From the moment I just came to check the place out, the staff has been super sweet and helpful. I could not be happier here. YAY for Magnolia Court! :)

It is a decsent place to live.  Property is a little old but you are close to I35.  Pretty quite around the evenings.  Bus routes are close to front gate and there  are a couple of bars within walking distance.

This place is nice. Office staff are great. Maintenance is quick to respond. Rates are alright. Place is usually kept pretty nice. All in all

Downsides:
* If you have a pet, be prepared to fork out a lot of money for pet deposit $400, pet fee $400 and monthly pet rental ($10/mo).
* Don't expect to pay your rent with your debit/credit card. That is unless you want to pay the $30 service fee.

If you can deal with the downsides, this place is great.

The move in process was super easy and Paloma was amazing at making sure I moved in quickly with a speedy approval. The pool is clean and this place is so pet friendly! Thank you ARYA for a cool summer.

We are set to move in 11/24.  Molly has been the best leasing agent!  Very patient, very helpful and so sweet!  We visited the complex in June and we were impressed with how nice everything looks.  The apt she showed us was very nice.  We were concerned that our king size bed wouldn't fit but the master bedroom is so big that we're not worried about it fitting!  
This is the best value for your buck by far!
Highly recommend!

The grounds are always kept up, and now the parking lots have been re-sealed. This apt complex looks brand new! 

My apartment is very sound-proof. Most people here are retired seniors, so it very safe.
I would have given my apartment five stars, but my apartment is so small there is not room for a dining table. Other than that I love this place.

Austin is getting more and more expensive, and there are 150 new people moving here everyday. Needless to say the rents here are high. This little apartment has a competative rent for the area. Staff is helpful and friendly. I have been here 5 years and love it.

When I first moved to this complex it was perfect for my budget and it had everything I needed. I lived here for 4 years and for the most part it was a pleasant experience. However, once the new manager took over and the maintenance staff changed everything went downhill from there. Communication was erratic and not clear; orders were unfulfilled, and services were not done. I went a whole year with the paint on my tub falling off and was giving a ton of excuses as to why the order service could not be completed. The trash valet doesn’t get picked up within schedule and there’s no way to opt out of the service. The property is old, built in 69, but I was willing to overlook that due to the “low” rent at the time. The current rent prices do not match the location, age of the buildings, quality of services or overall value of the units. Just go up the stairs of the building next to the office and you’ll get a feeling of the conditions you’ll be living in. There are newer apartments in better locations for the same price range.

This is the worst apartment complex I have ever lived in. The bathtub peels it’s so nasty I can’t even take a bath. There was mold all over the bathtub when moved in and called matenance and informed them they looked at it and look at me and said it wasn’t mold to my face and wouldn’t do anything. I have an auto immune and it’s made me terribly ill. The kitchen is minuscule for the price you pay. The water constantly leaks and there is no water pressure. The railings outside wave if a wind comes worrying me that they are incredibly unsafe. The walls are paper thin and the neighbors have complained about noise from just existing which I’ve never had a noise complaint from another apartment before. The dishwasher isn’t installed correctly and fell out on me. The AC doesn’t work at all and has been complained about many times in which maintenance never shows up to fix. It will day cooling to get down one degree cooler for over 4 hours and only changes at night when it gets cooler out. The floor in the bathroom is coming up due to the moisture in there and a non working fan. If I cook anything in the kitchen I have to open a window or die of smoke inhalation. If you miss one day late on rent they charge you a late fee which is fine but then also send you a note in your door about getting evicted. And give you only 4 days to get out even when paid. I have to call every time to remind them I paid my rent. The list of things wrong with this place just goes on and on. Please please do yourself a favor and look into one of the other apartments nearby because the ONLY good thing about this place is it’s close to mopac and HEB. Seriously this place is a dump. Do not be fooled by anything they show you because you will not be getting the place they show you!!!! Renter beware!!!!!

The complex is situated right across from a supermarket and a bus stop.  The primary reason I chose to live here was for this convenience.  However, for the past 3 years, the property has had issues communicating with their renters.  During their renovation process, less than 24 hours was often provided to move cars or have them towed.  There have been several occasions where no one was at the front office during business hours without notification.  A new online payment system was implemented in 2016 before rent was due and the registration code required was emailed only after rent was due.  Maintenance requests were moved to a new system that only allowed submissions through an iPhone app or an online portal. If the online portal errors on you, you are given a non-working phone number for support.

Located north of downtown Austin in a very nice area that is surrounded by family suburbs. It is walking distance to an HEB and also there is a bus running to UT campus very close. The management is nice and the people who live their are nice also. The only drawback is that sometimes the front office does not pick up the phone and you have to call more than once to reach them. Overall a nice place to live and I would recommend this place to older students and young professionals who are looking for a quite place away from the main city.

Don't be fooled by the decent reviews for this complex. The leasing agents are super nice but If you choose to live here, you will be greeted with incompetent and negligent management. Multiple units are infested with roaches and there are loud noises and parties every night, all night. Maintenance will be rude to you if you place any work orders. They also rarely empty the trash compactor and the scent will spread all the way across to the complex. This place is a dirty mess, and a horrible leasing experience. I would rate 0 stars if I could.

This is not a place to live. Other than having the worst management ever, you gonna live with mice. We had to move just after four months before our lease ends. It is a DIRTY place. Did you get it? dirty means DIRTY

Multiple large maintenance issues that they let sit for days or weeks at a time. Previously dealt with no electricity in the kitchen that took them more than a week to fix. Currently dealing with water damage from a leak in another apartment. Mold is growing. Visible green and black mold. Yes they’re aware of it. They’ve been aware of it for the last 7 days. 

What’s been done is they’ve put a few holes in the wall.  What’s yet to be done is fix the wall in the hallway by the stairs, fix the walls in the laundry room, fix the molding and door frame in the laundry room, fix the molding down the stairs, and rip up or dry the carpet. 

José has done a great job, but the apartments are VERY POORLY BUILT. We’ve been here since November and had four major maintenance issues (hot water heater, electrical, AC (still an issue), and now water damage. I do not recommend that anyone move here. It has perks but they’re not worth it.

I have had a really good experience here at Oakville especially with the new changes being made. The staff is awesome. I love Jeremy and Emily they are the nicest people and super helpful with everything. The only bad thing I can say is parking sucks!!!

I lived in bell tech for 6 years, it used to be rattan creek an imt property, the imt staff knew us and was so helpful and caring, the bell tech staff is rude and after you sign your lease does not care about you, the parking is horrible, my brothers car and at least 5 other cars were broken into last year alone. The back gate does not lock so people can just come in, the walls are thin so you can definitely hear your neighbors. They never call you back and you have to call more than once to get anybody to care. The pool is always closed crowded or dirty. I used to the complex but now am moving. It’s no longer a safe fun place to live, not a community, but now a residence:(

PLEASE STAY AWAY...
The Staffs, Assistant Manager or Manager are Rule. No Help if you got a problem while you live. their job just want your money as many as they can even you moved out already. No Parking lot after 6-7pm. Parking Area is dirty. So, very be careful if you still try to live.
Love the community and the response of the maintenance team. The walking trail around the community is very peaceful and amazing. Plus the office staff is very responsive and care for your needs.

We've been here for seven years. The staff I want to discuss has not been here very long, but it doesn't take long to recognize sincerity, desired helpfulness, job-intelligence, and courtesy. This complex is obviously a "happy" place to work because everyone from top management down are always smiling. Specifically, we want to call out Daniel in maintenance, Kendra who seems to do everything, plus Estella and Julia - the top brass. Everyone in every business tries to give good service, but this group delivers stellar service. You make our lives very pleasant.

I normally do not submit reviews. But after my experience with the management and stay at this community for over 2 and a half years, I felt compelled to express my frustration. I have lived in this community three separate times each under a different management company, Bell Tech being the worse!!! These apartments are located in a great area which is why I stayed for two years but their management and maintenence crew are horrible!!! The apartments are 17 years old and need a lot more attention then they are receiving. My apartment had a huge water leak the whole length of my stay and the maintenance never came out to repair the separating drywall from the water leak in my apartment. The gates around the community frequently are inoperative, the trash compactor is always full and overflowing with trash, the parking situation is atrocious, and the management has no desire to correct any of it. To make things worse when I moved out they sent me a cleaning bill for over 400$ when I left the apartment in the same condition I recieved it. I disputed the charges with Leo the manager at the time and they still sent me to collections. I could go on and on about how bad the management is at this community and if I could post pictures to this review I would!!! Bottom line, if you are thinking about moving into this community make sure you throughly perform a walk through of the apartment before signing the lease, marking any and everything you see. Especially bath tub not resurfaced, 120$ fine as I found out!!!! My suggestion to you if you are reading this before moving to this community would be to save yourself a headache and find another community to live in.

Truth be told look elsewhere.  The management staff here is rude and doesnt care a bit about the residents. Maintenance issues took forever to  be addressed when Bell Partners took over.  Gated community-well sometimes, usually the gates were broken and they were to cheap to fix them.  Grossly overpriced for terrible service and THEY WILL GOUGE YOU ON YOUR MOVE OUT...Everyone I know who has lived there has gotten a huge bill when they moved out for bogus cleaning charges even when the apartments were left in better shape than when you moved in.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND LOOKING ELSEWHERE

We moved here from Iowa 2 years ago and love the complex.  Great for the kids and close enough to downtown or the Hill Country to get out and enjoy the area.  Apartment was upgraded when we moved in and is still like new, pool area is great and the running trail out back can keep you on your toes.

Bell Tech Corridor is the perfect family starter apartment complex. The location is so convenient being close to multiple schools. We absolutely love all of the great food places that are within walking distance. The environment is fantastic, beyond our expectations. We have started our own little family here and we couldn't have picked a greater place.

Currently living in the three bedroom at Bell Tech Corridor. Its great. really spacious, nice new kitchen and cabinets. So far no complaints, it looks just as nice on the outside as it does on the inside. The staff there are so nice, they are helpful and are quick to any requests i need. It is in a really great spot on Parmer lane. quick access to HEB, 183 and mopac.

This is a great living community. Nice apartments, great amenities, and the location is fantastic. However, the property is aging, and the management and maintenance are having issues keeping up with needed repairs changes. These are second owners/management company, and not as customer friendly as the first owners, but they are getting much better. They have new staff who know and appreciate the tenants. They are renovating as they can, and new design/colors are very nice.

I have been in various Bell owned properties, mainly in NC where the headquarters is located.  Moved to Austin in March, and I am assuming the overall apartment quality of the city is higher than in North Carolina.

Pros:  Bell Tech Corridor is located in North Austin, near some pretty large employers, Apple etc. and conveniently located near a Metro Rail station (I work downtown) and various HEB(s) and shops.  Little Woodrows is a great neighborhood bar you can either bike or walk to and there is a park located right outside the gate's of the apartment complex.  I rent a one bedroom which I would say is reasonably priced for Austin (though outrageous for NC) so I cannot complain about the price.  The apartment is nicer than any of the other properties I've rented from them and offers more than enough space for my partner and I.  

The grounds need more attention, as kids throw toys and trash from balconies and people leave beer cans/bottles at the pool.  I also wish they would clean the pool more (at another apartment I saw them do it before 10am every morning).  Like everyone else says, the parking is atrocious.  I don't know who came up with the idea of reserved parking for $30 a month (I've seen this in other places in Austin too) but it's complete BS.  I have never experienced a place where I have to pay extra to park my car or either park across the entire complex or on the street.  This nor the $25 valet trash fee was explained to us, and as it turns out I end up having to take my own trash out on Fri/Sat anyways.  The dumpster situation also needs to be handled due to it looking like the dump on days when Valet trash isn't running.

I've had good and bad experiences with Bell Management.  The overall feeling that I get is that they couldn't give two craps about their residents.  I transferred from a property in NC and got a whopping $900 bill for carpet replacement (Apparently they have to replace the carpet for the entire apartment, even if one room is damaged) which left  sour taste in my mouth.  They also didn't bother to tell me they were sending the bill to collections even though I live in another Bell property and I would assume their computer databases could access all of their properties accounts and the manager here could inform us that we had an outstanding balance. 

Would I rent from Bell again?  Maybe, if the price is right. But they need to work on their customer service.

First of all I would like to say that there are NO flying roaches here, what a treat to experience here in Austin Texas. 
Management never has any complaints about me and I never have any complaints about them, pool is working 99% of the time and open all year, floor plans are spacious but simple keeping costs affordable, grounds are basic but clean, keeping it affordable, the pool and hot tub are luxury, making it awesome Big windows and lots of light, neighbors are normal and they don’t put random
rude letters on your door unless you forget to pay rent.

We recently rented apartment for my granddaughter who is going to school in Austin.  We have had such a wonderful experience with the office staff.  Margaret is so helpful and I called her to let her know the toilet was not flushing. The maintenance staff was there right away and fixed the toilet. We live 5 hours away and I can honestly say that the staff goes out of their way to help you. My son went to school and lived at these apartments years back.  He had only good things to say.  Thank you Margaret for all your help.

Very bad experience, don't trust the staff on what they say. Get everything written on the document. I was told that an apartment is available and as soon I completed the leasing document in 40- 45 minutes with successful payment, the apartment is leased out. They just make excuses and never understand the pain of the customer. the staff is just trying to exploit the surge in demand, Hence be careful.

My husband and I moved into the apartments going on 5 years ago, and we LOVE them!!  Where do I start?  My husband and I moved into the apartments going on 5 years ago, and we LOVE them!!  Where do I start?  My husband and I moved into the apartments going on 5 years ago, and we LOVE them!!  Where do I start?  My husband and I moved into the apartments going on 5 years ago, and we LOVE them!!  Where do I start?  The management is top notch with the manager, Margaret, being a wonderful, caring person.  The other staff in the office are friendly and care about the residents that live here.  Now to maintenance!  I can only say WOW!  The lead maintenance person , Daniel, is friendly, knows how to fix almost everything, and always willing to listen when I have a problem.  I cannot say enough good things about how the maintenance staff keep this apartment looking fantastic.  Yes,these are older apartments, but the location is great, and the rent is pretty decent.  This is one of the best apartment complexes I have ever lived in when thinking about the staff and the care they put into this place.  I love it!!!

My husband and I moved to Mackenzie Pointe as college freshman and we were lucky that we chose them because for 16 years they have been nothing short of amazing, attentive, helpful, friendly people in a fun community (the pools and pool parties will be missed!). We lived in 4 different apartments there as we upgraded jobs and eventually added a little one to our family, and each apartment had ample space (ridiculously fantastic closets) and any maintenance calls were answered quickly. We stayed so long because we were treated like people instead of an income source, and we were valued. We only left because we purchased a house, but we still plan to visit frequently!

Pests are very prominent here. Cockroaches and millipedes run rampant. Pest control doesn't know how to do their jobs because pests keep coming back. On top of that we have to pay for their terrible job. There's construction ALL the time, specifically very early in the mornings. Cars get broken into frequently (happened to my roommate). The structure of the apartment is awkward because the floors are sloped and uneven. Walls progressively crack as well. There's huge issues that occur periodically, like pipes bursting. The only redeeming quality of this place is the low rent. It's the only thing that makes me sign the lease every year. I already exhausted my chances with this place and thankfully this is my last year here.
I moved in about a month ago and recently found out someone was murdered in my building the apartment did not disclose this information to me

Excellent apartment complex. I lived here for about a year and a half on the first floor. The units are clean and spacious. I never really had any maintenance issues but if I did, they were always super quick for repairs. The property is well taken care of and maintained, office staff is nice and helpful. Everyone is quite respectful of others so I never really had noise issues. Hands down the best complex I've lived in.

After staying here for a year (2019) 
Here are some reasons in no particular order that made me upset with the community.

1) Changing the parking policy and not producing proper prior notification causing our car to be towed. Management only offered an apology and were unable to get us back our money for the tow. ($300+)

2) The neighbors smoke inside their house and it seeps Management took forever (3+ weeks) to come and do something about it and in the end they’ve only minimized the smell by slightly blocking the outlets.

3) The electricity is always going off throughout the day. I constantly find my alarm clocks all reset because of the power going out.

4) There’s only one Trash bin in the whole complex and it’s always full. 

5) The gate is broken very often and it allows for everyone to get in so that’s just a false sense of security.

6) The treadmills have not worked the couple of times I’ve been so there was no point for me to keep going.

All in all - not good management.

So, I'll try to give the short story. 

Pipes have been clocked for months. They've tried to bill me for blinds (that I never touched.)

They haven't started valet trash although that is the excuse they provide with rental rates being raised. 

They began a new policy for parking with tags, but did not ensure that all residents were provided with signed documents and cannot verify that everyone was informed. My rental car (parked for 1 night) was towed. I asked for documentation, signed a month ago and they did not want to provide it. When I went to the office Melinda said she did not want to deal with it. Mike (the "manager") ran out of the office. And to add insult to injury, there are bugs all the time. They say that an exterminator is coming and I've taken the day off to wait and no one came. Just crappy!

They have really nice apartments and are maintained very will by their maintenance staff, however the customer service as far as the Manager Mike and the Assistant Manager Melinda is terrible. I love the location of my apt. It's not in the heart of everything but it close to everything. Downtown, local stores, parks and food are all with a short distance. Perfect for a college student or small family. Being that this is a newer building, I haven't had many problems but the office crew is very helpful when I need something, especially Julianne.

These apartments are great, it is an awesome environment to be around also very child friendly. These apartments provide a playground, pool as well as track and doggy park! How cool is that? The staff are reasonable and will help you in any and every circumstance at hand. There are also so many great food places circling the apartments so if you are hungry... you wont be for long!!! I enjoy living here very much.
Nice apartment with easy access to I35 enjoy the floor plan and the great neighbors I have.
I feel very safe at this apartment. Anytime I need anything they always call me back and are very prompt.
Maintenance is great , respond very promptly and fix the issue . Office staff is very kind.
Price for rent is super reasonable here and the staff cares about their tenants and never rude. The apartments are being well taken care of .
There is nothing I did not like about this community.

SO. Let me warn off anyone who plans on coming to lease here...YES the property is beautiful. YES the pricing looks great. I came on Saturday, 2 days ago to look at the property and from the very beginning it was an absolutely horrible experience. The managers are SO very rude ! The woman,Lisa, who was doing my paperwork and giving me the tour was telling me that it was her first day (because she knew absolutely nothing) and that she didnt like the way they conducted business so I would probably never be seeing her again (why would she tell me that???). 2nd, the pricing on the website is untrue and the manager, Mike, gave a complete bs excuse for this...no matter the reason, people are interested in apartments according to information they see ONLINE, so shouldnt it be most imperative to be sure that it is CORRECT ?? And then when I changed my mind on which apartment I wanted to lease, they acted as if I was the burden. I also paid the hundreds of dollars in a deposit and was put on a "waiting list" but do you think they could still give a concrete answer on when the apartments would be ready?? NO. Hopefully the price and quality make up for it.

They will tow you and any of your friends cars out of the guest parking area. The tow company they use has 1 star on google and is a very sketchy experience. When I went to get my car the place did not even ask me for an ID. When I contacted management they did not care or even respond. They will offer you a good promotional rate to move in and then try to up your rate 10-15% when you go to renew it. Decent property but poor management from storage units in the garage consistently being empty because they refuse to charge a reasonable rate to threats of fines for having a doormat. 

Beware of any units that claim to have a view or a balcony. A lot of the units have a 1x6 foot balcony so they can say it technically has a balcony. A lot of the units claiming to be river view units will be blocked by the trees. They do not offer paddle board storage for free ($100 when I last checked) and the dock is a tiny floating one and they do not even know the code for it.
Plenty of other apartments in the area that have much better reviews.

I would highly recommend checking those out first before settling for the Berkshire Riverview.
I really enjoy living here. The amenities and staff make it a great community to live in.

All the benefits of living in this condominium are overshadowed by the lack of security! Despite having entry sensors, some access gates remain open 24/7 due to poor maintenance. There are no security cameras in the garage or storage areas, and no camera where deliveries are made. The garage gate is frequently broken, allowing anyone to enter. My experience has been frustrating: just two weeks after moving in, two locked bicycles were stolen, and the storage unit I pay $55 per month for was broken into, with all my belongings stolen. There is a severe lack of maintenance, security, and cleanliness, and a strong odor in the common areas. This condominium, although close to downtown and the river trail, offers very little security and shows no signs of improvement.

People's cars get broken into every other night. I'm not even exaggerating. Also, one of my friends had his bike stolen, his cage broken into 2 times, and his motorcycle raided 2 times. Security here is poor. It's legitimately a big reason I want to move out.

You know that scene in Home Alone, where Kevin's sister tells him: "Kevin, you're what the French call les incompetent?" That's how I'd describe the Berkshire Riverview staff. 

Now, working in an apartment leasing office is a hard, difficult job....Actually, not it's really not at all. It's a job mediocre people drift into when they don't have any actual skills or ambition. So that means the people in charge of keeping your home safe and running are one step above Walmart employees.

This has come to a head lately, as there is an EPIDEMIC of car break-ins. People's cars are outright BEING STOLEN OUT OF THE GARAGE! And they do nothing.

Management is "getting quotes" for a private security company. They've been "getting quotes" for a year and change. Those must be some thorough quotes!

Why is it taking so long? Probably because of the inept deadbeats stumbling around the leasing office all day. If you live here, your car might get stolen, but the leasing people work 9-6, live elsewhere, and probably make $12 an hour. So what do they care?

Answer: they don't. This apartment complex is incredible unsafe. I haven't even touched on all the other problems lately: wifis, broken amenities that aren't fixed, non-functioning elevators, etc. 

Don't live here. And don't heed the obviously fake positive reviews.

The apartments themselves are well built, repairs are quick and common areas are clean. The biggest problem is security - I've been robbed 3 times in the past 2 years here. Most of the residents here have either gotten locks broken, or garaged cars broken into and vandalized. Paying premium prices should mean basic security.

Riverview Apartments are a great complex to live and has easy access to I-35, Downtown, and East Austin Hotspots. The staff is very respectful and friendly. Ife and  Angeline are the two leasing staff I mainly communicated with and each of them goes out of there way to quickly answer questions and resolve issues. 

The complex manager Justin is a class act as well. He was very understanding when my family had to break out lease and move abruptly. The office was kind, respectful, and courteous to us from the day we came to tour until our final day as tenants. 

I forgot to mention all of the community events they throw for the residents. They are fun and help you meet your neighbors, which makes the feel/vibe of the complex more friendly and positive. 

I highly recommend Riverview for those of your having a hard time deciding which property to lease within the area. 

You will enjoy your time there!

Absolutely one of the worst customer services that you will ever receive as a resident. The apartments here could be cheaper than the rest of the area, but the management group makes it their full time mission to charge each resident some ridiculous fees to make up for their loss. They towed my car twice from the resident parking garage. I woke up early to start my day and go workout; the first thing I find is my car was gone, what's a more miserable feeling than that? they didn't even want to pay the $200 towing fees. I had to Uber everywhere that morning. The manager Justin didn't want to do anything about it and even took a defensive position blaming me for making this awful situation. When I read the rest of the negative reviews before I moved in,  I didn't think it will be this bad of an experience. I definitely advise against joining this residential complex and will personally rather paying a higher rent somewhere else where they respect their residents than continuing to live here. The complex has so much availability now because no one is joining them and very few residents renew their leases. You don't get what you pay for. The management makes it their full time mission to increase silly fines and fees on residents to make up for their general loss. Nonetheless the elevators and floors are filthy most of the day from dog and trash smells. some residents leave their trash on the door front and the smell of the hallway is disgusting.

Riverview Apartments also stole my security deposit and created additional charges after I moved out, which seems to be their standard operating procedure based on the reviews left by other former tenants.

During the walk through inspection prior to moving out, Delma, a Riverview Apartment employee, confirmed to my wife and I that we fulfilled our duty of returning the unit in the condition we received it. Delma actually praised us for the condition the apartment was left in!

If they tell you it's a deposit when you move in, do not plan on getting it back. If getting your deposit back is important to you because you’ve done the right thing, I would not recommend living at the Riverview Apartments.

Lived here for 2 years. Riverview stole my security & pet deposit after move out.

One of Riverview's staff members told my fiance and I previously that we didn't need to spackle over holes in the wall & that we could leave them. After moving out, we were charged $443 because they spackled / painted over the holes....

When I confronted Riverview via email, the girl (Delma) who I was writing back and forth with just dropped off and stopped replying...because you know, damage control. Instead of just owning up to their mistake they forced me to foot the bill. That's just slimy. 

Don't be fooled by their "professional" personalities in person, they won't solve real issues when they matter.
---------------------------------------------------------------

PROS

- Location. Being able to walk the trails & boardwalk   10 minutes walking distance to Rainey St & 15 minutes to downtown

- 1 BR APT. Roomy 1095 sq ft with a full bath & half bath. 
---------------------------------------------------------------

CONS

- Leaking fridge, broken door handle & TP dispenser upon move in. No new filters for fridge water. Two lights went out in the first 2 months. They don't do real maintenance prior to move-in.

- You can hear dogs barking through the walls.

- The dog poop epidemic here is unacceptable. It's not uncommon to find dog poop in the stairwells, elevators, or parking garage. It's all over backyard, gated areas, and side areas of Riverview. When it rains, the dog poop smell is absolutely atrocious.

- Riverview isn't smoke-free as advertised. People smoke off their balconies and throw their cig buds wherever they please. This especially sucks when you want to open your balcony door to let fresh air into your apartment and you're forced to smell cig smoke. One morning I woke up and found my dead plant had caught on fire and had been scorched. My chain smoking neighbor above me had dropped his cig buds into my potted plants. 

- Coffee Machine was frequently broken or out of coffee.

- The TV near the grill area was broken for months before they fixed it.

- Backyard & Dog Park area is so mucky / muddy that I stopped taking my dog back there. 

- Their online support is a hit or miss. It's either extremely fast or they don't respond at all.

Pros:
Quality construction, great location, lots of community social activities, ammeneties (including free yoga class 3 nights a week), sound (my unit faces the pool, and even on block party holidays, almost no noise comes through the double-pained windows), friendly neighbors of all demographics, pre-wired for AT&T Gig Fiber (other services are available, you're not held captive to one)

Cons:
Things like losing your barcode sticker or key fob (which is required to get in any door) out a lot to replace ($100 ), individual unit doors lock automatically (you can flip a switch to disable, but it goes back the next time you lock your door from the outside.), if you get locked out after hours, your only option is to call a locksmith, and this last one is just my floor plan (ADA studio , even though I'm not disabled).  Mine has NO storage space. Nothing at all in the bathroom, no pantry, and only one long hall closet. I think 1 br and up are different.

These apartments are a great place , right on the river and close to all downtown venues. The amenities are nice as well free bike and paddle board rentals and they throw neat community events every month.

The worst part about this place is the parking garage.  The rows and corners are very tight and people drive like morons.  If you work 8-5 add a few couple of minutes to your morning commute, turning right in the morning is a huge pain in the butt and forget about making a left. I’ve reported it and all they did was run bleach through the AC lines which burned my eyes and nose for days. Next.. You never know what you will get into noise-wise and how well the construction is.. I feel this varies from place to place.. but.. you never truly know til you live there. You can hear a lot of things here.. from aggressive walking, walking in general, walking up and down stairs, vacuuming, to arguments / loud talking and showers / water turning off and on.. like unbelievably loud. There is also an on-going roach/bug problem. I get that it’s in the trees but there will be endless roaches dead and alive.. if/when and you will need to constantly treat / ask for pest control. It’s not automatic that they treat inside your apartment. You have to request it. The maintenance is fast but they don’t always fix it the first time. This place is definitely not worth the price tag here given you can move into newer construction for the same and get better. Lastly, if you are noise sensitive you should definitely look elsewhere.

Your experience may vary greatly depending on what part of the property you're on.

Management: Some are overly/fake nice, and seem to just be there for the office job and nothing more. Some are fantastic and have that truly amazing above-and-beyond customer service attitude. I've had some great interactions and mind-blowingly horrendous and condescending interactions (management downplaying an emergency then refusing to apologize for making me feel incredibly unsafe, inadvertently exposing their lack of knowledge surrounding the dangers of water around live electrical wiring. Who knows, maybe they'll apologize after reading this! That'd be nice.). They're very good about communicating when work will be done on the property that will cause disruption.

Location/Grounds: Excellent. They're big on appearances so the grounds are always kept up and the location is fantastic. There's minimal vandalism.

Apartment: My building was never sealed off, meaning free range for all pests to enter. Spring - late fall there's cockroaches, scorpions, beetles, and spiders. For whatever reason Management decided not to do anything when they learned the building was not sealed until I reported rodents in the ceiling. It's possible this problem has since been fixed. But the apartments are beautifully designed, open, the private porches are amazing, and there's plenty of parking.

Smoking: It's against the lease but people do it anyway. I frequently smell pot blowing through my vents and outside select buildings on the property. If you talk to the right person in Management they really try to find who it is so they can address it. If you talk to anyone else their solution is to directly ask everyone if they smoke (residents know it’s against the lease), so everyone says 'no' and that's the end of the conversation. It's hit or miss. Guests who smoke cigarettes are usually pretty courteous if you tell them it’s a smoke-free property. Be weary if smoke-free is your reason for seeking out this property.

Maintenance: They're super polite but decently grumpy. I've only had a couple issues that required maintenance and had to ask twice both times before the issue was resolved.

Though it's advertised as a smoke-free property, individuals can be seen out smoking after management's office hours like clockwork. During COVID a ton of dog-owners moved in...now there are dogs barking throughout the day, often when one starts every dog in the building will start. Nearly every night the dogs will all start howling for a few minutes at a time, stop, then start up again. You'll find pests inside throughout the year. According to pest control, part of the problem is likely because not all buildings are sealed off entirely and some pipes are fully exposed. The exposed pipes means your apartment will smell on rainy days or if you like to have windows open.
If you don't mind the noise, bugs, and smells coming from the sinks, it's not bad.

I'm a graduating UT student who has lived at Ballpark for three years. It's not "luxury" by any means but it is a fair price for what you get. I will say that there can be a large discrepancies unit to unit on conditions. If you can, request an apt near the entrance of the complex because those have been the most recently renovated. Maintenance will fulfill requests but they have a system of prioritizing requests. So if your toilet breaks or AC goes out, maintenance (who lives onsite!) will be there ASAP-same day! If it's a lighting issue or something that can wait, you will definitely experience a delay. The worst park about living at Ballpark has been the mailboxes. In the past year, they have been broken into twice and we have to drive to the post office to receive our mail. It's a pain, and the worst part of living here. All in all, I would recommend Ballpark to any UT student looking to save some coins. There is a commute but you get used to it quickly, the price is better than anything in wampus, and you get more space.

Lived here for many months now, and here's what I would say I wish I knew before moving in:

Pros
- Great location - easily on I-35 within 5 min and nearby HEB, gas stations, restaurants, and walking distance to the river
- Fast maintenance (although they don't tell you when to expect them)
- Fees are low, about $10 for pest control monthly, $18 for trash collection, and $13 for renter's insurance. 

Cons
- The actual floorplan neither matches their website or the one in their videos.
- The so called "plank style wood flooring" is poorly-installed vinyl flooring that is peeling up with lots of glue gunk. The filtered water spigot also doesn't exist. 
- The units were renovated 8-9 years ago, so lots of wear and tear, and the only energy efficient appliance is the combo washer/dryer.
- They do have a roach problem, and the pest control isn't automatic, so you have to request visits. 
- You're billed collectively for water divided based on occupancy and sqft of your unit, so if your neighbor has a leak, you could end up with a hefty bill. 
- The water heater is outside the apartment in a non-insulated wood shed, so a 1/3rd of my electricity bill goes to water heating costs. 
- The furnace is probably 20 years old, but it does heat the apartment well, just slowly.
- There are over 100 units all sharing a gym with 5(?) machines

- Finally the sound proofing - what I most wish I knew about before moving in, as it's non-existent. I expect sound from my neighbors. However, I suspect given the water stains, the Element flooded at some point, needed to gut the walls and ceilings, and cut costs on re-insulation. Why? Because I know the health status of my upstairs neighbor's prostate, because we have the same floorplan, and I can hear him both walk to the adjacent bathroom due to creaking floor boards, as well as the quality and delays in his stream, followed by the clanking of loose pipes whenever he flushes. I can also hear the words, not simple murmurs, from his television and can easily hear the tune my next door neighbor is singing. Finally, the windows are thin enough to hear normal conversations 10ft away, so if you chose a unit near the dumpster, be aware trash pick up occurs between 12AM-4AM 3x per week, and even my soundproof curtains barely touched the noise levels.

TLDR: Can find better for the current price point, and definitely has some serious sound-proofing issues, but otherwise a good location and fast maintenance.

I don't seek to dissuade prospective tenants from interest in the property; I only want to give the heads-up i'd be looking for if i were in this position. It's a great property, but beware steep renewal rates and urban sprawl if you're planning to stay for more than your original lease term.

Parking spots. There is always a readily available parking spot available. This may seem like a small thing, but having visitors or coming home late is nice when you don't have to drive around searching for a spot.

I picked up the keys this week and was shocked when I saw our apartment.
