So here we are, a month + of no working air conditioning, a major leak coming from underneath our front door/entryway that even ARCO, the construction crew, can't seem to figure out. Our apartment reeks of mold and mildew now because there's been standing water underneath the floor panels for over a month, on top of hot temperatures inside our unit. It's unbearable.

Don't live here. Management has continued to prove themselves useless, and that they have no idea how to handle anything in a timely manner. They make so many excuses or they just straight up ignore you. This place honestly should not have residents living in it due to the number of problems they have. Take your money elsewhere. I regret ever signing a lease here and look forward to getting out of it as soon as possible.

Also to note, there's tons of puddles in the hallways I'm assuming that are also caused by leaks. That's an accident waiting to happen. Nothing has been done about those leaks either.

I have no clue who has been giving the property 5 star reviews but, everyone I talk to who lives here with me is in absolute shock at how bad the complex has gotten. We have trash everywhere, glass all over the property along with dog mess.  
The staff laughably hides behind privacy glass now while bragging “it’s great!  Everyone leaves us alone now”. The program they use to pay rent has additional charges, some upwards of 3.25% with no cap in fee.That’s a $75 charge for them to take my money, not including the nearly $400 price increase from AMC taking over the complex!  Ever since AMC has taken over the property, it’s been absolutely awful. Crime, gunshots, cops being called and cars being broken into.  Do yourself a favor and do NOT move here. Talk to the residents and not the staff if you want to consider it.  Your money and sanity will be much better spent anywhere else.

Everything about Elevate at Pena Stations is great! The property is wonderful, the apartments are amazing and Gino and his staff are everything one could hope for in management. I would highly recommend Elevate to anyone!!

The property is amazing and the staff are even better! Gino took very good care of us when we were applying and continues to take care of us now that we’re living here! I have not had one thing to complain about since I’ve been here. I would highly recommend this complex to everyone!

Brand new community with amazing features and amenities! Maintenance keeps the community very well maintained and clean. Gino and Kristen are extremely helpful and consistently go above and beyond to make you feel at home. Overall best place to live in Denver!
Gino and Kristen are literally amazing from start to finish they made the process so simple and our home is amazing. If you’re looking to come here, pack your bags your search ends here!

I am loving my new apartment here at Elevate @ Pena Station. Gino was amazing in the leasing office and made me feel at home before I even applied. The appliances are awesome and there is nothing better than being the first person in the apartment I rented. I am so happy and would definitely recommend my new home to any and everyone.
A super great place to live always clean, the leasing staff is always trying to help , I even saw the leasing staff picking up trash the other day day they truly care about the property!
Great management team! Always so helpful and nice. Teresa is the best
The property is great and the property manager is so helpful the whole team is amazing
The Haven is nice so far. The staff are accommodating and knowledgeable and thoroughly assisted with my and my father’s needs.

I like living in this apartment, I do. But I feel like the maintenance people can clean MUCH better. Elevators can be wiped and mopped more, especially the hallways. Beautiful buildings and modern but very dirty. Hopefully management can hire people who can actually clean the place and do some type of Power wash. Plus residents don’t know how to pick up after their dogs. I always see droppings every morning unfortunately.
Great move-in process, Good community, maybe inform residents on car/truck theft, and take precautions. And I would like for the gate to be closed at night, however, I haven't seen it closed.

I would give this apartment complex a two on a scale of one to ten. The oversell we got when we moved in did not pan out. Much of what we were told has not valid. It has the bones but isn't fleshed out.
The actual apartments are decent but in my experience the rest of the facility was been subpar at best and not worth the price.
Great apartment. Staff is very friendly and helpful. The property is maintained very well.
The Haven apartments are wonderful, quiet, calm and very clean. Everywhere is expensive so at least for the price the layouts and size are by far some of the best.

The staff is excellent. Apartments are brand new, clean, everything works great, and the maintenance team always fixes any issues very quickly. Outdoor cleanliness is the only thing that could be improved but the staff does frequently send out emails trying to fix these issues. I’m sure they’ll be resolved. Overall I greatly recommend these apartments. I truly believe they’re the best in Denver.
I really enjoy all the things The Haven has to offer, love the game area, the pool when it’s open and my absolute fave is the dog spa area!

Car was broken into with the first two months of living here, not a good neighborhood to live. People do not clean after their dogs, there is usually dog droppings on the sidewalk to be frank. The apartments themselves are not bad. For the new price they have this place at though do yourself a favor and run far away.

I love the community and the living space. Has really nice amenities and clean facilities. Maintenance is very respectful and nice. The office personnel are very engaged in any request you have. It’s been an absolute pleasure living at the Haven.
We LOVE The Haven! Everyone that works here is so attentive and the complex is very nice!
Very friendly staff with a clean apartment and very nice amenities. Community is quiet and has great access to the airport.

I've had a maintenance issue for six months, and it remains unresolved. What has been done is several holes cut out of the drywall, exposing the negative space of the building.

There are two parking gates. One is broken and locked up. The other is broken and locked down. The one that's locked down has been that way for four months.

Elevators are out constantly. It feels like one isn't working in any given week. And they are spaced out, so if the one by you isn't working it's a hassle to use the other ones because the layout of the parking is such that nowhere is a straight shot to anywhere else. You end up using a different elevator, then circling halfway around the building and walking up or down a ramp or stairs to reach your car.

When I moved in nine months ago I was told the clubhouse would have TVs for residents to use. But last I checked the TVs aren't hooked up to a feed of any kind. What can residents do with a TV that doesn't have anything on it?!

The elevators break consistently in the apartment as well as there have been many leaks, which flooded apartments. Also there is a lack of security presence. This is the most expensive complex in DTC but lacks the basic essentials to ensure the utmost safety for residents.
I love it at Vue West!  I have everything I asked for in my living situation.  I want to be here for a long time!

Vue West is an absolutely beautiful complex to live at! It is always so clean and well kept. The leasing staff is PHENONMENAL, which is hard to find nowadays. Victoria made the process simple and easy from start to finish. She was quick to respond to any questions and walked us through everything! We are very happy and feel very lucky to live here!

I was an initial resident and we had some early issues but they have been addressed.
I love the location for easy access to the airport plus the light rail and great restaurants are within walking distance.
And my floorplan is perfect and the entire staff here are true professionals.
The Vue West is a wonderful, safe and clean living community. I highly recommend it.
I hope you will come over to Vue West and ck out the beautiful apartments!!!! It is a wonderful and friendly place to live!!!! Hope to see you soon!!!
I appreciate the staff the area and being in a community full of go getters!!
it has been a wonderful experience so far... all the staff are wonderful...
Very conveniently located near Belleview Station. Nice and clean neighbourhood. Very peaceful atmosphere. Nice staff and very well maintained property.
The leasing staff were great to work with.  Victoria did a terrific job of finding me the perfect apartment!!  The complex and location are wonderful and I would highly recommend!

Great experience thus far. Hiring is the name of the game. The office staff has been met with a plethora of challenges, including being asked to deliver high quality service and professionalism while dealing with obstacles that are outside their control, like construction progress for certain parts of the building. They take accountability for their errors and do their best to make up for things they can't do much about themselves. Their responsiveness goes a long way and so far they've been consistent about following through. I look forward to seeing how my experience here continues to develop, but so far I've been quite impressed.

The team was very accommodating for me during my move in process. I was coming in from out of state and they were very helpful in making sure I got what I was looking for and helping me with the leasing and move in process. I'm excited for the amenities to all get finished. It's a beautiful property and a nice place to live!

Vue West IS a victim of the supply chain and work force shortage we are all experiencing. I was homeless and couch surfing for 2-3 months while waiting. I get it. But the location and the building are the best bang -for-buck one could ask for. And the staff is great. Never had any issues and they’ve been nothing but accommodating and quick to respond with a smile and laugh

Vue West has been a great place to live so far. The views are fantastic, and the management and leasing staff has been friendly, easy to work with, and very helpful throughout the move-in process and since we've been here.
Enjoy our life at Greenleaf Jayne. Could not ask for better leasing agents or maintenance staff. I would say it is the best apartment complex we have lived in in Denver!

Really enjoy living at the Jayne. The leasing staff is so friendly and helpful. Maintenance has been great dealing with a minor issue we had. The complex is beautiful with great amenities. There are community events held and residents are giving their ideas for future events. Great place to live!

This is my first time living in the Baker area and had no clue the amount of unhoused that would be coming and going (and living) in the alley behind the building at all times of the day and night. It makes it a little stressful when the garage door is not working and must be left open. Especially, since there are no security key pads on the doors from the garage into the building and stairwells.
People who live here seem to be insanely entitled and inconsiderate of others. They are constantly backing up the recycling shoot by not breaking down anything and just leaving it in the trash room.
The walls aren't insulated the best since you hear doors slamming and everyone and anyone walking above your apartment.

I am so pleased with the new management team here at Jayne. The building is so much cleaner and the south elevator is SO much more reliable. Leslie and Norman are so friendly and responsive. 
I have no complaints at all.

I have lived here for over a year now and it has been the best place I've ever had the pleasure to reside in. I was initially worried about the switch over in property management, but Leslie has been absolutely incredible. She is so kind and thoughtful. It really seems like she cares. Her door is literally always open and she always has the time to talk. And honestly, everything has been incredible. The amenities and property is kept in tip-top shape and the rare maintenance request I have are always dealt with in a swift and professional manner. 10/10 would still recommend. I simply just love it here are Greenleaf Jayne!
So happy to have discovered The Jayne.Has wonderful amenities, nice apartments, and a great staff. Some good restaurants and stores in the area too! Happy to call it home.
Love being next to the stadium on concert days, staff is very friendly and have been helpful since day one. Fun building to live in, so happy I moved to 1919.
I’m loving how friendly everyone is! The amenities allow me to stay home if I choose too
Everything has been great since I moved here! Great amenities, super friendly and helpful staff, as well as very friendly community and neighbors! Would definitely recommend this place to anyone!
I love 1919 Mile High! It is a beautiful building, great amenities and the location is hard to beat.

I love this place so much. The management is so friendly and personable and easy to get ahold of and any issues in your apartment are taken care of immediately! My favorite part is the gym which I use on a regular basis. It’s super clean and the equipment’s is incredible. My only complaints would be lack of visitor parking. I don’t host wild parties or anything like that, but when friends or family come to visit it is always a challenge to figure out where they can park, especially being so close to Empower Field. But other than that I’m super happy I moved here!

Current resident, for past 12 months.

Management (Angela, Janelle, and Hailey) is very tough to work with and ignores most resident requests unless you follow up a lot and make a big deal.

Safety is a HUGE problem. There are thousands of people on the property each weekend for Broncos games, concerts, monster truck rallies, etc. This causes constant chaos and break-ins/theft.

Also maintenance has entered my residence multiple times without notice. And other residents in the building told me they have had the same experience. My wife and the other females in the building feel especially unsafe because of this.

Good experience  The agent was very sweet and very knowledgeable.. 
I loved the property inside and out. I didnt like the fact that i am an adult and have to pay parking vouchers all hours of the day for company. This made me go with a different property. Other than that yall are pretty great
light repair was replaced in a timely manner, maintenance tech was friendly and professional
Great job  Maintenance was very knowledgeable and attentive to find a solution to the ceiling fan. Thank you for your help
They charge all the tenants $5 monthly pest control service but they’ve yet to go into units to do the job. Granted it’s fairly new but why continue to charge this fee and collect over $12000 a year.

Couple things could add to the property. There are orange tubes (?/O cables) that are about 8 feet tall and look bad to the right of the driveway.  Also, the sign on the left of the driveway blocks being able to see if there is oncoming traffic. 

It would be nice to have a recycle bin at the mailboxes
Overall a good rental experience. The townhomes have great access to the Highline Canal trail.  It’s an easy walk to the entrance of the trail. The grounds are nicely maintained.

Having to relocate from another state, I received great help, from the application process to getting furniture delivered while in another state, to ensure I knew all my options in picking the right unit, etc. I have not had any issues with anything. I am very appreciative of the staff

Property management is nonexistent. They don't respond to emails, phone calls, or maintenance requests. Please check the google reviews. So far, living here has been a nightmare: the units have several maintenance issues & there was a shooting a couple of months ago that resulted in one of the units having broken windows/doors - which still hasn't been fixed. If you're looking at unit 1155, please make sure you ask leasing for a discount before signing a lease.
All staff that I came in contact with have been great.  Kristen is the best!  She made the process seamless and non-stressful.  Thank her and the team.

Recent event with the shooting has made me uneasy and not safe. Hope the security car remains. 

The dog poop in my yard is not good.  Neighbors are friendly.
Nice community. Most folks will say hello or talk to one another. Town homes are only 2 years old. Only negative is that the grounds are not maintained very well of litter and dog waste.
New management is wonderful and they are super responsive. I love my home, the location is great, the amenities are great, the townhomes are beautiful.

We really love living here especially with the new management (Cushman & Wakefield). The townhomes are spacious with really great storage. Some of the neighbors are disrespectful especially when it comes to walking their dogs off leash and not cleaning up after them, but that’s just how people are everywhere. Most of all, we love how quiet it is and the proximity to the High Line canal trail. Super pleased!

Since Avere was sold to new ownership, the new management team has been absolutely top notch! It is great to see them around the property and they reply to my messages and concerns very quickly. They were also very accommodating during my lease renewal process.

Very clean property, friendly staff, with great follow up. 
 Once I decided to make this my home it was an easy process. I highly recommend this location for your new home.
Our experience has been good so far here at Avere. There have been a few things that have needed fixing and some issues with bugs, but as a whole it’s been pretty good.
Living at Avere has been a good experience. We are in our second year and have had no issues. We moved into a brand new townhome and we have not experienced any issues.

I love living at Avere. The staff is always so friendly, and the maintenance staff is always so helpful and quick when I put in a request. The floorplans are open and spacious, and you really can't beat the location. I would highly recommend living here!
Avere on the Highline is a centralized location to the city. It’s 25 minutes from DIA and 25 minute to foothills . Quiet community with the Highline canal in its back yard .
Love the actually townhome! The finishes / open space is perfect. Wish there was more parking. Stacy was super kind in answering all of our questions before we moved in.

We have thoroughly enjoyed being residents of the Avere on the Highline. The quick access to the Highline canal has been great for our athletic hobbies and exercising our dogs. The complex is quiet and safe. Despite sharing a wall with neighbors who also have dogs, we never hear them and its very peaceful.

We were super excited for this place and loved the tour. BUT, everything after that went to crap. We had to initiate every conversation after that. We had to push to get our information approved multiple times. After we got approved, we heard NOTHING! Still haven't heard anything. We decided to go with a different place because of the staffs LACK of communication and utter disregard for common courtesy. When I asked for our admin fee to be refunded we were told we only had 48 hours until after approval to get a refund. We were NEVER told this information from the start. We never heard anything back. ALSO, believe the reviews. These poor people are desperately trying to be heard and the reviews are what turned us off to this place. These are abnormally BAD, and from our own experience, I believe them!

Seriously AVOID THIS PLACE. Overpriced. Dog poop everywhere. Was told pool would be open by end of July and still isn’t open December 11th Our unit was clearly thrown together. There were giant gaps between the wall and stairs which led to a massive rodent problem in our unit. Scratched countertops. Plaster on the floors and INSIDE our vents. Trash compactor is always full so we have hundreds of trash bags piled up around it. Management is rude and has zero respect for the residents. They are highly focused on selling the property and have zero interest in fixing the issues with this place. Counting down the days until we can get out of this hell. After speaking to the regional manager, nothing has changed. If you like overpaying for a place where your packages stolen, where you’ll be surrounded by trash and dog poop, where you’ll never have the amenities that were promised to you when you signed your lease, where homeless people sleep in the fitness center and pet spa, and where management constantly harasses you for renters insurance (even though you’ve sent it over to them 3 times), then this is the perfect place for you. Despite the many attempts we have made to work with Ladora through the many challenges we have faced since our lease began, they continue to refuse to address any of our concerns. Additionally, they refuse to allow us to leave our lease without any financial penalties regardless of how much they promised and never delivered.

Within three months of opening up, a car has been stolen from within the private parking garage. Another tenant had their spare tire stolen from someone using bolt cutters. You need a parking pass to access through two sets of doors. Parking is $115 a month. Cameras in the parking garage, management did very little to help with either incident. Great location, amenities, and apartments.

The staff that works here are all great. Always super nice and accommodating. The apartments themselves are nice, can't beat brand new with a great mountain view, and they are also smoke free. Also super close to Wash park.

I'm a resident and agree with the other reviewer. I wouldn't move here right now. The building always smells like sewage. Many visitors have commented on the smell. Smells even worse when they try and mask it instead of addressing it.

The building is not complete and is going through improvements still to bring it on line. Also, residents are being incentivized $1,000 in rent credits to bring others in who sign a lease, so that’s something to consider when reading reviews. The building is still off-gassing so it smells really strongly, especially in the elevators and hallways. After move in connections to our dishwasher and washing machine had to be fixed. There was an issue with a bath leak into our closet from the unit above us. We have the unit design with the dark push open cabinets in the kitchen and the fingerprints left behind just to cook are a life lesson to everyone why cabinet handles or cutouts are normal. Also, the cabinets are so narrow and deep, without slider bins built in, that the kitchen is a significant annoyance to me as an avid cook just under 5’4”. We’re also still adjusting to the stove top, which is just electric glass and not actually convection. The heat temp numbers basically don’t align to anything normal in the US, so we’re still figuring it out. We’ll also be happy when the pool is complete.

The onsite staff are very lovely, including all the maintenance staff. The view is wonderful, tho dust builds up fast on the balcony surface and sometimes the river smells very foul. I love access to the Platte trail. The master bed/bath is peaceful, noise is almost non-existent. 

We do feel cut off from the heart of RiNo and FivePoints but it is easy to zip around places and Little Raven and Confluence Park are just a jog down the Platte Trail. We’re really hoping the neighborhood grows. It’s very transitional at the moment and lots of the local breweries- like blue moon - close for private events so we get out less now than when we walked places from Whittier to the RiNo Market and other places.

The interior design, community room, pop-up art parties, murals, free snacks, and more! Flora is the most fantastic apartment, and I'm so glad it doesn't look like a box-like many apartments. It has a sense of style and elegance you can see from afar.

I love the location of this property, it’s close to the city but also in a location that’s safe. We’re right by the river and have easy access to anything I need. The women who run the building are very accommodating and easy to talk to about any concerns or questions. By far the best building I’ve lived in - vibe, community and amenities wise. Highly recommend and can’t wait for our community to grow!

I've loved everything about this community!

The amenities, the homes, the storage, the parking, the views and the team!

I love this property for it's close proximity to downtown, the bike trail, bars, restaurants, the train station, groceries...everything is right at my fingertips.  There's even a public library and park right next door.
Nice amenities and friendly staff. Would definitely rent here once my lease is up
Maya has been such a pleasure to work with in finding my new home. So far everything has been great and my move was very smooth! Best community I’ve lived.
Great location, amenities are incredible and the staff are helpful!

I've toured several locations for my personal home so far and Aura Arts so far has some of the best amenities and views. The pool is actually a good size with panoramic views of the mountains and full sunshine. The fitness center is spacious with everything you need, including real Pelotons and the virtual mirrors with trainers and plans. And the Skylounge is stunning with views of the mountains and Downtown Denver.

The apartments themselves offer tons of cabinets and storage with huge walk-in closets.
Best community I’ve visited. Maya and Brittanie are so welcoming and the location is amazing!
Beautiful property and Maya is super personable !!!

One elevator works if you're lucky. Pool/spa are either poorly maintained or closed. Frequent leaks or fully broken pipes in the garage. Maintenance will not respond to requests unless you continuously call the emergency line. Management won't be much help either. I can't really blame the staff as much due to understaffing and high turnover due to poor upper management.

This is the worst run apartment complex I've ever lived in. When I first moved here from across the country, they did not have my apartment ready. I had to wait two days for my apartment to be available - and when it was, it was dirty, and several broken items. The manager at the time was very nice about it, apologized, corrected my rent and her doing so made the experience better. I let it go because the manager worked with me to correct the situation. However, management has changed. Since this change, I've experienced the garage leaking chemicals onto my car on three separate occasions. The manager won't call or email me back. They stated in an email that you must make an appointment with them to see them, but they don't answer their emails or phone calls. So you can't make an appointment with them. Further, when I waited outside her office to speak to her about the situation, she had someone in her office who appeared to be a friend. When a subordinate went into her office, she apologized to the employee and said "we were just chit chatting." The manager has no interpersonal skills and does not care to serve residents. I've also had problems getting a re-assigned parking spot because the management is unable to determine who is supposed to park in the garage. I'm really not sure why looking through the leases and collecting that data is not being done. 

Further they do not fix broken amenities and have been unsuccessful at fixing items in my house (dishwasher and bathroom sink). The bathroom sink has flooded my apartment twice now - ruining/destroying my personal belongings underneath. Further, they refused to fix the call box, and I've caught someone stealing packages from my building. Again, they will not fix it. They also refuse to fix the broken treadmill, and the hot tub rarely works. 

In sum, they do not care if they destroy your belongings, they do not care if your packages get stolen, and they will not call you or email you back. I would run from this complex.
I deeply regret moving here, it fas been one issue after another.  So many things are broken, management routinely just ignores emails about issues. Packages get stolen routinely.

I'd read up on this building on multiple review sites to make your decision.

BAD: I'm leaving after 5 years at 300 - I've experienced amenities down for months multiple times, limited elevators for weeks, accounting mistakes, arguments at the pool, fights in the hallway, misplaced documentation by managements office, stolen packages, non-residents in the garage, delayed apartment maintenance and high staff turnover. If they're talking about renovating something - just assume it won't happen in your lease time.

GOOD: Price can be very good, People are friendly if you're in the 20-30s. Easy access to Colfax. Current staff if they stay seem okay.

Its not the worst place to live - but it will frustrate anyone that is bothered when common reported items go an entire lease without resolution. Personally I travelled for work a majority of the time - so moving just wasn't a priority. If you want a cheap place that may or may not fix things - with OK amenities. You can try here.

I've lived in this property for approximately 6 months and would not recommend it to anyone. 

I have had really poor management experiences since the application process. Both my roommate and I had to keep calling and emailing them to hear back about our application. It wasn't until the day before our desired move-in date that they sent us the lease agreement and application approval. 

I am in the process of moving out now and again they are waiting until the very last minute to approve the resident change process. Every single document needed and requested by them was sent a week ago and they haven't even started the screening process with the new tenant, who needs to move-in in exactly 4 days.

I’m extremely frustrated with my living situation. Last time I put in a maintenance request it took 6 weeks to fulfill. In that time, my bathtub was completely unusable. I had to submit 7 maintenance requests before anyone ever responded.

They also added on an extra $90 charge for me back in July they assured me would be removed after it was processed through accounting. Not only has the charge not been removed, they continue to increase charges each month with zero explanation.

This place continues to treat residents horribly and disregard concerns. Security does nothing about noise complaints, even when the parties continue until 4am on a Monday night.
There’s zero security in the Logan building and sketchy people going in and out of the broken doors as they please: stealing packages, loitering, and who knows what else. None of my missing packages have been recovered.
I’ve emailed the management office 5x about the $90 charge, no response.

I’ve also called and stopped by the leasing office with the promise that someone would get back to me, no one has.
The buzzers by the door are always going off. We’ve had multiple faulty fire alarms.
At this point I’m trying to get out of my lease bc I don’t believe this place has adhered to a normal leasing contracts.

I’m so disappointed.

- unresponsive management: I don't know the name of a single person in the office, much less a contact email for any of them because they turn over every month or so. Even if you get a business card with an email address, your email won't get a response. With this, there is no way to communicate with management besides physically going in person, and even then they are unhelpful.
- When my roommate and I renewed our lease, I emailed a copy of our renewed renters insurance to the email on our resident portal. However, we were charged for insurance non-compliance for months despite repeatedly emailing proof, speaking with people in the office, and trying to work it out. To this day, they owe us $112.50 in bogus charges that we initially paid because we were confused.
- stolen packages: when we first moved in, we were told that the packages would either be put in the package lockers, or next to them. They justified it being unsecured by the cameras outside the gym facing that area. However, I have had easily over $300 in packages stolen with absolutely no help from the building.
- parking issues: upon moving in, I selected my parking spot. However, about two months later someone else started parking there. Turns out the person who help with my move in never recorded my spot, and they gave it to someone else. I was told to pick a new spot, even though I had been parking there for two months and it was an error on their end. They also recently threatened to tow my car out of the parking spot I have been paying for for over a year and a half, because they decided to update the parking passes without notifying any residents. 
- maintenance: while the maintenance workers themselves are nice, the response time is incredibly unreliable. My heat was broken for over a week in subzero temperatures last winter, and was not fixed for over a week despite repeated requests. My heat broke again last week. Additionally, I have had maintenance show up to my door without any company apparel or identifying information, which is obviously unsettling as I either have to take their word that they work for the building, or send them away and not have my issues fixed.
- one of the elevators in the 17th St building has been down for over a month. Management has not communicated anything about repairs, except only recently when they threatened residents with eviction for "vandalism" for writing on the out of order sign that was posted a month after the elevator actually went down.

Horrendous experience living here. We notified the emergency maintenance call center that our heat was broken. It took them 21 days to fix the heat and feel we do not deserve any compensation for the hassle. The matter was constantly swept under the rug and felt that the staff was just hoping we would forget about the issue. Forget about no heat... during the coldest days of winter. Valorie, the property manager, is doing everything in her power to refuse a meeting to discuss this matter in person. Aside from this horrible experience there are countless other issues. One being lack of security. There have been numerous car break ins in the “secure” parking garbage. My roommate had to chase down a homeless person who waltzed into our building with ease and stole his laundry. Elevators are constantly broken and appliances barely work. All of this combined with a staff who is unwilling to help or work with you has been a nightmare.

I cant thank John enough for taking the time out to go the extra mile...this guy is really amazing! I hope Maxx properties reads this review and rewards him accordingly. We flew to Denver from San Francisco to visit our son, who recently moved to Denver for a better job opportunity. He needed to find an apartment and fast because he had been renting a room at a hotel for $700.00 a week, plus it just wasn’t feasible. The hotel needed a cancellation call by 4 pm otherwise he would be charged another week. John heard about our dilemma so he took on the task of calling and checking every few minutes to find out if my son was approved. Not only did he make calls and check for approval but also offered us water and a snack while we waited. I don’t usually write a review unless the company or person providing the service does an exceptional job. John is not only kind but manager material. He will go far in life so take good care of him because he is a valuable employee. Noah also did a great job and was very attentive. These guys are great! Thank you, Gracie

If you want to do yourself a favor, do not ignore all of the negative reviews either here or on any other site. The property management company is absolutely non responsive to resident complaints or issues and fails to provide even basic maintenance for amenities such as the elevators, pool, sauna, dog park, landscaping, grills, or any other one they like to promote.

We've filed a BBB complaint which went ignored and seems to be the trend for them. Be sure if you are unfortunate enough to live here to document every issue you have, do your due diligence in reporting it quickly, and definitely be sure to have a lawyer. Not only are they unresponsive but their on site management is condescending, rude, and treat you with the lack of respect unparalleled by anywhere I've ever lived. 

Two separate instances our elevator has been completely down for 4+ months in the less than year and a half we have lived here. Each time we have been given an expected resolution, that date comes and is the subsequently pushed out another month without any notices. The most recent instance of this, residences were notified via channel 7 news in Denver that there was yet another delay to repair the elevator which has been nonfunctioning since May. (Update: we are still not expected to have it resolved until the end of October.)

Most of the residence that do live here have completely given up hope and have systematically left early or refuse to renew their leases. Yes, you'll save a little money, but the hassle of having to deal with maintenance that takes at minimum 3 days to repair any request is not worth it. The time wasted waiting for an elevator or for the water to be turned back on is worth an extra couple hundred bucks a month to live in any apartment anywhere else in Denver. 

With all this said, you've been warned. The positive posts on here are verified to be either employees or friends of employees who want to try to save this failing complex. Be mindful of this warning and save yourself the trouble.

We’ve lived here for nearly two years and have seen a significant decline.

Elevators are left broken for months on end, with no compensation for residents. I have been trapped in them twice since moving in.

Water is shut off for several hours on an almost weekly basis for “emergency repairs,” often with less than an hour’s notice.

Maintenance problems are usually only handled once several requests have been submitted. If you’re lucky, they will knock, but we’ve also had staff members unlock our apartment and enter unannounced. Apparently, someone had told them it was a vacant unit. 

Community areas are in constant disrepair. Amenities are removed, rather than fixed. Damaged elements are often left in unsafe condition (glass on elevator floor, shop lights dangling over pipes loose from extension cords.)

Emergency alarms go off for no reason so frequently that most residents now ignore them and don’t bother evacuating. When a disabled resident asked community manager Chelsea about their evacuation plan with the elevator broken, they were told to cease contacting her directly. 

Random charges are billed with no explanation or notification of any kind. Many residents are breaking their leases and incurring charges to move out early. 

Worst of all, when any of these concerns are brought to the attention of management, they are met with condescension, redirection and often outright falsehoods (if you ever receive a response at all!)

We have seen nearly the entire community staff turn over several times under Chelsea, and it is no surprise. She blames her employees, her vendors, her supervisors, and the age of her building for everything wrong while never taking any responsibility herself. 

The neighborhood is incredible, but I highly recommend you rent elsewhere.

The staff is incompetent and can't do their jobs, and the property manager is disrespectful, rude, and unprofessional. Renting from Maxx Properties has been one of the worst experiences of my renting careers, and I have had some shady landlords. 

Let's start with our move-in experience. The office staff that was supposed to give us our keys showed up an hour late and had the nerve to act taken aback that I was frustrated with the situation. The freight elevator we were promised we could have in a reserved mode to move in was down so actually moving in our stuff was a nightmare of having to try to share the one working elevator with the rest of the building. 

The apartments themselves are ok. The apartment wasn't particularly clean when we moved in. Not dirty, but also not clean. We were also told that our apartment would face the courtyard, but it actually faced 17th Ave. 

Lastly, our move out experience really solidified the incompetence of the office staff. We called a few weeks ahead of our move to reserve the (for once working) freight elevator. We requested it for a Sunday from 10am-noon, to which the woman on the phone happily said she had us on the schedule and we were good to go. It was our mistake not to get this woman's name. Fast forward a few weeks to our move out day, and no one from the office is there to put the elevator into the reserved mode. We had hired movers and we ended up paying them an extra $300 because it took so much longer to move out than it should have. 

When I went to speak with the property manager, I was told that the elevators could only be reserved during office hours, which on Sunday is from noon-5pm. This is a reasonable policy, however we were told by a staff member that we could have it earlier. The staff member's inability to know their own office hours cost my roommate and I $300. When I requested that Maxx Properties reimburse us for the extra time we paid our movers, he essentially laughed in my face and said that wouldn't happen. When I suggested I would explore other options of getting my issue resolved if he was unable to help me, he refused to talk to me further saying I was threatening him. All further communication with him has been disrespectful and rude, with him saying they "wouldn't cut a check for a miscommunication." 

Save yourself many headaches, hassles, and ultimately a lot of money by renting from literally anyone else.

Pool area loud 9pm-2am-EVEN ON TOP FLOOR-don't let mgmnt tell you otherwise. Up to you to call cops if you want to relax w/open windows. Staff IS responsive on other issues; heat, plumbing ,etc. Building renovations look modern and clean. An older concrete building-well made. Hallway doors are cheap-rude neighbors in the hall and cigarette smoke will waft in-door slamming constantly. Stainless appliances are cheapest builder grade-look ok but the fridge gurgles and runs. Fitness room not state of art. Laundry rooms are fine-people are respectful of others. Not an inexpensive place to live, but the rates are average. All in all, not a bad place to live, if you have decent neighbors. Convenient if you work downtown, but downtown is disgusting and depressing nights/weekends

Excellent staff.  Paul, the supervising manager, is fantastic...his energy, courtesy, and attention to detail are contagious amongst the entire staff.  The building is in a prime location.  Close to everything.  Surrounded by parks, restaurants, entertainment.  Great walkability.  Condition of the renovated apartments is excellent.  The property recently constructed a 24-hour dog park, complete with lights.  I just recently adopted a dog, and he and I love the park!  In addition to my pup making new friends, I have plugged into an entirely new population of the building: dog lovers!  Great people renting here.  Superb people managing.  

Billy Riesing
Logan Tower

I've lived at 300 17th Street for a year. It's a reasonably priced apartment in a great neighborhood. There are several nice restaurants and bars in the area. The building has undergone several renovations that have really improved the ambiance. My only complaint would be a lack of a washer and dryer in the apartment.

I have lived at this complex for over 5 years and have lived in multiple units (1 and 2 bedroom units, in 2 of the 3 buildings).  The 300 East 17th complex is in a great location, is priced decently, but can be poorly maintained.

The building is located in Uptown Denver which has great restaurants, and next to the Central Business District which hosts many events throughout the year.  It is also walking distance to the 16th Street Mall and the Light Rail public transportation.

The prices are definitely not the cheapest compared to other apartments in the area, but are not as high as the bigger or newer complexes.  The common areas are not nearly as nice as the newer complexes, and do not have things like a dig wash station, but the units are bigger (I have a king sized bed fit comfortably in my current bedroom).

Because the buildings are older and not new like some of the other complexes 1-2 blocks away, there are issues with the units and common areas.  The plumbing leaks in the underground garages creating large dirty pools of stagnant water, the main trash is on the same level as the Logan building lobby so the smell permeates throughout the lobby and onto the 2nd floor laundry room and hallways. The bathroom cabinets are metal and have rust on the inside, there are areas that are not caulked where ants and/or drafts constantly stream in, the windows and balcony/patio doors are old and not energy efficient so if it's cold outside it will be cold inside your apartment.

Overall the complex is not great because every time my lease is up I am always looking to jump ship to other complexes, but ok enough that I stay and keep signing rent checks to them.

On the whole, I love living here! It's a great location, close to downtown. Convenient to tons of restaurants, bars, concert venues, etc. Also easy to get around to the suburbs and the mountains.

The newly re-done courtyard is gorgeous! I don't have a dog, but I always see people using the dog run. There's a Game Center, pool, hot tub, grills, and a fire pit. So nice to walk through! 

I haven't used the gym, as I have a membership elsewhere, but that also seems well-used, if a little small. 

The laundry centers are large and usually open enough that you can do multiple loads at a time so you don't have to spend the whole day or evening doing laundry. They also take cards for payment; the readers are finicky, but it's still so much easier than collecting quarters! 

It's nice that the office signs for and stores packages in a locked room, but not always easy to catch someone to unlock it for you. You definitely have to time it right, or be left waiting. 

The maintenance crew usually responds to requests quickly and efficiently. My only complaint with them is that I usually come home to lights left on, or my belongings scattered. They recently fixed an issue with my bathroom sink and left tools there and the bathroom was a mess! 

Another very minor issue is that my name still isn't in the directory, despite turning in my form months ago. 

I have a space in the garage, which is nice, but the garage isn't very well lit and occasionally, one or the other set of doors will be blocked off with no warning. 

The staff is good about communicating upcoming outages or work issues, but it would be nice if they sent this out via email, too.

I really enjoy living here and if my rent doesn't increase too much, would definitely renew my lease next year! Recommended!

This place has some positives - good location if you like living downtown, nice neighbors, and friendly employees. Unfortunately it also has numerous issues.

Elevator outages are frequent and sometimes lengthy. Out of two passenger elevators and one freight elevator, only ONE passenger has been working the past 4+ weeks. With a building of this size, it means lengthy elevator waits and limited ability to move anything bulky (good luck if you’re moving in or out).

The fire alarm malfunctions. It happens during the workday, it happens at 1am. It’s not constant but it does happen.

The building has a garage but the doors sometimes break. Sometimes they’re stuck open or stuck shut, sometimes the entrance one works but the exit one doesn’t. This can last for days, it can last for weeks. Building management will tell you the different reasons, they are just powerless to prevent the failures and slow to recover from them.

The building requires key fobs but the actual building security is poor. The entry and exit doors break, preventing people with their key fobs from accessing. Conversely, people can and do gain access the building without key fobs. Even worse, because elevators don’t require the fobs, once someone has access they can go almost anywhere.

The building isn’t managed well. You can’t look at the frequency of issues and arrive at any other conclusion. To be clear, the on-site office people are nice. But they aren’t the ones who call the shots, their corporate managers are. So far, the corporate management has been unable or unwilling to make the necessary changes. The message is that they don’t care about their residents.

I have been living here since January 2023. They have an amazing staff with an amazing system. Jocelyn basically sold me through the phone and Tanner followed up and closed the deal! The maintenance group is very hard working. I put an a maintenance request thinking it would take days and they came within the hour to fix the issue and even any other issues that came to my mind. They have 24/7 security I believe as I see them all the time. I did a lot of research before moving here and you simply won't beat the price for what you get. While living here I have got 2 noise complaints from a crazy lady which is only like one percent of the building as everyone else is amazing here. When I was told of the noise complaint Tanner handled it with extreme professionalism to let me know, which I respect. The staff always handles everyone's concerns and treats everyone with respect as anyone should. They always gave me the best service possible. I recommend living here if you want to truly experience downtown living.

Where do I begin? Here's a brief list of what you can expect:

- Extremely expensive parking ($125 per spot).
- While it may look nice, all of the appliances and cabinetry are very low quality and break constantly.
- Speaking of breaking, the elevators, pool, hot tub, and rooftop patio amenities are constantly breaking and out of service. So, move here if you like walking up and down flights of stars and paying for amenities you can never use.
- The apartment proclaims the underground parking is secure, but the homeless population around the apartment (which is quite large) or drunk people wandering from Larimer St can quite easily get into the apartment. 
- Because anyone and everyone can get into the apartment complex easily, car break-ins and robberies are quite common (my laptop was stolen out of my car, my wife's purse with all of her cards was stolen, and I've witnessed multiple broken car windows). 
- Robbery isn't the only crime you can expect, within the past six months of living here (2022 - 2023), there have been four shootings blocks from our apartment. In fact, one person was shot and killed right in front of the apartment building. 
- To make matters worse, the apartment staff are not very helpful and have a very high turnover. We've sent multiple emails and left multiple voicemails that have never been answered. 
- If you accidentally get locked out of your apartment, good luck! Because Point 21 uses electronic locks and FOB keys and there's no locksmith in Denver that works with electronic locks. Nor does Point 21 staff have a master key...So, just don't get locked out!
- Finally, while the Point 21 groundskeeping staff do a decent job of making the apartment complex appear upscale and clean, in reality, that's not the case. Because of the previously mentioned homeless population, there's trash and excrement all over the surrounding sidewalk of the complex. The dumpsters behind the building are constantly being torn through with trash being thrown everywhere (we even saw a dumpster fire once). The stairwells are absolutely disgusting and smelly. And, the alleyway entrances to the stairwells are a popular place for the homeless to use the bathroom (we once had to beg the staff to clean up human excrement from the stairwell entrance).

We’ve lived in the building for three years and haven’t had an issue until the new management. Like the other reviews EVERYTHING is broken. That’s not the worst part though. The building has been absolutely infiltrated by homeless people. There is no 24 hour security and when we called the hotline to report a homeless man inhabiting the garage we were told they couldn’t do anything since it was outside of the contract hours so we got an extra resident for at least a nigbt. It is a major safety concern, our cars have been broken into multiple times. There have been multiple other homeless people in the building and trying to break into apartments. The cherry on top is they raised rent 15% with all this nonsense going on. please do not move here, save yourself a headache.

Used to be a great place to live. New management took over in 2022 and the whole building has fallen apart. If you love no amenities, broken elevators, management not taking responsibility for anything and the homeless people taking over the property and using it as a bathroom/drug use spot then this is your spot. Don't be fooled by the photos and the updated painting and hallways. They could've used the $ to fix the 3 month broken pool, elevators, secured locked doors, security cameras, useable garage doors to park your car, etc. Property is aware and still nothing is being done.  Spend your hard earned money at a place that fulfills your lease contract. Nothing is there fault here.
the apartments are nice and get lots of light but the property is dirty, including the pool. it is not in a very safe area. the management team is not very helpful with responding to questions.

Premier Lofts are great apartments with a fantastic location.  Kristen on the leasing team was incredibly helpful and professional when it came to finding my next home.  I really appreciate the management team here.

This place went from bad to worse. There have been three crimes committed in my time living here. (Probably because they fail to tell you when signing an apartment how more than HALF the apartments are Airbnb’s that they sell for $80 a night) This means there’s random people are in and out of this building everyday. While living here I experienced an individual drugged out of his mind screaming through the hallways, knocking on people’s doors until he broke into our neighbors apartment across from us through their glass door to their balcony. If that isn’t scary enough some sort of altercation happened on the fourth floor leading to pools of blood recently and possibly a death. (To which I had to find out through a neighbor as they did not inform us or ANYONE ELSE but it’s definitely there)And if that isn’t scary enough they don’t background check anyone on their Airbnb list. I’ve had multiple Airbnb clients ask me how they access their room when I have absolutely no idea and they can’t ask leasing because more often then not they’re never there. Nothing is updated. It takes multiple maintenance tickets or you physically going to the leasing office to get anything done. They thought it inappropriate for someone to let a tenant in who was locked out with her baby in below freezing temperature. (Claiming it was a safety issue which is ironic when they let anyone rent their apartments as motel rooms basically) All the amenities close at 11:00pm. They physically lock EVERYTHING but they can’t seem to ever close the garage door..which leads into the courtyard which has a door into the lobby which is also never locked. The elevators hardly ever work and will spit you out on random floors. The trash chute is always usually over filled and clogged. I have hair stuck in the grout of my bathroom from the previous tenant because they update nothing. All my cabinets are scratched. ( they won’t stain them but they did say I could get it approved if I wanted to do it myself. How nice of them.) My microwave and my dishwasher had to be replaced after multiple requests to fix it. The pipes are always leaking in the lobby. It usually smells like an actual sewage plant right when you walk in. Oh and they’re a dog friendly apartment building but..your dogs aren’t allowed to be ANYWHERE.

Last March, my fiancé and I were looking for an apartment in Downtown Denver while living in Los Angeles. We noticed that Premier Lofts was consistently receiving high ratings from various sources - which compelled us to book a tour. Russell gave us a tour and made us feel very comfortable, answering all our questions and being mindful of our time (we were just in town for a day and had back-to-back tours at various apartment complexes). Of all the units we viewed, we loved Premier Lofts the most and decided to apply. The process was easy and quick (thanks Chantal for all your help!).

Aside from the loft-style units with modern appliances, there is a dog wash room, game room, outdoor patio area, yoga studio, and roof top area (during the summer, they offer free yoga at sunset!). Of all the buildings we toured, Premier Lofts was one of the cleanest. They also provide free coffee and host a lot of events.

I highly recommend Premier Lofts. Like previous reviews, this is one of the best apartments I've lived in.

Recently, Premier Lofts started renting out a multitude of units throughout the building (you can check this out on Air BNB and stayalfred.com). There is now a constant stream of strangers and suitcases that parade through the building on a daily basis. This place no longer feels like home - it feels like a hotel. You would think that paying thousands of dollars a month would at least buy you a true community, but instead you're barely paying less than the average traveler. I would not suggest renting here unless you are comfortable with this atmosphere while paying exorbitant Denver rental prices.

Love living at Premier Lofts, the staff is fantastic and the building is kept very clean. Maintenance has always responded quickly and have always been professional. Beautiful apartments in a truly great neighborhood. Only issue is rents in Denver, especially this area...you could find a cheaper mortgage. Other than that - best apartment building I've lived in, would highly recommend.

I recently moved to Denved from Alabama for graduate school. I had no idea where to live when planning my move. I did my research and called different properties to ask questions. Macoy (asst. Mgr) at Premier was incredible when it came to answering my questions and making me feel at home. The staff is undeniably great (helped me move in!!!). The building is in great shape and STAYS sparkling clean. I used to work in property management and these guys go above and beyond! I was very lucky to find Premier Lofts in such a big transition in my life!

I hate to write this review because I loved living here, but I renewed my lease a month ago, and it has been a nightmare ever since. The new management is terrible and they are charging extra fees that are not communicated up front. There have been multiple issues like fire alarms going off at all hours of the night repeatedly, the water goes out several times a week, and the elevators were down for about three weeks. There was no apology or any explanation until people started to complain (and everyone complains). It's a great location and has good layouts for apartments, but be mindful if you are on a lower level the floors are thin and you will feel like the people above you are stomping nonstop (you can hear everything!) Hope this helps. It is a great place without the management messing things up!

My partner and I have lived in this complex for about two years and at the beginning, it was fantastic. Recently, a new company called Equity Residential has taken over and absolutely ruined the complex. They've begun charging residents exorbitant fees with no substantial explanation, they've imposed fees on amenities that once were included, and to say quality of living has dropped would be a vast understatement. Within the last month, the fire alarm has gone off at least four times. Today, November 14th, it went off at both 1 AM and 8 AM, forcing families with pets and children to evacuate twice. Water has also been shut off for days on end, leaving some residents with no water at all while others get brown water coming from their faucets. Additionally, (after a lovely 6 AM fire alarm), the main elevators to the building went down for nearly three weeks, requiring residents to walk through heavy snow and blizzard conditions to check mail or reach the leasing office. When confronted about these issues, management could not even pay the common courtesy of getting my name right while pretending to care. Equity Residential has had no shortage of furious residents, and they think they can placate us with half-baked (like AI-generated) "apology" emails. The residents are done, we demand change, and I cannot stress enough that you should avoid this place, and this management company, like the bubonic plague.

I would never rent here again. Just starting my 2nd year here and new management decides to charge an extra 300$ in utility fees with less than 2 weeks notice and blames the previous management for the issue saying they can't do anything about it. Absolutely atrocious. I thoroughly regret resigning.

I may as well list the other issues I've been willing to ignore up until they decide to be inconsistent with rent pricing.

1) My apartment is above a commercial dumpster. They never close the doors so you can smell the trash from my balcony. There is a very noisy garbage truck that does 2x weekly pickups, often at 5am in the morning.

2) Paper thin ceilings, I can hear everywhere my upstairs neighbor is going at all times. I've seen them and they are not large people.

3) They took away the 24/7 hot tub access a few months after we had signed. This was a major reason for us wanting to move in here as we thought it was an incredible policy. They said it would reduce the monthly utility charges but they never went down in the slightest and if anything have only gone up.

4) The on-site management team is incredibly unhelpful and unwilling to do a thing. They will constantly refer you to the corporate team for help who will never answer you.

When I moved in (end of August) I believe there was a property manager change and I don't have a single complaint about the facilities or staff. Maintenance requests are handled promptly, visitors at the front are called up during business hours, and in general everyone is very pleasant. The property is in a phenomenal location. As a female living alone I feel safe at night. And the parking garage has security to prevent non-resident parking (not crime!).

You pay a luxury price to be in the DTC area, but the Milehouse Apartments are NOT luxurious. Hallways are always dirty. There are holes in walls that never get repaired. The hot tub is frequently cold and not working. Elevator security doesn't exist (fobs are no longer needed to get up to the apartments). Pipes have burst and it took them months to repair from the damage. There is a total lack of overall care and maintenance at the Milehouse, and they want to increase my rent by 15% for the next year: NOPE! Won't be spending all this money on the raggedy Milehouse experience after my lease is up.

Do NOT move into this place. Here’s why: I moved here in August and it took maintenance 2 months to fix a leaking toilet and replace a bulb that was out the day I moved in. Around the time they got to fixing that, my dryer stopped working properly. I first reported the dryer in mid October. It is now mid January and my dryer STILL DOESNT WORK. They have been by to ‘fix it’ over 5 times. Aka... they come in and reset the dryer though I’ve repeatedly told them it is overheating. I was also told a vendor was coming to look at it... but that never happened? Communication is extremely poor from the staff that works here. Don’t expect them to make any situation right. Also, this is just the maintenance issues I’ve had. Not the other disturbances from neighbors in a domestic violence incident every other night. (Again management has done nothing) ohhhh & the garage door hasn’t worked now for almost 2 weeks. Somebody even had their car broke into because of it. It’s obviously a REAL luxury apartment complex.

From the outside looking in, MileHouse has it all: great location to the lightrail/public transportation, located above awesome restaurants, salons, etc., a cool rooftop, a garage, and decently sized apartments with good appliances. One month in, management changed, they implemented a new billing process, and the garage was broken. For the first 5 months, we didn't receive a bill and had to go to the office every month to ask what we owe (annoying, but not a deal breaker). My roommate and I pay in two checks (a completely normal transaction for anyone with roommates), and we have to pay checks because their online system can't comprehend splitting a payment in two when it's 2018, however the complex has consistently "lost" one of our checks each month for the last 8 months. Starting with month 2, we have them scan and sign that they've received both checks on time. The manager has given us issues with this every time, even after telling her the situation and having multiple payment notices taped to our door, which we then will bring the signed check copies down and they miraculously find the missing check. EVERY TIME. Next, the garage gate has been broken since the month after we moved in. We pay an additional amount of money for an extra spot. However, with the gate being broken, whoever can park whenever, which is completely unfair to those that actually pay. There have been multiple reports that cars have been broken into because of this. Further, this summer, high school aged kids learned that they can enter through the parking garage and drive to the top floor and enter the pool, throwing parties nightly involving alcohol. With no one monitoring and the gate open, the kids could care less and the pool has been emptied multiple times over the last couple of months due to broken glass, which has increased resident utilities bills. Finally, any stairwell you enter, reeks of dog urine and it's clear they don't get cleaned often, which I know is more the owners' faults than apartment, but they never send any notices. Finally, when there is communication to the residents, it is often unprofessionally written with grammatical errors, typically no greeting, and resident emails have been accidentally released multiple times.

But sometimes they are hard to find if not present at the desk in working hours. We are renting a studio apartment which is furnished on the 8th floor.
