They both told me they would speak with the tenants, provide warnings, inflict fines for repeat offenses. 3 months later and there has been no improvement. Shantell and Jessica do not care and have made it clear that I cannot end my lease. There IS NO LEASE BREAK OPTION, only the option to sublet. Good luck subletting for a full 12 month lease with excessive noise during a pandemic. To be clear, I had signed a lease renewal before the new tenants moved in; my first 12 month lease had not yet ended and I was still within 60 days of the end of my lease when I reported these issues. I asked for them to kindly allow me to end the final ~80 days of my current lease and withdraw my renewal. They refused. I am now TRAPPED here until next July because I cannot sublet with excessive noise in the middle of a pandemic. They are completely devoid of compassion and ill-treating to their front-line workers. 

My bathroom ceiling has been leaking for the past month. I have reported persistent leaking about 8 times now over that period. Each time, one of 3 repairmen enter my home, in the middle of a pandemic, to attempt to fix the leak. One of the repairmen apologized for how many attempts it was taking, stating that the usual leak guy was out as he was COVID-19 POSITIVE. Tomorrow, a group of 3 men will be trying again.
Love the prime Denver location with easy access to shopping and dining. I really like the sleek and modern look and layout of the apartments not to mention all the amenities!
Can’t really say to much. People that live at these apartments don’t have no common sense and don’t respect others.
I have been here a few years, mainly due to the size of the apartment and also the beautiful view

It’s a nice complex, great view from the upper floors, mailbox is in the lobby makes that convenient, staff was very helpful and watched over packages as well to a point with how they are delivered. There is a pool and outdoor grill area but it’s kinda messy. Not the cleanest pool either.

An apartment complex with a great future. The new building is awesome. They are very pet friendly, and go out of their way, should problems arrive. I'd definitely recommend Elm at the Panorama to all apartment complex seekers.
If you absolutely have no where else to go then this is the place for you but if you have options spend your money where it’s appreciated and you receive quality in exchange for the price
Un ambiente  muy bueno personal d oficina excelente trato personal y me siento segura d vivir en Elm panorama

We have lived here for over a year and have nothing but good things to say. Griffis Union Station is the best. The staff is incredible and living here is affordable and high quality (amenities and apartments). Everyone who lives here is kind, the maintenance is always handled quickly, and again, the staff is really hard to beat!! Finally, the proximity to everything downtown is awesome. We love walking to the grocery store, restaurants, parks, and rail. 10/10 recommend living here.
Great location, nice amenities, friendly staff! Community events, green areas, coffee<3

I’ve lived here a little over a year and love it. We are walking distance to a lot of local bars, restaurants and sights within the Denver downtown area. The apartments are well cared for and pretty decent sizes compared to most downtown apartments. Plus, the guys at the front desk and Maintenance crew are amazing and definitely care for the community!

Since one year ago living here is a good experience, it’s waking distance to every single good stuff in Downtown Denver. They’re always trying to improve good community living and hear you when you have a suggestion or a complaint to resolve.

The apartment itself is beautiful and spacious, and I absolutely love the concrete floors and high ceilings. But even more of a draw are the lovely outdoor areas. Whether you want to go for a swim in the pool, sunbathe, or just relax on the  patio, it’s so nice to have a peaceful escape, and the beautiful landscaping makes you forget you’re in a city.

Ever since the now current manager (Tamra) took over, this building has gone down hill fast.  The building is constantly dirty, awful rotting food smell by the mail boxes, broken outdoor stairs for over a year now, vehicles are broken into on a weekly basis, homeless people camp out in the parking garage and inside the building.  Management is non responsive to residents concerns as clearly evidenced by the degradation of the building.  Do not rent here and do not fall for the positive reviews.  Management reaches out to specific people that live at the building to write glowing reviews - I know, I've been one of them.

I am writing this review post conversation with management at Griffis Union Station due to the lack of tenant customer service and overall ‘horrible’ property management lead by their current manager! 

Let me begin with the parking garage. If you pay to park your car in their garage, get ready for multiple car break ins, theft, and homeless people exploring the parking garage all throughout the day & night even after multiple tenants complained about their cars being broken into. The lack of security for this complex is ridiculous and management could care less about your belongings i.e. bicycle and car. If you decide to lock your bike outside in their bike rack, prepare to see your bike’s wheels disappear one by one as security at Griffins Union is basically nonexistent.  

Next, lets go to maintenance of the exterior of the complex. When you raise issues like dogs waste being on the stairs, elevator, and hallways, management will take weeks if not months to clean the area. 

And finally, if you are a current tenant looking to resign in the same unit, management will ensure to raise the price regardless of your good standing (timely payments, no complaints, ect) due to their “Pricing model”. So prepare to pay more rent for the same exact unit if you plan to resign here and management clearly does not care about satisfying their current tenants. Once they sign you, you are trapped! The lack of understanding from management, especially during the pandemic (Covid 19) is extremely alarming and disappointing from a tenant’s standpoint.  Previous management was amazing and the most understanding apartment manager I know in Denver. She had this place up and running so efficiently, clean, and responsibly unlike the current manager. DO NOT SIGN HERE until management changes their ways and does not punish their current tenants with higher rental rates unless you sign long leasing terms. Once I see some actual changes around this apartment complex, I will remove this review ASAP!

The new management seems to make it hard to live here and is constantly changing conviences the community enjoys. I've never lived in a complex where they do forced entires to do biyearly apartment check ups even when you're not home. It's uncomfortable having strangers walk into your home, without you being able to be there, so they can make sure everything is in working order. (you cannot schedule theses reviews btw). They're also making everyone use this inconvient delivery service that won't let you use your own address. I can't wait to move out of this place and urge anyone considering this community to look elsewhere as it's been nothing but a hassle living here.

We recently relocated to Denver from NJ and Victoria went above and beyond to make us feel right at home! She is thoughtful, caring and just amazing!! We’ve been living here for about a week and we absolutely love it! We looked at many new apartments within LoDo and RiNo area, and we’re so happy we ended up at Griffis. The location is fantastic, the amenities are awesome (assigned parking for $50/mo, pool and hot tub open year round, good gym, and dog run), and we can’t hear the neighbors so it’s been great. Our biggest concern was management but Victoria and Jose has been a delight to work with and we’re very grateful to them!

It's incredibly apparent how much effort the new management company is putting into this property. Since we've moved in a few months ago, we've seen a number of the amenities be upgraded, with the addition of a few new ones. I'd have to agree with another poster in saying beyond the lovely accommodations and competitive pricing, it's the management team that makes this property stand out. Carla is an absolute godsend and the best property manager we've ever had. Can't see us leaving anytime soon.

If you had asked me a few months ago I would have given griffis an outstanding review but recently I have been left with a very tainted impression of what once was a favorable opinion. I've lived at Griffis for over a year now, and till date I have never been treated as nothing more than a paycheck. The management here has no regard for it's residents, their property or security. The courtesy security patrol for the building has a habit of absconding when there is a problem, crime in the building is more than any other community I've lived at from packages getting stolen to car break-ins, sometimes multiple times in a night within the garage as well as colorful characters and homeless people frequenting the neighborhood and premises. Additionally repairs are continuously being made to the community, which would be favorable but it seems like management likes to go out of its way to inconvenience residents, for example for garage repairs 500 /- cars had to be removed and parked in two temporary first come first serve dirt lots (that double as housing for the homeless) and patrolled by the very same absconding security or had to find parking somewhere within the neighborhood/downtown which is almost impossible or as far as the highlands for four consecutive days. No reimbursement was given to residents who pay top dollar in rent and parking fees. The amenities and apartments are very nice but it is not worth the disrespect and disregard residents receive from management. Definitely would not recommend Griffis, you're better off trying one of the many apartments downtown!

The staff in the front office is phenomenal! Super friendly and easy to work with. I have made several service requests for general things and they are fixed within 24 hours every time. The location is awesome and anything you need is within walking distance. Griffis is working to improve the community and the rent is very reasonable for the area

We have loved living in Griffis (formerly Skye). Sure, they had a management change, which will always cause some tenants to get upset, but we think that they have handled it well. It seems like they had some issues with their 3rd party vendors for awhile (security & elevator), but it seems like those logistics are being worked out, and the actual management company & apartment complex has been great!

We chose this apartment complex because we love the proximity to downtown &  King Soopers, yet it’s still a quiet neighborhood with free street parking. The inside is beautiful—tall ceiling, wood floors, washer/dryers, lots of light, etc. The building is built well, and we have never heard our neighbors, which is amazing! We also have a dog, and it’s so nice that there’s a dog park in the complex so that our pup can run around & get his energy out without having to walk a few blocks to a park. The team in the office has been WONDERFUL to work with, and they are so much of the reason that we love living here. They have taken their time to get to know us & our dog, and are always quick to answer questions. We recommend it!

This place gives you the downtown lifestyle with less of the hustle and bustle.  It's just behind the Rockie's stadium, but is still pretty quiet.  The one downside is the train tracks that it's next to.  I do not have an apartment that is train side so I don't really notice it.  The staff are very friendly.  I don't interact with them very much, but Carla still knows me by name.  The apartment itself is nice.  You get a new upgrade every year and I now have a ceiling fan.  There is difficulty with some apartments not getting good cell phone service.  I have a corner unit and the service is okay, but still have to go out on the balcony sometimes.  Parking outside of the garage is very difficult so sometimes guests have to park further away.  There have been issues with being charged pet rent and for parking spots when you weren't supposed to be.  The staff is very helpful with fixing those problems.  Overall, the apartment complex is clean and well run.

Location, location, location!  Two blocks from Coors Field, a 5 minute walk to Union Station, and a brand new King Soopers across the street.  The staff are lovely and they make everyone feel welcome.  The residents are nice and the building is very pet friendly.  There are several common areas, a pool, gym, and small dog park.  There's also a parking garage (for an additional fee), but that's super important for this area as street parking is limited.  It's usually pretty quiet--doesn't feel like you're in an apartment.  Lots of different floor plans to choose from.  Some units get noise from the train, but I don't know how bad it is firsthand.

Amazing community, they offer weekly free seminars and events for residences to get to know each other as well as the staff (and they are fun/legit events that you WANT to go to). They are always helpful and incredibly nice. The location is unbeatable as well. I would recommend Skye to anybody moving into the Denver metro area.

Skye is in a great location in Lodo.  There are new restaurants popping up every day in the neighborhood.  The pool is great on weekdays.  Weekends it can be a bit like MTV spring break.  The grills by the pool are great for entertaining at night.  My only problem with the company is they have raised rent about $100 every year.

Skye 2905 has great amenities, hands-on management, responsive maintenance, and a very friendly atmosphere. However, if you are going to live here, you better live on the non-train side of the building. It's loud. You might think that you can deal with it, but when you wake up every day at 5:15 from the abrasive sounds of the Coal Train, you will regret your decision. Dont let this deter you, train nerds!

My wife and I moved into Huntington Ridge the winter of 2017. We thoroughly enjoyed our overall experience living in their community. To start; maintenance deserves a lot of credit. We were there when they hired a whole crew of new faces to the maintenance team and we always saw them smiling and working together to do work on time and at a high standard.  Sheila and Pacha in the leasing office were the best support the whole time we were living there. Sheila especially always took the time to greet us at the office and make sure we were doing well. Chiquita, Sheila's cat is also always a welcome face! 
    The apartment was in great shape despite it's age and required little in the way of maintenance.  We were in a one bedroom and we appreciated the layout for it's  solid use of space and the outdoor storage/patio situation, and the washer/dryer in unit. The vaulted ceilings in the second floor units can make temperature management pretty hard, nothing a space heater can't fix though. Not having so many dogs around was a huge bonus and I will forever miss that. 
    Thanks again to Sheila, Pacha, and the management team for helping give my family a place to grow and make memories.

This is the best apartment complex I have ever lived in. It is quiet compared to other places as I don't normally hear my neighbors (can't hear them using the bathroom or doing stuff, the walls definitely aren't thin), the area is clean with no dog dookie laying around, rent is not over priced even upon lease renewal, water/sewer/trash included and so you pay the same every month, the staff is kind, helpful, and friendly, no cat rent (one time non-refundable deposit only), and the 105, 11, and 83L have stops nearby.

My apartment (cheshire) was spacious. It had a fireplace, balcony, full size washer/dryer, and vaulted ceilings. I chose this place because they have a washer/dryer inside the unit, reliable public transit nearby, excellent reviews, and it's a really good deal on rent considering the size of my unit and everything it had.

I don't have any complaints about the place. All my maintenance requests were done the same day. The only time it took more than a day was when they got me a brand new washer machine which understandably takes time. I was not expecting to get a new washer so I came home to a pleasant surprise! When I had issues with the heater, and told them the energy company says to get a certified person to fix it, that same day, the apartment manager immediately had a certified professional come in to fix it while I was at work, and I came home to a place with no problems.

The apartment managers Sheila and Pasha are great people to work with, always made sure I was taken care of. Pasha was gracious in calculating whether a month to month lease or lease break would save me more money when I was relocating for a job (I would have stayed otherwise).

I definitely would recommend Huntington Ridge Apartments to anyone who wants a good home and doesn't care for luxury. Actually, I think having a washer/dryer in my unit without really expensive rent is already a luxury. Many places would be more expensive even if they don't have washer/dryer in the unit.

Thank you so very much everyone at Huntington Ridge for a really great living experience, I will miss you guys!

I have lived in several apartments around the Denver area over the years and can easily claim that this was the best complex I have lived in! The grounds are clean, the neighbors are friendly, and the apartments are really unique. I am only leaving to be closer to work, but am sad to go...I would recommend this place to anyone!

My boyfriend & I moved here from Louisiana (June 2015) and we have lived here almost a year now. We didn't even see the place before we signed the lease because they made us feel so comfortable! This was our first place together after college and it has been a dream, everyone in the office is so helpful & understanding. Our heater has broken twice (no ones fault) and each time the repair men were here within 30 min and had it fixed in less than an hour. The management makes you feel at home the way they are so understanding. we have had to pay our rent late because of unforeseen health issues and they were so awesome about it. The only reason we won't be re-signing is because we want to get a dog and they are not allowed here:( I'm sure we will miss the the outstanding management here that is so rare these days. I highly recommend living here, its super quiet, all the neighbors are very nice. I also work a job that requires me to leave very early (4:30 am) and sometimes get home very late (3am) and I have always felt very safe here at any hour! With the rent being so ridiculous in Denver you can't beat this place! Sheila & Pasha are doing an outstanding job!

This is is good and affordable. It close to all shopping center. The rooms are big. Living is nice due to a big massive window. It's a little in the 2000's model homes but the space is bigger than most apartments.

I have lived here for five years and i love it.  They are friendly and the maintenance always comes out the same day. It's quiet and I've never had any issues with my neighbors.  I highly suggest these apartments!  The grounds are kept and they usually open the pool early!  They also have unique and cute Floorplans.

We love The Overland. We've had a great time living here. Highly recommend it to any young professional. Love the mountain views and the area is awesome. The staff is great - very well run and organized.
The move in process was quick and easy. Everything was handled with clear communication and professionalism. Living there has been great.

I have been a resident here for approximately four months. The things I love about this place include cleanliness, great communication with management, and a very friendly environment. Things I wish would be better is the trash service. A lot of residents leave trash outside their doors every day, disregarding the trash pick up schedule. I know we are struggling with a consistent trash removal pick up system but trash should not sit in the hallway for five consecutive days.
besides having a package thief and a management that doesn’t care to do anything about it, the community is great. super clean and quiet, the parking garage and property are relatively secure.

Great spaces and amenities. The neighborhood is great for biking to nearby restaurants and activities on Broadway & I like the gym at the complex. My only complaints are security of the garage and my mail was stolen a couple of times.

Muy buena, me siento cómodo y agusto.
Muchas gracias a GreyStar y The Overland por darme la oportunidad de formar parte de su comunidad.
Nos han ayudado mucho.
Una gran empleada se llama Samantha W. 
Destaca mucho, muy paciente, amable y maneja muy bien y fluido ING/ESP.

Would not live here again. Amenities are low quality and pool is always gross and breaking down or residents break glass. It’s been shut down for several reasons over the last year. The community is messy and people steal packages and leave the community areas gross.
Incredibly helpful staff, perfectly maintained ammenities, and overall amazing place.
Lovely building with lovely staff, in a convenient location and very clean!
Would not recommend unless you want to live in a mismanaged apartment building. Not worth the money in the slightest.

Honestly, not the best experience and I have only been here less that two weeks. Moved in only for convenience to work.  Poor treatment by office staff on move-in; hallways need deodorizing really badly, stinks of trash, and outside the building (all the way around just smells awful); constant smell of urine.  These things need to be addressed. An embarrassment.

1. Hazardous trash situation 
2. Transients actively breaking into the community
3. Mail room with no parcel pending or camera
4. Smell of urine around complex
5. Unclear utility charges
6. Bug infestation 
7. Dirty or unusable amenities 
8. Un-forthcoming staff

Definitely will not get your money’s worth, harassing emails, things are constantly breaking and taking weeks and months to fix, the mishandling of garbage has led to a fly infestation all over the building, charges and fees go up every month with the weakest excuses behind them. Plenty of other buildings in the area that are just as new.

This property appears to be fantastic "on paper"--terrific amenities, up-and-coming location, etc.

The reality is that the building is not well maintained or managed. Things like the pool and hot tub have regularly been out-of-service (~3 total months) since the building opened last summer.

Three main problems here: 

1) Multiple of residents do not respect the property whatsoever. From dropping trash, glass, etc. in the pool and hot tub to allowing their dogs to use the hallways, elevators, etc. as relief areas, there seems to be only apathy to how many of us perceive the building.

2) Whether it is the building's management, Greystar's representatives, or the owners of the building, not much is being implemented to curb all this bad behavior or compensate the upstanding residents for missing out on the experience they're paying for here. We routinely receive emails warning us of exorbitant fines if we're caught doing something like letting dogs pee in the hallway, but (apart from another resident informing management of a violation), there isn't a way to enforce any of these rules. A simple installation of security cameras in the elevators and hallways would probably resolve the issue, but either someone doesn't want to spend the money or they can't figure out how to drill a few holes.

3) While management should not be blamed for some of this bad behavior, I have to say the attitude in regard to our complaints has been unacceptable. When complaining we're brushed off or given a bunch of excuses but rarely are the issues solved.
I have been here for a few months now and have loved the amenities and community within the building!
Property is in an area undergoing rapid change. Very convenient for public transit! Absolutely fantastic views of the mountains and partial view of downtown.
The Overland is fantastic! The building is well maintained, the amenities are great, and the staff is engaging and helpful. Perfect location too!

A great place to live! The views are unmatched to many other buildings within the same price range. Staff is friendly and helpful and always encourage the community to come together. Building is maintained nicely- our cleaning lady is so sweet and awesome! I look forward to seeing her when I grab a morning coffee (another building perk).
Pool and hot tub have been closed for half my lease with the claim they are year around. Doors get stuck and never fixed. And the 5th floor stairwell has floods with water when rains.

Do not waste your time or money in moving in here and then having to deal with the stress this place will cause you. I have never been more excited for the day to move out of here I currently live here and signed a lease in August of 2023. I learned quickly after repeated breaking to vehicle no cameras that work and the community of vragrents that live in the area make this place unbearable. Don’t be fooled by there leasing agents they will be nice until you sign!
just renewed for a third time, new property manager and staff are awesome! Fun events, maintenance is on top of it, they just repainted, and custodians keep it very clean!
Front desk employees are amazing and go well above and beyond for residents! The main reason I live here still is for that! Lived here 4  years. Wish we had more activities again though!

Horrible  managment, Horrible  mateniance,  no response  to calls are emails,  garage shattered  my email, and tgey won't take responsibility,  that's only half tge nonsense. Can't wait till I move out of hete.

Está bonito, las áreas sociales están bien y los departamentos se ven bien también, en mi departamento se escucha fuerte el sonido de la autopista cuando abro la puerta del balcón pero al cerrar la puerta todo ok

-Current bed bug infestation
-There is NO management onsite - they have abandoned us, so fend for yourself!
-Homeless people all around the building, some pooping INSIDE the building
-Homeless people doing drugs right outside the building
-No guarantee that you'll get any of your packages
-Neighbors smoking weeds/cigs in a SMOKE-FREE building
-Poor ventilation.  You can both hear your neighbors and smell what they're cooking through the vents
-Disregarded maintenance requests.  I've been waiting for a new A/C unit since SEPTEMBER of 2022 (it's now JULY of 2023)
-Elevators are always down
-NO consistent hot water
-HORRIBLE billing system.  You'll be charged for random, incorrect things & you're ignored when you try to have the charges removed.  I was being charged $75 each for THREE parking spaces, when I only have one car.  It literally took MONTHS for them to remove the charges 
-Dirty, dysfunctional laundry room
-Sketchy neighbors, right on your floor

BELIEVE THE ONE STAR REVIEWS!! - I was supposed to move into my unit June 9th, when I walked in there were poop stains all over the rug, the place was dirty, and there was so much trash on my balcony I had to fill up a trash bag and throw it out. When I turned on the lights for the first time the switch was popping and buzzing so loudly that maintenance said it was unsafe and turned off my power for the first 4 days I was there until it could be fixed. The dishwasher exploded and flooded my unit the first time I used it because it was clogged with food from the pervious tenant. The oven and stove did not work and when I put in a maintenance request I came home to my oven gone along with all the pans I was storing inside of it. Maintenance has been amazing at responding but I have yet to hear back at all about the condition of my unit being completely unlivable for my first four days. No one is ever in the office to talk to even during their “open” hours, I can’t leave a message for anyone, and no one has responded by email. If you move in here you will be disrespected, given a disgusting unit, and ignored by the people who run it as they try to fill up more units with unsuspecting renters. The property managers are slummy, scummy, and ugly hearted. If you can avoid this place live literally anywhere else, I promise this place isn’t worth it.

Don’t even bother trying to rent here. Had a scheduled appointment and nobody ever showed or was even at the leasing office. TOTAL WASTE OF TIME. Listen to the other reviews. I asked other tenants going in and out the building and they all said this office is horrible with everything.

Baker Tower in a nutshell: 

If you take a look at their lease, you can see that it isn’t at all an equal agreement between tenant and building manager. You will notice that if your family lives in a far-off part of the country and you might want to sublet your room because you won’t be in it for a month or so and you feel weird throwing a thousand dollars at a place you’re not occupying, that’s not possible. They don’t allow tenants to sublet. Also, the person you talk to will give you a rental price which may seem reasonable, but you will be responsible for not only your utilities, but for the utilities for the entire building. Including the lights that always stay on in the hallway, and the heat in the hallway they never shut off, even in the summer months. So you’ll want to add at least $250 to the rent price they quote. And finally, if you want to get out of your lease for any reason, sorry. It’s impossible to get out of your lease without either paying them the rest of the least or a buyout fee, which can be two months’ rent. If you look at all of that stuff and don’t see the red flags, sign away! 

Next, you’ll be dealing with the management. After living there for a while, let me advise you on a couple of things: Don’t call the office and leave a message. You’re a resident, not a potential resident. They won’t call you back. And email is out of the question, unless you want a response from your manager that include the sentence, “I’m sorry I haven’t gotten back to you, I haven’t checked my email in a couple months.” No. Go into the office and talk to someone personally. It’s the only way to get anything accomplished with them. 

A couple years ago, they made renovations to every unit. They gave me a gift card and told me I had couldn’t be in my apartment because they were replace the balcony wall, which really amounted to replacing a really drafty uninsulated wall with an even draftier, even more uninsulated wall. You see, people had problems with their pipes freezing and exploding. In fact every time the weather outside drops below freezing, they put a sign in the elevators telling residents to keep their apartments above 70º so the pipes don’t freeze. The problem is, I’m not convinced that the 60s-era thermostats that are in every apartment are even connected to the heating system. If you hear a loud pop and then your apartment starts flooding, run to the office and hope to catch the maintenance guy.

The review titled "Great Location, Awful Building" is telling the truth: the entire complex went without hot water for three weeks while management pretended that it was fixed. If I had known the reality of the situation sooner, I would have exercised my right to move out during the outage. Maxx Properties billed everyone in the complex at full rent despite their obvious failing to provide a habitable environment. The slightly lower rent for the location and the downstairs gym are very nice, but I won't be sticking around at the end of my lease. This was a few months ago. We just have had multiple days of hot water outages since the previously mentioned multi-week one. No telling how long this will continue. I can't stress this enough: stay away.

I lived at Baker Tower for 3 1/2 years (cheap rent is hard to resist) and just moved out. The building is terrible, the neighborhood is sublime. If there were half stars available I'd give this 1 1/2, just for the location. 

For the last year and change we had no cold water at night. After about 8 PM the cold tap had to run at full blast for 20 minutes in order to get comfortably warm water, any time before that and it was literally steaming hot, scalding you if you're careless. After my 3rd report to management and 3rd reply of "the temp's fine from here", I gave up. Enough complaints came in for them to try something and the entire building had no hot water at all, at any time, for 3 weeks. It got so bad that people were scratching their complaints into the elevator walls. People were threatening to go to HUD about it. Hot water came back but I still had no cold water at night. I kept bottled water on hand in case of burns.

Heat is also an issue. They crank the (shared) heat well through Fall. You get one wall unit for A/C but the apartments are not designed for airflow, so if you've got your heart set on this place and you're sensitive to heat, plan to make the living area your bedroom, otherwise you will see essentially no benefit from your A/C. Average temp in my bedroom was 78, 365 days a year. I got rid of my comforter pretty early and slept under sheets only.

When I first lived here they had four sets of washers and dryers servicing the whole building, but they were designed for single family homes, to be used no more than once or twice a day, and so 2-3 sets were always broken. Sometimes all of them were. We complained about this for three years before they finally sprung for industrial-class equipment, and it works okay now. The AC units in the gym don’t work so the temp there pushes 80 .

I can't blame the management - this is a corporate building and the money men are out on the east coast. And as I said, the location is great. There’s reasonably priced, good food to the north and overpriced, decent food to the south. Trader Joes, Walgreens, King Soopers are all close. If you drink, there are too many spots to count along Broadway. I was actually offered a rent cut to stay for a fourth year but I had to get out of there. I would say that unless you’re fine with handling a lot of stress, you should stay away.
Via Apartments are nice and the leasing team was responsive and super helpful! They’re working on construction right now and I can’t wait to see the end result!!

DO NOT LIVE HERE. Trust the bad reviews that you see. The office staff is the worst I've EVER dealt with. I was sent a renewal offer, accepted that offer before the expiration date, only to be told they would not be honoring that rate anymore since it was a "mistake".....however, they didn't address this at all or send me a new offer letter UNTIL I went down to the office WEEKS later to ask them a couple questions.

The prices are ridiculous considering what you get. Communication is TERRIBLE. Elevators will break constantly without any word from the office staff, the dog wash doesn't even have a shower head (which they never sent notice about), packages are stolen ALL the time, homeless people get in, the hot tub is literally green, the pool has a capacity of 6 people because it's so tiny, and I know several people who have had their cars stolen and/or broken into out of the "secure" garage we pay an additional $100 per month for.

I've lived here for almost 3 years and can't believe how downhill this place has gone. Most people I know are not going to renew their lease due to the new office staff, raising rates, constant office staff turnover, and outdated amenities. Do yourself a favor and move somewhere else that actually gives you what they offer for the price you pay.
What a great experience, from the tour to move in! The leasing team was helpful and responsive, and maintenance resolved the couple of issues I had within 24 hours. Super excited to live here!
love how well maintained the building is-- I always appreciate how responsive the Via team is to dealing with any issues and helping out however they can
4 years plus and we could not be happier in any Denver rental property.  Location location location makes all our needs so accessible to us. Great amenities too
Best apartment community I’ve ever been apart of! The people here are super friendly and easy to make friends with.the staff is also extremely nice and helpful.

I signed my lease this summer in June. My dishwasher still does not work, and the other items I requested to be fixed when I did my walk through still is not fixed. There are used needles and trash in the entrance to your apartment, and a roach problem. The building has been without hot water for a week and no heat for a few days now. No one is ever in the leasing office and good luck trying to get a hold of someone on the phone for assistance. If I could give no stars I would. Please save yourself the headache!

Don’t let all these recent 5 stars fool you, the only reason they are there is because management offered a monetary reward to those who did so. They do NOT reflect the quality of this complex. If I could give a 0 I would. Ever since new ownership in May 2022 this place has continued to steadily decline. Do not move here unless you want stress, no communication to solve problems, and to feel unsafe. Over $2,000 in unjust charges have been added to my account and management is failing to respond to any communication about it. These charges include duplicate deposits, double charging on rent, and pet fees when I have submitted ESA letters upon move in. They didn’t charge utilities for over 9 months, with no official communication about it during those months, but now they are backtracking and adding $900 to everyone’s account for past utilities. This place is a nightmare, stay far away.

I've lived here for a few months now and absolutely love Stratford at Lowry. Kendra in the front office is absolutely amazing. Kind, full of personality, friendly and very accommodating. The maintenance team is quick to help out if anything should go wrong, even when off duty. These guys are the first ones up in the morning plowing the snow from the sidewalks, salting the area, and are very approachable if there are any concerns. The apartments themselves are great. High ceilings, skylights, and energy efficient. Love the dog park, and the kid friendly basketball courts. Price is very reasonable too. Overall, best apartment and working team I have encountered thus far. Thanks guys!

I had a scheduled 2pm leasing tour at The Ranch At First Creek, and I arrived promptly for the appointment. However, to my dismay, the leasing office was closed when I got there. This experience was incredibly unprofessional and left me extremely disappointed. 

As someone looking for a new place to call home, I expected a higher level of professionalism and reliability from a leasing office. The fact that they couldn't honor a scheduled appointment reflects poorly on their management and customer service.

This incident has cast doubts on my perception of The Ranch At First Creek, and I hope they take this feedback seriously to ensure a more organized and reliable experience for potential residents in the future.

These apartments are way to expensive for what you get. They look nice but it’s only a show. The windows don’t close properly, there’s always trash in the elevators or the grounds themselves, the snow removal of the grounds is placed in parking spots instead of non-parking areas and piled up next to parked cars, they constantly tow residents cars and worst of all the property management of this property seem to only hire incompetent people to run the office. Worst of all instead of not towing resident’s cars during a time when most people barely have money they choose to continue to tow cars. This property also does not have guest parking so if you have a guest over their car will be towed as well. The residents are charged to park on the premises but still get towed. This is to me just shows how greedy and uncaring this management company is. Why bother living in a place where you’re only viewed as a dollar sign.

We moved in 7 months ago. The day we moved in we had no heat, as we are moving in they had to bring in contractors to open up the ceiling in our living room, dining room, master bedroom and bathroom to repair pipes. We had a mess and no heat for 5 days in December. Since then we have had various charges for renters insurance added to our rent without prior knowledge that they were missing the documents that said that we did have renters insurance. That issue took 4 months and a call to the corporate office to get fixed. The is a non-smoking property and people smoke all of the time and leave the trash everywhere! This is also supposed to be a gated community, the gates have never worked. There has been numerous accounts of theft and stolen vehicles in just the six months. The pool has been shut down by the health department the majority of the time, in fact the pool has only been open a few days in the last year. What a joke! There are many other options, stay away from this money sucking place with poor management.

My husband and I have enjoyed living at Milo, the apartments are well designed and well maintained. We live in a corner unit which is quiet. Management and staff are always polite and helpful. The only bad thing is, that when the management closes, the building should be locked and most of the time it is not, which makes it unsafe.

Just don't move here. The worst horrible office people I have ever seen.

Yeah, the building is new and has a nice pool and amenities.
But you know what determines your daily life is actually people, the office managers.

They has a service called Luxer, which is a package service, and of course, their unprofessional office people did not set it up correctly for me. I lost my Amazon packages since the locker code was sent to a former resident.

I have talked several times with the office manager and she said she would contact the former resident and get back to me. Of course, there was no response from her and she quit last month. Talked to a new office manager last month, and he said he will figure out what he can do, yeah as you can expect no response for a month, and today he finally responded to my follow-up email and say the same thing. Contact Amazon. 

I am very frustrated with Milo and how they treat the residents.

I feel like I am just an annoying burden to them.

If you are thinking about checking this place out, here’s a dose of reality:

Terrible package process: If your package gets delivered to the large locker with other content, you are expected to remove & sort through 20-30 packages if you can’t find your stuff right away. Sometimes your stuff gets delivered to the door; sometimes it says it got delivered to the front office & no one knows where it is; sometimes it gets left out in front of the building on the sidewalk; sometimes it gets tossed into a pile in the front office or mailroom. 

Unsecured & broken access points: In the year I’ve been here, I estimate that 2 of the 4 primary points of entrance to the property have been broken. This means that the door is just hanging open for all to enter, or when you scan, the door doesn’t open.

Overcharged for parking & not private: I’m not kidding when I say that someone threw their old rims in a parking space & they have been there the ENTIRE YEAR I’ve lived here and counting. One of the “perks” you pay for is private/ gated parking, but on multiple occasions the gate breaks & it’s open game for anyone. In all cases, they have taken over a week to fix it. It’s broken as I write this, & we are over 2 weeks. I’ve already seen a car window shattered in the area that would otherwise be gated. Not very “luxurious.” 

Common spaces misused & filthy:  The counters around the grill are disgusting. This outside patio & the adjacent common room are regularly used for private & public parties, which is a great. Problem is, they sometimes don’t clean up the mess for days. I've got photos of a trash-covered common-space patio that lasted for two days (5/15-5/16) from a party the day prior. I would expect a “luxury” apartment to either enforce strict clean up policies or have someone come out early the next morning to clean the space (or both).

Getting tired of typing, but it’s important that someone calls them out on their poor operation (especially since they solicit reviews). I’ve also seen dog crap on the mail room floor that lasted 2 days, and the same trash in cans by the elevators that lasted 4 days. Beware before signing, it’s not what it seems.

This is my 3rd lease with this building and I can honestly say to spend your money elsewhere. I have never missed or been late on paying rent. However, I have had multiple packages lost by the leasing office, my mail stopped arriving because they changed it to a different box randomly and then I had to call and make a formal complaint with USPS to try to fix it. Then, my fob stopped working when the lease renewed and I couldn’t access my own vehicle or leave my apartment. The facilities look nice but if you are going to rent in this price range, I would recommend that you do so elsewhere at a non-Gables residential community.

Moved from out of town during Covid and we were only able to tour places virtually. One of our main concerns when moving was noise and insulation between units. We didn’t like any of the few top floor units available here, but after being promised “10 inches of concrete, and some of the best insulation in Denver” we decided to go against our gut feeling of sticking to a top floor, and sign an 8th floor apartment.

We moved to the 8th floor and we noticed issues right away. As soon as we stepped in, we could hear a lot of heavy stomping from upstairs. We mentioned this to management right away, and they told us nobody has complained about noise before, so the problem has to be the tenants above us. Management emailed them, and this only caused more issues, neighbors didn’t like that and the noise increased after that. Management never took any responsibility for the noise, even when providing evidence of excessive noise in the middle of the night, they just pointed fingers and blamed the people upstairs for being loud and not knowing how to live in an apartment building. The walls between apartments are paper thin, we could hear conversations from the side neighbors as well as music/bass and all sorts of noises.

Management decided to offer us the ability to move within the complex as long as the unit was more expensive and we pay a transfer fee. We were desperate enough to agree and decided to move to a townhome (they have 9 town homes, and only 2 are leased, should have been a red flag). We packed up, and moved across the building. If you haven’t seen the layout, the townhomes are two-story apartments, and there’s a flat on top of you. This was the biggest mistake we ever made. AVOID the TownHomes!!!!!! There’s a reason most of them are vacant after a year of being ready to lease. You can hear 5 times more noise from your upstairs neighbors, somehow they managed to make them even more paper thin between units. Our neighbors had kids, and we could feel (from our downstairs living room) our townhouse shake when the kids ran across, which was VERY often. It was so bad, we paid 2 months of rent to liquidate and moved out within 2 weeks of living here.
We hear EVERYTHING going on around us at all hours of the day - doors shutting, walking, talking, barking, and every other miscellaneous bang.

I lived in this building for just over 4 years. The apartment itself and amenities in this building are fine.

There were a few problems. The refrigerator in the apartment was extremely loud when it was running. I’d never heard such a loud refrigerator before. There was no way to fix this issue, so I had to buy a small refrigerator myself for the apartment. Also, the water went out much more often than any apartment that I’ve lived in before. But it didn’t bother me too much, to be honest.

The main reason for my low rating of this apartment was the following: 

When I moved out of the apartment, I had to move out before my lease ended, but with less than 2 months remaining on my lease. And the management charged me the 2-month early termination fee, even after I told them that I was planning on paying the remainder on my lease. 

This was very disappointing and did not seem right, since I ended up having to pay more in total than what I should have paid for the full term of the lease. It didn’t seem legal for them to do this, but I’m not sure, and with the amount of money involved, it wasn’t worth trying to figure out.

I could not have had a worse experience living here. The main problem is how mean and rude the management staff are and a complete lack of empathy towards their residents. They care about future residents and profits and don't have a care in the world about the experience of their current residents.

In the year I lived here the hot water was turned off at least a dozen time if not more (once for the span of 5 days), garage doors have been broken multiple times (at one point for 3 months). The building has been under constant construction with construction zones blocking entrances, noise all day every day (can't even imagine working from home), and amenities that we are paying an arm and a leg for closed down (gym, pool, etc.)

And the cherry on top was my unit as well as the rest of my floor flooding (supposedly at no fault of Griffis or so they say). It took them TWO MONTHS to repair my unit. I had no flooring and holes in my dry wall for two months before they were actually able to get repairs done. During that time, all I got was an insignificant discount on my rent and a property manager telling me "I know this is uncomfortable, but we aren't required to do anything based on your lease". Absolutely no empathy to me or the situation you are asking me to live in. 

Do yourself a favor and live elsewhere.

I recently had the pleasure of living at Griffis Lodo in downtown Denver and I have to say it was one of the best living experiences of my life. The building is in a prime location with easy access to all the best restaurants, bars, and shops in the area. The building itself is beautifully designed and well-maintained, with top-quality amenities and services that make you feel like you're living in luxury.

The apartment units are spacious and modern, with high ceilings, large windows, and stunning views of the city. The kitchens are fully equipped with stainless steel appliances making it easy to cook and entertain guests. The bathrooms are equally impressive, with sleek designs and high-end finishes that make you feel like you're at a spa.

One of my favorite things about living at Griffis Lodo was the incredible community of people who live here. Everyone is friendly, welcoming, and respectful, and there are plenty of opportunities to meet new people and make lasting friendships. The building also hosts regular events and activities, which are a great way to get involved and have fun with your neighbors.

Overall, I would highly recommend Griffis Lodo to anyone looking for a beautiful, luxurious, and welcoming place to call home in downtown Denver. The staff is amazing and always willing to help with any questions or concerns, and the amenities and services are top-notch. If you're looking for the ultimate living experience in the heart of the city, this is the place for you!

There have been numerous car break ins, intruders in the building stealing things and having violent outbreaks, as well as fireworks being shot off from balconies and landing on other resident’s patios almost hitting their pets. Also, we’re being forced to switch to Fetch, a service that’s notorious for stealing packages without any ability to opt out. RUN!

Condescending, cold and dismissive behaviour does not inspire a sense of community. I have lived at 1490 Delgany for over 6 years and have never felt the need to write a review...until now. 

Fire, Life, Safety - In late September my carbon monoxide detector started sounding on Friday afternoon. I immediately submitted a request with the front desk, and had to submit 2 additional requests until it was finally addressed that following Wednesday afternoon. Fire, life, safety is supposed to be addressed immediately. For weeks if you walked the halls at 1490 Delgany, you heard everyone's carbon monoxide detectors loudly chirping. And sadly, this happened to one of the residents while she was at work and her dog was home alone. The detector chirped so loudly and repeatedly for hours, that the frightened dog clawed at the 7th floor screen window and ultimately fell to its death onto the 3rd floor courtyard. Our neighboring building made attempts to notify Griffis of the scared animal, but no action was taken. This incident was never acknowledged by management. 

Communication - Communication is horrific and typically one sided at Griffis. They will impose changes but not engage in constructive communication with residents. This avoidant and dismissive communication style often infuriates people and escalates situations.  I think it's natural to assume when you live in a luxury apartment building that you receive excellent customer service. 

Construction - There is an incredible amount of construction going on at 1490 Delgany right now. So if you work from home, they're recommending you go sit in the common areas of the building and work. Constant hammering and 3rd party vendors walking through the halls. They are scheduled to do MAJOR construction on the gym and pool area, which we will lose access to and most likely not see an amenity credit in our rent fees. 

Concierge - Connie is the only amazing part of living here. But sadly it seems they will be ridding our building of this service as they are transitioning everything to be contactless and soulless. So it will become an expensive, contactless, soulless, and sterile community.  We will be one of the only downtown luxury buildings with no concierge. This is a concern as the homelessness and crime rate is rapidly increasing in the LoDo area. Last week 42 people were arrested from Union Station..which is a block away from our building. It will not be safe here for much longer.

Wow, disappointed and angry cannot even begin to describe how frustrated we are with the transition from The Verve to Griffis Lodo. We couldn't even come home to our apartment because of an "IT issue" (key fob doesn't work ANYWHERE; we were locked outside on the street with no way to our apartment "home") that has never happened in the almost three years that we lived in this building. We can't even get into the building or lobby. 

We sat in the lobby of the apartment (thankfully another resident let us in) for a very long time. I am interviewing for a new job and this restricted/limited access to our home or "apartment" is negatively affecting my performance and interviewing capabilities. I am so stressed, due to the fact that I don't know if my fiance will even be able to come back home or if I will have to interrupt my interview process to let him into our "home" / apartment (this should be a basic right for a "renter"). Not to mention, we are dealing with all of this and still paying above market average rent  prices. 

We pay an above average rate for this apartment, amenities, and location and this is unacceptable. The management shows a true lack of community and inclusion and the fact that we cannot access our overpaid "home"/ apartment due to "transition problems" (that we have never experienced before in the three years that we have lived here) is a major issue in our eyes and in the eyes of all who look for our guidance.

I've been here a month and in that time we have had 3 major building-wide issues.
1 The door access system went down.
2 The power went out for 4 straight days and off and on for a full week
3. The elevators have been down for a week.

Management tells tenants different things if they communicate anything at all.

Do not rent!

This property has a variety of studio floorplans and the way they are each designed is beyond what you'd find in a studio elsewhere. It was well thought out and the space is so well used. Also close to Sloan's Lake and so many new restaurants and bars in the area!

I've now lived at 1515 Flats for nearly 3 years now. This building is beautiful and well maintained. Sloan's Lake is just two blocks away along with several restaurants and hot spots. I could not ask for a better location while living in Denver. Downtown is less than 3 miles away. If you're looking for new and exceptional service, look no further. 1515 Flats is your place. I highly recommend!!

i am moving out so have no belongings left in my apartment but have to stay an extra night for cleaning. unfortunately my fire alarm has started chirping and the front office refuses to help me out with a ladder or any support since it’s in the lease that i have to replace the fire alarm battery. this is one of many instances and since i’m moving out in just over it...it’s very corporate and they’re honestly morally bankrupt people. avoid avoid avoid...
I absolutely love it here! It is beautiful. Also, it is conveniently located near a Target. The resident events are a lot of fun as well.
Super cool location close to downtown and the lake. Very walk able to shops and restaurants too! They run great specials and value their residents.

I have lived here for four years, and I can safely say that 2024 has been the worst year for Eviva. As of the creation of this post, the building is in a state of disrepair. We have near-daily hot and cold water outages, broken elevators that are not repaired until another elevator breaks, and broken garage door systems. The leasing and office employees ignore emails, and the out-of-control leasing managers pick fights. The community's utility bills double for no reason and with no data provided to back it up. Eviva is a circus. If you sign a lease here, you will encounter issues like this. You have been educated.

I strongly advise folks to avoid Eviva. It is poorly managed for what you pay, and working with the local community manager + general manager (as of April 2023) in resolving issues (caused by Eviva or contractors) has been painful and overly time consumptive.

I’ve had a number of disappointing experiences at Eviva, but the most frustrating incident was when a maintenance team entered my unit without proper notice for a repair while I was traveling. Not only did maintenance leave dry wall powder all over my unit (that I had to clean) and a hole in the kitchen ceiling, but they also left my front door unlocked for five days while I was out of town. Fortunately all of my belongings were safe, but it was an invasive experience to say the least. 

After spending a significant amount of time emailing and calling, Eviva finally offered to send a cleaning team to pick up after the mess that was made by maintenance. By this point I had lost trust in property management (this was the second time a maintenance team entered the unit without me knowing beforehand), so I carved out time from work specifically to be in the unit while the cleaning crew was scheduled to work. The cleaning crew didn’t show up at the time we agreed upon and we had to reschedule (ugh).

The icing on the cake was that Equity Apartments’ renewals team tried to increase my rent by $100/month as this entire process was going on. After spending several hours emailing/talking to regional and senior regional managers, the renewals team conceded and offered rent at a small discount.

For those of you running into issues with Eviva, I encourage you to try connecting with regional or senior regional directors/managers. In my experience, these people had greater willingness to help and improve my experience as a tenant.

I can’t say enough how amazing the apartment as well as the staff is at Eviva on Cherokee.

We’re moving from Columbus, Ohio and took possession of our place before officially moving. We ordered a bunch of furniture and it got delivered way earlier than we expected. The staff made sure all our packages were secured in our apartment despite us being on one of the higher floors. 

We arrived and was greeted by the amazing staff and couldn’t believe just how nice the apartments were. We have the best view in all of Denver and the amenities are fantastic. 

I am excited to call Eviva on Cherokee home!

Beware moving into this building.  Space and price are decent, but a rash of thefts from "secure" and locked storage units inside the "secure" building is a serious problem.  Equity residential is non-responsive to resident concerns.  They finally sent an email after months of bike thefts, and other items, from a garage that has security cameras but no attempt to provide any other type of security.The cameras are useless and do not provide any coverage of areas of theft. Residents are also required to pay a locker fee for package delivery. Today we had an expensive iPhone delivered and signed for, but left with dozens of other packages in the open package room, no security and no email to let us know the package arrived.  Do not rent here unless you do not care about your belongings being stolen and your security put at risk.

Camber has been the greatest experience to live since I got out here a month ago. The office staff are so friendly and always greeting people with the most friendly smile. They knowledge the residents by name. They maintain the pool side and gym so professionally, camber has been my favorite place and is still my favorite place. The club house is the place to go for some quite time, not only is a great place to hang out, you are also able to play pool watch TV and just be in a world or relaxation. I most especially love their in door fire place... For me that never gets old

If you love black mold and incompetent property managers, this is the place for you! Black mold comes through from the roof (which means it had to have been growing for months) and what do they do??  Stick “air scrubbers” in the unit which don’t eliminate mold but they did double my electric bill! 3 weeks after notification that we had mold, the dry wall was cut out and NO MOLD REMEDIATION WAS PERFORMED, just a little trash bag taped over the hole. I sat there and watched. They laid new dry wall days later and told me it was “all gone.” How ignorant do you have to be to realize that a new dry wall panel does not ELIMINATE  mold or spores? Educate yourself.  Do NOT rent here if you care about your health. Oh did I mention there was a shooting on the property that closed the amenities down for months too? No information was provided to residents as to what happened other than they would look into it. Property is supposed to have security that patrols (never there) but I’ve seen the cops here more than some security company.
Love living here! The whole process was very easy, the ladies in the office are so helpful and nice. Any maintenance issues reported Mike gets right on it and has it taken care of.

Overall amazing experience! Staff is wonderful, amenities are top quality, apartments are spacious and beautiful, and residents are generally polite. We’ve only had one noisy neighbor who leaves trash outside their door sometimes, but what apartment complex doesn’t? This is definitely going to be our final apartment destination before buying a home.

Seems like a fine place to live on paper but all the amenities are bad, laundry always on the fritz, communication is terrible. Move out costs are outrageous for no reason and all they do is milk out money from all residents. Their model is based upon screwing over residents for extra money at every turn and they are not in the business of the residents. Do not move here

Do not move here.
Management is some of the worst I’ve ever experienced. Communication is either non existent or incomplete and rude when you do get a response.

For maintenance, the doors were always broken which lead to safety issues and people entering the building that were not tenant (homeless people on the street, namely).
The place constantly smelled of smoke from other tenant. Noise complains were never addressed. Laundry / Dryers were always non functional or left your clothes smelling worse/damaged.
Elevators were consistently non functional.

My move-out experience has been HORRIBLE. I have been charged almost $1,000 in move-out charges that I can not get help or even an explanation from the building manager (I have called and emailed for days) or the parent company, they are even ruder and couldn't care less about their tenant's wellbeing or even treat you like a human.

Look elsewhere and DO NOT give these people your money if you want to live in a building run by people who actually treat you like a human being

Would not recommend to anyone. Over priced, no amenities, and awful security practices. I have been threatened by someone in the lobby who was not a resident, their procedure in today's world is for residents to call a security team or police if they feel unsafe or don't recognize someone as if that's not going to lead to someone getting someone hurt because they don't recognize someone. It is incredibly easy for people to sneak in. They say there is on call security but if someone was to follow you in.... you'd have to call security and hope nothing happens before then. The elevators never work, it costs 2.50 every time to do laundry at the min settings for wash and dryer. The people who work here are nice but AIMCO doesn't allow them to actually fix any problems. Also there is just constantly things going on late at night or early at morning in this area downtown with people yelling, fights starting, police being called, etc. and they really even address it. The other day there was like 20 cop cars outside at around 10 at night because some residents decided to try and get the guy who was yelling obscenities to stop through their own means. Honestly you pay way too much and get nothing significant to make it worth it. Literally terrible experience living here.

Before you think to yourself “oh it’s just because this person is bitter they were careless and damaged the apartment” hear me out. Because they specifically told me there were no damages.

They simply tacked on a bunch of charges (e.g. move out service fee - $20, wear and tear painting- $79). The deposit that was returned went from the original $400 to $132. The painting fee, they claimed, is in my lease, but they were unable to point it out. They essentially are just going to nickel and dime you for any opportunity to take your money.

Again with no damages, and that’s their words. So if you want your security deposit back when you move out, I’d reconsider living here.

Property Management is unresponsive and sends unable to help with any issue. They also kept a security deposit I was owed back. They've told me that I'm owed this money but they haven't been able to return it to me in over 2 YEARS.

I have been living at Bank and Boston lofts for 6 months now and honestly have nothing but good things to say about living there. The staff is extremely friendly and welcoming, the maintenance team is phenomenal ... I've never lived at an apartment with such Speedy service! The apartment itself is beautiful as well. The open layout of the kitchen and living room apartment make the apartment feel very spacious and the giant windows and old-fashioned brick walls are gorgeous. The location is also perfect...you are right next to 16th Street Mall and a few blocks from Union Station. The thing I love most about the location though, is how safe I feel. I feel very comfortable, even at night time, because of how well lit the area is and how much police security is around. Overall, I could not be happier with my decision to live at Bank and Boston Lofts and honestly feel like it is the perfect fit for me!!

I have been moved out from SR for 6 months now and they refuse to mail out my deposit. They are very money-hungry and completely disorganized. Many functions of the unit were inoperable (the dishwasher remained broken after several work orders, the shower in the master bedroom NEVER had hot water). They also have roaches. The cheaper prices really don’t accommodate for the massive headaches and vulnerability you have with living here. My car was also broken into and the management really did not care to respond at all. Save yourself the trouble and do not waste your time or money here.
Decided to not sign a lease and the company will not refund me the money I put down on the apartment. Stay away shady business.

This is the grossest, most disgusting place I have ever lived. Don’t put yourself through the hassle of dealing with the incompetent staff. Find anything else. Even if you were desperate like I was, this place isn’t the answer. It’s way more trouble than they’re worth.

I figured this review would be more beneficial from someone actually CURRENTLY living at Santana Ridge. I am an honest person and try not to make things seem better or worse than they really are!

That saying "You get what you pay for" stands true for this establishment. While the rent isn't bad, you definitely don't get comfort for the price. I moved here for a job rather quickly and didn't have time to physically view apartments in person. I ended up here at Santana Ridge. While I will say that my stay here hasn't been totally bad, for the most part, it also hasn't been very pleasant either.

Good things about Santana Ridge:

-Friendly Staff
-No signs of bugs (in my apartment) <--- I am a very clean person, so this may skew this. I cannot vouch for anyone else here. 
-Reasonable Rent Rates
-Location is pretty nice with the close proximity to shopping and the necessities. 

Bad things about Santana Ridge:

-Slow (VERY SLOW) maintanance 
-No central AC (I am very displeased with this one because when you see the website, it states "Air Conditioning". While this is true, is is definitely not Central. It's a wall unit directly behind your door that causes two issues:
      1. difficulty getting larger furniture inside the apartment 
      2. Being next to the door gives more opportunity for air to escape right out the front door before ever having the chance to cool off your apartment

-No Towing for people who park cars in your assigned spot. I have had people park in my spot numerous times and the only response I have gotten from the office is "Find out who it is and tell them"
-very outdated apartments

Let's just say that I plan on moving once my lease is up. I would rather pay more to live in better conditions than to live here. While Santana Ridge is a good place if you are really on a budget or just need somewhere to live quickly, it's not by any means a long term apartment home situation. 

Good luck!

This is a horrible place to live the floor is fake wood, the vathrooms have a permanent nasty smell in them the shower head comes out of the wall and the rooms carpets are very dirty and old. The worst thing about this place is when i first moved here almost TWO years ago there was mold all over the wall of the master bedroom, (which was making me sick and resorted to me sleeping in the living room for quite a while) time after time i told the leasing office as well as maintenance to come and fix the wall as well as clean it, after all these months from 2015 to 2017 they finally came but ended up just making it worse by taking a chunk of wall off that didnt even have the mold on it, leaving a dirty huge humidifier in the room with a hose going to my PERSONAL bathroom sink. they expected me to sleep with the humidifer over night and refused to get someone to come turn it off for me. to make all matters worse bugs like spiders and moths have been coming through the wall because they have left it open for FIVE days not returning any of my calls and not answering too. this is the fifth day the the wall has been left open and the mold is still there. terrible place that needs to be shut down

I am in the same boat as the other review. They do not tell you that you have to come fill out a form if you want to move out. If you don't do it, they automatically renew your lease for you. Even if you don't sign anything. It is a crazy policy, and hopefully they will change it, or be more clear about it, so this doesn't happen to anyone in the future. The staff could have handled it so much better. They seemed like they didn't really want to help. They need some customer service training.

Managers hide from tenants.
No returned emails/ phone calls NEVER answered. No one ever in the office.
Homeless people, broken elevators, random charges. STAY FAR AWAY!!!

My rent was too high at my current apartment so I needed to find another place close to downtown.  I was absolutely floored when I found The Elements!   My rent will be less but this building is so classy.   I was afraid that I’d have to sacrifice quality.  Can’t wait to move in at the end of the month.

Would have given 5 stars but construction is still in progress.

Charge for monthly parking fee or you get towed. $8 monthly 1 vehicle second vehicle $45 monthly. Waiting since 2017 Feb for vinyl floor repair, painted over grease on walls next to stove. High temp on stove blistered wall paint since stove is against the wall on the side. When I moved into Estrella Apartment Homes, I was really hoping this could be a place that I could stay for at least few years. But there' s just been too much that has happened here for me to consider renewing my lease. Between slow maintenance repair times, inconvenient office hours and lackluster customer service, the fact that some UPS packages are rejected and you have to pick them up from a nearby pickup location, the always broken laundry units (there's generally two washers and one or two dryers working, and there's only three dryers and three washers total for a whole building) and the fact my building was treated for german cockroaches (I have never lived in a building with roaches, so imagine my surprise when I got a notice on my door), I would not really recommend this complex. I feel like I could get a larger and far better apartment for just a tiny bit more money. 

That being said, if you are just looking for small somewhere to live (many of the one bedrooms are only 465 square feet), and are not all that concerned with the above problems, then it may be a good fit for you. It is close to I-25 and is the first exit on 36. It's definitely on the cheaper end of places available in the metro area. There's a Mercado down the street, and a King Soopers and Walgreens on 84th and Pecos (just a short drive). It's also down the street from Water World.

I never write reviews, but I felt my experience was worth sharing to give a heads up.

I recently moved in and I can't be happier.  The only thing better than the building, its location, amenities, etc. are the staff.  Shawna and Vanessa are are amazing!  They helped make the move in process as convenient as possible, they went out of their ways to take calls and so much more.  I haven't had to deal with any maintenance issues yet but from what I've been told, it should be just as easy and convenient for that as it was moving in.

The building staff are unprofessional, unorganized, and rarely answer emails and phone messages timely or even at all at times.

We have had 4 false fire alarms since moving in, 3 of which were in the middle of the night between 1 and 3 am. Families were out in the street at night with their pets and kids. People had work in the morning and got no sleep. Because this happens so frequently, people have stopped taking the alarms seriously which is a safety hazard. 

We have paid $15/month to keep our stuff in an indoor storage unit in the basement of the building. There was a break in and we had over $1,000 of camping gear stolen. The building staff wouldn't even do the bare minimum of giving us the $15/month we paid just to have all of our stuff stolen. There are no security cameras or any way to prevent this from happening again. 

The parking garage (that we pay the high amount of $95/car/month for is really unreliable. They have you evacuate the garage twice for multiple days throughout the year and sometimes we come home and there's an event so you can't find a spot or have a lot of difficulty doing so. 

The insulation sucks and our apartment is freezing throughout the winter even when we run the heat, which makes our bills extremely high. 

Do not walk, RUN away from this building and rent somewhere cheaper, more secure, and where the staff will show you respect.

This building is not safe. There are no security cameras at all. Our storage units were robbed and management did not tell us for several days. They also did not respond to multiple follow up communication attempts. 

The fire alarm goes off all the time in the middle of the night because people pull it. Management has no ability to stop this problem. 

Parking is very very expensive and you are kicked out of the garage two weeks per year. On top of that, sometimes there is an event at the Masonic Center and you can't get parking and there is nothing you can do. 

Our apartment is not well insulated and we pay huge utilities every month so the upfront cost is not what it seems.

You can do better than this building.

My apartment complex is nice, it's just pool-less and needs to be upgraded. The photos and the display unit DO NOT reflect the quality of the apartment nor the management you will be subject to if you rent here. Do not rent here. Drug deals in the parking lot, potholes everywhere your car goes. Place smells like stale cigarettes and very unsanitary.

This is bar none the worst apartment I have ever lived in my entire life.  If you value your health, money, and mental sanity, I beg you, DO NOT MOVE HERE! 

1.  My downstairs neighbor smoked indoors, despite being a "smoke free property, which lofted up into my apartment.  The staff did nothing about it, despite issuing warnings without repercussion.

I've been living in Arabella for just over 6 months and I can attest to how attentive the management is. A little dated and there are some flaws (old outlets, no AC, etc.), but it's a wonderful place to call home. Biggest downside is paper-thin walls. Otherwise, no major complaints. I've only had to request a few minor maintenance requests, but they were always extremely quick to respond and assist! Overall, I am very satisfied with my entire experience thus far. I could go on and on about how much I love living here-- give them a shot!

WARNING: DO NOT LEASE HERE! Arabella Apartments are fine on the outside and the location is great. But beware: the staff is rude and they dont care about any of their tenants. They continuously mess up rent bonuses/the software doesn't work half the time and they act like it's a huge burden for them to correct their mistake. The property managers have no idea what they are doing, and when errors are found, it takes forever to get them corrected.
