The doors to the apartments themselves are weak and there’s so much room between the door and the floor that mice are constantly running in and out, and you can even see inside some of peoples apartments. The walls are thin, and you can hear everything. People have no regard for others, and are constantly partying outside in the lot at full volume, or next door and banging the walls. People are constantly smoking weed, and the hallways stink because of this. The laundry machines are also terrible and have burned holes and stains into my clothes. My list goes on. This place is awful and by far the worst experience I’ve ever had living somewhere. If you can avoid this place, avoid it. I would give 0 stars if that were an option.

If you like bedbugs, mice, roaches, terrible management, and security issues, this is the apartment for you! The place is always in disrepair, constantly leaking and sewage being backed up. This place is something from nightmares. Please keep looking, don't let the pretty pictures fool you.
The entire complex is infested with bedbugs, cockroaches and mice! Management is not taking the proper steps to deal with them! There are no mailboxes availabile either!

Those who have left reviews of roach infestations, poor communication, unsatisfactory living conditions and safety concerns are all valid. They do not care about your living conditions and they do not have interest in taking responsibility for their tenants or property.

When confronted about these issues, the current management team (as of Oct 2022), likes to blame the last owner instead of providing residents with plans to actually make this place a decent place to live.

Upon move-in, all $5000 (pet fees + deposit + 1st rent + refundable and non-refundable deposits, admin fees etc)they charged up front and the management team refused to show me my unit until I signed the lease agreement. When we moved in, there were roaches in the kitchen, damaged countertops and appliances, broken closet doors, "hardwood" flooring that was peeling up, light fixtures that were unsecured, damaged tub, damaged walls, damaged ceilings.

Walk around outside and you'll find garbage, broken windows, broken down vehicles, dog crap everywhere, broken laundry machines, inoperable "locking doors" on the building (anyone, including homeless will find their way into the buildings), inoperable elevators, unkept common areas, a "gated" community that has no working gates and a really nicely maintained leasing office. 

All of this located conveniently located near East Colfax Ave which is in the top 10 for highest crime rates in all of Denver's neighborhoods.
 
Other issues I've had:
-My van/rv towed after paying to park on the app and being verbally told it would be ok to park in the lot
-Constant ROACH INFESTATION
-A GUNSHOT VITCTIM JUST OUTSIDE MY BUILDING
-No hot running water for almost 3 of the 6 months I have been here 
-Sewage backup and continuous leaking toilet that took 2 days of emails to get the apartment complex to repair. The 24/7 maintenance team was not available.
-An inoperable mailbox (current residents are being told to provide their own means of receiving mail)

This is not a safe or well maintained apartment complex. The headaches and constant "what's next" feelings about where you call home are probably not worth it.

If you are looking for a quiet apartment complex, this is not the one. Walls and ceilings are paper thin, you will hear every move your neighbors make above and next to you. Every night all I hear are cars racing down Wadsworth. The ceiling so thin I can tell when the 15 lb dog above me get the zoomies. Great location but not a place for peace and quiet.
The complex is centrally located in an area with lots to do and many good places to get groceries or go shopping our even walk to clement park!! Very happy to be where I'm living.
Lots of hot water which is great. A nice quite community. Beautiful view of the mountains and all my favorite food places nearby. We are very happy with our choice
Love it! Everyone has been great here from property management, to maintenance, to neighbors! I highly recommend this apartment complex if you’re looking to move
Love it here I've been here for about 10 years and I absolutely love it. The staff is incredible maintenance is always spot on no complaints for sure
Very its a nice quiet and friendly community

I lived here for over 5 years and would recommend this building to anyone.  The location is great and that you can walk to broadway in about 10 min or less and you can walk to wash park in just over 10 minutes too.  It’s close to downtown but the neighborhood is very quiet at night which is great.  The building manager here is amazing and will make sure if there are any problems to take care of them immediately.  I would recommend this building for anyone looking for a 1 or 2 bedroom

I have lived here for 3.5 years and have loved it! It is hard to find genuinely good people to trust and have your back, and the management of this building truly had my back.  They were always available to talk and address my concerns, and put my safety first.  They worked hard to accommodate my needs, and the maintenance crew on site were very nice.  

The building is a little older, but the apartments are renovated decently and are very spacious.  I particularly loved the patio each apartment had and the open format of apartment.

I also loved the neighborhood.  The Ogden Bar is literally on the corner, and is a great space to hangout and they also have great food.

I honestly would have continued to live there but I ran out of space with my partner and we moved into a house :)

I lived at the Paragon with my family for four and a half years. During that time, management was always there when we needed them. Any repairs were almost always done within 24 hours. The building manager was very receptive to our needs and made sure my family was comfortable. The neighbors that have been there for many years were friendly all the time. The price of rent went up only twice while we lived there and the increase was totally fair. One reason we stayed as long as we did was the location. Walking distance to S Broadway, Wash Park, Ross-Broadway Public Library, and other great restaurants in the vicinity. The neighborhood itself is beautiful. Crime is low which is also a plus. My family and I moved because it was time for something bigger, otherwise, the building is great!

Newly renovated units are done with poor craftsmanship and care. They look as if it were a home do it yourself project with paint left on the new flooring, bubbles on the wall where new paint coats have been added, closet door knobs not painted to match the other door knobs. The management doesn't seem to genuinely care about the property safety and have had multiple issues with reaching out to them and having them address it with due diligence. Letters are left on doors regularly stating new rules that clearly do not match up with what is stated in your signed rental agreement making them show breaches of contract time and time again. Notices for building maintenance is often not posted within a 24 hour time period so plan to have surprise water shut offs for entire days abruptly. Maintenance staff is slow, often seen standing around smoking cigarettes or drinking beer out back, and rarely make you feel comfortable when you see them looking into your patio areas whenever they think no one is paying attention. Residents also aren't the most neighborly and often rude and sometimes aggressive in their demeanor when in passing in common spaces. All in all I would never recommend this property to anyone looking within the area unless absolutely necessary. More often than not you have to deal with one thing or another here that you could pay a similar price within the area to not have to deal with potentially as well as maybe having an amenity or two.

Need I say more ? 
They are renovating some apts, but it is NOT first class.

My partner, daughter, and I have been to the apartment tour and we fell in love instantly! I was so excited to apply and start the process. But unfortunately the maintenance has been no help. We have contacted them multiple times about what we needed to be done on our end. We called, and sent them an email but, he only responded once and never responded to let us know our work has been done and that our application is processing. Like he never was able to just give us any information or feedback. I don’t know if our application is processing and we’re still waiting for his response. It would be nice to just be informed and know how our process is doing! This is a beautiful place, I just wish they have better assistance with communication! Feeling a little bummed out. :(

The leasing office has been of extreme help since moving in. One of the better apartment complex’s in Denver. Extremely taken care of and in a great part of town. Recommend for anyone looking for a place that won’t cause you stress!
Do not live here! Pervasive mice issue that was not fixed in over a year. Amenities aren’t as advertised (peloton doesn’t work, etc). Pest issue is why there are so many open units now.

The view from the rooftop is great, and the maintenance and management are responsive. However, I have been woken up by my neighbors slamming cabinets, can hear neighbors' conversations, morning alarms, and music in both my living room and bedroom, ALL THE TIME. The apartment was marketed to me as soundproof and has been anything but. If you don't mind hearing your neighbors sneeze, then sure, it's fine; a bit overpriced for no dishwasher or in-unit laundry.

West Washington Park, near to Denver's SoBo bars and restaurants, Cherry Creek Shopping Center, Washington Park.
Apartments priced right, clean and newly remodeled. Friendly residents, management responsive. Overall, a really good place to live!

This place is ran like a clown college. The administration is unaccommodating and they have had numerous "clerical errors" in our lease, The older residents here are not nice and certainly are not welcoming. They are upset that their 55  community now allows anyone to lease here.  I've lived here a week and want to move out already. The atmosphere is terrible. I hate it here - don't waste your time, look elsewhere.

We found Vita Flats, and fell in love right away.  Our space is amazing, and has a view of downtown and the mountains.  Vita Flats also has an amazing rooftop that is completely redone and one of the only rooftops in the area.  The management is great as well; they respond to problems in a reasonable amount of time.

Vita Flats is a 10-story apartment building located near Washington Park, but close to downtown Denver. They are renovating the building - putting in hardwood floors, re-vamping the common area, media room and kitchen. It is a mess!!!
But the outcome will be nice. We have a rooftop garden area - to watch the beautiful sunsets in Colorado. The people here are very nice.I have been here 2 years and I really like it.

Do not move here! Be prepared to have roaches all the time. They shut off the water in certain buildings every week and there are suspicious people prowling and hanging in the halls. There are people using drugs and no solution ever. Their idea of maintenance is to put a band-aid on a bullet hole. Issues are "resolved" in their eyes but the root of the problem is never corrected.

This was the worst apartment I have ever lived in! We had two sewer floods and one of the floods they waited 4 days to even remove the sewage from my apartment. There are constant water outages and windows would leak every time there was any moisture. The whole complex was infested with cockroaches and other pests. The amenities which were promised to us were hardly ever if ever available and one pool was removed after move in with no notice. The leasing office was rude and unhelpful. There was never a complete maintenance staff and the one guy who was there alway tried his best. We had several water problems where plumbers told us that things were installed wrong and that’s why we had these problems, the dryer did not work almost at all and we would have to dry loads 3-4 times for several hours. We had planned to move into a one bedroom apartment and one week before move in we were told that they no longer had it available and our leasing agent no longer worked there so our only option was move somewhere else or get a much more expensive two bedroom. They “upgraded” our buildings with locking exterior doors but did not put doors that would actually close so these doors remained open much of the time. This apartment is unsafe, unsecured, dirty and expensive!

I am a property manager and have managed multiple apartment buildings in the north Denver metro area, and I can tell you – I have never seen such negligence and disregard for Tenants as I have here, at Boulder Crossroads. What this management does not seem to understand is that without Tenants, you no longer have a business.

This review concerns what I have witnessed myself [numerous times] while visiting my daughter and her roommate. First of all, please note that there is ZERO communication from the office. We left messages by phone, email, through work orders, actual paper letters – no response. Our next step is through the courts, perhaps they will take us seriously then.

Management Issues - From what she has shown thus far, the Manager Nancy could not care less what problems you run into, much less actually doing something about them. You can call and send emails for weeks with absolutely no response. 

Sewage issues – plumber never even showed up! Believe it or not, all they did was have their Maintenance guys come and clean what they could. They replaced the padding, but not the carpet. It still stinks horribly and is a certain mold hazard. RAW SEWAGE sitting there for almost a week, and that’s their attempts to sterilize the contaminated carpets and flooring? 

Pest control issues – Newly renovated apartment has ROACHES, and a LOT of them! We have contacted the office numerous times to no avail. No response; no acknowledgment; no one cares! They are everywhere: in the buildings; in the apartments; in your beds. Yes, I said in your BEDS!

Maintenance/Cleanliness Issues – Just take a look for yourself at the pictures below. It doesn’t take much time to clean, sweep, paint, or repair simple things to make your property look good. It makes sense why this place is infested with roaches, bedbugs, and who know what else.

As I said, everything about the way this place is managed is absolutely horrible! We’ve given these people more than enough chances to make things right before I wrote this review. Enough is enough! It’s time people knew what they are walking in to. DO NOT RENT FROM HERE. YOU WILL REGRET IT!

THERE ARE BED BUGS, GUNSHOTS AT NIGHT, HOMELESS IN THE HALLWAYS, CARS ARE NEVER TOWED, AND OTHER THINGS, AND MANAGEMENT THAT EITHER DOESN'T OR CAN'T DO ANYTHING. On the very first I moved in (August '21) I found cockroaches in every room, when I told management they were unphased and informed me that I need to call them every week to be put on the pest control list. Are you kidding me? We also received a notice that we need to vacate our apartment for them to spray for roaches. We had to empty and clean all of our cabinets, trash cans, etc. and move everything away from the walls. They never even showed up. When I called to bring this to the office's attention they gave me a "?????". I asked if they or I could call the pest control guy to see about rescheduling or if they were running late, they said no. I asked if I should call again if he still hasn't showed, they said "You can if you want". When the friends that I referred here's apartment flooded (with literal POOP floating in water) they were denied any kind of rent credit, when this was the 4th time it flooded in 4 months, and were told that when the apartment company brought in a cleaning crew 3 days after it happened that they should be thankful because it was a courtesy. The salt they use in winter will burn your pet's feet & they said "pet friendly salt is not in the budget" (they claim to be a pet friendly complex). The pool hours in the summer are that of the office's hours, and is closed on holidays so if you have a day job, you'll never use it. There was mold under the sink on move in. Entry doors are always open because there is no gasket that closes the door behind you. The windows by the entries (at least at Building C) are constantly smashed. They're raising the rent due to "improvements" which has been exterior paint, door locks, an Amazon Hub that half the time Amazon can't even use for some reason, and maybe other things too small to notice. There isn't enough parking at night so be prepared to park on the street. Very aggressive squirrels are everywhere that will eat everything on your deck, plus, again at least in our building, they live in the roof. Wiring in our kitchen is so bad it causes our refrigerator, and all kitchen outlets to shut off randomly every day until you reset the outlet (I've lost a lot of food this way). The autopay randomly doesn't work and you get an uncovered and very public notice on your door about it. My fiancé and I regularly wake up covered in bug bites.
Communication is poor. They don’t keep track of who makes security deposits. Keep all receipts.

I have lived here a few months now and it has NOT been great to say the least. When viewing the apartment, it already did not look as shown in their photos that they use on their website, cheap carpet, extremely poor lighting, cheap Facets, bad fixtures, ceiling fan made noise right off the bat single shallow sink with no garbage disposal, washer and dryer do not properly vent outside as they should, there was a gient whole in the closet that cause a lot of damp air to fill the apparat meant that I had to fix and seal myself. The whole apartment was  repainted poorly. causing the paint to bubble underneath, stick in locations like the cabinets and door seals. And it was obvious that surfaces were not cleaned before the painting process because there is a dead cockroach in one of my cabinets that was just sprayed over. As well as all the hinges on the cabinets, and also the vents were also sprayed over with thick paint,It looks really bad. When we decided to just go with it we were told  a lot of information that was never true one being that there will eventually be replacing the entrance doors due to the poor condition and security of them, instead they just replaced the nob months later with a bathroom door or closet lever style nob with no lock! They also promised assigned parking and overnight security, both of which were never followed through with. Maintenance does not seem professional or certified, an example, aside from the building entrance door issue, would be when I had my shower valves replaced because they were leaking and broken upon move in. the diverter valve leaked more after the repair and now waste a lot of water, and the cold valve was installed with a wrong direction valve that twists the opposite direction of the rest. In conclusion,  I do not feel safe or happy about living here. 
Also Hallways are in terrible shape, some units don’t even have appt # plates, others are broken.
management and maintenance are top notch. location is great. I like the apartment layout. stores are close as well as restaurants and bars. rents are reasonable. amenities are very nice.

I lived in the Denver House for a total of ~5 years. The management was always friendly and very responsive. The location is perfect for walking to just about anything. My apartment was on the 11th floor facing West with an awe inspiring view. I would highly recommend it to anyone.

I love the management at this property, always helpful and nice and caring. I had the west facing apartment with an amazing view of the mountains with no buildings in the way. Great neighbors as well same with the amazing maintenance, they always responded quick and always fixed the issue in a timely manner.

I love it here. The facility itself, the location and the staff are wonderful. Big shout out to the maintenance team and the office team (namely Chris) as they are excellent to work with and  truly appreciated!

I would definitely recommend this apartment community. Excellent location, great amenities. The only issue I have had is resort pool lights being left on at night quite often; these lights shine directly into my bedroom.
Terrific overall. I was very pleased with the service provided.
I would recommended this apartment community. The atmosphere and everything about it is Beautiful.
The staff is very friendly and respond in a timely manner.

Great building and location! It's safe - packages were safe and the office staff was great and timely with any requests. Many of my friends living in other spaces have had many packages stolen, storage units broken into and that just wasn't the case at Hartley flats.   It was perfect!

These were surprisingly affordable and cute. Lots of character from original hardwood floors and archways. Great windows let in a lot of natural light and the layout of the apartment has a nice flow and high ceilings make it seem larger than it is. Building is kept clean and neighbors are respectful. However, the century-old floors are showing their age and squeak and creak for even the lightest of steppers, but what's worse is when your upstairs neighbor walks around, the squeaks seem to be amplified through the ceiling and are SO LOUD that my neighbor regularly wakes me up from a dead sleep just walking around. Often, I can't hear my tv if she's walking around. There seems to be no insulation between floors, so I hear every word my upstairs neighbor says, every pee stream into the toilet, every cough, a dish placed into the sink. Everything. I can hear her conversations like they're in my apartment. It's terrible. The windows provide very little insulation, so it sounds like my windows are constantly open. The worst part is that the building controls the heat and it only seems to run in the middle of the night so I'm constantly freezing as my large windows don't insulate much at all. The kitchen is TERRIBLE. The "vintage" sink is about 4 inches deep, so expect lots of water to splash out all over you, my vintage stove is a crapshoot to work with. There is about two square feet of counter space, which you need to put a drying rack on because there's no dishwasher, so you effectively have no counter/prep space. And forget about getting deliveries from Amazon unless you're going to be home to let them in the building because they can't get in to deliver them.
Overall, it feels very safe and I enjoy it here when my upstairs neighbor is gone. Everyone in the building is pretty quiet, not much of a party place. If you aren't bothered by hearing every intimate detail of your neighbor's life and don't like to cook, this could be a great spot for you.

Didn't tell me when I moved in that the air conditioner had been out for well over six months.  Sadly I still have another 9 months on my lease.  Wouldn't have rented this apartment had I known there was no air conditioning and as a result the whole building would smell like garbage 2/3 of the time.

The AC has been down for over a week during mid-July. People's pets are overheating and that doesn't seem to matter to ownership. People who complained about this on the apartment message board were called "entitled". Very frustrating. The lady who currently manages the building is kind and minor facility issues are quickly taken care of. If you need something fixed that's going to take some money/ effort though? No chance, not even if it means your pet's overall well-being.
The apartment could be better maintained for the price.

Just moved to Denver from nyc and had the best experience working with Eileen. She toured the apartment via facetime for me as I could not come see it in person beforehand. The apartment is just as described and staff members are so quick to reply with any maintenance issues. The garage, bike room and package room all feel really safe and the location is perfect. Very happy with my first apartment in Denver :)

I called twice and left 2 voicemails because I wanted to tour the apartments and didn't even receive a call back. If a prospective new tenant can't even get them to answer the phone I can only imagine what it's like for the people who actually live there.

I've lived in several apartments throughout Denver and this is by far the best experience yet.

The Kasserman is in the heart of the Lower Highlands neighborhood, close to downtown and even closer to trendy nightlife spots like Postino, Happy Camper and Avanti so it's the perfect community for anyone who works downtown and wants to be in the thick of it all.

Noise proofing is excellent  - you won't hear any noise either above or below you or to your adjacent apartments. 

The residents are mainly all respectful, working professionals. 

Would recommend for anyone who wants to be in a hip part of town close to the best bars and restaurants.
the power goes out every time the temperature changes bc the heating/AC units all short out. the fire alarm was left on for 12+ hours overnight while the power was out.

Although I ended up choosing a different location due to accommodations necessary for work, I was blown away by the professionalism and care shown by the staff. Specifically, the manager on-site Linda was willing to work around a busy schedule to offer several unscheduled tours and answer any questions. It's clear the tenants appreciate her and her care for them, a rarity in renting. The studio space is the largest I've seen, at a better price, than any in the area. Finished flooring and kitchen, and ample closet space. I would have really enjoyed living at Camellia House. Thank you Linda!

Building is under constant construction, parking garage might as well be under a lake its leaky and floods anytime there is rain or snow. Building manager could care less about anything going on and there is always trash littered around the property. DONT WASTE YOUR MONEY!

I lived in Camellia in a studio for a year, and loved it. In the time I was there, they completely redid the lobby area, which now has free WiFi, coffee, and tea. It’s a nice area to do work and quiet in the evenings. My studio had a great layout, and Linda (the main office person) was easy to communicate with and friendly. Any problems I had were fixed the day of or the next day, but I only had to put in a service report twice the whole time I was there. There is no recycling, which is a downside. But the courtyard is very well taken care of with flowers, and I felt safe even on the ground level because there are cameras at the entrances. You can’t beat the location, and the price is pretty on par with what you can get in that area but with nice, redone, bathrooms and kitchens. I only moved out because I needed a different location! Would recommend Camellia house.

Tangent has amazing units, a beautiful office, and friendly staff. Maintenance is timely and attentive, but the same can't be said for the front office and their responses to resident concerns.

Ordinarily, I might list off several "annoyances" we've had at Tangent (there are many), but I won't do that because this review isn't about our annoyances - these happen at every single complex, especially newer ones. That being said, typically when a resident raises a concern or legitimate complaint, management is quick to jump on it in a timely manner. 

We are gathered here today to discuss: GATES.

Our main issue is the gates to the community, as it relates to lower floor residents or those physically located closer to any of the 3 gates. These gates break CONSTANTLY. One inch of snow will freeze the gates either shut or open, which is ridiculous purely because of the fact that it's Colorado and it snows just a lil bit here. The gates being locked one way or another isn't a huge deal - but guess what?

The gates BEEP, incredibly loudly, a total of SIX times with every enterance or exit, and yes, you can hear them from inside your 2/3rd floor apartment with all windows/doors closed. So, when these gates lock up, we are blessed enough to hear constant, non-stop, incessant beeping all through the night as if someone is entering and exiting over and over until the gates magically start working again. 

I've written to management about this, to be met with a good ol fashioned "We'll look into it". After responding and expressing my concern for this to be more of a priority, I was met with 2 weeks worth of silence. I'll adjust this review when I feel that I've actually been heard by management, with a decent solution in mind to allowing me and my partner to live comfortably here. 

Otherwise it's good, move in. Just buy some earmuffs.
Super walkable if you hate driving like me, wish prices were lower but you do get what you pay for

I have been living at this apartment complex for about 6 months, and I can say that the location is great. There is a supermarket across the street, as well as many other shops, restaurants, and medical facilities. The apartments are large and spacious. The management team has been great, especially Misty, Chase, and Josh, who have all been very helpful in addressing any issues that have come up. Overall, I have been very happy living here.

Not a bad apartment at all. Nice and quiet community. Apartment was nicer than I expected and I never really had any issues. It was cool having  a grocery store and side restaurants right across the street. If you want a nice apartment but a little pricey, this is a good place. Also I would recommend getting a garage to. It’s a shared space with 2-3 other cars but it’s better than parking in the lot.

Living at Botanica Eastbridge is decent. Not really convenient to anything, for now! They'll be building a King Soopers & shops across the street in 2016. It will also be a lot better with the Stapleton light rail completed.

I HATE the call boxes/key fobs! I've gotten locked out of my apartment so many times (with my keys on me) because the call box doesn't work & I can't receive my deliveries either bc of them. They NEED to go back to a classic lock & key system. Not management's fault of course. 

Overall, it's a quiet community that's GREAT if you have kids/a family. As a 24-year-old single woman, I am planning to move to somewhere with a younger crowd when my lease is up.

I just recently finished living there 5 years. They've gone through three management company changes during that time. Unfortunately the last one is probably the worst of the bunch. They were not super concerned when the heat went out in the middle of winter. They were not super concerned when there was no AC in the summer. They were not super concerned when the balcony turned into an ice rink because they refused to add a new drainage hole. They were not super concerned when the water backed up into the house and all they did was cut a hole in the drywall. They're not very concerned  about  any upgrades  or updates or painting the inside or painting the outside or having the pool open until after 6 p.m. or  really doing anything. They are not concerned that you can't access the building if you are in a wheelchair. They are not concerned when they collect extra money when you have no choice to overpay your rent because they are not concerned to adjust the online portal. But apparently they're very concerned about charging a carpet cleaning fee in a house that is not remodeled and had somebody die in it. So was I charged a bogus fee and somebody's living in a house with old carpet that somebody died in, or was I charged a fee and they still replaced the carpet?

Friendly staff, pool, air conditioning, pets allowed! Everything I need to feel at home. Parking is always available and it's close to restaurants and shopping. It only takes me 15 minutes to get to work downtown in the morning. Best feature of all: super affordable!

Everything seems to run incredibly smoothly here, the staff is hands-off but always extremely prompt in the case of maintenance or anything else. Extremely professional, beautiful apartment units, fantastic location and a really great and secure place to live, especially relative to many buildings in the area.

I have loved the building and area since moving here but the security has been slipping. Anyone can get in without much hassle which is problematic. 

A few weeks back, I caught someone testing doorknobs (mine included) and was unable to get ahold of anyone to notify them. 

Just the other night (11/24) there was an apartment building on the pool deck that allegedly took multiple gun shots - thankfully no one was hurt, but there are some serious security issues that need to be addressed.

A recent change of building ownership has created a lot of new upgrades at this community.  They are upgrading the units with new paint, flooring, granite countertops, and a security system.  The new Manager lives on-site and is very friendly.

The saying looks can be deceiving applies here.  Although the apartments are nice to look at this complex is only two years old and falling apart.  I have experienced everything from broken elevators, cracks in the wall, cupboards falling, roaches and a broken washer machine.  Save time, keep looking!
Very nice apartments with beautiful finishes minutes from downtown.

“Common area electric” is over 120$ per month. This is in addition to your personal use. The building has not been cleaned in months and is filthy. Garbage has been left in the hallway for several weeks despite complaints. Stated rental prices do not reflect actual cost to the renter after utilities and hidden fees.

The buildings are okay, semi maintained, in a not so nice area. The company uses its “gate” as a way to advertise that even if the area isn’t great you don’t have to worry about it.

The rent has gone up 23% in 2 years. The apartment complex has managed to turn that extra profit into a new set of lawn furniture for the residents. What the residents have requested is simple cameras to deter the continuous break-ins and robberies that have infested this complex since we moved in.

Our vehicles and property have been broken into 7 times in 2 years. All after the gate was closed. After a few of them management hire “rentacops” that randomly patrol for 5 minutes every 4 hours. The only thing these security guards have done is assault me as i walked from my car to my doorway.

Again, we asked for cameras so that we could atleast make sure that the people committing the break ins weren’t members of the community and to create some peace of mind because the break ins escalated up to a car being stolen out of the driveway. Again, after the gates are closed, and management said “im sorry that happened to you we aren’t providing additional security measures at the complex”

So don’t move here. They will continue to raise your rent year over year, and they will do nothing to improve the lives or living situations of their residents in the process.

The Good: Allure has nicely designed and modern apartments, plenty of parking, and the option to rent a garage. The prices are somewhat high, you can get the same sized apartment in Cherry Creek for just about the same cost, and units having their own laundry set up. Lawns are key clean and green and the grounds crew and maintenance do a phenomenal job. 

The Bad: Rents raise on average 100-150 a year since my residency here started, slightly higher than the market dictates. There are constant break ins into mailboxes, causing residents to drive 20 minutes out into the middle of Aurora to get their mail, and packages being stolen left and right is now a commonality among residents. Staff at the font office seem not to care. 

The Ugly: Residents have had cars broken into at night, a police officer chased a man in his car through the apartment parking lots this past weekend, and I've personally caught several people simply driving around and looking into car windows at 4am (I get up early to workout). The lack of action put into place by Allure to protect and mitigate crime is simply abysmal. They rather pay someone 15$/hr to spin a sign up on the corner of tcautionary deterrents for crime inside the gates. If you care about your safety, personal belongings, or life in general not being constantly interrupted by missing packages, broken car windows, and other petty crimes, then Allure is not for you.

When echelon property group bought Devon Square and became Allure Apartments it went down hill. Especially with the grounds, cockroach infestations, dirty neighbors leaving trash on balconies, dog poop all over the side walk & grass, loud neighbors, crackheads smoking crack pipes in the middle of the day out on the lawn, people trying to break in, trash all over the place and a nightmare of a place to live especially for what they charge. They let anyone live there. There is also gang violence in the area that when you call police because someone is trying to break into your place it takes 30-45 minutes to arrive since they are overwhelmed with gangs in the area. The security company for the complex is lazy as well and the Cherry Creek School's Assigned to the complex is horrible especially the middle that has over 1800 kids that are out of control. The security gates break all the time or the surrounding Residents from other complexes break the gates cutting through the complex. South Willow Street is 25 MPH & crazy people drive past the school bus stop sign when kids get off the bus and they drive way too fast down that road and homeless people have been camping out on that street including drug addicts. I would not recommend living at Allure nor in that neighborhood. Also don't leave your cars parked along South Willow Street, they get hit, parts stolen off cars, looks like a neighborhood in Compton, CA They Honestly Don't Even Deserve The 1 Star They Are Getting. Allure they definitely stand up to the name by luring you in to a nightmare disguised as a nice renovated place. They will bug fog a place with infestations, renovated the next day & then let people move in 2 days later.

Lisa is wonderful we known each other for over 30 years and I followed her from the apartment she managed to this one. These apartments are big and spacey the rent is just right for now a day.  They are centrally located and you can find anything close by.  Anything that needs to be fixed, is done right away, their handy-man Jack, he is so nice and get things done. I been living at these apartments for over 10 years.  I would recommend anyone to live here you will enjoy it.

Lisa and Norma are amazing! They have always called us by name and knew our apartment number without having to be reminded. Anytime a request was put in for anything in the apartment, it was handled either that day or the next. Hands down the best customer service and hospitality I've ever had in a renting experience. The 2 years I lived there were hassle free. The rent increases were pretty mild compared to other properties in the past. It was a little hard to leave when we bought a house because they were so good to us. I highly recommend renting here. You won't find an apartment with this size and neatness for the price.

We absolutely love our apartment at Grosvenor Arms. The property manager, Paige, is extremely friendly, organized, and always prioritizes the resident's needs. The building has a lot of character, beautiful views of the city, and is in a prime location for experiencing all that Denver has to offer.

I just moved into the building about a month ago and so far it's been great. The amenities are nice, especially having your trash picked up for you! Building management is quick and gets back to you right away and everyone has been really nice. I like that I can trust my packages not getting stolen and the apartment itself is lovely. Only major points of frustration, lack of AC and being able to use a window unit, the walls are plaster so not easy to hang items, and the kitchen isn't great. Otherwise, it's a great apartment for the cost!
Increased rent by $85 an hour and a half before the showing then never showed up.

This old world charming building really allows for affordable living near downtown Denver.  It's less than 10 minute walk to 16th street mall and a 10 minute drive to I-25.  There is not A/C, but all the utilities, excluding heat are included in the rent.  I recommend finding a unit up and away from the courtyard as it is a common outside area for residents and the public to gather and keep you up at night!  But other than that, Grosvenor is great!

I recently toured this apartment complex while I was visiting Denver and was blown away by the amazing experience I had. From the moment I walked in, Haley C was incredibly friendly and accommodating. She made me feel so at home and comfortable, answering all of my questions and showing me around the property.

The apartment itself was simply stunning. It was spacious, clean, and had all of the amenities I was looking for. The kitchen was fully equipped with top-of-the-line appliances, and the living room was perfect for entertaining guests.

But what really made this apartment stand out was the amazing staff. Haley went above and beyond to make sure I had everything I needed and that I was comfortable during my visit. She was so friendly and welcoming, and I truly felt like I was part of their community.

Overall, I would highly recommend this apartment complex to anyone looking for a beautiful, comfortable, and welcoming place to call home. The staff is simply amazing, and they really make you feel like family. Thank you for such a wonderful experience!

I’m really excited to move into Mica! The amenities look incredible, and the apartments are HUGE. Haley has been awesome to work with and has done an excellent job communicating with me on move-in dates. I attend several shows at Mission Ballroom throughout the year and being able to walk home from my favorite music venue will be awesome! The only thing I can complain about is not being able to move-in now.

I have had my eye on the building for a while because you can't beat the location being located right beside Mission. What a pleasant surprise that the team was so unbelievably kind and welcoming. They seem just as excited about helping me pick out my new apartment home as I am!  Very informative and I can't wait to see the building in person.
Management does updates for photo ops, but doesn't maintain the building. Not worth the high prices, plenty of better options out there.

Scheduled a showing and confirmed a time with their team. Nobody from the property management company showed up to the tour, and when I called, I was routed to an answering service where they can only “relay a message” to the local team. I relayed 2 messages this way with questions before the scheduled  tour and nobody got back to me over the course of 3 days. Don’t live here if you expect to get ahold of anyone.

Management is unresponsive to or insultingly slow with maintenance requests. Fridge wasn't working right and after weeks of waiting we were given another faulty fridge. Stovetop stopped working months ago and still no response after repeated attempts at communication. Water pools and comes out of the walls during heavy rains. Water has dropped from the pipes and through the ceiling multiple times. There are many people with pets here and most available grass was replaced with rocks during renovations. There was a break in to the laundry room a while ago and the security cameras are still covered in red spray paint. A window screen that was broken during building renovations has been broken and not replaced for a year and a half. This apartment building as a whole is good, but it's a matter of luck on if maintenance requests or reports will be responded to or handled.
Nice area though, make sure to keep cars locked and have nothing visible at night.

The manager Sue allowed someone to take our motorcycle while we were in the process of moving out (to another state). We showed up on the last day of our lease to retrieve the bike from our parking space, only to find that it wasn't there. When we asked Sue where it was, she said that she had it towed because she needed the space for the new tenant (even though it was still technically our space at that moment). When asked who towed it she wouldn't provide us any information. We let the dealership that we were purchasing from know, so he could contact us when he received the call. We got a call this week from him, saying that he got a call on 9/20/16 that they had impounded the bike 5 days earlier (almost a year after we were told it was impounded). When they found it, it was being ridden without a plate. We are in the process of figuring things out with a detective, but if I have my way Sue will be spending some serious time in court trying to explain why she allowed someone to willingly walk away with our property when we were still within our timeframe, and then lied about it to our faces.

This building is a farce. Everything looks good when you come to view but there are so many issues, particularly cleanliness with hallways and public spaces that are rarely looked after, poor communication from the management team, and maintenance issues that take weeks to fix. For the price point I'd expect something better. Save yourself the trouble and look elsewhere for an apartment.

I've been living here for a few months. Everything was good at first, but the hallway has become extremely dirty with all kinds of stains, and the garage is awfully dusty. It seems like the carpet is never vacuumed, and I never see the janitor clean the garage.
Living here about two months. The building and units are well designed, the amenities top notch. The staff including Ashley, Maya, Josh and Steve are all very nice and attentive. Highly recommend.
The leasing and move-in processes were impeccable. Much thanks to Justin for the assistance every step of the way. I can only hope the experience remains positive for the balance of my lease!
Absolutely love living here. Staff is super responsive to anything you need and the location and amenities are top notch. Highly recommend living here!
Centric LoHi maintenance is phenomenal. Great location. Clean common areas. Fantastic space overall.
Centric is fine, very corporate. But the maintenance staff is incredible, best in the building

honestly quite disappointed of the condition of my apartment when i moved in one week ago. The shower and dishwasher were especially dirty, smelly, and moldy. Additionally the paint job in this unit is concerning. There is paint smeared on several spots on the trim, blobs of paint in random spots, and the ceiling edges have so many inconsistencies that I would tell whoever painted that this should not be their profession. I have years of experience in multi family property management at high-end companies and I would have never let a resident move-in with the condition my apartment was in.
It’s been a great experience living here so far. Jamie was wonderful throughout the leasing process. I’ve gotten the opportunity to attend a few social events and meet some people.

Unfortunately would not recommend this property and will not be renewing my lease after a year. Parking garage door worked for maybe 3 months out of the last year, has been opened the rest of the time with an empty security car stationed at the entrance. Cars have been vandalized and stolen. Pool and hot tub were not usable through the winter, and you have to fight for a spot on the weekends because of people partying. Only elevator in one corner of the building is shut down very often due to maintenance or move-ins; I’ve had to walk all the way around the building by myself late after work many times. Leasing agents in the lobby don’t interact with residents and come off dismissive when approached. Overall just an underwhelming experience for the high rent charged as someone who works in the property management industry.

We had a list of over 10+ issues upon move out. 
Bicycles are stolen, cars are damaged and the parking garage is not secure due to broken doors
HVAC issues making the issue unlivable 
Staff was subpar
Electrical issues
Delivery parking and entrance to the building is impossible and hallway signs are not correct causing confusion and frustration to guests and drivers.

I’ve rented for 8+ years and have never had such an awful living experience. I loved it here until someone moved in above me - the floors are not concrete poured and I hear EVERY single step my upstairs neighbor takes - it quite literally sounds like thunder and causes things in my apartment to rattle - my dog ever had panic attacks because of it.  Management basically did nothing and told me I could move out and pay $4K plus two months rent to do so or have them start eviction proceedings against my upstairs neighbors, both of which are absolutely ridiculous. The walls are equally thin and I can hear it every time my next door neighbor opens their blinds. I haven’t slept through the night in months and have resorted to sleeping with AirPods blasting white noise just to drown out the noise and taking melatonin every single night. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve mentioned this to management and called security with no change. My day quite literally starts the moment they get out of bed (which I can hear at 7:30 every morning) and I can’t sleep until they decide to go to bed (midnight every night). It’s literally been the most miserable living situation and no one should have to go through this. As nice as a building as it is, it’s like living in a pretty cardboard box.

I've had a great overall experience. Sal and Melody have been a pleasure to work with on my leasing experience and move-in. I appreciate the luxury amenities, conveniences offered, and exceptional standards here. Highly recommend the property and am convincing my own friends to move in!
DriveTrain is a very well-run apartment complex - I feel safe and supported living here.
Best apartment community in the area hands down. From the amenities to the apartments themselves. Also Autumn is the best leasing agent around, and was very helpful!

If you like your car broken into, stolen (like mine was!), your packages stolen (like mine was!), overflowing trash bins, and an ungodly amount for dog crap in the dog park area, then this is a good place for you. 
No security, you have to pay a monthly fee to get your packages from a kiosk that seems to never work, and you pay hefty rent to live in a really crappy part of town. Sure, they look nice, but I would much rather pay to be SAFE and in a CLEAN environment. I regret moving there, but I am happy to be out. Believe the negative reviews, they are there for good reason.

The leasing office never leaves the leasing center, they don’t fix any issues at all or respond to emails or calls. The maintenance team does nothing but smoke and leave cigarettes and trash all over the property. I’ve seen them hang out in empty garages for long periods of time. The buildings aren’t ventilated and the hallways and stairwells are unbearably hot. There are break ins, car thefts, assaults, homeless people on the property, gun shots weekly and packages are stolen daily. The rent is crazy insane for living in such a terrible place!! They don’t recognize service animals even though it’s the law. There is trash and dog poop all over the property. They leave sprinklers and tvs on all night, keep in mind residents have to pay for all water and electricity that the property uses. Most residents here are very unfriendly and rude. PLEASE DONT MOVE HERE IF YOU HAVE FURBABIES!!! This place is so unsafe and people frequently walk their dogs off leash that have zero recall. There’s glass everywhere and trash every five feet. The staff and owners of this property don’t care about residents at all. They just want to make a quick buck.

Update to a previous review. After a recent incident they emailed “always keep doors and windows locked" yet locks here have been broken for months as they refuse to provide on-site security. They are not taking proper steps to minimize the impact of unfortunate incidents on their property. Amenities and common areas are impacted. Often broken, filthy or occupied by non-residents and unusable for weeks at a time. As someone from NY who is used to private landlords with no physical address or working contact numbers, I thought reviews here might be by people who are sensitive. No, this property is being mismanaged. It takes weeks/months to obtain basic information that should be readily available. They have residents tip-toeing around parking policies that are not clear as their towing company destroys cars. They require wearing of wristbands to prove residency and if your wristband is stolen or lost, you’ll be charged $75. Yet amenities and parking lots are a free for all for criminals and people who don’t live here. Aside from issues with the property, their system and billing errors are awful. They made an error and voided our lease leaving me fearful their system would show the apartment as vacant as they refused to fix it for months. Contacting corporate resident relations gets me nowhere. Truly hoping for more effective management to take over as soon as possible.

Was so excited moving in several months ago but they have been upsetting to try to communicate with. It's been months waiting for information on security, amenities and my lease, as property is stolen/damaged regularly. We all know they can't stop crime. Leaving security to unreliable companies, waiting to install cameras, not communicating cohesively and shrugging off feedback, is not helpful. They send perfect updates about food trucks via the portal, text message and email. Anything important? You get an email with typos leaving out crucial information creating further confusion. You then have to spend free time reaching out several times for 1-5 word responses that don't even make sense. They respond publicly as if they're taking action. As a resident who spends a lot of my time here, I do not see or feel any positive changes.
Do not be deceived by the pictures. The Leasing Office does not care about the tenants at all.

Attentive security could prevent problems like trespassers staying for hours ruining amenities forcing them to close. The business center is in sight of anyone driving and walking by. Please hire security for the main building during the day. When the office is closed it doesn’t feel safe bringing electronic devices and work valuables with no security considering the repeated thefts and violence.

If I could give 0 or negative starrs I would. Feel very bad for new residents moving in - they will be gaslighted and manipulated by management. Management doesn't give any cares. You want mice? Feel free to live here. You want maintenance repairs that will never happen? Come on down. Spend your money somewhere else. Everything is broken, nasty, filthy.

Really pretty spaces, great location (not far from anything, not in the rougher parts either), great staff. Everyone's super helpful, but Gio has always gone above and beyond- whatever I need, he's on it ASAP so it's been great being here!

While filling out my application I was a bit confused in some areas but was helped by the lovely Esther. She was very kind and welcoming, answering my question in a very clear manner. Overall I was pleased with my experience and was glad that the Assistant Property Manager was there.
I really like the location here. The upkeep of the property is great. Amenities are nice here.
I love the maintenance crew here! They are fast, professional and super polite! They even wore shoe covers like I asked!
Every time Ive had a problem its been resolved immediately.  I just had an issue with a partial power outage and it was fixed within the hour of reporting it

I moved out of this apartment nearly five months ago, but my nightmare with Windsor Communities continues. After leaving the apartment, I received notice that Windsor would be keeping my entire security deposit and sending me an additional bill of $148 for vaguely worded, nonspecific issues. I called the number provided, and an employee at the central billing office was unable to meaningfully explain the bill. I told him that I’d like to dispute it, and he promised me that someone would follow-up with me.  Several weeks later, I never heard back from Windsor but was instead called on a Friday night be an incredibly rude debt collector that Windsor apparently sold my information to without ever explaining my bill.

The experience of living in this building wasn’t much more pleasant. Despite the faux luxury appearance of the lobby and central areas, the units are poorly constructed and ridden with maintenance issues. We had several multi day stretches without hallway lights in my building, and my apartment had a repeated loud, thumping noise above the bathroom that maintenance was never able to fix despite several attempts.
Beautiful place, good location but advertised prices vs actual quotes once you apply feel very bait and switch like and it was difficult to get the leasing office to take responsibility.

my wife & i moved to hanover platt park in october. from the time of our initial visit, we were immediately brought in as "family" and i couldn't say more good things about the facility and the entire staff! they are beyond amazing!! chelsie, aimee & sean are always there and always have an answer (or get one quickly) and all with a stellar attitude! we are always well informed as to things happening in the building and i can't imagine how many packages & deliveries they deal with on the regular!! to sum it up... they are THE best. period. #hanoverplattparkRULES

We absolutely love living here at Hanover Platt Park, it has everything on-site you could need and short walking distance to everything else. We moved from Phx back in May and Aimee and the rest of the leasing staff have gone out of their way ever since. I highly recommend stopping by and taking a tour for yourself, the theater room is my favorite but the whole property is top notch..

My husband and I have lived at Hanover since April when the building was still under construction. Some of the other feedback is accurate in that construction in certain areas did take longer than anticipated (the pool and theater). However, I think this is to be expected with any construction site, and the staff tried to be as communicative as possible through the transitions. 

The management team at Hanover is truly fantastic and professional in every way. I interact most often with Chelsie and Aimee, who are both extremely friendly, helpful, and take their jobs seriously. The Hanover management and maintenance staff is incredibly responsive and efficient. We have contacted management and maintenance a couple of times with issues, which have been resolved with ease. 

The location is perfect, you’re within walking distance to great restaurants on Pearl, within 15-20 minutes of most neighborhoods in Denver, and the surrounding areas (Centennial, DTC, etc.) The neighborhood is quiet and you hardly ever have noise disturbances. Like any apartment, the walls are fairly thin, and you will hear neighbors from time to time. 

The apartments themselves are very nice, modern, and well designed. The garage entrance/exit is definitely tight and you do have to pay attention. Overall, we love living here! It is very expensive, however that’s to be expected for a new build in Denver. I highly recommend Hanover- it’s clean, well maintained, and has excellent staff!

I happened upon Hanover Platt Park when I was trying to go to a different place. I am so glad I spotted the now open sign! From the tour, through move in, and the past several months of living here this has proven to be a great choice. Aimee is so friendly, knows every resident, and really cares about making this community feel homey. I would absolutely recommend.

From the beginning, we have enjoyed living at Hanover Platt Park. We have been here for over 7 months, and we are planning to continue living here until we buy a house. 
Months back, we had an issue with noisy, non-compliant neighbors. The management team here at Hanover was immediately on top of things - they handled the situation in a professional manner, and followed the policies they listed in our lease (we all know there are places that don’t). 
As for the more “fun talk”, the staff plans fun events every month - wine and cheese nights, pool parties, Easter eggs hunts, Halloween themed parties, etc. It is wonderful to live in a place that sees the importance of creating a community. 
Overall, we love the cleanliness of the buildings, the timely manner in which maintenance/other issues are handled, and the friendly and welcoming management team/staff.
We would highly recommend Hanover Platt Park as a future home for YOU!

The garage entrance/exit is a total disaster, trying to get in and out is a mess. I have already scratched the side of my car while trying to exit and someone else was coming in. The pool looks nice but is way too small for the size of the complex. 2 lights in our kitchen constantly flicker and after maintenance has tried replacing the light bulb twice, which hasn’t worked, we have realized it they were probably wired incorrectly. 

This apartment complex has some positives but for the price is honestly not worth it. We will not be renewing our lease. We would rather pay more somewhere else that actually warrants it.

Caution:  ANYTHING MANAGEMENT TELLS YOU, MAKE SURE YOU GET THEM TO WRITE IT DOWN IN THE LEASE OR RECORD THE CONVERSATIONS.  Management will take liberties in making promises and do not have a problem breaking them without any recourse.  I must admit, it pains me to write such a damning review of this apartment complex because I personally like the local management, however, I have noticed since the day we moved in here, one promise after another has been broken.  We are now 6 months into a lease for a “premium” apartment with a pool view that has been under construction the whole time.  We first looked at this property during the construction phase in August 2018.  Leasing agents sold us on this property saying that by Decemeber 2018, everything would be ready.  At the last minute in December, after signing a lease, we were told it would not be ready until January 2019, then February 2019, then March 2019.  Of course the pool or theatre was still not ready in March.  In March, we were told “it will be ready by Memorial Day, the traditional opening of pool season.”  Well, it is now June and the pool is still not open.  Because I did not want to write a bad review of a business without first giving them the opportunity to correct the issue, I voiced this above complaint to local and regional management.  They offered a very meager remedy which came with several strings we were not comfortable signing.  So in sum, I paid extra to look at a construction area.  I even held off writing this review hoping they would reapproach us saying they now understood the issue and want to make it right.  I hope after reading this, someone from management realizes that breaking deadline after deadline with no recourse to residents is not a good business practice.  During conversations, they have been quick to offer reasons why they could not make the deadlines/promises they made to residents but have been very slow (read: non existent), in making concessions to the residents.  They have done well in leasing up this building and making money based on unfulfilled promises and a lack of sympathy for the residents.

Viewed a few apartments in MAY, and we applied for one. We did not end up following through with renting at this complex so we should've received our $300 APPLICATION REFUND BACK. We have been in contact with them over two dozen times on an update for our refund. IT HAS NOW BEEN 7 MONTHS AND NO REFUND BACK! They have given multiple excuses of wrong address to send the check to, accounting department made a mistake, again sent the check to the wrong address, error on the account, etc. DO NOT RENT FROM HERE!!!

UPDATE: I posted to their instagram account and they blocked me!! Truly an awful company and staff that refuse to be held accountable.
homeless and prowlers wander around the buildings!!!!

Hi I got a lot to say about this place 

Within the first week me and my wife had my car towed,found mice ,had our new puppy threatened by our neighbors and had our dishwasher go out and not get replaced for over a month. The Leaser’s seem to loose all interest from help any renters after the first day.We’ve come home to our water being brown after we ran all the taps in our apartment for over 1 hour and we constantly heard neighbors threatening each other every weekend and after talking to the Leaser we never heard any updates. Please avoid at all cost
Do not live here!!! This place is horrible!!!! Management is rude, most of the time! Please please please learn from my mistake and go somewhere else!!!

Bad place to live, bugs bugs and bugs never leave this place, neighbors are loud blasts their  music outside all night long. Kids run around like gangs run around and scratch everyone's car. Not a nice place to be living at all. Even adults sit outside drink all night broken bottles the next mornings my all over the parking lot had to get my tires repaired twice in a year because of this.
OLD BUILDING , BED BUGS ,cockroach, noise , the worst building ever

The apartments are mostly quiet. Maintenance sometimes takes a few days to fix things. Parking should be better; this isn't Capitol Hill. I've had to park down the street a few times and guests must find street parking. They've raised the rent on my studio by $130/mo over 2 years, so I'm moving. But I've heard that rent hikes are common across Denver.

I've lived here for a year and a half and we have just recently gone to permit parking.  The lot is awful and the drivers are even worse.  My car has been hit 3 times in one month, with the last hit and run breaking my tail light cover and bay.  Management is not in any way supportive with assistance in repair bills or providing a safer lot. They refuse to install security cameras on the premises.  I used to think this was a good residence but the cost of car repairs due to the management's negligence in providing security makes this a dangerous and expensive place to live.

These apartments are truly amazing. I had been searching for months to find my first apartment before finally stumbling upon these at Apartment.com! I was hopeful and anxious but after finally moving in, I've been really enjoying this place. Although I'm in a studio, it's very spacious, has a huge patio, and I have my cat here with me, no pet rent! Everyone I've met here so far is really friendly too. I love this place.

I love everything about Line28—the people, the location, the service, the apartments. Literally everything. From the very beginning, Letty, the building's leasing agent, was responsive, attentive and helpful. She is amazing and a joy to work with. Sidney and the rest of the team are on point, taking prompt care of issues as they arise and keeping the building informed when we need to be. And entertained, the building throws some great parties for its residents!  The neighborhood is vibrant and the location is prime, with access to great restaurants and bars, as well as the highways/rest of Denver and beyond. The building is pet-friendly, so it's great for the pooch (Little Man Ice Cream even has doggie scoops.) I cannot say enough good things about Letty, Sidney, the team and the building.

Property management does a great job putting on social activities, and keeping the apartment clean and safe. Maintenance requests are answered quickly and with a smile. Rent is a tad high but that is to be expected for the area.

I enjoy living here, the location, apartments and overall feel are great and have almost everything i need. the new management is good and seems to be trying their best. but some things need to be better like the overall cleanliness, the elevators, hot tub etc

The ceilings leak weird substances, the halls and stairways smell like trash. This is not a luxury apartment by any means. The staff is so rude and act like fixing basic things around the building is not their job.

I have lived in many apartments across many states and this is by far the best apartment complex I've ever lived in.  The leasing office made me feel appreciated as a resident and the maintenance staff keeps the property beautiful.  I highly recommend the station at riverfront Park!

Do not live here. I do not feel safe in this building. Several of the "security" doors do not shut properly and you can just push open without scanning in. We recently had an incident with unauthorized visitors smoking illegal substances and having indecent exposure on the 4th floor trash room. Management has taken no responsibility and continues to blame residents. This place is way too expensive to not feel safe, live somewhere else.
The Station leasing agent made my transition nearly stress free and went above and beyond expectations.
A great place to live!! They have everything, and the cherry on top is the staff and maintenance team - they're so helpful and responsive!!

The walls are not sound resistant at all. Very Noisy. Every little noise is easly heard especially in the bedroom where I sleep. Noise from cars slamming doors, a person coughing and especially the traffic from E 56th Ave. I do not even live near the Avenue. Its going to get really bad in winter when people warm up thier cars.
I saw the apartment briefly and went to visit when traffic was not at its peak. The apartment looked good with stainless steel appliances. Washer and Dryer. New Microvawe. Central Heating and air conditioning. On apartments.com it says that it was built in 2020 so I assumed the insulation was not old and the walls would be quality.

As a renter for twenty five years, I KNOW what is an excellent living experience should be.  And this is it!  I have lived here close to a year, and WOW, if all management was even sorta  close to treating their tenants as we should be treated, there would be no bad reviews at any community!  The community manager, Paul, is exceptional.  He listens to what the needs are of the renters.  Shelby, the assistant  manager, is wonderful and helpful.  The two maintenance guys, Roger and Gary get to my work orders as quickly and humanly as possible. By humanly, I mean, they do their best to have our concerns addressed as soon as they can. The property is cleaned and maintained.  ALWAYS. The apartments inside are stunning!  Well crafted and built. Lots of sunlight!  Yes. I made the right choice living here.  This is BY FAR,  since living in Denver for ten years, THE BEST LIVING EXPERIENCE I have, well, experienced!!!

I have definitely noticed a difference in the community since Paul has taken over. It is actually quiet at night and they are making sure the grounds are well taken care of. I have noticed an increase in security which makes me feel safer coming home at night.
Connect at First Creek is a wonderful complex and I am extremely satisfied as a tenant. John and Janice in the leasing office go above and beyond and are always kind and helpful.

The Eugene Field building at 1055 Sherman Street is part of Denver's "Poet's Row" district conveniently located in historic and beautiful Capitol Hill.  It is the perfect location for those who like to walk, bike, or take public transit and is a good compromise between hectic and lively downtown living while remaining in a quiet, scenic neighborhood.  You can walk a mile east to beautiful Cheesman Park or venture a mile north to the heart of downtown Denver.  Pros: Lots of fun, local neighborhood bars and restaurants with a young professional demographic.  The apartment is a very good size for the area.  Everyone in the leasing office is very friendly and helpful, and maintenance is quick to respond with any issues you may have.  Gas, water, and trash is included in rent, and with radiator heating your electric bill stays very low every month.  Tons of storage!  Free WiFi for the building, and also a shared community pool.  Cons: No parking! Spots are available for a monthly fee, but there aren't many spots, they're expensive, and there's a waiting list to get one.  Historic building, meaning little to no modern amenities... No air conditioning (summers can get quite hot), no dish washers, no option between cable or satellite (you cannot make alterations to historic buildings, meaning no satellite dish).  Very cramped kitchens and bathrooms.  No closet in the bedroom, although there are several spacious closets in the main living area.  Radiators and pipes clang loudly at all hours of the night in the winter.  If you're a light sleeper, the noise of the local bars and clubs on weekends could be an issue for you.  Overall, this is a great place to live for young professionals who like to enjoy the outdoors and local neighborhood scene while staying close to the hustle and bustle of downtown.

Overall, this building has suffered by being in a part of town affected by many of the problems facing downtown Denver. However, these issues have been exacerbated by inadequate management. Below are some issues I believe every future resident should be aware of:

1. There is no hot water in the building before about 7 a.m. This is a huge problem if you shower before work. As other reviews of the building mention, on-site maintenance cannot do anything about the problem.

2. There have been various projects over the past year and a half that greatly inconvenience residents. I understand wanting to continue to maintain the building, which I appreciate, but some of the projects create undue and unnecessary inconvenience for the residents. One major upcoming project that I think all potential residents should be aware of is that from 9/13/21 to 7/8/22 they are upgrading the HVAC condensers on the roof, which will leave residents without heating/cooling for up to 20 days. The dates of the project even span some colder months (such as October and November) in which it is absolutely unacceptable to leave residents without heat. 

3. The above mentioned project is probably the worst project to date. However, there have been other incidents where management has been insufficient.

4. Another example is requiring residents to move their cars from the garage for garage cleaning during All Star weekend. Again, I don’t mind the cleaning, but why did it have to happen during All Star weekend in which parking downtown was impossible to find? 

5. Another example: The key fob system went down for about a week, and the garage doors were left open all the time, since none of the garage remotes would work. In an area like downtown Denver, this is unacceptable, and during that time, we experienced a homeless man doing drugs and sleeping in the stairwell, since he was able to enter due to the open doors. 

Again, I understand the difficultly of managing an aging building in downtown Denver; however, many of these issues for residents could have been mitigated with better building management. In a building where you are paying high rent, high car parking fees, etc. I would expect better management.
