2) Having your security deposit stolen from you even after you've cleaned your apartment from floor to ceiling. They will invent charges to make sure you don't get it back, knowing that you won't have the resources to fight it. Enjoy more blatant lying from the manager at this stage.
3) The soothing sound of endless barking dogs that go from about 6 AM to midnight (if you're lucky!). Yes, you many of you will be living next to (NOT near, but next to) TWO dog runs in a dusty alley. No, your neighbors won't care that their dog has been barking for an hour. Luxury living!
4) Car break-ins in the garages, random people hanging out on the steps in your "secure" building at night, and the fairly startling sound of someone trying your apartment door handle every once in a while
5) People letting their dogs go to the bathroom all over the stairwell. EVERY DAY FOR MONTHS. Management does nothing. The checks are coming in from that lease you are really regretting about now, so what do they care? I'm sure they will try to scrub this review.
6) Even more shameless lying from the management about all of these issues and so many more. Have you ever met someone who lies to your face even though they know that YOU know they are lying - and they do it anyway? That's the manager.

Do not rent here - you can do far better. Don't rent from Greystar at all, I would say, but definitely stay away from Mason at Alameda Station.

Let me start off by saying I did not rent at IMT Alameda Station. The two two-bedroom floor plans I liked which were available when I needed to move were located on the first floor, with one facing the pool. But having said that, I love the features in the newly renovated units. There was storage space and room in the bedrooms. 

While there isn't a lot of green space on property, I like the proximity to the rail station, grocery store and Downtown. The area is in the process of being revitalized, so keep that in mind if you're looking for things to do.

Finally, I want to compliment Claire S., Leasing Consultant. She is so professional, friendly, and knowledgeable about the property and surrounding area. While looking for a new home, I have had to deal with many leasing consultants who can't answer questions about their own property. Not so with Claire. I really enjoyed working with her, and I know that as a resident, she would make sure to answer your concerns. Thanks, Claire!

This place has great amenities and the apartments are nice. The location is convenient as well, but has so far made it a very noisy place to live. The only apartments that become available are either facing a construction site that starts at 7am and is super loud or you face Alameda, which offers loud traffic and constant sirens literally 24 hours a day, every day! Oh, and don’t forget the train! If you can live facing the pool or zen garden it may be worth it but otherwise you may want to choose one of the many other places just like it that is not so loud.

My experience living at Alameda Station has been wonderful. The staff is incredible. I had a bad experience living downtown because the staff didn't care. This is a night and day difference. The women in the office, Morgan and Brie, are super friendly, always helpful and just nice people. They care about my experience here.  If I have a light bulb out, somebody is here to replace it within 30 minutes. The grounds are beautiful. The pool is kept very clean and and people are respectful of other residents. The south Broadway area is fantastic so it's great to be able to walk to shops and restaurants. This place is just a few blocks from the light rail so it's easy to get downtown.
Been here for over 4 years, and have always received 5 star service from front office and cliff's maintenance crew. They rock!

Without a doubt, Skyhouse is the best apartment home community in Denver! The residents and staff are all very friendly. I've never had a bad experience with any residents or staff here - this place seems to attract happy, kind, positive people. The location is super convenient and centrally located around anything you'd need in a city. Choice Market downstairs has amazing made to order food and grocery. The rooftop lounge offers the best views in Downtown Denver and is an excellent spot to cook on one of the grills or read a book in one of the lounge chairs. The gym has everything you'd need to workout every muscle and cardio equipment to keep you active. Really don't think I could live anywhere else. This place is just amazing and words cannot explain how wonderful it is here.

If you are complacent with sharing a 50-100 square foot pool with 23 other floors of overly aggressive snots that will trash the halls, each other, and the concierges that try to keep the whole building safe, the low utilities and decent location may be worth it. Otherwise, just go home, put some fairy lights on your desk, and pretend you’ve got a few homeless people outside every day. It’ll be just like the city without rodents, a-holes, and an overpriced quality of life.

This is my departing message to management:

I will start by saying we have been living here for a year and a half. Our first impression was terrible as we moved from across the country and our apartment was not ready the day we moved in. It was filthy and had not been cleaned after the previous tenants. They sent cleaners out who rushed to clean the apartment in an hour, so of course it was not done well.

We discovered many maintenance issues. Some of these maintenance issues I have still not been addressed from when we found them a year and a half ago. 

The overall quality is terrible and can’t believe you call these apartments “luxury”. Our floors are bubbling up, paint is chipping everywhere, appliances do not work like they should, etc. The list goes on. 

Our mail around holidays was stollen almost everyday and you refuse to install gates around the mailboxes like other places have around here. 

The communication between residents and staff is the worst I’ve ever experienced. It is nearly impossible to contact anyone unless you physically go into the office. What’s even worse is when you do go into the office you are lied to over and over again, which means you have to go into the office repeatedly, wasting your time.

The worst part of all this is the new residents who have been moving in over the last 6 months. Not sure whats going on but we have two new neighbors below us and both of them smoke cigarettes and marijuana inside their apartments. Our neighbors below us also have about 10 people who come and go from the apartment daily which I know they are not all on the lease. They also prop both doors open (front and back) this allows strangers to wander into our building and steel our packages and belongings from our garage. Its absolute hell here. Did I mention we’ve sent emails, called, and stopped in in-person to address these issues? Oh yeah, because you don’t care, they haven’t been addressed.

Our lease has been violated in so many ways we have gotten an attorney and we are breaking lease early (Thank God.) and moving. 

We do not want to expose ourselves or our son to the harmful effects of second hand smoke, the rancid smells coming from the apartments below us, the shady characters going in and out of the building and the blatant disregard for safety or our belongings.

I feel horrible for those who have to endure living here. The poor people who have to move into our apartment after us have no idea what they’re in for.

I understand that there are staff shortages these days, but this place has no one. Getting ahold of a person to get an appliance fixed, a question answered or even to clarify the payment of rent is impossible. Garage doors don't work, exterior hallways are filthy, appliances are old and of limited functionality (I often wash my clothes elsewhere because the washer and dryer are so bad in the apartment), snow removal is non-existent creating an ice rink for those taking trash to the dumpster -- very dangerous -- and security is zero. Do not rent here. It used to be a great place, but since the current agency took ownership (Highmark Residential), it's been a disaster. Beware.

As noted in the header, but really, AC and washing machine were terrible! On top of that the managing team are terrible. Also, Fan in bathroom is always on when you turn in the light, and it is extremely noisy. No way to take a peaceful shower.

They claimed after 5 months of them not charging me utilities that it was not their fault that I was being charged all of it in a lump some when I moved out. Also, they claimed the stove was dirty and the drip pan needed to be replaced. I never used the stove. I travel for work and was rarely there. If I was there I would go out to eat. It was literally the only not new (cheap) appliance in my apartment as I got the “refurbished” deal. Now they fixed that issue too.

I consider this place as my new sanctuary. The property manager, in particular, is genuine, reliable, and diligent. Garfield Park Apartments has commendable and ethical business practices; prioritizes tenants through operational efficiency and high-quality customer service!

RENTERS BEWARE!!!  This place is a scam!!!!  I lived here for 2 years with very little issue until it came time to move out of my apartment.  I cleaned the apartment to an absolute tee before moving out and they still charged me over $500 from my security deposit to CLEAN the apartment.  There was no damage to anything.  I was charged a $50 cleaning fee for cleaning the medicine cabinet (there wasn't even one in the apartment).  I was charged $50 for cleaning the kitchen sink which was immaculate.  $50 for the refrigerator which was spotless.  $50 for not changing out the AC filter (which is a maintenance issue and should have been replaced by them).  Overall I would say avoid this place at all costs.  Way too over priced for an apartment that is nowhere near downtown and has no accommodations like a pool or balcony.  Even the fitness center is filled with treadmills that have no power; you have to adjust the incline and let gravity do the work.  Management is nice until it comes time to move out.  I would rate them 0/5 stars if I could.  Find somewhere that isn't scam!!!!

I have lived at Garfield Park Apartments studio space for nearly a year from summer of 2018 - 2019 and enjoyed the overall experience tremendously. I felt the need to write this review as note of gratitude and to help interested future tenants. 

I initially accidentally stumbled upon the apartment about a year ago in passing and super glad I chose to stay with it because its been one of the most comfortable and accommodating apartment living experiences Ive had in my history of renting in Denver. Considering how expensive housing has become in Denver, you truly get great deal at Garfield Park. 

I lived on the 3rd floor facing the street, had a beautiful sunny room. I love the large windows. The studio space is large, ample amenities, central location, and electricity fees are low for the rent price. I have never experienced any loud noises or noise complaints during my time here, the building is quiet and clean with courteous neighbors. Majority of the tenants are doctors, young professionals and international tenants.

The building has controlled security with coded/intercom door access and on-site management team including landlord who feel more like family. 

The current landlord and building maintenance team are superb. They are one of the most friendliest and kind people I have come across, responsive and helpful if you ever need anything.  

It was always a joy to interact with the landlord and the two maintenance guys. The landlord is a person of integrity and a person of his words which is rare to find these days. He has an inclusive attitude and welcoming of different cultures. From the get and throughout my stay, the management team was consistently welcoming, warm, supportive, flexible and professional. The courteousness of the management team truly amplified and made my experience enjoyable here! So much so that if I were to return to central Denver again, Garfield Park would be my first choice.

Hampden Village was one of the most affordable options I could find in the Denver metro area when I moved in several years ago. If you're looking for something that isn't expensive in Denver — where low-priced options are few and far between — this is a great fit. 

The place was clean, maintenance service was great and parking lot pavement was well maintained. The landlord was always responsive and helpful. The property is relatively close to Rosamond Park and is just off Hampden Avenue, a major road that takes you to I-25, the main highway in the area. It puts you within a short drive of many stores, commercial centers and dine-out options.

Again, the main attraction is the affordability. In an overpriced apartment market like metro Denver's, properties like this are rare. It's a good opportunity to take advantage of.

Terrible. 3 break-ins to the "locked gated" car garage in 6 months.  Bike was stolen and underground storage unit broken into.  Apartment management does nothing, didn't even inform residents of the break-in until the 2nd one happened... one week later.  Not a care in the world that their is effectively no building security.  They say they care, but haven't even fixed the broken lock on the storage unit so I don't store anything in there anymore. Claim to want to give compensation, 8 weeks later, haven't gotten back to me. Multiple emails, phone calls, etc.. all saying they care... They do not. Spend your money elsewhere!

Been emailing for weeks. Company that owns bldg doesn't return Security Deposit
Clean and updated unit, friendly property mgmt staff, great location!

Stay away! Crooks and con artists! Poor attention to detail and customer service. They  will say anything to get your business, but don't keep track of what they say or promise. Management team thinks they are infallible and refuse to take responsibility for their own actions.

When my thermastat went out called emergency maintznce number was disconnected. Fire department tried the three emergency contacts they had and fhe could do is leave a message. So if there was an actual fire one wonders what would oc happened. I have a baby and it was cold that night and we had to make other arrangements to sleep that night. I czll mamagement and property management and no one ever called me back in fact I am still waiting for that call back. There excuse was phone was broke as far as I am concerned nothing but an excuse. Could even offer a discount for displacing me. Parkside is greedy. I will break my lease the is a safety concern to my family. These apartment are even remodeled just refaced and overly priced.

I've lived here 3.5 years and while the building had never been amazing, constantly broken elevators, small pool/hot tub that has had a number of issues. The new management company that has taken over about 6-8 months is terrible. You will get no communication from the office staff. They will (legally) enter your apartment at any time to perform maintenance, which in itself is great, but everywhere I've lived before they at least provide you a heads up. Fixing things just doesn't happen quickly, if at all. There are projects unfinished from before summer. Rent prices here are plumitting for a reason, so be aware before you look at the prices and get excited.

Lived here for 2.5 years, starting from when the building first opened. It was nice being close to the city, the highlands and Jefferson Park. But at this point the cons far outweigh the pros. My car was stolen from the “secure garage”, along with many others. Packages and food stolen from inside. And it’s not that the elevators break “sometimes”. They are constantly broken. Having spoken to elevator maintenance and the original maintenance staff of the building, they can’t be permanently fixed. They were built/installed too quickly. They will always break and need to be fixed. Staff while I was there as of a couple months ago was impressive in their perceived care for your issues. But gave little care to execution and follow through. I’ve been working with corporate for going on 2 months to resolve issues with my final bill because all messages sent to management were ignored. 

Short summary of other issues over my time at the Alcott:
- shooting outside, bullet damage to front of building and gym glass (2021)
- stolen cars, bikes, packages, gym equipment and food
- homeless sleep inside parking garage and elevator lobby
- surrounding parking lots are used by local kids to do burnouts and set off fireworks. At all hours. 

Again, the location of the building made having fun, easy. But constant minor inconveniences and occasional major inconveniences make this place, overall, a dump.

I originally chose The Alcott based on location, but was very impressed by the property and units.
Cat made it very easy to move in, and is a complete joy to work with through the process.
The community events are also a blast to attend.

Overall, the apartment itself was decent but they should be since they newer, but parking is a hassle, and there is a lot crime including a known street racing gang that hangs out by the building. Ever been a building were windows were shot at. Yeah, very luxurious. Denver police even installed cameras because it has been such an issue.  
Homeless have been able to access common areas.  Tenants lack respect for the common areas.  Elevators work less often than not.  Codes required for the stairways but they are not provided. Don't store your bike in the bike area unless you want to off load it.  Maintenance is great and responsive but management was lacking.  Not really safe to walk after dark and really isn't close to much walking wise.

Since the new management took over (summer 2022) there has been increased issues on the property with no resolution. The new property team is extremely unapproachable and unknowledgeable on the property, current market trends, and general customer service. Do not recommend

Writing this simply as a warning, if you want to deal with thefts, gun shots in and at the building, along with a completely rude and incompetent staff then move here. Debating on terminating my lease due to how unsafe and how uncaring the management is about their residents.

I called inquiring about a rental and when asking questions I was told by their staff "I can't answer that" when I asked why they simply hung up on me. I find this to be very rude and poor practice of business.

Not truly AC, but more "air cooling". The difference is that there are no compressors in each apartment, just cooling coils. Not as effective as true AC but also not as expensive on electric bill.

No longer provides free Internet or wifi.

The single pane windows can be a problem during windy and cold days. 
Staff does do a good job of maintaining the building and grounds.

Never offered us a lease renewal then got ticked off because we “didn’t give them 60 days” to leave, so they took our security deposit and want to charge us 250 extra. They’ll get that over my dead body. Property management changed about 7 times over the 2 plus years we lived there, snow shovelers often waited 3 days to shovel our house, trash was usually everywhere throughout the complex, and the grill outside was never cleaned.

This apartment was infested with bed bugs while I lived there in April 2022 and we did not bring them in. They made their way through the whole apartment complex and cornerstone refused to do anything except spray individual units who complained (so not even all the units were sprayed).  They are most definitely living in the walls so spraying individuals units is not going to help anything. They also didn’t tell us about the bugs until we physically saw them. Then they refused to pay for our hotel costs. HORRIBLE COMPLEX, HORRIBLE LANDLORDS!!!!!!

I have had a very positive experience at Ten Ten Clarkson and with Cornerstone (the company that manages the property).  When I moved in I expected to spend the day cleaning but the apartment was spotless.  I pay for a parking space and when I moved in there was a car parked in the space assigned to me.  I contacted Cornerstone and it was handled quickly and appropriately.  The building is quiet and well maintained and the apartments have recently been refinished with hardwood floors, new stainless appliances, and new cabinets.  Everything is new and works very well compared to other old buildings in the area. The windows and doors are new as well and have a great seal.  There is a laundry/mail room with coin operated machines that are new and work well.  It is located in a great location walking distance to parks, whole foods, King soopers, Einstein bagels, starbucks, and pretty much anything else you could need!   The building has homes on one side and is on an entirely residential street which makes it very quiet.  Rent is very reasonable for the area especially considering they are one bedrooms and not studios.  It's a great place to live in Cap Hill!

So far I am loving my new place! It is very spacious, great storage, and the built-in desk is so convenient. The kitchen has a huge island so I don't have to waste space with a table. Loving every aspect! There's nothing about my apartment that I would change that the property do anything about/change - only downside I've come across is the noise from the street. But I love the location, so I can handle a bit of noise.
Living here has been great. I've been here for a year and the staff is always super accommodating and friendly to me and my dog.
I have been at this apartment for the past 4 years and I love living here. They are extremely generous and always good to my dog. We are very lucky to have found this place. :)

We have been living in our current apartment for a little over a month and are really enjoying the community. The location is fantastic, with close proximity to downtown (walkable) and to the highway. The community is welcoming with nice accommodations and comfortable spaces to spend time outside of the apartment. The property managers are attentive and helpful.

The facilities are really nice and management is super attentive. Maintenance requests are responded to almost immediately and the whole community has a very welcoming vibe. The location is incredible and the units are beautiful and you can tell well cared for.

This building has so many positives - excellent location (shout out to Zuni Street Brewing!), great staff, well-maintained building, and good community features. We are heading into our second year of leasing at 2828 Zuni, and could not be happier with our choice.
This was an amazing place to rent! Location and amenities were great and the staff were responsive. Would recommend to anyone in the Denver area.

I recently relocated from Los Angeles, and I signed a lease here sight unseen. I can confidently say it was a fantastic decision! Everything about the process has been smooth and above and beyond. Hannah and Morgan were really friendly and helpful, and my unit is awesome! Appliances are new and fixes are addressed promptly. Very happy here at 2828 Zuni. Truly.

This place is absolutely the best to live! It has a a great location and my apartment is beautiful! Sarah and Tony are two of the best property managers you could ask for though! They are always there to help and make sure you are taken care of!!! Seriously love living here!!!

-Triniti

The community is amazing. The staff is super responsive, always polite and truly care about the people (and the pets) that live here. Robert is always willing to come save the day when it comes to maintenance or even minor clean-ups. The community is well maintained and quiet, and it truly feels like a nice home to come back to after a long day at work or traveling around the country.

This is a fantastic location!  Sarah, Tony, and Robert are so kind and accommodating. It is a very pet friendly environment with great residents and a helpful community.  All of the residents are kind to each other.  This location is walking distance to great restaurants and also easy access to I-25 and downtown. The units and appliances are in great condition. Anyone looking to live in this area should definitely look here first. Like the previous review, you will not regret it!

Move here. You won't regret it. I signed the lease site unseen, and boy am I glad I did. I got a new job in Downtown Denver. I was living in Los Angeles. I had one week to find a place to live in Denver. I checked several neighborhoods and decided that Highlands was the right place for me. Why? Young professionals who want to live near (and be able to walk to) Downtown without having to deal with the vagrants or noise of living directly in Downtown. There were several options. Most of them looked nice from the photographs online, but it was the staff of 2828 Zuni that stood out. Michelle, Sarah, Robert - all of them are rock stars. Michelle was my point of contact throughout the entire process. I made her run around taking photographs of the fitness center, asking her all kinds of strange questions about living in the apartment like how much noise there is outside at night (answer: zero), and she responded to me promptly and without hesitation every single time. I looked at and read these reviews when I was searching, and it's a fact that the reviews are all stellar - especially about Michelle, Sarah and Robert. It's true. I firmly stand behind my 5-stars. The apartment is bigger than I imagined. Beautiful spacious kitchen. Big bathrooms. Gorgeous granite counter tops. It seems brand new. Everything is spotless. Even the downstairs garage is spotless. Not a single piece of trash! I'm beginning to think that no one lived in this apartment before me! The sunroom/grill area is beautiful. The lounge is warm and welcoming. Coffee in the morning downstairs if you want. Fitness center to get in shape (lots of cardio, rowing machine, benches, dumbbells up to 65lbs, smith machine for heavy lifting etc). Incredibly secure building (need electronic key fobs to get in and out). Small community makes the transition (especially from out-of-state) feel much more comfortable. Sprouts, Walmart, Home Depot a couple of miles northwest. Loads of restaurants, bars, coffee shops walking distance. Union Station / 16th St. Mall Downtown exactly 1.0 miles walk (15-20 minutes). I'm happy I'll be living at 2828 Zuni for another year. I couldn't imagine a better place to call home.

My husband and I moved here from Alabama, not knowing anyone! 2828 Zuni became our home instantly. We have lived at 2828 Zuni for almost a year! It is has been the best experience. We love the staff Michelle, Sarah, and Robert. They are so helpful, accommodating, quick to respond, and SO friendly! The few times we have need maintenance (VERY FEW) Robert has fixed the issue that day, usually within minutes of my placing a service order!

The location can not be beat! I think LoHi is the best location you can live in Denver! You are within walking distance of amazing restaurants, breweries (Zuni street brewery is right across the street!), shopping, and you can cross the pedestrian bridge and be in LoDo within 10 minutes. 

We have two dogs, and it has been really nice to live somewhere where dogs are welcomed! 

The apartment layout is very spacious and modern, with nice additions like new appliances, granite countertops, large balcony's, a really nice sun deck, free yoga classes on Thursday, and an espresso machine! 

If we were not moving we would be living here for years to come!  I can not recommend this apartment complex more! If you are moving to Denver, and want to live in the best location, at the best apartment (for an unbeatable price), with amazing staff and neighbors move to 2828 Zuni!

I lived at 2828 Zuni for five years (2014 to 2019) and intentionally waited to write a review until I moved out so I wouldn't be biased. I LOVE IT. The staff, Sarah and Michele as of Feb 2019, are both great. Always accommodating and easy to work with. The location of this property is amazing, I work from home and wanted some place that was both quite, but also walking distances to a lot of amenities (bars, coffee shops, restaurants, and grocery store). This building fit the bill. I also wanted a spacious floor plan with good views, which I had on the fourth floor in a one bedroom plus den. There are a lot of work from home and new to Denver residents in the building. The crowd seem to be mostly in their young 30's to early 40's. Great place to live.

2828 Zuni has been a great place to live. My husband and I chose it because of the floor plans and location and actually signed our lease without ever touring since we were out-of-state. I work from home and love the ability to walk downtown, or quickly hop on I-25 to get out of town. Having assigned parking in the garage is appreciated, especially during the winter. With the recent change in management to the Cardinal Group, I was concerned that perks like the fantastic coffee machine might change, but it’s been upgraded to local Boulder organic coffee and we got keep Michelle on the leasing team, who always brightens my day. They’ve also switched to healthier dog treats in the lobby. The new maintenance supervisor, Robert, is communicative and went above and beyond by taking out smelly trash when he was recently in our apartment for a repair while we were out of town.

Not a bad place to live if your trying to be right by the Highlands and Downtown Denver.  Great restaurants and a good night life.  Rent is pretty high and it doesn't appear to be slowing down.  Unfortunately, seems pretty common throughout the area.

Comments about the apartments - almost zero sound from hallways and next door neighbors.  Can hear upstairs neighbors walking and sometimes barking dogs, but it does seem to be thinner ceilings and floors than walls.  Not really annoying unless your upstairs neighbors don't utilize the gym.  Great little gym on the first floor, by the way.

Pretty large 1-bdrm apt with a big kitchen and a nice island counter to cook.  Good size bathroom with washer/dryer in the closet.  Wish there was a bit more storage in the apt., but they do have rentable space in house if you have a bunch of stuff.  Balconies aren't anything special, but enough room for a small table and couple of chairs.  Gets the job done.

Saw some comments on Yelp about issues with new mgmt and flooding.  I haven't experienced it living on the other side though.  Ugly rafter up to try and fix it, but hasn't impacted my experience.  New mgmt seems to have their hands full, but meets my few small requests exceptionally.

2828 is a great location if you are looking for an apartment building that gives you access to Denver without being in the hustle of LODO. The demographics of the building are high 20's professionals looking for quiet living in a trendy neighborhood. Recommended for those looking for quiet living in Denver.

The building is infested with cockroaches. The property manager is also very friendly until after you sign the lease and are tied into the contract. I highly recommend looking somewhere else. It's not worth the cheaper rent and nice-looking appliances.

I've lived at the Courtyard at Cherry Creek for almost a year. Isela (the manager) is responds very promptly to any concerns and maintenance does a wonderful job keeping the community clean. In the winter, the pathways are shoveled immediately and in the summer, the pool is always immaculate. 

I don't think I could have found a better place for the price in such a central location! My only complaint is road/street noise but that is to be expected in the middle of a densely populated area. I would recommend again but am moving out to have a yard for my dog. 

Also - very friendly neighbors! :)

Finding a cute place for a fair price is hard that’s why I enjoy my space so much! Love being close to infinity park where walking my dog is convenient. The complex also has a small dog park which helps in the winter days!

Terrific!
The location is unbeatable with terrific views and access of DU. Neighbors are awesome and rent is decent, Management is also pretty good. I look forward to staying here for a bit!

This place is garbage. The police are always here, people let their little kids run  ramped alone all day long, no one is ever in the leasing office, we have mice and ants, drunk people vomit all over the property all the time. I’m leaving immediately.

Do NOT move in here, unless you’re willing to pay over $200 in utilities ($230 for me in January with heat keeping at 65 at all times) for a 520sq ft apartment. I’m pretty sure Cornerstone is screwing people over considering the same situation happens with my girlfriend’s apartment, which is also managed by Cornerstone. The other possible issue could be poor insulation as the floors are freezing cold on the 2nd floor (right above the garage). They charge over $50 for common electricity, and the only amenity the building has is a tiny gym. The garage door was broken for 6 months but is now fixed. The trash is always full and messy (won’t be surprised if roaches appear soon). The apartments themselves are nice.

Reporting Botnick Realty to the city of Denver today. There’s zero security here with homeless people always on property, the maintenance person is lazy, often making the issue worst and the elevator has been broken for more than a month now just to name a few. They don’t care here. Don’t live here.

On June 4, 2024, my husband and I returned home to find a “Demand for Payment” posted on our door stating “if we do not pay $0 by June 7, we will receive a 50 dollar late fee.” We already paid our rent on June 1, which we have been doing so the past three years without ever being late. 

When we shared our concerns with the new office manager downstairs, (who was nice about the situation) he shared that everyone in the building received this notice but he did not know why or how however the office has yet to even acknowledge its mistake and/or take accountability. 

We loved this place year one. Year two, we noticed a lot of younger kids moving in who do not take care of the building. Leaving empty cans of beer in our community garden and leaving our roof with a beautiful view full of trash. They also removed our beloved library months ago with the plan of replacing it with a “rec room” which has remained empty only for homeless people to slew in. 

Which leads to our third year living here, whereby there have been consistent security issues with countless homeless people found sleeping upstairs, lobby and the stairwells. The building does not have a security guard full time but only one that is a contractor that only walks through the building once at night for less than 30 minutes. 

Unfortunately, year three will be our last year as it only is getting worst. We recommend searching elsewhere for a home.

People smoke on their balcony’s so get ready to become a second hand smoker. Plus they smoke in the stairways. Dog crap consistently in the elevators. Dog pee at every entrance if not in the building. Ignorant management who remind my partner and I of that one substitute teacher no one liked back in HS because they took their job too seriously and are always “by the book” even when it is just common sense. We do not recommend!

If you like paying high prices for tiny spaces, plus the bonus of having to share with homeless people...then this is the place for you. 

No care taken for tenants and rent prices keep rising.

10 months of communicating with the office about neighbors smoking in the apartments and it coming thru our vents.  No resolution other than filters that don't work, odor eaters that don't work.  Instead of dealing with the issue I'm offered to relocate to a different unit.  Also waiting months for a part for the fridge since the wrong part was ordered multiple times. The place was nice 3-4 years ago when we moved in but downhill ever since.  Homeless sleeping and doing drugs in the laundry room since the lock was broken for months.  Should I mention the drive by shooting and crime.  New management has taken over, I set an appointment, and the office was closed for my appointment.  When I went for my appointment a new renter was in their car waiting for 3 hours as they were supposed to move in but no one answered the door of the office, so new management is off to a bad start but I will acknowledge they are inheriting a mess.  We also pay $35 a month for trash pickup and they miss us all the time.  People use their patios for storage and it looks like a hoarder house.  Stay away.  I TRY TO COMMUNCATE TO NEW MANAGEMENT WITH NO RESPONSES.

Welcome to the dystopian apartment complex of Grammercy Apartments where children roam unsupervised, the pool is never open, crime runs rampant, and trash is everywhere.

This complex is a nightmare to start it’s disgusting and tenants apparently don’t know the concept of a trash can. I would see trash on the sidewalk and grass all the time. Speaking of trash it wasn’t emptied for a whole month last year and piled up really bad which is quite a health hazard.

Now on to crime, several of my previous neighbors have had their cars broken into and had parts from their car stolen. I’ve had to call the cops several times when I saw something suspicious or heard/saw domestic abuse. I would hear gunshots about once a month from the distance. And there was even a shootout in the apartment complex where someone was killed this past year! Look it up it was on the news. 

This complex has some questionable tenants too. I had a neighbor yell for no reason in the middle of the day and blast music outside while I was working from home he would do this several times a week. I believe he got evicted and started throwing furniture off of the second floor! (Mind you someone did live below him). After he left he let homeless squatters live in the apartment for a couple weeks. I noticed this and contacted property management which they didn’t believe me at first until I told them they should check because there were homeless people living there.

This is not a good location at all like as it is advertised and if you commute into downtown Denver have fun 40-50min in traffic going down the I25.

The only good things about this living in this apartment was that the maintenance was great and the high line canal trail was very close by. Other than that this place sucks and I highly discourage anyone to live here for their safety and sanity.

This area is experiencing an uptick of crime and it happens in the complex since it is not gated and there is no on-site security. A number of stolen and abandoned cars line Girard Ave. in front of the complex and the cars of residents are broken into or towed without warning. 

This is not a good place if you want peace or are raising children.

Lived here for a year, contemplated moving out several times. My car was broken into once. My partner's car was knifed. Security here is nonexistent.  Additionally, most people in the complex smoke tobacco and the smell permeates throughout the apartment. Pool is routinely closed because people smoke in it and then it must be cleaned.

Management is friendly and responsive. The apartments are also near parks which is convenient. Overall, it was not a horrible experience but there are nicer places in Denver.
I have been living here since last year and I LOVE it!!! The kitchen is real nice with granite counters. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They are my favorite. I wont be moving any time soon.

I have lived here for 4 years and I love it! The ladies are always there to help you, the maintenance are very prompt with work orders, and the grounds are always clean. Rents are comparable with other properties around the area, but not planning on moving any time soon. I would recommend this property to anyone.

I lived at Westover Garden apartments for almost 3 years and had nothing but the best experience. The apartment complex is well maintained and any maintenance requests in my apartment were promptly taken care of. The maintenance staff was always very polite and respectful. The best impression was the last one, when I was moving out at the end of my lease term. Due to circumstances beyond my control with the new residence I was to move into, I had  to extend my stay  by a few more days. I even had to leave my many moving boxes outside the building landing and just outside my apartment for a couple of days! I was so worried that I would be inconveneicing the maintenance staff who needed to get the apartment ready for the new tenants.  However, everyone was just so understanding! Not only was the maintnenace staff very courteous with me while waiting for me to get my belongings moved out, they even helped me by moving my couch. I was taken aback by the level of courtesy of the maintenance staff. And last but not least, I must say Lisa, the property manager and the leasing agents; Amari and Natasha, were all so very kind and compassionate and they went above and beyond, to facilitate my move. I was treated like a family member and not a tenant who is moving out.  I was teary eyed out of sheer gratitude as I was driving away in the moving truck, recollecting all the kindness shown to me by Lisa and her entire staff, including the gentleman who came to paint the semi-vacated apartment, and also my wonderful neighbors, John- my immediate neighbor who glides on his hover-board with his pet bird on his shoulder, his sweet wife, the very friendly sweet lady downstairs with the two adorable daughters and all others. Thank you to all of them. May God bless you all. :0)

This place, not just one unit is crawling with mold. Old pipes and cheap repairs during water damage issues and a result of mold growing. Management has even gone so far as to spray paint over the mold to present the place as “move in” ready. Once you get sick oh they will happily let you out of your lease but will keep your money and not even consider reimbursing you for your illness and time lost at work and money lost for the cost of moving into their place. A lot of people in the future will move here and get sick and not even know it’s a result of the mold, so they will treat the symptoms that will never really be cured until they move out. The owner is taking peoples money and allowing them to move into an uninhabitable place. Kids and elderly could have a serious reaction to this and could end up hospitalized or even end up in a fatal situation or lifelong illness. Mold is no joke! Cases with the health department have been opened. Greed over values is what the owner seems to be about. Do not waste your time renting here. Save your family from serious illness!

Westover Gardens was a good choice for me and worked for me for many years.  Lisa and Linny in the office were there the whole time and were great to work with.  Maintenance was good and fairly fast.  I would recommend this place.
Amazing! Quiet! Same day maintenance, very responsive team! Clean property. And great layout, if I could I'd stay forever!!!

I've lived here for 5 years now and it's been pretty good. The staff are great and the maintenance is pretty quick. For the most part it's a pretty quiet area. I recommend getting a apartment on the top floor because they're are times you can hear your neighbor upstairs. I gave only 4 stars since I do wish they allowed dogs here, especially since there's a dog park really close by, and covered parking. It's a good location. Most shopping is walking distance. I haven't had any major problems since living here.
I like so for the best apartment based on service quality and customer service I am so happy to move up.

Takes forever for anything to ever get fixed. Some things never do (i.e. the elevator). No one in management ever returns calls or emails unless they need something. In that case, they will just show up at your door unannounced. They are both so rude. I don't think I've gone one solid week without something being broken. It amazes me this place functions at all.

Current situation has led me to this review. I lived in the Tamai Tower complex with a resident/friend who has been living there for almost 2 years. I lived in the residence/friends apartment from May 23rd 2017 until I moved into a new location on June 1st 2017. Upon the agreement, the manager at the time had me sign some paperwork, just like any other complex when you sublet. Before I was handed the keys and a fob, I owed $45.00 for my application fee. May 23rd I walked over to 7Eleven on Lawrence to pay for a $45.00 Money Order and met with the manager at the time to pay. Fast forward to today on March 22, 2018. There is new management who has contacted the resident/friend of Tamai Tower saying "The Application Fee was never paid of $40.00" and is now trying to charge him $40.00 extra on his rent. After reaching out on my end to try and clear up some confusion. "New Manager" said that the old manager wrote it down as a "pay later" and never marked "Paid" on the ledger. This is where I was stumped. What business / complex would ever hand over keys on an "I owe you" Unfortunately it's been almost a year since I have lived in the residence & after searching all over, I have no receipt from the money order. I do have a transaction from the 7Eleven the same day I signed the paper work for $60. Allowing me to pay $45 in cash for my money order. After questioning the current management about some proof of paperwork showing I would "Pay Later" I have received no response other than management sending me an e-mail saying "I will no longer be going back and forth regarding this matter"

He sent me a picture of the ledger showing the $45.00, but old management never marked it. So now with new management having no idea, they just go by what they see & when you try to resolve the situation they try to give you the run around and tell you they are no longer discussing the situation. 

As a manger for the company I work for. I would never go about a situation in such a rude manor. 

If you decide to live in Tamai Tower. Make sure to keep every tiny bit of information & paperwork you receive from them because it may be a bigger problem than $40.00

Basically I would not choose this complex from the downtown area ever again after being treated this way. Many more options with better management.

I think another comment says this as well, but I have no idea why there are not more comments and reviews for this apartment complex. I think this place is perfect for me. I'll just begin by saying it has a good mix of people: All types of ages, races, and interesting people. It has a very diverse setting, and offers a lot of common parties and get together's for their residents. I believe that is because Cornerstone leasing company puts these up. They are a great leasing company that only wants the best for their residents and it shows through their employees. Zach and Deb are the ones that manage Tamai Tower, and are the ones I see the most often. Zach gave me a tour of the apartment without a moment of hesitation, and Deb is constantly helping me with anything I need through Tamai Tower. 

I have lived here for about two months now, and I have not found a single thing to complain about. I moved here for a new job, and picked this place based off the reviews and calling the leasing office. It was a very risky play, as I had never seen the place, been in the area, or even seen the room I was going to get; but it was a great payoff for such a risky move. 

I believe all apartments are fixed with a nice patio view of the city. Mine is facing towards Coors Field and I am about a block or two from all the bars for my age group (21-28 ish). This is the perfect area for me, and I love being able to sit on my patio and experience the city. 

The rent is probably the best in the area, and we pay a flat rate for utilities (AC, Heat, Electricity). You will need to provide internet, but the building is fixed for Xfinity, and it's really good while also being the cheapest option. I have no issues during high demand times. The only issue I had with Tamai Tower, and it was not their fault or blame at all, was the parking. Parking in this city is ridiculous and extremely expensive. They have a parking structure, but it serves the surrounding stores and daily/hourly/nightly parking. I was put on a waiting list to park in the structure, so I had to find parking for only a month until I was granted a parking spot. Not only is the spot I received from Tamai Tower located right next to my place, but it was also cheaper than the parking spot I had across the street. Isn't that crazy? 

Finally, this is a must pick if they have an available unit. We have a very welcoming community, so come by and be greeted with smiles!

First off, I'm very surprised that there aren't more reviews out there for this place..

I've been living here for about 4-5 months and I have had almost all positive experiences so far. 
The Management team are great, the location is perfect for my wife and I, and you won't find a lower price in LODO. I have looked and found other apartments in the area are a good 400 to 500 dollars more per month (minimum) than Tamai Tower.

Some Pros: 
- The only thing I have to pay for is rent, ALL other utilities are free (water, AC/Heating,electricity, etc.)
- The view is awesome from the balcony
- The trash shoot is feet away from the apartment door
- The neighbors are friendly
- Great location
- Great management (Deb and Jake are very nice and I can tell that they really care about the building and its residents)
- The penthouse has been newly remodeled. It has beautiful views, a small gym, conference room, study area, couches, etc. 
- The apartment itself is simple, in a good way. It has hardwood all over, white walls, and great window views. 

Some Cons:
- There have been times that I've seen some homeless people around the premises (2 or 3 instances)
- The elevators are not perfect, as one will be out of service every so often (there is always one working though)
- Building is older than most apartments in the area
- No dishwasher :(
- There are alot of older people living in the building, some can be a bit restless and want to talk your head off      sometimes
- There are bars and the Rockies stadium very close, so there can a bit of noise from the crowds and music. Has kept me up in the past when trying to sleep


Overall, this is a good place to live if you work/go to school in LODO, have no kids, and enjoy the city life. I would love to stay as long as I can.

I lived in this building now for 2 years and although there's a few things I wish it had I love the location. They are doing some updates that I look forward to, including a new fitness center on our penthouse floor. I have a 16th floor east facing studio with a great balcony and city views. Located 3 blocks from my work I can't beat that commute. It's an old building so they are needing to replace things and usually 1 of the elevators is always down.

New owners Birge and Held have driven this place to the ground. On-site management is surly and uncommunicative. Not a place to live if you care about yourself - 3 homicides in three months, poor plumbing and HVAC.

You're not going to get air conditioning or heat because staff doesn't know how to maintain it.   Need to do laundry well it better be between the hours of 10 to 6.   Want to use the pool.   Nope closed on weekends.    Want to work out?   Not if you work normal hours.   This private equity firm that bought this place has to be worst management company ever.

I recently renewed my lease with Nichole one of the managers. She went above and beyond to assist me. It doesn't matter what I call or email her for she always has the best attitude and resolves any issues I have had. Previous management was not so good but they have made great changes to my apartment and the property. Thanks again Nichole for everything.

This is a really great area to live in and the staff here is amazing!! Nicole has been such a great help from the very start!!! They are very quick to respond & my studio is such a perfect size and space for me. love living here!
You don't want to live here. No heat for months. The hot tub hasn't worked in years. The pool is ice cold. Nobody cleans the poop from the dog park. Very low water pressure.

When I moved in it was pretty great and the old maintenance crew was nice too. Unfortunately they were bought out recently and this new management company is terrible!!!

I have a novel to write, but basically I’ve had ongoing issues with my hot water, the laundry machines are always breaking no matter which building you go to and you can only input money on a card to use them. This card can only be refilled with a machine that’s only located IN THE LOBBY - so when you want to do your laundry on a Sunday and the lobby is closed, sorry you’re out of luck if you don’t have enough money on your card already. Also the communication between the management office and the residents is kind of sad, they tell you some things, but will not tell you about work being done on your building - right next to your window, and if you pay for a parking space it’s pointless, cause they don’t tow them out of the parking space and they can’t even confirm you pay for unless they look you up. I can’t tell you how many times they’ve messed up my rent either because it’s been too often.

Just do yourself a favor and don’t waste your time.

I was all set to move in, or so I thought. I was approved, but when moving day came, I heard NOTHING from the leasing agent. I texted & called all day with NO response until finally she answered her phone at 5:30pm! With no news except that the lease I was supposed to sign was WRONG. She supposedly fixed it but turns out it was right to begin with. Then, I could not access the online lease to sign. She told me she would take her work phone home “to assist me,” since it was so late & I was supposed to move in that night. I did not move in, she did not “assist” me with accessing the lease to sign, and I continued to try & reach her, into the next day. NO RESPONSE until around 1pm, when she gaslit me, & lied to me, saying she “doesn’t answer her phone after business hours” even though she specifically told me she was taking it home to “assist me!” Absolutely ZERO accountability, and ZERO  instruction about how the whole process would go! At this point I was over it and no longer wanted to move in. Luckily I did not have to leave my current home right away. Others might not be so lucky & could end up spending tons of $ at hotels or end up homeless waiting for these yahoos!

Good community, clean interiors, safe neighborhood!  I like the size of my unit and the security of the mailroom.  I wish that they would install a drop box for rent checks for residents that are unable to drive to the leasing office.
I like it here a lot, the rent is affordable. There was a problem with package theft around the holidays, but I just got everything shipped to lockers elsewhere. Great neighborhood and neighbors!
The Jeffersons are pretty nice! There can be some changes like the carpet in the hallway but other than that they are nice. Rooms can get pretty warm in the summer so make sure you have a fan!
I’ve really enjoyed living here, it’s quiet and I can walk to several grocery stores and restaurants.  I like the gym and the leasing office is very responsive.
Nakesha helped me every step of the way getting me into the Jefferson. She helped me figure out my finance options to be approved. She made it very easy finding my new home.

Day 4 into a 1 year lease... no enforcement of masks in the entire building, not even the gym.  These same maskless people want to cram into an elevator with you.  Residents gather and congregate in the parking lot right below your window so good luck with quiet enjoyment or trying to get fresh air without opening your window to their conversations.  Residents blasting music 4 floors up that you can hear clear as day because it seems this is the land of inconsideration.  Leasing agents won't call back or reply via email once you are moved in, they did their work of promising things that turned out to be false and care less about your living conditions or right to quiet enjoyment and a safe environment.  Gonna be a fun 361 more days! Dont rent here, I already regret it.  They want to charge you 85/mo for reserved parking but guests and outsiders can park here for free with no issue.  Dont feel safe, feel conned, now stuck.  :(

Don't live here if you have a dog.  Management will say that you can't hear dogs barking through the units but you can hear them more clear than almost any other place I have lived.  If your dog barks at all, management will issue lease violation paperwork to you but never try to actual help with the situation(ie. let you know who is complaining so you can talk with them).  If you don't have a dog it may be alright but if you are sensitive to dogs barking I wouldn't suggest it.

If I could give this place negative stars, I would. I lived here for a full year and it was the worst decision I could have made. The staff is a complete joke. I literally don't understand what they get paid to do. The parking there is awful. The place is one big gossip fest. I felt like I was in high school again - everyone talks crap about everyone (even the staff) and parties like they are going absolutely nowhere with their lives. On a different note, the quality over everything in that place is complete crap. For being a new building and the prices they charge to live in a shoebox, you think they would have put a bit more thought into design. Please don't make the same mistake I did. This place literally messes with your life in a very negative way. I've lived in many different places and this was by far the worst experience I have ever had.

The monthly cost of rent listed is not what you end up paying- everything is add-on and not a true amenity. The pool, gym, and lounges are free to use, but you pay for the shared electric. Also, the apartments are not individually metered, so you have to be willing to pay an average sum and not for what you truly used, which I thought should have been included in the lease. Storage, parking, and laundry are additional as well. Nice building overall, but not quality. If you're looking for more than laminate flooring and IKEA shelving, keep looking. It's not worth the cost in my opinion.

I was so excited to see that the building was being converted to residents. I liked how the exterior finishes were progressing, and then one I was driving by and asked myself, "why are the blinds red, yellow and orange!" Very juvenile.

Aside from the friendly staff, there are not many positive things to say about this place. Within the six months I lived there, the water was shut off at least 4 times. They overcharge you for parking and for the space you are getting. Our living room/kitchen was smaller than my bedroom; how is that enough space for 3 people? Sink is small, dish washer is small, oven and stove are all small. They advertise blackout curtains but the curtains are not. We ran into multiple maintenance issues (AC multiple times, dish washer, sinks, toilets, etc.). Emails would constantly go unanswered, even when asking about important things like rent. Dog friendly building which I don’t mind but constant dog pee in the elevators or in the lobby. Laundry situation is a nightmare. I bought a drying rack because the dryers DO NOT WORK unless you dry your clothes for like 20 hours. The staff does their best to keep it a friendly place but the building itself is not worth it. Would not recommend.

Convenient location for DU students, walking distance to class, good price for what is included. Really cool patios and you can see downtown Denver and the mountains. Overall, would recommend!
Pros:
- Private bathrooms for each person
-AC!
-The staff is friendly and helpful and they give away free food at events
Cons:
-The kitchen has a dishwasher but it is a little bit small
-All of the furniture is included (bed, desk etc.) but you need to get lamps

I have lived here for going on 2 years and love it!!! The apartments are so affordable for this area of Denver and so spacious. The Vista staff has been especially helpful with any problem that may come up. Would definitely recommend!

I just renewed here for a third year in a row & I've really enjoyed it, ESPECIALLY since the new managing company took over. Before they came in, we did experience a irritatingly high number of water shut offs & the furniture was... not great. But literally everything changed for the better SO MUCH once they came in! First thing they did that was AWESOME was renovating all of the apartments & replacing all the old furniture. The couch I moved in to was honestly trash and was constantly flaking every time I sat down on it. The new one they brought in in August is sooooo much nicer, this large leather couch that is so much more comfortable to the point where I actually fall asleep on it fairly often. The stove is so much easier to clean cuz it's flat & electronic, the fridges are wayyy bigger & all the other new furniture is a lot sleeker and makes the place feel a lot fancier & nice. I especially LOVE the entertainment stand under the TV, it looks so nice & has tons of drawers to put stuff like my roommates' switch and it's perfect for having video game systems (which is great cuz I'm strongly considering getting a PS5)! In general, the entire living situation has improved since the new company took over too! I never went to resident events before they did cuz they were pretty infrequent & the ones the old management company hosted honestly just didn't sound very fun. But now, I've been to a ton of them & I've honestly had a blast at every single one. The Halloween party & opening week grocery bingo were highlights for sure, & the Brunch event last week was also so fun (who doesn't want to drink a free mimosa at 10AM lol)! The team at the front desk are super helpful & seem to really care about the residents' well-being. The maintenance guys are also awesome & the few times I've needed a repair in the apartment, they fixed whatever needed fixing within 48 hours of me submitting the work order. Overall, I'm kind of surprised to see how many negative reviews I've seen for Vista cuz it's gotten soooo much better since I started living here in 2022. Highly recommend living here!

I absolutely love living at Vista. As someone who moved from a different state, I can say that the support from the team is truly admirable. They have been extremely helpful and have gone above and beyond for me. One other thing that I love is how they did renovations over the summer! The brand new furniture, appliances, and countertops are SO nice, and I genuinely think I couldn't have found a better apartment.

Do not move here unless you want to be sick. This property has a serious toxic mold problem, which management is well aware of but has failed to take proper action to remediate. My roommate was delayed 3 days from moving in September, 2016 because wet carpeting needed to be replaced. Towards the end of our lease (June) she noticed mold growing back on her carpet, causing her to live with her boufriend, while I separately submitted 3 service requests for a leaking vent in the living room, right next to the wall of her bedroom where the mold was growing. Management told her that it was a larger plumbing issue that would be too expensive to repair for one unit, and waited until she moved out to replace the carpet and cover the underlying health risks for the new tenants. Meanwhile maintenance was saying that my service requests were being completed even though absolutely nothing was being done. The last couple of months living in the unit I started experiencing respiratory and cognitive issues that subsided within a week of moving out. I would have given the complex a wonderful review if this wilful indifference to tenants health did not come to light, but people (primarily students) need to know what they're signing up for when they move in.

Buildings 1 & 2 are filthy and very often have squatters in the basement parking garage & stairwells. Wouldn't be a massive issue except they rarely ever thoroughly clean the shared spaces (unless it's a space on their tour routes, then it's immaculate).
The staff are nice and helpful, but getting a hold of one of them is like pulling teeth unless you have time to physically walk into the office. Their phones ring exactly one time before sending you to voicemail so I'm convinced they just auto-reject all calls. I have NEVER gotten an answer when I call the office. Not once. 
The surface lot is comically dangerous. Even ignoring the potholes and constant broken glass strewn about, I have witnessed 2 hand offs and been "solicited" to once in front of my building.

I want to like this place but there are far too many egregious issues that I cannot look past. I hope the new management company can get a grip on things around here, but it seems like they care even less than the previous owners.
The staff is great everyone is always friendly, really great apartments to live in there's a lot of space and having 2 patios is great.

This property was bought out and they are trying to make it better but the tenants make this horrible. Poop on the ground, trash, not in a safe area. Homeless live next door, drug addicts wandering the parking lot at night, utilities are $150 which is absurd for an apartment. Amenities are only open during office hours so if you have a regular job you won't be able to use them. Police are regulars accompanied by fire department and ambulances. This is an absolute last resort place to live.

The negative reviews are correct. Upon first sight online we fell in love with this apartment and the amenities it had "seemed" to offer. Long story short we are not dirty people but have had, a rat in our home, cigarettes thrown on our balcony, a Tennant spit on our dog from our balcony, and have heard horror story from other tenants about poop being thrown onto their balconies and even into their homes. maintenence is a joke they pay people to smoke cigarettes on the clock. The janitor is not good at cleaning, and tenants constantly tear stuff up. Not to mention that nice shiny pool was barely open and all amenities are closed after buisness hours so hard working people like myself pay for; but cannot even enjoy them. We are not renewing our lease and would not recommend to anyone unless you were very limited in budget to live here. You get what you pay for this is a place I'd move to if I lost my job or something. other than that. absolutely not fo not do it. They do not care about you its a money hungry company. period.
Cockroaches are everywhere and you get charged so high for “utilities” even though you pay excel separately

New management poorly manages. I’ve lived in these apartments for three years and recently they switched management companies. The place is filthy all the time. They’re already overpriced as it is. But if you are one day past the third with your rent no matter what the circumstances are emergency or not they begin charging you $75 and then $10 a day after that. Which can quickly add up. So not only are you over paying for rent you’re also overpaying service fees for a service you don’t get.The only perk I can say about this place is that they’re very flexible about having pets. But they do nothing to maintain the way the pets are cared for.
I had a wonderful experience to moving in Park 17! Jeffrey and Janine provided reliable and efficient service. The team is knowledgeable, friendly!

I've lived here for three years and have loved it... until they started allowing the amenities to be reserved. Now, the grill and community space are frequently unavailable on the weekends... with no communication to residents beside a paper on the door!! I hope this gets solved, especially as we go toward summer. Right now it feels like paying extra for things we don't get to use.
Love Park 17 staff and maintenance. They are always friendly and attentive.

From day one, the staff at Park 17 has been responsive and friendly. I recently put in a maintenance request and the team resolved the issue in under 24 hours. I continue to be impressed with how well this team takes care of their tenants.

We chose Park 17 for it's walkability to many of our favorite restaurants and City Park. The property management team goes above and beyond to make living here as convenient as possible! We love the pool and the residents are all very friendly and courteous. Highly recommend!

I lived here for about a year, and here are the following problems that lie. First there are bedbugs in every unit and even though they try to handle it it doesn’t get taken care of. Maintenance is extremely slow. The apartments are very outdated. And when it comes to people at the front desk a very rude and extremely disrespectful and they don’t answer anyone’s complaints or concerns. Even though the price is cheap it’s not worth it.

Bed bugs, Roaches and Mice all the time. If something breaks dont ever expect it to be fixed. Called to get a new dishwasher its been 7 years still broken. Called for a new refrigerator i had to get one on my own. Needed the sink fixed took 1 year of calling. Also they spray every month so you have to remove everything out of your pantries ect and then put them all back again that just sucks dont waste you time coming here it just sucks.

This is the first apartment that I've lived in, and the experience is incomparable. Michelle and her team do a marvelous job at every turn. They are friendly, kind, and personable, even when I bug them right before closing. Maintenance requests are taken care of the next day (even for smaller issues), and the public areas in the apartment complex are kept very clean (including snow being removed from sidewalks). They are also very transparent about rent/billing each month, providing a clear breakdown of expenses (which is nice for those of us that are a tad more OCD).

The thing I love most is the community events that Michelle and her team host. These include summer pool parties, trunk-or-treats, free "burritos on the way to work" day, and lots of others.

The apartments are very well maintained, with updated appliances, clean flooring (both un-scratched hardwood and brand new looking carpets), and good size storage closet on the balcony (which is incredibly rare and handy). The location is also key. There is a Costco on the other side of the street (~2-minute walk), as well as a Safeway (with very low gas prices), Target (with CVS Pharmacy), and a King Soopers. There are also a lot of restaurants close by like Red Robin, Applebees, Olive Garden, and Buffalo Wild Wings.

I can not praise Apres enough. If I were able to give more than a 5-star rating, I would. Thanks, Michelle and team! Y'all have been great!

Maintenance does a great job dealing with big and small issues, the office staff is friendly and attentive, and the property management company is working to improve the property. We’ve seen new paint, the clubhouse open, and other projects being worked on throughout the community which is awesome.

When I first moved in, the sound proofing seemed pretty well done – or maybe I just lived next to less noisy people at the time – over the years, it seems as if the sound proofing isn’t as good as it used to be. I just wish Valet Trash was an optional service since it’s easy to toss my trash into the dumpster when necessary.

I’d recommend Apres to those looking for a decent apartment in the good part of Aurora.

Close to Belmar, Sloans lake, and Lamar station, this apartment complex is perfect for someone who likes going out. The ease of access to downtown is great and there is plenty of shopping nearby. I have lived here 3 years now. The manager is very dedicated to her work not just in the office also outside by helping with grounds. The leasing staff are very knowledgeable. Maintenance is the greatest. They are on top of it when it comes to work orders and up keeping of the whole property no matter what season it is. I would recommend living here to anyone, the amenities are well kept up and very clean.

The Team: everyone is friendly, helpful, knowledgeable, and will work tirelessly to ensure your experience is excellent. 

The location: The W Line to Union Station is a 2 minute walk from the building. It takes no time at all to get downtown. For a person who used public transit for the past 4 years on the East coast, I love being able to continue that method of commuting. 

The building: The photos don't do it justice. The common spaces are beautiful, well designed, and easily accessible. I love hosting gatherings with friends here b/c there are a lot of places for us to gather. The individual units are beautiful as well. Spacious kitchens, wood floors, lots of natural light, in-unit laundry, and massive closets. It's rare you get all of those in one unit at a reasonable price and West Line nails it. 
Dog Friendly: There is a massive place for pets to play in the back of the property. It's great to find companions for my dog without having to travel to a dog park. There is a place for her, right on site. 

I've been really happy with my relocation and a large part of that has to do with my beautiful new home. I would recommend this location to anyone looking to move here.

The apartment itself is nice enough, everything is new and the people in the office are nice and helpful. It's quiet and in a lovely residential neighborhood.  My neighbors are fantastic. Rent is great (much lower than other places in the same area).  In other words - I love it!

Do yourself a favor and live in a place where the ownership and management are reasonable and treat you like a person, not income.
just dirty and unsafe all around. Things are always broken too.
