I've complained and they send the exterminator every week, and I still have them. I do not believe for a second that I am the only one complaining, but the management won't say.(i have asked, and I get the runaround for a straight answer.
What you get for the price here is really great. So many amenities both within the apartment and around it. Johana in the front office is very nice and professional. Gated parking is a big plus.

I've lived here for nine years. They've been through three separate property management companies since. In that time, they've lost my pet immunization paperwork, they've "forgotten" that my garage was linked to my apartment (so they left it open, with thousands of dollars of motorcycles inside). I wake up to people sleeping in the hallways. The "secured" doors don't work. Stay away. I'm only here because I can't afford to move.

What is good about this apartments is the nice location that is within walking distance of restaurents, shop, and Walmart!
Also,you are 1-2minutes walking distance from the RTD light rail.
The apartments are good and the service is great, what more can you ask for!

Upon my first visit to Artwalk at CityCenter, there were many features that I loved about the property. Specifically, the location to the rail station, the surround economic development area, and the amenities. Even though I was only shown a one-bedroom unit, I made an appointment to come back with my roommate on Saturday at 9:30 AM to show him the property and for us to sign a lease. We were ten minutes late, but when we arrived, the office was closed. 

While waiting for the office to open, I walked around the property. Many of the balconies were being used as storage. In fact, one balcony was full of cardboard boxes. 

When the office opened at 10:00 AM, there was one leasing agent working with a couple. We were waiting, and the leasing agent with whom we were to meet was showing another couple around, so we were asked to wait. We did wait for about ten minutes, but we had another appointment, so we left. The agent sent me an email three hours later to apologize and invite me back, but this lack of service was a good indicator to me about how I would be treated as a resident. We did sign a lease that day, but at another property.

The apartment are just okay, old appliance, saw lots of water damage and broken tiles. Hallways were dirty. For the same amount of money you can get something much much better. The only good thing about them are they are close to the light rail and walking distance to other shops.

I went by to view a unit that I had made an appointment for  and the young lady in the office who I was meeting told me she was too swamped with paper work to show the unit. She told me another associate would show it to me when she finished meeting with a tenant. After about 15 minutes of waiting while the lady who was too "swamped" was chatting to her coworker when she saw me about to walk out. She decided she had time to show the unit. We took a look at it and I picked up an application. When I had it filled out she said actually that unit is already taken I have another one for 100$ more. I won't be renting here.
These apartments have the best amenities and the location is prime. For someone who hates traffic or driving at all, these apartments provide all you need and more.
These apartments are located in the center of everything you could need. With everything within walking distance, driving becomes a thing of the past.

Alexan, is a great but not fantastic place. Approximately 10 miles outside of the City of Denver. The complex building is located right next a light rail stop making commute easy and accessible for those that don't own a car. Also neighboring with a Walmart, Ross,and  among other shops and restaurants. 
However, they present some con's as well. Unfortunately, the  neighborhood is very dark at night and harbors many junkies, making the walk around the community at night feel very unsafe. The leasing department promotes a gated community, but unfortunately that is not the case. As the apartment building is very easy to access from the outside and I have even witnessed the junkies from off the street wandering the halls inside the apartment building.  
Another concern living here, are the disgusting smells of urine and other feces along the hallways( very disturbing for a place priced at 1300$ p/m).

Have lived here for two years and love not only the complex but the location. I am right next to shopping for food, saloons, shops and the amazing downtown Englewood even including gyms and restaurants. Not to forget the RTD with in a block distance which provides access to the amazing downtown and surrounding areas of the denver area. Will live here for many years very happy..
Our apartment was newly remodeled when we moved in, so it is really nice inside. The outside could use a facelift. Great location though and nice amenities.

Living at The Stapleton has been a good experience. The location is super convenient, with easy access to shops, restaurants, and downtown. The apartments are updated and comfortable, and the management team is helpful when needed. No issues so far!

I have only been here a week now and it's been a great move. Office staff was informative and helpful, they let drink up their coffee everytime I came into office.

Apartment is great plenty of natural light for me coming in through the windows.
Laundry room had some machines out but submitted work orders in app and a few days later all were fixed. 
Security code to get into the building.Great locker to hold your packages. I feel right at home here.

I want to let German know that I really appreciate the work he did for me in my apartment. He was professional, efficient, considerate, respectful. He provided the exact work that needed to be done; and did it very well. Thank you, so very much German. You are an asset to your employer and the residents. Sincerely, M. Hames

they manage a different property that doesnt have staff on site but they host events and stuff here that we can come to and are always nice.  theres always raffles and food and holiday decorations.  friendly staff
I am very comfortable living in this property, very happy with the attention, they are always aware of everything we need so much in the offices maintenance.

Stefany who works at The Stapleton leasing office is the best, and The Stapleton gave me a thoughtful welcome on my move-in day, like a fancy hotel. I was welcomed on my move-in day with an outdoor mat that displays "Welcome" outside my unit, new essential items that came complimentary with the unit like toilet papers, towel paper, soap bars, kitchen items and Clorox to-go disinfecting wipes which were decorated with origami designs and in a housewarming goodie bag! I was told multiple times that if I need anything (to a reasonable extent of course), maintenance is a call away 24/7 and is included in the fixed monthly utilities which is super low. I love that everything in the unit was cleaned right before my move-in date and that even after I spot checked, I could not find any dirt or grime. My studio comes with 2 closets and one of them is a really big walk-in closet. The Stapleton has got ample parking in their 3 parking lots that are free to residents.

There are also free breakfast with lots of options and free lunch during the week at The Stapleton where you would be notified via text message at least a day ahead of time. The staff are really nice and chill. 

The building where my unit is has a private courtyard with trees and a gate, so I feel safe going outside to our courtyard where non-residents cannot trespass our gate and tall fence.

Had My vehicle vandalized and attempted to be stolen twice and all of my tools and property stolen from on the third time just this week.   I can't wait to move. The amenities here are not worth the crime You will subject yourself to. My multiple neighbors have vehicles broken into, doors drilled out, windows smashed out, etc.  The management company here Wastes your money on a security camera system they say protects you but never provides any evidence, brand new cameras that can't see people or license plates. So even the police say it's insufficient. They waste money on a security company to patrol that's never around when they are needed. Beautiful community and beautiful amenities but truly no security and no accountability.

Really like it here I’ve lived here for 4 years. Easy access to i70 and close to rhino/downtown. They have free beer daily  and a lot of events. The leasing agent Victoria is great. I haven’t had any problems while living here. The free detached single garage is a huge plus.

DO NOT RENT HERE. Got this place based on good review but was very disappointed. Lived here for 7 months. All the neighbors said the same thing about this place when moving out so I'm writing this review on behalf of more then just me. You basically pay rent for a place where strangers can come and go as they please when you aren't home. Maintenance came into our apartment unannounced while we weren't home and left a mess in the kitchen. When asked why they came and what they were doing and why we didn't even know about it, they said they "forgot" to call us. Also, they tell you they will give you the full deposit back but forget to mention that even if you leave it in perfect condition there is an "automatic cleaning charge and other fees". They also charge you for pre-existing problems even if it was noted when moving in. You will NEVER get your full deposit back. (Below review said the same thing) Management is very hard to get a hold of, voicemail doesn't work, if you catch them in person you MAY have some luck. Maintenance never response. People in the apartments across the street come use the pool as they please (regardless of the key pass). Also, parking is HORRIBLE even if you have a pass its always packed. I would not recommend this place.

So disappointed with this place. The service is horrible (Scott and David).They lie to you just to get you in and then they are never available for you.
Bunch of hidden fees. My utility bill is ridiculously high(and it's not electricity or gas)- they make you pay for common electricity areas usage when part of the areas closes at 6:00PM. 
The place is fairly new but it already falls apart. I can't wait to move out. Almost there. Never again!!!!

I really wanted to live downtown, but the cost was way over what I could pay.  I found this place a little over a year ago and I couldn't be happier.  From the day I moved in I have been treated like I am the only one that lives here.  The staff has been more like family than just money hungry landlords.  It is super pet friendly and treat my baby just like a resident.  On busy days I have to avoid going anywhere near the clubhouse because Charlie will not let me walk by without stopping in to see Scott.  He always has treats and gives so much love to her that sometimes I think she loves him more than me.  If you're looking for a place you should diffidently check this place out.

First, let me tell you about the property managers; they are very friendly, professional and helpful. The way they take care of your concerns and issues is like they care for you personally. The maintenance crew are wonderful. They gets things done FAST! I'm also noticing that anybody I've come to contact with (neighbors) they've been friendly. Even the dogs who live here are friendly :).  Being close to Denver's Zoo and a beautiful gulf course adds additional attractions to this community.

I would absolutely recommend AGAINST living at the Wilmark Apartments. I have lived in various apartments throughout Denver for 8 years and have never had such a HORRIBLE experience such as living here. 

I would like to acknowledge that it is not the management and maintenance team that made this place such an awful experience, as they are very receptive, but the infrastructure of the building itself, which cannot be changed.

Here is why I would highly advise you DO NOT MOVE HERE:

-The AC unit is in the main living room. Due to the layout of the unit, NO cold air ever reaches the bedroom, even when the AC unit is left on all day and night. I literally sit and sweat in bed in the summer months.

-The only heating mechanism is produced through radiators within each apartment. These are controlled by the building and not each individual unit- so you have no control over how hot or cold it gets. In my experience, the radiators blasted heat all day long (From Nov-May) so I would constantly get home to a 90 degree unit. It was pretty unbearable. Opening the windows would only bring in extremely cold air, so there was no happy medium to get a normal level of heat in the unit. Additionally, the radiators seems to produce less heat early in the morning so I would wake up to a cold apartment. 

-My biggest complaint is the EXTREMELY POOR INSULATION between units. I was able to hear every step, cupboard or drawer open, dog jump, drop of an item, conversation, etc of my neighbors above me. I have never in my life experienced such poor flooring in an apartment. I was woken up at 6am every day to my neighbors walking around, their dogs walking around, and them shutting doors, etc. The insulation is so bad, you can hear the front door of the building close every time someone enters.

-Not only was I able to hear the neighbors above me, the HORRIBLE INSULATION also caused the neighbors below me to complain. Even to the extent that my vacuuming was aggressive. I understand communal living arrangements, but there is no way to avoid the EXTREMELY THIN WALLS  of this building, so everyone has a bad experience. 

-The laundry machines do not wash close properly and leave dirt and stains on clothes when washed. I’ve had to take my laundry elsewhere to get a clean wash.

The apartment looks nice and the price is enticing but the building is old and continues to fail on the most basic of needs. 

1) the wiring for the internet is completely shot
2) i feel comfortable saying there is pretty much no heat outside of space heaters
3) the space heaters that you need for heat also happen to trip fuses every other day causing your power to go out. 
4) have had a mouse problem since we moved kn
Ultimately I would encourage you to heed this advice. Prior to moving in i saw maybe a couple of negative reviews and thought “they must have had a uniquely bad experience, that won’t be representative of my time there” i was wrong. none of these complaints are exaggerated.

This is an OLD building and you will realize it quickly. 
- After only a few months, the roof leaked and resulted in severe water damage to my bedroom. I slept on the couch for 2 weeks while it was repaired, and had to call  twice to ask when they would be fixing it (told me 3 days).
- There is one washer and one dryer in the basement "laundry room" which looks like a trash room and they are very old.
- Toilet broke and they had to remove and reinstall the entire thing.
- Wiring is so old that your internet connection will black out frequently.
- The building (especially if you're on the top floor) is super hot in the summer. I bought two window and floor air conditioners and they did nothing. The ceiling fans do nothing. In the winter, you have to request that your heat be turned off or it is unbearably hot.

Long story short- move into any of the apartment complexes around here that give you a gym, pool, hot tub, actual laundry room, and all the amenities for the same price.
I've seen a handful of car break ins, packages being stolen, and multiple maintenance issues. The gates hardly work and the Management only see you as a dollar sign.

The garage door is constantly broken, which opens up the whole building to safety issues. Packages get stolen all the time. The units are not well maintained or checked between residents so I have a maintenance issue almost every week. If the issue is something that will take some time to fix, you get almost no communication from the leasing office or maintenance team. They will knock on your door as early as 7 AM, and come anytime unannounced during the day. They also undertook a major construction project this spring, this type of construction usually warrants a construction discount. With so many people working from home they gave us barely any notice in advance to make other arrangements. Overall I’ve been very unhappy living here and am counting down the days until my lease ends. The management company is truly terrible even though I’ve reached out many times
A great location, close to bus lines and downtown. The hardwood floors aren't fancy, but are easy to maintain. It's a great basic apartment for a decent price!

I love my place, however, the rental property managers continue to raise the rent every year and my pay doesn't increase with the raise in rent in Denver. I love Denver, I love the mountains and the metaphysical fairs.

My concern is that the building manager says he can only do so much to change the circumstances. My cool part about my place is that it is tiled throughout and very easy to keep clean. I also love that everything is within walking distance, as north capitol hill is a very popular place to live. 

Anyway, I wish landlords would consider how hard it has become to be single in Denver, as far as affordable living is concerned. Since mary jane has been legalized, rents have gone sky high. What's an ordinary Missouri transplant to do?

We recently relo'd from Chicago and have found the Bromwell to be all it's cracked up to be. Great location for walking to the Cherry Creek Trail, restaurants, grocery stores and more.  Responsive staff, easy move in and in-unit amenities excellent.  Scenic rooftop and pool make it complete.  Glad we found the Bromwell.

We moved into the Bromwell about a month ago and it's been the most wonderful experience! From the initial tour, to the move in process, getting settled and living here since - it's been seamless. Everyone who works here is so friendly and helpful and really makes this place feel like a community, even during these weird and distant times.

My boyfriend and I moved in to Bromwell in September of 2020 right after the building construction was completed. Our expectations of not only the property, the amenities and the service have been beyond exceeded. We were worried about the public spaces with covid but the property management team has done a great job enforcing covid protocols with a amenity reservation system. When we were moving back to Denver we looked at a lot of new buildings in the area and are incredibly happy with our decision to move into Bromwell.

This place is an ongoing disaster. 

The good: Beautiful property, some friendly and helpful staff

The bad: Living here day-to-day is awful. The building was opened in September and NOT complete or up to code. It is a nightmare for residents who have the pleasure of paying thousands of dollars for no consistent hot water, daily/weekly construction, flooding, massive construction issues and projects. security issues, amenities that have been closed multiple times in less than three months, etc. Literally every week there is a massive issue within the unit and usually the property itself. They are struggling to rent these units and it’s no surprise why. The incompetence of how this property opened despite so many flaws is actually impressive. 

Steer clear. This has been the worst living experience of my life.

I have lived here 2 years at this point. Management has switched 3 times in those two years. The pool was never open (or clean), until this summer. The fireplace is not able to be utilized. The apartments are not “updated” as listed on the website. Paint is always peeling, doors are often broken. The trash dumpsters are always overflowing. Not to mention, since we got bought out by Four Star Realty, it is impossible to get the office/management on the phone. I do not recommend.

Very disappointed, once management switched the place has gone down hill.  Property management is never available even though she lives on the property.   They pick and chose what they want to enforce in the lease and have a very unprofessional attitude.

These apartments were newly renovated in 2015 with nice features and appliances. The community is small and the neighborhood is quiet. Any service requests I've submitted (all minor) have been dealt with quickly, and the online system to pay rent and submit service requests is great. They put in a gas grill and table outside in the common area, which is awesome! My only complaint is that the community manager is not very responsive to emails and they have yet to install a bike rack on the property. But overall my experience has been great and I love my apartment!

I just recently moved into Nuvo, and have been really pleased with the experience. The management staff, especially Cole, has been very responsive and has taken care of all my needs in my new home. Great experience.

I have never written a review for anything in my life. This apartment has been so bad that I had to. It is an unsafe and neglectful place to live. My mental health has never been worse thanks to the neglects that I will get into later. I read the reviews about this apartment before renting. I remember thinking "I'm sure it can't be that bad, everyone is always upset with property managers." Do not make the same mistake I did. I have lived in 7 different buildings, this isn't even comparable to a real building and by a long shot. It is unlivable and management repeatedly ignored safety concerns that I have brought to their attention.

Here are some details.

As other people have said, we were given less than one day's notice to remove our balcony furniture. Management wanted to paint the exterior. So they taped ALL our windows. The entire apartment was almost completely dark. This email said that the painting process would last "a few days," which even then, feels unreasonable to not see out of your windows. This paint process lasted 6 weeks. And management never once told us this. No timeline, no updates, no nothing. I emailed and called repeatedly until someone finally answered. This was after a few days. She said "we are not sure, it could take weeks." 6 weeks later the paint job was not finished. I had LOST my mind by then from not being able to see out. So I tore down the covers. Management still has not sent an email regarding the paint job. Meaning the tapes could still be up today, 5 months later.

In October, we spent three weeks in 45 degree temperatures with no heat. Management was completely unresponsive and again, after great effort, when I contacted them, they gave vague answers that frankly gaslit my experience. They told me it wasn't cold enough. When the truth was that they were late to get on the HVAC schedule. This was confirmed by a property manager.

My smoke detector stopped working in November. I filed for a work order immediately. The work order was not filled until February. For a smoke detector. Additionally, at some point in January, someone entered our apartment and took it. With no notice, follow-up, or a replacement.

These are a few examples. There are more that other folks have written about.

You don't have to believe me. I did believe the reviews that I had read. I hope you do because I genuinely wouldn't wish this experience on anyone. Wishing you all the best of luck with your apartment search.

New management that has taken over is AWFUL. Chose to paint the building with ONE DAY heads up (go get your furniture! We’re not responsible if it gets painted) chose to “update” fixtures in the hallway making it look ghetto. Maintenance requests were ignored at least one month (were looking to hire someone!) laundry unit (2 out of 6 dryers) broken and completely ignored for MONTHS (up to the residents to contact third party company!) completely ignored elevators being down- At one of two elevators broken at one time for an on going 2 months. (It’s because residents have a bad distribution of weight!) WHAT????? You can’t run a building and it’s OUR fault??? But wait, there’s more! There’s a door on the side of the building that DOESNT CLOSE. It’s broken which means anyone could wonder up and walk into this building. And the most recent fun- threatening that ANY dog owner will be fined $50 for EVERY bag left on the property. So if there’s 5 bags from other people left outside… every dog owner gets $250 fine.
Honorable mention of complaints- hot water turned off, no credit was given. HVAC heat was delayed turning on and apartments were freezing for weeks. Basement parking flooded, “come identify your vehicle and none of this is our fault”. Mind you- garage door has been faulty and broken on and off entire time I’ve lived here. Oh yeah, and they don’t give a crap about maintaining parking lot. Completely iced over after it snows. No salt no anything. Hope you own a winter car. UNACCEPTABLE. DO NOT RENT FROM THESE CHEAP PEOPLE.

Just a couple of weeks in and couldn’t be happier. Responsive property manager, easy self guided tour. Friendly and quiet neighbors. Great bars and restaurants nearby. Bonus Toast and Roast has the best breakfast burritos and right next store. It’s city life but the 24 hour surveillance makes me feel safe. I had somethings that needed assessing in my unit. Resolved in less than 24 hours thanks to Tony. Harrison helped my friend can get access when I was out of town and expecting a big delivery. It’s easy living and my newly renovated unit is beautiful.

was one of the first people to move in here. had 2 br on 2nd floor. upstairs neighbor was quiet. things were fine.
moved to 1 br on 4th floor... it was a nightmare. the insulation and noise reduction products are non-existent. upstairs neighbor constantly stomped when heard noise from me or the apt above him. I didn't realize how bad things were until my quiet downstairs neighbor sneezed and it was so loud that I thought he was in my bedroom. I had to move, my health was so greatly affected. also the water/sewer and electric bills are on one bill and it is divided up amongst all renters and the building. this increased every month and by. the time I moved it was outrageous. 
new owners now, and they may be more receptive but they can't fix the noise problem.  for your own sanity don't move here.   sorry new owners but I don't want others to suffer like I did.

16 Penn Apartments has been a great home for me. Julie was super helpful on tour and gave me exactly what I was looking for. The location is great and the apartments are nicely renovated. I'm very excited about the new renovations that will be coming this fall. I will be recommending these apartments and the team to my friends and family.

As a person over 55, I feel I am "in between" Too old to be young and too young to be old! I love that some of the apartments at 16 Penn can be rented to those under 55 because having younger people around helps me feel young too. This apartment community is very well run with attentive management and fun social activities too. Great location to walk to dinner, or to the fun boutiques and stores nearby.  Top marks.

Not a true 55+!  They cant lease it up so now they are now letting under 55 in!  Noisy if you live on a lower floor it sounds like the upstairs neighbor is going to fall through the floor.

Should be zero stars!

Security non existent.  Homeless in all parts of the building, always in the main entry way.  The urinate right by the front door!

You can do much better for a better price at other communities that are minutes away.  Notice the trend , after every bad review there are 3 good reviews that show up....hmmmm.

For starters, 16 Penn is not for everyone, meaning you or one of the residents with whom you reside must be 55 years of age. This was one of the biggest draws for me. I may sound like a curmudgeon, but where I currently live, the residents aren't respectful of their neighbors. Their dogs bark constantly, they leave dog waste all over the property, they leave trash out in the common areas and hallways, and park wherever they want.

16 Penn has none of that. The residents are so respectful of each other. The common areas are nice. You have 24/7 secure package pick-up. The parking area is gated as is the property.

Elanna B., Property Manager, was so nice, knowledgeable and respectful. As she was giving us a tour of the property, she was also giving us some background on the company's owners. You could tell she was proud of both the company as well as the community.

As for the two-bedroom, it was amazing! Huge open spaces, lots of windows, and a big balcony. Granted, the view is of the city, but it was nice.

16 Penn ranked high first on the "move-in list" for the longest time, but we opted for a property that had a slightly bigger floor plan. But trust me. If you are looking on behalf of yourself or a loved one who is 55 , please go look at 16 Penn. You won't be disappointed.
This apartment is great! Everything is renovated so I'm the first person to use everything. My neighbors are quiet, and it's in a super walkable location. I love living here.

Pros:
Parking was somewhat ample
Close ish to everything I needed

Cons:
- As soon as I moved in I saw roaches. There are still few bouts of roaches til this day
- 2 days after moving in the bath tub flooded with water from upstairs
- there will be a lot of issues related to units upstairs (plumbing) or the adjacent units (roaches)
- the toilet seat was literally broken so had to buy a new one
- the AC was supposed to be fix supposedly a week after moving in. Didn’t have that until about a month and a half (I moved in during summer)
- the management is literally offline on the weekends so they gave us this number for emergencies, but it’s to a call center so when I had a drainage emergency over the weekend, not only did I not have anyone to contact, but the call center which I called multiple (8 times) did not “have any recollection” of the calls I made. The floor was flooded for the entire weekend
- their maintenance line is literally a call to a call center, not the maintenance team.
- Heat and Hot water will be sporadically available. The fun is not knowing when your water will be freezing cold.
- paper thin walls and ceiling, you will hear everything
- paper thin walls made worse by noisy neighbors with kids (oh yes there are a lot of kids here) who are either constantly stomping on the floor, running up and down the stairs, or hitting the doors/mailboxes
- oh yes, the very loud fights too!
- if you live on the unit closest to Monaco the street, chances of you waking up to loud traffic noises is very high
- the hallways smell awful
- (because of the kids) there are trash almost everywhere
- you’re also likely to run into dog poop. It’s kinda like living on a dog park actually
- the water from “the drain” leaks directly onto my balcony/patio area and when I asked the manger if they can do something about it and the basic answer was a ‘no’

It’s an awful, smelly, decrepit little place. It’s “cheap” but honestly you get what you paid for. The staff (of which there are 2 I think) is nice, and I sometimes feel for them having to take care of/manage a run-down storage unit on a dog park, but then I remember that I’m paying to live here; it just makes me more angry at myself for not researching the apartment beforehand.

tl;dr Don’t waste your money here. Waste your money on an actual livable apartment complex.

Mice and bed bug infested. If that isn’t enough to keep you away the rude staff and maintenance don’t fix anything they rather receive fees then cover up holes made by mice. Id go down to the laundry room and find homeless men sleeping inside the laundry room. I would urge you to stay away from this place. 


Sincerely an ex tenant

NO HEAT AND NO CABLE!!! No Working Heat OR Cable Connection to Comcast! And they are charging me for NOT HAVING HEAT! AND REFUSE TO FIX THE CABLE! I AM EXPECTED TO PAY COMCAST TO HAVE IT INSTALLED IN A PROPERTY I DON'T OWN! They want me to pay $200 because of - I am not kidding - "Multiple Calls of No Heat" - because it's my fault their apartment heat system doesn't work in NOVEMBER and their HVAC guys SAID IT WAS FIXED WHEN IT WASN'T! It's just getting colder and I'm to pay them for not providing a basic human need? . 

On top of that - NO COMCAST CONNECTION! Cockroaches, big ones. A maintenance crew WAY TOO THINLY SPREAD to actually fix anything, I still have NO HEAT AFTER THREE MONTHS. There is no Storage as there are constant break ins, same with laundry. None of the apartments are as nice as mine as they ran out of money, my neighbor had to wait three months to get his dishwasher.

Well at first I wanted to just give one star but seems like they have been putting an effort to making this place better they do have an on going bed bug problem but they have new management and maintenance so things are very slowly getting better. Tip if your looking for a quiet place don’t rent here there’s lots of families with kids and you’ll hear all the movement from above below and next door

I live at the Wesley Apts for the past two years. During my stay here I have had no problems with maintenance or leasing personnel. They keep the property clean and do their best to keep tenants happy.
The Wesley are nice being upgraded and a friendly community for dogs & kids!

I am compelled to share my disappointing experience living at 1880 Little Raven, a Holland Residential property, highlighting ongoing issues that have significantly impacted the quality of life for its residents.

For the past four months, one of the two elevators has been out of service, with no clear timeline for repairs. The remaining elevator has also faced frequent breakdowns, leaving the 9-story building without a functioning elevator on multiple occasions. Additionally, the parking garage has experienced flooding, forcing tenants to navigate through water to access their vehicles. Persistent leaks from both the ground sewage and roof have added to the unsatisfactory conditions in the garage.

Regrettably, the management's response has been less than satisfactory. Despite these challenges, they have not provided any compensation, such as discounted rent or early move-out options free of charge. It's disheartening to see a lack of urgency and accountability in addressing these issues.

Potential renters should be aware of these challenges before considering 1880 Little Raven, or any Holland Residential property, as their residence. The current state of affairs reflects a lack of responsiveness to residents' concerns and an overall failure to provide a comfortable living environment.

My partner and I have lived here for just about a year. The management changed it over to Sarah and Jeanette in November and we truly notice a difference. From the small touches of having candy and dog treats in the lobby to the larger efforts of ensuring maintenance and trash services run smoothly we can tell the difference. We are so happy to resign our lease for another year!

My apartment at 1880 Little Raven was one of the best decisions that I have made living in Denver. The staff are attentive and great at planning events. I would highly recommend 1880 Little Raven. Thanks Madison and Julie!

I have never had such a great experience at an apartment complex. The landlords were always helpful and timely. I highly recommend living here!

Here's the catch: if you fail to collect your dog's waste (even accidentally) you will be slammed with a no-warning, even first time, $200 fine. The gated area is a good size, so your dog could wander out of site for a moment as you look away or talk to your neighbors. Or perhaps you pick up a pile thinking it was your dog's when it was in fact another's and you missed picking up your dog's. Or in the area covered in wood chips and hidden shrubs where it is hard to see, you will still be fined. It is mentioned only in the lease among 2,000 other things you are meant to remember. $200. Every. Time. No warning, no lower amounts. When I asked the apartments why the fine is so high, I was told it "has to be enough to cover the costs of the DNA tests." When I called the management company to try and plead for a break, my calls went unreturned. So now, even though I love living here, I have to consider breaking my lease because like most Colorado residents, I don't have $200 to spare. Furthermore, I find myself shying away from using the amenities I came here for because I have no idea how I missed it last time and am terrified if I don't keep my guy on a tight leash at all times, I will be charged again. 
Don't get me wrong, you should move here. You may even get my great apartment close to the dog park. And you will make a ton of new friends with the incredible residents, one of which actually works in the office! But beware, CLOSELY WATCH YOUR DOG AT ALL TIME OR YOU WILL BE CHARGED $200 FOR EVERY SINGLE MISSED WASTE, even in snow, even when they are out of provided bags, even if you pick up after any other dogs. Unfortunately this one flaw is big enough to smother out the many benefits.

They have zero problems accepting your rent but take YEARS to put money into the issues they say they'll fix when you sign your lease. Property managers are absolutely useless and don't have the capacity to solve ANY issues with the property.

I have loved living here. They have always been quick and helpful with anything I've needed. Maintenance requests are handled promptly. The leasing office is kind. I’ve had a great experience living in the Capri Apartments the past 2 years. I lived in a studio, and it was actually a pretty good sized space. It had 3 closets, which gave me plenty of storage space. It basically came with a kitchenette, just a fridge & freezer, stove & oven, sink, a few cabinets, and one counter-top. Other than that, everything else about the Capri was fantastic!

I’m 67, disabled and retired from the Navy. One of the reasons I chose 21Fitz was to be close to the VA Hospital.
One thing I’ve learned about apartment living is you must be very clear about your needs when choosing your next home. Apartment  staff aren’t mind readers. 
I have a 4th-floor Unit, less than 700 sq ft, and it fits my large furniture. The floors are solid wood, so I’ve put down lots of rugs. They put in brand new washer and dryer stackables that are huge! I love them!! 
Since the CU/Anschutz/VA campus is a 2-minute walk, most residents are med students and doctors. If I were a parent, this is where I’d want my student to live. This is not party central. These students are serious about their education and seem to spend most of their time studying,  sleeping and rushing off to class. There are comfortable study lounges in the buildings. I’ve seen students from all over the world here.  
I’ve also seen a number of senior citizens here and I know that peace and quiet is a priority for us. The 4th floor is the most quiet, and I suggest putting down rugs with rug pads to be a good neighbor. The students here are good, respectful neighbors, too, holding the door for my pup and me.
Management and staff are the hub of this community and they’re always cheerful. They’re professional and knowledgeable. They always have a treat for our 4-legged roommates. They handle issues quickly. They care about your contentment with your home.  
Maintenance is quick to respond to issues. They get out there to shovel snow and chip away at ice as soon as humanly possible when there’s a snowstorm. Housekeeping keeps the community sparkling. Trash and recycling disposal is easy with rooms on every floor that are kept clean.
When you move in, check your unit thoroughly from top to bottom to ensure everything meets your expectations. Take photos to help out management with your requests and for your documentation. When you move out, spend those extra hours making sure the apartment is just as clean as when you moved in. You won’t be charged a dime if you make the effort and you left no damage.
There will be a lot of construction going on for the next year because they’re growing. My place is insulated from the noise, so it doesn’t bother me. I think they offer special deals for units that are affected. If you can’t tolerate the activity, tell them so that they can help you choose an apartment in a quieter area. 
I just wish I’d signed a longer lease!

~ It's noisy with endless construction (not only is this property building/renovating more, it is surrounded by construction on three sides--trucks are CONSTANTLY beeping)
~ When birds arrive, they will build nests under the eaves and chirp for months! It's kinda nice, for a few days, but they don't stop until they leave! So, windows closed with air-conditioner noise, or windows open with chirping noise--either way, it won't be quiet.
~ Amenities are sub-par (pool, spa closed most of the year, when open construction surrounding).
~ Maintenance will come, eventually, and so will the snow and dirt from their shoes.
~ They don't remove snow from sidewalks, nor around the doors to enter building from parking lot (particularly behind building 6). 
~ Trash room is overflowing at least every other week.
~ Expensive!! Let's be honest, it's Aurora.
~ Staff smiles upfront, charges ridiculous amount for "General Cleaning ($150), painting ($48), and Carpet Cleaning ($45). Even though the place my be "clean" on move out, they require a "Professional Receipt" to show it's been cleaned (My unit wasn't painted when I moved in, nor were the carpets cleaned, however I would expect the previous tenant was charged!) 
~ When you move out, you will not deal with the people on site, in the Leasing office, but with Daniel or Vanessa in the "Aimco Customer Care After Move-Out Team" however I did not experience friendliness or "care" from them. 

This place may have been nice a few years ago, however management has changed and the facilities are not worth to cost. Yes, it's walking distance to the hospitals and the UC schools...but there are other places close enough I would re-consider.

Paying 50 additional dollars when you lose your parking permit is pretty ridiculous when you're already nickle and dimed for everything else. For every single military member I know that moves to Denver I will tell them not to rent here. 50 dollars for a piece of plastic is insane. I will avoid Aimco properties in the future.

Living at 21 Fitzsimons is like high-class living. The community is clean, presentable, the staff are always pleasant, and all of the amenities are wonderful. Hotel living in the middle of Aurora on old Montview.

If you work or go to school at anschutz medical campus there is no possible better location. The apartments are beautiful with wood floors and really high ceilings. Maintenance responds quickly and staff is always friendly. There is a resturant, bar, liquor store, pharmacy, and bank in the community. There are also study rooms with complimentary wifi and free coffee. Dog friendly community. Be warned this community is pretty quiet and people complain quickly for noise.

The apartments are really gorgeous, wood floors and high ceilings. The staff are always friendly and avaliable. This is a very dog friendly complex, people really clean up after their pets well too! This apartment t has 2 resturants, a bank and a pharmacy inside the community. It is also steps away from the medical campus. Only complaint is the community really values quiet and are quick to address any noise, even in the middle of the day.

My husband and I have lived here since they opened - so we like it here and we're too lazy to move :) A big con of staying here that long is going through all the property owner and management changes. With each new owner we've had to deal with policy and price changes. I think the newest owner will be here for a while so that shouldn't be a problem for new residents. A pro and con is the addition of the Light Rail. It's great to have better access to surrounding areas, but that means more people walking through the neighborhood from surrounding lower income areas. (I hate to be snob, but we have already had problems with loitering and theft). Also means that management might charge more for rent because it has better access to public transportation. 

Rent rates are at a high right now in the greater Denver area due to real estate pricing, housing availability, cash offers, loans, etc. Denver is always growing and first-time home builds are struggling to keep up with demand. In this particular complex, the are also high because of the CU Medical School. Students make up the majority of the residents here and there is often a waiting list to get into the apartments. So the management doesn't need to try to get residents with deals. Despite this place being a borderline dorm, it's very quiet because the students are always studying.

My roommate and I have been living at this location for a few months now while we're in college, and it has been a great place for a couple of students to live, close to campus. The staff is very friendly and willing to help at a moments notice. We had a pest problem during some very cold months, and once we informed management, they were quick to help and send someone to inspect our place. We also had a heating issue when winter started, but they were quick to help us once we informed them. The noise was never a problem, and we never received noise complaints either, plus the neighborhood is quiet as well, very relaxing at times. Laundry is available but can be pricey if you end up doing more then one load. Sometimes the washers will break which can be an issue, but its normally resolved quickly.  Location is great for many things, very close to a nice shopping center off of Havana, and quick access to I-225 and the airport. No view of the Rockies if that's something you are looking for, but for the price, location, and convienience of the place, you are getting a pretty good deal.

Our experience with Geneva Apartments has been entirely positive. During our original tour, we had several questions, some in relation to my medical needs, and the manager and office staff were very helpful and informative.  Since moving in, the staff has continued to be consistently friendly, and readily available for our questions or needs.  For instance, the staff is always helpful in coordinating my twice-monthly medical supply deliveries (which are often large).  Staff also accept smaller deliveries to the office for residents when they are not home to accept delivery. The on-site maintenance worker has responded quickly to our maintenance tickets every time and is quite friendly. Our building is quiet; we've never had a noise problem. There is adequate parking in the private parking lot, but when that is full, there is abundant parking on the street; neither choice is too much of a walk. There are lawn areas where we walk our dog, and small kids' playground spaces on the grounds. We are close to many retail areas, restaurants, and supermarkets, and not far from I-70 and I-225. They do not currently have recycling pickup, and the area is not the most scenic part of Aurora. But overall, a good apartment for the price, and worth a look.

review: This is a tax credit building in which I did not know what that is. I had really friendly staff explain the application process and what is required to live here and they were very helpful and informative in the process. As I got a tour people I met were really friendly and the apartment i applied for was very clean. I am really happy and grateful for my new home. They also provide activities to meet new people in the community that make me feel welcomed. I recommend this place to many other citizens that are looking for a nice clean quite community to retire to.

review: They help only when it is convenient for them and will find anything to charge you for! Tried emailing them and getting help but they only reply when it is convenient for them!

Our move to Ladera was exceptional. Brittany B, leasing manager, was outstanding and made our move everything we needed it to be. Our apartment exceeded our expectations and we want to thank the entire Legacy/Ladera team! Very nice area. Very clean! Our apartment is fully updated, new appliances, beautiful flooring throughout, beautiful counteracts and cabinets. All we had to do was lysol and move in...lol. No maintenance requests. We are so happy with our choice and so blessed that Brittany helped us 5 states away!

It would’ve been nice to stay if my spt was an upgrade., I have the old cabinets and water leaks on floor in apt because of old air conditioning unit. Pipes run around front door not a great site.. I complain and all I get is sorry., I am force to leave after paying for a year and 1/2.. WOW good luck for your future here!

This place is excellent I’ve never had a problem the staff is always wonderful especially Dave and Melissa as well as the managers at Ladera they’re always concerned about any situation you may have very friendly in the office Maintenance arrives on time My stay here has been wonderful they are very sincere to me and I’m grateful for all the staff between Legacy pointe luxury and Ladera when I move from here I’m moving next-door because it’s sister Property I have no complaints honestly I’ll give them 10 stars if I could they’ve been very kind through the pandemic they’ve worked with people that was struggling paying their rent just common decency at this property I would recommend this to anyone sincerely Macquelyn Green

I love the place, I love the location! But the walls are impressively thin. So my upper neighbor’s morning routine (4:00am to 4:59) wakes me up every week day and 7am on the weekends. I suffer a lot from anxiety and this triggers it. It would have been nice if they announce this as an issue, but they didn’t even mention it... It is truly horrible to have signed a 12 month contract and having this issue. And I am not kidding, it is not a soft stepping, you can hear the shower, the creaking of the floor, the water flow from the sink as if it would be falling in your face. It is so loud, it wakes everyone up the moment it starts.

The other thing is that they offer a tennis court and it is completely out of order. Not from COVID, but the floor is uneven, cracked and the door always locked. I really wouldn’t mind not having it, but I just didn’t like the fact they offer it and that is not usable.

The pools and social house are not open due to COVID and I completely understand. But it makes me wonder, why all Henderson’s restaurants, gyms, beauty salons, church, etc are open with restrictions, but in Legacy Pointe it’s not even an option to come inside and take a look. I am a new resident and they gave me my keys at the door and I have never even met the place.

All this I say with sadness in my heart due to the fact that I really wanted to love the place, I actually adore the apartment, neighborhood and all. Legacy Pointe let me down.
Love it here, nice clean apt, great area. Maintenance is always on top of issues. Haven’t had any problems here so far.

My family and I moved in last February 2015. We had so many issues with leaks and old appliances. Our washer broke and flooded twice and flooded the laundry room, bathroom and into the hallway. Instead of replacing our washer with new equipment they cut corners and use old equipment out of different apartments and where they store their old refurbished equipment. Our dryer broke and they did the samething. Our air-condioner leaked all over the carpet 3 times. Our unit outside ran out of free-on multiple times through the summer. Our NV energy bill was $280 for a 1100 square foot apartment. We came home to a roach problem and they blamed us for it. They claimed that we got roaches because we left our garbage outside. You don't get roaches from that. They replaced our fridge (that's where the roaches were nesting) with an old dirty fridge from a vacant apartment. Our sinks leaked, carpet was old and our doors had putty on the holes from previous Tennants. Before our lease was up, we had our last leak and the office manager told us that we weren't going to pay for the carpet since we had so many problems. Well, we ended up paying for it and a door that was puttied from a previous hole from previous Tennants. They used up all of our deposit and where we owe them. SAVE YOUR MONEY! DO NOT MOVE INTO THOSE APARTMENTS! So many more in that area and district that are newer with nicer amenities and you won't be stuck with huge energy bills because they are too cheap to replace their appliances with new ones. They'll stick you with the bill. The carpet hadn't been replaced since 2011 and they made us pay for it. Sneaky, lying office girls! SAVE YOUR MONEY AND STAY AWAY!

I lived in Promontory Point for 2 years. The sink and tub in the bathroom were plastic and always looked dirty. The countertops were painted pink and the baseboards had a faux paper wood coating on them and the laminate tile was dirty and outdated.
I lived upstairs in a small one bedroom. The dining room and bedroom were ok sizes and the closet was large. I liked the w/d inside the unit and the patio. 
The grounds were ok. The location is convenient and has great pathways nearby. 
If you're willing to look past the outdated features and put your own flare into the apartment, it's not a bad place to live.

I moved into my unit in 2013 and I do not believe that it had been renovated recently. However, the apartment is livable and worked for me. The complex is well staffed and maintenance was quick. If I asked for something to be fixed, it was fixed within 24 hours. The staff in the office is friendly and makes me feel like I am part of the family. After my first lease expired they offered to clean my carpet for free and did not raise my rent as long as I renewed for 12 months. I do know they are upgrading units to stainless appliances and horizontal blinds. Plus, two bedroom units are getting front loading wahers as opposed to the stacked washer dryer in the one bedrooms like mine. However, my washer dryer was new enough to be under warranty when  it needed looking at. Also, the air conditioners are being replaced in the units I can see when walking to and from my car and the dumpsters. The grounds are well kept as well. My only complaint would be that the units are not nearly sound proof enough. I can hear my neighbor upstairs walking and my next door neighbor's child screaming, but the former is not daily and the latter is only when she is really upset. Otherwise I would recommend this complex to anyone, family or bachelor.
Safe, quiet community with excellent, quick responding  maintenance service. The Location is excellent. We live here for about 12 years. They are the best.

Lived here for 4 years and after the pandemic things got tougher. 

Our rent was raised by over $600 over the 4 years. The front office said so sorry so sad but if you don't like it, you can move. 

The pool is out of service for a good 2 months in the hot months for never-ending repairs.  

Second-floor unit, my downstairs neighbor smokes week and cigarettes which floods our unit with smoke, and the front office says... nothing we can do about it. 

The front office is nice .. until they are not.  The general manager has been heard on many occasions saying how she doesn't like out-of-towners..especially Californians who oddly enough are the ones she is okay renting to.  She simply wishes they would go back to where they came from.  


The pros.  

The maintenance team is amazing and diligent though some things like my smelly garbage disposal are out of their hands.  The premises are generally clean and well-maintained.
I like the private feel of it, and it seems to be kept up really well inside and out! I also love the bathtub and flooring/carpeting! This is my favorite property so far!

My Mother lived at these wonderful apartments for many years. Due to poor health she sadly had to move.  During all that time she never had a complaint. The staff was remarkable, going way above and beyond what would be expected.  The apartments are beautifully maintained and the staff treats their tenants like family. I will never be able to thank them enough or recommend these apartments more highly.  Thank you Pacific Islands Apartments for everything.

They have been denying residents who haven't agreed to amenity upgrades new lease terms and served eviction notices as of the first of September.  They refuse to tell residents as to what their reasons are for evicting them. They are attempting to do this without cause other than a gentrification  plan with inflated rent costs. It’s has been 3 days and I haven’t received a call or email. Extremely disappointed to be disregarded because I live out of state.

The apartments are nice and the area is Great! However, I don't like that their is suppose to be security monitoring the location at all times but I have yet too see one doing so. I have heard the neighbors working out in the middle of the night in their garage for weeks now and have yet to see securing around to tell them to stop. That is real my only complaint about this property other than that it is a good place to live.

If you are looking for a nice, pet friendly, peaceful and upscale area where there is no trouble or crime then Horizon Ridge Park Apartments is great for you. 
For the past 6 yrs my wife and I have been living in these apartments and we can tell you that we have not had any trouble with the staff or other residents. The only two things bad about Horizon Ridge Park Apartments is that there are no bbq grill covers by the pool, And the rent is pretty high, but hey what can you expect for a town house apartment  in a high class quiet area.
 The apartments have their own large movie theater where you can put in a dvd and watch a movie in the theater room. And for all you pet owners, Horizon Ridge Park Apartments are so pet friendly that they even have a dog  parks for the residents dogs.Until we find a house, we are looking foward to staying here for a long time.

The apartments are fairly normal. The houses are nice size and have the option of a townhouse style which is good for roommate style living. The appliances are old and dated, as are some of the fixtures. However, the maintenance men are very nice and quick to respond when you have a problem. The pool and hot tub area are pretty, but often dirty or not working. All in all, this is a great place to live.

Personal in the office work with you with problems you might have the response time is great.if you're late with your rent they give you the time you need but of course you have to pay the late fees.the property is kept very nice,the pool is very nice! To win this prize would be a blessing!
beware thin walls! weed smells! roudy community! horrible maintenance! management does nothing for your concerns and will tell you to deal with your living situation or move out.

I have recently moved into this apartment complex. I could not have made a better choice for my family. Walking into my new apartment I immediately  felt a sense home. I know that this is the apartment that I will raise my daughter in for years to come. My unit is renovated and in immaculate condition. The grounds are clean and green. The office staff and maintenance team could not be more welcoming. I recommend this complex to anyone who wants to live in a safe and comforting environment. My move in day was a real Welcome Home experience. Thank you Palm Villas!

They have completely used the pandemic as an excuse to do almost nothing with upkeep. Our landscaping is half dead throughout the complex. Our new flooring in halls is ripping up after just months. Our hallways are dirty, smelly & have chipped paint throughout. Our entry gate is nearly constantly broken. There water & electrical issues. I could write 3 pages on the poor maintenance alone but that’s not the worst thing.

The worst is the direction the management staff has taken. In just over 1 years time there has been a 100% staff change throughout. All management, maintenance & security staff that used to care & at least try to be accommodating to residents have been replaced. We used to have a manager who lived on site to deal with emergencies that came up after hours. Now everyone is gone home by 5pm & good luck if there’s an emergency because you can rarely find the overnight security officer to deal with it. The staff here now seem overwhelmed by their jobs and the residents are the ones who suffer. It’s a pattern to be told that any part needed for repairs is back ordered and for your maintenance request to then be canceled without completion. On the flip-side of that if you attempt to resubmit claims or make inquiries about grounds maintenance, amenity upkeep, neighbor complaints or anything else you then are labeled as being a complainer & of harassing the staff.

There has also been an uptick in crime on the property. In just the last week there’s been 1 car theft, multiple cars broken into, criminals caught in the act of trying car door & apartment door handles & a homeless man seen sleeping in the pool cabana. I have personally seen police on site 5x this week alone. Yet there’s been no communication from management informing residents to be on alert. The security is sub par at best. As a widow living alone I no longer feel safe on this property.

This is not a place that exudes luxury anymore however we still pay luxury prices and have been subjected to rent increases that are much higher than any previous yearly rent increase we paid before. They also refuse to negotiate on lease terms stating all residents are now offered the same flat fee increase. This is illogical and unfair in a complex whose rental prices can vary by thousands of dollars.

I used to think I had found my forever home but I will be leaving after my current lease. It would nearly take a miracle to turn this place back into the incredible community…it WAS!

I lived at this property for three years it went through three different property management companies. Even after providing the proper noticed after my lease and they gave me a hard time and had to get a lawyer involved.

The building has had a class-action lawsuit by the tenants in 2015 and at least one death on the property. I moved out earlier this year.

We have lived here for 6 months and 6 weeks ago the property was sold and the new owner brought in their own management company.  I rolled my eyes when I heard because this will be the third management company since we have been here.  We relocated here from NY so we didn't miss a thing with what was going on here.  Well I gotta tell you, in five, yes five, weeks they have made Vantage a great place to live.  They evicted at least 15 troublesome tenants, cleaned up the place dramatically (yes power washed the garages) , brought in a great staff, brought in a true security firm that patrols 24 hours a day with an active must carry cell phone and has weekly special events for the tenants.  They are not fooling around and those of us that have been here for a while are well pleased.  Now I can say Vantage is a really nice place to live.  Kudos to the new owners and their staff

Terrible complex. Everything are broken. Maintenance won’t fix it. So dirty outside because after a garbage truck pick up a trash nobody clean it. A lot of strange people live there, drunk and marijuana smoke. Can’t wait to move out.

They don't even have a property manager, they have assistants doing the work of a licensed property manager. Staff is never on site. Moving here is the worst decision I've made in quite some time.  I should have taken the warning signs more seriously during my initial visit.  The office staff cannot seem to get anything right.  Any promise they make is a promise that will be broken.  Everything in our apartment is falling apart despite the claim that the unit is newly renovated.  The door was installed incorrectly, the paint is uneven, the socket covers are falling off, the water heater doesn't work, and the laundry room door literally falls to the floor if you open it.  Calling maintenance is a futile exercise because they never come.  You can call time and time again and they will tell you someone is coming today, yet they never do.  If you are one of the lucky few to get maintenance to come to your unit, they will always say they need to get a part.  You will never hear from them again.  The people in the office simply do not care and act like 16-year-old fast food employees.  I understand it can be difficult to care about a job that probably pays very little, but it helps to pretend.  If you are reading this, please do not move here.  I stand by every day and watch people tour the apartments wishing I had the guts to tell them not to move here.  There are many other options in the area that cannot be worse than what I have experienced at Ladera/Legacy Point.

Master bathroom tile and caulking in the shower were not sealed properly upon moving in and appeared to have been applied over existing mold. Our request to fix this was ignored. Shower started leaking in October (we moved in in July), contacted them over the phone and was told they would fix it. They never arrived. Tried the same method again to no avail. Then I went in to the office on a Monday (November) was told by an staff a work order would be put in and that it would be fixed by Wednesday at the latest. A week went by and no one came. I returned to the office and asked when my maintenance request would be attended to. The woman there said there was no work order in the system and asked who I spoke to. The person I spoke to before had no nametag and did not introduce herself. Why this was relevant I have no idea. She was attempting to shift their mistake on to me. They finally arrived a week later. Once they removed the shower tiles (one had already fallen on me in the tub) I peaked into the bathroom and saw that there was black mold covering over half of the wall near the faucet. They quickly shut the door to prevent me from looking in. They locked us out of the bathroom overnight to dry out the wall. Today they came back (while face chatting) and removed the fan. The all went into the bathroom (preventing us from looking inside again) talked a bunch, locked the bathroom door again, and left saying they'd be back later today. It's almost 6pm now and they've yet to return. Why we can't enter the bathroom to use the sink or toilet is beyond me since they've removed the fan. I assume it's to prevent us from photographing the black mold everywhere.

I wouldn't recommend moving here. You will have constant maintenance issues, patch up repairs if any! They will charm you and tell you good things about this place, but once you're in, don't expect to get good service, especially when it comes to repairs and air conditioning issues,
Good apartment community and I really enjoy the gym and pool. Maintenance has been doing better at keeping the grass areas clean from dog droppings

Outstanding community to live in,
Convenient for all my shopping needs, and to the superhighways for any travel I might need.. All my needs are met here.
The staff is considered and friend and there for all our needs.

Been here two years andI'm very happy.  It's quiet and nice.  Just pretty sad how much rent went up but other than that I'm happy.  Maintenance guys are very nice. Thank you.

Great place. Good amenities. The staff here is great and helpful. Quite neighborhood. Wish parking was more ample thought. No complaints other than that

The leasing staff turned off the payment portals for over a week, not allowing residents to pay online. After a week of inactivity, they emailed us on Friday letting us know the portal was active. Then, if you did not check your email over the weekend like me, you were charged a late fee for not paying rent, claiming it was past the "grace period" (again you could not pay earlier, and I did not even know it was an option). 

I have not paid late, and I would not have paid late if I was able to pay on time or if I was even told I had to pay by a certain date. Instead, I was charged a late fee because their website was broke and I did not constantly check my email.
Love this place. My floor plan is great and the amenities make me feel like I’m permanently on vacation.  Great place to live.

The apartments changed the management a few months back and they are AMAZING! They actually listen to me as a resident and complete work orders on-time. Very professional and very helpful. 10 out of 10!!!!
Very impressed with this property. It has such a welcoming environment! Also, very clean!!!

There are scorpions here ! We have found so so many in our apartment and have told the office repeatedly and they say there is nothing they can do ! Neighbors have also complained and even been bit by one ! Last night one of my family members was bit and no are at the hospital !! If you’re looking for the most value in Henderson, Chateau Calais is the place.
