Rent has increased and they have not agreed to issue any refunds for the problems everyone has experienced - they only sent out gift baskets in a weak attempt to offset the $2800-5000 rent the residents paid during all of this downtime. Residents are finally moving out as a result of this continued drama, yet lots of positive reviews are somehow appearing all over the internet. Final opinion is that this building is a major ripoff.
I've been living here for 3 months and the bathtub clogged 3 times already! There's DARK DIRTY WATER COMING OUT OF THE DRAIN!!!! 10000000% gross. Feel so dumb to have signed the 1-year lease

Lived here 9/10/2019-6/17/2020

Only rent from The Plaza if you have no other option.

When we first went to see the apartments, we were greeted by a kind and friendly young lady named Ruby. She showed us around a model apartment and mentioned that it was not identical to the apartment that we would be renting. Upon moving in, we found that the apartment leased to us was barely renovated and looked nothing like the model unit. We were not warned that our apartment would be significantly lower in quality compared to the model unit. 

Our apartment had termite damage in some of the baseboards at the edge of the bathrooms, and the cupboard under the sink in the bathrooms. We actually noticed the presence of termites as well. Although it was rare to find them alive, I would often wake up with a few dead termites in my bed, and termite wings would regularly be found in the bathroom in the morning. If you end up seeing the apartments, please ask them to show you the actual apartment they plan on giving you, not a model unit.

Numerous times I would be in the shower with the water set to lukewarm, and suddenly the water would spike hot. It would sometimes spike so high (without anyone touching the knob) that I would leave the shower with a red chest/back.

Many of the positive reviews have no mention of the security deposit. We cleaned extensively to avoid any charges. We were still charged $341 for painting. Our desks/beds had left some minor discoloration on the walls. We carefully read the lease agreement's sections on the security deposit and found that we are not responsible to pay for minor damages caused by reasonable use. 

Gisela, the landlady, immediately noticed the wall stains and told us we will be charged unless they're cleaned. We asked for the paint type, but they never got back to us. Without pointing them out, you can't really be certain whether they're shadows or stains. 

Please look up & read about wear and tear in this context; you'll find that anything similar to our situation falls under reasonable use and is paid for by the landlord. 

I would like you to form your own opinion. Would you feel comfortable giving up $341 for that? Come on.

They'll have some excuse for every claim I made here. Don't listen to them. No matter what they retaliate with when they attempt to invalidate my review, I assure you that the apartment I rented was NOT worth the money, and the security deposit charge had no merit. Look elsewhere.

Living in the Plaza apartment has been great thus far, all of the utilities were in great condition when we moved in,  The floors were brand-new, the cabinets were newly finished, and the counter was granite. 
 With an outdoor and open natural layout, you don't feel like you're in an apartment building, but rather a luxurious hotel.

 As for the staff, they are beyond exceptional. Throughout the whole entire process they were there almost 24 hours a day to help us complete our rent papers and submit maintenance request and process our bank information. 

 Additionally , beyond the complex itself, parking on the street is amazing as well. In a crowded area like Westwood,  parking is very valuable – which there is a plethora of. 

 As for the area, it's basically student filled, creating a lot of nightlife and activity for the weekends. The restaurants in the area are beautiful as well with a wide variety of international and local food choices. 

 Overall, I have to say that living at the Plaza Apartments has been one of the best decisions we have ever made. We looked all over Westwood for a unit for about seven months, and ended up here, and I couldn't have chosen anywhere better.

In a great location! Close to UCLA, Metro Bus Lines, as well as entrances to the 405 North and South. Quiet building, very clean and currently going through new renovations. Even in units that haven't been renovated, appliances are very up to date, and the rooms are decently spacious (fits 2 people in a room). Management is courteous and very helpful.
Sunset Tower is an exclusive and welcoming community.

I have been living here for 2 years and would recommend to avoid this place at any cost.
Residents are smoking weed and cigarettes in their apartments and management can’t do anything about it; you will enjoying not only the smell but also fire alarms at 3 and 4am regularly.
If neighbors party all night long- management is not here to help either. You can expect to enjoy your neighbors music till 6-7am.
If anything gets broken it takes 2-3days to get fixed. They have only one maintenance guy for a whole building.
When packages are getting stolen they remind you that it’s not their responsibility to insure safety of your packages.
Whether you enjoy listening rumors about residents or not- you cannot avoid it when you stop on the first floor to get your morning coffee.
You will have a difficult time to get your Uber eats orders - security is rarely on their post. Drivers are not able to get in the building so they leave.
Security is changing every other week - so you will see a lot of securities who dont know what to do.
I cannot say anything good about management - they rude and useless.
It’s also not safe around here - too many homeless people; few residents were attacked.

Sunset & Vine is a lovely community to live. The amenities are updated, concierge personnel are kind and engaging, maintenance staff are very prompt, efficient and knowledgeable, leasing staff helps to mitigate issues in a timely manner. This is the first place I moved to when I relocated to Los Angeles and I don’t regret my decision. Chris G

If I could give negative stars I would. Save your self the time and money and move somewhere else. A lot of the amenities they list do not even work. Used to be a nice place to live but since Jen left we’ve been through 5 managers and they get worse and worse. On top of the horrible management the place is cover in trash and smells awful.

We moved into CentrePointe a little less than a year ago and we have been so happy. The apartment itself is spacious and perfect for our family. Management is always friendly, responsive, and helpful. Lucia and Doug have always helped us out when needed. We also love the walkability of the community. We would recommend living here to anyone!

I have lived here for 3 years and it has been a great experience. The property is clean and secure, they often update and upgrade communal areas, maintenance is very responsive and easy to work with, and the on site management really is helpful. They communicate frequently and proactively. I have to move for work/ family, and I am so sad to have to find another place to live because I have never had a management company actually care about their tenants the way that this place does. I'm writing this review because I rely on tenant reviews to help me when I'm apartment hunting, and I want to pass it on.

We lived at CentrePointe for two years, early 2022-2024. It has been the best place I've lived in LA. Unlike many of the new complexes popping up, the construction at CentrePointe is very solid. In our previous building, the walls were so thin we could literally hear our neighbors having conversations, so it was super important to us that our next apartment had good sound isolation. At CentrePointe, our neighbors could have a party without the sound traveling to our unit.

Maintenance requests were always dealt with promptly (usually within 1-2 days). We also really love the community, and we miss hanging out with Lucia and Doug in the front office! They're the best! Blanca is an angel! These apartments aren't the cheapest in the area (they're also not the most expensive), but for the space, amenities, and location, they're kind of a steal. We're leaving to move closer to work, but we'd recommend these apartments to anyone.

The apartments are very nice and spacious, and good value. Management is great. Lucia has been very nice and helpful, and is working very hard (including on weekends) to quickly resolve any requests, usually done by the same day.

This has been the best apartment living experience we have ever had.  I truly cannot say enough wonderful things about everyone in the leasing office as well as the maintenance staff and everything and everyone in-between.  Only reason I'm leaving is because I need a 3rd bedroom otherwise I would stay for even longer!

We had a great experience living here and have lived at other LA apartments on the Westside in the past.

Their maintenance is quick and they have a helpful online portal to submit these requests and pay rent via check or credit card.

The staff has always been helpful and nice as well. We've been here for 4 years and love the 2 level floor plans! It makes the apartment feel bigger.
Management doesn’t care about the tenants at this location. It’s only about filling vacancies vs actually taking care of the tenants that are living here.

If it were labeled a frat house, no problem. But they didn't. It's just drunk college kids and loud music. No staff or patrol for hours so they party on!  And patrol only hangs in the lobby so don't call and expect a person to answer. If you are an adult, stay away!!!!!

Do Not Move Here! Worst office staff I have ever seen, I'm absolutely shocked how they ignore emails and calls. They will lie to your face and not follow up.  They put on a good show to get you to sign the lease, don't fall for it. A class action law suit should be filed on this place with all the construction issues and water shutoffs (some times with out notice).  Does anyone know a good lawyer?I recently had a water leak issue as the unit above flooded from construction. Maintenance entered my unit and damaged my property and also used my clothes to clean up the water on the floor, seriously? Residents pay too much money here to be treated this way. People do your research and look for better places in the area, I would pay more for better service than be treated this way.

For those of you who like the finer things in life, this would definitely be the place for you. Minutes from Beverly Hills and The Grove - you wake up feeling like your at a holiday home everyday. If you don't get weekly housekeeping service that isn't a problem either because there is washer and dryer in the unit and a broom provided in the suite. Lastly, I could not emphasize the views, I had the opportunity to stay on the 26th floor, so in the morning I got to enjoy breakfast on my balcony (yes! table and chairs are provided!!!) and night, enjoy a glass of wine with the city lights of DTLA. Would highly recommend LEVEL Furnished Living!
I moved here a month ago, and love the benefit of one payment, all inclusive. Great location, amenities, and decor. Very happy!

1. GYM machines have been out of order for months.
2. Manager never replies to your emails regarding the management of the property.
3. Garage doors are often not working, making me waste my time to get to the other side of the building.

At Alina, we thoroughly appreciate the quality of residents and staff in our building. The leasing staff, security, and maintenance people greet you warmingly and are attentive to your needs. The residents at Alina are very respectful and well-off people, many of whom we are great friends with. We've even started businesses with a few of the residents.

Alina is also a very dog-friendly building with the largest dog park in DTLA (to my knowledge). We've made most of our friends in DTLA from the Alina dog park.

The parking is private, clean, and very convenient, especially if you have an EV with a dedicated spot. The parking structure is 100% residents only. Many of the other DTLA buildings give priority to non-residents, making it take forever to get in / out of your spot. Alina is the opposite, so if you care about your time, you're going to love this setup.

The amenities are super great, but basic in the total offering. We don't care much for having every single amenity because there are options nearby that encourage you to engage with local businesses. The rooftop is my favorite, with a beautiful panoramic view of Los Angeles.

It's hard to really give any downsides to Alina. If you're moving to DTLA, you're probably aware that certain street conditions may not be ideal, especially for raising a family. But if you're a working professional, a business owner, or a student, you're going to love living the quality and convenience of Alina.

The leasing office team, Tim, JP, and Diana will take excellent care of your needs.  I hope you have a wonderful time here.

Bad building structure. Since Management is useless at dealing with bass and noise issues, they should have at least invested in high quality insulation. Luxury appliances mean zero if you live with someone playing basketball against your wall. Very stupid divider between balconies also guarantees that if your neighbors are loud, you will hear them in your living room. Why not to invest in better sound proofing and more private dividers? I know some level of necessary noise can be expected when you live in an apartment, but I've lived in at least 6 or 7 apartments in the past 10 years and I've never heard of anything this bad. The walls are thick enough that if people are sensible, they can still enjoy loud music/TV without disturbing others, but there are people who want to have a club like music experience, and make multiple units miserable. I complained to the office multiple times and they made multiple phone calls, sent security up, and spoke to them in person. However there are re-occurring disturbances and there's not much Management has been able to do apart from starting to shift blame, which is outrageous for the prices they charge.

When we were the potential residents requesting tour, and/or needing assistance to rent, Deja's were very friendly, however afterwards she is very short and rude. Two of my friends experienced otherwise during the tour. They felt rushed and no follow ups after when she mentioned she would share information about the floor plan that was toured. The other staffs are friendly and helpful. I continue my lease here because of the convenience of the location, up keep of the building, and all the staff minus Deja. The building and the other staff should not be scored due to her customer service.

I have lived at Hawthorn Regency For 7 years. I am over the moon on what an amazing experience it was. You will be working with the best management team any building can offer. They are professional, extremely helpful, friendly and just great people. I loved the high ceilings, amenities, apt layout, washer dryer, etc. There is nothing missing here at Hawthorne Regency. If I didn't have to move to NY I would have never left. A big thank you to Brigette and Her family for being the best management team any tenant can ask for. A+, 5 starts, 10 out of 10!

horrible experience living here. other tenants and I have complained of unbearable noise several times, yet no actions taken to prevent it from recurring over and over again! would never recommend this place.
walls and floors are thin, you can hear your neighbors' conversation and karaoke singing at 4am in the morning. living experience is terrible.

The units and their finishes are truly top notch. It's in a quiet neighborhood and street, but the best part, especially in K-town, is having plenty of reserved parking on-site. I never have to drive around the streets and can feel safe that my car is secured underground. The staff is quick to respond to any small item, they keep the common areas clean, and it really shows!

Don’t take them. They are a robber. I locked out my door and they want me to pay $50 for just open the door. It is crazy apartment and also there are lots of ants in apartment. Ants in anywhere in my room and they didn’t do anything for me. They are horrible.

Come live here, spend over $36.000 a year to experience the following…
- HOT WATER: No hot water for over two months, and the clock is still running. The issue hasn’t been solved yet. No reimbursement at all for this. $0. You read well. $0. But if you are late on your rent you’ll be fined with a minimum fee of $100. 
- ODOR FROM PINE & CRANE: If your unit faces Margo St. alley, if you leave your window/s opened, your apartment will get filled of the smell coming out of the vents from the restaurant beneath. Starting at 9am your unit will smell to burned oil, fried food, garlic, meat, onion and who knows what else. This is disgusting. You’ll get sick of it. You’ll be hostage of this forever !!! You cannot avoid it and get away from it. 
- WATER PRESSURE: The shower has a very low pressure. You’ll spend more time showering as less water than normal will come out.
- SMOKE IN UNIT & FAKE FIRE ALARM: Range cooktop ventilation. If you love cooking immediately discard the option of living here. Don’t doubt it one second. The ductless ventilation system will not extract the air from your unit to outside, instead, it will filter the air with a poor basic cheap filtering system incorporated in the microwave and recycle it back into your kitchen again. As a consequence your unit will smell for days, even if you leave your fake balcony door opened while cooking. That’s not all, wait, there is more. The “filtered” air will be pushed towards the top cabinet with doors, where the smoke/odor will be as well stored there for days. The rule to cook at any unit of this property is to avoid cooking any type of meats, and avoid any oils or fats, and after you cook, leave all your cabinet doors open so the odor gets out, and leave the window open for one entire day. Then, enjoy all the bugs and insects that will get into your unit because of leaving the window opened. Hence, cook yourself some pasta and eat a salad if you don’t want to get deaf with the sounds of the in-unit smoke detectors. //// Also it has happened many times already, that the fire alarm of the building gets triggered after someone opens the door of their unit to vent it, because as I just explained, the ventilation system of the range is the worse and cheapest one in the market. As a consequence the emergency protocol gets triggered and immediately all elevators are disabled for over 1h. Imagine having this issue often. It’s a nightmare!!!!!
The staff has been so nice and everything is clean. I feel safe here
I feel that every component of the Aven property has exceeded my standards! I love my apartment, community areas, interacting with staff and have had an excellent experience overall!
This apartment complex has a great price/quality ratio for Los Angeles.
The one downside is noise from other residents depending on were your apartment is located.
I would not recommend Aven because of your tyrannical mask policy

It was a pleasure living here,
Have never had an issue, neighbors are friendly, staff is great  whenever maintenance is needed, always fast, resourceful and respectful of being in your space!

Stay away! That night, at least 3 cars were broken into in a gated parking while security was present in the building. Absolutely not safe. They don't have the necessary cameras and can't spot the theft. That's one of many times and not the first time.

No one had even called me back from the management when I reported that -- reckless unwillingness and ignorance with this kind of issue.

Pick your safety over whatever deal they can offer, and stay away.

The management is lying to residents. THey just started the construction without proper notification, and there's no way you can sit thru it because if feels like they're drilling right into your head. Just don't care about tenants at all.

So far, I have been very impressed with my experience. Carmen & Nina care and attention appears as a game-changer and a high bar for other leasing management in LA. 

The on-site walkthrough was GREAT. Carmen was VERY friendly, super helpful, and knowledgeable about the property. She kept me up-to-date with the current status of the application. And she is always working with a positive attitude. That really helped my decision to move forward with my application. THANK you for that! 

Nina was VERY responsive and communicative via email. she scheduled my visits, answered questions and was always friendly so THANK you for that! 

The apartment is gorgeous and very spacious. It is newly remodeled and the VIEW is UNBELIEVABLE.

If you're looking for a place that offers comfort and safety in a perfectly convenient location, then this building is ideal. Located in the heart of Hollywood, this building is just a quick walk from shops, amazing restaurants, theatres, the historic Walk of Fame, and plenty more venues for nightlife adventures. 

The building has floor-to-ceiling windows with spectacular views and plenty of natural sunlight. The common areas are finely maintained and includes a large patio with a pool, gas fire pit, grills, lounge chairs and dining tables, all set above ground-level with panoramic views of Downtown's skyline. Enjoy peaceful and serene living amidst the movement of the city.

Love love love the location!! It is in a cute, clean neighborhood yet in the middle of Hollywood, walking distance to so many restaurants, markets, bars, etc. The parking garage is an amazing luxury especially for the price (not provided by many other apartments in the area)!! The apartment itself is clean and spacious with lots of storage space. Also, the walls are not paper thin which I've previously experienced and is something you don't discover until after moving in.  Last, a deal breaker for me, is the manager; Ted is very very friendly and attentive to his tenants and as the previous review mentions, he responds quickly via text and is always friendly and helpful. You can tell he truly cares about everyone's experience.
Definitely recommend!!!

Although the amenities are not the newest, the apartment in general is in a great area close to the Metro and the rent is very cheap, everything is very clean and very well put together.  The apartment also comes with a parking spot in the garage.  The best part about this apartment is the manager Ted.  He is ALWAYS available by text and quickly jumps on any problems that may arise in the apartment.  There is also a pool in the apartment and a grill.  Love the area, love the price.

I lived here in 2018 when I first moved to LA. Overall it was a great apartment. Everyone in the building was friendly. The area can be a little dodgy but I loved the walkability of the area. Ktown is great and it was really easy to get to downtown, Silver Lake, and Hollywood via metro or Uber. The building was pretty basic but it was just what I needed.

Avoid this property at all cost. The property management is extremely unresponsiveness. Work orders go uncompleted or half-way done, trash area and parts of the building infested with rodents (mice, and roaches). The building is not secure so if you have pets, children, or live alone, this would not be the place for you. Gates are broken, and doors are rigged to stay open allowing anyone to access the building. The laundry room here is coin laundry only but washer water is not filtered and oftentimes, the equipment is not working properly. There are no amenities on the property and the appliances inside the studio and one-bedroom and much smaller than the average stove, and refrigerator. Getting a property management company to answer the phone or respond to work orders can take anywhere for days, weeks, to months. 

Pro - the price point for rent is lower than in many places in the area. 
Cons - everything else. parking is a bare, building is poorly managed/kept up, there are many code violations here. I would not recommend this property to my worse enemy.

This complex is has decent sized apartments, larger than most in Los Angeles (comparing cost per square footage) and is conveniently located between downtown and Hollywood. There’s a Target walking distance as well as several other fast casual restaurants  which is helpful.

Cons
- building is old so it often has roaches

- there’s no air conditioning in the building, you’ll need portable A/C in every room if you want to keep the place roach free and cool

- Street parking is a nightmare if you own a car and live here. Put a budget away for parking tickets bc the meters turn on at 8am everyday except Sunday (no parking permits for the tenants)

- trash has to be taken to the basement (no trash shoot, or cans anywhere in the building) so be prepared to take trash to the bottom floor every few days if you don’t want it in your home

- laundry facility is very old. If you aren’t bothered by dust, dirt, or minor rust you’ll be fine. If you are - prepare to go to an outside facility

- maintenance isn’t on site so if you have an issue, or need something fixed, prepare an additional 3-4 days before getting someone

Jardine is the prime living experience in Hollywood - I previously moved out of Jardine, only to find myself returning due to the high quality of the experience I have received. The staff is tremendously helpful, and the amenities are unrivaled. I have checked out every other competitor in Hollywood (including SMB Hollywood) and none compare.
There's no better place to live in LA than The Jardine.  The amenities, build quality, the staff, the maintenance, the safety, and the friendliness of tenants make this a dream place to live.
It's been great living here so far, the staff is wonderful and very responsive and the amenities are amazing!

Residing at Jardine has been an incredibly enjoyable experience overall. There are numerous delightful aspects of living here, including the valet service, 24-hour concierge and security, the pool, and the charming café area.
Beautiful building, excellent and ample staff, and total security. Amenities are exceptional. Love the 24-hour staff available daily.

Jardine is a jewel in the middle of this crazy wonderful Hollywood insanity! 
Beauty and class , nothing less than perfection

Because it is secure, elevator and halls are clean  lighting  HVAC, flooring  and plumbing are in good working condition it smells nice there is no signs of pests or insects quite relaxing atmosphere helpful and very insightful manager/Tourist Ms. Ana,. It also has a very decent on site gym laundry-room and cafe along with  optional nearby parking lots.
Great studios apartment. Clean amenities, secured with friendly neighbors and the management is top notch.

The managers...coz i don't know who really is the real manager in that building has a poor customer service. They're giving attitude to their tenants. They're unreliable and the office is always closed. Try to call the number and it always goes to voicemail to think that their apartment is just 3 feet away from the office. 
They are being technical with the terms / contract that you signed. They also charge you $10 if you forgot your keys inside of your apartment that goes straight to their pocket (it is not written in the lease that you have to pay that amount) 
If you want to deal with that kind of managers, go ahead and lease their apartments. Oh one more thing, the owner of these building, if you have issues with your manager, they will contact them first rather than the person who called them.. Such a professional approach on descaltating

A) Few things I like with our apartment: 1) Our manager is fair in treating tenants. He is a very nice person. 2) Our rooms are liveable. 3) Free electricity and water. 4) It is located at the heart of the city. 5) It is the most affordable bachelor pad I can find in the area ($750/mo for those who started renting 5 years ago).
B) Few negative things: 1) No parking ( we have to pay public monthly parking across the street). 2) We get stuck with Time warner Cable. We cannot choose any other provider. The building has no place for discs. 3) Our digital main door and elevators always gets broken. 4) Cockroaches infest our rooms in summer.

I have lived in this building for nearly two years. Upon moving in to the building the landlord had said there was a hot tub on the roof. in the time that I have lived in the building the hot tub has never worked. One night when I went on to the roof I found a homeless man who had snuck in to the building, peeing in to the hot tub. The building claims to have security but it does not have a camera at the buildings front doors. This has enabled people to walk in to our building, take the elevator, and steal multiple cars. Lastly, the AC unit for our apartment broke. Whenever we would turn on the air, hot air would come out. I called Nora, the landlord, to fix it. Nora did not return my calls for weeks. I had to go to her apartment every night after work (she is never around on the weekends) and ring the doorbell insistently until I could get an answer from her face to face. It took over two months for the problem to be resolved. 

Why, you may ask, have I stayed here for so long. Well up until this point rent was extremely reasonable and affordable. This past month the landlords have raised the rent by nearly $400. When multiple tenants complained the landlord posted signs all over the building, essentially, saying pay or get out. I've made the decision to get out. to anyone looking to move here, I would not recommend looking elsewhere.

Modern apartment in the HEART of the city, between Sunset & Hollywood Blvd! It's a 2-5 min walk to the Walk of Fame, Hollywood/Highland, Theaters & great shopping/nightlife/restaurants. Love that it's located in a fun and lively area central to all of LA, but that it still has that neighborhood vibe. The building itself is a bit old, but the unit is newly renovated and has a winding staircase that rivals an NYC loft.

This place is horrible. Property unkept and not clean. Building entrance doors are always broken. Homeless people are frequently in the building living in the garage stairs. Residents have no respect for noise. Loud music constantly. Dogs barking all day. Kids skateboard in the garage which makes loud noises throughout the building. Dogs potty on elevator and in the halls no one cleans it up. Cigarettes smokers in halls and elevator even though it’s a “non smoking building”. Leasing manager and staff does nothing about it.

This is the BEST apartment I have ever lived in. Period. From the stylish updated apartments full of amenities including a dishwasher, washer/dryer IN UNIT, and a patio to a building manager named Maria that I can only describe as an absolute angel (she made moving in fast, easy, and effortless) to a maintenance team that responds immediately to any request to a building with a chill vibe that anyone is LA would love to SO MUCH MORE. I can see myself staying here for a very very long time. You will not be disappointed.

All I have to say about this building and the management is that they are great!! I’m a resident of this building and my apartment is super cute and I have an amazing view. Maria the manager is super nice and she will help you in whatever you need super  fast. Josue the maintenance guy as well, whatever you need in your apartment he will solve it ASAP.  The problem that I had in other buildings I used to live was that they have a super poor organization and a really bad management team. They didn’t help me at all and they took years to solve an issue. I’m super happy I don’t have those problems anymore :)

Trust me. I lived here up until recently. In the year that I lived here, the following issues took place. 

1) My living room was flooded from the dishwasher leading to the damage of the kitchen wall’s, baseboards and several personal items. 

2) My bathroom’s ceiling suddenly collapsed one day due to months of water damage from an unknown leak caused by an improperly installed bathtub drain in the upstairs unit (their plumber’s exact words) and a portion of the ceiling, the circumfrence of a tire, had to be removed and repaired.

3) The repairs on the bathroom ceiling were never fully completed or painted afterward. 

4) The provided Refrigerator malfunctioned three times destroying perishable contents inside each time and it took then 10  days to get it fixed the first time.

5) The elevator (in a three story building) almost never worked the entire time and had still not been fully repaired.

6) The weeks of construction in an attempt to improve the property lead to invasive construction workers who let themselves in without notice and did not securely lock up the apartment upon leaving. 

7) I experienced an assault by a transient man on the grounds shortly after moving in which I reported to the previous manager but never heard back on. 

8) Someone tried to break into my apartment on Halloween night this past fall and the local sheriffs department took two hours to come out and check on AFTER nobody was available to speak to on the apartments emergency maintenance line. 

9) Mice, rats and feral cats roam the courtyard and garage. 

10) The garage doors did not work for the first few weeks upon my moving in. 

11) the construction crew took my assigned parking space for 3 weeks causing me to have to park out on the street which lead to a few parking tickets. When I brought this up to the manager, nothing was done about it for weeks. 

12) Tenant’s mailboxes were constantly found open and packages have been stolen. 

13) The Management company is run by cold and inept individuals. 

14) Disruptive transients loiter around the property often. 

15) Despite several of the units being updated with new paint and attractive yet cheap flooring, the building is old and gives you the impression it has a lot of problems once you’re in it.

The price of the apartments is reasonable. The carpet is poorly installed and the building is quite a bit older. The water pipes are rusted so you get rust stains on the bottom of the bath tub. There aren't cameras so the grounds aren't very secure and there have been multiple instances of homeless people in the courtyard and even trying to get into apartments.

Every single morning (8:00-9:00AM), the parking garage smelled weed. During night, there are people peeing outside, you can also smell it during the night. Besides the bad smell, I have contacted the leasing office before signing the contact, they promised that there is no changing in management team. However, they have changed! Now they are under Moss Company, which is 2/5 rating here. The management never response to any requests, all they do is finding excuses and do nothing!!!! Do not live here! You will certainly regret about it.
The management is very professional. Maintenance is great. They take care of the issues in 24 hours max. I am a happy renter. I highly recommend this place

Property is very well maintained. Maintenance is always available. A lot's of amenities with quality equipment. They really take care of the place good. Units are very large and specious. Management is very professional and quick to respond to any issue. I haven't seen any residential buildings respond work request as quicker than The Woodmere team. I highly recommend this building on top of your building search. Good luck.
This apartment building is great to its tenants and has a lot of amenities. The location is not too far from Santa Monica and is a good neighborhood to live in.
The Woodmere Apartment offers luxurious living environment at a reasonable price. Staffs are responsive and friendly. Only downside so far is the road noise on the Sepulveda side.

We moved into Woodmere a few months ago and we find we fall in love with this nice, cozy apartment. There is a superb security system. The management team is nice and friendly. The maintenance is fast and efficient. whatever facilities you want to find in an apartment, you are sure to find it here. It is really a resident-friendly apartment and makes our stay in Los Angeles an enjoyable one.
It's a nice place could use a little maintenance and clean up, other than that the living areas are nice and the Internet is good.

My experience at 717 has been wonderful; the resident lounges with office space saved me on my first few days of move in,  I did not have my desk and internet set up and needed a place to work.   Shout out to the entire staff; all friendly and informative!  My first few weeks have been awesome!
717 Olympic is a great place to live. For the area, the value for an apartment is competitive. The apartments are maintained well and the staff is always friendly, no matter their position.

717 Olympic is an amazing community to live in and reasonably affordable for Los Angeles.  Especially for the accommodations and amenities offered at 717.  The convenience and walkability alone is highly sought after in DTLA.  The staff from Leasing, Concierge and Maintenance are accommodating, kind, approachable and professional.
717 is absolutely amazing! The staff is outstanding!

Awful move in experience from the very first phone call, random ppl roam the building, the leasing staff is rude, Follow up is horrible, still have broken and non working items in my apt. I’ve never moved in a place, and couldn’t wait to move out. Most likely I’ll break my lease as soon as I get acclimated with the city, to find a better living space!! I love Greystar properties, but this thee WORST place I’ve ever lived in. I’m not looking forward to this leasing experience, and mind you, I’ve only been here for two weeks! :(
The maintenance guys did a great job addressing the two issues i had, plus fixed another one on the spot I had not put in a request about. Very responsive team!
Overall, living here has been a positive experience. It's a nice building with a good staff.

As someone who has never lived in LA and was a little nervous about it to begin with, living in 717 Olympic was the best decision I could have made. The community is kind, caring and genuinely wants to help make your living as easy and smooth as possible. I feel safe when I go home and am in my apartment at 717 Olympic and that is the best feeling.

The management does not care about complaints and living here will be constant repairs and maintenance. Expect to have your water shut off for the entire day multiple times a month and have lots of people coming in and out of your apartment during a pandemic for maintenance.

717 Olympic is a great community, in a great location in downtown LA. If you're looking for a place to reside in the downtown area, I would highly recommend 717 Olympic being on your list of places to visit.

To sum up my living experience at 717 Olympic, I'd compare it to a wing suite at the Bellagio, with a smaller footprint. 717 Olympic is located in the heart of DTLA across from entertainment venues like, Staple Center, LA Live, Convention Center and great places to eat within blocks. Los Angeles, and Downtown LA is a destination on its own. Being a premier community residence located on the corner of Olympic and Figueroa in the heart of DTLA, is a destination all to itself. Billboard living at its finest. Must see.
The Management Team, Concierge Team, Sales Team, Maintenance Team and Security Staff are always on point. They are very responsive, accomodating and professional. Great Team at 717 Olympic.

717 Olympic is a great choice for apartment living in the DTLA area. The building is very clean and well kept. The staff is professional, courteous and helpful.  Our building manager Ashley always personally returns phone calls. Hector at the concierge desk is genuinely concerned about any issues I may have.  The staff as a group have made me feel important and that they care about my happiness, well being and safety in this building and the surrounding area.   The apartments are laid out very nicely and in great shape. It is surprisingly quiet considering where we are located. The amenities are great and the maintenance crew keeps everything nice and clean. I definitely recommend living here !
Living here has been a very enjoyable experience.  Nice building and staff
I love living here you get to see LA so clearly at night.

From Olga showing us the apartment and assisting us with the application and lease process. Hector assisting in the moving in. Mario assisting in move in procedure and Keesha assisting in evening matters, there's no question 717 was the best decision!

These apartments are great. They have a very helpful and wonderful staff that will help you with all you need. I'm so happy that they also allow dogs and cats. Also with one of the best views of downtown LA that really tops the icing on the cake.
Overall love the property and my apartment. Not happy with my experience with the leasing team. There was poor communication and customer service.

The move-in process has been smooth for the most part, and all employees have been a tremendous help! I would have enjoyed some access to the freight elevator during my process, however it was booked the entire day! :(

We applied during a transition of employees. 

Everyone is super nice, but not the most organized. If you’re applying, be prepared to hound them about progress. Also, it doesn’t seem like they are too familiar with the programs they use. We were delayed due to them not knowing how to use a service they require. If it wasn’t for us being tech savvy, we would’ve never moved forward.

Other then that, everything was stellar

I love this building and my apartment except my neighbors are the worst. I know all apartment living has noise and I can deal with that but this one girl is loud af screaming at her bf in the middle of the night, throwing stuff, moving furniture around at 5am, and stomping around like she Sasquatch. She also sounds like she plays basketball indoors against the walls. I would be more understanding if it was a kid but she doesn’t have one. She’s just inconsiderate! Another neighbor lets their dog go to the bathroom in the halls. Gross. 

Also I have nothing against smoking but the halls reek of it all the time. The noise is the worst part though. I can deal with pets and smoke honestly but the stomping drives me bananas. Management doesn’t do anything to help with the noise too or even ask people to be more considerate. Too bad too because all of my friends I have over love the building too and think about moving here until they hear my awful neighbors being loud af.

New management (Bozzuto) towed my truck and automatically charges “all residents” $270 cleaning fee when moving out. 

I stayed in a unit that faced Hill street and had a balcony. Not the wisest decision. Constant noise from the street - sirens, honking, screaming, and engines roaring. I was sleep deprived most days.

When Bozzuto took over, they decided to tow tenant’s vehicles for parking in an area where tenants had always parked (at least since I lived there). They towed without warning. It cost me $600 to get my truck. And the worse thing is coming to the parking lot and not seeing your truck - I thought it was stolen and this is a place I’m supposed to call home?? 

Then when I moved out and received my move out charges, I was charged $270 for cleaning. When I asked them what had to be clean they simply replied saying all residents are charged a cleaning fee. Okay? That’s not a reasonable explanation. 

Don’t expect to get your full deposit when you move out. The only convenient thing about this location is proximity to work if you’re working in DTLA. Other than that, it’s a dog town with it being close to 5th street. I hope your experience is better than mine.
The apartment is very nice, luxurious, and clean. The leasing agents and management are very friendly and accommodating. Concierge is professional and also friendly.

I've stayed at this complex for almost a year now and I have had great experiences with the building staff! The structure itself has seen better days but everything inside the building has been renovated. Floor plans are really spacious, and pricing is somewhat reasonable comparing to other apartments with similar amenities in the area. 
If you are apartment hunting I will suggest reading more reviews before you sign because that's how I decided on this place, and I'm glad I did my research! 8.5/10 would recommend living here.

Marie, Bill, and Mark are absolutely amazing, especially Marie, who goes above and beyond. They made my move-in experience less stressful and easy. Maintenance is also great. The location is wonderful and my studio is very roomy.

I have lived here for 5 years and I cannot rave enough how awesome our Service/Maintenance Supervisor Carlos.  He and his staff respond to our service and maintenance request with great customer service and timely manner.  He knows my family and makes sure that it is done the right way.
Beautiful apartment, amazing amenities, cool view of downtown, management and maintenance are top notch, they take very good care of their residents!
Excellent location with a staff to match! Very nice property with great amenities.

Canvas LA is a beautiful resort-style community right near downtown. While your right off the 110 you barely even hear the traffic because they sound proofed the walls so good. There's a pool that plays music underwater and a big hot tub (hard to find this large of a size in LA). The movie theater and two gyms and resident's two floor clubs are great for me to bring friends over for lunch (order LA CAFE so good and they deliver). I love showing off where I live. And the staff Bill, Edita and Mark helped me so much with my move and are always helpful everyday with whatever you need. There's a lot of choices in LA, you should go Canvas LA. apartmentName: AVA Hollywood at La Pietra Place
review:
First thing's first, this is a MASSIVE complex.  It's 5 buildings and each building could easily have it's own staff to support the tenants, but there is no where near that staffing.  So, it's really easy to get in the door, get your lease signed, and get moved in.  Once you're here, good luck getting any help from anyone in the lobby about any concerns you have.  The maintenance team and custodial crews are great, and take good care of requests you make, but anything that rises beyond a basic fix or clean up and you'll be waiting weeks to get it fixed, if at all.  Also, sound insulation is terrible here, you hear everything from every direction including the hallways.

All that said, there are some positives.  The gym is great and rarely busy.  Squat racks, heavy dumbbells, plenty of weight lifting machines and an entire level of just cardio equipment.  There are a lot of amenities like multiple rooftops lounges, a decent pool (although not large enough for the community), pool table, and they try with events like regular food trucks, comedy nights, and events like that.

The neighborhood is not that great, it's central Hollywood, but it's the media district, so lots of studios, but not tons to do.  If you walk about 20 minutes in any direction you're in centers with lots of great food and bars, but immediately in the area there isn't anything.

Also, the fire alarms.  I've never lives somewhere with even 2% of the disturbances created by fire alarms here.  There's regular "testing" where they sound the alarms throughout the entire complex, and once every few weeks you can count on the alarms being triggered at 3 AM without explanation.

Overall, just keep in mind that this place isn't "luxury" as it would lead you to believe, that being said the price point isn't outrageous, it can be convenient if you need to travel to the valley.  You could do worse than this spot, but if you're a light sleeper or are annoyed by noise, then you'd do better to spend a little more and find a nicer place.

apartmentName: AVA Hollywood at La Pietra Place
review:
I am highly concerned with this apartment's safety and vetting process of its residents. Last night, people arriving in an armored vehicle entered the premises with the help of several residents. The chaos resulted in tear gas, altercations, and a SWAT team swarming the premises. There is still an ongoing investigation, but the situation seems serious if a whole SWAT team was needed to be involved. Due to the tear gas, the fire alarm was also triggered three separate times every hour or so between around 1AM-4AM. It is unclear why the alarm was pulled again and again and again, even when the threat of fire was gone. A man also ran back and forth down the halls yelling "fire" and pounding on peoples' doors. In retrospect, this may have been a distraction attempt from the other chaos that was happening.

I believe that those in charge were/are not being transparent with what is really going on here. Please be aware that even though the rent is high and the amenities are modern, that this complex is not necessarily safer than more modest apartments. If anything, this complex may be more of a target. I am posting this review because last night's events were truly disturbing and made me question this apartment's safety and the effectiveness of the resident vetting process.

Lets be honest, living in Downtown L.A. is not cheap. After looking at apartments for nearly 3 months, I finally came across the Medici. The two bed and two bath is more than enough space for my roommate and I. At first, I was a little hesitant about how much the rent was (because it was at the edge of my budget), but I couldn't let the opportunity of living in the heart of L.A. slip away. 

Pros: Living at the Medici, I'm literally a 3 minute walk from 7th and Fig, a 8 minute walk to Staples Center / LA Live, and no more than a $5 Uber to any bars or restaurants I want to visit around downtown. The location is everything for this place. You're just out the edge of downtown where you're not dealing with the hustle and bustle, but also close enough to all the activities LA has to offer. You also don't have to drive far to get on the freeway, too (the 110 ramp is right down the street). Aside from the location, the amenities that the Medici offers is also a big money saver. Most apartment gyms don't come equipt with enough equipment to workout on - That's not the case here. The gym has just enough stuff that I decided to not renew my gym membership since I can just workout at home. In addition, the entire apartment complex is clean, quiet, and peaceful. It's just what you need to be around after a 12 hour shift at work. 

Cons: The only "bad" thing I would have to say about the Medici would be the street parking. Each bedroom comes with a parking space, so I don't have a issue with parking. However, when I have guest over, it's a little difficult to find street parking around the area. I usually just tell them to park at the 7th and Fig parking lot, and walk over. It's not a big deal, but it's something to be noted. (I'm sure most downtown complexes have the similar issue though). 

All in all, I'm extremely happy with my experience here. The only thing I hope now is that my roommate renews the lease with me, because I definitely do not want to move out!

Noise Issues: The reason we decided to move was due to noise from the apartment above. I don't know how the previous tenant managed, but for the past year, we didn’t experience any noise problems until the new tenants moved in. They have been making an excessive amount of noise, running around, playing with balls, and stomping from morning until night. Trash Problems: The neighbors have two large trash bins, but they don’t use them. Regardless of the size of the trash, it’s often left in the hallway.

Dog Poops: Dog owners don’t clean up after their pets, and I have to start my mornings stepping over dog poop. I’ve even stepped in it once.

Parking Gate Issues: The parking gate keeps breaking down. Recently, both the car next to mine and the car in front of it had their windows shattered. Also, non-residents frequently park illegally, making it difficult to use the parking lot.

NOTHING about this building is luxury.
