This is the 4th different apartment I've rented in the Phoenix area and its by far the best after living here for 2 years.  The maintenance staff has been the biggest surprise as they're unlike any other complex's staff. At Aria, they're always quick to respond, very communicative and do great work, all of which are characteristics I've never seen anywhere else. The office staff is always very nice, easy to work with and also good at communicating.  The amenities (gym, movie theater, pool, jacuzzi, inside and outside lounge area) are always pretty clean and well maintained. Landscaping and overall property cleanliness is top notch. All of this quality does come at a slightly higher price than expected, and is subject to going up or down yearly with the market, but I wouldn't call the prices 'expensive'. Lastly, while the location of Aria is super convenient, it is a fairly noisy area as most places in Phoenix are. If noise bothers you then just aim for a unit further West (away from Cave Creek Rd.) in the complex. Background: I was a resident for 7 months on a month to month lease. I’m moving due to relocation by my job. 

Like everyone else, I read the bad reviews but I have a friend that has lived here for 1.5 years that told me to ignore those. Therefore I gave it a try. I live in a Casita not one of the towers so that is what I will attest to... 

PROS:
I was the first person to live in my apartment after the “remodel” (see cons) so all appliances and bathroom fixtures were new. New carpet in the bedroom, laminate floors throughout, new sink, toilet, shower/tub combo. 

All utilities included: Lights, sewer, water, trash, antenna from Cox (I suggest buying a better one from Target because you get more channels if you’re too cheap for cable(me)). I purchased internet for about $65 a month. 

The front office and maintenance staff are friendly and helpful. Anytime I made a maintenance request they input it immediately and it was soon fixed. 

There are NO bugs/rats/roaches/critters. The greatest issue I had was the high volume of mosquitos on my back patio due to there being a pond and extremely too many trees. 

The neighbors are friendly enough and they mind there business. There is street parking which is good enough because if you’re in a casita you can park in front of or by your door. I’ve never had an issue w/ break-ins and I travel for weeks at a time and just leave my car parked under one of the towers. 

CONS: 
The “remodel” was not a full remodel. Although everything was new, the walls were plastered and painted but not smoothed. 
The windows are not insulated (which in the grand scheme doesn’t matter because I’m not the one paying the electric bill) and my apartment specifically had no screens, so I could not open them without mosquitoes or flys coming in. 
There is a lack of storage space because the apartments used to be a hotel. 
The walls are thin so you can hear your neighbors if they’re inconsiderate. I lived next to a young couple that often would fight, play music, or have sex really loud and I repeatedly had to ask them to keep quiet. 

Overall, it was a good place to stay that is reasonably priced for the great area that it is in. It is close to all the Biltmore shopping centers, downtown, and the airport.

Let me start by echoing what many recent reviews say, don’t bother reading reviews of Vitri that are a year old (July 2021 or older), as the management and ownership of the building changed at that time.

Vitri, it’s billed as luxury living, but this isn’t true, in fact it’s far from it.

Let’s start with the good. The location is good.

Now for the bad. Vitri is beyond poorly managed.

For a building opened in 2020 it has its fare share of problems. Take for example the trash chutes, an upscale building like Vitri couldn’t possibly have standard spring actuated trash chutes, no, this is luxury living. Instead, Vitri opted for pneumatic actuated trash chutes, which break all the time. This results in people dumping their garbage bags into the hot trash rooms, the smell is awful.

Speaking of smells, Vitri has a problem with sewer gas.

The parking garage has never been cleaned. The floors are filthy and you’ll be tracking that dirt into your home. Not to mention there are spider webs covering almost every light in the garbage. Good thing they charge you a monthly fee for pest control.

There are endless problems with the gym, the pool, the sauna, and the common areas in general. From broken equipment, unsanitary conditions, and some of your fellow tenants, we’ve got it all in this luxury building.

Many units have problems with their HVAC system. During the summer when you are forced to blast your AC, condensation will accumulate in the HVAC’s drip tray. If it was installed correctly the buildup of condensation will flow to a drain and you’ll never notice it. But, if you’re among the unlucky units that had the HVAC Installed incorrectly, then that condensation will begin to drip, make sure to have a bucket handy.

While the kitchens are nicely appointed with GE Cafe appliances, they seem to have forgotten about vent hoods. Unless you have a balcony, you can only open your window about two inches. Consequently, if you try to cook anything that will produce smoke, you’re going to set off the smoke detectors. Luxury.

Vitri features Whirlpool washers and ventless dryers. The dryers are terrible. Make sure to clean both lint traps, but don’t be surprised when that doesn’t help.

This is a Luxury building, and the rents are definitely in the Luxury price range. But, don’t expect your Luxury rent to cover everything.

Vitri had potential, it has a good location, but it’s let down by a subpar management company that appears to be in way over their heads.

Recently, many apartments have been converted to short-term Airbnb rentals by the property management, so be aware of that. The garage concrete will dirty your car daily, the stairwells are pretty dirty, but maintenace is usually pretty good. There are $200 worth of fees on top of the advertised rent.

The floor is really poorly applied vinyl as far as I can tell, and a basic office chair will tear into it with no problem. If you plan on having a desk and a chair, get a floor mat.  

I haven't had a good nights sleep since I moved in. 

Every day of the week I wake up between 7am and 8am to either the neighbors dog barking (usually lasts from 8am-5pm at least, I assume they are gone at those times), construction on the roof (I'm on the top floor) (but you have to sign a construction noise addendum that has no expected end date), or my other neighbor practicing the trumpet.

I've complained to management about the dog, and it usually stops for 3-4 days and then starts back up. Frankly, it seems like they spend more time trying to fill the rest of the rooms, than they do taking care of the people who live here.

And lastly, the parking here is a ABSOLUTE NIGHTMARE. If you are expecting to have someone over for any amount of time, for literally anything, good luck. There are around 10 guest spots (about 7 more after business hours) for the entire building. That's it. And now, you have to register them for 24 hours at a time. This means that my S.O. who doesn't live with me, who usually stays over from Thursday night to Saturday afternoon, has to have a spot reserved 3 times, and if we don't get it, even once, they will be towed or our plans cut short. 

To add to this, management recently started enforcing assigned parking spaces. Parking wasn't an issue before, the garage is barely 3/4 full. Originally they put me in a parking garage that didn't even connect to the elevator on my side of the building. After I complained they moved me into the main parking garage but still decently far from the elevator next to my apartment (my apartment is only about 40 feet from one of the elevators, but a 4-5 minute walk from any of the other ones). Finally they moved me a third time and now I'm at an ok place. I consistently got a better parking spot without assigned parking. Before I never had to park even remotely close to as far as I am now. Seems like they had little care about where your apartment actually was when giving out parking spaces.

By and large, parking is completely unsustainable and with the enforcement of guest spot reservations, almost unusable for basic living.

I have no plans to renew after learning these things. And the only reason I haven't broken the lease yet is that the buyout includes all concessions so I'd have to pay around $9k to buyout.

Issues such as shower heads with poor water pressure, noisy AC caused by the damper (in my unit in the bedroom), missing peep hole at front door, bedroom closet missing a rod bracket shelf support, kitchen drawers not properly closing, dryer always shutting off (error message), several pieces of the flooring lifting up and lastly the stove with no vent system and no windows to open (which at times sets the smoke detector off). Assistant PM & Maintenance Manager - confirms that this is typical build up for about 4-6 months, so it was most likely changed right when the last people moved out. VP of Multifamily - asked when is a good time to call and never called. Then proceed to pass me down to the Operations Manager

This is by far the worst experience with any rental community I have ever had and I will never recommend them to anyone.

The past year, however, has shown some growth. They've upgraded many apartments, torn out and replaced the basketball court, put in a dog park (small, but can run and play with your dog off leash), and improved the pool area. 

Maintenance still is not the best for certain things - they have been in multiple times every year to fix my air conditioning before they FINALLY fixed it (design problem in the plumbing so not sure how much of that is their fault). But they are responsive and friendly!

Pros: reasonably priced, many upgraded apartments, good access to necessities, gym (small weight room with cardio machines), excellent pool, responsive maintenance and management, as well as quiet - cement block walls between apartments minimizes much of the noise. 

Cons: not all apartments are upgraded, but rent on all have increased dramatically to pay for upgrades (my rent went up over $100/month and I cannot upgrade my apartment without transferring to a different apartment), dog rules not strictly enforced (many residents do not pick up after their dogs, have large dogs that they send to do their business off leash and unsupervised), and complaints about neighbors (reasonable complaints - parking/blocking assigned parking spot repeatedly, dog issues, being harassed by neighbors, loud music in the wee hours) not only not quickly addressed, but it is revealed WHO made the complaint (hence the harassment). 

Overall, this is a good apartment complex with complex issues. It meets my needs, and though there are flaws, the positive aspects FAR outweigh the negatives.

When I moved in I had to pass a background which I was so happy to do meant we all did doubt that's happening now. The property is super dirty now and it smells like nothing but weed everywhere, where before it even smelled nice. The pool is cleaned liked once a week. Just horrible don't make the mistake of coming here. Nice apartments at the same price around us!

Worst place ever... Yesterday (1/16/17) without warning or notification, they shut off water to the apartment to upgrade the water heaters. My wife went to the office to find out why, and was told they had no idea that the water heaters would be replaced today and that she should be happy they are replacing the water heaters. Water finally came back on last night some time around 6pm. Now it's 6:15am on (1/17/17) and there is no hot water, called emergency maintenance and was told it won't be fixed until sometime after 7am. This is just one of many issues me and my wife have had with the office staff of this place.

The Residences on High Street is a great place to live. The staff is professional, responsive, and personable. Many excellent restaurants are within a few minutes walking distance. The Desert Ridge Marketplace Shopping Center is just next door. The Mayo Clinic is less than two miles away providing easy access to world class medical care. Virtually everything one needs is within a few minutes of the Residences.
This is as close to getting an urban lifestyle as you can in Phoenix. Shops, resturants and bars just downstairs. Major shopping center (Desert Ridge) within walking distance.

The Residences on High Street provides a high level, urban styled living experience in the Desert Ridge, North Scottsdale community. It is an urbane, clean, enticing, and engaging setting complete with numerous shops, amenities and nightlife.
The Residences on High Street is a lovely apartment community in a convenient, bustling setting. I have lived here six years and consider it my forever home!

Great location for food and entertainment but complex has aged and management/ownership don’t seem to be in any hurry to keep up or renovate. Complex can be on the noisy side but units are built solid. Technology is way behind other properties and could use a big upgrade like electronic locks, wifi thermostats, and cameras. I get the feeling Management spends as little as possible to keep property going. Also billing is a little suspect with a lot of hidden charges in month bill.
I absolutely love it here. The thing that got me was not only the location but having floor to ceiling windows. I love the natural light!

There are multiple residents having issues with bed bugs.  The treatment provided by Mike's Pest control does not work.  My boyfriend's apt has been treated 6 times.  There are drugs, prostitutes and multiple homeless trespassing on property.  No on site security. Used condoms found in parking lot and drug paraphernalia!  Managment does not address issues rather they tell you other people have it worse off. I highly recommend skipping this property when you are searching for a place to stay.

My fiance and i got our first place together here almost a year ago and it's a very convenient location. There is a free bus that comes right in  front of the complex and takes you to Metro Mall and Christown Mall until the light rail is finished. Yes! the light rail is almost done and is right in front of our apartments! Maintenance is always very prompt to tending to all of our needs. within a couple of hours calling the office maintenance are here fixing whatever we needed done. The staff here is really nice and are always having a good time in the office but they are very quick with helping us out. I am definitely renewing my lease because the price they have is great for the location and includes everything but electric and the Mpower box is fine with me
We love this place. They make you feel like you are part of their family. They listen to you. They keep this place really clean. We want to live no place else but here! :-)

My daughter and myself don't want to be anywhere else but here! The office people listens to you and work with you! I just feel like I am truly home! We look at other places, but no place compares to this place! Everything you need is right here!

Numerous issues that you don't want to deal with.  Massive cockroach issue, parking issues, management issues, marijuana use issue,..the list goes on and on.  It's touted as a luxury apartment but it's anything but.  Still living here, won't in a few months when lease it up.   I'm a realtor, know what should be going on and what shouldn't.  There's a reason they offer free rent.  Don't do it!!!

Where do we start?
Rents raised more then 10% for last two years in a row.
Mandatory Cable and door-side trash collection fees of $100/mo.
Fire Pit out of commission for close to a year.
Hot Tub RARELY operating.
Key Fobs don't work.
No extra/guest parking as Cielo puts no limits on how many cars a 3-bedroom home can add to the already exhausted parking problems.
... and NOW... just as the weather is about to warm up, Cielo decides that THIS is the best time to remodel the fire pit. Doing so will shut down the pool area for at least 6 weeks as we head into the heat of late spring.
Why didn't they do it during the winter months when it wasn't working and children didn't need the pool for exercise and cooling off?
The answer i rec'd was "It's not my decision".

Living here however, IS YOUR DECISION.
I will be leaving at the end of my lease.

Since Stellar Management took over here, the renter's support is outstanding  ... maintenance workers Jae and Thomas are exceptional with any requests ... Scott and Heather, on site managers, are always available and very responsive to any questions or requests .... Calls and email are answered very timely ... neat exterior and well cared for buildings ... quiet community ... could not be happier living here ....
It’s quiet, the staff is friendly and the front office has such great communication with residents. This complex is both kid and pet friendly. Would recommend to anybody who asks!

I recently moved here and it is an amazing apartment for a relatively affordable rate! The community is very quiet and peaceful so if you want to keep to yourself you will have no problem doing that here. The staff has been nothing but pleasant and accommodating!
very peaceful environment. great interior design for a very reasonable rent price! management is very dedicated to your needs!

Villa Toscana is a great location. Banks, restaurants,grocery store, mall and many other things within walking distance. Apartment was not quite as advertised. Studio has no microwave and no dishwasher. Staff is nice and professional. Im four months into my 12 month lease and will most likely sign another year when this one is up.
Villa Tascana is a great place to live.  Many great amenities. Grocery store, gas station, banks and resteraunts within walking distance.

Great apartment, I had just a few issues I would like to share.  Since my time living there, which happens to be roughly about three years now, I've enjoyed my stay.  Rent was reasonable, office staff were nice, neighborhood is great, but one advice I would leave for future potential residents is before you sign your name on the lease make sure everything in your apartment works. Dishwasher, oven, fridge, etc...

I'm really surprised that a community of this size isn't more closely monitored by management, and that we don't receive regular communication besides announcements of office hours/closures and food trucks. I have had to call the security vendor numerous times for after hours noise. I live on the lap pool and it's party time on the weekends during the summer with loud, drunk people and music. As well, the apartments themselves are poorly constructed and you can hear neighbors having basic conversations, open and closing doors, drawers, flushing toilets, etc. A very noisy living environment, particularly in my location.
I have never lived in such an amazing apartment complex/neighborhood. My friend actually just moved in after touring because she loved it just as much as I do!
I have always thought the maintenance crew and office staff are incredible at this community. Five star all the way! Their kindness stands out above all others.

I loved living at Citrine but I am disappointed about the increase in rent. I had lived there for almost 3 years and felt like in the end the company would rather have me leave than try to work out a new lease agreement.
You cannot beat the location & I Iove my floorplan! I would just warn them about the cleanliness and poor condition of some of the amenities.

I do really like the idea of this building, however there are a lot of little problems like.....neighbors smoking pot on their balconies, smoking pot in apts, smoking in the park, very dirty stairwells and common areas that new residents dont really see, broken entrance doors and a lot of stories of theft from the parking garage.

Pillar/56th Street Management does not have security at night - 1 person walks through once a night and then on to other complexes. And management does not care that people have had their garages broken into and stuff stolen. Management/Pillar just shrugs their shoulders
Can't wait to end my lease.

Overall, this complex has it's good and bad things and my goal from this review is just to inform anyone considering it.
The goods: amenities are great, pool is awesome, gym is well equipped, location is perfect if you're a big fan of Desert Ridge (even if you're not , you'll become one), and a big kudos to maintenance. Even during the tough times of Covid they managed to come out and fix whatever they could! When you know that you can trust maintenance, that's a good thing in a complex.
The negatives honestly come down to the customer service, unfortunately. Everyone there is relatively nice however, I felt that my entire time there I was fighting to get anything resolved and the professionalism was lacking greatly.
From minor issues such as retrieving mail, they quickly dismiss and there's no assistance to help residents. It's kind of a you're on your own type of thing. To greater things like noise complaints that took months of trying to resolve. It just felt like anything you bring up to them and ask for assistance with, they either dismiss or it's a he-said, she-said type of situation . My noise complaint issue took 4 months to resolve and was only resolved when everything I've been reporting for 4 months was addressed by a police call in the middle of the night and proof of the incident was submitted. This type of thing leaves the residents feeling pretty helpless in my opinion. As much as it probably doesn't seem from this review, I tend to stray away from ever complaining about anything. I like to give people the benefit of the doubt and patience. I was repeatedly proven wrong though.
The summary of my review really is, if you have no issues, this place will be great for you and you'll enjoy it! It's nice and clean and neat and provides a great social life. If issues do arise, I can't say with confidence at all that they're there to back you up or help you. I know there are rules and policies that need to be followed. I just didn't feel like the complex help up their end of sticking to lease agreements and living in a place like that makes me a little uncomfortable. I hope the situation is different for others and I hope that they feel more supported! :)

Our company has rented these apartments for our executives and the experiences our executives and I have had with the apartments has been incredible. Specifically, the staff has proven to be incredibly helpful and kind. I work directly with Kyle Sobota on a regular basis. He responds to our company’s needs with competence and efficiency. I cannot thank him and the staff enough for all their help.

DO NOT MOVE HERE! Coming from someone who has lived here for 5+ years read this review. 

Construction - there is 360 construction around the entire community creating excessive noise and extremely unsafe amounts of dirt and debris. 

The desert behind the property was advertised to many as a Preserve... That is not the case.

This project will not be complete until the end of 2021. 

The property management has done NOTHING TO ASSIST. Not even allowing us to break our lease because of this unsafe environment.

Disgusting, dirty, rip off. Lie about their amenities. Pool not heated as they say. They don’t fix things when they break in the apartment. Dog poop all over the place, the walkways wreak of dog urine.

Amenities are good enough, not amazing but adequate. Gym is not as equipped but serves its purpose. Neighbors are quiet for the most part. Management is chill and professional most of the time except getting calls regarding fining for leaving out smelly trash before trash pickup time. 
First of all, there was no update of email received that trash pickup time has been changed back to a later time after curfew is over. In the email, it says "please be sure to have your trash bagged, tightly tied and put in the bin outside your door by 4:30, for collection to begin at 5 pm". That means, any time before 4.30pm is good to leave the trash out. Yet, we got a call that says they will let us go this one time for leaving out trash that smells (trash obviously smells), and that next time, there would be a $25 fine. That is not appreciated at all. We understand and appreciate the importance of keeping the hallway clean and odorless but warning us with a possible fine next time is not appreciated. Other than that, no problem so far.
Es un lugar tranquilo y con un espacio muy agradable y muy bonito
I've been at Esteban Park for 8yrs and my overall experience has been great. If something breaks or goes wrong, they're quick to fix it. Staff is kind and property is maintained well.

I have loved being a resident at Esteban Park! I have been here for over two years now. The office staff are always friendly and helpful, they've always been there to solve any issues first thing. they maintain the property beautifully, no complaints here. I love being here with my family; grateful to be apart of this community.

I've lived here for about 8 months and we've had a great experience. Everyone is so nice and friendly. They are very attentive and helpful. Management is willing to work with you and are fast and efficient when something needs to be fixed. The apartments are tranquil, clean and safe.

I’ve had a great experience working with Kathy & Lulu. They are always professional, friendly, and willing to go above and beyond to help. Whether it’s answering questions, assisting with maintenance requests, or providing updates, Kathy consistently makes sure that everything runs smoothly.
Overall got to say it's been one of the best places I've called home team members always work with me and never rude the maintenance is on top of their work and overall community is clean

My car was broken into property refuses to light the parking area will not hire security and will not dislcose to me frequency of break ins. I have lived here for 3 months. The staff is unhelpful and prone to mistakes and work orders no matter how impactful can take weeks to get done and water is shut off alot.

If I could give this a zero I would.  Very high turnover in staff. Had 3 diff office managers  in the 10mos I lived there. They surprise you with unexpected move out charges and have NO flexibility in giving you a payment plan, so if you live here save your $ so you can pay outrages unjustified sketchy charges at the end. You have to deal with corporate to pay those charges and corporate is very rude- you’re just a dollar sign to them, so good luck with that. They don’t do a very good background check for your neighbors.  I had to call the police on mine for drunkenly peeing off his balcony (above me) and exposing himself to me. I ended up having to unexpectedly move out for my safety and going to court. And after all that I’m still dealing with Serafina coming after me to put new carpet in my old unit. I’m a professional in my 30s and this place does not value their good paying tenants. This is the worst place I’ve had to deal with and the worst decision I’ve made for a place to live. The location is nice but not worth the turmoil this place caused me.  The staff may seem nice at first but they will have 90% turnover every few months and you’ll be constantly dealing with people who do not know how to handle things.

Location is great! Bus routes including the free circular are right in front of the complex. Shopping and dining are within walking distance. And easy access to major freeways. The neighborhood is quite with little to no crime, in the Ahwatukee foothills community. I am resigning my lease for the third year, this is due to the clean comfortable grounds, and the friendly staff. I like that they know me and my dog by name. Maintenance is handled quickly, we have had some trouble with hot water this past year but the staff kept us updated on shutoffs and repairs, and did everything they could to have hot water for showers available for us in non effective buildings. The pool is sparkling and the patio furniture is the nicest I have seen. Rent is fair compared to other complexes in the area. My biggest dislike is the kitchen, these are older apartments and the kitchens need to be updated. So if your looking for a great place to live in Phoenix AZ come to Serafina and tel them I sent you!

I've lived here at Serafina for 3 month's now and it's been a great experience so far. Not only is the community and staff amazing, but the location is unlike any other. It's close to anything you can think of and the i10 freeway is less than a mile away. 2 Thumbs up!
Beautiful flooring with a wood look, wonderful walk in closets in all rooms, very light and airy with many windows and patio doors. I love this place and have never lived anywhere like it.

I moved into Shade in 2019 and had a great relationship with all the staff - especially management. I talked to my neighbors frequently and we all enjoyed the property.

When knightvest took over, we all noticed how management did not seem to value good kind communication. Gates were mismanaged (codes not secure + cards stopped working), lights started being installed (terrible blue non-relaxing). Staff was quitting. Online accounts were bungled. Lots of ineptitude.

One day I heard someone out on my balcony installing a new light. I interrogated this worker and he said we were given notice. I went to the office upset by the intrusion. The office said they had given notice. 

My neighbors that I spoke with all said the same thing. No notice given. Nothing. Management was becoming brazen and nervous about their missteps was the consensus among the residents I spoke with.

So I moved. I worked out a deal with management to pay a certain amount and move out as early as possible. I covered all bills. When I called 2 weeks before my scheduled move out date to be done with everything, they told me I could not move out early and said some utterly ridiculous things to me. They manufactured a new bill for me that was nearly 700 additional to what we agreed to. I called bs and disputed. They would not budge. They sent me to collections and have told the collection agent I was aggressive and violent. I have even hired a law firm to ankle bite the credit bureaus to remove it. It's been a terrible experience.

So... think twice before moving here. Ask the residents if you can find one. Management does not have your back.

We have lived here for a year now, and it had been fine. A new management company just took over and now it's gotten scary in a way I honestly thought was something only seen in tv dramas. Now we have suddenly been charged for all kinds of things. For example, a garage opener with a dead battery cost me $51 to replace as a "damaged" garage opener. Another example, and this one really scares me... they gave 2 days notice that they were entering the apartment to install new electronic door locks and air conditioning control pads. And then we got charged for them! Have you ever had to buy the new fixtures or appliances that an apartment decided to install without giving you a choice. I don't own these fixtures... at least I don't think I do. Who knows. But I certainly bought them. Now im wondering how to get out of here without them messing with my life too much. I feel like complaining to them would just put us on the radar of the two lifestyle corporate live ins they installed in the front apartment. So slipping away quietly seems safest.  We keep getting new legal notices stuck to our doors letting us know exactly what they're allowed to do and what they aren't liable for in the future... it's majorly sketchy. I'd steer clear. It's too bad because they are really making the grounds look nice. But yikes...

Let me preface this by saying I've sold higher-end real estate for 25 years and just relocated to the area for family reasons.  I lived here for 6 months in 2018 while looking for a home to buy and have nothing but positive things to say about the staff, the apartments, and the grounds.  The staff was responsive, friendly, and helpful.  The apartments are clean, somewhat updated, and allowed good light in.  The grounds and pool areas were well-kept.  I never saw any signs of vandalism or heard late-night partying, and my unit looked out towards the main pool area.  I saw one cockroach while I lived there, but I noticed unsatisfied renters complaining about them in literally every complex I researched.  When you think about it, it's almost impossible to avoid in an irrigated, shared living situation where trash is collected from the units, and I thought they did an excellent job managing pests.

Parking for residents and guests is amazing as there's always a ton of it...much better than other places I looked at in Scottsdale, and the complex is really well located.  It offers easy access off the 101, is about 25 minutes from the airport without traffic (a good location to minimize traffic issues, by the way), and is next door to and across the street from a ton of different restaurants and shopping.  Overall, it was a great experience.

The people at the office is beyond rude and no one would take responsibility for their own mistakes making the tenant pay for their lack of irresponsibility and unfairness. There is absolutely no communication between them. I am completely baffled. And their appliances don't work either and multiple maintenance request has been submitted and maintenance would say they work just fine when they don't.  I regret signing a lease here.

The crime rate is terrible in this apartment and the  security dispatch is terrible as well.  Pool has been closed for vandalism on multiple occasions. Tenants have had strangers approach doors and attempt to come in to apartments. There is also a roach infestation problem and apartment units are dirty and poorly maintained. Worth looking elsewhere. I lived here for a few months and could not finish my lease . Only plus is that the staff is helpful sometimes.

This complex is outdated for the money.  You pat 1k plus for the smallest unit..and it is totally not worth it.  The hardware in the kitchen and bathrooms are dated..and or chipped... the stainless steel.. is a knockoff version.. the leasing staff in horrible.  The pool areas are always vandalized by the students or the rift raff in the complex.  I moved here and it was the worst decision.

We moved here because the price was great and we love the location, close to my son’s school and several places near by as well. I regret that decision…. They are always having problems with the water here it is getting shut off constantly to “fix” problems and then a week or two later same thing with very little notice as well. There are a ton of amenities and the pool is great but also small for a complex this big.  You can hear your neighbors… the walls and floor are not made well at all. On top of that stuff in the apartment is cheaply made and breaks easily (appliances). I would say pay the extra money for a better place and skip this one!

Listen to every bad review about this apartment complex. Everything is outdated, the pricing is outrageous, they do a sloppy fast job at prepping the apartment before you move in, maintenance requests took over 10 days for them to be completed (A/C leaking was one of them) because the have TWO maintenance workers, front office workers are rude and never have answers for you and overall it's just not worth it here. I moved almost a year ago and they are harassing me for a move out cleaning fee. I had the apartment professionally cleaned when I moved out. It was cleaner than I received it. If I could give zero stars I would. DO NOT RENT HERE or with ANY Avenue 5 affiliated company !!!!!!

I hope I can save a prospective tenant from living in this nightmare – chose anywhere else but here to live. 

My significant other and I moved into a 2BD 2BA in the fall. Since day one we have had nothing but issues with our unit and the property management. Prior to moving in the leasing office would rarely answer phone calls and never return any messages, our lease information was incorrect and needed to be corrected multiple times. This was frustrating since we were moving cross country. On move in day we discovered half of our major appliances were inoperable and it took the management a full week to replace them. We get kicked out of the office any time we voice any negative feedback. The property maintenance staff closes out work orders even when incomplete. The gates around the entire property do not work and gives the false sense of a gated community. The pool area is deceiving because the hot tubs rarely work and the pools have too many chemicals and have ruined multiple pairs of swim suits. One night when returning from the store we found a homeless woman inside one of the broken garages. In response to our email reporting the incident management replied “the office is not the one to take care of it (The Homeless individual) because the best we can do is ask them to leave”.  

The latest incident has been management’s choice of the exterior painting company. We have googled the company and they have a 2.4 star rating with numerous accounts of personal property damage and negative commentary about their business practices. We discovered this after our own personal account of personal property damage. When I went to office to offer feedback about their project I was immediately kicked out of the office and told to email the property manager. After emailing the property manager I did not get a response until I went back into the office and was kicked out again when I informed the assistant manager that I was going to pursue legal action. This finally elicited a response from the property manager. The only recommendation I received was to use our own renters insurance to replace the items that were damaged by their contracted painting company. 

After this last experience I am in disbelief that I will have to see this lease through. I hope this post finds someone looking at this apartment community and influences their decision to choose elsewhere.

This Avenue 5 leasing company is not pleasant to deal with. After speaking to the leasing agent,Veronica, I went online and completed an application. I then had some additional questions about  the property. I left several voice mails and emails with no response. My final email “cancel my application “ got me a response, finally, after a week. I explained I will not live in a complex  that you can’t get a response from in less than a week. She did apologize and assured  me  my refund of 256.90 (they keep 50 application fee, original payment of 306.90) would be returned and could take between 10 to 12 days. Here we are at a month later and no refund, no email response on inquiries and no phone call back from voice mails. I would seriously hesitate before renting here

I have been a very happy resident here at San Melia for 23 years since May 19, 1999 when first built. I hope to remain here forever.  Ahwatukee is the best Phoenix has to offer as far as convenience to grocery stores, Target, AMC, and so much more.
Great location. Dont bother trusting the amenities photos online. Its all broken, trashed, and unusable.

Melrose Villa Apartments is the perfect place to raise children.  The apartment complex has an onsite library for children to come and complete their homework as well as check out various educational books and pamphlets on just about any subject.  Melrose  Villa is in close proximity to schools and malls for shopping.  We are right across the street from public transportation which is a plus for those who do not have personal transportation. What i love most about the complex is the tutoring sessions after school to help students with their homework.
had a leak from upstairs after several day they came out to look at it then waited another day for a third party to make the repair and no one has come out to fix the hole in the ceiling yet
Staff was helpful during process also gave us an exclusive deal moving in the month of February . Has complex has lots of features like pool amd park for the kids area looks nice amd maintained
So far it has been great. The Office staff is very helpful and the maintenance team gets any issues done quickly. It seems quite and I look forward to making this my home.

I’ll start with roaches, myself and every tenant I’ve spoken too, has them as an issue, pest control only comes once a week. They’ll be nice to you your first month or two, then they’ll begin to hand out fines whenever they get the chance. Overly strict patio policies use words such as “unsightly items” as a fineable offense so they can charge you whatever they want (amount not listed in lease agreement) for any item they find ugly, with a 10 day notice to remedy or they’ll begin evictions. Even adding lights or some potted plants is against policy. On the patio is a laundry room and the water heater with a small shelf for storage, otherwise all storage has to be kept inside the home.They’ll even fine you if your window curtains aren’t white, So it’s aesthetically pleasing to visitors and potential residents. Even though they have the addendum in the lease agreement that they can change your assigned parking space, from day 1 of my lease, they have refused to change my spot from the opposite corner of the entire complex to somewhere even close to my apartment.
Pretty quite and takes care of things quick. Relaxing place.
Es bueno para vivir los parqueaderos estan iluminados y cuando llamas a mantenimiento para que arreglen algo te lo arreglan rapido son muy amables hasta el momento la experiencia a sido buena.
I moved in ten years ago and finally moved out recently.  The three key reasons I stayed so long were kind and fair management, good maintenance and no scorpions and spiders.  Check them out.

I have lived off and on at this apartments since I first moved in 2006. I lived there till 2011 moved out and return again in 2018. Moved out in 2019 to get married. 

But coming back home !  Staff amazing. Apartments clean and safe property. 

If you want a safety and staff that care.  This is your place.

I've been living here 4 over 10 years. Whenever I have an issue, it is dealt with. If something breaks down it is always fixed promptly. If I ever have a rent issue , they always work with me. It's been a great 10+ years. I am ready for a two-bedroom and I plan to stay here. Thank you Rancho Sierra Apartments.?

Management is awful unless you are liked. We have lived here way too long.  The apartments are average not updated at all. The apartments are infested with roaches and kids are everywhere.  The laundry room is not the best at all and pools are not sparkling blue.  I would look other places. Moving to Chandler

Inflexible and rude on several occasions. I wouldn't recommend signing a lease here. Slow to repair in every instance and repairs were shoddy when performed. There are plenty of other complexes in this area that will provide a much higher level of service and amenity.

My family has lived here for 2 years.  We liked the location (close to the 51 and Scottsdale), and the apartment (one of the patio homes).  We were initially told about recent upgrades, but upon move in, it looked more like they just put in a new stove, microwave and fridge, but the rest of the apartment was rather dated.  Not a deal breaker, but in 2 years, the rent has increased substantially while nearly no improvements to the overall property have been done.  
Understandably, when storms would blow through, clean up is not always immediate.  I found, that although the maintenance crews would travel through daily, all downed tree limbs were left for over a week, leaving the grounds looking messy.  
Any repairs we needed done were generally handled quickly and professionally and the office staff have always been pleasant to deal with.
Although we asked for our lease renewal terms 2 months out, we weren't given our renewal lease until 6 days before we would need to give our 30 day notice.
Overall, I would recommend the place as the cost was much lower than other places closer to Scottsdale, but personally, I could not justify the cost for what we were getting.
Roach infested, half working washer and dryers, maintenance requests never get filled unless you ask over and over, homeless people wandering, drug transactions in the parking lot.

Very peaceful and quiet. Great area! There's a park right across the street as well as the YMCA. Spectrum mall is also right around the corner along with Walmart, target, Ross, Petco...ect
Moreover the master bedroom is to due for! HUGE!

I have lived here for soon nine years.  When I moved in, the property was very underperforming.  Lack of care, indifferent management, etc.

That has all changed within the last two years since the arrival of the new manager.  The property fairly shines these days.  Yard maintenance is excellent, the laundry rooms have been secured so that they are no longer homeless shelters.  The manager walks the property daily.

The office ladies, who have been here years, are also one of the bright spots in the place.  Helpful, caring, involved, polite. I am very grateful that they are here.

My apartment is fairly soundproof and rarely do I hear the neighbors.  That being said, the property is relatively quiet both during the day and at night.  The remote-control gates, which in the past prior to the new manager, worked only sporadically, now work nearly 24/7, reducing unwanted traffic into the complex.

The Maintenance Department Manager takes care of repairs on an excellent triage basis.  Serious issues are dealt with immediately, etc.  Because of the labor shortage, there has been unfortunate turnover in this department and he is continually having to retrain new staff.  This manager, however, is very appreciated by the tenants.

The new manager is making noted efforts to turn the property into a community.  Community events are held throughout the year, especially now so since the worst of the pandemic has lifted.

There are two areas that require improvement, however.  One is the pool and the area around the pool which are not as clean as they were in years past.  The other is the jacuzzi and the same comments hold true.  In the overall scope of things, these are minor items that can easily be addressed.

3. Garbage disposal and dishwasher (but standard faucets).

Cons: 
1. Wall color and cabinets are outdated: walls are an ugly cream and cabinets are a very very dark wood that makes it hard to see inside them.

3. Air conditioning and bathroom fan are a little noisy.

Make sure that you get a full break-down of extra fees:

Parking - $15 + Tax
Trash - $47
Common Area Electricity - $12.46
Sewer - $10.20
Pest Control - $6
Common Area Gas - $6.46 (what the heck is this?)
Rent Tax - $44
Renter's Insurance - $15

These are all different charges that are not included in your rent (but billed to you in your payment portal on top of your rent) and are in addition to your Water, SRP and Cable/Internet bill.  None of the charges above were disclosed with my rent quote when I moved in (I asked what extra charges I would have and they said "none"). Not a big deal but some others don't charge for many of these things or all the above charges (except tax) are included for a flat $30 at some places.

I lived here for a full year and decided not to renew my lease due to the multiple reasons listed below:

***Hidden fees (monthly and at move-out):
1. I was present for the final inspection before move out and informed that we would have no fees except for the standard cleaning fees; however, to my surprise upon move-out, I was charged $642 to replace both carpets in our 2 bedroom apartment. 
2. Our monthly rent bill was incorrect 9 out of the 12 months we lived there. Although they always corrected it, it was an inconvenient hassle to spend about 30-60 minutes resolving this every month.

***Constant maintenance issues that take months to be resolved:
1. When I just moved into my new unit, the A/C broke and it took them 8 attempts over the course of 3 weeks to fix it. Worst of all, when maintenance finally fixed it on the 8th try, I came home to find bright orange paint all over my bathroom, which ruined both my bath mats and towels.
2. Our hot water would not stay hot for showers for more than 5 minutes. That required 4 maintenance appointments and was never fully resolved.
3. Glass kept popping out of the window frame, which posed a physical danger. We first made the repair request in 10/18 and it was not resolved until 4/19.
4. The Juliette balcony flooded every single time it rained. We were informed that "nothing could be done" to fix this issue.
5.The hot tub worked about 60% of the time I was living there.

***Frequent staff turn over: every time you had a question or concern you spoke to a different person. They routinely acted completely surprised and unaware of an issue that was supposedly documented multiple times. Resolving each of these individual maintenance issues took hours out of my schedule.

***Safety issues: there were multiple instances of motorcycle, bicycle, and package thefts. The cameras in the parking garage are inoperable and therefore useless.

***Issues with cleanliness: At first, the complex was clean and nice; however, the condition gradually deteriorated. For instance, the smell from the trash room would seep into the hallways. There was a rotting cockroach that remained in the same position in the stairwell for 5 months. 

***Lots of Short-term vacation rental units: they have been renting out a large portion of the units in the complex on Wanderjaunt (like Airbnb). With the large number of short-term vacation renters, they were not able to replenish the amenities (e.g., coffee) in a timely manner.

I’m very impressed with everything!! I got into the apartment without looking and I L??VE IT!! The ladies in the office are truly great, helpful, and they actually care. I would not look elsewhere. Come and see your NEW home!! ????
I love my new apartment complex. They are clean, discreet and very comfortable.

If I could give this place negative 5 stars, I would. 
The apartment complex itself is huge, ugly, and not maintained at all. 
This place is definitely understaffed. The staff here is useless and clueless. The maintenance crew is a two or three man group who I always see just driving around in messed up golfcarts just sitting around or chatting. 
If you need something fixed in your apartment, good luck with that. Even after you report something three of four times, no one will come by and fix it for you. You literally have to constantly remind them of your request everyday because they cannot handle how many apartments they have to maintain.
There are drug addicts everywhere and people digging around in the dumpsters all the time. 
The apartment themselves have ugly, old carpeting. There is always a roach or bed-bug infestation. The appliances do not work right or at all. Walls have patches and holes. 
The laundry facilities they provide are cheap.    
My car was stolen out of the parking lot here but thankfully it was recovered by the Police Department.
