Some tenants look like they just got out of prison. Other tenants are families with kids everywhere.
The staff says the complex is a drug-free zone, but that is very much a lie. As long as rent is being paid, I don't think they care about who is living there.
A couple was arguing very loudly, out in the open in front of their children using obscenities with no regard for others around them.
THIS PLACE IS THE WORST.
So please save yourself money, time, and many headaches and avoid this place/area entirely.

Lived here for 2 years and it was a good value for the money. The neighborhood is not bad and close to shopping, the airport, etc. There was a cute little dog park and no big things to complain about.

terrible management  I would never live here in a million years
 the worst experience I've ever had at a leasing office. I came here to look for an apartment  and the leasing office was locked so I had to call to get info.  Phone was answered by James G.  he was extremely unhelpful, unprofessional and   lazy. made me wait outside in hot sun for 20 minutes to take a tour. Gave me incorrect information, l was lost in the complex and he refused to answer the phone until I called with blocked my number !!!!  terrible

Living at Mandarina has been very nice! Pretty quiet community of mostly young professionals. The office staff is always friendly and helped me out with whatever I need. This is the only apartment community I found that offers a student discount which is very helpful! The pet rent is also very cheap! The only issue is parking. Sometimes it is hard to find a spot after 7 if you have two cars. There is only one assigned spot. Garages are available but pretty expensive at $65 a month! Besides the small negatives, I love living here! Very nice place for the price.

Our apartment community is nestled off the beaten path here on E. Washington street, and if you take the time to visit you'll find, our neighbors are the best you'll ever meet.  Easy access to the freeway, and any to business nearby, via car, bus, light rail or bike, whichever you'd like to try. They have many floor plans to choose from, and our fitness room and pool are really great. The walking paths are very well lit, all within a secured gate. Plenty of covered parking to go to around, but they have garages here too. The leasing staff is very helpful at finding the right options for you.  I really enjoy my apartment, but once I emerge outside,  I  love visiting with my neighbors and their  pets...yep, my joy I cannot hide. I am home!

Been living here for about a year and a half, and I have very few complaints.  The location is perfect; its only a five minute walk from the closest light-rail station (and Starbucks!).  Furthermore, it is nearly equal distance from downtown Scottsdale and downtown Phoenix, and downtown Tempe is only a few minute drive away.

The grounds are clean, and all the maintenance and office staff are very friendly and helpful.  There is a real nice pool.

There is nothing especially nice about the unit I rent out.  That said, I have no complaints.  Quiet, no bugs, friendly neighbors.  Never had any issues with anything breaking down.

Overall, I would certainly recommend this apartment complex to most anyone.

I lived there 3 years. Jacuzzi never worked . Office got broken into through Dirty laundry room .  Rats and Bed Bugs and Roaches  ; They Don't Tell You About. Be Through All Before You Rent. Get All In Writing With Time Frame . Watch Out For Drug And Drunk . Secure Your Place . Make Sure Your Information I Not On Desk . Visible To Other.

Ive rented here for over 2 years, I am very satisfied, I love everything about it, the closets are walk in, it has pool that was recently renovated, it also has beautiful sitting area and easy to access hiking trails I can walk to on the back side of the complex.
Ive rented here for over 2 years, I am very satisfied, I love everything about it, the closets is walk in, and has pool, It also has hiking trails on the back side of the complex I can walk too.
I stay in the apartments they are completely lying they don’t look anything like the pictures poor service

As a single male who prefers to have their own place, this place is perfect!  The rent is cheap and its in a gated complex where I feel safe.  Good sized bedroom and walk in closet.  A small community and a friendly staff who will work with you.

So far I'm really liking this apartment complex. Its a nice small complex. Its a great first apartment. I live the small one bedroom. The closet is huge!!! The grounds are well maintained and the common areas are nice.

This apartment staff is truly amazing! The apartments are clean and well maintained. The staff made me fell like family from the first day I went to the office. The apartment complex exceeded every expectation I had! They are the best!

The place now has trash everywhere all the time, and many tenants have had to call the police for homeless messing with their doors, drug use, and vandalism. The staff refuses to do anything about any of these issues and are very rude while they do so. The rent charge is ridiculous for the living conditions to be what they are.

I am going to be moving from out of town to Phoenix and called about one of their apartments listed. The woman on the phone was super rude when I was trying to ask questions. She was using a tone of voice trying to make me feel stupid because there are virtual tours online. It’s not even labeled which units the tours go with so how am I supposed to know? There’s very little information online so not really sure why she was acting so inconvenienced by my very normal questions. Won’t rent here since they can’t even be bothered to be decent to potential residents.

I live at Avalon Apartments and have been here for a year and a half. My car has been broken into twice after parking in the parking lot that has no cameras/any type of surveillance whatsoever. I called my apartment manager this morning, to warn them about a potential liability. The staff member that I spoke to interrupted me and told me to “just call the police” and that the parking spot “wasn’t their problem.”

 The recent purchase of this building was meant to improve it, but clearly that is not the goal. This company (Alliance Southwest, LLC) and its staff do not care about residential safety concerns, or much about residents at all. 

In addition, the light on my porch has been broken/burnt out for months. Where is maintenance? Nowhere to be found. My neighbors’ dog runs wild outside without a leash. Where is the apartment manager? Too busy trying to scam people looking for a home out of their money, I’m sure.

Save yourself a headache, lost possessions, and wasted money and look elsewhere.

I've lived here for 3 years.  Through constant construction/remodeling noise, hammering, electric saws... beware the 60 notice to vacate that is glossed over on the lease.  There are notices left at your door for things like the A/C being broken and worked on for days at a time in the heat of summer and notices informing me that my water will be shut off for days at a time as well.  Got kids? Because almost everyone that lives here does so it's like a gated daycare after school gets out. Some days toys strewn about the courtyard and disc golf frisbies thrown at your windows.  I was so excited to put my 30 notice in and move out only to be told that it is 60 day notice and oh by the way my lease was up in January but informing me of this was a "courtesy" that management did not feel was necessary.  Cash grabbing scam artists.  Maybe this is the apartment community for you!
If I could give negative stars, I most definitely would. Zero concern or respect for tenants. What are people paying you for if not livable conditions? Heartless thieves...

Now sitting here in my gym clothes with a non-working gym entry code for the FOURTH TIME. 

I knock on the door at 5:03 - no answer. Lights on, somebody's in there, but can't be bothered because it's 3 minutes after closing time. Oh, and I paid $25 for this non-working code almost a week ago, for a workout facility that was supposed to be open five months ago.

Management: may you receive the same level of customer service that you give wherever you go.
The property manager is really nice it's quiet and everybody minds thier own business.

Had been there for two years and the worst two years of my life. They wouldn’t do repairs and there was mold in the ceiling and walls. It was infested with German roaches from the beginning. Conditions were so bad I was in the hospital often with my baby at the time. We got out of there and within 6 months my baby was healthy again. The ceiling caved in in the bathroom and the room the kids had been in had a huge bubble in the wall that it shared with the bathroom to the point all four of us were stuck in one small room. I would say to avoid this place at all cost. No one deserves to live in conditions like that. They keep slapping lipstick on a pig and claiming it’s better but the real issues are never truly taken care of.

the bugs are horrible and they don't do Pest Control like they claim. the price is a lie. it says 845 but we pay 906. the head manager is rude. neighbors are loud and disrespectful of your property. doing everything possible to get myself and my family out of here. do not move here stay away.

Nothing has been updated since the 1970s. When you move in the roaches are there before you bring in a single box. Had to buy defense weapons to feel safe after my neighbor spit on me and ranted about his desire to kill me and/or throw rocks at me. Complaints from me and 4 other tenants but he still lives there. I finally got out. I know the prices sound great but trust me pay the extra $50 to feel safe.
Laura the manager is amazing so helpful, kind and patient. Property is beautiful and the office staff and janitors amazing. 100% recommended.
Worst place possible they give you a price and they charge you another The rude and disrespectful they never do the work order in a timely matter has been 3 months and still waiting

Nothing ever gets fixed and everything that is replaced is ALWAYS replaced with other used or infested appliances. Leading agents are rude and inconsiderate of their renters and the price for the run down, bullet riddled and heavily cat infested apartments is ridiculous. Especially since the pool has been broken for years and the mail boxes have been broken since mid-May. Do not rent here.

Roaches, roaches, roaches, aprtments shot up stray bullet came thru daughters window while she was sleeping. Appliances dont work. Oven over cooks cant use, had a dishwasher never repaired or replaced after one month of moving in. Mold, plumbing issue no hot water. Water heater never replaced just rigged.  Cabinet doors falling off hinges. Paint pilling. Management refusing to repair window where a stray bullet came through. Front gate wont stay up hinges rusty old cant repair. Dont put your family in danger by moving here and dont waste your hard earned money on this over priced dump. Maria hired at front desk to dodge calls for the manager.

I cut my lease 6 months early because of how bad it is the gates don’t work so there’s always crazy stuff happening around the complex. If I were you save your time and money and go elsewhere. Let me just add, office hours don’t matter they’re never there when you need them, & they don’t pick up the phone. Pool is NEVER open, kids have to hop the fence to swim because it was always chained shut during summer. Some of their laundry machines eat your change good luck getting into the office to get your change back. I could go on and on about all the stuff I witnessed in just a short 6 months but it would take another review.

I have lived here for 2 years. It is ok, but recently I have had a lot of difficulty getting in touch with the property management about repairs. I submitted a work request a week ago because my hot water heater isn't working, and have called multiple times but have not heard anything. My car was also broken into here last year. The apartment itself is nice with a good location, but I would look elsewhere if you are looking for management to actually respond when you have issues.

Save yourself from a year of HOA harassment and DO NOT MOVE HERE. A few months into our lease my gf and I were experiencing some strange problems. We kept seeing a woman constantly monitoring/photographing the windows of every single unit in the villa. We figured this person must own/rent property here, so we let it go. A few weeks later we realize this happens to be the board of director for red rox villa, Cindy. I wasn't aware that the Board of Directors of the HOA main duty was to look into every apartment window multiple times a week and take photographs. I've been talking to members of the community and they have had very similar issues. 

The primary purpose of a homeowners association is to manage a neighborhood's common areas such as roads, parks and pools.

I understand that homeowners/tenants have to follow the HOA rule book, but does this justify constant window inspection?!?

Do not judge this book by its cover, you will be very sorry and unhappy here, if you value your privacy.

I have lived at the Red Rox for nearly a year. They were extremely difficult to get into contact with, as no one really works at the front office. The people in there are from the Homeowners Association and are not representatives of the complex. After three or four phone calls to their main line, we were able to get into contact with someone.

First impressions that the grounds were impressive, they take a lot of pride in maintaining the plants and outdoor amenities (so much so that landscaping is at least 4 days a week and the noise starts at 6am) - oh and the windows are paper thin. The overall apartment quality varies because they have been turned into condos and the renters may upgrade the devices/counters/flooring. 

Now you expect some amount of noise living on the second of three floors, but when the music below you is so loud that the bass gives you headache and whenever it starts you have to leave (even though you pay an arm and a leg to live here)... it gets pretty aggravating. There is also noise above you that resembles a elephant in high heels pacing on hardwood. I mentioned those windows earlier, and so be prepared to perfectly hear everyone's conversations after they've parked their cars and are coming inside (oh, and also when they go outside, open their doors, start their car, idle... and then leave). You can hear everything people say outside.

The appliances are upgraded and nice - never had one malfunction, other than the dishwasher failing to drain. The carpet was clean but old and so it wears down easily. They are newly painted. The doors have damaged weather stripping and so don't be surprised if the air conditioner is always on.

Overall the apartments are a good quality. If you can stand/get lucky with your neighbors, then good on you. Also believed that these apartments are incredibly overpriced. No grocery stores/restaurants within a 15 minute driving distance.  It's a great distance from the airport (maybe a 5 minute drive) as well as ASU, downtown Scottsdale. You're also right next to the 202 and so getting to downtown Phoenix is also really easy.

The Red Rox is not just an apartment to me, it is my home.  I have lived there for 5 years and hope to for years to come.  The grounds are well taken care of, the pool is beautiful, and fitness center is always clean.  The location is great as well, close to anything you could need or want to do.

Moving from another state to go to school. The management made this as easy as possible and went out of their way to be helpful and timely. The apartment is very nice and updated, so cute! I wish we could get this type of fabulous service with other companies.

Spent two heat soaked years there and am glad I left. They cut out all the trees and surrounded the place with rock so it heats up like a metal clad oven. It's family owned and managed by the daughter and her husband who want to impress dad by cutting down on their outlay. They removed everything that would be a comfort including two of the three pools. Luckily they put ovens in the center courtyard so there will be even more heat to force up the electric bill to cool your apartment.

I've lived here over a year now. My apartment has had 4 floods (2 when I wasn't home and 2 at 3am) from the upstairs neighbors flushing something they shouldn't have down the toilet (a wet wipe will do it - very old pipes - can't flush anything save for single ply tp safely) and then showering, creating a blockage that comes out my shower and all over my apartment. My guest bath had similar issues. The plumbing here is finicky and the pipes are old. If you look on Robson Associates website (property managers) you will note that the entire C unit is available. The reason for this is that things don't get fixed for months (I think they only have one very busy maintenance fellow) and we haven't had hot water in 2 months (lukewarm at best and the dang shower head must gave been installed by short people. I'm 5'9" and I have to duck at least 2-3 inches to wash my hair) They let you move in and things aren't perfect, my bathtub and kitchen were dirty when I moved in and they go over everything with a fine toothed comb when you leave. Including searching your apartment with a K9 for pests (bedbugs and roaches) and doing a pre-move out inspection one month before you move out. Be prepared for that if you chose to live here. They want your animals out while the K9 is there...where the heck am I supposed to put my animals and all furniture 2 feet from the wall (heavy couch? Too bad, if you don't move it, they will charge you $40) Anyway, property has had some security update -gates added at front, lights added, but they let shady people live here too, so it's a toss up. Price is decent for sure and managers are nice.

Located in the Melrose districtwith a very quick walk to 2 grocery stores and only a few blocks from the light rail. These apartments are a bit older but the management is very attentive to getting maintenance in for repairs, though some things take a bit longer than you'd like. When our a/c went out in the summer they provided a portable a/c unit for one room and we did have to "rough it" for a week, but then they reduced our rent that month for our troubles. 

They've just upgraded the grounds with a new courtyard and barbecue pits. Last fall all the buildings were repainted and more trees have been planted throughout. This is also one of the least expensive rentals in the downtown area.
These apartments are so cute. Very urban and vintage. Quiet place with lots of trees for shade. Plus in the best neighborhood for a good price.

1. In the two years I've lived there, they have repaired one thing correctly. Usually, they send a guy in to stare at it, claim he needs to order a part, and never return, then they hope you'll just learn to live with it. 

2. In the last year, they've been sprucing up the place, which involves making the outside look nicer without doing anything to the insides.  My stove is from about 1972 and hasn't worked since the day I moved in.  The biggest "improvement" I've dealt with was when they decided they needed a new flood light that shines directly in my bedroom window, making it nearly as bright in there at midnight as it is at 8AM.

3. If you like bed bugs, cockroaches, and ants, this is a great place to live with all three.

4. Moving out because they're raising the rent by $100. This is on top of the $40 they raised it after I'd been there a year.  Looking around at my neighbors, I'm not sure who they think has $100 of extra income every month.  We're all lower class working stiffs.

5. The water all stinks.  When you go to wash your hands after using the bathroom, the water coming out of the faucet doesn't smell much different from the water swirling down the bowl.  And speaking of that bowl, the water will stain it. Clorox tablets and other bleaching agents in the tank have little to no effect.

6. For the most part, the neighbors are quiet.

7. The air conditioner in my unit is one of the most inefficient I've ever seen.  Last summer, I was averaging $220 for electricity.  June's bill went from around $40 all winter to $130 because I ran the A/C for 6 days in May.  I never set the thermostat lower than 82.

8. Convenient walking distance to Safeway, Phoenix College.

When you leave double check all your power and such have been turned off. They are trying to charge us for TWO WEEKS of power after we turned over the key AND the lease ended. I'm not paying for the power while they show the apartment and who knows what else.

Horrible office, messy fiflthy poorly maintained property, loud rude neighbors, disgusting greedy management, smelly garbage filled hallways, terrible parking, overcrowded shopping near by which fills up any room in the limited parking lots on weekends and holidays for guest parking.

When they "pick up" the trash they drop/throw the bins, and considering they come by after 10pm most nights. Its loud. It echos in the hallways. So have fun with the 10pm - 12am THUMP wake up.

If you dont have kids, never go to bed early, never get sick and sleep at different hours. this wont bother you - trash pick up is everynight

The utilities are much higher than represented.  They purportedly are based on square footage so if your neighbor leaves their door open to air condition their balcony during the summer, you pay for it.  There is no way to conserve and lower your utility bills.  The rent bill each month includes charges for water, sewer, sales tax, trash, gas & electrical plus a $6 monthly service fee to prepare the bill.  The bill on which the utilities is based is never shown to the tenants so you have no way to verify the charges and whether the owner pays any utilities for common areas.  The property does not have anyone on site 24 hours a day.  The manager works M-F and if something happens after hours, you have to hope they will respond to a call to the maintenance line.  One of the two elevators was out of order for over 2 months.  Management does not enforce rules regarding dogs & there have been issues with dog feces in the hallways, elevators and stairwells.  None of the apartments has a washer/dryer.  One of the 5 washers in the laundry room has been out of order over 6 months.  The retention rate for new tenants does not appear to be high.  There are a lot of vacancies.  The garage gates frequently malfunction and bicycles have been stolen and cars vandalized.  They claim there is no Section 8 housing in this property but yet HUD conducts an annual inspection.  The one good thing about the inspection is that it causes the owner to give the property a good cleaning at least once a year.  The negative side of it is that your privacy is invaded for weeks in advance when management repeatedly enters your apartment to get it ready for the inspection.  The rules seem to change daily.  Some people have been told they can't have certain items on their balcony yet someone was allowed to move in and put a refrigerator on their balcony.  The apartments are large in terms of square footage but there are few amenities.  The maintenance guy is great and very helpful.
Jordache is one of the best Maintenance Manager ever!

I've had a lot of bad experiences in a lot of complexes around the Valley, and this by far the best place I've ever lived in. Great location, remodeled building, the floor plans are ridiculously spacious, and the rent is completely fair for what you pay. Also, water and electricity are included in your rent bill (varies per month, but not much), so I've actually saved money living here. The staff is beyond friend and extremely professional, plus you get a sense of "city living" while being in Arcadia... tons of restaurants, bars, and friendly people. I just renewed my lease and I've never ever done that!
I'd recommend this place to everyone looking to be in a hip neighborhood while not breaking your wallet.

I am a resident of four years with Roosevelt Square and unfortunately I do not recommend this complex. The location is unbeatable, great amenities and amazing local businesses at your doorstep. However, the leasing office’s current staff is ill-equipped to handle any issues that arise and do not communicate with tenants on a professional level.  

Parking here is an absolute nightmare. The leasing office has a toxic partnership with a towing company named “AZ All City Towing” and it tows its own residents at the expense of their residents. Neither company takes responsibility and the fees are astronomical to say the least, let alone a waste of time. 

For the price we, as tenants, are charged monthly, the least we could be provided with is a secure parking area. And quite frankly, the leasing office could strive if it bothered to offer their residents a standard level of customer service and effective problem solving solutions.

Shockingly unprofessional leasing staff. Did a virtual tour - was told we needed to immediately apply with an immediate move in date to even be considered. Then took days of back and forth calling to even get our application processed.  Finally received an approval letter by email, only to be told the next we were denied by phone (and get a different letter later the second evening). Their Cox setup person wouldn’t stop calling to see when we wanted to start services. When I called the leasing agent, JT, to ask questions about the conflicting information - he was hostile, judgmental and straight up refused to put me in touch with the manager who made the decision change. The whole process was sketchy and felt so discriminatory. We only considered this place because of a current tenant referral and now will make sure to make it widely known how we were treated.

Mechelle from the office is so nice, but they are in the business of making money and you get nickled and dimed for everything. The property was good overall but quite dirty in shared hallways/outdoor space. Appliances are extremely old. Pool is freezing cold water year round. If they just didn’t recirculate the water during the day it would get to a manageable temp from the AZ heat, but it’s seriously so frigid I couldn’t ever handle going in. When covid hit, they offered zero flexibility and I had to continue paying rent there for 3.5 months after moving out.

I’ve lived in this complex for going on three years now. The community is beautiful and feels like home. I was looking for apartments with character that didn’t feel too overly nice. The property is well maintained and staff is extremely friendly. The leasing office staff is all incredibly helpful and friendly. They’ve personally taken care of every issue promptly. I didn’t give the community 5 stars because they really do charge a lot for everything, but this information really isn’t hidden. I plan on staying in these apartments for a long time!

At first glance it’s the perfect community. However after staying here, the leasing office misinform and hoodwinks those who move in their units. For example, utilities bills are part of rent and in our resident login you can see the breakdown of what the bills are. What they don’t tell you is “conservice” a third party is another site you have to pay for! So wait you mean to tell me I can see how much my water bill is on my resident login for free, but have to pay an extra fee to have another site tell me the same information? Crazy.. also, upon move in they give you a paper that gives you designated times and days for trash pick up.. yet the trash man may no come during those times. Why advertise a time if it’s not true?

Currently live here. I was very fond of the previous management, but now you have to jump through hoops and ridiculous fees to live here under the new management. Complaints are not taken seriously, which is disheartening coming from someone who follows all parts of the lease agreement. Walls are very thin, and parking is a nightmare. I will not be living here when my lease is up, and neither should you. Don’t be fooled by how “nice” it looks on the outside. They only care about making money.

I'd only recommend living at Roosevelt Square if you like being overcharged and underwhelmed. I'll start with move in costs. Admin fee. Application fee. Pet fee. Pet deposit. Regular deposit. Apartment insurance. If you like paying animal rent, trash service, water, sewer, exterminating  and billing fees on top of electricity and cable, than this place is for you! I had a problem with the online bill pay service 5 months in a row where it would tell me my balance was $0 but I'd get an email from management saying if I didn't pay my remaining balance of cents on the dollar, I'd incur a $50 late fee. Don't even get me started with move-out costs! I cleaned my apartment top to bottom and was still charged over five hundred in cleaning fees. Don't get caught without your "valet trash receptacle" because that thing will run you $50, are you kidding me?? Sure the location is great, the quality is just sub-par enough to convince you it's a good apartment, and you might feel fancy knowing you can park your car in an over crowded parking garage. Let me burst your bubble: if you're going to pay this much rent for a two bedroom downtown, save your patience, find a cute little privately owned house in Encanto or man, at least move in to one of the new developments and enjoy some brand new kitchen appliances and a bath tub that isn't stained with someone else's foot prints.

The location is amazing - but with the building boom, there are so many nicer, newer, and more reasonable places to live in the area.  This place is way overpriced, especially considering that the amenities promised are rarely even accessible (gates failing to open, doors locking you in the fitness center (yes - how does that even happen??), pool not maintained). The staff seem unknowledgeable and very unhelpful.  When you bring something to their attention about the property that needs maintenance, the answer is usually, "that's provided as a courtesy," as if to say "that's not our problem."  They treat the residents as commodities, and not people.  There is no sense of community as they don't do any events for the residents, nor do they even bother trying to get to know the people occupying their units. Save yourself the headache of dealing with incompetent staff, and disappointment with broken promises, and find one of the many other locations nearby.

PROS:
• The location cannot be beat. The place sits between a gorgeous little park and the edge of the arts district. Everywhere you look there's incredible food and interesting events just a short walk away. 

CONS: Everything else
• The property is poorly maintained, despite first glances. The entry gates are constantly broken - either permanently locked with a malfunctioning fob detector, or permanently wide open. The parking garage gates are the same story. Several times I found myself either locked in or out, with no clue how to get through. I advise you to get to know your neighbors so you can call them in these situations and have them let you in. This will happen a lot.
• Management is AWFUL. Every day you will receive a poorly spelled, poorly written update on some kind of emergency event (water shut off, gates not working, fire doors malfunctioning).
• Maintenance is a toss up. The staff themselves are great and very knowledgeable and friendly. But it may take anywhere from a few hours to a few days for them to show up. I had a malfunctioning smoke alarm attached to a vaulted ceiling going off for 5 days before management sent someone. This was after sending multiple service requests and pleading with office staff to take it seriously. Maintenance staff will also show up unannounced, so beware of wearing headphones or taking showers during the day because more than once I was surprised when I found a stranger hunched over in my living room.
• From 2014-2016 our water was shut off 45 times for "emergency repairs". In February of 2016 alone it was shut off 7 times.
• Bike theft is rampant. If you have a bike, do not leave it locked up in the stairwells.
• Although the parking garages have security cameras at the entrances, they are non-functioning. I discovered this after my husband's car was backed in to and we asked if we could review the footage. There was no footage.
• There are two enormous dumpsters in Building C's garage labeled RECYCLE and CARDBOARD ONLY. Turns out they are neither and everything in them is picked up by the regular garbage collector. The only true recycle container is in Building A's garage.
• The first floor hallways are prone to flooding so steer clear of the bottom floor.

I applied here and really wanted an apartment here.  I eventually figured out after I paid the application fee that the people that answer the phones are an answering service and can only schedule appointments for you to go see an apartment, and after that, they can't help you with anything.  Once I paid the application fee, they never contacted me and I was unable to get a hold of anyone.  After calling multiple times and leaving multiple messages and also sending emails, two weeks went by and I heard nothing.  At this point I had already visited the office 2 or 3 times just to apply and could not take any more time off of work to visit the office during office hours.  I had reached the time where I desperately needed to find a place to live so I ended up applying at a different apartment complex. The first Friday of every month  Roosevelt St. is closed to traffic and features unique restaurants, retail, galleries, music venues  etc., to the general public. If you are a dog walker the community provides numerous clean-up stations along the perimeter of the complex, with well tended grass, trees and park benches.  One block away is a clean,relaxing dog park with separate, fenced  areas for both small and large dogs.  
     When I park my car inside the attached parking garage, steps from my apartment, I look forward to entering a large, quiet home, with ample windows overlooking the city park and Japanese gardens.  A service picks up the garbage and recycling that I leave in a container outside my door.  Service requests  are promptly addressed.  Common areas are well tended, with comfortable seating, an outdoor kitchen, and water features which add to the sense of solitude and comfort.  There is a  large pool in one of three buildings, in addition to a well appointed gym.  A rooftop area with comfortable sofas, chairs and tables is the perfect place to view the expanding downtown, mountains and sunsets.

-Has not ever been renovated. It's just as old as when it was built.

As a former resident, I would never advise anyone to rent an apartment from Shadow Ridge for two big reasons: 

 1.  Mold problems: this alone should be reason enough not to move here.  Their contract contains an entire page regarding mold and instructs you to ‘promptly’ inform management if you find a mold problem.  Hilarious, since if you do this, they will just tell you to wash if off with a bleach/water mixture – or they’ll cover it up with paint.  If you read enough reviews, you’ll see this has been going on for years.  I found mold on sandals (that I rarely used) about a week before I moved out – they were in a vertical hanging shoe bag IN MY WALK-IN CLOSET.  Belts hanging freely in the same closet had mold on them.  The (very old) tub had a moldy black line where the top and bottom fiberglass parts fit together that could not be cleaned even with a bleach solution and scrubbing brush.  Disgusting.  I really didn’t realize how much it was affecting me until I moved out and within a week, felt better.  

2. Ridiculous rent increases: the corporate owners/management have raised the rent to ridiculous levels considering these apartments are old and rapidly falling apart.  The first year, after moving to SR in 2017, my rent was raised by $50/mo (which at the time I thought was a lot), the next year by $45/mo, the year after by $35/mo and then, all of a sudden, it was raised by $300/mo.  I finally moved after they decided to jack it up another $120/mo.  I don’t care one whit about the ‘market rate’ - these apartments are not worth anything close to the rent they are demanding and this shows they could care less about long term tenants.  Greed, not smarts.

I lived at Del Prado from 1996-2000 and since 2015. I can afford to live anywhere and I typically travel over 4 months a year. I have never had a break-in or even a stolen package despite my travels. Del Prado is very well built with block and concrete. So unlike most Phoenix apartments, the units are very quiet and you can barely hear neighbors even when the make excessive noise, which is rare. While newer complexes might have full size washer/dryers and more modern appliances, they are poorly constructed with wood and stucco and you will constantly hear your neighbors. Apartments at Del Prado are very large with walk-in closets. There are very few problems and when I have had a problem with plumbing or lighting etc, it has been fixed immediately and correctly. If on-site maintenance can’t address a problem an outside contractor is brought in within one business day. Management has been friendly and helpful. The location is great in the Camelback business corridor and you can easily walk to the Safeway shopping center, the canal or the Biltmore. I have looked at apartments in the area charging double the rent for less space and they do not have the location or the quiet. I could easily afford a house or condo but I prefer to rent here and enjoy the easy lifestyle.

Myself and several other tenants are looking into moving out and also taking legal action against Del Prado. My neighbors and myself were told the gate would be fixed by January 2021...and it's May and still not fixed! Though Del Prado is a non-smoking complex, one woman who lives on the first flood adjacent to the pool smokes on her patio several times a day. My neighbors and I have reported this woman countless times, and yet, this woman continues to smoke without repercussions. We have photo and video evidence of her smoking on her patio daily. She needs to be evicted! The hot tub has been broken for months. There has been NO follow up from the rental office on when things are going to be fixed. We have to continuously ask what's going on about the repairs throughout the complex and what's going to be done about smokers and things like that, and the ladies in the office just say they'll "take care of it." Well, nothing is being taken care of, and me and my neighbors have had enough of it. We've been paying rent for amenities that don't work, people continually violating smoking rules, and trespassers having access to ou community, and we want Del Prado to fix these matters immediately or reimburse us for the services and promises that they are clearly not providing!  No one should have to live with trespassers in the complex every day, constant cigarette smoke while trying to swim and enjoy the community amenities, and unfixed amenities with no communication from the rental office and company. Unacceptable!

I had a maintenance issue when I first moved in, and it was taken care of promptly.  The maintenance/groundskeeper is always friendly.  The apartments have well maintained landscaping, the complex is always clean.  The apartments are beautiful.  I find the washer/dryer just the right size for the apt.  The AC works well, and makes the same level of noise as any apt I have lived in.  I am so glad to be living here!

Unfortunately, despite multiple communications, phone call and a sit down with the neighbor, management is powerless to do anything about the matter, although I appreciate their efforts. It is worth noting that the city of Portland is also unable to help you. We have consulted 9 different noise proofing companies, all of them were impressed by the stomping noise. They have all informed us that there is nothing that can be done about ‘impact noise’, unless the building was built with further noise proofing to begin with - so really the solution is for the neighbors to take noise proofing measures, which is not enforceable. This building has loud tenants who often violate noise and smoking rules. Many who moved in recently are rude and inconsiderate. There is no way to buzz up guests and it feels like a gilded cage. The materials in the apartments are very pale, not life friendly— I suspect this is because they want to try to keep deposits. We have loved living at The Fitz so far, the location is perfect with all the lovely restaurants of 23rd, and if you drive to work the highway is quick to get on. It was a nightmare. Packages stolen, elevators not working, smell of sewage in the apartment, heater breaking in the middle of winter, last month sewage bill was over $100 just because. The list goes on and on.

I just moved into the Fitz and the aesthetics of the building and apartments are unmatched! Everything is absolutely beautiful. The building is also very pet friendly; The residents are so kind and so are their pups.
Major security issues (my locked bike was stolen in my first month of moving in), uncaring/unhelpful property management, and zero amenities (+ high rent $) = not a great place to live.
Look for a better place to live. Their charging way to much for apartments, the neighborhood is infested with homeless and you won’t get any peace.

The building has cool vibes, it feels more like a hotel than other apartment buildings. The apartments are nice and the cafe in the lobby is run by nice people and is a convenient place to hang. It’s been a good home.

Awful experience renting from these people. Dangerous neighborhood, filthy common areas, loud bar right by your window on weeknights, and arrogant, greedy landlords. One of the worst experiences of my life and I have rented in Boulder Colorado for years.

The building has great design, it's super clean and modern and its great to have a coffee shop right on the ground floor. It's also easy to commute from the Max stop right out front.

We stayed at the Sutton and it was an outstanding property with excellent management and amenities! Perched on the Willamette Greenway, a fantastic walking and jogging trail, and a few minutes walk from downtown, the property is extremely clean, has a fantastic modern gym and lobby, and is excellently managed! New management is extremely helpful, ended up signing a new lease with them! Great location, amazing amenities, fun property events!

My fiancée and I moved in six months after the building was completed. - Complimentary yoga sessions
- Weekly food truck at our building
- Whiskey tasting

In just one month, Sentral was able to offer tenants all these amenities, thanks to their amazing Experience team, lead by Diana. 

Sentral being the current management resolved my legal dispute with ownership and demonstrated that they genuinely value their tenants. They take care of their tenants and are invested in lease renewals.

I recently had the pleasure of staying at The Sutton for a week, as part of their Stay suites, and it was an absolutely wonderful experience.  We have booked with them twice and are returning again in August. 

From the moment I arrived, I was impressed by the luxurious accommodations and the stunning views from the rooftop terrace. The apartment was beautifully appointed and had everything I needed for a comfortable and relaxing stay.

The Sutton is located in a fantastic spot in the heart of Portland's Pearl District. I was surrounded by great restaurants, shops, and parks. I loved being able to walk and bike to so many places. The neighborhood is also very walkable, and I felt safe exploring the area on foot.

The staff at The Sutton were top-notch. They were friendly, helpful, and always went the extra mile to make sure my dogs and I had a great stay. They always had a treat ready to greet our pups with. I would highly recommend The Sutton to anyone looking for a luxurious and convenient place to stay or live in Portland.

3 months ago I couldn't wait until my roommate and I's lease was up. Trainwreck doesn't even begin to describe this building. Our unit was awesome but we hated the building. Nothing worked, nobody was around, nobody cared. It SUCKED. Sentral came in and started turning things around immediately. The staff is amazing and they are always available to help with whatever is needed. You can find a real live human greeting you from like 7am to 11pm. They even escort our door dash up instead of us having to come down.

The maintenance team is always working and respond to work orders same day. They also are easy to talk too. The sales people (Aubry and a new guy I don't know his name yet) are willing to help too which I think is super rare).

They are really working hard to build a community. Tonight we had a private whiskey tasting with a local company. We had drinks, fun, food, and LIVE music. Last night they rolled out a high end market in the lobby and we had a ton of local vendors come to the property sampling their goods. Every other week the experience team- Diane, Kora, Jordan arranges for a new food truck and they provide beer and wine and set tables up outside. Tomorrow we are having Brunch! Hell yess

For all the haters (we were too for a long minute) AC is totally fixed. Valet starts Monday. This is an awesome property with an awesome team that does fun stuff all the time. You can find cheaper apartments for sure  but now that this building is  being managed by people that care THERE IS NOT BETTER UNITS IN PORTLAND. Size, views, gas stove, full sized appliances. Sutton has it all.

I recently visited my daughter at The Sutton and was blown away by the stunning architecture and breathtaking views. The management team is incredibly kind and welcoming, always ensuring residents feel at home. The Sutton hosts a variety of engaging community events, fostering a strong sense of camaraderie among residents. This community truly exemplifies luxury living and is the perfect place to call Home!

I love that I’ve finally found an apartment where I feel truly welcomed. The location is fantastic, and the amenities, like the co-working area, are a great bonus. I also appreciate the beautifully designed kitchen appliances that came with the home. I’m especially excited to use the lounge area and library—they’re both amenities I know I’ll enjoy!

Broadstone Riva is a wonderful community with spacious and thoughtfully laid out floor plans. The building is always clean and secure and within walking distance of everything the Vancouver Waterfront has to offer.
Broadstone Riva offers an outstanding living environment with great furnishings and amenities, a wonderful staff, and a very nice location.

Living at Broadstone Riva has been an exceptional experience! The management team is incredibly helpful and welcoming. They made our move-in process seamless and have been supportive every step of the way. The amenities are top-notch, and our apartment is fantastic! We couldn’t be happier with our choice to live here!

I chose to reside at Riva for the main reason of where it is located.  Having a beautiful view to wake up to every day is priceless. Just the way this building was thoughtfully designed and beautifully furnished exceeded my expectations.  So far it has been enjoyable living here.  
No Complaints!  Thank you Riva for making it a wonderful residence!
We chose to Broadston Riva because the apartment was very sunny with a great floor plan.  We also love the proximity to the river, restaurants and coffee shops.

I moved in just over a year ago now, and it has been one of the best moves of my life. And I have lived in a lot of different places, renting and owning. ORO is a great value because even though I have my own washer and dryer and also my own heating and a/c, my power bill has been on average between 20-30% lower every single month. This just shows me how energy efficient the building is. The management AND maintenance is AWESOME!  And, they have taken care of any need or concern I've had in a very short turn around. The cleaning of the building is great and the staff is always open to any feedback you might have to give.
ORO feels like home. Safe, secure, and centrally located.

ORO continues to be a good place to live for me. They are handling outside events that are beyond their control by asking us all to take a stake in security. Which I think we all need to do as tenants anyway. But, they are actively working to correct anything that is wrong, needs to be fixed or cleaned, etc. All of my concerns are addressed right away and considering the state of downtown Portland (including The Pearl) over the past year, ORO does seem to be doing everything they can to help it be the nice place we all want it to be.

ORO is a good building to live in, with nice residents and it is well kept and clean. It's relatively new to The Pearl and I think will adjust over time, which is true for any new building. I think that the owners will listen to me if I say something. So, I feel good about that. And the maintenance is top notch.

Moving into ORO was the best move I have made in probably 25 years. After owning several times, I just decided it did make more financial sense for me to rent. But, trying to find a good place to live with the amenities I wanted was nearly impossible. Then, by chance, using a new search engine to find apartments, ORO popped up. That is how I ended up here. I am grateful every day to myself and my friends who made this all possible. The building is clean almost completely to my standards (which are ridiculously high, by the way) and the professional cleaners come twice per week for all the common areas. They actually CLEAN, so after the weekends, which always brings more traffic into the building, and on Friday's the place, every common area, the lobby bathroom, the bike room and dog wash- everything is very well cleaned. This is one of main reasons I chose to live here. The other reason I love it here so much is that the staff has been phenomenal with helping me with anything to get settled. The parking structure works very well, and there are never problems with the matrix or with the door. There are conveniently located trash cans to handle doggie bags after walks, etc. And, the appliances are top end and they perform as such too. Neighbors have been great and the Property Managers, regardless of who it might be are wonderful. Special shout outs to Brittney and Jackie! Marcus is the on site service man and he is available to help you with anything. And he is super nice, too. I think the amenities are awesome and the system they use to pay rent on line works very well. The common area utilities seem reasonable based on a number of factors, but I know unit size has something to do with it. Sound proofing is really good too. It's affordable, clean and nice living. And easy access to any of the freeways and 
several different neighborhoods and downtown and the Pearl as well.

I have lived here in the ORO building for over three months now. I have to say, it is, by far, the best home I've ever leased. I have owned many times in the past, and due to necessity and convenience, I decided to lease an apartment home again. The ORO has been an outstanding building in terms of the management, the communication and the maintenance. I have had maintainence completed in my home when I was present... and also when I was not home. Each job was perfect and not even a trace of anyone being there was left behind. The staff is extremely nice and seem genuinely happy to be there. All the other tenants I have met have been really nice, also. My apartment home has top of the line appliances and I LOVE them. The kitchen has inspired me to cook daily again. The bathrooms are huge, which is nice, too. I honestly do not think they skimped on anything in the engineering and building of The Oro. It is truly the best place I've ever leased to live in. I am very happy to have found a place that has everything I was looking for and many things I wanted, but did not think I would be able to get. I've been totally satisfied with everything. And, I also think the building has good safety and security as well. I know that is a big concern for a lot of people. And very rightly so. Having on site staff is also a game changer. The common areas are professionally cleaned twice a week, and they do a really good job. The elevator comes out looking great, and so does the mail and package area, the dog wash station and bike room- everything is kept up like I would keep my own home up. I think that is one of biggest reasons that I like it here so much. Everything they do, from communication to cleaning, managing things that arise and addressing COVID-19 concerns (including the cleaning I mentioned) has been really top of the game for this property. I'm very happy to be living here.

As others have said, zero sound proofing. Upstairs neighbor makes constant noise at all hours of the night with pounding footsteps. 3-4x/week it sounds like they pick up their washing machine and slam it on the floor at 1-2 am... I have pleaded with the front office to help as I cannot get sleep - their only recommendation is to call the police, file a lawsuit to have them evicted (?), or pay 1.5x rent to break the lease. I just want sleep. Cannot wait to move out. Do not let the location and appearance of the complex tempt you into living in Carson South.

The Carson is beautifully designed and Slabtown is a great neighborhood. Unfortunately, the experience sold does not match the experience lived. The Carson South (the one facing New Seasons) is the least soundproof building I have ever lived in over 15 years of apartment living, including time in New York. 

My upstairs neighbor was loud and inconsiderate all hours of the day and night. My coworkers could hear his daily workout routine as it rattled my floors. My mother wears hearing aids. During a visit, he woke her up in the middle of the night when her hearing aids were charging because he was playing a movie so loudly. It was 3:30am.

In 2 years I submitted 4 written complaints and numerous verbal complaints to the main office. Each complaint was met with, "we'll send a friendly reminder!". Meanwhile, my written complaints mentioned lost sleep, work interruptions, and emotional distress from the longstanding, unresolved issues. They did not care. One staff member made a point to remind me that he lived on my hall and also heard noise, suggesting that I was wrong to complain, I guess?

My complaints were pleading and apologetic and I was left completely unhelped. After two years, the staff tried to say they had only received one complaint from me, ever, when written evidence proved false, but required me to contact their corporate office in California to discuss because the gaslighting was so severe. I also noticed other residents in distress in their main office from time to time, so I wasn't the only one struggling.

I suffered this disruption for two years and paid for it in more ways than one (health, career, mental well being). The only solution was to move out. 

Beyond that issue, I (and others) had mail stolen multiple times from the Carson North package room. No communication was sent to acknowledge the issue or share a plan to stop it. When my door lock battery died, a maintenance worker no-showed three times without fixing it. When I reported my bathroom fan as broken, they argued with me that it was just "completely silent." Imagine my surprise when it suddenly turned on one year later with audible sound.

Since moving out, it has become wildly clear how uncaring the staff was and how little they attempted to help residents. The difference is night and day.

Humans aside, the apartment itself was gorgeous. Great design, the best lighting, flooring, windows. I miss the aesthetic, the neighborhood, and the rooftop... but nothing else.

We were so in love with the Carson when we toured it - beautiful apartments and a great location! But within weeks of moving in we quickly realized that the Carson is not what is seems.
--The south building is not soundproof at all. Expect to get constant noise complaints for everything - closing doors, closing cabinets, walking, your dog playing with a toy. You can hear everything from your upstairs and next-door neighbors.
-- The keyless entry system (Latch) constantly breaks, which can mean you don't have access to an elevator or the front door of the building won't open.
-- There's a major theft issue. Bikes have been stolen from locked storage rooms more times than I can count, cars in the garage are broken into, and the package room has been raided.
-- On-site management seems to be overwhelmed and is very unresponsive. There were multiple occasions where no one would answer the office phone during business hours and emails would sit without responses for days, if not weeks.
-- The fire alarms go off all the time, meaning you have to evacuate the building at all hours of the day and night. I've sat outside in pjs and had to abruptly leave zoom meetings from fire alarms going off. 
-- Their moveout process is terrible. They also charge insane fees, a 1.5x rent and a 30 day notice fee.
Recently moved into The Vue and Aaliyah the concierge is always helpful with the lobby cart! I appreciate her!

I had sewage waste explode out of my kitchen sink before leaving for work on the 4th of July, only a few months after moving in, and they refused to do anything about it. Tweakers run up and down in the staircases and make it feel super unsafe. I had to break my lease early (only a couple months but it was worth the trouble) because this place was so atrocious and unnecessarily expe

I've been here for four months and they've lost at least 3 of my packages and always manage to blame it on someone else. This building is a nightmare. My car has been broken into twice since parking it in their locked garage. The elevators stay broken for months at at time. The ceilings leak water into the hallways and apartments. I’ve had packages stolen from their “locked” package lockers on multiple occasions.

After bringing these concerns to their attention and asking for resolution steps I was told by the building manager, Christine, that I and the other tenants are ungrateful for the work done by herself and fellow employees.

I did an initial reach out via email, someone named jaxon was being extremely rude to me when I had some questions regarding availability and move in dates. cant imagine how they will treat their residents if someone that hasn’t even moved in was treated so poorly, good luck leasing with that service
Never disappointed…. Happy to call this my home here at meadowland !!!!

Andre did amazing  from showing the apartment  to get the paperwork  done and then walking  me through  it . Also after I moved in He and John 
made sure that all  any maintenance  concerns I had were fixed immediately. They had REDONE the apartments from the appliances to carpet and floors.

I've lived here 2 years now and overall the place is really nice, Andre is quick to respond if there's any issues, John's great at making sure things get done right the first time and Chris makes sure the place stays clean. It's definitely a place to look into

I just want to say how amazing Andre has been! I live down the street from this apartment complex and over the past two years the management has really let the property go downhill. This group is Amazing!  they are kind, super helpful, and Always there for us. I am very grateful!

mResidences is a great place to live. It’s in the heart of the Pearl District and feels like a small community within the city. The managers are always around when you need and the price is more than fair for the area. Would highly recommend!!

If you’re looking for an industrial modern vibe with the niceties of The Pearl and access to pretty much everything including effortless access to the highway(s), this is the place! I feel safe and comfortable. The parking matrix is a bit hit or miss. However, it is fabulous when it is working!
Great staff, great property manager, and great place to live!! Two roof tops, gym, and a log fire pit?! Sign me up (I mean I’m already signed up but still sign me up again!!)
This is a great place to live in a great location!

Greystar took over the building January 2023. Since then, this has turned into an absolute nightmare and has consistently required $100+/mo out of pocket to cover expenses from building shortcomings and failures.

- Recently identified that the majority of maintenance requests are not documented internally, and the bulk of the ones that are are closed out without inspection or repairs. No notice given to residents.
- Apartments have no physical keys, just fobs. The locks on the doors run on batteries. Multiple residents have had the batteries die. The solution from the building was to leave your door open - my neighbor has no functioning front door for over two months.

- After the parking matrix collapse, the technicians identified additional structural weak points. Building did not communicate this until weeks later and allowed residents to continue using.

I recently moved into mResidences in The Pearl and am so happy I did. The unit is wonderful and the management and staff are friendly and extremely helpful. Great community to live in!

The Janey is perfectly located in the coolest neighborhood downtown. Whole foods, Powell's, the gym & so many great coffee shops, food & fun are just blocks away. I am sad to say that after the recent change in owners and management, all of those things have gone downhill. And with this has also come the slow and very planned out process of trying to get rid of any of the long-term tenants. The management has also now been raising rents for everyone just under the 10% mark to price out people without causing them to have to pay for moving costs. I must say this was, keyword WAS a good apt building at once, yet, since the recent changes have fallen to become a greedy and a truly bad place to live. Overall, I do not suggest moving here until, if they ever do, the management company gets their act together.

The new manager Majesta is super friendly and helpful. The initial managers who assisted me at my move in:  Mallory and Michael were super. The building maintenance team has been right on it for the minor maintenance I needed.

Working and on the go and need a nest to sleep in these are perfect. The city is a great place to spend your day out and about. If your home is your nest I believe you will fit in to the cozy affordable and easy low stress atmosphere.

Building is doing upgrades that make my apartment noisy during business hours, but other than that, the building is in a great neighborhood, has the best views in the city, is dog friendly, and the staff is great. It  is pricier than other apartments, but worth it.

The 735 st clair apartments  are a wonderful place to live! They are centrally located to the trendy 23rd street but you can still walk downtown in minutes. The building itself is older and  while apartments are being updated, I prefer the more vintage style units. But the roof is where it is at.... You can literally see all of portland and it's set up is very cozy! The staff is also amazing. However because the building is old there is a lot of work currently being done!on old pipes.But they have been very accommodating and are working to upgrade. Despite the downs the units are cozy and building is well cared for. Oh and super pet friendly!
It is very poor management. do not let them fool you. Keep your peace and money for a better place
A nice place to live. The building is well cared for and the staff is efficient and friendly.
overall ive had a good experience, however, the design of the building does not allow for good natural lighting nor good ventilation.
Kearney Plaza is in a prime location for restaurants and services. It is a quiet building with responsive management.

Very responsive and caring on-site management staff. Easy to get along with while performing their individual jobs with precision. 
We are long time residents and are disappointed in Executive Management decision to change competent management staff so often!
Please reconsider that policy.
The staff here is wonderful and kind.  Everything is handled in a timely manner.

I have lived here for 3 months now.  I was promised a working dishwasher the day after i moved in…3 months later and multiple maintenance requests, still no dishwasher.  My dryer rips my clothes, i put in 2 requests, still no fix.  

My car was stolen on the property, no one alerted the community to the crime to warn them.  2 weeks later i have a strange man repeatedly trying to enter my home in the middle of the night.  I dont feel safe and am contemplating leaving before my lease is up.

I've lived here for 3 years now... it has gotten to the point where we live in a dump. The trash areas have rats and are constantly overfilled with garbage, spilling out into the streets. Pet waste EVERYWHERE. Residents too lazy to clean up and maintenance staff too pretentious to help keep our property clean. Stairwells full of dirt, bugs, and pet waste. They have NEVER been washed. Gutters... "cleaned". Parking, horrible and my car is constantly being damaged because the spots are much too small. Appliances are older than me, constantly failing, and my maintenance requests go unanswered. I can look past the shitty "upgrades" that were made before I moved in (contact paper over particle board as a "new countertop", LAUGHABLE), but the management staff has completely failed this community. It's basically every man for himself here when it comes to getting anything done in your own apartment. I'm embarrassed to have anyone over because it looks like we live in a 3rd world country outside. Too far? Good. Take care of your residents, we pay WAY too much for way too little around here.

Less than 1 month as a resident, and I definitely feel like I made a huge mistake moving here.

The property itself and all the nature is and continues to be a highlight of living at Scott Mountain. It's the staff that makes me want to move out asap.

Let's start with my maintenance requests. Upon move-in, my apartment was not ready. The shower curtain rod was laying inside the tub; the overhead bathroom light was dirty, nonfunctional, and dangling from the ceiling; the ceiling fan does not turn on; and a hole in the window screen had a hole that was allowing bugs inside. 

All of these issues were reported to Scott Mountain in mid-May, the moment I moved in. We are now approaching one month with no resolution. I followed up with Scott Mountain at the end of May, and was told my work orders were printed and on the maintenance person's desk. A week and a half later, I'm trying to follow up again, but my messages, calls, and voicemails now go ignored.

I ended up repairing the window screen myself, otherwise I could not have an AC or any way to counter the fact that my fan doesn't work (note that I'm a top floor unit and it's summer). I also had to superglue the shower rod myself to not get water everywhere each time I bathe. I could have done this myself from the getgo, but silly me assumed Scott Mountain would actually care about residents having functioning fixtures and no bug infestations upon move-in.

In my corner of the neighborhood, the outside of the apartment is just as relaxing as the inside. I have a pair of neighbors who get into loud, screaming arguments at all hours of the day, and escalate to a point of shouting and chasing each other across the parking lot. Scott Mountain claimed they were aware of the problem but it's still ongoing, and I'm just told to call the police without even knowing what unit is causing the noise. It's not annoying, but terrifying to hear loud screams and not know if these people are actually in danger. I don't feel safe going outside when they're around. 

I came to Scott Mountain hoping for the bare minimum: an older apartment with no broken fixtures, and respectful neighbors. Instead, I'm already figuring out where I should move to next, and praying I have no more maintenance needs arise before my lease wraps up.

This area is not walkable or bikeable because there is nothing but trash and homeless EVERYWHERE! Management never responds to emails or answers their phone or returns phone calls- so don’t expect any help from them. Everything was fine when we moved in 2021 now I’m looking at a little homeless community from my balcony. Location sucks!

Management and Office staff has changed like every other week and none know what is going on or how to communicate. Terrible parking. Homeless camps behind the buildings. Yes we know they are not on the property but maybe since it’s a fire hazard to the ACTUAL property the management could and should communicate with the authorities to fix it. Take ownership!  Security only comes if you call them so there is no ACTIVE security presence. Neighbors tires got slashed, broken glass everywhere on the road, huge potholes, random people illegally dump their huge loads of waste by our dumpsters, the list goes on. The mail boxes Were broken for 9 months. They had been broken into by someone mid to late 2021 and their communication about this the past however many months has been nonexistent, they blame everyone and everything else but themselves. Again! Take ownership of these issues, it’s not a hard concept. And after all of this, they have the gall to raise our rent. What a joke! I even emailed management about this AND corporate and I was ignored. And yes I know your generic response will be to please talk to us about these situations, lol.

My boyfriend and I lived here for a year and would have stayed longer had we not moved to Eugene. The community is great and the staff are so helpful and kind. The apartments are surrounded by a nice neighborhood with beautiful trees around the campus. Parking was always plentiful and maintenance requests taken care of right away. The community has a gym and pool, as well as washer and dryer in each unit. Reasonable prices for Portland, too! You won't regret living here!

This is the best apartment I have ever rented from. The staff is hands do the most attentive and helpful. Maintenance is fast and thorough. I have never had to wait more then a few hr's to have anything fixed unless they need to order a part. The office staff is polite, happy, friendly and always willing to help with what ever we need. The property is BEAUTIFUL and well kept. There is ample parking and the community here is warm and inviting! DEFINITELY a great place to live!

Save yourself the headache and rent somewhere else.
The staff is lazy and unprofessional.They expect residents to be security, noise control, 
There are car break ins weekly.
It’s noisy.
Homeless people always going through the garbage.
The neighbors are rude.
Pools constantly closed for maintenance every summer.

Great community! Beautiful well maintained property and fantastic staff! Repairs happen very fast and there always seems to be enough parking. Other places I have lived there was never parking. Washers and dryers in the unit make things even better! Great location and close to everything I need!

The apartments themselves are okay, however the management company treats the residents with a lack of respect and dignity. The amenities are great when they are open. Parking is extremely limited and the spots are almost impossible to park in due to their size. My car was also towed by accident. Furthermore, we reported a broken sink and it took the management team 3 weeks to fix. 

In my opinion a renter can get much better quality as newer units come online this next leasing season.

I lived her for about 3 months before my roommates and I were released from the lease because there was a seriously bad black mold infestation that the apartments refused to deal with and refused to acknowledge that it was from the faulty insulation. They constantly told us it was our fault because we didn't keep the blinds and Windows open. I'm not sure about you but opening the windows in the middle of winter makes heating pointless. The office didn't want to work with us until my roommate broke down crying. I would not recommend this apartment complex to anyone.

Scott Mt. by the Brooks have been amazing place to live in. It's has easy highway access, and the Max green line is down the hill. For the most part, people have been pretty friendly, and the apartments appeared to be sound proof. We love the fact that our patio over looks a forest, and it's always pleasant to just chill and relax. This complex has a new 24 hour gym facility, and a pool. They recently took out the sauna and hot tub, and changed it into some kind recreational area. It would be nice if they enclose the recreational area, since Oregon has only a few good summer days.

The cons with this place is the fact the rent keeps going up and up. The tenants are responsible to pay water, sewer, and garbage which is not included in the rent. Parking can also be a huge problem especially if you're a 2 car household, and there isn't enough parking space. For the most part, if you're okay with paying for everything, this place is pretty okay.

I love the quite location of the apartment.. its just far from my job, church and extended family. the only issue I have is there is mold that I have to maintain.. other than that, the grounds are immaculate.
These apartments have created a beautiful atmosphere, nestled away from the city hustle while still close enough to feel at home in portland. A fun, creative staff.

The apartment staff are very helpful and generally follow through on issues.  They are close to the highway and certain apartments can be very noisy, it all depends on where your patio faces.  I've lived in better and in worse, I'm just concerned that rent seems to be skyrocketing disproportionately.

My apartment is sufficiently sound proof, so it is very quiet.  The two bedroom is the perfect size for the two of us.  We are a few blocks to Tri-Met, train and bus lines and the freeway, but from here it doesn't really feel like it.  Great pool and hot tub.  Pets are welcome with space to run.  Birds and squirrels all around.  The maintenance staff is really accessible on a daily basis.

Scott Mountain By the Brook Apartments have a great management team that try their best to keep the complex family friendly.  The pool is great for summer fun.  The apartments are good sizes and the master has a walk in closet.  The grounds are well kept.  It is close to the Max, Springwater trail, Clackamas Town Center, tons of shopping and the local elementary school.

I've lived at this place for a few years now, saving up to buy a house.

The location is good- it's very close to a lot of conveniences.  I have no complaints about the maintenance staff- I see those guys busting their butts all the time.  The condition of my apartment is good and they respond promptly as long as I tell them directly that I have a problem.

In the last several months, the office manager has basically been absent.  Posted office hours are almost never adhered to, with the office closed randomly several days per week.  Many days it closes early or opens late, and one or two days a week they just post a crappy sign saying "office closed" and don't bother showing up at all.  The very irregular office hours make it difficult to find a time to pay rent on the day it's due, if you happen to have a job to get to.  Since packages get dropped off in the office if they are too big for your mailbox, I sometimes have to wait a week or more to get lucky enough to catch someone in the office so I can pick up my package.

The pool stayed closed this year, and they have stopped enforcing assigned parking spaces and use of the lot by people that don't live here.  A few vehicles have been abandoned in place for weeks with no action from management.  Either the company is going under and can't afford a full time manager anymore (and just don't want to tell anyone), or they hired the laziest piece of crap imaginable as an office manager after Wade and Lena left.  Either way, they are not interested enough to fix  the problem, and this place is going downhill fast as a result.

Extremely friendly staff, fast maintenance and  very clean apartments! My husband and I lived here for three years and we loved it. The only reason we move was for a third bedroom hoping to expand our family. The granite countertops in the kitchen and bathroom are very nice. I love that the whole apartment was tile floor. It was very easy to clean up and maintain.

Worst apartments ever! RUDE owner, manager Wade is great but the owner of this place is horrid. Mold problems (was told I had to keep my things FIVE inches off of walls connected to outside). Smokers (marijuana included) EVERYWHERE and you can smell it everywhere! Drunks everywhere too. Have had people banging on the outside of my walls and then hear glass bottles being thrown near the trash cans. This place is god awful and just purely for trailer trash. STAY FAR AWAY. And do NOT believe what they show you when you look at these places!

I was so excited when I was shown the preview apartment. It was gorgeous. But, then when I moved in I got an apartment prone to mold, ants, and one with so many problems.... They up rent every other month and now it's beyond expensive for all the problems it has. We plan on moving as soon as possible! Beware!

The owner is cheap and the apartments and facilities show. A tennis court without a net - a pool that is subjectively clean - laundry facilities overpriced and sporadically open.  The inside requires far more space than given here.  It is livable. Just livable.

More than one floor now has Air BNBs and it has completely changed my time here in The Louisa. Lots of traffic all night, parties, loud music, constant pot smoke and loose dogs. And sure, one can complain, and they can “send a warning” - but there’s new people the next weekend. I do not recommend it here and I used to. I like my apartment a lot but not what’s become of my floor.

Professional, actually helpful, 'can-do' staff.  Wonderful multi-generational, diverse residents, vibrant urban setting  for dining, arts, shopping. Stunning views, quiet, substantial units with great appliances, high ceilings and spaces that work for a comfortable,, aesthetic life. Thank you.
After living her for a little over a month I can not complain. The area is great and very convenient, the management is very friendly and helpful and the building is clean, quiet, and safe!
Love my new home and the residents I have met, Great place to be.
Great place to live.  Centrally located in the Pearl.  Leed certified building means that temperatures stay moderate throughout the year.
I have lived here for 8 months.  I love it!   The management is amazing.  I feel at home.    I see myself living here for a long time!

DO NOT MOVE HERE*** I wouldn’t give this place one star if I could.

I’ve lived here for 5 years and at first when John was the property manager everything was lovely and taken care of.
