Now since the pandemic we’ve had previous management transfers and to say the least the quality of EVERYTHING has gone down tremendously. We NEVER get solid communication when we call or email repeatedly. The lack of communication is astounding!

I’ve been waiting for weeks to get lightings replaced, a new kitchen door handle that has cut me several times. It obvious NO ONE CARES AND corporate has taken over this place. Even if location is great and floor plan is decent it is not worth feeling like I am living worse than low income housing and to be paying FULL price.

It’s very dirty, unsanitary, you never know when the laundry is broken/not enough machines and the maintenance staff seems impaired most of the time.

I truly HATE living here and with inflation it’s hard to find another safe clean place to move to. I know I will get out of here but save yourselves and DO NOT even consider moving to this dumpster of a place they call “home”

Such a disappointment. I cannot wait to upgrade my lifestyle with my family. I hope you reading this find a home you love and enjoy.

I have lived here so far for 18 months and couldn't be happier. The community is quiet. The people here are friendly and the atmosphere is very peaceful. I look forward to k hub hub my here far a very long time.

I've lived here for nearly 5 years. At first, it was a lovely place, with nice office people & maintenance. However, in the past 2 years, it's all gone downhill. The office staff never return calls or emails. The maintenance staff is a revolving door. Therefore, nothing gets done. The grounds USED TO BE impeccably maintained. Now, all the lawns are dead & shrubs are quickly following. When the shrubs die, they're yanked out of the ground & never replaced. I go out & dump gallons of water on my shrubs to help them survive. Sidewalks are dirty. Trees are over grown & too close to the buildings. I'm certain it would present a problem if a wild fire broke out. Very worrisome. We've been told the picnic tables that were damaged in a wind storm 2 yrs ago would be replaced. They never have been. We love to barbeque, but it's difficult when you have to stand there holding all your stuff while your food cooks. Many tenants have resorted to barbecuing on their patios. It's strickly prohibited. Strangers prowl the units. There have been several break ins. I personally saw a non-tenent person dumpster diving every trash shed on this property. I reported it to the office with complete details including license plate #. Never heard a word. Don't feel safe here anymore. Sad.
It was great before it got bought out and all the staff changed. Now it's impossible to get in contact with anyone and I've been having unaddressed issues for months as a result.

I love the beautiful setting, especially on the east side of Oleson Road, with the tall trees, the foot bridge near the south entrance above the ravine and the creek near the north bridge entrance - very lovely!

This apartment is not what it seems unfortunately. They have been short staffed ever since we moved in 7 months ago. Maintenance request take anywhere between 2-6 weeks to be fixed. Management is not friendly and has a massive turnover. There are good things. Parking is easy, gym is convenient, trash is clean. Price is reasonable as well.
I have been having a problem with my heating system that I escalated more than three times with no response. I am currently not able to use the heating system in my home because of cold winter.

We had the pleasure of touring the Osprey with Storm, and it was an incredible experience! Despite it being only his second-ever tour, Storm was exceptionally professional and knowledgeable, answering all of our questions with ease. His friendly and personable demeanor made us feel incredibly welcome throughout the entire tour. If we could, we'd give him six stars—he truly went above and beyond in making our visit memorable. Highly recommend requesting him as a tour guide!

Alexandra was very helpful and I plan on living in this community very soon. Great views and living space was open in the units I visited and fabulous river views with great places to walk. 

One thing to note is that I did not arrive on time due to not being sure where to park when I got there to view the unit, so letting prospective residents know where to park would be helpful.
Alex was willing to help anyway she can. The apartment is very quiet and has everything i need.
Management does not respond to concerns of tenants. The price of apartment is high considering the poor service.
Osprey does a poor job managing maintenance requests. Often delaying repairs for months.
Osprey neglects the maintenance concerns of residents and does not return deposits regardless of upkeep. Management is both negligent and dismissive of security concerns.

The staff are very professional. I’m looking for my first apartment so I went to osprey apartments for a tour and it was an incredible experience and I really love the place. I like fact that they followed up with me after the tour. Definitely a five stars!
The leasing agents are so nice & willing to help anyway they can. The apartment is very quiet and has everything we need!

A few months after moving in, construction started on a large apartment complex in the lot next to the building. Now I can’t spend my days off in my apartment because the pile driver right outside my apartment gives me a headache. There have also been 2 incidents where my car has been broken into and my catalytic converters stolen in their offsite parking.

Heather, the new GM of Osprey, is so close to getting her bonus she can smell it!! Valet Service- cut, bottled water- cut, barista service- cut, community events- cut, common area electricity- passed to the residents. I can’t wait to see what she comes up with next. She must be a super star for her corporate over lords. 
Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else. This place is terrible and you never know what to expect next.

As stated in other reviews, we used to have a wonderful community and management. The Osprey was recently sold, and new management has taken over. Since then, they have gotten rid of the free barista services and are intending to replace the valet parking with self-parking (which is going to be impossible because the garage is extremely small and spaces are double parked) and are actually going to charge tenants MORE MONEY to park their own cars. The free coffee they will boast about during your tour is always out of order, the elevators are always locked down by people moving in and out of the building and there are extremely loud parties every Friday and Saturday night in the community lounge. We have lived on the South Waterfront for 5 years and our communication with the Osprey office staff since the transfer of management has been the worst we have ever experienced. We have been looking to transfer our lease to a larger unit (paying more in rent) for the past 4 months. We have requested multiple times to be emailed when a larger unit comes available but unfortunately, we never hear from the leasing agents and instead have to constantly check their availability online. When we finally found a unit within our price range the leasing manager, Heather, told us that they could not honor the online pricing and that the cost would be $500 more per month than what was advertised online (despite having been told to check pricing and apply through their online website by multiple office staff). When we had friends and family call to inquire about the exact same unit, they were told that the online pricing was current. In addition, when we talked with the management company, Avenue 5, their staff told us it is company policy to honor the prices advertised online. Clearly the new leasing manager, Heather, has no shame in lying to the current tenants about pricing that is clearly advertised online in order to make her commission for bringing in new renters. If you are looking to move to the South Waterfront, I would highly discourage you from moving to the Osprey. Avenue 5 should seriously consider hiring a new manager if they want to retain their current tenants and compete with the other apartments in the area offering more sqft for less rent.

The apartment building recently sold and changed management. It’s terrible. Heather says the right things to your face and does nothing about it. She cancelled all the fun community events that we had. She’s hell bent on making her bonus and will sacrifice anything to make the bottom line. The new company has ruined the great community we had.

Osprey was my first home after college and was an amazing place to live. The office staff was incredibly nice and helpful with the move-in and move-out process making it an easy transition into my first Portland living situation. Osprey has the biggest gym in the South Waterfront so I could easily get my home workouts in. All of the other amenities such as ping pong, pool table lounge room, fire pits and deck overlooking water I had a great place to bring friends over on weekends for some fun. The location is perfect being right next to the water almost tucked away from the busy street in South Waterfront area, while still being in the heart of all the shops, food options, and pubs available. This was truly a wonderful living experience and I highly recommend living here!!

Had an Amazing year at the Osprey and sadly have to relocate for school. Excellent management and leasing staff and all the amenities are wonderful. Thanks for making our first year in Portland an excellent one, definitely recommend living here!

Great staff, beautiful location, and great price! You’re close enough to the city to get what you need but get to enjoy peace along the riverfront. Staff is always friendly and provides free coffee/tea/hot beverages daily.

What started out poorly has only gotten worse.  I was one of the first residents of the Osprey, and endured inept management, parties run amok; and various other things that are all part of new resident fun.  For a while, after they fired their horrible manager and got someone with manners, I was hopeful the upward trajectory would continue. And improve it did; they put in a new automated package system, drying cleaning delivery, nice little perks like free coffee and food - all good.  They even installed an operational window in my apartment (yes, there was none prior!).  However, they still have one tragic flaw - not enough parking for their number of residents.  To solve for this, they have instituted a MANDATORY valet "service".  The management is off their rocker if they think residents will want to pay premium dollars for valet - and only end up being inconvenienced.  There are 4 more apartment buildings approved to go up in the near future....choose wisely.

Asa is a great place to live! I almost never hear my neighbors and the floor to ceiling windows give a beautiful view. Happy hours with free beer and wine are super fun. The leasing agent Sage is very helpful and great to chat with! Very much recommend!

Daniel and Dixon help make ASA a great place to live. Any service request is answered almost immediately - and no job is too big or small. From light bulbs to busted washers/driers -- they're both on it and super friendly. Thanks you two!
Great community feeling. Residents are nice and. very dog friendly. Great place to live

Living at Asa has been really nice. We love the community, our flat, and the location. We feel like we lucked out! The flats are well insulated, so don’t hear our neighbors. The staff has been very friendly and we enjoy the amenities. We also love how pet friendly the community is!

We're looking forward to making Asa Flats   Lofts our home. So far, we've had a great experience with the staff and have had all our questions and needs answered. Everything went smoothly during our move-in. Thanks to the Asa Team.

Renter beware, say goodbye to your deposit, and hello to additional fees, on move out you will be given late fees for no explanation, monthly variable fees for the amenities that need repair or close early. On one occasion a person came in and bleed all over they lobby, probably got a fee for that.

I would recommend this place to someone but I would let them know that they need a top level apartment and a corner unit. Walls are extremely thin (thinner than I've ever experienced) and it has affected how much I like living here.
Yay for Manager Colleen and maintenance man Jeff. Yay for friendly tenants! Parking, parking lot, fireplaces need attention. Price point of apartment seems high.
Window AC units would be nice + a community garden, but the unlimited parking, reasonable prices, lovely scenic view to the pond, and great location all make this a pretty awesome place to live.
It's a little pricey, but the apartment is beautiful and we've really appreciated the level of service.
Location is great. The solitude and pond is wonderful. The grounds are very well kept.
I would recommend this community because the price for the value is unbeatable in Portland. We love the pond and the community feel.
Thank you for helping me with my maintenance needs in a timely fashion I appreciate the help
The pond and surrounding area is beautiful, and quiet. Most residents are very nice and friendly.
Complex is lovely (pond, lots of parking, pretty quiet), location is nice, rent is reasonable.
The pond and all of the birds are our favorite. Also, having a washer and dryer in unit is so nice. We love our cozy apartment atmosphere too!

Management has never returned a call or email. You have to pester them for a month for them to do anything. They also randomly changed my bill without any kind of notification. I do not trust them and am moving out ASAP.
I love these apartments. They are kept up nicely and modern. Any maintenance issues are handled within 24 hours.

This place is horrible. There have been 5 different management companies in the last two years that have run this place and each one is worst than the last. 

The current management team fails to communicate at all by both email, phone, and even in person about maintenance requests or other ongoing issues. They never seem to care or know anything that is going on with the property. On top of this, there are smokers on the property who just smoke on the premises and management does nothing. For the prices they are renting units, there are far better places in the area to look into.

Please avoid this place at all costs.

Well just so you know, I had a door slamming next door neighbor and the guy would leave his apartment 3-4 times a night, all after midnight and slam the door that was on the wall that my bed was against so it would wake me up EVERY - SINGLE - TIME.  These guys here at Harrison Tower solved my problem, silenced the door and made it so I can sleep...keep in mind the door is SILENT...something technical I don't get but SEAN and RICHARD and BIG and LITTLE MIKE fixed my problem like POST HASTE!! I am always eternally grateful and now I may never leave --

The building and community is clean, pet friendly and in the perfect location for my purposes.  The staff here - they are great -- from the boys: Mike Mike, Michael and Richard to  everyone in the front office the experience is easy peasy and I really don't have to sweat anything.  Sky from front office proved today just HOW FABULOUS they are - I found a house cat hiding by my porch, she alerted the community and cat and cat person reunited.  Seriously, who cares like that??  These folks do.  My experience only gets better.

We recommended Harrison Tower Apartments. They have nice living environmentsas a whole. When we ask many complicated questions and requests to Tim at front office, he support us quickly and kindly solving problems! Sky at front office provides plenty informations about Portland. Their work is perfect. Moving in Harrison Tower Apartments in this week, residents we met are so friendly.

We highly recommend Harrison Tower Apartments.  They have very nice units that are well maintained & have been updated...many with killer views. A very good value in downtown Portland. Super solid building. We had a really positive experience with the front office..from setting up a showing, viewing the apartment, all the way through the application process. Tim the Assistant Manager is so great.  Friendly, extremely knowledgeable, diligent & responsive.  5 stars.

I recommend living here for a multitude of reasons: Some are a great facility with sizable units, friendly staff that is always happy to help with any request, a good location in the city that isn’t too overwhelming/noisy, and lastly great views in all units with ample natural light for those who need it. 
I have lived here for about a year and have had no complaints.

Harrison Tower is AMAZING! The actual building is phenomenal, the sturdy structure of the building keeps the noise of downtown out and gives you the opportunity to live in a soundproof apartment while living in downtown Portland. The ladies in the leasing office are what truly makes this place feel like home. It is a great community, everyone is so kind and the staff is amazing! Harrison Tower provides the comfort of modern living with the reassurance of safety from the buildings foundation. I HIGHLY recommend moving here!

My partner and I have lived here for almost a year and I can say that it's the best apartment building I've ever lived in. There's three buildings right next to each other, but we live in the 'Velomor' one. I moved from the Bay Area and the prices here can absolutely beat the prices over there. 

Pros:
(1) We currently live in a 1bd/1bath + a den. The den is just a separate room where one wall is not fully connected to the ceiling, so it's the perfect office space. They still counted our apartment as a 1bd, so that's super awesome.
(2) Area is mostly quiet and transportation is super accessible. The MAX train and shuttle cars are across the street; buses are a block away. Area is just outside of the city on the east, and is right before it gets tricky on the west.
(3) There's a mall like 2 blocks away in case you want to hit up a Barnes & Noble, Hot Topic, get some boba, etc. and a small cafe across the street.
(4) The buildings do monthly events! I've never attended one because I keep forgetting but there is literally always another one around the corner.
(5) The interior of the apartment and the building itself is very nice. They upkeep the lobby space everyday. 
I can honestly list more, but these are our big five.

Cons:
(1) Personal con - We live right above a trash compactor, so it does get LOUD in the early morning (Window does a great job of keeping it quiet though).
(2) You do hear some arguing/loud yelling from the passing unhoused, but it's not often.
I can't really name anymore because this place has been absolutely great.

This building is very safe, clean, upscale, and well-managed. The concierge is always helpful and the maintenance staff are efficient, friendly, and prompt. I've lived here since 2018 and I love it. 

I have some issues but they're only with leasing costs and amenities restrictions, all affected by the pandemic.

There are a lot of areas in which this place cuts corners. The fake wood floors dent easily, AC units are loud and the wall control barely works, appliances are run of the mill and the paint they use for the walls is flat paint, which smudges and ruins easily. It's meant for ceilings, not walls. The hot tub and steam room are not kept clean and are quite gross. 

The concierge is awesome, however, it's not enough to justify paying the amount of rent that one pays to live here.

You're sold on luxury living but it feels like a cheap hotel.

Hassalo has been my home for about a year now and I've never been so happy with an apartment complex. I started in a studio unit in Aster Tower, but decided about a month ago that I wanted more space and thus moved across the street to a 1 bedroom in the Elwood building. Both buildings have INCREDIBLE concierge teams - they are polite and efficient and take security very seriously. The apartments are pet-friendly with no breed restrictions and have awesome pet amenities. Maintenance requests are fulfilled same-day or sometimes within hours of submission. Management and leasing was a dream to work with - they got me into my first unit while I still lived out of state, and the transition to my second unit last month was almost seamless (that dang snow storm!). There are loading docks, dollies, and freight elevators available for move in. Location is A  as you are right behind a TriMet Max line/station, streetcars, and several bus lines are nearby. There is a grocery store and a few restaurants on site as well as a medical office, Apple specialist, and H&R Block. You are in walking distance of Lloyd Center Mall, Holladay Park, the convention center/MODA Center, and the Irvington/Broadway shopping area. It is literally a 5 minute train ride across the river to downtown. It's not cheap, but nothing in Portland is these days. What Hassalo does is offer a LOT of bang for your buck. I haven't even had any issues with noise, and Hassalo has rules and procedures (quiet hours and concierge) in place for reporting and dealing with that if it arises. Paying rent and utilities is a breeze with the online portal. There are always community events and raffles going on to promote resident culture and happiness. Overall I have enjoyed every minute of my stay here and highly recommend it.

The Hassalo on Eighth complex is new to Portland and the Velomor is wonderful! The floor to ceiling windows and dark floors are beautiful and make the apartment feel even roomier. Also with high ceilings and an open floor plan 700 square feet feels like far more!

Nobody could dream better of an apartment close to grocery stores, restaurants, and at a walkable distance to almost everything. The Velomor is a dog and cat friendly environment with no size restriction. I wouldn't forget the spacious apartments with an affordable rent and energy-efficient appliance.

I moved recently to the Douglas and the experience has been excellent. I'm even recommending it to my son. Love the location as I can be at any place at a walking distance or just take a bus or street car. Car not needed, at least for me and my family as most of us work remotely.
I recently moved at the Douglas and the work requested on the condo was quick and efficient. The staff has been very helpful with all my questions, and able to respond them all. Thank you!
I just celebrated 10 years living at the Douglas and love living here!
The Douglas has been a great place for my family and I to live.  It is a safe neighborhood with great views of the river and walking paths.  We've loved it!

The Douglas has been a good place to call home. Having a townhome instead of living in a high-rise was the biggest selling point for our family. We also loved the idea of living in the south waterfront area which is close to walking trails, multiple bridges, and downtown. The property management team has been friendly but with many staff changes during our year at this property, there was difficulty with organization & management of the property.

I have lived at the Douglas for almost a year and I am so happy to be here.  I have met some really nice people and I love living by the riverfront.  We are close to everything, but also enjoy our quiet block.
There have been several recent changes that have happened that make this place less and less appealing. The upkeep is one of the concerns. Office staff has recently been making excuses for this.

This place is so gross. “If you want motel style accommodations for luxury style prices, this is the place for you!”
Theft is rampant here. Everyone’s packages are constantly being stolen and Management does nothing. I found a giant pile of opened and sorted through packages that someone picked through and only stole what they wanted! Cars get smashed in all the time- it’s happened to me twice in their underground parking structure that is supposed to be secure. Costs $150 per month to park! My bike got stolen locked up inside the garage too! And when you go to Management they could care less. I’ve never dealt with any management quite like these girls. They have no concern, they don’t want anything to do with it and do not help at all. It’s been an absolute nightmare living here! I’m not alone either! All my neighbors feel the same!

Our family moved here from across the state to attend school at OHSU last June.  The Sanctuary Apartments team did a great job of welcoming us and helping us get settled in our new apartment.  They also offered great benefits and discounts for being affiliated with OHSU. The property is only a few years old and is well maintained by great professional staff.  The apartment is clean, well-insulated, and has nice new appliances.  Since the property sits right along the Willamette River the greenway trail offers a great place to exercise and take the dogs out for a peaceful walk.  Also, the staff does a great job of promoting a community amongst its residents by hosting a happy hour with free drinks every Friday to allow residents the chance to meet and get to know each other.   Overall our experience with the Sanctuary Apartments has been a wonderful blessing to our family and we couldn't be happier with our new home.

You will be charged with $165 cleaning fee without warning upon move-out. This was taken out of my deposit. They did not state in the lease or at any point of living here that there would be a cleaning fee at move-out. Carpet was brand new except for 1 year of me living there. Carpet was vacuumed before move out. I even emailed them with copies of the lease and the specifics of why a renter would get charged; nowhere does it state a generic cleaning fee at move-out.

Living here was great. Awesome location. Lived on first floor of B building and it was mostly quiet. Could hear some noises through walls.

Great location! So many amenities! Only half of your packages lost! Lovely gym - treadmills sometimes work! Beautiful rooftop/grills - no sink or bathroom, just lick the salmonella off your fingers or head to the other building. Spectacular river views. Such fun loading wagons to carry groceries from a parking garage, through the rain, across RR tracks! You won't be lonely - sounds like neighbors are in bed with you! Responsive staff will totally get your lost packages, just as soon as they feel like it. And so sweet... They thoughtfully post a notice of eviction on neighbors' door for late rent after learning they're out of town due to a death. Don't worry about the 43 page lease, theres nothing hiding in there. Move here!

This complex has a lot of appealing features, new appliances, waterfront view, great amenities. However, I would not recommend renting here if you want to live somewhere quiet. I like to come home from work and be able to relax and go to bed at a decent house; but it is no Sanctuary living here. The insulation between the floors and walls is terrible. I feel as though I have a roommate that I've never met. I can hear the people above me arguing late at night, I can also hear every move they make such as getting something from their dresser, walking to the bathroom, cooking, knowing what time they get up in the morning, etc. When I have talked to management about mentioning to them that there is someone living below them who does not appreciate being kept up/woken up at late hours I get the response of it is just everyday noise. From experience of living in other apartments, this is not just everyday noise.

Unfortunately, Trion Living is a supremely poor management company. As many other reviewers note, the list of issues is long, from a months-long elevator outing that was not addressed (because the Management Company reportedly did not pay their bills), to bogus charges and unresponsive on-site staff. In the last year, utility costs have exploded without any explanation, service has gone down, and roaches have gone up. On-site staff is actively lying to prospective tenants that the reviews here are exaggerated or not true, which is simply mind-blowingly brazen. Don't fall for it! You'll regret signing a lease here.

Trion is an absolutely terrible property management company. Things went downhill almost immediately when they took over from the previous company.

Where to start - leaking effluence in the parking garage on my car that is still stuck on the paint, stolen packages, stolen TV in the common area that was never replaced, common area carpets are stained, rooftop is not maintained and has continually gotten worse, stolen bikes. Numerous key fob issues, moldy common area HVAC, burst pipes in mutliple locations with no mitigation strategies to help with cleanup. Their key control is abysmal so who knows who has access to the building.  They've specifically said they have no responsibility for safety or security.  The elevator was out for months, challenging our senior residents with walking up 5 to 6 flights of stairs and a general attitude that they should deal with it. Any attempt to get updates was met with a feeling that we should suck it up. There has been no attempt to compensate us for any of this. It's been comical to see how they avoid any attempt at customer service and aren't professional enough to have management respond to our concerns, only leasing agents.

Broken elevator. Black mold. Stolen mail/packages, WEEKLY. The building is not locked & anyone off the street can just walk in. Several renters have noticed their apartments have been attempted to be broken into. Several renters have seen street people walking the halls. They just recently evicted a drug dealer we all complained about. Management charges arbitrary fees & forces renters to pay, ie “Trash Concierge”, even if renters don’t want or use or even agree to the service. The building appears fine & good… but Trion Management is absolutely horrible.

Hopefully this review will save someone else from having the awful experience myself and other tenants have had...we've lived here over 3 years and while wonderful when we moved in when Trion took over we've seen a serious decline in both service and value. Rent continues to go up however the building has not had any improvements or updates in amenities (quite the opposite as we have a very small fitness center with old equipment, disgusting rooftop furniture, an outdated intercom system to let people into the building, parking garage where the gate has been broken multiple times, trash chute has also been broken more than I would expect, even the printer we could all use in the common room has been removed and the overall cleanliness of the building has also suffered). I'm pretty sure that there is also mold behind all of the water damage stains in the 1st/2nd floor stairwells, it smells bad too. In addition, there have been break-ins to the parking garage, and we have had multiple packages stolen from the "secured lobby" AND had an expensive bike stolen from the locked bike room INSIDE of the locked building where the bike was also secured with a lock to the rack...and when the building has said there is security onsite I have never seen them once. There isn't a single improvement I can point out since Trion took over. 

Valet Living is a  new forced cost to pay a company to take your trash from the front door to the trash room - which we do not want.

The building has 1 elevator and it was completely out for 90 plus days (Dec 2023 to Mar 2024). We received a one time bag of candy hung on our doors "with about 5 pieces of drug store candy" as a token of their appreciation for our patience with the frustrating situation. This would be a cute/kind little gesture for general resident appreciation but does not address the severity of what happened.

We have had issues with our account balance being inaccurate despite never once having missed a rent payment and the time it took to get this issue corrected was ridiculous (months). While waiting for this to be corrected we were getting text messages about late payments and late fees being assessed to our account. The building did remove all of the late fees when they finally resolved the accounting issue.

We are leaving soon, but never want others to go through this helpless experience. Trion Property Mgmt is an example of why there is a serious need for improved renters rights!

This is a great location and building, but unfortunately management has declined dramatically since taken over by Trion properties a few years ago.  There have been several serious problems including break-ins & thefts, flooding in apts, elevator out for months and mold buildup in HVAC systems.  Trion refuses to address tenant complaints, therefore tenants are forced to move out.

The livability at the Russell has deteriorated in the last few years since Trion Living took over.
Management routinely ignores serious problems and concerns of the residents. The one elevator was down for more than three months, multiple apartments were flooded by burst pipes, and there have been numerous break-ins and thefts. 
They have also discontinued the 24/7 emergency phone service. Now you have to call the main management number and leave a message. Then THEY will determine if it is an actual emergency or not. If they deem it is not an emergency, a maintenance person will get to you when they are available. There is no full-time maintenance person.
Many residents have decided to move out, so that is why there are so many vacancies available that they are trying to fill.

Their autopay system is buggy and sometimes doesn’t draw funds.  Their finances and documentation is all over the place, they sneakily REMOVED our reasons for leaving from the final sign-out forms and we had to email them to put that in.  Communication is haphazard and inconsistent.  They claimed they hired security for patrolling the sketchy Multnomah St portion, but I never saw anyone once.  They planted new bushes and then didn’t water them. The road to get into the parking garage is constantly blocked off by buses and ubers for the neighboring hotel. To top it all off, they had the GALL to raise our rent above the maximum amount allowed in Multnomah County.  Don’t move in here, at least not under current ownership (or whatever private equity acquires them)

First off, the management is terrible. Voicemails were never returned. Emails were never responded to. We even used the "suggestion box" with no response.
We left the apartment immaculate and in better condition than when we moved in and they still charged us $2600 early lease termination fee and $600 in "painting and cleaning" fees. I have left voicemails and talked to Chris in the office, who says he has nothing to do with it, and have not heard from anyone with an explanation for the $600 theft of our deposit.
The halls were dirty, the elevators were filthy and only one seemed to work at a time. We finally decided to move because of the constant smell of marijuana on our floor despite it being a non-smoking building. It is so strong it would fill our apartment and we would have to leave. I complained several times and never received a response. There are homeless people sleeping in the bushes and in the entry which made it feel unsafe to walk the dog in the morning. At least once a week a car window would be broken out in front of the building. Management posted a sign in the elevator saying they hired a security company to patrol but I never saw them once.
It is really sad because this is a decent building in a cool part of St. Johns. Like the other reviews mention, it is all management.

I’ve lived at the Union at St. John’s since January. There are many wonderful things about living here, but the highlight is by far seeing Mt Hood AND the St. John’s bridge from my apartment. I live in a 2 bedroom with my partner and our 2 dogs. We have plenty of room for living comfortably and a storage unit down the hall from our apartment to house our unused items. There is a lovely patio, garage parking, a nice community room and gym, there’s a dog washing station and monthly resident repurpose and recycle events. The apartment is really quiet except for street traffic, but it’s to be expected in the more urban setting. We love the aesthetic of the building, the attentive maintenance staff, the location (walking distance to several parks and Lombard street), and most importantly, this building is full of friendly people and adorable doggos making it feel like home.  If you’ve never been to St. John’s, it’s a great little community with everything you need nearby/within walking distance, access to disc golf at Pier Park, Chimney park for the dogs, lots of restaurants and bars, several grocery markets, and the most beautiful bridge in all of Portland. I highly recommend The Union at St John’s!

The Union is a solid apartment building, you can't really complain. I have lived here for 2 years and I've always enjoyed my experience. I'm always cared for and accommodated by management and others who live there. The one thing that can be tough is parking (if you don't pay for a spot inside the garage). It may seem like a pricey place, but you get what you pay for and it's a quality living environment.
The Union at St. Johns has been a great place to live. The building and its units are very clean and modern. The building is in a great location. Staff and residents are very friendly as well.

I really enjoy living here. The building is very new and the apartments are nice and modern. The location is great, within walking distance to many restaurants/bars/shops as well as the grocery store and Cathedral Park. The building feels very secure and the staff is helpful. Touring was easy and informative, and options for lease length are more flexible than anywhere else comparable.
Been renting 14 years smoothly. Dont know if it just Portland or this building. Honestly at this point it's a joke. Been here a year. thank god it's almost over.

I drove across town for a viewing at 2:00 today. They emailed a follow up to remind me about our viewing, I guess to make sure I was going to show up. When I got there, I called, emailed, and texted. I also knocked on the office door. No one responded after 20 minutes.

I took off work for the viewing and used gas.

Very disappointed. I guess it's good to find these things out before signing a lease, though.

You will literally hear everything above you. Footsteps, conversations, etc. We had awful upstairs neighbors and the mgmt did not resolve the situation after 5 documented noise complaints. The building is decent but they really lack any sense of their advertised community. Homeless people are in abundance here and it creates uncomfortable and unsafe situations as they loiter next to the recycling garage attempting to get in as you have to go outside the building to enter the recycling room. Would never recommend this company or building to anyone. There are better deals.

I have lived at the Holm for 18 months.  In that time I had my vehicle stolen out of their gated, underground parking garage.  The building itself has been broken into more times than I can count.  I have caught people breaking in the outside doors myself and had to stop them.  The management does not communicate to residents when break ins or theft have occurred. Storage lockers have been ransacked, bikes have been stolen, and cars parked on the street will get broken into.

The property manager means well, but she is in way over her head.  She often forgets your name and will ask you if you are a current resident.  If she has a question she will harrass you in the hallway at her convenience rather than calling or sending a professional email.   I have been charged accidental late payment fees on three occasions and had to email multiple times to get it fixed.  

Rent price will go up every year.  They will nickel and dime you for anything they can.  The amenities are subpar given the cost of rent.  

Sellwood is an awesome neighborhood but there are so many other apartment buildings that offer real value for the cost.  I would warn all my friends to never move in here.

This management company is terrible! I dealt with so many lies from the staff while I lived there. The conditions for pets is also unsafe--my dog had to be hospitalized for poisoning after walking through a cleaning agent they were using in the garage. Staff apologized for it, but denied toxicity. Not to mention that there is dog waste CONSTANTLY in the halls and elevators. I had a leak in my ceiling and they lied about it existing and then did a terrible job fixing it which was really frustrating because I am chronically ill. Management also lied about the state of my apartment when I moved out and charged me a ton for normal wear and tear after telling me it looked great and I wouldn't be charged.  They additionally charged me rent and bills for days after I had moved out. For two weeks before I left they stopped taking my calls or answering emails--they immediately turned my bill over to an intermediary where I was unable to dispute the trumped up charges and had to pay or else be turned in to collections. This company represents the worst of what is happening in Portland!

Please do not move into this apartment complex (or anywhere owned by fairfield!!) We were among the first to move into the  complex in Nov 2020. When we moved in, we discovered the water was turning the tub blue, and it was lukewarm. We submitted a request and heard nothing. We then contacted the landlord who sent a guy up to tell us that he wouldn't raise the water temp because it would cause the boilers to be replaced sooner. I informed the landlord that the water temp was reading well below the portland city ordinance. Shortly after the water got hotter. In March 2022, we notice our rent is $150 more than usual. They can’t raise rent without giving you at least 90 days notice so we ask our landlord who says the notice was sent back in Oct 2021 via mail, a our door, and the online portal. I ask for proof that it was sent - she has none. She looks at the online portal with me, and the letter isn’t there. She comes back a few minutes later and says she found it on there. She looks at my phone again, and it’s still not there. She refreshes the page and it magically appears. Luckily, I had taken a screenshot of the page earlier and I show her that it wasn’t there. She clearly added it after our initial conversation and lied about it. I ask for her supervisor’s information and she refuses to give it to us. She later calls and gives us an offer of $100 a month increase but refuses to budge on the 90 day notice. We counter offer and she eventually gives us a new notice which renews the 90 days so we start looking for a new apartment. We send our intent to vacate via email and we are ignored, and a follow up email which is also ignored. We ask again in May because our rent has not been prorated for the month. She gives us a number and says she will update it. Days go by and it’s not updated so we go back and make her do it in front of us. We move out May 15. It is now May 25 and I get an email from a debt collector, trying to collect $50 from me. Absolutely no description of what the charge is for, and I imagine that is in addition to the security deposit that they will likely not be refunding us. We were never told of an additional charge and there was no damage. We spent hours cleaning after we moved out so that we would not be charged extra. If I can tell you anything from this, please do not live here. We moved into an apartment downtown for the same price we were previously paying and the management is 100x better. Please stay away from this place.

The people are great. Complex is nice. But when it comes to being a person with disabilities it’s not great. People don’t know we’re the accommodation for is. They delayed my move in do to this. Takes a big effort to get a hold of someone and get a reply.

We have lived here for 2 years when the building first opened. It was a very nice and pleasant place to live. The staff was wonderful and very considerate. However, now the looks are just surface level. If you enjoy constant garbage in the parking areas, waste and dog pee/poop in the elevators and entrances, weed smell’s coming through your vents, security issues (car vandalism, storage locker break in, broken glass/doors) then this is the place for you! Further, the parking door hasn’t worked for 6 months while tenants are still paying for “secure” parking. I have witness over 10 vehicle vandalisms since living here. I hate to say it, but I am really disappointed with this place and the trajectory that management (not building management, corporate level) has allowed this place to continue in. I am sure if those in charge lived, here they would feel the same. Hope this review is helpful to those considering living here. So much for living in downtown Portland.

Don't, just don't. It looks nice on the surface, but the maintenance and security issues make it unbearable.

Garbage is constantly piled in the garage (they didn't plan accurately for the amount of garbage produced by this many units). 

Security features are broken (glass doors, main doors, glass around fire pit on rooftop). Rarely fix items when they break or wait months and months to do it.

Good things are the proximity to bars, restaurants and downtown. Love the open floorplan in my unit. Lobby is kept clean. Low deposits and fees.

This place has been broken into so many times. Management is so incompetent. I have had my belongings stolen twice and the only thing management has done is remove the security cameras from the “secure” storage lockers. 

The doors to the building are constantly broken and left open for days. Instead of fixing the doors, management just locks them so even the tenants can’t use them.  

Don’t live on the east side of the building. Trash gets collected at 3 am multiple times a week and it is unbearably loud. 

You have to pay a $14 monthly fee to receive packages. They have an Amazon locker but it hasn’t worked in the 1.5 years that I’ve lived here. 

Be wary of 5 star reviews on o their sites. There are a lot of reviews from the staff which skew the ratings and are very misleading.

The hot water doesn't work from 5:30 - 7AM.  I am not sure when it starts/stops working, but it always works in the afternoon.  

I reached out to maintenance, who came and took a look at my shower 6 weeks (!) after the maintenance request, and their hypothesis was that too many people take showers at that time. 

They did not give me any indication that the issue would be resolved in the future.  

In a similar vein, I have lived here 6 months now.  All elevators have been working ~1% of my stay here. 

I conclude that this property is either bad at maintenance or they do not fund it adequately.

There has been lots of noise for the past 2 months and I have  talked to the leasing office SO MANY times and each time they ensure me that it will be fine, but nothing happens. I have spoken to them so many times for the past month or so about aggresive dog barks that will literally wake you up every single day and they act like they are handling the situation but in reality the issue is still going on and I lost hope in this situation. If you care about noise and want to be able to relax and have peace in your own place, I don't think that this is the right place.

I had high hopes for this place as we had a good experience with Greystar in the past, and things were fine when we initially moved in. 
The staff seemed nice at first. Regrettably, after a year of living here, I've encountered major issues, including:
- a water leak 
- unpleasant odors of cigarettes and cannabis from neighboring units 
- and incidents of car break-ins. 

The water leak is the most recent problem affecting several units. While I am writing this review, there's currently construction taking place in my unit literally at the moment, making it challenging for me to focus on my work (I am working from home). This problem has persisted for a month. The maintenance team and vendor unexpectedly knocked on my door during my work hours and requested entry, causing disruptions to my workflow - there were no specific times in the given notices. Additionally, the management team failed to communicate the extent of the construction.
I love my floor plan, the location, and the building staff.

A small oasis among the hustle and bustle of city life, the building is clean, secure and the units are peacefully quiet.
Staff is very friendly and helpful, plus the amenities are wonderful and well maintained. 
Being a block away from the waterfront park is a great excuse to get some fresh air at any time.

Overall a very nice experience here. I feel safe because not only is the lobby door secure, but the elevators are too. The kitchen is incredible—all the cabinet space I could need or want, plus a pantry and gas range. The washer and dryer in the enormous walk in closet is exactly what I was looking for, and the soaking tub has already gotten a lot of use. The apartments are quiet and I seldom hear neighbors, even in the hallway. 

 The dog park has helped my rescue pugs to come out of their shell and mingle with other dogs—we really love that amenity a lot. There are nice community spaces as well, and I love having access to a grill when meal prepping for the week. 

My only critiques would be to make it easier and more convenient to recycle, and to have pre installed curtain rods on every window since we’re not allowed to install our own and the blinds don’t block out light or afford much privacy. The windows are huge and let in lots of light, and a tension rod simply isn’t up to the task for covering these monsters with the curtains necessary for blocking the city light at night.

Went for a tour, the staff were very communicative and helpful. The rooms were very spacious and clean, I personally like these apartments because there close to the lloyd district and shopping centers.

My apartments been flooding for over a month and I’ve had to fight with management to even get my questions answered. It wasn’t until 4 units flooded in one night that they even had someone come in to look at the damage. They still want full rent despite having to tear out my floors and walls.

This place is a bunch of old buildings with new paint. My apartment has been flooding for over a month now and management is taking their sweet time to “fix” it. I have to fight with them just to get my questions answered. It took 4 apartments flooding in one night for them to even get someone to look inside. They still want full price rent though.

The staff here is super friendly and helpful, there are great amenities, and the units are cute! Unfortunately though, I can hear every step my upstairs neighbor takes, and I feel bad for whoever lives below me. Obviously people can't be expected to tiptoe around their apartment, but it would have been great if their was better sound dampening in the floor/ceiling.

I can’t say enough great things about the staff! Especially the manager Mattie she is so thoughtful and hard working. She has been so accommodating when working with us to try and find a place here in the Portland area. We are new to Oregon and she ensured we felt taken care of and safe in their hands. Can’t wait to call this place home!

I was one of the first to move in to LMR, and the only real knock I had against it was nothing they controlled. The surrounding neighborhood roads are very narrow (which I don't mind) but the ongoing construction nearby made it a nightmare to get around. Now that it's all completed I can highly recommend moving in as it's in a great neighborhood and has a very professional staff.
We have been living in Lakemont Ridge for almost 7 months now, great apartments love the location and the view. Very near to Sato Elementary School.

This place is clean, beautiful and safe. I love waking up to a view of the hills up in Bethany. You are close to the Bethany town center as well! The staff is friendly and responsive! I love living here.

I’ve lived here for about 7 months now and I love it. I moved from the east coast. LMR is a really quiet community and you can’t beat the location. It’s close to grocery stores, parks, and easy access to downtown as well!
The Dylan is a great place to live and extremely convenient to everything around the Portland area. The maintenance staff is great, especially Vito. He is very timely and respectful.

Under no circumstances should you move here! Choosing this property and management group has been the biggest leasing mistake I’ve ever made. The Dylan has been nothing short of a nightmare. My locked storage unit was robbed TWICE, encountered rats and roaches both inside and outside the property, and witnessed drug addicts openly using on the property. Save yourself the agony and look elsewhere!

Also, I moved out only a few months ago so there’s zero personal gain from making this post. I’m sincerely hoping this post will prevent others from making the same mistake.
It’s a new, clean, and safe community in a nice part of town.
The units are very nice and cheaper then most apartments in the area. Lots of great amenities and located close to downtown.

Terrible experience with this building. Received a final statement after moving out and they are charging me $165 for "utilities" when I have paid every month, taking it from my deposit that I now have no control over. The manager Sydney reviewed this final statement and signed it without double checking my past utility payments. Now it's Wednesday and I have not heard back from them after I have been trying to contact them since Friday after I have emailed and called numerous times. Avoid this building. They are money hungry and do not care about you.
The crew at the Dylan made the whole moving process smooth especially because we were coming from across the country.

Living at the Dylan has been such a pleasant change from living on the East side. It feels like a community. The leasing office has been so helpful when I’ve had questions. Maintenance team has gone above and beyond to handle any service requests I’ve had since moving in.
The art, decor, music, the out door Amenities are all so nice,
The Dylan has great staff, but beware the level of quality for the price. The value is not there.

Dylan is a new development on South Waterfront. There is no view of river itself from the complex but it is super close to the water. It is in a safe and clean community with easy access to public transit street cars that go into town and electric bike rental. The community has a lot of important amenities for safety and comfort.

During my virtual hunt for a brand spanking new apartment, specifically in South Waterfront, I stumbled upon the Dylan. I knew that I had to spring into action quickly. Taylor has been super helpful, prompt, informative, and friendly in our communications which made our transition here run smoothly. I love the close proximity to the food trucks and blue star donut, nomnom.

The Dylan is a brand new apartment building with up to date appliances. The amenities are beautifully designed and make living here feel like home. The leasing staff are very kind and respectful and always ready to answer any questions I have. I would highly recommend The Dylan to anyone looking for a place that embodies the spirit of Portland with comfort and style.
A well done building with beautiful finishes. Solid and quiet.
The management team and everyone here are the best. They pride themselves on making sure your happy. It felt like coming home with Tina and Skye.
The Dylan has been an excellent place to live - from building amenities and spacious layouts to friendly and helpful staff. I have very much been enjoying my residence here!

If you are interested in living on the south waterfront, consider The Dylan. If you are an OHSU employee looking for the easiest commute ever, this is the neighborhood for you! My husband and I have only lived here for a couple weeks, but we love being part of the new and growing community here at The Dylan. It’s a brand new building and everything is so nice. We found a unit that suits us and our needs perfectly and the community amenities have been so fun to explore and utilize. The leasing team has been fantastic from day 1. They are kind and very welcoming. They made it an easy choice and we are honored to live here.
Love how dog friendly the Dylan and surrounding area is!
New apartment, clean and very well located! Polite and approachable employees.  Nicely decorated and very functional amenities!

My girlfriend and I stayed here for 6 months with our daughter and dog and it was a terrible experience. The neighbors were the best part of our experience because we could complain about outrageous policies like not being able to access your own rental account, being told not to let your pets go to the bathroom in the courtyard, and getting charged extra fees for things like other people leaving too much garbage in the dumpster…it’s clearly a space for people out of town coming to Portland that get stuck paying outrageous rent and in return having poor management on top of it. Living there made us take a step back and find something more local and actually worth the price and amenities.

Even before moving in this place was a pain, we had to constantly contact the property to verify they got certain payments or paperwork because they would never contact us or verify with us that they got what they needed. Couldn't even SEE the place 3 days before move in day "because it wasn't ready". There is NO A/C in the units (unless you PAY for them to install one) the only A/C is in the "lobby" and a little bit in the hallways. The "studios" are the size of a dorm room...If that much. Tiny fridges, no "storage" space (unless you count  a 3x3 alcove as storage.) Non smoking friendly at all (can't smoke ANYWHERE on property and management threatens to write you up if you smoke around the properties.) Poor management as well.  If my partner and I weren't on a time cramp to find a place before moving in here we would have gone elsewhere, and as soon as our lease was up we LEFT FOR GOOD!!!! I guess the half star it could even earn could be their security is half decent (if other residents don't leave the gate open and as long as the criminal can't jump fences.)

Laundry machines always broken. management is ghost. Side doors and front doors always broken so random people come inside the building all the time. Management never knows what is going on. All the so-called “new” appliances are cheap and break all the time. Kitchen is a joke, you can’t fit two regular size pans on the stovetop at the same time. No ovens in unit. the precious good reviews are very obviously fake. something weird is going on here
I have almost 2 months here! the neighborhood is quiet! the apartments are new! I am very comfortable here! the internet is very fast! and the manager is very friendly! I highly recommend it!

The price are pretty decent in comparison to other building near by especially for a brand new building. Management is great, helpful, prompt and courteous. The location is my favorite part and the neighbors are friendly, nice and respectful.
Emily and Megan are the best. They made the process easy and smooth. Solid communication. Quick action. No complaints.

One of the easiest jobs is being a leasing agent for an apartment, but apparently, the staff at Griffis South Waterfront is not even competent enough for this simple task. 

I've lived here since March of 2021, and can't say too many nice things about living here other than the view I had. I'll start with the cons (it's all cons), and end with the pros of living at the Griffis South Waterfront.

THE CONS:

- The ELEVATORS. Be prepared to constantly have elevators go down. While I know this is something that happens with all buildings, it's the duration and how often it happens that's of annoyance. It's as if management is skipping out on maintenance with Otis (the largest elevator manufacturer in the world).

The day I moved in, I had an elevator fail, and drop down a floor. It was quite a scare, and honestly, I'm surprised I stayed, and still use the elevators.
Most recently, there was a puddle in the elevator, and what did management do? They placed a "wet floor" sign instead of shutting down the elevator because it's leaking from the ceiling of the elevator. The elevator is now down for a month for repairs because of the water damage (no common sense on management).

- AC UNIT. This thing is down often. Thankfully it was working during the hottest days of the year during the summer, but living on the 22nd floor causes an issue even during the winter because there's no air circulation with how the windows open. So there's just static warm air all year long without the AC working. When I open the window, the neighbors downstairs think it's "cool" to smoke cigarettes or weed from their balcony. That smell travels through the windows and literally lingers for hours. It's never addressed other than a couple of emails advising residents not to smoke within the property (that does nothing).

- MAINTENANCE ISSUES. There are quite a few maintenance issues that arise frequently, but the maintenance crew is really quick at addressing them (this is a con and a pro). The unit was renovated before I moved in, but they used the lowest bidder with the lowest quality materials that never last. Which in the long run must cost them money having to repair often. This is more of an annoyance.

- PARKING GARAGE. Make sure you lock your vehicle and don't leave any valuables because I have had one break-in. I guess it should have been common sense on my part since this is Portland.

I love living here!!! Dacia, Megan and Chiyo are friendly, responsive, caring and always say hi to me and my dog when we walk by. Nate, Armani and Reyes in maintenance respond ASAP to any work orders and are professional and very knowledgeable. Marlis is so sweet and keeps the building looking amazing. The neighborhood is awesome and the food trucks are a nice bonus. We love walking to the riverfront at sunset. Would highly recommend!!!

Griffis only cares about appearances. They constantly are making "improvements" that don't really matter with total disregard for the inconvenience of current residents. Expect at least a few various inspections, replacements, repairs, and cleanings each month. All of these things are fine on their own, but the problem is the way Griffis conducts them. If you're lucky they give you a multi-day time frame, so you have to be ready for a 3rd party contractor or maintenance to enter your home at any time. If you need to park somewhere else because they are doing something the in parking garage you're lucky if they reimburse you.

Exactly that. No heating controls, not even over on or off. No paved parking. Up Marquam Hill, which can be interesting in the winter.  Good space for the price, however, especially being this close to downtown. 8 line right out front and a few blocks from the Portland Aerial Tram. Thai food place right down the street and a Plaid that closes at midnight. Satisfied, particularly on a student budget.

We've been living here for 3 years and have never had a bad experience. The staff is attentive, work orders are filled extremely promptly and apartments and amenities are new and well maintained. The area has also developed with new restaurants and bars popping up all the time. The street car literally stops in front of the building and downtown is a 20 minute walk.
horrible staff who don't care about tenants, maintenance never came and that's not what the apartments look like on the inside

The prices are good. The gas heaters don’t actually warm anything up and will waste your money, so be ready to invest in a space heater because it gets cold here. The laundry facilities are limited and break down sometimes. Not very soundproof and can often here people above or beside you. People often live or hang out in front of the building. Access to the streetcar right out front is great. Super close to PSU campus and safeway. Closet storage is big.

I love the feel of this historic building from the crown molding to the clawfoot tub. If you're looking for the dream experience of living in Portland than this is the place for you! Being that it's right next to the PSU campus, living here is especially convenient for students like myself who attend the University. The environment feels safe due to the fact that the occupants must be attending college to live here so there are no creepers to be found. I would suggest getting a corner unit for the balcony, which is great for people watching and catching all the action that goes on in this strange and beautiful city.

The property manager changed a couple years ago and the property management has suffered. Management is poor at communicating, often not responding to tenants. Pipes have burst, resulting in multi-floor floods several times. Management fails to provide alternative housing, causing tenants to live in flooded units as loud fans attempt to dry them out. Building-wide fire alarms go off routinely (about 1-3 times per month), resulting in building-wide evacuations. These happen without warning or follow-up, so there is no way to tell whether this is a drill or if the building is safe to enter.

This building is in such a great location, after months of searching it is one of the more reasonably priced places for how new and nice it is.  It is right in between 23rd/21st and the Pearl district, so it's kind of the "Portland area we know and love". There's no AC provided, which is something to keep in mind in case PDX has another crazy summer.  Aside from no AC the only other cautionary information there is, is that this area is full of new construction and so it can be pretty noisy.  Overall great price for a great central location.

We fell in love with this apartment the minute we saw it.  You get to pick the color you want your living room wall to be.   There is a recycle/trash shoot on every floor.  Granite countertops   And a great walk in shower and nice wood floors. Mail and  packages are safely delivered inside.  Located in the middle of a very happening area!
the hot tub is closed. The elevators are broken. The office ladies are nice. I hear my neighbors are very loud and not nice. i don’t like that there are mean random people in the lobby

Loving the apartment so far. Super cute little space that's perfect for my needs. The people working in the office are outstanding and incredibly helpful. Can't wait to spend the next few years of my life here!
Collective on 4th is amazing! Modern units, ideal location. Friendly staff, convenient, and great community. Highly recommend for students and young professionals in Portland!
It's good community to live . It has all the amenities like gym , swimming pool, parking space, party area, study room and has good environment around.

The amenities are nice but they are always broken. The apartment is nice but things are always broken as well. The pipes from the apartment above mine always squeak and I have asked for it to be fixed multiple times.
I love this community and my gorgeous apartment. The price is very reasonable and the views are amazing. Amenities are amazing as well. The leasing office is very attentive and helpful.
I love living in here great 1br apartment with large bathroom. Great location. Utilities include so worry free monthly no bills. Studios are quite small so i prefer 1br urban .
New manager ruined this place.She is very rude unprofessional with a nasty attitude. Do not recommend living here.
The set up is gorgeous. The natural lighting is perfect. I love this property! Even the people are lovely and pleasant to converse with.

Not perfect but it's a good building and the staff makes an effort to keep things running smoothly. Neighbors can be loud like with any apartment building. Frustrating though, to have to ask grown people to turn down surround sound, which shouldn't exist in an apartment. Unfortunately, maintenance has no consideration for how loud they're being, whether its while conducting maintenance on a unit or just talking on the phone in the hallways and empty units. I don't understand the disregard. The location is prime, IMO. A little pricey, but if you wait for a unit to reduce in price, you can get a good deal. The building is clean and in walking distance to great food.

I love the 1bdr apartment I moved into almost three months ago (as big as my previous 2bdr in LA!): The amenities, its central location and it is also surprisingly quiet (amazing vaulted ceilings, so I never hear the neighbors above me!), which makes it feel more like home everyday, if not a sanctuary on some days (like somebody "up there" likes me!).

The management team (Lucy and Christina): Fantastical! Easy to communicate with, genial and they're professional in a personable way, where they definitely have built a community atmosphere here that's inclusive for all the tenants. I feel confident and at ease with them around!!

I've been a resident of Grand Belmont for almost a year and it has been a pleasant experience. The location is ideal. The building is located right off of the train line with tons of local restaurants within walking distance. There is on the site covered parking for those who do drive. (I don't drive) There is also an indoor bike rack storage and pet grooming station if your dog gets a little messy during your walks. Maintenance cleans the floors daily and as far as management is concerned I've only reached out to them one time and they have been cool. The only thing that I would have liked to know before hand was the separate utilities bill for the building. Ideally, it would have been helpful for me to factor that portion into my overall monthly rent. The way it works is you'll pay for your rent, Grand Belmont's building utilities, and your apartment's utilities (lights, gas, wifi, etc.). So it's three separate bills instead of two. Besides that I have no issue.

We were initially happy our first 2 months here, but now a new property management company, Avenue 5, has taken over. We've been waiting 2 months now on urgent maintenance requests and our current office team has repeatedly lied to us about when we can expect repairs. Initially, the first few times we called, we were informed a maintenance man would come the following day. Fast forward to 2 months later and still no repairs. They are now ignoring our emails and every time we do get a hold of them, they can only unprofessionally blame our previous management team for their own disorganization. We've had to detail the repairs we need done 3 times now to this new team (after we had been assured they had been put into the system) because they can't seem to keep track of what needs to be done. We didn't have any issues with our prior office staff since they promptly addressed work orders. Now we are spending extra money on heating due to cold air getting in through our broken balcony door. We no longer feel comfortable in our apartment. We are extremely disappointed that we've been mislead multiple times by this new staff and would not recommend Harbor Sky to anyone looking to lease. Not worth the money we're paying to have such incompetent management that claims to care but does  nothing except try to shift the blame over onto the people they took over for. They've had 2 months now to get their act together, but we haven't seen an improvement.

This is the most uncomfortable living situation that I've been and you can't make complaints about the amenities because it's about the dwelling and then. They'll find a loop in a loop but they basically just dismiss you. It's the most uncomfortable housing in portland

Do not move here. I was one of the first tenants to move in when this building first opened and it has been a complete nightmare. Amenities are never functional, packages go missing despite there being a parcel locker, hallways are kept too hot, and management is practically nonexistent. The secure garage is a joke. My bike was stolen from the bike room, cars are broken into, and I have had to chase out people casing cars more than once. I sent an email to the front office with some lease questions and it took 4 follow up emails over the course of a month and finally a visit to the front office before I got any answers. I don't know how they expect to open another "annex" building when they can't manage the one that is open now. I cannot wait to move out of this place.

We’ve lived here for almost two years and have absolutely LOVED it! You can’t beat the location. The staff is always very helpful, and the shared spaces are always clean. My only complaint is that they really need to have the exterior windows cleaned. 
Move in here, you won’t be disappointed.

My apartment is amazing. It's spacious with great amenities which includes an awesome walk in shower, closest space and a roof top unlike no other. This is by far the best place I've ever rented from and when it comes to Portland I can tell you this is the best neighborhood in town but here in this building It's starts with the staff. They are quick to respond to emails and there is a very friendly maintenance lead person who will introduce himself to you and is more than happy to answer any questions you may have. Not to say the least the great people who maintain the housekeeping in this building do a fantastic job. This place is always spotless thanks to them. The property is top of the line

I moved in last month and so far have had a great experience. The building is clean and secure, the coffee machine is always stocked and the complex has some great events and perks for its residents. The rooftop is well taken care of and unlike the old building I lived in every amenity in the building actually works and is available to use. The only reason I give it 4 stars has to do with the management company, not the building or staff itself. Never in my life have I had such a difficult time getting my cat approved to live somewhere with me. The pet deposit is excessive for a cat and you have to get certain shots for your cat that even my vet was confused about for an indoor cat (it felt harder to get him approved than me haha) but overall I am loving renting at Solace so far!

Quality of life is something that's very important to me – that said, it's something I didn't realize I'd have to give up when I signed a lease here.

If you're considering moving into either of the buildings in this complex, know this: trash and recycling pickups for Solace as well as the retail/commercial spaces around it happen before 6am every single weekday. I suspect that this was a known issue due to the dismissive response and lack of empathy from building management. They did offer the option to move to another unit and sign a lease extension. However, moving to another unit doesn't solve the problem for myself or others. It only means that I'd end up coming out of pocket for a rent increase and moving expenses while also having to uproot my living situation, all due to an issue that was not disclosed to me before moving in. 

I beg of you, please think twice before signing a lease here.

I was so excited to move into this building. The folks in the office were friendly and helpful. The neighborhood is wonderful.

Then, I actually moved in. Now, I am counting the days until my lease ends and I can leave. The Solace Apartments stand as a testament to truly horrendous urban planning and development.

About 30 feet from my bedroom window, there is a nerve-center of the waste management system for the entire block of businesses and apartments. 5 days a week, between about 3:30am and 7:00am (I wish this was an embellishment, I've actually written it down as it happens) there are multiple trash trucks from multiple companies spending between 10-20 minutes collecting large dumpsters, small bins and everything in between from the area.

It's a nightmare. Well, it would be if I could sleep in this apartment. I've tried ear plugs, white noise machines and nothing dampens the sound of glass and metal. Not to mention, this is all taking place sandwiched between the two Solace buildings along Shaver so there's almost a sound amplification to the echoes.

The attitude from management is literally, "Oh shucks it sure can be tough to adjust to city living!". I've lived in cities for 15 years. I've had early trash routes. I understand the necessity of this service, and how fortunate we are to have it done for us. This isn't city living. This is a failure in the fundamentals of urban planning and development.

What I cannot understand is how this wasn't disclosed to me when I was touring the apartment. Which brings me to why I'm writing this. If you're considering moving here, just please for the love of all that is right and holy in this world --- do not move into a unit with a bedroom window along Shaver.

There's a chance I'll accept the offer from management to sign a new lease and move to a different unit. Regardless, this review will live on as a warning to anyone about to make the same mistake I did. Then again, that would mean agreeing to give this company more money than I'm currently obligated to. It would also mean hiring movers and packing everything that was just unpacked. I'm exhausted just writing that. Or maybe I'm just still exhausted from not sleeping.

The leasing staff are amazing and the building is well-kept. The only issue is the outside area can be pretty loud at night but that is to be expected in a downtown area of a city. I've loved living here for the last two years.
The parking could be better but other than that everyone is friendly and we have really enjoyed living here for the past 2 years. We appreciate all the community events
Lovely. Just simply lovely. Cyan Pdx is an amazing place of residency, it’s very community based in addition to the very helpful staff you’re lucky to have.

Cyan has taken over a month to repair a broken refrigerator which is considered an essential appliance. It is STILL not fixed! This should have been replaced within a week! They do not care about tenants. I do not recommend Cyan, there are much better apartments that actually do required maintenance.
I have loved living at Cyan PDX, the staff are always friendly & helpful. They support and work with each resident while providing a welcoming environment.
The team really cares about the residents. When you talk to them they listen and do what they can to help. I also really like the floorplans.

Management changed this summer and the new team is excellent. Friendly, knowledgeable and will treat you right. 

Beautiful spacious apartments with nice views and all of the in-unit amenities you want. Stunning rooftop too!

Perfect downtown location. Close to lots of shops, restaurants and shows and also close to the highway for when you need to go a bit farther.

11 Marche is an amazing place to call home!
I've lived here since November of 2021. I'm in the real estate industry, so I tend to be very particular about where I live.
Our apartment here is gorgeous, and the price is fantastic. The location and walkability of the neighborhood is second to none.
