If you are fine not dealing with management at all except to pick up your packages (which is another hassle, as they claim to be open until 6, but frequently leave earlier than that), then by all means, this is a fine place to live.  However, if you want a place that will actually care about the residents and help them resolve issues that the building should take responsibility for, then I would avoid this place at all costs. The building gets a 2 star rating because without management, the building is alright, probably about 4 stars.  It is nicely located near Buckman Field, is spacious, and quiet.  Management knocks down that rating completely.

It's far and away the nicest apartment I've lived in over the last 30 years. Brand new, so that helps, but it feels solid and well-constructed. I love the high ceilings, huge windows and all the modern luxuries like the electronic door locks. I looked at a few other apartments in this price range, mostly in the downtown area, but none of them really stood out and none of them were brand new. Also none of them were right across the street from Gabriel Park and the community center there. I'm planning to swim at least a couple times a week.
…living at Bethany West! Great neighbors, office staff and offset location to go with a gorgeous apartment!
Bethany west has an amazing view. Very clean apartments. Pet friendly.
I have lived here for half a year and I love it! Office staff, maintenance is awesome!
If you’re looking for a new apartment Bethany West has so much to offer! Friendly staff, location, nature and modern apartments.

Ella apartments are exceptional in both atmosphere and staff professionalism.  I have lived here for quite some time (years) and have consistently been satisfied.  The Ella Team goes out of their way to care for tenants. Common areas (i.e. the lounge) are inviting.  Frequently, community events are facilitated and create a community culture.  Location is definitely a plus, close to so much. Neighborhood parks are beautiful and well-kept.  Plenty of adorable dogs (and cats!) exploring outside.  I would highly encourage anyone to check out the Ella flat! Whether your lifestyle is entrepreneurial, a family with kids, young professional, in your golden years--Ella is the place to be.
Lived here for three years, had an overall great experience. Kelsey and the rest of the office staff were kind and helpful!

Would not wish this place on my worst enemy. Lived here for a few excruciating years and since I left my joy has been limitless! The management is awful. Nonchalant. Very slow to respond. Quick to defer blame and do ABSOLUTELY nothing to improve your situation. Multiple issues that could have been prevented with even the minimum effort. But alas, I get the sense they know you likely are busy working hard to afford the insane rent and will not have the time or energy to do anything about their lackadaisical approach to everything. PLEASE IF YOU ONLY READ ONE SENTENCE: DO NOT LIVE IN ELLA THERE ARE SO MANY MORE BEAUTIFUL APARTMENTS ON SOUTH WATERFRONT THAT DO NOT SUCK ON EVERY LEVEL. I am imagining your life, one where you never have the misfortune to live at Ella. It is a most beautiful life. You're welcome.

Kelsey, Jane and Patrick always have time for a hello when they see me. They have been responsive to my questions. Kelsey went out of her way to make sure I had a parking spot in the garage that I felt comfortable with.  The few times I needed maintenance, Ric was prompt and courteous. All of the events sponsored by the Ella were fun and delicious - especially the recent waffles. All and all I am very pleased living at the Ella.

Dianne
I've been living at Ella for 5 months and I'm most impressed with the staff.  Office and maintenance.  Always helpful and the place is sooooo clean.

Ella had been my home for the past 4 years - since moving to Portland I have loved my time at Ella! The facilities feel very modern/up-to-date, clean, and offer excellent amenities (gym, common areas, rooftop). The rent is very reasonable for the area and certainly competitive for the waterfront given the quality of the apartment. The staff have been very professional, easy to communicate with, and welcoming. Would certainly recommend Ella for anyone interested/new to Portland!

Management is terrible, it takes weeks to get them to acknowledge requests. The only good thing about me living here was having a good relationship with the previous maintanence manager who I would go to directly with complaints. You can hear literally EVERYTHING from your neighbors. I got to listen to all my neighbor's conversations, rounds of morning sickness, fights, make ups, break ups, drunken parties, etc. There is absolutely no sound proofing at all. The lights outside constantly go off all night long so get ready to invest in a good pair of headphones and an eye mask or you'll never sleep. The windows are drafty as hell so you can feel a breeze from them all year long and there was nothing they could do to fix it. You also cannot turn off your bathroom ceiling fan and it is loud.

I really enjoyed the place, it was small and expensive, but typical for the area. They used to have community events which were really nice. Parking is rather difficult unless you want to pay for a spot in the garage. They have a pet wash area which is great, however I would often run into off leash dogs in the hallway.

I lived at The Sovereign from 2017 until this month (June 2020). This apartment (seventh floor studio) was the best I've had in Portland. Great value, amazing location and a coffee shop in the lobby, which kinda is the icing on the cake. Excellent service from staff, who were very supportive during the covid thing. 

Simple, well designed studio apartments that really do the trick, easy to clean, easy to stay. Floors super easy to maintain, and the tiled floor in the bathroom really nice. Daylight bathroom with high end fixtures and tub/shower, really nice. Kitchen design and fixtures modern, all high end and again, easy to keep clean and maintain. I've been here two years and would add another year but work has disappeared after the covid thing, and time to go find work elsewhere. I have thoroughly enjoyed it here. Quiet neighbors, respectful, too. No air conditioning, but with a north facing apartment, I don't recall any night where it was a real problem. 

Another huge convenience is the one bill approach. Rent includes all utilities and even basic cable and wifi. Not the fastest wifi in town, but not the worst by a long shot. All in one bill. Made life so easy for move in and out.

Laundry in basement is credit/debit card operated, which I found a lot easier to use than trying to remember to have enough quarters. Building maintained impeccably, always clean and secure and concierge, Paul, made this place outstanding. Always a welcome greeting and any packages delivered weekday were secured and safe, and I always got notifications. I'm going to miss this place. Highly recommend it.

Pros-- the staff is friendly and helpful but not overbearing. The welcome packet is actually welcoming and helpful. The location is great-- close to a grocery store, a block away from the streetcar, a super short walk to the train or a bus, close to the park blocks and the farmer's market. Security is about as good as it can get without a dedicated guard stationed in the lobby, which is nice. My apartment (1/1) is spacious, has ample closet space and kitchen storage. The nook for a desk area has been clutch in a work from home situation. Bathroom is fairly large and I love that it's just a shower, not a shower/tub set up. The apartment comes with a washer/dryer and also has air conditioning (although not central air) although I didn't use it much this summer (I moved in in July). As for heat, I still haven't turned it on, but the main living area and the bedroom have their own thermostats, and you can program the one in the living room. Neighbors are all nice so far and there are a lot of dogs in the building! There is a gym and also a courtyard with a grill and seating.  CONS-- the gym is minimalist. You can get in a workout but might have to be creative if you're really into lifting. Not the biggest fan of the treadmills and elliptical (they just seem kind of flimsy, but they function just fine-- there's also a bike that's great for a spin workout). The only other drawback as far as I've experienced is just that you can hear people walking around (I'm on the top floor) and bass really carries when people are listening to music, but overall everyone seems respectful of each other. If you own a car, there's no dedicated parking, so keep that in mind if you're moving in with a vehicle, but there's a bike share station right outside the doors and scooters are usually parked somewhere on the block.

Moved here about 12 days ago. 
Honestly thought it would be way worse. 
The parking isn’t terrible. (If you come home at 9pm you may have to park a street away) the inside is very clean and feels safe. Keys to get into the building and to work the elevator. 
The price is good. The kitchen and bathroom in these units is beautiful granite. Neighbors seem to be friendly and respectful. So far so good :)

First and foremost, the staff here at Tempo are absolutely amazing, and were very much vital in my wanting to move in here. The staff (at Tempo) are not only very friendly, they also played a major role in helping make sure my move went as smooth as possible, which as we all know, moving can become a chaotic headache-of-sorts, but thankfully that wasn’t the case, not in the slightest. The entirety of the building is state-of-the-art, top notch and provides for a legit Portland experience. I highly recommend.

I've lived here about half a year. The apartments and amenities are nice. 
Location is very urban. Mostly peaceful with some weekend noise. Nothing too bad. 

Inside is fantastic. I love my place, the views, the kitchen, everything. Maintenance has been great. 

Unfortunately a neighbor has taken it upon themselves to spoil the place for me so I'm desperately seeking a way out now. They smoke and burn incense every night. There's smoke billowing out of their door filling the entire hallway and everyone who lives near apartment. Its become an absolute nightmare for me as it triggers migraines. 

I'd say give the place a shot but run for the hills if they try to show the 6th floor.

I lived here for 2 years and loved it, but unfortunately things really have gone down hill since the management changed. I've had 3 packages stolen within 2 weeks. My friend's car tire got slashed in the parking garage and had to pay $400 out of pocket to replace them. Half of the door the garage door is stuck open. There were multiple car break-ins in the past a couple of months. The garbage disposal has been broken for weeks which makes the entire hallway smells terrible. The management seems indifferent to all these issues and how residents feel. I'm genuinely disappointed.

I love this buildings uniqueness and maintenance has always been on time. The location is prime allowing access to all areas of Portland easily. The amenities are always clean and it offers a nice size bath tub in one and two bedrooms!

The only bad thing about this apartment is the parking situation. Other than that everything is really good quality - they don't cut corners. The community is great and the management is really nice. The amenities are great too.
I recommend Tempo because its affordable, cute, modern, clean, and the appliances are very big and very nice!

I absolutely have loved living in this building!  Everything's always clean, including the gym, and the soundproofing seems good (never hear through the walls). Everyone from the leasing office to the maintenance staff are personable and friendly. It's very walkable, and Portland's best bar is right next door.
Iike my apartment and the courtyard but the staff and management are terrible and useless

It's a great place to live. The location is convenient, staff is friendly, and amenities are beautiful. They also host virtual paint nights and have food trucks come by on the weekends. Everyone is pretty friendly too. Neighborhood has lots of eateries, is close enough to walk to super markets, and has parks nearby. The office staff is super friendly too. I'd recommend it.
The apartments and building are beautiful with good quality fixtures.
A wonderful building with luxurious amenities, staff that care, well kept and clean! Ive loved living at the Broadstone and will find it hard to beat anywhere else.

Broadstone Tempo is a classy and wonderful apartment home living,  I personally feel that I own the apartment and that is how the staff make you feel.  There is a sense of family her, even though you dont see or know people here.  The people that I have run into are friendly and polite and respectful.  The staff are very professional, friendly, attentive, and accommodating.  The building is kept in like new condition and is very well maintained.  You can walk to everything you need and there is a dog park just across the way for those with dogs.  Its the perfect location.  I absolutely love it here!!!

We've had a really great experience living here at Broadstone. The staff is friendly and helpful. The apartment is super nice. Maintenance is quick to help with anything you need. They're extremely dog friendly! Most of the other residents are really nice too! They've done a good job of making this apartment into a real community.
Broadstone Tempo is by far my favorite apartment I have ever lived in. You pay the price, but definitely worth the experience for a couple of years!

I highly recommend this new apartment complex.  The apartments are oversized—even the studios!  The kitchens are the size you would find in a house—so much storage, counter space and large appliances. The bathrooms are huge, again with much counter space and storage.  There are family size washer and dryers.  Tons of closet space. The apartments are very quiet—you cannot hear your neighbors,  the common areas are beautiful, both the inside and outside areas. The heating and air conditioning systems are great. The staff is kind and helpful. Commuting time to work over the Burnside bridge takes me under 10 minutes! I am so happy I chose this building!!! I recommend you tour Broadstone!

Do not rent from here.  I have lived at Revere for 1 year and have had both my bike stolen from their "secure" bike storage and windows smashed and things stolen out of my car from the parking garage.  The apartment complex sent their apologies but no compensation for this with recommendations to go through our car and renters insurance which often has a high deductible and still is costly.  For the cost of rent and parking I would expect Revere to do better and have a higher quality security system

We have lived at the Revere for over one year now, at first it’s been fine but like most shared living where you can hear your neighbors.  When we first moved in we were told that you could not hear your neighbors but you definitely can.  Recently we have neighbors whom we share a balcony with and they let their dogs use our section as a bathroom.  We notified management early on about this and the waste was cleaned up but it continued.  We just stopped using the patio all together and once we went outside we found that it was covered with flies from pet waste.  We have a 1 year old child and there’s no way we can allow them to play on the patio.  Recently we had another discussion with management about the patio since the dogs are now much more aggressive with each other and one has shown aggression towards our toddler  in the hallway.   So now we have paid for 6 months of rent for a patio that we can not use since it’s turned into a bathroom for neighbors dogs and most certainly unsanitary for our child. 

Don’t bother reading any replies of anyone trying to resolve this problem, there has been zero effort in trying to reimburse us for the money which we pay for on the patio which we have paid for over the last 6 months.  We have been told that a barrier would be put in place but nothing happened and that was almost a week ago.  Today we got to watch as one of the dogs took a dump right in front of our balcony door.

There are amenities, however restricted to the hours of business.  I work 8-5 and have no opportunity to use the amenities that I pay for.  When I voiced my concern about the amenities, I was told there isn't anyone you can contact about that and the owners are set in their ways...I think the best thing you can do is to not rent here and find somewhere else, which is exactly what I'll be doing soon.  The apartment itself is ok with nothing setting itself apart from any other apartment, however you pay a premium for that, because I'm sure the owners think they can charge what they want.  My unit is also by the garbage area which 1/2 the building is.  2-3 times a week around 2am, 4am and 6am you'll hear the banging of 3 dumpers or clinking of glass...Advise looking else where.

Revere did not live up to our expectations at all. 
8 hour backyard fires starting at 6 and going until about 2 am 1-3 night per week. Poor sound insulation, many instances of broken appliances, poor responsiveness from staff who value sales and gaining new tenants over serving those that are already here.

Update added below on 4.8.20 - First Review on 2.8.20
Unfortunately, I have been communicating with Revere/ Fore Apartments since April 2019 and living here since June 4th. I have postponed this review in hope that Revere would make up for their service, attitude, and empty promises. I tried to give the benefit of the doubt that it was just a very very long transition of a brand new apartment. (Even though Fore is a multi-billion developer of apartment buildings..maybe next one) Since the beginning they made it sound like it was too good to be true. Offering options, amenities, and services that they didn't have or didn't have the power to offer; leading to them being revoked after singing the lease. They have continuously been more occupied with potential tenants then current tenants. Doing everything they can true or false to get someone to move in. As one of the first 5 tenants to move in the brand new building I had the luxury to get stuck in the elevator on move in day, my apartment was dirty, I had green water, the promised storage didn't arrive for 3 months and they made me fight for amenities that were promised and so on and so on. Neither Revere or Fore property management was or have been helpful to make this feel like home. They pass all of their responsibilities off to someone else until it never gets resolved or simply do not care enough to hear or help.
It is unfortunate because the view, location and appliances are very nice. Although the building looks well put together, it was constructed too quickly leading to paper thin plywood flooring, (live loud and true) constantly broken elevators, amenities and parking arms/garage doors(amenities that you have to pay extra for). You might have some luck on the fifth floor when no one is on the roof. We could go on, either way, it has been a very long 8 months and looking forward to moving out. Thank you Revere

Update -
Issues have not been resolved. 10 months in. Almost there.
*We understand that there were some initial challenges at the time of your move-in, and we appreciate your patience and feedback as we resolved these issues*- Revere  - NOT RESOLVED
The transfer option includes losing any concession and paying additional transfer fee's and rent.
Satisfaction is not important to them - because they will not help.
Revere continues to provide no action, responsibility, or accountability for anything they have said or attempt to do. This apartment is not worth your time or money

The main thing that makes Tanner Flats a great place to live is the responsiveness of the office personnel when you have a question, or need some assistance. They have gone above and beyond to make us feel welcome. The close proximity to public transportation is also a big plus. We love being able to get to places we frequent with such ease! The property is clean, aesthetically pleasing, and secure. We really like it here. A lot.

I love this community! It has been one of the best apartments I've lived in in many years. Managing staff is awesome. Always approachable and friendly. Whenever there's an issue, they are quick to resolve the problem. I've been here for nearly four years and I love my home.

I can’t recommend this place enough, it truly feels like home. Both management and maintenance staff are absolutely wonderful and kind. The neighbors are all great and friendly people, I feel safe and welcomed at the Tanner Flats. I hope to live at the Tanner Flats for a long time! It’s the best apartment building in Portland!

Tanner flats is a great place to live, I couldn’t think of any other place I could be. I’ve lived here a full year now and my son loves this neighborhood the school nearby is great, the max line, rooftop & community room & the gym wonderful. Let me also add the office employees are very friendly & accommodating.
This is the best community in Portland  to be a part of.Always growing and always changing.
Wonderful units, staff and amenities. Prime location too!
super thin wall, expensive common area charge!!!! horrible management

I visited this apartment complex and was beyond impressed with the overall look and vibe in the building! Everything is very modern and tastefully decorated. I have lived in the Pearl for several years and have been in most buildings in the area, this one does not disappoint! The manager, Simona, who showed me around was so welcoming and accommodating! She took her time to answer all of my questions and definitely made me feel like I want to live there!
Kado NW is the PERFECT place with the best amenities in the city!!! The location is a fabulous place to be! You’re in the center of coffee shops, bars & restaurants!

Difficult to give this complex a fair shake since we haven't been able to take advantage of any of the amenities (gym, workshop, any and all common spaces really) due to the shutdown. I doubt we'll be able to utilize these spaces anytime soon, so really think about whether the high prices are worth it for the time being.

I'll just comment on what I can... the folks at the leasing office are super friendly and the interiors are tastefully done. There have been some thoughtful gestures coming from management in the form of gifts/contests, so kudos to them for trying to create a community feel. Unfortunately so far, the cons have outweighed the pros. 

We're literally a couple blocks from multiple homeless encampments underneath the highway, which seem to have gotten and continue to get worse daily. There have already been some break-ins into the building (the front door doesn't even shut correctly half the time), and we've encountered some threatening people on nightly walks. Tbh, I have a high tolerance for this kind of activity, but I thought it'd be important to mention for others.

The soundproofing is abysmal. It's pretty absurd that a brand new building touting itself as "luxury" could be this poorly insulated- except for the windows, which actually do a decent job at insulating outside noise. You can hear every footstep, word, and toilet flush from the units around you (not hyperbole, I know it's human nature to use the restroom but that's something I'd rather not be aware of.) The dread of knowing that our neighbors can hear our every move... really sucks. If privacy matters to you in the least bit, stay away. And if you want to come home to peace and quiet, look elsewhere.

As a previous reviewer said, this place is a pain in the neck. The apartments themselves are pretty nice, BUT . . . there's a main thoroughfare right next to the property, but there's no access to it. We have to drive 4 miles through a neighborhood with 20/25 mph speed limits in order to get out of the neighborhood. The rent is so high that you need roommates to afford it, but parking on the property is restricted to one space per apartment. Somebody is going to have to park out in the neighborhood, and the residents there are pretty quick to report you to parking enforcement if you park in front of their driveways, mailboxes, or fire hydrants. I've seen a lot of tickets on cars. Renter beware!

This complex needs to open up to NE 148th Avenue to avoid detours through lengthy residential streets and much better access to Glendoveer walking and tennis/golf courses, places of worship and elementary schools. And easier access to Gilsan for quicker access to Portand downtown. Opening up NE 148th also quickens access to businesses on Sandy and Airport Way.

Will be a nightmare due to PBOTs unwillgnesz to open NE 148th to see and drive into the complex. You have to circle around, get lost and loose your cool to finally find entrance. Then get out your hiking boots since these babies are 3 stories tall with no real privacy.

Have mixed feelings about being a resident here after 9 months. The two of us live in a cute studio that is 482 sq feet and in great shape with nice appliances so that's great. However the secured shared bike room is a joke and repeatedly broken into. Despite needing an electronic apartment key to get into it the bikes keep getting stolen (we've had it happen twice despite using heavy duty Ulocks/padlock/chains in our 9 months). They even cut the spokes off my wheel in order to get the ULock off enough and unhinged the bike rack from the cement floor. Obviously they requires tools heavy duty enough to cut off stuff and get the bikes which means it's someone within the building that has access to either letting outsiders in to do it or they are involved themselves because it seems pretty unlikely that some random outside homeless person happens to have all the tools they need to do this and finds a way inside (this is what they claimed happened the first time). The management is super nice but they don't do anything to actually solve the situation at all like installing more/better cameras that operate 24x7 or changing the key to the room and requiring people to register their bikes. Or using the electronic key to record who's going in/out and with a timestamp! Doesn't seem like it would be that difficult to hinder this or stop it and catch whoever is involved. But they just apologize and throw their hands up and things remain the same. You can read reviews dating back a long time and see this is an ongoing problem that they have done nothing to fix which is completely unfair to residents since when you are choosing a place that is a small studio being able to store your bike securely is a factor! So now we will have to figure out how to store our things inside this tiny studio since the bike room is completely unusable unless you have a crappy bike. The garage has been broken into, cars parked where they shouldn't be and broken into as well. The security aspect is surprisingly bad for looking like a very nice building!

I moved here in the summer of 2021 and will be leaving in the fall of this year due to the rent raising. The previous management and the current management were both excellent! The current management is so nice and even offered a concession if I was to renew my lease! I’ve never felt so safe downtown too, there’s security that walks around the building at night, I never had my car broken into while I didn’t have garage parking or while paying for garage parking too. It’s almost impossible to get inside and upstairs or anywhere in this building without a key which I love. The gym is so nice, the parking garage is spacious and definitely worth the $. The place is always clean and they have an espresso machine downstairs! There’s also baked goods downstairs in the mornings too. The noise control is excellent and I never had any noise complaints even when I thought I would lol. Will be sad to move but loved living here!!

I’ve been at 4 different buildings in Portland and this is by far the worst in terms of management. We had multiple flooding incidents in our apartment and maintenance does not respond to what is obviously an emergency situation until the next business day. The staff including senior managers are extremely incompetent and never reply emails for weeks, and only after being prompted with follow up emails. Their replies are usually along the lines of “your concerns are still under review.” Our leasing concession was not even applied to our account. Do not be fooled by the beautiful amenities, it is absolutely not worth living in this building. I would never recommend this building or any other Greystar building to anyone.
Office hours are like closed hours. They don't answer calls.
I recently moved from Multnomah Village to Evanbrook. I Couldn't be happier with my decision. Great staff and maintenance department, Thanks for all you do.

I've lived in Evanbrook Apartments for 6 years now.  The grounds are always well groomed, the complex is quiet and people are respectful of others.  

I have had three management teams and each have been pleasant to deal with. The maintenance crew are quick to respond and fix any issues that may arise.

Great place to live.

I moved in here in June and moved out by November…. I ended up getting roaches living here and the manager was spraying “select units” and not the entire floor that I lived on which caused the roaches to move to the other side of the complex’s and to the other floors. After my unit was “sprayed” I was still seeing more come out from under the walls.

First off the manager once you sign your lease papers she's absolutely rude to you maintenance takes forever there's trash everywhere on the halls and outside and around the neighborhood. The elevator goes out every week at least so I've got to hike it up for flights upstairs to get to my apartment. You do not want to live here if you want to pool and a really nice neighborhood

I'm deeply disappointed with the management of this apartment complex. Multiple security incidents, including package theft, threats from another tenant, and car vandalism, have been inadequately addressed. The property management has consistently failed to follow up on these serious issues or provide necessary security measures. Security cameras were installed all over the property in 2022, but the staff is so negligent that they are unwilling to take the time to review captured video, rendering them useless.

I've attempted to resolve these matters directly, but have been ignored. I strongly advise potential residents to reconsider their choice.
The ease with which the move-in happened was a genuine gift in an otherwise stressful long-distance move.  Couldn't have been better.
This community feels like a well-maintained and peaceful pocket of SE.

Goat blocks apartments are beautiful, the location is perfect, but the staff are unhelpful and the security in the building is horrendous. There are constant break ins and thefts and nothing is done about it.

The Goat Blocks is a fantastic property, centrally located in Southeast Portland and within walking distance of many business, has a good community feel and vibe, and the property and surrounding area feels clean and safe. The units also have modern fixtures and appliances, the property has great amenities, and the price is very affordable!
Wonderful community with responsive management.  The building construction is a wonderful. Ive never even heard a neighbor.
I felt every safe and secure here. Nice neighbors and in a nice location

I highly recommend looking anywhere else in the area. The physical location is excellent; however, the property itself and on site/ corporate management is inconsistent, highly disorganized, deceptive of their charges before/during/and at move out, low quality craftsmanship within their units, faulty major appliances, poor communication, and uncompromising when they are at fault.

Great location, it is close to everything. The staff is wonderful, always approachable and friendly. Any issues are addressed quickly. The layout of the apartment works really well and the amenities are a big plus for relaxing living. Thumbs up for all that is provided at this location on Lost Springs Terrace.

I can't say that I'll be renewing my lease, but like most apartments, this place has its pros and cons. Maintenance, management, storage, and location are all a plus. Unfortunately, the building feels inexpensively built with cheap fixtures that are starting to chip and hollow floors that carry lots of booming sounds from neighbors. I wouldn’t mind if these savings were passed onto residents, but rent is overpriced with the owners making money hand over fist probably. On top of that, I’m responsible for paying water, sewage, and garbage use. You wouldn’t know this without digging through the 41 page lease which says the owner pays for these utilities, but there’s an attached addendum which says I pay. How convenient for them. Also, there’s commuter noise from Sunset Hwy day and night, which drives me kind of crazy. All in all, not worth it.

I have given this a lot of thought so please read on. Before my daughter and I moved in I was a little apprehensive to sign a lease due to some of the reviews. Since we were relocating from Colorado it made it difficult to see the apartment in advance. Dixie, the Property Manager made all of those fears go away. From the beginning right through till we moved, she has been there for us. Before we moved in she sent several pics of the apartment, the grounds, and made our relocating very smooth. She went out of her way for us. Now some of the reviews are not kind or accurate in regards to Dixie and she can seem a little tough but I think it's because she is a strong business woman that gets the job done. She takes pride in her position and does it well. She is the one you will want in your corner when you need someone. She took care of things for my daughter and I during our stay and I never had to worry about anything. In regards to maintenance. They are by far the best around. If you do have an issue with anything in the apartment, the get it on schedule right away and before you know it, it's fixed. They don't leave a mess and are very kind when they are there working. The staff is great as well. They are always very kind and if they can't answer any questions they will get back to me with an answer. 

Yes, these are a little on the pricy side, that's why we had to move. If the rent did not go up, we would have stayed longer. It's an upscale, clean apartment with a great location. 

Not sure why people have posted about dogs not being able to pee on the grass areas. They can and in fact, they have those doggie bag dispensers all over the property. There are also people that complain that they didn't get their deposit back due to move out costs. They did give us a cleaning list and we cleaned the apartment perfectly. We did get charged an $85.00 cleaning fee and I got the rest of my deposit back because I followed the list. If you don't follow the list then you will get charged. Simple. 
Thanks Cedar Falls, you made our first year in Portland home

I disagree with the below reviews. After living here for almost a year, I can say these apartments are the best I've lived in. New appliances, spacious floor plans, super timely maintenance (which I rarely have to call) and friendly staff. I couldn't believe someone lived in the apartment before me, it felt like brand new. The apartments are well insulated, the grounds kept up throughout the year and the location is great - across from a bus stop, close to the Max and a shopping center. Being next to a freeway is a little noisy, yes,  but that's city living. I live in a 2 bed 2 bath with a garage (not attached) and pay a very competitive price for the Portland area. Any minimal issues I've had, the leasing office has taken care of promptly and professionally. If my rent stays the same, I plan to live here for the next couple years.

I have lived in 3 separate units in this complex. This was my first apartment out of college living on my own, and after living somewhere else for a year after that I had to come back. Absolutely loved my experience and wouldn?t be moving if not for my career. Tani is the best and has set my expectation for all leasing offices going forward.
The condition of the apartments could be better. I moved into an apartment with carpet stains and water damage on the cabinets. The base boards out side my apartment are always very dirty
The maintenance team has always been one of the best features of this living community. They respond quickly, they are polite, and they are competent. Mitchell was great!
Service staff were very friendly and helpful. My request was addressed very quickly.
The apartments and the building is very nice, the only think that I feel that the parking spots are very expensive. Also some elevator smell very bad.
I would recommend living here. I would tell them it is pricey, but everything in the city is. I like the trash chutes on the floor, but parking is tight and expensive.
Wonderful community. Older property, but very well maintained/clean. Super dog friendly. Abbie is amazing!

I toured ~30 different apartment complexes before choosing Altamont. My decision was based on finding a place in the area that was clean, safe, good quality interiors, unique, nice facilities, and decent pricepoint. Altamont had all of the above. Outside of this, when I needed things fixed during my initial walkthrough, the staff were on it the next day. The staff that helped me with my lease were phenomenal - kind and caring, sweet, honest, and they helped me find the unit that fit me- I can't recommend them enough. Run down units, have lowered their standards for new renters coming onsite which is bringing in lower quality renters & crime, garbage, junk vehicles are all on the rise at Waverly gardens!

Beautiful grounds, refreshing pool for all to enjoy!  Management is very helpful and very  understanding when times are tough.  Thankful to have found this place to live.  Fresh start with my boys since their Dad decided to start a life with another Woman and her son and daughter.  Lovely start to 2015!  Divorce stinks but better off without him.  Will move on and work towards a better life for my Sweet Boys!

The location on 81 Fifty is great. Management is pretty responsive and seems to take care of the things that they can. The buildings themselves are old and sound travels easily. Footsteps, conversations, pets, water running, garbage disposals. Anything moving can be heard inside your apartment from neighbors especially if you have neighbors that live above/beside you. People smoke here and don't abide to the smoking rules. The patios are a great touch but a lot of the wood is rotting away and the paint is peeling and looks tacky. The common walk ways to apartments are very loud and covered in moss/dirt so can get slippery when walking on it. Not a lot of uncovered parking. I wish there were more positive things to say about living here but I would say it is rather average. It does have potential to be great but the community here isn't the best and the apartments themselves don't offer much.

You probably don't want this spread. When anyone asks me where I live, I do not recommend this place. I tell my experience with my vehicle vandalism and theft, how high the rent and that it will be going up, rude and inconsiderate office management.
Do not move here if you want a functioning fitness room or the ability to keep your curtains open after the sun goes down. Way overpriced, especially for a place without those non-negotiables!
Excellent community, location and amenities.  Love living here.
We are very appreciative to live here at 81 Fifty at West Hills.

The maintenance of this property is deplorable. Trash bins are constantly overflowing, dog poop everywhere, mold and moss everywhere and the staff doesn't respond to maintenance request. The grounds that they don't take you on the tour are in very poop shape. Stairs to building and handrails shaky and falling off. I have had an open ticket for a maintenance issue for 4 months. 

The staff is nice but the manager is awful. Rude, condescending, and obviously does not take responsibility for her property or her actions. They will lie to get you to sign a lease and then harass you for the issues that were addresses before signing the lease. I would encourage you to look elsewhere, as I am incredibly unhappy here and most of my neighbors are as well.

The building was beautifully renovated but seems some corners were cut in the process. The heating is radiant heat (which can work!) but they installed them ABOVE the windows and heat rises.  Meaning the heating does not work effectively. The walls are pretty thin, which allows noise between units and hallway etc.  If you have a complex issue in your individual unit – know that it will likely go unresolved. The staff seemed willing to help in the beginning – but once it was apparent it was a costly fix – they abandoned the project and made it seem like it was the tenant's issue. I will note that the maintenance staff are super helpful but seemed unsupported by the property management to truly address issues. For example, there were rat’s underneath some of the first floor units—and those units had to be vacated. And there was a ceiling leak in the common area that was reported and never fixed (over 10+ months).  
 
Summary: If issues don’t arise in your unit, and you don’t mind poor heat & thin walls. This place might be OK for you! But if issues arise – prepare to be treated poorly, and for the issue to go unresolved. I wanted to love the place, but decided to move during the pandemic to get out of the situation.

Pros: 
Recently remodeled, although 100 year old building. 
Beautiful old wood timber flooring.
No carpet.
Good storage 
Nice location/near Forest Park
Internet is easy to setup; fios.
Free wifi although they keep adding "firewalls."
Homeless in the area way better than the rest of Portland.

Cons:
Garbage disposals aren't allowed.
Parking is hell. Car was broken into multiple times. Tent was even stolen from roof and car exterior was thrashed.
Despite "triple sound insulation" you can hear your neighbors talking
Single pane windows that let heat out and sound in (since its a historic building).
Heaters are only on the ceiling right above the single pane windows. 
Lost time (plus a good 10 bux) from laundry machines not working randomly.
Leasing office almost always empty and staff changed multiple times.
If you care about electrosmog: Wifi is on full blast in each unit even if they're not paying for/using Internet. There was some crazy emf field through our apt, where the lights even computer monitors would flicker 
Mild draft from space between floor boards.
Nearby construction started a few months after moving in with no warning.

Personal issues:
Cost to renew lease was much more than what we were paying (despite many units being totally empty).
One of our heaters was screwed into sheetrock and fell.
Thermostats would turn on even when "off" wasting a ton of electricity. Had to take them apart and jam something into them so they wouldnt turn on. We had a number of problems with our heater and went weeks without heat on and off. Eventually learned to just use portable space heaters.
Charged us over $1100 for replacing all the blinds after we left. So, if you have pets, don't use the paper blinds. You might end up using blackout curtains anyway. Mgmt told me to schedule an inspection on leaving, however they never sent me the email to schedule the inspection and it could not be scheduled otherwise; they told me they would resend the email but I never got one, even though I was the only one in the apt that communicated with them through email. 

Just make sure you're ok with the above before signing here.

i've lived here for 10 years, I have looked and looked I can't find a better price for its location. The staff and management here have been very pleasant understanding and patient and made me feel very welcome here. I am always looking for cheaper rent though I'm always looking for something cheaper because times are getting hard

If you value your sanity and well being, I recommend going somewhere else. 

When I moved here back in 2019, it was amazing.  Once they switched management companies and fired all the old staff it progressively went down hill.  The people in charge don't know what they're doing.

I had my car towed because they never put it in their system and instead of putting a notice on my car or trying to find me, they towed it.

70% of my outlets are almost unusable.  They're all so old, you plug something in and it just falls out.  I have to tape it in place or lean something against it to keep it in.  I've put in reports more times than I can count and they still haven't fixed them.

I have to send two or three emails and call a dozen times to get someone to answer questions or concerns and when they do, they usually don't have any answers for what I'm asking.  

Every couple months they'll fire people in the office and get new people who claim they are working on making things better but it's the same.  They don't communicate with each other or the tenants.

The last straw was when water started leaking from my ceiling.  I told them about it immediately but it took them two weeks to even look at it.  In the meantime, my neighbors and I were told to just not use our kitchens.  We ended up dealing with things like mildew and mold in the air and the water sat in my light fixture for weeks.  I finally had enough and broke my contract to leave but even that was like pulling teeth.  I kept asking for things like an exact move out date and final paperwork but they wouldn't tell me anything and insisted there was none.  What kind of apartment complex doesn't have you sign paperwork when you leave?

They said they'd waive any fees I had but then they turned around and said I did have to pay and that it was late so I also had to pay the late fee.  When I fought them on it, they did admit they misinformed me but they still said I had to pay.

Cars are constantly in danger.  I've had my license plates stolen twice and cars are always getting windows smashed.  I've had rat problems several times.  There have been many occasions where police have been called in because of armed individuals in the complex.  Utilities are included but changes every month so your bill could be an extra hundred dollars warning.

I only stuck it out for as long as I did because I held out hope it'd get better but it's not worth it anymore.  Good luck to anyone choosing to be here.

It was my first time ever moving out and let me say. The apartment looks great! It was ALOT more spacious than I thought. Very roomie for 1 or 2 people. Maybe even 3 if its a baby. Throughout the move in process Kelly, Amy, and Frank were amazing. They assisted me very well since it was my first time. Very patient, understanding, and joyful members. Nick in repairs was very quick to my requests of whatever needed fixing in my apartment. I highly would recommend if you want something peaceful and away from the "city". Parking was not bad at all inside the complex. It got a little too expensive for me as single income which is why I am leaving.. I wish I could stay but I definitely do plan to return!

I’ve lived in this complex for 3 years now. They are raising my rent $100 and the new management keeps leaving passive aggressive notes on our door. They told us we couldn’t have a tote on our porch, because it was an eyesore. Never mind the plethora of abandoned vehicles, broken glass and endless care racing down the street. On top of all of that my apartment was shot and a bullet went into my bedroom.

I have seen rats running in the laundry room. They relentlessly tow people daily inside the complex. The staff is unbelievably rude and quite disrespectful. The will find any way possible to find you. They also don’t do anything about the homeless who look through cars and dig in our trash. The apartment overall is very cheap at best. The staff is the real issue. I would advise strongly against moving here.

If you do end up moving here, you will need to pay attention to the plumbing and the air ducts. Make sure all the plumbing stuff is sealed properly. The air ducts don't get cleaned annually, and it looks like there is a lot of build-up on the shared ducts.

Unfortunately, I have to disagree with the previous assessments of this apartment complex.  I have found it difficult to obtain repairs in a timely manner.  Some staff are professional while others are rude.  It depends on which days you go in to the office. Depending on which building you dwell, it is pretty loud between the train, airport, busy street and the recycle plant.  If you live further up on 125th, then it is not as bad. Many people do not pick up their dog waste. Or, perhaps it is one person doing it over and over again?

On the positive note, the apartments are large.  The neighbors are generally quiet and you are close to the 205.  I find it helpful to have packages delivered to the office.  The office used to be closed a lot so it was difficult to obtain a package, but that does not seem to be a problem any longer.

If you're looking for somewhere to live, Wimbledon is not even worth considering.

I chose Wimbledon because I THOUGHT it was my cheapest option. However when you factor in the property damage, theft, and wasted time, Wimbledon has cost me MUCH MORE than nearby options would have. Save yourself the money and the headache - choose somewhere else.

This doesn't even mention the black mold, rude and innatentive staff, filthy pools, trash and litter, constant water and internet outages, horrible appliances, and nonfunctional laundry facilities.

Don't take it from me, they have already been sued for twenty million dollars over negligance. Their track record is awful.

Still considering living here? Well here's a tip for you: if you ever need to get in contact with the leasing office for any reason, call repeatedly, over and over and over again, until somone finally answers. They will never respond to messages that you leave them or to emails, so don't even bother with that.
I have not had working electricity for 65 days and counting. Building management is well aware and still has not fixed the issue.

While all staff at the Miller has been attentive, I truly appreciate Daniella and Ruth for their hard work keeping our building looking amazing! As someone who regularly uses the many amenities here, their attention to detail does not go unnoticed.

The Miller is a beautiful apartment building close to everything you need. kylie did such a great job during the apartment tour and Shanel was so helpful during the application and moving process. The building is quite, clean, and everyone seems so friendly! The apartment is comfortable and has everything we need. My family and I are really happy and grateful to be here.

First impressions begin with the leasing office and both Shanel and Kylie went above and beyond. They made the whole process from viewing layouts to the application process and reserving the elevator for move-in day a breeze. 

With The Miller being the latest building on the developing waterfront, there were some little maintenance ah-ha's that I needed assistance after move-in and Nick was there same day to assist. 

The Miller wouldn't gleam as much if it weren't for the housekeeping staff working hard every day. Daniella and Ruth keep the facilities and common areas immaculate. 

The amenities room, spa, fitness center,  3rd floor courtyard with its sitting areas with gas fire features and the pool, hot tub, plunge pool, and outdoor shower... let's not forget the roof deck with grilling! It's the place to be and close to Vancouver's finest!

Living in the Miller's apartment feels like residing at a resort! It boasts a fantastic location overlooking the river, surrounded by numerous delightful restaurants and exciting activities. The modern design and exceptional cleanliness define my current home. The incredible atmosphere here consistently keeps me in high spirits, and should I ever feel otherwise, Miller ensures I have everything I need to uplift my mood! Whether it's indulging in the jacuzzi, alternating between a cold bath and a refreshing dip in the pool after a hot soak, these revitalizing routines make the world seem brighter. Pair this with a visit to the sauna and a cup of hot tea in this cozy environment, and paradise truly takes form! Moreover, the friendly and attentive staff, including Shanel -Property Manager, Kylie -Leasing Consultant, Nick-Maintenance Supervisor; Daniella, and Ruth - Cleaners, diligently maintain our home's cleanliness and comfort. Being a resident at Miller fills me with pride! Life is truly splendid here!

This space is phenomenal! We love living at the Miller. Who could go wrong with a spa right at your finger tips? The amount of communal spaces is what drew us to The Miller. Hot tub, pool, cold plunge, sauna, steam room, high end furnished meeting spaces, rooftop grilling area with a view of the river and Mt. Hood and The Forest (a space to enjoy conversation outside with friends at the fire pits). Our teenage boys love the gym.  Shanel is so helpful and Kylie is a friendly smile every time you see her. Nick is the best maintenance dude with quick responses at every corner. We may never leave! ?? Except to walk to the nearest restaurants or parks and enjoy what the Vancouver Waterfront has to offer. We are thrilled to call The Miller home.

-Kelly Z

I can't express enough how fortunate I am to call The Miller (Vancouver, WA) my home. From the moment I walked in, the experience has been nothing short of extraordinary, and here's why:

First and foremost, the staff is the heart and soul of this community. Nick, the unsung hero, works tirelessly to keep the complex in impeccable shape. His dedication is evident in every corner, and it truly makes a difference. Shanel and Kylie, the dynamic duo, made the move-in process seamless and have been incredible at addressing any concerns promptly. Their commitment to customer satisfaction is unmatched.

The Miller is not just an apartment complex; it's a sanctuary of luxury and tranquility. The design is wonderful - it's warm, focusing on tons of plants, and images of our beautiful PNW. The amenities are a testament to the commitment to providing an unparalleled living experience.

The day spa is a personal favorite - a haven of relaxation with a wet and sauna area that's like a mini retreat. The outdoor pool and hot tub are perfect for unwinding, and the rooftop forest is a charming escape into nature. The rooftop terrace with gas grills offers breathtaking mountain views, making it an ideal spot for culinary delights. The fitness center is fully equipped, and the co-working lounge provides a productive work environment.

The community spaces, like the lounge room with a kitchenette, foster a sense of belonging. And for those who are environmentally conscious, the dedicated bike room is a thoughtful touch.

I also can't forget to mention that The Miller is a pet-friendly haven. I love meeting all of the furry friends around the complex - the overall pet-friendly atmosphere adds an extra layer of warmth to the experience.

In summary, The Miller isn't just a place to live; it's a lifestyle. It's a harmonious blend of opulence, comfort, and convenience. Every detail has been meticulously crafted to provide residents with an exceptional living experience. I'm proud to be a part of The Miller community, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a true gem in the Pacific Northwest.

Here's to The Miller - where living goes beyond the ordinary and becomes an extraordinary experience.

Cheers,
Scott

Moving into The Miller was a breeze. The process was incredibly easy, thanks to their efficient and accommodating approach. The crew provided clear instructions and guidance, making the entire moving experience seamless. Their proactive assistance and attention to detail contributed significantly to a stress-free move, and I appreciate the excellent service they provided.

I have toured three apartments on the waterfront, and this one blew me away, Kylie was absolutely great in the tour very fast and efficient but also knowledgeable. Moved in 48 hours later. Great experience!

By far the best apartment complex I’ve lived in. 
The staff is helpful, incredibly kind, and make you feel right at home. Kylie and Shanel are always friendly and quick to answer questions. Nick is genuinely helpful with maintenance requests and goes above and beyond with making sure our unit’s perfect. 

The amenities make this place stand out from other apartments in the area. Sauna, hot tub, cold soak, steam room, etc…
I looked at all the surrounding waterfront apartment properties and in my opinion the Miller had the best amenities, layouts and overall vibe. The staff is super helpful and friendly.

I viewed and moved into my apartment on the same day. Application to move- in process was seamless. The Miller is a great place to live for its location, amenities and price point. Thanks to the flats team for making the Miller home!

The Miller is a beautiful space whether in your own apartment or the community spaces. Modern and spa like amenities make you feel like you’re on a permanent vacation! Thank you to The Miller team for coordinating an easy moving process with smiles and efficiency!

I toured almost every waterfront apartment while looking and only The Miller felt like home the second I walked in! Moving in was so easy – all the paperwork was done electronically ahead of time, which meant I only needed to pick up my keys and had a super seamless transition. I love that of the common areas (gym, lobby, hallways, etc) are always clean (Daniella and Ruth do an incredible job). In the office, Kylie and Shanel are so, so nice and accommodating, and always ready to help with any of my (many) requests. And when it comes to maintenance requests, Nick is literally the greatest, I’ve never had to wait more than a day for any small issues that have come up. My favorite part of the complex, by far, are the amenities! The gym is HUGE, the communal workspace has free coffee, and there’s a year-round cold plunge, hot tub and sauna. All of that combined with a super-convenient location that’s within walking distance to local restaurants, wineries and a view of the river makes this my favorite apartment I’ve ever lived in. If you're looking for a taste of city luxury within a cozier town setting — this is the place to be!

Great location and amenities for a reasonable rent price!  Shanel and Kylie made the move in experience seamless, and Nick helped to get the elevator reserved and my work order completed quickly!  I love calling this place home!

Kylie and Shanel made our move-in experience a breeze – their efficiency was impressive! And Nick, the maintenance supervisor, was always quick to lend a hand whenever we needed assistance in our new unit. Great team, and we feel well taken care of!

We moved in mid August 2023. It was a seamless experience thanks to Kylie! We love all the resort amenities and feel right at home. If there ever is any issues that require maintenance, Nick the maintenance supervisor responds extremely fast and is extremely kind. We love calling the miller our home!
These apartments look amazing. Really looking forward to my move here. Kylie and Shanel have been super helpful with answering all my questions. Highly recommend.

Premium rents but the amenities are sub-par. Rents keep going up each year for existing tenants but new tenants have been moving in to larger apartments at lower rents. Lots of amenities previously promised haven’t shown up yet.

I toured with Matthew who was extremely pleasant to work with! The time he took to make the experience exceptional is a huge reason as to why I ultimately ended up leasing there. He has been very helpful and friendly through the whole leasing process! I definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for their next home!

This apartment gives uh a huge opportunity to my family. Kids love the playground. It's clean a calm. We enjoyed this place alot. Manager Alice is the best apartment manager I have ever met. She is quick to respond to tenants needs and request.

By Muana Khuptong

This is a well managed and well taken care of property. The manager really cares about her tenants and is really good at her job. This is a nice place for a small family or the working professional or student. On the bus line and close to MAX so local shopping is nearby or a short trip to Portland for all that it has to offer. 
If you are looking for a place, I would recommend coming to see the property and see for yourself.

I have lived at Powell street station on 2 different occasions. Both times have been great! It's a smaller community, I enjoy that. Stevie is the office is really nice, polite and very helpful if I have an issue. Grounds are clean. The units are a good size and I like to open kitchen. Would definitely suggest to a friend!

I was a resident at this property for two years and experienced numerous issues with the property and property management team. The most shocking is that I moved out in November of 2022 and received my deposit check a few months later. The deposit check was returned due to insufficient funds. Almost six months later, I haven't received my deposit despite numerous email messages, phone calls, and in-person visits to the property.  

The other issues are more mundane; they failed to respond to any of my maintenance requests for the entirety of the time I was at the property. The management staff was terrible at proactively communicating during times of need. Example: we had a massive snowstorm that was causing the carports to collapse and damage vehicles. We had no warnings or notifications from the property management, so proactive residents went door to door to warn those using covered parking.  

We had issues with vehicle break-ins. Lots of them over three or four months until they started fixing outdoor lights and patrolling the parking lots at night—no word from the management team.  

Last but not least, the property has RATS. I'm assuming this was because of how the property managed the trash. They have one trash compactor, and it was either broken or overflowing.

Management nightmare. They switch management all the time. The request to fix appliances have been ignored and took months. Prices are changing and high. They painted the parking spots and They towed my car after blocking off our paid for parking spot and having no guest parking available. Prior to this painting of the parking spots no car has been towed for the whole year.
They just do as they please and are unhelpful to the tenets.
Not to mention all the old dirty and broken pieces of the house. A broken window took 8 months to fix. Improperly “fixing” a garbage disposal then taking months to come back.
I don’t recommend living here unless you just want to be frustrated and in debt
Excellent place to live, with a pleasant treatment by the managers and immediate attention to any problem, it is a quiet and pleasant place for our families ??

I’ve been here for about 5 months and Powell Valley farms is great! I love the area! My only frustration is the office hours, they usually aren’t there in the mornings even though the hours state 9am but honestly really nice staff. Very quiet on my side of the apartments. 

Angelica
We have live here for 3 years and it has been awesome. The staff is awesome and they always keep the property clean.

Don't expect them to honor their verbal commitments on rent rate. Do not expect to have maintenance show up and after several weeks, do not expect them to do their job. IF you work in Portland, good luck finding time to get to see them in the office due to their bad office hours. Do not expect to get a clean and ready apartment when you move in and many more!!!
YES
The apartment is nice for the amount of rent you pay. The management is nice and swift with problems that arise.

A big family owns the property and owes nothing so you can see how that plays out. 

Rats, mold, mildew, bugs, and NO urgency to do anything about it.

Heavy sheriff and swat activity.

No parking.

Dirty shared washer/dryers/storage rooms.

Inoperable smoke detectors, the most unprofessional staff ever in history, Heat doesn’t work in winter, no A/C, apartments are heat death traps, brown water in sinks and tubs, pool is NEVER open, no bedroom doors, broken glass, mold, front door kicked in and unfit, mosquitoes and flies everywhere, mailboxes unsecured, people can access all night inside the very dirty, always dirty laundry room. Decks are not safe to stand on outside. Rotten wood, mold growth, old wood, nails exposed, loose railings, and more....

Waking up with a positive attitude? Check. Getting ready for work? Check. Walking to your car and realizing it’s vanished into thin air? Double check! Yep, it got towed for the heinous crime of (gasp) backing into a parking spot. Clearly, I’m a hardened criminal in the eyes of parking lot management.

Why did I do it, you ask? Well, the night before, I parked the 'right' way, and some gas-thief decided my tank looked like a Chinese buffet and siphoned a half of tank of gas. So, naturally, I tried to outsmart them by parking in reverse. Little did I know, the real villain was the parking rule itself.

And don’t even get me started on my experience at Lumina—what a circus (Although that's an insult to a circus since their management actually cares)! The weight room’s a relic, the dog run is basically a mud pit, and garbage collection must be some kind of mythical event, because it rarely happens. But hey, at least the ants in my apartment are living their best life. One star for Lumina? Generous, if you ask me. I’m already packing my bags.

the water gets shut off monthly at this point due to bad pipes and repairs that need to be made. packages are consistently stolen off of doorsteps with zero help with security from the office. loud neighbors with domestic issues. bad place to live.

Save yourselves the headache. Poor management is present. They never resolve issues and pretend they do. They use terrible language and are rude to you. None of your issues will be resolved. I regret ever moving here! They claim to be luxurious apartments but the buildings are breaking down.

this place has gone from good to bad over the last 4 years living here. I have had my car broken into 3 times, my truck in the parking lot was hit and they drove off. People fighting in the parking lot and causing property damage, When you inform the office of these things they shrug it off and give you  fake sympathy. This place is terrible! the staff are terrible, the corporate team is out for them selves RUN FROM THIS PLACE!

Over the past year this location has gone through several management teams. This newest one is the worst team I've ever dealt with, not just here but anywhere. They're the worst.  They've come in and been incredibly strict but also unhelpful, things we've had up for over 18 months told we had days to take down or it would be taken down by force, no prior issues and no communication beforehand just the ultimatum. They're refused trash pickups, citing "leaking bags" but it's the items they provided our apartment when we moved in. Something literally out of our hands. Our toilet is broken, doesn't flush properly, the maintenance guy they sent tried to 'fix' the issue, by putting a squirt of soap in the back tank. Bottom line, the people who work here are bad at their jobs and have no problem hiding they dont care about the property or tenants at all. You'd be better off living, literally, anywhere else.

Management is a joke. First of all, we were give the wrong unit on move-in day and had to sit around with our loaded U-Haul and moving crew for almost two hours while they tried to get the correct unit ready for us. Not a great start and it didn’t get better. A few months ago, I called to put in a work order and waited at home all day for maintenance to show up only to find out that the work order was never submitted. I have had at least four visits from Lumina maintenance and outside contractors and the issue is still not resolved. I even had to miss work due to their unwillingness to work with my very flexible schedule. Lumina management has made it clear that they don’t actually care about the people living in their community.

My apartment is very small with no room for my kids to play and if they are out side they are not allowed to play ball, ride bikes, or even run out side my manager is not very nice. I pay 890 for a 700 sq place. It is really unfair how much my manager charges for this little tiny place.
We love living here. The property manager is great, always communicative and keeps the common areas very clean. I would definitely recommend living here.

The Homeroom is a wonderful place to live. The manager is readily available as needed, and takes excellent care of the communal spaces. The lobby, windows and elevator are always so clean - as a quasi germophobe I deeply appreciate it.  The place seems to sparkle and the pretty bouquets make me feel I'm home by just entering the lobby. Secure, covered parking and modern appliances which run QUIETLY don't hurt either.

Currently in search for a new apartment. The young man Nick who gave me my tour was extremely pleasant and professional. While trying to schedule a tour, Nick was quick to answer not only availability but questions I had before touring. When we finally figured out a time for the tour, it was quite fun. Compared to the last time I rented, this was much less of a migraine. I still haven't figured out where I'd like to go, but I felt the need to leave a reply because I myself work in a customer service role and was pleasantly surprised by his friendly demeanor!

I’ve lived in these apartments for the past year. I have been experiencing a horrible smell emanating from my bathrooms In my unit. I have contacted management on several occasions but the answer i get is “it’s probably the sewage line.” No other assistance has been given.

great location - bus stop (serviced by two lines) practically at your door step.  the building were built to be energy efficient (very low electricity bills), with the exception of the windows - they were not sealed properly so there may be a problem with condensation at times.  washer and dryer in each unit ... floor plans are okay..  for the most part I enjoy living here, it is quiet and clean - the main selling point to this complex is it's location ... bus lines; 3 major grocery stores within a few blocks etc.,  

what I don't like about living here is ... the current management company ... they don't care about the tenants and when you call with a question/concern or a problem you are made to feel like you are causing them a problem ... plus the management office is not open during the weekend ... parking has always been a problem, there are enough spaces, both covered; garage slots but I seem to  have a problem with others parking in my reserved space A LOT and because most people know that the tow away signs are an empty threat and that there is no one to call it continues to happen.  regarding the "utility" bill that is now attached to your rent/lease payment - there has to be a better way, my utility bill is more each month and I know that I am not wasting water and have one bag of garbage and maybe one bag of recycled material weekly ... so make sure you know that in the last year, my "utility" bill has doubled within the last year along with a rent/lease increase - frustrating because you have no way of know what your portion of the utility bill actually is ... the location is what keeps me here, plus I rent because I don't want to have to take care of a yard work; up keep etc., that comes along with owning a home
Paper-thin walls, inconsiderate neighbors, unresponsive management. If you value your sleep and your sanity, this is not the place for you.

This building has its original 1960's aluminum windows, which are drafty as hell. Power bills are $300+ in fall and winter. There is no air conditioning, and baseboard heating is very inefficient.  I just hate wasting heat and electricity when modern windows could really help. Aluminum windows are only supposed to last 30-40 years. These are 60 years old.

The old single-pane windows fail to dampen street noise, which is extremely LOUD. 20th Street is a major arterial for heavy construction equipment coming off of Highway 26 into the city mostly between 3 and 7 a.m. Dump trucks,  cranes, backhoes, and flat-bed trucks RUMBLE through the residential streets grinding the breaks, and belching diesel smoke from one Stop Sign to another. It was difficult to live here the full 12 months, mostly due to lack of sleep. We almost didn't make it. I see that several people left recently  before their leases are up.

The plumbing in the building has major, unfixable problems, due to calcification in the pipes. This creates very poor water flow and low pressure. Also, the small hot water heater does not fill the tub before running out of water.   

The staff is professional, courteous and responsive. The maintenance fellow was very nice and sympathetic, but really cannot fix the basic flaws of the building, which are large-scale and structural.

I love the neighborhood, but do NOT recommend living at the 2020 Building. I wish I know about the noise, the windows, no loading zone and water problems BEFORE I moved in.

Through the pandemic, The Arleta has changed property management 4 times. Has denied any type of communication whether through email or in person. They have yelled through the doors of the office doors that they won’t be helping people. Refused to accept partial payments. Denied any type of request to have issues fixed. Finally after fighting for months to get rental assistance and getting money paid back they hit me with a 10 eviction notice 3 days later. They don’t work for you even when you work for them. Don’t recommend 0/10

Infested with roaches, while the management is in denial. Worst neighborhood in Portland. I did not feel safe after dark. I saw neighbors' car windows smashed in frequently. Could not sleep well because of constant sirens blaring all night long.

I lived in a one-bedroom ground floor unit with a large dog for the last year and was very happy with my choice to live at the Arleta Apartments! The unit was updated and extremely clean. It was pretty spacious for a one-bedroom in Portland. I was able to fit my queen sized bed, dresser, vanity and small loveseat in my bedroom with a little extra space to spare. There was plenty of closet space and it was really nice to have a brand new washer/dryer in the unit. I had a corner unit so I had quite of bit of patio space that allowed me to fit a small table/chairs and an outdoor couch. 

The noise from your upstairs neighbors can be a little loud, and I was living there when they treated for roaches, but only saw one bug in my apartment the whole year (and I wasn't even sure what it was). So, I would say "infested" is a mischaracterization and likely the result of someone not keeping their unit clean. Also, none of my neighbors said they saw any bugs in their apartments either. The staff was very apologetic about the situation and said the treatment was just preventative in most of the units. 

The on site manager is always friendly, helpful and made sure that my maintenance requests were processed quickly. The maintenance staff were also very friendly and professional. Generally, I would say the majority of the tenants around me were also quiet and respectful neighbors. 

The best part about living here though was how dog-friendly it was! It was nice not to have to leash my dog up every time I took him out because they have an "under voice command" policy instead of a strict leash policy. Within a few months of living there, at least 3 of my neighbors offered to check on my dog during the day while I was at work or dog sit while I was gone. Mt. Scott Park is within walking distance with lots of space to play fetch and the complex has their own little fenced in "dog park" with complimentary waste bags. My dog was always excited to go to the courtyard to play with his friends :)
I was very excited when i got rent this place then realized it was infested with roaches (a lot of them all over).. you can hear the upstairs tenant walking, squeaky floors.
I will definitely recommend this apartment community.
YES
I love it here. It's easily the best place I've lived in Portland for endless reasons. I may never leave! (Just don't change the management)
I love the layout and design of these apartments. The windows are a huge huge plus.     Overall this building is beautiful and definitely somewhere I can consider myself being for years

Terrible management, will have no concern for you if you have any issues. Expect to be locked out of the complex or have a broken washer and not have any help. Upon move out expect to be treated poorly. Management is constantly absent and changing as well. No AC. Too expensive. Cheap appliances. Electric fans will not work properly. I have lived at multiple complexes in the area and this one was by far the worst experience, I couldn’t wait for my lease to be up.

The location and quality of the finishes were excellent. If the HVAC system of the building went offline, it made the humidity very bad which could've led to window damage. Wood windows in a wet climate such as Portland is a bad idea. We did not like the ventless washer and dryer as they were difficult to use and gave us wrinkly clothes back. They also made the space very hot when running the dryer.

This place is perfectly located. It's too bad they only have 82 units. My husband and I went there to inquire about an apartment and they are full. The manager on site,David, was so nice. He offered us a water while we sat in the office. Took us on a tour of the property. Just a real genuine down to earth guy. I can see why tenants do not move. Keep up the great work David. Quantum Residential you have an outstanding employee.

My experience while living at cornerstone was great. I loved living here for over 18+ months. Despite a small rent increase, I was very happy with the management and how they were responsive when needed. Overall, I do recommend living here; however, understand that the area can have a problem with homelessness on the streets surrounding the apt. If you can handle that, you will love living here. Location is great when it comes to the Moda Center/Convention Center/Food/etc.

My husband and I have lived here for over a year and love it. The apartment just has enough of what we need, a gym, an underground parking lot, garbage service, but most of all, it accommodates our furbaby!

It is centrally located in the Lloyd Center area so we are close to a number of restaurants and fast food chains for those lazy nights when we don't want to cook.
