It's a short walk to the grocery store, the mall, FedEx, Walgreens, the Apple Store, Radioshack, Starbucks, the Rail Track, as well as some nearby parks--so you are not that far from nature. We are also not too far from our respective workplaces, which is great. It is also noteworthy that in spite of all of these in the nearby surrounding area, we haven't really had much of a problem with noise. 

Lastly, I do want to share that the apartment is worth its value. Considering the costs in Portland, it is actually a really good value for the space you get as well as its proximity to a great number of places.
Great place near the river and on the less expensive side of it.  It's also near a lot of great eateries, a mall, and just about everything you need an want in a nice neighborhood.

Elm Row is a dangerous place for us to live. Last Friday, at 11:30 pm, three scruffy-looking men were doing drugs in the lobby of Elm Row when my wife came from work. 
It happens every day from the early morning until late at night. We feel threatened and unsafe. The lobby space often smelled of urine and other unpleasant odor.
The promise to install a lock on the entrance from outside has never materialized.

When the new owners took over, they cut a deal with the trash hauler (Republic) to pickup at 3:30AM every night. It sounds like a bomb going off and makes it miserable to sleep. We therefore chose not to renew our lease.
Friendly and knowledgeable agent, had all the answers to our questions. Property location. Nice pool and community area.

For the value of the amenities, location, and community--I would say this is one of the best apartments in Portland. I just wish that the Leasing Office facilitated more events for holydays/cultural celebrations to bring residents together (i.e monthly brunch, fourth of July BBQ, Oscars viewing party)

It was extremely nice. The structure of the building was great, noise from neighbors was extremely rare. Everything was amazing.   If I had to be BEYOND nit-picky, I would say that the lighting was a downside. But a very small and work-around-able problem.   Thanks for everything !
It?s quite and fancy. Near to PSU, downtown, safe way, the max and street car. Perfect location

Elevator has been out of order since January. It's June 10 now. There's no security whatsoever. Packages get stolen. Can't use the bike storage room (no cameras). They must want everyone to move out so they can repurpose the building for something else.

The overall building is great. All the units are bright and open. Also the cost is reasonable. It all ends there. 

Right after I moved in, the 2024 snow storm hit. As the snow melted, a frozen water pipe between the 5th and 6th floor burst resulting in water draining all the way down to the ground floor on the west side of the building. This resulted in people having to move out while they fixed the units.

Another problem caused by the burst pipe was the elevator breaking. As of this writing on 5/1/24, 4 and a half months after the problem started, the elevator has not been fixed. Also, the hallway carpet was wet from the burst pipe and was ripped up. As of 5/1/24, the carpet has not been replaced. 

Because of the broken elevator, the stairs have had to be used. The stairwell has gotten very dirty and have not been cleaned. On two occurrences, the lights went out in the stairwell making the stairs we have to use unsafe with the solution of one tiny battery powered light used on the second floor. 

In my unit, both windows will not open and close. I let them know about on the first day I moved in. Four and half months later, the windows still do not function. 

The latest problem is that the front door would not unlock to enter the building. When I called the emergency repair phone number, I was told to contact a locksmith as if it was my responsibility to fix a problem. 

I’m currently considering moving out early because of the continued problems with limited solutions. 

Don’t live here.

Overall I like this apartment. I think every apartment nowadays is overpriced, including this one but it's more reasonable than other places I've seen. The location is in a nice neighborhood, close to bus stops, a dispensary, some restaurants on Burnside. Also has a coffee shop in the lobby. Maintenance can be difficult to get ahold of but prompt and helpful once you get through to them. The units are modern and nice, can be a little drafty and bad with temperature control as they don't have A/C and the tiny wall heater in the hall has to run 24/7 during the winter. The appliances are nice and units are very sound proofed. I can only hear my upstairs neighbors walking around if they're wearing boots or running, otherwise I don't hear anything from any neighbors. People who live here seem to work from home and mind their business. The garage is protected and I've never had any issues with people parking in my spot and friends who have parked on the street never have any issue with people smashing windows. The street parking is limited but this is a largely residential area so you may have to park a block or so away, but it's still safe and quiet. There's not many amenities, no gym or pool, but the rooftop deck is pretty nice and has a good view of the city. I really like the big windows, vaulted ceilings and floorplans for the studio, which have two separate areas that can feel like a living and bedroom instead of one big room like most studios. 

Management is not on site. I've seen them in the office in person twice. To get in touch with anyone. I've had to call one of the other properties owned by the same management companies. The management people themselves have been helpful and nice. I had no trouble moving in. I applied and had secured a unit within the day and it was easy to add a parking spot to my lease via the website. The resident portal is pretty straightforward too, and management is prompt to reach out and understanding if there's any rent payment issues, instead of other properties where you could get an eviction notice for being short a penny lol.

Pipes burst during the last ice storm and it was because the sprinkler system wasn't properly prepared by management. Residents units were flooded and the elevator has been down for over a month. 
There's a general lack of care amongst residents and everyone except maintenance that doesn't bother me that much because I like to be left alone but it bothers me a bit still. The trash room is treate

I have been looking at different communities to gain information about all the new buildings in SE Portland.  When calling the leasing office I received a super kind greeting and the manager was absolutely perfect at providing me with information.  The location of this building is perfect and the finishes, appliances, and final touches really shine throughout each unit.  The owner really put in effort and great care when designing the floor plans and quality of features, top it off with amazing customer service and a cute building name and this building truly is 5 stars.

The day we moved in dirty water from an apartment above filled our balcony. When pictures were shared with management they said "let us know if it happens again." It has happened at least two times. I was told to clean it myself with paper towels (it is thick foul water and a possible health hazard). I am having to hire a cleaning company myself to come and clean the balcony.

Management doesn’t care. They also lie about security deposit policies at move-out. It was the first time I ever had to pull out a lease and read it back (via email) to the person who asked me to sign it. 
It’s a decent location in terms of what’s nearby, but pretty poor in terms of safety. Vagrants yell outside at night constantly, and walls are thin so you can hear your neighbors watching movies. 

Like I mentioned, the location is convenient if you work downtown or go to PSU. And the units are decently spacious for what’s available in the area. Those are the only reasons it gets 2 stars out of me. It’s not the WORST, but it definitely has its problems. If you choose to move in, beware, and be ready to drop a couple hundred over your security deposit (which they “lower” to get you to move in) at move out.

Their management suck. Since day one, they show you they don’t care about their tenants. They raised the rent at the end of the 10 months “special offer” 
When my rent auto-pay didn’t go through one time on the first of the month, I gave them a personal check for the rent the next day. They didn’t cash it until the 10th. 
Still they charged me 125 late rent fee , no body listens/hears/understands or care when you complain. No wonder people are moving out almost everyday 
Be aware of the illegal fees 
#the linc doesn’t give a sh*t

Where I reside is pretty much a convenience.  Where I'm close to so many things and traveling is slim to none.  I must say the rent cost needs to be evaluated differently.  For the majority of time spent living where I do, I was living paycheck to paycheck, money was tight!  Since the end of March (2015), I've had a Full time job and have been able to start saving.
A Review of my Studio apartment:
It has a full bathroom, a roomy walk-in closet, small kitchen with plenty of cupboards, dishwasher, stove, refrigerator and sizeable open room.  Perfect for one, who doesn't need alot of space.  I like it, because it's high enough up and quiet.  That is why I rate it a 3 Star home!
Don't believe the ad information, it is misleading or down-right false.

We have lived in the Hawthorne Apartments for about 6 months and we initially liked the space and location. However, we have had several burglaries and vandalism events since being here and management has been unhelpful at best. After weeks of spotty contact their final solution for me was to offer to take away my parking so I could afford to replace my stolen items. Cameras in building do not capture incidents and the on-site Security phone number does not work.

I'm a native Portlander and I needed a place to live in between buying and selling a house. I also wanted to be close to a lot of bars and shops. This place was right on the money.

I was surprised at how quiet it was there, even though I had an apt that faced Hawthorne. Only noises I could hear was the occasional garbage truck in the morning and didn't hear other street noise unless I opened my window.

I also lived there with an 80 lb dog and a small cat. It is a very dog friendly place and many residence had dogs.

I had 2 or 3 maintenance requests when I was there and they were taken care of rather quickly.

I'd recommend this place to anyone that wants a nice, new quiet apt close to the best neighborhood in Portland!

I have lived here for more 4 years, it has steadily gone downhill, complete lack of management, poorly kept grounds, lots of drug activity, gross pool that’s never open. 3 cars have been stolen in the last 2 months from a “secure lot” but conveniently the management is unable to pull up the security footage. Don’t bother even applying here it’s not worth it.

While this complex offers a manageable rent with a still-in-Portland address, it's located on an unattractive strip of Division St. the main purpose of which is fast traffic to Gresham. Above 82nd Ave., Division St. is not an inspiring landscape to pass through, but there is a lot of surrounding greenery, a Buddhist temple around the corner, and convenient shopping at Division St. Center. The complex itself is very well landscaped and maintained, with friendly management, and has a recently renovated pool! The apartment is "servicable," pretty basic but with lots of closet and shelf storage. My least favorite feature is that the kitchen is right off the living room. A decent value for today's rental market but not a "real" neighborhood. Right on the #4 bus line.

The location and building is great. However, the management has been regularly absent and incompetent. If you're considering living in the building, do your research by stopping a resident to ask them about their experience living in the building and their opinion of management.

Nona in the leasing office was second to none.  She took care of me *and* she took care of existing tenants...while making each of us feel like we were the only people in the office.

There are a LOT of new apartments in Portland.  Few of them, though, have such a strong combination of location, amenities, and customer service. - Overlook Park is definitely worth a look.
Garbage staff and building. Everything is always broken, area is dangerous and read the fine print because you will be hit with prohibitively high move out fees

I want to make sure to leave this review for anyone researching this apartment that might have mobility issues. We have been here under a year and the elevator has been out of order several times, each time lasting several days. The frequency and length of these issues could be a serious impact if you are unable to use stairs.

In a community that does see a large number of issues, my biggest concern is the lack of communication. There was an issue a few months back where several storage units were broken into and there was never anything sent out to inform tenants (the office had brought in painters for the hallways/doors and painters left storage unit doors open to dry for several hours. Not the brightest move in this area). I was told by management that it would be a liability issue for them to have sent communication out about it. More recently there was an incident just a couple months ago where someone had their car stolen at knife point (in the “secure” lot) and once again, nothing sent out to inform tenants which feels like a serious safety issue to me. Not receiving updates around incidents like this does make it feel like management cares more about mitigating feedback from frustrated tenants than the actual safety of human beings.

I have seen some improvement in communication in the last couple months, but I still get my most timely/pertinent updates from other tenants. 

My interactions with staff have been good and I trust office staff does their best considering the limitations of their leadership/Avenue5. 

The actual apartments are great. We’re in a 2 bedroom and have lots of counter space in the kitchen and the appliances all work well. The main areas in the bedrooms as well as above the living room did not come with light fixtures which was interesting to see in a new construction building. But we installed lights with fans that help do a good job with air circulation in the summer. The Bluetooth stuff (like being able to control your lights/outlets through your phone) that was promoted on website and during tours does not work and is never going to so be weary of that. Community facilities are nice and mostly well kept.

Overall, it’s what you would expect for a new construction apartment in Portland located off a freeway that’s managed by a big company that lacks personal touch. Adjust your expectations based on that criteria and you’ll do just fine here.

I've lived here for over 4 years because it was across the street from my work and I just recently moved out.

New management is terrible, especially compared to the previous property manager who was incredibly accommodating, far less condescending and didn't hit you with tons of random move out charges.

Safety safety safety! There is none! Check their Facebook page/Community forums on their own site and you will see that there a ton of break-ins in the paid parking spots, houseless people using in the building/at entrances and wandering the hallways at times and tons of bikes stolen off property.

That being said, the office assistants, maintenance and security guards are all kind and helpful, but it certainly doesn't make it worth all of the other problems in and around the apartment complex.

Please know that the area is not safe.  I have had my car stolen and on another occasion broken into in the gated/secure parking lot (paying $150 a month to park).  In addition, there is only one working camera in this secure parking area. Management is difficult in every way possible. Location is the only plus.
Grant Park's location is great! You're within walking distance of multiple stores. The only thing that could use some improvements is street parking.

Everything is excellent here at Grant Park Village.  The staff, the maintenance, the overall sanity of the place.  Need to work up a better solution to package delivery.  I don't know what I'm going to do if I need to order something.  The only item I ordered to be delivered here was returned because the delivery person couldn't access the package room.  Upon re-ordering, the item was delivered but thrown into a pile of packages on the floor.  It was only a small item so the manager and I had to search through the pile for this one small item.  Terrible!  Needs a fix!
No response. Voicemail has been full for the past month
Wouldn't work with me on rent. I'm currently a full time student

they have pests here, the property is dirty. the apartments are small and halls reek of cigarette smoke. they won't be held accountable for their faults and only care about money. corporate sucks and is dismissive. the walls are super thin, maintenance requests get completed but look like they were done by a child. I lived here for 4 months and had to beg to get out of my lease after they failed to get rid of a roach problem. absolutely horrible.
It is difficult to find a place to live in Portland and it is sad that this serves as an opportunity for landlords to only care about getting your money without providing a decent place to live in.

I lived here for 6 months, absolutely terrible.

Expensive rent for the size, expensive utilities ($100 a month for water and electricity?). Shower took 30 minutes to warm up in the morning. Using a microwave blows out the circuits. Air/heat were awful, too hot in summer, freezing in winter.

I've spent a summer camping in a tent, and even that was better than staying at the Regency.

It felt like living in an insane asylum, just drives you crazy.

Adequate. I will try to be as honest and as objective as I can abd hopefully this comment will not disappear like so many recent previous comments.

It is a place to live that provides shelter, warmth, and the location is very nice.

PROS: Quite possibly the best thing about the building is the location. No need for a car with the close proximity to grocery stores, parks, gyms, restaurants, and public transit.

Very dog, friendly building/ community.

Diverse community of residents.

Large community room.

CONS:  Very austere, cold building, feels more like a facility rather than a home.

A "smart building" that allows you to enter and exit with the use of a key fob or app. If you leave your room without either, you're screwed and have to call a locksmith and pay for it yourself.

Crime: Even with the secured building access, careless people let strangers piggyback into the building. Packages have been stolen, people have snuck in and sleep in the building, and some residents' "friends" have even stolen furniture from the community room. I have encountered police in the lobby 3 times now and have recently called them because a stranger was loitering in the lobby.

Big Brother: I am uncertain if there has been a management change with regards to the cameras that used to be everywhere, but several "security" cameras were removed that used to monitor that trash room, the trash chute rooms, the elevator, community room, and hallways. This gave a very surveillance state vibe which really put me off and I am glad that the majority of them have been removed.

High Turnover: Since I have lived here for the last year and a half there have been 5 community managers. We lost the best and possibly the most capable community manager that has ever been here and now have a new one. Again, raises so many questions about the company itself and its values.

Size: As many have mentioned, the size of the spaces are very expensive for the square footage. In all this feel like living in a college dorm.

Moved in here early Feb 2021 and have had a great experience! The management is always changing, but I’ve never had any big problems with them. One of the most recent managers is a little difficult to communicate with. I decided to move here because I wanted a small space for myself, that was close to my school, and that’s exactly what I got. Good area for walking, and using public transportation. Friendly neighbors. I’ve met lots of great people here and when I needed help with my cat, I had sooo many offers to help out. I only took off one star because parking is a little sparse—but I didn’t expect any better, there was a weird week or so where the key system wasn’t working, and I was locked out of my apartment, which required me calling a locksmith over the weekend since the apartment staff wasn’t available. They did reimburse me though. There’s also been some spotty hot water issues, but nothing bad. I wish I could stay here but I’m done with school now and it’s really expensive to stay.

The regional manager and staff are terrible. Instead of giving the problem, they ask you to move out. Do not move here! This place used to be amazing, but the past two landlords quit because they were provided with little to no help. If you want a safe community, look elsewhere. The tv was recently stolen and homeless people continually get into the building because of carelessness. The tenants are not vetted so if you think you will live with a group responsible human beings, think again.

Jessica, the community manager, is supremely set on helping out and providing exceptional customer/tenant service. The Derby Slabtown's staff is responsive, unassuming, and kind to say the least. Of all the property's I have looked at, this one has the most helpful staff and makes me want to be part of the community.
The management staff is amazing! Super welcoming, respectful and considerate! The building is super well kept and just an amazing place to live!

Jessica truly goes out of her way to make sure residents are comfortable. The premises themselves are also very clean and well kept. I loved the community room with the coffee machine. Highly recommend!

This is the place to live happily. The apartment has an entry hall, coat closet, linen closet, large bedroom closets and full bath with bathtub shower. It has laminate wood floors in living room and bedrooms. There is a full kitchen with plenty of cupboard space. A sliding glass door opens to patio on the ground floor, outside amenities include swimming pool, laundry room, offsteet parking, and on-site manager. Outdoor spaces are well-maintained. I could not ask for anything better once I found this apartment.

I lived here for about 3 years. Mangement changes hands, what seems like, about 2 times a year. If you try to talk to someone in the Offices, you may as well just write a letter to yourself and burn it, because you won't get a callback. If you park off-street, don't leave anything in your car, because this area is a hot spot for car theft. We recently have been trying to get an itemized list of why they took half of our deposit and then tried to bill us for utilities that we didn't use. The best you get is a call from their "Property Managers" over at Avenue 5. Apparently, they don't believe in using email and like to blame the USPS for "Not delivering" mail that they claim "Was sent". If you can't send it as a PDF, maybe you shouldn't manage places where people live. If you do get a reply from management about your review, they say to contact them. This is great for them as they don't ever answer the phone and just wind up sending you to collections and ruining your credit. Once we got the City of Gresham involved, nothing changed. They simply wouldn't answer the phones or return phone calls to the city official.

This is a terrible place to live. The apartment interiors are old and run-down, with fixtures that constantly break. It’s located in a bad neighborhood - SW 11th is notoriously crime-ridden (ask any Gresham resident), with many cars broken into and lots of shifty people wandering around. The trash areas are frequently filled to overflowing thanks to constant illegal dumping (video surveillance doesn’t seem to help, unfortunately).
 
The management has changed several times in the past two years - a new (exterior-only) paint job and a sad attempt at “re-branding” isn’t fooling anyone. Their latest “improvements” include:

•	They have removed assigned parking spaces, allowing anyone & their visitors to park anywhere, ensuring that you will NEVER find a spot near your apt (the permit parking system is not enforced by towing, just empty threats). 
•	You are required to expose your bank account to a sketchy third-party website in order to pay your rent (they no longer accept checks or money orders). 
•	A new “energy-saving” device installed on all water heaters GUARANTEES that you will not have enough hot water for a shower…there’s barely enough to fill the kitchen sink! 
 
The management does not respond to issues or inquiries (except for snarky, condescending responses to bad reviews online), despite claiming otherwise. They are rarely in the office (their “hours” are a joke) nor do they answer the phone. They insist that all inquiries & maintenance requests be done online, where they can be more easily ignored. The only time you will hear from them is when they leave a note on your door telling you to remove items from your deck/patio every three months.

They never answer their phones unless it's a temp worker they change lease at will no pool for over 2 years no assigned spaces maintenance show up not going to happen unless you threaten to withhold rent and then they are going to do bare minimum not worth the price

Been here for almost five years and it has just gotten worse and worse. Parking is a joke, management constantly being replaced, to many kids that parents don't watch, paper thin ant infested walls, you can hear kids screaming clear as day like they are in the unit with you. Wanna go to the pool? Welp they only have it across the street and all the way at the back of the complex. Neighbor had two cars stolen right out of the parking lot. Residents park their second vehicles in visiter parking and play the car switching game. The demo unit they show you is not what you get in the real units. Their so called professionals they hire to do work the they can't are a joke and will slap duct tape on problems and call it fixed. Random inspection multiple times a year for no reason. Can't seem to keep hold of records of who lives where, everytime management changes they post papers at your door wanting you to tell them all the stuff that should already be on file. Wanna pay rent with a check or money order? To bad they no longer accept those forms of payment and they only accept online payments. They have blocked off the office drop box so you cant leave anything after hours and have to be there during office hours to turn anything in. All and all you are better off living somewhere else.
Maintance is terrible, parking is terrible, to many kids, that parents don't watch.

The living room is very large and the layout is very good. The master bedroom is very large also with its own bathroom. 
There is only 1 parking spot per apartment. That is why I only rated it only as good. 
Also the apartments need updating.

900 for rent, 50 water,sewer & garbage.  2 bedroom and 1 1/2 bath.  No washer and dryer hookup, no dishwasher, no outside hose access & no garbage disposal. No amenities at all all other then a tiny dirty pool and a onsire laundry room. Very high management turn over and they are extremely strict yet rarely ever open. ABSOLUTELY NO UPDATES AND MOLD EVERYWHERE. I DO NOT RECOMMENDED LIVING HERE.

I live in a 1 bd, 1 bth apartment.
Very large living room and dinning room.
It is very quiet and peacefull living here.
Storm windows and new carpet, and paint.
A play ground for the little ones,
It has been a delight living here at Country Square, lots of parking!
Great spot to live! Very easy to contact management and a very comfortable location.

I am absolutely thrilled with my experience at Northridge, and a big part of that is thanks to the amazing property manager, Terry. Terry is truly exceptional, and her level of dedication and helpfulness is rare to come by. I appreciate how she manages and helps me out so often, and the maintenance team is always quick to respond and fix any issues that arise.

Overall, I highly recommend this place. Terry's hard work and wonderful hospitality is what makes here such a special place to live.

I recently moved in to Northridge and the staff was so helpful! I moved here from out of state and they made the process so easy. When I arrived they showed me the apartment for the 1st time and it was just as advertised. The apartments are nice, spacious with a decent amount of storage, close to my work and shopping. I’m happy with my choice.

I signed a two year agreement, and when I was signing, they added an addendum for more money, so I was cornered into paying utilities. The broke their 2 year contract with me when I only have 9 months left here to do, and was forced to sign up for new terms under threats of lawsuit for non-complicance.  I didn't have the money to take them to court, so now I have NEW TERMS, which is unlawful.  Unbelievable how crooked they are.  Managers don't last more than a year, and our new one is a little 'nuts'.  Residents pay the owner's utility bill for the complex, and split it up by a 'formula'. It is about $100 more a month, but when you sign the surprise addendum, they will say it's $35-ish to get you to sign, and be super nice to you when you move in. This extra bill is variable, and whatever they say it is...and it's high. If you leave for more than 7 days, you have to report to the Manager, which is rude to require.  You must report all friends with pets, and if they visit you, must stop by the office to inform the office that your friend is over. It is loud; a major highway out front that is jammed daily, machinery at midnight, scavenger trucks troll the trashcans at night, night going over the speed bumps with a 'crash'.  This has been the worst place I have ever lived, and I have never met an honestly happy neighbor. No one in my building has stayed more than a year, and rent increases are a problem.  They don't tell the truth, treat you well until you are locked in, and illegal evictions are common.  I created this account just to warn families and young people, as well as people in transition (like me) who are waiting to buy a home and need a place to get grounded.  It's a problem here.

I've lived in a 2 bedroom / 2 bath apartment here for nearly 4 years. With nearly 1000 sq. ft. and lots of windows and light (including a window in the kitchen!), I'm happy with what I get for what I pay, especially compared to other nearby apartments in Bethany Village. There are no onsite amenities but that's okay for me because I'd rather pay less rent than pay more for amenities I probably won't use. Pros - the office staff, especially the leasing manager is courteous and professional. I always appreciate the extra care he gives the residents. The maintenance staff are very competent and friendly! The complex is generally quiet and the grounds are kept up. The floor plans are spacious and while I don't live in one, most of the apartments that are being vacated are being upgraded with stainless steel appliances and distressed vinyl flooring. Also, this complex is very pet-friendly and since I have two cats, I am very happy that pets are appreciated. Cons - the owner has become increasingly strict about things that end up making the complex look sterile and plain. Residents can't even have hanging plants on balconies or patio lights or shades during the summer. I really don't like that part of living here and it will probably be a deal breaker if I find something else I like that is affordable. I also don't like paying an extra $20 for a covered parking space which is mandatory unless you don't own a car.

I would like to point out that Tim is awesome. He understands and makes it so great. Christina is an awesome second in command. In other words management is on point. They fill work orders in a timely manner.Who more could ask for more?? We love it here!!!

My apartment complex is pretty nice but I would not by any means call it a luxury apartment. Cheapest of cheap appliances and linoleum floors do not constitute the luxurious title of Luxury Apartments. That being said, the nice thing about my apartments is the staff. The office is open 7 days a week save for holidays which is understandable. It is also open until 6:00 PM which doesn't matter much for me since I work until 6 but it is nice I'm sure for most that get off at 5:00 and can still make it to the office for their needs. 
Maintenance is on the grounds everyday and problems get taken care of quickly for the most part. The maintenance crew also keeps the complex clean. I have even seen one guy on his hands and knees scrubbing the hallway floor! I guess the price is alright considering I have looked all around my area and have found that there is no where close that is any cheaper. The walls are not thin either which is nice for apartment living. You wouldn't believe some of the things I have heard in the past living in other apartments. Or maybe you would believe... All in all, this apartment complex is a great place to live.

So, for context, I have lived at Heirloom for about 32 months now, since the very first month the place opened. 

The apartment units themselves are nice, as you can see from the pictures or a tour. However, just about everything else about living here pretty much sucks.

There are no breed restrictions! Awesome! There are also a bunch of big aggressive breed dogs running around acting like jerks without their owners correcting them.

There is a beautiful swimming pool! ... And the residents totally ignore all the rules, and do not care one bit about the quality of life of all the folks in their apartment just 20 feet away. Between the super loud bluetooth speakers, play beer pong in the pool while kids are swimming next to them, and have late-night hot-tub parties despite the fact that all amenities areas close at 10pm.

The maintenance staff leave the dog waste bins overflowing for a week or more at a time. The stairs up to my apartment literally had never been swept in the 3 years I had been here. Even after asking for them to be cleaned, they ignored it.

Lease at your own risk. This place is not at all what it seems.

Living here for three years has been marked by unsettling incidents and a concerning lack of accountability from management. A homeless woman broke into the unit below mine, triggering a pepper spray bomb, forcing us to seek alternative accommodations. Shockingly, management failed to communicate the situation to other residents or reimburse us. This lack of transparency and disregard for our safety is alarming. Promised security measures, like surveillance cameras and a security team, have never materialized; I've never seen the security team. A recent verbal assault I experienced underscores the persistent security risks. Neglect is evident in the graffiti-laden common areas. The mental toll of fearing break-ins into my own apartment after such events is significant. Overall, the complex's security lapses, management's dismissive response, and the absence of support make it an untenable living situation. Prospective tenants should be cautious before choosing to reside here.
The floors are thin and my neighbors are very active at night. This makes it impossible to sleep. If you get unlucky and have neighbors like mine you won't like living here.

The amount of theft in this complex is astonishing, and the management does nothing to combat it or mitigate it. It's like every other day, a car gets broken into. I have spoken to a couple of neighbors and they have all complained.

And the management does literally nothing about it, but send a clause in the lease that indemnifies them from helping. They might as well be helping the thieves. 

The parking spots still aren't assigned, and it's literally first come first serve. I'm just saying for this amount of rent, it would cost nothing to get a security guard to patrol the community to stop theft, but nothing has and is being done by the management.

I don’t appreciate that heirloom advertised 2 parking spaces per 2 bedroom units, and not 3 months after signing our lease we are only being offered 1. This is false advertising and slimy. I don’t like that the parking spaces have not been numbered so there is often no parking in front of my building due to residents having multiple guests. This is a result of poor management control. I don’t like that I was told of a community garden being created but now there are no future plans to create the garden. It is inappropriate to have maintenance staff living in the buildings. The maintenance person in building 1 regularly smokes on their balcony causing smoke to travel through the building. This is supposedly against heirlooms policies but no effort has been made to correct the situation. The “secure” gates are ineffective due to broken locks. Anyone can walk into the property without a key or fob. Finally, there have been more that 5 vandalism incidents on the property since December and the management team has made no effort to increase security during the day, add security cameras on more than just the club house. I myself had someone smash my window in on the property within range on the only security camera on the property that the staff refused to release the footage of.

Heirloom is a new community still growing as we speak. At this early stage, you can see that there are efforts to keep things very modern and fresh. We have only been here a few weeks but so far we are very happy with the apartment and the location. I look forward to experiencing the summer here.

Heirloom is the best of all worlds combined. Great price, great location, and the design of the units is to die for. I have been scouring the internet for months for a dream place that I was starting to think couldn't be real. Till you guys!
The amenities and location are ideal for our family. Staff is very kind and responsive. It’s gated which is a very good factor so you feel very safe and security is patrolled at night..
Perfect community. Gated, clean, all the amenities you can ask for. Great team that makes your application seamless. Highly recommended.

Living here so far has been wonderful! The staff are excellent and knowledgeable, the maintenance personnel are friendly, and the apartment complex itself is clean. Parking is a hassle until they assign spots, so I'm not too worried about that. Location wise, it's right off of 82nd so that's a positive and a negative, but I like to think more on the positive side of things. It's great here so far!

Living at Heirloom has been an awesome experience for my family.  The apartments amenities are top notch, the layout is open and spacious, and the kitchen is perfect for cooking and baking.  Theres also a bike trail nearby, which our Pittie loves to explore.  Were excited for the dog park and dog wash to open and cant wait to see the courtyard to finish!
Such a peaceful place to live! Quiet, brand new, nice amenities, and great staff!
So far, the place is awesome and the staff are super nice. Rent is relatively cheap compared to other new apartments. All the groceries are 3 mins away, which is cool.

Staff response is lackluster, dismissive, and company-branded emails are usually full of typos and misspelled words. Not surprising since I've lived here a year and have already seen a full office turnover from when I moved in. Rules and leasing agreements are not enforced unless it's about the pool. The gym is only open during office hours (and was closed for most of the first year I was here). Parking spaces are assigned and stickers are required but this is not enforced and our spot is often occupied by friends of the neighbors. Overall would not recommend as it's unpleasant at best, and unlivable at worst. The only pro is the in-unit storage off the balcony, which holds about as much as a 5x5 rentable unit.

I would not recommend that anyone move into these apartments, unless they are prepared to be met with frustration at the unfair conditions and lack of response from the management office when bringing up legitimate concerns.

Our downstairs neighbor constantly smokes cigarettes, weed, and other drugs in the apartment despite it being against the lease. They constantly park a myriad of cars in the assigned parking, without a designated parking sticker, despite it being against the lease. They have loads of people over from 6pm to 3am, making a ton of noise. They are constantly screaming at each other, and have gone so far as to shout obscenities and slurs at me as well when asking them politely to not touch my car.

The same neighbor hit our parked car one night in the parking lot, causing thousands of dollars of damage, and jumped through a window in the middle of the night the same week, damaging apartment property and scattering glass everywhere. 

We have reported them to management countless times, and while we have received empty platitudes, there is no action. The lease clearly means nothing, the rules clearly mean nothing, and while management can leave the office at 6pm and go back to their own residences without a care, we are stuck here living with neighbors who make us feel incredibly unsafe all the time.

Pick somewhere else to live. This is not a good or safe place to be.

I lived in a 2-bedroom at Columbia Ridge for two and a half years, and would recommend it -- with a few things to be aware of. 

MANAGEMENT/STAFF - 5 stars! Jamie and Michelle are super friendly and helpful. Management also goes out of their way to plan fun community events for those with kids, or who want to get to know their neighbors.

GROUNDS/MAINTENANCE - 4.5 stars. The outside is kept clean and well-landscaped by professionals. Maintenance requests were always taken care of promptly and by helpful, pleasant staff.

LOCATION - 3.5 stars.

PROS: Close to both I-84 and I-205 (15-20 minutes drive to downtown). Close to a Costco, which is nice. There are a couple of decent restaurants nearby, as well as a Plaid Pantry convenience store right next door for emergencies.

CONS: 1) The freight train on Sandy Blvd can be loud, and it's a busy street. If you're noise-senstive, try to get a unit closer to the Fremont St. side. 2) This is not considered the "best" part of town, though I never felt unsafe or witnessed any crime. 3) the area is right on the border of a residential and industrial zone. If you don't mind driving, you won't mind, but don't expect to find much enrichment within walking distance of your front door. I wouldn't live here if you rely on public transit, unless you work close by and get your groceries delivered.

UNIT INTERIORS: 3 STARS. We loved the HUGE kitchen! I've never had so much cabinet or counter space in an apartment. The washer and dryer in the unit is a great feature, though you can tell the apartment wasn't designed to accommodate them (they're located in what obviously used to be the coat closet, by the front door). Closet space overall is slightly lacking, especially if you have more than two people. We made it work by installing hooks where we could.
I would bump my rating up to 4 or 5 stars if management would remodel the insides to make the apartments look more attractive and modern, but our unit was completely adequate for what it was. 

AMENITIES: I never used the pool or sauna, but it seemed well-maintained. The little exercise room is nice and there's hardly ever anyone using it, which is great.

VALUE: Fairly priced for Portland in general, and the rent increases were very reasonable.

CONCLUSION: If the location is right for you and you're looking for a reliable, friendly place to rent, look no further! I recommend it

I’m very happy since I got here which is on March 3 I’m very happy with the manager Jamie and assistant manager michelle at Columbia Ridge. the people that are here to help us regardless. I am on the apartments I’m very happy to be living here and I would I would stay here regarding regardless anything if anything please be happy
Over priced for the quality of service received from management.

Management is okay with giving people broken stoves that have had fires on them. My stove totally caught on fire with flames and all!  Yet the VP of the properties decided to just "fix" it and put it in another unit.  I hope you don't get the unit burning stove!!

Our apartment was a one bedroom on the 5th floor, we had a great balcony, with a sweet view of the lovely neighborhood we were a part of. The apartment had a very interesting shape making it look and feel quite big. Killer Burger is across the street one way, there is a 7/11 caddy corner from the apartments, with a Whole Foods about 4 blocks down the street from there. Tons of  restaurants and fun shops. 
Back to the apartments, l just want to tell you Mariah, the manager, is the most accommodating managers I have ever had. She will do anything in her power to make your stay there better!

Mariah returned my phone call right away and within 3 days my application was approved. 

I just moved in and really love it so far. I sleep like a baby here!

Frank estate management will not call or email me back even though they owe money. I was a good renter and paid on time and they owe me money and have not paid me. I have tried many many times to get a hold of someone in management and I have had no luck. They said to call them so we could work things out and I do and they never called me back.  Living there was nice, but dealing with management is a terrible experience!

I have had a fridge that hums and shakes the whole apartment for 15 months, due to covid they could fix it. But when my washer broke they fixed that. I have been calling since I have been vaccinated for 5 months 1-2 times a week they finally put a work order in a month and half ago. Still nothing. The pool is still not open, due to repairs. The only reason why I gave it two stars is because of the scenery

I would give this one star if it weren't for the dog park and the beautiful setting, which, despite poor irrigation and constant issues with mud, are the only redeemable aspects of this place. The worst part is that it does not have nearly enough parking spots for the high density of tenants per unit. If you live past the entrance, parking is nearly impossible in the evenings and you can expect to spend an extra 15 to 20 minutes driving around and even longer walking up to a quarter mile to get to your apartment (sometimes through the aforementioned mud). If you have mobility issues and you can't afford an extra $200 for a parking spot, then I highly recommend that you don't rent here. Another negative aspect is the constant construction, which has been going 5-6 days a week for the last year that I have lived here. One of my windows was broken, as we're the windows of two others that I know of, and a stray nail popped the tire on my car. I know that these things are largely out of management's control, but after 6 years of living here it is obvious that the companies interests are always centered over the tenant experience. This "luxury" apartment complex makes me long for my bargain apartment above the plaid pantry dumpster in the city.
Our apartment was a disaster the day we got the keys. Resolving these issues has been like pulling teeth. Terrible communication here, and still no timeframes for fixes.

Second month of having a porta-potty placed 10 ft from my bedroom window and front door for the construction workers that have destroyed all landscaping and any appeal that there was to living here. Also, there is very little parking available and then construction workers place no parking signs and take precedent over the paying tenants and park throughout the complex. DO NOT LIVE HERE!

This place is definitely a mixed bag. If it were cheaper I would probably happily recommend it despite some of its flaws like the constant construction and nonexistent parking, but for the price they’re asking I feel like you could do so much better elsewhere. They have a lot of little “perks” that feel more like lip service to the idea of a higher end apartment complex than anything to actually justify the price.

Moved recently and wish I never left. The workers are friendly prompt and useful. This continued even through the move out process. I was afraid of losing my deposit or extra fees from other reviews but did not experience this.

I'm actually currently moving out of the Frank Estate, only because my sister and I would like to be closer to our jobs and school downtown. They have an amazing hidden neighborhood, it's beautiful and they keep it very well maintained. Work orders to fix something usually happen that day or the next. An amazing place if you have a dog, tons of open space. 

Only thing that concerns me is the moving out process.. I have read many reviews about people experience and I myself am concerned that I might get charged an arm and a leg for an apartment that we have kept extremely clean. Guess I will have to update my review after moving out. 


Only advise I would give a future resident would be to pay for covered parking... it is very difficult to find parking after 7/8 pm.

I agree with the last reviewer that too often people only leave reviews when they have a bad experience.  For that reason I've reviewed all the places I've lived, and so far they had all been fair and largely positive.  But I don't see any reason not to post an equally fair review when I have had a negative experience. I lived here most recently for just 11 months, from June 2015 to May 2016.

Will try not to make this a TL;DR...if you rate the FE apartments/property/neighborhood in isolation from the staff and objective value for price, it is an OK place to live.  Certainly the property grounds are beautiful, I liked the neighborhood, and always felt safe. 

One thing I wanted to make sure people are aware of is that the pictures on their website and on apartment search sites, with white and chrome interiors, represent only a small portion of their units.  They planned to do a major renovation (complete with major rent hike) but told me right before I moved out that the property owners had cancelled it. I suspect they realized that at the rate people are moving out (my lease renewal was going to be $150-$500 a month for a 2 bedroom), they would end up with a lot of empty apartments for many months at a time.  
Also, all residents received several mass emails asking them to review FE in April, and incentivized us to do so with a gift basket raffle for anyone who did a review.  Be sure to take the time to find and read the reviews from 2015 and early 2016.  You will find that many people had very bad experiences at move-out.  I moved out at end of May and have spent weeks and many, many unanswered emails trying to get basic receipts/invoices to document the cleaning charges they assessed to me, with no success.  They also charged me for blemishes/stains *that I marked as present upon move-in, on my move-in inspection sheet*, and have refused to even address my questions about that.  I finally just paid them what they claimed (undocumented) I owed, under threat of collections.  I made heroic attempts to resolve this with them prior to posting any reviews.

I summary I would no longer recommend FE. I am sad because I lived here from 2009 to 2012 as well, had a stellar experience, and would have recommended it to anyone back then (and did write a glowing review elsewhere at that time).

Lots of bad reviews, but seriously a great place to live. We were there for a year, have a 4 and 5 year old who made instant friends bc of pool and meadow area.  Building materials were horrible quality, but looked nice.  Maintenance folks became known on 1st name basis, but they were prompt and courteous.  That was the only downside, which was far outweighed by the sense of community, safety and peacefulness of the complex.

We did not have the move out experience that others have written about, but we also decided to write off the $200 cleaning fee rather than try to clean ourselves, assuming they'd ding us there anyway.  Bc of the reviews, we expected rate hike when we had to go an extra month before we moved and there was no crazy pricing.  We even considered extending a year instead of moving and our new lease quote was close to the same as our prior year, so nothing bad then either.

I'd chalk up the negative reviews to feedback areas being a place to vent bad experiences, which is a good thing, and I think easier to motivate yourself to do bc you're fueled by anger, right?  

Often seems harder to find time to leave a good review/feedback, which is kinda ironic.  But my family's experience was so good, I made the time:)

Do yourself a favor and don't live here! All seems great at move in, but when it is time to extend your lease or move out they will take as much as they can. The staff was always rude, especially Kim. The apartment is way over priced for what you live in. Portland has high rent anyway, but this place is delusional if they think their apartments are nicer than their competitors (I was fooled by their pictures). Don't let their pictures fool you. Most of their apartments don't look anywhere close to the pictures on this website (these are the newly remodeled apartments - which there are very few of). My wife and I recently moved out and had to go month to month for a couple of months due to us moving this summer. Our rent went up $400-$500 per month when we went month to month (a reasonable increase is expected but this is crazy). I've lived in many apartments, but this is the worst one by far that I've experienced. I read these reviews and didn't put much emphasis on them, and now I'm regretting it. Trust me, it isn't worth your time!

DO NOT MOVE HERE! I moved out a month ago after finishing out my 11 month contract because they were going to give us a $150/month price hike for renewing a 1 year contract and a $700/month price hike for going month to month since we doubted we would need a place for a year as we were actively looking for a house. I am a very clean person, always vacuuming, dusting, cleaning walls even and windows. No shoes in the house, etc. We were charged $200 for carpet cleaning and $200 for all over cleaning! I have never in my life been charged more than $100 for both of those things put together which usually comes straight out of the deposit. They nickle and dimed the heck out of us on top of those things, meaning after they took away from our initial deposit we owed them $394!!! So I emailed them asking to be set up on a payment plan because that was an expense I was not expecting (I have lived in many apartments over the last 10 years and have never been charged for move out fees on top of the deposit) and the lady, Kim, let me know that the manager would get back with me. Never got back with me. I got a call today (1 month later) from collections asking for payment. These apartments may look nice, but they are over priced, impossible to heat, they charge $100-$150/month for water sewer garbage whether you actually use that much w/s/g or not and there is never parking close to your apartment unless you are willing to pay the $30/month for a covered spot. Save yourself the hastle. We have since moved to Shadow Hill and they told us up front that they don't charge for cleaning when you move out. Hallelujah!

Never been to Oregon but decided to move here. Looked thru many apartments here at apartments.com and narrowed my choice down to a dozen places. When I came across The Frank Estate I knew it was the place I wanted to live. Such a stunning community spread out on 35 acres of historic grounds. Though the apartments are older, I don't mind. I chose a 2/2.5 townhouse in a peaceful little cul-de-sac just off the large open green. The dogs can run and play ball on the green and there is direct access to the Fanno Trail from the community. Centrally located to all the shopping and just 10 minutes from downtown Portland. The townhouse is spacious with good closet space. Washer/dryer in the unit is great and a wood burning fireplace for winter. And lastly the Staff and Maintenance so kind and helpful. I love calling the Frank Estate HOME!

I would love to rate my apartment... But, alas, I do not have one.  But if I did, I would have to say, it is so special.  Not only nice  colors, space, large closets and bathrooms,  beautiful grounds, lots of parking.  but the best neighbors anyone could have.  It's perfect!

I have lived her for about 6 months now and my friend that referred me has lived here for 3 yrs. The community is absolutely wonderful! the apartments are nice and the office staff is great! You truly can not beat the location!

I wish i found this apartment community sooner!

Woodlake Apartments are a great place to live if you are looking for a peaceful environment and beautiful landscaping. The stream that flows through the property is lovely and the grounds are meticulously maintained. The interiors of the apartments can be a bit dated, but the management company seems to be responsive to updating them. The complex sits at the end of a dead-end road which means traffic issues are minimal. Woodlake is located within walking distance of several excellent restaurants, a great community center and many upscale grocery stores. Highly recommended!

I’m extremely disappointed with King Street Lofts. After leaving an empty and clean space upon our move out, they still charged us an egregious cleaning fee that took 75% of our security deposit for a 500 sq foot space over items they would do regardless such as re-painting the walls we had left white and untouched. When I reached out to them over my concerns, my voicemail and email inquiries went completely unanswered, which sadly mirrors the broader issues we faced during our time living here.

Throughout our residency, police were called to our floor no fewer than five times due to domestic disputes or tragedies—a situation I have never encountered elsewhere. Perhaps most distressingly, our next-door neighbor tragically took their own life, causing our apartment to flood. Despite this devastating and disruptive event, King Street Lofts management made no effort to contact us, offer accommodations while we were displaced, or even provide a notice or acknowledgment to residents regarding the situation.

If these incidents weren’t concerning enough, here is a list of additional unpleasant experiences you might encounter while living here:

Frequent gunshots heard from outside.
Houseless individuals loitering around the building.
Multiple tenants allowing their dogs to relieve themselves near the main entrance and stairwell, resulting in pervasive urine odors.
Cockroaches in the dumpster room.
Noise from upstairs neighbors, sometimes continuing throughout the night.
Heather, the acting Property Manager, was consistently rude and unhelpful which was widely known throughout the building. 

Living here was an upsetting and unsafe experience. I cannot recommend King Street Lofts.
I called them using their phone number AND sent a request for more information via apartments dot com. It is now 4 days later they still have yet to respond at all

I was lucky enough to call this place home from Feb 2018 - Jan 2019 and this was by far the best living experience. The apartments look great, they provide plenty of light, they're quiet, and the property is well maintained. The property manager, Heather W. is a great person who is easy to communicate with and treats everyone with respect. The neighbors were friendly and respectful, I never had to complain about noise or disruptions. This is unit 203, or as I refer it to, home, and I wouldn't be surprised if in the near future I found my way back to King Street Lofts.
My unit was 203, I had a balcony, floor to ceiling windows, stainless steel appliances, a washer and dryer, and modern looking finishes. This was a luxury apartment at a great monthly price!

Brand new, so everything still works. Soundproofing is not as good as it could be, but isn't horrible either.  Shower water pressure is adequate if not incredible. Tap water tastes a bit funny but is drinkable. The bike rack functions but is a bit awkward to use, both due to its design and its placement. No built-in lighting for the bedroom (I'm in a single-room) but the lighting from the living room is adequate to cover for it, due to the open-wall plan. The appliances are equally new and all work great.   The elevator is conveniently large for bicycles and furniture. The stairs are useable and fully painted unlike many places, but still a bit cramped. 

So far, the manager has been extremely quick to respond to any of my questions via email and has been very friendly overall. I have yet to have a complaint, so I have no idea how that will go ever yet. So far the neighbors have mostly been respectful about noise on weeknights. 

The neighborhood emblamizes the gentrification process portland is undergoing. Whether that means "exciting new developments", "disgusting bougies", or "ew poor people near me" is up to you, I guess.

Has a one-application-per-apartment policy, which is a breath of fresh air compared to most places in portland.

My apartment complex name is Park Fiesta. It sits right off multnomah blvd next to Safeway. We have a pool that is nice but not heated. A communal bbq that the manager let's is use. We have a laundry room with a code so no keys to worry about. The Manager keeps the grounds landscaped and not overgrown. Pets are allowed. It is convenient to live here because everything is so close. No AC unit is allowed in the windows, however portable AC units are allowed. There are garages that are available to rent as well.

I lived here for 1 year now. The new management is poor. It always take a long time to address any issue you have in your apartment. It took forever for them to fix the elevators. There is only one elevator working now for more than 150 residents. Inside the building is messy and dirty. There are much better options than Essex in downtown Portland, I would suggest avoid Essex Apartment!

Essex Apt’s  new maintenancr lady  Michelle .
I really like  how hands on she  is  especially when she deals with all the repair issues  very aggressive to  resolve  it on the spot .accurate and even though she’s too busy she makes to the point to follow up  with us renters.
Very approachable, friendly and smart what else I can say she fixed my apartment toilet issue which  is a big deal for us busy people who wants to have everything in place .
In short  you feel that there’s always solution to most household repairs.  In some Apt’s it’s hard to get hold of maintenance  if your bulbs are out ,Leaking bathroom or  other malfunction  issues lastly she will leave your doorstep until you say it’s ok  I’m happy and problem is gone.

The Essex House is a pretty great place to live. It is very clean, newly remodeled and well maintained. The management staff, Jesse and Charles in particular, are extremely helpful and attentive. 

Due to the great location, there are often some frustrating groups of students that lease unites together. They can be noisy and smoke outside the door and forget their security entrance cards and make living with them unnerving. The office staff does a great job with responding to any complaints though and will do whatever they legally can to make things right. 

Overall, I would definitely recommend living at the Essex House!

Having spent over twenty years of my life living, visiting, and exploring in and around downtown Portland, Essex House remains a perfectly located fixture in the heart of the city.  True walking distance to all MAX transportation and Portland Streetcar lines, the convenience factor consistently ranks higher than the competition.  Whether a relaxing walk on the waterfront, exploration of the countless bars and restaurants, or night out for live music/theater, the Essex House is a hop, skip, or short bike ride away from the amenity of your choice.  With upstanding management, a caring core tenant base, and perks of any high level multifamily community, Essex House is sure to fit your unique needs!

I've lived in slabtown flats for a number of years. I've been here as it's been sold a couple times and through the pandemic. The maintenance team has always been amazing - quick and thorough if there's any issues. Management has been consistently nice and facilities are still overall decent. Definitely have seen the building decline though, no longer worth the increasing price tag.
Slabtown Flats is a wonderful home. Friendly stuff and neighbors, secure building and great community events and common space.
I recently moved in and am enjoying it thus far! Very satisfied!

Building has been well maintained during Covid with frequent cleaning. Staff have worn masks when necessary and still addressed any issues 

Throughout a year's time the dryer, dishwasher, bathroom sink pipes and garbage disposal have had minor issues. But the maintenance staff have quickly responded and fixed them.

Although this property is new, it simply is not worth the high rent. Parking garage rates are high and if you opt for the parking stacker, plan on having your car trapped inside. The car stacker repeatedly is inoperable and you will not have access to your car. Barking dogs can be heard at all hours of the day/night and management does little to help. There is one elevator to service the entire community. The elevator is closed down for hours (reserved) when a tenant is moving in/out. The elevator ALSO breaks down. This property has a high price for the quality in both management and construction. Service requests can take a long time to be resolved and plan to get alot of excuses about the timeframe of repairs. The doors are loud and can be heard shutting at all hours. This includes the garbage chutes which also smell terrible. Although this building looks nice, that is where it ends. We noticed many tenants moving out when there lease was up and we understand why. We are glad to be out of Slabtown Flats!

We moved to Portland a couple months ago and couldn’t be happier with our choice to live at Slabtown Flats. The management (Annie and Zach specifically) have been outstanding (to say the least).  They made the move in process seamless. They are always available and find a solution/answer to every question we have had. The management alone is reason to live here! We don’t have a single complaint. We have had no issues with noise and appreciate that we feel so secure here. And our apartment is awesome! We love the big windows and the finishes are beautiful. We felt at home almost immediately. Location is great. We feel like we found a special gem! We highly recommend Slabtown Flats!

It was a horrible experience living there, I happened to have a pathological neighbor, I got a lot of reports from landlord for being suspect of loud, smoking, dog attack, and more. We had 8 units in one building, they decided to target us. One time neighbor has a gun and pointed at me once by her backyard and i decided to call police and landlord on her, police came and that neighbor denied and later she claims it was a toy, why the hell did she show off and point at me. Landlord didn't do anything! Everyday living there was hell, neighbor harassment us every day. I can't have peace living there. Living here was so racism and homophobia, and so stressful. Landlord wasn't continued helpfully. After 18 months of living there I moved out and I clean my place after I moved out and it was spotless yet they claimed it was dirty and charged me a $75 cleaning fee. I've never been scammed as I have here. Don't believe the lies and don't live here. I wish I had a warning before I moved in!
Good access to the freeway, close to public transport. Mostly adults renters.

I live in the building next door and these apartments always have smokers standing directly in front of the main entrance, and spill out onto the sidewalk where they don’t even care if you’re with children. They also generally don’t pick up their cigarette butts or leave them in the tacky soda bottles left by the door. They also smoke on their balconies and don’t care if they flick their ashes on people below. I’ve lived in my place for 5 years. It’s never changed. Where’s the management?

The GHP and Tower is perfect place for a student to afford and to live !
It has a good space with the best prices across the whole student communities and housings.
GHP has its own teams maintaining everything to the maximum standards available.
Follow the rules abide to them and you will have the best experiences is the key takeaway from GHP.
Finally simple, great living , best community and the best especially for a student and easily affordable.

Good place for a student. There being many tenants, It's easy to acquire furniture and things for cheap or free, just check the bulletin board! The place offers convenient facilities, moving/ getting rid of things a breeze. Garbageman picks up literally anything you don't want. The tenants are generally respectful and nice. This is an AMAZING location nearby the MAX and some good business. Really is an ideal place for student. No complaints!

During my move-out inspection I was told that my place was move-in ready for the next person and that I would get a full refund deposit back. When I got my refund it was not the full refund price and I was charged a bogus fee. Management said that they would check into and get back to me, almost 3 months later and still no response back. Funny how they tell you things and can't remember to get back to you or get things done as promised. When I moved in I was promised a new deck because the old one was dilapidated and very unsafe, so I lived with it during my time there. I think management needs to retire and sell the place to someone who cares about their residents as well as their property.

I had such high hopes moving here, however since moving in nothing works, pool and hot tub down most of summer. Gym tvs do not work. Trash piles up. It isn’t safe or well kept. Multiple car break ins. Management does little to nothing to address residents complaints. For this price not worth it. Very disappointed.

Rowdy neighbors and little to no response from security (tells them to turn it down, lasts an hour) or management (we've done this four or five times now).  

It's a great location but ConAm management collects rental fees and does little else.  I will be breaking my lease to avoid potential conflict and liability, when I was younger it would have been otherwise.

What was once considered a luxury apartment, has now turned into medicre at best.  Promises to complete maintenance requests are unfulfilled, and management thinks simply scheduling "community" functions will make it all better.  Current lease holders are treated with the utmost lack of respect, showing favoritism towards some residents and disdain for others.  Rules are arbitrarily followed and enforced, based upon the "apparent" benefit management can achieve.  Just look at the illegal parking around the entry fountain (which hasn't worked in over a year as well), or the incompetent parking enforcement company hired which resulted in no improvements.  Finally, units are offered to the general public which are larger and more favorably positioned at prices well below the renewal offers provided to current residents.  Management believes that someone already here wouldn't be looking at the rent prices for the same complex.  Well, another holiday weekend just days away.  Rest assured the pool and hot tub will most likely not be working, or if they are, entrance into the  pool area will not be restricted in accordance with the property rules.

The pros: The floor plans are great and we have a stunning view of the Columbia River. The amenities are nice as well and units are modern. 
The cons: Rents increased 9.8% this year for my unit and the utility bills (managed by Conservice) have increased +30% in less than one month.  Management will never call or email you back since Jacob left, and you can wait months for a repair to be completed. The property management company (ConAm) is difficult to reach as well. Crime continues to be an issue in the parking garage and the surface parking area. They did; however, finally stopped allowing Retriever Towing from knowingly and willingly tow resident's cars for the smallest infraction.

The leasing agent Sharday is the best, so helpful, and has made moving in here the best experience. The grounds are gorgeous and the view out of my apartment is the best thing to wake up to every morning.

My friend moved into these apartments in April 2021. I also considered it, however after visiting her on multiple occasions, I decided I will never live here. There is CONSTANT crime in the parking lot. Cars are getting broken into. Cars are being stolen. There are always shady strange people hanging out in the parking lot. I do not feel safe walking from her apartment to my car. The icing on the cake was this past weekend. I stayed over at my friends overnight. Walked out to my car in the morning... all 4 wheels and tires are STOLEN OFF MY CAR. Gone. They managed to steal all 4 off my 2017 Subaru Legacy. They also stole the catalytic convertors off two cars near mine. Where was the apartments security?! You would think they can afford decent security for as much as they charge for rent. Or they can at least install a gate at the main entrance. There is constant crime here and management is doing nothing about it. DO NOT LIVE HERE!!!!

The property management company, JLE Properties consistently assumes a callous, deceitful, irresponsible, rigid and often outright-hostile posture with its tenants. Especially the property manager herself and especially in instances when a tenant reports or complains of: building and apartment malfunctions, lack of community patio upkeep, on-site crime, safety hazards, broken elevators, etc.  Lots of building malfunctions occur pretty regularly. 

Report any of these things to the property manager and the tenant will likely either get no response or will receive a response from her denying any responsibility for the problem — or even that there IS a problem — followed by a curt, retaliatory “offer” to move out if you don’t like living here — rather than engaging in receptive, courteous, constructive and professional conversation to solve the problem. This is the refrain I and many others experience and talk about with one another regularly.  The tenants have by and large been perfectly nice folks, and yet I hear people talk all the time about how it just FEELS unfriendly living here, especially if you need something addressed. Just as another reviewer said: I, too, regret every cent spent living here.  You’ve been warned.

Every year your rent increases 9%. The oven does not work and they deny it so won’t fix it. The dryer takes 3.5 hours to dry a load of clothes and they won’t fix it. The boards on the building fly off during wind and they won’t fix it. 
If you have any complaint it is met with an offer to move out. 

I regret every penny spent.

I moved to this building because I loved the location, real hardwood floors, and tall ceilings. However, the passive home design does not keep your apartment cool in the summer (if its 90 outside its maybe 88 in your apartment) and the electric dryers do not actual dry your clothes. The property manager is extremely rude and does not return phone calls or emails, and you can say goodbye to getting your deposit back.

Property management also took my deposit and charged me hundreds extra upon move out. I left the property in the same condition as it was when I moved in. The same company manages the Kiln Apartments where there are several reviews mentioning the exact same thing. Move anywhere but here, avoid the headache.

I enjoyed living in this apartment, but unfortunately had some issues with my deposit and charges after moving out. I moved out of the apartment and left it undoubtedly cleaner than it was upon move in, but I was charged for cleaning the entire apartment as they claimed every single thing was dirty. They also charged me over 300 dollars for something that was broken when I moved in.. and it was marked on the move in checklist. 
So unfortunately, I would not recommend this place as they will claim whatever they can to not return your deposit and even charge you more.

The parking lot is very small, the street is tight too. Felt very claustrophobic just driving through. It looks like the photos though so if the lot doesn't bother you it's probably a good place to stay :)

I absolutely loved living at Franklin Ide. Fantastic location, quiet building, secure access, very clean common areas. The secured garage was a major perk as well and I never had any issues with parking my car here. I loved my unit, it was clean upon move in and the layout was perfect for me. Shanel, the property manager, is so kind and friendly and made the move-in process very easy. Cannot say enough nice things about this place -- definitely recommend to anyone looking in this neighborhood!
Uptown NW is an amazing place to live. The location is amazing and the staff are so helpful. My apartment was clean and is the perfect layout for my first home.

If you like music at 3am or wooden shoe wearing riverdancers, this is the place for you. Let's start off with franklin ide is pet friendly, which is great if you have one. But with wooden floors between stories and hardwood floors on them, sound travels. Living on the fifth floor, our upstairs neighbor who had a younger dog of medium build loved to play fetch inside. That sounded like a 50lbs of mini clydesdal. On top of the rambunctious pup chasing after a heavy sounding toy, then you add the owners to what turned out to be much louder than most construction sites. Then we had the neighbor to our right that must have worked a graveyard shift cause he started up at 11pm and didn't stop till 5am. Then we had our downstairs that loved listening to bass during the day, which was great background music for my zoom work meeting. The residents living here are on the younger side, who apparently never lived in an apartment environment. I had sent seven emails to management. So that gives you an idea of the management staff. The franklin is directly across the street from Legacy Good Sam hospital which had deliveries and maintenance vehicles constantly in and out starting at 6am most days of the week. We started looking for a new place in December only four months in. While looking for a new place we gave the management staff a chance to compete on prices, but all we got was "We'll ask the corporate office." But never received answers. We ended up break the lease at the cost of $3100 and finding a larger place for the same as what we we're paying and it is quiet.
