Thanks to the friendly and professional staff (Shanel and Mia), moving into the Franklin IDE was a breeze. I was looking for a modern apartment that was within walking distance to great stores and restaurants, and this building fit the bill, especially with scoring a floor plan that I love! I have been here for over a month now and every request or concern I had were addressed immediately. I appreciate the responsiveness of all the staff and hope that this level of communication continues. Parking access is a huge plus too, and residents abide by the current COVID-19 guidelines as well which helps me feel a lot safer. Im very happy to have made a home here.

This building is great! Its clean, management is responsive, package delivery is easy and the property is secure. Im also impressed with how quiet the building is. Been here a little over one month and am super happy with my choice. Dog friendly too!!

I have lived in 2 apartments in the Franklin Ide.  Both have been architecturally well designed.  Leasing and repair staff are truly excellent.  Problems or repairs are addressed very quickly.  In pre-COVID times, management sponsored social events created a sense of community.  Soundproofing could have been better during construction, but that is the only negative.  Uptown NW Collection does an excellent job...and I used to manage apartment buildings in a college town.  Jim Y.

I've lived here since November of 2021 & it has been a solid place to live. Neighbors are friendly for the most part & stay to themselves. Rent is reasonable for the location & the apartment itself, which is mostly well maintained. Management is responsive & friendly. The only reason I am giving this building three stars is the WATER HEATER. I have lost count of how many times Affinity has "fixed" it. The last time I was to understand the engine/motor component was replaced, yet the water heater went out AGAIN over the weekend. This is ridiculous for the rent that I pay to live in Multnomah Village. Whatever the issue is, that they don't want to pay for, JUST PAY FOR IT! If this isn't actually fixed, come November, I will be moving elsewhere. Walking a mile to my best friend's house, just to take a shower, is completely unacceptable!

Constant maintenance issues, rude tenants that are incredibly loud and confrontational who park wherever they want even though it's assigned, cops are constantly showing up to our neighbors apartment, a car was stolen out of the lot, multiple apartments flooded and people were moved around and they over charge for these units. Do not rent here if you want to enjoy where you live. Definitely not worth the headache.

I'm convinced most reviews are fake on here and Google since we've had a horrible experience all around. It's way too much money for an "updated" complex that has had consistent problems. We make a combined income of $4k a month and barely qualified with a cosigner who makes almost $100k a year (so ridiculous). Our unit was not ready on our move in date since they were still cleaning/renovating it, we've had constant plumbing problems and little to no parking (even though you pay for a space), they have incredibly rude property management people working there(Olga), and even took a month to fix an oven light. Our bathtub needed to be resurfaced in the first week, our fan has been broken since move in and we have water damage on our ceiling that hasn't gotten fixed. We also pay $180-$260 a month just on energy bills since the units aren't properly sealed/insulated. I'm not sure how, but we have had many more problems than are even listed above. This is THE worst place I've ever rented from. Do yourself a favor and save your money for somewhere else. We will not be renewing our lease when our year is up.

Small community in a secure building just off I-5. Lots of square footage, especially in the living rooms, with plenty of storage space. 3 bedrooms have washer/dryer in unit. Small gym with racquetball court, showers, and saunas. Seasonal pool. Management is honest and flexible within reason.

Downsides: low water pressure and the water temperature is relatively the same between the hot and cold settings. Very few hot showers in the past couple of years I've lived here. Rent continues to increase with the market and renovations are planned in the next year.

Office staff are professional and friendly. Apartment size is sufficient for the price. Amenities are above expectations. (Fitness room, off street parking, close to public transit, pool, sauna, noticed a racquetball court, but not sure if it's in use) Overall, a nice place to hang your hat at the end of the day. 
Unfortunately, the location has a major drawback. I wouldn't recommend it to folks that are seeking a quiet place to live. While watching TV, if I open my windows, I have to crank the volume up to near blaring in order to hear it, due to Interstate 5 running directly out my back door...24/7 traffic noise.  When the windows are closed, it's still very noticeable, but not as invasive.  Also, the grounds and exterior halls to entry doors have been neglected for a long time, which makes the property look cheap & trashy.

I paid a monthly fee to have my motorcycle parked in the parking garage of Cook St Apartments. The motorcycle was stolen sometime between October and December. 

After notifying the management team they let me know the timeframe was too large for them to review camera footage. The most frustrating part was the fact that they did not notify any residents via email of the theft.

I've been a resident at Cook Street for nearly two years.  I have to say the staff, especially Sarah are absolutely amazing.  They seem to magically remember all the tenants by name. I recently had to have my window blinds replaced because of a frayed cord.  It took a while to complete the work order because they chose to use a small local company which I wholeheartedly support.  They were vigilant about giving me updates and keeping me in the loop.  My lease is up in December and unless i can find a place that feels this good I'll be staying.

I just moved into an apartment at Slogan Apartments, and I could not be happier.  It's brand new, and the finishes are great. I feel like I am getting way more than I am paying for.  Whoever did the design had marvelous taste.  The location is ideal, right on the MAX line, and close to food carts, parks, a New Seasons.  North Portland is a fun place to be right now, with lots of new restaurants and other apartments coming on-line.  The building is great - not so huge that you feel lost, and the views are outstanding.  Everyone is super-friendly. The icing on the cake for me is the apartment manager.  He is awesome - incredibly responsive, quick to iron out any new building kink (of which there have been, amazingly, just one or two), and helpful to the extreme.  I had to go out of town, and he stashed two rugs for me that were delivered after I was gone in his own apartment rather than leaving them in the hall.  He consistently communicates his willingness to help unravel any issue; he embodies the idea of being neighborly in all the best ways.  I looked at a lot of nice places before choosing Slogan, and I am really happy I did.  would recommend Slogan Apartments (and its manager) to everyone.

I moved to Portland from out of state and Shawnda has been incredible before during and after the move. I have lived here for a month and a half now and I absolutely love it here. Administration is friendly and responsive. The resident portal is easy to navigate. The apartment itself (I live in a studio) is well made, quiet, and beautifully open with a lot of natural light (thanks to the amazing floor to ceiling windows). I was also pleasantly surprised by the good amount of storage despite the size of the apartment. The communal spaces are clean, and the only negative I can think of is that the noises from the hallway carry through the door very easily but it is not very disruptive. This is also a very central and pet friendly area with a park a block away and a dog park a half mile away; not to mention the grocery store, shopping centres, restaurants, and pharmacy just blocks away as well. I am very pleased with this apartment complex, and I think that it is also pretty affordable especially given its location.
Very friendly staff. Breathtaking views, wonderful rooftop and amenities. It has everything you need! Carol the manager was so efficient during every step of the process.

Carol and Melissa were wonderful and took such good care of me from application to move-in. I feel so comfortable living here, and I love how accessible so many lovely restaurants and boutiques are walking distance from here. V happy! :)

The building is amazing. The location is amazing. The apartments are amazing. The management team however wont remember you, wont answer the phone, and. wont answer emails. So if you like feeling anonymous and unimportant, live here!
No security. Two floors of weekend renters. Common areas are routinely trashed and rules ignored. Avoid.
Great location. The appliances are really nice and patio space is big enough. I have lived here for three years now. Common areas maintenance and cleaning can be improved.
We originally liked our experience because we're low key and didn't need much assistance, but after the evacuation and lack of communication we don't feel as safe in the building.
We love living at Couch9. We feel safe and supported!

Extreme changes since Aug. 2018. Original staff is gone... new property managers. Utilities have skyrocketed. Feels like a hotel not a home. Money is what decides everything. Not real people with real concerns and issues. For instance we are forced to pay for valet recycling - no opt in. Questions go unanswered because management is transitional. They rent out apts. to corporations who come and go and abuse the space. But it doesn't change. No consequences. Parking garage is dirty. Broken glass from a break-in there for months. Overall, it has gone downhill. Corporate atmosphere.

The 3rd 5th and 8th floors have many air bnb type rental units. The key fobs don’t work for the door or elevator from time to time. They no longer have guest suites. I guess they want friends of residents to rent the short term rentals I mentioned above. But the icing on the cake is that Jordyn is withholding my security deposit after my 8 month lease although I cleaned the unit upon departure. She has disregarded the video that her agent took and my photos showing a very clean unit and says they had to spend $160 on a cleaning crew after I moved out! I’d attach my photos here if I could.

I recently stayed in the guest suite, as a friend of mine lives here. I'm not from Portland, but this location is amazing. Everything I needed was within walking distance and I was able to experience all the great food Portland has to offer; well not all of it but a decent amount. The staff constantly greeted me and made me feel like I lived there. They were very accommodating and always took the time to answer my questions or let me into my unit/the building every time I forgot my key. The building is kept very well and clean. The suite looked as though it had never been used, that's how clean it was. There is construction going on at the retail space but they don't tend to start till 9AM and are done around 3PM. It will be cool to come back and visit once the construction is done and the bar/restaurant opens up.
Good location, a lot of options for food and grocery near by. Great staff. Their storage is really well priced. All the amenities they have to offer are great and the building is always clean.
New building and friendly staff as well as great location and views.

So when we toured someone was raving about the staff and how amazing they are. Honestly, they were giving such a raving review I thought it was an "off-duty" team member or relative. We went on the tour and got a pretty good sense of the staff and felt they were pretty cool as well. We decided to rent here and now being a tenant for a month we have to agree that the staff is AMAZING!!! They truly make you feel like you're at home and a part of their community.

I lived in this building for one year. Amazing building. Solid walls so that you don’t hear your neighbors. The staff is extremely accommodating and friendly. They really take their time to get to know you!

The building, the staff and the tenants make this a really great  place to live. You feel welcomed and appreciated when you are here.  My dogs love the other dogs in the building and there are three dog parks that you can walk to.  You are centrally located to 4 grocery stores all within 5 blocks in 4 different directions. Lots of restaurants, shops and a great neighborhood drycleaner right around the corner.

I’ve lived in the Clermont Apartments since 2013 and have seen many positive changes.  The management and maintenance staff are wonderful and work quickly to accommodate requests.  The property is clean and well maintained and has proven to be a safe place to call home.  I definitely recommend!
I’ve lived here for a bit over two years now and I’m glad I chose this place. Everyone is kind and quick to respond if any issues arise. On top of that the area is quiet and nice and clean :)
Very spacious, beautifully cleaned. Well kept! Thank you so much
I have lived here for over 5 years and love the park like setting. Quiet and peaceful. The grounds are maintained and so nice. Very friendly management and maintenance personnel.

If you own more than one car beware the parking. Parking situation is absolutely terrible. They dont provide more spaces for the cars people own and tow your car if you park anywhere youre not supposed to. Road in the back toward the cul-de-sac is very bad. Pool and gym were closed during summer due to covid, which is understandable, but we were still being charged for both. Sprinklers are on during rain often times. Such a waste of water and money. Some sprinklers wet areas that dont even have grass.
Clermont is a beautiful complex with lots of kind staff. I love our home so much.

Clermont is the perfect community to feel safe and at home. The exceptional staff are so friendly and helpful, willing to address any question I have.
This is an excellent place to live.

I love living here! The guest parking can be tough as many people have multiple cars here, but that would be my only change. I love our unit, the property, the employees i get to talk to, the location, etc
Very Friendly Maintenance and office staff are very Good.
We have lived here for 5 years and are very pleased with the environment here. Nice neighbors and office staff.
We've enjoyed living here for almost nine years now. Thank you!
Clermont has been nothing but friendly to us. We love our home so much!

This apartment complex was pur savior. My friend Joshua and I moved from New York to Oregon around Mid-July. Reasonable on pricing, fantastic staff in the office and maintenance crew. The individual that sold us on the apartment was Carissa. She was honest, friendly, hardworking, and most importantly professional. Her new assistance is amazing also her name is Sherry I believe. She really helps run the office pretty well and is down to earth. Wish I could give more than Five stars. Friendly environment and just all around an amazing experience! Seriously check them out!!!

I like the location and the price of this apartment. This apartment is located close by the station, downtown and PSU, (Everytging is walk distance.) so it is convenience to go somewhere without the car. Compare to other apartments around here, the price is pretty decent for the students. Despite the building is little bit old, it is good to stay here. Overall, I'm satisfied staying this apartment.

The apartment complex is convenient for everyday commute to school and work. It has a excellent scenery and the complex works with students to afford the housing. The staff is eager to help when needed they also very kind and courteous. I have enjoyed staying there bur hope for a different apartment in the near future.
Management does not care about you. You will  complain and ask about an issue over and over and they will push it off over and over. Stay away.

We had a fantastic time touring the apartments, and the realtor lady was very clear about prices and options. what was weird was she kept pushing an option out of price range with vaulted ceilings, when she had listed about 4 inside our range that were perfect for us. When we went to apply we found out why-not only had the style of apartment we had been looking out, which had several available, have no availability, but all the prices had gone up at least $300 anyway. The only thing actually available was the apartment with vaulted ceilings. 

Just be honest! No reason to lie about prices or availability.

Lived here 3 years. This place goes to great lengths to create an aura of modern high-end living, but it's all thin window dressing on a very poorly constructed building. The walls and ceilings are very thin, and every footstep above you is magnified as the acoustics are similar to living inside a drum. Doors will slam all summer with unit-shaking intensity as an open window will create this weird air-flow dynamic.

While the staff is amiable, the tenants are a different story. There is constant abuse of the trash rooms, dog poop in the stairwell, fire alarms pulled in the middle of the night on a monthly basis, and the kind of person in the gym who loads all the weights onto the bench press bar and drops it as loud as he can. With the thin walls, this is a supremely obnoxious amount of aggressive noise and it's highly stressful.

Your rent will increase at a steady clip, greatly exceeding than what a new tenant will pay for the same sized unit.

I found an apartment for rent in the building and moved forward the same day, the online leasing system is very easy to get through and any questions I had was quickly answered by phone call. I have just moved in and so far its been great, very happy with the rental price and the location. At this point I would recommend the building highly.

These apartments aren't cheap.  But neither are any apartments that are right on the MAX line,  close to downtown, with washer/dryer in unit, that allow pets,  etc.  

The floor plan is nice and open, with lots of light. The appliances are newer and work well.  There's a hotel-style air conditioner/heater unit in the living room.  For some reason, the heater runs up my electric bill,  but not the a/c so much.  

The office staff here are all nice,  fun,  and most importantly,  competent.   There isn't much of a neighborhood feel in the area, but if you'd rather have that, pay the same price for a smaller apartment with fewer amenities up in Nob Hill.

I've lived here almost a year now,  and am renewing my lease, so that should say something.

I want to start off by saying that the management means well and do their best, and  the staff are excellent at fixing anything that needs to be done. 

On the other hand, for the price, the apartments are built cheaply & not insulated well, meaning that they are freezing in the winter and simmering in summer.  The layout is cramped.  The kitchen is so tiny that my husband and I have to "reserve" time to use the kitchen because only one person can fit in it at a time. 

Problems with the water pipes.  The water is frequently turned off at least once a month or so, & the management tries to let residents know, and sometimes it’s off for more than an hour.  Also, it randomly shuts off without warning.  Once we had a pipe break and the entire first floor was flooded with about 2 inches of water & it was rushing like a river.  Good thing for renters' insurance!

However, the worst thing is the high crime.  I've had my car parked in the outside parking area, & twice the window has been shattered in order to break in and steal...well nothing.  It's an old beater that clearly doesn't even have a radio.  Maybe it's just random violence?

My husband's car had its catalytic converter stolen.  My bike was stolen twice, even though it was locked inside the porch right next to our front door.

Amazon and other packages are constantly being stolen.

Graffiti everywhere.  Even on the rocks of the beautiful nature spot by the apartments.  No effort to clean it up.  Trash everywhere.  I pick it up myself around the premises and it's just back in a couple of days.  A lot of dog owners don't pick up their pets' poop.  

The management should lower the prices or try harder to lower crime by building a locked fence or getting good security cameras, although the one they have was aimed at my car one of the times the window was smashed, can't identify anyone, of course.

Update:   Our apartment just flooded again, this time from the top of the floor to the bottom. It’s a river.  Almost everything touching the ground floor is ruined.  I don’t even know how to get them appraised or what to do.  They have drilled all sorts of holes in the walls and have several dryers that are so loud I can’t get any work done, and they have to rip out the carpets and replace the actual walls, all while we are living here.  

“This is a nightmare all the time.” Said one of the facilities workers, 4/23/22.

We're trying to find another place to live, but in this economy, it's nearly impossible.

The paper thin walls allows you to hear anything your neighbor is doing. I have had to make over 6 noise complaints only being here 6 months. I've never had issues living anywhere else like this. I've also had my car broken into outside my apt, i've found needles on the ground, homeless people getting into the gated parking to dig for recyclables, and it doesn't feel like theres any improvement. The unit may look nice from outside, but the quality of the home is terrible along with it being in a bad neighborhood. The bike path runway allows anyone to come in and out of this cul de sac. There's an overpass with gang graffiti. Beware of this property!
You get the feeling you're outside the city but in actuality you're just blocks from downtown.

apartmentName: Rose City Center Apartments - 55 and Over
review: New looking and nice neighborhood! Everything is clean and it has a wonderful gym

I've lived here for 3 years and I can't wait to move out. At first with the old owners/management it was a good place to live with minor cons. It was super annoying that they forced you to pay for $18/ month trash services to just leave in the hallway. You can't opt out and half the days they forget to pick up trash. But ever since the owners/WonderDog Management took over, it has been awful. Emails, calls, and texts are never answered. We went through 5 front desk managers in 1 year, and each one was extremely incompetent. Maintenance Requests don't get addressed unless you find someone and talk to them in person on the rare occasion they are in person. There was a miscommunication with my window AC unit that they allowed 2 summers ago, but then last summer that said it violated the lease. The car garage breaks once a month. Last year there were also awful problems with vandalism. This place is just not worth the money.

When I first moved in I really like this place. Big windows, large ceilings, everything is pretty new. Great location.

However, recently everyone is leaving because the property management company is so bad. We are currently on our 4th property manager in less than 18 months. 

The property claimed to be building a gym when I moved in almost 2 years ago. The gym is built, but we have no access to it for at least 5 months. 

There has been some major crime issues in the building, gun shots and vandalism, and our packages get stolen often. Trying to contact the management company leads no where, they literally don't respond at all to any communications. It's really too bad.

I signed a lease remotely, without seeing the apartment in person. Here are the things I wish I had known then:

- The apartments are reached via a pretty gross carpeted interior hallway, with poor signage and lots of storage and apartment doors. Even after the carpets were cleaned major stains remained... a shabby introduction to the building. 

- Valet trash is sold as a benefit, but what it amounts to is a series of garbage cans out in the common hallways, every weekday night. You have to dodge cans in the hall on your way in and out, and smell everyone's garbage.

- Units have no AC. I found this to be extremely uncomfortable in the summer months. I bought one large standing window AC unit for the main areas but the bedrooms were basically unlivable in June, July and August. Cheap construction!

- The LEED status is real, but the building seems to have lost interest in sustainability measures: styrofoam cups in the lobby, seasonal scents pumped into common areas, toxic carpet cleaners, etc. Everyone seems to use window AC units.

- The north side is loud, bounding Hawthorne St.

- Cheap Cadet heaters in each room are tough to adjust and limit furniture placement. Oh, and that crappy product recently had a huge safety recall.

- Some apartments have no overhead lights in bedrooms and living areas. Little fans instead. Cheap!

- The standard refrigerator, freezer and ovens are tiny, apartment-size, so be prepared for that.

- The finishes just felt really cheap to me. I liked the marmoleum in the bathrooms, but the faux wood vinyl flooring throughout the unit was less nice, and the granite countertops felt downright old school. All of the counters (bathrooms and kitchens) have granite tile, so there are grout seams that are hard to clean. The walls and ceiling have orange peel texture. The whole place feels really dated, even for a building built in 2009, and sort of shabby.

- In the bathrooms the fan/light combo is on a motion sensor, so it goes on even when you don't need it, and regardless of whether you want it on. I tried to get that feature turned off and was told it wasn't possible. I found it really disruptive in the middle of the night, and wish there was at least an override switch.

- There are huge gaps under the front unit doors leading to the hallways, so you can hear the conversations of everyone passing by.

- Security has been a major issue. I had four different Amazon parcels stolen... and these were delivered inside the keyed lobby.

Applied online and received rent quote of $1355 for apt #308 to move in on 10/12/2015.  Was approved, sent email to office regarding no pets, lease term, etc.  Was told I would need to pay a half months rent of $677.50 as a deposit.  I agreed.  Next, I received my welcome letter and now rent was $1629.  I emailed the office back to inquire on the discrepancy. (please note: no one answers at 20 on Hawthorne, you have to call Tupelo Alley apts to get a live person.)  The girl who answered told me that the online system was wrong and that the rent was $1629.  I explained what the other person had told me and she said, "as I said sir, the online system is wrong."

Very rude and will not be living there.  Have contacted VP to get application fee back.  TOTAL BAIT AND SWITCH.
I love having everything new. If anything goes wrong management gets it taken care of immediately. Maintenance is awesome. I've never lived anywhere that they were so on top of things.

I lived here for quite a while in one of the studio apartments.  Internet was an intermittent issue, as CenturyLink is a pretty garbage provider and it's the only option. 

Ultimately, Atlas Management has a lot of the same problems corporate property-grubbing entities like it have had recently. The halls and common areas were RARELY ever cleaned, and frequently built up a lot of dust that can bother allergies. The only time they ever had employees on site was to show apartments to new potential tenants.  They WILL keep your deposit, by the way, no matter how much you clean up, so consider that money lost upon move-in. They also might try to bring in a new potential tenant BEFORE YOU'VE FINISHED MOVING OUT, and even when you contact them about how that's not okay, they'll show up with a potential tenant in the midst of your clean-up efforts and just request you leave the apartment a few minutes while they show it to the potential replacement.

The only thing saving them from 1 star in this review is that they did a good job installing a bike rack in my unit upon request.  Otherwise, garbage, hands-off management style that pushed me toward better prospects.

I recently moved into the Margot, and I wish I didn't sign a year lease. I have lived here a week, and the following has gone wrong:

1. All online sites said that there was one-month free with move-in and they would not give me this promotion.
2. NSF Fee - Before I moved in I tried to link in my account to set up automatic payments. I must have typed my account number incorrectly. I double-checked calling my bank, and they said that there was no attempted transaction. NSF means "non-sufficient funds" and it is a term that is used when the holder of a checking account is overdrawn and the bank returns a bounced check. Since no check was bounced and I was able to link an account before the payment was made I was wrongly charged a $35 NSF fine.
3. Broken Dryer - I tried to do laundry and discovered that the dryer does not work. I mentioned this on 7/5, and was called today (7/8) by Blomberg to schedule an appointment. The next available appointment is on July 28, which assuming that they are able to address the concern during the appointment means that I will be going an entire month without a functioning dryer after moving into a new place. 
3. Broken Air Conditioner - I tried to turn on the A/C for the first time as it is getting hotter outside, and I got the "E/C" error on the air conditioner. Despite contacting staff, they have not set up a repair.
4. Missing Window Screen/Refrigerator Shelf - One of my windows is missing a screen and the fridge is missing the tops of the climate control drawers.
5. I tried to contact CenturyLink to install internet but they said they couldn't do it until the previous tenant ended their internet service. This was a big headache to resolve and didn't happen at anywhere else that I've lived.
6. The mail key I was given was wrongly keyed and I wasn't able to get my mail for a week.

I have lived here for two years and recently renewed my leasing for another year.  The admin team maintains the units in pristine conditions.  Mr Leopoldo (Polo) is amazing, always finding the best way to promptly assist all residents with our service requests. Thank you Mr Polo for the great work that you always do for all the residents!  He is a great asset to the company and a fantastic team member.  The location of this community is very convenient as is only 10 min from downtown Portland but have a very serene living ambience, and the view from my apartment is beautiful, breathtaking!. I love where I live!

Just moved in and can say the girls in the office were very nice, which made for a smooth transition. Head of maintenance, Polo, was extremely helpful and the grounds are kept really well. Overall a good experience.
Constant construction noise, constant paint smells, constant blocked access due to construction  -- you are living in a construction site and there seems to be no end in sight

I moved in from out of state in April and really love living here so far. The current management is doing their best to keep up with ongoing maintenance of this large complex and have always responded to my needs quickly and in a friendly way. I like that we always get plenty of email alerts for maintenance projects or other community info.  Food Truck Thursday has been fun, too. Now that the amenities are available, it's even nicer. Pool and spa pool are lovely. Grounds are beautiful.  My unit is in a very quiet building and the layout is ideal for me. During the transition of management, my unit didn't get any flooring upgrades before I moved in. The flooring inside my door is very odd so it will be tricky to keep the carpet clean during the wet months. Another con from my perspective is that the package room is constantly jammed making it difficult to locate items. There's ample parking for guests and my assigned spot is included with the rent. Location is ideal for all my needs. At this point, I expect to stay here for quite a while.

I’ve been anxiously waiting to move into my new apartment here since June 1st, and I have to say, the customer service has been wonderful! Despite the challenges they have faced with a limited staff, they are professional, and when they say they’re going to do something, they do it! I’m looking forward to living here even more. Shout out to Rheina (excuse my spelling) for her dedication to excellence and her team! I appreciate your professionalism and quick responses. So excited to call this place my home, tomorrow!

It’s been challenging with new management but they are doing the best, considering the pandemic. They are taking care of us better than previous management.  Thank you Prime for doing your best...all things considered.  Keep doing what you’re doing.  That said, beautiful apartments with great views. I love my home.

I have lived here for 3 years, and loved every moment! Friendly helpful staff, impeccable grounds, quick responses to any maintenance issues, and very reasonable rent! I loved living in a 2 bedroom 2 bath apartment tucked into a quiet hillside neighborhood, but still within less than a mile of my work (St. Vincent's hospital). Added bonuses of convenient amenities, and within a quick walk of the grocery store! 

Do yourself a favor and consider this community. I would stay another three years if I could! (moving for work)

The view is spectacular!  The interior is in excellent condition.  I've noticed every apartment is being completely remodeled when someone moves out (carpet, appliances, everything), the owners are spending a lot of money on refurbishment and it shows.  Pet owners delight - very pet friendly and plenty of places to walk your dog.  The community seems friendly, everyone says hello.  The parking can be a bit cramped depending on what building you're in but for the most part ample and you never have to worry about getting towed.  The office staff is great, very responsive.  The repair guys are great, show up on time and make sure everything is taken care of before leaving.  I really like living here.

The best part is the view!  Looking out over Beaverton and Cedar Hills, puffy clouds in the blue sky, all of the lights at night - no other place like it on the west side!

This place charges an obscene amount for what is a completely basic, and aggravating apartment. Claiming to be "luxury," it's not anywhere near luxury (as anyone who tours one of the newer lofts downtown knows). This place charges the same as luxury apartments/lofts, but isn't anywhere near that. The appliances constantly break, the heating doesn't work either (uses cheap space heaters mounted into the walls of the living room, and baseboard heater in the bedroom). The gym is never cleaned (yes there is a gym, but it is not maintained in any way), the interiors are very poorly considered, and the companies they use to do repairs and such do such a poor job that there are gaps in walls, ceiling heights, (and that's only if you're one of the residents who didn't have construction workers outside (and inside your home for months on end). There's a real difference between quality/luxury and cheap knock offs. This place is a cheap knock off. People who live her pay for everything, water, all utilities, trash removal, everything. Even bikes! They won't even allow you to store your bikes in the carport, but are forcing residents to pay $5 to store them in the "clubhouse." The only good thing about this place is the people on staff who work the grounds and do repairs. But they are not treated anywhere near where they should be. I will also say that office staff have people come in and out of your apartment whenever they want to, or do not take care of requests in a timely manner. I've seen the staff be totally unaccommodating to people over serious issues. Seriously, for the money, rent a place downtown that is CLEAN, NEW, has legit heating and cooling and appliances, and actually gives you something for your money.

Sunset summit= a construction zone with no regard to its residents.  After living here for 2 years and going through 2 major construction projects it seems like it will never end.  The projects are very poorly managed and they will NOT tell you about them when you sign your lease.    

Year 1= blacktop project.   Instead of doing small sections at a time they tear up half the road all the way around the complex.  Traffic jams, poor planning, pot holes, and a rushed project I fed up with tar everywhere and road conditions worse then they began with. 

Year 2= complete invasion and hostile takeover.   Cosmetic repairs to the outside of the building= a take over of the apartment on the inside ( see pictures).  Going on the 3rd month of this now and management refuses to do anything to rectify the situation.  


I also highly recommend getting a printed and signed copy of your lease.  Management is known for sneaking things in at the end and trying to rush you through everything.

It would be best if you looked elsewhere.  

Pros:
1. There are great views
2. Apartments aesthetically look O.K. on the outside (and they're renovating so they'll look even better...on the outside)
3. They have a pretty cool mail delivery system for package handling
4. Their maintenance personnel are friendly

Cons:
1. Not pedestrian friendly at all.  If you want to walk west, you will need to cross the road at SW Miller Rd and SW Barnes.  Otherwise, you will need to cross blindly at another exit west on Barnes (that's a fun turn btw).  

2. The apartment complex is scattered across a hillside.  It snows more here than other parts of beaverton, so be prepared.

3. Our apartment had fleas upon moving in.  They don't seem to contract out to third party exterminators and use their maintenance personnel for that.

4. They have "smoke" alarms near showers and bathrooms which continually go off if there's steam.  Should they go off too often, and should your neighbors complain, the leasing staff seem to passive aggressively tell you that you should close the door, turn on the fan, and deal with it (for the betterment of all, of course).  Of course, this might also lead to mold, etc., as their fans aren't *that* strong

5. The leasing managers seem to want the apartment complex to look fantastic... on the outside...And they will go out of their way to do make sure that everyone knows.  Like the typical home owners assoc., they will write passive aggressive paper notices to you when things are not up to their standards.  A previous tenant had left a tire in one of our parking spaces; we left it there because it didn't seem to be in the way; the leasing office writes us an ultimatum to move it.

6. Look at the furniture & cabinetry carefully upon moving in.  Assess whether *you* think it's well made, or a cheap alternative.

7. Read your leasing agreement *carefully*, especially with regards to the end of your lease.  Remember what is written, and don't expect them to remind you directly.  They will, however, tell you about the various special deals they have on new lease renewals (always a nice gesture).

8.  Access to mail packages and various amenities is limited to leasing office hours.

I love the amenities and being so close to the city. The things I dislike are the thin walls and ceilings. You hear every step and activity of your neighbors above you. Also the rent hikes every year. You should lock in at 2 years if possible to avoid it.

I lived in Sunset Summit Apartments for a year and a half and I LOVED this place. The only reason I am moving out is because I am getting married and my fiancé owns his place. The apartments are nice and the amenities are fantastic. In full disclosure I only used the pool, basketball courts, gym, etc. a handful of times, but they were so great to have if I wanted to use them. The maintenance staff is amazing and what little interaction I had with the staff in the office was very pleasant. Though they might not know my name they always recognized me and were very helpful. No place is ever going to be perfect and this place definitely had some negatives, but overall it was one of the best apartments I have lived in.

Pros:
Easy access to just about anywhere in town. I work in NE, have friends in LO and Hillsboro and on the east side and it is pretty easy to get just about anywhere.
The windows! I lived in a top floor, one bedroom so maybe they were bigger, but they brought in so much light.
A/C, in unit washer/dryer, parking space - these three things are a must for me to live anywhere.
The maintenance staff was always on top of any issue or problem.
Amenities - gym, pool, hot tub, basketball and racquet ball courts.

Cons:
The walls are a little thin. My neighbors were particularly loud on one side which probably added to the issue, but they could use some more sound proofing.
Cost - I loved this apartment, but I did think that the cost was a little high. Not terrible, but just a smidge and it keeps going up.
The smoke detector/fire alarms were very touchy. They tell you to use the fan in the bathroom because the steam can set off the smoke detector just outside the bathroom door. But it also goes off if you use a humidifier or turn your heat on in the winter and your apartment has even a little moisture. It will just beep at you a little if these things happen, but when they really go off (thankfully mine never fully went off) all the smoke detectors in your section of the building go off. This happened a lot in my area. I think it had more to do with the people living there. It never happened in the middle of the night thankfully, but it was still an inconvenience.

I've loved living at Sunset Summit over the past five years! The complex is perfectly located among the scenic treetops in the west hills and very close to downtown, the 26 and 217 freeways, and Sunset Transit center. This beautiful complex is updated and well maintained inside and out. Both the office staff and maintenance staff are professional, helpful and friendly. Any maintenance issues are handled efficiently and courteously. I've always been treated fairly and respectfully.
The downsides are, you never know who you're going to get as a neighbor. Unfortunately that's the risk with any apartment living situation anywhere.
If you decide to move in with a "be responsibly considerate" mindset-you won't have issues with your neighbors, security or office staff. You do share walls, floors and ceilings.
In the years living here, I've met mostly kind and considerate tenants who are friendly and respectful.

The lady was extremely rude. Took multiple attempts to get ahold of someone in person or on the phone. They no longer take pets even though website says they do and their flier on their desk also tells you about the deposit. She said they already have their fair share of animals.

No storage, very noisy, I shared a kitchen vent with my neighbor (who smoked crack) no in unit laundry or trash chute so you have to haul both down stairs to the basement. Packages often get stolen since they just sit in the front forge. There’s a code on the door to get in but I have found it’s easy for randoms to just walk in and wander the halls.

Not a single thing is insulated. The upstairs neighbors sounded like they could fall through the floor at any moment. I could hear my neighbors take a shower as if it were happening in my living room. Can’t keep the noise out, can’t keep the heat in. It’s over priced and there is zero parking. The ring that was supposed to hold the shower curtain up couldn’t hold its own weight. The light from the bank sign outside kept my whole apartment extremely well lit 24/7 making sleep that much more difficult. But hey, if you like noise, deception, and throwing money away, you might like it. It is vintage and kinda pretty.
Have lived in three locations here in Portland Metro area and re-leased at Multnomah Village Apartments as this is my favorite by far!  Great location, community and apartment complex.
Well, it is a very nice place, but aside from that its also right smack dab in the middle of the village! Great place to be able to go out of or stay in! Just a wonderful place, I think.
Fantastic place to live, proximity to downtown, Beaverton, lake Oswego, Tigard. Then you get the shops below and off of SW Capitol Hwy. Highly recommend!

Great location for Multnomah Village living! I have always felt taken care of here. It is quiet and well maintained. In the rare event I require assistance, the staff is friendly, attentive, and timely.

Great amenities, location and neighbors, but bad sound insulation and management is reactive not proactive.  If your upstairs neighbors are noisy, forget about sleep, management will not enforce the quiet enjoyment clause of the leases.  They issue meaningless "citations" and tell you essentially to get over it.  I know other neighbors in the same situation.   Also, the garbage room is shared by three other retail businesses, so it's often dirty and smelly.  I had to beg them to address this issue.

I am a currently living at the Multnomah Village Apartments, this place is beautiful, very clean and the Staff is amazing. I love living here and the location is wonderful just down the street from the beautiful little town of Multnomah Village where there are amazing eateries and shops with a very small town feel just minutes away from downtown Portland.

The rooms are quite nice actually. The issue is a lack of proper security. Shady folks come in and out due to tenants handing out the code. Yes a code, the complex doesnt use fobs like every other rental complex ive seen, and there are no cameras to really track these people coming and going. Bikes were stolen. Cars were getting there gas tanks drilled into again recently out front which is awesome to worry about every night. Smells like meth is being sold and smoked on the 3rd floor at times. During the colder months you will be climbing over houseless people who have some how found a way into your hallway and small main area. There are a couple of tenants who are constantly fighting and throwing things around the aparment. About a year is gone now and nothing has really changed except a front door that actually closes and locks all the way. Good luck.

My husband and I have been living at Lower Burnside now for almost 2 years and I can't believe how lucky we got on our first place in Portland.  Our apartment is brand new, very well made, gorgeous wood floors, floor to ceiling windows, beautiful quartz countertops with solid wood open shelving system in the kitchen. We absolutely love the way we've made Lower Burnside our home and it's really all thanks to the awesome Management Team who make sure the property is always in it's best condition. (Thank you, Jessica, John, and Caleb!!)  They are always here for us and go above and beyond.  The building is not as big as other buildings in Portland so there is a close-knit sense of community - we have made life-long friends with some of our neighbors here.  John holds Friday night happy hours on the Skylounge, which are always fun and having the Skylounge with a grill, place to chill, and the East side's best view is such a huge bonus!  The location is as central as possible and so close to  some of the best restaurants in Portland.  Our favorite places to frequent in our neighborhood are:  Market of Choice and Sheridan Market (grocery stores), Modern Times (brewery), Enso (wine bar), J&M (breakfast), Thai Champa (fast food cart), Coava (coffee shop), Nicolas Restaurant, Century Bar (to watch games), and the list goes on and on.  I really can't say enough great things about Lower Burnside.  Oh, one last thing -- super dog-friendly building and close to a dog park.  We love it here :) Thanks again to the amazing Berkshire crew!

I've been here for about a year and they are nice apartments. The people who run the place are super friendly and they seem like they really try to work with you. For the price point, I couldn't really find anything better and I looked at a decent amount of places at the time. The living room, kitchen, and master bedroom are quite spacious and they come with a washer and dryer. The 2nd bedroom is quite small. There's a bus stop conveniently located just in front. I've also never heard any of my neighbors besides the front door closing; the walls seem pretty well insulated. Here are the things I don't like: 
1. There's no air-conditioning in my apartment, so you're required to use a portable air conditioner; they told me they don't allow window units either because of sliding windows and as a safety hazard. 
2. It's located on SE Division, which is a very busy street! Unfortunately, I'm near the front so it's quite loud to the point where I'll have to close the windows daily otherwise I can't hear anything but the traffic. It's quite annoying especially when it's really nice out. 
3. There isn't assigned parking. Sometimes when I come home late from work, especially a Saturday, I'll have to park near the other apartment buildings because they are full. Also a quick note, I've never seen the parking lot completely full so you shouldn't have to worry about parking on the street. 
4. The surrounding neighborhood is a little sketchy. A couple of months ago there were a couple of cars broken into on the next street, but as long as you stay within the parking lot and the apartments you're fine. The parking lot is very well lit.

I currently live at Tabor Pointe Apartments and Have lived there for about 7 months. So far I love these apartments, they have two spacious room and 2 bath rooms so my roommate and I have our own bathroom.  We have great washers and dryers in the apt,  And the best part is they have GAS stoves. That is what sold me on the place. We also have gas fire place but haven't used it yet. I think the only down fall is there isn't a whole of storage but we are making do. I really love this place I have lived at several apartments around town these are by far the best. No pets allowed and no smoking. No assigned parking but there are enough spaces for every apt to have one car. We close to a max stop so its convenient for my roommate who doesn't have a car. But the most important thing I think is the Manager is great very friendly and easy to talk to.

The interior of these apartments are nice but don't expect to have all the amenities working that they list. I've lived here less than 2 months and have a problem with my freezer. It's been over a month now and I'm still waiting for a fix. I asked to be compensated by having some money off of my rent and the owner said NO. . The managers are great people it's the greedy owner that is the issue. Also, the plumbing in these units are awful. You can hear each and every time your neighbor flushes the toilet. Fun times at 3am. Also, it lists A/C as an feature, only in the studios are there A/C. This is going to be a very long one year lease.

Mega, the on site property manager was AMAZING to work with.  So friendly, easy to work with and very responsive.  Lease was signed yesterday.  

Looking forward to meeting all the neighbors.

-Josh

Have been renting for over ten years. Over the years, managers changed, and now Diane is in charge. She is great! She has been the manager for several years now and is responsive and helpful when you need her. She cares and is professional. Maintenance team is quick to address issues too. A nice trail nearby for walks. Highly recommend.

Stayed here for 2 years and my time here was great. Diane at the front desk is amazing and responds so quickly to any maintenance issue or any questions you may have. The pool and gym were easily accessible and an added perk to the apartment. The property is well kept up; they always had people coming in and cleaning, mowing, etc.

I've lived at Sandstone Manor for almost a year now and I can't say enough about the management and the maintenance staff here.  While this may not be the most luxurious of apartments, I feel that the onsite managers and the maintenance staff more than make up for any lack of luxury.  Anytime that I've had a maintenance issue, it has been handled with lightening speed and always to my satisfaction.  In fact, my most recent issue was handled beyond my expectations.  Diane and Jan and Sergio are most pleasant to work with.  And I feel that they do a fine job of trying to make the property as nice as possible.  It is an old property and there's only so much you can do given budget restrictions, etc., but I always feel that they are doing their best.  I see some negative posts about this property, but I feel that these are from people who are looking for luxury living at an affordable price.  And that probably isn't going to happen in the City of Portland, unfortunately.  I've been very happy here so far, with the exception of some of the tenants who don't seem to know how to put their trash in the proper bins.  But that certainly isn't the fault of management unless they can convince the property owners to invest in some surveillance cameras to catch those who don't bother to read the signs.  But if they did that, I'm sure my rent would go up.  So I'll live with it.  All in all, this has been a great apartment and I hope to stay here until that day comes that I can afford that high end luxury apartment.  Or, better yet, buy my own house.

Recently viewed a one bedroom here and It's actually super clean and well maintained. Almost looks brand new inside! The only reason we won't apply is parking. You get one spot (free) but the lot only has 2 visitor parking and the street is pretty busy with another apartment complex and homes. Our two cars just won't work here.

We love it here, great little community.
Beautiful new apartments that you can be proud to show off!
It’s awful management is terrible. Don’t waste your money here it’s not worth it. You won’t be able to sleep or live here. You will never feel safe or at home.
They will give you no where to park then tow your car , management is incompetent and maintenance is slow and unresponsive. I would rather be homeless than live here.

Definitely the worst apartment I’ve lived in! 
I’ve dealt with violence, fighting neighbors pulling the fire alarms at 3am to disrespectful pet owners refusing to clean up after their pets…in the elevators and everywhere one would think. 
Catalytic converters are being stolen in “secured” parking ($160/month) with cameras and the management fails to even investigate. Parking is another story but if you want piece of mind, this isn’t the place. 
If you want to look over your shoulder when you leave your expensive apartment: this is the place for YEW!

This place is exactly what I needed, when I needed to move suddenly. All the staff have always been helpful and kind so it’s a shame people have reported otherwise. I’ve loved it here. 

With any apartment however there is the downside of sharing any space with others. Most of my poor experiences have been with other tenants, not staff. People slamming doors at 4:00 in the morning, letting their dogs poop in the walkways and not clean up after them, and on one occasion, one person making an accusation that I stole her package. I’m still confused by how she came to that conclusion, as I did not. 

If say the most negative thing about the complex itself is the parking situation. It’s out of control. I’m lucky enough to have a spot but I pay an insane amount for it every month. To a point where I would have rented elsewhere for a bit more if I would have known. 

Part of the problem, is that these are mostly studio apartments, that have more than one adult dwelling in a lot of them with multiple cars (as it was explained to me) and these units were just not built for that. It’s also not close enough to a transit station to justify not having a car for most people in my opinion. Again, this issue has been created by other tenants living here.

Otherwise I have enjoyed living here, and will continue to do so until I’m ready to move into a bigger place. I want to thank the staff for being so patient and kind with me, and always being so quick to be helpful when I’ve needed it.
Worst property management group. They are idiotic and do not care about their residents. completely useless staff!!

Management doesn’t have their things together. The manager gave false promises for holding an apartment and the interactions were rude, inconsistent, and rigid. Kept putting up road blocks for everything and not staying true to their words. Apartments may be nice but management is horrible.

I lived at Portland Towers for 10 years and it was a lovely experience. The location can't be beaten! Walking distance to NW 23rd, Washington Square Park, easy access to Hwy26 and so much more! If you're looking for a friendly neighborhood vibe with all the conveniences of city living this checks both those boxes. If you're new to Portland this is a great place to land and discover all the cool shops, pubs, and parks in the city. Plus, the paid parking option is super affordable and easy to navigate. The building interior is clean, the outside grounds well-maintained, and the rooftop is stunning! It was a great place to start my journey in Portland.

Fred Meyer, a Max station, a dozen restaurants, and banks all within a 5 minute walk.
 Safe, relatively quiet area yet you are right next to downtown.
 Friendly staff and neighbors.
 Thick walls. Haven't heard a neighbor once.
 Good internet. I'm getting 100  mbps down.
 Incredible view from the roof, and there is even a grill.
 Flat utility bills.

-Has some old building problems. Plumbing has been needing repairs and has been shut off multiple times. The shower controls are really finicky. Dishwasher doesn't work very well.
-Parking for guests can be very difficult if not nearly impossible if you don't have a temporary pass available, which you can't get while the office is closed.

With a Walkscore of 94, I assure you, the Portland Towers is a great place to live. Did I mention the view? The view of the Cascades, Mt. Hood, and the city at night is breathtaking. The spacious two bed, two bath I share with my lovely roommates could not be more fitting; the layout is perfect and the walls are thick, so you don't have to worry about hearing your neighbors. Bonus: You'll be able to enjoy the atmosphere of a Portland Timbers game from the convenience of your own apartment or on roof top without having to pay a penny!
Portland Towers is a great building in an excellent location.

So everything started out well. The prices were affordable. The interior was kept up with. We had a couple things fixed upon move-in, which they did pretty quickly. The neighbors were ok (for the area). We made it cute.

But then the pandemic escalated and so did the homelessness and crime. This area is huge on crime, ESPECIALLY CAR THEFT. Nowadays, you'll hear gunshots down the block every other night. A few weeks ago, a high speed chase ended in our complex where the guy ditched the car. Sirens are a common thing to hear. The restaurant behind our deck, next to Plaid Pantry currently houses multiple homeless people who smoke weed and are loud all throughout the day. Other people bring stolen cars in the back of the restaurant to part them out. We called the police multiple times when we moved in, but it got so bad that we just didn't call anymore.

You'll hear things outside your window in the middle of the night. Screeching tires, car races, arguments in the parking lot, gunshots, homeless people screaming, homeless blaring their stereos, homeless going through our dumpster and throwing things around, etc.

We finally had enough and moved out. While we were moving out, other residents noticed and told us they were moving as well.

So while the apartments are decent, the area is very scary and you are always worried about your car and the homeless people around you.

It's sad that it came to this. The apartments have a lot of potential... maybe some day...

The manager is very nice but she is really hard to get ahold of. The units look nice but are made of poor quality. I had my brothers car stolen from here and my boyfriends car broken into, both were completely different days. The location sucks because your only way out is Marine Dr and I always get stuck behind semis, but I tried looking past that. The maintenance guy is awful. He’s made my roommates and I feel bad multiple different times when we needed him because he “lives 2 hours away” and it is gonna take him a while to get there. Even during an urgent maintenance requirement he still tries to get you to schedule a time because he doesn’t wanna drive out here. I dealt with ants for about a month but that has died out. My neighbor upstairs dealt with dead flies everywhere. No idea why but thought I should put that in here. They have landscapers come here and however much water they use and whatever else it costs them to do maintenance on the outside, gets put into our rent which spikes up the water bill an insane amount. It’s not a terrible place but I just definitely would not recommend or renew a lease here.

The apartment itself is nice. However, the neighborhood is horrible. Homeless surrounds you and even the Sargent of Police for this area said the crime rate has skyrocketed. My sister was nearly car jacked right out on the same street as the apartment early in the morning. They charge you for everything. I paid less money for a house in California. Do what you will with this information.

If there were an option to give this place 0 stars, it would be rated 0 stars.

-management/maintenance never answer calls or texts.

-there is no a/c even though it is advertised.

-car was broken into, then roommates car stolen a week later.

-unfriendly neighbors.

-poor parking situation.

-very loud since it's next to the airport and road.

Would strongly recommend continuing your search for a good apartment, because this place is horrible.

Interested Renters beware - the apartments and location are nice, central and fixtures are new. Note that the fixtures are new because (regardless of damage) they will replace all fixtures and charge the tenant moving out for the cost. When the charges are disputed they will not engage, when legal recourse is sought they will send the full account to collections - no question. They require a cashiers check for last months rent, but then sent that amount to collections (likely knowing there’s no way to prove they cashed the cashiers check) - I strongly recommend interested renters look elsewhere.

Most of the residents at The Savona dont like the management, we have residents who clean up the sidewalks because management wont. The trash room have flies and maggots management solution put fly traps up and never change them. The homeless come and sleep in front of people’s doors and refuse to leave. The walls in the apartments are extremely thin, the washer and dryers are half size so a lot of people have to go to a laundromat. If you need to get into contact with property management good luck they will never answer and when you happen to see then at the property you dont even know its them but they act like they never missed a call.
Office group is so helpful and nice, made move in a breeze!

I've lived here two years now and each year they've increase the rent by the maximum allowed by the state without having to provide relocation expenses. This year, they offered a "discount" on the rent increase (still a 10% increase), if you signed a new lease. However, they sent incomplete lease documents and are currently refusing to provide completed documents to sign. The complex has a pool and hot tub, but because of Covid restrictions, they've only been available a fraction of the time I've lived here.

Beware getting a lower unit as well. There is virtually no soundproofing between upper and lower units...so you'll hear every step your upstairs neighbor takes.

I spent 3 years at Commons and it was not a great living experience. There is a lot of unwarranted activity being right off of Barnes Rd (cars being broke into, stabbings, shootings ect). Management is reluctant to invest in security cameras for public safety and it's really sad. So are the amenities. The complex has a pool and that's about it.

Our unit (#212) at one point had a leak in the ceiling that damaged my appliances, and it took over 2 months for management to fix the roof properly. Then when I finally moved out in April of 2022, they decided to take no responsibility for the leaking roof + damages,and instead charged me  $1200 dollars in cleaning fees and expenses to replacement a carpet that was 5 and a half years old. It's almost been 60 days now and I am still waiting for the rest of my $1700 dollar deposit.

Point being, do not move here. Property management only cares about collecting rents, not taking care of their community.

My roommate and I have lived at the Commons at Timber creek for just over two years. When we first signed our lease 2 years ago, the staff were very open and friendly, we got a good rate, etc. The grounds of the complex and pool area are lovely. It is conveniently located by the Timber Creek Shopping center too! After living there for two years I have seen the staff change countless times, they have become less friendly and helpful overtime, and the manager there isn't very friendly/helpful. The maintenance is quick at getting things done and responsive, but the quality of work is not great. We have had our washer and microwave replaced, our "new" washer is already acting up. I have had mold forming in my bathroom. When I wrote to them about the mold forming, all they did was clean it off and paint/plastered over it. It has since returned. We live on a bottom floor and the instillation is very poor in the summer and winter months, the temperatures are very extreme, the heaters do not help in the winter. And rent continues to go up there every year. Their office hours are not accommodating at all (9-6). Sometimes they don't open until 10 am because of meetings, it can be frustrating, especially if you need to get a package! I wouldn't recommend living here, unless you are in between places. We plan to move in the next few months. My recommendation to the staff there is to be more accommodating to your residents, we pay a lot of money to live there and the service and apartments aren't great.
We love this place, beautiful scenery, great area, and super friendly staff!

PROS AND CONS FROM A LONG TERM TENANT

I have lived here for five years. When I moved in I paid $750 for my small two bedroom one bath apt. Fast forward 5 years, I pay 1200.00. Same apartment, same paint, same carpet, same cabinets, same HORRIBLE tile job in the shower, same vinyl floors etc. etc. etc. When Tandem raised the rent here they said it was the going rate for the area. Not so much, the apartments across the street are $875 and the BRAND NEW townhouses across the way that people have bought and rented out are $950-$1000. 
Over the years The leasing office has gone through at least 7 managers and countless, I mean literally countless agents. The current agents and management is close to the best that have been here but Tandem pays them so little there is a lot of turn over. The maintenance is prompt and timely but the worst, half asked execution I have ever seen. Not to mention they are the grumpiest people in Portland. . The hot tub has been pumping cold water for 3 days now. None of the staff seem to care. They advised us they will be raising the rent again in 9 months after all the units are updated. Don't be fooled these places were built in 1973, they are not new. The "remodeled" units have new-ish carpet, basic white paint (not well done) and the cabinets have about 7 layers of paint on the. They just keep re-paintintg. The tubs and showers are so horribly done. Its like they were drunk when they tiled the whole area. I mean I have broken tiles that were clearly put up broken and caulked in like that is an okay thing.

On the upside the property (outside)is beautiful. There is a nice long creek with several bridges and walkways, the pool and hot tub are amazing, huge, and very nicely done. The pool area is brand new and again amazing. This is a huge complex with about 900 people living here, they estimate, so you blend in and no one is really in your business. There is more than adequate parking. The playground for kids is really nice and located in a good spot so I don't have to hear kids being kids. There are not any random cats or animals wondering around. The grounds are kept very clean. There is 24 hour maintenance, even if poorly done it helps in a jam. They are supposedly building a fitness center (been remodeling and old large laundry room for this fitness center for two years)

Not a great place to live, just a great pool and area of Portland
Absolutely horrible. Everything is always broken. Overpriced. Bad vibes. Break ins in parking garage. Thin walls. Management is never in the office. I do not recommend at all.

Multiple car break-ins inside "secure" parking garage. Key fobs have been stolen so access to building is not secure bringing a large problem of package theft that is ongoing. New management has not addressed this issue with the residents.

The building is in walking distance from downtown Portland. Most apartments have balconies, wich is pretty rare and our apartment also has a gas fireplace.The management is very nice and the entrance gives it a Melrose Place kinda feeling. I would very much recommend this building to others.
Absolutely the worst. Towing policy is no warning. Fire alarms go off at least once 1 week weed+cooking. Homeless make the area unsafe, orders stolen.

Living here has actually been pretty decent. There is a parking garage that costs $130 a month, which is a lot of money, but reasonable for the area. Recently, my car broke down. While in the shop, I got a loaner car from the dealership. On the back and sides, it has large decals stating the dealership that it’s from, and “Courtesy Loaner Vehicle”. Spoke with the leasing office that I would be parking it in my space, they said it wouldn’t be a problem. I came home to no car, to find it was towed by the towing company that the apartment contracts with. $339 tow bill, management not willing to help. Predatory tow company, sketchy management, wouldn’t recommend.
This website won’t let me go into specifics. But trust me, you don’t want to live here.
If you enjoy 24/7 break-in’s, constant suicides/deaths, drug dealers, syringes EVERYWHERE, sex in the elevators and SO MUCH more unsightly/hideous conditions, this is the place for you.

this building is located in the center of Oldtown/Chinatown. The apartment I currently occupy is the 5th floor. This particular apartment has wonderful views of the broadway bridge, and NW side of Portland. It's a very easy walk to both max lines, Gr/Yw & Rd/Bl, buses are easy to access as well. Burnside is a 7 min walk, so it the Portland Saturday Market. The bar scene and club scene is amazing. Perfect apartment for the night owl. I love this apartment.

If you love Portland then this is where you want to be! If you want to go into the heart of downtown just walk across the street and you are at the max line. If you want to relax and enjoy the pearl district or go to NW 23rd? Walk four blocks from the max and the street car stop is near by. The best part about this place is the water front. Just 2 minutes and you are there and you can just walk, run, or even ride your bike across the massive loop. The unwind on the rooftop patios enjoying the scenery that is Downtown Portland.
Awesome apartments to live in. One block from downtown St. John's. In bus line. Quite and respectful residents.
One of the best apartment I've lived so far. Clean, safe, and manager is always present to address concerns.

Creepy staff went to my unit when I was out of town and management didn’t bother to even notify me about it, so I came back from the trip and thought I was robbed initially because everything in my apartment was moved around. Maintenance guy would always follow me around and sprint over to me at speed to catch me in hallways so he can ask me irrelevant questions, not only I left the property because of that I also left Portland. I might make a movie about all the weird experiences I had living in this freaking apartment, there were just so many incidents… don’t move here if you are living alone.

I moved in in 2018 and lived at Glendoveer Woods Apartments for 4 years. We paid a total of 4,840 dollars in security deposit (730.00), pet deposit (750.00) and pet tent totaling $3,360. That is a grand total of $4,840. 

We got a refund of $155. Don’t live here.

We lived here over two years. The apartment complex staff, facilities, and neighbors were great. We were model renters and the maintenance guys sung our praises moving out. We moved here for better commute and decent rent despite sketchy neighborhood. 
Then they raised our rent every year . Two years in a row. We thought we would have money for Christmas from our security deposit. The. We found out they
Used our security deposit for all the maintenance work fees of the apartment - we only got less than 70$ from our just under $950 deposit. Wish we never moved here. Totally broke and when I tried to argue how ludicrous their fees were they called it “standard” aka money hungry practice. Do not live here and expect to get back any of your security deposit.
This complex is dirty and dingy. Nothing is upgraded. Crime is high. Repairs aren’t a priority.

Bad maintenence, bad management, bad drainage on the property which causes flooding in units every year, etc. Our apartment had heavy cigarette smoke damage from a previous tenant and they just painted over it on the walls, left the ceiling blackened by smoke with smoke filled insulation sticking out of holes. We never were able to get rid of the smell up until the flooding destroyed our and 50 other units. We were told by upstairs neighbors it happened every year for the past 7 years at least.

The carpet was already trashed when I moved in and I still got a massive bill when I moved out even though it was nicer and cleaner than when I moved in. I put in a work order and it took them three months to even see it. Mold everywhere. Honestly the most poorly kept apartment complex I’ve ever seen. Tons of police activity. I never ever felt safe living here. I would never recommend to anyone.

The apartment is in a beautiful location, it’s close to OHSU and is close to the freeway. There is also a plaid pantry and a Thai food place close by. While the apartment has its upsides, there are some issues that should be taken into consideration when looking at this apartment.
I love these apartments the view to the city is gorgeous. I love the trails and the insides to the apartments are pretty nice. Every one there is super nice. It feels very open and free.

This property has beautiful views also a wonderful trail to hike. Close to the college, so easy  commuting. Has a club house that feels like a home, with beautiful decor. Very quiet, away from busy streets.
