review: Talk about a ridiculous upcharge.  When a place lists itself as "pet friendly", that shouldn't mean there's a $50 add on to the rent every month for your pet.  That's not pet friendly. It's ridiculous.

apartmentName: Ascend Apartments: New Micro Studios and L...
review:
I’ve never been so displeased with an apartment complex before, considering I’ve been renting all my 20s and 30s. 
I should’ve not been so focused on the location because there were red flags I failed to consider when picking this place. 

Here are some red flags:

1) It was a hassel to even sign up for a lease/unit since the links on the main website didn’t work for me. I had to google search for the units to apply for even after making calls that I was interested but either got no response or management wasn’t accurate on their end. They kept sending me a link that didn’t work. 

2) I can’t say what they do for background checks on tenants here. I had 3 people living on my floor whom were doing drugs and stealing our packages back in November 2022.

3) The garage has been an ongoing issue. I like how they make you pay $200 for a parking spot in their limited twelve space garage with the main door not even closed, so securty for your vehicle is non-existant. Park in the alleywall for free if you don’t mind the first come first serve basis. 

4) Sometimes the garbage shoot isn’t active, for days at a time. Walk your garbage down or let it sit there by the shoot. 

5) Because the garage door is always open/not fixed, the bike storage rooms got broken into and bikes were stolen, including mine, and damage to a motor scooter. 

6) Key fobs to access other floors through the stairway don’t work. You can just open the door. Plus, because the garage door is open, anyone can walk in and take the stairs to your floor. 

7) Management is practically non-existant. I’ve called them the ghost staff because I’ve hardly heard back from them or no reply at all. Whenever I came to them with an issue face to face, they said they would work on it or send it to a higher person, and then I don’t hear anything. 

8) They forgot to apply their move-in special to my rent when I’ve asked about multuple tiomes. 

As you can see, I have may reasons why I dislike the property. There are a few good aspects to it such as location to a few good spots, and the loft style (with poor design). If you don’t mind all the points I’ve put across, then at least get GOOD renters insurance. 

Good luck…

From an unhappy tenant..

apartmentName: Ascend Apartments: New Micro Studios and L...
review:
I lived here from late 2021 to late 2022 in one of the lofted studios. I loved the way it was set up, it was perfect for one person, and I loved having the big window. As someone without a car, i love how close it is to bus lines, restaurants, groceries... that said, by far the most frustrating thing was the lack of A/C. In the winter it held heat so well; the hallways were heated and I rarely had to use my own heati because of how naturally warm the space kept itself. 
In the summer? It was horrendous. The hallways/lobby are cold, but the units were baking. I had 2 cooling fans that the heat just sucked the air right out of! Many neighbors and i would leave our front doors open to invite in some of the hallway air. As a disabled person, I physically can't withstand that kind of heat and most of June, July, and August I spent at a friend's house. It got so unbearable at one point that a neighbor of mine told me she'd actually saved up so she could buy out the rest of her lease and leave sooner! Global warming is not new and a place this new should 100% have AC. I stepped into my bathroom at one point and all my bar soaps had melted down the side of my shower! Showering was impossible, adding moisture into the air would then make the space incredibly humid as well

To add to this, the turnover rate in the front office made me uncomfortable. In the year I lived there, the front desk staffed changed a good 6 times, the service declining, it seemed, with every new person. I'm not by any means picky but it was irritating.
 I noticed a pattern of after the first 2 or 3 office people, the newer people stopped caring about the tenants as people (or were so stressed and over worked, they didn't have time). I emailed one person for a month with no answer until I finally was able to go to the office only to find she didn't even work there anymore and no one said anything. The office hours seemed sporadic and inconsistent. The newer people made it clear that having to stop and talk to tenants was not a priority and in fact started putting things in front of the office window so we couldn't see whether or not someone was inside! My partner went to ask them a question and said when she knocked, she literally saw the lights turn off and there was complete silence behind the door (during service hours, btw, not anywhere near closing time).
I was disappointed because I'd been so excited about this place, and again in the winter months and less warm days, it was lovely.

review: Wonderful unit, location, price and management! The best location in PDX.

I lived here back in 2021 when they were first open and they screwed me over when i moved out. they said i owe them 4500 just for ending my lease early. Save yourself and dont ever come here, Management sucks. very unresponsive and will lie to you

The management here does not care about the tenants. This  building is only 3 years old and falling apart. There are always fights in the hallways. The fire alarm goes off every month, if not more. Please do not move here.

Hampton Park apartments are very beautiful, they’re a safe and comfortable place to live. Managers are incredible as well as the maintenance team that they have. Very blessed to be here! This is the apartments you need in your life!!??????

We stayed almost 4 years here and experienced the best so far. Had to move out due to Transfer in Job Location. Got lucky the whole period we stayed. The memorable one for life, as we gave birth to both of our kids. Friendly management people, who provide services in time and try to listen to you requirements and act accordingly. Close to Walmart, Costco, Winco and Fred meyers. Definitely recommend this place to stay.
Nice community with great apartment units. Maintained well and Very responsive management. Department stores at walkable distance. Located at the junction of 217 and I5. Loved staying here ??
We have been living here for two years now and have not had a problem with the apartment. It would use updated appliances. When and if we do need something fixed it is done quickly.

I have lived at Hampton Park Apartments for a very long time.  I am very happy here.  The grounds are well kept, the community is safe, and residents are respectful and kind.  HP is conveniently located near freeways, grocery stores, a movie theatre and more.  My apartment is large, well-appointed (dishwasher, disposal, washer and dryer in unit), there is dedicated parking, and the community is very quiet.  Management has been very attentive and any repairs have always been made promptly and done right the first time.  I feel very fortunate to have found such a great place to live.

Here are the pros: The apartments are clean and well kept as are the grounds.  It's in a great location (walkable Fred Meyer, Walmart, movie theater, and restaurants) and close to major freeways.  The office staff is friendly and regular maintenance is timely and efficient.  There are some good amenities (washer and dryer, small rec room, seasonal pool etc.). No smoking is allowed on the grounds (which may be a con if you smoke, but as a non-smoker I found it refreshing).

Here are the cons: Parking is limited (you get one guaranteed spot but if you have two cars it can be annoying to find parking). The office hours are limited to a regular work schedule so if you work a M-F/9-5 job it could be a hassle to speak to the office for any issues.  While the regular M-F/9-5 maintenance guy is fantastic, I personally have not had good luck with the after-hours maintenance company (of the two times I called, one time they never picked up and the other time they said they sent someone but the person never showed).  The rec room is very small (one treadmill, one elliptical, and one weight machine)- I still appreciate and use it but felt like it was falsely advertised as a "gym" when we first moved in.

Overall, this apartment is worth the money.  Our 2.5 years here have been good and we've had good experiences with the management team.

I've lived here for a few years now, the apartments themselves have the usual issues that come with old buildings that aren't properly maintained: bad insulation, no AC, poor sound dampening, etc. But you can visit and see if those issues matter to you, for me, they didn't.

But the issue that you can't learn about until you live here is how the management is. Well, it's equally poor. They forget about issues you make them aware of and they try to squeeze you for as much money as they can. Heck, they just told me they want to raise the rent by $150 ... on Thanksgiving. What a way to enjoy the holidays.

"Pay us more to live at a place getting progressively worse. Happy holidays."

My wife and I have lived here for several years.  The community is quiet and safe.  We love walking around the neighborhood. The apartment is older and needs updating.  Our biggest issue is with the windows.  They are old and need replacing because some of them don't seal completely.  For other issues, we have always been able to get help from the maintenance team.  Nate is always kind, respectful, knowledgeable and dependable.  I know that if something comes up, Nate and his team will be able to take care of it.  Overall, the value is good which is my we have stayed here for several years instead of moving to other apartments in the area.
It can be challenging to find the right apartment home for people with pets and I found the staff at Westlake Meadows to be very friendly and welcoming.

4 dollars for a single load of laundry in a room that has a sunken in floor so the washer is literally tilted. 
RATS. 
Very limited parking no surplus option. 
Dumpster is a disabled persons nightmare, I’m talking steep lids and slippery mud all around the base literal flood zone when it rains.

I’ve lived at The York for a little over a year now and here is my (long) honest review and things I wished I knew:

1.  The water bill for a 2 bd/1ba is around  ** $140/month for two people in a 900 sq ft unit ** .  A 3rd party takes the entire water usage for the complex, “takes some off the top for landscaping and the laundry facilities”, then divides up the remainder based on the amount of registered people and sqft of each unit.  Most complexes charge anywhere from $0-$80, so this is an insane amount to be paying for water, and I really wish I had known!!

2.  Be prepared for some seriously poor maintenance.  It takes weeks for them to come, and you are lucky if they actually fix things well.  When they repaired our leaking bathroom ceiling they left the new bathroom fan attached with duct tape and never came back to finish it.  It stayed like that for months before we realized it wasn’t even working because our bathroom was growing mold. When they came back they fixed 75% of the repairs we asked about, and said they would be back soon for the rest.  They didn’t return for a week and a half so I expressed my frustration with the property manager, and she scheduled them to come the next day at 2:15pm.  The day they were coming we found a mouse in our unit and I texted her to send them ASAP.  No reply.  I sent two more texts throughout the day  - no reply & no show from maintenance.  The following day I threatened to call a pest control service myself and deduct it from rent. I got an immediate response  and was told that the property manager was out sick (so whoever had access to the messages just decided to ignore them).   By the end of the week the mouse issue was resolved, and they said they would be back for the other repairs.  Again, it took them a week and a half to come back, and only came because I reached out, again. This is a common theme.  When I try to talk to Trion about these issues they have short-term solutions and focus only on getting one issue fixed as opposed to hire more people for the maintenance team, or give them more billable hours

Lastly:  There are 50+ units, one dumpster for garbage, and four small trash cans for recycling.  Trash is overflowing by the end of the week, and the recycling bins fill as soon as they get emptied.   Parking is a nightmare for guests.  You get one parking pass per unit, but there are only 10 (maybe) guest spots, and almost guaranteed to be full.

It looks so much better then it did when my husband and I moved in. It seems that the empty apartments got fixed up really nice inside. And the manager on site has great communication he always keeps us informed. The workers on site are very friendly and very helpful. I personally think the rent is good for how fixed up they made the place. Anyways if I were you I would rent. Winco and Walmart are 5 min drives away and so is the dollar store.

Trust me as I have lived here through old management and now new. No one likes new management just do not rent this apartment it's not worth the cost. Pictures do not show or represent inside apartments

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review:
STAY AWAY FROM THIS NIGHTMARE PROPERTY!

Raised rent during height of pandemic and cut amenities.

We were denied our security deposit AND billed over $1000 to replace a floor that we received damaged by the previous tenant and their cat. 

It's also $600 to repaint a unit if you live in any unit less than 18 months. So don't plan on signing just a one year lease and definitely don't hang any pictures on the wall. THEY WILL NOT TELL YOU THIS WHEN YOU SIGN YOUR LEASE. 

Management is rude, cold, and terrible at following up on even the most basic requests. 

Mold. Lots of it, and the Ridge will deny it's existence. 

There were so many breaches in Landlord-Tenant law when we lived here. Trust me, it's much better a-n-y-w-h-e-r-e  else. Run.

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review: Apartments overrun with animals scratching at walls constantly, owners do nothing about it. Do not move in unless you like constant scratching.

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review: Shortly after moving in heard scratching. Informed management, assured me they knew about it and were taking care of it. 9 months later I’m inhaling typhus listening to a heard of rodents scratching in the walls

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review:
You can do better.
1: The management told me when I moved in that there would be washer/dryers put into the units end of March. It is now almost May and nothing has happened. Also, they said they would be switching to an online payment method in March. This also hasn't happened.
2: I had a coupe of maintenance issues. I never once heard if they had been resolved, or what occurred after they checked out the problems. At my old apartment, we ALWAYS got a summary about what was checked, and how they fixed it, or if some kind of part needed to be ordered. Here, it's like I have no clue if anybody even took the time to look at my maintenance request. 
3. If you live on the bottom floor, you will hear EVERYTHING above you. Literally every move the human above you is making, or even their cat. It's insane. 
4. For the price, this place badly needs all kinds of updates: cabinets, appliances, the whole bit.
5. It's pretty obvious the management company only cares about making a profit, and not really much goes into the residents. It's a lovely place with a lot of potential, but the management is just very very sub-par.

From my previous place, having good management makes a HUGE difference in where you live. I would not recommend this place to someone looking for a new apartment. You can do better, especially for the price.
To the management: learn to keep your word, and invest more into the place. Your residents will be happier and in turn, will recommend this place to others (and not write bad reviews online).

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review:
The Ridge at Mountain Park bills itself as an "upscale" Lake Oswego community but it's barely a hangnail on the foot of the actual city of Lake Oswego. This complex has zero community feel. Most residents are standoffish and keep to themselves. Its also billed as a "smoke free" complex. However, the grounds are scattered with cigarette butts and the noxious odor of second hand tobacco and/or marijuana smoke was almost always present. The management are the typical misrepresenting sales-focused type and are often nowhere to be found despite the posted office hours.

The units are very run down and in desperate need of total renovation. We wasted over $1000/year on our energy bill due to severely poor window & door flashing and the spent/useless insulation allowing cold winter air to blow into the apartment even with the windows and doors closed.

The unit was rented to us with filthy window screens, window sills full of dead bugs, dirt and grime and a sliding glass door track that looked like it hadn't been cleaned in months. Typical false claims of damages in order to confiscate our security deposit seems to be the normal business procedure with Ridge staff.

I brought many of these issues up to the inept and perpetually annoyed maintenance guy during their laughable semiannual maintenance check. His idea of maintenance was talking his way out of the problems by explaining how there was nothing that could be done about the issues. When we moved in, none of the bedroom outlets were controlled by the light switch so we had to walk through the dark room fumbling around with the lamp anytime we wanted to have light. He tried and failed to fix this annoying problem 4 times before I stopped bothering to ask him about it. We lived with that inconvenience for over a year. Quality maintenance? Obviously not.

Despite all of these known issues, our unit was declared an "upgraded" unit simply because of a flimsy 12 inch track lighting stuck in the entry & kitchen and some stick-on faux granite laminate that was sloppily slapped on the kitchen and bathroom counters that had sharp hastily cut edges left on them. Talk about capitalizing on some tricks of the trade.

The miniature water heater insured that we regularly ran out of hot water before 2 people could complete their showers. Not a pleasant experience especially in the winter. Speaking of water, be prepared to shell out nearly $100 per month on top of the quoted rent just for the privilege of having water.

apartmentName: The Ridge at Mountain Park Apartments
review:
Lived here many years. Nothing compares to the great area. Natural trails- views, great schools, recreation center (literally next door). Safe, fire places. 
Basic apartments. Great maintanance and nice managment. They are on the ball with repairs. 
Rent increases are the killer.
Been here for a few months and can’t complain. Great views. Good management and good maintenance staff. Wish I found sooner

Those other reviews are fake. It's an awful place to live. Trains blowing their horns and squealing their brakes all night long. The management is so awful it's almost nonexistent. There's frequently barf in the elevators and kids run up and down the hallways all day and night and it sounds like a herd of rhinos.

My one bedroom should be listed as a studio. The two bedrooms are better but the second bedroom is closet-sized. New managers (as of July) I am not impressed with as when you go into office, you're not greeted -- they just sit there and don't respond when you state your business!

The good? Nice location and neighbors. Janitor staff is good. The bad? Elevators are filthy even though they are cleaned weekly. No amenities except small lending library. Parking is also a major problem.

I have lived here for more than once. They are great apartments especially for the price and the convient location downtown. I love living here and although the complex could use a few more amenities, there is a reason why I came back here. The management is friendly and willing to accommodate your needs as well as fix issues that may arise.

I live In ester short commons and I live In a second floor there's 4 levels. There's restaurants and farmers Market there Is a New Waterfront  with  New Thanks to do. They have concerts and Movie's and  the Hawaiian day and more.

I really enjoy living at my building, and have lived there for about 5 or 6 years now. I have a lovely view overlooking the most popular community park, and a great balcony to enjoy the outdoors during nicer weather. I do wish that the building didn't have such a high turnover of staff. For years, it was well maintained and always clean, but now the new management doesn't seem to be as meticulous about cleanliness. I also wish that you could receive tenant improvements just like any other new tenant that moves in. I still have old flooring and counter tops and have lived here for quite some time, while a brand new tenant is receiving upgrades and improvements and we're still paying the same price.
This building is falling apart. The residents are on month-to-month while waiting for plans on demolishing the building.

You get exactly what you pay for at this apartment: a Small apartment close to the city with good freeway access. I work nights and usually have no problem sleeping during the day. Neighbors are mostly quite and respectful. Parking can be tight.

The apartment itself was fine. My upstairs neighbors stomping overhead without let up for a solid year was not. We contacted the office at least once a month in spite of their continuous promises to do something about it. The guy upstairs even hit my car and all management did was give me a video with the actual part of him hitting my car conveniently clipped out. Toward the end of our lease, they gave up even pretending they were trying to help. An agent texted to tell me I would have to provide video proof before they would do anything. They were on the spot to let us know they were going to raise our rent, though. We decided to find another place instead.
My family and I lived here for 2 years. Not a great area to raise your children. 2 drive by shootings had us packing up and heading South. The managers were nice and tried to stay on top of things.

It's nice on inside of a parents . the management is changing so alot of new things and rent increases going on . I really liked the two male managers I had when I first moved in they responded to my maintenance phone calls and emails very promptly. I got in very quick and promptly they have cameras and patrol units that come through and its permit parking I really like that I can sit on my balcony and watch my son play in the play area.

Apartment overall is pretty lovely! Really enjoyed the newer appliances, location and overall vibe of the spot. The only downside.. Walls are stupid thin. Like word for word can be heard and you are both the noisy loud neighbor to each other. The inner studio units are L shaped with the bottom ends sharing a wall. The bedroom wall to be precise..

Unprofessional management that will yell at you if you inquire about your rent amount being incorrect, stalking you outside while your letting your dog out, and will will tell you you can only email them (because they don't deal with issues, just give a generic response) and still doesn't get back to you. I've tried to address my concerns and Jennifer ignores them. They are rude, uninviting and do not let her fool you. They only want money and do not care for tenants which is why they have jobs. Both of our brand new cars got broken into and damaged and the area is a lot worse. Theres a reason why the specials are soooo great. Still live here, and can't wait to move. I feel so unsafe and uncomfortable. I don't leave my apartment and I don't go for walks at night. Parking is non existent in evening.

I just moved into The Cordelia and I've been blown away at how kind and helpful the staff has been. Since I'm starting over without any furniture, and it's just me, large deliveries and endless Amazon orders have been a bit of a stressor. When I bought a couch online and the company couldn't change the delivery time to fit my schedule, Jennifer and Ashley came to my rescue.

They were exceptionally flexible, allowing a humongous piece of furniture to take up part of their office for a few hours while I sorted things out at work. Then, when I arrived and realized there was no way I could move it by myself, a very kind person from their maintenance crew helped me load it onto a dolly and maneuver into the elevator and then into my apartment. 

This move could've been really difficult, but the staff here have helped and supported me at every turn. This has been the best move-in experience I've ever had. I highly recommend these apartments to anyone looking for a beautiful space with a friendly community.

My boyfriend and I couldn’t be happier with The Cordelia. Jennifer in particular has been such a life saver in making our move-in process go smoothly. She has been incredibly communicative and prompt and has gone above and beyond to make sure that everything went seamlessly. We can’t recommend them enough!

Current tenant unfortunately, there’s been several changes in management, the management is VERY neglectful about consistent issues occurring in the apartments, maintenance is TERRIBLE takes them forever to come do a single task (currently waiting on dw to be fixed it’s been a month), they allow homeless people to camp in their cars on the street where they’re free to use and do whatever else they please. Security? Oh they’re NEVER around. Overall sad terrible place and a joke to say the least

The manager is very helpful and quick to fix things. The playground was always well-maintained and clean for the kids and I always seem to be an open parking spot. The inside of the apartment was beautiful and I had wonderful Neighbors
I've lived here for 3 years, and never personally had a problem. Manager Christine is really nice and accommodates needs when asked.

We love it here so much! We are the first ones to live in our unit since we moved in on March 2021. The 2 bedroom unit is super spacious. The leasing staff has always been very accommodating and helpful. Abby made the move in process so seamless and speedy!

Los, Breeze, Lost Brazes, What is it again? Sounds like a Tropical Islands. I told my friends whom asked What is the name again ? ",  Las, Like Lost  , Breezes Brisas. They replied OH>>>>>>Everyone Laughingly , Agreed .Our Apartments sound like a Vacation Oasis. And it is a beautiful well groomed Property. Lawns are manicured to profection. We have 2 Spacious  Bedrooms a master and 2nd bedroom. with bathroom off master bedroom, and 2 full bathroom the Livingroom and Kitchen are joined in a rectangle shape. for easy access. Always and beautiful fireplace at the flip of a switch for instant electrical illuminating heat !!!.We have plenty of storage space in and outside on the patio deck . There is plenty of Closet space as well. Yes, this is our Private parking Oasis. If I close my eyes I can almost see the waves crashing in on the Beach. Why not come to Las, Brisas Apartments for your Oasis Vacation of a life time.
Great location, but the cider bar downstairs can be a little loud on week nights.

I haven't slept in 6 months. Do not move here if you work nights. It's a literal construction zone all the time. I'm listening to jackhammers and the beeping of large machines from 730 am on. The maintenance will start vacuuming at 8am, or start yelling across the building. I'm very close to moving and I've lived here 6 months. The person next door moved already and he moved in 2 months after me. It's hard to live here.

Old carpet, ugly linoleum, leaky pipes, rusty water. The whole place is a miss-match of generic, low-quality, old/very used and worn materials. They try to pass off "vintage charm" as a reason to never put profits back in to the building. It's not at all updated. Hallways always smell horrible. It says no smoking, but people do smoke in there units and the smell spreads to other units. Only one, small washer and dryer for the whole building, eats quarters, waste of money. Three flight walk-up, no elevator. No lobby and no management on site, so package delivery cannot get in the building (no Amazon, no UPS, no FEDEX delivery). No free parking. It's all street parking, pay to park, or move your car every two hours. The city no longer issues parking permits for that zone. The lower level, front side is a soccer bar. Drunk people constantly drinking, loud partying, smoking right in front of the apartment main entrance. The bar also has speakers outside that blast crappy, loud sports and/or music. You can here the bar through the apartment floor, and it doesn't close til 2am, good-luck sleeping at normal hours. The back of the building (street-level) is rented out to anyone that needs garage space. Last tenant down there was a pay-to-ride scooter company that went bankrupt. They built all the scooters in the garage, it was sooo loud. Before them it was a printing press. Large, loud machinery at all hours of the night. The apartment floors are way too thin, and not at all insulated. apartment was not cleaned prior to move in. There's no office and no one to contact for help. The building has changed hands three times in the last six months. They ought to just tear it down and build condos already.

I did a good amount of research when moving to Portland many years ago and found this place to be one of the best. Unfortunately most of what made this place stand out is long gone. In fact you may find your stay here incredibly miserable unless you can deal with the issues this building is currently facing.

NOISE - Nonstop traffic coming off freeway, including emergency vehicles at all times. Also a popular road for street racing, you cant go more than 30 minutes without the sound a modded out farting car roll by. Sometimes just to terrorize residents the streetracers hang out in the parking lot late at night blasting music and revving engines. Unless you are a very deep sleeper, don’t expect to get a good nights rest living in the South & East facing apartments.

UTILITIES - The great value these apartments were took a nosedive when the building switched to ratio utility billing (RUBS) in 2019. Previously, all utilities came at a flat $159/month charge. The utility bill amount now changes every month, and can reach outrageous values over $265/month in summer & winter. The units have old appliances, and the single pane windows do nothing for energy savings. The new average utility bill is just over $210/month, breakdown is $60 Electricity, $45 Gas, $12 Garbage, $93 Water/Sewer. Not only do residents pay all utilities, they also pay extra for every load of laundry, $3.50 to wash & dry.

The building having AC is just a plain lie. The units facing West & South get bombarded by sun all day, and are much hotter than the rest of building. These apartments easily reach over 90 degrees, a potentially dangerous situation for people sensitive to heat. Due to the masonry walls, the building soaks up heat all day and releases at night, making it so the apartment never cools below 78 degrees in the summer even when its 60 degrees outside at night.  

While this review may come off all negative its only because I know how great this building can be. Plenty of residents are happy here and I hope it can return some of its former glory.

The apartments are great, love it here.
But be aware the homeless population is
Starting to take a toll. The foot traffic thru the property is constant. Management is awesome just have a lot to deal with!!
Very spacious units, large closets and balcony. Not much to complain about!

The rent is very reasonable for the location and quality of apartment. Utilities are a set payment so you also do not have to worry about high utility bills. The only main down side is that the majority of the complex is senior/retiree. I would guess about 1/3-1/2 of the residents are over 50, which makes relating to other residents a little bit of a challenge.

We were going to be moving into one of these units, but decided to back out and forego our deposit after actually seeing it in person because it was THAT BAD. It smelled bad, there was no patio due to the construction they were doing to the unit above. It was extremely dark and drafty, there were gaps in the walls between the fixtures, only one sink instead of two, no carpet in the main room and to top it all off there was a surprise street-facing door directly from the sidewalk outside into one of the bedrooms. 

Do not waste your money or time on Powell Court.
the apartment I live in is no good for my son there is a lot of drug dealing and bad things in the apartment and the location

Month to month rate offered can be $400 over fixed term lease, which can make moving out more difficult, because you only have a chance to move out once per year without a large lease break fee.

Move out cleaning form specifies $10 per slat on blinds if you don't clean the blinds properly.  With 20  slats and 7 blinds, that's over $1750 to clean your blinds if they actually follow through with that charge.   

My recommendation is to take pictures of absolutely everything at move in and at move out with timestamp available on photo.

They use a large amount of imodocloprine here on the rhodendrons.

Can be a bit noisy sometimes if you don't like very old heater / boiler systems that tend to clang every once in awhile.

Now that all being said, the grounds are immaculate, you get a storage unit in the basement included in rent, and the maintenance person (Sam) is fantastic.  One bedroom units are very spacious, and has tons of closet space.  You can get a garage for $150 / month, which is nice to have the option.  Obviously location is great if you are looking to be close into the city center.

Beautiful property in the heart of north Portland. Super convenient to i5, and countless walkable amenities. Well maintained with a great community of other tenants, this would be a perfect spot for a young professional or a small family.

This place is great.  The spaces all have updated kitchens and new washer and dryer that’s shared.  There’s a shared bike garage, and the only utility tenants pay for is electricity. 

Great location with awesome older character.

This complex is such a gem!  I moved in about 6 years ago, and I’ve never had issues.

The landlord is responsive, fastidious and kind.  There are only 6 units, which fosters a quiet atmosphere with the opportunity for friendly connection with our neighbors.

The green space in front and back is a bonus, as well as the basement and free laundry.

I couldn’t recommend it more, just be prepared for someone knocking on your door with extra muffins!

I have lived here in almost 3 years.  The parking is horrible especially after 9 pm.  It's really difficult to find any space to park.    Because of this, sometimes I need to park on the street.  Our rent keep going up every single year ($50).  Also recently the dumpsters are often full and a lot of trash on the ground.  Some of my neighbors have issue with ants and mold.  I don't have any issue with ants because I have been using "ant killer spray" around door and windows by myself every 6 months.

Good things I can think are--(1) Maintenance clues are friendly and they take care of issues quickly; (2) The location is very close to Clackamas Town Center. (3) Max station and bus stops are within walking distance.   (4) I don't have any noise issue with my neighbors.

Great apartment complex on a beautiful property. Management is great and very helpful; maintenance requests are done in a very timely fashion. The only problem with this complex is the surrounding area which has almost no parking and a small crime problem. Regardless if you want to live near the Clackamas Town Center this is the best complex in the area.

Overlook Pointe apartments come well equipped with washer/dryer, oven, dishwasher (essential } and fridge.
The surrounding  common grounds are nicely landscaped, kept clean and tidy and are well maintained regularly.
Great facilities include large outside swimming pool with loungers in summer,  all year round large outside bubbling  hot tub, gym and basketball  court.
Management are courteous, friendly and helpful.
 
There is all you need to make life easy and comfortable for you  with a large shopping mall, 10 screen cinema, a variety or good restaurants, public train/ bus  services all just a stones throw away. So come join our friendly community and enjoy life.

Great environment; close to all destinations around Portland.
The community has affordable price with great feature in compare with other apartments in same area. Friendly and smoke free community.

Staff’s only response to issues is a smile agreement that it is a horrible situation and that they have no control over anything. 

My car was broken into twice in 3 months in the locked and secured parking garage. Other vehicles have also been broken into, and over 15 bikes have been damaged or stolen due to frequent vandalism. Elevators often appear as if damage is being done to them regularly. Staff told me safety was my responsibility as a resident not theirs. 

Towel rack fell off wall with one hand towel on it a couple weeks after moving in.

A month later my blinds broke.

The washing machine doesn’t drain all the way and never did.

Mask wearing is optional for staff and residents. Although they do have that one sign posted that says pleas wear a mask.

Lots of noise on Mississippi from traffic and people who are mentally ill and have no where to go. Oregon just doesn’t have resources for them.

Construction started shortly after I moved in (of course it wasn’t disclosed) and went on for months. On the upside if you are moving in now there isn’t any excuse for lobby construction it was just finished recently.

Paying a large fee to break my lease and move on.

Extremely disappointed since I lived at a Holland Apartment complex for three years in the past and had a wonderful experience, but I won’t rent from them in the future.  I think they must have changed some of their policies or treatment of their staff.

Having been recently relocated for work I was limited in the time frame in which I was able to select a new apartment. Scout did a tremendous job in showing me around the property and had a great candid approach since I was unfamiliar with the area. She was clear and concise with the information I requested and although I wasn't able to select this property initially due to my commute; I will certainly be revisiting this property in the near future.
Have lived here since June 2015 and it's been great! Great location--shops, bars and restaurants, awesome staff and nice property. Bonuses: parking, dog friendly and in unit laundry!

We just moved in a month ago and absolutely love it! The apartment staff was so helpful with organizing our move and making it super smooth. Scout was so helpful in showing us the unit multiple times before we finally committed to leasing! The location can’t be beat, right in the heart of Mississippi walking distance to tons of bars and restaurants! No complaints here :)

I have lived here for a few months and am pleased! Maintenance is handled within 24 hours. The staff always goes the extra mile! There has been 2 events for residents since I’ve been here which is awesome. I’ve gotten to mingle with neighbors, I probably wouldn’t otherwise meet. 

Overall, I’ve been happy and am excited for the year to come!

So far, this new apartment has been great.  Its right in the heart of Mississippi Ave and very close to "Por Que No" where they serve probably the best tacos in Portland.  Really the perfect place to live if you're really into tacos, its probably only a 5 minute walk. Although there's always a huge line so it's best to get there kinda early. I still haven't been yet but I'm sure I will soon.  Can't wait! 

My apartment has big windows, high ceilings, lots of light and nice neighbors which is pretty much the exact opposite of my last place, so I'm glad I'm here now. Wish they had a ping pong table in the ecolounge though.. than I'd have to give this place SIX stars!

We've lived at the Maestro for close to a year now.  While the building itself if pretty and some of the views are great, the management is a mess, and the amenities continue to decline.  

Recycling must be taken down to the (overflowing) basement now instead of left in the garbage rooms on each floor, the elevators are continually breaking, the amenities (gym, game room) are only open 8:00 - 6:00 daily, which obviously makes them useless to someone with a "normal" job, walls are thin (this was always a problem), and maintenance sometimes takes WEEKS to respond to issues.  When these issues are brought to the attention of the property/leasing managers, nothing is every done other than a half-hearted apology.  

For claiming they are a Class A apartment building (and charging rent accordingly), they are doing a very poor job of providing enough value to make sense to continue renting here, considering the number of alternative properties in the neighborhood.

I recently toured Maestro and Fell in-love! The amount amazing spaces in the building to just get out of your home, not that you want to leave the Beautiful apartment! They have an awesome rooftop with the best view of the city sky-line, a massive 24 hr gym, coffee shop & work pod station area, game room and club room! The staff was so sweet too. I cant wait till my lease ends!

This place is aesthetically beautiful and draws you in with the premise of being new with beautiful finishes. Unfortunately regardless of how nice the appliances, finishes or AC is.... the building is very cheaply made. The walls are so thin, you hear every toilet flush, every shower had nearby, and everyone walking up and down the hallway. Worst part, I can hear my neighbors word for word, every phone call, every, “hey Alexa” every social gathering. Considering this bridling is brand new, and the overpriced high rent this place charges it’s 1000% not worth it to constantly be woken and bothered by neighboring noise, not mention the lack of privacy each resident has. Wanted to love this place, but not even a month in and I can’t wait to get out. Save yourself the money and literal headache.
There is no air conditioning, and the parking is limited.

I read the five star review on here, and laughed audibly. First of all, the manager is great. Truly. She's responsive, and she cares. That matters. I lived here when it was Aura Burnside (July '18 - Aug '20). I was in a 1-bedroom unit on the 6th floor.

Pros
-Location. It's at the center of the city grid with easy access to I5.
-Unit amenities. Mid-range appliances, commercial-style sink, in-unit washer/dryer (small stacked, but still), air conditoning.
-Underground parking. However, it was expensive compared to similar properties ($125-200/m during my time), and there was a waiting list since there were fewer spots than resident vehicles.
-Great access to public transit.
-The rooftop patio was nice. However, it was only a small corner, so it regularly got crowded in the summer and could not be reserved.
-The community room on the 2nd floor was great for having friends over. But 1) there was a reservation/cleaning fee to get exclusive use (it varied from $25-200+ during my stay) and 2) the windows to the hall were NOT insulated. Expect to get noise complaints from that hallway if you're watching an exciting sporting event.
-Sound insulation in walls between units was good.
-Lots of convenient businesses within 2-3 blocks (bakery, coffee shops, bars, etc.).

Cons
-There were three management companies during my two years there.
-No fitness center, pool, hot tub, etc.
-No great parking options for guests. Free parking within 3-4 blocks was usually full until late evening, and metered started early in the morning.
-The downtown location (and some of the more aggressive clientele of the nearby Plaid Pantry) made some guests uncomfortable leaving late at night.
-Rush hour traffic on the surrounding blocks is rough.
-Door/hallway insulation is basically non-existent.
-In the spring of 2020, someone stole a bunch of bikes from the bike rooms, and management had the thieves on security footage. However, they chose not to notify residents for legal liability reasons. I noticed mine missing a month later when I planned to go for a ride. The police said several other residents reported similar experiences.
-There were ongoing issues with the elevators, the underground parking garage door, and the street door fob system the whole time I lived here.
-The parcel locker bank in the basement wasn't nearly large enough for the number of residents. Packages were commonly left on the floor there, in the mail room, and in hallways. Based on the resident portal, theft seemed somewhat common.

Overall, it's a decent place to live, but location is really the only major benefit over other properties in the same tier.
