Not pleased.

I've lived here for a year, and it's been exhausting to say the least. Unless you enjoy hearing a shooting in your same building in the middle of the night, dont bother. Maintenance is pretty horrible, our dishwasher has been broken almost the whole time we've been here, and the three times we've called about it, they'll come in and fiddle with stuff, tell us it's fine, and just to run it on a rinse only cycle every week, and apparently it's because they didnt install the hoses correctly so the nasty dish-water gets sucked back into the dishwasher, and causes horrible smells in the apartment. It's also caused quite a few flood problems in our apartment. our first day moving in it smelled like an old hotel and come to find out they dont clean the air ducts, just the filters! The water heater in our closet always leaks, and when we asked maintenance about the wierd puddle of orange water in our closet, they said it's normal. Thought this place was amazing since new property management but things aren’t always as they appear. I really wanted to love these apartments but it has been a let down.  *For reference, I live in one of the mid size 1 bedrooms at this location*. “Upgraded flooring” = new laminate over concrete.  “Massive, sparkling pool” = the swimming pool area might be large but the actual pool is small. Pool didn’t even open until august this year because it didn’t meet health inspection regulations in June and July. *facts provided by salt lake county health department*.  “Breakfast bars & pantries”+”chef’s kitchen” = no pantry, a square hole cut out of the wall. New appliances look nice but are cheap. Fridge leaks cold air from the door seals, oven range shorted out in 4 months, smoke alarm put right next to stove will go off every time you open your hot oven. EVERY TIME.  “Upgraded fitness center” = looks BEAUTIFUL but  all of the cardio equipment squeaks horrendously.   To sum the rest up.....  dog park is disgusting most of the time due to tenants not picking up.  Half of the grounds are flooded due to poor drainage.  Weather stripping on doorways are nonexistent and windows let in unwanted air so winter will get really expensive trying to heat. Walls are extremely thin so you will hear everything from all your neighbors.  Air filters get changed but ducts do not get cleaned so apartment smells like old hotel and gets really dusty when using AC or heat. Police are in the complex often for various reasons. No benefits for long term residents... price increases with every lease renewal.  Wall and trim paint wear down in less than a year if you clean regularly.  I could go on but I won’t because this review is already exhaustingly lengthy.  Just be cautious, don’t let the website or clubhouse fool you.

My girlfriend lived here for a year. I moved down and tried to get a new apartment compared to the one she had. I field out the app threw down $300 on a deposit to hold the apartment.. 
Before my girlfriend's lease was up (2 months) we go in and try to change apartment and get it all set up. They told us that they don't have anything to switch over into and they would call us and keep us updated. Well that day never came..

I have never seen or had this kind of treatment like this from any complex or company in my life.

If you want a low-stess place to live, do not live here. My car alarm has gone off due to some intruders, a few times. Obviously she didn't even apologize. Maintenance is the only good thing about this place.

If you are considering moving into a dirty, crime infested apartment this is the place for you! If not... DO NOT CONTACT THIS APARTMENT COMPLEX. Graffiti sprayed in nearly every corner of the place, police there at least twice a week and the management is a nightmare. Our heater quit working mid winter.. It took them 9 days to come fix it. Aweful place.

While the apartments themselves are fine, the management is dishonest, rude, and disrespectful. The "amenities" are not as advertised. In a year there I witnessed several instances of theft, vandalism, and gang-related fighting. My car has been broken into TWICE in the last month and management refuses to return my calls or put up cameras despite a massive monthly parking fee. Love to pay to have my stuff stolen by a fellow resident. LOOK ELSEWHERE FOR SOMEWHERE TO LIVE.

Alyna and Tyson were both very helpful and made the contract sign a pleasant experience. I can't say much about the apartment yet, having only seen it, but it's small, cozy, and I have a nice view... The location is good and the commute to work is pretty direct.  I'm looking forward to living there.

From having maintenance issues not wanting to come into the apartments and fix anything I have a dishwasher with water that stinks wont drain a washer and dryer that they so-called have been fixing over the past year or two and now my they came in two days ago dryer doesn’t work apparently what did they do? I don’t know. Worst place to live honestly don’t waste your money

I've lived here about three months now. My move in was delayed for over a month with very little explanation as to why. A week before I moved in, I went and looked at the apartment. The cooling rack of the fridge was completely encased in ice and partially collapsed. I told management and was assured it would be taken care of. A week later when I moved in, the ice was gone, but a puddle of water stretched across the entire kitchen floor and the cooling rack was still partially collapsed. I delayed my move in by a day and management assured me again that it would be cleaned up and the fridge looked at before moving in the next day. The mess was still there the next day and I ended up cleaning it myself. For the next couple of weeks I kept asking management to look at the fridge because the cooling rack was still collapsed. Every time I got the same response of surprise that nobody had been there and was always assured someone would be there that day. Three months later I've given up and I'm just dealing with it. There are also two outlets in the kitchen that haven't worked since I moved in. The walls have a weird brown goop on them, which apparently means a smoker has lived there. That would explain the awful smell of the apartment when I moved in. It also shows that they don't really deep clean the apartments well between tenants. 

Police presence is basically constant here. It's not a good area. Not much management can do about that but still worth knowing.

Really the only big positive of living here has been the complete lack of bugs. I haven't seen one spider, roach, or any other bug since I moved in. Could be just because it's winter, but it has been nice.

Overall, it's an OK place to live if you're on a budget. But just keep in mind, you get what you pay for here.

DO NOT LIVE HERE! Price is not worth the tiny 400 sq foot box you will be living in. Very old appliances including a tiny oven we had to buy smaller pans for which still barely fit. Gave us a notice saying we had to inform them that we were moving out 2 months in advance, they put that on our door 2 months before our move out day so absolutely no time to properly inform them. Then they make you pay pro-rated rent because you don't get to actually move out when you want it's exactly 2 months after you get the notice so had to pay and extra 2 weeks of rent when we had been moved out for a month PLUS month to month rate they added on for fun which is an additional 500+ dollars. Then they tell us that the final month's utility bill is 160, it's never usually over 100 and now it's 160 when we weren't even there for the past month? Finally they tell us that that there is enough damages to use up our entire security deposit and we still owe 50 bucks. Again do not live here they will find any way to take money from you that they can.

Thornhill park apartments has been the absolute worst apartment experience I have ever had. First off, When I moved in the apartment was filthy. I was told someone would come clean it, but they never did. There was black gunk in the shower and sink drains along with old strands of hair. The oven had grease and grime stuck all over it. I have tried to clean it multiple times but some of it does not come off. The appliances are all terribly old as well. Besides the nasty, old, tiny and overpriced apartment, there is dog poop everywhere outside. I literally have to watch every step. I never leave bad reviews but I am so frustrated with the management here and will be working to contact corporate to complain about how rude their staff is.

You can find a better place at a better rate. Please do not think of living at this place. Be ready to pay heavy fine when you are moving out. They will make sure that you are charged for everything as much they can. Charged me full price for the carpeting saying the carpet they used for the apartment is no more available for the market.

Really disappointed.

Don’t even think about moving here. This apartment complex is not very trust worthy and they charge way more than they should for the condition and size of the apartments. The workers in the office are friendly and like to say they will help, and work with you but it will never end up in your favor, once they feel the time for talking is over and they want money, the nice attitude wears off quite a bit. They try and bribe the residents to give good reviews while they live there. It worked with me but now that I am moved out they want almost $500 for a move out fee on a studio apartment (390 sqft) that was cleaned, vacuumed,  and professionally cleaned. All which I have a paid for already. Keep in mind my first cost was well under $200 to get the apartment cleaned better than it was when I first moved in. The staff are hard to work with in this mannor, there have been other occasions as well an it seems like they always have the upper hand.

Moving to Salt Lake from New York City, I had little knowledge about the areas of SLC and how the rental process works, which is extremely different.  I have had multiple issues since living hear, including re-signing leases multiple times due to issues with signatures, being given a smoking apartment when my lease was actually signed for a non-smoking apartment, etc.  When washers and dryers were "installed" I signed a lease 2 months before they actually were installed and had a closet removed the entire 2 months, and was initially expected to pay the increased rent without having the washer and dryer.  That being said, when the new hot water heater was placed in the apartment, they did not place it on a metal base, and is still to this day sitting on my carpeted floors (which is potentially a fire hazard).  Throughout the winter, my heat went out 4 times, and on the last "attempt" to fix it, the maintenance guy gave me a space heater to keep next to my bed because they didn't know how to fix it.  Needless to say, the next person who will be renting my unit will not have heat.  Lastly, after living in many apartments across in many states across the country, I have never heard of a 1 year lease switching to a month-to-month rental agreement without a 60 day notice that you will vacate, when your lease is supposed to end.  I thought that was the reason for signing a one year lease, rather than a month to month rental agreement.  I have also been told different days of my lease termination.... ranging from 3 different weeks, that being said, I missed my 60 day "notice that I will leave the apartment when I was supposed to" and am stuck paying for an extra month rent, without me even living in the state of Utah.  I am not one to write reviews or to complain, but especially for those moving from out of town, there are nicer apartments, in nicer areas (I caught a guy looking into my car and pulling on the handle one morning as I was leaving for work), for similar prices.

A little over 6 months ago I was living here at Thornhill Park Apartments in Taylorsville. At 3 am my whole building catches fire and burns to the ground due to "unknown causes" The official fire report did say that the only logical cause was the air conditioning/heating units they house on the roofs of all of their apartments. During my stay here I never once saw any one up there maintaining or cleaning these units. I did have renters insurance that the apartment complex provided and they are not compensating one dollar, they say its because of the "Unknown cause" of the fire. 20 units were destroyed  The really funny thing is that they are not allowing me to collect the "Refundable Deposit" that I provided them when I moved in. I have tried contacting managers multiple times just to get brushed off. 

If you want zero sense of safety or security move in here!

The other amenities are okay. 
From personal experience, the down stairs neighbors are smokers and we can constantly smell cigarette and marijuana smoke! 
We moved in during November, we wanted a five fire in the beautiful fire place, they never turned it on for our unit! 
In the description it says “air conditioning”. It is not! It is a 1 swamp cooler located in the living room. With the way evaporated cooling works, you have to have a window on the opposite side of the house open so you can have air flow and cool down the house. However, that does not help much when it is 100° outside! 
One good thing is all the storage, the modern look, and some friendly people!

We were supposed to be moving into a *Diamond upgrade unit* supposed to be modern and clean, well first Kristina told us we would be moving in on the sixth , and then called us and told us the 20th. So we waited and when the unit was “ready” it was an absolute horror. Mold spray painted over broken cabinets, literally everything you would be charged for if you were to move out was everything we was going to move into. Front door busted, baseboards ripped with nails sticking out. Currently about to give labor to my newborn and there is no way I would even have a child let alone toddler live there. Don’t let the unprofessional people Talk you into anything before you look at the unit we did not get our 150 back. Completely disgusting and so sneaky I’m so glad we didn’t get trapped I can only imagine what other people must go through here. Also don’t be tricked by the model unit either cause it’s NOTHING like what you’ll be moving into. Very sneaky business absolutely   Disgusting units and unprofessional employees. What a waste! I have never felt more humiliated and disrespected while living here. I'm sure that they'll reply with some generic "sorry you had a bad experience but it was totally your fault and we care so much about making it right!" line, but I beg you not to believe them. I read those responses too when first considering moving there, believed them, and I regret it tremendously.

This building should be condemned. There is black mold and I got very ill during my year living here. My pets became lethargic, smelly, and weak. I developed breathing and memory issues while also being chronically exhausted. Within a couple weeks of moving out, our symptoms alleviated. My pets are young and healthy, as am I. We had never, ever experienced chronic health issues like this before living at City Line. This place will slowly kill you.

The black mold issue aside, this building is just awful. The piping needs to be replaced. My water would turn brown and gunky multiple times a week. Management would shut off water to the building for days at a time during the summer with no warning or explanation. The heating would work maybe half the time in the winter. They also shut off heat to the entire building in early March, posting a snotty note on everyone's door advising us to simply use an extra blanket if we got cold. There is virtually no air conditioning except for a crappy little unit in the kitchen that can barely cool down a small room, much less an entire one bedroom apartment. During the summer I would suffer from heat exhaustion just from sitting in my apartment all day, multiple times a week. Keeping pets here is frankly cruel and I won't forgive myself or City Line for the suffering my pets endured from the extreme heat and cold we were forced to live in.

Management treated me like an inconvenience whenever I had the audacity of contacting them to do their jobs or provide me the most basic information. They tried to get my car towed from the dilapidated, sorry excuse for a parking garage I paid $50 a month for multiple times although I never once broke any rule or was late on any fee that could have justified that. Sometimes they would just lie and say they couldn't do something to get out of doing their job, but when I would call again a few hours later and speak to a different person, the task would suddenly become possible and the barrier magically disappear. 

I hope management gets sued someday and this place condemned.

My apartment is a pet friendly place that makes my family stay whole and complete. My boy Ash is a 254lb Saint Bernard. The building itself has its own wonderful like feeling and the neighbors act like a community of a whole, all interconnected. 
    Some move in and out but we share, feel and care about one another, not in a way that invades privacy but in a compassionate and empathic way that stimulates good feelings.
    I and Ash love our beautiful apartment, old style doors, molding and copper wall adornment all right in the heart of Salt Lake City.

We scheduled a tour online and they told us that that dont give tours after 4:30. It let us schedule for 5:00 on their website. We got here at 4:45 and they were not flexible at all.

This place was awful. They overcharge ridiculous fees when moving out even if the place was already damaged before moving in. They rented two places out from under me after taking my deposit and almost left me and my kids homeless. The apartment was terribly water damaged and poorly maintained when we moved in and maintenance often just wouldn’t show up to fix things after requests were made. I ended up getting charged for things I couldn’t get maintenance to come fix. Theft is a huge problem and they won’t install security of any sort. Walls are paper thin and we had black mold in our bathroom. Don’t move here.

To make a long story short, when my wife and I felt slighted and neglected, the staff of Hunter's Woods rose up and helped us feel better about our choice to move here. Now, I have no regrets. I'm glad that we're here.

it a big apartment. they are very good with fixing repair.     the rent is  about the same price of other apartment.  would say the office staff is the best. has a pool and a gym.  it been a fun place to live.  bus stop so close you can walk  right in front of the apartment.

These apartments are very spacious with decent storage. Great locatuon, Very close to freeway and shopping. Has a decent pool and hot tub, open year round. Wood burning fire place is also nice. One down side, the kitchen is small and not as much storage as I would like.

We just moved in a few months ago. It was amazing for the first month. They did everything we asked helped us quickly and efficiently.

Since then our AC has stopped working and has caused our Power bill to more than double. It went form $80 to $220 because the AC cannot cool the house and when I reported it to the staff they have told me it cannot be fixed because the unit is not large enough to cool the house. I find this to be complete BS as the house was cooled for a full month when it was hotter out then it is now.

They also have not fixed a single thing on our list of things that needed doing from the move in. We still are missing multiple screens for the windows (Only making the AC situation worse since we can't open them or bugs will get int the house)

We are still missing a door to our laundry room.

Our blinds were put up with tape and have fallen off on their own accord since we moved in.

I have asked for a call back from the property manager and never once received one. 

I was going to have a ton of my friends move in after the first month and now basically will tell them for the rest of my life how terrible this place is and how they lie and don't follow through with things.

I have lived miserably in many noisy, dirty apartment communities in Salt Lake over the years, including the one next door to Lakeside Village. But when I moved to LV, I was amazed how different it is. To start, living  in a 55 plus community DEFINITELY gives you a quieter home. But LV is also well maintained, clean, and beautiful. I have a lovely mountain view and a roomy apartment in excellent condition. The people are friendly and management is responsive to tenant needs. I have lived here 3 years and plan to stay indefinitely. I recommend LV to all my friends. One down side to living here is high fees, such as property taxes that are passed on to tenants, a $20 monthly fee for your parking space and a high water bill based on a formula rather than your actual usage. Also expect a significant rent increase of about $50 each year. The rents are about mid-range for nicer 55 plus apartments in Salt Lake.
This is absolutely the best Apartment Complex in the entire State of Utah. The Management is so awesome.

I've lived in many different apartment complexes over the years, but Lakeside Village is hands down THE best! The common areas are very well maintained and any maintenance items are taken care of immediately. The office staff is so sweet and always has freshly baked cookies in the office. As for the apartments themselves, they're updated and kept in great condition. Everything looked new when I moved in. Oh, one of the best things is that other tenants are so nice! Everyone says hi and waves. I love it. I don't ever want to move again!

Management has continually let me down. They are so disorganized and have never been able to help me the first time. I always have to visit them  multiple times on the same issues before they can come up with a solution. 
PARKING: There is none. You have a few spots, but they go quickly. Parking is so scarce that they actually have a towing company that patrols the lot. Many guests have been towed or have to park on the street. There is guest parking, but that is always full with the people that live here but don't get a sticker because they are not on the lease. They do have garage parking but its $50. Over the past year I have mostly parked out on the street. Cars have recently been broken into on the street, and now Murry city is banning parking on the street. There is no room for cars here.

I love living at Meadowbrook...my apartment is large and perfect for myself and my cat. The staff takes care of the outside really well. I love the underground parking and at $40 a month its very affordable. I love that my utilities are billed each month with my rent...i dont have to remember to pay extra bills each month. I feel very safe here and love the secure buildings. I plan to be here long term and definitely reccomend this place to anyone looking.

Meadowbrook Station Appartments is perfect if you are looking for a good location and quality living. 
Everything is at most a 10-minute drive away from everything you need. If you don't own a car, the Trax and bus station are located just across the street, and the Frontrunner is only 2 stops away from the trax station.
This place has great amenities. The garbage is picked up for you at your door, and when needed there are garbage shoots at your disposal too. The apartment is equipped with a washer and dryer, dishwasher, fridge, AC, storage, internet, and the living space looks great. 
Everything is kept in good condition, and if there are problems for any reason there is free maintenance available.
The pool and gym are also in great shape. There is a playground for kids, a basketball court, hot tub, lounge chairs, bbq station. 
The only thing that can be troublesome is finding parking close to your building. However, there is underground parking that can be purchased fairly cheap which, once purchased, eliminates this problem. 
The staff is also very kind and they do their best to help you out and make things easier for you. They are great and making announcements and letting you know of any activities or projects they have going on. They also don't rope you with extra fees like some other apartments do.

Overall I think this place is a very nice and convenient place to live.

If there was a problem with something in the apartment, I'd let them know in the morning as I left for work, and when I returned from work that night there would would no sign of there ever having been an issue. In addition to that, on the rare instances where something needed fixing, they always thanked me kindly and genuinely for bringing it to their attention; I have never felt like a nuisance, but rather, a valued member of the Royal Farms community. You get one covered spot, and people sometimes park in them that don't live here and they tow a day after. If you aren't a 100% sure you can afford it, don't do it. The late fee for late rent is $150 and your rent goes up to "market rent" which is I think $950 for our apt. Its ridiculous. We've never been late thank goodness. You get an eviction notice on the 4th if rent isn't paid. They just won't work with anyone at all. One person in the office can be snooty, gladly I don't have to talk to them often. Its usually pretty quiet. My main complaint is just how expensive it is for a 1 bed. You can also have pets that are restricted in other complexes, breed restrictions are crazy around here. They allow them though, which is why me moved here to begin with.

Miller estate's has been my home now for almost 12 years!  The 1st time I saw my apartment I knew I had to live here! I have a 2 bedroom apartment 1.5 bath with spectacular views of Mount Olympus and the small lake with 3 fountains which my balcony overhangs.  Full of fish and ducks and few geese!  The sounds of the 3 fountains hide the fact we are settled right in the center of Murray,  located close to everything! We also have such beautiful grounds here with well maintained landscaping and a resort like feel to the grounds!  I really enjoy living here and plan to stay for long time!

I recently moved into the Twenty Ones Apartments. The whole building has a fresh and modern feel to it, and it's in a great location. The apartments themselves have a great layout. There are a lot of shared spaces in the building with fun amenities like arcade games, a golf simulator, a pool table, and large TVs. The property manager has been very friendly, helpful, and accommodating throughout the whole process. I'm very happy with my decision to move here.

The building is a lot newer than other apartments in the area. The staff is respective of its tenant's privacy and has always been transparent with their rates and fees. The gym equipment could be better, but they've already sent out a notice stating they're upgrading it soon. Manager: Lisa holds the place down and is a pleasure to work with.

I’ve lived in this awesome community for quite a while now. The vetting process is very good. We have a building full of winners. If you want to have a peaceful, caring, and overall happy place to live…West Station Welcomes you!  
Also, these guys have gone above and beyond to accommodate for people and there pets. We have a dog run that’s gated in. Nice lawns. Don’t forget about the gym.

Writing this review because management has not responded to any attempts to reach them via email about a well known issue, but we know they read reviews regularly and might respond quickly to a situation they are well aware of.

All floors (except bedroom) are “hardwood” and create a constant noise challenge for those living on floors 1 - 3. 

Your only hope is that the people above you are considerate enough to take off their shoes AND buy a rug for high traffic areas/to put underneath their furniture — otherwise you will constantly hear the people above you moving around and be put in a situation management doesn’t know how to properly resolve. 

It is a true problem because after calling security enough times during “quiet hours” to resolve the issue, they just threatened to stop protecting the property anymore. They also won’t do anything in between the time management leaves and quiet hours start. When asking management to resolve the issue during the day, they say “We can’t MAKE them be quiet or charge a fee for their disruptive noises.”

If there is a solution, it should be reasonable to see management explain how they resolved the tenant’s concerns once it has been addressed in their responses to the online review, and not just leave readers hanging with something like “We are sorry your experience has not been entirely positive... Please contact us directly so we may proceed with the above concerns.” or “We are glad everything has been taken care of since then.”

...Especially if they aren’t really finding out about the concern through an online review in the first place. 

It is not fair that they get to go home and sleep peacefully while those of us here have to sit idly by, knowing that if we addressed the issue directly with our neighbors, we would be evicted (as they have done with someone who did that).
Currently, 10 Mar 18. This management team here now it's great. Both ladies do a wonderful Job. The building is clean and quiet.
They're unorganized, sloppy, and are constantly changing employees. Almost never in their office and leave whenever they want. If you have a problem it will take minimum 3-4 days to get fixed.

Where do I begin? Management that lies, deceives and is completely unprofessional.

I truly do not who is worse Danica, the Manager, or the "Leasing Agent." Danica claims she has 15 years of management experience, so apparently the "management qualification" bar is extremely low these days. Whenever I go to professionally speak with her about apartment issues  (like not have water for 5 days, not having proper internet, compensation solutions) she gets attitude, lies and starts crying.

The "Leasing Manager" is just as bad if not worse. She is RARELY in her office, shows up to work like it's a pajama party (wearing socks with slide shoes and a pizza box) and tells me after being without water for 5 days to "be an adult." Umm excuse me, I pay rent and utilities and have a full time job do not lecture me or ANY of your residents on how to be an adult. 

Do all the residents a favor and salvage whatever is left of West Station's reputation. Replace your management and add professionalism to your company's values.

Old, run down, out of date appliances and buildings combined with management that will not respond or help with any problem you might have. A convenient enough location but absolutely not worth living here.

Vey shady apartment with homeless crawling everywhere. They frequently break in cars and steal stuff. Management doesn't care even a bit.
Garage parking is useless as they've gates open all the time, gate never closes.
Apartment smells like dog and poop is everywhere.
Very dirty, very costly apartment and doesn't worth at all.

If you want roaches, ants, and rodents, this is the place for you! Do you like difficult property management companies that take advantage of their tenants! Then come on down to the Palladio where you’ll hate every aspect of where you live!

It's 10:21 am. Stopped by to check out an available apartment that is listed, however, no one's available in the office, nor are they answering the multiple calls I've just made. Darn shame, they may have lost a potential tenant.
The staff has all been incredibly friendly! The building is so well kept and I love how responsive they have been to any of our questions. We love our new home!

If you're looking for a great unit, the morton is awesome. If you're looking for usable amenities or a communicative office this is not the place. Starting with the gym, they closed it on Jan 20th for a week to move it floors, it didn't re open until mid march. The clubhouse "renovation" has been going on since February and was supposed to open beginning of May. When inquiring in the beginning of May if it would be open by memorial day so we could use it for  birthday party we were told yes, yet here we are the end of June still awaiting it's opening. Not to mention this renovation has caused limiting elevators down to 1 for residents, and constant noise and fire alarms. A fire alarm goes off almost weekly with either no correspondence, or if there is an email sent, it comes hours later which having  wife who works from home and multiple animals is unacceptable. On top of this, the morton is still charging residence for monthly "common area utilities". Outside of that the gym is too hot during the day and the treadmills are literally in the sun without a shade, and the dog area is so unsanitary that we take our pets outside rather than use it. Again, the units and hallways are 10/10 clean and awesome, it's just everything else that gets 1 star.

Why I regret living here:
The management was terrible at handling issues like noisy neighbors and cleaning the property --they collect the trash at your door, and it gets stinky; the pet area is always disgusting, especially on weekends. You are lucky if they answer the phone or are available at the front desk. The location is very close to restaurants, bars, and grocery stores. However, it is very unsafe at night or very early. There is construction next door, so traffic is horrible. 
I will never recommend Greytar. 
By the way, they keep your deposit for two months after finishing the lease, and if there are mistakes or additional charges, they won't justify them; you will receive a check with whatever they consider is right. To fix it, the building managers will not help you; you must call many offices in the Greystar company.

I love living here. The building is lovely with a great rooftop area and clubhouse and is diligently kept clean. It's conveniently located and has a great downtown vibe. If you don't like normal city noise, this place might not be for you. I have a dog and the building is very dog friendly. I have seen some complaints about the construction next door. I mean..............that's not the Morton's fault? Why would you complain about that? Sigh. Maintenance has always been lovely and responds quickly. I've had a great experience here and hope to be able to afford to stay here.
The Morton is one of the best locations in downtown Salt Lake City for a young working professional to call home. I Love it here!

I lived in a ton of rentals and this is hands down my favorite. The management is friendly and greet me by name every day, the mail lockers are incredibly convenient for receiving and even sending packages securely, the location is unmatched, and Ive never been anywhere where the facilities, staff and tenants are so dog friendly. My dog Cash and I have never been happier!
Terrible communication, especially for renewals. After telling me I could move to a different apartment, they gave it away without even telling me.

We live in unit 701. Directly believe the gym (why would they think that’s a good idea?) they never disclosed the excessive gym noise and shaking off the floor and walks every time someone is lifting weights or using the treadmill, etc. I can’t express in the slowed character limit just how bad it is. Management made a long list of broken promises to remedy the issue, but wouldn’t even enforce gym operating hours, so we would wake up to THUD THUD THUD at all hours of the night any time someone broke into the gym. 
The manager Kaitlin then blamed us for the issue saying we didn’t complain enough. If I submit an issue with the property numerous times, it’s the property managers job to address it and follow up. 

Expect these issues and many more. Stay far away.
The Morton has been a great apartment to live in and the services are top notch. The management is always quick to respond and works with you when you have an issue.

I have loved it  here. The location is quiet and feels a little tucked away which I personally enjoy. You can walk everywhere in downtown SLC and the apartments are perfectly modern. I love my apartment.
The staff at the Morton has been nothing but helpful throughout my time here and I would highly recommend it be considered by anyone looking for apartments in the city
Beautiful new building, but it is the helpful team that makes this place better than most.

The Morton has been a fantastic experience. It's in an amazing location with so much to do. Getting the lease situated and move in was phenomenal. The building feels safe and secure and the amenities are great. Everyone is super friendly and I couldn't ask for better neighbors. 
The leasing/management team is also amazing. They put in a ton of work, are very kind, and make the moving process so easy compared to other rental management experiences.

The Morton is very unique! Not the typical cookie cutter apartments you find in the rest of downtown. I love the New York style loft feel. Amazing views in both the apartment and from the roof top lounge and gym. You can't beat the location! so many amazing places for food and drink within walking distance.

I went to the morton just this tuesday. I had a tour with Jardee, who i found out was the manager, and it went so well!! He was charismatic and the place seemed nice. I went through the janky application process (which jardee wasn't confident with at all and had tons of issues processing the application which took about an extra half hour). I explained to him that I was on a time crunch and he nodded his head, said ofcoursed and told me hed be ready probably on thursday and definately friday. I lined up some friends to help me friday and even took the day off from work. I call and find out jardee isnt in thursday and the application isnt ready. same exact treatment thursday. Im livid. saturday I call and find out they wont be ready until next tuesday. THIS IS A SIGN. take it as one and stay the heck away from these bums. If the managers this bad, I can only imagine.

I really like living here. The staff are very kind and excellent at what they do. And knowledgeable and helpful.
Perfectly clean community. The additional services provided such as valet trash makes life so much easier. It’s a quiet and safe community. Overall the best apartment experience I have ever had.
Great apartments! We have a corner 3bed 2 bath that overlooks the western Salt Lake Valley, and the sunsets are breathtaking.

Personally I can only say good things about this place, the leasing agents are all very friendly and willing to help with any questions or concerns that may come up while I’m here. Well Maintained property and overall can’t complain about anything here.
This is an enjoyable place to live.  Its easy acess to freeway. Nice dog park for pets

I've been living at this apartment complex for the better part of a year. Since moving in they have renovated the Gym, Pool, and exterior of my building. It actually looks really great. I have had minor issues here and there, nothing out of the ordinary and the management team has always acted on each issue quickly. 

I have been through many life changes while staying here, and the management has always been very understanding to my circumstances. They are very helpful and personal; Trinity and Michela are especially wonderful to work with.

I see a lot of reviews from people who are failing to live within their means, seems silly to slander a good place because of poor planning.

I genuinely have enjoyed my stay here. Thank you Joshua Tree!

Although you might be charmed by the facade of a quaint community with modern amenities, you will be greatly disappointed. 
These units are poorly constructed and overpriced (scaffolding has been up for over a year with no progress made, flat paint on the walls, cheap flooring, incorrectly installed hardware, cheap appliances, etc). 
They charge WAY too much for rent, which includes hidden fees that they won’t explain. 
They will lie to you about the availability of advertised amenities. 
They do not enforce leash & pet waste rules. 
They do not offer recycling. 
No one there knows how to properly install or operate a sprinkler system. 
Fireplace never works. 
Neighbors smoke inside even though it’s a smoke-free complex. 
Neighbors steal mail and packages. 
They charge an unnecessary $300 for late rent. 
The employees are unresponsive to questions and concerns. 
They will charge you hundreds of dollars after you move out for things you should not be charged for. 
Their responses to poor reviews on google are literally all the same, like they copy and paste the same empty apologies over and over. 
WORST experience I’ve ever had living at an apartment complex. Do not waste your time and money here. I’m currently in the process of working with my lawyer to dispute my unwarranted charges after I move out. Save yourself a huge headache.

Absolute worst experience ever! I moved into these apartments understanding that they were under construction and I would have to put up with some inconveniences. But I did not expect to be verbally threatened by the construction crew at 6:15am when I kindly asked them to check the time (against city ordinance and no permit to be working that early). I was given a $20 gift card from the office for being called vulgar names and physically threatened by men. The construction crew repeatedly worked from before 7am and after 9pm upstairs in the unit above. There was no peace. They threw cigarette butts down into my patio, where there was a pile of bird poop. This was because there was a huge next in the eaves of the building above my patio. No one would remove the birds. They also would hang out in the carports so when you got out, the birds would swoop down and scare you to death. Then my apartment was broken into, drug addicts sitting in front of my front door smoking in the halls, random cars always parking in my assigned spot, and the pool didn't ever open all summer. My ground level unit had raw sewage coming up through my tub, overflowing into both bedrooms and the rest of the bathroom/laundry area. They didn't provide professional cleaning nor did they come out promptly. I had a six inch stain up my baseboards and walls. Towards the end of my stay, they changed all the USPS addresses and unit numbers. This resulted in not getting mail and packages for weeks! This equaled about $500. She told me I would receive it within 30 days. I handed over my keys and signed her paperwork. I never received my money. When I called to see what was happening with it, another manager told me that she had given me wrong information and it was MY responsibility to get this from the person I found to take over my lease. I have it in writing and they would not honor their own mistakes! BEWARE. They are dishonest and unprofessional!!!

The people at the front office were great. Everything’s else about the experiences living in this complex are disgusting. They literally will take every penny from you. The last months rent wasn’t posted until the 2nd so I thought I had already paid but when I checked again on the 3rd it hadn’t so I called to explain the situation and they “graciously” cut the $300 fee to $150 for they’re own doing. Then, come moving out, they said my sister could turn her key in on Monday then ended up charging her $150. They took our ENTIRE deposit for an apartment that was hardly damaged, and called it cleaning fees. After we moved out, we were locked out of our AMC rentpay account, and were charged rent and took it from our account EVEN though we didn’t live there and they only gave half of the money back. If I would have known how this place would try to take every penny I had I would have NEVER lived here and I will not recommend it to anyone. On top of the fact that there weren’t numbers on the parking structures when we moved in so we took one allotted covered parking spot and someone slashed our tires. So done with this place and can not wait to tell everyone NOT to live here. NONE of the amenities promised at signing were available after a year of living there and they couldn’t give us a timeline of when all the construction would be over. 

Literally this and so much more.

There are couple things you might wanna know before you rent this place.
1, when you apply for the apartment it doesn't mean you get the unit and move in on the date you wanted unless you pay $225 initial leasing fee to hold your spot, and the fee doesn't go toward the first month rent. It is just there for them to charge you. And they said it is for processing paper work, in which I don't see what paper work that need to process that requires $225.

2, the manager and the secretary are not on the same page. One told me no available unit for my move in date after I send my application, the other person told me it is still available. 

3. When you don't get the unit that they told you, the only thing they could say is I am sorry, nothing they can do about it. 

4, They are nice but not professional. They wouldn't let you know that other applicant are looking for the same apartment unit, cos they said it is first come first serve unless you pay the $225 initial leasing fee in which it is the first time I have heard this kind of fee. 

5, you need to keep contacting them to check on the status. They are not being proactive unless you ask them. But still, when I ask them they don't even know what type of unit I am looking for. 

If you got that 40 dollars to waste then go ahead and apply. Other people might have good experience, but hope no one has to go through what I went through.

The management here is pretty awful.  They turn a blind eye to all sorts of bad behavior.  Fights in the common areas-- don't care.  Shouting and fights in the parking lots in the middle of the night?  Couldn't care less.  Obvious drug dealing with physical evidence?  Whatever!  Honestly-- they don't care for their residents.  They will add lots of unexplained charges to your rent, then fail to respond to requests for work to your apartment.  I've rarely seen a management company be more negligent about actually running a property than here! Don't be fooled by the new coats of paint and the work they've put into the remodels-- they run the place like a slum.  You can find safer and quieter places to live.  Let all renters beware!!!

I have mixed feelings about 4770 Settlers Point. Here’s the good and the bad.
The good:
-Maintenance is usually really quick to come fix any issues that may arise.
-The living room and master bedrooms felt very spacious, especially since there was a bathroom in the master bed.
-The grass is very green, even in the summer (more on that later).
-Being next to a golf course, the loudest thing you hear from outside the complex is someone yelling “FORE”.
-If you have a ground-level apartment, you can do your own landscaping.
The bad:
-They lost our maintenance check-in sheet and charged us for everything that we complained about when we moved in.
-They raised rent by 20% after our first year.
-They promised that there was a ground-level apartment we could apply for, and just as we applied for it, they said it was taken. This happened to at least three other families over the course of a year.
-Packages were stolen several times.
-Packages sometimes didn’t make it because of how confusing the numbering system is.
-The back parking lot is full of holes and occasionally people taking catalytic converters off cars.
-They run their sprinklers every. single. day. Even when it just rained. Even when it’s raining. In the middle of the worst drought in Utah when we’re being asked to conserve water. It becomes a marsh to try and walk on.
-Dumpsters can become so full of furniture (from abandoned apartments) after just one day that there’s nowhere to put your household trash.

I have lived in over a dozen rental properties and the current management at Settlers Point is probably one of the best I have ever seen for a large complex.  I have lived here almost a year and they may be a little more expensive than I am usually comfortable, but they generally make up for that with great service.  Maintenance is very quick to respond and with an older apartment we have had several situations where we needed their help.  The office is also very quick to answer questions and we have never had a negative experience working with them.  This past year they updated a ton of things on the property making it very nice.  They have several ammenities that I have really enjoyed including the recreational areas, the trash pickup, and the gym.  I also have appreciated how reasonable they are with pets, it is definetly the best pet friendly apartment I have ever been in.  One other small criticism that isn't entirely the apartment's fault, but there is a little bit of a problem with theft in the area.  We don't keep anything on our patio because people have messed with it and a few other friends here have had things stolen.  But generally it still feels very safe here, just know that alot of homeless people walk by and grab stuff just because of the location.  To save you the time I have looked up the crime stats for the area and they really aren't that bad.  Anyway, overall I have really enjoyed living here.

This place is the worst place I have ever lived. It is poorly managed, poorly cleaned, poorly maintained, and the people that live here are loud and obnoxious.

Any attempts you make to get something fixed doesn’t help anything and is usually ignored for months at a time. Once someone comes into your apartment, they just look at it and claim it’s working again.

DO NOT MOVE HERE, unless you want to hate your life for a year.

I did request maintenance to control the water speed in bath tub. Because it is annoying to bath on full speed all the time. The repair guy came in and changed the bottom faucet with a new one. I do not understand how come changing the faucet will control the water speed. I did expect to have some sort of mechanism so that I can control the speed of the water. Now, If I do bath for 2 min, my bath tub is becoming ocean I had to swim out to get out.

I am very happy with my apartment, it is the major location where I lived,the attention in the offices is very nice its staff 
I definitely recommend it
Great place to live overall, and pretty quiet most of the time.

I have been here twelve years and continue to be impressed. The convenient location to everything, the outdoor pool, exercise room, clubhouse, covered parking, and security make this the place to rent. My two bedroom unit is very spacious and quiet. The office and maintenance staff respond quickly to any request.

They purposely do not keep move in records or resident complaints. They then use it as a means to overcharge at move out. During the pandemic, they acted kind and helpful. They moved me into an apartment that was not clean and had damage. I appreciated the place during COVID but I should have taken steps to protect myself. During lockdown all of there business practices changed like anywhere, but now it is an excuse to over charge on move out since no pre move inspection was preformed or allowed do to CDC or management rules. Make this place s last option to live.

I never benefitted once from my interactions from staff, instead they have been a constant source of annoyance. They lost my package because they moved it while trying to do some sort of cutesy photoshoot to attract new customers, and did nothing to help me recover my losses. They closed down all the amenities during COVID, the exact features we were paying their incredibly high prices for, but offered zero financial assistance while they made bank by not having to maintain the services. Every time we don't do exactly as they ask they make threats instead of trying to compromise. I'll never forget when they threatened to charge us for having "holiday lights" up in January; the lights had nothing to do with the holiday and had been up since August.

I have been living here for over 5 months nd did not have a problem till now. As many of the reviews have mentioned it before, the management is outright cruel. I made a mistake of a late payment by a day. They charged me, and I am not even kidding, 400 DOLLARS for it. I told them that it`s Covid times and I am in a bit of a crunch, and they said we will send you an eviction notice and told me go back home. I get that apartments have policies, but a small mistake like this landed me a dent of 400 dollars. I was warned about the management before moving, but now I want to write this out to add my two cents to it.

Besides noisy neighbors, car break ins, and an influx of transients around the general area, It’s on the higher end for rent without an abundance of amenities. It’s in Sugarhouse but there are several other superior apartments that would be leaps and bounds beyond this place. Take all pictures when you move in and document everything. A scratch, carpet, blinds anything. Or you’ll get charged for random old things that cost your security deposit and more when you move out that you did not damage. The apartment complex proves to be dishonest and deceptive when you move out, obviously, I get nothing for writing this but hopefully this helps someone else from moving here.

DO NOT LIVE HERE!!! Walls are paper thin, the whole building shakes when someone walks up the stairs or a semi-truck drives by, and simply walking around your apartment causes your neighbors' apartment to shake. I've lived in apartments my entire life, and this was by far one of the worst.

Management is lazy and dishonest. They're hardly ever around on the weekends, if at all. So if you have any issues, like drunk college kids blasting music at the pool (which happens every weekend in the summertime), it's your problem to deal with.

Get everything management says in writing. Your lease agreement doesn't allow management to make or honor any verbal agreements, and they know this. So they'll say or promise whatever you want to hear, but won't honor anything not in your lease agreement. Their favorite form of communication is eviction and collection notices. They charge fees for everything, including parking and collecting your mail.

Crime is bad here and their rent-a-cop is feckless. We witnessed multiple broken car windows, stolen bikes, and homeless people living in the garage. But when you ask to see their cameras, forget about it. They're probably just up for show.

Save yourself a lot of money and grief and just DO NOT MOVE HERE!!!

This place is the worst apartment complex. The office management staff are very unhelpful. You have to communicate the same thing over and over again because they are so forgetful or they just don't care to help out their tenants.  Overpriced, lots of car break-ins, amenities are always broken.

I am surprised too see any negative reviews of the Irving Schoolhouse Apartments. Reading them I noticed almost all of them were 4 years old and I felt compelled to defend the property and management. My experience at Irving Schoolhouse has been great. I sold my house in Sugarhouse last year and needed a place close to Highland High School for my daughter. I looked at every property in Sugarhouse close to Highland High and Irving Schoolhouse was by far the best choice. They have the best pricing, floor plans, sq. footage., staff, and parking. In Sugarhouse parking is always an issue but not with the Schoolhouse. There is more parking then you could ever need. The staff (Kiera, Winter) treat you like family and I have never had an issue that they didn't solve. The property has just been renovated and the clubhouse is amazing. The staff helped me have my daughters graduation party there, and we are having our family Christmas party in the clubhouse too. The pool in the summer time is by far my favorite. You can barbecue right by the pool and run across the street for all kinds of good food including Whole Foods. Irving Schoolhouse apartments is like living on a resort right in the heart of Sugarhouse. I have never had a car broken into and I park 2 cars and a motorcycle there. 5 stars staff, 5 star property.

Don't rent here. This apartment is overpriced, unsafe, and the management does not care. Our car has been broken into (rear window was shattered) and our storage unit was broken into twice due to the flimsy storage locks. The surveillance is a joke. No one was ever caught and cars continue to be broken into with high frequency. If that wasn't enough of a reason to look elsewhere, the rent is high and they are now making you pay $120 a year for the privilege of having a packaged delivered. If you don't sign up, they will return your package to sender. Or decline to have your mail delivered. It's ridiculous. We cannot wait until our lease expires. There are so many new, less expensive options in Salt Lake where you can be secure and don't have to pay to have mail delivered. Don't waste your money here. I truly wish I could give it 0 stars.

We are disappointed about this place and NOT recommending it to you at all.

First of all, the rent isn't worth the apartment condition and services they provide.
Here, I am giving only a few examples:
1. Once, someone hit my car in my paid stall.
I shared pictures of the scene with the office and asked them to help me find who did it.
Despite paying monthly fees for parking lot, camera, etc., they did not help us. we were told that cameras do NOT cover our parking stall! (I don’t know why I was charged for cam every month!)

2. I have not seen services this bad anywhere else I lived in the past.
I called the facility guys multiple times on several things, such as fixing tub stopper, ceiling fan, and fireplace.
