they will charge you for the most random things and neglect any communication with you. you will find out issues they have with you through fines or threats of eviction or towing your vehicles. dont move here!
It's convenient to the highway and stores.  Essentially it's a cheap place in an expensive city.

Riverfront Apartments the place you can have your kids play outside and feel safe. The grounds are maintained, the seasonal pool is nice for the family. The year-round hot tub is amazing! My family and I have lived here for over 7 years. The staff and maintenance team are friendly and quick to solve any maintenance issues. The office managers are friendly and ready to help you find your next long-term home. I love the fact that if you have an animal in the apartment.  Ours is a service animal . We were treated with respect and dignity with our special needs child. They accommodated my son's needs and our family. The managers showed  kindness and empathy to my son. We were told to reach out for whatever we needed for his needs.


Riverfront Apartments is a  hidden gem, people should take notice. Take a look and call Riverfront Apartments home.

I been looking at a lot of apartments lately. Riverfront really stood out above the rest. I love the play area. The pool area is nice. The  property is kept up. The floor plan was great, Love the large kitchen. the staff was very friendly, Terrell was great he took the time to show me around and he was very friendly and helpful. I am really looking forward to the prospect of living there. Thank you Terrell for your kindness and time.

My husband and I have lived here for three years . We first moved in when they first built the apt, the managers were wonderful then. Everything was wonderful until they changed managers and the company they go through. Living here then became a joke. They don’t work with you, my husband and I tried to ask to move out 1 month early to get another apt we really wanted. They refused to let us and told us if we did we would have to pay mote than double our rent in fees. We paid our last month of rent on time, called and asked if that was all we need to pay, they said yes. Now we are receiving a bill saying we didn’t pay June’s utilities. They are sending this for July 1st. We paid more than our normal rent for June and we paid utilities. They are trying to make us pay for July, we are moving out June 30th. The manager Devin is very helpful we liked him but their assistant manager sucks. His name is Terrel. My husbands aunt passed and he was late one day for a payment, called Terrel and he did not even tell him sorry for your loss. All he cared about was the money. We have felt with him several times and each time is a disappointment. He is rude, does his job very poorly, and make people feel unwanted. We literally will wait until Devin is in the office just to avoid dealing with Terrel. I’m would not recommend moving here. Toward the end I was so unhappy with the managers that is what pushed us to find a new apt.

Absolutely horrible. If you want to live somewhere that you feel like you are actually living WITH your neighbors then this is the place for you. I can literally hear the people above me having conversations, walking (sounds like stomping), exercising, dogs playing, you name it you can hear it. It’s so poorly built that it wouldn’t matter who lived above you, you’ll experience extreme noise. There is NO sounds proofing at all. If you want to get out of your lease early because the noise is unbearable you'll need $3,000 to do so.

I was one of the first tenants to move into this place. You would think you get some loyalty for that in return but they really just try to milk you. This place is not that nice, and I promise for the price you can do better. You’ll hear your neighbors, when we moved from a one bedroom to a two bedroom it had stained granite countertops (not really the touch you want in countertops), carpet wasn’t new and the floors had scratches on them. Saw all of the paper buildings go up, plus the place is consistently messy. Although I’ll give them some credit that it has improved since they finally decided to hire someone to clean. Management was rude to me on several different occasions, really just one guy. As we discovered, this place is “fake” nice. 

My advice: don’t move here, you can do better

The location and views are amazing! Maintenance requests are addressed immediately. Apartments are spacious but rent is higher than expected. Rent on lower floors could be lower than that on higher floors.
Best views for the price I guess. Every apartment has stunning views all times of the year. Old building but not terrible just needs maintaining.

So close to the U campus with amazing views and is the perfect size for me and my roommate and our friends (we love to entertain and our apartment has become very popular for watching the sunset). The building is a little old but overall I love it!
This is my favorite apartment I have lived in! The view is stunning and the residents are all so friendly! Its the best place in central salt lake!

Good
Well priced
Active management
Good mailroom
Amazing location, 3 frequent bus lines within 2 blocks, near university of Utah

Bad
Very little bike parking
old appliances and building
poor interior construction specifically painting

Office and maintenance personnel are very prompt in taking action if you raise a concern. Building is secure because of the FOB given to each tenant, even the packages are secure because of the Amazon Hub located at the ground floor…
Good location. I would like the AC to be better, and the dishwasher doesn’t work great. I don’t like carpet but other than that I like this place.
Best views in all of Salt Lake City! The price is also one of the best you'll find and there's great public transport. Grocery within 15 minutes walking distance.
Positive experience! I appreciate living here so far. Great location and amenities. Managers are kind and responsive. Quiet street despite the location.
It is ok, there are a lot of things that don't work throughout the apartment and the laundry situation needs to be fixed asap. Other than that, they are pretty responsive when you reach out.
The fellow tenants are friendly, the leasing agents are responsive, and the common facilities on the ground floor (gym, laundromat, mail room) are clean.
I've been obsessed with Hightower since my first visit, and living on the 14th floor has been a dream! This is the best place to live in SLC!

Hightower apartments will nickel and dime their residents through inflated prices while also providing inadequate service. When moving out, I was charged $30 for 12 small, flimsy plastic blinds this was also billed two me two months after I moved out, acting as if it was my fault they didn’t get in contact with me sooner. 
I was also charged an absurd $200 for a late fee when I paid rent on the 4th of the month. The worst part is the disfunctional air conditioning unit. Trying to sleep while it’s 85 degrees in your apartment is unbearable. Management would not do anything either. Stay away from Hightower apartments at all costs. I would give zero out of five stars if possible.

Location is great, other than that this place is terrible. Appliances are extremely cheap, the shades break by themselves from the sun and management wants the tenants to pay for it (which they charge a lot,) rent is late on the 3rd not the 5th and the late fee is $150 which is absurdly steep. The worst part of all is the Air Conditioning though. If you live on the south side of the building your place will be 82 degrees with no hope of getting it lower. My suggestion: find another place to live and don’t be fooled by the pictures.

Perfect location between the University of Utah and downtown Salt Lake City.  Most apartments have excellent 180 views of the whole valley or avenues and foothills.  Excellent amenities with outdoor pool access across the street in new apartment building by same owner. 24 hour surveillance.  Pet friendly. Secured building.
They do not enforce garbage rules so trash is always in the hallways. The pipes are old and they intentionally do not fix them. So your apartment will be flooded ... at some point.

I had a loft here for a year and I loved the whole experience living here. Everytime I put in a maintenance request they were there within the day I put it in or the next day and the repair men were always so kind and quick. The front desk and everyone in the main office were always very kind and helpful whenever I called or needed assistance. For the apartment itself when moving in everything was in great condition when moving in. The amenities were always clean and taken care of well and the security that comes and checks the clubhouse were very kind when letting everyone know that the clubhouse was closing. For the comments about their cars getting broken into and homeless folks being around, It’s really not a big problem the folks that walk around tend to keep to themselves and the complex sent out multiple emails about the car break ins warning people to keep them locked. My only complaints are that if your registration isn’t up to date they will tow you and they won’t give you any assistance getting it back besides telling you who towed it and there is not a lot of uncovered spots for guests or other residents that don’t have a parking pass. Overall this place was amazing to live and I will be recommending it to future friends!

I cannot overstate how strongly I urge you to not live here.  Awful area, I was harassed by vagrants more than once.  Lived here three years, they raised my rent three times and never improved or renovated a single thing.  Cant fathom how they can justify charging what they do for what you get (or dont get rather).  The "amenities" were all too often closed or broken, but they certainly had no issue charging you for those things which you cant use.  Furthermore after I notified them of my intent to vacate they still send me a note saying "thank you for renewing".  What a sorry excuse this place is.  Cant stress this enough DO NOT LIVE HERE.

Very sketchy neighborhood. Car was broken into and stuff was stolen and when telling the office no one even showed the slightest bit of sympathy. Neighbors dont even smile at you when walking by. Apartments feel very small and very outdated. Very rude and inconsiderate staffing.

If you enjoy worrying about having your property being vandalized and solicited by the homeless, then this place is for you. This apartment would be much better if it was closed and/or monitored by security. If you decide to stay here, then carry a weapon with you when you walk out the door.

management is very polite here. they will have maintenence fix issues asap. I moved in and one of the burners on my stove wasn't working. I told management about it when I did my inspection and they had someone by the next day to fix it. The guy who fixed it also told me about another concern I had and was very nice in doing so.

I lived here for a year with a roommate. The property management only care about curb appeal. They do nothing to keep residents they have already. I suppose it's cheaper to bring in new tenants than to fix things and keep the old ones. Looking at all of the obviously fake reviews gives you a pretty good idea of what the office staff really spends their time doing. There are also a lot of reviews posted by people who took tours. Super unreliable, seeing as these people see the two hot tubs, but never realize that the majority of the time one or both of them are broken. They've never seen the maintenance staff fish someone's old tampon out of the pool and then leave the contaminated water as it is. They've never had to throw away a family heirloom because mold - which is everywhere, btw - destroyed it. They've never had to listen to neighbors screaming at each other at three in the morning because walls are paper thin. Don't trust any of the "I just took a tour! 5 Stars!" reviews - they have only seen the curb appeal.

The safety issues while living here have been numerous, despite reporting homeless people entering and sleeping in common areas and in front of my own apartment door. There are huge issues with people picking up after their pets, in the garage and stairways. The rent is higher than advertised and will likely have a big jump after your lease renews. I would not recommend living here to anybody. Thin walls and odors from the trash room are also an issue.

I lived here and had an ok experience with the management but when I asked for help due to roommates not paying rent they didn’t even respond. Price is outrageous. They should lower the pricing and maybe they will get people to actually stay and not have to deal with snobby people

I came across the Mercer right at 5:30 and Kirsti let me pop in and take a look at a vacant apartment. She was really helpful and worked around my schedule, which is awesome cause most places are pretty inflexible when it comes to closing hours.

I used to live on the East coast, so easy access to the city is important to me. The location is close to grocery stores, restaurants, the airport, trax, city festivals, you name it. The apartments themselves are updated, open and I love having the washer and dryer right there. The gym access (not to mention great view!!) is awesome in the freezing winters - you can enjoy the snowy city through the big window walls... without having to be in it : ). My contact with property management was great. Kirsti was helpful, warm and professional.

The walls are paper thin, and are so thin; you can hear your neighbor coughing at all hours of the day or night. If you want to watch TV, good luck, because this place is so horribly built, you will get a noise complaint if you do, even if you can barely hear it yourself, your neighbor will hear it. You will always know when the person above you is home, because of the wood floors, all you can hear is them walking around. So good luck trying to enjoy your apartment, because no matter what, it’s so loud, you won’t be able to escape your neighbors in your own apartment. The most enjoyable times for me at The Mercer, is when I wasn’t home, because I couldn’t stand to be home, because this place was so horrible.

The people that live here are very rude, and no one is friendly, if you say hi to someone, good luck getting a reply back. That also could be, because most people here don’t speak English. If someone sees you approaching the elevator they will hurry and close it, right as you approach it. Also you could be carrying stuff to your apartment, and hands completely full, good luck getting someone to hold the door open for you. This place is just filled with super rude people, which makes sense, because they’re just like the people that manage this place, rude people.

The transition from the old management company to the new one, was absolutely horrible. Things that were agreed upon with the old company are no longer valid with this new company Alliance Residential. The new company, Alliance Residential could care less that the old company made promises, and they will screw you, just like they did me. I feel like I have scammed out of money by this new company, and they probably will scam you too.

So all in all, do yourself a favor and avoid this place like the plague, because if you don’t, I can guarantee, you’ll be the next person leaving a review like this one. You will not enjoy your time here at The Mercer, and that’s a fact. I’d rather be homeless, then experience living here ever again.

I do not recommend living in these apartments, they're horribly built for the price. The floors and wall are paper thin, and you will hear your neighbors 24/7. The manager doesn't care about the appearance of the building, it's so dirty it's disgusting. There are stains all over the carpet on every floor, and it hasn't been cleaned in over what looks like a year. I pay a lot of money to live here, and expect it to be maintained and cleaned, it's so dirty, I'm embarrassed to bring anyone ever, because it's so disgusting. The management used to care about this place, and took pride in their job and building, but not the new manager. I have shopped around, and you can find places that are around the same price, with better amenities then here, on top of them being overpriced and dirty, and always smelling like trash. I feel like I've been ripped off now, where I didn't used to feel that way. A little work would go along ways, but they just don't care. Can't wait until my lease is up, so I can get out of this horrible dirty, noisy, and stinky place.

We’ve lived at The 500 for about 18 months now and we intend to extend our lease. Our experience has been a positive one. The apartments are spacious (perfect for your cats to tear through the house). The kitchen is sizable. The bedrooms are large and the water pressure is great. The patio/porches are big and comfortable space to relax. 

The Management group is great to work with. Maintenance is quick to respond and friendly. 
The laundry room is tidy, the pool is well maintained and the new gym is a plus!
Tenemos 5 años viviendo aquí y nos hemos sentido muy tranquilos y seguros, los vecinos son amables y los espacios buenos para que los niños se recreen.

My family and I have lived here for over 5 years, and the whole time it has been a good experience, from workers coming when we need repairs, to being kind to us, we really appreciate everything they’ve had to put up!
Excelente lugar para vivir tiene muy buena atención y es un lugar seguro.
Great place, good communication with people always at your disposal

Tenemos 5 años viviendo en este complejo de apartamentos y la verdad que nos sentimos cómodos, seguros y con la confianza de que tenemos a nuestra familia en un entorno tranquilo y confiable, gracias 500 Apartments por brindarnos un excelente servicio….

I’ve lived here for almost 2 years now and have really enjoyed it, the location is great and the apartment is perfect for me and my dogs. The most enticing part was of course the private fenced in yard area. Staff have always been amazing and see to whatever needs I might have. Really great place to live!
I have lived here for seven years and  I really like it here. They have a dog park a place for kids to play and it’s really clean. The management is wonderful. We couldn’t ask for more.

We have enjoyed living there for the last 7 years. It is nice and quiet.  The management and the other employees are nice and professional.  The pool is great in the summer.  And have a fence in yard is great for my dogs.

Marbella is so sweet and easy to work with! The community is fun (especially if you have kids or dogs) there’s so many nice people that love to chat and get to know you. The maintenance lady is also so so kind and helpful and if you have time to chat she’s the one to do it with! I’ve been here for over a year and love it.

SO much has changed since the new management has taken over! Now I can say that I am excited and very pleased to live here at The 500 Townhome Apartments. Jacqueline is an amazing manager who is not only professional but understands the importance of being more personal with the residents in her care. Also, Angie is still my all-time favorite head of maintenance, she can do just about anything. Thank you to the new management team for making me see how wonderful this place could be.

My wife and I have only been here 15 days but have received excellent response and repairs when they have been requested. I would recommend the 500 to anyone looking.

Terry Sanger

This apartment complex is very portly run. Nothing is done right or fixed correctly. It's a vary old apartment complex that need a lot of help. But I needed a place to stay for school and it's extremely expensive to pay for both school and rent.

Thinking about living here? Don't come, the apartment has mold, everything is broken, dirty, nothing works, management lies and deceives you. They promise to renovate the apartment and deliver rubbish to you. Complaining is useless, they are cynical, they receive your complaints with disdain. They are incompetent and irresponsible. Don't waste your money and time on rubbish like this. But the worst part is not the council, but the irresponsible and dishonorable administration.

Showed up to rent a place. Paid everything they told me upfront. 2wks later I get a text saying I owe $299 plus a late fee for not paying something that day. Side note: I don't even live there yet but have already paid the month's rent and ALL other fees presented that day 2wks ago. I call up and ask questions... no cursing or raising of my voice, just good old fashioned, "why are you charging me a late fee when it was YOUR fault?" Guy tells me nothing is going to get solved this way but that he can "wave the late fee just this once." Like he's doing me a favor by not screwing me over due to their incompetence??! Sadly, I'm stuck there and I haven't even moved in yet. Word of advice: RUUUUNNNN!!!!!!!!!
nice priced nice staff allow dogs kids are kids welcomed without grumpy neighbors

Moved in to a joke.  So many maintenance issues... Been here for a month and they have fixed NOTHING. Talked to the (so-called) property manager almost 2 weeks ago and still NOTHING has been fixed. 

Every weekend the dumpster bins become non existent and people just throw their trash on the parking lot. It's disgusting. Maintenance does clean it up on Monday, but they shouldn't have to. Residents don't respect the property because management does not respect the property (or the tenants). 

Make sure you see the unit you're moving into before you sign anything or give them any money.... Definitely not as advertised

The dumpster situation is horrible they come once a week (never the same time or day occasionally) and the trash piles. It piles on the side and they don’t take it when they come to pick it up they don’t take what’s on the side or come back for it. So that (if maintenance wants to) just goes in once that comes back and it fills up super fast. THE SMELL DURING THE SUMMER IS ATROCIOUS!!!
Parking is ok depending on your schedule. There are a lot of parking options under a ramp near the office if you want to pay for it. Finding your packages in the office is hit or miss. Management is nice. Utilities for the apartment alone (not gas and energy which is charged by separate companies) comes to about $100 on top of rent. No microwaves, appliances are old, as is the wooden flooring, lots of weird bubbles that don’t have water in them. Cabinets and such are old as well. Price wise it’s pretty good though. Maintenance is on top of things when you need help though and door dash is great. It’s fairly close to Costco and Walmart.

My experience is contradictory to the bad reviews I have read. I’m amazed how the staff handles the strange and demanding  residents on a day to day basis. They take their job serious and entertain the silliest requests. Keep up the good work ladies!
Not enough parking, so they'll make you pay $25 a month for the open lot on the side. And I got a ticket despite parking in an outlined spot and they won't help you with it, look elsewhere.

Well, I have not been able to look at the inside yet but the team took me on a virtual tour and has been great to answer all my questions. They even call/ Text you back! More than I can say about most I have reached out to. 5 Stars to a good start! Thank you for bringing back the art of Customer Service!

This is not a good place to live. The managers do not respect their tenants. Maintenance requests are outright ignored, even when they pose health hazards. We have been requesting maintenance on our shower because the bottom is cracked open and the walls are breaking apart and has been moldy since we moved in. We were charged a cleaning fee when we moved in and the apartment was absolutely disgusting. There were crumbs and hair under the couch cushions and food on the floor in the kitchen. In the six months I've lived here the washing machine has been broken 3 times and they did not offer us any kind of discount on that months rent. They have been claiming that the spa will be fixed "this year" since 2015. Do not live here.

My daughter rented an apartment at University Gardens for a summer and my perspective (as the paying parent) is that this is an okay property - UNTIL YOU NEED SOMETHING from management.  Unfortunately, maintenance issues arose, and it became evident that the property was not well-maintained.

During a severe heat wave with temperatures exceeding 100 degrees, the air conditioning unit in her apartment broke down. It took several days for a technician to arrive, and when they did, they found that the compressor was broken. It then took an additional several weeks to repair the unit because they were "waiting for corporate to approve the expense." During this time, the apartment was uninhabitable due to the extreme heat, as it was a second-floor unit. She was forced to stay elsewhere for over two weeks and couch surf. At our request, they provided a very small standing AC unit, which it was insufficient to cool a room let alone an apartment.

While I understand that issues can arise, I believe I should be refunded for the period during which the apartment was uninhabitable. Despite sending over TWENTY (yes, you read that number correctly, TWENTY)  follow-up requests, all of them were ignored. Phone calls went unanswered, the voicemail box is always full, and messages sent through the resident portal are ignored, text messages, and emails also receive no response. It seems their strategy is to ignore problems in the hope they will disappear, which has led me to consider filing a claim in small claims court. Ignoring over twenty outreach attempts requires a deliberate effort.

If you are considering renting a property for yourself or your child, ask yourself if you are willing to deal with such unresponsiveness. If not, I recommend looking elsewhere. Like many college properties, they are efficient at collecting rent but fall short in providing adequate support and maintenance.

Its location is great, the only reason why I rated it good is because of the thin walls and creeks in the floor. Since I am a full time student and also am employed I am rarely home. If you are a student at the university I recommend this place because of its location. It is also close to shops and awesome food restaurants. Down the street from the park and right next to a hospital. All you need within a block away!
Doesn't have many features but does have a great price for 3bedroom also too pricy for the animals:( would not want to live here

I have been a resident at North Temple Flats for a couple months now and so far I love it. Parking is a hassle sometimes but management did warn me before I even applied that this would be an issue. That is the only downfall. Otherwise I like having the pool in this heat and the fitness room. also with homeless you see them everywhere downtown I mean we do live in the city what do you expect. as far as management they have been so kind and maintenance has always taken care of my issues with my unit. I am glad I chose this place to call home.

First off, before I forget, I don’t know what “security system” they’re talking about in the “featured amenities”. The only “security system” is the “gated community” part but the gates are always accessible except ONE which is easily bypassed by others such as the constantly broken parking gates. No assigned parking and it constantly fills up and then they started allowing “guest passes” for 24 hours which makes NO SENSE if you can’t even guarantee a parking spot for every person that lives here and drives. The apartments themselves are really great (I think) for what you pay; however, management is not the greatest. The main manager is so rude and unprofessional (the others in the office are always super nice though). The other thing that I don’t understand is how during this pandemic, they require masks to be worn when entering the office and yet NO ONE that works in the office wears one and they’re the ones who have had outbreaks within the office (July for example, the office was shut down for 2 weeks due to an outbreak)! Someone else has already said this too but you have to go into the office to get packages but that’s only when someone is ACTUALLY there which there frequently is NOT.
So if you’re looking for a place to live, just keep all that in mind. 1) biggest issue is the parking, as stated before. My lease says I am guaranteed ONE unassigned parking spot, yet my job (which has me home at different hours day/night) doesn’t always allow. 2) no security. Gates don’t always mean it’s secure (and yes, the homeless and drug do happen frequently and are a problem). 3) poor management running the office. I’ve been here for over 2 years and have seen 3 different managements in and out. 4) it can get really disgusting with trash and dog poop. People let their dogs poop in the walkways or in the elevators. There was also a time a couple months ago where garbage trucks didn’t come for almost 2 months so the trash was overflowing into the parking lots really bad! Not like a normal “yeah it reached the top of the dumpster/there’s a couch or furniture piece on the side” no, piles as large as all FOUR dumpsters we have surrounding them all!

Your packages? Always sent to the front desk and they lose them. 

Your trash? They grossly underestimated the trash output from this many people stacked on top of each other. Things tend to overflow here.

The gates are always broken. If you have more than one car you'll get towed. Drug deals are always happening and homeless people now sleep here. Management never answers your emails and when you schedule a time to pick something up they're never there.

We've been living here since July. Our first week we went without AC in the middle of summer and weren't helped with it. Upon moving in we were supposed to have storage units and amenities. The pool and gym weren't completed and the storage units now cost money due to limited availability. Also, no matter if you have roommates or not, your apartment gets only 1 parking tag. This past week we had our bike locked in our stairwell with the wheels stolen. More than likely, a neighbor took the wheels because no one was seen walking out the gate on the security camera. They are not willing to do anything about it. A lot of empty promises when you move here and disappointment.

I have lived here since the beginning of day 1 and my experience has been disappointing from the start that I do not know where to begin. This will be a very concise review but rest assured I hope the message reaches you on why to NOT live here.

Apartments: Poor design and the kitchen is so small there is nowhere to put your big pots or cook as there is barely any counter space. Amenities are alright but gym is very tiny. Perk is that we are the first ones to live here since it is brand new.

Staff: Constantly changing and always leave empty promises. Always miscommunication between them and the maintenance as well as tenants. They are nice, but not very helpful to the tenant.

Maintenance: Takes forever to fix your issues and also changed people. 

Neighborhood/Community: Alright. Loud since right next to the 215 and the police are always on-site at night for who knows what.

Parking: Biggest issue here. Kiss having guests over goodbye. Super limited with only 1 parking pass available per apartment. If there was any guest or street parking this would be okay but there isn't any whatsoever.

Overall, I am miserable living here and will move out as soon as possible.

Village Station at Eaglewood Apartments is the best apartment complex I have lived in! They have incredible amenities, floorplans, and the best staff ever! Some amenities are a large pool, hot tub, BBQ, bike & Ski(snowboard) storage, doggie wash, movie theatre, and a large Gym with everything you need for the best workouts. There is even a movie theater with a small fridge and microwave to enjoy popcorn or heat a warm drink in the cooler months. There is an elevator for those living on the upper floors. Maintenance staff are quick, efficient, and friendly. They work hard for even the littlest of tasks. 24-hour maintenance is also available for after-hours emergencies. The buildings are secure with an app or fob entry! The neighbors are great, and the neighborhood is quiet. If you are looking for your next temporary or long-term move, I recommend Village Station at Eaglewood!!

Apartments are extremely small in terms of square footage. The kitchen takes up a lot of the space and the bathrooms are too big. You end up with a small living room, small bedroom and tiny laundry room. Where can I fit my clothes? The buildings are only half way rented (if that) and the pool is extremely loud. Walls seem fine but the sliding glass doors and front door let in a lot of hallway noise from dogs and parties at the pool. Seems like people invite a lot of guests over on the weekend and the pool music is insanely loud. Can't wait for more people to move in and the noise will be even worse.
Had a wonderful time touring here. All the staff in the office were so kind and helpful to me. Some of the best people I’ve met while touring around apartments.

The property and location are amazing. I work downtown and it is a perfect mix of staying away from the chaos of the city, but close enough. The staff here are super cooperative and try their very best to resolve any issues. Maintenance has been fantastic at knocking out my work orders. The community is friendly and caring. I an definitely enjoying my experience so far!

I've lived at the zeller for 4 months, and I've got to say it's the best apartment I've ever lived at. With a heated pool and spa combo, gym, and gorgeous roof top lounge, The Zeller offers a lifestyle I've been wanting for quite some time. Zach is also really nice and intentional with the residents. I would HIGHLY recommend living here! I love how clean and safe the area is. The train right next door makes it really easy to commute.

The Zeller has such a strong team I communicated to the office about a work order for my shower. Maintenance came in quickly to address the issue and were very professional. I love feeling at home with The Zeller team and feel like I can always reach out to them with any concerns, and they will address it and find a solution.
The team really cares about the residents, and even when things don’t go as planned they’re always willing to go above and beyond. My experience was fantastic.

Here's everything I wish I knew before I lived at BrickLofts for 13 months. 

1. Noise. You will be woken up every morning to your 3-5 neighbors alarms going off. When you hear their alarms crystal clear, you realize they hear everything single thing that happens in your apartment. 

2. You will pay for things you do not need or even want.

Like paying $120 for DirectTV and internet + $70 to have someone take your trash from your door to the trashcan 100 feet away (but only between 6pm and 8pm) and a parking pass fee of $25-$50

What they advertise is far from what you end up paying every month.

3. Parking in the lot is dangerous. When parked in the well lit lot outside BrickLofts, our car's Catalytic Convertor was stolen which ended up causing $2,000 in damages to the car and making it un-drivable. When asked about the footage to submit a police report, we were ignored. When confronted about the footage with the main office, we were told the cameras are for show and don't actually record. 

4. The units themselves are poorly built. In July of last year, I was without Air Conditioning for 2 weeks as I was tasked with managing the maintenance men one my own time and told to deal with working from home in a home that was 87 degrees. 

5. The windows do not open. Period.

5. The water and electricity tends to stop working at times. My water has gone off 6 times in my 13 months here, and I was told to shower in another unit before starting my day. My hot water has gone out 3 times now for days at a time. The electricity went out 5 times. 

6. The construction. There is a giant apartment building being built next door and we are constantly left notices that construction will begin at 4 am and they are sorry for the inconvenience. 

7. Even though its awesome this apartment complex welcomes animals, you will hear every bark, and every step of every dog in a unit within a 3 unit radius. Makes working from home, extremely difficult. 

8. The price. Absolutely ridiculous for the quality of the units. Also beware of the renter as they will try to trick you financially. In my case I was told my month to month fee was an additional $500 after the lease ended (when my paper lease said $100) and they welcomed me to extend my lease at the same cost as move in, when the market value (as well as its price online) was $200 cheaper. 

It was a decent year, in a great location and I was able to make it work for me but beware of the fees. xoxo

I’ve been living at brick lofts for five months now. While the neighbors and dog friendly atmosphere has been wonderful I can’t say the same about the units. There is a serious sound issue in this building. I can often hear the elevator ding from the end of the hallway at the other end of the building. I can also hear conversations from my neighbors to the side and below. Something else prospective tenants should watch out for is the inefficient heating system. I pay over $120 for a studio to keep it at 69. While the windows are beautiful they are very drafty.

Good:
* Optional covered parking
* Complete set of appliances
* Very fast Internet
* Near freeway, shopping and parks

Neutral:
* Pet friendly
* "Entertainment Package"
* Lawn area for dog walking and kids playing in dog poo
* Smart home controls for door and some lights
* Very industrial, unfinished look if that's your thing, complete with bad door alignments and uneven cheap flooring.

Bad:
* Absolutely no sound insulation
* Visitors can't ring or get to your apartment outside of daytime hours
* Can't air out apartments
* Expensive to cool or heat

Overall this could be an excellent property, if not for the fact that the walls might as well not be there. You can hear every word your neighbors say, dogs barking 24/7, people watching TV, people trying to make new babies... you get the picture.

Another gripe is that smells travel between apartments, the only way to combat this is to run the AC fan. The windows don't open.

Lastly, the outside doors are locked at night. You absolutely MUST use the Dwelo app to open many of those, and while it works per se, it's not at all intuitive or reliable. Consequently there is a lot of door banging day and night. The doors to the park deck have an RFID chip reader which works a bit better.

This combined with the major sound issues and thin walls means the dogs on your floor decide when you get to sleep. 

The HVAC unit is extremely low on efficiency. If you look at the unit you can see it has the lowest legal rating. We have spent thousands of dollars on electricity here. I’m not exaggerating. If you like a unit go outside and check the meter. Contact the electric department to get the history so you can get an accurate idea of how much you’ll be paying. Our July and August electric bills were both over $300 maintaining the temp at 70 degrees.

When we said we were no longer interested, Candy told us that we could not have our deposit back. 

AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Amazing Experience Seasons on City Creek has been such a special place for us.  We renewed our lease, and are grateful for the ongoing service we receive.  It is a delight to live in the premises.  We recommend it,
Door Remote  I needed my batteries charged in the door and Mr K. Fixed it quickly.
Great customer service  Love the Seasons on city creek staff amazing people and great customer service
Great Place Staff is very friendly and helpful. Maintenance is very skilled and responsive.  Great place to live!

A Home Without Yard Work  I’m on my second lease and I can’t think of a better place to live. It’s a 3 minute walk to the Delta Center and Trax. It’s a quiet place and friendly neighbors. Don’t miss out on your last place to call home.
Quick and easy  Maintenance came by and fixed my smell which was in the washer drain and fix my patio lock.

I renewed my lease here twice and was living here for my 3rd year when I moved out of state. I can confidently say this was the only apartment I liked enough to ever renew my lease with.

PROS:
* Location is perfect. Close to IMC; walking distance from many great restaurants (Tea Rose, Pho Saigon, Tea Shop, Soy Sushi, etc.); close to downtown; close to Chinatown market.
* GREAT rates. It is the most affordable apartments I have ever lived in and I have lived in several different states. The increase in rates with every renewal was also very reasonable.(Compared to other apartments that would increase it so unreasonably high, which is why I never renewed at any other previous rentals.)
* LOVELY management. I have never not been able to reach them. They are very communicative, very attentive, and very nice. You can tell they actually care about the residents and I don't say this lightly.
* Even though I had to break my contract early to move out of state (for work promotion), they were super understanding and worked with me. I don't think I can say that about many other apartment managers--if at all.
* The maintenance staff is amazing. I put in a request and it is done promptly. They're also very nice people, too.
* Last but not least, very safe place to live. Close to the Murray police station and city hall, so I imagine that helps, but the entire area is great. I was never scared to go out for walks even after sunset.

CONS:
* No in-unit washer/dryer or hookups. However, this month, they just redid the entire community laundry room and it looks great! I will say that the cost can add up.
* It is a slightly older apartment complex. However, they do a good job with upkeep, so everything works great.

Hands down most helpful staff, reasonable pricing and great layouts. Originally had a hard time finding a decent place to live but came across Lost Creek and hit a jock pot. Totally would recommend this place to anyone who needs a nice and affordable apartment.
I love the location it's across from Trax and the local music store, staff is very friendly

I have wanted to live at these apartments for a few years now because they look nice and are right in the middle of the county. The apartments are well taken care of and look newer than they are. They are right next to the commuter and light rail line. The lady who works in the front office is super nice and friendly. They have a limit of 2 persons per bedroom and only 1/10th of the apartments are 2 bedrooms. Not many crazy kids running around--mostly single people who work at the hospital next door and many students. Everyone pretty much seemd to have things together. The only downsides are the laundry facilities are on one extreme end of the complex and the pool is not heated (also no hot tub).

Me and my girlfriend live here and we LOVE IT. Everything is near here, including hospitals, post offices, theaters, restaurants, park, rec center, etc. You have everything within a 3 mile radius. The office managers are wonderful and accommodating to our needs. Lost Creek is extremely affordable and consistent with their rates. Whenever we had issues, it was fixed within the same day, they even have an emergency maintenance number that you can call. Best of all, it's a smoke free community and the people here are respectful and kind. The environment is amazing and relaxing, my girlfriend loves the Koi fish pond. I can't recommend this place enough.

Lost Creek Apartment are one of a kind, I've been here almost 4 years. The management are awesome, The grounds are well kept n the swimming pool is always clean n is a good place to raise kids. Lost Creek Apartment are GREAT!

apartmentName: Wasatch Manor Apartments - A Senior Community
review: Very good amenities, friendly and caring management staff, friendly people, excellent property

apartmentName: Wasatch Manor Apartments - A Senior Community
review: Spacious apartments with super prices for adult senior living.  Covered parking offered.  In-house activities offered. The building is close to the biggest library in town and one of the largest in the world.  From there you can hop on the trax train and ride downtown in the free zone to enjoy many sites of downtown Salt Lake City and shop at City Creek Mall and enjoy world class music every Sunday morning with the LDS Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square.
Love living here at Harmony 3900! The staff here is terrific! Grounds are fairly well kept, given how the community is pet friendly. The maintenance crew is spectacular at what they do!

When I moved in I believe a temp was the person who met with me. She told me until I received a parking spot I could park in guest parking, she pointed at uncovered empty spots near the office. She then showed me on a map the same parking spots. I parked there and my car was towed. I now owe 375.00 in towing fees that they refuse to help pay even though one of their employees told me to park there.

Harmony3900 has been a wonderful community to live in. It’s in the perfect location for lots of restaurants and grocery and convenience shopping. Applying and the loving in process was super quick and manageable, the leasing staff was very helpful for the whole duration of the application process. I’ve been living here almost a month now and have absolutely loved it.

Looking, leasing, and move in processes were stressful but made much simpler by Natalie and the leasing office staff. Maintenance quickly fixed any small issues I had at move in, and overall it has been a pretty positive experience. Close access to the freeway, stores, restaurants etc has been nice. Great quality and design to the apartment. Love it here so far.

Harmony has beautiful apartments at affordable rates. They also have a very professional and helpful leasing team. There is a wide range of amenities for the community. I also feel very safe with all the security measures.

Staff is incredibly helpful! My original apartment had its opening date pushed back and I had to be in SLC by a particular date for school. I found Harmony3900 given the extensive filters I checked (i.e. in unit washers, AC, pet friendly, covered parking, etc…). Immediately, I received a response from the office with videos of the units I was interested in as well as unit information. I was in quite a time crunch to move to SLC and the office staff were nothing short of professional, timely, and kind. Luckily, I was able to move in on time and am incredibly satisfied with my unit! Thank you to the office staff!

Management has arranged for a service to pick up everyones garbage every morning. The halls are line with trash cans, and the entire building smells like baby diapers and garbage. You walk in the front door and want to throw up... don't even think about inviting guests over. No amount of complaining to management has any effect.

Lived here when I first moved to SLC!  The location is stellar and the apartments are a great loft space. But the kicker is Tina.  Best. Property. Manager. Ever!
The place is always spotless, everything always works, if there is ever ANY issue she’s on it!  
Lots of places have great space, But Tina makes Paragon Station a great PLACE!

From the very beginning the management at Paragon treated me like family. They are so accommodating and nice. Hands down this has been the best experience renting. Tina is always available for anything you need and will make it happen. I am sad to be leaving but they will always stay my friends. Oh and the apartments are dope! Their ammonites are over the top, brand new appliances, and very very very clean.

In a downtown area filled with cookie cutter apartment buildings, Paragon Station stands out.  The unique floor plans and apartment designs feel transported from the lofts of SoHo - but with the luxury of modern appliances and the reliability of new construction.

I spent a year living there, taking advantage of the short walk to restaurants and nightlife.  The advent of scooters opened up a wide area accessible without worrying about driving or parking.  When I did need to leave the area by car, it was a very short hop onto the freeway.

The building manager, Tina, is wonderful.  Resident in the building, she provides quick, responsive service and always has a friendly smile and kind word to brighten your day.  Anyone looking for a little higher-end experience in downtown Salt Lake should take a hard look at Paragon Station.

I moved to Salt Lake City for work over a year ago and immediately begin searching for an apartment. After looking at countless locations with the same drawbacks, bad parking, noisy neighbors and standard construction, I discovered Paragon Station.
Upon spending 5 minutes at the facility with most wonderful property manager imaginable, I knew that I had found my home in SLC.
The units are modern but retained the original foot thick concrete walls, which make them virtually sound proof.
With only 43 units, parking is never a problem even though it located so close to restaurants, The Gateway and the Vivint Center.
I am a light sleeper, and my bedroom there was almost sound proof. I have never slept as good and I already miss it.
Maintenance was great, and what few minor issues that arose were dealt with swiftly and efficiently.
I have never written a review, good or bad, for any place that I have lived. But I've never lived in a place like Paragon Station either.

I looked at a lot of apartments in Salt Lake and nothing stood out until I went to Paragon Station. The first minute I was there, I knew my search was over. The apartment was beautiful, and with a perfect location was enough to more than meet my needs. But then the management were the most attentive to any issues of any place that I have lived. Which was as refreshing as the apartment was quite. I am a very light sleeper, and I have to say that I never heard a sound from outside my apartment. It was so quite, that I got used to it and had trouble sleeping if i went any where else.
I have never taken the time to write a review of any place that I have lived for work, but I have to say the year I spent at Paragon Station was so incredible, I wanted to make sure that anyone looking for a unique and special place did not overlook the best place in SLC.

Paragon Station works for us!  Easy downtown and freeway access are a bonus.  Our apartment is beautifully appointed with modern appliances and is super efficient.  As the area continues to grow and improve, we are excited to be right in the middle of the evolution.  Pet-friendly with warm, welcoming tenants, the apartment manager makes the experience top-notch!

We have been living in downtown Salt Lake since we arrived here over 5 years ago. We were able to watch Paragon Station evolve from a concept to the beautiful home it is for us now from across the street. We love living downtown, the building and our unit are great. We have made friends here to include our wonderful building manager. I walk out the door and turn right to attend spin class, turn left to run through downtown. Have a particular craving? Walk and within minutes you are able to satisfy it...it's a great place to call home.

Often when they say luxury apartments they look good but appliances are not great and other aspects seem cheap. This place I have been very please with, the appliances are high end and the space is very modern open and clean. Two bedroom is a perfect amount of space for our family. Management is also super great!

I moved in recently from out of state. My new job has me here in Salt Lake City for three years. I wanted to find a place that I could truly call "Home" and settle in. I looked around at a lot of different properties - Paragon Station checked all of my boxes!! 

This luxury development is only 38 units with amazing tenants and management! I love that the building is an old warehouse from 1901 - the builder respected the historical aspect and coupled it with modern amenities!! Fantastic units built with great care and quality!! I love my unit and have really felt like I have a haven in a busy downtown area.
 
There is an Onsite Client Service Manager, awesome tenants that look out for each other and since the development is smaller - the residents get together in the amazing roof-top deck and common area to enjoy cocktails or BBQ's, etc!!

I love coming home to Paragon Station. I feel very lucky to have found such a great property!

I currently live here in a 2 bedroom and I couldn't be happier! My german shepherd is very happy here too. The community, my apartment and management overall is amazing and I couldn't speak more highly of it here!

I lived in this fine community for a year until I was transferred. The unit and common areas are something one only sees in New York, Chicago, or LA. The industrial modernism provides a profound experience that makes you feel both at home and creative. The management and other tenants have great care and maturity. Upon my departure I felt as if I was leaving a new family.
This place is beautiful to live at but management makes it impossible to enjoy yourself. You pay for amenities that you don’t get and when you email and ask about it you are ignored.

The staff here is very friendly and accommodating.  Work orders are handled in a timely manner.  Heat/AC keeps me warm in the winter and cool in the hot Utah summers.  There is a community laundry facility and once in a while, I have to wait to use a washer.  There is also a mandatory entertainment package included in rent, which is about $90.  We are walking distance from Trader Joes, Sprouts, Smiths, Whole Foods, and a number of eateries.  Trax and bus lines also run right along 400 S.  Super convenient if you don't have a car.  Overall the complex is quiet, and I feel safe.

Great location in between downtown and University of Utah.  Decent rent price. Utilities are not individually metered and run about $75 - $90 per mo. (some think it's great;  but that's high for my usage). Studios, 1 and 2 bedroom lifts available.  Quite neighborhood.  7 ft outdoor swimming pool.  Laundry in clubhouse. Small gym.  Open, unassigned parking (which is convenient). Safe Ave quiet neighborhood. Wood-burning fireplace in each unit. Love the location and the staff!  Gave 3 stars because of the utilities,  popcorn ceilings, bumpy walls.  AC unit on patio (for all tenants in 1st floor) are a bit loud. Updated models are nice, but do not have granite countertops.

The elevator has been broken multiple times since I moved in. The management are disorganized. They made a mistake and did not charge me for pet fees and deposit when I moved in. I didn't realize it. They suddenly posted a $400 charge for it to my account without warning and gave me only a few days to pay it, right at the end of my lease. They lost the records I provided to them about my pets then accused me of violating my lease when I didn't want to provide them a second time. It's over-priced and poorly managed. I've never left a bad review for any landlord before in my life. Run!

The management has been incredibly difficult to deal with. Didn’t have our apartment ready on move-in day, wouldn’t follow through on agreed price, and don’t care to fix things that are constantly broken. We’ve had 34 cars broken into this year and all they have done is put up a few cameras in the parking garage that should’ve been there in the first place. This place just wants your money!!!
Horrible experience. Lots of noise with zero soundproofing. Management has a bad attitude and acts easily inconvenienced when you ask them to do basic functions of their job.
It is true that they will nickel and dime you to death. It's a relatively new building and there's always something broken -- fire alarm system, elevator, electrical, etc.

This community is very unsafe, check the SLC police logs for yourself.... There have been multiple shootings resulting in a death across the street and on the property. Also a SWAT team had to take down a resident making threats to other residents. Way too overpriced for this/ what you get. There's a required media package even if you don't watch tv, you need a rentable storage closet bc the apt doesn't have a utility closet, and you pay heating and electric for leasing offices, gym, community spaces (=$80  more a month on top of your own utilities). And management doesn't provide any extra perks you see at other communities like regular happy hours or yoga classes. I know many people who have said they feel afraid for their lives living here, some have broken their lease and left. Only time we've seen the security patrol is when they're telling residents to leave the community room or hot tub at 9:58pm, you don't see them when the cars are getting broken into for the 3rd time in 2 months or when an intruder sets a fire on the 6th floor. Residents weren't even notified about the fire because they were too busy "handling it". The first we heard about it was when they sent an email the next day to blame the residents. Working with your residents to create a safe, fun place to live is not a novel concept- there are many other apt complexes that provide this!
Renter beware. This place is not what it seems. The rent is to high for substandard conditions and they will nickel and dime you to death.
Current resident. management is abysmal, old broken appliances, broken gates, no security cameras

When my lease renewed last year management sent me a renewal offer. After reviewing, even though it was an increase in rent, I still chose to accept the offer. Fast forward a couple days later and they all of a sudden want to change the offer terms and increase the rent even more...I explain to them I already accepted the offer that THEY sent me but they could’ve cared less. I was completely brushed off and disregarded. This happened in Summer 2021 and unfortunately it’s just gotten worse...there’s been multiple instances since where management has really dropped the ball. To name a few....:

The security gates no longer work. I was locked out for 2+ hours one night after the front door’s keypad failed. The afterhours management crew had no idea where the spare master key was, he couldn’t get ahold of anyone. It was so frustrating.  Ultimately we had to get a locksmith to drill through the keypad. And management took way too long (several weeks) to repair the keypad after the fact.

And believe it or not I was locked out another night after the keypad failed AGAIN  (!!!) and management didn’t even bother to answer their phones to help this time. Ultimately I had to break in the door myself since they literally did NOTHING. It was literally midnight and I had no other option. This was in December 2021 and I’m still dealing with getting them to finish the repairs to my door. It’s a joke. Oh and don’t worry, they charged me for this too. 

There are more and more homeless people and stragglers roaming around the apartment complex each and every day. I rarely, if ever, see management onsite to address these issues. The other day the police were here because a drug deal had happened literally on our complex’s driveway and the buyer ended up using and running around the property knocking on peoples doors. Management’s response? Literally NOTHING. 

Can’t wait to move. If you want to be treated like an object, disregarded and disrespected by management, then this place is for you.

Previous apartments I have lived at had a 30 day notice but Moda Sego has a 60 day notice. I gave my notice 30 days before the expected move out date. When the management told me that they had a 60 day notice I understood but asked if anyone interested could take my apartment when the lease ended. The management said that if I wanted to do that I would have to find someone to take the apartment. They refused to help and wouldn’t even direct interested renters my way. Moda Sego would not even lose money so this just goes to show the characteristics of the management. I am now going to have to pay an extra months rent. Don’t expect anything out of the management here, they will not help.

This has been a fantastic place to live until around a month ago. New gates were installed that unfortunately were mounted to the outside wall of the units. Every time somebody comes in or out (which everyone has to in order to get to their front door), it sends a thunderous boom through many of the units next to the gates. On top of the sound it vibrates through the house. 

While this may not seem like a big deal, it is loud enough to sit you straight up in the middle of the night. And yes, it happens every night without fail. I'm young and don't go to bed that early but it happens past midnight quite frequently. Not to mention it'll scare the crap out of you when you're awake. 

While this seemed like a simple oversight, the owners don't seem to care to change it. I've reported the issue 5 or 6 times now over the last month only to be given vague responses that they are looking into it.

At this point I am strongly considering moving away because of how poorly this has been handled, how I've been treated by the management and the fact that I haven't slept well in weeks (and they don't seem to really care).

We recently moved out after living at Moda Newhouse for a year and had a very negative experience. It's somewhat cheaper than other "luxury" apartments nearby, but in retrospect I would not choose to live here again. 
1. Our bike was stolen from the bike rack in the garage. The apartment manager showed us security footage which revealed two people who had broken through two secured doors in order to get to the garage. We understood that not much could be done about the bike, but we expressed concern that people could break in so easily and asked what would be done. Our concerns were dismissed. It's clear that management could care less about their tenants' wellbeing and safety. We also posted a sign alerting other residents of the theft and received a curt message telling us to take it down.  
2. We also happened to run into police officers outside the building when another break-in occurred, but this information was never disseminated to residents. We feel that it is responsible practice to alert tenants when their building is broken into. 
3. On move-out, we were charged a $110 cleaning fee which we were told is "standard" despite the fact that we had cleaned the apartment and left it in much better shape than when we arrived. I spent the whole first day after we moved in cleaning off dirty cabinets, floors, etc. 
4. Windows don't open, so it gets very stuffy in the apartments.
5. Noisy with dogs. Walls are thin.
6. The hallways and stairwells smell like urine at baseline. 

Positives:
- Location is great. Many grocery stores nearby and within walking distance of downtown, 9&9, liberty park, etc.
- Parking is convenient (indoor garage vs outdoor) and reasonably priced. 
- Maintenance was quickly responsive to requests.

See the "Don't be surprised" review below. My experience was the same. 

I would add that the new management (started at the beginning or 2017) takes forever to get repairs done. 

The building is newer and the location is great, hence the two stars. I moved here from out of state but now that I know the area better, I would look elsewhere. The management is going to hit you with lots of hidden costs. 

Don't bother spending much time cleaning your apt if you do choose to live here and eventually move out. They pay a cleaning crew to come service apartment and will take it out of your deposit no matter what.

When I found the property I loved the location.  I am able to utilize many of the close resources for shopping and quick access to most of downtown SLC.  The management went above and beyond to help me get into a unit that fit my needs.  I use and love the workout facility and command area with TV, Pool table and kitchen area. The apartment feels great with great space and well designed. 

I have a Dog and the pet run and pet wash was perfect.  It is located in a quiet area with a nursery behind the property.  I know animals can be an issue in an apartment,
but this one works out great. 

I highly recommend this property.

Pros:
- Location Location Location
- South Facing Apartment (in my case)
- In unit Laundry / Dryer 
- The apartments are having good size and style

Cons: 
- No amenities except small gym and clubhouse with pool table and tv
- No swimming pool or hot tub 
- you CAN NOT OPEN YOUR WINDOWS

- $109 for slow internet and basic cable from DirectTV / SKY Satellite - nobody can provide you a description of what you are paying for, you don't get a real IP address so if your neighbor gets banned from any website / service you are going to be banned too. 

- $25 for Valet Trash that comes after 8pm exactly while you might be cooking but your trashcan have to be outside and if you forget to tie the trash bag they will not take your trash.
the Valet trash is available Sunday - Thursday

- $50 for inside parking or $15 i think for outside 

- You have to pay a solid amount of money for the Common Area Utilities 

- Lots of pets in the building so everywhere smells bad... The building is less than 2 years old but it feels like it's 10 because of the smell and the dirty common areas / hallways / elevator.


The base price of the apartment is $1500 but with all the things that you cannot opt out like media package, common area utilities and parking the total rent is close to $1700. 

Maintenance is slow since you need to wait for couple days to get something fixed - the guy is every day in different property but when he is available he is helpful. 

Weird office hours - good luck talking with somebody ... on the website it says 9am-5:30pm but after 5pm office is closed...  Days are Monday, Tuesday and Friday .... 

Nobody explained to us that the common area utilities are not included in the rent so that came as a surprise - you have to read very well the contract to figure that out. 

Tips:

if you want your pet to live here for free just don't tell anyone from the management - they are not here most of the time so you are totally fine. 

if you ask if the previous tenant had a pet and you get NOT TO MY KNOWLEDGE as an answer this means you are getting apartment with tons of fur in the carpet. 

Ask for cable activation form - you cable might not be active but you will pay for it!

I spoke with many people in the building and everybody is looking forward to move out!

The base cost of the apartment looks cheap but after all enforced services you might end up paying a lot more than you expect.

It’s excellent from the beginning!
Easy communication, easy move in! Beautiful views! Lovely people!
The new management is awesome! The building is nice and clean and well looked after!!

I've lived here for a couple months. I've complained 5 times to the management about people smoking pot out of their apartment and they don't do a thing about it. It clearly states in the lease agreement that smoking is prohibited. The windows are absolutely terrible, there's gaps that let in cold air. They also don't fix the elevators when they are clearly loud. Can't even relax without the noise of screeching.

Consistent noise problems, that forced me to leave due to resulting health concerns. Tried to exit lease early due to extenuating circumstances, but the rental company had zero leniency in this regard.

In addition there was constant vandalism by tenants. The complex would fix, and then there would be more next week.

I've been much happier in other apartments. A shame there is no fair evaluations of circumstances.

This is by far the worse place I've ever lived in. Management would ignore multiple issues brought to their attention. Was impossible to get any response from maintenance after hours. For example, had windows that turned into a waterfall during a complete downpour. It was on a Friday night and tried to get maintenance due to the issue and having small children and it just puddling in the wall. His response was it can wait till Monday. 
Nothing was ever done and when brought to management they said they were unaware and would get it fixed. It wasn't until almost a month later after mold had formed in the walls it was sealed up. They did nothing about the mold.
Tenants would rummage thru the dumpsters and would even try to break into the laundry room to steal from others. Management was well aware of all issues because they had nicknames for the "problem" tenants. There were complete floors full of drug users. Even found dirty needles and told management immediately and it was left there for two or three days until another tenant picked it up and disposed of it.
Don't waste your time

Dirty and small. We had roaches that took management way too long to take care of. Will shake you for every nickel and dime you are worth. Will screw you our of your security deposit. Poor management overall.

(There is new management since I moved so things could have changed)
But- got charged big time when we moved out for a bunch of unnecessary fees when we left the apartment looking exactly as when we got it.

The neighbors trashed the lawn, cigarette butts everywhere and there was broken glass from a shattered window for months that didn't get taken care of.

Laundry constantly didn't work- found a bag of poop in one of the washers. 

Sketchy neighbors- never felt safe coming home late at night and cops were constantly having to patrol the area.

Came home one night to our dog getting stolen right out of our house while my husband was in the shower (door was closed so dog didn't get out on its own) 

Neighbors children drew all over my husbands car with nail polish and crayons.

So, good luck.

The location of our apartment complex is amazing! Close to several major grocery stores, dry cleaners, Walmart, and local restaurants.  We really appreciate the maintenance guy who always takes care of us whenever we have an issue.  We have renewed our lease already and plan to renew again!

The staff is always incredible helpful and always have their door open to residents. The location is centeral to most things and people are always friendly and welcoming. Best part is that, for the price, this place can't be beat.

I recommend this apartment for your family, if you need some repair they will come quickly to fix it.
clean area, the stuff manager are kind and friendly. Thanks for always look after your tenant need.
The staff is wonderful! Since UV Residential has taken over the place just shines! The outside of the apartment is always clean and the office staff is wonderful at talking care of us.

A 2 bedroom, 1 bath tucked away in the corner of a nice quiet complex. Affordable housing it's called. The managers are super friendly. When I moved to Salt Lake City, my car gave all she had and quit just a few days after getting here. Having limited funds and not too many people to rely on. Where home was going to be became a major concern. I needed centrally located, so I could get around easy without a car. The managers worked as a team to quickly get me into a home. Cats welcome! They walked me through the paperwork step by step and took the extra effort when I missed a few boxes on the application. I am now quasi settled and actively pursuing my AA in small business ownership. The neighbors are good and I feel at home. Parkway Commons is a really nice place to live. SO glad I made the move!

I have loved living in this building.  The neighbors I've met have been very nice. I feel safe here. Everything in my apartment is in good working order.  The building is clean and well kept.  The laundry rooms, the common room, the workout space, etc., are all clean and well cared-for.  The building manager has been wonderful to work with.  She has always provided very clear answers to all my questions. She keeps residents informed. She has been most kind and helpful.  The only drawback was the construction noise, as there are a couple of new apartment buildings going up just behind Casa.  I expect that noise will disappear when construction is complete, probably by the end of summer 2023.
They were very thorough  in answering our questions. Made the application  process very easy. I hope we are accepted  to join this property.

So I lived at sun river for over 1 year and it was pretty good. I lived in a loft the price was good for the 1 bed apartment. Maintenence was very quick about fixing my clogged sink.I spent the whole summer at the pool. The thing I loved there is that there were hardly animals. The only thing that I didn't like was parking during the weekend it was full after 6 pm. In the mornings I would see maintenance outside cleaning . The nice office lady's helped me when I gave my notice to move out .About a month after I moved out i did get most of my deposit back.
they will keep money from your security deposit no matter what, even though they write on the contract that you can be refunded in full. be careful what you sign for

I usually don't write any reviews but I thought to myself what the heck this place deserves one. I have lived her for about a year now and I truly love my stay here. I agree, the interior is not upgraded but let me tell you how clean and well kept it was when I moved in, and still is. The grounds are my absolute favorite. My lease will end in a couple of months and I will be moving out but that is only because I am being transferred jobs. Otherwise I would renew my lease with a heartbeat. 
The staff is so wonderful, they're always super sweet to me and they do help me with my needs. I was surprised to read the above review. I am honestly writing this review to simply say, thank you.

I am regrettably a current resident and fully intend to move once my lease is up. the apartment is not in great shape but you get what you pay for, what upsets me the most is the office staff whom are always nasty, ornery and NEVER willing to work with you on anything. i work a steady 9-5 in downtown and fighting traffic to get here by the time they close is impossible so if i have a package dropped off, issue to discuss or whatever the case may be they aren't available. i've always paid my rent early and maintained my living space yet they still treat me like trash and i'm sick of it!
Dirty and not well maintained.  Several apartments had problems with bed bugs and office tried to get tenants to pay for treatments.
These people never answered their phone or responded to my emails when I was apartment hunting. If they can't be bothered to communicate with potential renters then they don't need my business.

DO NOT RENT AN APARTMENT HERE. I would give it zero stars if I could. This place is a complete joke. Completely incompetent office management and staff. I came home twice to unwarranted eviction notices taped to my door which I had to pay legal fees for, even after the office acknowledged that I did pay and that it was the fault of their own online payment system. My heater didn't work the entire time I lived here, even though I was charged for the gas usage of my building divvied up by sq. foot of apartment. Maintenance requests for this, as well as the two massive leaks and broken sink took weeks. Not to mention a yearlong infestation of cockroaches.

Management is unresponsive, I’ve had to fix every issue I’ve had with maintenance by myself with no reimbursement. Constant screaming outside from homeless. Dirty and unsafe. I feel uncomfortable leaving my apartment due to the state of the building and surrounding areas.

While the apartment units themselves are nice, that is about the only good thing. The neighborhood is full of homeless, trash, and people living out of their cars. I have had several interactions where I walk out the front door and there are people either shooting up or smoking meth. SLPD are in the neighborhood almost daily arresting someone. The management company is really hard to get a hold of and repairs take months. Not to mention there was a week when the front door was locked indefinitely and could not be used as an entrance or exit which is a HUGE safety violation. Building is also not ADA accessible. 

When I moved in the apartment was dirty even though they charge you a $200 cleaning fee when you move in. If you're looking for a clean, safe place to live this is definitely not the right place for you.

The management company is difficult to contact and terrible about making repairs.  Heating was out for weeks and now the AC doesn't work in the middle of a heat wave, despite many calls to the managment about this.

Also, they have mice.  It doesn't really work well to trap the mice in your own apartment if the adjacent apartments all have mice as well--they need to be exterminated in the entire complex, but management does not respond to requests about this either.

The gate that separates the parking lot from the street is always broken so the parking lot is often full of homeless people at night which is not comfortable if you have any pets you need to take out. There isn’t any parking outside and the homeless population has gotten so bad on the street that cops seem to avoid it almost completely. There is almost no way to get ahold of management. Many of neighbors and my self have mice.

Unfortunately greedy and unhelpful. I would not recommend this property or company. I would suggest looking else where for a community that values people over money. Will switch up policies without notice and then use the excuses that they can do whatever they want with notice as it’s not “in the lease”.

Classic greedy landlord vs tenant type of property. Stay away and keep you and your family’s safe.

I will start from the beginning. When I first moved in I got sent the wrong contract. I should have taken that as a sign but I believe people are human and mistakes happen. So I didn't even think twice about it. Fast forward to my second week living there, they assigned me a parking spot. I came home to an angry note I had parked in some ones spot. I emailed them to get help, they gave me a new spot. So I switched, the following morning I come out to someone blocking in my car with the most angry note because I had parked in their spot. I ended up having to uber to work because I couldn't get my car out. So again, I email in and got a new spot. One month later I came home and someone was parked in my spot. So I emailed in AGAIN and got a new spot. My apartments constantly wreaks of weed for months. I asked them what they were doing about it they said trying to find the culprit. Months later same question. They can't figure it out. Meantime I have mold growing in my window and instead of fixing the problem they just come clean it, now the mold is back. I gave a 60 day notice and asked with all of these issues if I could please just give notice and move out. They wrote back no, I have to give 60 day written notice anyway and I will pay out my lease. I have never worked with such terrible management who truly couldn't care less. They changed owners half way through my renting and the cornerstone is absolutely terrible.
