I swear this place is low income housing and they didn't disclose it. They make all the pictures look intriguing by acting like there is a workout studio within the apartment, you have to pay a full membership for.  After all of this I moved out of my apartment deep cleaned it so they could list it (which they said they would do) and haven't heard a work back in days.

Avoid unless you’re desperate. Despite being one of the first tenants, so many things broke. I was left without AC for over a month and was met with silence/rude responses “have you tried turning it ON”. Elevator was out multiple times, there is poor service so sometimes the remote access app could not connect to open the garage. 
There is a fire station down the road so be prepared to be woken up throughout the night by sirens. Pilates studio is not included (no resident discount), and resident ‘common area’ has essentially been stripped of furniture. So if you’re wanting the bare minimum while being charged a premium this is the place for you.

Living at 27 nine flats for the past year has been a mess. The management is the worst i’ve seen, they rarely reply to calls or emails, and when they do it’s with an attitude for no reason. My roommate even got stuck in the elevator (that constantly breaks)and i had to call the fire department to get her out. when we tried to tell the management they responded two weeks later with a sassy reply and didn’t do anything about the safety hazard. To top it off the internet speed is very inadequate for the amount of apartments and there’s not even enough parking spaces for half the apartments leased. it’s a nice building and great location but not worth the hassle they put you through.

The management is disorganized, unprofessional, and never available. They never return your calls or emails. My apartment has sewage leaking all over my bathroom and management doesn’t answer their phone.

I really want to like this place. And honestly it's a fine place as far as where you actually live goes, but the management makes it unbearable. I'm talking lost checks, ignored calls, texts, and emails, their voicemail is always full, and they don't have an official leasing office. I have hounded them about a check they lost for three months now and it's still not resolved even though I have record they received it, but they got rid of the person who sent that confirmation so now it's my problem. There's always someone new working there and it shows because they don't have anything together. Have a problem with your apartment? You're probably better off just living with it because it'll take them a month to get it fixed. You want to sign a lease and pay them? You'll have to wait a few months and constantly bug them. Great location and fine enough homes but cheaply made and with management who's impossible to get a hold of you're better off somewhere else.

Construction is poor and multiple units have had problems with leaking roofs.  Break-ins have occurred with little to no acknowledgement from management (to even denying it happened even though multiple police officers are onsite and the tenants state they were broken into).  Overflow parking is TERRIBLE yet management doesn't require people to park their vehicles in their garages.  Inconsistent rules and non-enforcement of current rules.  No clear-cut property manager since the management company is off-site.  Many more issues not listed here.  Not worth the money.  Stay Away!

Management company is an absolute disaster and horrible to work with.  I caught them on multiple accounts trying to overcharge me for renter's insurance (to which I had my own), real estate tax, and trash fees (when they had a dumpster to clean out another unit then charged all the residents for it).  Buildings are poorly built and even poorly maintained.  It was just my wife and I and we were the first to live in the unit for about 8 months.  During the walk through they noted it was in perfect shape and would require no reconditioning.  However, they proceeded to charge us for several items such as repainting, wall touch up (whatever that means), and light bulbs.  Absolutely not worth living here.  Avoid!

My husband and I currently live here and we cannot wait to get out. We have had to go through several changes in management. Parking is a disaster. Our home has continually tried to fall apart, we have been fined and received unreasonable notice, and the price is not at all fair for what you're getting. Do not live here!

Great place if you're on a budget and need to be near downtown. Very close to Trax and many bus stops that go directly to key places like the University of Utah, City Creek, or Gateway.

The property management is very responsive and friendly, one of the best parts about living here. Unit itself is great for what you're getting, no real complaints.

The new Broadmoor is a really cool place to live. There is a nice sense of community with a good mix of people living here. Having my own washer/dryer and my own parking are a huge plus. There are tons of restaurants around the neighborhood, a trax station and a little mini mart across the street. The apartments are very nice inside, central air/heat, new carpet and newer appliances. Rent is super affordable and the property manager Brandon is very on top of things, he is highly accessible and it's great to know that he is there when I need something. The new Broadmoor is a great place to live in SLC!

I have lived in the Broadmoor for about a year so I feel I have an interesting perspective on the realities of this location. First off, Rent is VERY reasonably priced for something close to downtown and the University. There are many food options in the area(4th south, downtown, bars and restaurants along 2nd and 3rd south, 9th and 9th, etc...). They recently renovated some of the units (possibly all of them, but I can't say for certain)-including my own- and they look very good for the price. Nice carpeting and flooring, nicely painted and the kitchen is adequate with a decent amount of storage, lament countertops, and decent appliances. It is nothing fancy but has been perfect for what I need. Rooms are good size and easily fit a queen bed and my dresser. There is a big closet in each room as well. The bathroom is pretty standard with a shower/tub combo. Utilities are one of the few downsides to the Broadmoor. There is no central air given the age of the building and heating is done through steam heat radiators. I didn't think I ran the heat that much in the winter but the money did add up a bit more than I expected. Given the price for rent however, it isn't a huge deal. Reality is, with many older buildings in SLC this is probably standard fare. Each unit gets one reserved parking spot and if needed, there is always plenty of street parking available. The building manager, Derrick, does a good job and is consistently available if needed. The building looks awesome in my opinion, and provides plenty of charm. All in all, I think this is a great place to live as it combines, great location, great price, and well maintained living quarters.

We lived here for almost 6 years, and are moving across the country for work - but will certainly miss living here.  It's a historical building with high ceilings, amazing archways, and nice hardwood flooring and tiled kitchen.  The building manager, Kim, and maintenance are always easy to reach and quick to respond.  You will love it here!

I have never been inside the building, so I can’t say anything about that. However, scheduling a tour with this building was ridiculous. They canceled 20 minutes before my scheduled tour, took days to respond to emails, and kept changing the dates I could come for a rescheduled tour. I would recommend going in person and demanding a tour if you want to see it.
Es un edificio muy nuevo , muy buen servicio en todos los sentidos, es muy económico. En general es un complejo de apartamentos genial.
The property is brand new, and the manager is nice and attentive. Very convenient to the Trax station.

I toured this place four days ago, the studio apartments were so nice and clean and all you could wish for. But there is a huge homeless people issue at this place. A shirtless man was leaning against the entrance along with a bunch of other homeless people. You would have to carry pepper spray or something to defend yourself just to get inside. You do need a key to get in which is nice, but I toured the place at 10am and there were people doing hard drugs with tin-foil in front of the entrance so I couldn’t imagine what it would be like late at night. I saw needles on the curb in front of the building as well. On the backside of the building next door there were multiple tents that homeless people were living in. I could not see myself living here as I’d be much too scared for my own safety as well as worrying if my car would get broken into as there is no garage parking, only street parking. I really wish there wasn’t a homeless people issue here because the apartment complex was so nice. In the pictures where the people are is the front entrance to the building. I hope this can get fixed as it’s such a nice and new place.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review: No fitness center, not well kept, no yard, playground is a safety hazard. Porches are full of rot. Maintenance is very slow to fix anything of they ever do come fix things. Avoid at all costs. This ad says they pay for A/C, they do not.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review:
First, this listing is misleading. There is not a useable tennis court, and they do not have an exercise facility.
Second, the apartments have not been upgraded since the 70’s and they they no longer maintain them or the grounds.
Repair requests are frequently ignored, but the rent is raised every year. This is no longer a good value.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review:
My roommate and I love the amount of space in our apartment! Shelby is wonderful and management is quick to fix things. Very family friendly and affordable!
Only negative to living in the lower-level apartment is spiders and earwigs in the summer.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review: We have been extremely satisfied with living at Willow Brook the past year and a half. Shelby is awesome to work with and management is prompt to fix any problems. The area is quiet and an awesome location, anything you need is within ten minutes. There is plenty of storage and the floor plans are homey. My only complaint would be that snow removal is usually later in the day, not when you need to go to work.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review: This is a great place to live.  The apartments are spacious.  The neighbors are so nice and watch out for each other.  I have never had a problem with parking, but I only have one car.  The maintenance men come within a business day after a request is made and Shelby is very nice, organized, and professional to work with.  Some of our favorite features are the grounds, the playground, and the pool.  It is nice to be able to just go outside and play in a lovely place.

apartmentName: 1455 E 4705 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84117
review:
This used to be a great place to live. Shelby is great to work with on major problems, but her follow through needs work. The rules are not followed by everyone and management doesn't do anything.   The parking is terrible because the residents don't care if they park in two spaces or park at an angle. I have complained about this, but the residents continue to park like crap. There are bikes and toys in front of the doors to the apartments, which not only looks bad but I believe it is against the rules and a possible fire hazzard. The kids run around and not supervised by the parents. Sure a newsletter comes out every once in a while telling parents to watch their kids. The kids play in the parking lot and sometimes won't move out of the way and they play ball too close to the cars. 
When our car was vandalized by one kid, not being supervised, Shelby was a great help in finding who did it. Work orders take forever to be taken care of.  When he does come he doesnt have the right tools to do the job. The parking lot is bad. It is like driving off road and my car isn't made for that. I do like living here and for the most part, management is ok.

apartmentName: 3450 W 2700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84119
review: The owner and manager are extremely rude.  They have about six inspections of your unit w/in a year and you will be given an amount to pay depending on what they fixed or replaced.  They do not provide you with a detailed or original receipt(s) for what they repaired or replaced in the unit.  Just written $ amounts on a walk through form.  For instance, one blind was broken and the entire blind was replaced for $34.  Just got the form that says $50 just to replace the blind.  They just leave a notice on your door saying to pay ASAP!  Once your rent is late an eviction notice besides the threatening texts messages will be delivered.  They are never willing to work with the tenants.  They are so mean and evil.  So many restrictions on using your patio.  They even fired their last landlord and kicked her out of the apartments because the landlord has done her best to help the tenants who need more time to pay their rent.  I do NOT recommend this place!!  Thinking of contacting GET GEPHARDT regarding this place.  They need to be on media so future tenants can avoid trying to rent from here.

Amenities and resident events make this property outstanding. While the apartments are a bit small but quite nice, it’s the gym classes, parties, social events, gym pool and roofdecks that make Nema unmatched to live at. If the pool was a bit warmer this would be 5 star review! Note most amenities are closed Or restricted as of May 2020.
NEMA has amenities such as valet parking, pool area, bbq area, and a rooftop where you can relax and take San Francisco living all in. They are also pet friendly!

Looked at many apartments prior to moving to SF and Nema stood out.  Rents in the city are sky high anywhere in the city and Nema offers relative value with nice apartments and great amenities.  There are always community events and the staff are excellent.

If you can afford inner-city rents check out Nema.  Great apartments, great staff and multiple amenities including an excellent gym.  Noise is minimal and location is within walking distance to the city and easy access to Muni and Bart.  If you have a car the building has a Valet service which is included with the parking fees.  The early stage crowd is slowly transitioning - a good thing.

Fabulous apartment well located to downtown and Mission.
Great view of the city and amazing amenities at your disposal. 24h staff on call to help you with anything.

I am deeply dissatisfied with the service provided by Gateway Apartments. After initially booking an apartment and paying a $500 deposit, I later decided to cancel within the acceptable timeframe outlined in their refund policy. Despite this, it has now been two months, and Gateway Apartments has failed to return my deposit.

Throughout this ordeal, their communication has been consistently dishonest. Despite repeated assurances via email and screenshots supposedly showing the refund process, the reality is they have not returned my money. It feels like a blatant case of theft—Gateway Apartments has essentially withheld $500 from me under false pretenses.

This level of deceit towards customers, whether they are confirmed renters or potential clients, is completely unacceptable. I strongly advise anyone considering renting from Gateway Apartments to reconsider. Their conduct is unethical and demonstrates a lack of respect for customers' financial trust.

In conclusion, I urge prospective tenants to think twice before engaging with Gateway Apartments. Their treatment of my deposit has been unacceptable, and I will pursue its return through all available avenues. This experience has left me deeply disappointed and wary of their business practices.

Great views is all you get. 
If you like to live in an apartment that will constantly shut off water and call it an emergency, this is the one for you. (How about 3 times in one week? Followed by - oops we need to shut it down again cause we screwed up!) 
If you love living in a place where they constantly have to check fire alarms every few weeks and have it fail when there is an actual fire, the gateway is your answer. 
Want to be troubled by fake noise harassment claims in the middle of the night? come here! 
Want to live in the 22nd floor and get fit? You’ve come to the right place, the gateway will disable elevators for you and make you climb the stairs every other week.

My stuff got stolen from the laundry room and building management did nothing. They kept ping ponging me one to another for a couple of days with zero outcome.

Area is not super safe either - there are some homeless / drug addicts hanging around, especially around Safeway.

Each time I had issues with apartment staff did nothing and didn't show any intention to help either

I feel like I struck gold when I moved into The Gateway seventeen years ago.  It has everything I could wish for: a well-maintained building, a spacious apartment with a fabulous view, a downtown location with a park outside the front door and spectacular bay views from my living room and bedroom windows.   It also has a balcony which was indispensable during 2020 when Covid kept us indoors more than usual.  My balcony became an essential part of my day-to-day outdoor pleasures.

People come from all over the world to live here so it is an exiting environment.  It is also a very friendly one.  I have made many friends here who share my interests and participate in similar activities like walking, working out, dining out, and enjoying the many cultural activities near-bye.

The Complex’s management and maintenance  team has also played an important role in my appreciation of The Gateway.   They respond promptly to my requests for service or maintenance and are very knowledgable and respectful.  I am very grateful to them because I know that they are exceptional, as are both our doormen who are very friendly and maintain a high level of security.

 If you are reading this with the goal of moving to an apartment, The Gateway would be a great choice. Helen J.
I have lived here since 1995 and love it ! The office staff, security guards, doormen (lady) and maintenance are the best.

Other than the price of renting in San Francisco and the two and half months deposit, the complex is not bad. No noisey neighbors, great views, excellent location minus the noisy parrots at 6am or homeless in the parks. It is well maintained minus the trash shoot getting clogged. My only complaint is they keep the heat on even in the summer when it's above 85/90 degrees. I know state law mandates heat but perhaps we should inact cooling mandates or limit heating like they do in Canada (air mandatory at temperatures above 78degrees outside) I'm guessing the amount of retirees need to stay warm instead of moving to Florida. Perhaps get a blanket if you are cold at night at 75 degrees?
Property is great but leasing management is non-existent and super not helpful.

Pretty upscale building with relatively quiet neighbors, but some of the cost cutting practices here are pretty shady. They only clean the windows once a year, which means your beautiful floor to ceiling glass is usually dirty. They also fold the utilities cost of unoccupied apartments into occupied ones, so you end up paying over $100/month just for water and sewage. These are things you don't learn until after you move in and it's too late.

Moved in about 4 months ago and couldn't be happier.  The amenities are exceptional (large gym, great common lounge space) and there's a roof deck with the best view of SF available.  The one bad note would be that there seem to be a few bad eggs in the building who don't like to pick up after themselves, and this has trickled down to the rest of us in the form of restrictions on common area usage.  In general though, this is a great building!

The rooftop of this building it's worth all that we're paying for it. 360 view of the city 28 floors high, simply amazing. The gym is decent, and management is great. There is washer/dryer in every unit and the apartments are spacious with great views to. Only complaint is that there is not enough parking but doesn't matter if you don't need a car. Great apartments overall so far

I literally can't believe how nice our apartment is and how nice our amenities are for the price we are paying. Everyone working at reception is extremely helpful and friendly. The rooftop views are truly incredible. Couldn't be happier living in this building.

388 Beale is run by a community that is solely interested in taking as much of your money as possible. Regardless of how you fill out your pre-move in inspection, clean the apartment before moving out, or how you maintain the apartment, their goal is to add as many charges as possible at the end (which you are not present for and cannot dispute), and take all of that money from your deposit in order to ensure you get none of it back. It is sleazy and underhanded and I was extremely disappointed to have gone through this experience recently.

great property but horrible application progress. UDR sucks. UDR property management is horrible. They reply every 3 days or more, sometimes they just ignore my emails for forever. UDR is never reachable.

I live in one of the towers.  The elevators break down about twice a month.  One of the other towers had an explosion when a meth lab went bad.  Your car will be broken into.  The grounds are poorly kept and filthy.  Maintenance is slow to respond.  Asking for help at Resident Services will only get you a runaround with typical corporate stock responses, such as "I've sent a message about this and they will get back to you" and then they never do.  Mention it, and the response is then "that wasn't my fault, I sent the message" with zero follow-up. They will string you along until you give up.

Security is a joke.  Call them, and they will just tell you to call the police.  They are not there for your safety.

Eventually, you will find homeless people living in the storage locker areas, doing drugs.  Park Merced has been notified repeatedly about this, and has done nothing about it.  Your belongings are not safe in the basement storage areas.

I moved in August (2022), and at the end of March (2023) there was a leak from raining that day that eventually broke into a hole in the ceiling of the bathroom. After putting in a maintenance request it took more than a week for someone to look at it, and they tried to tape it and said "there's nothing I can do right now, we’ll reach out." A week later someone else checked it and they gave me a dehumidifier for the bathroom, and now I have to pay a higher electric bill due to the dehumidifier being on. I asked the worker how long it would take to get this fixed and I’m told to ask another day. Since then, I’ve been calling maintenance several times a week asking for an answer, but they won’t even call back even after they told me they would reach out the next day, all they say is “we don’t know right now”. The first several times I called they didn’t even know the maintenance request existed. It’s now May (2023) and there’s still a hole in the roof, in the ceiling of the bathroom, and it leaks whenever it rains. I would make a longer post about how inconsiderate the staff is but I’m just trying to get this ceiling fixed, it gets really cold in the morning and night inside my apartment since there’s a hole in the ceiling.

Definitely a mold problem and bug problem here. There are many squatters here with many suspicious looking people going in and out. When reported, they just say there is not supposed to be people living in the unit, but does nothing about it. So people live here rent free, while actual renters have to pay for these squatters water bill too. Do not move here. Many car jacking around too. Just not a safe place.

I have to laugh at the Excellent blended rating on this site, something must be wrong with the algorithm. 

Today's episode with the Maintenance Department. Last week I kept hearing noises either on the roof or in the attic (rats?!) so I submitted a request gave them permission to enter. One day I came back, I could tell someone was in my apartment because the workers lock the door with a special button in the door that residents don't usually use. (why do they keep using it, I don't know). There was no prior notice, or any notes afterwards to let me know someone would be in my place. How hard would it be to leave a sticky note?

Same thing happened today, except for this time I had trouble opening the door. I call the maintenance number and wait on hold. I ended up walking to the office (about 10 minutes away), and when I arrived I was still on hold. The woman told me she just got off the phone and was going to answer me, in the meantime there was an entire office full of people behind their screens, guess no one was told to answer the phone. As I was talking to her the maintenance director came out of his office, and told me to go back to my place and someone would meet me there. I walked back, no one was waiting. I called again, was asked to wait another 10 minutes, and finally someone showed up to open the door. 

A more serious case was about six months ago.  On a Monday morning in March I turned on the gas oven which I rarely use. Couple minutes later I smelled gas, so I turned it off. I turned on the oven light, didn't see anything. I opened the door, a ball of flame jumped in my face. My hair, eyebrows, eyelashes, all singed. Days later there were still small pieces falling off. I called maintenance right away and they sent the Director of Maintenance. He tried to turn on the oven, smelled the gas and turned it off. He called one of his guys, and said on the phone "there is something going on with the ignitor, come check it out." An hour later the crew showed up and the first thing they said was "that's an original, that's old."

After all this Residence Services still insist that I should be grateful I got a new oven out of this. Why? It's not my house! Why was there an old oven in the apartment that would suddenly spew fire? I didn't ask for this, just like I didn't ask for smoky hair, burned hairline and missing eyebrows. 

So far all the workers I met are nice and very competent at their jobs. Communication and organization is the problem.

All around excellent experience! Andy was a great listener and worked with me to find my perfect home. Parkmerced has so much to offer as far as activities and events. I'm really looking forward to being a part of the community.

I witnessed my first police chase here... My partner and I play a drinking game every time we hear sirens or drug addicts fighting. There is mold everywhere and If you call them, they just paint over it and blame you for not keeping your window open.But that’s hard to do when you have to decide between getting robbed or living with mold. I’ve lost so many dresses and shows here due to mold The leasing office only exist to collect rent and tell you when your bill is due. They are no help what so ever. However, the apartment is very spacious with large windows, which is how they trapped us...
Absolutely horrid management and maintenance.  Never ever seen anything like it.

They say they have working security cameras. They have a security team. When your mail get stolen from the common area or bike stolen from their "secure" bike area (that you pay for the privilege of using) they refuse to do anything. Not check security cameras or even take a report. They are horrible. Absolutely horrible service.

These apartments are really nice and close by to the university. I walk to school everyday and the Bart station is also a rough ten minute walk. Literally almost any store you can think of and a movie theatre is nearby. The downside is three things: 1. Parking. I personally do not like that in already paying a lot of money plus $150 to park in the garage!  Parking in the street is available but very limited and it's hard to find a space.
2. Fire fighters everyday. Since I have been here for about a month since August there has been a fire alarm pulled multiple times in this apartment and nearby ones late at night. Min. 10-15 times. 
3. Rent. It is an ok price but as far as the luxury of the apartments it is very barren and with metal doors which to me doesn't give a home feeling.

It's very rare to see such a huge nice apartment community in the city! it's like you are in your own city! I love the quietness and the green space around. But behold LOTS of students and young ppl live here so loud parties and screams never end all days and nights.... also property management really lacks here they never pick up phone and ignore many maintenance requests leasing office staff mostly not that friendly either. Apt finishings and kitchens are all very old original ...

I've lived in this apartment for 6 years now and have sent in numerous Maintenance requests to fix the mold that has taken over my apartment. Also, there seems to be a never ending supply of potato bugs in the carpet. I think they realized that the apartments are rent-controlled, so they made themselves at home! These mold and bug problems aren't my fault. If you ask anyone in Parkmerced, they'll share the same story. These building are so old and don't have proper ventilation. I've bought charcoal bags, fans, humidifiers.. it's crazy! This is seriously bad for my health and feel that allergies are crazier than ever.

I've heard that these apartments are awaiting demolition in the next few years, so maybe that's why Management has changed numerous times and does the bare minimum. 

Yes, there is rent control, but the amount of mold and bug infestations are just not worth it.

I am currently a student at San Francisco State University and I had to find an apartment that was close to school and on the low side price wise. I live in a 2-bedroom 2-bathroom apartment, which I share with three other people beside myself. I have been in the apartment for a year now and will only continue to live here for one more year. The apartment itself is pretty spacious but honestly there are only a few pros and then some major cons. Some of the pros include allowing pets, being close to public transportation and SFSU, community events, work out facilities, and an online portal. The cons include terrible upkeep with apartment maintenance, No screens in windows whatsoever, rent increases without direct notification, the staff does not get back to you on your request unless you pester them in person, and it's impossible to make changes to your lease without moving out completely and signing a new lease. Bottom line I really only live here because it's so close to my school and because the rent is reasonable for San Francisco, but the service is mediocre at best.

Apt. Bldg.has: Cable,Internet,Laundry Room, Business Center, Exercise/ Weight Room, Elevators and Courtesy Patrol.
The Apt Complex is right across from SFSU. Next to the Olympic Gulf Course,
A couple of blocks from the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Zoo.
The City bus (Muni) comes right onto the complex.
The Bart is only one bus stop a way.
Lastly, there is city and reserved parking at Parkmerced.

Not sure how the tower units are, but I live in one of the townhouse units and generally, I like it. Original hardwood floors, a huge kitchen sink and lots of light in every room. Rent is lower than a lot of neighborhoods in the city. It's also right along the M line. There are a few negatives though. Being next to SF State, there are a ton of student renters around here that treat the complex as an extension of the school. There are often broken bottles and plastic cups littered around, and the neighborhood is significantly louder during the school year. The parking situation is not ideal. The parking garage is pretty far from most units, covered parking is $$ and pretty tight to fit into for a lot of cars, and during the school year, finding street parking is almost impossible in the evening.

Con: I've lived at Parkmerced for several years in one of the towers and it is absolutely disgusting. They're very good at slapping paint on new apartments, but as soon as you become a tenant you're just a number and you're neglected. I've seen several (about 7) massive rats in the basement while going to the laundry room and have informed management, but they've done nothing about it. These rats are massive, about the size of  footballs. I've also seen roaches everywhere, both in my apartment and all over the basement. Again, I've informed management and they pretend to do something about it. Lastly, I along with several neighbors have dealt with bed bugs. I am a working professional, and i dont have random people staying at my house, nor do i travel, so we believe they are spreading through the building. Also, another complaint I have is parking. I pay over a hundred for my parking spot which progressively they increase rent on; while some people have theirs at 50... it's incredibly frustrating.

Pros: The location of the property is great, and the apartment itself is large. That's about it.

Happy apartment hunting!

Constant additional fees and increases. All residents are now required to pay $70 a month for new “Technology Rent” because the apartment has a contract with a ISP  called Gigstreem, with no way to opt out. If you work from home at all this is 100% a reason to avoid this building, since you will essentially be paying for internet twice if you don’t want to use this company (they are constantly sending emails about internet outages). They also sold off a floor of parking and turned it into hourly paid spots, and then forced all residents to pay for reserved parking. Expect the actual price you pay to keep increasing with fees

Channel is a lovely place to live! Beautiful amenities, beautiful courtyard. Close proximity to the Caltrain is hard to beat. SUPER busy neighborhood during concerts, baseball games, basketball games, and other events. 

However, policy changes have made this place a very difficult place to live for the last six months. No one seems happy. Changing parking policies mean there is nowhere to park, despite paying $370/month. Forcing everyone to move to the second floor was done - until they didn't have enough spaces to accommodate everyone. Imagine to overnight worker who can't find a space at 6:00am after 12 hours at work. It took months to get the security gate fixed, and they allowed it to stay open during that time. This likely accounted for all the illegal parking on the second floor. Changes with gate access left residents stranded outside the entire building after 10:00pm outside. 

A change to the gym meant removal of all spin bikes with a SINGLE rowing machine. Very disappointed that they didn't consult residents before making the change. 

Sure, rent seems to be market value. When you figure in the cost of $380/ month parking and their incorporated $200/month utilities, your cost-of-living is much higher than expected, even when they give you an "all-in cost" on their website. 

Glad I had someone to splits costs with, but I won't be staying here past our one year lease.

I moved into CMB last week and had an outstanding experience. The leasing team Derek and Cliff were and continue to be so helpful and friendly.

Also, the servicing team, especially Chris the Service Manager, has been so helpful. The service is prompt with a focus on quality and they go above and beyond to help.

I highly recommend CMB. It's clean and maintained extremely well.

Best place to live in SF.  Beautiful apartments, well maintained and the management team is awesome!  The pool and outside space is gorgeous and they have fitness classes with great instructors.  5 stars!!!

The location is great, close to CalTrain and Muni; will only get better whenever the Central Subway is completed. 

Unfortunately management is terrible. One of the doors on the Third Street side of the building has been stuck and requires a double pull of the door to open for at least 3 months and now one of the doors on the Fourth Street side of the building is out of commission as well. I am still unsure if the fire alarm actually works since it went out of service a few months ago. We were told it was fixed about a week after it broke, but there was a sticker on the front door stating that the alarm was not working. That sticker is gone, but no communication was sent out stating it was fixed. 

Channel utilizes the Luxor Locker package delivery system, but charges you $100/year to use it. That wouldn't be so bad if they used it properly. Half of my packages go missing because (and I have seen this happen) the concierge will let the delivery drivers into the lobby package room without scanning the packages. This means I get no notification and have no way of getting my package out of the room without having the concierge let me in.

The security here is also very weak. The garage gate stays open all day due to the addition of Gus's Market downstairs and management has promised to put a second gate going to the second floor, but that still has not happened (it has been 6 months). This means that anyone can just come in and park in the garage or peak around in the cars. The elevators are now secured with fob access only, but that means nothing because the stairs still are completely insecure. I guess the hope is that the "bad guys" are lazy and just won't take the stairs.

I have lived in Channel Mission Bay since June 2016 (13 months) and will not be renewing my lease this fall.

My rating is solely due to repeated failures of air conditioning. In 6 written requests over 9 months, I document failures of the A/C compressor, thermostat, and coolant systems. This has resulted in the A/C only being functional for 20 minutes every 24 hours, insufficient to cool the unit below 75 degrees, sometimes blowing hot air instead of cold, and reaching over 80 degrees during the May/June 2017 heat wave.

As a sufferer of migraines triggered by heat, the reason I chose CMB over comparable buildings in Mission Bay was air conditioning, which they advertise widely. Since the unit is detrimental to my health, I will not be renewing my lease. There is no reason to pay the premium for A/C in this building when this feature does not work. Other features are equivalent to less-expensive neighboring buildings on 4th St (Venue, Strata, MB 360, Azure).

Because service on these requests has only fixed issues temporarily and the issues above remain after 9 months, I conclude that the faulty HVAC was known to management. They did not disclose this issue to me when I signed the lease, when I asked specifically about it. I was misled on the condition of the unit.

I have a lost confidence in the overall condition of the unit and in the management company, UDR. I will be forwarding this to my HR department to no longer recommend UDR properties for short-term housing.

Ever since UDR took over as management there has been nothing but issues. Tenants not able to receive their packages, issues with the parking garage multiple times a month, and no clear way to reach anyone accountable to anything on the property. 

As much as I love the location I wouldn’t suggest that anyone live here.
The location is excellent. The residents can get to Target, Best Buy, Costco, Bed Bath & Beyond very easily. Not to mention that the apartment is clean and modern.

I initially requested a parking spot within the building at the end of October 2023. In March 2024, I was finally offered a parking spot in the building across the street for $450 per month, with the understanding that I would remain on the waitlist for a spot in my own building. Despite this, the promised parking spot in my building only recently (October 2024) became available—after one year on the waitlist.

During the period I was parking across the street, despite the parking fee of $450 per month, I frequently returned home from work around 9 or 10 pm to find the parking garage completely full. On several occasions, I couldn’t find a parking spot and had to park elsewhere. I often had to return late at night to move my car into the garage because I was uncomfortable leaving it on the street overnight, especially in this neighborhood. On other occasions, I was allowed to park in the 150 Van Ness service spot but had to move my car by 7 am to avoid towing, disrupting my schedule.

Despite paying a substantial monthly fee for what was supposed to be a guaranteed parking spot, I often found myself without one. The garage frequently hosts vehicles from the Academy of Art and other events, with cars sometimes parked outside designated spots, reducing available spaces and making navigation in the garage difficult.

When I was finally offered a parking spot within 150 Van Ness, it came with an increased monthly fee of $500 for a flat space, compared to the $450 I was already paying. My requests to maintain my current rate, given the numerous inconveniences, were declined.

They also offer stacker spaces for $350 per month; however, these come with inconveniences such as waiting for the stackers to move into position, which takes around three minutes. There are about a dozen cars in one stacker, and if someone else is moving in or out, you will have to wait. And even after I accepted a new parking spot at 150 Van Ness—which was supposed to be my assigned spot—I came back late from work to find another car parked in it. So I had to park outside again!

If you rely on parking and value well-maintained amenities, be prepared for potential challenges and additional costs. The decline in service and maintenance has overshadowed what could be an excellent living experience. While I otherwise enjoy living at 150 Van Ness, these ongoing issues have made it difficult to recommend this building to others.

Despite its promising amenities, such as the golf simulator and basketball gym, the apartment building falls short in several areas. The decision to implement a reservation system for the golf simulator, even after the COVID era, seems excessive and inconvenient for residents. Moreover, the recent introduction of pickleball at the expense of basketball in the gym reflects a disconnect between management and resident preferences, compounded by the alleged dismissal of resident feedback through purportedly fabricated polls. 

Additionally, the discrepancy between advertised 24/7 security and the reality, along with misinformation regarding access to the basketball gym and deposit procedures, undermines trust and transparency within the community. Addressing these issues with improved communication and genuine resident engagement is essential for fostering a more harmonious and fulfilling living experience for all tenants.

Despite promises of top-notch amenities and round-the-clock security, the reality of living here has been far from satisfactory. I've been a resident since 2019, and the decline in quality has been glaring.

Initially, the amenities were impressive, but they've steadily eroded over time. What was once a freely accessible golf simulator is now bogged down by cumbersome reservation systems. To add insult to injury, management has begun nickel-and-diming residents with charges for gym, basketball, and pool access.

Worst of all is the false sense of security touted by management. Claims of 24/7 security are laughable at best. In truth, I've never seen security personnel patrolling the premises, and safety concerns are routinely ignored.

The basketball gym situation epitomizes the mismanagement plaguing this place. Residents are barred from playing basketball on days reserved for pickleball, despite the gym lying empty. It's a slap in the face to those who pay a premium to live here.

In conclusion, the broken promises and declining standards make it impossible to recommend this place to anyone. Management needs to address these issues urgently if they hope to salvage any semblance of reputation.

I've been a resident here since 2019, and while initially impressed with the amenities and management, the experience has taken a sharp downturn. What was once a great living space has become increasingly disappointing.

Firstly, amenities have been steadily stripped away without any significant additions. The golf simulator, once freely accessible, is now reservation-only, and additional charges have been introduced for gym, basketball, and pool usage. This feels unjustified given the already high rent we pay.

My primary grievance is the mismanagement of the basketball gym. It's frustrating to see it sit empty on days designated for pickleball, while basketball enthusiasts are denied access despite having paid for the privilege.

In short, the decline in quality and unreasonable restrictions make it difficult to justify the high cost of living here. Management needs to address these issues promptly to retain residents' trust and satisfaction.

No one responds to you, you need to call and email multiple times for a simple message and you may not get a response, there is no parking space, the elevator often needs repairs, if you are going to choose a high-end apartment, do not choose them because of their discounts, live in The experience was terrible, the smell of the trash cans in the corridor was disgusting

In the picture it looks nice but if you go there yall see what im talking about. I dont recommend this place

So we have been living here for many years and unfortunately, things are getting bad. Leasing office does things without give advance notice that they are going to change some things around the apartment complex. We always have broken laundromats and elevators. The only plus is the parking space and quiet location away from the city.

I currently got very lucky and landed a private bedroom/bath in a house with 6 other girls. I moved into this building in March 2015. I found the Apartment on Apartments.com great site btw. I have lived in SF my whole life and didn't really know about this place. The rent is affordable (for SF standards) pool, jacuzzi, steam rooms, sauna's, tennis courts and right across the street from Lake Merced. You are a block from the beach, but it doesn't get too windy because the sand dunes block the heavy winds. I definitely recomend. Oh and you cant hear your neighbors at all.

This building has packages stolen 24/7 and the manager Gunther does nothing about it. People break into the property all the time, break into apartments and time after time, nothing is done about it. All of UDR’s other properties require fobs to get up the elevator, Edgewater is the only exception. This company cares very little for its residents and their safety. West Elevator is always broken, property needs to be renovated ASAP.
The amenities are nice however the location is not very safe and I have had packages stolen as well. Area is not too safe and the price is very expensive

PLEASE BE AWARE: EDGEWATER IS NOT A SAFE COMMUNITY!

Over the past few weeks, three apartments have been broken into at night when the occupants were at home and had property stolen. There have been numerous cars broken into, windows smashed, common area furniture and TVs stolen, bikes stolen from a double locked enclosure and a homeless woman has repeatedly been trespassing in the common areas. Patio furniture was thrown off the 4th story onto Berry Street. Yesterday, my neighbor's dog barked at someone trying to open her locked door.

We had a community meeting about these incidents in which about 30 residents attended. The representative from Edgewater spent the 1st hour refusing to answer our appropriate and rational questions about details of the crimes. For example, would they consider more lighting, a faster garage door, more cameras, even if they don't work, security guards, etc... anything to help keep us safe? The representative informed us that those security measures were "too expensive."

There are renovations happening throughout the public areas of the complex: new carpets, a giant chess board, a jacuzzi, new landscaping being installed. We questioned whether funds, when available, could be re-directed towards safety measures instead in the future. The answer was no. Edgewater, we were told, is part of a "publicly traded company that has a responsibility to its shareholders" to produce profit. 

Edgewater's focus during the entire meeting was only on how *we* are responsible for keeping our community safe. At the end, the representative stated simply: "Edgewater is not responsible for your safety." That is an important policy statement that the residents of Edgewater and those thinking of becoming residents here need to be aware of. 

"Edgewater is not responsible for your safety." 

Until this policy changes, we can expect very little to be done about the security issues in our community. Please keep this in mind and live elsewhere, where your safety IS a concern.

-Fitness center
-Nice lounge with fireplace and large TV

I have lived here for three years. 2000 Post has very few redeeming features, and I will leave as soon as my rent increases from covid rates.

UDR and the management teams that run this building are grossly incompetent. In every situation where the building needs repairs, changes, cleaning, or service, the management makes it abundantly clear that they paid the absolute lowest bid. Communication with them is impossible. Each time I've tried to correspond with managment via email, it is ignored. When I go to the onsite staff in person, they passionately promise and guarantee they will resolve whatever it is, and immediately forget about it. Here are some examples of problems we've been facing as a community in 2000 Post recently.

In the past two months, at least one of the three elevators has been broken each week.

In the past year, a car and a motorcycle have been stolen from the "secure underground garage" and two more cars had windows smashed without so much as an email from management.

Cleanliness - Trash often piles up in common areas and dirt builds up in the pool. When presented with picture evidence - management's response was "The pool is cleaned every day". Apparently not.

I have been around many of the different high rises in SOMA and this is by far the worst one.

I have been a resident at The Rise for four years. I moved here at the end of 2020, and was offered a rent concession as a move-in offer, which I gladly accepted. What attracted me the most to the building was its proximity to the freeway (I work in SSF), its amenities (mostly for my dog) and appliances offered in the apartment. After spending a lengthy amount of time at this residence, I have few comments:
Pros
Amenities - Beautiful rooftop, bbq, dog wash, dog run, communal kitchen, outdoor movie/game area
Apartment - Spacious for price, with newer appliances (dishwasher, washer, dryer, range)
Off street parking available - I initially parked on the street when I moved in, but my car was broken into three times within the first year. The management was nice enough to offer me free secure parking, as a concession.
Building maintenance (the staff is very helpful and timely in getting things done)

Cons
The neighborhood - The Rise is located directly behind a homeless shelter and on a daily basis one can find people sleeping on the street or rampant drug use in any direction, within blocks of this building 
Building security - Despite the many attempts that the building has made at securing the site, there have been multiple break-ins and robberies in the garage, mail room and lobby every single year that I've lived here
Front desk - There has been so much turnover with the people that work at the front desk, that I can barely remember any of their names. They generally stay for only a few months, then move on

Overall, I've enjoyed living here with my dog mainly due to convenience, but as the neighborhood and safety around the building has shown no improvement over the last four years, it might be time to find a new residence.

At once I was greeted with friendly and helpful staff members who were quickly able to solve some of my initial problems before I’d even had a chance to voice them. I admit, having my own washer dryer has a lot to do with that!
The Rise is well maintained and managed. I'm comfortable living there and would recommend the building to other's.

I love living at The Rise Hayes Valley! I have been provided excellent service from the leasing office while living here, and although there were some hiccups, I feel like that's to be considered whenever moving to a new place.

I've been here for about a month, but everyone is so kind, the space is clean, and management really tries their best to assist you with your needs. There are also a ton of amenities which is what I love, and the lounge is a super comfy area for anyone that is a resident here.

Living the Hayes valley for almost 3 years it has been, nice and staff are very friendly and ready to help we you need it.  I am happy living here and is also pet friendly and they have treats for the dog.

The Rise is a well located premium property.
I'd recommend it to others.

When I read all the reviews here, I still didn't believe that the noise issues could be so bad in the new building. Don't make mistakes like me. There are terrible insulation issues. You can hear how your neighbors walk above you. Just normal walking, not even running.

Walls are as thin as the other reviewers say. Water has been shut off multiple times during this experience for various reasons - at times there has been no hot water, and at times no water at all. 

Amenities are nice, but the basics (a quiet place to live, consistent water) just aren't there.

I had a horrible experience living here. I specifically had asked for a quiet unit and thought I was lucky to get one on the top floor, corner. However, since they couldn't show me the actual unit but only a model of it, it turned out that my bed was right above the main entry doorway, which was extremely loud when anyone entered or exited, and this happened very frequently. I asked them to put some kind of damper on the heavy metal door, but they did nothing about it. They gave me the option to move out, but I lost my concession and had to find another place to live after just two months.
It's a wood-frame constructed building. You can hear every sound from neighbors. Please don't consider to move-in here unless it's top floor unit.

Totally agree with a majority of the reviews here that mention the noise levels. Living here was great until the neighbors started moving in. However, after a majority of the units became occupied there isn't a day that goes by without being woken up by noise coming from upstairs and from the side neighboring units. I noticed at one point that my neighbors were not the problem, but instead they were just going about their daily lives. The wood frames must be made out of single ply cardboard.
Do yourself a favor and either live on the top floor of this apartment or never move here at all. Unless your neighbors know how to levitate you will never be able to sleep in peace.

The noise insulation between rooms is unlivable.  If you have a a shared bedroom wall, the other room can hear everything and vice versa.  Also from the the bedroom you can hear every room in the apartment.  And not just a little, in clear detail.  This is a red flag and I would not have moved in if I knew this.

The building amenities are nice, but they don't make up for the super thin walls.  Also I second all the reviews about the ceiling and floor noise insulation between units.  Although for me, that's not nearly as much of an issue as the in unit noise insulation.
Excelente servicio muy eficiente por parte del personal
The building is brand new, clean, smells good, and luxurious. Amenities are awesome. Staff are polite, respectful, and efficient.
New facilities, clean and hygienic Spacious room, convenient parking Service is also very good Praise and praise
It’s the community that would satisfy all of your needs for home comfort, family/friends gathering, relaxation and fitness.

I have been working with Bobby P and I couldn't be happier with my experience. He has been incredibly helpful and responsive, answering all of my questions and guiding me through the leasing process. He was patient with me as I deliberated on which unit to choose and provided me with all the necessary information to make an informed decision.

I would say I am not an easy customer to deal with. I am really impressed with how responsive via emails, chat, etc.

I would recommend this place if you are looking for someone to walk you through the process.

They also have a lot of different benefits and parks and the pricing is a great value compared to other places!

Dealing with The Civic’s property management has been one of the most frustrating experiences. Getting responses from them on basic issues was nearly impossible, and every request felt like an uphill battle.

	•Utility Costs: I was told my utility bill would be around $60/month due to low-flow faucets, but my first bill was $180/month—triple the expected amount. Turns out, they use RealPage, a system under DOJ investigation and banned by the Board of Supervisors.
	•Move-in Chaos: Once I signed the lease, I never received move-in instructions. I had to scramble on moving day and even lacked access to the freight elevator.
	•Noise Complaints Ignored: When I asked for updates regarding excessive noise from a nearby construction site, management simply sent a generic monthly pamphlet with no useful information and told me to reach out to the construction team myself.
	•Locker System Issues: Instead of helping with access issues, they referred me to the locker provider, even though the contract is with the building, not residents.
	•Gym Wipes: I requested sanitizing wipes for the gym six or seven times via email. After they assured me it would be resolved, I returned to the gym—and nothing had changed. They blamed maintenance, acting as if they had no control over the issue.

If you’re considering living here, just be prepared to handle everything yourself because the property management is either unresponsive, incompetent, or just doesn’t care.

Since posting my other online review, I’ve noticed a shift in how the new leasing personnel interact with me—there’s a clear sense of coldness whenever I walk into the building, and it’s happened multiple times so far.

5 days a week, a garbage pickup truck stop by and make a ridiculous noise almost everyday around 3am. 
That and you can hear people screaming and making noise at the building right next to it (San Francisco Department of Public Health).
I work from home so I spent few months everyday at this place, and not a moment of peace here 24/7. 

It was slightly cheaper then other similar buildings nearby, and you'll find out the reason for it in the first night. 

Please, Don't make the same mistake I made.

It's important to be well informed before making a decision about this apartment building. In my personal experience, the construction of the building lacks proper insulation and soundproofing. This means that you can hear many things happening between floors, including your neighbors' footsteps, the dropping of even small/light objects, and yes, even conversations. Unfortunately, this is not an exaggeration and can be very disruptive for anyone who needs or wants to study, read, watch movies, sleep, or concentrate on anything. I feel bad for potentially impacting any business' revenue, but it's important to share my experience so others can avoid the frustration and stress that comes with living in this "luxury" apartment building. Despite the nice appearance of the building, the lack of soundproofing is a major issue that cannot be ignored. My time here at 450 Avery has easily been the worst housing experience that I have ever been through. However, you don't have to take my word for it. You can just ask the leasing agent, and unless they are willing to lie to you, they will have to confirm most everything in this review. Management here is almost completely feckless, so if you move in and have any issues, don't expect much help. The only positive aspect is the friendly and helpful concierge staff.

The apartments have a defect in kitchen ventilation so regularly I smell burning oil and smoke in my apartment.

The floors between the apartments are not very sturdy (I hear my neighbor’s every footstep and vibration). Another neighbor of mine has cigarette smoke fill his unit.

So unless you are lucky and get mannered neighbors who actually read the house rules (this is why I gave them 3 stars instead of 2), this is a hard place to live.

Management should do a better job of enforcing house rules. If you lease here, ask about the unit your moving in if they had any problems with adjacent neighbors and do not accept the “this is San Francisco and normal” because it is not acceptable answer — the house rules specifically state no smoking and no noise at night. Make sure you find the truth before making decision to move in.

I have moved out of Paramount for over  3 months now but never managed to get back my deposit, despite calling and emailing management and account manager multiple times. They have stopped replying to my emails in the recent weeks. Had to write this review because it ruins the whole experience.

Lovely views in a wonderful neighborhood. The process of moving into the apartment proved to be a major letdown. Staff knowledge was inconsistent or non-existent. We love living here, despite the shortcomings.
The appearance of the apartment complex is lacking. It does not look like an upscale apartment complex at all

Very unprofessional team. I recommend leasing with Windsor in Dogpatch over Potrero Launch. 

We had multiple difficulties finishing the application. We were not able to use the online application due to an error on their portal. We had to have multiple calls in order to have our application filled out over the phone. We did not receive any communication during this process and furthermore we had to reach out ourselves multiple times to solve the issue. Their office was quite unresponsive. Their office put no effort into informing us of the problem and no effort into fixing it until we prodded them to do so.

Excellent location by Crane Cove Park, retail and dining. Pretty community, contemporary units with high ceilings and polished concrete floors. Rooftop deck with stunning views of the Bay and park. Friendly and helpful management team.
Overall good experience. Only thing, would like the maintenance team to be quicker in their response times to come fix issues in the apartment. They should hire more than one maintenance person.
Potrero Launch on 3rd Street in dogpatch has been a good place to live. The staff are very responsive and authentic, and I have come to really love the neighborhood despite all the construction.

Advise any potential renter to reconsider before they rent at 1700 California

The Pros:  
- Great concierge/front door staff
-Very convenient location (across from whole foods and near cable cars). 
- Great views on upper floors  (almost makes up for the fact that the apartments are such low-end quality)
- Very pet friendly (but seems most buildings in the area are)

The Cons  (and there are many):
- Beware if you rent from these guys.  Get everything in writing with a signature before you move in and have a penalty clause with $$ amounts if they don't deliver. They will promise you everything to get you to sign up as a tenant and then will not deliver.   New gym and whirlpool? Never happened.  Bike parking?  Never happened.  Repair the elevators?  Happened but only after many weeks of elevators that wouldn't run consistently or go to upper floors. Fix the plumbing that you hear like a sewer anytime someone uses water - day or night? Never happened in 8 months.  
- On moving in we were given no building or apartment orientation at all.  We only discovered where the emergency stairs were because the elevator kept breaking down. 
- Several of the units on the upper floors are being converted to condos and demolished.  Be prepared to hear a lot of noise during the construction. This building reverberates noise.
-  The building is attached to a medical facility which means there are medical vehicles blocking traffic and driveways throughout the day.
- No window insulation and units are old so apartments are exposed to Van Ness, Franklin and California street noise.  It is loud and never-ending.  The worst time for me was around 4:30AM when the garbage trucks and whole foods deliveries begin. 
- Bad interactions with building manager and the managing company (Mosser). Lots of verbal promises to fix things or make amends.  Then no delivery. This created a major lack of trust.  Shouldn't they at least try to make you feel like they value your tenancy? 
- Priced significantly over current market rates for similar properties

It's a shame that such a potentially great building is so poorly maintained and that the management seems not to care at all about the tenants.  We moved here with such high hopes but were quickly disillusioned. 

My advice:  If you like the general area, check out the Rockwell across the street (modern, new, beautiful units with car and bike parking and a real gym for less money) or any of the many great apartments nearby.

We lived here for about 10 months and overall was pretty negative. We had to move early due to very loud sporadic plumbing noise that woke us up throughout the night - it started about 2 months after we moved in. We notified the property manager 5 times but it was never repaired. We later learned than several other units have the noise problem as well.

Further, we received notice from the City a couple months after we moved in that major renovations to the building would occur including demo of many units including ours. We never were told that by the building when we moved in although they filed for permits 2 months before we signed the lease. Disappointing that the property manager didn't disclose this when we signed the lease.

We were made several promises that weren't kept by the property manager including a bike cage, ability to terminate our lease without a penalty after we learned our unit would be demo'd and we'd have to move. We were also promised compensation for no bike cage, elevator issues, and the plumbing noise but never received anything. 

The elevators were out several times forcing us to walk up or down 10 flights of stairs. 

The unit we were in had great views and decent closet space. However the windows were old and leaky - street noise and cold air came through them easily. The appliances were newish but very low end. 

On the positive side, the front door staff are super nice and friendly. There are many really nice tenants as well although many are or have moved out already.

Location and the apartment facilities are very quiet, safe, and clean. 
Facilities and amenities are very modernized and convenient.
Nice community, Apartments, clean and management is very friendly and they're always there for service if needed.
It's a nice cozy community. Like the new maintenance and how are their managing the building.

Correction to your listing.  There is no onsite maintenance or property manager. There is no courtyard. There is no pet washing station. 

Management turned over after 9 months. New management is worse. They talk a good game but do nothing. Exterior landscaping is dead. With no one in office packages Are left on the street and stolen. Key fobs don’t operate doors. Lockouts with long delays. Families with 4 kids living in small apartments and using rooftop furniture as trampolines. Rents as similar buildings are down 15-20% bs STLY but not here. Better value found elsewhere.

Stay Away from here because new property management company is accepting any tenants even if they are obviously not a right fit (e.g big family in a junior one bedroom on the top floor!) which results in you hearing constant dragging furnitures, jumping, running, screaming, some weird machinery (!) sounds all the time.
Great apartments.

While it is a classic old San Francisco building, more and more the emphasis is on old. The elevator goes out frequently (it was out close to 3 months at the end of last year), and they turn off the water to apartments 2 to 3 times a month for hours at a time. Because of old wiring, internet options are limited and you compete for bandwidth with your neighbors, which is not ideal in this current environment of remote work and streaming entertainment. Only see all of these problems getting significantly worse in the next few months.

And the neighborhood has deteriorated significantly in the past few years. It was always Tenderloin adjacent, but the Tenderloin has expanded to where it pretty much engulfs the building. Property theft is up, and several times a week one needs to ask people shooting up or smoking to leave the front entryway. Noise levels have also gotten much higher both inside and outside the building. More people screaming in the streets (through windows that do little to keep noise out, when they are not contributing to it from rattling), and the units themselves are not sound-proofed in any way, so hopefully you have considerate neighbors. Only see these all getting worse when the recently-approved homeless shelter opens a couple doors down (another one opened a year ago one block away and neighborhood has seen noticeable increase in drug use and crime since).

And if you ignore all this and move in anyway, enjoy your apartment as much as you can at the very beginning, because the building management will NEVER do anything to help keep up your apartment moving forward. They will re-furnish vacant units (of which there are a lot, further reducing the safety of the building) in hopes of getting high rents from people moving in, but once they have you they have no interest in doing anything to keep your unit from deteriorating over time. More than 15 years in and they have never approved even a new paint job.

It is sad - would have recommended this building maybe 10 years ago (maybe even 5 years ago) but to see the level the management has let it slide is disappointing. Like many other people from the building, will likely be moving out sooner rather than later. Tired of the crime that has hit the building, and the management's disinterest in doing anything to make for a better living situation.

Telegraph Hill feels like the top of the world, with all of San Francisco at your feet. I love the restaurants, cafes, parks, and people of nearby North Beach, and the beautiful gardens along the Filbert Steps up to Coit Tower and down to Levi Plaza. And I'm thankful for the 39 bus!

The Telegraph Hill is an Oasis in the heart of North Beach. The Greystar staff are beyond amazing and actively help transform an apartment into a home. From the moment I walk through the front door the world transforms and my day gets a little better. When the weather in the city is a little cold I have my brick fire place and when the day is hotter I have an incredible patio to enjoy the sun. The neighborhood, tenants, and staff are all awesome! I wouldn't live anywhere else in San Francisco, they do it right here at 350 Union!

My apartment is located at a pretty good area. The view there is spectacular. This furnished apartment provides high convenience to people who do not have the time to purchase new furnitures. The apartment is also located right above Little Italy and it's about a 10 minute walk to China Town. Other than the rent being a bit too expensive, this is a great place!

Love the location, and love the building. There's a doorman, and a gym, and there are residents from various parts of the world.
This building is right in the Nob Hill, and is literally walking distance to everything. Restaurants are just round the corner, its a 2 minute walk to the shops, and it has a great vibe and energy.

I have finally moved out from this place and I can not be happier. I would not recommend this place to my friends, family or anyone who wants a good and comfortable condo in an apartment complex. The Landing is presented as luxury apartments with super high rent, utilities and parking (final number will be way higher than you think). In reality this place is way below average. This includes low quality materials and equipment, thus resulting in many problems (not repaired in time); constantly clogged trash chutes (so keep your trash at home), not properly working locks (you may not be able to enter the building or apartment whenever you want), constantly not working garage door (homeless are sleeping in their garage), no communication with management (they do not care about your problems) etc etc. Remember you are paying a lot for everything!! And of course when you move out expect all kinds of extra charges, damages for reason only they know but they are not going to inform you (100% get ready to pay a lot).. WORST LIVING EVER.
The Landing feels grand from the moment you walk into the lobby and the staff are spectacular!

The Landing has a great building and the best staff onsite. But have serious problems outside their control, unfortunately. STAY AWAY from units facing Pennsylvania street (especially units X01-X08). 

Staff on site - 6/5
Super responsive, always wanting to be helpful. Always smiling too. They try to get to know you too. Nothing but praises here.

Building and facilities - 5/5
Still new, very well maintained. Love the style too. Modern. Gym is better than most apartments gyms out there. The sun deck is lovely.

Now on to where it's not so good.

Smell - 3/5
You'll still get the smell of weed seep into your room every now and then. I don't know where it comes from but I'm assuming it's in the building because I can't smell it beyond a few dozen feet radius of my unit. And you'd be stuck with the smell of weed inside your unit for 1-2 hours. Could never find the source. Tried posting on the tenant forum. Manager sent reminder emails. Nada. Nothing can be done unless landlord investigates each unit, which is too intrusive.

Noise - 2/5
It's right next to a wood working shop and a MUNI vehicle dispatch center. Every day (weekends too) 7am you'll get woken up by vehicle backing alarms. It'll last through 8am. Then every now and then throughout the whole day - at times even at 11PM. They'll sometimes turn on the machine that hums for hours. Nothing can be done. Even after closing all windows (which sucks, because there's no other air circulation) and putting on white noise blockers - you can still hear the sound reverberate in your ears. It's so so hard to take meetings without getting distracted. Unfortunately, it's outside of the property's control. I tried escalating to 311, nada. So if you want to work at home peacefully, which we all do now, don't get units facing pennsylvania.

Value 2/5
Premium pricing, even relative to other buildings in the neighborhood with similar or better amenities. They acknowledge that their prices are above market but won't lower their price.

Lease terms 1/5
Just note that you'll have to pay 2 months of (premium) rent to break your lease. It's above market.
It's a great place to live, I feel safe in my apartment.

My experience has been very good here at Water Bend. Management promptly and effectively addresses any concerns I may have had.  I really appreciate the relationship I have as a resident with management. I feel valued as a community member and I actively demonstrate my desire to remain a resident here. I look forward to greeting my neighbors as they go about their day. Thank you Water Bend.
Maria was very helpful with all I needed during the move in process. My unit is very nice, clean and comfortable. Definitely glad I chose Waterbend.
Es una comunidad que está trabajando eficientemente bien en la necesidad del alquilino

Waterbend apartments could be a great place to live, but the experience as a tenant of three years has been nothing short of terrible. Management takes weeks to respond to any needs, follow-through is nonexistent, and no one seems to accept accountability for the following challenges: you never receive your mail, facility requests are not completed, and the community is disruptive, filthy and unpredictably.
Response time is terrible.  Service work is excellent.

SOMA Residences has become the serenity point of SOMA living.  You will find peace in this secured environment with plenty of underground parking. SOMA is your escape with spacious units, on-site laundry facilities, landscaped courtyard, and 24 hour fitness center.  Residents experience a calm oasis of city living on SOMA grounds.  Conveniently located very close to Civic BART Station, the Westfield Shopping Center, the Metreon and the best Bay Area Restaurants. If you seek peaceful living in the city, you will enjoy the SOMA Lifestyle.

I had a great experience living here! The location is excellent (walking distance to the 9th and Irving corridor and Golden Gate Park), while the complex is quiet and has amazing views. The management is also very responsive and accommodating.

Highly recommend this apartment complex! Perfect location, quiet area with beautiful views and the apartments are in great condition. Management is very helpful, attentive and kind. Had a wonderful experience with Kirkham Heights.

I've lived here for nearly a year and I couldn't be happier. The grounds are beautiful and well-maintained. The neighborhood is safe and friendly. The management company is fair, professional, and kind. I highly suggest considering this community!

It’s been a fantastic 2 years of living at Kirkham Heights Apartments! We enjoyed our home a lot, specially its location in the City. It’s the best! The maintenance tech is knowledgeable and fast. He always responds to service requests promptly and efficiently.

I have lived here for 11 years. The view is amazing. I see the Golden Gate Bridge. The apartment is ample (smallest one) for a single person. The current manager, Kate, is very attentive to the concerns of us renters. She is the best manager since I have been here: kind, courteous, and trying to accommodate us. The place is old, but filled with nice people, and I have a little place outdoors to keep my potted plants. My 2 cats love it here as well.

Location: quiet, clean, safe, and views are great

Fantastic building and incredibly spacious units for San Francisco.
