Richard the maintenance guy is amazing and incredibly responsive. Building utility expenses are absolutely bonkers. Our experience has been slightly soured by the unresponsiveness of the property manager post signing of the lease. They changed my paid parking spot without notice and refused to talk about it. I wish I had the sense to get it in writing.
Nice area, apartments, and staff! Really enjoying my time so far. The building is really conveniently set up with parking, mail room, and outdoor spaces and the area generally feels safe

I am in an O&M apartment and am impressed. The open spaces, clean environment, pet-friendly amenities, great community, and friendly staff created a fantastic experience. The location is perfect, close to public transport. I highly recommend this residence for anyone seeking comfort and convenience in a vibrant area.

The apartment manager didn't take a valid or acceptable action when the neighbourhoods are making so much noise. The resident above me is always making big noise after 10pm until 2am in the morning. My ceiling and windows are shaking while they're walking at the apartment, and they keep doing laundry after midnight. Sometimes when I work from home, their steps are much loader and seems they never care about other residents. I've tried to communicate with them and the apartment manager, and there is what I got from them: 

The apartment said this kind of noise is common because this is an apartment. And they could do nothing about it because they could not disallow the resident to walk at room. Then I emphasized, even if it's not about playing music or having party, the noise level should be controlled in specific range. I also said, making noise at daytime is totally fine, but after 10pm is not acceptable. And eventually they let me talk with that resident above on my own, and I did, then immediately I received a warning from the apartment manager that I'm not supposed to drop the note on that neighbour's door. 

In addition, the apartment manger told me that apartment  above me kept empty for about 100 days, which is reason it was always quiet before. However, I've moved here for over 1 year, it's over 365 days, but for the other ~265 days, it was always good until the new resident moved in. So, empty apartment for ~100 days obviously is not a valid reason.

Also, the apartment manager said maybe that resident is unaware of that his steps are so loud; and he didn't do that intentionally. Thus, the apartment manager asked me stay with the noise because of the unawareness. However, unawareness is never a reason a person can negatively impact others' life or hurt others' feeling. It's unfair to me. 

Right now, all my emails to the apartment manager would be ignored and they never responded. As they said, they could do nothing about such problem. Thus, I have to stay with the noise. I would move at the end of this lease.

Therefore, I'm not saying you shouldn't move into this apartment. However, if you are planning to move in, get well prepared without help from the apartment manager when you get in trouble with your neighbourhood.

Good Luck!

After 22 years in San Francisco, I have found my dream apartment! My unit is quiet, well maintained, and the open layout gives me so much space. The building is literally heavenly with all those floor to ceiling windows, and all the staff equally divine! 0:)

el lugar es seguro hay lugares como el chase Center y también el estadio de los gigante y también el caltrain

maintenance crew is excellent! Work orders are done very timely, especially with the requested time frame requested.

Living here is ok. The biggest problem I have is that people keep smoking. Do not move here! I have loved here for 13 months. In that time I have had 2 bikes that were securely locked with a U lock in the bike room and multiple attempts at break ins to my apartment. Loud, disrespectful neighbors and utterly unresponsive management.

Not to mention:  STILL ongoing construction, with more LARGE building to erect causing even more construction noise, dirt, dust, and traffic congestion.  P.S. Laguna St is really the Octavia Blvd Byway ie. freeway.

I went to see these places, very nice. But there is a pot dispensary moving in one block away. There have been murders, muggings, and other violent crime because if these dispensaries in the past on this block. Why would I move into a new luxury apartment where I could get shot? No thanks
It’s a nice and well managed apartment. Neighbors, management and maintenance team are all nice and friendly. I’m enjoying living here. :)
Poorly managed but lobby is nice. Usable floor plan
Pipes leaking, constant plumbing issues, mold developing under sink, no eta on fix
Do not live here if you have another option. Construction, revolving door of building managers, constant water shut offs, and non existent maintenance support has made this place a nightmare to live.

They're currently under renovation and will tell you this is temporary, with the objective of making the building even better and more modern. The true is: the construction has been going on for months and they have permits until 2024. Construction has revealed asbestos issues and affected structures not only in the units being remodeled - nearby units have had their walls explode, our water pipes are full of dirt - which you'll be able to see and smell some days, and when things get really bad they will close out water for 24-48h weekly - THAT MEANS YOU DO NOT HAVE WATER FOR DAYS! Plus, multiple units have been dealing with water dripping from the ceiling which can be dangerous.

No compensation is made here and their staff will leave the property in the middle of day so while this is all happening, no one is around to help. They will also ignore your calls and e-mails and  currently have 28 cases on the renters board with petitions to address the issues listed here!

I truly hope this helps you to make the decision to never live here and that no one has to ever deal with what we, the current residents are going through!

If you want to live in a building which looks like a top-flight residence in a nice area of town, this is NOT the place for you.  Ongoing construction debris and noise, elevators frequently not in service... all the nightmares of home. Keep looking.

Don't sign here. Active flooding in the apartment due to a faulty HVAC pipe bursting. Residents can't live in their apartments due to big fans running all day and night. Management refuses to offer concessions for this situation. Avoid!!

On apartments.com, it said that the company is offering 2 months free. Then during the tour, the agent said that I will get an opportunity to get 6 weeks off if application is made within 24 hours. And then past business hours on the same day, I get a text to make a decision before midnight. If this is how management makes decisions, I don't know if I feel safe with other decisions that the management makes. I will not recommend 500 Folsom to any of my friends because the management will not uphold to their words and can change on me anytime
This apartment sucks so much I moved back to Detroit. Far too dangerous, stolen packages, etc

Apartments and perks are pretty good. But the crime situation in the building got ridiculous. We had effractions, unwanted visitors, and stolen package to a point where you can’t get anything delivered at your address. The management is fully aware, and rather than taking any significant measures, like having staff or security in the entrance, gently reminds occupants that they are not responsible for stolen packages. Funniest story in all of that was that they actually leased to a group that was trying to break in their neighbors appartements, and would regularly open/steal ALL packages in the mail room.

For your safety do not consider MB360! I saw a burglar hanging in our building last week, I have had 5 packages stolen in a month. This building is highly targeted for crimes because everyone knows the management don’t care!
 I have spoke to the management 2 weeks ago regarding to the same issue. It has been over 2 weeks now, more of my package got stolen, nothing has been done! Still more new opened and stolen packages everyday!! 
The management was very rude to me, they told me if I took time and read the contract properly, I would understand managing crime is NOT PART OF THEIR JOB! He even said “we also have the options to use Amazon locker or UPS pick up” like as if it was totally our responsibility that our packages got stolen. 
I have also try to break the lease but looks like I will need to pay a penalty.

I moved in here on August 1st, and it’s currently mid October. I usually get my deliveries from Amazon or other places around once a week. I’ve had something stolen from the mail room at least once a month (3x so far). Other times people opened boxes, decided they don’t want my stuff and then they leave it. I’ve texted the management office and they refuse to do anything. They could easily find out who it is because there is a camera in the mail room, and you can tell between when you go to pick something up and when it was delivered, who possible suspects are. They refuse to do anything. Other residents complain all the time too. It’s clear it’s another resident or someone who works here that’s the thief.Come tour the place, ask any resident if they’ve had anything stolen recently, and I’ll bet they’ll say yes. Management and building are nice otherwise, but it’s ridiculous that nothing is done about something that happens so often.

Do not move here.

Where do I start? The constantly stolen packages, the unresponsive management, the pink mold, or the arbitrary $500 bill they slapped on us upon move out?

Mission Bay is gorgeous, convenient, and finally post-pandemic becoming more alive. MB360 is even located near some great coffee shops (Cafe Réveille), a grocery store (Gus's), and a fun beer garden/food truck area (Spark Social). Despite the great location at the heart of these locations, I have walked away from MB360 with such disappointment and resentment with MB360 management and Essex leadership.

We lived in MB360 for a year during shelter in place, with mostly radio silence from management. Delivered packages were strewn about the mail room. Our packages were constantly stolen. Never got a response from management- not even an apology. My partner and I are pretty self sufficient, so with the lack of responses from management it wasn't the end of the world. Annoying, but not the final straw.

No, the final straw was that upon move-out, the wolves descended. We don't smoke, we won't have pets, and it was just my partner and I in a 2br/2ba. Somehow however, MB360 claims we left our unit in unlivable conditions. Photos of vacuum lines marks, indentations from heavy weighted items on the carpet that will return to normal in a day or two, and normal wear-and-tear images were used as fodder to claim ridiculous move out charges for cleaning and painting. We are hounded daily for these incorrect and unreasonable charges. Now it's clear the Essex business plan to recoup for their poor performance in the 2020 market. The burden will fall to you, the renter.

MB360 is the cheapest rent you can find in Mission Bay for good reason. Take your chances moving in, but you'll pay for the difference in unfeeling managers, arbitrary bills upon move out, and hours spent wracking your brain for why you ever decided to move into an Essex property.

Good luck if you decide to move here.

Unsafe. Look elsewhere. We have lived at MB360 for about 3 years now and while the building is nice and so are the amenities, all the residents feel worried about their safety. Packages are constantly being stolen (lost multiple) and vehicles broken into. My vehicle is in direct line of sight of a camera and when asked for the footage to forward to police, management said "the camera does not work". Packages are dumped into an open room, garage doors are left open due to mechanical failures and building security only roams at set times.

Pick any other building in this great neighborhood. Or live here and get a PO box to secure your deliveries.
lease decisions very quick, smooth automated onboarding, amazon locker, clean and modern apartments
No heat in the hallways. Bridge between buildings always has puddles due to uneven concrete pouring.
I am very disppointed with how they treat their residents. Irreponsives with urgent services even after multiple reminders.
Awesome complex so far! Staff is super nice and helpful! A little pricey for my taste BUT I've been told I found a good place for a good price!

I just moved to the city and I love the apartment I chose! They are extremely helpful, the maintenance team has even giving me some hardware to hang some things on the walls when mine didn't work! They are very supportive! It's a property management company so it's easy to handle things that need to get fixed. We haven't had any issues apart from a burnt out light bulb. I recommend it to anyone, who is moving to or within the city!
Everything is bad about Potrero 1010. Trust me stay away from this building or in general stay away from Equity Apartments.

I'm a current resident of Potrero 1010, posting this anonymously on behalf of many frustrated residents as we're all fearful that sharing the truth will cause retaliation by the landlord.

Potrero 1010 has significant security, safety, and maintenance issues over the past 1-2 years. One of the buildings has been completely without elevators for the last month, elderly residents are having to walk up 6 flights of stairs. The other building has multiple broken trash chutes leading to the entire building smelling of trash (especially shocking considering monthly trash costs at this building are nearly $100/month).  Meanwhile, maintenance requests are ignored. Residents have started reporting maintenance requests to the City as the landlord completely ignores them until they get cited by the city (The building was cited by the city for both of the above requests).

In addition to the cost saving measures by the corporate landlord mentioned above, the building has significant security and safety concerns. The mail room is robbed almost every other week leading to tens of thousands of dollars of resident packages being stolen. In large part due to a broken door, that once again the building refused to repair until they were cited by the city.  They encourage residents to buy UPS boxes at their own expense, and have started threatening residents that they are considering cutting off mail delivery for all residents because of the constant thefts which they refuse to control with something as simple as a security service and moving packages back into the office; out of the garage.

At the end of the day, at Potrero 1010 corporate profits are prioritized over resident safety, security, and property.
Safe location in SF, nearby UCSF medical campus. Nice neighbors and apartment social events! Fast maintenance services (0-1day)

My goodness it's been a year of never-ending plagues. First, there was the broken air conditioner that took three months of nagging for them to fix. Then, there was the broken electrical outlets that took another month of following up. THEN, there was (still is) a building-wide ant infestation. THEN, there were (still are) broken fire alarms that go off at 2 AM for no reason. I've literally learned to sleep through fire alarms (!) because it's happened so often. NOW, there are break-ins and package thefts, for which the building's answer was to cut off residents' access...to our own packages?

It's a nice location? I guess? That's the only nice thing I can think of to say.

I've lived here for two years. What they don't tell you when you move in:

- The paint gets marked up SUPER easily. You will be charged upon move out for repainting the apartment. It appears they do this to every tenant to recoup their turnover costs. They don't just repaint the marks but the whole wall. They will charge you $28.20/hour plus $25/min for a gallon of paint. 
- They will charge you $140 as a standard cleaning charge upon move out. If you don't do this, you have to pay someone else to clean your unit and provide them with receipts.
- CalTrain is very loud as is the highway, which means we can never have our windows open.
- Your rent will go up a lot every year. We are moving out because they want to increase our rent by about 15%. No thanks.
- People are nice, but no one actually talks to each other other than in the dog park. The idea that this is a "community" is a total facade.
- The package room guy is SUPER nice. We love him. AND, it always takes us forever to find our packages in the package room and it's not uncommon for them to be put in the wrong place making it take 15-20 minutes to find a package.
- The park is covered in dog pee and is not a place you will ever want to hang out.

The market in SF is cooling and you can find a better place.

Enjoy the attention you get during the leasing and move-in process because it's likely to be the last time any of the management or office staff pay any attention to you.  Any future issues reported by email will likely be responded to after multiple days with emails that don't actually resolve your issue, and if reported in person may be delayed if the minimally staffed office has a tour with a future tenant, that obviously takes priority. But not to worry, all will be forgiven due to the pizza parties twice a month sponsored by such "neighborhood" companies such as Xfinity.

It's a shame as the building is nice and has a lot of potential, but in a SF market where people will pay for anything, the building management seem to understand that they don't have to give anything. We've looked forward to the end of our one year lease since about 3 months in and am sure that others will too!

There are just so many problems here. Unchecked package thieves, elevators constantly out of service, inspectors entering your apt and leaving it fully unlocked when they leave, leasing office doing absolutely nothing about notoriously problematic tenants until they've literally burned their apartment down (and irrevocably damaged everyone else's via flooding while putting out said fire). To top it off, when this occurred, Fox Plaza did not even care to notify affected (or potentially affected) tenants. Meaning that if you were out, you may come home to an an absolutely wrecked apartment without warning. Completely unacceptable.

I just moved into a 2-bedroom apartment at Fox Plaza about a month ago. Though it hasn't been that long, I like the apartment/building so far.

About the building:
Hooray rent control! They recently remodeled the hallways before I moved in (apparently they were terrible before) so the aesthetic of the older building has gone up. The security and leasing office staff are extremely nice and accommodating. The office has a package room where you can receive and pick up packages 24/7, so it was very convenient for me, having moved here from across the country and shipped most of my belongings. There is a laundry room in the building, but the number of machines is not proportional to the number of apartments, so timing is tricky. There is also a fitness room, and changes are going to be made sometime this year regarding expanding/moving the fitness and laundry rooms.

About the apartment:
There are only 15 2-bedroom apartments in the building; one on each floor. My particular apartment was remodeled by the previous owners (Archstone) in 2013 so it was not upgraded this year, like some other apartments in the buildings were by Essex, with stainless steel appliances. Even so, the apartment is still great: white cabinetry and walls, hardwood floor throughout, and balconies off the living room and bedrooms – meaning two views out of different sides of the building (look at a floor plan to see what I'm talking about). Overall, sounds are contained within the apartment. I've only ever heard noise when people are standing outside our front door or close by. I can't even hear much from the living room when I'm in my bedroom. The bathroom is not spacious like the rest of the apartment, but it isn't problematic. One con of the apartment is that the internet outlet (where you plug a modem) is in the corner of the living room, so signals reaching the bedrooms at the other end are relatively weak. We had to get a router and a bunch of cables to extend the signal.

This is a perfect apartment for me. I have been living here since 1993. I have moved out twice to another state , but each time came back with in a month to the same building. It is located in the middle of the city, has a great view of the Bay. Close to all kinds of transportation, restaurants, Museums, theatres. The apartment is very well kept, has good security.  Staff is very helpful.

Today at your property I received a beautiful tour it has a lot of space NICE PRICE,most importantly the woman who showed the property was very respectful and knowledgeable about the area polite and patient. I was so before I saw the wonderful rooftop! I’m just waiting on my application to come thank you

I've been living here for many years and it was quite LONG overdue for a full gutting and facelift... 

Richard, Sean, and Michael continue to make life here so much better. 

More improvements in the works, but thanks everyone for making massive strides!

We are long-term tenants at 5285, and the building has much improved with the new Management Company and remodel that is almost completed. Office staff go out of their way to be helpful and Maintenance (thanks Sean and Jose) are quick to respond to all requests. Dog owner heaven as there are 3 parks within 3 blocks. With Safeway, Walgreens, great sushi and a Post office across the street make for easy living.

I’ve been living at Delphine on Diamond for years and love the building and it’s location. It’s convenient to shopping, buses and Glen Park BART, walking, pet parks, and yet it’s a quieter area with a more neighborhood feel than a lot of the city. Here, the office staff and maintenance staff are excellent. They have quick responses, are friendly and wish to do it right the first time.

Our Maintenance Manager here at Delphine on Diamond, Sean, has recently completed several maintenance requests in my apartment. I decided to write this review, because in the forty years that I have lived in this apartment community, since 1982, he is definitely one of the best maintenance personnel we've ever had. His work is always top rate, response times are quick, he leaves the area looking totally clean, and overall is very professional. It's quite evident that he cares a great deal about the property. Sean's great dedication to customer service excellence is to be highly commended.

In addition, Delphine on Diamond is located in one of the few San Francisco neighborhoods that has free street parking: with no expensive permits or parking meters. Plus, just across the street, there is a convenient shopping center with a post office, grocery store, pharmacy, restaurants and much more.

i have been here for 20 years...i've seen many changes...the new managerial team is the best i have ever  encountered...they walk around ...ask questions...what we would to see on the premises improved and generally get to know the occupants providing an atmosphere of familiarity..they are working to renovate the property.....i have mostly used the social lounge for parties...they  provide tables and chairs making things easier...there is always coffee at your disposal...great tv...there is a pool table...sauna...beautiful pool....outstanding and plentiful grounds for all and our dogs....wonderful place to meet dogs and dog owners ..exchanging information about our little critters...the landscaping is been renovated...just about everything...i have never been happier with richard and eric who have created a special ambience....we are across from the diamond heights shopping center...safeway...post office..coffee shop...starbucks in safeway...little restaurant...mailbox where you can have anything and everything performed...printing...notary....all special services with a smile...walgreens....christopher park which has been renovated...the childrens'  playground is a work of art...the "52 bus usually runs down our block stopping at both ends with kiosks to keep us protected from rain and wind....we are on rock which is why i moved here...safe for earthquakes!!we have blustery winds but i'd rather live in our cool and sometimes warm jweather than 100 degress which can be horrendous inland....am i satisfied...?  more than satified....it is idyllic to live here...the buses take you to bart and muni...what more can you ask for...!! i highly recommend a superb living setting with suberb amenities..|

For over 25 years we have called this paradise our home - high upon a hill in San Francisco with hummingbirds, squirrels & the occasional skunk our woodsy neighbors.  From our balcony we can see from the lights of downtown San Francisco clear to the San Mateo Bridge some 25 miles south and across the Bay to Oakland and beyond.  Yet out our front door are 3 bus lines, quick freeway access and a wonderful shopping center directly across the street.  We never have to move the car to shop for groceries or do banking or take our cat to the vet.  Did I mention the full Nautilus gym, heated swimming pool and management that repairs things almost before they break!  With fog that creeps over the crest of our home on cool summer nights, we truly live in a castle in the clouds.
Nice-sized space but plumbing and structure issues run amuck. Prime location.

If you have a pet, this is an excellent location to consider due to proximity to Lafayette Park and because Management allows certain pets! Other than being pet friendly, the units are modest compared to some of the other buildings in the area. The location cannot be beat in SF. Walking distance to Fillmore, Polk street, Whole Foods, a host of other great spots, and centrally located in SF overall. On premise management is friendly and takes care of simple maintenance needs; however, expect some difficulty if there is ever anything complex that requires upper level management involvement.

Worst renting experience of my life. The biggest issue is the severe heat within the apartment which can get up to 100 degrees. I had several episodes of dehydration just due to how hot the apartment gets. It's unreal ! And very unhealthy to live here. My cats struggled a lot with the heat as well. I tried air fans and bough my own AC but still couldn't keep up with the extreme heat. The glass in three of the windows began to spontaneously crack due to the heat and it's been more than a month and no one has fixed it yet. They just put tape over it. The management person is not helpful at all. I'm worried about the windows falling down on my cats when I'm not home. The bedroom has pipes within the wall that make a ridiculously loud noise at night. The whole thing is a bad joke. The neighborhood is dangerous and i had several packages stolen. I'm moving next month and I've never been so happy to get out of a place as I am now. My biggest regret is not moving earlier.
Nice apartment, above average finishes (great refrigerator). Management is a bit draconian and they are aggressive with rent increases.
Changed showing dates twice and gave incomplete information

This is the worst place I have lived in my entire life (not mentioning the building manager’s attitude towards it’s tenants). Having lived in Asia and Europe I never heard neighbors talk on the phone from below and above. The old hardwood floors were squeaking at every given occasion and would wake us up at 5-6am depending on when people would wake up above us.  
Unpleasant and emotionally distressing experience. It looks all pretty from outside and inside, but a lot of hidden issues with this building. 
I would recommend to check carefully yourself before moving in.

The management company for this building is incredibly incompetent and they do not take good care of their units. I lived here for about 3 years and it was a constant battle to have any maintenance performed from the time I moved in until I moved out. There was work that was promised to be completed before I moved in that wasn't done until months later. To even get them to complete that work, I had to constantly call and email them. They just ignore requests or if they respond to them, they promise that it will be fixed on a certain day and then the person never shows up to fix it because the management company doesn't communicate with maintenance. I had to contact the rent board multiple times and eventually filed a complaint with the dept of building inspection. Its really a shame that the property management company is so awful because the building has a beautiful garden and a very nice building manager.
The building was built in 1960 so it is a little dated.  But it has an elevator and a pool!  Very close to Castro Muni stop.

For the price, you are 100% better off elsewhere.

Management is extremely difficult to deal with and slow to respond and fix things. 

1 elevator, which rarely works, and is not large enough to move furniture. Routine maintenance requests take weeks to be addressed. 

This is a very old building, with almost no modernization done. Units are decent sized, but bathrooms are small and outdated, paint is a tired color, walls and floors are very thin so sound travels. 

Not worth the price and dealing with the management. Better off at any of the newer buildings for the same ballpark price, or a similarly old building for next.

As a tenant in an affordable SOMA apartment in the Yerba Buena Community, I found living in Yerba Buena Commons for the last four+ years an easy-going and comfortable experience, with a responsive, accessible management team close at hand. Even during the long years of the pandemic, when downtown San Francisco emptied out, I felt safe and protected with YBC health protocols routinely enforced. Though the YBC studios are small, they are efficient and adaptable to a private, self-sufficient life style. Fortunate to have a quieter, inner apartment facing the courtyard and garage, I was an eyewitness to the historic changes in downtown San Francisco as it hollowed out and is now returning to life, 2019-2024. An exciting neighborhood, close to world class sports, museums, and entertainment, YBC is an affordable home in a beautiful City.

This has to be the last cheapest apartment in San Francisco! For those who do not have a 100,000 salary and lives and works in the city this may be a great place for you. I have been at YBC for about a year now and I am still curious how I was able to find this place (craigslist). Its a small 190sq ft apartment in SOMA its SMALL! but perfect if you travel a lot, work long hours, or just a single guy/gal who needs a safe affordable place to live. It is a SRO so please be aware ( I make about 30,0000 a yr. I feel safe when I come into the building at night, parking is available if you have a parking pass, very close to bars, SF giants baseball park and just a walk away to Powell street also there is a bus stop right in front of the building SWEET!. I only pay $865 a month which is very affordable for me I work really early so all I want to do at the end of the day is go home, crash and it's perfect. I've almost never have an issue with noise, there is security watching the front door to the building (ALL DAY)  which you need a code to enter. The only issue I have had is once I had bed bugs ( I believe it was one of my neighbors had them) but as soon as I spoke with the building manager I had the issue resolved by the end of the week. Its a month to month agreement which is very ideal for me because I plan on purchasing a home soon and helps me build my rental history. Very few weird looking san francisco people I have seen in the building before, but not once did I feel unsafe especially because I have a child! all in all need a temp spot to save your money for something better this is you place

Quality for value luxury living at Geary Courtyard Apartments that is hard to come by in pricey San Francisco. My unit was equipped with modern amenities and it was so comfortable inside, I never wanted to leave, except to the peaceful courtyard garden for fresh air and to the the rooftop for stunning downtown views! Geary Courtyard is centrally located with easy access to any direction in the city you wish to go. It was like living in a 4-5 star hotel, and enabled me to see most of San Francisco during my time there!

I lived in 639 Geary Street from 5/5/2019 to 5/5/2020. Then I was on vacation in Hawaii because I am a teacher. I had very good experience living in here . The staffs are friendly and responsible. Especially Sydney, she left deep impression on me  she was so active in helping me with all my request. Mike the manager, he is very kind, keep answering my questions no matter how busy he was. Boris, the repair engineer , he did help me twice, every time he finished the repairing, he would left a note. Very professional. So even the rent  in other places are inexpensive, but I am back in this building again, this time, Daniel helped for my paperwork and preparing the lease. He is so kind with great patience. All these made me feel more confidence to live here as my home. As we all know, in this society, something that is very important to us, but money cannot buy it.

Use to love living here, but can’t even have peace in my apt Bc of all the construction noise. Most importantly no notices given preceding the construction. It’s really turned put to be a nightmare. Why am I paying rent to only be able to sleep at night here? Not worth it.

This place is expensive and has a lackluster gym with a broken sauna. The apartments are small, the rooftop normally has at least one dog poo on it, and I regularly find silverfish in my apartment. Management's response to most issues is to acknowledge your problem but respond with "sorry, but it's our policy". The area is not good, even though we are a short distance from some of the best parts of San Francisco.

If you plan to live on an upper floor, just don't. The elevators are constantly out of order. Even worse, you can get stuck in them. I was stuck in an elevator for about 50 minutes on one occasion. Management refuses to accept responsibility for this, blaming the residents for "mashing and holding the button".

I was excited to move in to this apartment, but have grown to despise it. Worst place I've ever lived.

The only reason I leave two stars is because the food around the building is very good. Just avoid any apartment run by Equity Residential. It's not worth your money, time, or sanity.

apartmentName: FOUND Study San Francisco | Student Housing
review: Found 3 small bugs , holes in the walls , paint chips ,bath tub was dirty but other than that it’s a Great living and outside isn’t as bad as people make it. I just kinda feel uncomfortable P.s My view is unpleasant

apartmentName: FOUND Study San Francisco | Student Housing
review: Great place. Renovated. Quiet. Property manager Nereyda is very helpful and professional.
This community has gotten worst and worst - especially safety and cleanliness wise
Alea helped us to move in very easy, she is very helpful, I would recommend anyone to live here at 33 8th because it’s a very nice apartment complex.
Horrrible experience with this appartment! Staff doesn’t help resolve any issues and doesn’t cater to tenants needs

The apartment is great. The management team sucks. They never respond to my emails. They all take lunch at the same time and so good luck trying to find someone to help you between the hours of 12-2pm. Just not helpful at all. The shared grass space between all four building has restricted hours that makes no sense to me. I have to use a fob key to go in and out but that doesn't matter. Hours are from 8am-7pm. I get off work late and is forced to walk my dog on the streets where drug addicts are and I just feel unsafe. Wish I was told that the grass space has time restrictions before moving in. It was a big factor why I chose to live there. My windows are horribly dirty on the outside and I have no way of cleaning it. Don't know if they'll ever clean them because they do not respond. You share the water bill with the entire building so it doesn't matter if you use or don't use water, do laundry, or use the shared bathroom in the building. You're paying for it. Thought that was odd and unfair.

Overall, I like living here at Trinity place, it is in a very convenient location and it is easy to get out even during traffic rush. It is close to 101 and 280 and it is also close to many venues and entertainment. I love the sunset in the view, and I love the rooftop lounge. The staff is friendly and super helpful. If you simply ask politely for help. From the leasing office to janitorial and security and garage. Employees, they’ve all been super helpful. Whenever I needed anything. The rent pricing is very competitive compared to other apartment complexes I researched in the area before choosing this one. I had found some nicer apartments, but they were way more expensive. I feel that this complex has just about everything that you would need and it definitely feels like luxury living. I’m very happy and excited to live here.
It is a horrible place to live. I would say find another place. They only care about cutting corners to increase a profit. It is a joke.

Trinity Plaza is a great community of apartments with attentive management and maintenance. It's a rougher area of town, but definitely feels like a diamond in the rough. The team are very responsive on any issues that arise, and repairs generally are done promptly. Tyler is always very kind in the office downstairs when something comes up, and we really do love how central the location is, even if it's a bit Wild West out on the streets in this neighborhood.

I have resided here at 33 8th Street  26 since June 1, 2022 and  I have not had one single negative interaction with any of the other residents or management team. It is peaceful and quiet throughout the building. All the residents I have had encounters with are respectful and courteous and it appears that way in the numerous interactions amongst other residents  I have witnessed over the years.
Great people, great apartments and great property!

I love living at 33 8th St. Everything feels very safe (which is a big deal living in downtown SF). Everything is very convenient, especially the garbage and laundry set up. I love the gym and rooftop lounge! My apartment is beautiful! (I love the big refrigerator and the fancy bathroom with the walk in closet.) The location is very convenient being right next to the BART and the farmer’s market. And the staff are very helpful! (Thank you Tyler!) I would absolutely recommend living here.
Ever since graystar took over there has been many problems with building maintenance.  Especially elevators

33 8th Street is a great building! The fitness center and rooftop community area are just a couple things that make it a fantastic place to live. Our unit is just right for our needs with a cozy floorplan, lots of cupboard space, new kitchen appliances, huge walk-in closet and a spacious bathroom. We're in the heart of downtown - close to farmers markets, the main library and transit that will take us anywhere around the Bay we could possibly want to go. We're happy to call 33 8th Street home!

Since I have moved in I have been in awe, overwhelmed with joy with how beautiful and comforting, secure the building is. Everyone is very kind and helpful. Also being surrounded by everything you need , transportation, groceries store, local stores, etc. it’s just beautiful hands down the best Christmas for my daughter and myself. Thank you guys for making this the smoothest move I have ever experienced!
33 8th Street is a hidden gem in the Civic Center area. Walking into the building and looking down at the courtyard I feel like I’m in a different part of the city, which is something great!

I have been living at this location for about 2 years now and I love it. Giving the property 4 star rating (only thing stopping me from 5 star is the age of the building with respect to newer properties available, but price is great!)

I’ve lived in this building with my mother for about two years now. The current Manager is amazing and really cares about the building and tenants. The location is so convenient and close to everything, we don’t have a car so that makes it ideal for us.

I haven’t moved in yet but I love it, they’re very professional and they seem to care about you. Rey & Adrian and David is awesome as well as the rest of the leasing office department.

It one of best places to live in San Francisco, located Sough of Market, South Beach Marina, Waterfront Embarcadero, only few blocks from Ball Park and from Downtown and easy access to public transportation. Really awesome place to live. Bummer they closed the sauna and have been working on the gym for a year. It also wasn?t too cool that they cut down all the beautiful trees. But all in all one of the best places to live in the city
Safe, nice and friendly place to live.
Great location - view of the bay only 1/2 block away. Free parking nearby for guests. Hard to beat.

Bayside village has 2 central package rooms from all carriers, and all residents have access to these rooms if they have something in the package room. This means anyone can easily take packages from other people. 
I have lost 4 packages in the past 3 month. I have filed missing package requests to the management office, but they cannot find anything through their security camera records. I don't even have things delivered unless I have to, but I still lose them.
If you lose a package and ask management office to find it for you, they will give you the most obvious answer first "well, have you looked?" and then try to blame the delivery carriers.  This is not a great place to live if you buy things online.

Here is a list of complaints

1: Heat in my unit has never operated. When I filed a service ticket maintenance team came out and said all the baseboards would need replaced. They then closed the ticket until parts were ordered...this happened in June, it is now December and I still don't have working heat.

2: Mail boxes in building 2 are broken and have been broken for some time. USPS is leaving mail with the leasing office who doesn't always sort same day. Recently leasing office sent mail to the concierge building who lost several days' worth of mail including a new credit card and some other time sensitive documents. They say they are reviewing security footage but unless I go and ask in person, no communication or update has been proactively sent to myself.

3. Safety: There are ongoing break-ins within the complex, into individual people's homes and in the garage that is managed by a third party but is attached to the complex via elevator access. They say they have improved security, but the reality is all these third-party companies managing the property don't really have an accountability.

I enjoyed living here for first few years. For the past year I’ve had constant problems with my toilet due to water pressure and the management lacks any motivation to fix the problem long term. I don’t recommend living here anymore due to maintenance headache.

I no longer can recommend living here. My wife and I have had our bikes confiscated by management, and stolen twice now from within the supposedly secure bike rooms in our building. We like the apartments, but the way these situations have been handled has left with no desire to stay.

To top it off, this week a used syringe was found on the bench in the dog park, which should be open to residents only, and people have seen individuals walking in the parking garage looking in cars with flashlights. Environment is good but has a little noisy in evening. The toilet often blocked. Management is loose sometime. In general it is nice place to live. The traffic is convenient to everywhere, and it near by Target, cinema, bars and shopping malls. So there are a lot of entertainment around here.
This apartment is amazing. Excellent views of the city. The staff is wonderful and super helpful. You should live here forever.

I recently moved in to Chroma and the property management, especially Tracy, made my move very comfortable and easy! From arranging video tours to addressing all of my questions/concerns, Tracy and the team have been very helpful, kind, and friendly!

I've been a CHROMA resident for almost 3 years. The staff has been amazing and helpful, and they've always been responsive to my problems. The amenities are also great -- I'm especially fond of the free weight setup in the apartment gym, which is complete with a deadlift platform and a squat rack.

(You can use this review once you add a squat rack to the gym)

My expensive e-bike was stolen from the underground parking garage after just one month. The bike locker had a broken door and a history of theft, which staff was aware of, but didn't communicate or address in time.

Warning: STAY AWAY 
Warning: Avoid Onni South Lake Union Apartments 
If you're considering living at Onni South Lake Union, I strongly advise you to think twice. My experience with this building was nothing short of a nightmare, and it cost me nearly $15,000 to break the lease after signing what seemed like a promising agreement. Here’s why:
False Promises, Rudeness, and Unprofessional Behavior
When we first toured the property, the staff and leasing team were friendly and professional, eager to help us with anything we needed. However, after our first complaint about the conditions and our request to break the lease, their attitude changed drastically. They became rude, dismissive, and careless. What started as a seemingly professional relationship turned into complete disregard for our concerns. The moment we expressed dissatisfaction, the kindness vanished. They showed no empathy and refused to help, making the process of breaking the lease even more difficult.
Health Issues and Abandonment
Unfortunately, after breaking the lease, we had to leave Seattle for health reasons and never spent a single night in the apartment. We asked Onni to hold on to a couple of our furniture items while we sorted things out, but they discarded them without warning, claiming they only held onto them for 30 days. No one reached out to inform us about this policy. It felt like they wanted to make things as difficult as possible for us.
Unsafe and Disturbing Environment
What they don't tell you is that Onni South Lake Union isn't just a residential complex—it doubles as a hotel. This brings in a constant flow of transient guests who are not invested in the community, and it drastically changes the building’s atmosphere. The lobby and common areas are often crowded with groups of people who do not live there, which includes young women who appear to be using the space for gatherings that made us feel unsafe and uncomfortable. It felt more like a party venue than a place to call home. The combination of the hotel and constant strangers made the building feel less secure and far from the peaceful, upscale environment we expected.
Facilities and Maintenance Neglect
On top of that, the building’s facilities were a disaster. From the broken sauna to filthy pool areas and drainage problems, nothing was properly maintained. The building was not up to the standards that we were promised. The common areas reeked of marijuana, and there were safety hazards everywhere.

I have been a resident at Onni for over a year now, and have loved my time here so much! I am moving into a new unit in the building and appreciated the streamlined abilities of the staff, especially Sarah Ahn, in advocating to have the perfect apartment unit held for my partner and I until we could move in. Sarah has been there to support us, offer resources, and answer questions along the way. I highly recommend Onni not only for the amazing resident services team, but also for the incredible amenities and overall experience Onni provides while living in SLU!

Onni is a great new building, but what makes it truly special is its guest services. Khadra, T, and Marlee make Onni a wonderful home to live in. Their kindness, reliability, and care elevate the experience in the building and bring joy to residents. This team makes all the difference in our experience! Whenever any issues or concerns come up, I can always count on them to understand and help. For example, Khadra was working on the night that we encountered a minor flood in our apartment, and she managed to get us help repairing it even though it was late and we’d arrived home in the middle of the night. Her help fixing this allowed us to prevent further damage and more serious problems, and allowed us to get a good night’s sleep knowing this was resolved by someone who genuinely demonstrated care and concern. It brings us so much peace of mind knowing that we have this level of support!

As a resident, I am extremely disappointed with the current state of the hallway in our building. The overwhelming smell of garbage is making it difficult to even walk through the hallway without feeling nauseous.

It is disappointing to see such a lack of concern for the basic hygiene and well-being of the residents. I am extremely dissatisfied with the living conditions in our building and cannot recommend it to anyone until this issue is addressed in a timely and effective manner.

I urge the building management to take immediate action to remove the garbage and eliminate the odor, and also to put in place a more proactive system for garbage collection and disposal to prevent a similar situation from happening in the future.

We recently moved in to OSLU and love it! Joey was our leasing agent and was super helpful, knowledgeable and professional. He made the moving process a breeze! He gave us multiple tours of different units and floor plans until we found the one that was perfect for what we were looking for. Thanks, Joey! :)

From my touring the property as a prospective resident to my getting settled in as a resident, everyone I have met here has been so kind and helpful. In particular, Hans in leasing was very friendly and knowledgeable, and he went above and beyond to help me find an apartment I would love living in. The building is beautiful with great amenities, and it is in a great, walkable location. I highly recommend considering Onni South Lake Union!

My boyfriend and I signed our lease moving from out of state, so we did all the research we could online but never saw it in person. It's a nice complex, is cleaned every day, feels safe, apartments are new with new appliances, and has a super nice rooftop deck. 
But it is SO. FREAKING. SMALL.
400  sq ft doesn't sound that bad, but the way the apartment is set up your kitchen is the same as your bedroom. And we did NOT get a studio, and yet it feels that way. There is a huge gap in the bedroom wall and the doors are sliding, AKA absolutely no privacy in this apartment, which is essentially a hallway that we live in. The only normal sized part is the bathroom which I like. But having a small apartment also means the fire alarm goes off SO easily and any smells, good or bad, instantly permeate the place. We had to measure every inch to make sure the furniture we were ordering would even fit because the living space is so small! The people that have come over have always been so shocked by how small our apartment is, it is actually kind of uncomfortable so we just stopped having people over. 
If you're living alone the space is tolerable, but FYI - you're paying outrageously high rent by yourself for such a teensy space that's poorly laid out.
You ABSOLUTELY should look at this place in person before moving in, and decide if that's a compromise you're willing to make. I definitely wasn't.

RENTER BEWARE:  My daughter and her friend were 2 summer interns who decided to live in Seattle instead of in the suburbs like they had done the prior summer.  They liked the Lightbox apartments and the location.  The problem is, Lightbox has a history of scamming you after you vacate the premises.  There are many reviews out there just like ours that attest to their experience.  They do this especially to out of state students who are naive and vulnerable.  Once you leave and go back home they hit you with made up and unsubstantiated charges like smoke damage and having to paint the entire apartment and ceiling twice!  They can't supply pictures or receipts for the repair work.  The comical aspect, if there is one, is that during their 3 month stay, the girls did not cook and they don't smoke.  Lightbox knows that the amount they charge is not high enough to expend the money necessary to retain an attorney, fly out for court appearances, and fight them, so in the end, after you try to reason with them, you end up begrudgingly giving them the $1100 they require just to make the situation go away.  The irony, they wouldn’t allow them to pay online or mail them a check.  They had to give these unscrupulous thieves their credit card number over the phone.  They were told if they didn’t pay that day over the phone it was going to collections and their credit would be ruined.  Bad credit is a big concern for college students who have yet to graduate and embark on their careers.  This was a horrible situation and these girls were so taken advantage.  We have all learned a lesson the hard way.  Before moving into any apartment, read reviews first, check with the local police department, and force a final walk-through prior to leaving.  We feel it is now our duty to warn everyone about these scammers!

But the crown jewel of the building is the rooftop deck that overlooks Lake Union and downtown Seattle, with a view of Rainier on clear days. Overall it's a nice, newer building with good amenities. It's somewhat pricy but they do sometimes offer move-in specials, so that could make that less of an issue!

I’ve been at Anthem for about 2.5 years. The folks in the office have been great whenever I needed, queried and expressed concerns. For my few concerns actions are normally taken quickly. Hannah (leasing) and Robert (Maintenance) are always fab and responsive. Community activities tied residents together at this community pre-Covid, but the bldg has Ben active in mitigating any spread of the virus with signs, social distancing and hand sanitizer.

This is a new building, just opened this year with a super cool music theme to it - they are even working on building band practice rooms right now!  We love the rooftop view (especially the fire pit at night) and the fitness center, plus the whole place just looks amazing (very well designed) and the guys in the office are so genuine and easy to get along with.  They are pet friendly and even have a dog area up on the roof.  Definitely recommended!

this is a brand new building. Unlike some new buildings Anthem has character! From the outside you'll see bright colors, nice landscaping which that this area of Seattle needs. Inside you'll find a gym, a community room with free wifi, TV and kitchen and on top of the building a rooftop deck with BBQ's, a fire pit and a beautiful view of Mount Rainier and downtown Seattle. 

The apartments themselves are well designed, lots of storage, stainless appliances, big bathroom and stackable washer and dryer.
Awesome cool new place to live! Staff is always around for assistance. There is a community page that is a great way of communicating with staff and other residents.

Kudos to Mason and Main Management for taking care of my concerns regarding security issues. Great new apartment!! Everything is so well maintained and clean. I appreciate the security as well.

I'm having a great time at Vantage Park. It is a great community. The office and maintenance staff are so friendly and helpful. I would recommend this place to anyone considering a move!
extremely convenient location to UW system hospitals. very responsive staff.

Vantage park is an oasis amid an otherwise hectic community.

Good place to stay. Location has easy access to the restaurants nearby, walking distance to my workplace and bus stops. The staff are quick to response for issues that need to be fixed.

These were the features that really sold me on the place. I normally won’t do business with a property that charges both pet deposit and pet rent, but opted to give them the benefit of the doubt. I asked point-blank twice whether the unit I would be getting would look like what I just saw and was told yes except the bedroom would be lofted and the main floor would be wood. I raved about how excited I was about the kitchen and nothing was said to the contrary.

The application process was a pain as they send everything via text message to complete on your phone. There were technical problems that took a day to work out and I never was able to view the unit I’d move into via the link they sent.

When I finally did arrive for move-in, I found a place that had a small kitchen with laminate counters, a laminate vanity that extends only inches from the sink, and top-loading apartment-sized washer and dryer along with a host of problems such as scratches, chips, paint splatter, and some safety issues.

It took the manager three days to get back to me only to disregard anything I had to say even when asked what I wanted them to do. Some negatives would be the apartment does get pretty hot in the summer and it doesn't help the windows suck. I park my car on the street and have had them broken into a few times but they do have garage parking available at extra cost. The build quality is okay, seems like it could have been better.

Great location. Right off I90, and a five minute drive to Capitol Hill and Downtown. Area is very well maintained and the staff is great. Love the rooftop, amazing views of Mt Rainier. Overall great place to live!
Not a bad spot for begginers. I love the gym its my favorite.

Management is totally ineffective and does not care about enforcing any of the rules they’ve created, so community lives in a rogue state.

Staff operate out of quiet hours (towing dumpsters across the parking lot at 8am), many people smoke all over the campus and in the hallways, people party (loudly) on the roof all night long in every season, hallways often have trash, hall carpets covered in dog hair, the ev station has been broke for over 2 months. It’s so loud, all day, every day.

I love this beautiful apartment It's awesome
And peaceful

I had no issues interfacing with the staff on the floor at any point. The mail was easy to get to, the laundry rooms were usually very quickly if not immediately available, and any needed repairs were quick. One of the strings on my fan broke when just pulling the string and it costed $250 because they replaced the whole fan. I could have repaired it myself for just the cost of one part, but their reasoning made some sense and I wouldn't count that against them. 

I had an easy time getting to bus lines and onto the University of Washington campus and other locations (shops, restaurants, light rail) in quick time even when walking. For the most part the other residents are quiet with the occasional louder night - nothing crazy. It's a high traffic area and an older building, so some noise is to be expected. The units are in good shape and *some* of the kitchens have been updated. Look for one of the newer ones if possible. 

The only major complaint I have is my move-out costs. They charged $200 dollars for a deep clean and another $200 for floor damage. I had expected losing some money as one of the cabinets with glass in it had been broken by a friend inadvertently, but my family and I cleaned the apartment before leaving (maybe could've used a sweep?) but nothing warranting a deep clean. Same with the floor - I still have no clue what the floor damages are. The move-out costs came way out of left field, but I had a very pleasant time for the rest of my (12 month) stay.

This was the first apartment I've ever had so I wasn't quite sure what to expect but after living only a week here at Stream Belmont, I can tell it's everything I'll ever want and need! First off I have the sweetest onsite management! Rosetta helped make me make my move and she was the most helpful and kindest person I had talked to while searching for a place. I live in a studio apartment and it comes with a spacious balcony which is nice when you don't feel like going up to the rooftop that has the most beautiful view of the city and the mountains (which is never). The layout is well-thought-out with nice closet space and a big bathroom. Plenty of storage. Huge windows that bring in so much light and that makes my studio feel way bigger than it is! A huge bonus is this building is LEED®-H Certified which results in sustainable living not only for the residents but community as well. 
The location is definitely unbeatable. With a walk score of 96! I've never had to use a bike or car. I live in Capitol Hill which is known for having a good time and I slept like a baby this weekend. It's even pet friendly! :) I feel safe in my home and I would recommend you experience this too!

The previous management team was amazing and I was planning on staying here for years, however when they sold the building things went down hill and have no sign of returning with this new building manager. 

The new building management is horrible here including the regional team on site at the beginning of the transition. Since taking ownership there has been nothing but issues with hot water, trash and recycling not being picked up for weeks and piling up, loud noises during the day while trying to work from home, rude front manager who - ignores tenants, sends the worst emails to building tenants and doesn't respond to work orders. 

The pipes damaged my vehicle in the parking garage and when notifying the front office manager, she acted like i wasn't standing right in front of her asking her questions. Her and the regional manager couldn't give a care about any of the tenants or their attitude towards tenants. 

They sneak charges onto your bill with generic titles and then don't respond to questions or provide detail on what the charge is. 3 months now I've been waiting on clarity for an extra charge with no response to follow ups.

The staff do an outstanding job at making you feel like family. We moved into our apartment several days ago and are loving every second of it. Close to work, close to grocery stores, and close to the Junction.
A big perk is not hearing much traffic! 

P.S., Josh will bend over backwards to make you feel welcome.
Everything I've needed and helpful staff. I suppose there have been issues with the laundry machines but they've been fixed.

Parking is bad. It can get loud if your unit is near 15th Ave cause of constant car noise, sirens, and crazy people screaming middle of the night. The buildings are old. The landscape is well maintained. It was hard to move in/out because of the layout. It is an affordable place.

This was my first apartment and I was very pleased with the space I had in my room and living room. Throughout time I met random neighbors across this large complex and there are some really cool people here. The staff was always nice and understanding. Location is nearby the bus and a QFC is right across the street. Very good place to live especially with the crazy prices and small apartments you find nowadays.

As a young professional, I’ve really appreciated my time at Executive Estates and just recently signed another year long lease.  The office has been great to work with and the apartments are well maintained.  The security patrols are also fantastic and I truly appreciate the steps the owners have taken to keep the complex feeling safe and protected.  Thank you for everything you do guys! :)

Worst managenent ever. I had lived there for more than 4 years. The manager before was really nice and the managment was good but since kristina came as the manger, the management has become wrost. The staff has manager has no respect for its tenants and donot know how to speak to people. The apartment is really nice and I love the area but management really sucks. Our apartment has water leakage problem and they donot even care after we put the maintainance request 4 times. WORST MANAGEMENT.

I had an apartment at Executive Estates for almost nine years.  The complex itself is ok, but the office ruins it.
My time there was very stressful, and I was never treated with any respect or consideration.  I have lived in several other apartments, and the management at all of them was so polite and helpful- exactly the opposite of Executive.
There were plumbing issues from the beginning, never resolved in the whole time I was there, and , at the last, I became seriously ill there , at least partially due to this.
It was no use trying to get them to do anything about it- if there is any problem, the tenant is blamed for it, and they take no responsibility. The management was rude and inconsiderate , and they did not care one bit about their tenants. I never understood why they were like this, and 
I wish I would have left there years before I did,instead of continuing to give them money they did not deserve to receive. I am only now recovering from the illness I got while trying to live there. At the last they charged me more money  after moving out .  I feel they owe me a lot of money instead for what I went through at that place!
It was a bad experience.

I signed the lease site unseen since I was moving to Seattle from out of the area. The building is nice enough, somewhat plain and without fluff, but it provides the essential functions of an apartment building. The office staff has been pleasant enough, being helpful a few times when necessary. But despite these things, I really wish I was aware of the location prior to moving in. My apartment sits right on top of a busy street that is near I-5, multiple hospitals, late-night bars, and downtown Seattle. With this comes two serious annoyances: noise and crime. I am awoken every night several time by sirens and speeding cars going up the street. And there are consistently dozens of dirty homeless people and druggies hanging around withing a block or two of the building. On the block and even inside the parking garage there are frequently cars broken into and bicycles stolen. My recommendation is to find something else that is close by but not so centralized and busy.

There's lots to love about this beautiful 1910 building in the middle of Seattle's Central Business District, starting with the building's gorgeous beaux-arts style architecture.  With more and more modern, lackluster boxes being erected throughout Seattle, this ornate brick and terra cotta faced beauty is a real stand out.  The inside, while still classic and retaining a few of the building's original elements, is mostly brand new as the building was taken down to the studs in 2006 and rebuilt from the outside walls in metamorphosing from a medical/dental building into luxury apartments.  Herringbone dark wood floors, granite and marble countertops, and air conditioning (yes!) are just a few of the many things that set this building apart.  While ours may not have the biggest roof top terrace in the city, ours is classy.  While ours may not have the biggest gym in the city, ours is in an old bank vault.  And while ours may not have a game room, a pool, a bike-repair station or a dog-washing room like some apartment buildings in Seattle, ours has timeless class.  

Building aside, our location could not be better.  We sit above the University Street Station for the light rail.  Downtown's public transportation hubs surround us.  Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square, Belltown--all a few blocks away, and yet a world away.  Ours is a quiet block as we are surrounded mainly with office towers that empty out at 5pm, but the nightlife offered by our neighboring 'hoods is just a short walk or Uber ride away.  

Overall, The Cobb offers classic style with modern amenities that appeal to those of us who prefer a building with a soul over one with an outdoor fire pit; one with a storied history over one with a modern sterility.

We moved here when the building was just completed, it was called the Vue at that time.  We were drawn by its convenient location to downtown Seattle, it's wide array of local dining options as we'll as boutique shops, and of course, the 2 minute drive to Alki beach.  I work in the heart of downtown and it's just a 5 minute bus ride with several bus lines going directly into Seattle.  However, there is still a quietness and 'local' vibe you get living here.  Since it has become Marq West Seattle, the place has only gotten better.  There are so many amenities living here.  Fitness studio, rooftop lounge, resident events, valet trash, dog wash (they are very pet friendly) and it just goes on.  However, I think the real jewel here is the staff.  Kristofer, Greg, and Jackie are always so friendly and helpful.  It's nice to know that when a problem arises or you just need help, there is an on site staff that prides themselves in making your living experience comfortable and stress free.  We love this place and you will too!!!
Very well maintained building with modern apartment. Staff has been very helpful over the years. Great views of Mt Rainier on the South side of the building.

I love living in the Vue. Spacious common area and roof top with 2 grills are amazing. The only drawbacks I can think of are fitness room is too small and dysfunctional, and for a studio unit, we can only open one window, which even can't be fully opened.

It's very clean, and in a good centrally located area next to several restaurants and bars.  The people are friendly, but also know how to mind their business.  The common areas are fantastic with amazing views of Seattle at night.  The staff are very friendly as well, plus they put out cookies and have a fully stocked Keurig in the front entrance area. The only thing bad is the sparse fitness room the size of a walk in closet, and the only window in the apartment that opens less then halfway.  Otherwise, it's delightful.

My dog, my fiancé, and I are in love with where we live!  The Vue is brand new, and in the perfect location in West Seattle.  We renewed our second lease in May, and are enjoying our 2BRM space with full views of the Seattle skyline.  April, our leasing office manager, is wonderful.  We would be SO EXCITED to win free rent for this upcoming year, so that we can stay here longer.  Thanks!

Vue is a nice, big-box type apartment building in West Seattle. The apartments vary from studio to two bedroom, all with washer/dryer (as someone who lived on the east coast for five years, this fact never ceases to amaze me!). The common areas are all very nice, with spectacular views of the city and Mt. Rainier.  The dog run out back is nice if you have a pup, and the maintenance team is quick and responsive. I have found the building to be pretty quiet with not too much noise transfer between apartments (though I've heard otherwise from a few other tenants, so maybe I'm just lucky).  The building is built green, so our utility bills are generally pretty low. I'm pretty happy to live here.

A few cons:
1. The windows don't open very far, so the apartments can get H-O-T during the summer (especially if you have an east or west facing apartment). The building-provided air conditioners are ineffective (plus, you have to pay extra for them).
2. Management can sometimes be difficult to work with. Miscommunications have been unfortunately common for us. Because Greystar is a massive corporation, you don't get the kind of human-to-human service you would get at a smaller building.
3. Parking is inadequate for all tenants, and expensive (over $100/month). Street parking is mostly adequate, though.

I love our apartment. We are located with in walking distance to restaurants and bus lines. We have great roof top deck looking on to downtown Seattle and mount Rainer. Hardwood floors throughout, except bedroom is carpeted,large den for home office and storage. My only complaints are the bathroom contains the washer and dryer which leaves you with only a walk in shower without a bath tub. Also the bedroom can only really fit a queen bed and our bedroom closet is designed in such a way it renders part of the space almost unusable (long and narrow,a good foot of it is behind the front wall)We have lots of storage, and a modern kitchen with great sturdy counters with extra space to do dinner prep,it has a dinning bar attached as well. Great one space for a couple close to the city, in one of the most up and coming neighborhoods in Seattle wa.

The floor plans are designed to maximize the amount of usable space in each apartment. The layouts are quite open, and the windows are large. If you're on the street side of the building, your view is of the apartments across the street, but if you're high enough you can probably see Seattle over them. On the opposite side, your view is of either trees or of Mount Rainier if you're high enough to see over the trees.

The amenities are quite good. The common room has a kitchen and a TV, and while it in theory has a BluRay player, not many people have ever gotten the BluRay to work. The kitchen doesn't get much use, since the stovetop has induction burners and there aren't any induction compatible pots available in the room, so you have to provide your own. The terrace is a pleasant place to relax, and has two barbecues. On the roof there is a pleasant lounge with a large dining table and some extra seating and a beautiful view. The rooftop terrace has even better views than the lounge, plus two barbecues, a TV and a firepit. Same situation with BluRay of course... and it took nearly a year for the building maintenance to get the firepit working. There is a fireplace, but it offers no warmth, just a  pleasant ambiance while watching TV on the roof.

The staff are invariably friendly, and the ladies (currently) in reception are no exception. If they have a package for you and you're going to get home too late to pick it up, you can e-mail them a request to leave it in your apartment.

The building is quite secure, requiring a fob for access to basically everything. The visitors' garage is open during the day as is the lobby, and that's about it.

From what I understand, parking is a bit of a trial. The garage is to small and has too many parking spots, so getting in and out can be difficult.

The location is great; it's a short walk to Trade Joe's, QFC, Beer Junction, and even the Luna Park Cafe, plus there is plenty of transit available, including express buses that take around 15 minutes to reach downtown Seattle, though the rush hour traffic tends to hold them up a bit.

Overall, I recommend The Vue in spite of the fact that it is pretty expensive.

I decided to downsize and SIMPLIFY LIFE, so I sold everything I own and decided to find the smallest, nicest studio apartment I could find with the best view of my favorite city (and home town), Seattle. I could not have asked for better at THE VUE in West Seattle. It has THE BEST view of Seattle and the waterfront (180 degrees from Mt. Baker to Mt. Rainier!), BRAND NEW awesome studios with large decks (in additions to great 1,2 & 3 bedrooms & amazing lofts!), indoor parking and the best bonus of all is a super professional,  extraordinary and caring staff. The rooftop garden has a unique outdoor large screen TV, TWO gas fireplaces/grills and the staff hosts GREAT parties for the apartment community.  I don't have a pet but the building is extremely pet friendly. The staff insures that this community remains an awesome place to live, day after day. After one year, I am still happy as can be and have NO intentions of leaving. THE VUE is some of the best living that Seattle has to offer!!

There are three reasons why I love this building. First the location - it is right of of Avalon way, close to the bus stop and situated on the hill with Downtown, Mt. Rainier and West Seattle Stadium views. Second the facility - the amenities are outstanding and the facility is kept clean. The staff responds quickly and appropriately to requests for service. The third reason is that when we were renting the apartment we were going through some challenging changes and the manager was responsive even after hours which made everything so much easier.

"This community was an extremely beautiful, well kept and peaceful community. Everything was so beautiful that I felt like I was at a resort. The office staff was extremely accommodating and friendly also. It could not be better located and was amidst a lot of shopping, restaurants, transportation and schools. It offered amenities that most communities did not."
Great place, great price and great manager. The Vue apartment is definitely a place to check out.

Between the super helpful always smiling staff ready to assist in any way possible to the breathtaking views and immaculately kept rooftop deck, the Vue is a place myself, my daughter and my dog will never forget

The vue has a great location and is very clean and modern. The rooftop has the perfect view and is great spot for a weekend hangout! The gym is a little small, but at least they have one! There is street parking that can be a little hard to find, but it's there. I enjoy living here and probably will for awhile!
The staff are great, but the property is built poorly. I've heard some horror stories, but haven't had any issues myself.

The office manager (April) is by far one of the most fake people I've every come across. David, the maintenance person, on the other hand, is great! Very real, seems like he works hard. I always see him cleaning, fixing, etc. I don't know how he does it! This whole property by himself, and with so much to do!

Super awesome amenities, close to literally everything, yet far enough to be able to find street parking. Safe area.

My experience with trying to lease here was initially a positive one until the day of moving in. On the day of my lease start date, I arrived to find an unkempt apartment that had a stench of smoke, cleaning items, as well as an ozone machine sitting on the kitchen counter. A week earlier, I had been shown this same apartment and was promised a clean and smoke-free environment. After bringing these critical issues to the attention of the staff at this building, I was told that they would need an additional week to clean it and get it ready for residence. Sigh. I was also given three options because of their negligence: the first was to lease a slightly larger floor plan that was $450 more per month, or to move into a smaller floor plan that was not desirable for about the same cost. No other concessions were given nor was the property manager willing to make any other exceptions to ensure that I could still move that weekend. The final and only option was to be let out of the lease altogether with deposits and fees returned. I made them aware of my timeline since it was very narrow and specific, and they kept assuring me that all would be fine. To be asked to wait seven more days wasn’t possible for me.
