The only other time available to make a big move would be in July. Even after explaining all of this to them, they still only apologized and I left that day angry, besides myself and in shock that my entire time used to get myself moved there was for naught. In the days after this experience, I began to file formal complaints with their regional offices to explain my situation. I asked to be compensated for all the time and trouble their lack of follow through created for me. Their messages were a mixture of, we are sorry and there isn’t more we can do for you. In summation, here is $500 for the trouble this has caused you. While I am appreciative that they were taking ownership of this mess, the amount given does not fully compensate for the extensive amount of wasted time, energy, mental wellness, and troubles experienced. I was pigeonholed back to the same residence. I asked AvalonBay to help make this right by providing me the exact amount needed to pay back this current lease buyout. Their response has been more of the same, even when they acknowledge that this was their doing. In short, what I have experienced in all my years of leasing will not compare to this disappointment and the handling of it.
Received a reservation fee on top of the application fee months later after making an application. This additional fee was not clear in the application or website.

Don’t live here. They’ll raise you rent like mad after 1 year and then offer it for a lower price to the next person. It’s like they want people to leave. 

There are constantly broken elevators and serious security issues. The cherry on top is how the leasing office always pushes these problem onto the residents. They take no responsibility for keeping the residents safe. 

If you live here; they will screw your over at some point.  Bet.

The building has had multiple break ins. 
They raised the rent over 16%
They attempted to charge an 1800 cleaning fee on a basically clean apt after we signed up for the cheap 135 fee. 
Creepy stalkers in the building threatened my bf. 
The staff changes over every other month. 
Homeless people will break in to the lobby often as the building has no security. 
Overall regret living there. Kinect towers, excelsior, pike motor works, there's multiple better newer cheaper options.

I did enjoy living in AVA for the 6 months I was there, mainly just based on location. Unfortunately when I moved out they kept my deposit and charged me for a full cleaning fee even though I spent a lot of time cleaning  and making sure the place was spotless. When I reached out and asked why I was charged for that, I got a response from what I assume is the corporate office basically stating that the charges were valid and that I should pay promptly to avoid being forwarded to a third party collection agency.

In fairness getting a deposit back is usually a fantasy with any apartment complex, but this one was especially annoying.

The floors and ceilings are paper thin. You can hear people walking in the hallway above you (it's really loud) or your upstairs neighbors walking back and forth to the kitchen or bathroom.

Not built to last at all. Elevators are often out-of-order. The doors and gates to enter the building and property from the street can be very frustrating. The key reader on the eastern gate was broken for a week or so on multiple occasions. The southwestern door leading towards the elevator is malfunctioning in that you have to push it, then pull, otherwise it won't open. If you just pull, it snags or something. 

Common amenities can sometimes look like a stampede came through. Many walls are already scuffed and dented. 

There's no shade on the roof, so you and your guests just melt in the sun or freeze in the rain.

I don't even think some of the apartments have bathtubs. Maybe it's just me, but that seems crazy cheap.

The lounge area is pretty cool.

Constant construction due to it being a very old complex, cheap and outdated finishes, horrible elevators (be prepared to wait a long time for an elevator), basically no security or secure entrance in 3/4 buildings (only one building has a concierge who keeps track of who comes and goes - in the other buildings anyone can get in behind a resident at the doors), huge water leak took out several floors of one of the towers recently (again old complex, so a lot of things go wrong), constant break ins in the parking garage and water leaking in when it rains (this honestly scares me in terms of structural security of the complex).  Completely overworked and understaffed management, leasing, security, and concierge staff.  Not worth whatever you think you like about this complex!  Plenty of nicer and better run buildings downtown.

The first couple years here were great, but don't move into this place as it is now. Pros: close to the light rail, close to Target, near lots of things to do. The cons: everything else. The constant construction is louder and more disruptive than they will imply at the point of reviewing the lease. There are so many Airbnbs in these towers that you basically feel like you live in a hotel with zero consistency in who is around. I don't have many comments on the management because they are largely absent, not communicating any safety concerns and doing the bare minimum to look after resident welfare. The elevators are constantly under construction, making it a nightmare for anyone whose movement is impaired by a disability or injury. The prices are too high to justify the constant breakins, package theft, non-functional security and concierge, and noise levels. Not to mention the number of people I have spoken with who have dealt with roaches and similar pests. Oof, just look elsewhere.

I have been so disappointed in Harbor Steps.  The location is so good, but it's not worth the price you pay for the lack of security (this is a huge problem!), old buildings and outdated units, lack of service (there is one concierge doing the job of at least 3 people meaning they can't keep anyone in the job for very long and service is HORRIBLE - basically don't rely on them for anything).  Also lack of elevators and them constantly breaking down or reserved for moves means you'll wait a LONG time every time you come and go from your apartment.  The worst part of living at Harbor Steps though?  They rent out a ton of units as AirBnB's to tourists (even during Covid!).  This means loud parties with no accountability from management, tourists packing elevators with all their stuff (leading to longer waits), using the consierge to check in and out and ask questions meaning they are not available for residents, and packing and abusing the common areas (gyms, pools, etc).  Do not rent here!  We've been touring other properties in preparation for our lease expiring and no place we've toured has these problems.  Look elsewhere, trust me.

Having rented regular and luxury apartments, I can whole heatedly say that the price tag associated with these apartments does not equal to the value you receive. They also AirBNB multiple units across the buildings and allow them to treat our homes like hotels with littering, noise, and parties during Covid. Security is almost non existent. I have seen many transients in the building and was even threatened by one at the locked entrance once. Maintenance is hit or miss, the dog park trash is sometimes full for days and there are no doggy bags. I saw the same gutter step(which is a safety issue) broken for days. It’s essentially maintained by “not my job” maintenance. Because they airbnb they also never reopened the gyms or any of the amenities we pay insane rent for. No discounts. No help. Just regurgitated replies. I think the tipping point for me was when they allowed an Airbnber to enjoy over five days of noise complaints and did nothing to prevent it. They’re constantly telling you to call concierge when you make requests but they have never NOT ONCE answered my call in the 7 months I’ve lived here. There are so many better options available that I would personally never rent here again or recommend this place to anyone. Spare yourselves, you’ll be happy you did.

This is going to be the most real review on here. 

Pros: 
-Location! It’s literally in the middle of everything.
-Concierge: Amazing staff and lots of convenient accommodations
-Well kept property and great service staff 
-Many different floor plans to meet all needs
-Resident discounts for property restaurants 

Cons:
-If someone is moving in/out the elevators can be super slow. I have waited 5 minutes just to get back up to my unit 
-Von’s restaurant is amazing! But if you are in the SE tower facing the courtyard and 1st Ave, you’ll get smoked out by the restaurant’s exhaust. I haven’t been able to have my windows open during most of the day due to the smoke. And with no a/c, that’s a problem 
-Community utilities: The sewer bill is paid equally by all residents. So if there are less residents, you pay more. I don’t think that’s a fair system given that someone else flushing their toilet more often means you pay. Also, we are all charged for gas due to the hot water heater that apparently everyone in the building shares. Finally, the utilities are paid through a service that charges all residents a service fee. That’s not really fair given we don’t have a choice and are made to pay this fee against our will.

Lived here for the past three years. The first two went ok but at the end of each of my lease terms I'd have to try and fend off at least a 10% rent increase per month for the following year. The past year was even more difficult. Rates increased but no access to the facilities due to COVID. I understand that is out of Harbor Steps' control but there was no discount or credit offered to off-set the lack of use or to address the noticeable decrease in the standard of living. In-fact, rates stayed the same even as people started moving out quickly. 

The concierge team is the only part of living there that was top-notch. They were enormously helpful and always followed through. Couldn't speak more highly of that team. 

That area of the city has turned into a pretty unsafe place to walk around (especially at night) and the security guards in the building don't offer much to keep the residents safe. I had to personally throw homeless folks out of the building on multiple occasions. It got so bad in that area that it drove me to leave Seattle all together. I will not miss the homeless camps across the street, local stores closed down, constant drug use and seeing needles on the sidewalks (on a daily basis). 

When I moved out after three years I got stuck with partially paying to paint and clean. Open for interpretation as to whether that is fair but after having paid rent for three years, living solo (no pets) and being a super clean person, I felt it was unwarranted. 

Don't live in this area. The city is falling apart and your rent will be far too high to justify what you will be required to deal with.

Great place to live. Excellent location with easy access to capital hill, downtown, and slu. The apartments strike a good value balance for quality and features. Sometimes isnt as fancy as competing buildings but the important stuff is very well done like appliances, layouts, amenities, community events. Would recommend.
Excellent location, quiet throughout the building, helpful and friendly staff, great room layouts and generous amenities.

We've been here for 2  years and we can't recommend it enough. Staff, amenities and the community in general is great. AMLI really spoils tenants by ensuring you have a stress-free experience. Price is average for the area but completely worth it.
5/5 Community! Perfect place to live in dt Seattle :)

Excellent place to live with a variety of floor plans and price points. Shared spaces are best in class- the 41st floor is an amazing perk! Friendly and super helpful staff. Location is very central and convenient to multiple locations (10-15 minute walk to Capitol Hill, SLU, and Pike place) Highly recommend!
AMLI Arc's staff was absolutely wonderful throughout our leasing and move-in process, and continue to make the building feel welcoming, comfortable, and secure.
It is a nice, cean, quiet neighborhood, close to downtown and grocery stores. The building has all amenities to feel yourself comfortable. It has very nice and professional team.
The staff is phenomenal, very nice and helpful, amenities are amazing, and property feels clean and safe/secure.
Great place, great staff, great location, great maintenance.
Cypress has great leasing staff and community. The upkeep of the building makes it a great place to live.
Cypress is a great option for people who work in downtown Seattle. excellent neighborhood and great transportation options. Reasonably well maintained and courteous staff.

My overall experience at the beginning was good but recently it has been the worst.

The security of the building is horrible. The car garage gate has been broken most of the time which made some of un authorized vehicles to park in the parking garage.

I parked in a reserved parking lot and for the 5th time, some other vehicle parked in my spot not for a little bit but for a couple of days! I have reported it to the security as well as management but they haven’t done anything about it. I have to patiently wait for the vehicle parked in my Spot which I pay for every month to move. I tried calling the towing company listed everywhere in the parking garage that suppose to tow any unauthorized vehicle parked there but the towing company will only entertain you if you work for cypress.

I think that in general this is not a secured place as people can park freely in what’s supposed to be a secure garage and management won’t do anything about it. This can compromise residents safety as when you get in the garage, you can access some part of the building.

Cypress management touts community but fails to understand what's necessary for a community to thrive. The amenities eventually are reflected in your monthly invoice which, ostensibly, adds another $100-$200 to your rent. If you don't see yourself utilizing the community spaces it will not be worth considering this place at all.

I love living here at Cypress! The staff is so friendly and professional and the community events are great. The building is very clean and modern and I like all the secure entrances to keep us safe. My favorite place is the rooftop with the amazing views of Mount Rainier and watching fireworks from the TMOBILE stadium!
amazing community, everyone is beyond helpful and friendly. community is kept clean and beautiful. highly recommend!

Living at Cypress has been a great experience because the property is very modern and well maintained and the amenities are amazing if you like a top notch gym and spectacular views from the rooftop. Also the staff here is genuinely courteous and very prompt to help with any maintenance needs or questions.The common areas and grounds are very clean and the modern appliances in the apartment are wonderful. I also like the security of the entry doors and common areas for our safety. I am very pleased I moved here and would recommend  this apartment community to anyone.

Living at Cypress has been fabulous. The residents and staff have all been incredibly helpful, friendly, and professional; the community areas are beautiful and well-maintained; and the apartment is well-maintained.

There are a lot of nice amenities and its pretty close to Capitol Hill and downtown where theres stuff to do. My apartment also has most of the stuff I need and storage space. Big windows too for a lot of light.
Aesthetically pleasing building and common areas.  Room for improvement from office staff in regard to response times.

Moving to Cypress has been such a great experience! The leasing team (I worked mostly with Kody) is so great and definitely a tipping point in my decision to apply to the building. Even after moving in, they have made themselves very available for any questions or concerns. The building is gorgeous. Everything feels very new and well maintained. All staff at Cypress are friendly and helpful. The building offers plenty of opportunity to join the community.

Overall I like Cypress and the nice amenities. The regular rate of the apartments is pretty high, but the location and close proximity to both the light rail and mini train are a great way to get around. They have great promotions to new residents, I'm curious to see if they offer any to residents at renewal?

This place is amazing in almost every way. Rooftop area is really nice, with high-quality grills and fire pits. Fitness center is the best I've seen from an apartment building in my life. There's a dog room if you have dog/cat pets. Beautiful courtyards. Security measures for apartment and doors and mail are solid. Leasing office staff is the best ever! The building and amenities are very clean, also. This has been by far my favorite place to live in the city.

The only negative I can think of is parking in the First Hill neighborhood is basically the worst--near-zero parking initially, add on some nearby construction and it becomes actual zero parking available. Worth it to get s few $300-$400 tickets per year than pay for monthly parking in the garage (which according to my recollection is at least $200/mo), but if you plan to pay more than $2400 in tickets per year, then you might want to pay for garage parking.

I'm very disappointed with the poor service and outcome of my experience with Greystar. Greystar took over Cypress Apartments near downtown Seattle from another company. In doing so - as we called frequently to check in and try to help - took more than a month to process our application. By then, the move was no longer suitable for us. They are an enormous company, but rejected our request and pocketed the $80 application fee, instead of refunding it to us. That is not the right thing to do and Greystar needs to treat people better.

I have been living in this place for 1 year and a half. Their management is awful. They change their management a lot. The only thing doesn't change is that they are always trying to charge you something extra. For my past 3 leases, it has never been right. I have to talk to their staff again, again and again to make it right. The other thing is that the isolation between each apartment is extremely bad. My neighbor smoked marijuana and that makes my living room very smoky. I've reported this issue 4 times and they never took any effective actions. They are trying to be a nice person much more than caring about the life and health of their residents.

I just moved here from Chicago and love my new apartment. It’s in a good location, near restaurants and shops but also off busy roads making it have minimal traffic noise. It’s also within in walking distance to work, about 11 minutes to my work at Amazon Brazil building. The staff was friendly and helpful as well. Only downside is my view which mainly looks at an old building but the rooftop is awesome and has a great view of a lake and downtown. Would definitely recommend this building!

Honestly, you're better off NOT renting here. I've been here for about 3 months now and there have been so many issues that your safety is at question while living here. 

Since living here, we've had issues with the front and side doors where the doors did not lock and despite telling the staff, they did not care to fix this until months later. A side door was broken into and bikes were stolen with management's only reaction is leaving a piece of paper with tape saying not to leave bikes in the bike storage.

Another issue is how overpriced it is. You pay a premium for what, the location? The sterile SLU where there is no nightlife, culture, or anything ever happening here other than homeless people breaking into buildings? If you care to use parking it's an ALL or NOTHING deal where once you sign up for parking you're locked in for $200 a month until the lease ends. You can't use it on a per-month-basis.

Management neglects the tenants while treating them as a source of revenue - your well-being and safety are not a priority to them. You're only $$$ to management of this place. Save yourself the stress and live elsewhere.

Apartments themselves are OK, but almost everything else is awful. From cleanliness, to maintenance of community areas, hallways, stairwells, outside areas, trash chutes, parking, elevators, leasing office, noise, crime, intrusion of outsiders, mail, places for pets, rooftop… the worst of the worst. Depressing place.

I've lived here 2 years and this building has gotten considerably worse - garage door breaks constantly. Recycling chute has been down for MONTHS, paying for Fetch delivery service (when residents didn't want it and even with that, packages get stolen from doorsteps INSIDE the building). Noisy AF. Homeless people seem to break in hide out in the stairwells. Cars and storage lockers getting broken into. Not a safe place to walk around at night, especially in the Harborview block. 

Do not recommend.
Having ac ports does not give you the right to advertise air conditioning as an amenity. They are two completely separate things.

Management is forcing all residents to sign a contract with a 3rd party delivery service called Fetch. Many residents have complained of delayed deliveries or packages intercepted from residents who have not agreed to be a Fetch customer. Being close to the hospitals means constant noise from emergency vehicles. Also, the neighborhood is overrun with sketchy individuals and safety is a concern at all times. Do Not Recommend.

Poor management. They do not listen to your problems. Now they are switching over to a new package delivery service called Fetch(they sell your data to 3rd party individuals). It’s also very loud by the hospital and we get a lot of sketchy behavior around the building. I wish security was better as well. I would not recommends living here. The price is not worth it.

I rented an apartment and there was a loud noise resonating throughout. The noise was particularly loud in the master bedroom. I called and informed the staff at Saxton immediately. It took a month before they resolved the issue and then only after I pleaded with them to send someone to see what it was. I averaged about 3 to 4 hours of interrupted sleep during this time since the noise cycled every 20 mins, rumbling and then subsiding. I requested they comp my rent since the conditions of my unit effected my health as a result of sleep deprivation and should not have been rented in that condition. They empathized with me and said they were there to listen but wouldn’t do anything more than that since I said it sounded like a freight elevator, even though I’m not near a freight elevator and it took numerous complaints before they investigated what the source of the noise was and resolved the issue. This could have been accomplished in 3 days of my moving in if they cared enough about their community of tenants.

Building manager admitted that they have no idea what goes on after hours. The common area sound system started blaring music at 3:30am and again at 5:45am and instead of providing solutions to make sure that it doesn't wake up the entire neighborhood again, his tone was rude and condescending because of the numerous people who complained about the noise, no one called the police. They don't have any maintenance or staff after business hours so the (under resourced) Seattle police are apparently the only way to stop the technical malfunctions of a luxury apartment building...  There apparently isn't a fix, so it could easily happen again.

Too much theft and break ins happening and not being disclosed to residents for safety.  Several packages of mine were stolen, and they won't even investigate. Property manager just said to tell amazon that package was stolen. They don't care at all.

Trash rooms are filled with trash and very unsanitary. Garage parking is too expensive for the area it's in. 150-250 is the price range for cap hill area, this is central district/little Saigon area and garage parking is 250.

Property manager isn't consistent very rude and not helpful.

Amenities are not kept up, and theft and break-ins are rampant. Not safe.

I picked this place for price and convenience. Which it has pretty well.

On the amenities, it says bed, but like the other reviewer mentions there is no mattress. Transparency is always appreciated.
No Stove or mattress, I cant live with only a microwave.

When I first called around looking for an apartment, Kylee was on top of things immediately. She was so helpful& I hadn’t even decided yet if this was the right home for my family but the process was so easy, the apartment & amenities were so beautiful & the stuff was so great - I didn’t want to look anywhere else. Thank you everyone who helped my little family find our home (=
Staff here is great! Always so helpful - thanks guys!
Great location and a very modern building  with nice amenities. Staff is helpful and maintenance is top rate..
Maintenence has been 10/10 amazing. My only issues are with the cleaning crews not properly cleaning the appliances in the community spaces.
Beautiful, spacious homes — modern appliances and built-in air conditioning. What more could you want?
I love how central I am to everything I need, and have had no issues in 5 months.

Connection on Broadway is a lovely, brand new community in the heart of Capitol Hill. So far, the apartment has been great. It has the newest features and the view is amazing. The amenities included are a great addition and kept up to date which is always nice, and the leasing team are fun and friendly.

Newly moved in— so far, the building is pretty calm & quiet, considering its location (Broadway, Capitol Hill). Additionally, I have yet to have a poor experience with members of the leasing office, and the security on property are all quite kind and considerate.
Connection on Broadway is a great place to live and i especially enjoy the modern appliances in the units.
Maintenance service requests are done quickly and professionally.
Maintenance and office staff have been very quick to reply to me for any issues.

The only good three-bedroom unit in Capitol Hill.

The perfect proximity to transit for an urban lifestyle.

Since new management, this place has become determined to charge you through the nose, and offer nothing in exchange.

Let's take a journey and see what $2000/mo rent and $300/mo parking gets you:

I was locked out of my unit for 6 hours, and both their after hours lockout and emergency maintenance numbers were unreachable. Only when the 1 security guard for 4 buildings found me preparing to sleep on the lobby floor did I get back in. But now, the building announced security can no longer help with lockouts.

Packages will get stolen within the hour, unless you sign up for an unreliable personal delivery to your door.

Toilet broken? Gas leak? No heat in 30deg weather? No emergency maintenance, see you in 1-3 business days.

Stuck outside in 40deg rain without your phone? Tough luck, there's no lockout help. 

But don't worry, if you do enough tasks on their app, you can get a $5 gift card.

I love living in this community. While the apartments have undergone many changes since our arrival, the staff seem to have managed great! The apartments themselves are brand new, spacious, and the design is intuitive. There are various recreational spaces that are absolutely fabulous! The location is the best in Capitol Hill. There are three buildings to choose from, each with its own unique appeal. The staff has been responsive, courteous, and always welcoming when I visit the office.

The reviews about having a hard time contacting the office is true. It’s terrible. I called the number on Google to inquire about leasing and it goes to their answering service. I was given a direct line, left a voicemail and still no return. I’m concerned that if it’s like this normally, how do tenants get their concerns addressed in a timely manner? Other reviews stated the managers number: voicemail not set up.

Update: I had to email them. (Rather than making sure someone returned my calls.) I was able to schedule for a viewing but due to the snow, we rescheduled for 12/31/21. I get there, offices look closed. I call the answering service and the confirmed the office is open. No one ever showed up. Unprofessional. I don’t know how this is ok and continues to run like this even when the manager has promised changes over the last few months based on what I’m seeing on the reviews here. I’ve noticed a lot of open apartments. Some haven’t been filled since they opened and now I see why. I hope current tenants are able to post honest reviews to help others out. There definitely needs to be some changes when they’re charging a premium.

Location is good and the building is new, so there is that.  The buildings are a smokers paradise.  People smoke in their units, on the sidewalk right outside your window, in the entry ways, everywhere and mgmt does nothing about it.  Even members of the leasing team smoke in areas designate as non-smoking, it's terrible.

Lived here for over a year, and it's a huge disappointment. Maybe the biggest sin is that the parking garage gate has been broken for over a month - it's bent and warped, missing panels, and has caution tape and wooden boards on it. It looks like a crime scene or a trash heap. Coupled with the fact that the hallways and parking garage have rank smell, trash, and furniture everywhere, it feels like a broken down, abandoned building. Can't wait to leave when my lease ends.

Management is helpful and responsive. Khai is great! I’d describe my individual experience as decent and unproblematic, while still acknowledging that there are others who have not been as fortunate. A flooding incident caused a lot of damage and garage doors / elevators have broken down. Despite these challenges, management has done their best to communicate and get things fixed.

If you’re looking for a convenient, modern space to call home, Iron Flats Apartments is a great choice. Ignore reviews posted before mid-2023, when a new, responsive management team took over. Virtually every matter posted in negative reviews has been corrected. A new package receiving protocol and building entry system are in place, and management is working hard fixing water damage to East Building caused by a Winter 2024 frozen pipe. I moved into the building just after it opened and would still be there if I hadn’t moved out of state. You’ll find a friendly welcome by the office and maintenance staffs

This place is comfy and situated walking distance from great food, the light rail, Green Lake, and much more! New management is very welcoming and easy to talk to. If you ever need anything, they are there to help! Go Larry!

Having lived at Iron Flats since its opening, here are the list of realities of living at this location that you do not see on tour. There are some reoccuring themes:

1) Package Theft 

On 4/17/22, there was a break-in resulting in package theft ; On here was a break-in incident on 9/28/21 resulting in package theft; after October '21 I stopped keeping track as it was becoming a regular occurance (and just getting my packages upon arrival.

The package room is too small for the number of residents, so they keep packages outside the room (making them easy to steal). Additionally, many residents are incapable of picking up their packages promptly, so finding your own package is often a hassle. 

2) Parking Garage 

Multiple break-ins in the parking garage, including someone stealing our garage remote. We were still charged for its replacement. 

The garage has no mirrors, making the turns dangerous 

3) Too Small of a Garbarge/Recycling Room

Every single week, without fail, all garbage bins overflow and recycling overflow because they do not have enough bins, given the number of residents. 


4) Building Was Built Shoddily & Management does not fix promptly 

Multiple false fire alarms - they are sensitive and will send residients out for a false alarm at least once every eight weeks. Response from management is “Better too sensitive than not sensitive enough” and there has been no move to fix the problem. 

Inconsistent hot water - sometimes it is lukewarm 
Multiple broken elevators in the west building, hindering a

Unlocked lobby doors for a month in the West Building 

Our door has needed fixing twice as the building settles 

In April 2022, there was a flood in the West Building that led to water being cut off from our apartment, which also led to concerns about the quality of the building. Residents from the flood had to move our of their apartments for weeks on end while it was fixed. 

Misc Issues

West building units are very loud - you can hear the highway. There is also a fire station down the street so there are often sirens 

You cannot let guests up by buzzing them in at any entrance to your apartment. You are required to go down to get them because they need a key to get up the elevator. 

High turnover of units As of Oct. 2022, they are offering 1 months free rent because they are DESPERATE and people are leaving because of the poor experience they have had here.

High staff turnover - there has been 100% staff turnover.
Perfect location, close to Green Lake and Whole Foods. Charles (asst manager) is awesome! Very responsive and willing to help. Great move in experience!

It has been very pleasant settling into REN.  The team have been extremely helpful with getting us information quickly, and making sure our first-hour experience was excellent, as was the first 24 hours. The residents are very friendly, and the community has a great vibe and activity throughout.  Very pleasant first few days, indeed.

The REN is a well built residential building with great units and amenities. It’s an elevation of living and in a great location. The energy is pretty positive from the lobby, lobby bar, and the rooftops.
Exciting new building that should be on everyone’s shortlist for luxury apartments in SLU
I love my place. Definitely will not be disappointed
Very happy with my decision to move into REN, as it's everything I expected from a luxury apartment building.
Beautiful apartments and great experience working with leasing office.
Great building, terrible leasing options and resolution. Maintenance for the gym is also bad.

I simply love my new apartment. My one bedroom corner unit (B11) is incredible. Modern, stylish, with many high end touches, like a wine rack at the end of the kitchen island. Rooftop is amazing, the well equipped gym means I never have to go to a real gym again (we could use some heavier dumbbells, like 60-100 lbs, but the free weight rack allows heavy lifting, I still give the gym a thumbs way up). Five minute walk to Whole Foods, nice. The apartment is a breath of fresh air from my studio apartments over the past decade.
The leasing process was seamless from start to finish. It was definitely a positively professional experience.
Amazing views, located in the heart of downtown Seattle, Ren is the place for you! The staff are friendly, supportive and helpful. Living the dream :)
Beautiful views, great location, useful amenities and spacious floor plans.

Living at the REN is real deal.  The quality of the apartments, appliances, amenities and technology are perfect.  We are especially pleased with the safety and security of the building and the responsiveness of the outstanding staff.  Add to all this the wonderful location and you’ve got the best place to live in downtown Seattle.  We love it here!

REN is truly an incredible place to call home! They have an amazing staff that makes you feel welcome and taken care of, fun and intelligent community to become part of, and smart features throughout the building that make living here so easy! Everything has been thoughtfully designed in a beautiful way and we have never enjoyed an apartment building more than this one. The location too is perfect, in a calm and safe area, close to everything one would ever need. We are truly grateful to be living in such a wonderful place.

Choosing the REN to call home during a cross country move was the best decision we made. The building, units and amenities are obviously stunning, and is a place anyone would love to live, but the staff is what makes it feel like home.
One of the most amazing views! Great-new building with super friendly staff :)
All the of the staff are super awesome and nice, and attentive.
Great community but building still missing final touches, great if you dont care to wait till everything is finished

My husband and I moved to Seattle temporarily for school and we could not have picked a better place! We loved team here. Gloria at the front desk was always so kind to us. Larry stole my dogs heart the moment they met. And Ben always made sure we were taken care of. The team here is SPECTACULAR. This building is well taken care of and always clean! The apartment had a great layout and worked perfectly for us. It was a very modern space that looked great with little to no décor (which was huge for us since we aren't good interior design). The amenities were a huge plus. We loved the location of the place! It was close enough to all the main attractions but also had easy access to the freeway that led us on many great adventures.

I have been living at the Melody for a couple of months and I love it. The amenities are well thought out and the community is diverse, mature, and thoughtful (example: quiet hours are observed). The rooftop views are unbeatable.  Moving is always hard and super stressful, but the staff at Melody made it easy from a walk through of the property to filling paperwork before the move in date.

The location is perfect…great food, public transport, and a strong neighborhood that is community focused. Highly recommend.

All of the staff here are very nice and professional, they always try to assist me with anything I need. I love my unit so much, the design is very modern and new. This apartment complex have a very unique layout! There is a beautiful courtyard on level two which allows all residents to have window access. When needing fresh air I like to walk the court yard and or roof top. The roof top is spectacular, I can’t wait for it to be summer so that I can enjoy it more. There’s a lot of seating areas and even a few fire places. On the roof top there is also a designated area just for pets. The lobby amenity area is also nice. I love hanging out there with my friends since there is a pool table and complementary coffee! All in all I really recommend this place for anyone who is looking for a place to stay in Seattle!

If you work from home, have young kids, or want any semblance of peace, I would not suggest moving here until changes are made by management. We moved into Melody by Jabooda a few months ago and are having a nightmare experience despite reaching out to leasing agents multiple times throughout the last few months. It is impossible to sleep in these units without being woken up during all times of the early morning hours and night with loud bangs and terrible outdated music (please, for the sake of my ears, let Chris Brown go). Despite the disturbances from other apartments, they won't do anything about this, and yet I'm sure they are still expecting full rent for an apartment I can't even stay in. I wish there were more care given, or at least empathy, to residents, and they were able to hold other occupants accountable to the leasing terms they signed. Until then, again, I suggest not moving here if you value your sanity. Besides the constant disturbances, I've had three packages stolen in this building so far, and I'm not banking on that stopping soon. Stolen packages have become a massive problem here; they now have signs posted by the mailboxes about that. So, while the apartment is nice, the location is okay, and the building itself is well taken care of by the staff, it's just not worth the price if you don't feel comfortable or safe.

These apartments aren’t available until the middle of May 2022 for move in and I’m already obsessed! These units are brand new, spacious and very modern looking. They haven’t finished building the rest of the location yet but you can clearly tell they put in hard work because these apartments look AMAZING and spacious for the price. I hope my application gets accepted because the tour I did already made me feel at home!

Listen, I've enjoyed living here, I love my apartment, but I’m frustrated with how the staff, particularly maintenance, treat residents. It's unprofessional, childish, and weirdly aggressive.

On multiple occasions, they’ve left a box of trash outside my door—the great majority of it not even mine, but other residents’ trash stuffed into a box I placed in the trash room—without any communication about why. This has forced me to gather it up and return it to the trash room. Not a single time this has happened has any person from the office ever emailed, called, texted, or left a notice on my door to explain why they were doing this, so I truly didn't understand what was going on.

And then, last week, they took my package out of what is allegedly supposed to be a "secure" package room and wrote a nasty and really unprofessional note in permanent marker on it (which was NOT trash, but an empty box that was sent to me by Fedex so I could send back my computer monitor to a previous employer, which I needed to do at the end of the term) because they assumed it was trash because it felt empty. I didn’t raise the issue at the time because I didn’t want to escalate things and my anxiety was high, so I broke the box down as I’ve done in every apartment I’ve lived in, and as I did before green leaf took over, by taking off all the tape, and left it in the trash room. Despite that, they continued to leave the box outside my door without any explanation, which felt incredibly passive-aggressive.

Mind you....this was my property that was taken without permission and willfully damaged and yet they're the ones with an attitude?? Like, y'all know I could have filed a report on you, right?

Anyway, I thought our last conversation, where I reached out to the front office over phone about this, ended on a positive note, but this happened again just this morning. Again, they never communicated their expectations and in fact never even sent the follow up email they said they were going to send (twice they told me and twice they didn't follow through), so how am I supposed to know what they want if they don't tell me. I am not a mind reader, and I don’t appreciate being expected to be one or being treated poorly when there’s a misunderstanding or miscommunication that THEY caused. I really do enjoy living here, but this has really soured my experience.

I am very disappointed with this community and do not recommend it for living. I lived there for 14 months and I can say with confidence that this is the worst thing that happened to me. Everything was fine for the first 12 months, but when the owner changed, everything became bad. Moreover, there is no air conditioning in the apartments and it is impossible to live in the summer! You have to sleep with the window open, but the noise from cars and the constant sound of ambulance or police sirens does not let you sleep. That last, the theft of parcels has become more frequent, there is a constant smell of marijuana in the common corridor, dirty and very unfriendly staff. I wouldn't put a single star if there was such an option!

Ellie, Akina, Kailey, Ainsley, Leia, and Dominique at the front desk of Accolade are simply exceptional. Their warmth and professionalism create an inviting atmosphere from the moment you step in. They handle inquiries with efficiency and a genuine desire to assist, making every guest feel valued and attended to. Their attention to detail ensures smooth operations, and their friendly demeanor leaves a lasting impression. Accolade is fortunate to have such dedicated individuals at their front desk. Highly recommended for their outstanding service!

These are extremely nice apartments. Great community rooms and places to relax outside. But best part are the amazing views. The staff is also very nice. Especially Kailey she was very knowledgeable and helped me out a lot. This is a great place to live.
Took a tour with Kailey. Fun girl, answered all of my questions. Good location and seemed like some friendly neighbors. Thanks

Lots of cons.

1. Way more expensive than what was originally understood due to monthly utility fees that are added on each month.
2. The most egregious act is that The Accolade continued to take rent out of my bank account even after my lease was up! After calling 3 times in 3 days without a response, they finally responded by telling me it would take them up to 3 months to return any money that they erroneously took from my account. The manager acted like it wasn't their fault that this happened, as it was a "system issue". 
3. Be very, very careful renting here as they have no problem committing grievous financial acts towards it's renters.

Every interaction I have have with the Accolade staff has been wonderful, they are all extremely friendly and very helpful when it comes to answering any questions I have. They made the signing process very easy and smooth, and I can’t wait to live here!
Signing at the Accolade was a very easy smooth process. Their staff is great and friendly and I can't wait to live there!!

My time at Griffis Belltown has been marred by ongoing issues that reflect poorly on the management's ability to maintain a livable environment. The recurring pest infestations, elevator outages, and prolonged closures of amenities like the gym, pool, and hot tub have significantly detracted from the overall living experience.

Despite efforts to communicate these concerns, the management has been unresponsive and failed to take adequate action. The recent removal of the yoga room, a major selling point, without proper compensation or alternative facilities, further highlights their disregard for tenant satisfaction.

Additionally, safety concerns such as reported break-ins to storage units raise doubts about the property's security measures. Prospective renters should exercise caution and consider alternative options until these issues are effectively addressed.

There are so many other options in Belltown and Seattle, I'd recommend checking out newer communities that wouldn't have all the issues and lack of management action that this one does. 

The elevator was down on 13 separate occasions during my two years there, and each occasion was days - not just a few hours. The pool was closed on 3 separate occasions, sometimes for weeks at a time. The exterminator told me he visits the property frequently due to silverfish infestations. The property was built on an old trash dump, the bugs have invaded over the years (according to him).

I moved out as soon as my lease was up. I never leave reviews, but for this place I had to. There was construction for over a year when I lived here. The construction noise was really annoying throughout the day. Also, there is a serious silverfish infestation. For those of you fortunate enough to not know, let me fill you in. Silverfish are these gross little bugs that are difficult to find and kill, and some people are allergic, as I found out the hard way. There are also a fair number of spiders and other bugs. The no smoking policy is never enforced, and the elevators break down all the time. Management is friendly, but don't expect too much from them. The view from the roof is great, but the handrails on the roof deck are unstable, which is a serious safety hazard. Within walking distance of a really nice park, but overall, so not worth the amount of money they charge.

This complex was better under the old management (Berkshires). Since Griffis came in, they've been under construction for the better part of a year, so those "amenities" we're paying for are never available. They redid a perfectly functional pool deck in the middle of summer, so the pool was only open for a month. They have now decided that they don't like the work that was done on the pool deck so they're closing the hot tub (supposed to be open year round) for the foreseeable future- based on how long its taken all the other projects to be completed, I doubt it will be open until summer of 2018 (and that's being generous). They started construction on BOTH clubhouses at the same time, and neither are finished, rendering both rooms unusable. Equipment in the fitness center is never functioning properly (exercise machines, A/C, water cooler- you name it). They have yet to finish the courtyard (construction on that began in March of 2017), which means that there is no longer a safe place to take your dog out after dark; Belltown is not the most secure area, which they are well aware of, since there have been multiple break-ins, and not 1 BUT 
2 assaults on women within the "secure" building. They didn't even notify residents the first time an assault happened on the property; instead, we found out about it from news crews which were stationed outside to interview unwitting residents regarding the attack. 
Now that we've found a safer and more secure location that we can be comfortable residing in, we are being penalized for breaking the lease. But what penalties can we impose on a negligent apartment complex that isn't living up to their end of the bargain? If you're looking for a place to live in Belltown, you're better off at one of the other hundreds of communities within the area- especially for the rates they're charging (get a brand new apartment with functioning amenities; you'll be happier).

My apartment is like a little townhouse.  The bedroom and laundry room are downstairs from the living room/kitchen/dining area.  The bedroom is spacious and has a nice walk-in closet.  I work nights, so the quiet atmosphere of the downstairs bedroom is very nice.

This complex has great amenities as well as excellent management service. I stayed here for 1 year and I had a wonderful experience. If you enjoy walking around downtown, it takes just a nice 5-10 minute walk to be at the market or enjoying the views from sculpture park. Although the complex is relatively larger for downtown, it is still easy to get around since the elevator is fast and the buildings are easy to navigate. The rooftop has a limited, but beautiful view and has a decent amount of activity during the summer. This place is also great due to the pool which is mildly used and not overcrowded. The building is relatively older than others nearby, but that it's not old enough to have any structural complications etc. There are many dog owners at this property and although the management tries very hard to keep it clean, there are parts of the property that make this fact abundantly clear. The walls are also thin and the demographic is mixed in age so not the place for blaring the music. All that being said, the day to day experience here is pleasant and if I were to move back to downtown Seattle, this would be my residence.

A good place to survive, it has great community that keeps on organizing events, well maintained complex, huge pool and great gym. Since it's in downtown, the heat of the city everything is accessible and at walking distance. It's close to pacific science center, space needle, coffee shops, restaurants and Pike market, all the big shot offices like Amazon and disney are close too.

Overall the place is really nice and the staff is amazing. 

I also really  like its location in SLU. However, in the year and a half that I've  lived there the phase II building's package room has been broken into twice. 

As a result of this they've had to close the package room and tried to have all phase II packages delivered to the leasing office at the phase I building. This was just a minor inconvinience which was  supposed to be temporal, but after three months it doesn't seem like a  temporal thing anymore. 

It has become a real problem since for the  packages that are delivered to the leasing office you are required to  pick them up at leasing office hours which can be complicated for people  on a busy schedule. For example, for my food delivery packages (e.g.  Freshly/Blue Apron) if they are delivered to the leasing office I have to make sure to be able to pick them up before the leasing office closes or else I'd have to pick them up the next day and hope for the food not to be spoiled by then.

For other packages the delivery companies just leave them at phase II's lobby since they don't want to make the trip to phase I one block away. This has resulted in two packages being stolen for me, and while I know this is not management's fault, it is a result of them neglecting to fix the root cause of not having a package room for months now. 

This just feels like a downgrade from the state of the  building when I first moved in and after months of asking the leasing  office and getting a "who knows when it will be fixed" as a response it just seems like this is not something management cares about. 

Overall a pretty good place but if I were to move here knowing this I'd either  make sure I rent on phase I building where this is not an issue or rent on one of the nearby apartment complexes which offer very similar  amenities/appartments for very similar prices but don't have this type of issues.

I really like living at Amli SLU. My move was managed very well, and the staff is amazing. They have all been super helpful with everything. I really like the units - with the large windows, high ceilings and the modern steel appliances. I am also very impressed by the sustainability initiatives at Amli. It's a place I can call home.
After living in various downtown Seattle neighborhoods for 8  years prior to moving into AMLI, I can honestly say this is the most homey feeling I've had.
The best staff and amenities out of all my apartment tours and that was my deciding factor, they are very nice, helpful and efficient!
AMLI has good, clean amenities and their response time for inquiries and maintenance requests are quick! It's pricey but its a good place to live in the city.
AMLI SLU is located in great area. Apartment managers are very helpful. If you are looking for quiet, modern, and simple style apartment, then this is the apartment you are looking for.

I've lived here for over a year and just moved back home. I had a wonderful experience here. Amber the manager is very attentive to making the space as beautiful and welcoming for everyone. I loved her seasonal themed decorations and community building events. When I moved out, she even offered me to help me sell some of my stuff, which no manager has ever offered.  If I come back to Seattle, I will definitely chose to live at Illumina Apartments.

DONNOT RENT HERE, Ridiculous Fees after you move out
Been living there one year and moved out.
Location 2/5: OK, close to the bus station, but the apartment building is near I-5, can be very noisy when you open the window, very disturbing when you cannot sleep, plus the pollution from I5 vehicles. I lived in the top floor, room temperature can reach 90F in the summer.
Amenity: 2/5The apartment itself is built in 2000s so do not expect it to be too good. No fitness room, elevator broke regularly. When I moved in I had to lift heavy bed frames etc to 6 floors with the elevator out of service. So get yourself ready before you move in, you'll never know when the elevator is usable.
Leasing Office: 3/5 was responsive and friendly. Possibly the only good thing.

The previous ones were tolerable to me, but after moving out I found there was more than $200 balance of "Sewer&Trash fee" showed on the resident portal, I didn't think too much and I paid it, then waiting them to return some of my deposits. And just now I received the moveout inspection list, found out it is not "Sewer&Trash Fee," actually they deducted all of my deposit $400, plus this $200+, for some items such as dusty counter-$15, dirty floor-$100, dirty dishwasher-$15(which I did not use ONE TIME during my residence), -summing up to ridiculous $650.

So my comment is, find somewhere else to rent if you don't want to kiss goodbye to your deposits, you can rent a much MOREcomfort and convenient place in SLU or UW, with only adding a few hundred.
Useless management, horrible neighbors. Do yourself a favor and stay far away.

When a friend and I moved to Seattle for fun back in Sept 2018, we were so surprised at how expensive it was to live in the city! We looked high and low for a place with everything we wanted - something close to downtown with in-unit washer and dryer, dishwasher, garage space and bicycle storage. When we found Illumina Lake Union, they met all these needs and more! The rooftop view is amazingly beautiful, especially during New Years and Independence Day celebrations on Lake Union, which is only a couple blocks away. Restaurants and bars are within walking distance, Capital Hill is right across I-5. The staff is the best part of Illumina, however. I absolutely love how warm and friendly they are, and so willing to make sure you feel right at home. Could not recommend it more highly!

Great apartment in a great area but what makes Illumina stand out is the management and staff- big shout out to Amber! There are tons of other apartments in Seattle, but I choose to live in Illumina because of the staff. The staff are always available when you need something, very friendly and always greet you with a smile, knows everyone's names and their pets- even know my friends' names! I barely need maintenance done in my place but when needed, they are very quick to respond. Even though it's in the city, there is a sense of community in Illumina. Grounds are always kept clean, the rooftop has an amazing view with beautiful furniture and a BBQ grill to use, updated furnishings, and washer in dryer in unit. Location is perfect, there's a bus stop right outside although very close to everything. It's in a quiet neighborhood with restaurants in walking distance and has a sense of community. There's an off leash dog park right behind the building which my dog loves, and access to I-5 and I-90 is just a breeze. Been living in Illumina for at least 6 years now and couldn't think of anywhere else to stay in Seattle. Definitely recommend this apartment!

Finding an apartment in Seattle is hard no matter what you're looking for. Finding an apartment, that accommodates a couple working in two different areas of the city, who has a cat and a German Shepherd and who doesn't want to spend all of their salary on rent, is next to impossible! We started our apartment hunt in April, to move in August or September, looking through all renter's and apartment websites, as well as Craigslist, Facebook and other sources. Either it was too expensive, in a location that didn't work for us or we couldn't bring our cuddly German  Shepherd, Ardie. One day, finally, our current apartment showed up on Craigslist and we immediately scheduled a viewing. The administration was super helpful with everything we needed in documents and after a short, informal pet interview, bringing Ardie was no problem at all! We love it here: We're right on five bus lines, the dog park is our neighbor and from the great roof top we can enjoy the view of Seattle and the lake. The apartment has lots of light and space, great updated appliances and wonderful wood floors, that makes cleaning after the pets a breeze. Big french doors let in light and the open plan kitchen/living room allow us to be together, even if we're doing different things. Living at Illumina was definitely the best option for us of all and we're so excited to get to stay here as long as possible!

It's an amazing apartment building. Its location is very convenient, close to everything, it's in downtown. You don't need any transportation if you live in downtown and close to your job. The team is very helpful. I would recommend it to anyone!
Via6 has wonderful living accommodations for any need, with friendly staff and a perfect location to boot. Pat and Trent are superstars

Elevators constantly broken, trash chutes often broken, maintenance requests are often slowly fulfilled, Victor tavern taking community space away, broken grills, broken / removed TVs, etc. Longtime resident growing frustrated.

Great location, decent living spaces, friendly concierge staff (shoutout to Isa and AJ!)--amenities come up a little short:  small weight room / workout room (would be great if they were connected), and with the construction, losing the movie room was unfortunate. 7th floor terrace is great to relax. Maintenance requests may never get addressed unless you hunt down concierge / management, and price jump into second year leasing options can be shocking.

Via6 is amazing place to live in Seattle. I enjoy living in this building immensely! First of all it's situated in the best location in Seattle, it's close to everything - grocery store (WholeFoods), Pike market place, great coffee places and restaurants. It's close to all the sports studios, if you are an active person, you will find all the options to try out to be fit. It's clean and safe - security works at the front desk 24 hours a day. Leasing team is very helpful and pleasure to speak to. The building has a free gym and a beautiful roof top. There's a bagel place and an open terrace restaurant downstairs. I feel very comfortable and enjoy my experience at Via6 very much! It's my favorite place to live in.
Via 6 do not respect your schedule, is non communicative and allow strangers to trespass apt without prior authorization.
Overall my experience at Hana has gone very well. Management is amazing and very helpful and maintenance requests are answered quickly and work is efficient
Ha sido gratificante vivir aquí en jana apartaments
I love my apartment it’s perfect for me and my commute to work and the location and rooftop view is amazing
Hana is a quiet safe place to live the workers are great no issues

I knew the first time I walked in a friend's unit that the apartments were nice and modern. Stone counter tops in the kitchen, full sized bathroom with washer\dryer. An excellent staff, cozy floor plans makes the Hana an wonderful place to call home.

This place is amazing. Friendly professional staff who attend with concern to my needs. The apartment is beautiful and the open kitchen and stone counter tops makes everything feel very fancy. The view is spectacular and my 2 minute commute to work puts the cherry on top.
A place that actually feels like home with a lot of natural light and lake view. All of this at a more economical rate than other fancy apartments.
East Howe Steps is my first resident of many to truly feel like home!
I live here since my day one Seattle and I like it.
This is a great place for interns to rent an apartment!  The building is right on a major bus line, and is in a nice neighborhood!
Excellent location, friendly staff and overall positive vibe

Hey so currently live in this apartment complex and we have been broken into multiple times by people using a crow bar on the doors to go down to our “secure” storage units. And the response from management was “theft can happen anywhere and we are looking into getting new doors and replace your storage unit locks with a more secure one ” but there was no immediate action done to keep us and our belongings safe. I would think that the first time it happened they immediately would have fixed the doors but a week later the doors into the complex our still broken. Don’t live here the management does not care about you and your belongings.

We decided on visiting the Rivet on a recommendation from our corporate housing liaison. We rented an apartment on the spot. We looked the previous week at about 20 other apartment complexes. The Rivet was clean, well maintained and suit our needs. My wife walks five minutes to work. The staff is warm and friendly and any issues are taken care of immediately. I was glad to hear that the corporate housing part of the building is being phased out. 
We look forward to living here for a long time.

As I found myself in an unlikely situation with my hotel I booked upon my arrival to Seattle I passed by the Shelby building and instantly was drawn to the only leasing sign that had green balloons. This was  the first sign I’ve seen in this city that had such an inviting energy. I met both Rochelle and her associate Jade who undoubtedly removed any hesitations I had on if I would be housed or not. To have these two beautiful and kind women show me such diligent dedication to their job and to getting me settled in one of the many  STUNNING unit’s that are still available was a god send. The entire process was more streamlined and accommodating (offered a refreshing array of artisan keurig coffee I’ve never seen) that I felt truly at home here at the Shelby and I hadn’t even received my keys. As a Philadelphia native I was nervous at how I would be received with seattle being known for having the infamous “seattle freeze” but thanks to Rochelle and Jade I know for certain this city has outstanding individuals that are making a difference and literally saving lives.

Ive been doing apartment living nearly a new city a year for the past 4, and after months of sloughing through emails and contacting dozens of buildings for my most recent move, Ive never met a team as committed to helping me have a smoother and easier transfer. If youre looking to move anywhere in the king county area i couldnt recommend a better building and community to accommodate you than The Shelby.

I moved to Seattle from jersey City in the middle of Pandemic. Taylor was very easy to talk to and could accommodate my needs as a fully online applicant. In 3 weeks of being here, I have had a very good experience.

The Shelby is wonderful. The building is in a great location and very well taken care of. The staff is wonderful and they take such amazing care of their residents. I highly recommend this for anyone looking for an apartment.
Love living here! The staff is very friendly and helpful. The location is convenient to transit and shopping needs. Great, quiet, secure building. Very happy about living here.
The apartment is just what I need. I know other apartment buildings can offer so much more, but I stay because it's a smaller community and the staff are excellent!

This apartment community is well maintained and in a great location. Blocks from the space needle and pikes market! Great and friendly management and quick responses to any service requests. The building is secure with a fob entry which was very important to me! The layout of the apartment is phenomenal and spacious!

Applying, signing, and moving into the Shelby was a convenient and easy process. The management has been great with communication and has addressed any needs and concerns I have had. My studio apartment is in incredible condition. The Shelby's location is in walking distance of nearly everything one might need to live in downtown Seattle. I have yet to have any issues with noise from the street or other residents. I have no complaints so far!
Awesome location, modern interiors, and super friendly staff.
During the covid crisis rent relief was never offer even when I extended my stay.  Do not rent a apartment near the alley it is to noisy.
If you are new to Seattle, this is a good place to start living near the downtown. Everything is close by and easy to access.
The leasing agent I signed with was professional and made the leasing experience easy. I love my space and living in the middle of Belltown.
I really like the apartment and even the community. The location is prime, walking from downtown. The apartment has all the basic amenities and the floor plans are good too.

I just moved to Seattle from Michigan, and initially, I was very scared about the move because I didn't know anyone else here. I had called over 20 apartments in the Seattle area to learn more about their available apartments, and out of all of these apartments, The Shelby had the best customer service. Specifically, Chelsea, the apartment manager, was outstanding. I kept in contact with Chelsea almost every day until the move, and she answered all of my questions quickly and effectively. My flight landed in Seattle after The Shelby's office hours, but Chelsea waited 3 hours after office hours so she could give me my keys into the apartment. I was immediately impressed when I entered The Shelby - the pictures online don't do The Shelby enough justice. The lobby area has beautiful lighting, fast elevators, and is clean and quiet. My studio looked brand new with beautiful hardwood flooring. The only issue that I had was the blinds on the windows were damaged, and I couldn't open the windows at all, but I'm hoping maintenance will be able to fix this soon. With exception to the windows, I couldn't have asked for a better move-in experience, studio, and location. I'm really looking forward to spending my first few months and maybe years in Seattle here in The Shelby.
We moved in on February 1st without having an opportunity to view or tour the apartment and building. We are very pleased with the overall experience and would recommend this community to others.

This is a fantastic place to live! Always accommodating and quick to respond any service request. I moved in never seeing the place in person. While that can be scary I was helped through the entire process by the staff and it was an amazing experience. I would recommend this place to anyone wanting to live in Seattle. It’s an excellent location and I feel safe and secure in the apartment!

I've lived at this building for a few weeks short of 6 years and really can't say anything bad about my experience. It's downtown, you get the strategic location near everything including the Link Light Rail which is a very cheap way to get to the airport. I love the restaurants  on the ground floor and there are many coffee and desert options available in a 3-4 block radius. In unit W/D was key for me and the on site storage has been a life saver. My cat has been happy here too.

This apartment building and the management are great. The apartments are clean, big and have all that an ordinary tenant  needs. The layouts are great and very comfortable to live in. One of the things I want to metion is windows. The view and the floor to ceiling windows make a unique experience of living in the center of Seattle, with the amazing view of the downtown and the Space Needle. Highly recommend it! It is a little bit expensive but it is mostly because of the high rent market in the area.
P.S Try  the conference room, as well as BBQ place and the lounge area is amazing for  meeting with friends and enjoying spare time. Loved it

I'm a current resident and I would recommend against. It's an old building so problems are to be expected. The issue is that getting repairs done are always an unnecessary hassle and it seems as though problems would rather be ignored than fixed. Not really sure why, I mean you'd think they'd want to upkeep the units they lease out, especially given their age and location.

I've submitted 4 maintenance requests to have my furnace fixed and each time they've resolved my issue without a response, except once to tell me they found a vendor but are waiting and blah blah blah ignoring the issue and delaying a fix. It doesn't take 2 months to fix a furnace, plain and simple. Plenty of vendors in the Seattle area that can fix a furnace.

I had a leak in the ceiling and they came and looked at it, ran upstairs for a few minutes, came back down and told me "it's all fine, you're good"

Hopefully that issue doesn't return.

If you're fine with never getting things fixed, loose outlets, loitering, broken elevators, and a general lack of responsibility for the building, this is the place for you.

The package situation is also a mess. While they have parcel pending, it's extremely small so packages end up in the lobby. Unfortunately, as with many Seattle apartments, there are people that sneak in and steal packages. Making the parcels pointless when a lot of packages are delivered through the week.

Management was pretty rude when I asked about a package notification I received saying it was in the main office. Immediate dismissal with "we don't accept packages" Alexandria was cool, though.

The rooms are spacious and the area is usually quiet though, save for the occasional increase in traffic noise on the highway.

Mainly, they need to fix issues and improve their communication with residents

Overall, my experience here was just okay. The location is awesome and the view is great. However, getting a hold of anyone in the office is very challenging unless you try to stop by in person. Sometimes I'll receive email responses, but forget calling them. I can think of 2 VERY painful experiences I had here which have completely overridden any positive feelings I had about their "community." 

1) I paid Rent online once (normally pay via check to avoid the additional $2.50 processing fee) but the one time I ever paid online, apparently it didn't go through. I never received any notification that it didn't go through until I received a notice on my door of being evicted due to not paying my rent. As soon as I finally heard back from someone about the charges ($400  for missing 10 days) I was told that I had to pay the charges even though I never received any notification, which...fine. But then I find out after multiple phone calls and emails of trying to reduce the charges, that the management had been on vacation and THAT'S why I was never notified. But I still had to pay the some of the charges. I was livid. 

2) The elevator, which is constantly out of service, has been out of operation for the past month and a half. I was told it would be fixed by the 14th this month and it is still out of service. I am getting ready to move out tomorrow and have some pretty heavy and big furniture that will not fit through the stairwell. Not to mention I live on the 5th floor. I have been trying to reach someone from management for a while now trying to figure out how I'm going to be able to move any of my stuff out. There has been no conclusion or offer to help the situation. 

These are only a couple of examples. I had many other maintenance issues in my home which they claimed to fix but every time I came home didn't find the issue to be resolved. Overall, I would NOT recommend living here to anyone.

I just moved out of this apartment and had a really unfortunate experience with the management company. Do yourself a favor and choose somewhere else to live.

The deposit is non-refundable, which is not communicated on the lease. There are a couple other non-refundable fees outlined upon moving in, but this is not one of them. A few days after leaving, I was sent a move out statement listing a series of costs that had been applied to the deposit including complete re-painting ($250), unit cleaning fee ($105), Drip pans ($11) and carpet cleaning ($35) as well as final utilities. Ultimately, I owed them more money. I attempted to discuss these charges with the assistant building manager and expressed dissatisfaction with the company's poor communication and the charges I felt were unnecessary. In particular, the complete repainting fee, when I had neither painted nor damaged the walls to warrant repainting. The assistant building manager was unhelpful in dealing with these charges and I've noticed a similar response style throughout reviews on other sites. The company pretends to care, but does not follow through with action. It's pretty sad.

Essentially, this company wants to get as much money out of you as possible, so expect to pay for every single little thing, including the drip pans.

Other pain points: 

- Larger projects take a long time to complete, including rooftop deck, grill and patio furniture. No updates or written communication about progress provided to tenants.
- The main elevator is consistently broken. 
- Parking is expensive and poorly managed. I've also experienced people parked in my spot or blocking my spot and leaving their vehicle unattended. This made it difficult to enter or exit the garage. The towing signs within the garage instruct residents to call the associated tow company, which is unhelpful. I tried this on 2 occasions and spoke with a man each time who informed me they do not provide service to that area or company. I informed the assistant manager and suggested removing the signs, but these were still up when I moved out, several months after complaining. 
- The carpets were disgusting for a while with layers of dust and dirt that was visible along the edges.
- High turnover rate of management and cleaning/repair team.
- Rent and utilities raises are extremely high.
- Most floors and even the entryway has smelled strongly of weed.
- The package delivery system is broken.

If you want rent increases of $100 or more a month every time you renew a lease, if you want an owner who owns 250 apartment buildings and doesn't care about individual renters (a consortium out of Salt Lake CIty), if you want an apartment that springs leaks from under the sink, broken water heaters, leaking dishwashers, washing machines then this is the place for you.  They say its pet friendly, then charge you $25 a month; they decide what you will pay for water, sewer, garbage and landscaping) and you end up paying $145.  Run, don't walk away from this place

The apartment: this one bedroom apartment is fairly small (630 sq ft) but is considered affordable ($1300/month) by Seattle standards.  The carpet and paint on the walls were both brand new when we moved in and have held up nicely in the last two years.  Very little (if any) noise pollution from apartment above or next door neighbors. The appliances (stove/oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine, dryer) are old on average but get the job done. Cabinet doors in the kitchen are cheap white melamine and the counter tops are the faux stone spray-on kind. One of the drawers in the kitchen only opens a few inches before hitting the oven handle and stopping.  Similarly in the bathroom, the door hits the toilet before closing. Most units have a gas fireplace in the living room although ours did not. Electric heating wall units but no A/C in the apartments.

Apartment amenities: Rooftop deck with absolutely stunning views of Puget Sound and downtown Seattle. There is a barbecue on the deck that is hooked up to the building gas line so no need to worry about empty propane tanks. Tables and chairs make the deck a nice place for a meal or sunset watching but a lack of umbrellas or shade of any kind makes it difficult to enjoy the roof on a hot day. There is a small fitness center on the main floor that has one elliptical, one treadmill, one recumbent bike, a squat rack, bench, a set of free weights, and a sauna.  While small, the fitness center is rarely busy and has all the basics.  Parking garage spots available for an extra $150/month (limited availability).

The neighborhood: These apartments are located at the top of a steep hill where downtown, Chinatown, and Pioneer square all collide.
