The hill is quite steep to walk up and you need to be in fairly good shape to do so comfortably.  It's probably not possible to ride a bike up the hill.  It's just a 15 minute walk to Pike Place Market or Capitol Hill so lots of nightlife is easily accessible.  Easy access to many bus routes including the routes that pick up in the downtown tunnel system. The I-5 is right behind the building and there is a fire department at the bottom of the hill which means that there is a good amount of freeway noise and sirens at all hours of the night.  The building next door is a retirement community and sees more than its fair share of ambulance visits.

Overall: A decent place for anyone just moving to Seattle and trying not to break the bank.
Lived 2 years there. Flawless. Great amanetiies. Amazing building management

We have lived here for 7 years and have seen a lot of changes in quality. The 2023-2024 renovations have been very frustrating (mess, noise, stenches, closed amenities for a year, delays) but those aside, the building is not being maintained. The elevators and garage door break down every other week, and the hot water goes out once a month. The maintenance and office staff are doing what they can with what they are given but building management has become desensitized to inconveniencing residents. And on top of all of that, our rent just went up 30%. For the same price, you can live in brand-new buildings within a few blocks. Do yourself a favor and avoid this place.

Recently moved here in mid May’2023. Staff is very co-operative! Amenities are good, good terrace garden for walk and fresh air! Great community events which brings people together! Overall great stay so far! Lots of light! Recreational space! And many more.
I had a great experience living here! The staff is friendly and so helpful, it’s clean and safe as well! Would definitely recommend!

If you decide to live here, don't plan to live here for more than a year since they will completely screw you in the renewal process. Also be sure and ask if the amenities will be going away or if there are any other planned changes. Only 2 months after moving in, they closed the pool, business center, and community space for almost the entire duration of our lease. They did not tell us about the planned renovations when we toured and the pool and community space were the main reasons we selected Met Tower. Management was completely unapologetic, did not give any concessions, and instead increased our rent dramatically. Now they want to increase it again while the same unit on a slightly lower floor is advertised for less than the lowest renewal rate they are offering us. 

There are large particles that come out of the showers, so plan to buy a few shower filtration systems and several filter replacements. Again, Management does not care about this and will tell you it's in your head despite picture proof. 

Package handling was great when we first moved in and that was changed (not for the better) within only a couple months as well. 

I believe there are far better options for a better value and more pleasant living experience in the downtown area, so my recommendation is to look elsewhere.

We've now lived here for 9 months and on an almost weekly basis my work is still being disrupted by BZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ for hours and hours as the renovations continue around our unit - renovations that we were told when moving in last year would be completed by the September/October timeframe. Almost six months past that date and they're still happening and have cost me money from how it has affected my ability to work with how paper thin these walls are. 

That's also not mentioning the night before last being one of many times maintenance people have come into our unit after midnight, sometimes while we're asleep. These are not the kind of conditions people should live in when paying $3000  per month. 

I understand construction can take (much, apparently) longer than originally anticipated but we're now looking to move and they're not willing to let us out of the lease even a month and a half early as a gesture to make up for the issues or anything... 

With how many new apartments there are being constructed in the area you'd be much better off elsewhere, others will almost assuredly be more caring and honest and give you a more peaceful living experience.
Axle is a really nice apartment complex that meets the needs of all residents. Clean at all times including, available to assist when inquiries are needed.

Okay, let's keep this simple.

1. I've had $9,000 worth of items(Italian motorcycle and a Cannondale mountain bike) stolen from secure areas here. A car was broken into and robbed this month.

2. Rents go up 30 percent a year as the neighborhood declines.

3. Turnover in the front office tells us they aren't happier than the tenants.

For the amount of money you pay to live here, over time you will have more and more things taken away from you, little to nothing added, but rent will go up significantly anyway. Also, like the other review says, your stuff is not secure here.

PROS:
The design and internal trim is nice. The bathrooms are very nice with a big illuminated mirror and a huge bathtub. Two giant windows on the wall facing the outside. An onsite community team that likes to do monthly events and snacks. Gym is decent but missing some weights. Free B&W printing in the shared workspace area. Proximity to QFC and some eateries is great. Very close to Ballard and West Queen Anne.

CONS: 
Rent was already expensive but they just increased it by over $400 a month with no services or amenities added. Had an expensive package either not arrive or was stolen, I'll never know which because it took the assistant manager over 3 weeks to look at security footage just to find that they only keep 2 weeks of footage on hand, then deflected responsibility by only repeating "we're not responsible for packages" over and over like a robot (so hope you like reporting to robots when you have an issue, they have zero human flexibility for issues you're facing). Building retains heat in the summer; the 2021 heat wave was trapped inside for 2 weeks. The "smart" door lock system is constantly breaking down. You can only have one key fob per name on the lease, so good luck with pet sitting if you travel for work. Units don't have many windows so prepare for a lot of darkness and the feeling of living in a prison cell. Located off 15th street means transients and sketchy people are everywhere, constantly. I've seen many posted notes and emails about stolen bikes. No guest parking except very limited street parking.

Overall I do not recommend living at Axle unless you like leasing from a company that cares more about profit margins than resident satisfaction.

The staff at Axle is great! Very nice people.  Unfortunately,  Lennar, the corporation that owns Axle and other properties,  does not take security seriously. 

In the past year, I've had a $3,000 bike stolen from the "secure" bike room ( it was locked to the rack) and last week I had a $6,000 motorcycle stolen from a parking space in the "secure" garage (it had a column lock so guys had to lift it into a truck in the garage).

In both cases, management's response has been "We'll check the video." No additional security measures have been put in place.

So, if you are planning on coming here and storing a car, a motorcycle, a bike or anything else outside your apartment,  think twice. Your personal stuff will not be safe. 

My hope is I will update this posting the future to tell you what management has done in response to this problem.  For now, don't bring your valuable things here.
We really appreciate the Axle team. They care about the resident experience and have also insured Covid safety protocols are in place to protect everyone at Axle.

Staff is friendly and extremely willing to help you. The location is amazing, being beside Gas Works and Fremont, and you are able to get the big city feel, without the noise that downtown and other areas have. The amenities are a plus, especially the rooftops where you have an amazing view of downtown Seattle. The community is friendly and eco-friendly. The apartment themselves have great layouts and feel extremely spacious.

We have been at the AMLI for over one year and I cant say enough about the staff. All are courteous and responsive as well as knowledgeable. The grounds are kept well and community activities and opportunities are numerous. Cant say enough positive.
My living experience at AMLI WALL is extremely good, because of the before mentioned excellent location, overall design &  functionality of the building, and attention from the personnel.

The community managers at AMLI Wallingford have gained our utmost trust and respect with their consistent reliability, professionalism, responsiveness, and friendliness. We know that they are always working to proactively prevent issues from arising, but when something pops up, they take care of it right away. As a result, we have a peace-of-mind in rental living that we have not experienced anywhere else. And we truly feel valued in a way that adds quality to our everyday lives. We are so grateful to the AMLI Wallingford Team.
Great location and excellent roof terrace, game room and fitness center

The AMLI Wallingford is a beautiful and safe building, but its best quality is that it is a place that fosters tight-knit community. In the midst of a pandemic in the Seattle freeze, our management and maintenance teams ensured that residents felt seen and cared for. We have good relationships with our neighbors, and have made friends through simple programs like the Pet of the Month. We feel valued as residents by the staff at the AMLI, and I don't know if there is another community like this one in the area. We're incredibly grateful to have lived here for three years!

After living here for 2 months now I greatly regret my decision to move in. After merely 2 months I hear loud music, theft all the time, vandalism of my car, theft of my bike, and more. DONT MOVE HERE FOR GOD SAKE

I lived here for two years and these are my pros and cons. 

Pro:

- Maintenance completes work orders quickly 

Cons: 
- Horrible management that will not answer any of your calls, be in the office, or answer emails (unless it is a situation they may be liable for). 
- My apartment flooded due to heavy rainfall and lack of proper drainage on the patio. Ultimately, resulted in the apartment management allowing contractors to enter our apartment without our notice days later to pick up the equipment they had dropped off.

The management staff is rude, arrogant and incompetent. It is very frustrating working with them. Stay away from these folks if you can help it.

I loved the layout & location of my apartment when I lived at Ivy Ridge-- I lived in two different units and enjoyed them both so much. Work orders were super easy to put in, and maintenance was always so fast and nice. Adonis and the new management has been handling things extremely well and quickly resolved a balance issue with me. I can definitely see a huge improvement!

This place will take all your money and still ask you for more. They charged us $80 for cleaning carpets, a separate $260 fee for “cleaning the apartment” and $240 for painting all after not giving us back our security deposit. It was my me and my sister living here and we were barley home. On top of all that, it’s essentially like living in a frat house with all the noise and parties that people throw what seems like every night of the week. DO NOT LIVE HERE.

staff is fairly competent but i hear that people don't get their deposits back. when things are broken/not working they reply pretty quickly. one of the only real studio apartments out in u district with a full kitchen. fairly quiet too even though it's near some frat houses. 5 min walk to campus, and 10 min walk to u-vill and to most buses

I lived at these apartments for two years and have been ripped off for unnecessary damages and expenses at the end of my contract. They not only take all of your damage deposits, but they add extra charges to steal more money from you. They have poor maintenance solutions and waste your time not fixing any issues you have with their apartment appliances. One of the office managers, Brad, is rude to the tenets living there and falsely accuse them of actions they did not commit. These apartments are way too overpriced, some office managers are not kind, you will not get your damage deposit back and you most likely to pay extra at the end of your contract for damages.

Management was not helpful , Cars broken into every month as no security measures are taken, shared kitchens constantly dirty. I have had pending service request , as well of lack of the "free" Internet that was included with the amenities. Overall horrible experience living here , would seriously consider breaking a lease just to escape this dump.

I would not recommend anybody live here. They charge you an arm and a leg for move out expenses because they know there is nothing you can do about it. Even when I had my own pictures and the agreed to reduce the charges because of the insane prices they charged, they still went back on their word. Someone please tell me how it costs $110 to clean a shower door?

Also, do not even think about parking here. My window was shattered when I parked in their "secure garage". When I went to management they conveniently said the camera pointed right at my car was broken and so it wasn't recording. This place is a joke and the management is a joke. Do not rent from here!
Nice and spacious but loud. The management fixes any problems promptly.
Great place to live  Only complaint is office hours

I am only staying in this apartment for the summer. I know I am living in the basement, but the spider and ant problem is out of control. The entire downstairs is completely infested with daddy long legs and the ceiling is just covered in spiderwebs. I would not have moved in if I knew this beforehand.
They also allow LARGE dogs, which when left alone when the owner is out all day bark really loudly all day long.
There are washers and driers in the apartment, but they are located in the bathroom, which is completely ridiculous.
I have to say, it is a fair price for how big the rooms are. Living in the basement also keeps it somewhat cool during the summer.
So if you don't have a problem with spider infestations, it's an okay place to live.

I moved in two weeks ago and well it has been a bit of a let down. The staff are not very accommodating at all, especially when the internet that is included in the utilities doesn't work at all. Until this morning the stairwell smelled of mold. Everyone in my building is super shy and won't even make eye contact. But the apartment is fine, everything they say it would be.

The current staff at Ivy Ridge are very professional and extremely polite. Tabitha was very understanding about my friend, who's first language isn't English, needing an english speaking companion to help with the application process. Tabitha was very patient and understanding about changing our move in date when the manager at our old apartment building gave us a hard time about moving out.

The apartments are very clean, and the shared kitchens are spacious and clean. The neighborhood is a little undesirable on the university side of the street because of all the fraternities leaving garbage around, but the area directly around Ivy Ridge and to the north is really nice with quaint homes and trees etc.

These are popular among undergrads and my guess is that most of the complaints/bad reviews are coming from younger tenants who don't show the same level of respect and courtesy that the Ivy Ridge staff shows them. I highly recommend this place for it's affordability and professional staff.

Recently a friend and I had put down money to hold an apartment here, a few weeks later we found out that moving was not going to work out and even though it was past the date for a deposit refund they returned all of our money!

Close to campus, not too noisy neighborhood, and okay price for the size of apartment. However, when you made any mistake, the management will try to ripe you off as much as they can. For instance if you missed the rent deadline, they will charge you $100 late fee, plus with $10/day . The worst part is that they would not notify you as soon as possible, meaning that they will try to delay from giving you late notice and get as much as $10/day as they can. Unless if you personally go meet the management soon after you realized that , the $10/day will continue to add up.

I would give 5 stars but for one thing(which is easy to overlook considering how great everything/everyone has been since moving in May 2022. The management is top notch. Super friendly and easy going. Each member of the staff has made me feel extremely comfortable and right at home.  Which one should feel when at home, right? The property manager, Ethan is the best. He does his job yet keeps things friendly and personable and has a sense of humor that's right on my level. Which, mind you, is NEVER sarcastic, (I'm being sarcastic.)The thing that knocked it to 4 5 rather than 5 stars is the fact that maintenance has, per THEIR request, booked times on 3 separate occasions to come paint part of my wall that they had to remove the day after I moved in because of some snafu in the apartment above mine. I work nights, therefore I sleep during the day, making it difficult at first to schedule a time. Since then, THREE times maintenance has said they'd be there to paint and didn't show or call or email. It's only kind of annoying because every time he's supposedly coming, I have to move my furniture off the wall so he can paint. I've moved it three times and nada. It's still not a huge deal because I adore everyone here. Yes, maintenance included!

This community is undergoing a great renovation on the entire building, all while keeping the original charm. A great management and maintenance team make this place a must see when looking for a new home downtown!

They have good staff and they’ve address the problems and concerns I have had right away.  They communicate and are always upfront when I have any questions on issues.  I would highly recommend them to potential renters.

Great views , great staff , office has always helped when I needed something , ... 
Maintenance follows thru and follows up on completed work orders , once they have been finished , 
Staff is always friendly and goes the extra mile ,

CONSTANT issues with communication with management, maintenance gives no warning and is completely unreliable, does not follow safety protocols (no mask, no personal sanitization) Going through HUGE renovations in the building for which we have gotten little to no notice, appliances busted, building fire alarm has gone off 5 times since I have lived here, building has been broken into multiple times, just bad bad experience.

Building security is non existent, property management is constantly changing, maintenance does not respond to requests. In my year living here, the building has been broken into at least 6 times that I am aware of. Property management does not care about their residents.

Where do I even start? 

Cons: Major cockroach infestation. Ongoing bed bug battles. Poor construction. Holes in the walls. Get used to the smell of urine (thank goodness for masks). Filthy. Janky elevators
Frequent staff changes (one manager even quit on his lunch break!). Boiler leaks/flooding/water seeping out of walls. Recycling bins are a joke here | Pros: Security guard. Good water pressure. Unlimited hot water. Air conditioning.

Poor management, 
BedBugs, Can’t Buzz in guests, Broken elevator.

Slightly newer construction in downtown, where many buildings are older. While that may lose some of the charm, it affords you other things (A/C! Washer/Dryer in unit!) which are pretty nice. It is more affordable than other downtown apartments, though still definitely not cheap. Overall pretty nice, if on the smaller size for the units. As with any apartment, there is always the risk of a noisy neighbor but what are you gonna do. That comes with apartment living. In Pioneer Square which has had a recent business/restaurant boom, so there is lots to do.

The noise between floors clearly indicates that there is no insulation between floors. You will hear the neighbors above you and the people below you will hear you so be careful what you say. A week doesn’t go by without something being broken and then taking days to weeks to have fixed. The staff also won’t care to help you once you have moved in. Worst apartment I have lived in.

AMLI Mark 24 is a beautiful community and I'm thrilled to call it home! The building is in great shape and the staff is amazing! The amenities are excellent and have a lot to offer! The location is perfect and in a cute neighborhood. There is a lot to do, close to everything, just a few minutes from the beach and downtown too!

I have been living at the AMLI Mark24 location for a few years and the staff here are exceptional. They truly care about the residents and make an effort to make our experiences here an enjoyable one! I also love the location!

This is a wonderful place to live. I work remotely from home and Mark24 provides a quiet, comfortable environment during the day, and a fun location that is surrounded by restaurants, stores, and social scenes at night. The staff is incredibly supportive and helpful, and I have really enjoyed my time here.
Amazing property, staff and community, happy I chose Mark 24
Nice building thats close to everything great in Ballard! Super dog friendly. Nice place to live.
I wouldn’t recommend the Eden to anyone, by far the worst renting experience I’ve ever had.

I am deeply disappointed with the lack of action taken by the apartment complex management regarding frequent break-ins!

Despite multiple incidents, security measures remain insufficient.

Please be wary if you are considering moving into Eden.

This complex has a nice location but major burglary issues!

My car has been broken into multiple times despite having a car alarm. What makes it worse is that parking costs $165/car per month! 

Management has no idea how to combat this and doesn’t even have a single security camera anywhere on the premises.

I would not move here!

Constantly over charged on a monthly basis with zero invoices … you have absolutely no idea what you’re being charged for … and when you ask for invoice … crickets … 

There’s no one ever to talk to … the office is constantly closed … it’s beyond frustrating living experience 

Run from any Thrive Community… horribly managed … and a extremely unethical in their business practices

Such a gorgeous community. The grounds are kept tidy and clean.  The office is responsive and pro active. My apartment was ready on time and I was even given a cute welcome home gift. The events are catered to the people in this community, not cheesy - very very fun to attend! The bark park is so adorable and kept up! Could not choose a better place to live.

Great location and beautiful apartments. Love my little tucked away home! I am always telling my friends and family to check it out and the ladies in the office are always so sweet, definitely 10 out of 10!

I recently moved into Garden Point Apartment Complex, and I couldn't be happier with my decision! From the moment I stepped onto the property, I was impressed by the beautifully landscaped grounds and the welcoming atmosphere.

The staff is incredibly friendly and attentive, always willing to help with any questions or concerns. The leasing process was smooth and straightforward, making my transition seamless. My apartment itself is spacious, modern, and well-maintained, with high-quality appliances and plenty of natural light.

One of my favorite features is the community amenities. The pool area is perfect for relaxing on sunny days, and the fitness center is well-equipped for all my workout needs. Plus, the location is fantastic—close to shopping, dining, and parks, making it easy to enjoy everything the area has to offer.

Overall, Garden Point is more than just an apartment complex; it feels like a community. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable and enjoyable living experience!
Staff are amazing! Maintenance is always on the run and going above and beyond! I am a very picky person and I have 0 issues. Staff is always willing to work with residents.

Quick and painless application process! Staff is quick to respond and set up a tour. Communication between staff and tenants is reliable and ongoing! Maintenance does quality work! Parking can be a pain depending
on what side you live on! The cabana/office hosts a monthly community event for the residents. The pool and hot tub have been a deal breaker! Respectable and fair staff! Family friendly complex!
Been living here for a couple of years now and management has been great. Parking spaces are nice. Good schools are the neighborhood which is important.
I been here living for a few years and I am happy. The property it’s great. Good neighborhood and good location.

This is an excellent place to live it's close to downtown it's close to shopping close to gas stations close to a mini Mart the grounds are very clean the managers are awesome people are saying they're rude and the manager has never been rude to me neither has assistant manager and the maintenance man he gets stuff done with the quickness the grounds are clean it's close to good schools is an overall great experience I've lived here for over 12 years and I'll continue to live here I strongly suggest renting from here

This is an amazing location for those working around the city, love to go out, or stay active. Located in the Eastlake neighborhood just a block away from Lake Union residence can enjoy all that the city of Seattle has to offer. It is an easy walk to many great restaurants along Eastlake and Fairview as well as a great central location to drive or cab to anywhere in the city for dinner or drinks. It is also located on the main bus line, so it is easier for commuters to get to their jobs every morning throughout the city. The building itself is quiet and well maintained. It's also a steal for the location and size of apartment. In unit washer/dryer and dishwasher makes chores around the house easy. There is also a lovely common area and patio for gatherings of friends. For those looking for a great place in an amazing location for the right price should definitely check out Lake Union Terrace

The staff at Sedona are great. The two girls in the office are very nice. If I have an issue it gets resolved almost instantly. Sometimes I can hear my neighbors, but no more than any other apartment I’ve lived in.

Stay away. They don’t care about the tenants and are extremely rude. Broken things never get fixed even after multiple complaints. My apartment had no hot water for 4 days because someone forgot to turn the hot water back on. The other tenants are so noisy and play music all hours of the night. The apartments smell like marijuana and cigarettes, despite smoking being against the rules.
All workers took time to make sure my needs were cared for and my living arrangements set in place. Love the workers, thank you!!!

I was drawn in by the hardwood floors, contemporary fixtures, and general appearance of the building.  However, upon signing a one year lease and spending my first few nights in my apartment, I was extremely disappointed to find out that one of my neighbors plays loud music into the early hours of the morning.  Despite others complaining they continue to do so on most nights.  While the facilities look nice, the tenants make this an uncomfortable place to live or sleep.
Run for your life. This place cares nothing for their tenants.

One of the worst apartments in the area. Apartment is ok but the management is so terrible that it has resulted in a quality decline over the years. Car break ins are a regular occurrence and there is no screening of people coming in. Management only works to make tenants life harder. They only care about money and have no concern for people living there.
crime-ridden place. Managers don't care at all. You will rue the day you moved into this place

If you value your safety, peace of mind, and financial well-being, do yourself a favor and avoid this apartment complex at all costs. It's a terrible place to live, and you'll regret every moment spent here! BR property has ruined this place

I love the space and location for the price. Maintenance is super nice and responsive. But there are definitely some cons because management just does not listen.

- This is a confusing building and I’ve been requesting to put up basic signs for delivery people and it has not been done in months
- The buzzer system does not work in 2 out of 3 entrances and all requests to fix it have been ignored.
- I was promised while moving that there is budget set aside for gym equipment like weights which has not been ordered after following up for almost a year
- The property manager Peter is not professional at all and is very dismissive of resident concerns.
- A man literally broke into the building and stole packages and residents were not informed. I only knew about it because my package was stolen. When this was brought to Peters attention he just shrugged and said “this happens”

Garage security issues, entrances that aren't secure, and an ensemble cast of ever-changing management (including temps, a higher-up from Guide Property, and at one point nobody) suggest that this place has some deep-seated issues which nobody is keen to address. 

I'll start. 

1. The Motel across the street is a heavily-rumored hard drug hotspot. How might this interfere with the Hudson? Well, on your tour you may find needles in the stairwells. If you don't find them on your tour, a concerned neighbor may take a picture and distribute them among the residents. Either way, fun for the whole family. 

2. People don't shut doors behind them, and some doors don't just swing shut as many expect. This relates a lot to 1, but there have also been break-ins at neighbors apartments. I don't care how many PMs tell me that they're "committed to our safety", I'll believe it when I see it. 

3. Not JUST apartment break-ins, but car break-ins too! I love walking out to the car at 6 in the morning and seeing my neighbors' car window in a million pieces all over my spot. I'm sure they love it too. 

4. Don't bother getting to know the management, they'll be gone by the time you learn their name – and probably won't let you know. We're on the sixth or seventh PM in a year. Things were said to temps that never passed on to new staff. For a time the emergency number just went completely offline. For a time there was just no one ever in the office. Fees, timing, and understanding of issues are ever-changing. Seems like a great way to run a business. 

All told, I think my recommendation is clear. Stay away.

Its a poorly maintained building. Management is doing such a poor job in maintaining common areas. And the new thing is some residents are shouting in the middle of the night and when you call security its goes to voicemail. This property sucks and we are going to leave soon... just waiting for my lease to end.

Do you enjoy your packages getting stolen, homeless people in the lobby, no hot water every morning, construction above your apartment at 7 am, water getting turned off 10+times a year for the entire day, and constant construction in every amenity? If so Centennial Tower and Court is the place to live. We currently live here and we cannot get out of our lease fast enough. Management is horrid and the building is falling apart, anytime you complain they give you some crap excuse and make absolutely no changes. Lived in about 8 different apartments and this is the first one I genuinely have massive complaints about. Please please save yourself the time and money and don't bother looking at this place unless you prefer to have a very long miserable year. If I could go below one star I would.

The elevator here go out of service at least a few times a week, most of the time only 1 out of the 3 elevator is working, and with 27 floors and many residents, you could be looking at 10-20 mins to get an elevator. And when ask the property manager about it, she literally told me I should be glad that I wasn't trapped inside the elevator for hours like some others have experienced (which in my short time living here happened at least twice).  When you are paying this much for a high rise apartment, you would at least expect working elevators, right?

Besides the elevator issue, this is a decent place, but I highly recommend stay away from here until they fix the elevators which they told everyone it will take at least 9 months...

They will say whatever they can to get you to sign your lease paperwork. Will fail to respond to any work orders that are submitted. Amenities were constantly out of order. Then when they decide that you owe them money, they hire the collection agency with the worst reputation that they can find. AVOID THIS COMPANY AND THEIR POOR BUSINESS AND TENANT PRACTICES!!

Centennial Tower and my experience there were the worst! Elevators constantly out of service, amenities (steam room, gym, common room, pool) on a rotating schedule of being out of order or broken. neighborhood was misrepresented as being safe and quiet. Drug dealers openly walking the street, prostitution, needles on the sidewalk, constant noise from the fire station across the street (that I was told I wouldn't be able to hear), utilities are billed whether you use them or not, no air conditioning for actual units, continual exterior noise from the remodel (coat of paint), unresponsive staff. Verbally told the agent that I was leaving the building as they were unable to follow through on their description of the building, neighborhood and available amenities. 4 years later I find out that they decided to sue me (I never received any notification)and sold the debt to some shady Collections/Law Firm.... Equity Residential has refuse to even have a dialogue, and their "Fair" collections company has echoed the same. Avoid this building and Equity Residential at all costs.

The Tower building has a massive exterior restoration project ongoing for up to a year (!)with dangling, suspended-in-air workers with serious pneumatic jack hammers that are relentless in disrupting everyone, all day long. The tower is currently unlivable to all but those with turtle shells to keep out all of the construction racket, we've gotten used to tuning it out of our minds. They helpfully post work-from-home people, stay-at-home parents, can use the nice amenity room, sigh, to escape the drilling. There is a building being built from the ground up just across the street, so get used to concrete pouring, hammering, banging, cranes, trucks, more racket. And word of late is a tower building storage locker got its lock snipped and all of the stored items went bye bye. Overall a decent property. They should pony up the moulah and have 5 or more teams instead of the current team of 1, to accelerate the process of selectively drilling the living daylights out of nearly every exterior surface of the Centennial tower building. The hot tub on the grand deck is the size of a bird bath; eco friendly yes, but not even an option due to its tiny, tiny, tiny wee size. Many common areas with standing water, black growth. If it weren't for the construction, we would recommend in a heartbeat. Front office service is excellent.

If I could rate this business zero stars, I would.

My experience while living in the building was okay, not exceptional, but for the most part, I didn't have too many complaints. The moment I gave my notice to vacate was when I grew to despise this business.

My lease terminated on the 16th of the month, and I had no intention of renewing. So my very last bill included prorated rent and utilities. The rent was calculated accordingly, I verified it myself, however when I checked what they were charging us for the "prorated" utilities bill, it was 1.5 times the maximum amount we had ever paid during my two years in the building. When I questioned this, Jill conveniently stopped responding to my email messages, though we had exchanges in the same email thread just days prior. Very professional, Jill...

Before I moved out, I vacuumed and shampooed the carpet, cleaned the floor, windows, walls, counters...everything. The apartment was spotless. I was expecting to get most, or at least some of my deposit back after inspection. Neither my roommate and were present during the physical inspection because we were out of town, but Centennial didn't hesitate to take full advantage of that opportunity to rob us blind. I got a bill weeks later and turns out, not only had they blown through my entire deposit ($900), but I was being charged an additional $150 for repairs. Took a look at the statement, and they had charged us for a carpet replacement...when it was absolutely not necessary. The carpet was near brand new, just installed before I moved in and I kept it clean during my stay. Didn't have the energy to refute this, they would've probably ignored my emails anyway.
This building was purchased and changed to "Griffis Waterfront Seattle" and ever since this new company took over it's been a living cost-cutting nightmare. Avoid this building at all costs.

While I started looking for apartments to move to Seattle, The Post was probably the very first apartment I had a look at, and it was really love at first sight. It was slightly out of my budget at that time and I looked at other apartments as well, but this place was always in my mind. After 20-30 days of exploration, my budget increased and I finally got this place. This was the best decision I made and I love this place.
The Post is a great community! The location is perfect, the amenities are first-class, and the Staff is extremely professional and helpful.

The building structure is high quality, but there seem to be mechanical, and plumbing issues at times. You may have this happen, and end up dealing with it until its fixed. The noise from neighboring pets will start to annoy those that dont want to hear it. The bar across the alleyway will have late night parties past 12am, and you will hear screaming, and yelling from their partying. If you want peace you wont find it here especially with the homeless encampments, and homeless wondering the area also creating loud noises, and dirtiness.
Moving into the Post has been an exceptional experience. The amenities, my apartment, the leasing/building staff,  and just the building in general have all exceeded my expectations!

I've lived in multiple apartments, condos, houses, and cities, including Barcelona and NYC. So far my experience at The Post has been the best - and I don't say that lightly, I'm giving it critical thought. The staff has been great and the building is awesome, with impressive amenities, well kept, and for a very reasonable rate.

Tower 12 Apartments
Address:** 215 2nd Avenue

My experience at Tower 12 Apartments has been a mix of positives and negatives. On the bright side, Steven, the office manager, along with the security personnel and front desk staff, especially Jose, provided exceptional service. Their professionalism and helpfulness stood out.

However, the service from the rest of the staff was disappointing. The building has three elevators, but one has been out of order for over a year, leaving residents with only two elevators. Often, another elevator is also down, leaving just one functional elevator. This causes significant delays, particularly when someone is moving in or out. The elevator issues were so severe that we frequently had to use the stairs, which is incredibly inconvenient for a 34-floor building, especially when carrying bags.

The gym amenities are subpar. There is not enough proper workout equipment, and the yoga room is a letdown; the system for online classes never worked. Additionally, the building’s location in an area with a high homeless and crime rate does not help justify the overpriced apartments. The amenities and service provided do not compensate for these issues.

I recommend finding a better building with more reliable elevators and better amenities.

I'm new to Tower 12.  From day #1, when I first made my first phone call to the property, was impressed.  

Christina in leasing is gracious, kind, and patient in always answering my questions about the property, and my lease.  Steve and Taryn her team, are also very, very, very accomodating in her absence.  I LOVE THIS TEAM.  

The concierge desk with Mike, Michael, and Ryan is top notch; so much better than the front desk at Helios Apartments.  They are kind, polished, professional, accomodating, and bend over backwards to help residents!!!  I can't tell you enough about the people here.  I REALLY LOVE THIS TEAM.

The package concierge being available here is also better than Helios Apartments (they didn't have a secured system for packages and once I had $60 of merchandise stolen there).  But here, they take package security very seriously.  They also have community activities here!  That's something they didn't have at Helios.

While the facilities aren't perfect, no place is, I can deal with a few things such as drafty apartments, or the trash chute going down from time to time, or the loading dock not available for usage on Saturdays (most people's moving days).  That's the only reason I didn't rate it 5 star.  But would I recommend living here? Absolutely, and I already have a friend who's agreed to move in.  

Please consider Tower 12 if you're a responsible, conscientious tenant who wants to be a positive addition to this community.

I have lived at Tower 12 since shortly after it opened in 2017. This is a great apartment building. The management and staff have been great to deal with and have relatively low turnover and treat residents with courtesy and respect. There is a street level convenience store which is well-run and has friendly staff as well. Unlike other apartments I have lived in, I have never had a package go missing, and I order a lot of packages. I have a 2 bedroom plan and the apartment has been very quiet due to the concrete construction. The bathrooms and kitchen have a lot of storage and the appliances are top notch for the price range. If you are looking to move or stay downtown definitely check out Tower 12.

I have been a renter for 16 years and living at Tower 12 has been the best experience by far! The location is prime with a walk score of 98, the views are incredible, the building is efficient and always clean, and the staff/concierge team is top notch! 
If you are considering Tower 12 as your next home, you won’t be disappointed.

Amazing views. Friendly staff. Amenities are homey and actually used by the residents. Resident events are perfect for making new friends where you live. Fitness center is state of the art and with its views, very motivating to work out.
We have been more than satisfied with everything this place has to offer
Always changing management, extremely unprofessional, not well kept. And advertise a gym there is no gym. And alot of fees you will encounter when billed or moving out. Don't do it.
The team at 700 Broadway is fantastic. Katja helped me find my dream apartment and made moving in so easy. I couldn't recommend this building more highly.
I really like the location of 700 Broadway Apartments. It feels safe, the apartments are well-built, and the noise-level is definitely adequate.

This is a great and unique community. Building is very original in its design and the inner courtyard helps create a more intimate space for everyone there. Apartments are larger than average and have different layouts vs everything else that I searched, and trust me I did a lot of searches before I decided on this place. Katja, the community manager's amazing and she creates such a good environment that you want to be part of it.

I stayed here for almost three years and the rent was raised twice. Management doesn't care about your complaints. My toilet went bad and wasn't fixed by a plumber for a month. Had to use Fed Ex office downstairs. Creepy maintenance man! Garage broken into. Management tried to say that I needed to replace the whole carpet because of stains, which I said I would get a professional carpet cleaner to do. They got their own carpet person who wroye up a statement saying it needed to be replaced. When questioned they said that's the way it is. Threats then made (collections) if payment not forwarded for carpet. Lack of integrity and dishonest. Management personnel just not nice. Stay somewhere else.

Clean, newly renovated apartment in an excellent location. Located just at the top of the Broadway East strip, you have shopping and restaurants directly to the South, and a quiet neighborhood and parks to the north. The apartments are spacious and practical, residents are courteous, and staff is incredibly helpful, knowledgeable and friendly.
Love living here! Perfect location and great staff !

Fire alarm went off at 3am and the whole building had to stand outside the other night. We are cleared to go in building, and it goes off AGAIN. No explanation given by building management. Everything in the apartment is cheap and the building is dirty. People dump stuff near recycling and trash chutes are gross. Location is super convenient, but this place is really not worth the price of rent. Tiny and dark apartments.

Great location. Prices used to be good, but are now average for what you get here. Security used to be no issue, but recently has had some problems. Complex company does not seem to care as much about residents well being as they used to (i.e. taking responsibility when problems occur).

Post Alley Court is a great place to live! The location is unbeatable, its pretty quiet, and the apartments are nice. The property manager, Erin, is fantastic and always available to assist with questions. Alex in maintenance is SO helpful and always goes above and beyond no matter what is needed. He even offered to help me move my stuff in. I would strongly recommend Post Alley Court to anyone looking to experience downtown Seattle.

I've very much enjoyed my time here! However, the long delays in service requests and the issues with the building (faulty wiring for the microwave, windows that are not properly weatherized for the winter) prevent me from wholeheartedly recommending it.
Post Alley Court is great community not only because of the views, or area but also because of the people and management who always provide a welcoming environment.
Great building and management.  Roof top, what is missing is a gym.

I am very happy with the services and amenities at the Edge Point. The maintenance is actually serious about getting the jobs done. The facilities are always kept clean and readily usable which is also great.

I moved into EdgePoint in June and have loved living here. Brian, the assistant manager helped me find the perfect apartment for me and my dog. The leasing process was a breeze and moving in was actually really easy. Since living here I have really appreciated how clean they keep the common spaces and how friendly the staff have been. The neighborhood is a huge plus, I can easily walk to the grocery store, multiple restaurants/bars and there is even a beautiful park just a few blocks away.
Love living here, the building is well maintained and the staff are friendly and helpful.

Edgepoint is a lovely place to live. Great location, clean new building, beautifully designed, soundproof living space, plenty of closet and cubbard space, lots of natural light, good indoor lighting, friendly and efficient staff. Mary O.
Great location, safe, LEED certified, and cool folks? What’s not to love?

The process from start to finish went quickly and smoothly. I got an appointment to tour the apartment building quickly, and began the application process right away. Brian in the leasing office, worked swiftly and promptly to make sure my application was in its best shape prior to submission. The move in preparation was communicated to me clearly so that I could have a smooth move-in day, as it was. The neighborhood is beautiful with many things to do; and plenty of essential stores within walking distance.

Very unethical management. It has been three years since I lived at Stream Fifteen and I am now receiving spam calls from a collections company saying that we owe cleaning charges that were worth more than the deposit on our apartment from three years ago. When we moved out, money was taken out from our deposit for our cleaning. We cleared with management at the time that we did not owe any more money and we got almost our full deposit back. It doesn't make sense to give us our deposit back if charges were pending. We received no correspondence after move out from Stream 15 via our mailing addresses, emails, or phone numbers about further charges. I'm very disappointed in the way that this has been handled and the way Stream 15 management has given all of our information to a collections agency who is now contacting us three years after move out regarding charges that are not valid. They are extremely difficult to get ahold of and have made no effort to correct this situation. It seems like other tenants have had similar experiences.
Walls are paper thin. I can hear neighbors washing dishes and having low key conversations. Can't wait for my lease to end!!!

Don't EVER rent apt from Pacific Crest! The management told us not to worry about cleaning our unit because they will provide us a cleaning service for 120$. Couple weeks later I moved out from the unit they sent me "an itemized list of charges" charging me for unit painting and unit repairs and this was NEVER mentioned by the management!!!   WORST experience EVER.
Unfortunately, another real estate company in Seattle that knows how to get the most profit off of their tenants. Save your money, try to find an independent landlord.

BEWARE OF THIS SHADY APARTMENT AND THIER UNCONSCIONABLE BUSINESS PRACTICES! 

I would strongly suggest AGAINST renting from this company!!!

I viewed the apartment building while still in construction phase; then put a holding fee down to hold the unit I was interested in. The management harassed me to sign a pre lease but verbally told me that the lease would not be in effect until I handed over the deposit and received my keys. 

Ten days after signing and sixty days prior to move in my hours were cut at work. I then notified them immediately that I would no longer be able to afford the unit. They let me know that they would keep the holding fee. 

Now seven months later I'm shocked to find that streamfifteen is suing me for breach of contract. 

In the thriving rental market of Seattle they were able to fill the unit prior to the move in date. 
It's so very sad that a company would take advantage even though there was no loss to them. 

I imagine construction costs got too high and now they are trying to recover losses in anyway that they can.

AVA Ballard is close to quite a few things...Safeway, Walgreens, and plenty of other things down the street in Ballard. Located right at 15th Ave W and NW Market St, it's a fairly busy area, so avoid it if you don't want a bit of ambient road noise during the summer months of open windows. It's a huge building, so you'll likely run into quite a few new people after moving in, which can be nice, or not, depending on your personality. My only complaint is the fact that they pass-through the sewer capacity charge, which is a fee that builders are supposed to pay or be responsible for (it's separate from the sewer usage fee, which you'll also pay). Overall...good!

I've lived here over a year and have loved every second! The layout of my apartment is unique in a way that truly maximizes the space and creates quite an open feel. The building is also unique for the area and includes multiple roof-top barbecues, a 24 hour gym, and a "chill space" complete with arcade machines. The staff have made me feel at home since the day I moved in, remembering my name and even apartment number. My favorite aspect of the apartment are all of the modern touches, particularly the chalkboard wall, equipped with a "Welcome Home" statement upon our move-in date. I love my home!

If you live in the 107th building you have zero access to amenities unless you want to pay for an extra key fob, even as your monthly payments are usually much higher than what your rent is. The carpets in 107 usually smell horrible, walls are visible falling apart, package thefts have been at an all time high because it’s very easy for people to break into this building. I’ve had many former residents on their move out days come up to me to warn me about apartment break ins as well. The parking structure is meant for compact cars which doesn’t really feel worth paying at a certain point. I saw someone say these apartments claiming to be 1 bed room say they are glorified studios with a half wall and that is literally what they are. The leasing office is hardly used and should be made into something actually convenient like a mail room or even a smaller fitness center that 107 residents have access to. The only redeeming factors of this building are its maintenance team that are incredibly kind and get things done quickly and the location of the apartment building.

These are nice apartments and newer construction, however the quality of appliances and fixtures is very cheap and things break frequently. The maintenance team is very responsive, though and typically can complete repairs within 24 hours. The Office staff is also friendly and responsive to issues, and the two combined are why I rated 3 stars. However, The property management company will increase rent by double digit percentages every time you renew the lease. The elevator in one of the buildings has constant issues, and has broken 3 separate times within a month. The neighborhood is safe for walking a dog in the dark, but there are a number of car break ins in the area/ even the parking garage,  and packages are frequently stolen from the mailroom. Overall, an okay place to live, but a bit pricey and has some issues.

I am a current resident and haven’t lived at a Weidner property before moving here.

From the online leasing experience to the lack of attention this building gets from the property management team - you do not get any value from living at 107 & Leilani.

Rent is expensive for the size and “features” available to you (half walled studios) which are not displayed properly on the leasing site.

You are charged a monthly fee and forced to use a 3rd party service for your utilities, which are 2x more than I was paying before moving in.

There is no weight room, no community lounge, and the rooftop deck is small compared to most rooftop spaces around the city.

Parking is extremely expensive considering the garage is open air,  full of compact spots filled by non compact cars, and the locking door to the Main Street is broken every other week.

The office downstairs never has property management staff inside and it takes 2-3 days for them to reply even though they list 7-days a week as their availability.

We’ve had Herion needles left outside the main entrance for days on end. The office window has a bullet hole in it....

I feel with the amount they charge for rent the property is managed in a way to maximize profits, not maximize the resident experience, and it shows.

The maintenance staff is great - same day fixes and friendly.

Do not rent here. They are rude, management unhelpful. Seriously terrible service and please pay attention to all the negative reviews here. Save yourself the headache and move anywhere else. Regional manager hung up on me after explaining legitimate safety concerns.  Tried to make me divulge confidential information to him. Absolutely atrocious.

Resident at for a year, DO NOT RECOMMEND living here
All the care about is duping you and extracting money in all possible ways. Hidden electric charges, fake management fees, processing fees, cleaning fees. Guess what they will also ticket you even if you have permission to park for loading/unloading. Very unfriendly management. DON'T BE FOOLED. I am out as soon as my lease ends.

I lived here for 2 years in several different units.  The apartments are nice, with good amenities, and there is a nice little community, though with a lot of turnover.  The biggest negative is the management.  Expect a rent increase with EVERY lease.  There is little room to negotiate, since it comes through a large corporate ownership.  The amenities are nice (lounge, pool, fitness room, theater), but maintenance is really lacking.  Pool is open in summer, but often closed unexpectedly for maintenance.  Lounge is nice for planned and impromptu gatherings, but little things keep it from being a better experience- TV remotes go missing, and with no instructions there's always a period of figuring out how to watch what you want, or even run a movie.  Office-based wifi for common areas, but unpredictable connections that frequently go out.  Yes, there's a fitness room, but small and ill-equipped.  A nice place to live, that could be a lot better.

The leasing staff has been inflexible in their policy not to allow bikers to go through the garage exit, and instead we have to awkwardly cram with our bikes into the elevator and squeeze past the other tenants in the lobby everyday. Management was not at all accommodating when I discussed with them.

Also, their elevators take a really long time standing around waiting during commute hours.

There are new town homes being built behind the B building and you will listen to nail guns at least six days a week. Right now there is hammering at 8pm. If you work from home, have small children, or enjoy peaceful nights, do not move in here.

you can see the amenities the complex boasts about, and they are, for the most part, available and functional. what they will not speak about is the abhorrent security. there is no security guard at night, as we have had in other complexes in Seattle we have lived in. in the half year I have lived here, we have had problems with storage units being broken into leisurely - enough time to go through many of the storage spaces. cars have been repeatedly broken into, and neighbors told me that they have had this problem for over a year now. the complex reacts by blaming the residents and stating they have no means of bettering the security. we're left alone with the dangers of living here, without help offered by the owners.

This complex is the most dog friendly place Ive ever lived. There's plenty of neighborhoods to walk around in, a dog run/play area on the roof, and a dog washing area that is super nice for my big dog. The community areas are very inviting and comfortable. The parking is protected and easy to get in and out of and the building as a whole seems very safe since the key fob is needed at every entrance point.
Spruce is clean, modern, and has nice amenities. Fair rental pricing.
Very pet friendly building with easy access to grocery stores.
Ive really enjoyed living at Spruce. Move in was so easy and managers are incredibly friendly and helpful. The apartment itself is modern but comfortable. Overall, Spruce is a great place to live.

Pros:
- managers are friendly.
- building is well-maintained.
- Safeway is right in front of the apt.
- big windows make you feel less compacted.
- wall sound proof is magical.

Cons:
- noise of ambulance.
- noise from the people, who need Jesus or whoever in the heaven, yelling outside (I mean you live on the Ave).

This is my honest feedback and I did not find any cons of "The Stax" specifically. Cons may also apply to any other apts. on the Ave.

TL;DR: it's worth living in "The Stax".

The property has rats, mold, and water leaks. Packages are stolen regularly. Management is incompetent, unhelpful and will find any excuse to charge you fees with no notice and no option to remedy. Lastly, they will raise your rent every year until you are forced out so they can become a parasite to the next tenant.

Alicia and Taurus are the best thing about this place. When they're working you're in good hands. However, the building has had 4 or 5 managers in the year I've lived here so there's no consistency, only one elevator has worked for the last year meaning the roof is only accessible by stairs and moving in or our takes DAYS, maintenance is non-existent and broken things stay broken, and there is a serious problem with trash piling up in the elevator lobbies. The weird garbage valet means there are piles of stinky garbage lining the hallways everyday between 5-7pm. If you receive a package and it doesn't get put into an amazon locker, you need to pick it up quickly or it will get stolen.

I was here for 2 years and these are my thoughts on living here

Pros:
+ The walls are fairly thick. I never once heard anything from my neighbors on either side of me
+ Plenty of cabinet and closet space (at least for a single person)
+ Relatively fast elevators
+ Built in internet modems (via CenturyLink / Lumen) to quickly get internet for 100 mbps at $40 / month the day you move in
+ Dedicated Amazon delivery lockers 
+ Property management team is receptive to security concerns. They've added more locks to doors so it's not as easy to get to resident property
+ Property management team is good and friendly with communication (via email) regarding issues that impact the entire complex (e.g. broken elevator, broken door to parking garage, no hot water, excessive heat warnings). Thankfully utility issues like this are uncommon.

Cons:
- Some units do not have windows that let in a lot of air, making circulation a concern (specifically floor plan S2)
- No A/C. Strongly recommend buying a portable unit for yourself for the summer months. A good floor fan is a minimum. Especially if your windows are west facing
- Inadvisable to go out at night in this neighborhood, especially near the Ballard commons park
- The trash and recycling service is mandatory and is $18/month
- The floors are relatively thin in the building. It can be easy to hear your neighbors above you walking around if they're not mindful of it. Property management isn't much help here. It's better to talk to your neighbors about it directly and exchange phone numbers. I recommend renting on the top floor if you can afford to.
- There's construction that's planned to take place adjacent to and across the street from the apartment complex. However, construction has not yet started (and possibly may not even ever begin at this rate)
- The main reason I moved was for work.

Highly recommend looking at other buildings nearby like Valdok.

I’ve lived here for around 12 months and it has been a circus:
-Trash chutes are constantly broken
-They use a “valet trash” service so many residents leave their smelly trash in the hallways all afternoon
-Elevators are often out of service. They have two elevators and at a point one of the elevators was broken for +3 month
-Management has changed so much and has extremely poor communication, you can never count on a call back and have to frequently check back in
-Maintenance is good
-The apartment layouts have poor design such as where cable outlets and air conditioner ports are located, they are placed in the only spots you can fit a sectional couch
-What makes me most livid is we requested a 3 week extension on our end date since we are traveling and they said it would be $10,000 which is 4x our current monthly rate
The Wilcox is a clean and quiet building.  The park down the street has been cleaned up of tents but still unusable at this time. Close to many amenities
The Wilcox Management and Maintenance team is outstanding!
Have a work/loft in gated area.  I use it as my office space.  Very friendly and professional management and maintenance.   Appreciate the quick response to my recent maintenance request.

Worst touring experience ever!!! Flew all the way from NYC to Seattle to check this property (together with 2 more apartments in the area). Because the previous showing lasted a bit longer, plus it was my first time in the area, I was like 5 mins late to this showing. Texted the showing agent I would be there in 2-3mins. But she still left. And the rudest thing is --- I saw her walking down the hill, and I waved at her, but she ignored me and left anyway...Would definitely NOT recommend rent in this property. I can imagine how bad the service would be if you live there and want to get something fixed. NOT RECOMMEND!!!!!!!!!!!!
The responsiveness from the community managers and maintenance team was greatly appreciated, and am very happy to be a resident here.

I have been living in the mResidences community from last 3 years and have experienced the improvements in the community with the new team.
Apart from sound of the construction from nearby building, pretty much every aspect of living here is convenient

Just moved in a few weeks ago and I love this place! The studio is just right for me, the common areas are a great plus, and the location is perfect. Most of all I have appreciated the staff. Everyone I have communicated with has been a great help, and I have to give a call out to Mike for dealing with/helping when I had some move in packages/big boxes delivered while I was out of town. Thank you so much Mike!
Everything about the mResidences from leasing, touring and moving in has been seamless and very easy. One of my easiest moves thus far.

I live here and the place is like very good.good bathroom, Good space,  very conducive Environment.  Cleaned, well maintained.
This is the best place to live.
Love the clean modern design and layout! Great location.
I'm the first to move in and loving it. Light rail and bus stop are right around the corner making getting anywhere a breeze. With that and the move in special, this was the best choice hands down.
This property met all my needs, and and as a bonus, it  was new, building was clean, quiet tenants, and the manager Paras was always friendly and attentive.

The worst move-in experience ever! Extremely rude manager. I wish I could give a 0 star.

Move-in Issues:

Key Denial: I was assured, in writing via an official community email, that I would receive my apartment keys through a pending parcel to accommodate my early morning move-in. However, on the moving day, the building manager denied providing the keys, causing significant inconvenience and financial loss.

Promotional Offer: Despite touring the apartment twice and booking it within 48 hours of my second tour, I am being denied the promised promotional offer for 2 weeks. The leasing agent had committed to honoring this offer, but broke this agreement after moving-in.

Exorbitant Camera Charge: I reported a dislodged camera during my move-in, and while I was willing to cover the repair costs, the billed amount of $1,425.80 seems unjustifiable. After receiving the invoice, I observed that the camera cost is $455, while the installation cost is an exorbitant $840.

Service Issues:

Delayed Bathtub Repair: The bathtub was clogged on day one, and despite multiple escalations, it took 10 days for the issue to be addressed. No compensation was offered for the prolonged inconvenience.

Dishwasher Drainage: Within a week of moving in, the dishwasher stopped draining water, causing a foul odor and making it unbearable to reside in the unit. It has been six days since I reported the issue, yet no action has been taken.

Managerial Concerns:

Manager's Conduct: The property manager's behavior has been extremely disappointing. Her rudeness, dismissive attitude, and lack of concern for residents' problems have created an unwelcoming atmosphere. It is crucial to address this managerial issue promptly for the well-being of all residents.

The management team at Leeward went above and beyond to help me during my apartment search and all aspects of my application and move in. They were much more service oriented than most other apartment complexes in the area. The Leeward is what every complex should strive to be.
Leeward is a beautiful property which is conveniently located in the South Lake Area, with very well kept amenities and friendly staff
The amenities are nice but feel like they are for show because the sound systems and TV/Cable situation and grills and firepit hardly ever work.
The location is prime and the buildings are nicely layout.
Leeward is a great building in SLU. Well kept with great amenities. Leasing staff is top notch.

The other review is exactly what is happening to me. They left me without a place to live , saying the move in day would be Oct 1, and the 3rd at the latest and told me the day my lease (at my old apt ) was over that they have no idea when the building will open. They have never reached out to me once , and also tried to get me to move to a different unit, then claimed they thought I was someone else . 
I don’t know what going on, the building is real, and looks finished. Very strange and management has very poor communication. Don’t apply if you need to a place to live, cause you might not have one.

I applied for a unit late August with an expected move in of early October. After a lengthy paperwork process and many in person meetings to fill out paperwork and provide documentation, and after being told I was pre approved in late September for my specific unit, and all my paperwork was done, they decided to wait until the day my lease was up at my current place, after giving them my notice to vacate, that I actually was not approved and if I still wanted to live there I would have to switch to a different unit at a price that was way higher than the unit I originally applied for. During the entire process the communication was only started by me reaching out asking for updates and being told very little information. They also got who I was mixed up twice,telling me I needed things that I did not need because they thought I was someone else. Overall the management there had horrible communication, they were very behind on getting my paperwork ran (obviously), and only told me what I wanted to hear instead of the truth, which is they have no idea when the city will start to allow people to move in. I will never recommend anyone lease through not only this building, but the leasing company as a whole.

The staff here is absolutely incredible. Apartments are very worth the price and the location is great. Close to California Ave but far enough away to not be bothered by any parades or events. Right by a bus stop, only a 20 min ride to T Mobile Park and a 10 min ride to Alki. Sirens from the nearby fire station get noisy sometimes but eventually you get used to it.

I have been a tenant at The Link Apartments for almost 9 years now.  This is the longest that I’ve stayed at one particular rental, which is a testament to the quality of the place.  I’ve always found the staff to be friendly and accommodating.   In particular I’d like to shout out for the maintenance staff.  The speed and quality of the service is without doubt the best I’ve ever seen in Seattle (where I’ve rented at various buildings for over 25 years).  Every issue I’ve had has been resolved within just a couple hours of submitting a request.  Excellent work!  I’m most grateful.
Absolutely horrible place to live. There is no such thing as community in this place, and the management and working staff is absolutely so rude and will never do their job!!!

After moving from a quiet neighborhood to the heart of West Seattle’s Link community, I could not be more pleased.  The staff, our home, the amenities, and the walkability are a tremendous contribution to our new beginning.

This apartment complex started out nice, and then it got horrible management. This new management has ruined this place. They are so rude, they do not care about the ongoing issues in the building, like security concerns, break-ins, loitering, trash in the garage elevators stairwell and lobby. They only care about trying to shove more people into the building and lie about the leases, lie about the security, lie about everything. My car was broken into and they wouldn't provide the camera footage to me or the police. They are in the middle of fighting BBB's constantly and will not improve. I will be contacting Greystar immediately to speak with them about the awful experiences that multiple residents have been having. IF YOU CARE ABOUT PEACE OF MIND AND A NICE PLACE TO LIVE YOU WILL STEER CLEAR OF THIS PLACE!
Great, quiet complex with respectful neighbors and a walkable location near a busy part of West Seattle without dealing with the crowds.

Worst place I have lived over the past 7 years!

I do not recommend this apartment for anyone looking to live in Capitol Hill.  The biggest upside to the apartment is the location and price but the downside does not balance out the heartache of living here.

Throughout our stay here, many of the appliances in the unit had to be repaired.  The washer and dryer unit could never wash or dry our clothes thoroughly.  Maintenance attempted to fix this issue multiple times but the problems kept on occurring.  At one point, the laundry machine leaked water and caused significant water damage to our belongings.   The property manager suggested that we use the machines in the laundry room on the first floor even though one of the reasons we moved into the apartment was for an in-unit laundry machine.  The sink and garbage disposal had a lot of issues and were clogged.  Management told us to avoid using the sink for multiple days.    The bathtub and tiles began peeling less than a year into our stay.  

The elevator in the building is very small and slow.  There was a period of time where the elevator did not work and was under repair for months.  This was an issue for our guests that needed elevator access.  We were told that the elevator would be fixed at a certain date but management waited until after the date they had promised to give us an updated date.  They were unable to hit the updated date and did not fix the elevator until months later.

The worst part of the apartment was the charges made upon moving out.  Throughout our renters history, we have never been charged for wear and tear on a bathtub.  I have never seen a bathtub peel like the ones in Violett.  We were told that general wear and tear would not take away from the security deposit.  However, we were charged $600 for the bathtub and tiles.  

Please heed my warning and do not live here.  We were constantly lied to throughout our stay in the apartment.  Until they find better owners that are responsible for the product they are selling, then no one should live here.  The lack of accountability at Violett apartments, managed by Azose, is unacceptable.  They do not care about their tenants!  Do yourself a favor and live somewhere else!

I moved to King Arthur's Court nearly a year ago, wanting to get closer to the city but still staying in a relatively inexpensive area. Honestly you can't beat having quiet neighbors, a huge living room and all updated appliances! It even has full size W/D in unit which was hard to come across in Seattle for the price! The maintenance team has always been super quick and the community within is clean! The manager there; Carlin is AMAZING! He is so helpful and is so responsive to any questions or concerns I have! He even hosted a Breakfast event so I was able to grab a quick bite before work! Oh and another great value is the one free parking spot in the garage! Many places I looked at we upwards of $100-$200 per month, but here it is FREE with the apartment which was a lifesaver for me! If you don't drive its also a short distance to the bus line as well. The neighborhood is great and you are minutes from shopping and a short lyft ride to the airport or downtown. Honestly this is the best apartment I have lived at in Seattle and hope to stay here for a long time!

First few years was nice, with as our manager. After the change in the management, getting a new manager, it start to go downhill. Problems kept piling up, 2015 was bad.
 
There’s too many things to list, I’ll try to keep it short and sweet. We had issues with our major appliances, they was getting old. This includes the dish washer (doesn’t clean, you have to hand washing before using it, plus after washing everything is over soaked, weird - see photo), oven (takes too long to cook anything), and refrigerator (humidity was too high).

RCW 59.18.085

Rental of condemned or unlawful dwelling—Tenant's remedies—Relocation assistance—Penalties.


(1) If a governmental agency responsible for the enforcement of a building, housing, or other appropriate code has notified the landlord that a dwelling is condemned or unlawful to occupy due to the existence of conditions that violate applicable codes, statutes, ordinances, or regulations, a landlord shall not enter into a rental agreement for the dwelling unit until the conditions are corrected.

(2) If a landlord knowingly violates subsection (1) of this section, the tenant shall recover either three months' periodic rent or up to treble the actual damages sustained as a result of the violation, whichever is greater, costs of suit, or arbitration and reasonable attorneys' fees. If the tenant elects to terminate the tenancy as a result of the conditions leading to the posting, or if the appropriate governmental agency requires that the tenant vacate the premises, the tenant also shall recover:

(a) The entire amount of any deposit prepaid by the tenant; and

(b) All prepaid rent.
