Provided new places to eat and parks in the area to walk, he made sure we were well taken care of. The maintenance staff is always available during business hours unless it is an emergency. We Have bin hear since FEB and we love it more and more every day. We are excited for the summer on the newly landscaped balcony/patio they just re done. So far this is the best Apartment We have ever lived in and Highly recommend it to anyone. 

Jaron & Elizebeth

My girlfriend and I lived here for a year. Then you first look around your apartment it seems kind of nice but as the year went on it became more apparent that the place needs a complete remodeling. All the windows in my apartment had broken seals and were constantly wet 8 months out of the year. Mold was a constant problem around the windows and in the bathroom. The walls in the right light were covered in slightly different shades of beige so we where charged at move out for painting. They put in new carpet before we moved in but it was so ruff I could lay on it. At move out it was determined to have been unsatisfactory after one year of weekly vacuuming, never wearing shoes on it and an arsenal of rug cleaners at my disposal. When we were moving out I had $1500 worth of magic cards stolen from beside my car and when I tried putting up fliers asking for them back management continued to remove them. When we moved in the utilities were $60 a month after 3 months they quickly jumped to $150 or more a month and that's just water, sewer and trash.
This building has great access to North Seattle, I-5, the University District! The building is clean and the communication between tenant and landlord is excellent.

Title says it all. My boyfriend and I have lived here for exactly a year now, and the management is the absolute worst. I have no idea how they continue to stay in business. I had been bitten by a dog in the hallway, they did nothing. They're never in the office, yet they never send out emails to let anyone know that they're taking a(nother) sick day or leaving early from the office so that we can make other arrangements to speak with them or pick up packages/mail. I've had extremely important mail and packages stuck inside their office for 4 days while they've been closed, but did not notify any of their tenants. We leave voicemails, send e-mails and they never respond. I have a service animal in their pet friendly complex but they have been charging me "pet rent" and took $400 deposit, which is illegal to take for a service animal. The handy man is very hot and cold, he yells at you when you require maintenance and tells you that it's all your fault that the apartment is falling apart. My brand new, $600 bike and two locks, as well as my boyfriend's back bike tire were stolen from INSIDE the garage, and guess what, they did absolutely nothing.

I moved here for the price (which will be going up by $100/month) but have not had one positive experience in this place. Needless to say, I will be moving out when my lease is up in a couple of weeks.
The Fox & Finch team has made living here a joy, Alex and Dylan have greatly improved the quality of the building and we are very satisfied.

We have never received this level of personalized service for our specific needs at any apartment complex before. We’ve been here for years and haven’t received anything other exceptional service. Darcy is especially amazing and really shows you she cares about you as a tenant. Highly recommend.
Google Cielo, Yelp Cielo and you’ll find the real truth. The building is nice on the surface but is plagued with issues, the biggest being the property management. Avoid at all cost.
I recommend it to everyone. If you looking for a great place to live Cielo is the best place.
I have loved living at Cielo, it is a great community with great staff and management.
Great location, friendly staff, excellent amenities
Beautiful building, great location and terrific staff. Definitely you get value for your money at Cielo!
A beautiful building with a friendly and responsive staff. Superb location between downtown and First Hill. I have lived in the building for five years and have never loved a place so much!

I lived at Lane Apartments for 4 years and I loved it. The building itself is amazing and everything is so detailed. When I come home I feel really safe. I enjoyed the 7th floor amenity room and being on the rooftop and relaxing. I want to give a huge shout out to Crystal my leasing consultant. She always responded to my emails and phone calls whenever I had a question. I want to give a shout out to Toye, my property manager for assisting me with all of my paperwork along the way and helping me to understand things more. The maintenance team is spot on and they always responded promptly to my service request whether they were big or small. I HIGHLY recommend you live at Lane Apartments. You will not be disappointed. 

- Meron H.

Pro:
* Really good location - Northgate mall, QFC, Target, BestBuy, many dental clinics nearby 
* Really nice & Friendly staff
* Modern and new amenities
* Spacious room
* Reasonable price

Cons:
* Garbage truck noise in the morning
* Parking spot is a bit small
* No in-unit AC
I used to live near by the site and it's really great location close to everything and in front of northgate mall.

My family of four rented a 2x1 on the third floor here with large south-facing windows and LOVED it! The property is older but the staff keeps it immaculate. This is one of the cleanest apartments we have ever lived in/moved into - even the washer and dryer were spotless! They had a team that came to clean weekly or so in the building so all the common areas were pristine.
The staff is wonderful - we loved the maintenance team - they always came by within 48 hours, didn't mind our dogs/kids/chaos, and completely remedied our issues on the first try. 
And the location can't be beaten. Super close to coffee (Monkey Grind, Preserve + Gather, Coyle's), bakeries, grocery stores + pharmacies, a big park for kiddos literally 2 blocks away, and the freeway/Hwy 99.
I'm only giving it 4 stars instead of 5 because the unit was small, though very thoughtfully laid out, and the amenities were more simple than those offered at other buildings (though they aren't charging the same rent, so we felt it was fair).
Also, in case you were wondering, the photos they post are accurate to the apartments / spaces - something we loved about this place.

If I could give Guinevere 0 stars, I would. My sister and I lived here for three years (2017-2019). We were clean, responsible and reliable tenants. We moved out in August and 4 months later we received a call from a collections agency saying we have an outstanding bill with Guinevere. After we moved out, Tom (the Manager) said that the paint on the walls was worse than the typical wear and tear, referring to candles and pictures on the walls. Note that we had a couple pictures in each room and would light candles periodically, nothing excessive. The lease contract we signed never said anything about this, or else we wouldn't have moved in. Guinevere management mailed us a letter to our OLD address, knowing that we already moved out. They didn't have the courtesy to call or email my sister or myself before sending this to a collections agency (even though they had both). If you're not concerned about your security deposit return, living a normal lifestyle (burning candles / hanging photos), being nickel and dimed for EVERYTHING or your credit rating proceed with caution and don't move in here.

BEWARE!!! Move out was a NIGHTMARE! On the contract we have it says we wouldn't be charged for painting after 2 years, yet they tried to charge us $500 plus for painting when we moved out after living there for 3 years total. Mangement used to be great, but has gone down hill - they will try to nickel and dime you for just about everything. Be prepared to pay a hefty bill when you move out, even if you were clean and took care of the place! WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!!

Awesome place for folks with big dogs. Some places I found wouldn't let me get my pup in for less than $1000 in deposits and fees, and this place has by far the best pet policy of anywhere I found. The building has all the features it needs to keep up with the rest of the nice buildings around, and the neighbors are pretty cool... Never met a jerk here :) maintenance is quick and easy to set up service with, and the office has enough folks working in it to be able to catch someone when you need them.

I love living here. We have been here for almost 2 1/2 years. My apartment is quiet and clean and has everything I need. They could vacuum the halls a little more often like when we first moved in, but it's not that big of a deal. Things have gotten fixed when needed ASAP. Haven't had many issues though! We have a deck which is really nice and face the quiet courtyard. I recommend this place!

The apartments look nice, but are small for the price. There's crushingly little in the way of closet space. Also, the smoke detector is right outside the bathroom door, which means that a steamy shower will set it off. 

The parking garage is cramped, which make parking a tough proposition, even if you have a small sedan. I'd hate to imagine parking here with a truck or SUV. 

The access call box only allows for one phone number per apartment. 

Packages are delivered to the central office, which means if you're not living in the main building, getting packages is a trip, and you need to arrange to pick up your packages during business hours. 

On the plus side, the apartments are clean an well maintained. The office staff is courteous and responsive. The location is nice, and it's walking distance from most things, but there's no problem with traffic noise.

Living here was uncomfortable because there is no soundproofing between the units, much worse than any building I’ve ever lived in. Loud footsteps, cabinets shutting, and other noises from neighbors are a constant factor. Noise cancelling headphones only go so far because you can feel the vibration of things in your skull. If you work from home or spend time reading, studying, or need to focus in any way, avoid Mark on 8th.

The apartments inside are nice, the location is nice. However the apartment vibrates rather hard at night, you will absolutely feel it in your bed. Particularly on the upper floors. It's very prevalent in the winter months and pushes into an unbearable rumble.  The building is wood framed and transmits vibrations from rooftop HVAC really well, particularly if you're in one of the end units. 

Other things to note is the garbage trucks will be slamming dumpsters really hard around 5 to 6am so be ready for that. 

I would avoid leasing from here unless you can get a really good assessment of the unit regarding this and any other potential environmental discomforts.

I have been living in this apartment building in SLU for 7 months, and unfortunately, my experience has been quite disappointing. The leasing agents have not been friendly or helpful, and the building itself is old with poor insulation. The extreme temperatures in winter and summer make it uncomfortable to live in, and the noise from traffic and old water pipes is constant. The management team has been unresponsive and lacking in support for tenants. Overall, my time here has been challenging, and I cannot wait for my lease to end.

Current resident here. We moved in on a Saturday over Labor Day weekend. After a brief tour, it seemed nice enough. From the second we started the move in process, however, we were met with one problem after another. First, they failed to properly schedule my move in appointment on several different occasions. No one was there to let us in when we showed up with the uhaul. Took 30 minutes of calling and calling before we got an answer. We were told our move in appointment was at 9:30 but whoops, they don’t open until 10. Then, we get to our apartment. The place was dirty and so many things were damaged that I set out trying to document so we didn’t get blamed before we even moved boxes in. Shower head spraying everywhere, base boards falling off, bedroom door literally won’t close due to misalignment, and probably most annoying of all, the windows barely open (unless you remove some screws) so airflow is nonexistent. Took a week to track down management before I could get this fixed and get some answers. We were also told when we toured that the gym was getting a facelift in the few weeks before we moved in - a month after moving in, nothing had changed except a downgrade in number of treadmills. So much for justifying the cost of this place because I wouldn’t need a gym membership. The leasing people are lovely so I’m not sure if this is even their fault but living here has been a nightmare. I’ve lived in many nice and expensive apartment buildings and have never had this many problems. After a few months of living here, our standards have lowered so we care less about all of this but rest assured, we will be leaving when our lease is up. Proceed with caution before renting.

They advertise a secure garage,but you will come back to smashed windows and stolen bikes from the lockers .

They do nothing about it, and demand that the cops take the report elsewhere because it looks bad if they're in the lobby.

Also, there is a key required for the elevator but not the stairs, so there's no point.  People break in all the time and use their stairs to get to the mail room and steal packages and bikes.
Property is not secure - my car was stolen on a Friday night and the front office/management refused to provide access to security footage to police until Monday.

This place is a waste of time and money. You won’t be able to get in contact with anyone, your apartment and the hallways smell terrible at all times. This place is unsafe and not properly managed by any means. No communication, no effort. And the “renovated” apartment was done so poorly that I’m afraid to see what it used to look like. The walls and floors are paper thin to the point where you can here others peoples normal conversations…through the walls, and you can’t forget the stopping from the upstairs neighbors that apparently have stones for feet. Your mail will get stolen by the shady tenants that live here, You will also be stepping over trash that your neighbors leave on the stairwells 24/7. It’s disgusting and the overall smell of the place is repulsive. They need to be shut down or made into a homeless shelter which is how they’re treating it.

Lived here for 6 months. Got charged for a sewer fee/water bill of $200 when they were working on another floors hallway leak. They nickel and dime you, overcharge on utilities, then charge you fees for not paying the extra charges after never responding to you. You can try and email them, call them and 9/10 times they will not pick up or respond. After I moved out they are still trying to charge me a $1100 fee for not returning the key on time even though I tried to contact them to find out where/when to leave it, and not receiving that information until 2 weeks after moving out. It has high management turnover. Maintenance constantly even though they never seem to fix any of the problems. And the best part yet, bugs! Found bugs all over my apartment, wasn’t ever handled, had to try and exterminate myself but still kept finding them in different parts. Overall, I never leave reviews, but this company is terrible and they should be out of business, I highly recommend you look elsewhere to live.

You may be able to find better amenities and more living space elsewhere for a similar cost, the location of this property is unbeatable. It is in close proximity to the Link, supermarkets and parks. Additionally, the leasing office and maintenance team are both very responsive and friendly.

I lived in Maude for a year and recently moved out. I had a great experience here, and I would give the complex a 4.5 out of 5 rating.

The location of the complex is convenient. It's close to Roosevelt and has easy access to many good restaurants and bars.

The experience with the management team is positive - they were always friendly and responsive to any issues or concerns. Maintenance requests were always taken care of promptly.

The only downside I experienced was the occasional noise from your neighbors. However, this happens all the time if you are living in an apartment complex I guess.

I have lived here almost a year and will be moving out soon. I must say this apartment was a last minute rushed decision and when I was trying to apply for a unit I had so many problems with the management telling "oh that one's gone, oh now that one's gone. They go really fast," 
Already off to a bad start I guess. 
This place is very expensive for such a tiny little living space but it did the job. People keep to themselves for the most part but be warned that the walls are THIN and doors slam HARD. Scares me every once in a while. My biggest complaint would have to be the absolutely atrocious conditions of the laundry facilities. I have never had more problems doing laundry than I have had at this complex. This is a pet friendly complex and with that comes LOADS of animal hair build up in the washers and dryers. Tenants do not care and do not clean up after themselves. Management does absolutely nothing about this (other than bring someone to clean once a week) and if you express concerns, they send out "friendly reminder" emails. Happy to be leaving to say the least.

For anyone that has a car and is looking for an apartment in the Seattle area (parking garage or parking on the street), you won’t find it at Maude for a long long time. I wish I had the ability to add pictures... NOT CAR FRIENDLY. 

When I first moved in on May 2018, I was informed that the apartment had off site parking and that construction was going to be done across the street sometimes near September 2018. It is now well into March 2019 and they are not done with the project. And on the same street (67th St.), they have started a new construction project right next door. I was not informed about this new construction development and this most likely would have changed my choice in living have I had known... but why would they tell me? It’s been a massive headache with workers parking on the street as well as big equipment making loud noises. 

Days before moving in, I was notified that the apartment had sold their off-site parking lot. How convenient!!! Now I don’t have parking on my own street due to construction and now I have to park several blocks away because of no offsite parking. Feel free to drive by Roosevelt and 67th and you’ll know what I mean. At least it’s good to know that the apartment is “sorry for my inconvenience” after bringing some of my challenges up to management. So I have decided to review :)

Workers also leave trash everywhere making it a very pretty place to live. Save yourself the hassle and stress of living in this area and find a new place. And find an apartment that’s willing to be honest to you, no matter what...

apartmentName: Promenade at the Park Apartment Homes
review: My new apartment is AWESOME!  New counter-tops, carpet, Plank flooring, and clean clean clean.... We toured 8 apartment communities in the lake city area.... This was the best unit for size, price, convenience, and service. The new manager here is amazing  always happy, getting things cleaned and organized. Free K cup coffee every morning during the week. So many cute and friendly dogs. Maintenance is on  it...It all gets fixed ASAP....  I love Promenade

apartmentName: Promenade at the Park Apartment Homes
review: The apartment complex itself is very nice, but the surrounding area is very not nice. Several low-income apartments are across the street. A few months after I moved in a woman was mugged literally in front of my living room window. There was a major police raid just the other week where they actually blocked off several blocks. No one was allowed in or out as they tried to apprehend 5 suspects in a shooting. People in the other buildings frequently play very loud music in their cars with heavy bass at all hours of the day and night. I'm a runner and I stopped running because I don't feel safe outside in this area.

apartmentName: Promenade at the Park Apartment Homes
review: Tiny unimpressive apartments that look nice from the outside, in a horrible neighborhood, i the worst school district.  If your going to pay this much for rent, there's much better neighborhoods.  The one plus is the staff here is great.

Everyone I dealt with was professional, courteous, and most helpful throughout the application and moving-in process.
Moreover, I am pleased with how friendly everyone is here which makes living here comfortable, and safe feeling.
The management and maintenance personnel here are all doing an excellent job.

On the first day we moved in, we ran into someone else moving out. They said their reason was because Neptune was raising their rent way too much that they had to move. We hoped that wouldn't be the case for us, but now we're being met with that same problem where Neptune is raising our rent so much just in 2 years that we have to start looking elsewhere. It's disappointing to see that Neptune is another corporation that doesn't care about their tenants like many others when it comes to rent control. It's really too bad Seattle hasn't passed any laws yet to prevent rent hikes. 

Neptune also makes you pay for a mandatory $30 valet trash. We wish it was optional because we would rather take down our trash than pay $30 for valet trash.
Best maintenance service experience in 5 years of living in Seattle area
I am only concerned about the proposed building behind the apartment which would block my view from unit L501. A major issue that may cause us to move.
The apartment is cozy and located in a good area!  Value for money is definitely true here given the amount of space the apartment has.
Amenities are well maintained. The location is close enough to the city, but far enough away from the noise and the bustle.

Over the past few months, the fire alarm has gone off multiple times per week, causing the entire building to evacuate. It happens in the middle of the day when I am working and also at 4am so my entire family has to wake up and evacuate the kids. There has been no action to fix this faulty system so I anticipate it will continue for awhile… stay away
Since the management company changed, everything has gone downhill. Terrible customer service and workers don’t seem to want to work here.
Everyone here is very friendly and helpful. The rooftop has astonishing views and the amenities are always spotless, I use the fitness center on the daily and is equipped well.

I loved this place when I first moved in, we had a great manager that cared about the people in the building. He was fired for giving our maintenance man extra time off. The man they hired to replace him is as corporate feeling as they come. Aside from how uncomfortable it became to live here and the numerous complaints I have about the man, the biggest injustice about living here is the unlawful withholding of our deposit and extra charges for cleaning and painting a unit that was only lived in for a year. We also hired someone who cleaned for 3 hours. There was nothing beyond normal wear and tear and it was spotless. Also, our "estimated" final utility bill was twice what it normally was and we were only in the apartment 1 of the last 4 weeks. 
I now have to contact a lawyer. Save yourself the trouble, live somewhere else.

I have been a resident of Hillcrest in West Seattle for slightly over two years. The building itself is in a good location on the bus line and there are a few restaurants within walking distance, and apartments are decent size. It is especially good if you have pets, since it is by two medium sized parks perfect for fetch - Myrtle Reservoir and EC Hughes. 

The building tends to be very quiet and premises are kept clean. There are multiple w/d on each floor and a laundromat conveniently across the street if you need quarters in a pinch, and I have never experienced any of the machines in the building to have been out of order. Trash/Recycling are in the back away from view and seem to be kept orderly and it's very rare that there's a build up. The water pressure has been great and hot water has never been an issue.

Since we have moved in, the building manager Jay was always very friendly and extraordinarily helpful with any of our needs and questions or maintenance concerns, and always made the building seem like home. Having a great manager on site was really a blessing and it will definitely be an essential criteria when selecting our next apartment.

One thing to note, rent was an awesome deal when we signed two years ago but since has increased about $120 a year.

I have been in Hill Crest Apartments for three years now, and I feel very lucky to have found such a great place to live. 

The super-friendly, live-in manager, Jay, is one of the reasons that I continue to stay here. His service commitment to residents and the larger Hill Crest community is impressive, and he’s remarkably flexible and supportive when you’re experiencing temporary difficulties. Jay prefers to try to find ways to keep good tenants in the building, and will work with you as much as he can to help you find a solution that is optimal for both parties. I’ve seen him recommend charities that provide emergency financial assistance to tenants in distress, and when he hears about job opportunities, he passes them along to tenants he knows are looking for work.

The neighborhood, like the building, is quiet. I feel safe knowing that only residents can enter the controlled-access building, and that every exterior door is monitored by video cameras. I like that the building is smoke-free, and that Jay enforces the building’s no-drugs policy. Maintenance requests are completed quickly and cheerfully.

Every month, Jay puts out a table filled with free Top Pot donuts and coffee for residents. Every October we have a pumpkin-carving event, with free refreshments.

This location is *very* convenient. I like that I can hop on a Metro #21 just outside the building to get downtown in 15-20 minutes. The immediate neighborhood includes cafes, pubs, a wine bar, a sports bar, salons, a gas station w/ minimart, a laundromat and a dry cleaner/tailor, all within 1-2 blocks. The public library, Walgreens, U-Haul storage and Pizza Hut delivery are just a mile away on the bus route. Home Depot is a mile downhill, next to the police station. I frequently take the bus 1.5 miles to Westwood Village shopping center, which has a Target, QFC, Staples, Barnes & Noble, Rite Aid, Bed Bath &  Beyond, Big 5, a  McDonald’s & a fantastic Toshi’s Teriyaki, along with salons, a fitness center, restaurants, post office and banks. 

The rents here are no more expensive than the average 2-bedroom in Seattle, but the best thing about Hill Crest is that it accepts pets. I couldn’t live without my two cats for company. Most places in Seattle don’t accept pets. Jay keeps dog treats in his office for regular visitors, and always has free coffee for everyone.

I’ve been very happy here, and nothing—short of an extremely high rent hike—could get me to leave.

I moved in almost 2 years ago and have loved every minute of it.  The office staff is very friendly and attentive without being "in your business"; Mile', the maintenance technician, is very dependable and helpful; and the other tenants that I've met are very respectful and welcoming.  I have a courtyard apartment, which is a great space to do container gardening or catch a few rays in the summer.  Security is a high priority for the management, so I feel very safe here.  My apartment is very spacious with lots of closets, and almost everyone here has a dog.   As long as the rents don't go sky high like everywhere else, I plan to be here for many years to come.

I can't express how much we love living here. From day one, the staff has been nothing but awesome. Issues are resolvedoing quickly and efficiently and always with a smile. 

The units are comfortable, well laid-out and all have a patio or balcony. Since it's at the top of West Seattle, the views are great, even from the 2nd floor (not so much the first). Jay, Jocline and Mile really work to make it feel like a community, not just a bunch of people living in the same building. Generally, the neighbors are friendly and noise is not a big issue.

The location is great, right next to a route 21 stop, with easy access to Westwood, and a 10 minute drive to downtown. There are several restaurants in walking distance and a corner shop in case you don't feel like going out.

We never want to move.

Property management will promise one thing and then do another and will be extremely cold and disparaging when trying to discuss issues with them. There is construction across the street and they are raising rent anyways because they can, even though they know they shouldn’t. Only amenities are bike storage which has been broken into and the backdoor is still not fixed after 1.5 months so property management encourages people to lock their bikes in their homes instead. Only other amenity is the roof top deck/lounge which they list separately but are the same thing. The rooftop is extremely small and only has one barbecue that works 50% of the time. Maintenance guy is great and the apartments themselves are nice, but it isnt worth the price point for where you will live and what you will be next to. I was assaulted across the street and have had many close calls being attacked by others as the neighborhood is extremely dangerous. Being off aurora means you will never get any peace and quiet with the cars and people constantly going by.

Approved my application and let me know with 1 DAY of notice that it didn't go through after being "approved" two weeks prior. Made arrangements, gave up my apartment and spent money on move only to have it cancelled the day before move in. Now I'm scrambling for a place to stay and out the money I put already put in because it was supposedly a done deal. One day of notice is completely unacceptable. Apparently the guy approved my paperwork before actually putting everything through (completely negligent). Offered me a smaller apartment at a higher price at a later move in date. That's not making it right.

Moved in August 24, 2022 and out March 4, 2023 allowed to break lease because the apartment was in such despair to include: broken appliances never fixed, counter tops ripped my clothing walking by catching my sweaters. Scalding hot water random causing 1st degree burns on skin. The dishwasher handle broken and caused my finger to bleed more than one occasion. The cabinets are broken as well as closets. They charged me close to 200.00/month for water sewer and garbage each month for 634 square foot carpeted apartment I was not in well more than 40 hours a week at work. My electric bill was approximately 100/every 2 months. Parking I was charged 225/month. The patio door so poorly insulated I was not able to be on that side of room in winter it was so cold. If you think you’re moving in there prepare for SWAT to bang down neighbors doors at 4 AM and the fire alarms aren’t a drill! Day before I was moving out the Seattle fire had to come out due to more broken issues in the run down building. Expect to add extra 500.00 per month to your rent on top of what their base rent is. Upon move out I got water bill 210.11. Less than week later it went to 301.01 for the same bill. They make up their math and when I tried to fix it proving with bank statements all of my emails came back undeliverable. Run far far away from any Thrive community. This one is a total dump too.

Living here was mostly a good experience, especially once the construction ended. Great location, dated, but sufficient interiors (e.g., washing machines from the 80s that the maintenance guy said "we will replace when they fully break down"). However, this one star review is due to my ongoing experience with the move-out process.

I contacted Tony N. on Dec 3rd, 2021 about my intent to move out at the end of the December month. I had been on a month-to-month lease and decided to move out officially once the new rates were presented. In that email I communicated my intent to not continue the lease, well before the 20 days notice they required. No response. Interestingly, my new landlords were able to contact Union Park to confirm I was a resident, so someone in management had to know I was moving out.

Trying to avoid any issues and make sure they were aware and preparing for a new listing, I followed-up again. And again. And several more times throughout the month. Several emails, several phone calls, and a longer voice message left on their listed phone number to contact them. No responses.

It is now 1/5, I am fully moved out. As far as I know, the apartment is still unlocked with the keys on the counter. I have yet to hear anything from Union Park Management, but lo and behold, I see a charge on my account for January 2022 rent.

The new rates really are not worth it, as someone who spent a lot of time browsing new apartments during the month-to-month lease, they are now overpriced and not worth the lack of service and overall quality of apartments.

Not only were we misled about what our apartment would look like during our tour, but renovations that were promised disappeared, packages were constantly stolen so they increased fees and brought in a poorly performing package service no one likes, and to top it all off our rent got hiked ~20% over a year while they refused to even put a grill in a patio. Union Park represents corner-cutting at it's final stage. Glad we can move elsewhere now. Maybe their elevators won't break, and maybe their emergency systems won't wake us up at 2 AM IN THE MORNING.

The staff are very friendly, but they mislead us about renovations. Scaffolding is going up, balconies are off limits, windows must be closed for privacy as construction crews demolish the outside. And they’re kicking residents out after leases expire, so the renovations will not help you. We were also assaulted right out front. Stay away.

This apartment was one of the most affordable in the area when I was looking for a one-bedroom, and has a wonderful management team.  They are kind, helpful and very security-conscious.  They respond quickly to your maintenance requests (usually within a day) and put packages inside your apartment if you aren't home, which is awesome if you've had packages stolen from outside your door before.  There aren't many amenities, but the gym is decent and always clean, and there is an outdoor patio/garden area only accessible to those living in the building, and almost always empty and peaceful.  It's an amazing location for bars, restaurants on Capitol Hill, plus about a ten minute walk to the heart of downtown.  Several bus lines run within minutes of the apartment.  Pro tip: ask the management about any units that have been renovated -- our apartment just got new hardwood (gorgeous) floors which we were lucky to get at the same rent price.

As a Seattle transplant, I'm excited that I managed to snag an apartment in this complex. First of, it's in an amazing location. I can't express how convenient it is to be able to walk to target, but also walk to nice restaurants and clubs. Even better, you don't get the loud noisy folks from Capitol Hill which just makes living here all the more enjoyable. The management staff is super nice, and they're really attentive to any issues. I've filed a few fix requests and they were taken care of within the same day. If you want to be able to explore the city, but don't want any of the craziness that comes with it, you have to live here.

Management keeps falling through on promises about fixing the passenger elevators, which have been off-and-on for over a year, and haven’t worked at all for at least 10 months straight. The freight elevator was their intermediate solution, but they would turn it off after the office closes in the evening (who knows what ADA residents did to get in and out of their units at night), and now even the freight elevator has been broken for over a month.

The ‘renovations’ they have been doing seem like they picked the lowest bidding contractor. Fresh paint applied (landlord special-style) less than 2 months ago is already peeling and bubbling in places. They have painted over door hinges and other hardware. The cheap laminate flooring they installed in the lobby has not yet been installed everywhere the old flooring was, so the subfloor down one hallway has been visible for over four months (since April 2024).

Maintenance is very good, though they show up unannounced/unplanned, often while I am at work, which makes it hard for my dog, who has anxiety.

Inconsistent office hours, losing packages, and poor communication with residents are a few other things that have made living here frustrating.

I have lived here for two years and I regret it immensely. The elevators have been broken for 9 months while the management made continual promises of repair with no follow through. Meanwhile, management refused to let anyone out of their lease so they could move elsewhere or offer any level of rent reduction. 
Furthermore, there have been continual security concerns that have not been properly addressed. Certain tenants have threatened and harassed women repeatedly and management has dismissed our concerns or said that they would be evicted, but lo and behold- they’re still there.
Instead of prioritizing maintenance and repairs of their rented units and elevators, they have renovated the lobby and advertise their non-existent amenities.
They will tell you anything to sign a lease, but good luck getting them to follow through, or even get anything in writing. This is the worst, most unprofessional, and predatory management I have ever lived under. 
Managers will avoid meeting with residents and if you manage to corner them, they deny any level of responsibility for their actions.
Know your rights as a tenant (such as working elevators and ADA access) and don’t rent here unless you want a 2 year long headache.

These apartments are in an excellent location and have a great layout. The bedrooms are a nice size with a good closet. The kitchen is cute. Easy parking. They also throw awesome events!  Great option for off-campus housing!!

It’s a beautiful property and  just moved in. The staff is super nice and liya helped me move in. 

The community has a lot of events. 
Pretty good.

Nordheim Court is a great place to live! The apartments are spacious and fully furnished, with all utilities included in the rent. The location is convenient, close to the University of Washington and local shops. The community is friendly, making it a perfect spot for students. Highly recommended!

This apartment has a great environment. U Village is close, and the area feels really safe. Plus, the staff are super helpful. I can feel home here. They organize many events, and it feels like I’ve been accepted as part of the community in this area. Thanks to the apartment’s community, I haven’t felt homesick.
As for the room, it’s plenty room for me to enjoy all on my own, so I’m very comfortable. I truly feel like I made the right choice coming here.

The Nordheim Court staff is fantastic! They are very approachable and make living here a great experience. They regularly plan fun community events that are a good way to meet your neighbors and make friends.

The community is located a very short walk from the University Village QFC, so it is quite easy to get groceries on foot. UW campus is only a short bus ride away, and conveniently, the bus stop is directly across the street from Nordheim Court office!

I do not feel like I am away from my home country. The staff are very friendly. Also, everything is so convenient for me. It is just a minute away from the bus stop which makes my life easier when I am in rush, and I have a lesson on campus. It is also located next to U- Village which is a great place for shopping.

Very spacious and includes all the necessities a person really needs. Also, transportation is within a 3 minute walk which is really convenient. Overall, it’s a nice and well managed apartment to live! It’s also really nice to have kind apartment staff that are always willing to help.
The place is very well kept and clean. The staffing team is wonderful and they can help you with all of the wonderful amenities included with the housing here. Thank you Nordheim Court team!!!

I moved into a studio, it was so clean and just what I need to complete my program at UW. The areas outside and inside the building are very quiet. Friendly staff and they will always help you whenever you need it! The busses are a walk across the street which is very convenient if you don't have a car!
As an international student I highly recommend Nordheim. The staff has been kind and helpful during the process even before arrival. They are always willing to answer questions and help you. :)

We just moved our daughter from Arizona into the wonderful Nordheim Court to pursue her masters at the University of Washington. We had a fantastic experience from beginning to end.

The staff were warm, welcoming, engaging and helpful. They attended to every question and need promptly with great follow-up and sincerity! Our move-in was a breeze because of the simple directions and signs the new management posted, snacks and drinks offered and huge rolling carts available for lots and lots of suitcases! Best move ever!!

I honestly enjoyed the experience so much that I've recommended Nordheim Court to several other students .... and I'm not even the one moving in!! Very impressive team.

The grounds are charming with a surrounding walkable community that is safe, beautiful and well-equipped with lovely markets, shops and restaurants.

My daughter's apartment is clean, bright and airy with a 2-story ceiling and large windows in the living room. The personable, close-knit environment curated by the staff has made my daughter and several other new residents feel at home amongst friends. Thank you, thank you. Job well done!!
Very spacious and bright rooms, right next to public transport so it’s an easy ride to campus and short walk to Uville, great kitchen and cute living room, perfect for student or grad housing.

Second year living here, and it’s been great so far. Last year, i was in a two bed but now i’m in a studio. Super close to u village and bus stop across the street for 372 is nice. Has more of an outside vibe because it has a green area in the center of the property with trees and a pond which is super cool for living in the city. The windows in the studio are also floor to ceiling which is great!

I've been at Nordheim Court for a month now and it's fantastic! I pay $925 per month for a room in a 4 bed-2 bath apartment (all utilities   Ethernet included). The facilities include Cable TV (minus TV set). The bedroom and living room space is not completely worth the price. But the location is brilliant! It's a 15 min walk to Red Square at UW. It's a stone's throw from U-Village which is the largest and most comprehensive shopping center in the U-district area. You'll get everything you need in this area which is a huge plus for a busy student without a car. There are bus stops right next to the complex. 
The complex is very well maintained and has a gym, community center, laundry, bike (free) and car parking (paid). The registration and payment process is super convenient and everything is systematic. Residents can manage mail, payments and interactions with fellow residents on a dedicated Nordheim website. It's green all around and only two floors per building so moving in wasn't exhausting. There are weekly food events and tons of board games, cleaning equipment, etc. that can be borrowed from the office. 

In short, it's the all-you-can-ask-for place to live in if you don't mind shelling out a bit too much for the space in your bedroom.

I been living in Elara at the Market for over 3 years now. It's been a great experience. The apartment is well maintained and its in a very convenient location for activities. The apartment is close to many shops and restaurants but its far enough where we don't get many noise. The staffs here are all great people, they're quick to help with any issues that I might have with the apartment. It's a pleasure chatting with the staffs here.

Elara at the Market has been one of the best places I've ever stayed in Seattle. If there were any issues, they were resolved asap since property management is always there to help and answer all of the questions! All amenities are well maintained and clean, so it's a pleasure to spend time on the rooftop, gym and many other public spaces of the building. Overall, I would definitely recommend to check out Elara at the Market if you're looking for a nice place to stay in Seattle!

Been living in Elara at the Market for several years now. I am still here because the apartment keeps up with their maintenance. The building is always clean, and the staffs here are nice and helpful. The location is one of the best in the city of Seattle.

I have lived at Elara for over 2 years. I love this place, it's close to the things you want and far away from the chaos of DT Seattle. Locust Cider is right in front so I don't have to go too far for happy hour.

Unit is nice, but management communication/action and security of the building leave much to be desired. People don’t wait for garage door to close, allow anyone to walk into the front door at all hours, and generally don’t think of the other tenants that live here. The dog owners here continue to disrespect other tenants by allowing them to run freely on the roof, as well as using the ‘people grass’ area for their dogs even though management had asked otherwise and the dog run is literally right next to it. Frustrated at the lack of respect and consideration from other tenants that don’t understand this is a community and we all live here together. Adding outside groups such as a hotel or Airbnb would be a disaster to what is already a building struggling with security, ownership, and responsibility issues.

A waterfont Gem. Amenitites are amazing. The leasing staff are great, always keeping communication. The resident events are amazing. Guess that Kiss, Game Nights, Drag Bingo. The coffee machine and snacks are amazing. I just signed my renewal and the community manager asked for feedback, which is something I never experienced before. He truly cares about the property.

Things have declined since the end of last year. The familiar faces I used to see at the office have left. The community just doesn’t feel the same. I complain and get vague responses. The trash rooms get filthy and the trash shoot doesn’t work all the time. And then there’s car break-ins in the garage that’s supposed to be safe. Homeless people are let in by residents and packages get stolen. Also, the Peloton bike in the gym hasn’t worked for months. I’ve complained that I hear my neighbors walking upstairs and they don’t do anything about it.
If you’re looking for a nice cozy community, at a great location with an awesome leasing property team, Elara at the Market is the place for you!
I've only lived here a few months - but what a great place to live!   Great staff, friendly neighbors, secure.  I really enjoy living here.

I've lived in Elara at the Market for almost 2 years and I enjoy my experience here so far. The location is walking distance to many attractions like Pike Place Market, Olympic Park, Space Needle, Westlake Mall, and many restaurants and bars. Its close to attractions but far enough to not get the noise. The building here is new and luxurious with many amenities (2 lounges / wine room / gym / conference room / rooftop / dog park ). I use the amenities often and see that it is always clean. The management team here have been one of the best management team I've experience from all the apartments I've lived in. The management team is constantly hearing feedbacks to help improve residents' experience and theres been many community events. 10/10 rating :)

I could give the building and its amenities all of the praise in the world, but the staff is genuinely the best part of Elara. Venus, Habib and everyone else here have made Elara the easiest and most enjoyable place I’ve lived in.

Fantastic location, Elara is located just steps from the market and the Seattle waterfront. A quiet oasis in the craziness that can be Belltown. The building itself has great amenities and a welcoming feel to the front lobby. The building is well-maintained and designed in a way that it will always retain its original style and grace. 10/10!
Great community. It is quiet and near the waterfront. It is walking distance to many restaurants and bars.
Amazing management team with the apartment located in downtown Seattle. Many things are near the apartment in walking distance.

I have good experience at Elara at the Market. The location is close to Pike Place Market. I like being able to walk to the shops at Pike Place Market since it is only a few blocks away. It is next to the waters and its surprisingly pretty quiet at night even though it is in Downtown. Some of the key things I like about the apartment is their amenities. There is a lobby at the entrance with free coffee and spacious area to do work. And there are 2 lounges at the top floor that have seats to do work or relax. The outside rooftop have a BBQ grill and nice view of the waters and mountains.

I had toured twenty-plus buildings in Seattle in various neighborhoods and chose Elara based on the proximity to Pike Place and work.  The amenities were darling, though--I was really looking forward to using the wine room and the fitness center had a Peleton (which is really important to me).  Sadly, the job in Seattle fell through and I'm actively pursuing other options in the city from afar.  I will eventually live at Elara and remain in contact with Andrea.  I feel like I have a home base in Seattle already.  

Perks: Great amenities (not as robust as the towers I toured, but more useful and more personal.)  The vibe: I love the feel of the community and the residents I met in the elevators were really sweet!  Closets: I have a lot of shoes and make no apologies.  The custom closets are large and well-designed.  I didn't expect to find this and Elara was one of a few buildings that met my needs.  Pike Place: I love to cook--I've read that several local restaurants source from the market and that's my plan as well. I discussed starting a cooking group in the building with Andrea and she was open to it.  

Negatives: The Viaduct.  I believe it has come down since I toured.  Yay!    Small: It isn't a tower so it has a few less amenities than some of the larger places I saw, but I weighed my needs and found that everything that I would use was there.  I actually found the highrises overwhelming.  I'm a little shy in that way.  Budget: Elara was actually in line with Seattle rates, but I'm coming from the Midwest and still adjusting to my future Seattle expenses.  I can't really blame the building for that.  My sense is that Seattle is going to be worth the cost of living, though.

We've lived at Willow's Court for four years and it is the best apartment we've lived at in Seattle (I've lived in many). The building is well maintained, secure, and several upgrades have been made to our unit over the years, which has been great (especially the new granite countertops). During the first year or so of living here, it was sort of a revolving door of staff in the office, but in the last few years they have had the same AMAZING staff, which has been an absolute blessing. The few maintenance items we had over the years were always resolved really quickly. It's also been great to witness the transformation of the up-and-coming Lake City neighborhood (including the Thursday Farmer's Market right across the street). As a bus commuter, I've also really appreciated how easy it is to get to the U-District (route 372) and Downtown (route 522).

The reason for the low review is because they are saying we did not return garage openers and several keys which is a flat out lie. For some background we had spoken with Sheila, who has always been kind, and let her know we may not be out of the unit until later in the night when she was off of work. She said that is ok and that we can just leave the keys on the counter. We called in the morning to ensure they had received everything they had needed but the lady who answered (who has been rude several occasions, including this call) said that's not how it worked and that we needed to give them permission to enter the unit before she can even do so (even though our lease was officially up). This wasn't what we were told, plus we had already given written notice which they had acknowledged and verified.

Now they are saying that we didn't turn in any garage openers- which is utter BS- all three were left on the counter where we were told to with 100% certainty. They also say we are missing several keys which is also BS. We did forget to leave the parking permits at first-which we brought back.

BEDBUGS!!! BEDBUGS!!! BE FAR AWAY FROM THIS APARTMENT. I will give zero star if I could to Willows Court apartment and I'll never recommend it to any one. It's a nightmare and we experienced most painful days during our life there. Stay away from it if you don't want to get stuck into such case like us. First, actually the rent is not low, we rent one bedroom six months ago, the rent is about $1100 per month but the utility fee is almost $150 per month, it is much higher than other apartments. Secondly, the officer is not polite, when we visited the apartment at the first time, she seems nice. But when we moved in, sometimes we meet her, she didn’t say hi to us pretending she never sees us. Thirdly, there are some people smoking marijuana, you would smell it in the passage way all the time. Lastly, after we moved in, we were bit by bedbugs, deadly all over the body. We were bit for five days until we finally know it's bed bug, we never experience it during our years' rent in Seattle. Then we argue with the officer, the first thing they did is to try all they can to escape from taking responsibility. At first she saw my wounds all over the body, she was afraid and promised they would compensate. But after the treatment of the bedbugs, they compensate nothing. We try to argue to move out but they are requiring us to pay 3 month rent for that, you'll never imagine how hopeless we are and how terrible the officer is.The officer pushes us to talk with her supervisor, who is worse. The supervisor is unresponsive and never cares how you feel. After several un-responded contacts, the supervisor finally replies, however, tries to push to responsibility to us!!!!!! How terrible those guys were! During the treatment, we should package all of the stuffs and put them in the kitchen and wash and dryer all the clothes, you can image how time consuming it is, especially for people has daily work to do. Again they compensate nothing and were rude to us. During the treatment of the bedbugs, I found a bedbug in the laundry room. So it illustrated there are bedbugs in the whole buildings. But the officer lied “This is the first time we meet bedbugs.” And the treatment of bedbugs destroyed our mattress.They didn’t even apologize to us, let alone compensation. We lived three apartments in Seattle for a couple years, the Willows Court is definitely the worst. Never move into it unless you want to feed BEDBUGS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I've come to Willows Court twice in the past couple months looking for an apartment and both times the staff was extremely helpful and friendly. The building is just off the main road but it's far enough away where it's surprisingly quiet. The apartments I toured were all updated within the last year and the apartment I moved into is gorgeous! Shelia really listened to what my boyfriend and I were looking for and we got everything we needed. Upon move in, there were a few small issues that we discussed with Shelia and she had maintenance come fix them the following weekday. 
I couldn't be more pleased with the staff and the location- even the few neighbors we've met are nice and helpful! This is a great place to rent and it's reasonably priced for the area.

Great place to just live.  A nice park around the corner and across the street from the public library.  Also, easy access to so many public transit line to get you to Downtown Seattle, Bothell, U District, Northgate, and many other places.  Walking is just a nice as well.  The complex itself is nice.  Nothing special, but a good place to just live.

I was renting 2B/2B  apartment at Willows Court

the master bedroom with attached bath is really spacious in comparison to other apartments in the same area.  The apartment is in close proximity to bus-stop, park, grocery stores and bank.

Washing machine is not inside the unit but since it is on every floor it works fine to share with other people. Gym does not have many equipment for work-out.

RENT IS VERH HIGH IN COMPARISON TO SERVICES PROVIDED

It really is funny how most reviews here are terrible for this place, but the overall rating claims to be 5 stars. This place is an absolute joke.
Not to mention, Enclave has deleted a recent review mentioning this, as well.
This place is a nightmare to live in, from the constant noise amongst your neighbors due to the paper-thin walls, cheaply made appliances and cheap building materials, and poor management and lack of action. 
I will emphasize that peace does not exist in this horrid apartment complex that is NOWHERE close to "luxury living."
Do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. Your mental health will thank you.

This will be a long review, but in short avoid this place as best you can.
To begin, the Enclave is a typical 5+1 mid-rise apartment, meaning the first level is retail and the next 5 levels are living spaces for residents. Typically the way these buildings are constructed is the barrier between the retail level and the first level of living space will be concrete with insulation to keep out noise from below, with the rest of the building being wooden frame. The Enclave, for whatever reason, does not have this. There is no sound barrier between the retail level and first level of living space, and so you are able to hear EVERYTHING that happens below you in the very busy Total Wine garage, this includes them loudly moving freight at 11 pm and 6 am. The upper level frame does not get much better. There is zero insulation, if you put your ear up to a wall you can literally hear the air blowing through it. Sound CARRIES through this building, from below, from the hallway, from your side-to-side neighbors, upstairs, and even diagonal. Whether people here are inconsiderate to this fact or don't realize, I'm not sure, but it doesn't really matter. Management does not really have any control over the frame of the building, so, what can you do about that?
At the beginning of our lease, I liked the management here, they're nice and will listen, but ultimately are kind of useless. They were kind enough to allow us to switch units as our neighbor below would scream out of his window every night at 3 am and bang on the walls, probably in retaliation to another neighbor keeping him up, as I mentioned previously the sound carries. After we switched units, they hit us with a $230 cleaning fee for our previous unit. When asked, they said it was a a flat fee they charged all units. Note, the lease mentions there is not a flat fee but rather managements discretion on whether or not they charge. What this means is that, no matter how clean you leave the unit, if management decides it needs a cleaning service they will charge you $230 no matter the work needed. When asked for proof of what was needed to be cleaned, I was sent a picture of an oven with some build-up on the bottom, a faucet with a small soap stain, and the living room carpet with the shadows of light fixtures bouncing weirdly off of it. $230 for that? They will charge you for it, no matter what you do. Might as well not clean on your way out, honestly.
AVOID

It really is funny how the overall rating for this place says 5 stars, when most of the reviews are truthfully 1 star (0 stars really). 
Enclave is not even close to "luxury living." Most everything is broken and cheaply made. Units are overpriced for what they are worth. 
Worst part is constant NOISE from inconsiderate neighbors, due to low quality building materials in this cheaply made building. You can hear people from all walls, including those units diagonal from you. Absolutely ridiculous.
Management does absolutely nothing about noise complaints, as if they do not care about the well-being of the residents. 
Peace does not exist here. Do yourself a favor and do NOT live in this awful hell.

I would put zero star if I could. Everything looks beautiful but horrible place to live. If you want to see homeless people walking in hallway, sleeping in garage, then this is the best place for you!!! These are not the only amazing things that you will have... you can feel living in Goodwills when you step out of elevators and see tons of trashy furnitures that other residents left out. If someone broke into your car, do NOT waste your time to go to office for checking the camera. There is nothing recorded. There tones of other amazing things that I would mention here if I had time.

Cheaply made, overpriced, low quality apartment. You can hear your neighbors above and below you opening and closing drawers, walking, closing doors, and talking. Privacy does not exist in this poorly constructed apartment with lacking management,and even the residents living here are careless, insensitive people.

Apartment is poorly built, as if made out of cheap plastic and cardboard. You can hear every single step and sound of your neighbors both above and below you, and most people living here seem to be very inconsiderate. Management truly does not care about your well-being. 
All in all, an overpriced, cheaply made apartment with terrible management.

I am writing this review after I waited 3 months to get my money back. At the time of leasing, the management asked to deposit $250 and said they will return the money in the end if nothing is damaged in the apartment. After I moved out of the apartment, I got a bill for $495, that too, they sent this bill to a collecting agency. I was shocked to see what the bill was all about, but I did not understand because of the complicated format of the bill, I went to the management to ask if they can explain me the bill as there was nothing due when I left the apartment but again no one was available to help me with that. I understand that they would need to clean the apartment professionally and $100-$250 is sufficient for that but $495 was not justified. I had to pay the bill because I was getting emails from the collection agency to pay soon. Now it was time for them to return my deposit of $250, and its been 3 months but there is no update and I don't have time and patience for all this. I went to meet the management twice, every time they are sorry by saying I am new here and my manager will look into the matter, please drop an email. It's been 4 months and now I know they will not return my money. So, the total move out cost was $745. I feel cheated and would not suggest someone stay here until the management changes their behavior.

Maintenance gets the buildings mixed up and enters our apartment without our knowledge or consent, packages go missing, we receive emails and letters intended for other residents - sometimes the emails say our lease has expired so it leaves us feeling stressed and scrambled. 

The hallways and parking garage REEKS of garbage and old food, we often find dog poop in the stairwells, and the elevators break down at least once a month.

The management used to be friendly and helpful when we moved in (June 2015), but for the past year it's been a revolving door of unhelpful, incompetent "leasing professionals" who will not go out of their way to help you.

Do yourself a favor and save your money.

Constant car theft even though it is in closed garage. They say they have security cameras but they are only facing the elevators and enterance. Staff doesn't nothing for you after you sign. They talk the place up and it looks nice, but they constantly have problems. The elevators constantly smell. Walked in and there was dog crap and pee on the ground of the elevators. Stayed there for two days. Fire alarms went of late at night twice in one month. Power went out but no buildings around the apartment lost power. Countless number of other issues. Save yourself the headache that I didn't and don't move into this place.

I would rather pay more to live elsewhere than staying here. The service was extremely poor, and the staffs were impatient with their residents. I mean why are we paying for those people? Even high school kids nowadays can do a better job than them.
Nice apartment but the management team is the WORST I've EVER seen! They will ask YOU to pay for their FAULT! Be nice to yourself and don't waste your time here!

This place is awesome!  The one thing I love about living here is the location.  Right next to Target, Starbucks, and QFC!  Not only that, the management staff are very friendly and easy to work with.  They made the leasing process very easy.

Amenities are great.  I can always get a workout in and use the lounge area to watch football games.  

Lastly, the open one bedroom is very spacious for one person.  The bedroom is large enough to fit a queen size bed.  Absolutely love living here so far! :D

My wife and I have been living in this apartment for almost year since the place opened on Oct. 17th.  The apartment features a fitness center with studio/yoga/dance room, theater room, game room (console gaming), and extra large resident lounge with a game room (pool and shuffle board) that has sliding doors that can be utilized to separate from the resident lounge.

Off of the resident lounge is the courtyard which features 2 BBQs although they're relatively far away from the lounge at the other end of the courtyard.

These are all great amenities. The on-site staff from Pinnacle are great too. You can probably find reviews where tenants complain about problems with staff, security, and other #firstworldproblems, but it isn't anything that you would not find at any other apartment complex. If use your common sense, have awareness, and pitch into the well-being of your apartment community - it'll be smooth sailing!

I've enjoyed my stay here thus far and would encourage anyone to definitely consider this spot! Thanks!

I have to start the good; new modern apartment, best amenities(fitness center, business center, residence lounge, movie room, game room, outdoor courtyard with fireplace and Gas BBQ grills) great location, great leasing staff, honestly I don't want to leave here.... So for the bad; we need night security, our closed garage is always being robbed, trespassers,and just for extra safety issues. The other big complaint is for new modern apartments and the cost of living there's no AC. All summer inside my unit has been 81 to 86 degrees. Not very comfortable even with fans on, and blinds closed. I have heard of some early noise complaints from the garage men picking up garage but that's not a serious matter. All in all I would have given this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the AC and people reporting their property stolen from their cars or in our bike storage.
Spacious, modern, sleek living.  Professional, clean, and teeming with amenities.  Bureaucracy and rules abound, however, not to mention $$$.
Horrible staff and apartment. It is loud, dangerous and the staff are unresponsive to real issues in the apartment for tenants.

Extremely unsafe building. Several thousand dollars of stuff was stolen from my storage unit which was broken into. Several people have had their car windows smashed.

Many shady people show up to the apartment and creep out the residents. 

Things are always breaking down - apartment fixtures, the elevator (which was down for 2 months straight). 

Management does not care and does not respond to resident safety concerns. I don’t recommend living here.

I love this building! It's new, with nice fixtures and some great amenities. This building houses only micro studio suites, so they are quite small, but if you're single, they are the perfect size. You have your own private bathroom with a nice, easy to walk-in, shower. The room does not have a kitchen, but a small kitchenette, that includes a mini fridge/freezer and a microwave built-in. However, each floor of the building has a common kitchen and the bottom floor has a huge kitchen that you can use. There is also a rooftop patio, with a grill and plenty of tables and chairs for those sunny days. The building has a laundry room on the first floor that accepts coins and credit/debit cards. 
There is a Fred Meyer right across the street, so you can get just about anything you need. Since this building is directly off the road, there is no onsite parking, however, you can easily find a parking spot a block or less away. 
Overall, this is a fantastic community to be a part of!

If you're single, this is a great, easy place to  transition to a 'real' apartment. And I say single because some of these units are very small and could be considered 'pre marriage counseling' if you're in a relationship, due to the studio style.  All utilities included, free Internet and washer/dryer on site. Roof top amenities and quiet neighbors. Down side is no stove or oven in the unit and the refrigerator is teenage size and hard to store food in. There are stoves on each floor and an oven on the second floor that's hardly ever used. Management is easy to get ahold of and it's right across the street from a grocery store and blocks away from downtown and bus stops.

Cheri/ Brandon has been very helpful and friendly from the time I moved in 5months ago till date, as and when I need assistance.

I recently had a package stolen from the secure package room. Turns out, theres no camera in there, and I also was told that nothing came out even after the video footage right outside the package room was checked for.

This experience did leave a bad taste in the mouth since the package for pick up costed $350 and we have no clue where it disappeared. So will need to go to the cops now, to see if I could get any help from them.

The management provides up to 6months of free parking to new residents, but won't do a thing to help existing residents with issues of theft (pretty sure mine wasn't the first case!)

The Lake Union Tower, affectionately known as the 'LUT', is a community to truly call home.  There is a fantastic sense of community in which many neighbors would literally offer you the shirt off their own back.  Sightings mostly include young, vibrant 20 and 30-something's socializing on the rooftop or planning a building-wide outing to local breweries.  It only takes a few minutes to walk to the MOHAI/SLU and 30 to Belltown/Downtown. 

The units are spacious and well laid out and have great balconies with unobstructed views of Lake Union.  Besides the rooftop with grill, there aren't too many amenities in this building which keeps the rent from entering the 'ridiculous' zone.  The only down side is the relatively old or worn finishes, fixtures and appliances.  

Overall, it's a perfect building for young and fun city living. Close proximity to downtown, the waterfront and access to casual organized social events rivals amenity spaces offered by new apartment communities. The relaxed sense of community is best described as reminiscent of college years if they were refined, just a bit.

Its a phenomenon that is hard to explain, it's a unicorn, it's a Lake Union Tower thing.

Three years after I moved out, these people sent the move out bill, which was paid in full, to a collection agency.

According to other review sites, this is a thing that happens. Allegedly a bug in their automated system, which they make no effort to resolve.

Absolutely disgusting regard to their tenants time, stress and credit.

It's still not clear if it's incompetence or malice, potentially getting paid from the collection agency for their already paid bills.

I have just moved into Verse however, I feel a review is warranted for the quality of service, the price, and location of this community. This place is amazing! The gym is great, the community room is beautiful, and the parking is reasonably priced. Some parking spots can be a little tight however, there are more then enough as finding parking at night during the week or other times when everyone is home in the community is not a problem at all.

My unit is super spacious with tons of luxury features from beautiful flooring to GORGEOUS white counter tops. I do have carpet in the bedrooms but it is very nice and none of the cheap stuff you sometimes see in some post reno units at other places. My neighbors have been welcoming and my overall experience has been lovely. The prices are unbelievable for the features and amenities and I don't know if we just got a stellar deal but this price was wonderful and warrants at least a look at this community if whoever reads this happens to be looking.

Lastly the staff are amazing here! There were issues along the way such as a power outage the day before my move in and the system having slight hiccups but it was nothing Amanda and team couldn't handle. Jorge *I call the friendly maintenance person* has been friendly, nice, and helpful. Amanda and Jorge both have gone above and beyond and I must say this place is a true gem in central district! RENT HERE!!!!! 5/5, 10 stars, there is even an amazon fresh right across the street and great dining options close by so this place ticks all the boxes. OUTSTANDING COMMUNITY!
We spent a super long time trying to find a place, so when we asked for a tour we were about to give up. Althea and Amanda were so nice and they made the process so easy! So glad we live here!

We moved in couple of weeks ago. The staff explained the facilities well and helped with providing assistance for the move-in. We had a few things checked and fixed after we moved in. The response for fixing things was quick. We love the up and coming neighborhood!

We moved in 2 weeks ago, and so far we love it! The location is great. The neighborhood is vibrant and just a few blocks away from Capitol Hill. So you get the benefit of it being a bit quieter while still having access to fun eateries and nightlife. The staff is super kind and accommodating (shout out to Kiara, Ming, and Althea). My partner and I moved to Seattle from Nevada, and we reserved out apartment sight unseen. The management team were very communicative throughout the entire process and were very accommodating.

The reason I am giving it a 4/5 however, is because when we reserved the apartment, we were told it was a fully renovated unit. Meaning that our unit would look like the updated, modern apartments that are prominently displayed on their website. However, upon the prior tenants moving out, we discovered that our unit was actually an older unit with updated appliances despite the backend listing it otherwise. This is likely due to an error made by the prior management team. Kiara and her team were willing to meet us halfway and had the carpet that was throughout the entire unit removed and replaced with brand new vinyl floors which have made our lives much easier considering it requires much less maintenance to keep clean.

I look forward to living here for the foreseeable future!
I was trying to get rent prices and unit availability but no one seems to be back to pick up the phone....

Sunset Electric Apartments is a great place to call home. The property is pretty well-maintained and offers prime access to Capital Hill businesses. The apartments themselves are spacious and modern, with updated appliances and plenty of natural light.

Sunset Electric Apartment's senior property manager, Betsey is always available to help residents with whatever they need, whether it's answering questions about lease agreements or coordinating maintenance requests. She goes above and beyond to make sure everyone feels comfortable and happy in their homes.

Overall, I highly recommend Sunset Electric Apartments.

I was looking at many other places but after touring sunset electric I knew its where I wanted to live. The apartments are clean and bright and made to make life easy. My leasing agent, Derrick was super and made viewing apartments easy and fun. Moving in was great and every step was quite easy. The espresso machine in the lobby makes my mornings so much easier and I truly enjoy living in this building.

Living at Sunset has been a major upgrade for me. The staff is very helpful. Maintenance requests are dealt with in a timely manner. Our unit has huge floor to ceiling windows, yet it is so well insulated from sound and cold weather that we rarely turn on the space heater. The price is great for being right in the middle of CapHill.
Fantastic modern building design with friendly staff and two elevators big enough to make move-in easy.
Fabulous apartments in the heart of the city - what's not to love?
Location is amazing. Quite noisy on the weekends, but that's urban living. Easy as pie application and leasing process.
This is the worst building in SEATTLE that is literally falling apart and sinking into the lake.

Like the name says On The Lake.  Getting to teleworking from home has taken on a whole new level of efficiency.  I can get a paddle in during my lunch break and work at my tan while on a conference call.  The 1Bdrm unit has an efficient floor plan with the balcony working like an extension of the space.  There are a few quirky modifications to work around like in any older apartment building but the wood floors and great euro efficiency w/d make up for it. Great location

I’ve been harrass since day 1. Everyone looking into each other windows, hearing everything, getting into people business.
