The apartment was overall good but I had a bad experience with security deposit.They totally lied us ,so be careful while signing the lease.Despite this the maintenance guy and the manager were great.

I've been living here for 3 months and so far the place is great. Emmanuel the manager helped  me with the whole moving process as life wasn't the best for me then but he made moving a lot easier. Maintenance fixes problems in my apt very quickly and Armando is great and fast when he does work orders. Parking can be a little tight at night so I purchased a garage space so I wouldn't have a headache in looking for parking when I got home or if I go out on weekends. Location is quick to Seattle and the grounds always are well kept. So far real good!!

We used to live at the Overlook at Westridge Apartments for almost 2 years. Unfortunately, we are very disappointed with the management and the place. Here are the reasons:
1) We kept the studio very neat and clean. I was at home during the moving out inspection tour, and the maintenance engineer said he was absolutely satisfied with the apartment condition. Also, we cleaned the studio thoroughly just before moving out. However, when we received the move out letter, we found that they charged us for some ‘Damage’ as well as for ‘Standard Cleaning’. The letter did not provide any details, however the sum of all those charges was magically equal to our security deposit. We were really puzzled with it. We are absolutely sure we did not leave any damages and our apartment was really clean. We sent the email asking the management for some explanations about those damages and the amount of cleaning works. We never received any answer.
2) This winter construction works started just in front of our building. These produced really much noise. Even if you are at work during the day, this construction is still a huge problem because they work on Saturdays and in April and May they worked even on Sundays. I don’t even mention that the view from the window is blocked and as the result the apartment is even darker. Also, when proposing to sign the leasing agreement again, the management didn’t take into consideration this discomfort.
3) The studio apartment is very dark. The windows in the building are tiny and we used electricity almost all day long.
4) They say, they have a gym. And they do have a gym. However, the gym is opened during the office hours only, so if you work 9 to 5, you have no chances to get there.
5) The location and the apartments are nothing special. Nothing interesting in the neighborhood, and the nearest grocery is 10 minutes to drive. The quality to price ratio is very disappointing.
6) Several more facts about the management. They are extremely incompetent. If you want to find out if you need to sign any papers before moving out or if you want to get some explanations regarding your security deposit, they either have no idea or just ignore you. In fact, they don’t demonstrate any respect.
Don’t live there, guys. A total waste of money.

I am currently residing at the Overlook at Westridge apartments in Seattle. This is the best kept secret of Iiving in Seattle, and If you need to be close to the freeways to get to work or venture out on the weekends this place is centrally located to 4 different highways that are just minutes away for access. If you are like me and like to stay close to home, there are shopping centers, food stores restaurants and wholesome entertainment all within 15 -20 minutes from here. The complex itself is quiet, secured with a timed gate and nightly deputy patrol. The management is professional down to earth and very helpful. I have only great reviews regarding these apartments thus far. The Overlook is family friendly and also great for the single people looking for a wonderful and affordable place to live that's close to work and play!

I have been living at the Overlook at Westridge for just over a year and am still loving it! The apartments are good sized, priced well for Seattle, and they are very dog friendly. There is a great pool that is never too crowded, and the grounds are really nicely kept. The location is great with easy access to downtown Seattle and freeways. Plus, even though you are in the city, you are off the beaten path and you feel like you are in a little oasis. It is a great place to live!

Lived here for two years and love the apartments themselves. Rent is going up so much though, and for very little space. Not enough doggie poo stations so it's a little inconvenient to dispose, but there's a little off leash park. Staff is nice, but their notices are a little passive aggressive. Also, they pick favorites. We almost got kicked out because of our dogs "excessive barking", but the neurotic dog right next to the assistant manager hasn't stopped barking for years and the thing is still here.

I moved here 2 weeks ago. If anything changes, I'll be sure to update. The apartment has been as lovely as I hoped.

Staff: Easily available over email, friendly, professional. They've checked in shortly after my move and about a week or so after as well.

Concierge: Quiet, very friendly and professional, happy to answer any questions and happy to greet guests.

Security: It feels secure, the area directly in front of the apartment is clean and safe, the alley behind to get into the parking lot is clean. No concerns. With an app I can monitor whether my door is locked or unlocked and provide guests with temporary access codes.

Noise/Environment: I toured a handful of other high-rises in the area and Helios is comparatively quiet. You can hear the occasional siren from the streets, and neighbors/dogs when they enter the hallway near the door. Other than that, I can't hear anyone above or on either side of me.

Maintenance: Everything has been well-maintained. Elevators are working well. Appliances are either new or look new and clean. Any questions I have had have been addressed, and the service request I submitted about my blinds/shades was promptly answered and fixed. I have not experienced any bad smells.

Space: The generous windows really make my apartment feel extra spacious compared to other buildings I toured with similar square footage. Many of the units I saw during my tour at Helios have ample closet and storage space. This apartment almost has more than I need, and I would even consider choosing an even smaller unit when my lease is up, but I'm otherwise very happy with the walk-in closet space I currently have.

Location: Perfect for walking to several nearby coffee shops, restaurants, and several grocery sources within a 5-10 minute radius. From H-mart to Target to several places at Pike Market, to Walgreen's - it's perfect. Close to at least one bus station.

Guests: No guest suite but the Charter Hotel attached to this building seems more than adequate to house guests.

Amenities: I love the rooftop views and fresh air. The area is immaculately kept. I look forward to enjoying it more often through the year. I have not used the dog lounge yet but it is kept nice and clean. The gym is well-attended and their equipment works well.

Parking: Parking is hard to get as it is in other buildings. There is also a garage or two within walking distance, and street parking.

This is a good one.

I lived in unit #2004 for over 2 years in the middle of the pandemic (foolishly signed a lease remotely as I was moving to WA and recently moved out) - the unit’s second bathroom smells of sewage, it’s truly awful. This was reported to management repeatedly. They sent engineers after confirming the smell and could not figure out the cause. They ultimately gave up and then denied the smell existed and would not reduce my rent even though the bathroom was unbearable - multiple guests felt I’ll and ended up using the primary’s bathroom. Would not recommend this place to anyone especially given management’s handling of tenant issues. Will be reporting to the City of Seattle so hopefully they actually fix the issue rather than pass it on to another tenant that will be overcharged.

So far this place has been horrible to live at. The day I arrived one set of my keys didn’t work and two elevators were not working. They assigned me a parking space and storage space that didn’t exist. My apartment walls were all banged up and my freezer ice drawer didn’t work. They fixed the ice drawer a week later and now my freezer doesn’t freeze my food. They never fixed the damaged walls or cleaned the apartment that was dirty when I moved in. They took over 3 days to fix the keys and get me in an assigned parking and storage yet I paid for the days I was unable to use. Someone had parked in my reserved space twice and when asked to have them leave a note on the car I was told nothing can be done and I have to wait for them to leave. I was a previous resident here and loved it but coming back to a new team and property manager was a mistake. They don’t address any issues for days and the customer service is horrible. The concierge team and security team on the weekends helped as much as they could and are super nice but the rest of the team needs to address issues and take action.

It took me some time but after several months calling Helios home, I feel its time to write my honest opinion.
Those who follow my reviews regularly, you all know how particular I am about the standard and the high expectation i have from any service providers, Let me start by saying that Helios delivers on every single aspect I ever wanted from my home.
I know it might sound strange but I'm not a huge fan of being a landlord and invest myself with a Condo/Home for many reasons... this fact brings me to have pretty high expectations of my rental as I call it my one and only home.
Helios is absolutely what you'd call a luxury residence and it absolutely feels that the management as well as every single employee at Helios family shares this understanding. From the outstanding customer service with the leasing team, to the Concierge team who somehow manage to remember you by name even when there are over 400units... to the maintenance team who always take care of anything you might need... Helios keeps me proud to come home every day.
Dont get me wrong... it's not all perfect without any issues or problems that anyone can experience with something like needed maintenance or maybe a customer service misunderstanding, but there is always someone to listen, there is always someone who not only will give you that polite smile but will actually take actions and resolve any concern you might have.
Yes, it is relatively expensive property but you get what you pay for and above all - you truly feel Home! something that is not as easy to find these days even with so many new properties around.
I do hope Helios will keep being what it is today... some improvements could be a coffee/espresso machine for residents to use, bottled water  and towels at the gym like many other properties around offer but none of these are an issue- just a matter of convenience.

I’ve lived at Cascade for 5 months now on the 5th floor in an open 1 bedroom. The community is clean and nice. 

This winter, my heat has not worked in my apartment for 2 months now. While I have been consistently working with the staff to resolve this issue, they have taken very little care or time to resolve the problem. They have told me multiple times that my heat is working; but I truly do not believe they are even staying in my apartment after turning the heat on to make sure it works. 

There has been an ice storm, snowy days, and temperatures below freezing outside. Somehow, I am expected to just deal with the cold. I was advised to contact Seattle Housing due to the landlord neglecting my safety from the cold. I’ve begun this process. If you find yourself in the same situation, do not hesitate to contact Seattle Housing for help.

I’ve never given any apartment less than a 5 star rating. 

I would recommend avoiding this property in the SLU neighborhood.
Great apartment at a reasonable price and very spacious rooms. Fast maintenance services.

Terrible maintenance service. They never answer your calls after the lease nor fix issues reported to their portal. Old building and things get broken often. After 2 weeks I still haven't got my leaking ceiling fixed. Dish washer and fridge have been broken more than a year.

We toured property. Building older run-down compared to others in SLU. Unit showed faced busy highway 99. Stained hall carpets, door buzzer doesn't work, no visitors parking but units nice with open kitchen but mini w/d and no AC. 

Very loud if unit facing street or next to elevator like in hotel or near interior stairway doors.    

Safety most important when moving new city for job.  Asked if any crime - they said nothing to worry "now" had added guards at night. Why to stop car breakins and bike thefts.   

Our work did crime check - tons of crime included recent (25 April 2016) robbery in building when occupied, car prowl (9 April 2016)  auto theft (5 April 2016).

Just moved out - New CA owners want new tenants. Posting is wrong -No fireplaces. No air conditioning. No fans, No high speed internet unless comcast. No walk in closets. No furnished units. No storage units (or the few that exist are taken). 

Raising rents - no long term leases unless you move into new units for 25% more. Some units have nice views but the remodeled ones lack carpets in living rooms and are super loud for people below. click click click when walked on in heels or dogs scamper around 

1970s building with on-going under the table (no permits) units under construction for past six months with endless stream of non-english speaking construction workers wandering through the building and blocking doors open to Aurora and alley. Another construction project next to building C just started after a year dealing with one across the alley. 

Run down public spaces, both the Hot tub and sauna were broken over Christmas/NY week, dirty carpets, leaking roof in stairwells and lobby. Smokers under our windows. 2 buildings face Aurora and loud so you can't open the windows but close to bus routes on Aurora & Dexter. Top of a pretty big hill so tough if you bike downtown. Difficult to have food deliveries (no place to park and buzzers don't work in two buildings)

Problems with homeless camp across the street, sleeping & peeing in stairwells, car break ins and thefts common  (gotten better with new night guards) in neighborhood and if you park on the street (vs $145 car parking) you will get hit. Check crime map. NO visitor parking and 2 of 3 buildings don't have anyplace for delivery trucks to move (in/out). Poor package notifications. 

Constant churn in front office - requires 3 staff? Focused on renting new units vs current tenants. New Manager is "snotty" and not a good cultural fit for Seattle. Put current tenants first. 

There are tons and tons of newer, safer apartments in South Lake Union with staff that respect tenants. 

.

You almost get what you pay for. 

An older group of 3 building (so the carperts in the halls are old but the units are average but not competitive with other newer buildings on Dexter) between Aurora and Dexter half of the units have a great view but the others face Highway 99 and there is a fair amount of crime in the parking garages (multiple cars broken into in December alone just as we were moving out)and lots of turn-over in the cheaper units. You rarely hear your neighbors next to you but you will hear them walking on the ceiling or out on the decks late into the night. It is a nice mix of urban professionals with a few 20 somethings packed into units 3 at a time but the growing Amazon presence has made it far less friendly (no eye contact) .  

The A building has a nice lobby but B and C face Aurora so there is no way for friends to park and enter easily but the front office in A will accept packages.  The south facing units get very hot in the summer and the listing is wrong there is NO air conditioning. 

The new owners from California seem very confused despite 3 people in the front office and the billing was wrong in both Nov and December. They also cut the maintenance staff in half (he works hard though) and the garbage is often overflowing both in the building chutes and in the garage. Their wanted to raise our rents but with less services than the former national chain had and tons of new apartments at the same price we moved to Wallingford. 

BTW the 5 star review below is for an apartment in Wisconsin since there is no outdoor pool or lake.

The complex is kept in pretty good shape and the staff is quick in fixing any issues.  For being on a main road, the overall feel of the complex is pretty laid back.
Overall decent experience living here.

I was looking for a new apartment in the capitol hill area and this property was the only one that responded quickly when I was inquiring on several different options. I worked with Jennifer who was super responsive and helpful through the unit selection and lease execution process. Thanks so much!

I moved out months ago and still dealing with the issue of receiving emails, texts, phone calls from the package concierge. Never got my security deposit and my last months rent, over $2000 and kept being told that they would have someone call me back with information about that. Not once have a I received a call back from management. I moved out under an agreement of termination of lease.

This apartment is super convenient to everywhere in Downtown and Cap Hill in Seattle. You cannot hear any noise from the surrounding units in proximity to yours. The staff is attentive and helpful and everything was a great experiece.

Lived from June of 2022 to April of 2024. It was a horrible experience. Went through 5 different leasing managers over the less than 2 years I was there. Maintenence was atrocious, I had my appendix taken out at one point when my dishwasher broke. Asked for help fixing it and was told it was be taken care of the next day. I received no response after that and no one ever showed up, I tried following up and was given no reply (BTW I still have those text messgaes). It's located next to a bus depot so you often hear loud beeping from the backing-up of busses not to mention the depots' security alarm going off at weird hours of the night. In the summer of 2023 the parking lot was re-paced, this messed with some drainage systems as now when it rains the water sits and pools by the front entrance and creates a mini lake. Its insane. Only thing this place has going for it is the affordability.

My husband and I moved in to a 1 bedroom apartment when Coast Management was the property Managers we put a deposit down in the amount of 1415. We moved in Aug of 2017, prior to move in we got the okay from the leasing manager that our scale baby was approved to live there. December of 2017 we added a puppy to our lease and also paid another 300 bringing our deposit to 1715. We gave our notice that we were leaving in March of 2018, after giving our notice the owner came to do a move out inspection. When the owner came in he was very upset that we had our scale baby in the apartment and told the new leasing manager at the time that we had three days to get rid of her or leave. Well we never got ANYTHING In writing stating that and she said she was waiting to hear back from the owner on the next steps for that. We moved out the end of March and don't receive anything from anyone until almost May. In the letter we got they were coming after us for an additional 2100 on top of our deposit. I immediately asked for receipts  and invoice regarding the damages and repairs they said they needed to have done.  Come June I still don't have any information regarding the so called damages but did get some more info stating that they over quoted me on some things and I should be receiving a refund of anywhere from 200-500. When Indigo took over they went back and forth on what needed to happen. I was told something different EVERY TIME I called, that is of course when they answered. It is now almost September 2018 and I still don't have refund nor are they returning ANY calls I put into them. Please just beware of the management. Record all encounters with them as well as get written letters of any approvals they give you so it doesn't hurt you in the long run and ask for receipts upon move out so you don't get overpay back money for damages that they clearly didn't do or overbid you on. Good luck on your stay here at Andante, hope you have better luck than us!

My fiance and I our moving from Southern California and the process though exciting has also been stressful. Our most important priority as we transition was where we would feel safe resting our head. Upon calling Andante Apartments we were introduced to Telisha! Wow! What a kind and service driven individual. She answered all our questions and put our minds to ease. She was friendly, compassionate, and knowledged! She is why we're renting at Andante Apartment Homes!

Majority of the reasons why it’s such a terrible place to live is due to the assistant manager Mark. 

He will say he will get back to you by a certain time (using  assuring language like “definitely” and “for sure”) and you will never hear from him again until you bring it up. And once you bring it up, it isn’t done so you go through the same process. This has happened a DOZEN of times. 

Mark is also very passive aggressive and hard to get a hold of, he’s only in the office 2 times a week for half days. 

Our fridge has been broken for the whole duration of us living there (6 months); even though we’ve made multiple complaints. We have been waiting for a new one for 2 weeks now. 

We’ve even had to throw away food because the fridge is broken and over freezes things and we have no been reimbursed. Our electricity bill skyrocketed due to the broken fridge and we are not being reimbursed. 

Our heaters were broken for a couple months during the winter. 

No door stops were installed, we had to ask multiple times for them. 

We’ve had 3 different events with out toilet being broken. 

Save yourself the biggest headache and avoid this place at all costs.

I was sent a video of my apartment before I moved in because I could not tour in person. When I arrived, I found out that they had showed me a different apartment with a much bigger balcony. I specifically asked about the balcony, and was told that they were exactly the same.

If you are moving in DO NOT expect the apartment to be clean. When I first arrived, the floors were caked with dirt, there were nail clippings in the bathroom, rotting food under the fridge, and so much dust on the blinds that it made me choke. 

Shortly after I moved in, I saw that many tenants were moving out. I asked why they were leaving, and they said that they were informed that the only elevator was going to be under construction for THREE MONTHS! I was never told about this before signing the lease, and I've also never heard of a 3 month elevator construction project. 

During the elevator construction, the key scanner to enter the building was removed without the tenants being informed. I got locked outside and tried to call the building manager, but his phone was turned off. I was locked outside the building for over 2 hours before someone let me in.

If you are moving in here, good luck.

My wife and I moved in about 2 months ago and we couldn't be happier with our decision! After looking all over Capitol Hill, what really made us choose this place was the location, management, and the water pressure lol.

From 2021- as of the current year of 2023, there is major construction going on right next door to the property. I was warned about this when I leased, but was not told there would be a full-on demolition to start. It lasted months and shook my unit so hard that my cabinets slid down the wall! The construction is very loud and sometimes there is an awful smoke that smells terrible coming from the construction site. It's hard to keep windows open in the summer for these reasons, but that sucks because there's no central or portable AC rental options. Virtually no parking on the street because the construction has blocked off the entire left side of the road. The fire alarms go off all the time, as the alarm system is connected in each tower, so when one goes off, they all go off in every unit and hallway. So many times where I've been woken up in the middle of the night to the alarm going off. The property is also not ADA compliant- no elevators on site and all amenities + units are only accessible via up to 5 flights of stairs. The package locker is not very trustworthy. The past 5 times I've used it, it either was delivered but not connected to my account to access or just left outside, which inevitably resulted in it getting stolen. The residents at this property are also not the best to live around- if you're a woman and trying to be neighborly, don't haha. There've been many instances where my male neighbors have made me feel uncomfortable and made inappropriate verbal advances. I've found a resident passed out in a bush before, my bike was stolen from the locked bike storage room on site (most likely by another resident, did not receive any help from management), and I don't feel safe doing my laundry anymore because on a few occasions, I've found someone sleeping in the dark stairwell leading to the laundry room. Rats in the trash room, which makes it kind of scary to take out my garbage. The property has switched management a few times, now with Avenue 5. In my experience, they're by far the worst at communication. Very frustrating. No on-site leasing office which has pros and cons. Maintenance, however, is very responsive, kind, and helpful! Noise from units can only be heard in the bathroom & by the kitchenette, where you can hear your neighbor's cabinets close. I lived on the top floor so I can't speak to noise levels from above neighbors. It's also cheap base rent and fixed rates for utilities, which is amazing.

If you have another option, don’t move here. 
There were at least three squatters in the community kitchen in the year I lived here (and no bathroom for them to use so that was lovely). Emails to the property manager will go unanswered or they will be condescending and won’t do anything.  There is always dumped furniture and dog poop out front. Noisy neighbors that don’t keep regular hours. Four washers and dryers for 70+ units, and there is usually at least one machine broken at a time. 
If you are desperate, then fine. If not, don’t do it.

Terrible management that's rarely on-site. 

Elevators always down.

Payment system screwed over everyone in the building with double charges and missing payments.

Will lose your check or say it's late to get you to pay more.

Terrible communication between management and whoever manages them.

Management has switched over 4x and they will most likely screw up your lease.

If you read the other 1 star reviews, they're absolutely right. The units may be good but the place is run by trespassers, drugs, and garbage. 

I lost count of package thefts, the bike room has been broken and hasn't been fixed in months, multiple doors have been broken at this time, and the fire alarm goes out at least once a month. I'm afraid of leaving my unit every day. Despite all the horrible things in the building, management won't release anyone from their lease and you have to stay. I honestly can't wait to move out of this place.

After living here for 9months, this place has become a nightmare. The building although it looks nice, harbors drug addicts that will smoke and cook their drugs in their units and the fumes will spread and cover the entire floor. Myself and my neighbors have been hospitalized from amphetamine exposure. On other floors, there's issues with fentanyl and drug dealers. And if you don't have the drug dealers, then you have the homeless doing drugs on your floor. There's been multiple aggressive dogs that will try to attack your animals unprovoked. The drug addicts that live here constantly break the property, steal packages, bikes, and let other drug users and homeless into the building. If you try to ask them to leave, they will threaten you or try to hurt you. I've been complaining and calling police for MONTHS and it's only gotten worse. This building isn't safe. I'm always on edge unlocking my door and leaving my unit. Ive had someone even try to break into my unit before. If you wash your laundry here, you should watch it the entire time or else people will steal your clothes. It's so sad how this building fell apart. It's nowhere near the image they sold me when I first moved in, but then again the entire office staff was different. No one from the original team is here because it was too dangerous for them to continue working here. I no longer believe they want the community to thrive here nor help people. They see us as dollar signs only. Security does nothing, fobs don't seem to matter since the secured doors are broken. My floor hasn't been secured for months. Also there's so many blind spots with the cameras and there is no audio on them so good luck relying on footage to help you in emergencies unless you're on the elevator. It's honestly a tragedy what this building has become. DO NOT MOVE HERE you will thank yourself for doing so. I'm embarrassed to live here and bring anyone over to visit.

The first week I moved in someone tried to cook meth in their unit and started a fire after it exploded, from there I've been feeling increasingly unsafe in my own home and apartment community. There's homeless camping IN our building in our amenity spaces, stairs, and lobby. They will get let in and jump on an elevator with a resident ride to their floor then take the stairs to whatever floor they desire, which wouldn't happen if our security actually did their job or there was overnight front desk. The trash chute is ALWAYS clogged and the trahs rooms are literally rooms piled with trash, I have a back flow of trash in my unit that NEEDS to go and when I asked about a trash room they said I had to use the chute which has been clogged for 2 weeks now. Our "security officer" I've only seen once for a brief moment and he let me in after only verbally confirming I was a resident then let a group of non residents in without making them use the call box or even asking. There's also been a huge problem with package theft and food delivery theft throughout the building with laundry included in that. Someone tried to break into our package room with a crowbar! That's insane! I shouldn't feel the need to get things delivered to my work and not my HOME! Nor should I feel paranoid doing laundry in my building I pay to live in. I also on a regular basis pretty much all around the building smell smoked opioid pills and it's just disgusting, never mind the fact that its a litteral health risk with my lungs being damaged and having asthma on top of that. I like my unit but I'm so scared of living here and would honestly never reccomend it to anyone, I mean hell even a staff member that did live here moved out because of how unsafe it is. I felt the need to get a security system! For a top floor unit that in theory should be safe with a fob entry only policy but this building is out of control and I'm not sure if I want to continue living here after JUST moving in.

I have been living at the property for about 2 years now. The building and the amenities are good. But the people living here have no respect for others, especially during the quiet hours. You may expect moving furniture at 12am in the morning, or doing laundry at 2 am, or listening to music very loud at night. And the most frustrating part that the management can't do anything about it. Hopefully, I'll move out soon.

I signed up for a tour for this place. When I got there the leasing staff could see me through the office windows. I rang the call box so they could let me in but they closed the office shades and no one answered my call. Major red flags. I left.

I just moved in a week ago, and the manager and maintenance guy are very professional, trustworthy, and very nice. The unit is very spacious. The office is always open and when I call the manager always answers the phone. I am happy to be a resident at Whisperwood.

I moved in as the pandemic started. This place was supposed to be safe. It has not been. Bedbugs, falling branches, cloudy tap water (filter is a must), and all work orders take weeks to months. 

I don’t like leaving bad reviews. However this place will eat at you. The bed bug issue was with the whole building but management tried blaming those who reported it. 4 sleepless months later I was allowed to move units as they could not solve the bedbug infestation. This cost me so much in cleaning cost, time, lack of sleep and the added stress of arguing with management. 

This unit has a dishwasher that hasn’t worked since I got here (over a year). Hot water went out for 3 weeks while it started snowing. That’s not even mentioning the Highway and airport noise nearby. I could keep going on. This place ate away at my mental health and am lucky to have a support system that helped me get better.

This complex fails at so many things. Most importantly it fails at providing a safe place to live.
Dirty common area, very small room. poor soundproofing
Had a very friendly and responsive agent when looking for units  Free food every now and then as well!
It was so cool having this little pizza party! We just moved in and this was so friendly

I really enjoyed my stay here @ Novo. Location is great, building is well managed and management crew was always responsive and attentive. In times of Covid, which are especially difficult, Property Management was coming out with several incentives to smoothen the impact and make life of the residents easier - that includes partnerships with local restaurants and services. Common spaces are sanitized and cleaned up periodically by a dedicated person. You’ll find all basic amenities fit for micro apartments lifestyle. Special shout out to Natalie and Zoe for their professional attitude. Highly recommend this place.

I lived in one unit that had black mold in it due to the upstairs washer leaking and flood my kitchen every day and it took them over 5 months of living in it before I was offered another unit. Then the other unit wasn’t even cleaned before I moved I. Carpets were disgusting cabinets and drawers broken. Not once has anything been fixed and they’ve ignored my multiple requests to get things fixed. That’s not to mention they raised my rent over $500 in this broken down unit. Then of course there’s the extra charge for hot water usage and hot water sewage usage, WTF?

Office is very unhelpful and rude! I drove an hour to tour the apartment and was not made aware of documents I needed to bring. I was then asked leading questions that led me to not be eligible to rent from the location!

The building is not well managed, it’s dirty and unmaintained. There is a lot of package theft and other vandalism that is never addressed. The laundry machines are often broken. Homeless people often get into the building and sleep under the stairs. The street is very unsafe. I witnessed a homicide where a man was shot six times right outside this building.

All of these problems and the building managers have the audacity to increase rent. You can find much better deals, in safer areas, with better building management.
It's not the worst experience I've ever had. The large amount of homeless people that sleep on the steps of the apartment are usually pretty nice.
The apartment is great. It has a small gym and a large rooftop! My studio unit is spacious with brand new appliances. Everything works great. The management is also really helpful.

Quiet and close to everything. Outside is a mess but so is every city in America right now. From my living space I see old beautiful brick and trees along with city and it’s lovely. I have been able to leave a package outside my door all day accidentally. The neighbors are solid so far! Maintenance responds quickly and management has been nothing but helpful and gracious. Thank you! I feel excellent about this move. -Aur
Best property manager, He went through everything apartment tours, perks, Gym, In Unit Laundry.Everything was great during the move in process thanks Jay.
Great property management, made moving in really easy. Great community and great amenities. I've only recently moved to the community but I'm having a great experience so far.
My experience has been very good. The place is clean and well maintained. It is quiet. I highly recommend staying here because it has a very good atmosphere.
Love the property and people! Great location and easy accessibility to the I-5 and public transit. Lots of options! Great amenities for the size and area of the property!

I like it. The only thing that kind of surprised me were the outdated appliances. When I checked the reviews/site.. it said that everything was updated that was the largest downside for me. Also, being so close to a shelter where there are a lot of unhoused people who are often outside of the building is something to consider.

The Living room is spacious and the gym is nice. The roof top complete with grills is wonderful to relax on after work. If you get the one bedroom it watch out for non locking doors to the bedroom itself
Arrive First Hill has been great so far. I just moved in approximately two and a half weeks ago. Since then Arrive First Hill has been great.

I think that the leasing manager is super friendly, experienced in handling situations and she made me feel extremely comfortable with my move in. I feel totally at home here at Arrive and I am glad to be a part of the community. Keep it up! And thank you thank you
The trash system is not my favorite, the elevators are a bit slow and I’ve gotten stuck in them a few times, and someone stole my package. Otherwise good.
Has been good so far! Very responsive and easy to communicate with. Fixes most issues on time and has been easily undeerstanding of any issues.

Arrive First Hill has undergone a quite the transformation under new management, and the changes are simply stunning. The updated décor has created an inviting atmosphere from the moment you arrive. The upcoming upgrades to the rooftop and gym look so good, I can’t wait till they officially open. I can hardly wait to see the rooftop views and BBQ with friends this summer! 

The Staff is also extremely sweet and easy to communicate with if you are having any issues.

New company came in and started raising rent while not addressing tenant concerns. The grounds have been filthy ever since they took over. Okay location but not worth the price or management induced headache you will endure.

They collect a fat rent but don’t want to be bothered with tenant concerns.  No one will answer the phone if you need assistance. Expect your delivery packages to get stolen. And don’t expect any response or help from the so called on-site staff. THE worst. Stuck till lease ends.

Look no further. We loved our 4-years at The Point and would give a 6th star if we could. 

The property manager and owner are incredibly nice people who have cultivated an amazing community and take such great care of their tenants. They responded quickly and kindly to any and all requests and were so thoughtful in assisting us with move-in and move-out. The units are modern, spacious, and have great lighting. The rooftop is a great vibe and arguably the best view in all of Seattle - we enjoyed countless days up there over the years. The location is prime because you're so close to the Pike/Pine downtown of Capitol Hill, but you're tucked away enough that it's usually quieter and with less commotion. Yes, there is some homelessness in the surrounding area, but I never felt unsafe at or around the building in my time there.

I lived at the Point apartments for a year and had to leave because I was moving out of the state but it was the best building, great location, great space, excellent units, and the most understanding and flexible landlords you could ask for. This apartment is fantastic - wish I could move back to Seattle and live here for another year.

We chose The Point three primary reasons: excellent kitchens with gas ranges and ice & water makers in the fridge, the quality of the construction (built in 2019), and the location. Units are large with higher than average ceilings and lots of natural light as well.

Condo level finishes throughout.  A/C in all bedrooms and living rooms was a huge plus and hard to find in Seattle.  Only 36 units in the building so felt more like a community than other larger buildings I've lived in.  Management is great and always looking out for the tenants and ways to help.  Building is also only a year old.

I love living at The Central. So close to Capitol Hill but also removed enough to be a quieter and slower pace. The apartment has great amenities with parking and storage you can rent. The management team is amazing, communicative, and friendly. The maintenance staff is so helpful and responsive. I love living here and highly recommend to anyone looking for a well-maintained building in a great location.

We love living at The Central Apartments. The apartments have a premium feel with luxury vinyl flooring (wood plank appearance) atop solid concrete floors, stainless steel appliances, and quartz counters. There's even a nice community/party room and two rooftop decks!
The front office staff, management, and maintenance teams are excellent. They respond quickly and efficiently with a smile for any needs at move-in or needs that arise with maintenance.
We like the location, which is walkable to all that Capitol Hill has to offer, and situated at the heart of the Central District's amenities. In or near the building are a post office, coffee shops, and restaurants/bars. There's a PCC market and All The Best Pet Care across the street. Easy to get to downtown by walking or taking one of the bus lines that run down Union or 23rd Ave.

Love the area and location BUTTT..

Thrive takes advantage of people upon moveout, we were lucky enough to find a home and closed with 2 months still left on the lease. We were forced to pay 2 months worth of rent ON TOP OF PRO RATED RENT FOR HALF A MONTH. We tried to talk to management regarding the fees and they were more interested in citing the contract than helping people. We were residents for almost 4 years and were treated like complete garbage upon moveout. I would be warry of living here if you plan to own a home or be prepared to pay $5,000 to move out. STAY AWAY

The Central was an easy choice for me. Between the management and the apartments as well as everything else it is exactly what I was looking for with places to eat near by and public transit across the road. When I walk in the lobby after work I am greeted by name, welcoming me home.

Thank you to the Central apartment for such a great living experience. I really enjoy the atmosphere and location of the central apartment. Everything I need is within walking distance and there is a great public transportation system in the neighborhood. 
The staff here at the Central are amazing they have always went above and beyond if I needed anything. Kevin is great a great maintenance man. He fixes what needs to be done very quick and is very informative. He also is good about being respectful of your home and belongings when he does come by to fix stuff. Justin And Aliesha work in The leasing office. I love having them in the building. They work very hard at what they do, but are always so welcoming and caring about how your living experience is going along with being very kind, professional, and personable. The apartment festivities they plan are also very fun to attend. I love living here at the Central and I have been a resident for 8 months now and I look forward to staying even longer. If you want a great living experience I recommend staying at the Central! :)

I am very pleased and fortunate to be able to stay in the central . It is in a great location lots of restaurants nearby and groceries stores ,15 minutes away from downtown ,walking distance to cap Hill and also Lake Washington. The lounge and roof top are absolutely stunning with 24/7 acess. The staff here are amazing. They make sure you're taken care of. They love answering any questions you may have .

I was extremely excited to move into this apartment complex in a central location but immediately found it to be overpriced with poor amenities and poorly designed/built apartments. 

The freshly-renovated unit had a broken laundry machine. It took 2 months for a replacement to arrive with no updates from management. After I complained, the then-Assistant Manager finally told me the building’s owner is cheap and wants multiple bids to pick the least expensive option. Other amenities (rooftop furniture and gym equipment/HVAC) remain broken/unusable for long periods of time. Gym HVAC stopped working during heatwave, and management did not notify residents or provide alternatives for cooling and safety/

Security issues are huge issue management doesn't address. My unit was broken into and robbed. On top of this, I personally incurred cleaning fees due to the burglary. While the building did move to me another unit, management made me pay a higher rent. This new unit also had severely outdated fixtures and appliances, making it grossly overpriced then and now.

Ongoing issues include
-	The “gym” is poorly equipped and always reeks of body odor.
-	Package room not secure and in garage. Even with gate, people break in. A tenant could get hurt encountering a thief. Current management was unresponsive to my complaint in writing.
-	Units on the very top floors are only accessible by garage elevators, which is unsettling because of car break-ins. Rear elevators are often vandalized.
-	Poor window insulation everywhere, Aurora-facing apartments are especially noisy.

The maintenance team, current manager and assistant manager have been reasonable and nice to chat with. That said, this doesn’t make up for the multitude of issues I encountered. I’m very excited and relieved that I finally managed to move out of this building.

I am compelled to express my profound dissatisfaction with the management and overall state of the apartment complex, which has significantly impacted my living experience here. One of the most pressing issues is the condition of the trash rooms. They are consistently neglected, overflowing, and unkempt, which not only detracts from the cleanliness of the complex but also poses health concerns.

Additionally, there is a serious safety concern due to the frequent presence of homeless individuals in and around the building. This situation has made many residents, including myself, feel unsafe and uncomfortable. The lack of effective security measures and management's apparent indifference to addressing this issue is alarming.

What is most frustrating, however, is the apparent lack of accountability from the office staff. Reports and complaints seem to go unheeded, with little to no action taken to rectify ongoing issues. Requests for assistance or intervention are often met with apathy, leaving residents feeling ignored and undervalued.

This experience has been deeply disappointing, and I urge potential renters to consider these serious issues when making their housing decisions. Management's failure to maintain basic standards of cleanliness and security, combined with their overall unresponsiveness, makes living here untenable.
Toured recently and loved the spacious floor plans that were offered. I hope to come back later to look at the two bedrooms since they were not ready to view yet.

Dexter is a great place to live. While the building is older than most on the block, in my opinion older buildings are built to last. The new team has been working hard to make this a better home for us and we appreciate it.
The new office staff are very helpful! We have great views of the lake and absolutely love the area.

This is the worst place to live, leasing office staff are lazy and don't do a single thing, office is supposed to be open 7 days a week but is always closed on the weekends with no one there, that is ridiculous
The building is beautiful and modern, and the management is the best I've ever had in my long life.

The Janus staff is the best, they seem to care for their tenants and are very quick to respond to your issues if any. The building is quite modern-looking and well-maintained. The common amenities are great too.
Excellent management team.. The apartment complex is super clean and well maintained.. Super attentive and caring Manager which helps immensely creating a warm and accepting community.

Amazing place to live! Everlyn and Kevin are very helpful and genuine in their interaction. They are always available whenever needed. The maintenance and upkeep of the property are top-notch. Communication between staff and residents is handled very well whenever there is something going on on the property. Highly recommend living here long-term, you would not find a lot of place that will value your quality of living and care for your needs.
The management and on-site staff at Janus make living there a true pleasure.
Feels like coming home! Comfortable living in the heart of a such a vibrant neighborhood, the best of both worlds.

Everlyn is legit the best property manager Ive ever had the pleasure of working with and Janus really does feel like a community. Everyone here is nice and courteous and the complex is always clean and I feel safe.
Beautifully maintained. Friendly, efficient staff.

Janus has been the first apartment where it felt like coming home. I love my unit, I've got a garden going on my balcony, and the location can't be beat. Everything is perfect for me and my pets to have a great life here.
Amazing place to live in. Thanks Everlyn and Kevin for taking care of your residents.
Janus has become my home. I enjoy the convenience, the safety, the excellent maintenance and overall friendly atmosphere
Awesome apartment with a convenient location, friendly property manager, and great facilities!

Everlyn was fantastic in making the move from out of state a lot less stressful. I feel secure living in Janus and love the building and spacious apartment. I highly recommend living here. Especially if having good property management is most important to you.

Janus is a great community with amazing management/staff, thank you Everlyn and Kevin! Weve lived here for 3 years and we feel very taken care of here. While we are looking forward to purchasing a home of our own, well always remember the apartment we lived in as newlyweds and new parents!
I love living at Janus! It is located in a walkable/residential area. The staff are wonderful. The building is quiet and there is a nice sense of community here.
Janus has been extremely comfortable and a wonderful place to live. The grounds and building maintenance is exceptional.
Janus has been my home for 3  years, throughout that time the experience has been consistently amazing. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a spot to call home in Seattle.

WARNING!!!!!! DO NOT MOVE HERE!!!!
This is the most accurate review I can write for a place because I just moved out a month ago. If you want to live in a place with hallways that smell of garbage everyday (because a specific tenant brings in FULL GARBAGE CANS and RANDOM FURNITURE that smells of garbage that they collect and leave in front of their front door), lost packages, ignored complaints that REMAINED UNRESOLVED, disruptive and mentally unstable tenants on every floor, domestic abuse fights, police coming in and out like its domino's pizza, terrible washer/ dryer machines that charge $5 in total to wash and dry ONE LOAD (while they are also broken half the time), and just an overall FALSE REPRESENTATION on their own website; If ALL of that seems professional, and well managed then go right ahead.

Absolutely ridiculous. I don't even write reviews, and I generally prefer to handle things professionally and in person, but this place is AWFUL. They go through so many different apartment managers because THEY THEMSELVES CANNOT MANAGE THIS PLACE. I lowkey felt sorry for a few of them I met through my one year there, but it makes no sense how terrible this place is. I have been far beyond patient with them but I can't let them mess over other people and their money. 

Also be warned that THEY WILL KEEP YOUR DEPOSIT after you leave, even after you cleaned it more thoroughly than when THEY RENTED IT TO YOU. When I got there they still had the previous owners things in the kitchen drawers and cabinets. They will also not even give you a letter listing what they are charging you for from your deposit.

I paid my rent on time every month, made complaints rather than handling things myself, did everything they wanted and still I dealt with all these issues; while there were plenty of tenants not paying any rent, destroying their property, AND GETTING ON EVERYONE'S NERVES.

Bottom line is DO NOT MOVE HERE. Because once you do, and you try to break your lease, they will charge you 2 months rent to terminate. 
Unprofessional.

Have switch management a few time but these have to be the worst. Trash piles up every week in and outside the dumpster/area. Terrible housing the maintenance doesn't let you know before they are coming to your door, took months to get anything looked at or fixed. The washer was unbalanced so the lid locked and told us it was 450 to get a replacement lock. The drain on the roof is messed up and flooding the bottom floors. And today they replaced the washer without us asking or paying the 450. Then towed too cars from our paid parking with no notice or anything. I think it's because I called them out on above. They towed my car at noon and told residents it was towed yesterday. Also they only have a limited parking and a small lot, if you park on the street side you are capable to get your catalytic converter stolen.

On the surface this complex looks nice, but it's a stressful place to live. Within the first few weeks we noticed cockroaches, which we've had to get sprayed multiple times and they're still here. We saw multiple reviews online about cockroaches, but figured the issue would be resolved by the time we moved in... We were wrong. The roaches are strong here.

Management is super unorganized and unwilling to help unless it affects them. I've been having the same issue for a month and a half without resolution; it doesn't matter how many times I reach out. It's like once you sign the lease you suddenly don't exist. The issue involves me being threatened by another tenant.

We've also got extra charges on our bill that we have been given no explanation for, and we pay everything on time through the proper channels.

Avoid this place if you can. I wish I could go back in time.

So far I have loved my stay at Bogtown. The facility is gorgeous and the managers are extremely amicable. Also, the rent pricing is extremely reasonable. Greenwood is actually a great place to live (there are plenty of bars and restaurants within walking distance) and there is a park literally one block from the apartment!
Management is unresponsive to concerns. Neighbors are very loud and you can hear parties every night. It's kinda miserable and not worth it in my opinion.

There is no AC and it gets up to 90 degrees even with the use of portable fans. You can install an AC unit but it will come out of pocket for hundreds of dollars. The Wifi goes out like once every hour. The walls are paper thin and you will hear every neighbor, including the frats that surround this area. They party every night from so the noise is high and it's hard to sleep. Also, there is no elevator which makes this place very inaccessible - stairs only. The laundry units smell like urine. It's also only two washers for a five level building! Additionally, they advertise this as a UW only building, but any college student can rent here. I have also seen children and elderly people in the building. I would recommend living elsewhere if you want peace, convenience, and comfort.

The apartment is surrounded by 4 fraternities which host parties every night on a daily basis. The thin walls mean that you have no choice but to 'attend.' The amenities listed in the website are greatly exaggerated: there is no lounge area or outdoor space. Delivery services won't deliver your packages to you because the entry is confusing. The management sends passive aggressive emails encouraging tenants to spy on each other.

Communication is absolutely horrible. Rent is expensive and the walls are thin. What really got to me was communication with management. Absolutely TERRIBLE. They will offer you verbally or through email one thing, and then reject it the next day and raise the price or not honor what they originally offered. Very dishonest and hard to communicate with. Save yourself the hassle and stress and find somewhere else.
The leasing company was responsive and fair. Can't beat the location (although it is very loud being right across the street from a frat house) and the apartments are new and clean.

This apartment is great for students of the University of Washington. It is only half a block away from campus and not far away from stores. Almost everything is walking distance, but I would recommend getting a bike since it is very cheap to store here. The wifi included is good for everything. I have been here for a few weeks now and it is a very cozy place to be. This building is also practically brand new so everything looks excellent and works perfectly.

Don’t get me wrong the space and storage options are great…but that’s about it. Maintenance is practically a joke, tbh I’m not even sure if some of them really know what they’re doing. We’ve had a a leek in our bathroom ceiling for months now and every time they come and fix it they just patch over it. On top of that we’re still missing drawers in our kitchen, and the main front doors lock is always broken. Do yourself a favor and don’t move here, the fact that they’re upping rent without trying to fix a large number of maintenance issues is a joke.

Lived here for two years. This place is not how it seems in the photos. Things you should know:
1) The apartment in the photos is a model unit that has been renovated. They have only renovated a few units, so you will most likely not get a unit that looks like that. Units are in poor condition. I've spent countless hours of maintenance on my own unit just to make it livable. 
2) The front lobby looks very nice -- the rest of the building is dingy, smelly, poorly lit, and falling apart. 
3) The advertised amenities are very poor and often unavailable or unusable. Pool was only open for 3 weeks last summer.

Bed bugs, broken glass in the hallways, doors smashed open or otherwise broken into. Management has switched hands multiple times with no improvement. Lots of cute dogs live here which I found to be the only positive. Happy to be leaving!

My husband and I have lived here for nearly two years and that first year was great. Around the 1-year mark, the building was sold and was put under new management. Our rent went up and the quality of the front office staff went way down. 
The apartment itself is actually very comfortable and the only complaint I have is that I can hear everything that neighbors do and say - be aware if you work nights or dislike loud pop music - especially since our new neighbors moved in down below. 
The communication between the front office and the tenants is my biggest gripe - lots of reminders for socials and community events, but rushed communications or none for things like office closures or maintenance updates, like when I was waiting for an update on the backed-up water in my bathtub.
Needless to say, we're riding the lease out, but looking for a better-managed apartment complex.

My fiancee and I were looking for an apartment building that could do two things: 1. Provide us with a comfortable and safe space to live, and 2. Be inexpensive enough that we could start saving for our future together.  With The Galleria, we were able to check both items off of our list.  The Galleria is located conveniently near my favorite shopping center, and has easy access to bus lines going all over Seattle.  The building has a huge courtyard with a clean pool, well kept lawn, and several barbecues; the perfect combination for a weekend get-together with friends!  There is also a great workout center that my fiancee has been really excited about, and that I will hopefully start making use of soon lol...
Overall, we could not have asked for anything better in our first home together.  It's clean, well-priced, and has a friendly atmosphere that makes us feel really comfortable.  I would highly recommend this apartment to everyone, but especially to young couples like us whose priority is saving money.  The Galleria has the best bang for your buck out of any apartment I've seen in the area, and we've truly had nothing but great experiences here.

This is the worst place to live in Seattle! They tell you it is secure, that's a lie. In the first two months my storage was broken into and no one told me! The emergency lights didn't work most of the time. The front door was broken into twice! The building caught on fire this past April. They didn't offer any concessions until 3 months later. And the final straw, in Oct my storage unit was broken into again, after they promised to replace the doors, and no one informed me. Save your money and live somewhere else.

I went for a self guided tour and the elevator was broken so I climbed 6 flights of stairs only to find out that there was no lockbox on the unit I was supposed to tour. I called the leasing company and kept getting redirected to voicemail. The hallway floors were torn up and there were about 10 construction workers there. I went up to the rooftop to check out the "balcony" and it was full of trash bags and discarded construction materials. I emailed the company and days later and still, no response. What a completely rude and unprofessional thing to do. I literally traveled from 45 minutes away to look at these apartments.

I lived here for about 3 years, and in the beginning management was wonderful. During my stay, management changed and wow did things go downhill. I moved out in November 2019, and at the rate things improved around this place I imagine nothing has changed. BEWARE BEWARE BEWARE. Oh my gosh I cannot express this enough. Literally anywhere else in west Seattle will be better for you if you’re looking for a new home. Stay far far away for this garbage fire. Management is awful, the building is not maintained in any sort of way. Is there maintenance? Other than the scary ted bundys y’all hire/ fire every so often? The rooftop is a literal safety hazard (before the construction obvi). The ceilings / walls are PAPER THIN and you can hear the resident sneeze above you. They NEVER answer the phone, so good luck getting help with anything. Oh, and expect a large move out fee as well.     

Since all the reviews below reflected the wonderful management prior, I just thought I would give an update! Thanks for reading.

Craving the West Seattle life, are you? Well, The Residence at 3295 may be the place for you! The building is directly next to a bus stop that is 2 stops away from downtown, so that is one thing this place has going for it. Being so close to downtown make the rooftop deck even better because you get an amazing view from up there! Another thing that makes this place so great is the people, I have been here for about a year and everyone I have interacted with during that time has been super nice, including both the workers and the neighbors. Considering quality of these apartments and the prices of other nearby places, The Residence at 3295 is pretty fairly priced. I have lived in 3 different apartments here in West Seattle since I packed my bags and left my east coast life behind and The Residence at 3295 is my favorite and I think it will be yours as well!

I would not recommend living here. Garbage trucks pick up in the ally next to the building... all night long. You will never sleep. The building management is bad at management. Don't be fooled by the building security either because the upper doors can be opened with a hard pull. Caught quite a few people sleeping in the hallways.

I am not a resident here, but once applied for a unit at this property. I have wasted $40 application fee with it, and want to warn other applicant about their application process.

I found the property online, and saw they have an available unit. I contacted their leasing agent Gerry. Gerry confirmed me with availiability, move-in date, price, and sent me several photos of the unit. I'm good with the unit and submitted application after that. Three days later when I asked Gerry again about the application, he told the unit has been rented to another applicant. Being asked by Gerry to consider other properties managed by their company, but I refused with his options as I feel their business practice lacks transparency about what is going on.
Car thefts, cars broken into, no security cameras to watch cars on premises, package thefts.

Bed bug bites started not long after sleeping in the apartment. [Never had bed bugs before, didn't recognize the bites.] Two zero-result pest inspections and two months later, I have to catch the bugs myself before the office would do anything. I will never forget when I told the manager Kriste how difficult it’s been working from home knowing I had something in my space biting me and she said, “Well, at least you can work from home right now. A lot of residents can’t right now.” 
The chosen fumigation process is that the pest company (Paratex) takes everything possibly affected to a special gas room. So when you get it back, you have to wash it all. Shared laundry in the basements and no dishwasher. Got the full treatment and caught a bug 5 days later. A half treatment, fogging without taking stuff out, was done and the bugs returned 17 days later. Second full treatment resulted with new bites a month later. Beginning of July the manager offers to do a full treatment and return all of my belongings to a different unit in a different building. At this point I have five months left on my lease. I’m denied the possibility of breaking my lease early without penalty. 
I asked management for expense reimbursement for all the laundry, medication/doctor’s visits, hotel stays (for when the pest company had all my stuff) I’d incurred throughout this 6 month experience. After providing a detailed list of expenses totaling $800, I was offered a $200 rent credit. I was told I did not have to stay at a hotel since I could’ve returned to the apartment after so many hours of gassing-- All my bedding and furniture was gone, so their expectation for my welfare seemed low. 
In my time at this complex, the dumpster shared with Bldg 4 has had 4 mattresses put out. Apparently the apartment below mine also had bed bugs. While the bed bugs did not come back to me after I moved buildings, new tenants were still being moved into Bldg 4. 
____tldr; 
Had bed bugs for 6 horrible months. Had to move buildings. Left as soon as I could (5 months later). 
Location wise- It’s in a great spot if not for the West Seattle Bridge closure. Being on a hill lends to some nice views. Parking is hit or miss- it’s free, which is nice, but fills up in the afternoon. Mail to the office- make sure you know when a package is coming because the office notifications were at the leisure of the staff. 
Maintenance is excellent.
Big takeaway: Possible bed bugs for long duration. *Would not recommend.*

First of all, LOCATION. 1.5 miles from water taxi, 1 mile from The Junction, and 2.8 miles from Alli Beach. Management is awesome (I've dealt solely with Mary so far and she ROCKS), maintenance is friendly, and one can sign a lease from 2,000 miles away. The building is clearly old but they just installed new everything, so they look nice inside, and the price is FANTASTIC for the area. I dont think ithe description says recycling is included, but it is included everywhere here, and there's a fitness room. There's also a great view of the skyline from Avalon.

Take your business elsewhere. You will get trapped in a bad contract as the management company neglects the residence. The balcony doors have been broken for many residence. The management is aware of the situation and will let your electricity bill soar and provide no mitigation for cost or the actual problem. The price is not worth all the inconvenience

ANTS. ANTS IN THIS APARTMENT. I’ll tell you that there were multiple ants trap I had to set up. The management is not working to fix ant  problem.The management never answer to issues unless they get contact by their corporate. 

I moved in to this place and moved out during covid. The manager cares about getting new people to apartment but not responsive to people living in the units, at all.

Phone booth didn’t work or never got a chance to set it up while I lived. The package room breaks every other month or so. The UPS, FedEx don’t have access to package room or to the door so they cant deliver package. 

Every Friday, there’s lot of parties going on including smoking even though they advertise the place to be a non-smoking facility. 

The maintenance, I requested on the first week of moving in, it was never responded. I lived with kitchen light not working, bathroom fan running randomly, broken window blinds. 

The contract paper had multiple errors and issues, had to re-write and re-request multiple times. On Moving day, manager didn’t pick up the phone call 10 times. I had to ask someone else to open door for me and knock on a unit they used as office. The manager said they never received phone calls. Well, their phone system not be able to take phone call took over month to fix.

Management lies, doesn’t respond at all and if you are lucky, it will take weeks to weeks for a response if you call the head corporate to notify the management. 

I broke the lease to move out from this horrible apartment. I paid to break the lease to get out of this nightmare. Please read reviews, these are actually helpful.

Pros: 
great location, beautiful new building with above-average construction. 

Cons: 
-no security - building keys were stolen(management notified tenants via email and decided to remove all locks from every door while they waited 6 hours for all the locks to be re-keyed, basically removing ANY security we had for that window of time). I've have multiple packages stolen while waiting for the "secure" smart mailroom to be setup (still isn't setup) and the secure parking has had 4 break-ins in the past 9 months (my car included). 
-elevator breaks on a regular basis, i've personally been stuck in it. 
-management never answers the phone or responds to emails and when they do it is defensive and rude. 

it's not worth it.

I have rented for years all around the greater Seattle area.  I have never ever had this much trouble with where I have lived.  Michele the manager is very nice.  The building it self is beautiful.  The elevator is broken 80 to 90% of the time.  It takes days to weeks to get them to fix it.  It is three large flights to each floor so if you on the fifth floor and park in the garage that's 18 flights of stairs!  It is a huge inconvenience and they will not get it fixed promptly which is ridiculous.  Why will they not get a reputable repair service and get it fixed within a day or so? Because they do not care!! But no its out for days and weeks!! And the mail.  NO ONE seems to know that actual address of the building and the US Postal Service does not recognize the address is it 2100 E Madison or 2112 E Denny Way??  No one in management will follow up and try to resolve the issue and now its week 5 with nooo mail? I have done everything on my end and yet they don't care and will do nothing.  If you go to rent here they will just tell you lies about it and say it will be resolved but, it won't be resolved I promise you.  If you care about your life and well being I would seriously consider not renting here.  I never would have if I had known.  Also they rarely if ever respond to phone messages, texts or emails.  Its the worst customer service I have ever received.

As a first time renter, I've found this apartment to be just what I need for my current lifestyle. They are a pet friendly apartment, however, they do have breed restrictions. Maintenance is okay, however, the plumbing has issues and the outside noise is incredibly distracting. Great neighborhood, but it's a bit too close to the Capital Hill night life for me.

Before moving to Cambridge park villa I checked out a ton of other places in the area and from what I had seen before moving in Cambridge is the best. And that opinion stays even after I moved in!  For me it was the amenities like the gym and the indoor pool,  Maintenance knows what they’re doing and that is hard to find at apartments nowadays,  Catherine and Maggie in the office are awesome and quick to help if anything comes up ! Staying here is great and I wouldn’t want to live anywhere else.

Maintenance requests are communicated effectively when they're needed, the office staff is always available for concerns and info, but best of all the pricing here is cheaper than most other apartments closely around Seattle. Highly recommend. Good price, apartments, and location.

I didnt think this apartment complex was bad. the price is good for what you get.

Pros: close to I5, 20 minutes away from seattle, parking spot provided, pet friendly, nice people, nice maintenance crew, take care of their landscaping, "gated". no thefts, car break-ins, or worry about them

Cons: THE MAILMAN IS TERRIBLE. i cant say how many time the usps guy loses the mail, but the people are so nice in the complex we always got it back even when it was delivered elsewhere. i heard gunshots nearby so its not the best area, the gate is there but doesnt close until night so almost anyone can come in. buzzer on doors dont work.
NO VISITOR PARKING. garbage piles and smells often outside

overall had a good experience but i just wish i was closer to public transportation so i dont have to pay for parking at my work.

Major waste of time.  The office staff here lie about the application criteria and the criteria are not fully disclosed before you apply.  The application criteria are not what they describe on the website nor what they describe to you in person either. Do not get hooked in and run the risk of losing your 35 dollar application fee and 300 dollars holding deposit. They will also keep all of your personal information. I have asked several times for my file back and why they are keeping my personal information but they do not reply. 

The premises are disgusting and unkempt. The garbage area is overflowing with garbage. The one-bedroom she showed me smelled of garbage and backed-up sewage. The hallway smelled of garbage and the carpet was old and dirty.  All of the appliances, countertops, and carpets in units she showed me were old and worn out.

Ensure the property management follows their end of the lease agreement.

My security deposit was returned late, and a fee of $150 was wrongfully deducted from it. When initially inquiring via email about the arrival of my deposit, the manager told me it was being processed and I would not be receiving the full amount back. I asked why but she didn't respond. A week later, I receive my deposit and a "Basic Maid Service" charge of $150 was deducted. I contacted the manager who claims that it is a standard procedure/fee for professional cleaning upon move-out--however this seems to have been arbitrarily tacked on to my move-out fees because:
1) NO WHERE in the lease agreement is it stated that this so-called "standard" fee will be charged to the tenant upon move-out (it simply says that the carpets must be professionally cleaned to avoid a fee and the rest of the apartment be cleaned and returned in the condition in which it was received).
2) What could the professional cleaning service possibly clean after I had thoroughly cleaned it?  I have two witnesses and photo/video documentation of the apartment's condition when I moved out. The manager again defended that it has to be prepped for the next tenant. Well, again--where in the agreement does it say you will tack on this fee without my knowledge if it truly is a "standard" fee.

I would have accepted the fee if they told me the apartment needed to be professionally cleaned, otherwise I wouldn't have wasted any time or money to even bother leaving the apartment as spotless as it could be. What is even more ludicrous, is even after the manager acknowledged the fee wasn't stated in the agreement, that it is simply too late to do anything about it because the cleaners already went in to the unit.

 I have filed several complaints with several department agencies, because it is too exhausting trying to claim a small amount in court. This isn't right and they know it but they also expect you won't bother to try and fight it because of the process it takes to claim $150 back. I have had no issues with the unit itself or maintenance or even the front office staff--all exceptional, but management did me wrong at the very end.

I have been a tenant at Cambridge since it opened in 2013. I rarely have had to have any type of interaction with the management staff, however, just recently I have been in constant contact due to a change in my household. The management staff (Maggie and Leah) were super helpful in helping me navigate this change and providing options that could work for me. Ultimately, I am pleased with the response time of the staff here and have enjoyed living at Cambridge for the past 5 years, I appreciate the professionalism and overall kindness the staff show here.

There has been increased gun violence and loitering in the neighborhood. Seems to be a gun related incident in the neighborhood at least once a month.
Property manager is very rude and unprofessional. I honestly believe she is racist, as she offers decent service to my white neighbors but not myself or an elderly Asian man or a young black woman that resides here.

Monica and Ed are lovely.  Great building and secure garage with full size appliances including washer/dryer. The building allows smoking on the balconies which is a major downside for me and a lot of people. My upstairs neighbor smokes A LOT and I'm really starting to notice it affecting my health even though I have only lived here for two weeks. It's hot out right now and my balcony is my only window that can be opened. My throat and chest are irritated from it.
building is really nice since its brand new. Management has been reallygood so far, very responsive.  Very close to bus station and the bus goes straight to downtown seattle so commuting is easy.

Very nice apartments. New construction with high end finishes.  Price is a bit on the high side but for the excellent property management staff and the new modern apartments it makes it worth it. 

Pet friendly and one of the few I found that all for gas grills on the patio.
