The building is new and the apartments are nicely setup.  I like the location since I am able to easily access either Highway 99 or I-5 from there.
False advertisement, this property does not have a community bbq, or fitness center, I wish there was or I would have renewed my lease. Trash is always overflowing.

Landlord is accommodating and responsive. Pet friendly. Only 1 washer/dryer, but I rarely had to wait. The kitchens have a decent amount of cabinet space and there is a surprising amount of closet space as well given the size of the apts. It's a good deal for the location, and there are a few parking spots in a lot behind the building. If there isn't a spot open, it's never difficult to find nearby street parking. There's a nice courtyard and the property is well-maintained.

Great deal for what you're getting.  
Perfect location, lots of free street parking, cute shared outdoor area.  Only downside is there is only one washer/dryer in the building but there is hardly ever a problem getting to use it.  Great neighbors.  

Landlord is pleasant and responsive.

I was not informed, I must perfectly clean the room before I leave it, so they charged me 450$ for taking out 2 bags of trash and a few more things. It may be says in contract, but I did not read it, They could advise me to clean it perfectly.
I did not break a blind, but they sent me a picture of it on the bed.  Also, you can meet homeless people in the building.

Absolutely love the location It offers so much to the people like me and my partner who love the city and find nothing more fitting of our dreams then being somewhere together in a place like this. I’d like to thank Benisha so much for everything I truly appreciate how caring and understanding she is and helpful she was during the whole process. Im so happy she was able to give two young adults who are starting there lives, the kindest they needed to experience to know that there are great people in the world who want to help any way they can.

Benisha is always helpful and responds quickly if there is an issue, and the location is perfect if you work in Seattle. Great view from the roof. Street parking is surprisingly not a problem, and there is a streetcar station right outside that can take you downtown or to Capitol Hill. Cozy units for a price that’s hard to beat.

Living here August to November for the 3rd time, my wife's work brings us here every year for a few months. Never had any issues, units are small but the pricing is the best you will find around. Benisha the community manager is always helpful and made move in effortless. On site laundry and proximity to everything make this place a great value. Great rooftop views and grill!

Terrible. Just stayed there for a period of about 2 months from start of June till end July. Paid a security deposit of $500. No parking spaces and just got a security deposit refund of $179.99 after cleaning the room. No amenities as promised. The top rooms were hot during the summer. Planning to pursue this case further. Avoid at all cost. There're better apartments around.

We've been living here for more than 3 years and not very happy with the previous property manager. They were nice; they just did everything slowly. Then Benisha came, and she took care of everything that was supposed to be done years ago in days (mail key copy, replaced a new fridge and a new microwave, paper printings,...) She's the best!

I've been living at Malmo for about 3 months now and I really don't have any complaints. Move-in was smooth, my only complaint is that getting things into the elevator is kind of a hassle. You either go into the garage (which blocks half of the entrance to the garage, go through two doors to get to the elevator or climb a set of stairs to access the G2 level elevator. The staff is amazing, they are always ready to attack any concern a resident may have. The amenities are pretty cool, the building has grills on the roof top, a community room on the top floor, a decent gym with basic work-out machines, and a courtyard on the 2nd floor. They also have a coffee maker in the lobby, not sure if it's for residents- but it's there! The residents that occupy the building are pretty quiet, there's the occasional thud, but people are living above you... The apartment is in a good location for walking; bus stops at the top of the street and there are various grocery stores that are 3-15 minutes walking. I  definatly would recommend Malmo to a friend.(:
I gave Malmo 4 stars because some amenities were not available at move-in.

These apartments are a bit on the small side but pack a punch for design--polished concrete floors, high ceiling and modern finishes give it a nice urban, industrial feel. Our neighbors are nice, lots of greenery on apartment property. In fact, it's landscaped with lavender and blueberries. The neighborhood a bit sketchy, and they are getting more strict here with amenity rules, but overall the staff and neighboors are friendly, little noise between apartments and an overall affordable place to live very near to Seattle. Would recommend.

I've been living here for about 1 month now and I must say that I'm truly pleased. The staff is very responsive to any queries or requests that I've presented so far. Considering the location, the view from my apartment on the 5th floor is amazing. There are more windows in my apartment than I had in the house that I moved out of; and that house is about 50% larger than the 2 bedroom apartment that i share with my girlfriend. There's an adequate fitness room with about 3 or 4 treadmills; a rooftop patio with 2 gas grills and a fire pit; a decent sized community room for hosting parties; as well as a few other amenities. It's very close to the E-Line, which is a straight shot to downtown Seattle, making my commute to work very manageable. There's also plenty of retail shops within walking distance.

0 stars. Shoot, if I could it would be a negative 5. Ever since management changed over, they have been very incompetent and unorganized. I am being blamed and charged for their mistakes and lack of detail. This place has gone down since the new manager took over the place. I highly recommend you staying away unless you like being nickle and dimed with bogus fees and threats. They do not care about their tenants at all. There is a reason they have so many empty units. Nothing but complaints I have heard from other tenants just waiting for their lease to be up so they can leave. The person in charge needs to be demoted or fired before they completely ruin what once was a decent place to live more than they already have. I urge you to stay away at all costs.

My apartment is conveniently located near several bus stops,and walking distance to a mall. When you are hunting for a apartment, check to see what the tenants think about the management, and make sure that all the amenities that you want are available there like a swimming pool, fitness center, and parking garage. Also, ask if you are required to have your own renter' insurance, and if dogs and cats are allowed there?

My experience at Nova has been a mixed bag; overall, management is alright. They are friendly and get to maintenance requests in a timely manner. The tenants more or less keep to themselves. 

Onto the issues:

The garage has been repeatedly broken into the last several months. Several tenants had their cars broken into (including mine) and personal items stolen. There is street parking in the area but is limited to 2 hours max. You either have to pay for garage parking or constantly move your car to avoid getting ticketed on the street. 

It is LOUD. Newer apartments aren’t known for their soundproofing but combined with the apartment’s location, you will hear a lot of street noise, especially on the west side of the building. Nearby is a lumber yard, a YMCA, and every week Swedish Healthcare parks a trailer on the street with the generator running the entire time. Due to the area’s zoning all of this is permissible, even during quiet hours. 

For the most part I don’t hear my neighbors but one has taken up loud yelling and turning up the volume on their speakers during quiet hours. 

If it matters to you, there are not very many amenities offered, like a gym, but it keeps the rent lower than comparable buildings in the area. 

Overall, Nova is a mixed bag. I want to like it because of its location (close to lots of grocery stores, parks, etc.) and the rent is decent. However, security issues and at times inconsiderate neighbors are the biggest drawbacks. I would look elsewhere if I were you.

As I'm writing this review, building management finds it acceptable to install a new carpet in the apartment above me at 8 pm. When my washing machine broke it took 2 months to get a working replacement

The noise is so bad that you can hear every footstep when the person above walks and you can even hear when they flush their toilet. The room that holds the recycling has not been cleaned in years

This building gets really hot in the summer, you need a portable AC to survive

Any option has to be better than renting from Nova

Ive tried reaching out multiple times through phone and email and no one returns my calls. ive left voicemails and sent emails asking about availability but have yet had anyone communicate back with me about a simple tour of any apartments. The website doesnt list rent prices, it instructs you to call to inquire about the rent...did that, but no one seems to work there. Ridiculous. 

Not a good sign. if customer service is this poor for interested tenants, i cant even imagine how they treat the current residents. ill look elsewhere.

Packages were being stolen frequently. Maintenance does a terrible job at repairing and a long time before they come in and fix it. You can hear everything through the walls and floors all the time. I can hear foot steps from above and my neighbor flushing the toilet or using any type of plumbing. The trash and recycling bin is always over flowing.

Since being turned over to the new property management company, this place sucks.

Nickle and dime for every last thing. Pet rent is $100?? That's up by about $60 a month. 

Package delivery has gone away, no notifications of packages, and they sit out in the lobby for any and all. I've had three packages go missing in 2 months. I get everything delivered to work now. 

The ice machine on the roof was removed, the plants are dry and dying, cigarette butts litter the ground outside and finding anyone in the front office to ask a question is hit or miss. 

Go elsewhere and don't pay for a building that has literally one amenity. Or do. They'll probably take that away too.

Pro's are the building is clean, safe, and quiet. The finishes are modern and sleek which makes the small 1 bedroom seem more spacious. Storage space is limited, the bathroom is large and a linen closet instead of all the space would nice. Most of the appliances work well, the washing machine sometimes is fussy and you have to 'give it a break' to start it.  The building is located adjacent to a lumber yard and food truck company, which if you are facing that side both businesses are very very loud at early morning hours. Although there is a Trader Joe's, LA fitness and convenient bus stops to downtown Seattle, there is not much else in terms of coffee shops, restaurants, stores in walking distance and it does not have neighborhood feel. Overall a nice building, but for the cost I have seen comparable buildings in better locations.
I used live in unit 7 in this building, and always love to see the ocean when I wake up. Nice view and property management
Small quiet apartment Community, Friendly onsite management. Clean and well kept grounds, Close to transit, shopping,  Very well maintained units.

The management staff is super friendly and always checking in with the residents to ensure our time at Citizen is going well. I know that if I need anything or have any questions, I can call or email the front office and they'll help me right away. This plus the fantastic location makes Citizen a great place to live!

Citizen Apartments is in an incredible location—everything you could possibly want is within a few minutes walk, from Trader Joes & QFC, to bars & breweries, restaurants, shops, and green spaces. 

Despite being so central, there's never any issue with noise, safety, or loitering. 

The staff is super friendly and helpful, they've been great at answering my questions and helping me get settled in when I first moved in.

Staff is friendly, genuine, and truly care about residents. Work orders are taken care of quickly. The location is great as it is within walking distance to almost anything you would want to do for fun.

Lived at this apartment for almost a year and had a good experience.  All the people working there are awesome, Savannah and Rick really went above and beyond.  The apartments are on the smaller size but you won’t be disappointed cause there is plenty to do around the area.

Management is incompetent to the point of negligence.  Fire alarms go off for no reason.  Packages end up missing or trapped in the office for obscure reasons w/ no notifications.  Basic maintenance is neglected e.g. wd-40 applied front door so it doesn't make a horrific metal screeching sound every time it is opened.  Cleanliness of grounds has diminished w/ removal of trash cans in key areas.  i.e. trash regularly in elevators that are sticky w/ spilled liquids.  It isn't very secure property as folks from outside can just follow people in.

The staff is rude and disrespectful i.e. almost as though I work for them instead of the other way around.  Past management was much much better

This building is directly in the heart of Capitol Hill Seattle. Less than a block to the Elysian brewery, and directly next to Pike and Pine streets which are the center of social life. For those working at Microsoft, it is only a few blocks from the nearby connector stops for an easy commute and security deposit is waived. Being located on Madison St, it is a bit noisy being located very close to the hospital, the fire department and the police station, but very secure. The underground parking is also a nice touch along with large storage units available.

I've been a resident here for a little over a year. When we first moved in, it was a solid 5/5 star property. The former property manager, Piia, and the maintenance crew, were wonderful and this felt like a cared for and safe community. 

We received a new property manager and new maintenance crew around 3 months ago and, while there is something to be said for a transition period, at this point it is clear that the quality at City Watch has steadily deteriorated. There have been a lot of changes and issues including the elimination of package delivery, building doors being unlocked/accessible to non-residents during late nights, non-residents sleeping in the lobby, garage break ins, elevators breaking down and being inaccessible for days (currently on day 5 with no elevator in one of the towers), lack of communication from management and the garage to be inaccessible for at least 3 days in January (the only reason I know this is because a resident shared this info). 

Of course, things happen. Elevators break down, break ins happen, packages can't always be delivered, etc. But what is disappointing has been the steady degradation of the services and amenities previously offered by CW, and the building and area no longer feels safe and secure. I would encourage those seriously considering CW to look at other apartments in the area as well, as most units in the area are similarly priced with more safety, security, and amenities. We had truly felt like we had found the best priced and best cared for property in West Seattle, and it is so sad that we are now having to consider leaving when our lease is up. While the complex is pretty centrally located and decently priced, it no longer feels as though residents are being placed first.

This place is the real deal! Piia was a delight to work with and is a true asset to these apartments. Always quick to respond, transparent and easy to communicate with. Not to mention the sweetest most genuine person! The apartment itself was clean and spacious with lots of natural sunlight. The location can't be beat, it's 3 blocks from heart of the Alaskan Junction! Less than 5 minutes to restaurants, bars, shopping, the gym, 3 (soon to be 4) grocery stores... it doesn't get any better. I will recommend these apartments to anybody and everybody, I loved living here!

I’ve lived here for three years and the situation has only gotten worse when it comes to building security.  Homeless people regularly congregate in the garage, and you will not be able to have anything delivered here.  I have had thousands of dollars of packages stolen, and now have to resort to sending all my packages to a PO Box.  When I’ve contacted them asking if they’re going to do anything, I get a standard “sorry you had a bad time!” Form response, with no change.  Do not rent here, it is not safe.

Units aren't so bad. Weirdly crappy washer/driers for a "luxury" apartment. Short walk to the train station. Packages are impossible to get, and you can forget getting takeout. Getting a delivery person in through the labyrinth of doors, gates and locks is Herculean.
Fire alarms are constant. Minimum once a month, frequently twice. Always in the middle of the night, generally between 2-4am. You and your pets will develop an anxiety disorder. Do not recommend.

There are so many issues with this place. Staff is miserable to work with, had problems since before moving in and every instance since. The most recent issues was when we put in a maintenance request today for a leak. We requested they came in the afternoon since I was busy with something and asked for them to contact us beforehand. Imagine my surprise when I hear a knock at the door while staring into a webcam in front of other people; apparently they had decided to just ignore the requests we'd made, they acknowledged they'd seen them, but had chosen to ignore them. Obviously having people randomly show up to go in and out of your apartment if you work from home is a huge issue. Got no notice that they were going to show up whenever they felt like either. Spent the rest of the day frustrated and irritated. Place is a complete joke.

This place has been a complete nightmare from the start. Our tour was interrupted by a current resident who tracked down the leasing staff to complain about a problem. Wish I had paid more attention to this red flag and not moved here. The staff our completely inaccessible. The leasing office's windows are now blacked out and their our signs everywhere stating the office is closed to current residence. We have had an issue for a while now and there is no one to contact. No one seems to work at this property anymore.

The apartments are atleast 10-15% more expensive than similar apartments in the area. Which begs the question, what does Patent 523 bring to the table that these other apartments don't? And the answer would be - nothing at all. There is no air conditioning so you're left to suffer incredibly hot temperatures in the apartment during summer. There is no cross ventilation, most of the apartments looks like a shipyard container, closed on all sides except we can crack open windows. No patio or balcony. They attempt to redeem themselves with roof top, but lets be honest, there are apartments with better view than that, in Seattle and they don't have the problems which clearly this apartment has

Patent 523 apartment complex is a very well kept environment that you would look for in Capitol Hill. Once you decide to live here, things will not go wrong. I lived here for almost 2 years. Stachio must be complimented for his dedication and efficiency.

The Velo building and units themselves are nice. The cleaning crew did a great job keeping the lobby and main areas clean despite residents of the building not knowing how to use a garbage chute. Maintenance requests are answered very quickly. 
Why I'm giving them 1 star is because the move-in and move-out process is absolutely terrible. I was initially interested in a very specific unit, made an appointment to see the unit, and on the day of was told that unit wasn't available and my appointment was made in error. I had to take time off work to go to that appointment. I contacted them by email and let them know I was interested in that unit only and to let me know if the application fell through. A week later I don't hear anything and I see the same unit listed again on their website. This time I just applied and paid the deposit to secure the unit. Red flag. Once I move in they forget to add me to their Amazon locker system and or notify me about said system. Received zero orientation on the building. 
When my lease was up I emailed to ask if they would consider lowering the monthly rent since the second bedroom was marked incorrectly and had no windows. They told me no, that it was already below market value. However, unit ended up going for $100 below what I was paying.
Lastly, the move-out process was terrible. They scheduled a pre-move out walk thru on the day I had movers! I tried to schedule a formal move-out but they ignored me and posted a 2-day notice on my door anyway. The maintenance person that did the pre-move-out inspection told me I would be charged for cleaning regardless of how clean I left it and then tried very hard to look for issues to charge me for. The bathroom wall had some light scuffing and he told me the whole wall would need to be repainted. When I asked why the whole wall and not just a touch up he very rudely pointed at the light scuff marks in a sarcastic way and proceeded to tell me that's how their paint was, that they can't touch up they have to paint the whole wall. 
Moving out, I received zero deposit and a bill. The itemized receipt not only contained information for my unit but for another unit as well. They seem to be pretty careless with confidential information. I was charged over $300 for paint and almost $200 for carpet cleaning. However, receipt also showed the carpet was replaced for regular wear and tear. Ultimately, I had to contact them and fight the charges and they returned my deposit.

I moved in about a week ago so I will update this review as time goes on. But this is an excellent place to live. The management team is very helpful and supportive and made the move-in process easy. They allow self-guided tours of any available units. This property is fairly new and really well-maintained and clean. Package lockers, lounges, fitness center (latter two closed right now due to COVID), and an incredible rooftop patio with grills, lounge chairs, and gas fire pits with a stunning view of Seattle, Lake Union, Queen Anne, Aurora Bridge. Gated parking garage but I have to start off with a compact spot next to a pole, so parking takes a lot of precision unless you have a small car (which I do not). Very nice unit with large windows (though only a little bit of the window opens), fresh paint job, nice Whirlpool appliances and tons of cabinets, washer and dryer, large closet. And the location is PERFECT! Walk to Gas Works Park or into Fremont, or across the bridge and climb up Queen Anne Hill. Bike along Burke Gilman Trail to U-District (and beyond) or Ballard and Golden Gardens. Short walk to Fremont Brewery. Delicious BBQ joint literally next door and plenty of food options in all directions. Easy to get to freeways or into downtown or up to Green Lake area.

Velo has really gone downhill since the management changed from Greystar to a company called Essex. 

Previously, we would have community events and services, the front office would store packages when the Amazon hub was full, and the leasing staff would answer emails from residents. The building was also much cleaner and better-maintained.

Now, our mailroom is overflowing with packages because the leasing offices refuses to store any. This has led to an increase in stolen mail. The leasing staff has not answered a single email or phone call of mine, and there have been no community events. The building is dirty, the management did a horrible wax job in the front lobby, there are often washing machine units just sitting in the front lobby for days on end. It's horrible.

I'm moving from DC to Seattle, and looking at apartments remotely was rough. In addition to the great pictures online, the leasing agent, Marco, gave us a tour of the apartment using facetime. The lease signing was all online with digital signatures, so there was no printing and scanning necessary. Once we signed, Marco texted us pictures of the apartment so we can plan our move around the layout.
Happy with 2900 I love living in 2900 apartments.. Ryan and Mahdi are very supportive and also they keep on improving our gym and the property .

This apartment has horrible service. everything has gone downhill after there was a change in management. The elevator has been down for months and any complaints made to the building Mgt is met with indifference. The hallways stink and everything has just become terrible. it took them several months to set up their systems which made it difficult for us to pay rent and put in service requests. The new management is unwilling to be flexible and they are very slow to respond. they are quick to collect money from you  but in all other things they are slow and indifferent and this makes the living conditions in the apartment vey unbearable. do your self a favor and rent somewhere else. definitely leaving as soon as my lease is up.

I don't know how this management deserve 4+ star since they basically just get you sign up and forget about you the moment you do.
We moved in about a month ago and at the time we expressed concern about potential noise, and make it really obvious that it's something important to us. Whoever was handling us made it  sound promising that should there be a noise complain, the management will work on it immediately. On the first day we move in, there has been consistently noise from kids above us stomping the floor 7 am in the morning. We all understand there can be noisy at time in downtown area, but 7AM EVERYDAY??? REALLY??  We tried contacted the management, and it's been A MONTH WITH NO REPLY AT ALL! so for whoever that's looking, this apartment has zero sound prove and management shows zero care.
Update: they are trying to make people pay 300+ more in rent moving to another similar unit when they have no fault in the situation, not allowing you the find someone to take over your lease, or charge you 6k to break a lease, you pick the option! :)

I cannot recommend living in this apartment building at this time due to my experience with the ending of the lease. I got married and needed to end my lease early so I could move in with my wife. I was given two options: move out and continue to pay my rent until they found someone to take over my apartment. Or pay two months' rent as a termination fee. I chose the former as I was told that it would be easy to have someone move in quickly. 

I was then told, after signing off on moving out on the conditions listed, that the option I agreed to was not going to be available. Communicating with the office was by no means easy, with weeks going by without any response from the management team. The Aimco Customer Care After Move-Out Team was not responsive either. 

This is a $3000 dollar difference. If you have the sort of money where $3000 doesn't matter, this might be the building for you. I'll post an update if anything changes.
No comments provided.
No comments provided.

The building is not to big, therefore it feels like living in a boutique concept place. 
Neighbors are very friendly and polite. We all know each other and  gather frequently.
For single people, this is the right place where to live. 
Location is exceptional, wonderful and friendly management.
Apartments facing the street are the best ones.

Recently moved in and IN LOVE with our new home. The management team worked overtime to help us get moved in quickly and most of our worries were non-issues thanks to their help. The level of customer service is as good as it gets. The building is in the perfect location to experience this very special neighborhood in Seattle. Our room is well thought out, space was maximized to feel bigger than it it, hugeeee bathroom, lots or room to cook... I could go on and on. Again, everything has exceded my expectations. On top of all that, the building is filled with incredibly nice neighbors. Everyone is welcoming and talks to one another. They even throw parties and play sports together! There is so much more I could say but I feel like I've already written an essay. If you are looking to be a part of a vibrant community and you enjoy being social with your neighbors, I highly suggest you check out 4730 California.

P.s. the rooftop view will knock your socks off

This is truly the best apartment I've lived in. Our unit has plenty of space and is light and airy. The location is great off, we walk almost everywhere which is saying a lot, we moved from California where we rely on our cars, but we got rid of them when we moved and we don't miss them. The staff is really great too, they make a big effort to bring everyone together, which we really appreciate since we didn't know anyone when we first moved. After living there a few months, we have a lot of friends and I don't know if that would have happened anywhere else. Needless to say, I would recommend it to anyone that asked.

This apartment complex is wonderful, the leasing staff is incredible and attentive. The gym is small but new. The apartment is modern, has a lot of light, and has incredible views. The location is great, in the junction around everything.Parking is hassle, but it seems to be like that everywhere in west Seattle. The best part about the apartment complex is the view from the rooftop deck, it gives you a view of Mount Rainier, the Puget sound and downtown Seattle, as well as all of West Seattle.
This building is so beautiful and the Manager is very nice. Its great to have a garage in a vintage building. Lobby nice and there is always candy!

Avoid at ALL COST! 
I will post more when I have more time, but I want to warn you that this is a horrible complex. Dirty, overflowing trash, theft, unresponsive management. Storage unit robbed! Car damaged in the parking lot! Unable to access garage repeatedly, office consistently closes early, always short staffed.
Stratus is a wonderful community and the staff here are excellent.  I would totally recommend Stratus!
The apartments are very nice and love the location

Living at Stratus has been a wonderful experience! The management and leasing staff are incredibly responsive and always go the extra mile to ensure residents are taken care of. The concierge team is friendly and helpful, making everyday tasks easier. I highly recommend Stratus for anyone looking for a comfortable and welcoming place to live!
I put in a request from maintenance and it was done the next day.  Stratus is a wonderful place to call home!

This is my second year leasing with Stratus and I personally have no complaints so far. The apartment layout I chose is perfect for me and I’m yet to see one that comes this close in other buildings previously viewed. Communication with management is always transparent and easy, the concierge are always warm and helpful and make you feel at home, maintenance when I have needed it has been stress free and timely. It is super convenient by way of location as well.
Maintenance here is fantastic. Quick, professional and communicative. Best I’ve had in a building!

I made an appointment to tour Prism about a week before I was going to be in the area to see it. When I first called the leasing office no one picked up, but someone from the property called me back in 10-15 minutes to schedule a tour. The day of my tour I attempt to call their office multiple times and get no response so I take the risk and head the apartment anyway. I end up using the call box multiple times and get no response. I waited around for an HOUR before giving up. If management cannot even abide by a scheduled tour or bother to pick up then this is not a place I want to live

I drove all the way from Kent to tour this property an when I got there the office was closed. I did call many times but nobody answer. It was Friday Feb 4 at 2:30. I come back at 4 and still nobody there. Why is office open online but not when I get there

I am super disappointed with my experience here. The building is nice but my bike got stolen with a lock in the bike room on 12/13/2021 and I didn't get any notification about the break-in. The manager Shelby handled this situation poorly. She didn't let the resident know the bikes were gone and the footage was erased when I found my bike is gone.

Noise problem with upstairs neighbor because of the thin wall and floor.
FYI do not want any help from management. They would not do anything for you.

Office mgmt is so sweet, lots of natural light, beautiful appliances, brand new apartments, Amazon hub lockers...only gripe is that there is no fitness room! There is a huge space that has a bunch of bike racks, seems that they could have put some fitness equipment there.
It's very clean, easy access to public transportation, staff is awesome!
It's location is perfect various forms of transportation, there's no carpeting! (Yay!), the neighborhood is nice!
It's a great location, clean building, friendly staff, the layouts of all the floor plans are all great!
We have already recommended Prism to one of our friends that is going to be looking for an apartment in December!
Would definitely recommend because of natural light around the house and transportation is easy to get around.
Office staff is responsive, kind and professional. The building is new and quiet in an up and coming area.
Loud upstairs neighbors, and limited parking for guests otherwise have loved everything.
I would because the overall quality vs cost and the "newness" are really there for me.
Great location and the units are beautiful. Management is awesome.
aside from the repeated issues with the elevators and lack of a fitness room, this is a good place to live.
