DO NOT MOVE HERE!!! It is so unsafe!! In December 2022 the place got shot up almost all the glass windows were shot out in the lobby. Luckily this happened in the middle of the night and no one was hurt. There is a lot of criminal activity on this block with cops sitting on the street all day because of it. There is a parking garage but we have lived here over a year and we still can’t park in it because of a “waitlist”. You email and call and they never respond. We have to park our car on the street and there is over 10 tents behind the building. One time there was a homeless man throwing giant rocks at cars parked behind the building. Our car gets broken into almost daily. It takes months to get approved to even get in the place. Even when you do get approved the amenities that they show are all broken. The movie theater room doesn’t have a remote, the pool table is missing balls. Homeless people get in and smoke fentanyl in the stairways. The one good security guard is leaving because he was almost shot at on duty. Mail gets stolen. Also there is gunshots heard at least once a week in the middle of the night. It is a cheap low income housing but is it worth your safety??
The view and location. Walk to Lake. I grew up here and went to the Jr. And high school near by.

Just for some context I didn’t tour this building before moving in and this was one of the few apartments in Seattle that was in my budget and not the size of a shoebox. Review: I really liked the 1 bedroom + balcony, it was plenty of space for me. Heads up, the washer/dryer is not in unit, instead, there are shared laundry rooms (one washer and one dryer) on each floor. The maintenance guy, Memsud, is the nicest person! The only person from leasing I communicated with was Mercy and she’s also very nice and responsive. However, I moved out as soon as my 6 month lease was done. It seemed like there was a healthy number of college-aged residents. I’ve lived in the University District and I lived on Roosevelt Way & 65th while the light rail station was being constructed and all of that still does not compare to how loud some units were regularly. Ultimately, I could not stand the combination of the walls being too thin / loud neighbors, living on a busy street, and not being able to conveniently walk to restaurants or stores. If you are interested in moving to this building look for units on the upper floors (Floor 4-5), corner units, and avoid units facing east if you don’t want to be above Lake City Way. Happy Apartment Hunting!

The manager is barely responsive. The walls are so thin I can hear my neighbors on both side having intercourse almost daily and you will hear every car passing on LCW day or night. The property itself is meh in a very undesirable part of Maple Leaf (views of a strip club, anyone?). Its a lot of young couples and college students living here which makes for a bad time all around. Cannot wait for my lease to be up ($1800 to break is insane for such a trashy property). AVOID.

Sketchy area, poor communication with management, unresolved issues with apartment.  Other friends who have lived in other ICON Real Estate properties have said similar things and I didn't listen but here we are. 

If you know what you're getting into and you're okay with it, you're probably fine, but good luck if there are issues requiring upper management.

The apartment it self is great! The living room is very spacious but I think some of that space could've been allocated for the bedrooms. There is also a Thai restaurant underneath the building and the scent from it tends to go into the building. The landlord is nice but I unfortunately found several little issues with the apartment upon move in

Title says it all. 1AM, 4AM, 6AM - constant stream of garbage trucks every night emptying tens of metal bins. Good luck getting any sleep living here. 

Plus there is no AC so have fun with your apartment being 90+ degrees during the summer

This is my first year living in Seattle so I didn't really know where to look location wise, but Ive been living here for 6 months already and I love it. For my boyfriend and I, its decently priced for how small it is and now I see they've raised the price a lot from what we are paying now so I would say its too expensive for the size however I LOVE the location - the heart of SLU. The staff is very helpful - we always go to Paul when we need something and he is always a big help - The noise is minimal here and people keep to themselves. A huge downside is we have had a view facing the city, but theres a pretty decent sized building being constructed now so we don't have a view at all anymore. The gym is tiny but it does its job - we use it probably 5 times a week. All in all I love this tiny little apartment, probably would look elsewhere when my lease is up for the price raised a bit much and the view of the city is completely gone but we really loved it, it welcomed us very well to the city.
Very dirty and unsafe apartment please be very careful and do not sign a lease here. You will regret it!
The heating never worked, the staff won’t respond to your messages, blood in the floor, cold water in winter days. Just inhumane. Worst experience ever.

The location is pretty nice, but overall wouldn’t recommend at all. I’ve been living here for almost two years and package’s keep getting stolen, and have seen people sleep in the hallways. Weird smell too.

Common areas are not regularly vacuumed and smell like strong carpet cleaners. The carpets in the hallways are badly in need of replacement. My rent was raised twice in a year! There is only one electrical outlet in the living room. Summer heat is unbearable inside the small units and they charge $80/mo for “common” utilities plus your individual unit’s utilities!

Once James left the building as management. MANAGEMENT WENT DOWNHILL.

Garage everywhere , roaches everywhere, Non residents coming in and out with drugs

Do NOT live here. Day 1 the office manager was not here on my move in day and I had to call emergency maintenance to make me a key. She has since left and now there is nobody in the office. Trash literally piles up in the garage because the dumpster has been out on the street for weeks. The hallways are dirty with dog poop on the carpet and carts full of trash in the hallways. There are ants all over my apartment and packages are stolen every day since there is nobody in the office. Seriously the worst.

In addition to disrespectful neighbors and the building being super dirty (and smelly), the management is absolutely awful. The manager changes about every 6 months. Nothing is secure here. Packages get stolen and cars get broken into despite the building being advertised as “secure”. Can’t wait to move out of this place.

This is a well maintained apartment building with convenient location with beaches, parks, and transit nearby. The management is wonderful and attentive to residents needs and concerns. I have lived here for almost two years and am very happy with my choice.

I have been living here for the past 2 years and the staff has been always helpful. 
Teresa takes care of resident’s needs and listens attentively to feedback. 
I have no major complaints about the place. I’d totally recommend staying here.
I’ve never thought of staying in one place for a long time, until I stayed here and been renewing my stay with no second thoughts.

DO NOT LIVE HERE. I did and I regret it. Please read everything. 0 stars if possible. It is good on first appearance but once you move in is when the issues happen. The staff is rarely available, work requests are not responded to timely, even if they are serious. I had ants crawling in all corners of my apartment and submitted multiple requests for pest control to come but it never happened. I even woke up with them crawling on me at times. I also had issues of broken appliances and a hole in my ceiling caused by a leak that was left there for weeks. I was overcharged for bills and the property never helped me. I attempted to reach the portfolio manager from the management company multiple times and never got a call back. I lived there for 3 months when I had to hire an attorney to fight the landlord to get out of my lease and get my deposit back. This building should not be in business.
Apartment building right off broadway in Capitol Hill, clean hardwood floors, great apartment rooftop.

This is a perfect building if you want to be around many places like parks, Safeway, bus lines, the airport, and much more. The staff there are incredibly helpful. The manager Kelly is one cool chick. She's helpful if you stuck on paying for rent and if you need help with other problems. Don't take my words, you just have to see for yourself.

I have been here for 10 years and i Like living here. it is very chill and not very much activity. the manager is wonderful i love her. the property is so nice and they are upgrading the units right now and the beautiful.

This is a perfect place for a single person and for anyone with family. It's a quiet place to be. Plus it's around bus lines, the airport, Safeway, and more. The common areas and pool are well maintained and clean. The staffs are helpful and friendly. Unlike other apartments, Kelly the manager is really a cool chick. She helps out when you stuck on rent or having problems with roommates, and other problems. This place has a pool, gym, nice and safe playground for kids to play in. When you walk outside everyone is friendly. The apartments are nice sizes, but don't take my words..... Just go and check it out for yourself.

Currently living at the Larkspur apartment on Summit Rd and it has been an awful experience.
1. Management is difficult to get a hold of when I have an issue, more info below.
2. I reported a clogged shower 3 days ago and have yet to receive so much as an update. Last issue I reported (no hot water in the shower) it took management 3+ weeks to send someone out.
3. There was a break-in at the apartment building because there was no security on site, and there was no auto-closing doors/gates. It took management 5+ weeks to install additional gates and they are still constantly left open. After reporting the open gates to management they, didn't acknowledge the complaint.
4. Parking garages are often blocked by trash, or parked cars so I cannot access my carport, and again management has done nothing to address or even acknowledge the issue.
5. There is no AC and the heat is controlled by the building (you cannot control your own heat), this has lead to days where the apartment is freezing, and other days where the windows are all open because it is so hot in the apartment (in November).
6. All of the building garbage is stored in a hallway you need to walk by every day to access the parking. Since it is not in a bin, it piles up so high that you need to step over garbage to pass the hallway.
7. If you do not run your shower for a few days, the water comes out dark brown (not yellow, dark brown). Management said that this is normal, but I have never seen this happen before, after running the water for 5 minutes it clears up but who knows what's in the water.
8. While signing the lease in August we were promised that constriction would be completed by September, in November there are still days where I wake up to loud construction noise of contractors working on improving the building.
9. The elevator has an issue where sometime the door doesn't open all way, or the door won't close properly

I lived here for more than one lease and the only reason I moved is because I bought a house. Kinda sad because this was not only one of the most affordable apartments I've found, but the quality wasn't what you would expect from being so cheap.  I found out that it is a family owned complex, which is why they aren't out to get you on pricing and charges. Not only rent but wsg and parking is cheap ($30-$50 range/ea).
Clean apartment, attentive staff, security on site, cameras all over the place to help feel secure. For all of these things at the cost they charge, easy 10/10. Nothing's perfect but even when I had a small leak needing repaired from before I moved in, it was handled quickly. Unless you want the most modern and new appliances and counter tops, there's not much to complain about.
Couldn't ask for more

Pros:
-Attentive and involved management team
-Responsive maintenance team
-Well landscaped and maintained grounds
-Private patios for all the units
-Spacious apartments with lots of storage (THREE big closets in the living room area!)
-Year-round indoor heated pool, hot tub, and sauna! (Hot tub has only been out-of-service once in my year living here, and they fixed it in no time.)
-On-site laundromat only accessible by other residents (You can also buy your own machines or rent machines from management for an extra $60/month, but if you don't have kids, it's cheaper to just use the laundromat)
-Closed-circuit security cameras in parking areas, building-entrances, pool house, and laundromat. Makes me feel very safe from theft or vandalism.

Cons:
-Freeway noise/view from the units facing east. (Though they do have triple-paned glass to reduce noise)
-The gym equipment is minimal 
-Pool house is locked to residents from 10pm-9am (Doesn't really make sense to me since you need a resident key to get in at all times, and there are security cameras throughout the pool house.)
-Older building (Not the prettiest stairwells, hallways, and parking garage, but at least they aren't stinky, moldy, or dirty.)

Do not waste your time and money here. No matter what condition you leave the apartment in they are going to take 90% and say you “damaged it”. Unless you wanna fight them in court there’s nothing you can do. The manager of the building is rude and can be creepy to the tenants. The building needs a lot of work and is not up to code for sure. Absolutely wish I didn’t live here at all. But you can avoid it! Don’t waste your money.

Staying for 3 years now and truly enjoy the quiet ambiance and open courtyard. 

Also like the clean and well maintained building with good management.  

Keyless entry is a plus, no worry of loosing key. Entry gate added security to the building.
Staff is very helpful and friendly. Nice apprtment.

The people that work on leasing office really they don't like people. I don't know why they see them selves from another planet. I'm sorry that the owners put this disrepectfull persons work their place. I will never recommend your appartment

It’s cheap for a reason. Move in and find out for yourself, management is probably the worst. Zero privacy from management who work and live on site making my daughter feel unsafe in her own home acting as if they live here. Elevator constantly broken, pools closed constantly. Amazon packages always getting scheduled for redelivery because of building issues, let alone packages getting stolen from hallways from neighbors, management did nothing. We didn’t last a year in this apartment before moving out due to all the hassle.

Brentwood square apartments is by far one of the best communities we lived in past 8 years.
They have strict non-smoking policies which we appreciated alot.
Their rent is not too high as compared to average rated apartments nearby.
The apartment size is pretty good and parking isn't too expensive either.
A kudos to their staff members, who are always there. Be it fixing something in the apartment or cleaning. 
Thanks Brentwood for these good 2 years, definitely recommend living here

Currently living here and have been for a while. Very reasonable price for what you get. Good location—pretty quiet and a relatively safe area. No amenities here (just apartments and a small parking garage), but the apartments are spacious and comfortable. Units are very well maintained and the building as a whole is kept up very well. Shout out to Carl the maintenance guy. Getting in and out of the parking garage can be a nail-biter! Within walking distance of Fred Meyer, restaurants and bus lines.

Lived there for 11 months... management was fine until moveout. 

We had great management for the first 5 months. Then beloved C. went to a different job. Didn't have a manager for quite some time, finally got a new manager D. D is nice to your face, and will fight to keep all the deposit. 

I have never had a deposit withheld from me before until this apartment. We were given a checklist to clean, and we spent days filling the checklist (it was over-the-top; clean each individual blind slat, which we did).  We rented a professional carpet cleaner & shampoo from Home Depot.

When it comes to get our deposit back, the items on the checklist were simply declared "not up to our standard" and deducted. We are furious at them telling us to use a professional carpet cleaner, then charging us anyways! 

Live here if you don't want your deposit back. Location is good, fun things to do across the street.

Park 3025 is in a great location, and I enjoyed my 2 bedroom, 1&3/4 bath layout. The apartment manager Kathleen is friendly, informative, and helpful. I enjoyed my neighbors and it was nice to have convenient parking in the garage. Although some of the amenities were shut down to COVID, I highly recommend park 3025.

The location of this apartment can't be beat! It is nestled between major streets/highways, but off-street so hardly any road noise, parks and beaches are a quick drive, and the neighborhood is bright and walkable to nearby restaurants, coffee, sweets, banks, and groceries. The complex is always well kept with on-site and friendly maintenance (thanks Steve!). It is also has beautiful interior decorating so it feels more like a home. The common area when open is inviting and fun to have company over. The community is courteous including the pets. The best part of living here is Kathleen, the property manager. She is the warmest, most thoughtful, and thoroughly communicative property manager that exists. You will feel completely taken care of if you live here. I hope to be back one day!

I just spent a wonderful year at these apartments and am sad to go! The only reason I left is because I relocated to Oregon to be near my boyfriend but wish I could have picked up this complex and brought it with me. The apartment itself is beautifully upgraded and so spacious. It's truly a hidden gem in Seattle and great pricing. The maintenance worker, Kyle, became great friends with my pup and was always super friendly and attentive to any needs we had. The bottom floor of the complex has multiple TVs that residents can access 24/7 to watch whatever your heart desires. I never needed to buy cable and watched lots of Sounders games and weekly tv shows with no issues. The fireplace in front of one of the TVs is super cozy! :) The bottom floor also has a pool table and shuffleboard which is fun on a night in with friends or whomever. The gym is in great condition and was awesome to pop down to without even leaving the complex. The sense of community is great; friendly, quiet neighbors that aren't nosy or overbearing. My dog and I made lots of friends there. It's super close to the light rail to head downtown, Fred Meyer is walking distance as is a brewery, it's really easy to jump on I-5, easy to get to Greenlake, and I had a great nail place in walking distance too. Kathleen always made sure residents were aware of any entries to apartments a week in advance usually and I fully trusted them going into my apartment without me there. I had to have Kyle do so a few times and nothing went wrong. Last but not least, Kathleen, the office manager, truly holds this place together. She is the best person I've ever dealt with when living in apartments. She's so friendly and helpful and really cares about making this the best place to live. She hosted parties for residents and always had fresh coffee for me in the mornings, as I work from home. Anything I needed, she was readily available to assist and just a wonderful person to know! I'll miss her most of all! Thanks to Park 3025 for making my living experience in Seattle top notch!

I sold my home and chose Park 3025 for a comfortable retirement residence.  It is kept clean, the grounds are well kept and the interior is well decorated.  The management has responded well to all repair requests.  The neighbors have all been pleasant. The management and maintenance staff are friendly and care about their tenants. All units are being renovated after they are vacated.  Sure there is noise, which is expected, work begins at 9 AM and finishes fairly early in the evening.  For the most part it is quite here at Park 3025.  The contractors have always been courteous to my wife and me. We enjoy the workout room with it's ample equipment and especially the dog bath facility.  The secure underground parking and elevators are a great features.

The overly positive review on here was obviously written by apt management.

Do yourself a favor and keep looking.

Paper thin walls, overpriced and poorly designed units, guaranteed rent increases, passive aggressive notes from management, ridiculous decor rules, lazy and incompetent staff who will not respond to maintenance needs...this place is a headache.

So glad to be out.  They will not return your security deposit. They will enter your apt without permission. Not a good idea to rent here.

If you love being over charged for nonexistent amenities, loud construction and nosy neighbors, this is the place for you! 
I currently live here and it's the worst. The agents will tell you everything you want to hear in such a friendly way, until you sign your freedoms away in an over priced lease. I pay about $340 more then other apartments in the area and for what? A loud, rude and uncaring construction crew? Or maybe noisy, nosy and intrusive neighbors. No, it's definitely for the lack of parking, false aspirations of nonexistent amenities and unprofessional staff. 
"It's a good neighborhood." If you enjoy finding needles and drugs in the parking lot, crack heads wandering about the streets and gangs of people dancing chaotically in the roads. My apartment was (an attempt to be) broken into the first two weeks I was here.  
Now they want to charge for parking in the parking lot and the garage or you have to park on the street and have your car be keyed or broken into.
If you have any sense you'll find a better, less expensive, more professional place to live.
Sincerely,
A regretful resident.

Amenities and views were fine, could use an upgrade to get A/C in bedrooms since summers are getting hotter and the building gets a lot of sun. Make sure you do your move out tour in person, we ended up with a $500+ charge for stove top replacement (normal wear and tear).  Threatened to send us to collections. Paid it and moved on, want to make sure it doesn’t happen to someone else in the future so make sure you do the walkthrough in person.

I applied online and when I filed the application the leasing office stated that the $22 application fee was non refundable but didn't state that if I ended up changing my mind the security deposit of $300 would also be gone. Sure the contract says that but it is also in a very deceptive manner. Every other apartment I've applied for kept the base fee but did not keep the deposit. Avoid this place at all costs as it is very deceptive in their contract.
Quick! Only took two days for the washer to be fixed and maintenance guy was very friendly. Thanks for the speedy resolution to my issue!

We have lived in Shelton Eastlake for several years. The property is in a wonderful location, the units are well-designed and offer lots of natural light, and the views from the rooftop are gorgeous. If it weren't for repeated issues with management failing to address serious safety concerns, we would be very happy here.

Since moving in, we and other residents have voiced concerns regarding theft of packages, car break-ins, broken/malfunctioning security gates, and broken/malfunctioning garage doors. In addition, last winter, our building experienced a serious mold issue, and management offered us little support in addressing the underlying issue of moisture building up in the walls.

We have repeatedly dealt with secondhand smoke from neighbors, despite this being a nonsmoking building, and complaints have yielded little to no action. This often prevents us from using the balcony during the summer months, when residents smoke outside, and has now become an issue during the winter, as smoke is infiltrating our unit under the floor boards.

It's really a shame, because we love our apartment, but it is unlikely we'll renew this year.

When we first moved in we loved this place but it’s gone downhill. 
-“secure” parking garage has broken multiple times with cars either locked in or locked out for days at a time. An amenity I pay hundreds extra for a month. 
-incredibly loud parties in the game room multiple weekends in a row until past 1am shaking the entire apartment and no security around to help the situation, even though they say there’s 24/7 onsite security they are no where to be found 
-mail room is a disaster with packages piled high in the hallways, had packages stolen with no help from management, another amenity I pay extra for 
I would not recommend living here

This property is good in all kinds, but absolutely noisy and loud. I lived here for 4 months now and I regretted living here for 3 months. Staff is very helpful, the gate is locked, it has a package room, you can also sign up for the locker that keep your package safe, there's kayak rental/bike fix, and a gym that unfortunately not open yet. Those are all good aspects, however, if you are sensitive to noise or not a party/music person, this place is not for you. The wall is too thin, if you happen to have neighbors like mine who love streaming music, you would have to listen to that music as well, especially your heart with beat with the bass. The floor and ceiling is also too thin, if you happen to also have neighbors who live upstairs that are heavy walkers, you would have to have the same sleeping schedule with our neighbors. And if you live facing the driveway or facing the streets, there are constant urban noise that is not that hard to live with, but for this price, you can find someplace better. The staff will be happy to help you resolve those issues, I transferred unit once, but I guess I'm just unlucky with neighbors, so I'm thinking about moving out of the apartment if the noise still goes on. Again, this apartment is a ok place, if you are ok with noise, I would be recommend this place to you. But if you are not ok with noise, look for somewhere else.

I have lived here for over 20 years and never regretted a day. The management are friendly and keep both the grounds and apartments in excellent shape. The apartment itself lives large because of the view and the 6x25foot terrace. There is lots of storage and the living/dining/kitchen gives it that open feel. I love 1960 interiors because it is not just a box. There are some niches that make the floor plan interesting. I love the neighborhood as there are lots of trees and though you are less than a mile from downtown you feel hidden in your own world with the lake as your front yard. The laundry and gym are convenient and well kept and the covered parking is a plus. If you are looking for more than an apartment, you are looking for a home I suggest you see this property!

While the manager is helpful, the staff don't appear to listen to the manager's request to not smoke nearby. Multiple tenants complain about several staff member's ciagrette smoke wafting in to their units. If you dislike cigarette smoke, look elsewhere.
Simple building in a convenient location. Grocery store is across the street. Leasing process was short, sweet, and to the point. Application fee is lowest that I've ever seen, only $14!

Greed at it's best! Required $600 holding "deposit" is non-refundable after 48 hours of application. Fair?? Property manager makes no mention of that in any exchange or in person. Gotta read the fine print. THANKS! No way the cost of some emails and the time to show a unit is worth that, nor the short time of opportunity cost.

The leasing staff is incredibly helpful and do the best they can with the information they have available. The overall building is mismanaged and does not take safety as a priority. This is not a property to live in during quarantine and please walk the grounds at night before singing your lease!

Be very certain you want this place when you apply. Unlike the many places we applied to in the seattle area. The fountain court will not give your deposit back if it has been longer than 24h from the moment you put your application in.

They pressure you to apply same day.  We found larger accommodations for the same money not near a firestation.

These are very nice apartments in the heart of Belltown in Seattle. Nice neighborhood with great restaurants, bakeries and coffee shops all within a few blocks. Anywhere in Downtown Seattle is walkable from this location. The amenities are also really nice and the staff is responsive and helpful. Good sized studio apartments with sizable closets and bathroom. Only downside is a very small kitchen with limited space for pots and pans. 4/5 stars due to kitchen size, but overall very satisfied with this apartment.
To find a property at this price is unheard of in Seattle. The area is Seattle but its a locked building so that helps. Being cleaned weekly and smells good.
Homeless utilize and break washrooms, sleep in stair cases, use water faucets in backside parking lot.  Mold Issues, Lighting and Electrical Issues.  Would not recommend even if on a budget.
Constant break in’s, loud neighbors, unresponsive management. Bad neighborhood.
Noisy and disruptive to neighbors. Very loud on weekends and not respective to neighbors who work early mornings on weekends

Make sure you tour the apartment and thoroughly inspect it first before signing anything. Place is smaller than what they post about. Mold problem all the time since the bathroom doesn’t have proper ventilation. There will be leaks from the outside when it rains even though all windows are closed. Management will try to “fix it” and come into the apartment for MULTIPLE DAYS ON END and not finish the job. Crackheads yelling in the middle of the night, needles surrounding the complex. So many wrong things with this place I could possibly write a book about all of them. Trust me, you can do better than here.

They will enter your apartment multiple times per year to do inspections and will have no concern about your schedule at all. They are rude and lie. Packages get stolen constantly. The neighborhood is dangerous. The apartments are infested with roaches and management will do nothing about it. This place should be condemned.

Monticello is great! Small apartments with functional layouts and a great on-site team! Trevor, Chris, Eddye, Kevin, and Sue (when she was still there before her promotion), are so willing to ensure you have what you need to make your stay enjoyable. Service requests are complete within 48 hours max, usually within 24, and when you can’t make it to the office to pick up a package before they close, you can ask them to put it inside of your apartment and they do! Great service!

This is our first apartment when we move to Seattle and we were so excited about this place for the first few months we were there I have no complain about our stay till the new management came in. It went down hill for the last 3 months we have left,they keep switching people. I don't mind the noise cause it wasn't that bad at all especially that its close to downtown and the nightlife. Everything is accessible here but was just surprise how they treated us. They increased our rent for another $200 for a 360sq ft home if we decided to stay for 1 more year and that's the first reason why we didn't wanna stay there. Not a safe place to leave stuff either cause our item was stolen inside our apartment not just us but our friend living at the 3rd floor lost two item that he owned which really sucks. I know that's what insurance are for but just knowing you are not safe leaving the house is terrible feeling. And a week after we left we receive a mail that we still owe them money and used all our security deposit. We didn't leave the apartment like a mess. The carpet was fine it just need to be vacuum and we got charge for HEAVY DEEP CLEANING. That just doesn't make sense for a small apartment. Overall we left the place feeling like we got robbed for something unreasonable.
Great location close to buss stops and down town. Affordable nicely sized 1 bedrooms, quiet neighborhood, friendly and helpful management. Wonderful place to live.
Me my wife and 6 yr old currently stay in a 1 bedroom we share alot of bonding but theres no room to have to breathe

The building was new when I moved in, but eventually problems with inconsiderate neighbors started happening, like people partying up on the rooftop lounge until 4 am, which would wake me up in my top floor apartment.

It took quite a while for management to respond properly to the issue, and even after they did it still never really went away. Other problems were some extremely bad cooking smells from neighbors drifting into my unit from both the hallway and the sliding glass door to the balcony, which was my only ventilation. Some times this would happen late at night and wake me up as well.
I was willing to put up with this, but the last major problem that really upset me is that I've been charged a rather large cleaning fee upon vacating the unit. This is even though I left it perfectly clean, and went through great pains to keep everything like new while I lived there. I have never once in all of my rental history been charged a cleaning fee, as I am quite meticulous in my treatment and cleaning of the places that I've rented. Additionally, I also received a "final bill" from Minol, the company that handles their utilities. The bill amounted to more than double what a normal monthly bill would have been, even though the bills were already quite high, due to what I believe was the company Minol basically ripping off the tenants. I'm not sure why a company from Texas would be handling utility bills for residents in Washington State, but I guess that Spur gets some kind of benefit from the deal. This bill also came in well after my final statement that I paid the day after I moved out, so I have no idea what they are trying to charge me for.

Finally, I've tried to reach out to the property manager several times to discuss my security deposit, which they still haven't returned, but I'm basically being ghosted by them at this point. They never reached out to me, and they also never forwarded those last "bills" that I mentioned. These are now listed as "past due" and the only way I found out about them was by going to the old rent payment app to see if there was info about my security deposit. I never received a paper statement in the mail to my forwarding address. As I have decent credit, I'm now worried that the property manager's handling of the situation will hurt my credit score, which is the worst part of the whole situation at this point.

For the high rent they charge, I'd avoid Spur. There's definitely better options in that price range.

Very disagreeable experience with a lot of indiscreet questions at the beginning. In the end, the visit finished with a very distasteful disparagement comment. I haven't been treated like this in any of the apartments I have visited so far. BTW I think the amenities are poor compared to other properties located in the same area. In my opinion definitely not worth it!!

We lived at Aperture for a few months and the staff is beyond amazing.  Nick, Chelsea and Justin are phenomenal and accommodating.   Always willing to help and very responsive not to  mention friendly.  We had a great stay and would have loved to stay longer.  Rooftop is great, location is perfect and the staff is really the best we have encountered in our number of years renting.

The apartment is pretty expensive and pretty small. But the location is just a couple minute walk from the space needle and the rooftop is amazing. Really can't complain. You're paying for location here.
Good space for the price-- things break pretty easily, though. Flooding dishwasher upon moving in. Weird situation with the parking garage. But otherwise, I'm satisfied.
For the first time in my tenure of living in Seattle, I finally love where I live! Great layout, great location, great manager!
When looking for a new place these apartments were our first choice! Management was quick to respond and very kind. Apartments were clean and safe!

If you love listening to everything your neighbors and roommates watch, listen to, and do; having your walls vibrate when doors in the hallway close; having your water shut off for hours at a time with no notice; laundry facilities that work ok sometimes; occasional cockroach infestations so bad they crawl over you at night; and neighbors that steal laundry, stare you down, and have band practice in their apartments, then THIS IS THE PLACE FOR YOU!!  All at the affordable rent no one in their right mind would pay to live in a creaky floor board decaying army barracks-turned-minimal amenity apartment complex!! Believe me! if the pandemic hadn't taken my job, I would have moved a year ago! Look elsewhere, do yourself a favor.

I really enjoy living here. 

It feels like a tiny community. People will bring packages left outside in the rain inside the building. Regardless of whose package it is and sit it in the main lobby. 

It feels very secure. There are two secured doors which require a fob to open. I never worry about people tailgating in or things inside being stolen. 

They also have a free Concierge Package delivery program for residents. Basically, you will be notified of any packaged received under your name. The packages are also stored in a locked storage area. Which requires a Fob to access.

Also, the staff is very accessible. They complex Manager Josh works out in the main lobby. (Lobby wifi is nonexistent. So, do your research before you live your apartment) He is always there if resident need him. 
He is always good for a laugh and  available to address all questions/concerns a resident might have.

Thats it!

All the shared areas are always clean. The complex also provides cooking utensils, pots, pans and etc for use amongst the entire community.

I also really appreciate the emails they send via the resident portal. Ensuring that the resident are aware of everything in relation to the complex.

Also, the top floors have AC/Heat units. 
I might just make it through that Seattle 114 degree heat!

I lived here for some time, and found that the management is very responsive. If something in the apartment got broken, someone would address the service request very quickly. Rent payment via the portal was seamless. Also during move out, Charlotte helped me print labels/coordinate with the USPS, so having delivery come to the apartment to pick up boxes was a GAME CHANGER. If I were to live in Seattle again, there is no better building I would live in. Finally, the staff even helped me with a reference letter for my next building. I have never experienced such a nice, helpful staff. I have now moved, and definitely just miss my amazing apartment (with views of Elliott Bay and the Needle) and the staff. Can't find this in a lot of places in Seattle.

I have lived here since June, while I love the front office staff, the apartment company is awful and truly do not care for its residents. Since living here, we have not had all three elevators working at the same time. In fact for the last two plus weeks only one elevator has been operating for all 26 floors of the apartment. We have been told it will be at least another week until one of the other two will be potentially fixed. Additionally, the garage door has never worked, and apartment security has been very touch and go. There has been a car stolen in the parking garage, multiple bike stolen in the bike locker and drug use directly out the front entry. I would suggest looking outside holland residential properties for your apartment search.
Friendly and professional staff, clean and secure building with great views. Rooftop lounge was amazing. Shout out to Mike, Charlotte, and Gloria for the amazing experience.

This building has some of the best views in Seattle both from the apartments and from the rooftop. The staff are top notch here, especially Charlotte. They made move in easy and continue to be great with updating residents if there’s going to be noise in a specific area of the building. The gym here is small but one of the higher quality apartment gyms I’ve seen and it’s open 24 hrs. Location is great, right near all the restaurants and bars I like. I can’t recommend this place enough.
Trust me, I’m not the only one who says that it is not worth living here due to poor management

Life at Dimension Apartments in Belltown Seattle satisfies my desires of travel!  I feel like I'm on top of the world in this new apartment with the 11th floor balcony (1 of only 10 total balconies offered in the building). And, the rooftop views are absolutely stunning during the day times 10 at night!!!  I used to have an aversion to sunsets because they remind me of not affording to travel & enjoy romance since I'm so busy with my career but I've grown to love them and never want to leave here....I can't imagine what would ever take me away!  My two dogs are loving the balcony and roof also, just hanging out in the sun privately with no street noise to bother them!  Plenty of TV's & seating all throughout the apartment building keep things interested and fullfilling to help rebalance myself after a busy work day/week. I love Dimension Belltown!

The apartment has the basic necessity washer & dryer, but nothing as fancy Dishwasher or Garbage Disposal. I had a horrible experiencing the with the management. The accounting has been off multiple times. I'm still owed my security deposit and overpayment balance. I was told they will get it to me. It is going to over 6 months now.

I would recommend this location/apartment in a heartbeat. I have lived here a little over a year now and not only is the location amazing but management has also been great! It is within easy walking distance of major bus lines and downtown Ballard (nice not to have to worry about parking!). Any time I have had a question, management responds in a timely manner and helps me feel like I have options, which is hugely appreciated! The apartment itself is also nicely situated and while a small studio, it still felt spacious. I loved the full size refrigerator and convection oven/microwave!

The property manager and staffs seemed friendly at first; however, by the time you move out, they showed their real color. They don’t provide a clear move out  instructions, yes they’ll gave you some “papers”. But when you asked them questions about the “instructions” and move out process, you get different answers; eventually you’ll be charged for this or that kind of fees.
The laundry was so dirty, I even found lighters inside. Extremely unsafe elevators, always in the maintenance, sometimes it just stopped even when people were inside.
Also, this property is at a dangerous area. Crazy people  screamed, yelling, played music around the buildings in the middle of the night very often. Honestly , this is the worst rental experience ever. Wish I had never rent here, wasted of money.

I've been at the Cornelius for a year and have had a very positive experience so far; I plan to renew my lease for another year.

The staff is very courteous and makes an effort to know you by name. They constantly seek feedback and look for ways to improve the residential experience. For a great Belltown location, I find the rate very competitive. The mailing system could improve, which the team is working to address.

If you decide to live her make sure you read the lease thoroughly also make sure that you get everything in writing that the leasing agents and especially the property manager say. They are a company that will try to take every last sent from you. I had to cancel my lease early and pay 2 months rent. I asked since I turned my notice in 4 days late not to be charged for those extra 4 days since I would be moving out at the end of the month. I received a confirmation email from the regional manager that that would be ok. I even tried to confirm with the on-site site multiple times that I would not be charged the 4 extra days. I also got the answer” as long as it is ok with the regional”. I paid my 2 months cancellation fee and asked again that I don’t pay those 4 extra days and they said it was fine. They actually just decided to take it out of my security deposit and when I called the property manager stated that the email from the regional manager didn’t “specifically” answer my questions to not pay for the 4 days. Then I emailed the regional manager to ask her what was going on and she blocked my email. It’s not about the money at this point it’s about how they lie to you to get your money so be very careful and get everything in writing.

Also the 2 years that I lived there, there were 2 shootings and the hallway constantly smelled of urine. With all the other apartments in Seattle, for the price you can find better places to live

I’ve lived at the M for over two years now and couldn’t be happier. The apartment is so clean, the staff are amazing, and you can just feel the difference between here and a standard apartment down the road. 
I love how they always keep everything clean and well stocked. They always respond to any questions or concerns I’ve had, and I appreciate them helping me understand how promos and deals are with apartments since I originally signed for a higher rent than my roommate’s, and was a bit frustrated with it to be honest. But after talking to the office, they helped me as best they could given the circumstances since I signed my lease at a different time than my friends (always sign together!). 

One thing I’ve learned from this is that deals and promos for apartments change constantly , and you never know what will happen and have to be on your toes about such things because things change by the hour with renting in a very fast paced community.I love the fact that the M is next to Safeway and is one of the best run apartments I’ve ever lived in. I would fully recommend it!

If I could I would give the M 0 stars. Put on a great cover for the amount of issues I had. Still haven’t received my full security deposit. Greystar is also terrible, sent me to at least 15 different numbers of people who all said they couldn’t help me or that my problem didn’t lie in their department.
Excellent living experience! Like how the M integrates technologies into living.
Great amenities, lovely view, modern interior, the best apartment to stand in the udis area.
does not respond to security issues, does not take security nor safety of residents seriously
Most of the Staff is really nice and helpful. Every person who lives here is nice but some are not considerate of others

Been here since November 23, New manager and already I can tell Allynne is really making a difference and having a positive impact in our community with the newsletter, asking for our suggestions, key lock updates along with a high level of communication.  I didn’t have complaints before her, but I can still tell a difference in what she is bringing to the community.  I really appreciate that.  I feel safe and all staff are stellar in my opinion.

Weeks and weeks of countless false fire alarms being pulled by homeless people resulting in 6-8 minutes of piercing one note alarms. Urbana offered ear plugs. Mix that with elevator failures (elevator dropping and people getting stuck requiring fire department) AND stairwell failures (failures with stairwell system that allow you in and out of the stairwell) on the same days as 2-3 fire alarms are going off. Response from Urbana, "No negligence on our part." They do not care about your safety. They definitely do not care about your comfort. They care about locking in your money.
There is a fire alarm accessible to people on the street and it is always pulled. Management does nothing about the issue. This has been ongoing for months.

I will NOT be renewing. Current management is good, but fire alarms go off all the time. 5 times in the past 2 weeks, from the same lady that pulls it, but nothing is being done. I've lived here for nearly two years. There was a system issue with the fire alarms summer of 2020, and since there have been people pulling it, all hours of the day and night. Prior to me moving in, I knew alarms went off regularly here but didn't expect it to be this bad.

I wish I enjoyed living here - but being right on one of the busiest streets in Ballard it gets extremely loud and noisy! Also lots of pollutants/dust from cars since its facing a busy road. Fire alarms also go off pretty often

I felt like I was walking on to a movie set and into a dreamland.  It had everything I could have wanted, a wonderful community and pet-friendly policies.  In the heart of the city, I can keep my big dog!   There is a rooftop garden and solarium, as well as a beautiful gym and easy access to public transportation. 

This will be my first apartment in the big city, and I'm a little nervous, but finding this apartment has been wonderful.

I rented a one-bedroom at Mysa for 18 months. I recently moved out so that I could live closer to work. I had an excellent experience living here.

Positives:
- Very new building, well designed and constructed. I didn't have any major maintenance issues. The apartment interiors look very nice and the appliances were mostly good quality.
- The front desk, maintenance, and management staff were always friendly and easy to get in contact with. I never had any negative interactions with anyone from Epic Asset Management.
- Kitchen layout was great and functional, with plenty of cabinet and storage space.
- Vinyl plank flooring was durable and great for pets and also looked pretty nice.
-Good sound proofing, I could rarely hear noise from neighboring apartments. Noise still comes in from the hall but not much gets through the walls.
- It was easy to make payments and submit maintenance requests through their online portal.
- Convenient trash and recycling chutes on every floor.
- The secured package lockers are great, I never had any problems with theft.
- Extremely quick access to transit and businesses on Lake City way.
- Move out was easy and painless. Many other management companies will take most of your damage deposit for no good reason, but Epic only took a small and reasonable amount.

Negatives:
- There is paid parking only and not enough spaces for every unit to have a spot. Only one permit was available per apartment. Some of the parking spaces are really small and at times unusable if people don't park perfectly in the lines, so occasionally you can't find a spot in the garage even if you have a permit.
- Street parking is competitive on the blocks by Mysa so you may have to park a few blocks away if you aren't using the garage.
- Bums often hang out in the parking lot on the north side of the building. The lot is separated from Mysa by a high fence so it's not a big security issue, but could get pretty loud and disruptive at times. There are some major encampments a few blocks away.
- Wifi was easy to set up from the pre installed routers and usually worked well, but would occasionally slow down a lot. Maybe due to interference from neighboring apartments?
- Washer/dryer were a cheap top-loading combo model that were loud and rattled around when in use. Worked fine but the noise was pretty bad.
- I was in a south facing, upper floor apartment and it got quite hot in the summer. There is no AC in the apartments so I got myself a small portable unit.

I was excited to move to this building but it has been a HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT so far, primarily because of two issues and the management has not solved those effectively:

1. Lots of noise comes in from the bedroom window: The building maintenance keeps on saying that it’s not something that they can solve. So they have just taped it up. When the window vendor came to inspect it, he apparently couldn’t hear any noise even though all the other people in the room could. And he said that there is nothing that he could do. DO NOT MOVE HERE IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO. Do not be fooled by the seemingly nice units. It's not worth it

Absolute garbage apartments

The living space is unbearable. The landlord takes weeks to get back to you. The sink in the room is smaller than my foot and I can't even use it because of its position on the wall. Make this your very last resort.

The Clearwater Apartments is located in Seattle in the Capitol Hill district. It is conveniently located a few blocks from Seattle University, Swedish Medical Center and Harborview Medical Center. I would have to say everything is within a 10-20 minute walk to the grocery store, Pike St., even the International District. I do not have a car and don't really need one unless you like adventuring outside the city, but it does make everything easier. There is not a lot of street parking around the area due to nearby construction taking it up, but you require a zone 7 pass or else you'll get a ticket. The apartment has their own garage and the last I heard it was $100 a month additionally. The mail boxes are located as you enter through the secured gate - which they will give you a pass code for. Large packages generally get delivered to the back office of the property manager and you can sign them out. Most days they will be there around 9-5:30 PM but depending on how they feel they could leave early or go on extended lunch breaks. During the weekends packages might be placed by the mailboxes since the office is closed and people generally leave other's packages alone. 
Now the apartment it's self is alright, it's relatively new and good for the money. When I was moving in the apartment was not that clean as I could find hair (dog or human?) all over the apartment - in the bathroom, in drawers and in the refrigerator. There were still scratches on the wall, a shabby painting job (unsure if it was the apartment company or the previous tenant). The unit comes with a washer and dryer that is pretty good, my dryer was a little messed up in the beginning with rattling parts and the previous tenant duct taped god knows what. The kitchen does not come with a microwave and has adequate shelf space and counter space. It comes with a dishwasher as well which functions. 
My unit comes with a "veranda" except I'm on the ground floor and has  a double door that extends out, but it has no screen and bugs and what not can come in. This is actually the only airflow into my apartment as the window would be where this door is. So at night it can get a little hot considering I don't want to leave a door open through the night. 
The bathroom is alright, I was missing another towel rack and they did a shabby job covering up the screw holes. The bathtub is fine except that somehow parts of the tub was chipped and dented.
It's a good place to live for the price and location.

I attempted to tour this building and on my way to the appointment, I got in a car accident. I informed the landlord of what happened right away and she would not let me reschedule. She (and her very rude co-worker) assumed I was lying. I was told, "we need to save appointment slots for serious renters". I offered to show them the traffic camera footage of the accident since I had it pulled to show my insurance what happened, but it felt as though they were so dead-set on making a point that they're the ones in control and holding the power that they wouldn't even look at the proof of what happened... must have had a few no-show dates in their days. Luckily I found a better place in a way better area, just be aware if you are considering renting, usually a management team like this will treat tenants worse than they treat prospective renters. Once they lock you in a lease they can be as rude as they want. Looking back on it, the whole situation was a blessing in disguise.

Living in the city can be expensive, but this property is the perfect fit! Not only are all utilities included with these gorgeous studios, but you are walking distance from tons of great local restaurants, pharmacy, movie theater, grocery store, coffee shops, and so much more! You can also enjoy the rooftop area, it has a propane BBQ grill, outside seating, and A BEAUTIFUL VIEW of Seattle! This community is a true gem!
Cockroach problem, severe mold problem, unhelpful management that doesn't fix anything, garbage everywhere, stolen packages, fire alarm goes off all the time, building smells and is unsanitary.

Since Coast has taken over this property their have been a lot of changes both inside and out. All Units have new appliances, update cabinets and hardware it's a nice modern look. The new manager and maintenance staff are really great and easy to work with. I am excited about seeing all the upcoming changes they are making.

Hidden is the way it should stay until updates are done. The building is outdated but holds some charm. The One bedrooms are spacious with plenty of room for two people to be comfortable in. The kitchen is adequate but the appliances need updating. Current rent rates are high for what this community offers.

With over 40 units per building they only have 5 washing machines. Sometimes they break making the problem worse. You have to pay a 6$ “connivence fee” every time you make a payment so expect to add about 10% of a months rent per year. My key broke inside they door so they charge a $50 a key. Moral of the story this is a hotel apartment that’s only good for a month or 2 max in emergencies any minor inconvenience will make you pay massively out of pocket

It is brand new. It just opened in March 2022.

It is in a great location near Chase Bank and across the street from Target and CVS. It is walking distance from Northgate Light Rail.

I have called them multiple times and left my name and number but they never reply to my emails or call me back. They probably just lost a future tenant. Office says it opens 9-6 weekdays. Called them multiple times during their business hours, the automated phone system tells us to call back during their business hours (interesting). Awesome experience.

I recently moved in here, and so far, my experience has been very positive. The application process was smooth, and the leasing person was friendly and helpful. The apartment itself is clean, spacious, and well-maintained. I appreciate the modern amenities like the gym and pool, and the grounds are always tidy. The manager is responsive to maintenance requests, and I’ve had no issues with noise or security. Overall, it’s a great place to call home, and I’m looking forward to living here long-term!

UPDATE: They also towed my vehicle from the complex, less than 24 hours after I moved it there. Do NOT live here.

This place is a cheap band-aid on the bullet wound of the apartment it used to be (Linden Square I believe) but a coat of paint and some new mismatched cabinets isn’t going to do it. The location is super convenient. It's very close to the bus stop and multiple grocery stores. Also, the girls in the leasing office are always really nice and typically get back on maintenance requests very quickly. They're making a ton of improvements all the time.

I've been residing here for work and school for a few years, and I'm thrilled to announce that I'll be relocating this summer. Unfortunately, BonaVista is a poorly managed company that shows little concern for your well-being. The building experiences frequent break-ins by individuals struggling with addiction, and they often loiter in the lobby. The staff does not take adequate measures to address noise issues from neighboring apartments. Additionally, they may attempt to persuade you to sign a new lease after going month-to-month, claiming it will save you money, but it often results in higher costs in the long run. Your best interests are not a priority, and even as a good tenant, you may find yourself being taken advantage of. Limited internet options are available, with the "free" internet being subpar at best. It's best to avoid this place altogether.

Honestly ending my lease here is the best decision I’ve made since moving to Seattle two years ago. Staff is cold, unfriendly, condescending, and unavailable majority of the time. If you need something fixed don’t count on them to respond right away, if at all. I went two weeks without being able
To lock my door since the pin pad died, and the toilet paper holder has been consistently broken since I moved in. Won’t be shocked if they charge me to fix it either.

Honestly save your money and move into a comparably priced but much larger studio apartment or 1 bedroom at another property. This place isn’t worth the money.

Can't have your own internet (you HAVE to use the really bad community WiFi that not only is slow but randomly disconnects you all the time) and if that isn't the case, then the office people are entirely unhelpful in figuring out who you can use and how to set it up. In fact, the girl pretty much said "I don't know" when the tech was here trying to help me. You can hear everything going on in every apartment around you, which is super great (sarcasm). My bathroom has a public bathroom style sink with no counterspace at all, making it next to useless. My apartment has the weirdest shape that makes it impossible to have my full size bed in any sort of logical spot.

The rooftop is pretty cool, and the view is a bargain. Considering the local type of traffic, you couldn't ask for better. It's great, not perfect.

relax, its not a forever home. a comfortable living section.

It was exactly what I needed: a decent space on a tight budget.  I've been happy here during my lease but plan to move at the end of it.

The concessions packages might seem difficult to understand at first but are actually pretty solid.  The leasing staff was super helpful when I signed.

The photos misrepresent the common spaces.  The gym is smaller than the photo but it's nice enough. The "game" area is just the lobby, not at all what I would call a real common space. The roof is nice though.

Unit appliances and condition are generally good. 

The free/included "High-speed internet" is overall pretty good but would get either throttled or overloaded at times. Just about every night right at 9 I'd start having serious issues streaming from live sites (like Twitch).  And it would happen occasionally randomly during the day. If you stream games, be ready to pay for the higher speed.

Most of the reviews mention that parking is a huge issue... This is definitely still true. With the light rail and surrounding apartment construction, it's likely to remain that way at least another year or two.  I consistently found parking a few blocks west but it means you might be walking alone at night. 

Anyway, overall, it's a really great transition option if that's what you need. Also probably good if you're not working from home.

I live here and it does not look anything like the photos advertised here, don't let that fool you. The rooftop is ok, the gym is small, and the PARKING IS TERRIBLE!! I've gotten towed twice. Save yourself the hassle and don't live here

This apartment complex has exceeded my expectations! Tara, the apartment manager, is always helpful. The neighborhood itself feels very safe, and the residents who live in the complex are generally quiet and friendly. If you're looking for a place in the Wallingford/Fremont area, this will likely fit your needs.

My partner and I lived at Milan for one year and found the property manager Tara was not clear with communication. We had issues with the facilities that were not properly managed. We were told that we would get a "free month" of parking which ended up being "the remainder of the month free," which was 4 days instead of what it had originally been marketed to us as.

There was also a time where we did have access to water for more than 24 hours and they were not responsive with offering us a place to use the bathroom. It was frustrating to try and be patient with a property management company that did not seem to care at all about the people living in the building.

I had a fantastic opportunity to call this my home sweet home for 4 years and hands down- there is no place like Milan! A hybrid of modern and historic building, this place is a Seattle Emerald treasure. The roof top is very relaxing with amazing downtown views. The gal at the rental office was incredibly nice. Thank you for the amazing experience.

My husband and I lived at the Milan Apartments for three years from 2017-2020 and we'd highly recommend it. The manager, Tara is so kind, responsive to maintenance requests, and proactive with keeping the property well maintained.  The people who live in this building are very friendly as well and most people have pets, which is fun for us. The amenities like washer and dryer, good decks, and rooftop deck have all been features that we've enjoyed. The proximity of Aurora was the only downside but is what made it affordable for us to live in such a great neighborhood. Our bedroom was facing the road and I have worn earplugs pretty consistently for the last couple of years for sleep. My husband is a heavier sleeper and has no issues.

I have lived here about 2 years and so far I find it’s a good place to live. Apartment is spacious with gorgeous views of the east side  mountain,lake union & downtown. Wallingford town is a 5 minute walk to grocery, shops, restaurants & easy bus access to travel downtown for some fun adventures. I would recommend this place to any of my friends just as I am recommending it to you, the readers of my review.

The Milan apartments are a great place to live. Whether you are single or if you have a family. It is close to many great schools and is centered around many important locations.The apartment is located in a very nice Wallingford neighborhood with walking distance to shops, bus stops and easy access to I-5 and 99. The staff is attentive and helpful. Maintenance is on top of any request. They have an excellent rooftop/barbecue area. This is a great place to live.
I've lived at Milan since last September. Great rooftop, quiet neighborhood, and administrative staff that's always welcoming and quick to address any issues. Price is incredibly reasonable as well!

I have lived here for over a year. 
The apartments are in a great place. Very close to Restaurants & Green Lake.
Very friendly environment with a nice rooftop area. I am happy & I hope you will be, too!

With misleading information, it is apparent that the management isn't keen on details...and not so considerate of potential tenants when they're looking for a decent place to live in. Thumbs down.

I have been thoroughly impressed during my time at Milan. The location, apartment, staff, cleaning, rooftop and common areas are all fantastic. Having done a significant amount of research before moving in, I believe the rent is also very reasonable for what you get. Highly recommended!

I know the staff went through some changes in the past but the Manager now is very amazing. She knows how to handle people with the best services that you won't find anywhere else. Excellent customer service skills.... Quiet, Clean, nice people around, great commute almost to all destinations within the Seattle area, especially Green-Lake & all the shops. Great value for the location.

I did not live at Milan Apartments, but I toured it looking for a 1 bedroom. The pictures listed are only for a handful of renovated units on the bottom floor that are very small compared to the pictures. The rest of the building is falling apart and the outside hallways into each unit look like they've never been cleaned!

I lived in one of their apartments and was truly sad to leave. The location is amazing, and their office is right around the corner. Management was one of the best experiences I've ever had  timely, maintenance was always fixed and they were extremely easy to get in contact with. They are also very personable and get to know who is living with in their units.
Love it. Amazing units, tons of amenities, and incredibly helpful staff. I've had no issues with maintenance, noise  and with staff. Friendly neighbors, good location.

This place is absolutely a gem! Everyone in the office is so helpful and nice and maintenance always comes within 24 hours. The whole team is amazing and makes living there a breeze. The grounds are beautiful and always maintained. They have an abundance of amenities and activities available throughout the month every month which are always a blast!
Fantastic residences. Great team, amenities, service, cleanliness. It honestly doesn't get better. They take great care of their residents.

Amazing place to live. Great views. Delicious restaurants are a short walk away. I love being able to walk across the building. There is always something fun going on because of the location. It's also a beautiful building with helpful and friendly staff!

This was a perfect place to live, particularly because it was located directly across from my law school. Many good restaurants are located nearby, and many of them give a facilities to residents. The staff is friendly, and I really enjoy having a gym in the residence. It's extremely convenient. It is worth checking out!

My time living in Bode 88 has been a living nightmare. From the moment I moved in, I IMMEDIATELY encountered a series of problems that made my stay here unbearable. 

First and foremost, mail theft was rampant within the complex. Countless times, I found myself missing important packages, which were undoubtedly stolen and found on the street. Despite raising this concern with the management on multiple occasions, no effective action was taken to address the issue. There is a camera for "security purposes" but I was told by maintenance that it doesn't even work. 

Additionally, the presence of tenants constantly fixing their cars on the road within the complex posed a severe hazard. Oil spills, exposed machinery, and discarded car parts became a common sight. This not only created an eyesore but also endangered the safety of pedestrians and residents alike. No tangible improvements were ever made.

Furthermore, communication from the management was abysmal. It seemed as though the management team lacked any interest in addressing the concerns and needs of the residents. Multiple unanswered calls and text messages made this apparent towhoever the leasing agent was ... AT THE TIME. 

Adding to the chaos, there was a constant rotation of management staff. With each transition, it felt like starting from scratch, and N O T H I N G ever seemed to get better. 

Lastly, the overall cleanliness of the living environment was appalling. The courtyard was neglective, while the hallways were stained and dusty year round. It seemed as though no effort was made to maintain even BASIC standards of cleanliness and hygiene. 

In conclusion don't live here. I would strongly advise anyone considering renting here to think twice and explore other options. The quality of life in this apartment complex is far below the standards one would expect, and it is simply NOT, I repeat ... NOT ... worth the frustrations and disappointments that come with it.

staff here do not care about you. buildings built too fast. Too many maintenance problems, leasing office will not get back to you until 6 months later

Wonderful units, great amenities.  Staff is always available for your needs.
