Great building, modern touches, and Leed certified efficiency.

What I like: 1 bedroom is a good size. Bright and airy. The gym is great, it's plenty big. Dog washing station and dog treats in the front and back entrances. Storage unit is behind my parking spot. Across the street from QFC. 2 bars in walking distance. Red Mill burgers. Whole Foods is down the road and Ballard is close by.

What I don't like: So many dogs, the back entry permanently smells like wet dog. Units do not have garbage disposals or ice makers - I thought this was weird for a brand new building. The building's roof top deck is actually on the 2nd floor and is often taken over by younger college aged tenants.

Details: Street parking is free but can be hard to find. As of 9/2015 I pay $200 per month for 1 parking spot and a storage unit.

Amenities and efficiency is the hallmark of Slate Apartments. I love my apartment complex because there is a 24 hour gym, several wifi-enabled community areas, an outdoor patio.patio, cable TV rooms, parking, and a great view of a soccer and baseball field in our front yard. It is especially wonderful in summer where I live because it stays cool with my clean concrete floors and my high-efficiency fixtures including a built-in washer-dryer and energy star refrigerator. Because the building was built less than three years ago, I am able to enjoy nearly brand new everything in a well-designed, modern, efficient, and LEED awarded apartment building.

The "Terrible Corner" in my title is deliberate. Belltown is awesome. I would still live their if my girlfriend wanted to. But the corner of 3rd and Bell is the worst corner North of pioneer square, in my opinion. Possibly rivaled by 3rd and Pike.

I lived at Moda for two years. I have nothing but positive things to say about the leasing and maintenance staff. All of my requests for repairs were handled immediately and it was very easy to get face time in the office. If you would like any of your security deposit back upon move-out make sure you request to be present during their walk through. They will charge for any imperfection in the apartment (normal wear and tear not considered).

My main complaint with Moda is a result of the above market rent in a sub-par section of Belltown. I moved from the East coast. I love city life. Belltown is the most walkable neighborhood in Seattle and always has a great energy about it. That being said, the location of Moda in particular is overrun with homeless individuals. I cannot overstate how much the drug scene has enveloped 3rd and Bell. Go anywhere else in Belltown and you're fine, down by Olympic Sculpture Park, near the bars on 2nd, over towards Seattle Center, down by Amazon country, wherever. But 3rd and Bell is basically a safe consumption zone. There was a shooting a block over two weeks before I moved out. Twice, I had homeless dudes knock at my apartment door asking for money.

I appreciate the Moda Team's hard work. The units are comically overpriced. Honestly, for as much as they charge, there should be a permanent lobby attendant. I can only imagine they get people to move in from out of town and entice them with the low security deposit (my story to a tee). Whatever works I guess. If you move in to Moda, just be prepared to move out in a year or two.

Easiest rental process I ever had- I drove cross-country for a job and the Moda leasing people were very helpful over email and had me approved and leased in one day. The interiors are new and clean and I've never had an issue finding a parking spot. The roof top is hands-down the best amenity and even has a separate part for dogs. The only drawback is the sound if you're in a unit facing 3rd. You get used to the bus noises but we also here a lot of homeless rants and drunk Belltown bros "Woooo!"ing. When my lease is up I'll probably stay with Moda but pick a unit on the quieter side.
Moda is a nice community for people new to the city. The building has cleaning problems in general

This is the perfect building if you work at South Lake Union; but want to experience the city AFTER work.The common areas are well maintained and the staff is incredibly helpful. Unlike other apartments in this area, it has a large rooftop courtyard with a grill, firepit and chaise lounges. All the apartment finishings and appliances are top-notch!

A guy from the  leasing office told me "I have to end this conversation because you're not listening to me" over the phone... I called to ask what they have available, and what the units are like, what amenities do they have- all fair questions. However, the person on the phone seemed very unhappy to answer any of those questions, and blamed me for not looking at their apartment.com advertisement. However many ads are for a certain unit and most times if you ask information for a specific unit it might be different than the advertised one. Especially since they say the advertised one is actually already not available.....I also explained how my move in dates are flexible and that if a studio is available at a later time it would be okay. Then he said I wasn't listening to him... Never had any issue with any leasing agents before, very wired conversation... I don't know why he has an attitude at work, did he have a bad day or something? very hard to work with even for just requiring some information. Can't believe how it would be like to live there....

Though I did not end up renting from Skyline House, my experience with Olivia was the most welcoming and human experience I had while apartment searching. She was friendly, clear, and prompt and drove to the complex at the drop of a hat to show me another apartment. I will absolutely look at renting from here the next time I move.

Excellent, easy access, quiet neighborhood. Please consider becoming a tenant if you desire a quiet in-city, older building, kind of experience.
Please don’t be convinced that your neighbors “can’t hear you”. No different than any other shared walls you’ve experienced.
Yall lie, you raise the rent without fixing any issues, alarms go off, hot water doesn't work. I'm still waiting on the front door to be fixed and it's been 8 months. NO!
The manager is terrible and doesn't care about the property and how to run it.

Living at Sheridan Beach Terrace has been such an amazing experience. Of course there's the view which is next level. What really makes living here so enjoyable though is the community. Neighbors are friendly and say hi. When I moved in everyone was so welcoming. Bradley, the community manager, goes above and beyond for the residents. He actually makes it feel like a community and values the residents input. On special occasions he will leave out treat bags which I find extremely endearing. Both Bradley and the maintenance team are super responsive and help in anyway they can. Could not recommend this place enough!

Since moving in at Sheridan Beach Terrace in 2018, the apartment complex has shifted to a new management, and there have been lots of updates and improvements to the building and grounds. The maintenance team is prompt, courteous, and efficient. The courtyard is pretty unique with its landscaping and a multi-story waterfall that pleasantly cancels out any noise from Bothell Way.  The rooftop patio is wonderful for hosting guests and watching seaplanes out of Kenmore Air. UV Residential really encourages a sense of community, which I appreciate. It’s refreshing to see community get-togethers (which are socially-distanced and responsible) on a regular basis to combat the dreaded “Seattle Freeze”. My neighbors are quiet and respectful. Parking is a little tight, and the driveway can be icy and slick in bad weather, but other than this, it’s a great place to live!
I lived here for 2 years and the property is very quiet and they have the best pool!

I've been renting at Watercrest for a little over a year now and I'm counting down the days until the lease is up.

Top Complaints:
Mail theft. Mailboxes were broken into and packages are constantly stolen. The mail theft is so bad that the USPS has refused service to all 46 units in Building A. I have to go pick up my mail at the Post Office, which is extremely inconvenient. The apartment management's advice is to get Amazon packages routed to a locker and continue picking up mail from the Post Office. Management could not give me next steps on how they were trying to improve the situation. This building has no security, residential background checks are nonexistent, or both. 
 
Attempted truck theft. Someone broke into my spouse's truck, stole a lot of small items plus tried to jam something into the ignition (didn't work) and pulled a panel below the steering wheel and fiddled with the wires (also didn't work).  We had to pay $1,000 to get everything fixed and repaired. Management was notified and did absolutely nothing. 

Constant laundry issues. About half of the time I wash and dry my clothes, I have "extras" that someone has snuck into my laundry. I thoroughly check the washer and dryer before I put my clothes in and I've never caught someone messing with my clothes. My spouse and I have also had gross residue on our clothes after using the washer/dryer - like gum/oil or something was left in the unit. Also, machines are out of service sometimes without a note, so you pay the $2 but don't get to use the machine.

Shoddy appliances. During the first 2 months of living in this apartment, I had my stove replaced with a stove from a different unit TWICE. Maintenance was nice, but outdated appliances need replaced instead of shuffled around. 

Other issues that haven't directly impacted me:
I've seen three dead rats outside of the building that take more than two days for maintenance to clean up.  There's a trash can next to one of the gates that is constantly overflowing. This week there was snow and ice and management put a bucket of salt out and told us to salt the walkways ourselves.  

I've noticed at least 3 units flood bad enough that water goes into the hallway. I'm fortunate that this hasn't happened to our unit, but it seems like it must be a matter of time.  

The mail was the tipping point. Management is doing zero and if you HAVE to live here, avoid building A like the plague.

We were charged for things that we had bought new, repaired and cleaned. They even claim that their team members were bitten by fleas when in fact, we have never encountered fleas my whole life living at watercrest or anywhere else!!

My roommate and I have lived here for about a year now, and we love it. The price is not bad, covered parking isn't too expensive (get one while you can), the apartments are such a nice size compared to most places in WA, and in general the layout is great and very cozy.  Alyssa, Nicholas (who has moved to another property), Andrea, and the maintenance team are GREAT! We've had a few minor issues (i.e. the sliding screen door falling off its track, the laundry door knob loosening, etc.) the team has been so great at communicating and fixing problems in a timely manner. We've only had one major issue however, the team was quick to assist us and very helpful with taking care us of and solving the issue. Despite COVID restrictions and not being able to workout or use the pool last summer (obviously not their fault lol) I would recommend this property to anyone and everyone looking to move to the Lake Forest Park area. If you've come this far in my review, hopefully this helps with your decision on where to move. Thank you Watercrest team, we are happy to call this place home.

No matter what they tell you, parking is a nightmare if you don't pay for a spot. In my building, the hallways always smell like mold/mildew, since I have developed lung problems, I often worry about the amount of mold in the building. The rent increases by a large amount every year, while the services provided decreases. The water bill will occasionally double in amount with no explanation. We found mouse droppings in the outdoor grill, which is not appetizing. This place is definitely not worth the money as far as I'm concerned. I finally couldn't take it anymore and had to move. I do not recommend.

Sadly I am writing a mixed review of my 19 months at Watercrest.  They were great as far as giving me a good deal to move in, and the initial deposit and move in costs were lower than most.  

I never had any significant issues in my time there, other than occasional reserved parking problems which were handled by management in a reasonable time frame.  (There is inadequate unreserved parking so be prepared to pay for a reserved spot if you want to make sure you have a spot in the lot)

Likewise the process of moving out was relatively easy, however, I was not impressed with the "move out charges" that I was assessed against my security deposit.  I left the apartment much cleaner than when I moved in, however, it was deemed necessary to charge me a cleaning fee of $75, a carpet cleaning fee of $60 (even though my very last act before returning the keys was to rent a carpet cleaning machine and clean the carpets in the entire apartment), as well as a$50 painting fee, despite the fact I made sure to use wall hangers that did not damage the paint.

As I said, my time there was uneventful and my apartment was a decent size for the money.  Just be prepared for some questionable fees when moving on.

I've been living at Jackson Greens for about 6 months now, before that I was subleasing a smaller more expensive apartment in Capitol Hill, and after that this has been a great way to integrate into Seattle. The price is affordable especially when looking at other apartments in the area and downtown. There is a bus line that goes to the University of Washington Link Light rail and from there you can get wherever you need downtown. There is also a Safeway, Target, 24 Hour Fitness, and a mall less than 10 minutes away by car and even a relatively short walk away. There are also many things to do more north in Shoreline. I like the feeling of still being in the city but enough away from downtown to feel the comfort of being at home. As far as the apartment complex, it is unique for a Seattle apartment to have a lot where guests can park and the paid parking within the complex costs less than half of what I was paying at my smaller apartment in Capitol Hill. It's also rare for an apartment complex in Seattle to have a normal sized washer and dryer in unit. Any maintenance requests that I fill out have been taken care of in either the same day or next day. The online portal makes those requests as well as paying rent easy and stress free. In general, living at the Jackson Greens Apartments has made the transition to Seattle easy and stress free.
Like this apartment, I like my backyard, and bus line is right outside the apartment, very nice location.

I looked at several studios and micro studios before I decided on montisi and montisi is the best. It’s clean and quite. All residents I’ve met this pas year have been respectful and kind. A lot of micro studios are glorified dorm rooms but that’s not the case here. I’ve lived here for a year and am sad to leave. Only didn’t renew my lease because I got a new job too far north to make the morning commute worth it. 10/10 would recommend to a friend who worked either downtown or west Seattle.

There is so much to recommend the location. You can walk to coffee, restaurants, trader joe's QFC or Safeway. Studios are small-these are of course small-but they are sleek, well maintained and modern (just opened last year). Utilities are included in your rent-so only one bill to worry about each month. They also include wi-fi for your first lease term (takes the sting out of moving costs). Neighbors are nice, quiet great walkable neighborhood very close to the bridge if you want to be downtown. There is lots of space in your kitchen and bath to store your stuff-great cabinet space. Closet space is okay for a studio and bathroom is pretty good sized for a studio. There are nooks that easily have space for a full or queen sized bed and space for bookcases plus table and chairs-didn't feel like stuff had to be crowded in. Windows are well placed so the room is bright. Nice lounge in lobby, with TV for while you do laundry...bike storage-secured with a pin code and INSIDE is a nice touch. Laundry is also inside downstarirs-and machines can be operated with an app or cash.
Latitude is so well cared for and you see the staff (Kara, Brett and James) go the extra mile for the people that live here.

Pluses: Brand new apartment building, all wood floors, awesome roof an very pet friendly. Well located in lower Queen Anne. Dog park in walking distance and myrtle Edwards trail just down the road. 

Negatives: I've never known an elevator to break more frequently and loud alley

FOR SENIORS AND IT IS SORTA OF NICE.THE BUILDING IS SORTA OF NICETHE TENTES ARE FRIENDLY .THE BUILDING IS ON THE BUS LINE WHICH IS NICE AND CLOSE TO THE GROCERYS STORE. THEY HAVE PARKING WHICH YOU PAY FOR BY THE MONTH . APARTMENTS ARE NICE .

We liked the size and layout of our unit (a two bedroom) for the most part and the location cannot be beat. The management also seemed to make a lot of COVID hardship accommodations and give people with financial difficulty some options. Other than that, not much good to say. The unit which faced Stone Way was incredibly loud as were the noises between units. The building material did not block or absorb any noises whatsoever. The building is clean and amenities up to date but, not luxury, so it made no sense that dogs weren’t allowed. Management would take days to respond to emails if at all and the place was constantly being broken into.

I've lived in Howard Park apartments for awhile now and can't wait to get out. The most horrible part is there are wood floors throughout all the units so unless you're on the top floor it is extremely loud. Additionally, the building has been broken into countless times with packages stolen. The management does not seem to care nor do they come up with alternative solutions to help prevent the break ins. Finally, it's really hard to get an email response from management. Not happy here at all, can't wait to move. 
There's also a homeless man who lives outside the building who is constantly yelling and singing. He has woken us up numerous times and makes it hard to sit in my apartment and read or do a quiet activity because I can just hear his screams.
I called them over and over many days but no one responds. I even went to check out the units but nobody there either

These apartments are teetering on the brink of being condemned.  The staffing is petty  and unqualified and the tenants are treated like less than and with a high level of disrespect.  The hallway carpets are 20 years old (or more) and are disgusting and rotting in place.  Just an embarrassment.  The tenants are given a tiny refrigerator that does not even accommodate a gallon of milk.  If your self-esteem is already damaged by poverty and homelessness, this place will just heap on an even worse state of mind.  Maintenance is third-rate, staff is unprofessional.  and rude.  And the staff takes zero responsibility for the dangerous tenants that they house.  So it is not only disgusting, but also highly unsafe.  The SPD has even joked that they should open a satellite office here.  Horrible place to live.  The Josephinum is better than sleeping on a park bench.  But just barely.  Abandon All Hope Those who Enter Here.

This is a good place to get back on your feet if you have become homeless.  Good staff on hand for helping anyone in need of a home.  A fairly safe environment to get a fresh start.  The apartments themselves are quite large for one person living spaces.  Decent kitchen, separate bathroom and adaptable to roommate living quarter styling.  If you need help in the seattle area to get back on your feet this is one of the best places.  plenty of community events happen here for nice family get togethers and the staff help out to ensure safe living space on a monthly bases.  Truly a place to help the body and the soul.

The building was recently remodeled, and all remodeled units were prices as "luxury apartments," well beyond comparable market rates. The problem is - nothing about this building or the apartments is luxurious. The remodels are an upgrade, but substandard materials were used. The building has zero amenities, and the units themselves have cheap cabinetry, flooring, and appliances. Not to mention, the building is situated between two group homes and half way houses, which means every time you come home, you get to trip over junkies doing fenty on the streets. Adding insult to injury, the building recently adopted an "amenity fee" of $60 a month. This is for -- wait for it -- the luxury of having a mailbox and a package locker, and internet (which is the worst service I have ever had). Long story short, many great places to live on Capitol Hill. Pass this place up.

My girlfriend and I had an extremely complicated move-in coming from Charleston, SC. The leasing staff and especially Jose, the maintenance manager, helped us with organizing a temporary parking space and making sure the apartment was ready for when we arrived. The location has been ideal to access amazing restaurants and work. They are also pet friendly and the apartments are sound proof.

I've lived here for a little over a year now and the management is incredible and friendly and accommodating to ALL of my needs. Whenever something needs fixing it usually gets done the same day! The maintenance is impeccable and the pool and outdoor grill are such a nice luxury. My neighbors are respectful and I've never had a single issue with finances or contracts/leasing. They even leave out fresh baked cookies every now and then for the tenants! It's in an ideal location across the street from groceries and the mall and food and entertainment within walking distance. Couldn't be happierr.

My apartment is in a perfect location. It's right across from the first mall in America, the Northgate Mall in North Seattle. Along the side between the mall and the apartment building is a large park with a skateboard area, basketball court, grass, outdoor exercise fitness area, and plenty of park benches and chairs.

Right across from my apartment is Target, Best Buy, and fast food. A block away is 24 Hour Fitness SuperSport. Two blocks away is the library. Three blocks away is QFC, a large grocery store, and Walgreens. I don't need a car where I live because I could walk to everything or take a bus. My apartment building has a huge parking lot that wraps around the building giving everyone plenty of space to park free.

Next to my apartment building which is located between 3rd Avenue and 5th Avenue on 5th Avenue is the bus stop where bus 41 stops. Bus 41 is a double bus and there are anywhere between 4 and 10 buses an hour, depending on need. It only takes 15 minutes to get downtown on bus 41. I can take the bus as a senior for $1.00, get off at University Station, ride the elevator up into Benaroya Hall and go to the symphony or walk a block and go to a Broadway play or the Seattle Art Museum or walk to the Aquarium on the waterfront, or stop at Pike Place Market. If I want to go to SeaTac and catch a plane, I change to the train at university station and continue all the way to SeaTac.

Seattle has everything. Perfect weather. All the arts and cultural activities that is found in a major world city. Seattle is one of the fastest growing cities in the United States and people from around the world come to live and work in peace together. I live in a neighborhood in Northgate where 1/3 of the population are new immigrants from around the world and for many English is their second language. 

My apartment building has a large pool in the center with grass, tables and chairs, and a space for barbeques. With a secure entrance, I feel safe.

My apartment is spacious and open with high ceilings. It is very quiet on the third floor. During the winter months, I rarely have to turn on the heat. My kitchen has plenty of space. 

My front room is huge with a large open area and sliding glass doors that open onto a large balcony with room to grow plants, and l have room for lounge chairs. I have two bedrooms that are spacious. The master bedroom has a spacious walk-in closet and storage. My 1 ½ bathroom has everything I need.

This is the first apartment that I've been in as an independent, instead of living with family. It's close to not only the shopping mall, but the transit center, which means getting downtown for work or otherwise is easy. There's plenty of restaurants nearby as well! There's a swimming pool and a public bbq grill for those clear summer days, and the landlady is incredibly nice! They're even remodeling the entire place to make it even better! I enjoy living here and my only non-issue issue is the price of the wash machine and dryer to use here, since there's a public laundromat on each floor. It's definitely a great place to stay for someone like me without a car since it's so easy to get to a lot of places.

Management has proven friendly and reliable during my two years here, always greeting with a smile and keeping a steady supply of fresh baked cookies in the office. Maintenance issues are quickly addressed by the on-site handyman and management is proactive about following-up to make sure things are still running smoothly after a problem has been addressed. 

The Court features a heated outdoor pool and community BBQ. Hubbard Homestead park is immediately adjacent to the  apartment complex and has a jogging track, basketball court, outdoor gym area and skate park. It's wonderful having so many outdoor activities nearby!

The Court is conveniently located less than 2 minutes from I-5 and two blocks from Northgate mall.  For those who prefer community transit the Northgate Transit center is less than a 5 min bus ride away and from there you will have easy access to routes that can take you to anywhere in the Seattle metro area, Bellevue, Lynnwood, Sea-Tac, and beyond. 

I've never enjoyed living at an apartment complex as much as I have here at The Court and I hope to remain here for years to come!

Where do I start. This place Loud at the expense of the residence. Management cares very little if if you work at night or the noise they make at 8 a.m. in the morning. It's a constant thing. They don't even care about inconveniencing you by parking in your space that you have to pay for. Packages get stolen from this apartment. The manager does nothing about it. Constantly leaves the door open so anybody can walk in. The wall seem to be really thin. Not to mention the constant rent raises.
